tom_tat: In the same sentence, at Mount Bo Da Lac Ca (Potalaka), an island in the south of India, is considered to be the place where Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara often resides. We can be sure of that, because of the Thien Thu Thie Sutra
noi_dung:
The Great Compassion Mantra is drawn from the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes Sutra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Great Perfection and Unhindered Great Compassion

In the same sentence, at Mount Bo Da Lac Ca (Potalaka), an island in the south of India, is considered the place where Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara often resides. We can be sure of that, because the Thien Thu Thien Nhan Sutra opens with the familiar saying of Ananda, "Thus I heard", as well as through the question and answer content between Ananda and the World-Honored One, recorded in the sutra.

In this dharma assembly, Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, out of great compassion for sentient beings, wants "sentient beings to be happy, to be free of all diseases, to live long, to be rich, to destroy all serious evil karma, to be far from obstacles, to increase the merit of good dharma, to achieve all good roots, to destroy all fears, to quickly fill all their desires" and said the Mantra. this.

He gave the reason for the birth of the Mantra as follows:

Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara was only at the first level at that time. After hearing this mantra, he immediately attained the eighth level. Delighted by the power of the mantra, he made a great vow:

- If in my future life I can bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings with this mantra, then please cause my body to immediately give birth to a thousand eyes and a thousand arms.

Immediately, He achieved his wish. From then on, the image of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a thousand hands and a thousand eyes became a symbol of the supreme ability of a Bodhisattva, carrying the mission in life to save suffering and bring joy to all sentient beings.

A thousand hands and a thousand eyes speak of the ability to freely transform, the boundless application of the all-pervading divine power of Compassion and Wisdom of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Thousands of eyes to be able to illuminate all realms of human suffering and thousands of hands to save and support, as the Buddha explained to Ananda in the sutra, "represents the conduct of following the desires of sentient beings".

The Great Compassion Sutra and Mantra were later translated and transliterated from Sanskrit into Chinese by Venerable Pham Dat Ma (Bhagavaddharma: meaning Venerable Dharma), an Indian Zen Master, and translated into Vietnamese by Venerable Thich Thien Tam.

With its power and effectiveness proven over space and time, the Great Compassion mantra has been respectfully recited in ceremonies and main chanting rituals of countries following the Mahayana Buddhist tradition such as: China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam,..

The inspiration when reciting the Great Compassion Mantra

One is to not die of hunger, thirst, or misery;

Second, do not die from shackles, prisons, or whips;

Third, do not die because of unjust hostility;

Fourth, do not die because of war;

Fifth is not being killed by tigers, wolves, or evil beasts;

Sixth, do not die from snake, centipede, or scorpion poisoning;

Seventh is not being killed by water or fire;

Eighth, do not die from poison;

Nine is not dying from harmful effects of ancient poison;

Ten means you won't die from madness or insanity;

Eleven is to not die from landslides, falling trees, or collapsing cliffs;

Twelve means you won't die because of an evil spell;

Thirteen means you will not die from evil spirits or demons taking advantage of the opportunity to harm you;

Fourteen means you won't die from a serious illness;

Fifteen means you won't die from suicide."

The effectiveness and epiphany of the Great Compassion Mantra have long been understood by Vietnamese folk in particular and people all over the East in general as the "mantra of Buddha Dharma". The inspiration of the Great Compassion Mantra is miraculous: to save suffering and save people from being harmed by demons and evil people; protect people from the difficulties that people must face.

Cure people of both mental and physical illnesses; Has the power to transform the universe and create auspiciousness from karma; Resolve conflicts and conflicts; Bodhisattva incarnation, helping people have boundless strength to escape the prison of others... There have been thousands of stories passed down about the magic of the Great Compassion Mantra in real folklore and therefore, people come to the Great Compassion Mantra as if they were looking for a salvation in times of trouble.

In general, the function of the Great Compassion Mantra is to help sentient beings eliminate suffering, bring people joy and have the ability to heal mental and physical illnesses. Great Compassion's divine power is unparalleled.

When we are in the most difficult, painful, miserable, desperate, and tragic situations; the times when we find ourselves falling into a dead end, deadlocked, with no way out; Please have faith in Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, single-mindedly recite the Great Compassion Mantra, he will certainly help us with skillful means, taking us through suffering to a place of peace and happiness.

However, for the Mantra to exert its power, when reciting it, we must reflect on ourselves why we fall into suffering but others do not, and why does the Mantra have the power to save suffering? Buddhist teachings tell us that nothing in this world happens by chance. All the pain and misfortune that we have to endure in the present life: the shackles of prison, illness, and poverty are the results of the evil karma that we have committed in many previous lives or in this life, and now it is time for us to pay. The reason the Great Compassion Mantra has the ability to help us overcome tribulations is because of its super ability to destroy bad karma.

Come to Mother Goddess Avalokiteshvara through the Great Compassion Mantra. Recite with RESPECT, ABSOLUTE TRUST AND COMPLETE CONCENTRATION OF THOUGHTS. Stand up straight or sit upright before reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, that is your body karma being purified.

The mouth that recites sutras does not speak lies. A pure mind does not pay attention to distractions. The external environment is absorbed inside, it is a contract to realize the source of the mind, to enter the Dharma. The mantra is released like a pearl found at the bottom of clear water. The clarity of jade is revealed in the wish to achieve as well as entering the sea of wonderful meaning, truly mysterious

tieu_de: Why in the world are there rich people with broken walls, poor people without a place to live, homeless people, and the amount of money they have?
tom_tat: Hello everyone, I wish everyone a happy evening. Today I will talk about the perspective of money, rich and poor, as well as the fate of each of us. First of all, thank you Ms. Thach My Nghi for translating the book into a book.
noi_dung:
Why in the world are there rich people with broken walls, poor people without a place to live, homeless people, and the amount of money

Why in the world are there rich people with broken walls, poor people without a place to live, homeless people, and the amount of money for each person in this life is regulated?...Correct! Of course we all know that it is cause and effect, the rich people in this life are all people who gave alms and gave a lot in their previous lives, so they received back (note that this alms is not necessarily just material things, folks) poor, homeless because they created a lot of heavy karma in their previous lives, including being greedy, stingy, stingy....but there is a question: can the amount of money in our destiny be changed?

The answer is yes, guys! Because the nature of having money to keep money in a person's life is due to their blessings, how much money there is depends on whether the blessings are large or thin, and the blessings are something we can change, because if we do a lot of good deeds, we will accumulate many blessings, if we do evil deeds, we will lose our blessings. So if we actively do many meritorious deeds, we will surely accumulate a lot of money. However, this money may not reach you immediately but will reach your children and grandchildren, because blessings and retributions both come, it's just sooner or later. Previously, when An was still studying at university, one time cleaning the classroom, she accidentally picked up 500k. For students, that amount was a lot of money (and if she hadn't said it, no one would have known), but An took that money and returned it to the classroom manager and they returned the deceased. All my friends say this guy is so stupid, wouldn't it be better to take 500k and take him out drinking!!!. But am I really stupid, guys!

let me tell you the next part of the story. After the incident happened, I went back to the dormitory and suddenly came up with the idea of ​​installing windows and software to earn extra income. Then suddenly a lot of people came to my place to install, I didn't have to go anywhere, each person I took 30k, 50k, 80k depending on the type but it was also a lot cheaper than on the market because most of them were students. I did that job for about a month then suddenly they stopped coming to install it. The total amount I installed was exactly 2 million VND. Only later did I suddenly remember about the other 500k, perhaps it was the amount of money God gave me in fate, but with my honest nature, I returned the above amount so I received a reward that was four times the amount I received with my labor!!!. If at that time I took the above money to eat and drink, who knows, I might lose more :))

you see, the law of cause and effect always exists, whether it is slow or fast, it depends on each person's karma. Although each person's fate is destined to be like this, it is to encounter many adversities, sufferings, etc., but as Buddhists we know that this is what we have to go through and we cannot avoid it, so we will bravely confront it. It's okay for people to trick us, it's okay for people to criticize us for being foolish, it's okay for people to be smarter than us... if you can let go and live like that, blessings will definitely come to you. And when you see your fate is miserable, don't rush to feel down on yourself because if you always live a good life, do many meritorious deeds such as printing sutras, propagating Buddhism, helping the poor, building bridges and roads,... then your destiny will change, believe me and this is definitely true because I went through many things until I learned about Buddhism and lived a good life!

Finally, no matter living in these circumstances, always and everywhere you should have good thoughts, because although mortals do not know our bad deeds, the invisible realms in our world know it! Wishing everyone to always maintain faith in Buddhism and progress on their path of practice! Namo great compassion Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara!

tieu_de: UNDERSTAND ABOUT SUFFERINGS AND Blessings
tom_tat: According to the Buddhist Doctrine of Dependent Origination, every problem that occurs in this world is caused by many causes and conditions coming together, and then, due to many causes and conditions, it changes into something else.
noi_dung:
UNDERSTANDING ABOUT SURPRISE AND Blessings

According to the Buddhist Doctrine of Dependent Origination, every problem that occurs in this world is caused by many causes and conditions coming together, and then, due to many causes and conditions, it changes into something else. In general, no one person is born the same. Some people are born with a beautiful, balanced body. Some people are born with all six faculties like everyone else, but do not have outstanding beauty. There are also people who were born unlucky because they lack this or that sense. Some people are born smart, active, and agile, but at birth they fail up and down. Some people are born stupid and slow but easily succeed even without competing for profit. Some people are born into a rich family, but others live their whole lives in poverty. I wonder why there are so many different situations?

In response to disabled beings, scientists say: It may be due to the influence of a father or mother who has a certain disease, causing the child to be born with a disability. In addition, there are also cases where the mother takes birth control pills and then forgets to take them for a day or two during conception, which affects the formation of the fetus. Another case in the homeland of Vietnam was that many babies were born with disabilities attributed to the effects of the toxic chemical "Agent Orange" during the war. From the world's perspective, this answer may be correct for parents who have fallen into the above situations, but what about countless other cases happening in the world that are not in those situations? Many parents are healthy, intelligent, successful, have high status in society, and have given birth to healthy children, but in the meantime there is a baby with a congenital disease or disability, so what should we answer? Or is it that in this world there are babies who are incredibly intelligent in many areas such as music, mathematics, or have super memories, that people call "prodigies" while that baby's parents are just normal people? In this case, scientists do not have a satisfactory explanation.

According to the Buddhist Theory of Cause and Effect, all families, whether rich or poor, all individuals, beautiful or ugly, healthy or disabled, and all lucky or unlucky people, are gradually rotated in the wheel of Cause and Effect. Thus, from a Buddhist perspective, everyone born in this world cannot escape the law of "Cause and Effect", also known as Karma. Karma from many previous lives has contributed to shaping people and continues to influence people's lives in this life and will continue in the future, if people do not know how to practice and continue to create new Karmas in the present life.

No one in this world can predict how long they will live? One year? Two years? Ten years? Twenty years? Seventy years? Ninety years? Or hundred years old? No matter how long one's life is, people still cannot escape the words "Pain Phuoc" in life. Why? Because people born in this life lack enough blessings to have a completely satisfied life, the reason is because they have created Karma from concepts, actions, thoughts, and words through their lifestyle in many past and present lives. Because we ourselves have created the cause, when we meet the predestined conditions, the old causes will bear fruit. That fruit will be transferred to us so that we will suffer disaster or enjoy blessings.

THE CAUSES OF PHUUUONG DISASTER

When talking about Disaster, people often think of the phrases Disaster and Accident, which are things no one wants to encounter. Whenever people talk about Accidents, they think of Disaster as unspeakable suffering and sadness. Disasters often come unexpectedly, such as when a family is living peacefully and suddenly a disaster occurs, causing the house to be destroyed, the business to be destroyed, and debt to pile up. Such miserable, calamitous situations cause people to fall into a state of sadness with no way out, leading to confusion. In mild cases, they suffer from depression, and in severe cases, they think about death to avoid suffering and pain. Falling into this situation, people call it "Pain".

In recent times, those who have followed the news know that in the United States as well as in many other countries around the world, natural disasters such as earthquakes, tsunamis, thunderstorms, floods, fires, wars, terrorism, epidemics... have claimed countless human lives. Besides, there are also lucky people who were saved. That luck is called "Phuc" or "Phuc". Or there are people who are lucky enough to make a living, win this or that deal, have a peaceful, happy family, and that person's mood is peaceful and happy, then people say this person is "blessed" or "happy". When mentioning happiness, people think of states of peace, happiness, joy, luck...

Blessing is the factor that creates a happy and peaceful life. Disaster is the factor that causes people to live in chaos, unhappiness and suffering. Blessings and misfortunes do not come naturally, nor do Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Gods or Gods intervene to bring misfortunes or blessings to anyone. Because they are people who have compassion and compassion for human suffering and vow to practice, find a way out for themselves and help sentient beings escape suffering, no one can bear to act unjustly and cruelly by giving happiness and peace to one person and spreading misfortune and pain to another. In this world, there are countless good people who have to endure many disasters and suffering, while evil and dishonest people are always seen living in good circumstances.

Those unfair, almost absurd, disparate phenomena, with the eyes of ordinary people like us, we cannot see the profound cause. Only the Buddha, who is Fully Enlightened, can clearly see the correlation or mutual generation of Karma and teach it to us. In the Small Distinction of Karma Sutra No. 135 (part of the Majjhima Nikaya III) tells the story of the Buddha answering a young man named Subha Todeyyaputta at Anathapindika's monastery in Savatthi city, Jetavana, when he asked a number of questions about what is the cause, what is the reason, that among human beings there are noble people and lowly people, short-lived people and long-lived people, sick people with few illnesses, beautiful people with ugly people, people with great power and powerful people. people with small status, people with small assets, people with great assets, people from lowly families, people from noble families, people with weak intelligence, people with full intelligence. The Buddha said that such different phenomena occur due to Karma. People who cause karma must be born into a certain situation to repay their karma. He said: "Sentient beings are the owners of karma, the heirs of karma. Karma is the womb, karma is the kin, karma is the fulcrum that divides sentient beings; that is, there is weakness and there are advantages." Speaking more broadly, the Buddha pointed out a number of Karmas that lead to typical Karmas that lead to the differences between humans and between sentient species as follows:

- Premature death and short life are due to the Karma of killing sentient beings, not having a compassionate mind... Living a long life is due to abstaining from killing sentient beings, having compassion, mercy, and caring for the happiness of all sentient beings and sentient beings. - Many diseases are caused by previous lives that often harm sentient beings. Less illness is due to not thinking about harming sentient beings. - Ugly appearance is due to frequent anger, a lot of resentment, the slightest mention of someone is discontent, dissatisfaction, anger, and opposition. A beautiful appearance is due to not being angry, not having much resentment, not being dissatisfied, not being opposed, not being dissatisfied, having a gentle and loving mind. - Lack of authority is due to jealousy and envy towards those who have rights and those who are respected. Much authority comes from not being jealous or envious. - Poverty is caused by not giving alms and offerings. Being rich is due to giving alms and offerings. - Being born into a vile family is due to being arrogant, arrogant, often looking down on others, not respecting respectable people, not respecting respectable people. Being born into a noble family is due to a humble and humble mind, and often respecting respectable people. - Stupidity without wisdom is due to not often going to monks to learn. Having wisdom comes from often coming to learn from spiritual practitioners."

According to Buddha's teachings, Blessings and Misfortunes are all due to Karma, which are the actions and creations of humans through body, speech, and mind, i.e. thoughts, words, actions, and deeds. Creating good karma is called good karma, blessed karma. Creating bad karma is called unwholesome karma, disaster karma, poor karma, and evil karma. In the present or past life, sentient beings have created countless good and bad karma, so they have to experience happiness and suffering mixed together. Those who create more bad karma than good karma will have more ups and downs in life than those who create more good karma. Therefore, there are people who are rich, happy, and extremely powerful, while there are people who are extremely poor and miserable. However, in the world there are also many difficult situations such as rich people with short lives. That's because he knew how to give alms in his previous life, so he was born into a rich family in this life, but he had the karma of killing sentient beings in his previous life, so he didn't live long in this life. Or poor people with unusual beauty. Or a person who is incredibly beautiful lives in poverty and is abused by her husband and children, etc. That is also due to the good and bad karma of that person created from the past. That's why the Buddha said: "Sentient beings are the owners of karma, the heirs of karma. Karma is the womb, the relatives, karma is the fulcrum, karma divides sentient beings; there are bad things and good things" is like that!

BLESSINGS IN LIFE

In life, everyone wants to have many blessings. People who live with many merits and virtues are less likely to suffer disasters. People with less merit and virtue are more likely to have disasters. As for unlucky people, no matter where they live, it is difficult to avoid disasters. Whoever has complete merit and virtue will have no misfortune. That is true according to the Law of Cause and Effect. But in reality, in the world, it is rare to see people who never encounter sadness in their whole life. Perhaps because those who have great blessings, when they die, they will be born as Brahmas in Heaven and enjoy all the blessings!

As humans, no one wants disaster to come to us, but how can our lives always be peaceful and happy, away from all dangerous things? Superstitious people believe that disasters or blessings are decreed by God, Buddha, Bodhisattva or God, so when they encounter misfortune, they run around to this pagoda, that communal house, that temple... to worship and pray. When faced with a disaster, confusion, fear... the general mentality is that when someone tells them something, they immediately do it without thinking, just hoping that God will save them from the disaster they are suffering. Sometimes when they encounter a minor accident, it passes quickly, making them believe in God even more. But if the problem cannot be resolved in one day, then their minds are confused, depressed, confused, and can only cry and complain to God and hate the earth, and slander the Gods to create more karma.

In fact, in this world, whoever sins is his own responsibility. No one can deal with worldly laws based on personal feelings. As for my sins, I must bear them. Even though parents feel sorry for their children and fear their children will suffer, they cannot volunteer to be punished on their children's behalf. The same goes for the Law of Cause and Effect. If we cause light karma, we will receive light consequences. If we cause heavy karma that harms others, we must bear the consequences of heavy mental and physical damage. Even if we cry and beg, no one can reduce the karma we have caused, no one will take the blame for us.

Buddha taught that our lives are ours to control. Whatever Cause we create is what Effect we will receive. Therefore, having been born in this Human world, we will certainly have to endure more or less ups and downs, enjoying blessings and sufferings. What's important is how we behave when disasters come to visit, or blessings come to visit.

When we understand the Law of Cause and Effect or Karma, we know that when we are living peacefully and happily, we are enjoying Blessings, then we are not too proud, arrogant, or look down on the less fortunate people around us, because we know that this is the result of some good deeds that we have done in many past lives. The correct action of a person who knows "fear of Cause" (*), is when enjoying Blessings and Fruits, we need to be diligent to create more Blessings, save Blessings, which means we concentrate on practicing more, doing more good deeds, just in case when Disaster comes, we still have Blessings to share to alleviate the Suffering. The Buddha also once compared good Karma (Blessed Karma) to a cup of water, while bad Karma (Damaged Karma) was compared to a bowl of salt. If you do more meritorious deeds, your share of water will increase. The more water is dissolved with less salt, the less salty the water becomes, which means that thanks to meritorious deeds, the sins that we have caused to harm others in the past can be alleviated.

When disaster suddenly comes, as people who have studied Buddhism, we know that it is caused by our own bad Karma in the past, now it bears fruit, we cannot avoid it, so instead of panicking, trembling, crying, resenting... it only makes ourselves and our family members more miserable. Let's try our best to stay calm, endure patiently, find a solution and continue to do good within our ability. When the mind is calm and unwavering, our observations and judgments will be clearer and more lucid. That's the way when we encounter Calamity and accept the reward of wisdom. It is also paying for bad karma, but paying with a calm and accepting mind will make serious misfortunes become light, and light things will be considered as nothing.

The story of Hoa Phuoc came unexpectedly and no one knew. It is rare that Blessings come many times in life, but Misfortunes come more often. The ancients went through that experience, so there was a saying: "Blessings do not come again and again, Disasters do not come in one direction", meaning that Blessings do not come twice, but disasters do not come just once, that is, Disasters often come to people many times. We also often hear: "There is good fortune, there is misfortune", implying that in life there is bad luck or vice versa, like the story in the Classical Classics book that says: "A man dried grass at the foot of the fence. The next day, he went out to gather grass and heard a "prick" sound in the grass. He dug up the grass and caught a pheasant. He was very happy, leaving the grass as before. A few days later, he went to the pile of grass to listen, and there was also a "prick" sound. He turned over the grass and caught a pheasant. He hurriedly used his hands to dig up the grass, hoping to catch another pheasant. But unexpectedly, he was immediately bitten by a tiger snake. There was no time to save him, so he died on the spot."

Another famous story about Hoa Phuoc, everyone knows, is the story "The Lost Horse Again". The story goes: "In the north of China, near the border with Ho country, there was an old man named Tai Ong. Tai He had a horse. One day the horse ran across Ho country and disappeared. A neighbor heard the news and came to offer condolences. The old man calmly replied: "Who knows, maybe the horse running away will be a good thing for me." A few months later the horse returned, carrying a tall and healthy Ho horse. The neighbor heard the news and came to congratulate him, repeating what the old man said. trước. Ông lão chẳng vui mừng chỉ nói: "Biết đâu việc được ngựa này sẽ dẫn đến tai họa cho tôi". Quả nhiên việc này đúng như thế. Cậu con trai của ông rất thích cởi ngựa, thấy ngựa Hồ cao khoẻ thì thích lắm, liền nhảy lên lưng phóng chạy. Không ngờ ngựa Hồ chưa thuần nên nhảy loạn xạ. Cậu con bị ngựa hất xuống đất gãy xương đùi mang tật lớn. Người trong xóm biết chuyện, đến chia buồn. Ông lão lại nói: "Biết đâu nhờ họa này mà được phước khác". Một năm sau, nước Hồ pulled troops to invade the Central Plains. All the men in the border area had to join the army to fight the enemy and died because his leg was broken. The content of this story shows that Hoa is the root of Phuoc, Phuoc is the root of Hoa. Both appear alternately. Therefore, when receiving Blessings, you should not be so happy that you forget to guard against the disasters that will come. When meeting Hoa, you should not be so miserable that your spirit will be damaged.

In life, it is true that from luck to misfortune, from misfortune to luck, it is difficult to predict. Although that is so, in reality it is not always true that when there is a Blessing there is immediately a Misfortune, or when there is a Misfortune there is immediately a Blessing. Sometimes Phuoc Hoa goes together with Hoa, sometimes Phuoc Hoa doesn't go together, because in the middle there is still good karma and good fate to decide in your life. Even that Blessing, if you consciously cultivate more Blessings, Blessings will add Blessings. Even if that Blessing creates bad karma, Blessing will give birth to Disaster.

TURN TO CAREER

As in the sutras, the Buddha teaches us that whether we live in this life will bring about Blessings or Disasters because of our Karma. In terms of phenomena and conventional truths, we must live well, do good deeds without harming others, maintain the Pham Hanh, create good karma, so that in the next life we ​​will not have to suffer from the disasters that often befall us. When Phuc comes, don't be too happy. When disaster comes, don't be too sad. Because that is the Fruit we must accept and cannot avoid. In terms of the ultimate truth, we practice how to escape the cycle of birth and death, not just worrying about doing good deeds and avoiding evil deeds, because then we are still in the cycle of treating good, bad, and evil and continue from life to life, having to suffer in the six realms.

As ​​lay people, we still have to go out into society to make a living to support ourselves and our families, so it is difficult to avoid creating Karma, most of which is bad Karma. To help living beings keep themselves pure in daily life, the Buddha forced Buddhists to promise to keep the five precepts. 1) Do not kill or harm animals. 2) Do not steal or take what is not given. 3) Do not commit adultery or destroy other people's family life. 4) Do not lie or speak cruel words, causing suffering, division, or hatred between one person and another. 5) Do not use intoxicants that make your mind dull and stupid. Those who keep these five precepts are people who live ethically and do not create evil karma. These are the five basic precepts. Anyone who practices them correctly will gradually move away from the three poisons of Greed, Anger, and Stupidity. In the sutra, it is recorded that those who keep these five precepts will not fall into the three bad paths. These are Animals, Hungry Ghosts, and Hell. Anyone who can keep the five precepts and eliminate the three poisons can be born in Heaven and enjoy whatever blessings they want. But what they want in Heaven makes many Gods completely forget their practice, so when they enjoy all the blessings, they fall into human or animal life depending on the Karma they have caused many lives ago.

Practicing and keeping the precepts is practicing according to the external appearance that is still within the scope of good-evil, good-bad, some people keep the precepts, there are precepts to keep, so they are still reborn in the six paths. The issue of practicing and keeping the precepts is considered necessary. Besides keeping the precepts, the most important thing is still cultivating from the root, not from the top. Rhetoric originally means "meditation" to clean the mind, keep the mind quiet to develop wisdom.

In the Dhammapada, chapter Two Essentials, the two opening paragraphs clearly state:

2) The mind leads all dharmas, the mind is the master of creation; If with a pure mind, Speak or act, Peace and joy follow, Like a shadow, never leaving the image".

If good thoughts arise, the body and mouth will speak and do good deeds, creating good karma. If evil thoughts arise, the body and mouth will speak and act evilly, creating evil karma. But if you do not have good or evil intentions, then your body and mouth will not follow your intention to speak or act, creating good karma or bad karma.

Simplify the meaning of the two words Hoa Phuoc in current life so that we can easily practice. What agrees with your mind is Phuoc, joy, joy, and happiness. Anything that goes against your mind is disaster, sadness, and suffering. Whether it is a Blessing or a Misfortune is caused by Karma. To escape Karma, we must first practice gathering the six senses and not let the six worlds drag us down, causing the three Karmas: Body, Speech, and Mind to be polluted. How to gather the six senses? That is when the senses come into contact with the object, the signal affects Feeling. If you know that without attachment, there is no more Happiness or Suffering in this place, meaning there is no Misery or Blessing. At that moment there is no Misfortune, that is, at that moment there is no Karma created. The longer this time lasts, the longer the three karmas will be pure.

Another practice is the True Dharma. Seeing as it really is, knowing the truth about worldly phenomena, what is the Misfortune and what is the Blessing? Even higher, all worldly phenomena, their essence is "Like That", without good or bad qualities, big or small, heavy or light... it is just Like That! So Hoa is also "like", Phuoc is also "like", I am also "like". Eliminate both sides: "I" and "Disaster or Happiness", then which is Misfortune and which is Phuc? Therefore, with a view beyond the world, beyond the category of conditioned things, all things are not real, so it is said "Drawings and Blessings are not real".

Blessed Painting comes from the Mind. When the mind is moved, Hoa Phuoc is born. When the mind is pure, Hoa Phuoc will be destroyed. If we master the mind, where can Hoa Phuoc be born? Only then can we escape from Karma, from the cycle of birth and death. The repentance verse below also falls within this meaning:

"The nature of sin is not created by the mind.

If the mind is destroyed, its sins will be pure

All sins in the mind are eliminated

That is true repentance."

CONCLUSION

We are born in the human world and must obey the law of borrowing and repaying. We have to pay back as much as we borrow, if not both capital and interest, so as humans, no one can avoid Misfortune. Therefore, when we have studied Buddha and believed in Buddha, we should practice according to Buddha's teachings to save ourselves from the cycle of birth and death. We cannot know how long it takes to practice to achieve our goal, but looking back at our own ups and downs in life, we can reflect on how many of our sins and blessings we caused in previous lives. And with our current way of life, how can we perceive our future life? The Buddha taught us very clearly that our lives are controlled by us, and our blessings and blessings are also controlled by us. No one gives us blessings or misfortunes. Therefore, we should wake up early to choose the appropriate lifestyle in this life to prepare for a peaceful and happy life in the next life. In short, gradually practicing according to Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom is the right path for Buddhist students to choose to reach liberation. Practice step by step to transform your mind. When the mind changes, Karma also changes. Once the karma has been transformed, the shore of enlightenment, although far away, will eventually come./.

tieu_de: Miraculous fate in marriage in past and present lives
noi_dung:
Magical fate in marriage in past and present lives

Cuộc đời của chúng ta vẫn luôn có cảm giác như vậy, có người chúng ta gặp thoáng qua rất nhanh, có một số người ở bên cạnh ta suốt ngày, vài người trở thành bạn, vài người trở thành đối địch, hết thảy đều là duyên phận từ tiền kiếp.

Nhiều khi chúng ta phát hiện, người tính không bằng trời tính, cho dù hai người có bát tự xem ra rất hợp nhau, nhưng trên thực tế họ lại không có duyên phận như thế, hoặc cũng biết rõ hai người có bát tự không hợp nhau, lại hết lần này tới lần khác bàn chuyện hôn nhân, kết quả cũng không tốt.

Sự kỳ diệu trong mối quan hệ nói rõ một điều, người với người gặp hoặc kết duyên với nhau đều là dựa vào duyên phận.

In previous lives we were together, in this life we are together again

Những năm gần đây, có một loại liệu pháp hồi tưởng tiền kiếp đang lưu hành trên thế giới. Liệu pháp này dựa trên cơ sở rằng bệnh tâm lý và căn nguyên những cơn đau trường kỳ của kiếp này thường đến từ các kiếp trước.

Liệu pháp hồi tưởng tiền kiếp này đưa người bệnh vào trạng thái bị thôi miên nhập định, mà tái hiện lại trải nghiệm của cơn đau ở kiếp trước, đồng thời đọc và giải thích cause and effect đã trải qua, thế là căn bệnh của kiếp này tự khỏi một cách thần kỳ. Những người đã thể nghiệm trạng thái nhập định của kiếp trước nhớ lại một cách rất sống động, các chi tiết ăn khớp và nối liền nhau, tuyệt đối không phải sản phẩm của trí tưởng tượng.

Dr. Brian L. Weiss, chief of psychiatry at Mt. Sinai ở thành phố Miami, bang Florida, Mỹ, là một chuyên gia về điều trị hồi tưởng với quyển sách “Many Lives, Many Masters”. Trong lúc ông giúp đỡ một người bệnh hồi tưởng, đã phát hiện ra nhiều trường hợp có mối nhân duyên từ kiếp trước, đến kiếp này lại tiếp tục.

Một cuốn sách khác của tiến sĩ Weiss có tên “Only Love Is Real” ghi lại một trường hợp liên quan “duyên phận” và hiện tại vẫn đang tiếp tục. Có một người nam và một người nữ vốn không quen biết nhau đồng thời đến tìm tiến sĩ Weiss để tiến hành trị liệu hồi tưởng. Hai người nhớ ra kiếp trước ở Jerusalem vào 2000 năm trước, khi đó họ có mối quan hệ là cha và con gái, người cha bị binh sĩ La Mã tra tấn, chết trong vòng tay con gái.

The two met once in Weiss's treatment room, but because of work principles, Weiss couldn't tell them about the other's memories. However, after the two people's treatment ended, the hand of fate once again miraculously arranged - the two "coincidentally" sat on the same flight, met and fell in love.

Many people may think that they and their partner met each other completely by chance. So in the above story, two men and women accidentally become friends, is it not a continuation of fate from 2000 years ago?

When researchers compiled a large number of past life recall cases, they discovered that there is a very common phenomenon that many couples in this life, in many previous lives, have experienced love stories of all kinds.

Let go of resentment, your life will flourish

Her husband is an extremely successful businessman. But for 18 years, her husband was completely incompetent in marital life. In modern society, such things can become reasons for divorce. But this girl couldn't bear to do that, she still loved her husband and did not have the heart to hurt him.

During the first years of her marriage, she could hardly endure the torment of desire and also had an affair. But gradually, through religion, she learned to meditate and overcome this desire. Years passed like a quiet flow, until one day, a former suitor came back to her life.

This young man loved her when he was young, but when his family had economic conditions, she got married. The two met and at one point seemed unable to control themselves, but this girl also ended that relationship. She couldn't bear to leave her husband, because he was a good person. She also didn't have the heart to hurt his mother, she didn't want to harm anyone.

Thông qua những hồi tưởng về kiếp trước, thì ra cô gái này và chồng mình hai đời trước tại Pháp cũng là một đôi vợ chồng. At that time, her husband joined the Crusaders to go to the East. But before leaving, to make sure his wife did not live with anyone else, he forced her to wear a chastity belt. This made the wife always angry, she was determined to take revenge on her husband in the future.

So the two of them met each other in this life and became husband and wife. The husband has lost his obvious ability to sow the wind and reap the whirlwind. But why does the wife encounter this trouble? Because the wife in her previous life was filled with hatred and desire for revenge towards her husband.

In this life, she has a beautiful appearance like a flower and has all the abilities to make her husband feel jealous and ashamed. Cô có thể ly hôn, để đạt được mục đích báo thù, nhưng cô đã đề cao tinh thần của bản thân, không đành lòng làm tổn thương bất kỳ ai. Because of her loyalty to marriage, she sacrificed her own desires, beauty and youth.

Cause and effect awaken, cause and effect are difficult to avoid

According to "The story of predestined fate", it is said that it was written in the late Ming and early Qing dynasties by the author of "Liao Trai" Bo Tung Linh. In the book, it is described as a story of unjust fate and destiny for two generations. Chapter 22 of the book is a story about fate in a past life, the main character Tieu Nguyen kills a fox with spiritual energy, then takes prostitute Tran Ca as a concubine, then Tieu Nguyen lets the concubine abuse his wife, to the point that wife Ke Thi cannot bear it and hangs herself.

Later because of predestined relationships, Tieu Nguyen was born as Dich Hi Tran, a fox with a spirit was born as Dich Hi Tran's wife Tiet To Thu, Ke Thi was born as Dich Hi Tran's concubine Ky Thu, Tran Ca was born as his concubine's maid Tran Chau. In retribution, Tran Chau was eventually forced to death by Ky Thu, Dich Hi Tran was humiliated by To Thu and Ky Thu, and To Thu's cruelty was very unusual, she used any terrible tricks on Di Hi Tran such as imprisoning, pricking, beating, and using fire.

After reading the entire story "The story of fate and fate" you can immediately understand clearly that sowing good causes reaps good results, sowing evil causes receive evil rewards, the law of cause and effect is not wrong at all. The so-called "If you practice for ten years, you can sit in the same boat, practice for a hundred years and have the same pillow", on the surface Buddhism says it from the perspective of regretting fate, advising people to cherish the fate of difficult encounters between people, but the real meaning is to awaken people, everything in the world is created by compatible fate, regardless of how our fate is formed, whether the fate of this life is good or not, we must cherish the current fate to do good to overcome evil. fate, continuing good fate, also ending all kinds of resentment.

In a life where suffering and happiness intersect, it is often necessary to reconsider, stand from a different position or perspective and look at the problem, perhaps you will have a different feeling. For example, in the story "Life of many lives", when mentioning that girl, she chose to improve her own character, rather than using revenge to face an incomplete predestined relationship, so she ended the resentment of her previous life and the unhappiness of predestined relationships.

tieu_de: Story about hell
tom_tat: Yesterday my mother recited the Ksitigarbha Sutra from morning to evening. At night, my mother dreamed of a very strange scene: she saw a person taking her to see a place and saw that the place was dirty, smelly, and filled with mucus.
noi_dung:
A story about hell

Yesterday, my mother recited the Ksitigarbha Sutra from morning to evening. At night, my mother dreamed of a very strange scene, that is, she saw a person taking her to see a place and saw that the place was dirty, smelly, and full of slimy feces. . . . There were many people struggling down there. My mother felt very scared. Suddenly she saw Mr. I didn't see him answer, I just saw him huddled in a dirty excrement pit, looking very miserable. When my mother told me, I asked her to describe more clearly that "hole" which was indeed a urine and feces mud pond as described in Ngoc Lich Buu Adventure and Journey to Hell. My mother had never read it before nor knew there was this kind of pond in hell. Tell me more about Mr. L. When he was alive, Mr. L did not believe in cause and effect, in gods, and did not believe in god. When he was still working as a district administrator, he did so many bad things that no one in the area knew him. After that, he was disciplined. One day he returned home to slaughter pigs to sell. He specialized in gambling and beat his wife and children. One day, he even forced his wife to lick her sandals @@. Haiz, sentient beings in this life do not believe in hell, and do not even believe in cause and effect, allowing them to do evil will result in retribution and hell that will never come out!

tieu_de: Reincarnation story: Dau Nga's unjust soul demands a 500-year debt
tom_tat: Dau Nga's oath was immediately fulfilled: Blood splashed on the white silk, snow fell in June, and the So Chau region suffered a drought for 3 years. But the story is not over yet, the story continues after that
noi_dung:
Reincarnation story: Dau Nga's ghost demands a 500-year debt

Dau Nga's oath was immediately fulfilled: Blood splashed on the white silk, snow fell in June, and the So Chau region suffered a drought of 3 years. But the story is not over yet, the story that continues after that is the same as "injustice, there are debtors, there are owners".

“Oan Dau Nga” is a famous musical play by writer Quan Han Khanh of the Yuan Dynasty, the work was composed based on the unjust story “Dong Hai Hieu Phu” in “The Story of Lieh Nu”. The story tells that Dau Nga was harmed by scoundrels and was unfairly beheaded by the governor Dao Ngot.

The main character in the opera is a poor girl from So Chau area, named Dau Nga. Her mother died when she was young. Her father, Dau Thien Chuong, had no money to pay the debt. He quickly went to the capital to take the exam. There was no money for travel expenses, so he sold her to a widow, Thai Ba, to be his young daughter-in-law (that is, the daughter-in-law bought from a young age, and when she grows up, she must become the wife of the buyer's son).

Dau Nga had not been at the Thai family's house for 2 years when her son, the Thai family, fell ill, leaving only her and the Thai widow to live and depend on each other. Truong Lu Nhi is a scoundrel in So Chau. He and his father, Truong Lao Nhi, saw that there were only two women in the Thai family, so they went to stay there and forced the old woman to marry Truong Lao Nhi. Thai Ba was so lonely that she had to accept it. Truong Lu Nhi forced Dau Nga to become friends with him. Dau Nga resolutely refused and cursed him severely. Truong Lu Nhi was angry and immediately thought of a revenge plan.

A few days later, Thai Ba got sick and ordered Dau Nga to cook porridge. Truong Luu Nhi secretly put poison in the bowl of porridge, intending to kill Thai Ba and then force Dau Nga. Dau Nga brought porridge to Thai Ba. Suddenly Thai Ba felt nauseous, didn't want to eat anymore and passed the bowl of porridge to Truong Lao Nhi to eat. Truong Lao Nhi was poisoned, rolled on the ground and died.

Truong Lu Nhi blamed Dau Nga for poisoning and had her taken to the governor of So Chau. So Chau's governor, Dao Ngot, a notoriously corrupt official, received bribes from Truong Lu Nhi, arrested Dau Nga for questioning, and forced her to confess to poisoning. Dau Nga was beaten to death and refused to confess his crime. Dao Nggot knew that Dau Nga was very filial to Thai Ba, so he took Thai Ba out and beat her in front of Dau Nga's eyes. Dau Nga felt sorry for Thai Ba in her old age, could not bear the torture, so she had to accept the injustice and admit her guilt. The corrupt man Dao Ngot used every trick to force her to confess, immediately sentenced her to death, and took her to the execution ground.

In the play, there is a deeply touching scene. Before being executed, Dau Nga made three ironclad oaths to the beheading officer: 1. If I am wronged, "a single drop of hot blood will not fall from the knife cutting through my head, but will shoot up on that white silk strip"; 2. If I am wronged, then "after I die, the sky will bring down three meters of snow and cover my body"; 3. If I am wronged, after I die, "from now on, this So Chau will be in drought for 3 consecutive years".

But the story is not over yet, it has already responded to the "unrighteousness of one debtor and one owner". At that time, the Crown Prince Dao Ngot misjudged this unjust case because he accepted a huge bribe, so Dau Nga never let him go.

First of all, after the death of the governor Dao Ngot of the Yuan Dynasty, he had to go to hell and suffer the torture of casing (burning human skin with a red-hot iron) countless times; During the Ming and Qing dynasties, he was reincarnated as an animal and was killed hundreds of times. These things are all too distant and vague for us, the most interesting and alarming thing is that this unjust case still lasts until today, Dau Nga's debt collection with him also lasts until today. Dao Ngo must finally receive the retribution he deserves in this cycle of reincarnation.

Below is the story of Dau Nga's reincarnation and revenge against the prince Tao Ngo in this life:

Ms. Truong currently lives in Los Angeles, originally from Taipei City, Taiwan. An extremely strange thing happened in her family. Ms. Truong's great-grandfather, grandfather and father all passed away on her 36th birthday. Until this fifth generation, all the eldest sons in her family had no way to avoid the tragic fate of having to leave this world as soon as they turned 36.

As for the eldest daughters in her family, her aunt died on her 34th birthday. Although Ms. Truong's mother knew about this strange incident, she never dared to tell her, afraid that if she found out, she would not accept it, because Ms. Truong is also the eldest daughter.

In the year when Ms. Truong was 33 years old, she had three sons. In May of that year, she discovered she was pregnant again, the estimated time of birth would be on her 34th birthday.

When Ms. Truong was pregnant with this child, there were some very strange phenomena. First, it's so uncomfortable that you keep banging yourself against the wall. Second, when she has morning sickness, she needs to tell her husband and three sons to spank her so she feels better; Moreover, at night you need to fight hard to be able to overcome it. If her husband and son didn't want to beat her, she would be angry with them. This is a phenomenon that has never happened before in previous pregnancies.

Ms. Truong's mother has a friend who is a high-ranking monk. One time this monk came to the house and saw Ms. Truong. He was shocked and sighed, but did not dare to tell her the truth.

When Ms. Truong was 6 months pregnant, one day her mother wanted to eat rice rolls and wanted her to buy them. So Ms. Truong immediately went to a restaurant in Taipei City to buy it. When she returned, she got on a bus. After getting on the bus, everyone on the bus saw that she was a pregnant woman with a huge belly, but no one was willing to give up their seat for her; Some people even close their eyes, as if they can't see.

Miss Truong kept standing like that the whole way. Suddenly, the car hit a heavy object, the car braked suddenly, causing her to fall, and she was then taken to the hospital. That evening, she felt very painful in her stomach, and eventually had to give birth to this child prematurely. Although the child was born prematurely and very small, it can be seen that he is an extremely cute baby boy. The doctor said, this baby was born prematurely, we can only do our best, we don't know if it will survive, please don't get your hopes up too much.

A few days later, the doctor told Ms. Truong that she could go home first, but the child needed to stay in the hospital for continued follow-up care. On the night of the child's first month, she had a nightmare. She dreamed of the baby pulling her, she also pulled it, suddenly her hand let go, the baby's face turned black. Dreaming of this, she woke up startled and realized that this dream was a bad omen, so she told her husband to call the hospital and ask how the child was. It was 3 a.m., her husband originally didn't want to call, but she kept begging so she had to call the hospital.

At this moment, the hospital called again, saying the baby had passed away at 3am. When Ms. Truong heard the news, she began to cry. Around 6:00 a.m. that morning, the monk in Taichung took a bus to their house. As soon as he entered the house, the monk said to Ms. Truong's mother: "Congratulations to you." The mother couldn't hold back her anger, thinking, her grandchild just passed away, how can she say congratulations to me? The monk said: "Did the baby die at 3am?". Ms. Truong's husband asked in surprise: "How do you know that?". Only now can a monk clearly state the source.

It turned out that, around 12 o'clock last night, the child came to say goodbye to the monk. The child said: "I originally wanted to take her (referring to Ms. Truong) with me, but now I can't take her anymore. Because, first, she is very filial to her mother. Her mother wanted to eat cake, so she did not hesitate to work hard to carry her big pregnant belly to buy it for her mother. Moreover, having had such a car accident, I no longer had the strength to stay in her belly. I was originally planning on her birthday. Her 34 years will take her with her.”

The monk asked: "Do you have any deep hatred for Miss Truong?"

The child said: "In a previous life, she was a corrupt person, mishandled the case, causing me to die unjustly. I made her suffer torment from the beginning of her pregnancy, exactly the same torment I had to endure in prison. Making her bang her body against the wall, telling her children to beat her, was just like the torture I had to endure in prison. But now, after she gave birth to me, because Her house has a Buddha hall, so I have no way to go into her house, I also want to drag her away, but I can't drag her away; that's it, I have to go to a place in Changhua to reincarnate.

This is a true story about Dau Nga's reincarnation and revenge that happened in this life.

People living in real life are not the "people who die like a extinguished light" that atheism propagates. Good and evil are both recorded in cause and effect retribution. Therefore, do not do evil, only do good, should be the morality that every person needs to follow.

tieu_de: The Complete Book of An Si is a collection of books promoting charity that was highly praised by Master An Quang. From then until now, though
tom_tat: The book is over a thousand large-sized pages in the original Chinese text. The first part is an extensive explanation of the essay Ton Qua (Quang Nghia Van's Acoustics), which takes up more than 400 pages, and has now been completely translated into English.
noi_dung:
An Si Complete Book is a collection of books promoting charity that was highly praised by Master An Quang. Until now, although

The book is thicker than a thousand large-sized pages in the original Chinese text. The first part is an extensive explanation of the essay Ton Qua (Quang Nghia Van Ton) which takes up more than 400 pages, and has now been completely translated into Vietnamese and elaborately annotated by translator Nguyen Minh Tien.

Regarding the book's content, the author of this book relied on a very brief essay "Ton Qualities" (only about 800 words) to compile a book with more than 400 pages of large-format Chinese characters. The presentation is quite consistent throughout the book. For every sentence that is analyzed, An Si's Complete Book always has an extensive lecture section that he calls "invention", followed by a section of comments and discussions, which he calls "project". Next, most of them have an additional section citing stories, including stories drawn from the classics or Buddhist stories, for the purpose of illustrating the meaning of the above sections.

It is Mr. An Si's extensive lectures and comments that have explored and expanded the meaning of the text completely in the spirit of Buddhism, helping readers receive the quintessential teachings and good knowledge in the spirit of compassion, altruism and wisdom. It is not difficult for us to realize that, although it is based on the essay Sound Quality, most of Mr. An Si's writing completely dominates the content of this book.
