tieu_de: Feeling the pain, struggling, and struggling of animals when they are close to death caused by humans, they
tom_tat: Feeling the pain, struggling, and struggling of animals when they are close to death caused by humans, we can open our compassion and forgive them. When our souls become sensitive to pain
noi_dung:
Feeling the pain, struggling, and struggling of animals when they are close to death caused by humans, they

Feeling the pain, struggling, and struggling of animals when they are close to death caused by humans, we can be compassionate and forgive them. When our souls become sensitive to the suffering and pain of others, even animals, empathy and sympathy are nurtured and grow significantly. Thanks to this sensitive mentality, in life, we can easily understand and sympathize with the situations of others with a tolerant and generous mind. So, at first glance it seems that not killing and compassion and sharing with others have nothing to do with each other, but in fact, they are closely related. When the psychology of empathy and sympathy is nurtured and practiced, the mind of love, tolerance, sympathy, and generosity towards everyone grows as an inevitable consequence. Thus, not killing is also a dharma that supports the practice of other good dharmas in our lives....

tieu_de: EACH PERSON'S Aura
tom_tat: Most people only see halos radiating above the heads of the Highly Wise (from heaven and above), but in reality, for humans in the human world, when each person is born, they have a halo.
noi_dung:
EACHER'S Aura

Most people only see the halo radiating above the heads of the Highly Wise (from heaven and above), but in reality, for humans in the human world, when each person is born, there is a halo surrounding their body. That halo is not eternal and immutable, but it changes depending on our karma. For example, if a baby is born into poverty and must fall into poverty, the halo around the baby will have a dark color as soon as it is born. The halo around each person's body can be temporarily divided into 7 different layers with different colors and thicknesses.

- The first layer at the bottom inside is the Yellow layer: This is the layer that stores the good roots of mind and the Dharma enlightenment of each person. A person's good nature is more or less, gentle or evil, located in this layer. This can also be called the BUDDHA NATURE of each person. No matter who is human, they have this layer, but it has different thicknesses. People who have gone through many lifetimes of practice, when born, this layer is thick and bright yellow. light, and people who do not have good roots with deep Buddha nature, this layer is thin and dark yellow-orange, these are people with evil roots, or have just transformed into human beings after many lives of being reborn as animals, buffaloes and horses.

- The second layer: Is a layer with a GREEN color: This is the layer that collects all the good and bad karma carried by each person from the beginning to today. This layer is the thickest layer among the layers of ordinary people. It contains endless GOOD & BAD karma from endless lifetimes long ago, because it is located deep inside the aura layers, so only unless one attains Arahantship or higher can one be able to see through it. to reach this karmic cycle of another person. (Some people can also see external things in their present life, but the story of a fortune teller saying this or that is a fictional lie, don't believe it immediately).

- The third layer is the RED aura (SOME PEOPLE ONLY COLOR ORANGE): This is the aura that stores fate with everyone, for example, I have known you in a previous life or this woman has been my mother in many lifetimes, this aura stores those things, this aura will be our bridge with everyone around us.

- The fourth layer is the layer colored BLUE: This is the layer that stores the feelings of that person's soul through many lifetimes of training. People with rich emotional lives, emotional and sad, this layer is very thick, that is because their souls have been trained for many lifetimes with many emotions, many vibrations, a person can see the suffering of others and also cry, or see another person die and still be awake. As if it has nothing to do with you, it is reflected in this layer of aura, which is different in thickness and thinness.

- The fifth layer: This is the layer of aura that has the color of FRESH PINK, OR PINK: It is the layer that has accumulated our fate over hundreds of thousands of lives, which in the world is also called (husband and wife's fate), Mr. Nguyet Lao Sinh is also just an immortal who can understand the depths of this layer to determine the fate or separation in this place! HUSBANDS/LOVErs who love something are in this class, this class will be thick and bright pink for people who have a lot of love between men and women, or just blush for people who have little romantic love feelings, so they are in this class!

- FINALLY THE OUTER LAYER IS ALL MILK WHITE: This layer is a collection of the positive life and health of our current life. If a person is sick, this layer will gradually thin and turn light gray, and for people with a long positive life, this layer is very thick and milky white or blue white.

The reason why I say this today is not to prove that I am superior to others or that I have any intellectual achievements, but I want to say this so that everyone can understand that everything we do, everything we think is stored and will never go anywhere. LOST, SO AFTER THE GENERAL FALLS DOWN TO THE NINE SUNSET OF PLUMS WILL SHOW US AGAIN ALL OF THESE THINGS AGAIN SHOCKED IN PANIC AS TO WHO RECORDED IT, WHO SAVED IT, IN FACT THE PERSON WHO RECORDED IT, THE PERSON SAVED IT IS NO ONE OTHER THAN YOURSELF!

WAKE UP AND CORRECT YOUR MISTAKES TODAY BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE!

tieu_de: TRANSFORM ANGER
tom_tat: Anger is a form of negative psychology that exists latently in every human being, often arising and erupting whenever appropriate conditions arise. The Buddha considered anger to be a type of poison that has the ability to destroy
noi_dung:
TRANSFORMING ANGER

Buddha considered anger to be a type of poison that has the ability to destroy the human soul and body not only in this life but also in future lives. In the sutras, the Buddha often calls anger along with greed and ignorance the three poisons. The Buddha also compared anger to evil fire, like robbers, and poisonous snakes: "Anger is worse than evil fire, we must always be careful to prevent it from entering. Thieves of merit are nothing more than anger... If in the mind there are poisonous snakes of greed, anger, and ignorance, they must be eliminated quickly, otherwise they will be harmed" (Education Sutra).

Anger not only makes oneself oppressed and miserable, but also brings insecurity to others and society. For themselves, people who hold anger easily make mistakes and create unwholesome karma that causes suffering in this life and the next. When anger arises, people cannot control their emotions, thoughts, actions, and words, thereby easily creating bad karma. Anger clouds the mind, making people unable to recognize the nature of things and unable to handle situations in a positive and correct way that benefits themselves and others. Anger makes people not have peaceful and happy emotions, life loses joy and meaning.

According to Consciousness Only studies, anger is one of the six basic afflictions: Greed, anger, ignorance, pride, doubt, and evil views. Because this is the root affliction that is deeply rooted in the human mind, it is called the fundamental affliction. Anger belongs to the type that causes afflictions, i.e. afflictions appear at the same time as humans (born-together). It means that when born, people already have this type of affliction in their minds.

According to the theory of Dependent Origination, anger as well as other dharmas arise due to causes and conditions. When appropriate conditions and causes are encountered, the inherent seeds of anger (seeds of anger that have been accumulated for many lives) in the mind will arise. The more seeds of anger that are accumulated, the more they will be nurtured and empowered to have the conditions to arise. If the seeds of anger are regularly planted and watered, they will become habits (habits), these habits create a personality, a human personality: angry, full of anger, rude, rude, fond of violence, aggressive.

Anger has many different states, levels and expressions, for example: anger, resentment, anger, resentment, hatred... sometimes expressed through facial expressions (frowning, frowning, rolling eyes, grinding teeth...), attitudes, words (yelling, shouting, screaming, threatening...), gestures, actions (throwing things, torturing, killing...), but sometimes not expressed. appears but is kept secret in the heart.

In terms of health, when angry, the body immediately increases adrenaline secretion, causing the heart to beat faster, increase blood pressure, and abnormal breathing. If you are constantly stressed, the glands in your body will function incorrectly, leading to cardiovascular and digestive diseases. According to Eastern medicine, illness is caused by the loss of love (7 types of psychology): joy, anger, love, hate, compassion, fear, and terror (or joy, anger, love, hate, love, attachment, desire). Loss of love hurts the spirit, disrupts the balance of yin and yang, which is the main cause of illness. Among them, anger (anger) is anger. Oriental medicine also adds: anger harms the liver, too much joy harms the heart, anxiety harms the spleen, compassion harms the lungs, panic harms the kidneys... In the field of psychology, anger can lead to symptoms of depression, sadness, melancholy, boredom, self-destruction...

Anger is contagious like an infectious disease. Living in an environment of anger, tension, and heavy atmosphere, it can spread from one person to another. A person who is angry, angry, and frustrated will make those around him feel suffocated, stressed, and frustrated as well. One angry person can make others angry. Anger is like a fire, it can spread everywhere.

According to psychology, there are two ways to deal with anger: one is to suppress it, the other is to let it explode. Suppressing anger will cause unhealthy consequences, so it is recommended to use the second method of letting anger explode. Of course, we cannot let anger harm ourselves or others. People vent their anger on objects to relieve their psychological stress and frustration. People throw broken plates, hit sandbags, hit pillows or turn their faces to the wall and scream to vent their anger.

According to Buddhism, both of the above methods are not good methods. Because suppressing anger in the heart is not only harmful to health, but it is also a form of cultivating anger, keeping anger in a hidden form. At some point, when the right conditions arise, when the anger cannot be controlled anymore, the anger erupts, even more terrifying than the initial anger. Ways to let anger out (screaming, beating animals, throwing things) can partially relieve anger but do not completely eliminate anger. So this is only a temporary solution, not the optimal solution. Buddhism has many ways to effectively neutralize anger.

1. Mindfulness method: Be aware of the anger present in your mind. Recognizing the presence of anger helps us control it before it overpowers our minds. If we direct our attention to the object that makes us angry, our anger becomes even greater. But if we turn our mind inward, observe and monitor our anger and angry emotions, our anger will gradually subside. In the method of contemplating the Four Foundations of Mindfulness, the Buddha taught the Bhikkhus to contemplate the mind in the mind in that way. The practitioner watches his mind, knows that the mind has greed when greed arises, knows that the mind has anger when anger arises, knows that the mind has delusion when ignorance arises. Practitioners are always mindful and alert.

The breathing mindfulness method also helps us control anger. Whenever you are angry, you should breathe deeply, slowly, evenly, smoothly, gently, so that your mind can focus on monitoring your inhalation and exhalation. This measure helps stabilize our psychology, we can be calm, and only by being calm will we be clear enough to consider the situation and have appropriate solutions and behavior.

2. Method of using thoughts to transform anger: After clearly recognizing the anger arising in the mind, using the method of mindfulness of breathing we can calm the anger. Then we continue to use the idea of ​​transforming anger so that anger completely disappears from our minds. This is the method to eliminate anger if the mindfulness method has not made the anger disappear completely.

In the Dhammapada, the Buddha taught: "The other person does not understand that: Everyone will be destroyed by the law of impermanence, so they waste their energy arguing over losing. If they clearly understand that, there will be no more arguing." When meditating on Buddha's teachings, I see that everyone will die, and everything has no meaning. Anger for what? What about more? What if you lose? Why don't you let your heart be at peace and live happily, but instead cause more trouble, making your life chaotic and insecure? Spend your time and energy doing things that are useful for yourself and your life.

Contemplating causes and karma also helps us get rid of anger. When we think that everything that happens to us has a cause, we easily accept things that don't go our way. We know that the attitude of letting go, accepting to repay karma and not continuing to create negative causes is a wise attitude. In the Dhammapada, the Buddha taught a lot about that: "It insults me, beats me, destroys me, robs me", whoever can give up that thought will automatically end their resentment"(PC.4).

3. Practicing the Four Immeasurable Minds: Loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and renunciation is the optimal method to help us completely transform the seeds of anger in our hearts, remove resentment, spread love, and spread compassionate energy to everyone, even if it is the object that makes us angry.

tieu_de: THE RESULT OF ABORTION LEADS TO BEING IN HELL
tom_tat: (Collected) This is a true story, extremely thrilling and Quang Tu was fortunate to have a small part in it. Le Thi Ngoc My (born 1991) currently lives in Ho Chi Minh City. Address: 29/19 Cach Mang Thang 8
noi_dung:
THE RESULT OF ABORTION LEADS TO HELL

(Collected)

This is a true story, extremely thrilling and Quang Tu was fortunate to have a small part in it. Le Thi Ngoc My (born 1991) currently lives in Ho Chi Minh City. Address: 29/19 Cach Mang Thang 8, Tan Binh District. She is married and has a fairly stable online business.

In August 2015, due to some problems in life, My texted Quang Tu to ask about how to solve those problems, and received advice that she should regularly chant the Ksitigarbha Sutra and repent of karma.

America followed suit, and practiced very diligently, chanting diligently morning and night. Originally, from a young age, America had the special ability to sense the spirits around her. When she first returned to her husband's house, she felt that there was a spirit always following her, but even so, she was not afraid. After chanting the Ksitigarbha Sutra for a few days, My began to gradually see that spirit. Then the more she chanted, the more clearly she saw the face of that spirit.

It was a female spirit in extreme pain, her hair was falling apart, her hands were constantly scratching her body. Wherever she scratched, blood gushed out, blood all over her body, looking very scary. Every day, the ghost scratches its body, tearing pieces of flesh down to the bones, then dies, dies, then comes back to life, then continues to tear apart, and so on...

It seemed like the ghost really wanted to resist, but couldn't stop her hands from tearing herself. One time in her dream, America saw that ghost girl appear, begging her to find a way to save her from her damnation... When she woke up, America really wanted to do something to help this ghost girl, but at that time she really didn't know what to do.

At noon on October 27, 2015, My was sitting and chanting the Earth Organ Sutra. She suddenly came up with the idea of wanting to meet that spirit, and ask clearly why that spirit was so miserable. Suddenly she fainted right there, her mind saw that she had gone to another realm, and that female spirit was holding her hand and pulling her away, blood and tears poured out, falling even on America's hand.

America looked around, not knowing what kind of scene this was, but it was so scary. The sky is dark, gloomy, dark red like blood, the ground is filled with an extremely gloomy black color. Around there are black, leafless, dry trees that look very scary.

Everywhere was damp and there was a strong stench like the smell of something that had died for a long time. And here, there are countless other ghosts, sitting far away from each other, also scratching their bodies like the other ghost.

The nails were sharp, no matter how much they scratched, blood flowed out. The more blood flowed, the harder they scratched the body, the flesh fell out in pieces, exposing the bones. Just like that, they fell down, died and then came back to life, and continued to scratch...

There was also a woman drenched in blood, reaching out and hitting the American, causing her to jump. (According to this description, it is very possible that this is Hell. Due to some unknown fate, the dead woman appeared on earth to ask for help). At this moment, the ghost girl held her hand tightly and would not let go, she was scared and almost panicked. At that time, her mind immediately remembered the Buddha, and immediately she chanted non-stop "NAMO Amitabha BUDDHA! NAMMO Amitabha BUDDHA!...", just like that she chanted a lot.

A moment later, America saw a stream of light slowly appear in the sky. And the BUDDHA appeared, like the sun rising in the morning, the Buddha appeared in a large form throughout the sky, breaking through the dark night. Seeing the Buddha, she was overjoyed...

My still did not take her eyes off the Buddha, she tried her best to see clearly, the Buddha was beautiful beyond description, with a pale yellow aura radiating from behind. The faster He rotates, the brighter the light becomes. The Buddha's face is full, although he does not smile, it is full of joy, making people incredibly happy.

It can be said that the world's words cannot fully describe the beauty of the Buddha, nor is he similar to any Buddha image or Buddha statue in the world that can be compared. But it seems that other than America, no living beings in that terrible world have seen Buddha. America only saw that the other woman became afraid of her and was pushed away. Perhaps from within her, due to the power of reciting Buddha's name, a certain power emanated.

At that moment, she suddenly woke up and found herself in the hospital (it was 3am) surrounded by her family. The doctor said she showed signs of sudden death, like clinical death. She saw that her hand still had bruises that the other woman held while in the other world. Feeling very fortunate to be blessed by Buddha, she constantly turned to Buddha and expressed her deep gratitude.

The next day, My had a general check-up and was assured by the doctor that her health was normal. She returned home to her family, she continued to see the other woman, but now she seemed afraid of her, not daring to stand near her anymore. His eyes turned towards her with a pleading, pathetic look as if he wanted to tell her "Save me, save me..."

To find a way to help the dead woman, My sent a message to Quang Tu, explaining the story and asking how to save the dead woman. At that time, Quang Tu remembered the Hoa Nghiem Sutra that praised the boundless merit of generating the mind of Supreme Bodhisattva (also known as "First generation of mind"), and also, in the Earth Store Sutra, it was thanks to generating the Great Vow that Mr. Quang Mu (predecessor of Earth Store Bodhisattva) saved his mother from Hell forever. Later, he also became a Great Bodhisattva.

Based on that, Quang Tu boldly instructed My to make the Great Vow 10 times a day, for 10 consecutive days, the prayer as follows: NAMMO SHIKAMUNI BUDDHA! NAMMO Amitabha Buddha! NAMMO Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva! NAMMO Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva! I would like to bring all my good roots, vowing that from now until the very next life I will save all sentient beings throughout the dharma realm of the ten directions to attain Buddhahood, without missing a single sentient being. May the TEN BUDDHAS of all directions prove “.

Then dedicate it so that the dead woman can be liberated from all suffering. America followed suit, during this time she no longer saw the other woman following her. After two days, a strange story appeared again. That afternoon, suddenly My husband woke her up.

Her husband's expression was very strange, his face was blank, he told her: - Whatever you do, you must be persistent, maintain it continuously, try to keep your promises, don't remember and forget sometimes. America was also stunned, not understanding what her husband was talking about.

I pray for rebirth but kill, my merit has not yet been achieved, my pity is already heavy. – I've been vegetarian these past few days, so why do you call it killing? – On Friday night, I saw some ants crawling on the wall. At that time, I thought about killing them so they wouldn't burn my children.

This morning I used an insecticide spray to kill countless ants and suffocated. Don't kill for no reason, the ants come because you don't clean the house, they don't come naturally. Only then did My realize that she had used a spray bottle to kill ants in the morning.

She immediately asked again: - I will repent for this. But tell me how do you know that? Instead of answering this question, My husband continued to explain: - When learning to practice, you must practice from the heart first, a good mind will then do good deeds, if a mind is not bright, the work will not be clear, a blind mind will do many bad things, then karma must be carried. – I understand, I will change and try harder. - For the sake of your promise, keep your mind pure. Saving others to liberation is also saving yourself to be reborn in the Pure Land. – Why are you so strange today?

The answer was only silence. Her husband remained silent like that for a long time, from afternoon until evening, when a friend came over, he naturally returned to his old self. Surprised, America tried to ask him again: - Why did you say so many good things today? – You keep babbling about something I don't understand.

You didn't say anything? Why do you keep asking? In fact, it was someone who, wanting to remind America in time, relied on her husband to admonish her. Truly, one must have a very strong affinity with the Tao to receive such blessing and guidance. From that day on, she became even more diligent, chanting many sutras and repenting to dedicate the deceased woman to a quick escape.

After 10 days, while developing the Bodhi mind, chanting sutras, repenting and dedicating it to the deceased woman. Late at night on November 7, 2015, the US saw the female ghost reappear, but no longer in the same suffering as before. Instead, there was a bright and serene face (this time America saw the female ghost more clearly than usual). The female ghost came and held My hand, and they talked (not with their mouths like we always say, but directly from 'mind to heart'). Through this "mind to mind" conversation,

America learned that the female ghost who had been following her for a long time was named Nguyen Nhu Tam. In her previous life, Tam practiced abortion for others, often using machines, knives, scissors, tongs, and sharp tools to cut up the fetus and then remove it. Because of this crime, Tam had to enter that terrible realm. This is the place where sinful souls often use sharp objects to cause pain and suffering to others. They must enter this place and use their hands like sharp knives to scratch themselves, the pain is indescribable. Also in a previous life, the two were friends, once My promised Tam that "When you are in pain, just come to me".

Because of this saying, Tam found and followed America, waiting for enough fate to be saved. The right conditions were met when My started chanting the Sutras and focusing on repentance. When she began to develop the Bodhi mind and chant the Sutras to dedicate to Tam, Tam gradually let go of the attachment to this temporary body, let go of the "I" to move towards peace. When there is no more regret or attachment, there is no more suffering. The mind has seen the light appear...

Tam spoke at this last meeting, earnestly asking My and many people to chant for Tam to be completely liberated from that world and be transported to a good realm. Tam is extremely grateful for her help. If it weren't for someone who created merit and then dedicated it to her, the sentient beings who were doomed to this realm would never be able to escape. In that terrible place, they earnestly waited ten thousand times for their relatives, or for some great compassionate person to develop merit for them and save them from suffering.

Tam also added that she had planted the seeds of Buddha in her heart, praying that her future lives would be supported and enlightenment soon. The next day, My immediately went to the Buddhist Association and asked everyone to chant together to dedicate the last time to Tam. Pray that she will soon be born in a good land, have peace of mind and body, and soon attain Buddhahood....

tieu_de: REACTIONS OF BUYING AND SELLING LIVE ANIMAL MEAT (TERMITE SNAKES
tom_tat: Mr. Ngo is an overseas Chinese in Thailand, a trader who buys land products. Due to low capital, you can only buy and sell immediately, so the profit is not much. Recently, someone introduced me to
noi_dung:
PREMIFICATION OF TRADING AND SELLING LIVE ANIMAL MEAT (TERMITE SNAKES

Mr. Ngo is an overseas Chinese in Thailand, a trader who buys land products. Due to low capital, you can only buy and sell immediately, so the profit is not much. Recently, someone introduced him to buying snakes and termites, with very high profits. But Mr. Ngo only worked for three months and refused to do it anymore.

His friends all felt sorry for him. He encountered a highly profitable business but refused to continue, instead he was willing to do things with little profit like buying onions and garlic. But Mr. Ngo still doesn't feel sorry, he must have some reason?

Why is buying snakes so profitable? Then we have to discuss the dish "Great tonic gecko wine". In the ancient manuscript of famous physician Ly Thoi Tran, it was written: "Gecko nourishes the lungs, benefits the qi, nourishes the kidneys, benefits the blood, calms asthma, stops coughs." Oriental medicine to treat phlegm and asthma all uses gecko as the main medicine, so the easily sold product on the market is great tonic gecko wine.

Geckos are bought to be prepared with medicine and soaked in alcohol, the demand is increasing. Overfished geckos are almost on the verge of extinction. So the pharmacy used snakes instead of geckos. Now in China, caught termite snakes are almost extinct. So the pharmacy turned to buying snakes in Thailand.

Farmers in northeastern Thailand, when they have free time during the harvest, gather together to catch snakes to increase their income. Some people even quit farming and switched to catching snakes to get rich, including the typical To Vuong family.

To Vuong's family, including husband and wife and one child, was very poor in the past and had to rent fields to work. But since switching to snake catching, within three short years, they have had more than a dozen acres of land and even bought a small truck. With such generous profits, the villagers were eager to see it. So the movement to catch snakes rose like a tide.

But farmers can only catch more than ten snakes every day. While To Vuong is clearly rich, he also has money in the bank. Because in addition to catching termite snakes himself, To Vuong also buys live termite snakes from villagers to dry, then sell them. The number of snakes that died in the hands of To Vuong's family is estimated to be several hundred.

There are two reasons that motivated Mr. Ngo to quit his job as a snake collector:

The first reason: The other day, Mr. Ngo happened to pass by To Vuong's house and witnessed To Vuong making dry termite snakes. He caught and bought a live termite snake, then used a knife to cut open its abdomen and extract its internal organs... But at this time the termite snake was still not dead, To Vuong used a sharpened bamboo stick to pierce its mouth straight to its tail, causing it to constantly struggle in pain. It died with its eyes wide open, glaring at the person who killed it. After that, To Vuong took the snake out to dry in the sun.

The second reason: In March of one year, Thailand had an annual water slapping ceremony, the whole country was able to enjoy it. That day, Mr. Ngo returned to Bangkok from Thai Mai (Chiangmai). While passing through a mountain pass, he witnessed a tragic accident. The small truck overturned into a deep abyss along the road. Three people died at the scene, To Vuong's family, including the couple and their son.

That day, even though it was a water-slapping ceremony, To Vuong did not take a break from work and continued to drive to buy snakes. As a result, the whole family had an accident right on the pass, the goods vehicle overturned into a deep abyss. To Vuong's wife and children flew out of the car, completely dead. When he died, his eyes were still wide open, glaring, like the eyes of a termite snake when he died. Even more terrifying that I didn't dare to look, it was To Vuong himself. He flew out of the car as fast as a bullet. Without tilting or deflecting, he slowly fell right on the sharp bamboo stake that the road repair worker had just cut down at the deep abyss along the roadside. To Vuong had the tree pierced straight through his mouth to his anus, his tragic condition was exactly like the scene where Mr. Ngo once witnessed him killing a termite snake.

Because he witnessed the tragedy of To Vuong's entire family dying so tragically and horribly, he was so scared that his whole body was goosebumps, and he could only blurt out: "Retribution! What retribution!". Since then, he completely quit his job related to animal trading.

noi_dung:
ENCOUNTING THE DEMON OF YIN TY

(According to the story of Thanh Ngon Buddhist)

I had a particularly strange experience. 29 years ago, I encountered two demons. Not ghosts - souls of dead people, but demons.

I am a Buddhist in the city. HCM, dharma name Thanh Ngon. I myself am alive until today because Guan Yin saved my life, so I believe in Buddhism very much.

In October 1991, I gave birth to my second son, both mother and son were healthy. On the third day when I was about to leave the hospital, I suddenly had a continuous high fever.

In three days, all the tests were done but no cause was found. The doctor decided that if I wasn't better by the next day, he would be transferred to a higher level of care.

That evening in feverish delirium. In a trance, I saw Am Ty's ghosts appear. Even now, when I tell the story, I'm still scared and remember those two faces clearly.

The ghost has a human-like shape but is thin and naked, its head has horns like a Buffalo's head, but its face is like a Horse's, and it holds a trident in its hand. Those two ghosts aggressively grabbed my hand and dragged me away. I refused to leave. In my unconsciousness, I was still aware that I still had a newborn baby and had to take care of her. So I held the baby in one hand, the other held the bed tightly, and shouted:

-I'm not going anywhere, my child is still very young!

The next morning I woke up and my fever was gone. To the Doctor's surprise, my illness was not cured but healed on its own. By reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara, he compassionately saved me and escaped the hands of demons.

I was discharged home and have lived until today. From then on, I vowed to follow Buddhism all my life, and have been a vegetarian for 15 years.

Because I am grateful to Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, I named my son Hong An. My son grew up believing in Buddhism and sincerely worshiping Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

tieu_de: THE INSURANCE OF THE GREAT BODHISATTVA IN THE SATALAND
tom_tat: Since Buddha Shakyamuni's passing until now, humanity has entered the age of the end of dharma, natural disasters, fires, and epidemics have become more terrible than ever, because of the karma of sentient beings.
noi_dung:
INFORMATION OF THE GREAT BODHISATTVA IN SATALAND

Since the passing of Buddha Shakyamuni until now, humanity has entered the age of the end of the dharma, natural disasters, fires, and epidemics have become more terrible than ever. It is also because of the karma of sentient beings that they are so susceptible. In the time of the end of the dharma, right and wrong are confused, many people easily believe in deviant sects that go against the teachings of Buddhism. Bodhisattvas are compassionate and merciful to sentient beings. They do not want sentient beings to be deluded and misguided or suffer damnation in the three evil paths, so they use hundreds of thousands of manifestations and skillful means to educate sentient beings and pass down Buddhist sutras to help sentient beings follow the correct dharma and be born in the heavenly realms and the pure lands of the Buddhas to enjoy wonderful and wonderful peace. In the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra, chapter 12, Shakyamuni Buddha said to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has great karma with sentient beings in the world of Jambudvipa. If we talk about the beneficial things through seeing and hearing of sentient beings, it cannot be counted for hundreds of thousands of eons. Therefore, Avalokiteshvara! Please use your divine power to transmit this Sutra and do it for sentient beings in the Kham World. Throughout billions of lifetimes, you will always enjoy peace and happiness." That involves reincarnating into the human world to educate sentient beings. Therefore, we just don't know that many great bodhisattvas have manifested themselves in the samsara world to educate sentient beings, because those bodhisattvas will not reveal their identities because once revealed, they will have to leave. Many people believe that the Mahayana sutras were written by Chinese patriarchs, not by Buddha, without knowing that those Patriarchs are also the reincarnations of bodhisattvas who appear in the world to pass down the Dharma to save sentient beings.The following are some stories about the incarnations of great bodhisattvas that I personally collected and carefully selected because if what I write in this article and on this page is not in accordance with the spirit of the Dharma of Buddhism, I will commit the crime of lying and fall into the endless hells. But if I write it down, many people will gain many unimaginable benefits, so I decided to write this article and post it on this page. Only you can see this wonderful benefit for yourself. But I myself cannot know for you. I would like to take the liberty of writing it like this:

The story says that Bodhidharma, whose real name was Bodhi Da La, was the third son of the king of Huong Chi, south of Thien Truc. Although he is considered the founder of the Chinese Zen school, Bodhidharma has his roots in Thien Truc.

Prajna Da La, the 27th Patriarch of Buddhism, once came to the country of Huong Chi and met Bodhidharma. At first glance, this prince had many special features. Prajna Da La asked Dat Ma and his two brothers to discuss the word Mind. Prajna Da La saw that Bodhi Da La was a man of high enlightenment, young but could speak the important points of the word Mind. Prajna Da La advised Dat Ma: "The prince has already mastered all dharmas, so he should take the name Dat Ma, which means vast and well versed." Since then, the third prince of Huong Chi Quoc took the name Dat Ma, became a monk and worshiped Prajna Da La as his teacher. After many years of practice, with his great intelligence and enlightenment, Bodhidharma was chosen by Prajñāra as his successor, becoming the 28th patriarch of Buddhism in Thien Truc land. The story goes that, before transmitting the Dharma to Dharma, the 27th Patriarch Prajnaparamita called Dharma and asked: "Of all things, what is formless?" Bodhidharma replied: "No birth, no form." Bat Nha Da La asked again: "Of all things, what is the greatest?" Bodhidharma replied: "Buddhism is the greatest." After listening, Prajnaparamita decided to choose Bodhidharma as the 28th successor of the Buddha.

After Prajnaparamita passed away, Dat Ma remembered his teacher's advice that he must go abroad to spread the Dharma to have a great career, so when he was old, he got on a boat and sailed to Dong Tho land. That was around 520 AD, during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty. Emperor Wu was famous for being a Buddhist devotee, building countless temples for the Buddhists. As soon as he heard that a great master from Thien Truc was coming to the East to preach, Emperor Wu immediately invited him to the capital of Liang, Jianye, to meet and discuss Buddhism. Dat Ma accepted the invitation and went to meet Emperor Wu.

The meeting between Bodhidharma and Emperor Wu was recorded in the records as follows:

As a person who served Buddhism, Emperor Wu of Liang built many temples and stupas in his country.

Dharma replied: "There is no merit."

- "Why no merit."

- "Because the king's actions are "artificial" causes, there are only small consequences in the world of human beings, like images depending on the shape, although there are but not real."

- "So what is true merit?"

The king asked again: "What is the supreme meaning of the holy truth?"

- "Once you are clear and clear, nothing is holy."

- "Who is facing me?"

- "I don't know."

Those were very clear statements about the essence of Buddhism, but Emperor Wu did not understand them.

Emperor Liang Wu sent someone to see off the guests. Patriarch Bodhidharma crossed the Giang Bac River, went straight through the country of Wei, and climbed Mount Songshan.

Legend has it that after Bodhidharma left, Emperor Wu of Liang met the monk Chi Cong (who composed the book Luong Hoang Sam that you still read today), and told the story. Venerable Chi Cong asked:

- Now do you know who that person is?

Emperor Wu replied:

- Don't know.

The monk said:

- That is the great Guan Yin who came to transmit the Buddha's mind seal.

Emperor Wu regretted and sent an envoy to visit, but Bodhidharma did not return. Later, reminiscing about the past, Emperor Luong Vo composed his own epitaph as follows:

Alas!

See as if you don't see

It's as if we never met

Facing is like not facing at all

The past is now gone

Resentment equals hatred. .

Why did Emperor Liang Wu have such hatred?

That's because the king could not distinguish between the tainted merit and virtue of doing good deeds that will reap blessings in the circle of relative cause and effect, and the anadromous merit of cultivating with the ability to cross the river of birth and death. Because of this misunderstanding, the king attached great importance to the issue of giving alms to do meritorious deeds, thinking that was enough on the path of practice, without paying attention to the issue of attainment.

As for Bodhidharma, he is an enlightened Zen master, he teaches the essence, belonging to the Buddha vehicle. He taught people to practice to become enlightened and become Buddhas. Therefore, Emperor Wu of Liang did not understand him.

Through that conversation, Dat Ma knew that Emperor Wu's Buddhist ideals were not the same as his own, and it was difficult to promote his ideas, so he decided to leave. The story goes that, after saying goodbye to Emperor Wu, Dat Ma took a blade of grass and threw it into the river, then stood on the blade of grass and crossed the Yangtze River, going north, to Luoyang city, the capital of Northern Wei. In the third year of Xiaochang's reign, Emperor Hieu Minh of the Northern Wei Dynasty (ie 527), Dat Ma went to Tung Son to Shaolin Temple to spread Zen Buddhism. That was the time when the famous story of Bodhidharma's nine years of meditation took place. The story goes that, when arriving at the Shaolin Temple, Bodhidharma sat facing the cliff and practiced meditation, without saying anything for 9 years. In addition, during his spiritual practice, Bodhidharma many times demonstrated miraculous powers to save sentient beings. You can find more on the Internet.

2. THE INSURANCE OF THE GREAT SHI BODHISATTVA - GREAT MASTER ANGUANG

STORY I:

Excerpted from the words of Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa:

Now let's talk more about Old Master An Quang. He was originally from Son Tay province; After receiving the Full Precepts, he went to Putuo Mountain to "retreat." During this "retreat" period, from morning to night he sat upright, focusing on reading the Sutras with utmost reverence. Every time he went to the bathroom, he changed his clothes and put on different sandals. After going to the bathroom and purifying himself, he changed out of that outfit and then put on the clothes he usually wore when reading sutras. Even though the restroom was very clean, He still changed his clothes like that—the clothes he wore while reading the sutras were not worn when entering the restroom, and the clothes he wore when entering the restroom were not worn when entering the room to read the sutras. From morning to night, he read the scriptures with a very respectful and careful attitude. He practiced at the Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva ashram on Putuo Mountain for eighteen long years, and devotedly read the scriptures every day, never distracted.

After eighteen years of diligent study, Old Dharma Master An Quang came to Nanjing to preach the Amitabha Sutra; Do you know how? Such a highly virtuous monk preaches sutras but no one comes to listen; except for one person, who diligently came and sat on the bench every day. Seeing this, the Old Master thought that this person must really like listening to the lecture, so one day he happily asked him: "Do you understand everything when I listen to the lecture?" The reason he asked like that was because he was originally from Son Tay and his accent was a bit difficult to understand.

The person replied: "Oh! Master, I don't understand anything!"

-"Don't you understand!? So why are you sitting here?"

Alas! The old Dharma Master felt extremely sad when he heard it and told himself that from now on he would no longer come to preach in Nanjing! You see, no one came to listen when he preached the sutras. If there was one person who came regularly, it was not to listen to the lecture, but to wait for him to finish preaching so he could clear the benches!

Later, the Lay Buddhist Association in Shanghai invited Elder Dharma Master An Quang to preach the Amitabha Sutra; He accepted and this time, when he preached in Shanghai, many people came to listen. Because Buddhism in Nanjing at that time was not very prosperous, even though he was a highly virtuous monk, because there was no one to announce or disseminate the news, no one knew enough to come and listen to his sermon. And Shanghai is where a large number of his disciples who take refuge reside; These people knew that their Master was about to come to preach the Dharma and immediately announced it everywhere, so many people eagerly invited each other to come and listen to the Dharma. Among that audience was a female student about eighteen or nineteen years old, and not yet a Buddhist. One night this female student had a dream and saw someone telling her: "You should go to Ku Si Lam to listen to the sutra lecture. Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva is propagating Buddha Dharma there, and He is currently preaching the Amitabha Sutra!"

The next morning, she read the newspaper, and sure enough, she saw that there was a news about Amitabha Sutra being preached in Lay Si Lam and the preacher was Old Dharma Master An Quang. She was surprised and asked herself: "How strange! Why did I dream last night and hear that Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva preached the Amitabha Sutra?" So she immediately invited a few more classmates and together eagerly went to listen to the lecture; and she also told them that she dreamed that this Dharma Master was Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva!

Later, this female student also took refuge with Old Dharma Master An Quang. In that dream, she was also told that this Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva would only stay for three more years, and after that he would have to return, no one would be able to see him again. Sure enough, three years later, in the 33rd year of the Republic of China, Old Master An Quang passed away. After he passed away, everyone knew that he was Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva. During his lifetime, Old Dharma Master An Quang loved to copy the chapter "Great World Bodhisattva Reciting the Buddha's Recitation to Perfection" in the Shurangama Sutra; and many lay people still keep these special manuscripts with His own autographs.

Thus, Old Dharma Master An Quang is typical of a highly virtuous monk who was enlightened in modern times; Therefore, it cannot be said that five hundred years after the Buddha's nirvana, no Arhat appeared in the world! In fact, there are not only Arhats but also higher Arhats! After Old Master An Quang passed away and his body was burned, many relics remained. People who have not attained fruition or enlightenment will never have relics; If you have relics, you are not an ordinary person.

Recently, there have been Elder Venerable Hu Van, Lawyer Hoang Nhat and Elder Dharma Master An Quang—all of them are high-ranking monks of modern China and Arhats, Bodhisattvas. More specifically, everyone recognizes that Old Dharma Master An Quang is the reincarnation of Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva! Thus, after Buddha entered Nirvana, in China there were still many great virtuous monks appearing.

SECOND STORY:

September 23, 1950 Bon Khong, on the occasion of the 10th anniversary of Master An Quang's death, intended to write a nostalgic article about his teacher. Before he put pen to paper, he sincerely burned incense before his portrait. On the evening of the second day, in a strange dream, he saw his teacher again with a tall appearance and bright aura. The monk couldn't help but wonder so he asked:

– I see the teacher's appearance shining brightly. Could it be that you are Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva?

– Yes! That's right.

3. THE INFORMATION OF THE BUDDHA Amitabha, Manjushri, and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva

The late Venerable Tuyen Hoa preached at Zen That, December 1980

During the Tang Dynasty there were two great masters, one was Han Son, the other was Thap Dac. Mr. Han Son is the reincarnation of Manjushri Bodhisattva, and Mr. Thap Dac is the reincarnation of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. Both of them, Han Son and Thap Dac, were very good fellow practitioners. Mr. Thap Dac (who was raised by Venerable Phong Can at Quoc Thanh Pagoda since childhood and educated to become a good person) specializes in cooking in the tru house (the kitchen at the temple).

Every day, Thap Dac collected leftover food, put it in a bamboo tube, and offered it to Han Son. Mr. Han Son lived in Nguyet Quang cave on Thien Thai mountain, and every day he went to Quoc Thanh pagoda to pick up leftovers to eat. Because the two were "like-minded and compatible", they often laughed and joked with each other, so everyone in the temple thought they were crazy people, so they didn't care about them at all. No one expected that the two were Bodhisattvas incarnated "travelling in the human world" to save sentient beings in need of salvation!

Mr. Phong Can replied: "Yes! Because the Prefect did not recognize it. Now in the chef's house of Quoc Thanh Pagoda on Thien Thai Mountain, there is a monk who specializes in cooking, he is Samantabhadra Bodhisattva! He has a friend named Han Son, that is, Manjushri Bodhisattva. Why does the Prefect say there is no one?"

The Thai Confessor was overjoyed after hearing this, then he said goodbye, quickly headed towards Quoc Thanh Pagoda, and with sincerity bowed to the two Bodhisattvas Han Son and Thap Dac. When Venerable Tri saw the Thai Prefect coming to Quoc Thanh Pagoda, he was extremely attentive and welcoming. But when Master Tri heard that the Thai Prefect wanted to pay homage to Han Son and Thap Dac, he was extremely surprised; I don't understand why the Crown Prince wants to meet two crazy guys.

Even though he did not understand the reason, Master Tri Guest also led the Thai governor to the chef's house. At that time, Han Son and Thap Dac were talking and laughing, their crazy looks making everyone laugh. However, La Thai Thu extremely respectfully bowed to the two, then also said very respectfully: "My disciple La Khuu Yen would like to request the two great Bodhisattvas to compassionately point out the confusion."

Mr. Thap Dac asked: "What are you doing?"

After hearing Thap Dac, he stepped back and said: "Phong Can talks a lot! Phong Can talks a lot! Phong Can is the reincarnation of Amitabha, why don't you bow to Amitabha and come here to bother us?" He walked back and forth as he spoke. When he finished speaking, he had just reached the temple gate. When they reached Nguyet Quang cave, the two of them hid on the cliff and disappeared.

The Chief Minister saw this and was extremely disappointed, because the two Bodhisattvas had hidden themselves in the cliff and would not come out again. Therefore, the mandarins thought: "Well, let's go back and bow to Amitabha Buddha!" However, by the time the Prefect returned to the temple, Venerable Phong Can had already passed away! It's true that "I'm too busy" (missing the opportunity in front of me)! It's also called:

“Unconsciously facing Avalokiteshvara.”

(Meet Avalokiteshvara but did not recognize Him.)

Through the above stories, you can know for yourself whether what I say is true or false. Nowadays there are too many people preaching sutras and discussing the Dharma, many Buddhists do not know where to turn to practice, not to mention that some teachings are wrong in the Dharma, but because each person's style of speaking is different, and low capacity is very difficult to understand and absorb, I would like to take the liberty of introducing to you some modern monks. If you follow their Dharma and practice, it will definitely be in the right Dharma and will never go wrong:

tieu_de: PREGNANT WOMEN - SHOULD PRACTICE SUTRAS, REMEMBER BUDDHA AND PRAY FOR PEACE OF MIND AND PEACE
tom_tat: Buddhism guides us through the method. When you know you are pregnant, you should immediately read and recite the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra every day, or recite thousands of verses of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name. It is necessary to use a sincere heart
noi_dung:
PREGNANT WOMEN - SHOULD CHAIN SUTRAS, REMEMBER BUDDHA AND PRAY FOR PEACE AND PEACE OF MIND

Buddhism guides us through the method. When you know you are pregnant, you should immediately read and recite the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra every day, or recite thousands of verses of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name.

If you use a sincere and respectful mind to chant, the blessings will be extremely great.

Even if the unborn baby comes to the family to take revenge, and is an unjust bondholder, but because we take care of the baby like that, the unjust debt will be resolved. Because we are kind to it, it no longer repays hatred but turns into gratitude.

Conversion must be right at the beginning. The scriptures emphasize that it must be at least seven days before birth. Of course the sooner the better. When we understand this principle and know this method, it is best to recite it as soon as we know we are pregnant and practice according to the method.

For mothers, it is necessary to have a peaceful, sincere, respectful, pure, and even mind, because starting up thoughts will affect the fetus.

If this is said according to modern scientific theory, it is even easier to understand. This belongs to the phenomenon of wave motion.

- Venerable Tinh Khong -

________________________________

* Comment: In the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra, Shakyamuni Buddha talked about the benefits of reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra as follows:

Great wishes are quickly fulfilled: Wishes and desires in the present or future life will certainly be fulfilled. All those who make great vows, want to save sentient beings, and want to achieve Bodhi are helped by the Bodhisattva's mighty power to achieve their wishes.

Eliminates sin and illness: People who are terminally ill, bedridden, half-dead, are because the karma-path of impeachment has not yet come to a definitive decision, so it is difficult to die as well as difficult to heal. During this time, relatives should use the patient's property and precious objects to paint images, make offerings to Bodhisattvas, inform the sick person, and continuously recite this sutra. That person, because of karma, has to suffer a serious illness, will be cured of the disease, live a long life, and if the karma is gone, at death all karma will be eliminated, will no longer fall into the three evil paths, but will be reborn in Heaven.

Buddha also revealed the work that relatives need to do during the 49 days when the soul of the dead is still wandering, always looking forward to their relatives and flesh and blood to cultivate merit and virtue as their luggage, capital for them to be able to easily enter the supernatural. The main efforts of relatives during this time should be expressed by positive actions such as not killing creatures or making offerings to gods or demons. After 49 days, the deceased will receive retribution depending on their karma.

Perhaps the "Tibetan Book of Life and Death" of Tibetan Buddhism is a book that describes quite clearly the stages of change of consciousness - or the intermediate body (bardo) of humans from the moment of death until 49 days later, in accordance with the teachings that Buddha expressed in the Ksitigarbha Sutra. In the section "Warnings before the place of rebirth" the author said: "Those who have to be born in hell will hear sounds like lamentations and will be irresistibly forced to go in. There will appear dark spaces, black and white houses, black holes in the ground, dark paths that people will have to follow. Entering there, people will enter hell and will suffer from being too hot, too cold... and will have to suffer for a long time. It takes a long time to get out". Therefore, for the dying person, the presence of a master or a good intellectual who at that time the dying person respects, believes in, recites to them the scriptures or recites the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, specifically Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara or Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva - or any Bodhisattva that during his lifetime he chose to worship as his Great Master will be of great help to the dead person to quickly ascend to the next world. Buddha. And through my own experiences, I would like to confirm with you that the things in the Mahayana Sutra, every sentence and every word, are not wrong, friends. It's just that when you practice diligently until the conditions are perfect, you will understand.

( Tran An)

tieu_de: FIRST, IF YOU THINK IT IS BENEFICIAL TO YOURSELF, EVERY DAY REMEMBER TEN TEN TEN, BUDDHA'S SIGNS AND PROGRESSIONS.
tom_tat: ------------- There are many fellow practitioners who often say: "Our karma is very heavy, we pray to eliminate our karma every day." Can karma be eliminated? Quite difficult! The origin of karma
noi_dung:
FIRST, IF YOU THINK IT IS BENEFICIAL TO YOU, EVERY DAY REMEMBER TEN TEN TEN, BUDDHA SIGNS AND PROGRESSIONS

-------------

There are many practitioners who often say: "We have very heavy karma, we pray to eliminate our karma every day." Can karma be eliminated? Quite difficult! What is the origin of karma? You find it, then you will eliminate it from there, eliminate karma from the base, don't eliminate it from the branches, it's very painful! Very difficult! Can't spend it all!

The root of karma is self-interest; Those who are self-interested will have all kinds of karma. If you can eliminate your own selfish and self-interested mind and start thinking to always benefit all sentient beings, your karma will be completely eradicated and there will be no more karma.

Why do you say "no more karma?" There is no self! Without self, how can there be karma? What else is there to hinder? That's called "eradicated completely".

If you first think about whether or not everything is beneficial for you, your karma won't be eliminated in any way! Reciting ten thousand verses of Buddha's name every day is in vain! Every day, I bow to Luong Hoang Sam and kowtow until my forehead is cracked, but my karma still does not go away!

If you can expand your mind, start thinking about always thinking about benefiting all sentient beings, basically not thinking about yourself, then you don't need to recite Buddha's name, nor do you need to worship Buddha, but karma is completely absent! These are true words, we must correct errors and innovate. The root cause of mistakes is selfishness, that is, thinking about yourself in everything, that is the root of the disease!

Therefore, Buddhism from beginning to end is about breaking the Ego. Why are you taught to make dedication vows during the study process? Dedication is giving all the merit and blessings that you have cultivated and learned to give to others. You don't need it yourself, you practice it for others, not for yourself.

In other words, you must forget yourself, this is the wonderful method of breaking the Ego in Mahayana, expanding the Ego, expanding it to transform it, making the small Ego no longer exist. What is ego? Exhausting the void throughout the dharma world is the Self, thinking for all sentient beings is thinking for yourself, thinking for yourself means thinking for all sentient beings, that is eliminating karma.

-------------

MAGIC THANH KONG

http://vetinhtv.com

tieu_de: WHERE DO THE LEFTOWNERS COME FROM? FROM THE PAST LIFE UNTIL TO THIS DAY, THESE WONDERLES HAVE BEEN SUFFERED BY
tom_tat: A fellow practitioner came to tell me that he had a friend whose oldest son, about 2 or 3 years old, often told everyone in the house that he saw a lot of people in the house, some with red faces, some with red faces.
noi_dung:
WHERE DO THE LEFTOWNERS COME FROM? FROM THE PAST LIFE UNTIL TO THIS DAY, THESE WONDERLES HAVE BEEN SUFFERED

A fellow practitioner came to tell me that he had a friend whose oldest son, about 2 or 3 years old, often told everyone in the house that he saw a lot of people in the house, some with red faces, some with blue faces, some with white faces, he said there were many, many people. After this fellow practitioner finished speaking, he asked me if this story was true or false? I say this is all real, children can see things that adults cannot see. Why? Because a child's mind is pure, it has no delusions, no discrimination or attachment, so it is easy for it to see. Only when this child's mind begins to have delusions of attachment and discrimination will he no longer see.

If you pay close attention, you will see very clearly that when a baby is just born for a few months, when it lies alone, it often smiles as if someone is joking or talking to it, and sometimes it cries out loud as if someone is bullying it. What is this? It is that he has seen and is in contact with the unjust bondholders in the house. Where do these unjust bondholders come from? From past lives until today, these unjust people have been persecuted by the people in that family, so now they always follow, waiting for the opportunity to take revenge, to collect debts from the people in that family.

So, now that we have studied Buddhism, we must know that we need to resolve the resentment with these unjust bondholders. In addition to dedicating to them every day, we should also encourage them to come and be our dharma protectors, practice reciting Buddha's name together so that after giving up this retribution body, we can be reborn in the Pure Land.

We need to study according to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who practice self-transformation and transform others. So what is self-transformation? Is to make an effort to diligently practice reciting the Buddha's name, first to be reborn in the Pure Land in the future, and second to save sentient beings. In saving sentient beings, the most important thing is to resolve the injustice of our family's misfortune. Not only can we resolve the unjust family of our own bondholders, but if we have the ability, we can also resolve the unjust family of all living beings. The unjust bondholders see us every day making efforts to practice, making efforts to resolve grievances, they will be very happy, and will all agree to practice with us.

The fellow practitioners in Singapore all know that the old Lam chief of layman Lam, when he passed away, left behind a very formidable legend. He also has many unjust bondholders who always follow revenge. At the time of his death, in Lam's ashram, there was a class to train talented people in the Dharma. There were twenty students in the class. They were divided into many groups, each group consisting of 4 people who took turns day and night to pray for him. One day, when the students returned to the Lam ashram, an incident happened. In the ashram, there was a young female student. I still remember her name was Do My Tuyen. She was possessed by a ghost. The ghost said:

" There are many of us who are the unjust bondholders of Elder Lam. Now Elder Lam has reborn after reciting the Buddha's name. We are very happy to see it with our own eyes. We did not prevent him from going to rebirth."

This is his unjust bondholder coming to tell us that he has truly been reincarnated. After that, these unjust bondholders followed the guardian students back here. At Lam's lay ashram there was a Dharma Protector, and the Dharma Protector agreed to let them in. We asked them what they wanted to pray for? They say they want to receive the Three Refuges and listen to the Sutra, they also intend to listen to the Ksitigarbha Sutra. We invited them to the lecture hall to listen to the Sutras, but they said the light in the lecture hall was too bright, they did not dare to enter. Finally, they asked to listen to the Sutra in the hall (ie the dining room). We immediately played a tape teaching the Ksitigarbha Sutra for them to listen to day and night without interruption. About 2 months later, they all left. We can also guess which path they were born into. If they work hard enough, they will be born in the Pure Land, then they will be born in the Heaven world, and some may be born in the Human world, that's for sure. This is a real story that we saw with our own eyes, it is not fake.

Please recite "Amitabha Buddha" often 😚 😉 😁 😗 😉 😄 😂 😚 😉 😗 😙

Resources for Learning Traditional Culture Ethics.

tieu_de: STARTING A GOOD AND BAD MEMORY ALL CREATES CAUSES FOR THE AFTER LIFE
tom_tat: There is nothing more precious in this world than life, insects still desire to live and are afraid of death, let alone humans. Even though a person has committed a heinous crime, he still shows remorse when he is about to die. We must have mercy on n
noi_dung:
GIVING A GOOD AND BAD MEMORY IS CREATED FOR THE AFTER LIFE

In this world, there is nothing more precious than life, insects are afraid of death, let alone humans. Even though a person has committed a heinous crime, he still shows remorse when he is about to die. We must sympathize with the person who is forced to leave his parents, wife and children, and countless other relatives who are heartbroken by this scene of separation and death. Seeing this scene, wouldn't you feel pity? Seeing and killing angry people is a person who has no mercy and is also an evil person.

Luong Vo De was walking outside the city one day and saw a melon seller standing in the middle of the market offering to customers. A person dressed in luxury came and paid a very high price. The melon seller not only refused to sell, but also angrily chased him away, thinking that this rich customer despised him. Customers saw that the melon seller was angry and left. A while later, Emperor Wu saw a man in shabby clothes coming to buy a melon. The melon seller saw this customer coming and smiled and talked to the customer as if he had known him for a long time and gave the melon to the unknown customer without accepting any money. Emperor Wu felt strange and asked the Zen master Chi Cong about what he saw.

The Zen master replied:

- The melon seller in his previous life was a criminal. When he was taken to the execution ground, there was a person who saw that the criminal was a great villain in the village. Not only did he not show mercy, but he was even more angry and cursed silently: "A criminal like you must die early to avoid harming others, and must die many times." There was another person, when he saw that the criminal was about to die, he expressed pity and thought to himself: "Young people are about to suffer extreme torture, what a pity. If the big man reduces his sentence, maybe he will repent in the future and change his ways."

(Excerpt from "Thai Thuong Touches the Heavens)

• Comment: Through the above story, and from what the Buddha taught in the scriptures, we can see that everything from body, speech and mind creates karma. In the above case, giving rise to a bad idea about a person will result in retribution in the next life: that person will not like you even though they themselves do not know why, so today if someone does not like you, you should think that it is because of my previous life. Because of bad thoughts towards them, they are like this now. We should welcome them with joy and not blame them. Once we become like that, the cycle of karma will be resolved! The retribution for having bad thoughts about an ordinary person is still the same, let alone the retribution if having bad thoughts about noble monks, pure virtues, Bodhisattvas, Buddhas, you should be very careful of this!

( Tran An)

tieu_de: WE DON'T KNOW THE TRUTH OF THE HUMAN UNIVERSE. WE ASSUME THAT WE HAVE SEEN, HEARD CLEARLY, BELIEVED.
tom_tat: (🔖The story of Great Master Phap Chieu [the 4th patriarch of the Pure Land Sect] coming to court at Ngu Dai Mountain and being taught by Bodhisattva Manjushri the method of practice in the Dharma-ending period will clarify this issue.) ✳️Sutra: Dear
noi_dung:
WE DON'T KNOW THE TRUTH OF THE UNIVERSE OF HUMAN LIFE, SO WE SHOULD SEE THAT WE HAVE SEEN, HEARD CLEARLY, AND BELIEVED

These things mentioned in the Ksitigarbha Sutra cannot be verified with a modern scientific perspective, why? Our present-day science, to be honest, is still relatively childish. How many people know the truth of the universe before our eyes? Don't think that what you saw with your own eyes is true, it's not trustworthy. What your own eyes see, the ultimate function of your eyes is great. You don't know. [Say] I saw with my own eyes, twenty-some people in our lecture hall, I saw with my own eyes, in this lecture hall there are also Bodhisattvas, Thanh Van, Pratyekabuddhas, heavenly dragons, ghosts and gods, have you seen these people? If you don't see it, how can you say you saw it with your own eyes? How can you confirm that? Why don't you see? Because the function of your eyes is very limited. We know that the eyes can see thanks to light, when it's dark you can't see, you have to rely on light to see. The waves of light are not the same, what we see belongs to some light with very short waves, our visible waves are all located in this short segment, [objects with light waves located] in this segment we see very clearly, we do not see objects with longer light waves, nor can we see shorter ones. I don't know how many longer light waves [this section] are, and I don't know how much shorter. If one day the obstructions to your eyes' functions disappear, all your light waves will be unobstructed, and the world you see will immediately change and will never be the same as before. So how can you believe that what you see is all real? The eyes see colors and the ears hear sounds all in the same situation. Here I tell you the truth.

Nowadays, talking about these things, you can quite understand, we use scientific and technical machines that can measure light waves that our eyes cannot see. Everyone is familiar with the 'ultraviolet light' we cannot see, the X-ray we cannot see either, relying on machines we know it exists. Scientists know that many light waves are different and our physical eyes cannot see them. So the light waves exist at the same time, if you could see them all, this ashram would be very unusual. How big is this ashram? How big is this room? Destroying the void, all over the dharma world, it is inconceivable. Why is it so big that it reaches into nothingness, covering the entire dharma realm? If your eyes are open, all obstacles are no longer there, you can see all light waves, these light waves spread throughout the emptiness of the dharma realm. These pillars and walls are transparent and have no obstacles. You sit here looking up, seeing the immeasurable emptiness of the dharma realm above; Look down, to the left, to the right, the boundless worlds of the ten directions are all in front of you, you will not be limited by such a small range, this is the truth. If you use the current scientific method to test the evidence, the test will not come out, the proof will not come out either, it must be said that scientific and technical capacity has not yet developed to this level; Actually, science and technology are still relatively childish when compared to Buddhism. There is a part of Buddha's words that has been proven, just a very small part, most of which science and technology have not yet reached, so we must trust Buddha's words.

'Mem Phu De mountain in the east', there is Thiet Vi mountain, which we cannot see with our physical eyes, nor can scientific machinery find it. When I was still in Taiwan, someone came to ask me: "Currently, the nuclear core has reached the bottom of the sea. The Dragon Palace has not been discovered. Is the Dragon Palace real or not? The Dragon Palace is at the bottom of the sea, and the submarine peak has not been found. There is a Moonlight Bodhisattva on the moon. Astronauts who have set foot on the moon cannot see it, is it possible?" Have! People do not see ordinary saints living together. To be honest, people who know a little about Buddhism should know these things. During the Tang Dynasty, when the magician Phap Chieu visited Ngu Dai Son and saw the Great Saint Truc Lam Tu, this is something he personally experienced, we believe that he did not lie. Meeting Manjushri, Samantabhadra was preaching the sutra and preaching the Dharma to an audience of more than ten thousand people. He listened to the entire session and also asked Manjushri Bodhisattva to teach him: "In the End of the Ages, sentient beings have low-born natures, what Dharma method should we learn?" Manjushri Bodhisattva advised him to practice the Buddha's name. How to recite the Buddha's name, and teach him to recite it for a few hours. The 'Five Assembly of Buddha's Recitation Dharma' was transmitted to him by Manjushri Bodhisattva. He left Ngu Dai Son, making signs as he walked to make it easier to find the next time he came. After making signs in a few places, he turned around and looked back, [Truc Lam Tu] was no more, only seeing a desolate hill and mountain. Think about it, how can we find it using science? Manjushri Bodhisattva's ashram is pure and dignified, only those with predestined relationships can see it. Readers of 'Sam Mui Thuy Sam', National Master Ngo Dat saw that Venerable Ca Noc Ca's ashram in Sichuan was also in a desolate mountain area, how could scientific machinery find it? When he went there, he truly healed his illness.Therefore, you cannot trust yourself. Seeing and hearing it yourself is not trustworthy. This situation is very complicated. How much can you see?

So we don't know the truth of the human universe, we think we have seen very clearly, heard very clearly, believed in our own knowledge, but don't we know that it is all wrong? Therefore, in the sutras, the Buddha teaches us very clearly: "If you have not yet reached Arhatship, do not believe in your own ideas", [this] is very logical. What is Arhat like? The Arhat has already passed through, there are no more obstacles, the Arhat has attained the End of Stalks. Therefore, his six senses are in contact with the six external realms unlike ours. He breaks through all the limits of light waves, sound waves, and magnetic waves. He sees the truth, we see illusions. Why did Arhat have this ability? Very simply, Kien Tu's afflictions have been ended, meaning the six obstacles I mentioned earlier have been ended. Arhat cessation is nothing else, that is, cessation of greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, doubt, and evil views; Evil views are the Five Benefits, which is also like the word we often call: Views of afflictions. Having ended this affliction, their obstacles no longer exist, and they can see the truth of the human universe. These words must be said first, otherwise these things in the Ksitigarbha Sutra will be very difficult to understand. What would you consider these things to be? If you are superstitious, you will think that these things are not scientific, and you will not gain even one cent of the benefits of this sutra. Not only does it not achieve anything, it also creates the crime of blasphemy. Benefits are not achieved but harm comes. This is not the Buddha's intention. Therefore, when we preach sutras of this type, we must explain this principle clearly and transparently.

🌐We invite fellow students to read more at: https://hoasenvanno.files.wordpress.com/2014/01/dia-tang-giang-ky.pdf

tieu_de: THE POWER OF THE GREAT BIOGRAPHY.
tom_tat: There was a young man named Tieu Phi. After I advised him to stop eating salty foods, become a vegetarian, and practice meditation, in less than a few days he gained some miraculous powers. One day he came to my house and asked: -
noi_dung:
THE POWER OF THE GREAT BIOGRAPHY.

There was a young man named Tieu Phi. After I advised him to stop eating salty foods, become a vegetarian, and practice meditation, in less than a few days he achieved some miraculous powers. One day he came to my house to question me:

- Are you talking about reciting the Great Compassion Mantra that has power over heaven and earth? But every day, every morning, I recite the Great Compassion Mantra ten times, but I don't see any good appearances, I only see ghosts and gods passing by, looking at me half-eyed, what's the matter?

At that time Qua Dat (my son), 15 years old, was also there. So I told both of them:

- Now I chant the Great Compassion Mantra, Tieu Phi is worried about watching the feeling in the sky, and Qua Dat is watching the feeling in hell![10] After giving instructions, I immediately sat cross-legged, tapped the bell (at that time I was still very attached to appearances, in fact there was no need for that) and started chanting the Great Compassion Mantra. I hadn't finished reciting a few sentences when I suddenly heard Tieu Phi sobbing in my ear. After finishing reciting, I asked him:

- Why are you crying?

Y replied:

- As soon as he rang the bell, I saw many heavenly beings and demons gathering. As soon as he recited the mantra, many heavenly beings knelt down and clasped their hands to listen. Sometimes they stood with clasped hands to listen, and two flying dragons also landed and lay on the ground, listening. After he finished reciting, everyone bowed and left. I was so shocked that I burst into tears.

As a result, while I chanted the mantra, all punishments for sins were suspended in hell. All those who received the punishment knelt there, clasped their hands and listened to the Great Compassion Mantra. After chanting the mantra, the execution in hell begins again, but the level is reduced, and the suffering of the person being punished is also lighter.

Listening to them, I suddenly felt excited, so I told Tieu Phi:

- Keeping the precepts is not only about not killing or eating meat, but also: Not doing evil things, diligently doing good things, and sincerely repenting for the sins committed in the past.

The more diligent you are in correcting your faults, the more distant the sound of chanting the mantra will be and the more sentient beings will come to listen to the sutra! Chanting is like that! Chanting the mantra is to rely on the power of the mantra to eliminate karma. Demons, gods, and people who hear it will immediately eliminate their karma.

Chanting the sutra can make sentient beings understand, know their mistakes and repent, and permanently end ignorance. If a true practitioner chants the sutra, it will make the Heavenly people hear and gain longevity, and the ghosts and gods will soon leave the evil path and be reincarnated into the good realm. Anyone who does not do evil things and always does good things will gain immeasurable merit when chanting sutras and mantras.

At that time, I had just observed the precepts and had not been fasting for long, so I could only gather many heavenly beings, ghosts, and spirits to listen to the mantra. If I practice well, countless sentient beings will come to listen to the sutra and receive benefits. Furthermore, while chanting the mantra, the mind must be focused and calm, otherwise it will be difficult to achieve absolute results.
