tom_tat: (A TOUCHING STORY). This time (in 1961) the Ksitigarbha Sutra was preached at the Great Vows Platform, Ksitigarbha Hall, Gia Nghia district. It is said that this temple was built more than three hundred years ago. At that time, there was a person from Gi
noi_dung:
INFLUENCE OF KITITA KIṣigarbha Bodhisattva.

(A TOUCHING STORY).

This time (in 1961) the Ksitigarbha Sutra was preached at the Great Vow Hall, Ksitigarbha Hall, Gia Nghia district. It is said that this temple was built more than three hundred years ago. At that time, a person from Chiayi, Taiwan province, went on a pilgrimage to Jiuhua mountain, Anhui province, invited a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva back, and immediately built a temple to worship it. Since then, visitors from all over have come to worship endlessly, and there are many records of the miracle. The fake pen would like to write down a story as follows.

I/ Lam Dang Chuong was unjustly imprisoned in prison, the wife sold her child to redeem her husband's life.

The story happened more than a hundred years ago. There was a man named Lam Dang Chuong, residing in a village about ten miles from Gia Nghia, who was an honest person. Unfortunately, he was falsely accused by a group of thugs, taken to the mandarin's gate, and then imprisoned. The wife, seeing that her husband was unjustly imprisoned and the family was in poverty, went everywhere to complain for her husband. She sold all the things in the house, used the money to take care of work, but still could not take care of her husband to escape the crime. Then, hearing that the district official insisted on forty taels of silver to release her husband, she was in a helpless situation and had no choice but to grit her teeth and close her eyes, sell her only beloved son for forty taels of silver, and the matchmaker took a commission of three taels, leaving only thirty-seven taels, not knowing if it was enough to atone for her husband's sins. Every time I visit my husband, the prison guards curse and make things difficult for me, with the intention of extorting money. They say: "Lean on the mountain to eat the mountain, lean on the water to drink water." That's right, if you have a lawsuit, you can go to the mandarin's door, if you don't have money, even if you have a reason, you won't be able to enter. This is something that has always been the same. Mrs. Lam, every time you come, you have to smile and talk politely, and you also have to bring some gifts, otherwise you won't be able to visit your husband. There is an ancient saying: "The King of Hell is easy to meet, but the little devil is difficult to deal with." That day, I brought money to ransom my husband, of course it was no different than usual. At that time, the prison was at Dai Nhai, currently Ngo Phung street. Nearby there is a shop selling betel and areca nuts. Mrs. Lam went there to buy some as an offering as a gift for the prison guards. Unexpectedly, after taking the money to buy betel and areca, when wrapping it up, the bag containing thirty-seven taels of silver suddenly fell out. Then, when she came to hand over the money to the mandarin, she reached in to get the money bag, only to realize that the money bag was missing. Mrs. Lam was terrified, her face was white, there was no blood left, she was so scared that she cried without making a sound. She sold her beloved son, only hoping to get her husband back. Now the money is gone, her husband can't get out of prison, the only option is to commit suicide. At that time, Mrs. Lam was not discouraged, so she followed the old road to find it. If she couldn't find it again, the only way was death.

II/ A poor child sees wealth without greed

In Gia Nghia district, there is a street, currently Quang Minh street, with a temple worshiping the Earth. In the temple, there resides a beggar child named Tu Luong Tu. Not only was he orphaned and poor, but he was also disabled. One leg was paralyzed and could not move, so he had to crawl on the ground to walk. During the day, he spends time on the side of the road begging for food, and at night he sleeps at the Tho Dia temple. That day, while he was begging for food, he suddenly saw a woman from afar buying betel and areca leaves and hurriedly walked away, her money bag falling on the ground. He then crawled to the place, picked up the silver bag, intending to chase after it to give it back to her, but unfortunately he could not keep up. Even though he called out loudly, the woman did not hear, so he opened the silver bag to look, and saw that it contained thirty-seven taels of silver. Even though the friend had seen such shining amounts of silver, he still felt dismayed. However, it did not give rise to desire, but thought that the woman just now looked very hurried, must have had a very important matter, could not just take the money away, if that person came back to look for it and could not find it, he would probably commit suicide, so he waited there for the woman to return. After waiting for a long time, I saw a woman with a very worried look on her face, running east and west as if looking for something. He knew that the miserable owner was coming back, so he waited until the woman approached, then pulled his hand on the hem of her shirt. Mrs. Lam thought the boy wanted to ask for money, so she frowned and shouted: "I'm worried to death, I can't give you any money. Go somewhere else. I'm looking for the lost item."

Tu Luong Tu has a good heart, yet he was unfairly scolded, but he still answered softly: "Grandma, what are you looking for so urgently? Tell me, maybe I can help you." When Mrs. Lam heard that, it was like a dying person being saved, so she happily asked the baby: "Really?" The boy replied: "Of course. I just picked up something. If you're right, I'll give it back to you." Mrs. Lam's pale face said: "I lost a cloth bag, which contained thirty-seven taels of silver. This is the amount of money I sold my son. My husband was falsely accused and was imprisoned. The mandarin demanded forty taels of silver to atone for his crime. I had no choice but to sell my son. The matchmaker took all three taels, leaving thirty-seven taels. I didn't know if it was enough to ransom my husband or not, but unexpectedly it would be lost. If I couldn't find it, my husband wouldn't be able to get out. Hell, my child has been sold, my people are gone, I have no choice but to commit suicide! After speaking, she cried.

At that time, there were many people surrounding eagerly asking questions from east to west. Tu Luong Tu no longer had any doubts and told her: "I'm not lying, I'm keeping that silver. This is when you bought the betel and areca nuts and lost it. Because I couldn't run after you, you didn't listen when I called out loud, so I was here waiting for you to come back. Now the silver is here, please try counting again." After the boy handed over the bag of money, he left without saying a word.

Mrs. Lam received the bag of money, her heart was filled with joy, she completely forgot about the beggar boy, she didn't even bother to ask his name, she hurriedly brought the money to the mandarin's door to atone for her husband's sins. When the district man heard the story, he realized that the money was earned by selling his child. He also heard the story of the little beggar who was not greedy for money. He thought to himself, what conscience do I have for taking money from selling someone else's child? By the way, the next morning he ordered the husband to be released, without demanding a ransom. This is because the story of the child beggar named Tu touched the mandarin's heart.

After leaving prison, Lam Dang Chuong knew that his son had been sold, so he went to find his son's whereabouts, spending a lot of money, but in the end he still couldn't find him. The couple set up an iron shop near the market to make a living.

III/ Kindness receives good results, ending disability

Talking about Tu Luong Tu, after returning to the Tho Dia temple to stay one night, the next morning was the Qingming period. Early in the morning, he went to the public grave site, called "Dong Lang Phien Gian" in the suburbs, to ask for the printed bread that people had offered to his ancestors to eat. Because it was a long way and it was raining, it was a bit late to return, so it dragged slowly, so when it reached the city gate, the city gate was closed. Reluctantly, he went to Ksitigarbha Temple in the vicinity (currently 81 Dan Quyen Street), begging him to let him stay overnight in the main hall. Mr. Tu also knew his face, so he let him stay temporarily. It slept until midnight, then suddenly cried out loudly, begging the devil to forgive its sins. He thought it was having a fit, so he yelled at it twice, but it still didn't listen. He was disturbed by it all night and couldn't sleep, his anger boiled over. The next morning, as soon as he woke up, he went to the main hall to chase it away, and saw it sleeping soundly like death. Mr. Tu shouted loudly for him to wake up, scolding him for calling him a ghost last night. Tu Luong Tu heard the loud cry and was startled to stand up. Without even knowing it, he ran in front of Mr. Tu. When he saw that, he felt extremely surprised to the point of trembling and hastily retreated. Didn't expect it to be able to walk naturally in just one night? He asked and found out that last night he was sleeping in front of the statue of Ksitigarbha. He dreamed that Bodhisattva called two demons, one high and one short. One demon held his upper body, one grabbed his legs. The two demons pulled him away, making him scream in pain. The two demons ignored it and continued to pull its crippled leg, causing the pain to become unbearable and cause it to faint. Then I fell asleep without knowing it. Right now, he still doesn't know that his crippled leg has become normal. The joy was even greater than when I picked up the silver bag yesterday. When he saw it had such inspiration, he no longer scolded it, but was also happy for it. Tu Luong Tu now knew that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva had manifested and cured his disability. He knelt before his statue, tears streaming down his face, deeply grateful, bowing his head in gratitude.

IV/ After getting over his disability, he carried water for a living.

After Tu Luong Tu was no longer disabled, many people came to congratulate him, but he began to feel worried again. When I was disabled, I could still beg for food. Now that my body is normal, I can no longer beg. You must definitely be self-reliant. However, until now we have only known how to beg, what should we do now to solve the problem of food and clothing? Doing business without capital? In the end, he found a solution: he took some of the money he had saved, bought two buckets of water, and then hired water to make a living. Back then, there was no running water, and well-off families called water delivery people to come to their homes every day. Tu Luong Tu from a beggar became a hired water bearer.

V/ Call to deliver water, meet a grateful person.

After Lam Dang Chuong was released from prison, he learned about his wife's lost money bag, the beggar's child who had picked it up without being greedy, etc. He also searched for this benefactor, but he didn't even know how to find his name. Lam's family lived in the countryside at that time. They didn't know where that beggar child was, but they always thought about it. Three years later, the Lam family's ironmongery shop became more and more prosperous, and their thoughts about their benefactor became deeper and deeper.

One ​​day, the Lam family called Tu Luong Tu to bring water. Lam Dang Chuong had never met Tu, so he didn't know who the water bearer was. At that time, women rarely went out. Whenever men came to the house, they often stayed away, so for many years they have not been able to find their benefactor. Fortunately, Tu Luong Tu carried water to the kitchen, when Mrs. Lam accidentally saw it and felt very surprised. This man's face looks exactly like his benefactor, don't you know it's him? Surely not, because that boy is crippled, can't walk normally, and why is this person exactly like him? For several days, she was half in doubt and half in doubt, not knowing what to think, so she brought the matter up and told her husband: "This young man carrying water, his face is exactly like the benefactor's, I don't know why he is not lame, but can carry water. Tomorrow, please invite him in and ask him kindly, what job he used to do?"

The next day, when Tu Luong Tu came to carry water, Mr. Lam specially invited him to stay for dinner, then asked him his name, what was his job before working as a water carrier? Are there any other relatives? Tu Luong Tu also answered honestly without any concealment: "It's a shame. Three years ago, I couldn't carry water, nor could I walk. For many years, I could only crawl on the ground. At that time, I had no choice but to beg to live. That year, during the Qingming Festival, I stayed at Ksitigarbha Temple. I dreamed that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva caused two demons to treat me. From then on, I was no longer disabled, so I worked as a water carrier to make a living." At that time, Mrs. Lam came out of the room, grabbed her husband's hand, the couple knelt on the ground, calling out: "Benefactor, please accept my bow."

Tu Luong Tu didn't know what to do, so he stood up and retreated in fear, waving his hands wildly. After listening to the Lam couple explain the story, they learned that the story happened during the Qingming period three years ago. At that time, I realized that because I had done a good deed, Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha appeared to come and treat the disability. In my heart, I was both happy and scared. Everyone sat down together to talk about what happened over the past three years. Tu Luong Tu stood up to say goodbye, but the Lam couple insisted on keeping him.

VI/ Lam Dang Chapter of Appreciation, Plans for Retribution

From then on, Tu Luong Tu no longer carried water for hire, but stayed in the ironmongery shop to help the Lam couple. Within a few years, Mr. and Mrs. Lam not only prospered in business but also bought a lot of land. They also wanted to help Tu Luong Tu get married many times, but he refused. Mr. Lam knows that Tu is an upright person, saying one thing and not saying two, so he lets him decide naturally.

A few years later, Mr. Lam received a letter from his uncle from Guangdong, wanting him to return to his hometown to inherit the family business. Mr. Lam and his wife decided to return to their hometown, asking Tu Luong Tu to manage all their assets, not daring to say they would completely hand over the assets, letting him believe that they would return soon, otherwise Tu Luong Tu would not accept.

Tu Luong Tu kept waiting for Mr. Lam and his wife to return, but did not hear any news. Many years later, they received an envelope from Mr. Lam, clearly stating their intention to completely hand over their assets to Luong Tu, and advising him to start a family soon. However, Tu Luong Tu remained single for the rest of his life. He sees himself as a maid who manages everything on behalf of the Lam family. Finally, before he passed away, Tu Luong Tu made a will and donated all his assets to the Tho Dia Temple, thanking him for staying in this place for many years in poverty. When Tu Luong Tu was still alive, every day on the first and full moon days he went to Ksitigarbha Temple to thank Bodhisattva for saving his disability. It is said that after Luong Tu died, he handed over sixty-one acres of land to the local government to manage.

tieu_de: Third Prayer: Widely practice and make offerings!
tom_tat: "...Hey good man! Among the dharmas of offerings, the dharma of offerings is the most precious. That is: offerings by practicing according to the teachings, offerings by benefiting living beings, offerings by taking care of them.
noi_dung:
Third Vow: Widely practice and make offerings!

Hey good man! The immeasurable merit and virtue of offerings as above, compared to the merit and virtue of the dharma offered in one thought, is not equal to one hundredth, not one thousandth, nor one part of a hundred thousand verse-chi na-do-tha, ca-la part, math part, number part, simile part, up-ba-ni-sa-da part[31]. Why is that?

Because the Tathagata respect the Dharma, because practicing according to the teachings will give birth to Buddhas. If Bodhisattvas practice the dharma of making offerings, they will achieve the accomplishment of making offerings to the Tathagata. Practicing like that is true worship. With this vast and supreme offering, the realm of space is ended, the realm of living beings is exhausted, the karma of living beings is exhausted, the afflictions of living beings are ended, and my offering will end. But because the realm of emptiness and afflictions cannot be ended, this offering of mine also has no end. Reciting continuously, without interruption. Body language and mind karma are not tired at all)

Making offerings is cultivating blessings. People cannot be without blessings, without blessings they often encounter suffering. With blessings, your life will be extremely free, extremely happy. Where does blessing come from? Blessings come from cultivating alms and offerings. In the Six Dharmas of Mahayana Bodhisattva, the first is Almsgiving. Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's alms giving is called Offering. Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's giving mind is sincere, pure, vast, and equal. Using such a mind to give alms is called Offering; If you don't have such a mind, it's called Giving. Giving alms brings small blessings, offering alms brings great blessings; Because the amount of giving is small, the amount of offering is very large. Blessings are proportional to the amount of mind, great amount of mind means great blessings.

There are many types of blessings, Buddhist scriptures classify them into three major categories: wealth, intelligence, wisdom, and good health and long life. Living a long and healthy life without needing others to look after or care for you is truly a blessing. Buddha teaches us: the three types of blessings are retributions. If you don't practice, how can you get retribution?

a) “Alms giving” (giving alms with material things) brings wealth. The great rich people in the world have good luck, good lives, and make a profit in everything they do; Whatever you do, you will lose money and lose capital. To be honest, it's not because of chance, it's not about luck, it's not about intelligence or wisdom, it's because they practiced cultivating in their past lives, so in this life they naturally receive that blessing. Using one's own resources to give alms and offerings will enjoy the reward of wealth that will never end. Nowadays, relying on your children to support you in your old age is difficult to expect. People in the world think that they must have some money to be sure of their livelihood. In case you encounter an unexpected accident such as a fire or flood, are robbed by the enemy, and all your money is lost, what should you do? Still not sure what to eat. Depositing in a bank is not guaranteed, the bank may also be closed. The surest bet is to practice Almsgiving, use your alms to make offerings to all the masses, and only by hoarding like this will you be sure to eat; When I need someone, someone will come to me and make offerings to me. Many people do not clearly understand this principle, think that they are not sure about it, and do not dare to do it. If you don't dare to do it, you don't believe in Buddha, because giving alms to make you rich is what the Buddha himself said. If you have money then give alms, give alms cleanly, in the heart there will be real pleasure, at that time "in Buddhism, if you ask, you will be fulfilled", whatever you think about, it will come.

I have studied Buddhism for twenty-six years. Great Master Truong Gia taught me: "In Buddhism, if there is a request, it is true, but you must know how to practice, you must know how to practice humanity! You don't need to be afraid, you must trust Buddha, Buddha does not deceive us." I listened to my teacher and lived extremely frugally. I used less money to give alms, used it to free animals, help pay for medicine for the poor, and bought books with a lot of extra money. Until now, we still give alms like that. Last year, in Duc Chau (Texas), America, fellow practitioners there wanted to set up an ashram, which was a good thing, but I had no money. Just thinking that, less than three months later, many people sent money, of course they had money to build a Buddha hall. That room was built by Buddha and Bodhisattva. If you use money to spread the Dharma to benefit sentient beings, it is most appropriate. I studied Buddhism, listened to the teacher's teachings, and practiced the teachings for forty years. I was inspired, and it was true that "my wish will come true." Blessings must be sown in the field of blessings; Propagating the Dharma and benefiting living beings is a field of blessings. All my money is used to print sutras,

b) "Dharma of alms giving": If you have the opportunity to present your own theoretical method of practice and the good things you have achieved to everyone, making everyone follow that method of theoretical practice. This is called the Dharma of Almsgiving. In recent years, I have been going to places around the world to lecture and popularize the Pure Land Sect, which is the Dharma of Giving.

c) "Fearless Giving": In the minds of sentient beings there are doubts, fears, and difficulties. If we have the ability, then we can help them solve them, making their minds at peace and their bodies at peace; Such help is called Fearless Giving.

Practice almsgiving to gain wealth, practice the Dharma of almsgiving to gain intelligence and wisdom, practice fearless almsgiving to live a long and healthy life, we all need these three types of retribution; Therefore, we must make an effort to practice and practice the three types of Almsgiving in order to have the ultimate reward. If you don't cultivate, pray to Buddha and Bodhisattvas every day, offer incense, flowers, water, fruit, and flatter Buddha and Bodhisattvas so that they will bless you with blessings, there is no such thing! Buddha and Bodhisattva teach us to cultivate cause, only to cultivate cause can we get results!

“Among offerings, the dharma of offerings is the most precious”: people only know that the Dharma of Giving gives them wealth, the Dharma of Giving gives them intelligence and wisdom, and do not know the perfection in retribution to concentrate on practicing the Dharma of Giving. If you have wisdom, you will not be poor. If you have certain wisdom, you will be able to control your body and mind, so you will be healthy and live a long life. Therefore, we know that: The most precious thing in the world is not wealth but wisdom. A word of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva speaks out: Among all offerings, the Dharma of offering is the most superior.

The scope of Dharma Offering is vast and boundless, Bodhisattva symbolically mentioned seven types:

1) Make offerings by practicing according to the teachings:

The principles preached by the Buddha in the scriptures, we must clearly understand and understand. Buddha and Bodhisattva teach us what we should do, we must do it, what we should not do, we absolutely do not do. According to the teachings of Buddha and Bodhisattva, correct our wrong ways of thinking, looking, speaking, and doing. That is called "making offerings by practicing according to the teachings". Making offerings of incense, flowers, water, and fruit is only to show our respect, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not need those things!

In every recitation, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas hope that we will quickly become Buddhas, become like them. We study Buddhism with the aim of becoming a Buddha, rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is an important way to become a Buddha. The scriptures that are based on Pure Land Buddhism are the Five Pure Land Sutras and a Treatise, the things said in which we can all understand and follow, which is "making offerings by practicing according to the teachings". Last year, in Singapore, there was an old lady who heard about the Buddhist recitation method and was extremely happy. She stayed at home all day from morning to night reciting Amitabha Buddha. She recited for seven months and knew before her death that she would not get sick and sat down to be reborn. Therefore, currently in Singapore and Malaysia there are many people reciting Buddha's name. There are also people in Taiwan who recite Buddha's name for half a year and then die standing up. "As the theory of practice" is the teaching and practice, it is the true offering.

2) Making offerings by benefiting sentient beings:

Bodhisattvas recite and recite to save sentient beings. They recite and wish to help sentient beings so that they can achieve the best benefits. The best benefit is to help them recite Buddha's name, to help others know before they die, to help others not get sick, to stand or sit and be reborn, that is the greatest benefit; As for all other physical or mental enjoyments, when they die, they must reincarnate in the six paths. You give them other benefits, but they enjoy them for a few decades, and after a few decades, they stay for a long time. Helping them escape the ocean of suffering, escape samsara, become Buddhas, become Patriarchs, that is the ultimate benefit.

The benefit of sentient beings is to save all sentient beings. Printing sutras, making statues, or printing images of Buddha, preaching sutras, preaching the Dharma (regardless of large or small scale), circulating audio tapes or video tapes of teachings, using television to propagate Buddha Dharma are all offerings by benefiting sentient beings. Practicing this type of offering is truly making offerings to the Buddhas. We introduce Buddha Dharma to sentient beings, create opportunities for sentient beings to learn Buddha, help them quickly become Buddhas, which is in accordance with the original vows of all Buddhas in the ten directions, so the Buddhas use the power of their original vows to bless you, you will have three freedoms: Freedom from wealth, freedom from wisdom, freedom from health and long life.

3) Making offerings by receiving sentient beings:

The benefit of sentient beings is popular, promoted, and widely introduced, but the benefit of sentient beings is not like that. Not only does he introduce Buddhism to them, but he also directs them to practice, leads them, and makes them practice together. Reception is an extremely close relationship, truly establishing a relationship between teacher and student or fellow monks who practice together. Not only do we use language to help them, we also use actions to help and set an example for them to practice and study Buddhism. That's called making offerings by receiving sentient beings.

4) Making offerings by suffering on behalf of sentient beings:

Bodhisattvas have a vow to bear their sins and suffer for sentient beings. Suffering for you, in terms of things, each person creates karma, each person must receive retribution; Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have no way to suffer for you. However, it is true that Bodhisattva can bear a part for you. For example, early in the morning when you go to buy food, planning to buy fifty dong, in your mind you think: "There are a lot of people suffering, let's buy a little less, buy something a little cheaper, it only costs twenty-five dong, save twenty-five dong to help others." It is suffering for others. You were originally able to eat fifty dong, eating very delicious things, now you cut your mouth by half, you eat a little bad stuff, that is suffering for sentient beings. Originally, I could live in a luxurious house, but change to a small house that is sheltered from the sun and rain, and save some money to help poor people; shows that it is indeed possible to endure some of that suffering.

Every day, if you spend one penny less, you can use one meritorious practitioner; Instead of spending ten dong, you can use ten dong to give alms and offerings. Save yourself to help others; that is to suffer on behalf of sentient beings; As for living beings who create good or bad karma, we cannot bear it for them. Let's save a little, have a little extra to support the propagation of Buddha Dharma, and help needy sentient beings; That is the Bodhisattva who makes offerings by vowing to endure suffering for sentient beings.

5) Make offerings by diligently cultivating good roots:

In this life, whether one can practice successfully or not depends on this key point. Good roots: all good dharmas are born from this root [so called good roots]. Can means to be born, [the word Can] is used in a simile sense. Just like plants have roots so they can grow, germinate, bloom, and bear fruit. Cultivating good roots is an extremely important practice. Good roots have good roots in the world and good roots beyond the world.

The good roots of the world take the good roots of the world as the basis. The good roots in the world are not greedy, not angry, not ignorant, these are called the three good roots. The Buddha taught us to diligently cultivate the three good roots, which is making offerings. Regarding all worldly dharmas, famous literature, benefits, five desires, six senses, do not give rise to greed. Regarding all undesirable situations, evil people, evil things, do not give rise to anger. With regard to all truth, understanding, understanding, not being confused, not going crazy, not thinking wrongly, not seeing wrongly, not being foolish. Those are called the three basics of worldly good dharma. People who study Buddhism must actively strive to practice, not be greedy, not angry, not ignorant, and believe in deep cause and effect.

Why do people not dare to listen to Buddha's preaching of good causes and good results? It's because you don't clearly understand the cause and effect and don't have enough faith. But if you understand clearly, you will devote yourself to practice. For example, if we give away all our resources, we will give them away, so what will we eat tomorrow? This is very realistic, where to eat tomorrow? Just thinking about tomorrow, the alms money will be a little less, tomorrow we still have to eat! Thinking about the next day, and the day after that, I did not dare to give alms. That is unclear reason. I often advise fellow practitioners to cultivate the three good roots by first reading the book Lieu Pham Tu Hoc three hundred times, to have faith, and to be devoted to the truth of cause and effect and retribution. Giving alms is cultivating the cause, the blessings will naturally appear, the cause and effect will not be wrong at all. The more afraid you are, the less you dare to give alms, the more limited your blessings will be.

Good roots beyond the world are what Bodhisattvas practice, there is only one thing: Diligence. Diligence is the good root of Bodhisattva. Practicing according to the unerring method of reasoning, the more diligent you are, the happier you will be, the more you will be like Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, without fatigue or boredom. Think about it: a person's life has a lot of freedom and a lot of pleasure because of diligence. If you are not diligent, you will be lazy, negligent, your practice will not be effective, you will have many troubles, and you will have many tribulations. Therefore, one becomes skeptical of Buddha's teachings, one's faith wavers, and one becomes lost.

Tinh Dien: Diligence is the pursuit of progress, Tinh is pure and unadulterated. Such progress is useful. In this matter, some fellow practitioners put in a lot of effort and put in extraordinary effort, but they were not diligent! They study a lot, so they are busy. Wasted a lot of time and spirit, the effect was not ideal. The most precious Dharma is diligence!

6) Make offerings by not giving up Bodhisattva karma:

Karma is a career, a Bodhisattva's career is to educate living beings. Bodhisattvas in the world as teachers have only one goal: to help all sentient beings overcome delusion, become enlightened, leave suffering and be happy. Bodhisattvas appearing in the world can use different types of status, the status of a lay person, a monastic status, and the status of old, young, male, female, actions, and karma. If the Bodhisattva appears in the world of merchants, he will be the leader of the merchants, teaching you how to make a profit and how to use money. They have wisdom: How to earn money is very painful, how to make profit is very happy, how to spend money is very painful, creating a lot of karma; How to spend money to cultivate a lot of merit and receive great blessings in the future, the Bodhisattva businessman clearly understands. Old, young, male, female, all actions and karmas all have Bodhisattvas. Bodhisattvas only draw the rules for you.

In Buddhism, the Bodhisattva's career is symbolized by "propagating the Dharma to benefit living beings", this cannot be abandoned. The Buddha's career is to propagate Buddha Dharma, to do it wholeheartedly, that is the career of the Bodhisattva. There are many people who say: "I don't have money, I can't build an ashram. I can't do anything to help the ashram. I also don't have wisdom, I can't preach the sutras or preach the Dharma, how can I propagate the Dharma to benefit sentient beings?" You bring the schedule of preaching the Sutras here to inform others, and advise your friends, family members, relatives, and neighbors to listen to the Sutras. That is the Bodhisattva's career and you are capable of doing it. It's very good that they come, it's okay if they don't come, our Bodhisattva career has already been accomplished. It can be seen that anyone can do the Bodhisattva career, it is not difficult!

I see others put their hands together and recite Amitabha Buddha's name. That is the Bodhisattva's career. It doesn't matter if they like to hear it or not, they can all hear the chanting through. "The first ear root, forever the path seed" (once passed, forever become the same path); The seed of Amitabha Buddha planted firmly in that person's Alai Da Consciousness, that is the Bodhisattva career. Career depends on dedication, it's not difficult to practice!

7) Make offerings by not leaving Bodhi mind

Bodhi is Sanskrit and translated into Chinese means Enlightenment. In daily life, when dealing with people, things, and objects, maintaining a highly alert mind, not being confused, that is making offerings by not leaving the Bodhi mind. An unenlightened thought leads to confusion, an unenlightened thought creates karma, so it is necessary to maintain an alert mind at all times. How to maintain it? One day from morning to night, one sentence of Amitabha Buddha is firmly stuck in your mind, never letting it go, you can maintain a highly alert mind. As soon as Amitabha Buddha passed away, false thoughts arose. Miscellaneous thoughts are delusion, a Buddha's name is enlightenment.

Among all the dharmas, why do Buddhas specifically praise the Buddha's name? This method of reciting the Buddha's name is easy, walking, standing, lying down, sitting, no matter where or under what circumstances, a single sentence of Amitabha Buddha in your mind will never stop, making practice convenient. I would like to tell you that this is an extremely specific way to make offerings by not leaving the Bodhi mind. Therefore, we know that: Above, we worship all the Buddhas in the ten directions, below we worship all living beings in the nine dharma realms, all of us make offerings to them all. One Buddha's name makes offerings everywhere. Very few people know the merits and benefits of the Buddha's name. This Samantabhadra Vows from beginning to end is all about praising the title of inconceivable merit, every sentence and every word in the scriptures all summarizes the merit of the title.

The realm of practice is the same as above. The world of space, the world of living beings, the karma of living beings, and the afflictions of living beings cannot end, nor can our extensive practice and offerings end; It is also one mind and one thought, thoughts continue without interruption. Body, speech, and mind are not tired or bored. Must actively make efforts, must diligently practice and study.

This vow to "widely practice and make offerings" is extremely important. The Bodhisattva Dharma takes the Six Paradigms as its guideline, the first dharma in the Six Paramitas is Giving. Why put Almsgiving as the first dharma in the Six Dharmas? In fact, the Buddha Tathagata does not have any dharma that can be said. All the dharmas that can be said are nothing but "treating the disease and giving medicine"! When sentient beings have a disease, they give medicine to cure that disease. When the disease is cured, the medicine is no longer needed! There are many diseases in living beings, the root of all diseases is greed. All sentient beings who practice cannot achieve enlightenment, create the six paths of reincarnation, and fall into the three evil paths because they are harmed by the disease of greed. Therefore, giving alms is a good medicine to cure the disease of greed and greed. Without greed - anger - ignorance, all good dharmas arise; If there is greed - anger - ignorance, all good dharmas will not arise, all evil dharmas will arise.

Among offerings, the dharma of offerings is the most outstanding. Among the offerings, "practicing according to the teachings" is the most important, that is, following the teachings. The purpose of studying Buddhism is different, the pursuit is different, and the method chosen is also different. This ashram of ours has been chosen by the Pure Land Sect, with the goal of hoping that in the future we can be reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss. The sutras for us are just five sutras and one treatise. You must definitely follow the scriptures and make an effort to do it, that is called Cultivation. Cultivation is "right practice" (correct correction), Action is behavior. Cultivation is about correcting our behavior. What are Chanh's standards? Everything Buddha taught in the sutras is the correct standard.

Buddha's way of thinking, looking, and doing is decidedly correct; Letting go of our thoughts and understanding, following Buddha's way of thinking and seeing to modify our own views and behavior is called Cultivation. Practice right where the mind begins to think, right where you treat people and receive things, not by reciting sutras, knocking on bells, singing praises, bowing your head, or clasping your hands every day. Pretending to practice, but having false thoughts in your mind is not real practice.

Offerings in the same way as the theory of practice can be said to be almsgiving and offerings that all Bodhisattvas have practiced to the ultimate perfection. For example, if we accept and maintain the Infinite Life Sutra, all the Buddha's teachings in the sutra, if we can do each thing, each sentence, then the Six Paramitas, Ten Paramitas, and Ten Great Vows are completely fulfilled...

TEACHING STRATEGY

tieu_de: Conscious Talk to Forgive
tom_tat: Until now, you've been asking about people treating you badly, and honestly, we've talked a lot about those things... already! Today we will talk about Mind Talking to solve
noi_dung:
Consciousness Talk to Forgive

So far, you've been asking about people treating you badly, and honestly, we've talked a lot about those things... already! Today we will talk about Mind Talking to relieve the Resentment Karma they have caused us in previous lives!!!

When we owe them, as soon as we meet, they hate us, they criticize us, they scold us, or when we are close to them, we hate everything we do, everything we say, we get nagged and we have to endure the disadvantage, not daring to argue: Regardless of whether it's about mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law, husbands and wives or parents and children, or employers and servants or bosses and employees, or brothers and friends and colleagues... There are so many cases that it's impossible to mention.

Here we talk about them owing us! They owe us no matter what class they are: children, parents, parents-in-law or parents-in-law, youngest brother, employee or boss, friend or girlfriend, husband and wife, daughter-in-law, family... but on the contrary, we always resist, nag, disobey, disobey, and don't obey, but strangely enough, they don't do anything to us!!!

In the above cases, the best way is that we also need to talk to them in the Mind as follows:

Pray for the world to soon be at peace, for all living beings to be at peace, for no species to accidentally or intentionally harm or kill any species. Everyone lives in harmony, peace and happiness, helping and caring for each other in harmony.

If from countless lifetimes until now, whether by accident or on purpose, you have murdered, harmed, beaten or scolded me... then I would like to happily forgive and forgive you everything. From now on, even if you do anything wrong or make a serious mistake, I will not be offended or have any trouble with you at all!!! I respectfully ask you to join me in practicing diligently, to soon be liberated from the cycle of birth and death!!!

Let's just sincerely talk to our minds like that every night before sleeping and every morning before waking up! Mental Talking is when we talk silently in our head, heart or mouth for ourselves to hear, not for the person we want to talk to hear. We just need to sincerely send all our love and thoughts into cosmic space like that for a few weeks and the universe will send it to their hearts. Just like that, in a few weeks we will no longer see them as annoying no matter what they do. That is the best way for us to stop and stop saying words that create bad karma and resentment!!!

Let's just see why bad people always deceive love, money, bankruptcy... everyone related to them, such as parents, brothers, friends, spouses and children...??? The reason for this is because in the past life they lent to many people like that so now they have deceived and taken it back. But that is the work of dull people. Instead of deceiving and snatching them back to live properly and ethically, if those who owe them resentment, if they do not voluntarily come to repay them in this life, then in the next life they will also turn into kindness and come to serve them. However, because they are ignorant and ignorant, they do not clearly understand Cause and Effect and the resentment of the past has caused their Karma to follow the call of Resentment!!!

When we follow the Karma Consciousness from past lives leading to this life following the flow of Karma and act like that, we are intentionally killing ourselves and are content to drift in life and death through the 6 paths of reincarnation!!! If we continue to play like that, we are clearly "playing recklessly to gain a reputation for being stupid"!!!

tieu_de: BUDDHA MEDITATION - A DAILY METHOD OF PRAYING FOR SUCCESSFUL LIFE
tom_tat: (During the morning meditation session, we should only meditate and recite the Buddha's name.) Before starting the meditation session, we should first bow to the Buddha and repent, as many times as we want.
noi_dung:
Buddha's MEDITATION Dharma - DAILY METHOD OF PRAYING FOR SUCCESSFUL BIRTH

(During the morning meditation session, you should only meditate and recite the Buddha's name)

Before starting the practice, we should first bow to Buddha in repentance, as many times as we want.

When starting the practice, clasp your hands in front of your chest and sincerely pray:

NAMO Amitabha Buddha (3 times)

NAMO Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva (3 times)

Pray that the 10 Buddhas of the 10 Directions GIVE THE GRACE LIKE THAT OF THE BUDDHA, THE BLUE LIGHT OF HEAVEN TO SHINE ALL THE SENTIMENTAL BEINGS WHO ARE Suffering Around Me, My Ancestors, Relatives, and Oan Clans Who Left My Past and Present RELYING ON THE POWER OF THE BUDDHA WITH THE POWER OF MEDITATION, TRANSFORM, LEAVE SUFFERING AND BE HAPPY, AND BE LIVING TO EXTREME Bliss.

NAMO Amitabha Buddha (3 times)

When we are tired of reciting Buddha's name out loud, we recite it silently in our mind, rhythmically following our slow, deep breaths in and out....even if we recite in our mind, we must clearly hear each sentence and each word Amitabha Buddha.

When the pain in your whole body is unbearable, let it go.

This is called Zen-Pure dual practice. When sitting and reciting the Buddha's name, we should sit on the ground without anything to circulate blood and balance yin and yang. Do not sit on the discussion mat.

If you sit on something, that object must be natural such as grass or a mat made of sedge, and anything artificial will not be able to circulate blood.

When the practice is finished, we all clasp our hands and pray for dedication as follows:

After praying, we pray three times to Buddha, both praying and reciting:

NAMO Amitabha BUDDHA: WE PRAY FOR THE REVIVAL OF THE WEST OF UTILITIES. (3 Times)

Thus ends the perfect morning session.

***DARK Elaborate Class***

Before starting the practice, we should first bow to Buddha in repentance, as many times as we want.

When starting the practice, clasp your hands in front of your chest and sincerely pray:

NAMO Amitabha Buddha (3 times)

NAMO Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva (3 times)

Pray that the 10 Buddhas of the 10 Directions GIVE THE GRACE LIKE THAT OF THE BUDDHA, THE BLUE LIGHT OF HEAVEN TO SHINE ALL THE SENTIMENTAL BEINGS WHO ARE Suffering Around Me, My Ancestors, Relatives, and Oan Clans Who Left My Past and Present FOLLOW THE SOUND Dharma Of Buddha, Listen To The Transformation Sutra, Leave Suffering And Be Happy, Rebirth In Ultimate Bliss.

NAMO Amitabha Buddha (3 times)

(Note: Read whatever prayer you feel is appropriate)

After reading the prayer, we all clasp our hands and pray for dedication as follows:

After praying, we pray three times to Buddha, both praying and reciting:

NAMO Amitabha BUDDHA: WE PRAY FOR THE REVIVAL OF THE WEST OF UTILITIES. (3 Times)

Thus ends the perfect evening session.

The mind always remembers Buddha, the mind always recites Buddha's name. When you encounter anger, recite Buddha's name. When encountering unpleasant circumstances, gradually recite Buddha's name until you go to sleep. From the moment you close your eyes, just focus on reciting Buddha in your mind until you gradually fall asleep.

That means we meditate on the Buddha's name rhythmically with the in and out breath, not just when sitting. And all daily tasks, walking, standing, lying, sitting, in the mind, chant the Buddha's name Amitabha Buddha rhythmically with the in and out breath.

DAY TWO MORNING - EVENING METHODS.

IF YOU'RE BUSY, DO IT ONE TIME IN THE MORNING OR EVENING.

IF YOU'RE TOO BUSY, YOU CAN JUST SIT AND REMEMBER THE BUDDHA FOR ABOUT 15 - 30 MINUTES AND DEDUCTION IS ALSO ALLOWED AS LONG AS YOU DO NOT MISS A DAY SO THAT YOU DON'T RUIN THE Circulation.

tieu_de: LIFE IS JUST A DREAM
tom_tat: “All conditioned dharmas are different from an illusory dream, different from electricity and dew
noi_dung:
LIFE IS JUST A DREAM

“All conditioned dharmas

It's different from a dream, different from electricity or fog

Like water bubbles like an image

Do not forget to think like that”

(Quote from the Diamond Sutra)

Sometimes my teacher analyzes and explains, but I still can't really understand.

I tell you this dream:

I had to open many doors in the rooms to find my way, and every door had a lot of corpses floating, even smelling disgusting in the water. What a horrifying sight, a dead ship! The extreme fear made me have even more will to struggle out of that place. And in my dream, I was so lucky, I finally got out of that ship and reached the surface.

Around there were many people who had escaped like me, and everyone was raising their hands to hold the hands of the rescuers.”

Here I woke up. Unlike usual, I lay down and went back to sleep. Suddenly I had some questions, and thanks to that, I found the "code" to solve those 4 mysterious verses. This has a great meaning, not just for me, but it will really help you a lot.

In the dream just now, everything was very real and vivid, no different from when awake. The images are sharp, the sounds are clear, every touch is lifelike, the emotions, thoughts, and actions are no different from real life. That's why, in the dream, I confirmed that the sinking scene was real, so I was very scared.

And yet, as soon as I woke up, everything disappeared. Turns out, what I THOUGHT WAS REAL in my dream just now was a complete IMAGINATION.

SO WHAT IS REAL?

Is this life when we wake up REAL? Up to now, out of habit, I still think so. Maybe you are like me, just like everyone else thinks so.

But is it certain?

In the past, I went through many things in my life. Of course it must be true, now I remember the past, and at the same time compare it with the dream I just had. Oh, they're very similar.

If in real scenes of the past, there are images, sounds, touches, smells, scenes, this and that, problems... (Buddhism calls them form, sound, scent, taste, touch, Dharma), then in dreams there are also everything, sometimes clear, sometimes faint, but still there is everything.

In the past, when I encountered problems in life, I could think. In my dreams I can also think. In the past, I could act, do this and that, meet this person and that person, love and hate, be happy, angry, and sad, etc. In my dreams, I could also do it.

In the past scenes, I assumed everything was real. Then in my dreams, I also think everything is real. I never know when I'm dreaming that I'm dreaming.

And now, looking back at two things: the past and the dream, they have all disappeared, whether real or fake, there is no more, what is left is only a little memory in my mind, at some point I forget, whether it is the past that actually happened, or the dream scene in my mind, there is nothing left. So, they are the same.

Now I know that the shipwreck was fake, for sure, I don't need to be afraid of anything. But isn't my past the same?

I am a reincarnationist, not because I follow it by faith, but because I know it, because I have read many books and witnessed many things about reincarnation. I won't prove this to you here, let's leave it for another time, or you can learn about it in other books.

What I want to say is, the memories of my previous lives, are absolutely nothing. They are the past I have experienced, but now there is nothing left, even worse than the dream, because at least I can remember what happened in the dream, but in my past life I don't remember anything.

Suppose, I cultivate to a certain level and can remember my past lives. Oh, that's great. But... aren't they no more than the memories of dreams?

I can't go back to the past, just like I can't dream that dream again. Everything in a dream cannot be possessed when you wake up, so clearly, people often have the phrase "gold in dreams" to refer to this.

But the things I had in the past, they were considered real, but they weren't any better, now I can't take them out and continue using them, these two are the same, think carefully about this, it's very important. Buddha called it "unattainable", meaning impossible to have, impossible to possess.

I know a woman, she remembers her past life as a queen, a royal life full of gold and happiness. But now she has reincarnated into another life, as a normal person. She cannot get back the gold, silver, power, body, talent... from her previous life and continue to use it. They have disappeared, just like everything in the dream has also disappeared, these two disappearances are identical, no different, truly IMPOSSIBLE.

Now we have talked about the past, sitting in the present tense and judging, they are no better than dreams. So what about the present and the future???

What is present now, won't it also become the past tomorrow? Oh no, just a few seconds, a few hundredths of a second later, will it immediately become the past? As for the future, they will also become the present, and eventually the past. All of the same nature.

Past – present – future, they are just like successive scenes in AN ENDLESS DREAM. Everything in it, money, fame, family, friends, etc., including this body, including this thing called "ME", which alternately appears, then alternately disappears, are IMPOSSIBLE - impossible to own.

Of those three "I"s: Mai - David - the cat, which one is real?

This is assuming 3 lives, but in reality I, like you, like everyone else have countless lives. In any life, I think that that thing is "ME", but that "ME" immediately disappears when passing to another life, everything - my body, my property, my family, my husband and children, my gender, my hobbies, my talents, my country... everything will immediately disappear. There is nothing STILL THERE forever.

Oh, now I understand, what the Buddha means by "impermanence", nothing lasts forever, they are all constantly changing forms, replacing each other, taking turns replacing each other, but nothing is eternal. Yet I still attach too much importance to them, following them with happiness - anger - love - sadness, bringing me sadness.

Whoever calls me beautiful makes me happy. Whoever calls me ugly makes me sad. But whether it's ugly or beautiful, won't it all die, rot into rotten flesh, turn into bones, and gradually dissolve into dust? Will everyone forget everything in the next life? So that happiness and sadness have no meaning.

If I get something added, I'm happy. If I lose something, I regret it. But every life that passes, everything disappears, I don't even remember what I had or lost. They are just illusory scenes of illusion, once you gain it you will lose it, but when you think about it, you will never get it, like "gold in a dream", which you will never get, because it is not real.

So why run after them, cling to them to ignite crazy ambitions, and then suffer bitter and painful losses? Understanding this, I felt so relieved, like an invisible burden had been lifted from my soul.

Of course, this is only a small part, not all, but it is still very meaningful.

The Buddha called it "inverted dreams" which is not wrong. I woke up from the dream of being shipwrecked. Luckily, that dream woke me up from this dream called "life". However, there are many other doubts surrounding this issue, because I am just starting out.

The above is just one idea among countless ideas of the Diamond Sutra, and the Diamond Sutra is also just one of many Buddhist scriptures.

I know I still have to learn a lot, a lot more. But at least I have reached an important milestone in my spiritual journey of countless lifetimes.

Hopefully I will be able to share with you in another article, writing about this same "dream" topic.

If you really want to learn more, please comment below and voice your questions so we can write the next parts accordingly.

(Dieu Ngoc - Quang Tu)

The King of Thủ-Lăng-Nghiêm appears in the world,

Eradicating countless lifetimes of twisted thoughts.

Unceasing in cultivating the Dharma body,

Vowing now to attain the fruit of becoming a jewel-king,

Thus saving beings like grains of sand,

Deeply dedicated to serving sentient beings of the world,

This is the name and position in repayment of Buddha's grace:

Humbly requesting the World-Honored One to witness,

Great – heroic, great – mighty, great – compassionate,

My sacred self quickly attains unsurpassed enlightenment,

And sits in the Dharma assembly of the ten directions;

All kinds of subtle faults can be eliminated,

With an unshakable Ca-ra heart it turns.

Namo to the eternally abiding Dharma of the ten directions.

Namo to the eternally abiding Sangha of the ten directions.

From within the mass of flesh,

Radiating the powerful jewel-light,

Benefits of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra

The Buddha said: Ananda! Today I am declaring the Thủ Lăng Nghiêm mantra for you, and also to help people in future generations practice in order to gain many benefits.

A Nan! The Thủ Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, if anyone sincerely recites and practices it correctly according to the Dharma, will achieve success in the Thủ Lăng Nghiêm Samadhi. At that time, entering fire, the fire will not burn; entering water, the water will not overwhelm. All kinds of poisons will not harm. Ghosts, spirits, and evil beings cannot disturb. Those good men and women who either write down, recite, or propagate the Thủ Lăng Nghiêm Mantra will receive boundless merit. In this lifetime, they will not fall into poverty or lowly conditions. Even if these people do not have the opportunity to perform good deeds, all the merit from the Buddhas of the ten directions will be given to them, and they will dwell together with the Buddhas.If a woman wishes to have a son, she will give birth to a son with merit and wisdom; if she wishes for a daughter, she will have a daughter with a good and virtuous appearance, respected by everyone. Even those who pray for longevity, for blessings, for strong health and vitality, or for peace… all will have their wishes fulfilled.

In a country unfortunately plagued by many hardships: epidemics, crop failures, wars, armed conflict, droughts, and floods, if the king, officials, and the people all sincerely believe, record, chant, perform rituals, show respect, wear, disseminate, and practice cultivation, then the heavenly dragons and the eight classes of divine beings, along with virtuous spirits, will be delighted, allowing all hardships to be overcome, favorable rains and gentle winds to prevail, peace in every place, and prosperity for all people.

The Shurangama Mantra is wondrous and inconceivable. This mantra is excellent for subduing celestial demons and controlling heterodox teachings. From beginning to end, each verse is the spiritual practice of the Buddhas; each verse has its own function; each word has its profound and subtle meaning; all possess inconceivable divine power. Simply reciting one verse, one word, one assembly (one gathering), or the entire mantra can cause the heavens to shake and the earth to tremble, make ghosts and spirits weep, drive away demons, and dispel confusion and ignorance. The radiance on the Buddha's crown symbolizes the power of the Mantra, meaning it has the ability to dispel all darkness and allow practitioners to achieve all virtuous merits. If one upholds this Mantra, one will certainly attain Buddhahood in the future and achieve the supreme, perfect, and complete enlightenment.If one frequently recites this Mantra, it will slightly eliminate karmic obstacles from many past lives. That is the miraculous effect of the Shurangama Mantra.

Although I have taught for many years, I still cannot fully explain all the wonderful points of this Mantra. All Buddhas of the ten directions arise from this Mantra, so the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra can be called the mother of the Buddhas. All the Tathagatas of the ten directions rely on this Mantra to attain the unsurpassed, complete enlightenment. They manifest countless forms like the grains of dust in the world realms to turn the wheel of Dharma, educate sentient beings, bestow empowerment on sentient beings in the ten directions, save sentient beings from suffering, enabling all beings—great and small, of provisional or authentic capacity—to attain liberation; all these Buddhas rely on the power of the mind of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. If one wants to attain the Arhat fruit, one must recite this Mantra to avoid demonic disturbances.

In the era of the declining Dharma, if anyone memorizes this mantra or encourages others to memorize it, fire cannot burn that person to death, and water cannot drown them. No matter how potent poison is, it cannot harm them. For those who often recite this mantra, poison will turn into ambrosia upon entering the mouth. Those who recite this mantra will not be reborn in evil realms; even if they want to, they cannot. Why? Because this mantra holds them back and does not allow them to go to such places. If one has never accumulated merit before, reciting this mantra will result in the Buddhas of the ten directions bestowing virtuous merit upon them, which comes from regularly reciting this mantra. Moreover, if one recites it frequently, they will always be born in the times of the Buddhas' appearances and will cultivate under the guidance of the Buddhas.

Suppose the mind is often scattered and cannot concentrate to generate meditative stability, but if the mind thinks of the Shurangama Mantra, and then uses the mouth to recite it, the Bodhisattva Vajra Treasury King will quietly protect you until the scattered mind gradually subsides and meditative stability arises. They will silently assist you in opening wisdom and turning the mind to focus on attaining complete understanding of all matters over the 84,000 countless eons.

Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

(Collected in the Two Sessions Commentaries by Venerable Thich Khanh Anh and in the White-Robed Shurangama Mantra published by Duong Sang An Quan, No. 712N. 9th Street, San Jose, CA 95112).

Practitioners of Mahayana Buddhist Sutras all recite Mantras during their practice sessions with the aim of eliminating karmic obstacles and increasing accumulated blessings. The meaning of the word 'Mantra,' as previously explained, is the secret speech of the Buddhas (Esoteric Words or Buddha Words). This special language is only comprehensible to the Buddhas of the ten directions and is not the ordinary language used by sentient beings in the three realms; therefore, ordinary people cannot fully understand it. Those who wish for the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions to bless them through the sufferings of life only need to practice the Mantras as guided, and they will respond according to the seeker’s request.The mantras of Esoteric Buddhism come in many types, and each type has its own use, but the Zen practitioners in the Zen schools only select a number of mantras to recite in ceremonies such as prayers for peace, prayers for the deceased, repentance, etc., including the Lankavatara Mantra, the Great Compassion Mantra, and ten other mantras called the Ten Mantras. The meaning and uses of the aforementioned mantras are explained as follows:

1)- The Lăng Nghiêm Mantra:

The benefits of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, according to Buddhist Philosophy or the General Outline of the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra in Popular Buddhist Studies Course VI and VII by Venerable Thích Thiện Hoa, pages 255 and 266, the Buddha said: “If someone has heavy karmic obstacles that cannot be removed, he (referring to Ananda) should teach them to sincerely recite this Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and all karmic obstacles will be eliminated,” and the Buddha further said: “After I pass away, in future lifetimes, if anyone recites this mantra, then disasters such as: floods, fires, poison, poisonous insects, wild beasts, demons, ghosts, etc., will not be able to harm them.”

If we want to fulfill our aspirations for a peaceful life and achieve results on the path of liberation and enlightenment, we must diligently practice and deeply penetrate this Lăng Nghiêm Mantra to rely on its power for transformation and protection. This is exactly what the Buddha said in the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra: “Even Ma Đăng Già, who is a lustful woman without a mind for practice, can attain the result of a Saint. So how much more can you, the noble disciples, who have the aspiration for the supreme path, recite this mantra, and surely it will be very easy to become a Buddha, like wind scattering dust, without any difficulty.”

Merit of the Lăng Nghiêm Protective Mantra

Anan, the mystical verses, the secret stanzas of the Buddha's crown light gather, Tathāgata manifests in all ten directions. The Buddhas of the ten directions, relying on this mind-mantra, attain unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. The Buddhas of the ten directions, holding this mind-mantra, subdue demons and conquer external heresies. The Buddhas of the ten directions, wielding this mind-mantra, sit upon jeweled lotuses, manifesting as countless worlds. The Buddhas of the ten directions, keeping this mind-mantra in their mouths, turn the great Dharma wheel in innumerable realms. The Buddhas of the ten directions, safeguarding this mind-mantra, anoint and prophecy for the Bodhisattvas. Those who have not yet realized their fruition, relying on this mind-mantra, will receive prophecies from the Buddhas of the ten directions. The Buddhas of the ten directions, using this mind-mantra, rescue beings from the sufferings of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, the blind, deaf, mute, the enemies they encounter, partings from loved ones, unfulfilled wishes, the fluctuations of the five aggregates. Both major and minor disasters are simultaneously liberated.Enemies, soldiers, kings, nations, wind, fire, prisons, even extreme hunger and poverty, are all dispelled. The Buddhas of the ten directions, following this mantra, everywhere serve virtuous teachers and offer as desired. In the assembly of countless Buddhas, reciting this mantra is revered as the great Dharma prince. The Buddhas of the ten directions use this mantra to protect relatives, causing followers of the Lesser Vehicle who hear the secret teachings not to be frightened. The Buddhas of the ten directions transmit this mantra, and after passing away, entrusting Dharma matters to be the ultimate guardian, the precepts will surely be kept pure.

If we say that the mantra of the Buddha's summit light emerges from the Bhadra from morning till night, the sounds follow one another, the words and phrases do not repeat, enduring through lifetimes as countless as the sands of the Ganges, it will never come to an end (29). This mantra is also called the Tathagata Summit. Those who still have learning and seek the result of Arhat, without reciting this mantra, will definitely not escape demonic troubles. Ananda, if you write this mantra on bark, palm leaves, white paper, silk, store it in a scented bag, wear it on your person, or enshrine it at home, for a lifetime all poisons will be harmless, and across lifetimes, one will not be born in wretched and lowly places against one's desire. Ananda, I proclaim this mantra again to help the world escape suffering and fear, and to fulfill wisdom that transcends the mundane. After my parinirvana, in the age of declining Dharma, whoever recites it or teaches others to recite it, the evil spells of deities, dragons, demons, spirits, and mystical sorcery will all be powerless.Even before attaining complete reception, all poisons—ancient poisons, metal poisons, silver poisons, and all toxic gases—placed in that person's mouth will turn into ambrosia. All evil stars, demons, and spirits cannot generate evil thoughts. Daka and the evil poisonous demon kings, having received profound grace, usually protect and support. This mantra is accompanied day and night by 84,000 innumerable types of Vajra Treasury King Bodhisattvas and their followers. Even if the practitioner’s mind is distracted, they do not abandon them. For those determined to achieve Bodhi, they secretly assist in enlightening the divine consciousness, enabling recollection of 84,000 innumerable past lives. In every lifetime, they are not born among evil beings.

All the merits of the Tathagatas in the ten directions are given to those who recite the mantra. For countless aeons, one always dwells in the same place as the Buddhas. Infinite merits gather like clusters of akshas. Because one cultivates in the same place as the Buddha, even if one breaks precepts and returns to purity, has not received precepts and brings about precepts, does not observe fasting precepts and naturally completes fasting precepts, has not been diligent and becomes diligent, lacks wisdom and gains wisdom—in the past, if one violated prohibitive precepts, after reciting the mantra, all heavy and light offenses are instantly eradicated. Drinking alcohol, consuming pungent substances and other impure things, all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, celestial beings, and spirits forgive. All actions and movements are considered pure. Torn, filthy, and dirty clothing is also not a fault. Even without establishing an altar, entering the Dharma assembly, or practicing the Way, reciting this mantra still brings perfect merit.The five rebellions, uninterrupted, the four forces, the eight forces; once this mantra is recited, it disperses the pile of sand like a strong wind. Reading, chanting, copying the mantra, wearing it on the body, placing it in the dwelling, all heavy and light karmic obstacles from countless eons will disappear like snow meeting boiling water, and in no time, one will attain the patience of non-arising.

With a sincerely focused mind, reciting the mantra or wearing it on oneself can lead to having children—sons or daughters endowed with blessings and wisdom. Praying for longevity will grant long life; praying for quick fulfillment of karmic results will lead to swift completion. Concerning health, appearance, and strength, whatever one wishes for can be achieved as desired. At the time of death, one can, according to their wishes, be reborn in the Pure Land of the Ten Directions. Certainly, one will not be lost to lowly or inferior realms, let alone various distorted forms.

O Ananda, write this mantra on the four gates of the city, on towers, or on the rooftops; allow the people to respectfully receive this mantra, worship, and offer with utmost devotion; have each person wear the mantra or place it in their residence; then all kinds of calamities such as famine, disease, and warfare… all the misfortunes will completely vanish.

Hey Anan, wherever this mantra is, the heavenly dragons rejoice, the weather is favorable, the crops flourish, the people are happy, and both day and night, they sleep peacefully without nightmares. In the world of Ta Bà, there are 84,000 evil spirits, with 28 major evil spirits as leaders, headed by 8 chief evil spirits, appearing in many forms, causing strange disasters. Wherever this mantra is present, within 12 divisions of time, those terrible accidents will no longer occur.

Therefore, the Tathagata taught this mantra to protect future beginners in learning, helping them enter right concentration with body and mind at ease and peaceful. Past grievances, old karma, and previous debts will no longer cause harm. Ananda and the learners, those who will practice in the future, following the method to establish the altar, with preceptors and novices being pure, should have no doubt or repentance regarding this mantra. If, even in the very body where one is born to parents, one cannot attain a connected mind, then the Tathagatas of the ten directions are all false words.

The Vajra benevolent spirits make the vow to protect:

An infinite number of thousands of Vajras join hands, bow, and declare: As the Buddha teaches, we sincerely protect those who practice the Bodhi path.

King Brahma, Indra, and the Four Heavenly Kings also simultaneously respectfully prostrated and said: We wholeheartedly and sincerely protect those who practice, so that their lifetime may be as they wish.

Countless great generals Yaksha, the kings of Asura, Pundarika, Kubandha, Viśākha, ghost kings, and ghost commanders respectfully joined their hands and said: We vow to support those who practice, so that their Bodhi mind may quickly reach perfection.

Countless solar deities, lunar deities, wind gods, rain gods, cloud gods, thunder gods, lightning gods, along with deities overseeing the months, stars, and their attendants, respectfully prostrated and said: We protect those who practice in the sacred place so that they may be free from fear.

Countless Mountain Gods, Sea Gods, all spirits of the land and creatures, those who walk the waters and lands, the Wind God Kings and all the colorless celestial beings simultaneously bowed and said: We protect the practitioners so that there are no more demonic disturbances and they may soon attain Bodhi.

84,000 Bodhisattvas of the Diamond Treasury King, paying homage, said: World-Honored One, we have long attained the Bodhi path and have not entered Nirvana, often using this mantra to assist those truly practicing Samadhi in the age of the declining Dharma. World-Honored One, whether they are in the temple walking the sacred path or meditating while traveling in villages, our retinues often follow to protect them. The Demon King, the Great Freedom Deity, wants to use means to disturb them; we use our jeweled club to smash their heads like dust. Lesser spirits and demons must stay ten yojanas away from those virtuous beings, unless they take the resolve to support them.
