tieu_de: Actors, MCs, and beautiful women who vow to be vegetarian for life when they are still very young
tom_tat: Angela Phương Trinh Angela Phương Trinh was born in 1995 and is known to the public for her role as an actress in many films such as: Mùi ngò gai, Bà mẹ nhí… On the evening of January 2nd, the 9X unexpectedly shared an image of a garlic
noi_dung:
Actors, MCs, and Beauties Who Made a Lifelong Vow to Eat Vegetarian While Still Very Young

Angela Phuong Trinh

Angela Phuong Trinh was born in 1995 and is known for her role as an actress in many films such as: Mui Ngo Gai, Ba Me Nhi… On the evening of January 2nd, the 9X star unexpectedly shared a photo of herself at her most recent meditation session on her personal page. Along with that, she also revealed that she has decided to follow a vegetarian diet for life.

"Yesterday, on January 1st, I made a vow to practice lifelong vegetarianism with the cultivation of compassion, a deep faith in karma, respect for life, and love for all sentient beings in the spirit of a Buddhist follower," wrote the 25-year-old actress.

In the past, Angela Phương Trinh was involved in quite a few controversies for wearing provocative outfits and using gimmicks every time she appeared on the red carpet. However, recently, the actress has limited her appearances in films and events. Instead, she has focused on going to temples and participating in charitable activities. At the same time, Phương Trinh has also attracted attention for her simple image, wearing plain clothes and not showing off her body like before. This has earned the actress praise from the public.

For more than a year now, Angela Phương Trinh has chosen a vegetarian lifestyle, attended meditation retreats, eaten vegetarian food, and only participated in certain entertainment events.

On her personal page, the actress also does not post revealing photos or make statements that spark controversy as she did before.

Helly Tống

Helly Tống's real name is Tống Khánh Linh, born in 1995, and she once studied abroad in Australia. With the advantage of an ideal height (1.72 m) and a pleasant face, she has become a familiar face on major magazines.

Helly Tong started venturing into business at a very young age. At that time, she made waves on social media with the news of "a 19-year-old girl starting up with three projects at the same time." After those successes, she concluded her entrepreneurial journey, grabbed her backpack to travel around the world, and then returned to choose a green and meditative lifestyle.

It is known that currently, the 9X generation individual has been a vegetarian for 8 years. “At that time, after seeing a few animals being killed, the emotions, feelings, and sadness within me were very strong. Becoming vegetarian happened very naturally, without a plan; I voluntarily became vegetarian, which surprised my family and friends,” Helly recounted.

Besides being vegetarian, she is also one of the young pioneers in a green lifestyle, reducing plastic waste. This completely stems from her understanding and love for the environment.

Currently, besides working as a model and brand ambassador, Helly Tống is running 2 companies based on the ideas of green living and reducing plastic waste.

MC Hạnh Phúc

MC Hạnh Phúc is a familiar face on the program Chuyển động 24h of Vietnam Television. In 2012, Hạnh Phúc was diagnosed with type 3 Hodgkin’s – a very rare blood cancer. Alone in Ho Chi Minh City, he only dared to tell his parents that he had bone marrow inflammation and fought the disease on his own. His lover also broke up with him because of this matter.

At a time when it seemed the darkest and most hopeless, Hạnh Phúc turned to Buddhism as a form of "salvation." He practiced vegetarianism, spending 4-5 hours each day meditating and chanting sutras.

A month later, Hạnh Phúc went for another medical test, and the results showed that he did not have cancer. "Perhaps it was the spiritual strength that helped me get through that difficult period," Hạnh Phúc shared.

In particular, the shock of standing between the boundary of life and death and filial piety motivated MC Hạnh Phúc to decide to become a lifelong vegetarian. The male MC also shared that he is aware of the miracle of vegetarianism. Not only limited to its spiritual significance, vegetarianism also helps purify the human soul, directing it toward good deeds.

Đại Nghĩa

Born as a comedian, the audience is often familiar with the image of Đại Nghĩa cheerfully enlivening television in various roles such as MC, film actor, and stage artist. However, few people know that he is a Buddhist who has been a vegetarian for many consecutive years and leads a pure life.

On his personal page, he always updates unique and eye-catching vegetarian dishes that he cooks and demonstrates himself. Dai Nghia believes that since eating vegetarian, his mind has become peaceful and more compassionate. From there, he has become calm with everything, smiles at controversies, and comes up with skillful solutions.

Truong Thi May

Miss Runner-up Trương Thị May, who was once honored as the most attractive vegetarian beauty in Asia. Born into a family with a tradition of following Buddhism and practicing vegetarianism, Trương Thị May's affinity for the faith came very early. At the age of 13, she became familiar with going to the pagoda to listen to sermons and eat vegetarian meals.

Trương Thị May shared that vegetarian food is the purest natural food, very easy to digest, and brings a sense of relaxation to those who eat it.

In addition to being vegetarian, every day Trương Thị May also practices meditation and worships Buddha at home. The act of bowing to Buddha is a vow made by Trương Thị May with the wish to atone for the mistakes she inadvertently or intentionally causes to sentient beings and others on a daily basis. Besides that, in the afternoon, if she returns from work early, she goes for a run or jumps rope to maintain her health and figure.

The beauty Trương is famous as one of the vegetarians in the Vietnamese showbiz.

Dung Nguyễn

Source: BÁO MỚI.

P/S: If you know anyone else, tag them right away or leave a comment.

tieu_de: CASH ADVANCE FOR BUSINESS
tom_tat: Most people often think: rich, poor, noble, humble, sick, healthy, .... Happiness, suffering.... ARE ALL PREDETERMINED BY HEAVEN! Is this notion really right or wrong?!
noi_dung:
CASH ADVANCE FOR BUSINESS

Most people often think: wealth, poverty, high status, low status, sickness, health, ... happiness, suffering ... ARE ALL PREDETERMINED BY HEAVEN!

Is this belief really right or wrong?!

Let's discuss the operating law of the Three Heavens and the Three Realms!!!

In the Three Realms of Karma, the majority of sentient beings (more than nine-tenths) experience the self-transformation of karma in the human world!

What is the Self-Transformation of Karma?!

That is, resultant karma includes (past karma, present karma, and future karma).

- Past Karma: Will generally manifest within a maximum period of 36 years of a person's current life, (except for those with extremely good or extremely evil predetermined karma).

- Present Karma: Refers to karma generated from actions performed in our current life.

- Future Karma: Refers to karma that arises in a future rebirth due to actions we performed in previous and current lives!

So, roughly, it can be understood that: A person is mostly influenced by fate during the first 36 years of life. In this period, almost all karma created in past lives will be manifested, whether wealth, poverty, nobility, humility, happiness, or suffering.... Everything will be appropriately rewarded or manifested.

After this period will be our Present Karma, meaning that if someone is born into poverty but knows how to strive, create good karma, and avoid bad karma, they can subsequently become wealthy, prosperous, and happy.

Understanding this truth, we will no longer automatically blame or entrust it to FATE, to God, or to Buddha anymore!

Everything is the karmic result of ourselves, we sow it ourselves, and we reap it ourselves!

If we are born sick or poor, that is indeed the (cause-and-effect) of the previous life manifesting.

But if we are not poor or suffering yet create it ourselves, then that is not the karma from a past life; everything is created by us, and we are the ones who receive it!

Without the Karma Lord, all karma naturally rotates; sow good deeds and reap goodness, commit evil and inevitably meet retribution.

Strive and you will succeed.

The lazy one will forever live in mediocrity.

The Three Realms of Cause and Effect are truly fair!

No one can escape Cause and Effect!!!

tieu_de: What Is Tantric Buddhism
tom_tat: This is a secret practice of Buddhism, teaching about how to 'seal hand gestures', 'chant mantras', etc... This practice is of a complete (thorough) nature, based on the mind of the esoteric teachings. Among the practices that the Buddha has taught
noi_dung:
What Is Tantra

This is a secret Buddhist practice, teaching about how to "seal," "recite mantras," etc. This practice is of a conclusive nature (complete), based on the mind of the esoteric Dharma.

Among the methods that the Buddha has taught sentient beings to rely on for practice in the later period of the "Degenerate Dharma," each practice has a supreme and subtle principle.

For example:

· In the Pure Land School, the guiding principle is:

"Attain rebirth in one lifetime, unshakable" as the foundation.

· The Zen school adopts the guiding principle:

“Point directly at the human mind, see one's nature and become a Buddha” as its foundation.

· The Huayan school adopts the guiding principle:

“Leave the mundane world, enter the Dharma realm” as its foundation.

· The Lotus school adopts the guiding principle:

“Discard the mysterious, reveal the true” as its foundation.

And specifically:

· The Esoteric (Tantric) school adopts the guiding principle:

“The three secrets correspond, the body becomes Buddha” as its foundation, etc...

The three secrets are: Body secret - Speech secret - Mind secret

In summary, although there are many methods and different principles, ultimately they all aim for a single purpose: liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

Now I will briefly talk about “Esoteric Buddhism”. It is called “Esoteric” because this is a practice that belongs to the “Secret Dharma”, specializing in teaching how to recite Mantras and make Mudras, and therefore requires a Guru (i.e., a teacher to transmit teachings).

1. Why is it called Recitation/Maintenance?

RECITATION/MAINTENANCE means to keep continuously (to hold), not to lose, not to forget.

2. Why is it called Chú?

CHÚ in full is Thần Chú, which means secret words. Now for convenience, it is shortened to "Chú".

Some people do not understand and say:

Thần Chú was proposed by the divine way. That is incorrect, it is a mistake.

· The word THẦN here means "magical, spiritual, transformative".

· The word CHÚ can also be called CHÂN NGÔN.

The mantras spoken by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas possess unimaginable power and merit. One should distinguish between RECITING a Mantra and CHANTING a Mantra.

· RECITING a Mantra:

This means a mantra must be repeated continuously for several hundred repetitions (hundreds of times) in order to be called recitation. If it is only read 3 times or 7 times, it is considered chanting, not recitation.

· CHANTING or MEMORIZING a Mantra:

It means to just skim through it once. For example, the "Ten Lankavatara Dharani" can be recited quickly just once, and not recited a second or third time.

A Dharani in Sanskrit is called Dhàrani, in Chinese it is translated as Zongchi, and in English it is called Mantra. Because it encompasses innumerable dharmas, it is called "Zong" (total); because it contains and preserves countless meanings, it is called "Chi" (preserve). A Dharani carries the meaning of encompassing (zong) all dharmas and preserving (chi) the noble thoughts from the boundless wondrous meanings within the mind. The phrase "Dharani" represents the entire "mind and intention" of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas toward sentient beings.

The meaning of a Mantra is extremely secret, no one can understand it, except for the deity (the master) of that Mantra and the Buddhas alone.

There are three types of Dharani, which are: single-syllable, multi-syllable, and wordless (no characters).

The Mantra of the Buddha is different from that of heretical paths. The Buddha's mantra has the power to destroy evil and establish righteousness, eliminate bad karma, dispel false and harmful thoughts, generate wisdom, cultivate blessings and virtuous roots, prevent sins, save oneself and others from calamities caused by demons, especially to deliver spirits to transcendence in an extraordinary and rare way, swiftly bringing people from the mundane realm to the holy realm, closely connecting and resonating with the teachings alongside the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, and Saints, and achieving spiritual attainment.

Meanwhile, the mantra of heretical paths only harms people and objects, brings disasters upon people, and those who die following it must descend into the three evil realms.

Although mantras cannot be literally interpreted, if one sincerely and reverently recites and upholds them, they will yield miraculous effects beyond comprehension. It is like drinking water: only the one who drinks it can feel whether it is warm or cold – others cannot know, understand, or believe it. The efficacy of reciting a mantra is similar; only those who devote themselves to it can truly know how effective it is!

Typically, a single mantra can encompass an entire sutra. This alone is enough to understand that the power and merit of a mantra, as spoken by the Buddha, are inconceivable.

For example:

1. The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sutra (ĐẠI BÁT NHÃ) consists of 600 volumes, but there is only one Mantra that summarizes all 600 volumes of the Great Prajñāpāramitā. That is the mantra:

Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā.

2. The Great Compassion Dhāraṇī Sutra (ĐẠI BI TÂM ĐÀ RA NI) summarizes 85 mantras as follows:

Ān, tat diän dū màn tārä, bā tà yà, ta bà ha.

3. The entire Cundi Sutra (CHUẨN ĐỀ) is summarized in the mantra:

Ān chiết lệ chủ lệ Cundi ta bà ha.

4. The LĂNG NGHIÊM Sutra consists of 9 volumes, summarized in the sentence:

Án, a na lệ tỳ xá đề, bệ ra bạt xà ra đà rị, bàn đà bàn đà nể, bạt xà ra bàn ni phấn hổ hồng đô lô ung phấn, ta bà ha.

5. The BỔT ĐẢNH TÔN THẮNG ĐÀ RA NI Sutra, etc., is similar in the same way.

Furthermore, it should be known:

The CHÂN NGÔN (Sacred Mantra) phrase here belongs to the 'inconceivable spiritual power'.

As for:

The NIỆM PHẬT (Buddha Recitation) phrase belongs to the 'inconceivable merit'.

Both, one MYSTIC and one PURE, sharing the same origin from which they arise, both have the ability to lead practitioners to the Pure Land (in general) and rebirth in the Land of Supreme Bliss (in particular), not:

Reciting Mantras alone does not result in rebirth. Only exclusively Nianfo (chanting Buddha's name) leads to rebirth!

Now, Master Thích Thiền Tâm has combined both parts (MYSTIC and PURE), thus the efficacy increases manifold. The "power" of the mind leading to the Land of Supreme Bliss will be swift, peaceful, and unobstructed.

Like the INFINITE LIFE TATHAGATA Dharani,

· Reciting it once will eradicate all the four gravest sins, the five heinous acts, and the ten evil deeds. · Reciting it three times will eliminate all hindering sins. · Reciting it seven times can restore to purity the fundamental precepts for laymen of good faith, and for monks and nuns who have committed the four offenses, eight offenses, or other major precepts. When a practitioner performs the mudra and recites this Mantra, all BUDDHAS radiate light upon the top of their head and receive them.

Reciting up to ten thousand times (10,000 times), the Bodhi mind (Buddha mind) manifests in the body without forgetting.

Those who chant gradually enter into a perfectly bright, pure, and cool serene mind like the autumn moon, dispelling all afflictions. At the moment of death, they will see Amitābha Buddha, along with countless tens of billions of Bodhisattvas surrounding them, comforting, protecting, and guiding them. The person will then be reborn in one of the nine lotus grades in the Pure Land. (Please refer to the Scripture of Buddha Recollection Perfection of Wisdom).

About the SIX-SYLLABLE GREAT BRIGHT TRUE WORD:

Om Mani Padmé Hum

(The Sino-Vietnamese transcription according to pronunciation by Phạm is: “Án ma ni bát di hồng”) consists of only six short syllables, but its power is immeasurable (equivalent to the power of the Great Compassion mantra), because both mantras (Great Compassion and Six-Syllable Great Brightness) are a "combination" of the virtues of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva and many Buddhas, encompassing the entire "mind and intention" of the Bodhisattva and the Buddhas, helping sentient beings overcome all disasters, eliminate evil karma, eradicate illnesses, attain fearlessness (no longer afraid in any circumstance), and achieve all aspirations (corresponding to one's "merit and virtue," but in a proper way).

The power of the Great Compassion Mantra and the Six-Syllable Mantra can move mountains, fill seas, turn drought into rain, transform storms into warm sunshine, have the ability to deliver people from hell, and elevate them to the realms of Heaven and Buddha, escaping the three evil paths.

Except for the “Main Deity” (that is, the owner) of the Mantra, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, and the Buddhas, no one can understand its miraculous power and profound meaning (including all other great Bodhisattvas in the ten directions cannot fully comprehend it)...

There are people who do not clearly understand the above, so they waste effort translating it into meaning, inadvertently diminishing the efficacy of the Mantra. Especially when they use a "discriminating" mind (this mantra is correct, that one is wrong, this one is strong, that one is weak, this one is long, that one is short, etc.) while reciting the Mantra, resulting in endlessly reciting it but achieving very little.

Up until now, Buddhist practitioners in China, Vietnam, etc., when reciting Mantras often have a slightly distorted pronunciation compared to the Sanskrit sound (that is, the sound of the Sanskrit letters from Northern India), but this is not a concern, as long as one uses "sincere heart and belief" when chanting, it will still be effective as usual.

In the "Great Compassion" Sutra, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva teaches:

"Anyone who harbors doubt and does not believe in this Dharani should know that they will forever lose the benefit..."

Therefore, to be effective on the path of tantric practice, the key is not to let doubt arise, distinguish right from wrong, or understand or not understand the meaning, nor to disparage anything. Even if that 'doubt' is as small as a speck of dust, it must 'not exist'. Wholeheartedly following and practicing it is called reciting the Mantra 'according to the proper method', because the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas never speak falsehoods.

We are lucky in this life to still encounter the true dharma, to still learn the true dharma, and to have an enlightened teacher and virtuous friend guide us in the methods of reciting mantras to resolve karmic offenses. If we still stubbornly refuse to practice, then how heavy will our stubbornness be in the next life? And once we are stubborn, it is difficult to gain the wisdom to do good deeds. In this life, there is already a stingy and suspicious mind; if we have no merit left in the next life, what will happen?

Therefore, we sincerely hope that fellow practitioners will make an effort, diligently reciting mantras, chanting Buddha’s name, and must "put in all their heart, all their strength, and all their effort" in their practice to ensure their own rebirth in the Pure Land, as this is the hope to escape the cycle of birth and death and to achieve the fruition of the path. Only by doing so can one truly not fail oneself, and repay the countless lifetimes of parental care and nurturing, in accordance with the saying:

"One person practicing the Way benefits nine generations. First save oneself, then save others, and extend salvation to all people."

We all want to ensure that our parents are always materially well provided for. However, no matter how completely we manage this, it is only a form of 'Small Filial Piety,' because it merely helps our parents temporarily suffer less, but cannot help them escape the suffering of the cycle of birth and death. Instead, if we strive diligently in practicing this Pure Esoteric Dharma, and know how to encourage our parents, family, friends, etc., to practice as we do, then we will be reborn in the Pure Land and become Bodhisattvas after passing away. At that point, we can return to this world to liberate all our parents from many past lives, thus fulfilling 'Great Filial Piety'!

We are in the era of the Self-Fortified Tower, transitioning into the era of Fierce Struggle; the Dharma declines, demons thrive. The minds of sentient beings are increasingly more wicked. The Buddha has mystically predicted that:

In this Degenerate Dharma period, false teachers who "destroy the Dharma" are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River (Lăng Nghiêm Sutra). In addition, there are also 96 heretical sects and false religions that try every possible way to eliminate Buddhism, not allowing anyone to attain enlightenment. In the future, there will be no more printing of sutras or teaching of the true Dharma. Currently, we have already noticed that Buddhism is being destroyed in such a subtle and skillful way that few can recognize it.

They try every possible method:

· Internal investigation, external investigation, proper investigation, improper investigation…

· It makes human nature no longer HUMANE (increasingly wicked).

We find it difficult to attain mental strength, right mind, right wisdom, and right view. Currently, human minds are increasingly polluted. There is greed, stubbornness, competition, anger, lust, etc… therefore, this leads to the whole world suffering in misery, accidents, war, and eventually, conflicts will erupt sooner or later.

If you want to know what is inside the minds of sentient beings, just look at the outside world today and you will immediately know. Inside the human mind, there is full of afflictions; outside, there are too many temptations. How can society not be in turmoil?

Demons are infiltrating everywhere, sparing no one; they enter every home, every market, and go into the consciousness of each person (both while awake and while asleep, knowing faces, names, homes, etc.) causing disturbances all over the world. Every house is covered in black smoke. Everyone suffers and is filled with sorrow and resentment… leading to storms and floods, large fires, unemployment, widespread hunger and misery, homes and families destroyed, loss of houses and jobs, increasing illnesses that are difficult to treat, and so on…

It is also because of the evil heart of humans that all these things arise. If everyone had a good heart, a peaceful heart, a heart full of compassion, then families would be happy and harmonious, and the world would be peaceful and prosperous. No matter how powerful demons and evil spirits are, they cannot do anything; sometimes they even respect and submit to worship!

VIRTUE IS THE RESPECT OF DEMONS AND SPIRITS.

Hopefully, we will soon let go of our bad habits and stubbornness, repent and strive to improve ourselves (from bad to good), let go of things that are pleasing or unpleasing, right or wrong, etc., to redirect impending disasters, so that we may live safely to a hundred years old.

The Patriarch (Đại Ninh) THÍCH THIỀN TÂM foresaw that in the future most Buddhists in particular, and people in general, would be influenced, possessed, and controlled by evil spirits, with few being able to practice in a way that they would be reborn as humans, let alone achieve liberation to the realms of Heaven or Buddha.

With great compassion, He opened up the practice of SECRET PURITY, composing mantras from the SECRET TANTRA (of the Mahayana Canon) in order to save Buddhist practitioners with good roots (and sincere practice) from the disasters of demons, so that their path of practice remains firm, thereby ensuring rebirth in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Anyone who sincerely practices must also recite MANTRAS to protect the body and mind from being tested and led astray by demons, which would obstruct the path to rebirth.

As mentioned above,

· RECITING THE BUDDHA'S NAME yields inconceivable MERIT

· Reciting charms gains immeasurable DIVINE POWER (this power will help us escape suffering)

If one only focuses on CALLING THE BUDDHA without accompanying it with RECITING CHARMS, it is like a person suffering from various diseases, surrounded by evil on all sides, never at peace day or night, groping along and dragging themselves forward, and if unfortunately encountering a sudden attack by robbers (Demons), then:

· There is no MENTAL POWER (not knowing how to use the mind)

· There is no PHYSICAL POWER (to resist)

· There is no WISDOM POWER (to distinguish right from wrong)

· There is not a bit of DIVINE POWER (to resist) at all

At that time, I was so scared that I couldn’t even remember to chant Buddha’s name, stunned with my heart stopped to death. So can the spirit still be at peace to return to the Pure Land?

Compassion must be accompanied by wisdom. Chanting Buddha’s name must be accompanied by Mantras (these two cannot lack one).

Those who do not have a righteous mind, are not sincerely practicing, need to seek liberation, or possess a MIND OF DOUBT, DISCRIMINATION, EVILNESS, MALICE, etc., will find it difficult to recite the Mantra properly and may easily experience "spiritual derangement" (because that Mantra embodies the mind and intention of the Buddha, which is purely "RIGHT", and if one with an "EVIL" mind recites the Mantra, it cannot resonate or achieve efficacy). Therefore, in this era of the complete decline of the Dharma, very few people "dare" to recite the Mantra or have a clear understanding of the Mudras and Mantras of the Buddha's teachings.

There are even many people who are afraid to recite the Mantra, and even slander and prevent others from reciting it. But they do not understand that:

The Buddha himself in the past also used the Mantra to subdue the armies of demons and save his disciples from demonic dangers!

Let us try to ask:

What Mantra does a MONK (the abbot residing in the temple) use to purify the temple, to purify himself daily (whenever eating, drinking, bathing), to offer to spirits, to pray for the deceased, to declare mourning, to end mourning, to summon souls, to make food offerings, to release living beings, even for the morning practice, etc.? Oh! How many people actually BELIEVE, recite the Mantra, and carry out exactly according to the Buddha's law?

Currently, most Buddhists only like to chant Sutras, recite Buddha's name to seek BLESSINGS for the day, or prefer sitting in Meditation rather than Reciting Mantras (which is to practice according to the true TANTRIC Buddhism of the BUDDHA).

If you want to know whether your world of Taking Refuge in the Three Jewels still exists or is lost, look back at your own mind (whether you do evil deeds, whether you are close to or friendly with evil people), and you will know immediately.

For example:

· Greedy for money, greedy for fame,

· Committing any bad deed.

· Speaking of gossip or slander.

· Not saying 'yes', but saying 'no'.

· Speaking badly of the Buddha, speaking badly of good people.

· Often angry, selfish, miserly

· Often jealous, envious

· Disputing right and wrong, high and low

· Stubborn, harboring hatred without letting go

· Fighting tirelessly

· Grabbing the good things for oneself

· Ungrateful, lacking integrity

· Insulting genuine practitioners

· Disrespecting teachers and destroying the lineage

· Killing the teacher, harming friends.

· Leading Buddhist followers to practice incorrectly (not in accordance with the path of the Buddha, as intended by the Patriarchs).

Just briefly summarizing the above is enough to see that even the Three Refuges and Five Precepts are hard to keep, let alone the Bodhisattva precepts or the Bhikkhu precepts!!! Which gods or spirits would continue to grant me protection?!

If the body smells, people will avoid you.

If the mind smells, gods and spirits will avoid you.

If one has completely lost the Realm of Refuge, then automatically the 25 Deities who protect them will also leave. At that point, demons can easily come in to harm, capture the soul, and seize the body...

Many Buddhists do not understand this thoroughly, so they think that:

Practicing Pure Land Buddhism (chanting the Buddha's name) is very easy; anyone (righteous or not) can practice it. On the other hand, practicing Tantra is very difficult (reciting mantras constantly without seeing any results), and those who recite mantras will find it hard to achieve spiritual fruition, etc…!

Or:

If you want to reach the Pure Land quickly, you must focus exclusively on chanting the Buddha's name and should not recite mantras. Practicing both methods (Esoteric and Pure Land) at the same time will lead to distraction, preventing single-mindedness and obstructing rebirth in the Pure Land!

Therefore, nowadays, most Buddhists who have practiced the Esoteric-Pure Land methods gradually give up reciting mantras (such as the Protective Mantra, Śūraṅgama, Great Compassion, Prajñā, Rebirth mantras, etc.), and even stop using the Vairocana blanket.

It should be further understood that the threefold path of ethics, meditation, and wisdom symbolizes Enlightenment, Righteousness, and Purity, and also symbolizes the Three Jewels: Buddha, Dharma, Sangha.

· Buddha means "Enlightenment".

· Dharma means "Right Dharma".

· Sangha carries the meaning of "Purity".

Studying Buddhism is nothing other than these three aspects: Enlightenment, Righteousness, and Purity. This is also likened to the three gates of the Triple Gate in front of the temple; entering one gate is entering the house of the Tathagata.

For the Zen school, it advocates seeing one's true nature to become Buddha.

This follows the practice according to the "Enlightenment" aspect.

The Teaching school advocates studying the Sutras and scriptures.

This follows the 'Right' path in practice.

Esoteric Buddhism and Pure Land are similar because they require a 'Pure' mind.

This follows the 'Pure' path in practice. In addition, Pure Land and Esoteric Buddhism are both 'Two Powers' methods. This means that apart from your own effort (self-power), you also receive help through the 'Power of Compassion' (other-power) of the deity of the Mantra and the 'Mind-power' of the Buddhas' blessing.

Therefore:

Practicing both 'Esoteric' and 'Pure' paths together is very suitable for one's capacity.

On the contrary:

The two disciplines of "Zen" and "Pure Land" practiced together are incompatible (with one's capacity), unless one is of the highest, highest aptitude, because one follows the path of Emptiness (Zen), while the other follows the path of Existence (Pure Land).

Therefore, both Esoteric Buddhism and Pure Land are equally difficult and equally easy.

Why are they easy?

Easy because the phrase "Amitabha Buddha" or the mantra "Um Brum Hum" can be recited by anyone.

But why are they difficult?

It is difficult because both require the person who Recites (Chú) or Reflects (Buddha) to have a pure mind, only then can "mental power" arise, and from that mental power gradually "spiritual power" can be obtained.

It is this "self-power" that cooperates with the "other-power" of Amitabha Buddha to bring oneself to the Pure Land.

Only with a pure mental power can one catch the wave of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, resonate spiritually, overcome natural calamities, and be guided toward rebirth in the Pure Land.

As for using a discriminating mind, a dependent mind, a stubborn mind, or an evil mind to recite the Buddha's name, it will inevitably attract the waves of Mara, causing demons to fill the house, chronic illnesses, relentless challenges, family unrest, and unfulfilled desires, etc. Even if one recites the Buddha's name continuously, one will not attain rebirth in the Pure Land; on the contrary, one may become an "enemy of the path" (because unknowingly one has assisted evil beings in destroying the Dharma, all while thinking that one is performing Buddha's work!).

It must be known:

Both, one Esoteric (MẬT), one Pure (TỊNH) share a common origin from which they arise. Now combining both parts (MẬT and TỊNH) together, the success increases manifold.

In the treatise Mahāprajñāpāramitā Śāstra, Master Xuánzàng clearly explained:

· Reciting mantras means to preserve and protect.

· Preserving is gathering virtuous dharmas so that they do not vanish.

· Protecting is preventing unwholesome thoughts from arising.

· Reciting mantras helps to increase wisdom power and spiritual power.

· Maintain mental strength, preserve vital energy

(like a person who has lost all vital energy will constantly fall ill, the body and mind often tired, increasingly exhausted, wisdom clouded, no longer self-controlled, easily possessed by demons).

· A person who recites mantras attains correct mind and right intention.

· Unite and preserve countless Buddhist teachings, ensuring they never perish.

When reciting mantras, the hands should form mudras, the mouth should chant the mantra (vocalized), the eyes look at a Buddha statue, and the mind contemplates (remembers) the syllable Râm (seed syllable symbolizing the essence of the Buddhas).

The practice of Mantra Recitation helps practitioners "develop wisdom" to control their actions, speech, and thoughts, and to clearly distinguish between what is right and what is wrong. In this way, actions, speech, and thoughts become pure, and delusional thoughts naturally do not arise. When discriminatory thoughts do not arise and the mind remains pure, "spiritual power" can emerge (this power is capable of saving oneself and others, helping to overcome natural disasters, and attaining liberation).

The way of chanting the Buddha’s name and reciting mantras loudly is called “Bố Ma” (to scare away demons so that they flee), which can purify the body, speech, and mind, and grant the following special benefits:

1. Eliminates drowsiness and sluggishness

2. Keeps the mind undistracted

3. Prevents worldly matters from reaching the ears

4. Grants bright eyes

5. Produces a resonant, strong, firm, and powerful voice

6. Develops a strong and majestic demeanor

7. Speaking frankly and boldly

8. Upright spirit, not timid, not afraid, charging into battle to subdue evil forces

9. Valiant and diligent

10. Mental and spiritual power arising extremely strong

11. Karmic illnesses are eliminated

12. The Four Elements are harmonized

13. Mind and body are at ease

14. When reciting the Mantra, a halo emerges surrounding the body of the reciter

15. Talismans, venomous insects, and poisonous winds cannot harm one's body

16. Celestial demons must be fearful and respectful

17. Wandering spirits around who hear the sound of the Mantra will be liberated

18. Insects, mice, ants, cockroaches, spiders, beetles, will automatically leave, or will be freed from their cycle of life

19. Spirits with affinity, and those of nine generations will also be liberated

20. Heavenly Dragon Dharma Protectors are always nearby to protect, comfort, remind, and teach, etc...

21. All wishes are fulfilled as desired

22. Fame gradually spreads throughout the ten directions

23. Samadhi appears before the eyes

24. Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions are all joyful and give their blessings

25. At the time of death, maintain mindfulness, know the exact day and hour, and be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Practicing according to the Tantric Pure Land method means to "train" the body and mind to be disciplined; it requires the practitioner to have an earnest desire, determination to abandon negative thoughts, and always seek liberation, rather than only practicing because one has a "foundation" (Tantra). If one has a high spiritual capacity and a purified mind, is there even a need to practice (reciting Buddha's name or chanting mantras)?

In the previous section, it was mentioned:

To achieve good results on the path of tantric practice, the first and foremost requirement is not to harbor doubt or contempt in your heart. Even if that sense of "doubt" or "attachment" is as small as a speck of dust, it should definitely not be present. If one firmly resolves and practices accordingly, it can be called "in accordance with the Dharma"! For the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas never speak falsely (do not utter lies)!

Therefore, to ensure rebirth in the Pure Land in this lifetime, alongside reciting the Buddha's name, we also need to practice mantras, which will help resolve disturbances (when enemies or negative forces arise) and increase the certainty of rebirth for ourselves.

The two words MẬT TỊNH imply:

A practitioner must first RECITE MANTRAS (Mật), and only then PRACTICE PURE LAND BUDDHISM (Tịnh). Why? Because reciting mantras generates POWER (to help the body feel light, the speech pure, and the mind clear), so that when practicing Pure Land Buddhism, one attains complete merit. If one consistently practices in this way, maintaining a clear mind throughout life, one will certainly be reborn in the Pure Land and permanently escape the cycle of birth and death.

(It is recommended to refer to the sutra “Mahāyāna Adornment of the Treasure King” to know more about the efficacy of the Mantra, the benefits of the Vairocana robe, wearing the Mantra, carrying the Mantra, drawing the Mantra, and the secret practices of those who receive the Bodhisattva precepts (for the salvation of sentient beings) as well as the merit of the practice of “drawing blood to transcribe the Sutra,” etc…)

In summary:

If one wants to NEUTRALIZE NATURAL DISASTERS and ESCAPE DEMONIC CALAMITIES, and practice peacefully until the day of REBIRTH IN THE PURE LAND, it is necessary to practice the Secret Mantra path with the dual cultivation.

Reciting Buddha's name while in the mind one does not leave the sound of the Mantra, it is always resounding in the ear (at home, one should keep a machine reciting the Mantra all day and night)

The magical Mantra "replaces the command of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas," so it has an inconceivable power to resolve karmic disasters, helping to PROTECT THE BODY FROM HARM (from water, fire, storms, floods, evil people causing harm, spells, demons, nothing can harm the person who is reciting this Mantra).

As long as one can 'resolve' peace for oneself, it will also help those around to be at peace and escape danger. All natural disasters, wars, and fires are entirely caused by the MINDS of sentient beings.

Because sentient beings often have:

·AN ANGRY, FEROCIOUS MIND, which attracts VIOLENT FIRE

A DESIRING, GREEDY MIND, which attracts RAIN, STORMS, FLOODS, TSUNAMIS

·A KILLING, HARMFUL MIND, which attracts WAR, SMOKE AND FIRE

·When the mind is confused and deluded, it tends to attract gusts of wind, storms, and an endless series of suffering, which will not be simple or easy to deal with.

Because all natural disasters are caused by the evil mind of sentient beings. The more wicked, more fierce, more inventive, and more scheming a person's mind is, the more it creates consequences that will relentlessly "strike back" at that being.

"The Buddhas of the ten directions and countless Bodhisattvas are manifesting and covering our Saha world, yet they cannot prevent the waves of black divine forces violently surging in…"

If you want to NEUTRALIZE natural disasters, you must start from the "good" mind of sentient beings by practicing self-improvement, repentance, reciting mantras, and stopping doing evil.

Then:

Use the "POWER OF GOODNESS" in your mind to "focus" far and wide to neutralize evil occurrences.

Use the "POWER OF PURITY" from the mind to neutralize disturbances.

Sitting at home and reciting mantras can still relieve disasters for sentient beings.

It should be understood that the Buddha only saves those with affinity. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas only assist those who have the good seeds to PRACTICE AND TRANSFORM THEIR MIND AND NATURE, regularly examine their minds, and practice good deeds; only then can they help alleviate disasters.

Therefore, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas cannot SAVE BEINGS WITH EVIL MINDS.

Just like the Demon King, he cannot stand in the void and "destroy" all beings who have sincere hearts and practice genuine cultivation!

The Demon King cannot harm those with good minds who practice genuine cultivation.

Buddhas and Bodhisattvas cannot save those with an evil mind.

Both Buddhas and Mara rely only on the good and evil minds of sentient beings.

Bodhisattvas along with Buddhas in all ten directions hear and see all cries for help and words of suffering from sentient beings, but there is no way to save them, because it must come from the mind of those sentient beings themselves, sincerely and truly wanting to be saved.

Those who sincerely cry for help have already been rescued by the Bodhisattvas, allowing them to overcome suffering (the number of sentient beings saved is very small). As for the number of people who are or will be in danger, amidst fire and calamity in the future, it is countless. The bodies of the dead float like water plants on the river.

The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas can only watch with their eyes and shed tears, because they cannot save sentient beings who have extremely evil minds.

According to the law, one reaps exactly the results of the causes one sows.

Therefore, whenever a natural disaster comes to you, you should not blame Heaven or Buddha to avoid adding more sins, but instead use both hands to hit your head and face while scolding yourself, 'Why are you so evil, that now you have to pay for your evil deeds, and no one can save you!'

Good, evil, virtuous, wicked, exalted, fallen, misfortune, and blessings all come from the MIND. As long as one maintains a joyful Mind, the house will be affected with coolness, lightness, and stable work. On the other hand, if the Mind carries much worry, attachment, and irritation, the house will be covered with dark energy, heaviness, illness, work will face difficulties, and there will be quarrels between husband and wife, etc. If one person's Mind has already had such an influence, then imagine how the collective influence of many evil Minds would be?

Whenever the MINDS of sentient beings are peaceful and joyful, the whole world will also be safe, peaceful, with harmonious rain and favorable wind. This is demonstrated through a story in Washington D.C. about “4,000 peaceful MINDS”:

Twenty years ago, the American Scientific Journal announced a sociological experimental study first conducted at the University of Maryland, located in the Washington DC area. In the summer of 1993, 4,000 people from all over the world (81 countries) registered to attend the TU "MẬT MEDITATION" course (Meditation of MANTRA) for 2 months. They taught these 4,000 people the method of RECITATION to help FOCUS their MIND, in order to reduce the "INFLUENCE" and "COLDNESS" of evil acts, assaults, murders, rapes, robberies, violence, and crimes, etc., that were extremely prevalent in Washington, DC at that time.

The result in 2 months is: They discovered and showed that: the rate of crime, violence, including murder and rape – was reduced by 23% during the trial of the MENTAL CLEARING of 4,000 people.

Physicist Dr. Hagelin has previously studied and stated that:

“Meditation and Mantra techniques help create a deep state of 'relaxation.' The MENTAL ENERGY of 4,000 participants generated a wave of PEACE, LIGHTNESS, and GENTLENESS that influenced the surrounding ORDERLY environment and also affected other people (who were unaware and did not participate in this experiment). The combined mental energy of these 4,000 people produced a 'GENTLE' movement that influenced the 'climate' so that even the number of 'offenders' in society became 'calm.' The results show that the field of 'Consciousness' (Study) has an incredibly strong and unimaginable influence.”

The deaths, sufferings, and violence are caused by the extreme "stress" from the "Collective Mind" of sentient beings.

The deceased still carry old karma, reincarnate to create new karma, and add the collective karma of the society's environment. The combination of these three karmas is too heavy, making it very difficult to seek liberation.

Scientists like Edison and Marconi have also shown us that waves (of electricity, radio) have the ability to carry light and sound, and the same applies to the Mind-force of sentient beings. Whenever one recites a mantra (with a pure mind), the aura of that mind immediately shines forth, carrying the Mind-force of the person reciting the mantra, and that person is also transmitting all the Mind-intention of a BODHISATTVA, and even the Mind-force of the BUDDHA, which instantly spreads far, RESOLVING all surrounding disturbances, averting misfortunes, avoiding calamities, and bringing peace to everything.

In summary, Buddhists practicing Vajrayana should know that:

Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, together with the Buddhas, out of compassion for sentient beings, have granted us an inexhaustible treasure, but sentient beings do not know how to use it properly and according to the Dharma, so they receive no benefit or response at all.

People do not clearly understand the miraculous transforming power and the infinitely profound spiritual energy of the Mantra, so they develop wrongful intentions and misuse the "Seal, Mantra" of the Buddha and the Bodhisattva (to control people, harm good people, act contrary to the "Compassionate Heart" and against the "Mind and Intention" of the Buddha and the Bodhisattva), then it will cause great destruction, and the consequences (downfall) will also be boundless!

One must be careful about this.

People have too many selfish desires, greed, anger, and fame-lust, and often seek (things that cannot possibly be given), yet they are lazy and refuse to seek knowledge or learn anything themselves, refuse to practice, refuse to act according to the right teachings (of the Buddha), refuse to give alms, refuse to do good deeds, only wanting all wealth, fame, and desires to fall entirely into their hands. They are not afraid of death, not afraid of sin, not afraid of damnation, not afraid of consequences, so they recklessly kill countless people just for a bit of false fame!

Many people do not know that:

All the mantras of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are very miraculous. Considered as a 'wish-fulfilling' mantra, they have the power to save people from all suffering, to help them escape from torment, and to liberate them from the three realms and six paths. They cannot be used contrary to the evil intentions of worldly people; doing so will cause them to backfire immediately, resulting in undesirable outcomes. Whenever one harbors malicious thoughts and desires to harm others, they will bring upon themselves equivalent consequences.

“Spit someone else's blood and dirty your own mouth,” is like looking up at the sky and spitting.

Therefore, those who recite the Protective Mantra, Great Compassion Mantra, Six-Syllable Great Brightness Mantra, and other mantras (of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas) must have sincere devotion, and their mind must be pure and clean to recite the Mantras. They should only wish for good things for others, benefit others, and save others from suffering, karmic obstacles, or disasters occurring everywhere. If one has a good intention, creates means, and guides others to practice according to the true Dharma, etc., then the Mantra and Seal can be used in any situation (without incurring fault).

The wrong person speaks the true Dharma, and the true Dharma transforms into the wrong.

Righteous people speak against false teachings, false teachings always go against righteousness.

When reciting the Mantra, one must maintain a pure heart, follow the Bodhisattva conduct, and let compassion arise. Only then can one develop the POWER OF MIND, the DIVINE POWER will travel thousands of miles, and the clear mind of the person reciting the mantra will reach all the Buddhas in the ten directions. Countless Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas will radiate light to illuminate and surround that person, so there is no fear of not attaining spiritual response and connection. The spiritual power will continuously increase, and all wishes will always be fulfilled. Everything from family matters to worldly affairs will be completely harmonious and good.

The compassion of the Buddhas, of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva (specifically) and of the great Bodhisattvas across the ten directions (in general) towards sentient beings is boundless.

They always perceive all the thoughts and intentions of sentient beings, but the mind of sentient beings is not pure, their thoughts are very unwholesome and are always obscured by wrongdoings, overwhelming anger, ambition for fame, pursuit of profit, and harming others in a violent manner, and therefore it is impossible to resonate with the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

One can only quietly stand and watch while shedding tears. The Bodhisattva is close to a sentient being who is suffering, who is in distress, yet cannot truly sympathize, nor can they save that sentient being.

The Bodhisattva feels very sorrowful because it is difficult to teach or clearly show the sentient beings. The Bodhisattva's teachings cannot fully reach the ears of the sentient beings, so one must use the hands of others to save them in this way.

Therefore, a person who is focused, wholeheartedly reciting mantras, as if a Bodhisattva is standing in front of them, sincerely repenting and purifying body and mind, will attain extremely strong "mental power, intellectual power, spiritual power," and will be spiritually connected with the BUDDHA and the BODHISATTVA. This is neither hard to believe nor hard to understand.

When the clouds disperse, the moon shines; when the water recedes, the pearls are revealed. When the mind is pure and bright, the Buddha appears. Even natural disasters cannot arise.

Once the mind (stress) of sentient beings settles down, the mind is at PEACE, the mind of “loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity” can arise (no longer evil, greedy, angry, jealous, envious, or attached). Everyone will become a generator of order and peace in society, forever happy...

If sentient beings practice generating a “good mind” more, and wholeheartedly practice the method (Tantric Buddhism), it will resolve natural disasters, and ensure the path to “liberation” and “rebirth in the Pure Land” in this life.

Ohm Mani Pad Mi Hum

🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏

Respectfully,

Venerable: Thich Thien Tam

tieu_de: PEOPLE WHO STUDY BUDDHISM MUST KNOW WHAT IS IMPORTANT - OTHERWISE, THEY WILL GAIN SMALL BENEFITS AND SUFFER GREAT HARM
tom_tat: People nowadays more than half are fond of reputation, building towers in the air. Having a part or half, they then claim to have a hundred thousand myriad parts. As in the book 'Yu Lu' by that layman, the realms he
noi_dung:
WHAT BUDDHIST LEARNERS MUST KNOW IS IMPORTANT - IF THEY DON'T, SMALL BENEFITS TURN INTO GREAT HARM

Nowadays, most people are too concerned with appearances, building towers and lofts in the air. If they obtain a part or half, they claim to have hundreds of thousands of parts. As in the Record of Words by that lay scholar, the realms he described are all matters imagined by his pen, not scenes created by the mind. Naturally, he doesn't lie, but I truly fear that he may be caught in this habit, which is no small misfortune.

The Buddha classified false speech among the five basic precepts precisely to prevent this evil. If one says they see what is not seen, or claims not to see what is seen, it belongs to the sin of false speech. If one constructs lofts in the air or fabricates supreme realms, it violates the precept against grievous false speech. Claiming to have attained a treasure when one has not, or to have realized a treasure when one has not, the sin is heavier than killing, stealing, or sexual misconduct multiplied hundreds of thousands of billions of times.

If that person does not thoroughly repent, at the moment when one breath goes out and does not return, they will immediately fall into the Avīci Hell for corrupting the Dharma, causing sentient beings to be deluded.

You must be very careful; when observing, you cannot speak even one point more than what you see, nor can you say it is nine point nine. Speaking too much would be a mistake, and speaking less is also not allowed. Why is that?

Because the knowledge has not yet attained the Tha Tâm Ðạo Nhãn, one can only make judgments based on what has been said. Sharing this with those who possess that knowledge to have them verify whether it is false or correct, right or wrong, is not a problem.

If it is not for proof, but only for showing off, it is also a fault! If you speak to everyone, it is also a fault. Except when seeking knowledge for verification, nothing should be spoken. Once spoken, in the future, that supreme state will never be attained again.

This is the first barrier for practitioners, which has been mentioned many times in the Tiantai Sect.

The reason why many practitioners recently have been possessed by demons is due to their restless minds, hastily longing to attain superior states. Do not say that such a scene is a demonic illusion; even if the scene is truly a superior state, if one's entire life is filled with delight, greed, etc., it will still be harmed rather than benefited. Moreover, how can we be sure that the scene is truly a superior state?

If that person has cultivation, the mind does not become agitated, hurried, or greedy, and does not become attached. Seeing various realms is as if seeing nothing, no feelings of joy or attachment arise, and also no feelings of fear or alarm arise. Then, not only will the appearance of excellent or superior realms bring benefit, even the appearance of demons will still be beneficial! Why is that?

Because he is not possessed by a spirit, advancement is possible. I do not usually say this to others, but since you have these circumstances, I cannot not speak. The Great Master's statue that you saw when you first worshiped Buddha is not accurate. If it were truly his statue, it would not have hidden just because you thought it did not match the Sutra of Contemplation.

But because of that, your faith becomes even more earnest, which is also a good cause, though you should not expect to see the statue regularly. You should only sincerely worship and venerate it, and I hope you do not think otherwise.

When sleeping, seeing light before your eyes and seeing Buddha statues standing in the void during worship, although these are auspicious signs, do not become attached. From now on, do not take these as things to desire; such appearances will no longer manifest.

Considering your temperament, perhaps in a previous life you practiced Meditation, which is why you have seen these signs multiple times. During the Ming dynasty, Mr. Ngu Thuan Hy lived on Thien Muc Mountain, secluded and meditative on the high mountain peak. After a long time, he became a soothsayer, able to predict whether the weather would be cloudy or clear, and the fortune or misfortune of people.

He took refuge with Master Liên Trì. The master, upon hearing the story, sent a letter strongly reproaching him, saying he had fallen into the trap of demons. After that, he was no longer heard of.

It should be known: those who study the Way must understand what is important; otherwise, small gains will result in great harm. Do not even mention those realms; even if one truly attains the Five Superknowledges, one must still disregard them in order to hope to achieve the Complete Ending of Defilements.

If one indulges even once in craving, it will be difficult to progress, and one may even fall back. This cannot be unbeknownst!

MASTER AN QUANG'S RECORD OF WORDS! (129)

tieu_de: WHY DO WE STILL ENCOUNTER ACCIDENTS EVEN WHEN CHANTING SUTRAS AND RECITING BUDDHA'S NAME?!?
tom_tat: ----------------- Question: In the “Sutra of Kṣitigarbha,” it is taught that descriptions of heaven, earth, ghosts, and spirits often protect those who recite the Buddha's name and worship the Buddha – preventing disasters from entering their doors, and avoiding calamities such as floods, fires, theft, robbery, etc.
noi_dung:
WHY DO PEOPLE STILL HAVE ACCIDENTS EVEN WHEN RECITING SUTRAS AND CHANTING AMITABHA BUDDHA?!?

-----------------

Question: In the “Kṣitigarbha Sūtra,” it is explained that celestial beings, ghosts, and spirits often protect those who recite Buddha’s name and perform Buddha’s ceremonies – preventing misfortunes from entering their doors, and protecting them from disasters such as water, fire, theft, robbery, etc., meaning that all evil deeds are eliminated. However, I notice that many laypeople who worship the Buddha and recite sutras still encounter misfortunes such as illness, evil people, car accidents, plane crashes, etc. Even I myself often face undesirable events. I have also observed virtuous high monks and laypeople suddenly fall gravely ill and pass away. Although I do not doubt what is described in the “Kṣitigarbha Sūtra,” it is hard to avoid having questions, so I respectfully ask you to explain it to me for my understanding.

add.

Answer: Please read the “Kṣitigarbha Sutra” carefully and do not break the sentences to extract meanings or interpret them according to your own ideas. You must know that whenever the Buddha or Bodhisattvas teach, when mentioning those who will receive benefits, the paragraph always begins with the phrase: “Good men, good women.” This clearly indicates: anyone who is a “good man or good woman,” if they worship the Buddha, recite the sutras, or encourage others to believe in the Buddha and study Buddhism, will have hundreds of thousands of spirits guarding them day and night. It can also be phrased this way: “If one is not a good man or good woman but worships the Buddha or encourages others to practice Buddhism, they only make a connection with the Buddha and plant the seeds of goodness, but cannot immediately attract the spirits of heaven, earth, or demons."to seek protection, because they have only just believed in the Buddha, not yet truly studied Buddhism or practiced cultivation! How can one reap good results without planting good deeds? Therefore, they have not truly benefited.

So what are the standards for “good men and good women”? The Buddha calls laymen and laywomen, as well as monks and nuns, “good men and good women.” Good means: liking to listen to the Dharma, and having faith in the Buddha. Although laypeople have husbands and wives, they maintain all their speech and conduct as if they were monastics. As for those who indulge in drinking, gambling, drug use, causing loud quarrels, adultery, promiscuity, theft, lying, committing the ten evils… they cannot be called “good men and good women.” These people, because they plant evil deeds, will surely reap evil results, so how can they hope for the protection of heaven, earth, demons, and spirits?

-------------------

Namo Amitabha Buddha!

Namo Amitabha Buddha!!

Namo Amitabha Buddha!!!

tieu_de: The Latest Confession Essay by Dharma Master Tinh Khong
tom_tat: Although this essay is quite long, its meaning is complete; those who are ill or those seeking to resolve grievances and misfortunes will gain practical benefits from applying it. When reciting this essay, one should use a sincere heart, a respectful heart, and a remorseful heart.
noi_dung:
The Latest Repentance Essay by Master Tịnh Không

Although this text is quite long, its meaning is profound, and those who are ill or those seeking to resolve injustices can gain practical benefits from applying it.

When reciting this text, one should use a sincere heart, a respectful heart, a remorseful heart, and a repentant heart, contemplating according to the words; surely it can resonate with and transform the grievances of adversaries, resolving injustices. (Recite twice daily, ideally followed by 15 minutes of chanting the Buddha’s name, during which one may help transcend the grievances of adversaries.)

Turning towards all (adversaries)

Repentance and making vows

The noble Bodhisattvas whom we have harmed in many lifetimes

Extremely remorseful, I apologize (1 bow)

Sorry, I was wrong (1 bow)

Sorry, I was wrong (1 bow)

Sorry, please forgive me (1 bow)

From beginningless birth and death until now, I have been deluded and insane, creating all kinds of karma, intentionally or unintentionally offending, harming, even killing you, causing your body and mind to endure extreme torment in samsara, to endure immeasurable suffering, increasing countless afflictions, making it so that you remain in ignorance without liberation. I deeply feel that my karma is heavy, my sins are extremely evil, truly unforgivable. All of this is due to greed, anger, delusion, arrogance, doubt, and the threefold karma of body, speech, and mind over many lifetimes, by which I have committed all obstacles and all errors. I cannot use language to express the shameshame, regret, and remorse in my heart. I also fully understand that it is not one or two apologies that can resolve the extreme pain in your body and mind caused by me. I do not dare to ask for your forgiveness, I only sincerely wish to help you forever leave suffering and find happiness.

If taking revenge on me could relieve your suffering, I would absolutely not resist or escape, and I would also have no words of resentment, because this is the consequence of a crime I committed myself, deserving of retribution. But now I have taken refuge in the Three Jewels, have listened to the Buddha's teachings, understand clearly the principle of karmic cause and effect, and know that if in this life you take revenge and harm me, due to the force of karma, in the next life I will also take revenge. Thus, from this life to the next, we trouble each other, generation after generation lives in affliction, in suffering, and no one truly benefits; this is indeed a foolish way to destroy each other. Generation after generationLives of injustice are repaid in kind, with no end, and no one benefits. Even if you have taken revenge on me, wherever you are now, you still cannot escape; this is the most painful thing. We can no longer be deluded, we must find a broad and bright path to leave suffering and attain joy.

Now I understand: all beings are my parents of countless lifetimes, having boundless grace and virtue toward us. All beings have Buddha-nature, and all can certainly become Amitabha Buddha, being one with oneself. Every single moment of life from now to the far future, toward every being in the empty Dharma realm, is filled with gratitude, filial respect, loving-kindness, sincerity, reverence, shame, humility, deep faith in cause and effect, abandoning evil and practicing goodness, observing precepts, refraining from killing and eating vegetarian, releasing life beings, chanting Amitabha, knowing contentment and constant joy, being gentle and harmonious, magnanimous and tolerant, understanding and forgiving. I will forgive through all lifetimes. Forgive beings.The past has killed and harmed me; forgive the beings of the present who kill and harm me; forgive the beings of the future who will kill and harm me.

But this mind of anger, revenge, and unwillingness to forgive, will cause you to endure countless eons of all sorts of painful punishments of mountains of knives and forests of swords in hell, without end. There will never be a day free from extreme suffering, beyond imagination, dying miserably seventy thousand times in one second. I sincerely wish that you will never have to suffer any more pain. The Buddha tells us that: all conditioned phenomena are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, a shadow, like dew and like lightning; all that have forms are false and illusory. The past mind is unattainable, the present mind is unattainable, the future mind is unattainable, all dharmas are non-attainable, everything will inevitably...no, unattainable, all phenomena are empty, the transformation of cause and effect is not empty, continuity is not empty, circulation is not empty. (translator's note: because I have not yet understood the 'profound principle' of 'EMPTINESS', I dare not translate the meaning, only temporarily transliterate this passage into 'Sino-Vietnamese phonetics', I ask fellow practitioners for their understanding.)

Esteemed Bodhisattvas of great wisdom: you also do not wish to merely feel momentarily pleased, only to eternally immerse yourselves in the sea of suffering. In this life, I am fortunate to hear the Buddha Dharma; my body and mind have never before experienced such joy, like a long drought encountering the rain of amrita, my body and mind are cleansed, awakened from delusion. Especially having heard the supreme practice of reciting the Buddha's name, a practice that leads to liberation and Buddhahood in one lifetime. There is a Pure Land in the Western Realm, where there are no three realms of hell, no six destinies of samsara and rebirth, no hatred, no suffering or calamities of any kind, and not even the sound ofthe name of suffering, that place is truly our eternal and peaceful home.

There is the most kind and benevolent Bodhisattva together with us, within the warm compassionate embrace of Amitabha Buddha. The sound of the wind, the sound of the rain, and the sound of water all expound the wondrous Dharma. White Cranes and Peacocks, day and night, six times a day, sing harmoniously, praising the wondrous Dharma. The Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss is pure and solemn, vast and flat, wondrously magnificent and extraordinary, bright everywhere, exceedingly fragrant and clean, the ground paved with gold, pavilions of seven treasures, nets of pearls spread out, four seasons like spring, day and night, six times a day, heavens shower marvelous flowers, and the sky resounds with music. Lotuses are in full bloom on the eight-merit water in the seven-treasure pond, shining in all directions, as sentient beings of the ten directions recite.Buddhas are guided by Buddhas, born in this Buddhist land, all are born from lotus flowers.

Virtuous and noble people gather in one place. Whether they like to give dharma talks or enjoy listening to the dharma, they are all joyful, without worry or sorrow, free from entanglements and busy matters, naturally relaxed, at ease, harmonious and peaceful, smooth and gentle, eternally youthful, with radiant golden bodies, unlimited lifespan, free and unimpeded, full of supernatural powers, carrying palaces, clothing, and food as they wish, with jeweled banners and parasols, flowers, incense, and music instantly available at will, offering to all Buddhas in an instant. The entire space of the dharma realm is freely traversable by us, with a pure and ethereal body, a limitless form, innumerable emanations, universally saving all beings.pervading the entire Dharma realm.

In the Pure Land world, there is a Buddha named Amitabha, who has made forty-eight great vows. He is compassionate, joyful, and infinitely forgiving. Even if we have committed the five heinous sins and ten evil acts, He does not abandon us nor turn away; instead, He proactively and unconditionally saves us with equality.

He is like a parent longing for their only child, always hoping for our return. Up until now, ten kalpas have passed, day after day of waiting. Releasing His hand to guide us, year after year He waits for us --------- the child suffering in the three realms, the wanderer in the six paths. He vows that as long as we repent our karmic obstacles and recite the Buddha’s name to seek rebirth in the Western Paradise, He will surely lead us to be reborn in the Pure Land, forever liberated from the suffering of birth and death, forever enjoying bliss.

Now we also introduce this superior method to you, hoping that every day you can follow me in bowing to the Buddha, reciting sutras, and chanting the Buddha’s name while making vows to be reborn in the Pure Land. When I am absent, you yourselves must diligently listen to the sutras and chant the Buddha's name. In the future, we will all be reborn in the Western Land, becoming disciples of Bodhi, attaining the realization of the deathless Dharma, and returning to Saha to save all sentient beings. This is the method that is good for you, good for me, and good for everyone. If you achieve realization first, when my life ends, please follow the Three Pure Land Sages to come receive me. If I achieve realization first, I will definitely return to Saha to save you.taste. Let us encourage each other, urge each other, diligently practice cultivation, sincerely recite the Buddha's name together, pray to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, soon leave suffering and attain happiness, and together accomplish the path of Buddhahood.

The killers who harm us throughout life and successive lives, causing us to suffer in the six realms, are the illusions, distinctions, attachments, greed, anger, ignorance, pride, and doubt within our own hearts. Therefore, we should hate and eliminate our true enemies, which are our own greed, anger, and ignorance, rather than external people, events, or objects. Thus, we are all victims of greed, anger, and ignorance; let us together repent before the Buddha!

Shameful repentance from beginningless time until now for being unfilial to parents and spiritual teachers, for blaspheming the Triple Gem, harming sentient beings, obstructing others from practicing and spreading the Dharma, and the sins created by body, speech, mind, desire, anger, and ignorance. Completely eradicate the roots of arrogance and conceit, pride and egoism, lustful mind, selfishness and greed, resentment, anger and revenge, oppositional and rejecting mind, jealousy, impatience and restlessness, desire for fame and vanity, possessiveness and controlling mind, egoistic clinging to self-identity, false discriminating thoughts and attachments, laziness, drowsiness, restlessness, distracted mind, liking trivial talk, and careless entanglement, thoroughly eliminating all these bad habits at the root. GreatFrom great compassion, bear suffering on behalf of all sentient beings, mind like ashes that cannot catch fire, abandon the greed for sleep, keep a pure speech, let go of myriad attachments, single-mindedly recite the Buddha's name, in this life be reborn in the Western Pure Land, countless emanations, universally liberating sentient beings.

Time is life, and life is for attaining Buddhahood. I vow: to develop great determination, to let go of myriad attachments, to decisively maintain pure speech, to resolutely recite the Buddha's name, to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss in this life, to manifest countless emanations, and to universally save sentient beings. In this life, I truly observe precepts and recite the Buddha's name, not daring to arise a single evil thought. I have blessings, and everyone will share them.

I vow: to dedicate the merit of my own practice of Morality, Concentration, and Wisdom to my parents, my spiritual teachers in many lifetimes, to the Bodhisattvas who have been harmed, and to all sentient beings like mothers in the ten directions of the world, that they may be free from suffering and attain joy, and be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Amitabha Buddha's forty-eight vows, the vow to be reborn through ten recitations, are universal at all times and places, receiving all sentient beings to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. All sentient beings in the ten directions of the world who have faith and recite the Buddha's name will surely be reborn in the Pure Land and perfectly attain Buddhahood.

All sentient beings have Buddha-nature; reciting the Buddha's name will surely lead to becoming a Buddha. With one-minded recitation of the Buddha's name, one will definitely be reborn in the Western Pure Land and perfectly attain Buddhahood.

Sincerely, I make this vow: to all parents and teachers in the ten directions, to all virtuous Bodhisattvas, and to all sentient beings, may you practice and study the Buddha's teachings, deeply believe in cause and effect, abandon evil and cultivate goodness, dispel delusions and awaken to enlightenment, recite the Buddha's name with one mind, and freely be reborn in the Western Pure Land, perfectly attaining Buddhahood.

Namo Amitabha Buddha! Amitabha Buddha! Amitabha Buddha!

Story 3

A 30-year-old young man in Ha Bac (China) had serious acne all over his face. He went to Master Tan to ask about the cause-and-effect. Master Tan asked him:
