tieu_de: ERADICATE LUST BY RECITING THE FOUR TYPES OF PURE AND CLEAR REPENTANCE
tom_tat: (Excerpt from the Leng Yan Sutra, Volume 6) We all fear the mind of lust; this mind is very difficult to control because it is a habitual tendency from many lifetimes. If we do not eliminate the mind of lust, it will continue to circulate in samsara and
noi_dung:
ERADICATING LUSTFUL DESIRES BY RECITING THE FOUR PURE CLARITY REPENTANCES

(Excerpt from the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, Volume 6)

Everyone is afraid of lustful desires; this mind is very difficult to manage because it is a habit carried over from many lifetimes. If one does not eliminate lustful desires, they will continue to circulate in samsara and even fall into the three evil paths. Lust leads to immoral sexual behavior, masturbation, which results in losing many blessings, and even the thought of immoral desire causes the loss of merit. A person who often has lustful desires attracts spirits that suck life energy, keeping company day and night, taking turns to sleep with that person to drain their energy, causing the person to be lethargic, easily irritated, anxious, distressed, fearful, unhealthy, or frequently ill... (because yang energy is low and yin energy is high), and may encounter misfortune in career and fame, and people around them naturallydespising... etc. There are still many other bad karmic results. Therefore, eliminating lustful thoughts is very necessary. This matter is very urgent, so the Admin provides this method for those who are not yet able to recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. Everyone should read it 1-3 times aloud or in mind in the morning before getting up, and the same in the evening before going to sleep. Doing it continuously for a period of time will naturally overcome lustful thoughts. In addition, it also generates countless merits!

Recite from here on:

Namo Lăng Nghiêm Assembly Supreme Buddha Bodhisattva (x3)

Namo Original Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha (x3)

Namo Vajra Treasury Bodhisattva (x3)

Namo Great Compassion Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva (x3)

Namo Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva (x3)

Venerable Ananda adjusted his robes, turned to the assembly, and joined his hands in reverent salutation. His mind was completely clear, both joyful and sorrowful. Wishing to benefit sentient beings of the future, he bowed and respectfully addressed the Buddha: “Homage to the Greatly Compassionate World-Honored One. I have now realized the method of attaining Buddhahood; by practicing within it, I am free from doubt.”

I often hear the Tathagata teach that: 'If one has not yet attained liberation oneself, but helps others first, that is the Bodhisattva's act of generating the mind. If one has already attained perfect enlightenment oneself, one can then enlighten others; that is the Tathagatas' worldly application.' Although I have not yet attained liberation, I vow to help all sentient beings in the degenerate age of Dharma.

O World-Honored One, these sentient beings are growing increasingly distant from the Buddha. Heretical teachers who preach are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. If we wish to gather their minds into the three stages of practice, how can we guide them to establish a proper place of the Way so they will not fall into demonic paths, nor withdraw from the mind of Bodhi?

At that time, the World-Honored One was among the assembly, praising Ānanda: Well said! Well said! Just as you inquired about establishing a monastery to help sentient beings who are sinking in the degenerate age. Now listen carefully, the Tathāgata will tell you. Ānanda and the assembly respectfully obeyed the Buddha's teaching.

The Buddha said to Ānanda: “You often hear in my Vinaya, I expound the three essential meanings of practice. To restrain the mind and thoughts is called precepts; from precepts arises meditative power; from meditation comes wisdom. These are called the three trainings of freedom from defilements.

1. ELIMINATING LUSTFUL THOUGHTS

Ananda, why is restraining the mind called precepts by the Tathagata? If beings in the six realms have minds without lust, then they will not continue in the cycle of birth and death.

One cultivates samadhi primarily to escape worldly suffering. If one does not eliminate lustful thoughts, one cannot escape worldly suffering. Even if one possesses great wisdom and present meditation, if one does not eradicate lustful mind, one will surely fall into the demonic path. Those of a higher class become demon kings, those of a middle class become demon subjects, and those of a lower class become demonesses.

Other types of demons also have followers. They all claim to have attained the supreme path.

After the Tathagata passed into nirvana, many types of demons and beings caused chaos in the world. They engaged in many lustful acts, claiming to be virtuous teachers, leading sentient beings into the deep pit of attachment to views and causing them to lose the path to enlightenment.

He taught people to practice the three grounds of steadfastness, first by eliminating lustful thoughts. This is a pure teaching, the first decisive instruction of the Buddhas, the Tathagatas, in past lives.

Therefore, Ananda, if one does not cut off lustful thoughts but practices meditation, it is like cooking sand and hoping it will turn into rice. Even after hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, it will still only be hot sand. Why? Because that is not the inherent nature of rice; it is only sand and stones.

If one uses a lustful body to seek the marvelous fruit of the Buddhas, even if one attains marvelous enlightenment, it is still rooted in lust. Once the root is lust, it must drift through the three realms and certainly cannot escape. So, what path is there to practice and realize the Nirvana of the Tathagata?

One must eliminate all lustful seeds in both body and mind. Once the nature is cut off, it is also eliminated. Only then can one hope to attain the bodhi fruit of the Buddhas.

As the Tathāgata says, these are indeed the words of the Buddhas. If it were not so, it would be the words of the Māra of three worlds.

2. MUST ELIMINATE THE MIND OF KILLING

Furthermore, Ānanda, if beings in the six realms throughout the worlds do not have a mind of killing, they certainly will not continue along the cycle of birth and death.

When one cultivates samādhi, the purpose is to exit the worldly defilements. If the mind of killing is not eliminated, it is impossible to escape the worldly defilements.

Even if one possesses many meditative insights in the present moment, if one does not eliminate the mind of killing, one will surely fall into the path of spirits. The high ones become powerful spirits of demons. The middle ones become flightless demons, yakshas, and various demon generals. The low ones become earth-walking rakshasas.

These kinds of demon gods also have followers. They all consider themselves to have attained supreme enlightenment.

After the Tathagata passed into parinirvana, during the end times of the Dharma, many of these kinds of demon gods become active in the world. They claim that eating meat will enable one to attain the path of bodhi.

Ananda, the Tathagata allowed billions of monks to eat five kinds of pure meat. That meat was all created by the Tathagata's spiritual power and originally did not have any life seeds. In your Brahmin region, the land is mostly damp and hot, with sand and stones, making it impossible for vegetables to grow. The Tathagata used the power of compassionate blessing. It is called meat due to the mind of great compassion. You also receive the taste as if it were meat. Why, after the Tathagata's parinirvana, do those who eat the flesh of sentient beings call themselves disciples of the Buddha?

You should know that those who eat meat, even if their minds are enlightened, like the Tamhade (tam-ma-đề), are still great reptiles. When their karmic retribution ends, they will again be submerged in the sea of suffering of birth and death. They are not disciples of the Buddha. Those people kill, destroy each other, and merely devour one another. How could such people escape the three realms?

You should teach people to practice the Tamhadiya (tam-ma-địa) method, which requires ceasing the act of killing. This is a clear and pure teaching, a decisive second rule of the Buddhas in past lives.

Therefore, Ananda, if one practices meditation without eliminating the act of killing, it is like someone covering their own ears and shouting loudly, expecting that others will not hear them. Such a person is called someone who wants to hide but only exposes themselves more.

A pure monk and the Bodhisattvas, even when walking on the road, do not step on young grass, let alone pull it up with their hands. Why, when practicing the mind of great compassion, would one use the flesh and blood of living beings as food?

If the bhikkhus do not wear silk, which is a product of the East, and do not use shoes, woolen garments, knitted clothes, or items made from milk, ghee, or sesame paste, those bhikkhus are truly liberated in the worldly Dharma. Having repaid all past debts, they will no longer enter the three realms.

Why using the bodily parts of sentient beings always affects them. For example, if a person consumes hundreds of types of grains from the earth, then their feet never leave the ground. One must firmly detach their body and mind, not use or consume anything from the bodies or parts of sentient beings. Only such individuals are truly regarded as liberated by the Tathagata.

As the Tathagata says, this is exactly what the Buddhas have spoken. If it is not so, then it is the words of the Māra of three weeks.

3. ERADICATE THE STEALING MIND

Furthermore, Ānanda, if sentient beings in the six realms have minds that do not steal, then they will not continue in the cycle of birth and death.

One cultivates samādhi with the purpose of transcending the world of suffering. If the stealing mind is not eradicated, it is impossible to transcend the world of suffering.

Even if one has many present meditative insights, if one does not eliminate the mind of stealing, they will inevitably fall into a heretical path. The higher ones become spirits, the middle ones become enchanted by demons, and the lower ones become heretical humans, being bewitched.

Those heretical groups also have followers. They all claim to have attained the supreme path.

After the Tathagata's parinirvana, during the final period of the Dharma, many kinds of demons and evil ways emerged vigorously in the world, secretly deceiving people while claiming to be good teachers. They all claimed to have attained superior dharma. They deceived the ignorant and intimidated them, causing them to lose faith. Wherever they went, people's families suffered losses.

The Tathagata taught the monks to go on alms rounds in order, so that they would let go of greed and accomplish the bodhi path. The monks did not cook their own food and relied on their bodies as if living as guests in the three realms. They manifested for a brief time and, having gone, did not return.

Why does that kind of enemy borrow the robe of the Buddha, trade in the Tathagata, create countless karmas, and claim that these are all Buddha's teachings? They also criticize monks and nuns who practice the precepts as followers of the Lesser Vehicle. Because they cause countless beings to fall into doubt and error, they will be condemned to the uninterrupted hells.

After the Tathagata passes into Nirvana, if a bhikshu generates the resolve to practice the threefold meditation, he may, before the image of the Tathagata, light a lamp himself, burn a finger; or burn an incense offering on his body. The Tathagata said that this person, whose debts from far past lives are now entirely repaid in one lifetime, separates from the world and permanently escapes all defilements. Although this person has not yet fully understood the path of supreme enlightenment, he has a resolute mind toward the Dharma.

If one is unable to sow that small seed of self-sacrifice, even if one attains effortless enlightenment, one will still be reborn as a human to repay old debts, like the karmic retribution of consuming horse-grain as experienced by the Tathagata.

He teaches people to practice the three stages of Dharma, and moreover, to eradicate the mind of stealing. That is called a clear and pure teaching, the third decisive instruction of the Buddhas of the past.

Therefore, Ananda, if one does not eradicate the mind of stealing but practices meditation, it is like pouring water into a leaky vessel and hoping it will fill. Even after countless lifetimes like dust particles, it will still not be full.

If monks, besides their robes and alms bowls, do not accumulate even a tiny bit, if they have surplus from alms, they give it to hungry beings. In large gatherings with many people, they join their hands to respectfully venerate the assembly. If someone strikes or scolds them, they regard it as praise. They see their own flesh, blood, and bones as similar to the bodies of all beings. If they do not take the teachings of the Tathagata that are of ultimate meaning as the place for their own enlightenment, so that novices are not led astray, then the Tathagata certifies that person as genuinely attaining samadhi.

As the Tathagata has spoken, it is the word of all Buddhas. If it does not accord with that speech, it is the words of Mara.

4. ERADICATING FALSE SPEECH

Ānanda, sentient beings in the six realms, although their body and mind no longer commit acts of killing and sexual misconduct, and the three virtuous practices are already perfected, if they fall into great false speech, then the samādhi will not be pure, will become like the demon of desire and attachment, and will lose the Tathāgata seed.

It cannot be said that one has attained; one cannot claim that one has realized. Or in order to seek the utmost respect from the world, telling others: Today I have attained the stage of Sotapanna, Sakadagami, Anagami, Arhatship, the path of Pratyekabuddha, or the stages of Bodhisattva in the Ten Grounds or before the Ten Grounds. Hoping to receive worship from everyone, or to receive offerings.

Those utterly insane beings destroy the Buddha seed within themselves. Like a person using a knife to chop down a Bodhi tree. The Buddha marks that person as having completely lost their good roots, no longer possessing right view, sinking in the three realms of suffering, unable to accomplish the dhyana practices.

After the Tathagata passes away, he instructs the Arhats and Bodhisattvas to manifest in the world during the era of the degenerate Dharma, appearing in many different forms to save sentient beings still caught in the cycle of rebirth.

They may appear as monks, white-clad laypeople, kings, officials, boys and girls. Even so, they may appear as courtesans, widows, deceivers, thieves, butchers, or merchants. In order to work alongside them, praising the Buddha Vehicle, bringing their body and mind into the stage of samadhi,

Ultimately, do not tell yourself that you are truly a Bodhisattva or an Arahant. Carelessly speaking to those who have not learned, revealing the secret teachings of the Buddha.

Only when it is near the end of life can one quietly leave a testament. Why do such people deceive sentient beings, committing the great sin of false speech?

You teach people to practice the three stages of Bodhisattva training, but ultimately must abandon the act of speaking great falsehoods. That is a clear and pure teaching, the fourth resolute precept of the Buddhas of the past lifetimes.

Therefore, Ananda, if one does not eliminate the words of great falsehood, like carving a sculpture of a sheep tree, and wants to attain fragrance, that is truly impossible.

The Tathagata teaches monks to use the upright mind as the field of the Way. Even in actions among the four dignities, one must not be deceitful. How then can there be someone who claims to have attained the superior Dharma?

For example, a poor person claiming to be an emperor brings about their own destruction. How much more so a position of Dharma King; how dare one arrogantly claim it! When the cause is not real, the result will certainly be convoluted. Seeking the Bodhi path of the Buddha is like someone wanting to bite their own navel—how could it be accomplished?

If billions of hermits have hearts as straight as a string, behave sincerely in all matters, and enter into samadhi, there will surely be no dealings with demons. The Tathagata seals this person, enabling them to attain the supreme wisdom of a Bodhisattva.

As the Tathagata says, these are precisely the words spoken by the Buddhas. If it were not so, it would be the words spoken by the demon Marasu.

tieu_de: EATING FIVE NEW SPICES: SPRING ONION, GREEN ONION, GARLIC, SHALLOT, AND ONION (INCLUDING SHALLION) ATTRACTS THE DEMON GUAI - ENLIGHTENING MASTER HOÀ
tom_tat: I am 95 years old this year, and the time has come for me to pass away. I have tried very hard, but in fact, the friends who practiced Buddhism with me at the same time have long followed the Buddha. I remain in this world to meet all the
noi_dung:
EATING THE FIVE SPICES SPRING ONION, CHIVES, GARLIC, SCALLION AND ONION (INCLUDING SHALLOTS) ATTRACTS DEMONIC SPIRITS - INSTRUCTION BY HOA THUONG

I am 95 years old this year, and the time has come for my life to end. I have also tried very hard, but in truth, the friends who practiced together with me have long followed the Buddha. I am still in this world to meet all my brothers, which is very rare. I, being old and with weak health, cannot speak much, so I only say the essential things to remind all my brothers.

In practice, the highest Fruit of the Saints mainly relies on the Principle of Nature (Emptiness). But we are all beginners; in the Six Realms of Samsara, even if fortunate enough to have a human body, we are still entangled in the cycle of birth and death—in plain terms, we are ordinary mortals. Therefore, one must know one's capacity and position in the present to walk steadily. Why is that? Because days, months, years, and age wait for no one. The Sutras say that the lifespans of beings in other realms are measured in kalpas, calculated according to the time spent in that realm, which is countless millions of years. In contrast, the human lifespan in this realm is only a few decades, very short.sniff. One day in the Heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings is equivalent to 50 years in the human realm, and in the Heaven of the Devas of the Power it is equivalent to 100 years in the human realm... Therefore, human life is short and impermanent. Just because we are ordinary beings lost in ignorance, one day seems long, one month or one year is mistakenly thought to be even longer. In truth, time passes very quickly, so we must make the most of this short time and not let it go to waste.

…I sincerely tell my brothers that the body cannot be abandoned. Use the body's practice of chanting sutras and reciting Buddha's name to counter the body's tendencies of the three poisons: greed, anger, and ignorance, as well as afflictions, aging, illness, and death. Time cannot be ignored; it only urges one toward death. For example, I am 95 years old this year, and next year I will be 96; I cannot return to being 94. This body is surrounded by seeds of illness from inside out, always waiting for an opportunity to arise. Ahead of us is the board of aging, sickness, and death, and we can only crawl into it. Everyone must reach that place, only sooner or later. The body is like that, and its end is like that. AllThe person must clearly understand, and should not be misled. I also have three things to guide everyone, both monastics and laypeople. Because those who believe will practice accordingly:

1. Vegetarianism must be practical. Because if one eats the flesh of sentient beings every day, what evil deed would one not dare to do, and what good deed could arise? It is because animals are killed, cooked, and roasted that humans have meat to eat. Moreover, Buddhism regards Compassion as fundamental, but if one eats the flesh of sentient beings, where is Compassion left? The benefits of vegetarianism are:

• Not being entangled in the cause and effect of the karma of killing. The karma of killing living beings in the world is very heavy, because it is only when sentient beings are captured and killed that we have meat to eat.

• Eating vegetarian out of compassion, unable to eat the flesh of animals. When compassion arises, one wishes for all beings to be happy, therefore performing good deeds. In this way, the mind of loving-kindness is generated. For example, if one loves a younger sibling or a niece/nephew, one does not want them to suffer; not wanting them to suffer means not committing unwholesome acts. Thus, the mind of compassion arises and leads to performing good deeds.

Compassionate heart comes from practicing vegetarianism. When I was a child, my neighborhood friends would set up rubber bands to shoot birds, and I did the same. Friends bought fishing rods to catch fish, and I also bought a rod to go fishing. Since I started eating vegetarian, I have felt great affection for chickens, birds, and other animals. If one eats meat, love cannot arise. For example, if we have a child and eat its meat every day while claiming to love it, that would not be possible.

Affection that arises influenced by "Compassion" promotes healing, while that influenced by "Mercy" prevents causing harm. Good deeds increase, and bad deeds gradually decrease and are completely eliminated. Thus, by naturally practicing vegetarianism, we accomplish two things that the Buddha once taught: "Abstain from evil deeds, always perform good deeds." Therefore, a compassionate heart is the root for progressing on the path to Sagehood.

2. In the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, the Buddha spoke of three progressive items. First, one should not eat the five pungent spices (scallions, chives, garlic, shallots, onions). The nature of these five pungent spices increases desire and anger; their influence is to attract hungry ghosts, while the deities and benevolent spirits avoid them. They tend to aid in generating karma linked to afflictive emotions.

Therefore, the Buddha said that eating the five pungent vegetables will affect those beings. Nowadays, many temples are filled with the smell and taste of the five pungent vegetables. Even in surrounding temples, garlic and onions (shallots) are hung all over the kitchen. It is very difficult for the monks who want to avoid this, because every day they attend ceremonies where people cook food using onions and garlic; if they don’t use them, they have to go hungry. Therefore, I do not attend these offerings. Up until now, I have never eaten these five pungent vegetables. Sometimes when I visit Hue Nghiem Temple (Binh Chanh), I have to instruct them not to put the five pungent vegetables in the food. When I come to temples and the vegetarian food contains this smell or taste, I only eat a little rice and some sweets, then leave.

3. From that foundation, one practices mindfulness in cultivation: mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, mindfulness of the Sangha. Mindfulness of the Buddha is the recitation of the name Namo Amitabha Buddha. Mindfulness of the Dharma is observing and maintaining the Buddhist scriptures. Mindfulness of the Sangha is the recitation of the names of Bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteshvara, Mahasthamaprapta, Kṣitigarbha…Among these, mindfulness of the Buddha is primary. Practicing this every day gradually increases right mindfulness, thereby growing wholesome roots, and both merit and blessings increase from this.

In daily life, there are things that can increase or decrease one's merit that we often do not pay attention to. In the Ten Great Vows of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, the fifth vow is "rejoice in others' merits," which is very easy to practice, making the merits of others your own. This is a gentle and relaxed method of cultivation. Regarding the good deeds of others, if we feel displeased and even try to obstruct or criticize them, it diminishes our merit. On the other hand, rejoicing in them (delighting with them) increases our merit. For example, if someone builds a large house and visitors enter and praise it for being spacious and cool, the owner will be happy. Another person might think the house is too big and cleaning it would be tiring.Additionally. The owner felt a bit sad upon hearing this. For example, when building the main hall of Van Duc Pagoda, some people praised the Bodhi tree for being tall and beautiful. But others said that looking up at the Bodhi tree was too high and really made their necks tired. Just this small matter, one side gains merit, the other side loses merit. Brothers should take note to apply this in daily life: things that increase merit should be done. Things that decrease merit should be avoided. Accumulating a little each day will turn merit from small to large, from little to much.

Time passes quickly, and the brothers take vegetarianism as a foundation, always considering the practice of Buddha recitation and sutra chanting as transcendent merit. From these points, they strive to maintain, then cultivate other good deeds. May all brothers wholeheartedly be diligent and steadfast in the Buddha's teachings. One must engrave the two words: "Steadfast" in mind.

Reciting the BUDDHA is the CAUSE

Becoming a BUDDHA is the EFFECT

Please often recite Amitabha Buddha

Source: Huỳnh Huy Cường

tieu_de: SECRET TO HELP BRING WEALTH TO THE OTHER WORLD
tom_tat: In your opinion, is there any way for people to bring their current possessions, such as houses, money in bank accounts, gold, precious metals, USD, etc., to the other world?
noi_dung:
SECRETS TO BRINGING WEALTH TO THE OTHER WORLD

In your opinion, is there any way for a person to bring their current possessions, such as a house, money in a bank account, gold, precious metals, USD, ... to the other world?

Meaning to take them along after death.

Many think it is not possible; even if you put them in the coffin, they would just remain in the ground and cannot be taken along.

But in my view, it is possible to take them along.

I see many people who, while alive, have quite a lot of wealth, even extremely rich.

Yet near death, when they pass it on to their children or relatives, some are ungrateful or do not know how to value the wealth, they gradually squander it until it is depleted.

This is very regrettable.

Meanwhile, the person who had that wealth, after dying, becomes a hungry ghost, hungry and suffering.

This is because that person did not know how to convert it to take the wealth along.

Here I will guide how to take possessions along:

That is, you should convert those tangible assets into intangible merits.

Because intangible merit will follow you like your own shadow and cannot be separated.

Even if you undergo death, or even are reborn in other realms, the intangible merit will still follow you as usual.

For example, if you have a beautiful, expensive motorbike that you do not use.

Now if you want to take it with you to the other world, I will convert it, but it will not be the exact same car, you can only take the value of the merit from the car that I convert for you.

You should sell that car, or if you do not want to sell it, you can donate it to a temple to be used for Buddhist activities.

If you sell it, you can take that money and start doing charitable deeds immediately.

For example, give 20 portions of rice to people who are hungry, donate to 10 temples each with 10kg of rice, and if there is any remaining, give money for meals to patients in need,.....etc....

When your possessions are given correctly, to the right place, and to the person who really needs them, those possessions will generate merit or gratitude,.....

This merit or gratitude will follow you without ever leaving, even when you receive it in another realm; from a car, it could transform into a fully equipped house, good health, or a very fulfilling and happy life.......

Therefore, in daily life, do not wait until you are close to death lying in a hospital bed to think about converting them.

But calculate and convert gradually and steadily while you are still healthy and still doing well in business.

Do not be greedy, thinking you can just accumulate everything when you see a lot of profit. Saving is necessary, reinvestment is also important, but for the excess net profit, you should divide it and start converting it through acts of charity, like the car example I mentioned above.

Remember this.

Otherwise, later when your life ends, you will regret it.

Because from being a rich person, you may die as a hungry ghost, with nothing to eat.

Namo Amitabha Buddha.

Source: Hang Dinh

tieu_de: REVIVING YANG CAUSE AND EFFECT
tom_tat: (continued) The judge read the next verdict:
noi_dung:
REAWAKENING YANG CAUSES AND EFFECTS

(continued) The judge read the judgment: - The Hong family in Thien Hung district, the father held the position of Dianlai in Vo Xuong district. When Hong was young, he clashed with his father, and he shaved his head in a temple. Later, he violated the law and was expelled, returning to grow his hair, eating meat like a layperson. He deceives everyone he meets, without any honesty. Behind people's backs, he often speaks ill of them! He likes to pry into others' private affairs and those of promiscuous women, instigating quarrels. His tongue fabricates many things, committing unlawful deeds.

King Tần Quảng shouted:

- This man’s crimes are severe and hard to forgive.

The judge reported:

- This man is not very evil, only his words are harmful.

- There are three aspects of speech crimes, and this person has violated them all. Lying about obscene matters is considered a crime of lust. Lying and embellishing to make people quarrel and attack each other is a crime of anger and madness. Lying to deceive people and take their possessions is a crime of deceit and greed. One act of lying that causes lust, anger, madness, greed, or sexual misconduct. How can the judge still say that a speech crime is a minor offense? Cutting the mouth and lips, splitting teeth, pulling the tongue wide like a plowed field, and committing a speech crime—though the person is still alive and has already received punishment for self-destruction, the crime is not yet over; now, being punished by being sent to Hell, they cannot reincarnate.

The judge reads the verdict:

- The wife, surnamed Uông, is Miss Trình Thị from Giang Hà district. In her previous life, she practiced vegetarianism, refrained from killing, did good deeds, often donated, and was filial to her mother-in-law, caring for her sickly with utmost dedication. Because she had not accumulated enough virtue to be reborn in heaven, she is allowed in this life to enjoy wealth and prosperity, being born into a wealthy official family, meeting a virtuous husband, giving birth to three sons and two daughters, destined to live 82 years, and will pass away without illness.

Unexpectedly, because her parents spoiled her too much and she was a privileged child, she developed a spoiled habit from a young age. Having servants at home made her accustomed to being the master, often scolding and mistreating subordinates. Years of ingrained habits made her very cruel. When she had a gentle husband, she abused her wealth and power to dominate and overly oppress him. Moreover, accustomed to a life of comfort, she killed many living beings. She lent money at excessive interest, was harsh to tenant farmers, forced people to work without pay, and never forgave even in times of crop failure! In this life, she did not give a single coin to poor relatives, let alone to strangers. Every day, she abused her servants verbally and physically. She would beat them to death.

The girl servant is Vuong Nguyet Mai, and she gouged the eyes of the boy servant Truong Hung Nhi, causing him excruciating pain until death. She also punished another girl servant, Ngo Ha Huong, forcing her to eat a whole bowl of raw soybeans, making her belly swell for three days until she died! Many other servants were also injured, with scars all over their ears, noses, hands, feet, lips, and mouths!

Some people used the concept of karmic retribution to advise Trình Thị, but she, relying on being from a high-ranking official's family, scolded the person teaching karma and said: “I have never given alms to anyone, yet now I am wealthy, living in luxury and comfort, with children and grandchildren all around, my fortune overflowing. Who can believe what you say, that one must practice virtue and accumulate merit to receive blessings and longevity?”

After saying that, he immediately drove that person away. Those words had already been reported by the Kitchen God to Heaven, and each month a notice was sent to the Imperial Bureau, detailing many of Trình Thị's crimes. The wronged souls also filed complaints. The Jade Emperor decreed a reduction of lifespan by three kỉ (36 years) and ordered Trình Thị's soul to be captured for punishment, so he died at the age of only 46.

King Tần Quảng judged:

- Not respecting one's husband is the first sin that heaven's law does not forgive. Let alone being cruel and harsh to servants, causing the unjust deaths of three people. A cruelty greater than a tiger is unnatural for humans, and having committed many other sins, such a person deserves to be imprisoned in Hell, never to be reborn for ten thousand lifetimes.

The judge reported:

- In her previous life, Trinh Thi was very filial to her mother-in-law. In this life, the eldest daughter Trinh Thi, seeing her mother being rude to her father and living wickedly, practices cultivation by reciting sutras and chanting the Buddha's name, doing charitable deeds, to pray for her mother's atonement, as well as practicing on behalf of her mother. Therefore, I ask the prince to allow karma to be repaid, and once the debt is settled, further actions will be taken.

- If her daughter repents like that, then I pardon her from hell, allowing her to be reborn. In the first life, she is reborn as a poor, destitute woman, with the spirit of Hà Hương entering her womb as a ghost fetus (cancer), causing unbearable pain, lasting three years until she goes mad, cuts open her own belly and intestines, and dies, thus paying back the retribution for making Hà Hương die from swollen stomach after eating raw soybeans.

In the second life, she is reborn as a mute, scabby beggar, wandering until 50 years old, stealing rice from the Trương family, and is beaten to death by the Trương daughter (the spirit of Vương Nguyệt Mai reborn), thereby repaying the previous life's debt.

In the third life, being a girl until 18 years old, she was attacked by a ruffian (the soul of Trương Hưng Nhị reincarnated), who stabbed her eyes blind and cut her tendons, and she crawled in the market begging for food until death, then she finally paid for the three lives. In those three lives, enduring crimes such as being mute, having sores, suffering from extreme hunger and cold, and begging, were the penance for oppressing her husband and gaining wealth immorally. If in those three lives she suffers, repents, and lives kindly, it will temper the subsequent lives.

Trình Thị reported that:

- My husband is too foolish and doesn’t know how to take care of the household; how could I not scold him? I beg your highness to judge fairly and show leniency.

- Women follow the Three Obediences: when at home, they obey their father; when married, they obey their husband; when their husband dies, they obey their son. Women do not have autonomy. Your husband is a kind man, yet you criticize him for being foolish, and are insolent and contemptuous in every way. At this point, and you still do not understand your fault?

- I deserve being rude to my husband. As for being beaten and scolded, it is because they could not complete their work, yet were lazy and deceitful in every way, spoiling their character. Moreover, they are stubborn because they do not obey, foolishly obstinate, not understanding anything. The reason they are so offensive is that they invited being beaten; I ask the prince to reconsider.

- In this life, serving as a servant, their temperament is not like that of noble people. Either they are souls reincarnated from animals, or from wicked people, losing intelligence, their nature foolish according to lowly standards. And if they are reincarnated in ignorant, lowly families, their character becomes crude and stubborn, obstinate, blindly ignorant, which is naturally decreed by heaven. As a superior person, one must teach patiently, and in tasks, explain clearly, and remind repeatedly. Even if they make mistakes, punishment should depend on the severity of the fault; one should not angrily scold or hit continuously, beating too much may frighten them to the point of madness.

Why not consider, they are also children from good families, only because of extreme poverty that they were sold to me as servants. Although in name I am master and they are servants, they are like children in the house; their eating, dressing, sickness, and health, I must care for them. Therefore, male servants are like adopted sons, female servants are like adopted daughters. How could one be cruel and harsh to them? Suppose your own children were beaten and insulted by someone, wouldn't your heart ache? Yet you give your servants insufficient food, inadequate clothing, and even have the heart to illegally execute and harm three lives. Truly, you do not fear the law of heaven, yet dare to argue many things. Hurry and lead them to be reborn.

...to be continued...

tieu_de: FOR PEOPLE WHO PRACTICE SPIRITUAL DISCIPLINE, IT IS NECESSARY TO TREAT YOURSELF A BIT HARSHLY. BECAUSE IF WE DO NOT EXPERIENCE SUFFERING, IT IS EASY
tom_tat: Nowadays we see that there are many people reciting the Buddha's name, but there are very few who can truly recite it sincerely; most of them follow their own habits day by day.
noi_dung:
FOR THOSE WHO PRACTICE SPIRITUAL TRAINING, ONE NEEDS TO TREAT ONESELF A LITTLE HARSHLY. BECAUSE IF WE DO NOT EXPERIENCE SUFFERING, IT IS EASY

Nowadays, we can see that many people chant Buddha's name, however, very few can chant sincerely. Most are guided by their own habitual tendencies, daily arising with delusions, as well as actions. We can clearly observe this in their behavior in daily life; they still have greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, and especially, they still do not regard chanting Buddha's name as important. Although they know that chanting Buddha's name is very good, they only consider it secondary, always putting it after all other matters, and they still prioritize fame, literature, profit, nourishment, eating, sleeping, and resting.most important. So in this life, can they achieve success or not? It is very difficult to succeed.

If one wants to have a smooth rebirth in this life, one needs to completely let go. Letting go of what exactly? Letting go of one's own bad and evil habits, and one should not continue to follow them to create karma. What about fame, literature, or material benefits? One must know how to refuse them. From there, sincerely recite the Buddha's name, and then everyone who practices will be reborn. However, our biggest problem is that we are not sincere. Sometimes, when thinking about the frightening cycle of rebirth, we want to stop, but we do not entirely retreat; we really want to escape the six realms of samsara, but we cannot truly let go of anything.whatever it is, in the heart there are still many attachments to the matters of this world.

Therefore, the Buddha always teaches us that we must take suffering as our teacher. Why? If a person always lives a life full of suffering, they will no longer want to cling to this world, and from there they can focus diligently on practicing the Dharma, hoping to soon escape the cycle of birth and death. The ancients have a saying:

_ "Wealth makes it difficult to learn the Dharma".

Why? Because in this place you have pleasure, you have enjoyment, so you will not be able to let go, and your path to liberation will become extraordinarily difficult. If we think carefully, we will see that the Buddha's words are very reasonable. If we really want to let go of greed, anger, and delusion, what must we do ourselves? We must treat ourselves a little harshly.

I studied with the elder layman Lý Bỉnh Nam for 10 years and noticed that every day he only ate one meal, and the food was extremely simple. He cooked by himself, and his pot and bowls were just a small pan with a handle. Since he was from Shandong province, he loved eating noodles, and he rarely ate other foods, only having a few vegetables in each meal. When others looked at his food, they would say that eating like that is impossible, yet he continued to eat like that every day. His clothes were patched many times; who patched them? He patched them himself. If he gave them to someone else to patch, they definitely would not do it and would surely throw them into the trash.Then throw it away and buy new clothes to offer to the teacher. So, has anyone offered new clothes to the teacher? Many have, but the teacher does not wear them; they are all taken to be offered for others to wear. This is exactly taking suffering as the teacher.

In the Vinaya Pitaka, the Buddha often said:

_ "Monks often carry three kinds of ailments".

What are these ailments? The Buddha is not telling us to pretend to be sick, but these three ailments are:

1. Eating not to fullness.

2. Wearing not warmth.

3. Sleeping not much.

This is self-mortification in order that every moment does not forget the thought of renunciation. Because if we do not taste suffering, we will forget the idea of wanting to escape this world, and as a result, our practice career will become sluggish and lax. In the end, we will still have to be born according to karma, continuing to drift in the cycle of six realms of samsara.

Amitabha Buddha!

The dharma words of Dharma Master Jingkong

tieu_de: MANY GENERATIONS WITHOUT ILLNESS
tom_tat: At the time of the Buddha Dipankara's birth, Venerable Bhakkula was a poor man. Seeing a monk suffering from a headache, he sincerely offered a beryllium pear, and the monk thereby
noi_dung:
MANY GENERATIONS WITHOUT ILLNESS

At the time when the Buddha Sakyamuni was born, Venerable Baccula was a poor man. Seeing a monk suffering from a headache, the venerable sincerely offered him a pear, and the monk was healed as a result.

Because of that karmic connection, from then on, throughout 91 lifetimes, the Venerable, whether born in the realm of gods or humans, never suffered from illness.

*********

Laypeople, when they are old or sick, are cared for by their wives, children, and relatives, but monks and nuns, when they fall ill and are bedridden, have no one to care for them; looking around, there is no one close by, making their situation truly extremely miserable. Therefore, in the Scriptures, people are encouraged to offer alms to sick monks and nuns, which will bring the greatest merit.

In this realm of the Dead, there are tens of thousands of types of trees, eight thousand types of grass, seven hundred and forty types of medicinal plants mixed together, forty-three types of plants with various fragrances, and one hundred and twenty-one types of precious plants, all of which can be used for saving people. For those suffering from illness and affliction, nothing can be more precious than medicine to treat them.

Using medicine to save people is practicing the virtue of giving and letting go. Just sharing a remedy with someone is also practicing the virtue of giving and letting go. Treating the poor without calculating costs or benefits is practicing the virtue of giving and letting go. Advising others not to sell fake medicine is also practicing the virtue of giving and letting go. There are many methods to cultivate the virtue of giving and letting go, but the most important is that it must stem from a compassionate heart that cares for others.

Ten thousand years ago, the drinking water had an extremely sweet taste, like the flavor of condensed milk. By the time of King Kỳ-bà, in India there was still a precious tree called the medicinal king, which could be used to see inside the human organs. During the Ming dynasty, the best ginseng, whose roots had clearly developed into human shapes, was still abundant, and the price per kilogram was only equivalent to a kilogram of white silver. Today, the price has increased four or five times, yet the color and taste are not like before. In the future, about 5,000 years from now, the average human lifespan will be reduced to only 20 years, and catastrophes of diseases will arisebirth, the dead lie exposed all over the fields. This calamity lasts for seven months and seven days before it ends. At that time, common necessities like sugar, salt... cannot be found, let alone precious medicines like ginseng, Poria, cinnamon, aconite...

The Ba-sa treatise says: “If someone brings a pear to offer to a sick monk, in the future that person will certainly not encounter calamities or epidemics.”

Sickness and suffering are not inherent at birth; they must have causes to arise. The Great Treatise of Extensive Preservation teaches: "Harboring evil intentions and looking at those who generate the Bodhi mind will result in the consequence of blindness. Using evil words to slander those who generate the Bodhi mind will result in the consequence of being born without a tongue." The Lương Hoàng Repentance says: "Being born mute is due to past life karma of slandering others. Being born short is due to past life karma of despising others. Being born ugly and unfortunate is due to past life karma of obstructing the light of the Dharma. Being born with a body afflicted by boils and pain is due to past life karma of beating others“tormenting other sentient beings.” The Lotus Sutra teaches that: “Those who suffer from edema, headaches, scabies, leprosy... it is because in a past life they slandered this sutra, and therefore must endure such consequences.”

Accordingly, it can be understood that every illness has a cause rooted in the karma of previous lives. Prescribing medicine for treatment is to help people after illness has arisen; advising people not to create evil karma is to help people before illness has even arisen. If we borrow Confucius' teaching for comparison, one aspect is like "judging fairly the disputes of the people," while the other is "advising so that people no longer have disputes." Both actions can be carried out simultaneously, without hindering each other.

Source: cause and effect.

tieu_de: Mantra of Manjushri Bodhisattva.
tom_tat: Manjushri is the embodiment of unobstructed wisdom, of countless Buddhas. Whoever recites this mantra will have immeasurable great merit. Wisdom increases, intelligence .... The mantra of Manjushri
noi_dung:
Mantra of Manjushri.

Manjushri Bodhisattva is the embodiment of unobstructed wisdom, of countless Buddhas. Whoever recites this mantra will have immeasurable, vast merits beyond imagination. Wisdom grows, intelligence ...

The mantra of Manjushri Bodhisattva has the power to help practitioners increase wisdom while penetrating the nature of emptiness.

His seed syllable is Dhi.

He has one head and two hands.

The left hand holds a Prajnaparamita sutra, and the right hand holds a flaming sword of wisdom.

The sharp sword cuts through the veil of ignorance.

The Dalai Lama said that this is very suitable for students to study ....

Sanskrit:

Om A Ra Pa Ca Na Dhih

Om A Ra Pa Cha Na Dih (the 'Dih' sound is prolonged)

Sino-Vietnamese: A ra bạt giả na.

Vajra Throne Sutra's Five-Word Mantra of Supreme Deity says:

If a person recites a single time, for example, reciting the eighty-four thousand and forty-two Vimalakirti Sutras. If they recite twice, Manjushri and Samantabhadra immediately accompany them, along with Dharma Protectors and benevolent spirits in front of that person.

Furthermore, if they recite once, it removes all suffering and calamities of the practitioner.

If recited twice, it eliminates countless karmic offenses accumulated over aeons of life and death. If recited three times, ignorance will temporarily disappear. If recited four times, it ensures continuous protection without fail. If recited five times, it quickly achieves Supreme Bodhi. If a person wholeheartedly stays in a secluded place, writes the five Sanskrit letters to form a spiritual circle, and follows the practice of recitation for a full month, Manjushri Bodhisattva will immediately manifest, appear in space, and expound essential teachings. At that time, the practitioner will obtain the wisdom of previous lives, be skilled in debate without obstacles, possess supernatural abilities freely, have their vows fulfilled, acquire complete merit and wisdom, and swiftly realize the Dharma body of the Tathagata. Only with faith and observance is it certain that after sixteen lifetimes, one will attain Perfect Enlightenment.

tieu_de: Diligently reciting every day, relying on the Power of the Great Compassion Mantra to prevent and deal with the coronavirus epidemic.
tom_tat: SCRIPTURE: Sound:
noi_dung:
Diligently recite daily, relying on the Power of the Great Compassion Mantra to prevent and cope with the coronavirus epidemic.

SCRIPTURE:

Sound:

"Evil dragon, pest demon spreads poisonous air,

Heat disease invades, threatening life,

Wholeheartedly recite the Great Compassion Mantra,

Epidemics are eradicated, prolonging life."

Meaning:

"Evil dragon, pest demon spreads poisonous air,

Feverish illness invades, nearing death,"

Sincerely reciting the Great Compassion Mantra,

Epidemics are eliminated, lifespan is increased.

BRIEF EXPLANATION:

"Evil dragon, demon spreading poison gas." 'Dragon' can refer to dragons in the sky (heavenly dragon), dragons living in the sea, or dragons living on land. Dragons also come in many types—poisonous dragons (poison dragon), fierce dragons (evil dragon), black dragons, white dragons, fire dragons, and there are even golden dragons. In the northeast of China, there is a provincial capital called Heilongjiang, because of its connection to a black dragon. This black dragon often appears on the river, so the river is called 'Heilongjiang' (Black Dragon River).

"'Dịch' means epidemic disease. Epidemic diseases, or cholera [hoắc loạn=hùo lùan], or other infectious diseases, are all caused by the 'epidemic demon' creating havoc. This 'epidemic demon' spreads harmful pathogens to humans everywhere, and anyone who inhales the poisonous air it disperses will immediately fall ill and may die.

'Fever disease approaching death.' The patient suffers from heat and fever, the disease invades the body, life is nearing its end, and death is imminent.

"Sincerely recite the Great Compassion Mantra,/ Epidemics will be eradicated, and lifespan will increase." If you can sincerely and earnestly chant the Great Compassion Mantra, contagious diseases will be eliminated, no longer persisting, and your life span may also be longer.

(Chinese translation: Tang Dynasty, Western India, Monk Gia Pham Dat Ma)

Brief explanation: Ten Thousand Buddhas Sacred City, Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa.)

Note: Practitioners who recite the Great Compassion Mantra and wish to receive its blessings must cultivate deep faith, observe vegetarianism and abstain from killing, maintain a heart of great compassion, feel pity for living beings, and refrain from harming or eating them. Only then will it align with the Great Compassion Mantra, and the recitation of the mouth and the intention of the mind must correspond in order to achieve good results.

How to Request the Great Compassion Water from Avalokiteshvara

After repenting for karmic obstacles, reciting the Great Compassion Mantra (at least 5 times), and requesting the compassion of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva to dedicate merits to all enemies and pretenders attached to the body, from this life and past lives, recite "Namo Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara" 10 times, then continue by reciting the Six-Syllable Great Bright Mantra "Om Mani Padme Hum" (21 times), afterwards recite the following verse praying for water:

Namo Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara

Perfect in wisdom, with a great compassionate heart,

Hearing the cries of those in need, immediately appears to respond,

O merciful one, save us quickly!

There are sentient beings here suffering,

Please grant the pouring of sweet nectar,

Drinking it purifies the inner mind,

Illness and suffering are quickly eradicated.

Homage to Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara

Please dissolve into the water,

Granting the great compassionate nectar to sentient beings,

After drinking it, the Bodhi mind arises.

Relying on the Buddha's power, Avalokiteshvara

Transforms ignorance into wisdom quickly,

Transforms a mind of anger into a calm and patient mind,

A compassionate heart following Avalokiteshvara's practice.

Homage to the Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara,

The great compassion of the nectar has swift effect,

May those who drink it become pure,

And all afflictions and ignorance quickly disappear.

Today I vow to cease evil and cultivate goodness,

I vow to turn away from evil and return my heart to righteousness,

Diligently practice, love, and protect all beings,

Dedicate all merits of virtuous deeds.

With a deeply sincere and wholehearted mind, think in this way; then recite 10 times "Namo Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva" before drinking. While drinking, maintain a mind of repentance and overflowing gratitude. Use your mind to visualize the water emitting white light.

Note: Those who recite the Great Compassion Mantra and want to achieve good results should ideally maintain purity in speech and follow a vegetarian diet, or at least eat vegetarian on the days they recite the Great Compassion Mantra and receive the Great Compassion water of Avalokiteshvara.

Text of the Vow to Repent

With sincere heart I kneel,

To all sentient beings,

I have caused harm,

From beginningless time,

Please accept my repentance. ( 1 prostration )

I sincerely apologize,

Please forgive me,

Because of delusion and madness,

I have committed many sins,

Evil deeds of body, speech, and mind,

Intentionally or unintentionally offending,

Even to the point of killing,

Sowing many wrongful karmic acts,

Causing endless suffering and torment,

You all have tasted bitterness and pain!

I am deeply ashamed,

With my heinous crimes,

I sincerely repent. (1 prostration)

I pray for forgiveness,

Compassion to give me a chance,

To correct my mistakes and be a new person.

From today onward,

I will always be careful,

Constantly maintaining good thoughts,

Guarding every mental impulse,

Being cautious with every intention,

In words and actions,

Abandon evil and practice goodness,

Correct wrongs in the heart and return to righteousness,

Diligently cultivate all good deeds,

Love and protect all sentient beings,

And dedicate all merits,

All the good deeds I have done,

To all of you.

I pray that you,

All leave suffering and attain happiness,

Soon break through ignorance and awaken,

Be saved by the compassion of the Buddha,

Freedom in a place of peace. (1 prostration)

I sincerely repent,

Since beginningless time,

The three kinds of evil karma I have created,

Body, speech, and mind have been negligent,

Now I am fortunate to seek enlightenment,

Clearly understanding cause and effect,

I wholeheartedly ask for repentance,

Vowing to correct my mistakes,

Earnestly praying for the Buddha's blessings,

Causing烦恼 and karmic obstacles,

Gradually diminishing day by day,

Merits and virtues increasingly grow,

Wisdom becomes ever clearer,

Wholeheartedly I focus on reciting,

Namo Maitreya,

May I be born together in the Pure Land,

Attaining unsurpassed Bodhi. (3 prostrations)

tieu_de: EATING VEGETARIAN MAINTAINS A COMPASSIONATE HEART, NOT EATING THE FLESH OF LIVING BEINGS. THEREFORE, EATING VEGETARIAN IS TO CLEANSE, CLEANSE ONE'S NATURE, CLEANSE THE MIND. THIS IS WHAT
tom_tat: Buddhists teach people to preserve life; this applies to all beings, one could say without distinction of species or religion. The most important concern is how to maintain good health.
noi_dung:
EATING VEGETARIAN PRESERVES A COMPASSIONATE HEART, DOES NOT CONSUME THE FLESH OF LIVING BEINGS. THEREFORE, EATING VEGETARIAN IS HYGIENIC, PROTECTS CHARACTER, AND PRESERVES THE MIND. THIS IS THE TRUTH

Buddhists teach people to nurture life; this applies to all living beings without distinction of species or religion. The most important concern is how to maintain health, longevity, happiness, and joy—that is nurturing life. If one wants to have a healthy body and live long, the most important thing is to have a compassionate heart. This is a point that many people often neglect. A pure heart and compassion will prevent illness. All suffering and illnesses arise from where? If we observe carefully, we will know that this isBorn from pollution. This principle is not difficult to understand. These past few days I heard people say, in newspapers and magazines there are reports that European beef has again caused problems, making it inedible; even in wine, there is mixed cow's blood, dyeing the wine red. Everyone in their minds is frightened; it is very clear that pollution is the root of disease. A pure mind, without pollution, will not generate illness. Compassion can transform all harmful things; not only can it detoxify oneself, but a compassionate mind can also resolve all misunderstandings and hostilities between people.Different religions, different races of the world. Therefore, all unwholesome things, a compassionate mind can transform.

My aspiration, I have pondered for many years, is to hope to establish a multicultural school. What does multicultural education teach? It is to teach a good heart, a compassionate mind, and the benefit to all living beings. The Department of Multicultural Studies, the Faculty of Multicultural Studies, and the teaching program content focus on these three points. These three points in Buddhist teachings are what is called the Bodhisattva. In a compassionate mind, the most important thing is not to kill. In "Purity of Karma in Three Paths," the first principle is "filial devotion to parents, serving the monastic elders, a kind heart that does not kill, and practicing the ten good deeds."karma”. “Loving all living beings”, “beings” refers to all sentient beings, with respect to all sentient beings, one is not allowed to have the intention to kill; not only must one not kill, but one is also not allowed to harm them. This is true compassion, and it is the foundation of all moral precepts, the basis of ethical conduct.

Bodhisattvas teach us the cultivation of life, especially emphasizing the mind of compassion. Ordinary people who cultivate life only know about physiology, that eating and drinking must be hygienic; "hygiene" means protection, protecting physiology, hoping for healthy physiology, but they have not discovered the true factor of healthy physiology. Therefore, even when choosing the healthiest foods, they still get sick, they still age, and die. Why is that? For health and longevity, maintaining healthy physiology is not the primary cause, it is the secondary cause; this treats the effect, not the root cause. From this, it can be seen,People who focus on hygiene are treating the symptoms, not the root. What is the root? The root is the mind! In Buddhist scriptures, it often says: 'The physical body depends on the karma, while the mind is the principal karma.' Our body is the dependent body, the mind is the principal body. When the mind is healthy, our physical health is largely healthy; if you pay a little attention to diet and drinking, then life is extremely healthy. If the mind is not healthy, no matter how well you maintain your physical health, it is of no use. We have seen this typical case too many times.

In ancient times, kings and great civil and military officials, regarding physical protection, would seek some experts, those extraordinary people who came to take care of them, yet they still died prematurely as usual. Please check: how many kings throughout history lived to 70 years old? Not many; the majority lived only 40 to 50 years. Reaching fifty to sixty years old was already considered a long life. Those who reached 70 and above were truly rare; the ancients called it an exceptionally rare age. What was the reason? They neglected psychological hygiene, only knowing about physical hygiene, but they did not know aboutpsychological hygiene. Therefore, a compassionate mind is more important than anything. We nurture the body, but we must also know how to nurture our temperament.

Eating and drinking in a Buddhist context, why choose vegetarian food? Long ago, Gautama Buddha encouraged us to eat vegetarian, but He Himself did not practice vegetarianism, that was due to the living environment not allowing it. The Buddha was extremely compassionate, and a compassionate person does not want to cause trouble for others. Every day, the Buddha went out on alms rounds; during the alms round, whatever people offered to eat was accepted, so it was convenient. If the Buddha wanted to promote vegetarianism, then each household would have to prepare a bit of vegetarian food to accommodate the alms seeker, which would be troublesome.

How complicated it is. He does not want to add trouble for people, this is according to conditions. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are okay with depending on conditions, because their minds are compassionate, they have no discrimination, no attachment, their minds are pure and not defiled. We are ordinary people, our minds are not pure, our minds will be defiled, so we cannot avoid having to make choices.

Chinese Buddhism applied vegetarianism starting from Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty. Emperor Wu read the Lankavatara Sutra, in which the Buddha encouraged Bodhisattvas not to eat the flesh of sentient beings. After reading it, he was deeply moved. He himself adopted vegetarianism and encouraged monastics to also adopt vegetarianism. This is how the movement for vegetarianism was implemented. There is no vegetarianism in Buddhism worldwide; vegetarianism exists only in China.

Buddhism of renunciation exists throughout the world, but burning oneself at the peak only occurs in China. What does burning oneself at the peak mean? In Buddhist scriptures it says: "Illuminate yourself, illuminate others," which means we make vows to dedicate ourselves for others. Understanding this meaning is sufficient; it does not mean you should actually burn your own body. Once your body is burned, what can you use to help others? The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas serve sentient beings; they serve because the people exist. If you do not have a healthy body, what can you use to serve?Incident? The Buddha said that burning the body, burning a finger, burning an arm, all are acts of self-sacrifice for others. If you misunderstand the meaning, truly burning your body, losing a finger, burning an arm, you become crippled and cannot do anything. Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara does not have enough with just two hands, needing a thousand hands and a thousand eyes. We have two hands and still want to burn them; then what will it become? The meaning is misunderstood! The great master teacher teaches us to burn sparingly on the crown of the head, so that you remember every second, every minute, I have once made a vow to sacrifice myself for others. However, there are many people at the topHe has burned many doses. I have seen a monk, on his head alone, burned about three or four dozen marks, burning so many. This is self-glorification, arrogance! He burns a lot, others burn less, 'I burn more than you,' arrogant and conceited, completely misunderstanding the meaning of burning the doses! Therefore, whether a person burns or does not burn on their body has nothing to do with it; one must remember well in the heart the Buddha's teachings, truly developing an unconditional mind, selflessly serving all beings.

Vegetarianism is extremely important. Eating vegetarian is nurturing life, nurturing the mind, and nurturing one’s nature. Nature, using the current term, means spirit, that is, in eating vegetarian, there are also things that are not good for temperament, and the Buddha would filter them out. Everyone knows, the Buddha talked about vegetables called 'ngũ huân'; 'huân' has the grass radical at the top. Huân is not meat, so many people say eating huân is eating meat, which is wrong! Huân is not meat; huân is vegetables. Meat, the Buddha calls 'huân tanh.' Huân refers to five kinds of vegetables, everyone knows, that is garlic, pickled onions (we call it kiêu đầu), chives, shallots, hưng cự (we call it onionThese (foods) affect physiology. People who do not have skill or discipline, if they eat them, it will cause bad effects, so Buddhists avoid them. These five types are called habits. In the Lankavatara Sutra, the Buddha clearly said that eating can easily provoke anger, agitation, and restlessness. That is why the Buddha advised beginners that if you want to protect a good state of mind, you should pay attention, because eating and drinking will affect your mental state. Vegetarian eating preserves compassion, as it does not involve eating the flesh of sentient beings, so eating vegetarian is about hygiene, moral purity, and mental well-being. This is the best choice, the best way to nurture life, it nurtures life.Nurturing temperament, nurturing the mind. This is great learning. From this place arises the mind of love, the protection of all beings, joy, unconditional care for all beings, and helping all beings. The Bodhi mind is born from here.

(Excerpt: Thái Thượng Cảm Ứng Thiên, volume 18)
