tieu_de: What is dedicating merit
tom_tat: & HOW TO DEDICATE MERIT LIKE THAT? Slơone Slơone :
noi_dung:
WHAT IS DEDICATION (OF MERIT)

& HOW TO DEDICATE MERIT?

Slơone Slơone :

- Brother, how do we dedicate merit?

Quang Tử :

- Dear friend, dedication is a very important matter when we do a good deed or some merit; in fact, dedication is even more important than the good deed or merit itself.

According to the law of cause and effect, when we do a good deed, there will be corresponding blessings in the future, such as giving alms leading to wealth, healing others leading to health, releasing animals leading to longevity…

However, that is only the basic part of cause and effect; at a higher level, we can completely direct the blessings in the direction we want through dedication (of merit).

It means that instead of normally giving alms to become wealthy, if one does not want the merit of wealth, one can use dedication to transfer it to other merits such as recovery from illness, escaping danger, attaining rebirth in the Pure Land, or achieving wisdom, etc.

Not only can one direct merit for oneself to enjoy, but one can also dedicate it for others to enjoy, like an invisible gift, yet extremely effective.

And karma will redirect so that the merit will manifest exactly as we have dedicated it; it can happen quickly, it can take time, but it will certainly be accomplished.

SO HOW DO YOU DEDICATE MERIT?

Dedicating merit is actually very simple. Whenever you do any virtuous or good deed, either before, during, or after doing it, if you intend in your mind for the merit of that good deed to be directed toward certain future outcomes, that is precisely dedicating merit.

To be clearer, you can read silently, or aloud, the dedication of merit phrase, which always has the following structure:

"I dedicate the merit of …(1) to wish for ...(2) to receive ...(3)"

Where,

“I dedicate the merit of ....(1)” where (1) is the virtuous deed you are doing, have done, or are preparing to do, such as releasing animals, printing scriptures, giving alms, chanting Buddha's name, reciting sutras, etc. For example: “I dedicate the merit of reciting the Kṣitigarbha Sutra today...”, or “I dedicate the merit of releasing this eel...”, and so on.

As for the part “praying for…(2)”, it refers to the recipient of the blessings, which can be yourself or someone else.

And finally, “to be … (3)” is the result that I desire, for example, “to be cured of illness,” “to eliminate karma,” “to become intelligent, wise,” “to be reborn in the Pure Land,” and even, one can pray to “become a Bodhisattva, a Buddha to save sentient beings.”

The recipient of the dedication can be anyone; if praying for oneself, one would say “praying for myself,” or for someone else, for certain sentient beings, one recipient, multiple recipients, or even all sentient beings, it is up to oneself to choose.

For example, 'pray for mother and child named…' or 'pray for these sick people…', or 'pray for all sentient beings throughout the dharma realm', etc…

We can dedicate merit to ourselves, to our relatives, or to others, to other sentient beings, as many as we wish. However, the more we dedicate to others, the more the merit is divided, but it still can be received, and having it is always better than not receiving any at all.

As for dedicating merit to ask for something, that is the most important issue, which needs to be studied carefully.

According to the highest ideals of Buddhism, virtuous merits should be dedicated (transferred) so that all sentient beings can attain Buddhahood, or at the very least, wish for all sentient beings to be reborn in the Pure Land, escaping the cycle of samsara.

As in the Avatamsaka Sutra, Bodhisattva Samantabhadra teaches the tenth practice - the dedication part as follows: “...all the merits that exist, dedicate them all to all sentient beings throughout the Dharma realm of space. May all sentient beings always be at peace, ...(excerpted) so that sentient beings can all attain liberation, and ultimately achieve the supreme Bodhi.”

Surely, this is the most perfect, greatest dedication, and the future blessings will be supreme, the most magnificent.

If at present we do not have any urgent problems, then this dedication is the standard that we need to apply whenever we perform any good deed.

Whether it is as grand as printing sutras, making statues, reciting sutras, chanting Buddha's name, or reciting mantras... or as small as offering a few grains of rice to an ant, if we dedicate the merit with the above dedication verse, the blessings will continue from this life to the next, making us gradually wiser, more virtuous, creating more connections with sentient beings to gradually guide them to practice, slowly advancing in cultivation until we ourselves attain Supreme Buddhahood, and then teaching countless sentient beings who will also attain Supreme Buddhahood.

However, we also need to know that the greater the desire, the more time it takes to achieve it.

Praying for all sentient beings to attain Buddhahood is so immensely great that it requires going through countless—immeasurable—innumerable—endless lifetimes like the grains of sand in the Ganges River before it can be fully accomplished, just as the dedication verse says.

In real life, there are often urgent matters that demand our attention and need to be addressed first. For example, we might be sick, or a loved one might be sick, or we might be unemployed and need to find a suitable job, or we might want to be less impatient, less resentful, etc. And we also need to dedicate merit to certain people to resolve those immediate issues, because simply put... we cannot just leave those problems unresolved; we still have to live, and we are forced to solve the problems that life continuously presents to us.

On the other hand, if we do any virtuous deeds, we only hope to achieve worldly goals, such as health, wealth, beauty, passing exams, getting a raise, a promotion, etc. So, even if everything goes exactly as we wish, we still remain trapped in the cycle of birth, aging, sickness, and death, full of endless suffering.

So, how should we dedicate the merit in a way that fulfills both, both addressing immediate problems and helping us progress in spiritual liberation?

Actually, there is nothing difficult at all. When we dedicate the merits to someone, we still pray and dedicate that they can resolve their immediate problems, such as praying for recovery from illness, for finding a job, for intelligence, wisdom, etc. Then conclude with the sentence: "May they soon attain the Supreme Buddha Fruition and widely save sentient beings."

Suppose that we are sick, we immediately go to release animals or do some meritorious deed depending on the circumstances, then dedicate the merit as follows: “I dedicate this merit, praying that I may eliminate karmic obstacles, recover from illness quickly, and swiftly attain the Supreme Buddha Fruit, extensively saving all beings.”

Or, for example, if we have a child and wish for them to study well and be obedient, we do some meritorious deed depending on the circumstances, such as releasing animals, chanting sutras, reciting Buddha’s name… and then dedicate the merit as follows:

"I dedicate the merit of this deed… praying that my child named… will be intelligent, study well, be obedient, and soon attain the Supreme Buddha Fruit, widely saving sentient beings."

For example, if I have a husband who is abusive, addicted to gambling, and indulges in excessive drinking… I perform some virtuous deed, then dedicate the merit as follows:

"I dedicate the merit of this deed… praying that my husband will soon change his heart and character, give up abusive behavior, gambling, and excessive drinking, grow in virtue, and soon attain the Supreme Buddha Fruit, widely saving sentient beings."

Thus, for the time being, if we solve the problems of life, and still ensure that our Bodhi Mind and that of others grows, we will certainly gradually advance in practice until we achieve the fruit of Bodhi.

As in the dedication verse above, we only dedicate the merit to one person, but all sentient beings benefit. Why? Because when that person becomes a Buddha, or even before becoming a Buddha, when they are still a Bodhisattva, they are always saving, teaching, and benefiting countless sentient beings.

When we dedicate merit and pray for others to achieve success in such a way, even if we do not pray for anything for ourselves, we will still attain success as in that dedication. For, no matter how we dedicate merit, the person who directly performs the good deed and creates the virtue always receives the majority of the blessings, and when we wish something for others, we ourselves will also receive that.

Above is a brief outline of the method of dedicating merits; it is only a brief overview because the cause and effect of dedication are very complex, requiring the supernal wisdom of a Great Bodhisattva and the Buddhas to fully comprehend. I hope that this somewhat shallow sharing, with many shortcomings, will help you in some way on the path of practice.

tieu_de: SAMANTABHADRA'S TEN GREAT VIRTUES, THE MEANING OF SAMANTABHADRA'S TEN GREAT VIRTUES AND THE MERITS OBTAINED WHEN RECITING AND UPHOLDING THE TEN GREAT VIRTUES OF SAMANTABHADRA
tom_tat: The ten great vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, you should make these vows, and by observing them daily you will obtain immeasurable merit and eliminate countless sins. In the Avatamsaka Sutra, Samantabhadra said: "...If there is anyone
noi_dung:
PHO HIEN TEN PRACTICES, THE MEANING OF PHO HIEN TEN PRACTICES, THE MERITS GAINED WHEN RECITING AND UPHOLDING PHO HIEN TEN

The ten vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, you should make vows to practice and uphold daily to obtain immeasurable merit and eliminate countless sins. In the Avatamsaka Sutra, Samantabhadra spoke: "...If there is any good man or good woman who uses the seven most marvelous treasures, and the supreme pleasures of the heavens and humans in all worlds as numerous as the dust particles in innumerable Buddhalands across the ten directions, to give charity to sentient beings in just as many worlds, to make offerings to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in just as many worlds, over lifetimes as numerous as the dust particles in just as many..."In that Buddha realm, if one continuously gives alms and makes offerings like that, without interruption, how much merit would one accumulate; if compared to the merit of a person who merely hears once the ten great vows, the merit of the previous virtuous man or woman is not equal to one percent, one thousandth of the merit of the latter, not even equal to a part of the Upanisad. Furthermore, if someone with deep faith upholds and recites the ten great vows, even just copying a four-line verse, they can immediately eliminate the five uninterrupted karmas; all suffering and afflictions, whether physical or mental, in the world, as well as all accumulated evil karma.like the countless dust particles in the Buddha's realm, all are dispelled; all kinds of demon armies, yakshas, rakshasas, or demon spirits that are fierce and specialize in eating flesh and drinking blood, such as kumbhanda, piśāca, vetāla, and so on, must all be avoided, or if approached, one should generate the intention to protect.... The merit of you all is truly immeasurable and boundless, only the Buddhas can fully comprehend.

(Excerpt from the Great Vehicle Avatamsaka Sutra, Chapter on the Aspirations of Samantabhadra)

At that time, Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, after praising the supreme merits of the Tathagata,[1] then spoke to the Bodhisattvas and Sudhana[2], saying: "O good men! The merit of the Tathagata, even if all the Buddhas in the ten directions, across countless eons[3], in innumerable Buddha lands, were to continually expound on those merits without ceasing, it still could not be fully spoken. If one wishes to accomplish those merits, one must cultivate the ten great vows. What are these ten great vows?

One is to pay respect to all Buddhas;

Two is to praise the Tathāgata;

Three is to make widespread offerings;

Four is to repent karmic obstacles;

Five is to rejoice in the merits of others;

Six is to invite the Buddha to preach the Dharma;

Seven is to invite the Buddha to reside in the world;

Eight is to diligently practice and study according to the Buddha;

Nine is to always be harmonious with sentient beings;

Ten is dedicated to all beings.

Thien Tai asked: Great Sage! What is the meaning from the practice of 'paying homage' to the practice of 'dedicating merit'?

Bodhisattva Samantabhadra told Thien Tai:

O virtuous man! The aspiration of 'Respectfully paying homage to all Buddhas' means this: For the World-Honored Buddhas as numerous as dust particles in all the Buddha realms throughout the ten directions and three times, throughout the entire space of the Dharma realm, by relying on the power of Samantabhadra's vows, I deeply believe and understand, and see all Buddhas as if they are present before my eyes; I will purify completely my body, speech, and mind, and constantly offer respectful homage. In the abode of each Buddha, countless Buddha realms manifest that cannot be fully expressed, and within them, countless manifestations of myself appear; to each of these manifestations, I respectfully pay homage to all Buddhas, as numerous as dust particles in all the inconceivable Buddha realms. Whenever the realmMy practice of reverent homage will only end when emptiness is exhausted. But because the realm of emptiness never ends, my reverent homage also never ends. Likewise, my practice of reverent homage will only end when the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted; but the realm of sentient beings, their karma, and their afflictions never end, so my practice of reverent homage also never ends. Each thought follows another without interruption, and the three karmas of body, speech, and mind are never weary or tired.

Moreover, O good man! The vow 'To Praise the Tathagata' has this meaning: In every particle in all countries throughout the ten directions and three times, to the ultimate of the dharma realm in emptiness, there are countless Buddhas as numerous as particles in all worlds. In the dwelling of each Buddha, countless Bodhisattvas gather around. I will take all the profound understandings I currently possess and, before each one, I will use a tongue more subtle than that of the celestial maiden Bian Cai[5]. Each tongue will emit an endless ocean of sounds, and each sound will generate all oceans of words, to praise and exalt all the oceans of merits of the Tathagata, covering the entire ultimate dharma realm, successivelyforever until the end of future lives, never interrupted. Just like that, until the realm of emptiness ends, the realm of sentient beings ends, the karma of sentient beings ends, the afflictions of sentient beings end, then my practice of praise will cease. But because the realm of emptiness, the realm of sentient beings, the karma of sentient beings, and the afflictions of sentient beings never end, my practice of praise will also never cease. Each thought follows the next without interruption, the three deeds of body, speech, and mind are never tiresome or weary.

Again, O good man! The aspiration "To offer extensively" means this: In all the Buddha realms throughout the ten directions and three times, and throughout the entire space of the Dharma realm, no matter how countless the tiniest particles are, within each of those tiny particles there are Buddhas as numerous as the particles in all the worlds. In the dwelling place of each Buddha, countless Bodhisattvas gather around. I, relying on the power of Samantabhadra's vow, generate deep faith and understanding, seeing the Buddhas as if they are present before me, offering all superb and excellent precious items to the Buddhas. Such offerings include flower clouds, garlands of clouds, heavenly music clouds, heavenly parasol clouds, and heavenly robes clouds.Serving the heavenly realm, the clouds above here are all as large as Mount Sumeru; there are also many kinds of heavenly fragrances such as sandalwood incense, burnt incense, powdered incense; and many kinds of lamps are lit, such as butter lamps, oil lamps, fragrant oil lamps, each lamp wick is as large as Mount Sumeru, the oil in each lamp is as abundant as water in the great ocean; I often bring offerings like the above to make offerings. O good man! Among all offerings, 'offering the Dharma' is the highest; such as: speaking about the practice of cultivation is an offering, benefiting sentient beings is an offering, protecting sentient beings is an offering, enduring suffering on behalf of sentient beings is an offering, diligently cultivating wholesome roots is an offering, not abandoning one’s pursuitsA bodhisattva is offering (dana); not departing from the Bodhi mind is offering. O good man! If one compares the immeasurable merits of the offerings mentioned above with just a single thought of merit in offering the Dharma, it is not even a hundredth, not even a thousandth, a hundred-thousandth, a ten-thousandth, a fraction, a portion, a part, not even equal to a single upanisa-dha. Why is that? Because the Tathagatas hold the true Dharma in great respect. If one practices according to the teachings, one will give rise to Buddhas. If bodhisattvas practice the ways of offering the Dharma, they will accomplish the merit of offering to the Tathagata. Practicing in this way is trulyTrue offering, and that is also the most vast and excellent offering of all. Only when the realm of space ends, the realm of sentient beings ends, the karma of sentient beings ends, and the afflictions of sentient beings end, will my practice of offering come to an end; but the realm of space, the realm of sentient beings, the karma of sentient beings, and the afflictions of sentient beings never end, therefore my practice of offering will never end. Moment after moment continues without interruption, the three deeds of body, speech, and mind never grow weary or fatigued.

Again, noble son! The vow of “Repenting of karmic offenses” has this meaning: The Bodhisattva thinks to himself: Since beginningless past lives, due to greed, anger, and delusion, my body, speech, and mind have created countless, innumerable evil karmas. If these evil karmas had forms, even the entire space could not contain them. Today, before all Buddhas and the assemblies of Bodhisattvas in countless worlds throughout the Dharma realm, I sincerely repent of my three karmas with a pure mind, vow not to commit them again in the future, and always abide in the merit of the pure precepts. By repenting in this way, when the space ends, when the beings end, karmaWhen all sentient beings' sufferings are gone, and all sentient beings' afflictions are gone, then my practice of repentance will end; but the realm of emptiness, the realm of sentient beings, the karma of sentient beings, and the afflictions of sentient beings never end, therefore my practice of repentance also never ends. Moment after moment, uninterrupted, the three karmas of body, speech, and mind are never weary or bored.

Once again, noble man! The aspiration “Rejoice in the merits of others” has this meaning: The Buddhas Tathagata, as numerous as dust particles in all the Buddha realms throughout the ten directions and three times, throughout the entire space and dharma realm, from the moment they first generated the aspiration, in order to accomplish omniscient wisdom, diligently practiced merit without sparing their bodies and lives; over lifetimes as countless as dust particles in the many Buddha realms, in each lifetime they gave away their heads, eyes, hands, and feet as numerous as dust particles in these Buddha realms. In this way, they endured extreme hardships to perform all difficult deeds, perfected all methods of liberation, and attained the lands of wisdom.of the Bodhisattva[14], attaining the supreme enlightenment, until entering nirvana and distributing relics. I rejoice in all those virtuous deeds of the Buddhas. Not only that, for all sentient beings among the four classes[15], six realms[16] throughout the ten directions of the world, if they have merit, even as small as a speck of dust, I also rejoice. All the learners and non-learners[17] among the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, whatever merits they have, I rejoice. All the Bodhisattvas who practice diligently with great effort, who have carried out countless difficult deeds, resolutely seeking supreme Bodhi, accumulating great merit, I also rejoice. I rejoice in this way; even if the space were to end, theAll beings end, the karma of beings ends, the afflictions of beings end, but my joy in rejoicing still does not cease; each thought follows the next without interruption, the three karma of body, speech, and mind are not wearied or tired.

Again, O good man! The vow of 'Requesting the Buddha to expound the Dharma' means this: Among the dust particles in all the Buddha realms throughout the ten directions and three times, in the ultimate space of the Dharma realm, each dust particle contains countless vast Buddha realms that cannot be entirely spoken of. In each of those Buddha realms, in every single thought, there are Buddhas who have attained Perfect Enlightenment as numerous as the dust particles in the unspeakable Buddha realms, surrounded by bodhisattvas as numerous as the ocean; before these countless Buddhas, I earnestly use my three karmas of body, speech, and mind, employing all means, to respectfully request the Buddhas to expound the wondrous Dharma. By making such a request, evenThe realm of emptiness ends, the realm of sentient beings ends, the karma of sentient beings ends, the afflictions of sentient beings end, but my practice of requesting all Buddhas to expound the Dharma never ceases; each thought follows the next without interruption, and the three karma of body, speech, and mind are never bored or tired.[19]

Again, O good man! The vow 'To request the Buddha to always remain in the world' means this: No matter how many Buddhas Tathagata there are—countless as the particles of dust in all the Buddha realms of the ten directions in the three times, throughout the space of Dharma realms—whenever they are about to appear or enter Nirvana, I sincerely request them not to enter Nirvana, and to remain in the world through as many lifetimes as the dust particles in all the Buddha realms, for the benefit of sentient beings. I make this request continuously, even if the space were to run out, even if sentient beings were to run out, even if the karma of sentient beings were to run out, even if the afflictions of sentient beings were to run out.but my frequent practice of inviting the Buddha to dwell in the world never ends; each thought follows the next without interruption, and the three karmas of body, speech, and mind are never weary or boring.[20]

Again, noble man! The aspiration of "Diligently practicing learning according to the Buddha" means this: Just as the Buddha Śākyamuni[21], in this world of Tāvatiṃsa, from the moment he first generated the mind, diligently never retreating, repeatedly used countless lives to practice charity; he once peeled skin to make paper, split bones to make brushes, pricked blood to make ink, in order to compile the scriptures, piled high like Mount Sumeru. Out of respect for the true Dharma, even his own life was not spared, let alone the throne, and other dependent things such as palaces, gardens, or towns, villages! Moreover, he endured hardships to do difficult things, until he attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree, manifesting manymiraculous powers, many transformations, many Buddhas, in many assemblies such as in the assembly hall of all the great Bodhisattvas, or in the assembly hall comprising the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, or in the assembly hall of Wheel-Turning Kings, lesser kings, and their retinues, or in the assembly hall comprising Śākyas, Brahmins, wealthy householders, and laypersons, up to the assembly hall comprising the eight classes of beings, both human and non-human, and so on. In many such assemblies, the Buddha used a perfect voice like thunder, and according to what the beings delighted in regarding the Dharma, He made them all attain maturity, until He manifested entering nirvanaNirvana. In all such monasteries, I ask to follow the Buddha in practice. Before the World-Honored One Tī Luó Jiā Nà today, and before all the Buddhas as numerous as the specks of dust in all the Buddha realms throughout the ten directions and three times, reaching the ultimate empty Dharma realm, it is the same: in every thought, I ask to follow the Buddhas in practice; even if the realms of emptiness end, the sentient beings end, the karma of sentient beings ends, the afflictions of sentient beings end, my practice of diligence in following the Buddha will never cease, thought after thought without interruption, the three actions of body, speech, and mind without weariness or fatigue.

Again, good man! The vow of 'Always benefiting all beings' means this: In all realms throughout the ten directions, throughout the ultimate space of the Dharma realm, there are beings of various kinds born in different ways such as egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and transformation-born; or there are beings who live relying on countries of wind and fire, or there are beings who live relying on space and plants; numerous species, numerous forms, numerous appearances, numerous features, numerous lifespans, numerous clans, numerous names, numerous mentalities, numerous views, numerous desires, numerous thoughts, numerous manners.many kinds of clothing, many kinds of food and drink; residing in many villages, towns, and palaces, for up to eightfold beings, both human and non-human; either without legs, or with two legs, four legs, many legs; having form or formless, having thought or without thought, neither thought nor unthought; toward all these various beings I adapt flexibly to serve and nourish them, as one respects parents, as one honors a teacher, even up to the Arahants or the Buddhas, with no difference. For the sick I will be a physician, for those who have gone astray I will show the right path, in the darkness Iit will be light, I will help the poor to obtain treasure. Bodhisattvas benefit sentient beings in an equal manner like that. Why? Because if a Bodhisattva accords with sentient beings, it is as if according with offering to the Buddhas; if they respect and serve sentient beings, it is as if respecting and serving the Buddhas; if they make sentient beings joyful, it is making the Buddhas joyful. Why? Because the Buddhas take the mind of great compassion as their essence; due to the existence of sentient beings, they give rise to the mind of great compassion; due to the mind of great compassion, the bodhi mind arises; due to the bodhi mind, one attains equal enlightenment. For example, in the midst of a vast desert, there is a great tree; if the roots absorb water, then the branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits will flourish.Yes. The Bodhi tree in the vast sea of birth and death is the same. All sentient beings are the roots of the tree; the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are the flowers and fruits of the tree. By using the water of great compassion to benefit sentient beings, one will achieve the flowers and fruits of the wisdom of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Why? Because Bodhisattvas use the water of great compassion to benefit sentient beings, they will achieve the supreme Bodhi fruit. Therefore, Bodhi belongs to sentient beings. Without sentient beings, all Bodhisattvas cannot achieve the supreme Bodhi fruit. O good man! Regarding the meaning of the practice of "Always Harmonizing with Sentient Beings," you should understand it like this: Bringing an equal mind towards sentient beings will achieve the mind of great compassion perfectly.Complete; bringing the mind of great compassion to follow sentient beings, one will accomplish the merit of offering to the Buddhas. In this way, the Bodhisattva follows sentient beings, even if the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, yet my practice of following sentient beings never ceases, moment after moment continues without interruption, and the three actions of body, speech, and mind never grow tired or weary.

Again, dear good man! The vow of 'Dedication to all beings' means this: From the first vow, which is 'paying homage to the Buddhas,' to the ninth vow, which is 'being in accordance with sentient beings,' all the merits obtained are dedicated to all beings throughout the entire expanse of the dharma realm. May all beings always be happy and free from suffering and illness; may they fail in doing evil deeds and swiftly succeed in doing good; may all doors leading to wrongdoing be closed, and the path leading to heaven, humans, and nirvana be opened. If beings, due to abundant negative karma, must experience resultsI take upon myself all their heavy suffering, allowing them to be liberated, until the very end achieving the unsurpassed Bodhi. In this way, the Bodhisattva practices the virtue of dedication; even if the space of emptiness ends, even if all realms of sentient beings end, even if the karma of sentient beings ends, even if the afflictions of sentient beings end, my practice of dedication never ceases, moment after moment uninterrupted, and the three actions of body, speech, and mind are never weary or tired.

O good man! These are the ten great vows, complete and perfect, of the great Bodhisattvas. If the Bodhisattvas skillfully cultivate according to these ten vows, they can benefit all sentient beings and also accord with the supreme Bodhi path, perfectly fulfilling the vast vows like the ocean of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Therefore, this good man! You should clearly understand the meaning of practicing those ten vows as follows: If any good man or good woman uses the seven most wondrous treasures, and the most excellent pleasures of the heavens and humans in all worlds, as numerous as the dust particles in countless, limitless Buddha realms across the ten directions, to give alms to beings in that many worlds, to make offerings to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in that many worlds, continuously over lifetimes, without interruption, how much merit would they accumulate; if compared to the merit of a singleIf a person only hears once about these ten great vows, the merit of a virtuous man or woman previously is not equal to one percent, one thousandth of the merit of the latter, not to mention even a fraction of an upa-nisa-da. Furthermore, if someone sincerely believes and observes, chants, or recites these ten great vows, even merely copying a four-line verse, they can immediately eliminate the five uninterrupted karmas; all suffering and illnesses related to body and mind in the world, as well as all evil deeds as numerous as the specks of dust in a Buddha's realm, are eradicated; all kinds of demons, yakshas, rakshasas, or other kinds of evil spiritsferocious, specializing in eating meat and drinking blood like cưu-bàn-trà[30], tì-xá-xà[31], bộ-đa[32], and so on, all must be avoided, or if close, one should cultivate a mind of protection.

Therefore, whoever recites these ten vows, if practiced in the world, will not encounter obstacles, like the moon emerging from a foggy cloud, and will be praised by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. All heavenly beings and humans should honor them, and all sentient beings should make offerings. That virtuous person will attain a human body endowed with the full merits of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and soon will be like Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, quickly accomplishing a wondrous physical form, complete with the thirty-two marks of a great man. If that person is born in the Human or Heavenly realms, they will belong to the most noble lineage, capable of destroying all evil deeds, avoiding all evil companions, and subduing all...non-Buddhist, liberating all afflictions, like the lion king driving away all beasts. That person will receive all offerings from sentient beings. Furthermore, at the moment of death, in the final instant, all faculties will decay, all relatives will depart, all power will vanish, all great ministers, officials, palaces, inner and outer cities, vehicles, elephants, horses, treasures, and so on cannot be taken along; only these ten great vows will not depart, always leading the way, and in that instant the person will be reborn in the Pure Land. Upon arrival, they will see Amitabha Buddha, Bodhisattva Manjushri, BodhisattvaSamantabhadra, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the Bodhisattva Maitreya, and so on. These Bodhisattvas are adorned with noble appearances, possess complete merits, and stand surrounding [him]. That person sees himself born in a lotus, receiving the Buddha's prediction[36]. After receiving the Buddha's prediction, over hundreds of thousands of myriads of nayuta kalpas, throughout countless worlds in the ten directions, he uses his wisdom and follows the minds of sentient beings to benefit all, and before long, he will sit in the bodhi assembly, subdue the forces of Mara, attain the state of Perfect Enlightenment, turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma, and cause the beings in worlds as numerous as dust particles in that Buddha field to all generate the bodhi mind, according to their individual capacities.perfectly cultivated in teaching; for countless future lifetimes, that Buddha will also broadly benefit all sentient beings in this way.

O good man! Those beings who either hear or firmly believe in these ten great vows and uphold, recite, and widely explain them for everyone to hear, their merits, apart from the Blessed Buddha, cannot be fully known by anyone else.

Therefore, when you hear these ten great vows, you should not harbor doubt, but sincerely accept them. Once accepted, you should read them; once read, you should memorize them; once memorized, you should practice them regularly, including writing them down and teaching them. Those who do so will, in a single thought, accomplish all the vows, gain immeasurable and boundless merits, be able to save sentient beings from the great sea of suffering full of afflictions, and all attain birth in the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha.

At that time, the great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra wanted to expound again the meaning of these ten great vows, so he observed all ten directions and then spoke this verse:

Before all the Buddhas of the three times,

In the worlds throughout the ten directions,

I bring my body, speech, and mind pure,

Respectfully paying homage everywhere without omission;

Through the power and virtue of Samantabhadra's practice,

I manifest before all the Tathagatas;

One body appears as countless bodies,

Each body pays respect to countless Buddhas.

Countless Buddhas in a single dust particle,

All reside amid assemblies of Bodhisattvas;

Throughout the Dharma realm it is the same,

The faith in all Buddhas is complete,

I use all the seas of sound,

To speak beautiful words offered everywhere,

Praising the profound merits of the Buddhas,

Forever into the infinite future.

I use the most solemn offerings:

Such as exquisite garlands,

Music, canopies, and lamps,

Fine clothes, the finest fragrances,

Perfumed oils, powdered incense, and incense sticks,

All items precious,

Stacked high like Mount Sumeru,

All are offered to the Buddhas.

Due to my vast understanding,

I deeply believe in the Buddhas of the three times,

And thanks to the power of Samantabhadra's vows,

I make offerings to all Buddhas everywhere.

For a long time I have created many evil deeds,

All arising from body, speech, and mind,

Due to greed, anger, and ignorance since beginningless time,

Today I sincerely repent for them all.

All the merits of sentient beings,

Those who are learned and those who are unlearned belong to the two vehicles[37],

And all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,

Whatever they do, I sincerely rejoice accordingly.

The Dharma Masters throughout the ten directions,

From the moment they first attained Supreme Enlightenment,

I sincerely and respectfully entreat,

Please turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma.

Whenever the Buddhas intend to appear in Nirvana,

I sincerely and respectfully entreat,

May you remain in the world for countless kalpas,

Transforming and saving all sentient beings.

Merit and virtuous seeds arise from praise,

Respectful homage, offerings, and rejoicing,

Confession, requesting to stay in the world, and preaching the Dharma,

Dedicate the merit to all sentient beings along with the Buddha path.

I follow the Buddhas in seeking to learn,

Perfectly practicing the Vows of Samantabhadra,

Making offerings to the Buddhas of the past ages,

The Buddhas of the present are everywhere in the ten directions,

Together with all the Buddhas of the future ages,

All their supreme vows are fulfilled.

I vow to follow the Buddhas of the three times,

Quickly attaining the fruit of Perfect Enlightenment.

All the worlds in the ten directions,

Vast, pure, and adorned,

The Buddhas sit under the Bodhi tree,

Surrounded by assemblies of disciples in full.

May all beings throughout the ten directions,

Be freed from suffering and always be happy,

Gain much benefit from the true dharma,

Completely eradicate afflictions and have no remaining traces.

When I practice the bodhi path,

I know my past lives in all realms,

I often take monastic vows and uphold pure precepts,

Without impurity, without fault, without falling through[38].

All beings have as many languages:

Heaven, dragons, yakshas, kumbhandas,

Even humans and non-humans,

Depending on the language I use the Dharma.

Diligently practicing the ultimate purity,

Preserving without losing the bodhi mind,

Eradicating all defilements, sins, and obstacles,

Accomplishing all virtuous conduct.

Even in the world, attaining liberation

From afflictions, karma obstacles, and demonic states,

Like the lotus flower that does not cling to water,

The sky and the moon do not stand in emptiness.

Eliminating suffering in the path of evil,

Bringing joy and equality to all beings,

Thus, throughout countless lifetimes,

The benefits in all ten directions are endless.

I often follow and accommodate all beings,

Extending to the countless lifetimes of the future,

Practicing the great conduct of Samantabhadra,

The complete fulfillment of Supreme Bodhi.

May all fellow practitioners,

Everywhere gather together,

With body, speech, and mind karma all in harmony,

All practices and vows cultivated together.

The virtuous teachers who have helped me,

Taught me the practice of Samantabhadra,

May they frequently gather with me,

Always holding joy in their hearts toward me.

I wish to always have the honor of seeing the Buddhas,

Together with all disciples surrounding the Buddha,

I offer all things with devotion,

Until the far future without growing weary.

May I preserve the miraculous Dharma,

And glorify all enlightened virtues,

Practicing throughout countless future lifetimes,

Finally attaining the pure practice of Samantabhadra.

I dwell in all realms,

Virtue and wisdom continuously cultivate without ceasing,

Meditation, insight, skillful means, and liberation,

Accumulate boundless treasure of merit.

One speck of dust contains countless realms,

In each realm there are countless Buddhas,

Each Buddha among assemblies of beings,

Constantly expounds the practice of bodhi.

The realms spread throughout the ten directions,

On each hair’s tip exists three lifetimes.

Buddhas and their countries are countless,

Across countless kalpas I have practiced.

The words of all Buddhas are pure,

One word contains all sounds,

According to the language of sentient beings,

They all hear and understand the Buddha's Dharma sounds.

All Buddhas in the three times,

Use a limitless sea of words,

Always turning the wheel of the wondrous Dharma,

Through wisdom, I understand everything clearly.

I enter deeply into all future lives,

Countless lifetimes gathered into a single thought,

How many lives are there in the three times,

Within one thought I enter all of them.

All Buddhas of the three times,

I see clearly within a single thought,

I also frequently enter the Buddha realms,

Like illusion, liberation, and power.

Countless hairs in all ten directions,

At the tip of each tiny hair,

The waters of Buddhas of all three times appear,

I devote myself to diligent and pure practice.

How many Buddhas will arise in the future,

Attaining enlightenment, teaching the Dharma, saving sentient beings,

Their Buddha work complete, entering Nirvana,

I always stay close and diligently study.

The power of supernatural abilities spreads swiftly everywhere,

The power of the Mahayana pervades all dharma practices,

The power of merit pervades all learning, conduct,

The power of great compassion and sacred awe protects everywhere,

The power of virtuous karma manifests purity everywhere,

The power of wisdom no longer clings to anything,

The power of concentration, wisdom, skillful means, and sacred awe,

The power to accumulate causes similar to bodhi,

The power to purify wholesome deeds,

The power to destroy all afflictions,

The power to subdue all obstructive demons,

The power to fulfill all the practices of Samantabhadra.

To purify all the lands,

To liberate all sentient beings,

To thoroughly understand the profound meaning of the Dharma,

To reach the depths of the ocean of wisdom,

To practice all virtuous deeds purely,

To fulfill all aspirations completely,

To be close and make offerings to all Buddhas,

Countless lifetimes of cultivation without weariness.

All Buddhas of the three periods,

Each practiced the supreme vows,

I offer and cultivate them perfectly

Following Samantabhadra's practice to Enlightenment.

All Buddhas have a foremost disciple,

The name he is called is Samantabhadra,

Now I dedicate the merits of my good roots,

May my wisdom and conduct be no different from his.

May my body, speech, and mind always be pure,

The practices and realms as well, in the same way,

Such wisdom is called Samantabhadra,

I vow to be like him without difference.

I practice the pure conduct of Samantabhadra,

Together with the great vows of Manjushri,

That work will be completely fulfilled, without omission,

For all future lifetimes, tirelessly.

I practice the method of limitless teachings,

Having amassed immeasurable merit,

Abiding in limitless deeds,

Understanding all supernatural powers.

The wisdom of Manjushri is mighty,

The wisdom and virtuous conduct of Samantabhadra are the same,

Now I dedicate all wholesome roots,

Vowing to always practice and learn from them.

All Buddhas of the three times praise,

This is the great vow beyond all else,

Today I dedicate all the merit,

May I attain the supreme virtue of Samantabhadra.

I vow that at the moment of death,

All obstacles will be completely removed,

In front of my eyes I will see Amitabha Buddha,

And be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss immediately.

Once I have been reborn in that realm,

I will fulfill this great vow,

Completely and perfectly, without lacking anything,

To benefit all beings.

The assembly of Ultimate Bliss is all pure,

I was born from a precious lotus,

Immediately seeing the Buddha Infinite Light,

He conferred upon me the fruit of Bodhi.

Hoping, through the Buddha's grace in conferring,

I manifest countless incarnations,

Wisdom vast throughout the ten directions,

Benefiting beings throughout all realms.

The realm of emptiness and the realm of sentient beings,

Karma and afflictions can end,

But those four things are not exhausted,

My vows and aspirations are also limitless.

Some people bring precious jewels to adorn,

Offering them to the Buddha in all ten directions,

The most wondrous gifts given to gods and humans,

And so it continues through countless lifetimes;

Some people hear this king of vows,

Once heard, generating true faith,

The heart yearns to attain the Bodhi fruit,

Gaining merit surpassing that of previous beings.

That person abandons evil companions,

Escapes from all evil paths,

Quickly sees the Buddha Amitāyus,

Fully accomplishing Samantabhadra’s supreme vows.

That person is granted a long life,

Born among humans with freedom and ease,

In a short time, it will be accomplished

Vows and aspirations as vast as Samantabhadra.

Since beginningless time, due to lack of wisdom,

One has committed the five heavy Uninterrupted sins,

By upholding and reciting this great Samantabhadra vow,

Even a single thought of karmic sin is eliminated;

Offspring of the same lineage with similar appearance,

Form, intelligence, all are fulfilled,

Evil beings and heretics cannot destroy,

Receiving offerings in the three realms;

Then going to sit under the Bodhi tree,

Subduing all kinds of demons,

Attaining the state of Supreme Enlightenment, speaking the wondrous Dharma,

Bringing benefit to all sentient beings everywhere.

If one recites, upholds, and expounds

These ten great vows of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,

The resulting merit is known only to the Buddha,

And will undoubtedly accomplish the Bodhi path.

If one recites this Samantabhadra vow,

I say: Even a small portion of merit,

In a single thought filled with virtue,

Can fulfill the vow of purifying all beings.

The supreme practice of my Samantabhadra,

All boundless merits are dedicated,

To all beings who are still immersed,

May they soon be reborn in the Pure Land.

When the Bodhisattva Great Samantabhadra, before the Buddha, finished reciting this verse on the vast and pure practice and vow of Samantabhadra, the youth Sudhana was exceedingly joyful; all the Bodhisattvas were also delighted. The Buddha praised, 'Excellent! Excellent!'

At that time, when the World-Honored One along with the great bodhisattvas expounded the supreme Dharma of the unsurpassable liberation realm, the Bodhisattva Manjushri, being the foremost among the great bodhisattvas and having guided six thousand monks, the Bodhisattva Maitreya, being the foremost among the great bodhisattvas of the Bhadrakalpa, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, being the foremost among the great bodhisattvas destined to attain Buddhahood in one lifetime, dwelling in the state of Perception Sovereignty, and all the great bodhisattvas, as numerous as the particles of dust in all countries of all worlds in the ten directions, gathered together; the venerables Sariputra, Maudgalyayana, and so on were also the foremost among the assembly.Monks, the lords among the heavenly beings and humans, along with the heavens, Dragons, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Asuras, Kinnaras, Mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so on, all the great assembly, after hearing the Buddha's teaching, were very rejoiced, all believed in it, and vowed to practice it.

Note:

[1] At the end of volume 39 (of the Avatamsaka Sutra), Bodhisattva Samantabhadra praised the extraordinary merits of the Buddha with a verse consisting of 380 lines.

[2] Thien Tai: that is Thien Tai the youth, a Bodhisattva seeking the path mentioned in the chapter "Entering the Dharma Realm" of the Avatamsaka Sutra. On his path of seeking the way, he once traveled south, passing through many countries, learning from 53 (or 55) virtuous teachers including monks, nuns, male laypersons, female laypersons, young boys, celestial girls, kings, queens, Brahmins, wealthy merchants, doctors, tree spirits, earth spirits, etc., learning many Dharma methods. Finally, upon reaching the practice site of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, he attained the realization of the birthless Dharma realm. Mahayana Buddhism often uses Thien Tai the youth (similar to the Dragon Girl in the Lotus Sutra) as a typical example to demonstrateI propose the theory of 'instant enlightenment to Buddhahood'.

[3] Vi trần: are very tiny dust particles. In space, there are countless such dust particles, impossible to count; therefore, mentioning vi trần also means referring to an extremely large quantity, even more than the "sand of the Ganges River".

[4] The four words "the vows and practices of Samantabhadra" were not spoken by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra to exalt himself, but in fact, at that time, "the vows and practices of Samantabhadra" had already become the name of a method of practice.

[5] Goddess of Rhetoric: she is a goddess in charge of arts in Hinduism and ancient Brahmanism; also called Divine Sound Goddess, or Beautiful Sound Goddess. In the Rigveda, she is the name of a river goddess, capable of cleansing impurities and helping humans be courageous, wealthy, and have many descendants. In the Parashara Samhita, she is the wife of Prajapati, once a goddess of language and knowledge, inventor of Sanskrit letters, overseeing poetry and music, protecting art and science; eventually she became the goddess of wisdom and eloquence. This goddess is also mentioned in Buddhist scriptures.

[6] Offering to the Dharma: is the practice of all means aimed at propagating, promoting, and preserving the Buddha's teachings.

[7] Acceptance and nurturing: receiving people (students, disciples) in order to teach and educate them.

[8] Câu-chi: a unit of measurement in India, equivalent to 1 yue (10,000,000) in China.

[9] Na-do-tha: also called na-do-đa, a unit of measurement in India, equivalent to 1 million (some theories say 10 billion) in China.

[10] A kala fraction: that is, a fraction of the smallest amount, a portion of the extremely tiny.

[11] Upanisasada: is an extremely small part. According to the book Trí Uyển Âm Nghĩa, “upanisasada” is translated as a subtle fraction. Suppose a hair is divided into hundreds or thousands of parts, then take one of those parts and divide it into hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands; continue dividing in this way until it is almost nothing and can no longer be divided, that final part is called upanisasada.

[12] The term "developing the mind" here means to cultivate practice until attaining the fruit of Supreme Enlightenment; in other words, it means to make the mind aspire to become a Buddha.

[13] All-encompassing wisdom: that is the wisdom of a Buddha, clearly understanding the true nature of all dharmas, all sentient beings, all worlds, and all matters in the ten directions throughout the three times.

[14] The Bodhisattva's wisdom stage: refers to the aspect of wisdom of the Bodhisattva, while the other aspect is compassion; wisdom refers to benefiting oneself, compassion refers to benefiting others, and when both self-benefit and benefiting others are perfected, one becomes a Buddha. Furthermore, when mentioning the "Bodhisattva's wisdom stage," it refers to Bodhisattvas from the First Stage upwards to the level of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

[15] Four kinds: Buddhist scriptures often use the term “four kinds” (tứ sinh) to refer to four modes by which living beings are born into the world: 1) Born from the womb (胎 sinh) in the mother's belly, such as humans, and animals like cows, horses, deer, etc. 2) Born from eggs (noãn sinh), such as birds, snakes, turtles, etc. 3) Born from moisture (thấp sinh), such as insects and bugs, etc. 4) Born through transformation (hóa sinh), such as butterflies, silkworms, etc.

[16] Six realms: are the six planes of existence of living beings (the six paths or six beasts) in the cycle of birth and death, including: the realm of Devas (Heaven), the realm of Humans, the realm of Asuras, the realm of Pretas (Hungry Ghosts), the realm of Animals, and the realm of Hell.

[17] Practitioners who are still studying, such as Sotapanna, Sakadagami, Bodhisattvas, etc., are called "disciples with learning" (meaning they still need to study); those who have attained the holy fruits, such as Arhats, Buddhas, are called "disciplines without learning" (meaning they no longer need to study).

[18] Perfect Enlightenment: means true enlightenment, realizing the ultimate truth with nothing more, that is, the Buddha's true wisdom, which is also the Buddha fruition. There are many terms to refer to the Buddha fruition, such as Right Enlightenment, Perfect and Equal Enlightenment, Perfect Enlightenment, Right Equal Perfect Enlightenment, Supremely Perfect Equal Enlightenment, Ultimate Enlightenment. Among these terms, the word "equal" refers to the truth that the Buddha has realized; the word "ultimate" refers to the complete eradication of ignorance and afflictions.

[19] Regarding the vow of "Requesting the Buddha to preach the Dharma" (requesting the turning of the Dharma wheel), in the practical life of our current lay Buddhists, it is the act of inviting esteemed Dharma teachers (monks, nuns, and laypeople who both deeply understand the teachings, possess intelligent eloquence, and have a zeal for propagating the Dharma) to preach and teach the Dharma. When the Dharma is taught regularly, the practice of cultivation will yield good results, and the Buddha's teachings will endure in the world for a long time.

[20] Regarding the vow "Request the Buddha to remain in the world" (inviting the Buddha to stay in the world), in the practical life of us Buddhists today, this refers to inviting venerable and virtuous individuals to reside permanently at our local practice centers (temples, Buddha chanting halls, etc.) to consistently teach and guide us in our practice. This venerable and virtuous individual could be a monk, a nun, or even a layperson, with radiant virtue, worthy of being a refuge for everyone.

[21] Vairocana: means light illuminating everywhere without obstruction; in the scriptures, it is often used to refer to the Dharmakaya of the Buddha. The Fa Xiang School calls Vairocana the self-nature body (i.e., Dharmakaya) of the Buddha; Lu Shana is the reward body (i.e., Sambhogakaya) of the Buddha; and Shakyamuni is the transformation body of the Buddha; the three together are called the Three Honored Ones. The Tiantai School also establishes the Three Honored Ones, calling Vairocana the Buddha's Dharmakaya, Lu Shana the Buddha's reward body, and Shakyamuni the Buddha's emanation body. In Esoteric Buddhism, Vairocana is Mahavairocana, the principal Buddha, the teacher of Esoteric Buddhism. Thus, the Buddha Vairocana is also the Buddha.Shakyamuni, the spiritual leader of this Tu-bha realm.

[22] The Eight Legions (bát bộ chúng): is a general term for the deities who are devoted to protecting the Buddha's teachings; also called the "eight divisions of devas and dragons" (thiên long bát bộ), or simply referred to as the "eight divisions" (bát bộ), consisting of: Devas, Dragons, Yakshas, Gandharvas (music deities), Asuras, Kinnaras (golden-winged birds), Mahoragas (serpent spirits), and Garudas (serpent-eating deities).

[23] Not human: In Sino-Vietnamese Buddhist studies, this is called “phi nhân,” a term used to generally refer to beings that are not human, such as Devas, Dragons, Gandharvas, Pretas, Yakshas, Asuras, Hell beings, etc. In some contexts, this term is specifically used to refer to beings in four realms: Devas, Asuras, Pretas, and Hell beings.

[24] Always compliant: meaning always accommodating; here it refers to complying with the mind and intention of others in order to find an appropriate method for spiritual guidance, rather than blindly following people's vices, which would only lead them further into degradation.

[25] Lifespan: is the length or shortness of life.

[26] The Five Anantarika Karmas: that is, the five heaviest sins that cause one to fall into the Avici Hell. These are: killing one's father, killing one's mother, killing an Arahant, violating the harmony of the monastic community, and drawing the blood of the Buddha's body. The term "anantarika" means uninterrupted, without gap, unceasing. The Avici Hell is a type of hell that has five layers of uninterrupted torment: 1) Going through countless lifetimes of suffering, day and night without a single moment of interruption; 2) In this hell, there is an iron bed of fire, each side tens of thousands of miles wide, and those undergoing torment lying on it perceive their own bodies as huge, stretching across the entire bed, along with tens of thousands of others.The suffering forms also lie on that same bed, also feeling their bodies large, spreading across that bed, yet between this person and that person they do not feel obstructed by each other, meaning that even ten thousand people are like just one person; 3) All kinds of punishments, all kinds of implements (like mountains of knives, swords, boiling water, cauldrons of oil, etc.) continuously fall upon the sinners without ever stopping; 4) Whether gods, humans, ghosts, old or young, male or female, rich or poor, noble or humble, as long as they commit sins worthy of hell, they must enter hell to receive the suffering results; therefore, the number of sentient beings in hell is never interrupted, because sentient beings create limitless karma; 5) Sentient beings who have entered that type of hellThis prison is extremely difficult to escape from for countless eons; and during those countless eons, every day and night one must go through ten thousand births and ten thousand deaths, continuing this cycle of life and death, never pausing.

[27] Mara: Mara is also called a demon, meaning one who kills, harms, obstructs, and seizes life; it is a term used to refer generally to evil beings that specialize in hindering good deeds and destroying the Dharma. These are types of malevolent spirits, evil ghosts, cruel and treacherous individuals, full of greed, hatred, ignorance, representing evil forces, afflictions, attachments, doubts, etc., which often harm sentient beings. In general, Mara encompasses all forces of ignorance, constantly seeking ways to obstruct practitioners and interrupt the path to enlightenment and liberation.

[28] Dāśā: is a type of evil spirit, extremely ferocious, specializes in eating humans, has a light body, can fly in the air.

[29] Rākṣasa: is also a type of evil spirit, similar to Dāśā.

[30] Kumbhīra: is a type of evil spirit that specializes in drinking human blood.

[31] Piśāca: is a type of evil spirit that specializes in sucking human vitality.

[32] Buddha-born: is a type of evil spirit that appears through spontaneous generation, without parents.

[33] 32 marks of a great man: means the 32 good characteristics of the Buddha.

[34] The faculties: here refers to the six faculties, that is the entire body and mind of a person, including: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

[35] Here it means that even kings and rulers are no different.

[36] Prophecy of fruition: that is the Buddha confirming that a person in a future life will attain Buddhahood.

[37] The two vehicles: here refers to the Śrāvakayāna and Pratyekabuddhayāna.

[38] Not falling into: that is, not falling into the cycle of birth and death (saṃsāra).

[39] Like an illusion, liberation, and power are the three characteristics of the Buddha realm. The Buddha realm is a manifested realm, full of miraculous transformations, so it is said to be "like an illusion"; the Buddha realm is completely free from afflictions and errors, so it is said to be "liberated"; the Buddha realm is truly majestic and full of merits, so it is said to be "powerful".

[40] Eldest son: that is, the disciple whose practice is most complete and whose spiritual attainment is the highest among the Buddha's disciples.

[41] Practice and karma: that is, the career of spiritual practice.

[42] Buddha of Infinite Light: namely, the Buddha Amitabha.

[43] A Lifetime to Become a Buddha (nhất sinh bổ xứ): The term "nhất sinh bổ xứ", abbreviated as "bổ xứ", originally means the final cycle of reincarnation; that is, this one life is still within the cycle of birth and death, and in the next life, one will become a Buddha in the world, permanently liberated from the cycle of reincarnation. This is the highest attainment of the Bodhisattvas, called "Bodhisattva of Equal Enlightenment" or "Bodhisattva Bổ-xứ". Bodhisattva Maitreya is regarded as the typical example of this attainment. In the present life, Bodhisattva Maitreya resides in the Tusita Heaven, and by the end of this life, in the next life, He will be born among humans to become a Buddha, continuing the Dharma of Shakyamuni Buddha.

[44] The position of Quán-đảnh (Quán-đảnh position): also known as the Enlightenment level, the highest position of Bodhisattvas before becoming Buddha.

noi_dung:
Cultivating blessings and practicing generosity but not yet free from greed, anger, and delusion, your karma will be in the animal realm.

Ordinary people rejoice in practicing generosity, but if they still commit the ten evil deeds, will they receive blessings? They do receive blessings, but their blessings are enjoyed in the three evil realms because they have not yet eradicated greed, anger, and ignorance. They may fall into the animal realm. The animal realm also has blessings. Nowadays, we see many people keeping pets; you can see how blessed they are. A family keeping a pet, it is the darling of that family, and there is no one who does not like it, no one who does not care for it. That blessing comes from practicing generosity in a past life. If this pet is very intelligentIt is because in past lives it practiced the giving of the Dharma; or if it is healthy and long-lived, it is because it practiced fearless giving. Therefore, carefully observing how people take care of pets, you can know which animals in past lives practiced the three kinds of giving. Because they have not yet abandoned greed, hatred, and delusion, they must experience this result.

If the merit is great, they will transform into a Rakshasa, into an Asura. An Asura is a leader in the animal realm, a demon king in the hungry ghost realm, receiving such merit. This kind of merit, after being fully enjoyed, then causes karmic retribution to appear, and that is when true suffering begins. From this, it can be seen that if one does not practice the ten good deeds, all the merit gained is not genuine. Only by practicing the ten good deeds, relying on the ten good deeds, as well as practicing generosity, observing precepts, and the six perfections and myriad virtues, can this merit be genuine; at the very least, it results in enjoying the merit of the heavenly and human realms. But you must understand, the merit of the heavenly and human realms is still not the ultimate goal. Wesee, in the past we could still see people with great blessings, but nowadays we no longer see people with such great blessings.

(Excerpt from The Buddha’s Teaching on the Ten Wholesome Karmic Paths - volume 41)

tom_tat: 'BAO KHIẾP AN DA RA NI' Sutra Bao Khip An Da Ra Ni:
noi_dung:
THE SUPERIOR MERIT OF

‘VAJRADHĀRA DHĀRAṆĪ’

The Vajradhāra Dhāraṇī Sutra:

I HEARD THUS:

Once upon a time, the Buddha was at the Lake of Radiant Jewel, in the Wú Gòu (Infinitesimal) Garden of the land of Virtuous Triumph. At that time, countless hundreds of thousands of great Bodhisattvas, great Śrāvakas, gods, dragons, scent-seeking spirits, flying deities, golden-winged birds, mystical beings, great nāgas, humans, and non-humans were surrounding the World-Honored One.

At that time, among the assembly was a great Brahmin named Vô Cấu Diệu Quang, intelligent and well-learned, a person who always appeared cheerful, and consistently practiced the Ten Wholesome Deeds. He had taken refuge in, and deeply revered, the Triple Gem. He possessed sharp wisdom and always wished that all beings would be fully blessed with benefits and enjoy wealth and prosperity.

Then Brahmin Vô Cấu Diệu Quang rose from his seat, went to the Buddha, circumambulated seven times, and offered incense and flowers to honor the World-Honored One. Next, he presented the Buddha with luxurious, priceless robes, a string of agate beads, and a jeweled necklace draped over the Buddha.

Then, he paid homage with his forehead touching the feet of the Tathagata, then stepped aside and respectfully said:

"I respectfully invite the World-Honored One and the assembly to come to my house tomorrow morning to receive offerings!"

At that moment, the World-Honored One silently consented. When he knew that the Buddha had accepted the invitation, Phạm Chí immediately hurried back. That very evening, he prepared a great deal of food and drink with various flavors, sprinkled water, cleaned the hall, and hung banners and canopies.

By the next morning, Phạm Chí, together with his followers, carried incense, flowers, and musical instruments to the place of the Tathagata, and then said:

"The time has come, we respectfully hope that the World-Honored One will descend."

At that time, the World-Honored One used gentle words to comfort Phạm Chí Vô Cấu Diệu Quang, and then He told the entire assembly:

"In order to allow that Brahmin to receive great benefit, all disciples should go to his house to receive offerings."

At that moment, the World-Honored One immediately stood up from His seat. As soon as He stood, the entire body of the Buddha emitted countless kinds of light. They blended with beautiful colors and shone throughout the ten directions. When all places had become aware of this, the light then gradually withdrew.

With reverent respect, escorting the Tathagata, at that time Phạm Chí held exquisite incense and flowers, together with his family, the heavenly dragons and eight classes of deities, Năng Thiên Đế, Phạm Vương, and the Four Heavenly Kings, going ahead to lead the way.

At that time, the World-Honored One went forward not far, and came to a garden called Phong Tai. In that garden, there was an ancient tower that was decayed and ruined, leaning to one side. Thorns grew thick in front of the yard, weeds covered the doors, stone tiles were buried, and it resembled an earthen fort.

Then the World-Honored One went straight to the tower. At that moment, the tower radiated great light and shone brilliantly.

From within the earthen fort, a voice of praise was heard saying:

"How auspicious, how auspicious, Noble Enlightened One of Great Tranquility! The deeds you perform today are truly of the highest goodness. And as for Phạm Chí, today he will receive great wholesome benefits." At that time, the World-Honored One paid respects to the old stupa, circumambulated it three times to the right, and removed the upper part of his robe to cover it. Then, the tears mixed with the blood of the World-Honored One flowed down. After choking up and shedding tears, He smiled.

At that moment, the Buddhas of the ten directions looked at each other and also wept. Then each one radiated light to shine upon this stupa. At that time, the assembly was extremely astonished, their faces changed color, and everyone wanted to resolve their doubts.

At that time, Bodhisattva Vajra Holder and the others also wept.

He held the flaming vajra mace and waved it around, then went to the Buddha and said:

"World-Honored One! Due to what causes has this light appeared? Why do the eyes of the Tathagata shed tears like this? And for what reason do the Buddhas of the ten directions also emit auspicious light to this place? I respectfully hope that the Tathagata, in the midst of the great assembly, will dispel my doubts."

At that time, the World-Honored One said to Vajra-Hand:

"This great precious stupa contains the entire body relics of the Tathagata. In it are contained the countless secret esoteric dharmas and the essential heart of all the Tathagatas."

O Vajra Hand! Because of this weak Dharma residing therein, the tower immediately transforms into layer upon layer, without a single gap like sesame seeds piled up on top of each other.

Also, you should know that the hundreds of thousands of myriads of Tathagata bodies are also densely packed like sesame seeds piled up on each other.

The entire relic bodies of hundreds of thousands of myriads of Tathagatas and even the 84,000 Dharma gates are also contained within it.

Nine hundred ninety billion myriads of Tathagata heads are also within it.

Because of those miraculous things, around this tower there is miraculous efficacy, supreme virtue, and it can cover all the auspicious affairs of the world.

When the masses hear the Buddha's teachings, they all distance themselves from defilements, cut off afflictions, and attain the pure Dharma eye. Since the faculties of the masses are not the same, the benefits that each person attains also differ. Some attain the Fruits of Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, or Arhat in accordance with the Truth. Some attain the Path of the Solitary Realizer. Some practice the Bodhisattva Path and attain Omniscient Wisdom or achieve non-retrogression. Others attain the First Bhumi, Second Bhumi, and up to the Tenth Bhumi. Some complete the Six Paramitas. As for the Pratyekabuddhas, they distance themselves from defilements and attain five kinds of supernormal powers.

When seeing this rare and extraordinary event, Bodhisattva Vajra Hand said:

"How marvelous it is, World-Honored One! The assembly has only heard about this, yet they have received such supreme merit. How much more merit will there be for those who hear the profound and wondrous truth and sincerely generate faith?"

The Buddha said:

..."Listen, Vajra Hand! In the future life, if there are devout men and women along with any four of My disciples who set their minds to compile this Scripture, it will be equivalent to compiling 9 trillion times all the Scriptures that all the Tathagatas have preached. This merit surpasses the virtuous roots they have cultivated in front of 9 trillion Tathagatas. Moreover, they will also receive the blessing and protection from all those Tathagatas, as dearly as one treasures their own eyes, just like a kind mother loves and protects her child.

If anyone reads or recites this Scripture, it is equivalent to reading and reciting all the Scriptures preached by the Buddhas of the past, present, and future.

Because by reciting this sutra, 9.9 trillion Tathagatas, Worthy of Offerings, Exactly Equal to Enlightened, all come, piled layer upon layer, densely packed like sesame seeds stacked upon each other, without a single gap. Day and night, those Buddhas manifest to confer blessings on that person.

Countless as the sands in the Ganges, all the Tathagatas gather, the prior assemblies not yet departed, and the later ones arrive in layers again. The Buddhas appear and disappear, like fine sand swirling in a swift river. The Buddhas go and come again—without any interruption.

If someone offers flowers, incense, garlands, clothing, and wondrous decorative items to this Sutra, it is the same as if they offered heavenly flowers, clothing, and ornaments made of the Seven Treasures, accumulated to the extent of Mount Sumeru, and dedicated in front of 9.9 trillion Tathagatas. The merit they cultivate by sowing in this Sutra is likewise.

When the devas, nagas, asuras, humans, and non-humans heard these words, everyone was astonished, and then they said to one another:

"The virtue of this ruined earthen fort is truly marvelous! It is because of the divine power bestowed by the Tathagata that such miraculous transformations appear."

The Vajra Guard then addressed the Buddha:

"World-Honored One! By what cause does this seven-jeweled stupa appear as an earthen fort?"

The Buddha said to the Vajra Guard:

"This is not a mound of earth, but a magnificent and wondrous treasure tower. Due to the low karma of sentient beings, it remains hidden and does not appear. Although the tower is concealed, the entire body of the Tathagata cannot be destroyed. How can the vajra body of the Tathagata be subject to decay?"

After I pass into Nirvana, during the later days of the Degenerate Age of the Dharma, if there are sentient beings who commit unwholesome deeds and thus must fall into hell, who do not believe in the Triple Gem, and do not cultivate wholesome roots, because of these causes and conditions, the Buddha Dharma will disappear. However, this stupa will remain firm and indestructible. This is due to the divine power of the grace of all the Tathagatas. Because of karmic obscurations, ignorant sentient beings do not know how to excavate it for use. Therefore, I now shed tears, and the other Tathagatas also shed tears.

The Buddha further told Vajra Holder:

"If any being were to transcribe this Sutra and then enshrine it in a stupa, that stupa would become the adamantine treasury stupa of all Tathagatas, the stupa that maintains the secret heart empowerment of all Tathagatas, the stupa of 9.9 trillion Tathagatas, the Buddha-capped stupa of Buddha's vision of all Tathagatas, and would be protected by the divine power of all Tathagatas.

If this Sutra is enshrined inside a Buddha statue and then placed in a stupa, the statue will be made of the seven treasures, be efficacious and responsive according to one's thoughts—there will be no wish that is not fulfilled.

Depending on your ability, build towers using earth, wood, stone, or bricks, and decorate with canopies, nets, circular paths, altar platforms, roofs, wind chimes, foundations, or steps. Due to the power of the Sutra, the tower will naturally become seven treasures. Furthermore, all Tathagatas will increase the power of this Sutra. With sincere words, the Tathagatas will continuously bestow blessings.

If there are sentient beings who can perform worship and offer even just a stick of incense or a flower in front of this stupa, then their severe sins accumulated over eighty billion kalpas will be instantly destroyed. In this present life, they will be free from calamities, and upon death, they will be born into the houses of the Buddhas.

Suppose someone is destined to fall into the Hell of Avici, but even if they worship or circumambulate to the right of this stupa only once, the gates of hell will close, and the path of wisdom will open wide.

Furthermore, all Tathagatas will use their divine powers to protect the place where this stupa and the images enshrined with this sutra are located.

- That place will not be harmed by storms or lightning.

- That place will not be disturbed by venomous snakes, scorpions, or other poisonous insects.

- That place will not be harmed by lions, mad elephants, tigers, wolves, wild dogs, bees, or centipedes.

- That place will also not be terrorized by crippled demons, violent demons, spirit demons, life-draining demons, goblins, or epilepsy.

- That place will also not be infected by any fevers, ulcerations, leprosy, or boils.

If anyone just catches a glimpse of this tower, they could eliminate all accidents. Six types of livestock, adults, and boys and girls will not be infected by epidemics.

- They will not die unjustly or die suddenly at a young age.

- They will not be harmed by knives, sticks, fire, or water.

- They will not be attacked by robbers or enemies.

- They also will not have to worry about hunger or poverty.

- Spells and curses will not be able to harm them.

- The Four Great Heavenly Kings along with their retinues will protect them day and night.

- The 28 generals, affiliated with sickness, the sun, the moon, the five planets, and the cloud wisdom stars, will protect them day and night.

- All dragon kings will bring rain at the proper time and enhance their spiritual energy.

- All deities, including the deities in the Thirty-Three Heavens, will descend to make offerings to them three times a day.

- All immortals will gather three times a day to circumambulate the stupa, sing praises, make offerings, give thanks, and admire.

- The Heavenly Emperor Năng Thiên, together with the celestial maidens, will descend to offer at three periods during the day and three periods during the night.

That place is then protected and blessed by all the Tathagatas. It is because this scripture is in the stupa that such things occur.

If anyone uses earth, stone, wood, gold, silver, copper, or lead to build a tower, and then inscribes this mantra and places it inside, once it has just been placed, that tower will become a tower of seven treasures. The steps above and below, the platform, canopy, wind chimes, and wheel hall will all be made entirely of the seven treasures. On the four sides of the tower will be images of the Tathāgata. Because it contains the essential Dharma, all Tathāgatas will steadfastly protect it day and night without leaving. Due to the power of the mantra, the seven-treasure tower, containing the miraculous relics of the entire body, will soar up into the middle of the Heaven of the Pure Abodes; the tower will stand towering. All the deities day and night will behold, guard, and offer homage.

Vajra Hand said:

"World-Honored One! What is the cause for this Dharma to possess such supreme merits?"

The Buddha said:

"Know that it is due to the power of the sacred Treasure Seal Mantra."

Vajra Hand said:

"We respectfully hope that the Tathagata will have compassion for us and expound this mantra."

The Buddha said:

"Listen, contemplate, and do not forget! The radiant emanations of all Tathagatas of the present and future, and the complete relic bodies of past Buddhas, are all within the Treasure of Sealing the Mantra. The Three Bodies of all Tathagatas are also contained within this."

At that time, the World-Honored One immediately spoke the mantra as follows:

"NA MA SI T’RI DA ĐI VI KA NAM

SA R’VA TA THA GA TA NAM

OM BU VI BA VA NA

VA RI VA CHA NA VA CHA TI"
