When the Buddha finished reciting this mantra, the Buddhas Tathagata in the land resonated with voices of praise saying:

"Well done, well done, Noble One! You have been able to appear in this impure world, in order to benefit sentient beings who have no place to rely on, no one to depend on, by expounding profound Dharma, and causing such subtle Dharma to endure in the world to bring great benefit and stability, happiness, and joy."

At that time, the Buddha said to Vajra-holder:

"Listen, listen! Such subtle Dharma has limitless power and boundless benefit. It is like a wish-fulfilling jewel on a ceremonial canopy, always showering treasure and fulfilling all desires."

I will now give a brief exposition of a part of those countless benefits. Please remember and uphold it for the benefit of all.

After death, if any wicked person is condemned to hell to suffer continuously with no time limit for release, and if any of their descendants call out the spirit's name and recite the above mantra, then immediately after seven repetitions, the heated iron cauldron will suddenly transform into a pond of eight virtues, with lotus flowers supporting the sinner's feet and a precious umbrella shading their head. At that moment, the gates of hell will break open, and the Buddha's Path will be widely revealed. Then, that lotus will carry them flying to the Pure Land. Upon rebirth in that realm, the One Supreme Wisdom will naturally manifest. They will take immense joy in preaching the Dharma and attain the fruit of the One-Time Fulfillment of the Path.

Again, it is said that some beings, because of their serious karmic retribution, have to endure hundreds of ailments in the body, causing intense suffering and mental anguish, but if they recite this mantra 21 times, all their diseases and countless sorrows will be simultaneously destroyed, their lifespan prolonged, and their merit and virtue boundless.

Suppose there is someone who, due to the karma of greed and stinginess, is born into a poor family, with clothes insufficient to cover the body and food not enough to fill the stomach, thin and withered, looked down upon by everyone. But if this person feels shame and embarrassment, they go into the forest to pick wildflowers, grind rotten wood into incense powder, then go before the stupa to make offerings, circumambulate it seven times to the right, and weep while repenting their mistakes, then due to the spiritual power of the mantra and the authority of the stupa, their karma of poverty will immediately be eradicated. Wealth and honor suddenly arrive, the seven treasures fall like rain, and they will lack nothing. At that time, they need to respect the Buddha and the Dharma andGive alms to the poor. If they are stingy and miserly, their wealth will immediately disappear.

Suppose there is someone who, wanting to cultivate wholesome roots, uses mud or bricks to build a stupa according to their ability. That stupa might be as small as a mango and four finger-widths high. Then, they inscribe a mantra and place it inside the stupa, then hold incense and flowers to make offerings and pay respects. Because of the power of this mantra along with their faith, a great fragrance cloud naturally emanates from the small stupa. The scent and light of the cloud pervade the Dharma Realm, mildly fragrant and vast in its benefit to the Buddha's work. The merit they gain would be as mentioned above. In short, there is no wish that will not be fulfilled.

In the era of the Degenerate Dharma, among the four assemblies of disciples, if any good men or faithful women devote themselves wholeheartedly to constructing a stupa and placing sacred mantras for the supreme Path, the merit obtained cannot be fully expressed.

If someone comes to the stupa to seek blessings, bringing a stick of incense or a flower branch to offer, worship, and circumambulate clockwise, because of that merit:

- Positions of honor and distinction will not require asking.

- Wealth, nobility, and longevity will increase naturally.

- Enemies and robbers will be defeated without fighting.

- Resentment from curses, will not vanish on its own.

- Epidemics and evil spirits, will not go away on their own.

- A gentle husband and dutiful wife, cannot be obtained without asking.

- Good sons and beautiful daughters, cannot be expected to appear on their own.

- All wishes can be fulfilled at will.

If there are crows, hawks, sparrows, mynas, cuckoos, pigeons, owls, wolves, wild animals, flies, mosquitoes, ants, or other insects, and they merely come under the shadow of the stupa or step on the grass there, their karmic obstacles will be immediately destroyed, and they will realize ignorance. They will suddenly enter the Buddha's house and freely receive the treasure of Dharma. Moreover, if anyone sees the stupa, hears the sound of the bell, hears the name, or is under the shadow of the stupa, all their karmic offenses will be eradicated, their wishes will be fulfilled, they will have peace in this life, and upon death, they will be reborn in the Pure Land.

If someone, according to their ability, takes a lump of mud to fill a broken tile, or holds a small stone to prop up a leaning tower, due to this merit, they will gain increased blessings and longevity. After the end of their life, that person will be reborn as a Wheel-Turning King.

After I pass into nirvana, if any of the fourfold disciples wish to save sentient beings in the realms of suffering, they should stand before this stupa to offer incense and flowers, sincerely make vows, and recite the mantra. At that time, every word and every phrase of the mantra will emit radiant light, shining upon sentient beings in the three evil paths, and eliminate all suffering. When sentient beings have escaped the bonds of suffering, the seed of Buddha will sprout; they will be able to rebirth freely into the Pure Land in the ten directions.

If someone on the top of a high mountain sincerely recites this mantra, then all sentient beings within their sight—including those with fur, scales, or shells—whether residing near or far, in valleys, forests, streams, rivers, lakes, or the open sea, will have their karmic obstacles destroyed. They will recognize ignorance, manifest the inherent nature of the three kinds of Buddhahood, and ultimately enter the peace of Great Nirvana.

If anyone accompanies the one reciting the mantra on their path, whether as if they are a breeze passing through clothes, or treading on footprints, or merely catching a glimpse of the face, or just conversing briefly with the one reciting the mantra, the grave offenses of such people will all be eradicated, and the body, speech, and mind karmas will be perfectly fulfilled.

At that time, the Buddha said to Vajra-Guardian:

"I now entrust this secret mantra and these scriptures to you. Respect, protect, and transmit them in the world. Pass them on to all sentient beings and do not let them be discontinued."

Vajra Bodhisattva said:

"I am greatly honored to be entrusted by the World-Honored One. In order to repay the profound kindness of the World-Honored One, we will day and night strive to protect, proclaim, and spread it throughout the world.

If there are sentient beings who copy, uphold, and always remember it, we will send Nandana Deva, King Brahma, the Four Heavenly Kings, along with the eightfold heavenly dragons, to protect them day and night and never be far from them."

The Buddha said:

"Excellent, Vajra Hand! You uphold this Dharma because you wish all sentient beings in the future to receive great benefit." After the World-Honored One had expounded this Treasure Seal Mantra and extensively carried out Buddha’s work, He went to Pham Chi's house to receive offerings, intending for gods and humans to gain great merit. Afterwards, He returned to His original place.

At that time, the Great Assembly, which included: Bhikṣus, Bhikṣuṇīs, laymen, laywomen, devas, dragons, various spirits, incense-bearing deities, flying celestial beings, golden-winged birds, guardian deities, great serpents, humans, and non-human beings, all generated a mind of great joy and reverently accepted and practiced accordingly.

noi_dung:
Episode 449: The Chapter on Great Wisdom Bodhisattva in the Surangama Sutra specifically introduces Bodhisattva Great Wisdom, Great

The following part continues to introduce Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta, “Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta, the Bodhisattva of Great Wisdom and Great Power.” Here, 'power' refers to strength, great wisdom, and great force. “Can go anywhere” means that because of great wisdom and great power, he can travel everywhere, to the realms of space throughout the Dharma realm; there is no place he cannot go, which is why he is named Mahasthamaprapta, and this is the origin of the title.

According to the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, “Great sages use the mind to contemplate the Buddha to enter the patience of non-arising, without relying on expedients, the mind naturally opens. Now, guiding people who recite the Buddha's name in this realm to return to the Pure Land, together with Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara attending Amitabha Buddha.” “Standing on both sides” here means supporting Amitabha Buddha in teaching and transforming sentient beings.

The Chapter on Great Wisdom and Perfect Penetration in the Lankavatara Sutra specifically introduces the Bodhisattva Great Wisdom (Mahasthamaprapta). Great Wisdom is a Bodhisattva who practices the method of reciting the Buddha's name. "Using the mind to recite the Buddha's name to enter the realm of cessation of birth and endurance," how does he achieve Buddhahood? He becomes a Buddha by reciting the Buddha's name, just with such a simple method, reciting to the extent that the mind becomes one-pointed and undisturbed. The one-pointed and undisturbed mind is on the same level and in the same realm as the clear mind that sees its true nature, the great enlightenment of Chan Buddhism. Chan uses the method of meditation to attain it, whereas the Bodhisattva Great Wisdom uses the method of reciting Amitabha Buddha to attain it. It's the same principle, but the method used is reciting the Buddha's name. First isLet go of worries, doubts, and attachments to attain undisturbed single-mindedness; then let go of distinctions, arising intentions, and moving thoughts to reach the principle of undisturbed single-mindedness, which means becoming a Buddha.

Reciting the Buddha's name without being able to let go of afflictions, views, and thoughts cannot escape the cycle of reincarnation in the six realms. What will be the result of reciting the Buddha's name? It is only the merit for the heavenly and human realms. Those who are wealthy in this world all enjoy the merit of reciting the Buddha's name from previous lives. If one is not a Buddhist, one certainly cannot achieve such great rewards. If one is not a Buddhist and wants to cultivate merit like kings, at least one must do good deeds for ten generations. But according to Buddhists, they can achieve it in one lifetime.

Using a sincere heart to cultivate goodness, one still does not eliminate afflictions of view and thought. Once these afflictions of view and thought are eliminated, the results of one's practice will transform into merit, meaning it is not luck or blessings. Merit can help you transcend birth and death in the three realms, but luck cannot; what luck brings are the rewards for humans and the heavenly realms.

But let's think, are those great virtuous people really without creating karma? They have power, influence, become kings or lords, kill whoever they want, and others would be sentenced to death for killing, but if they kill, it's considered okay. Killing others is not free from crime, but cause and effect must still be paid, lives must be compensated, and consequences must be endured; if too many people are killed, one must descend into hell. After suffering all the punishment in hell, one still must compensate, there is no escape; everyone must clearly understand this truth. Do not kill, not even for eating meat, because eating meat also brings consequences. The Buddhist scriptures have taught that in the past, great virtuous teachers often advised: eat only half a catty,In the next life, you will have to repay eight taels, so don't be smug. Why create that sin to bring trouble upon yourself? Therefore, understanding karma is the most important thing of all.

Reciting the Buddha's name is the simplest practice; 'using the mind to recite the Buddha's name to enter the realm of non-arising patience' is precisely attaining enlightenment. 'Not relying on expedients, self-realizing the mind's awakening'; the expedients here are other practices. He did not use any of the eighty-four thousand practices, only pursuing a simple Buddha name and achieving fulfillment. Therefore, he had a very deep affinity with Amitābha Buddha, and Amitābha Buddha also uses a simple Buddha name.

The method of Amitabha Buddha was not originally created by him but comes from the ancient Buddhas who existed before Amitabha Buddha. The so-called "penetrating a single practice and cultivating it for a long time" cannot be changed; once reciting the Buddha's name has been accomplished, the mind becomes enlightened, and understanding arises, leading to great clarity and great realization.

“Nowadays in this world” refers to the Saha world, which is our world here, “guiding those who recite the Buddha,” specifically guiding those who recite the Buddha “to return to the Pure Land.” Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta leads sentient beings together to the Ultimate Bliss. Everyone who recites the Buddha, genuinely wishing to recite the Buddha to seek the Pure Land, will surely receive the blessings of Mahasthamaprapta, that is certain. Practicing the same Dharma method with him, he and Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara are all assistants to Buddha Amitabha, serving as Dharma helpers for Buddha Amitabha in the Pure Land world.

Master Kinh said: "Using the light of wisdom to illuminate all, one departs from the three realms and attains supreme power, hence the title Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta." This is the Bodhisattva teaching others; the Bodhisattva symbolizes wisdom, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva symbolizes compassion. Mahāsthāmaprāpta symbolizes wisdom, wisdom illuminates everything, helping all sentient beings to dispel delusion and awaken, and wisdom is necessary to dispel delusion and awaken.

When confusion is broken, then the three evil paths and the six realms will disappear. Where do the six realms and the three evil paths come from? From afflictions and conceptual views; if we follow the words of the Infinite Life Sutra, the words of Amitabha Buddha, it will naturally be accomplished. Amitabha Buddha represents the power of vows, achieved through the merit of practicing over five lifetimes. We are afflictions and conceptual views, afflictions and ignorance, afflictions like dust; even if we practice over countless lifetimes, we can also be accomplished. Accomplished in what? Accomplished in the cyclic existence of the six realms, accomplished in the suffering of the three evil paths—a real principle, not fanciful, all is fulfilled. But we have gone in the wrong direction; the person walking the right path is still there, yet we walk the wrong path, and therefore everything...Worldly or transcendental dharmas, there is no dharma that is not accomplished naturally.

In Buddhist scriptures there is a term called: 'Dharma is inherently like this,' all dharmas are naturally like this. Therefore, we must understand that religion is about teaching and learning; if it is detached from education, religion becomes superstition, and superstition is not religion. It is necessary to clarify the definition of the two words 'religion'; when we have religious faith, we must first understand the two words 'religion.' Believing in the Buddha, we must understand what Buddhism is.

Tôn, in Chinese vocabulary, if you try to look it up in the dictionary, it carries many meanings and concepts. Among them, there are three main ideas: first is 'chiefly', second is 'important', and third is 'to revere'. There are these three main ideas. Giáo means education, teaching, or moral cultivation. Combining the two characters Tôn giáo, it means principally education, emphasizing teaching, and revering moral cultivation. How to teach? Lecturing, instructing, not only lecturing, instructing, but the teacher also sets an example and practices what they teach.

The success of a Bodhisattva in teaching lies in setting an example and giving advice. First, one should set an example and only then give advice, which is how trust is built with everyone. In other words, one must practice all the teachings of the Buddha in the scriptures; if one cannot practice them, one should not talk about anything else. One must practice first and then speak.

The Avatamsaka Sutra says: “Because I vow to take the Great Thousand World, my name is Great Strength of Wisdom,” this is the content of a passage from the Avatamsaka Sutra. “Because I,” here “I” refers to the Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta, who vows to take the Great Thousand World; the meaning of “take” is to support and help all sentient beings in the Great Thousand World. Therefore, the Buddha gave the Bodhisattva the Dharma name Mahasthamaprapta.

“Again, Kinh Tu Ích said: 'The place where I press my toe'—Here, 'I' is the self-reference of Mahāsthāmaprāpta, 'shaking the world of three thousand great thousand and the palaces of demons, hence the name Mahāsthāmaprāpta.' 'The place where the Bodhisattva presses the toe'—this meaning precisely indicates: The place where he resides, in his dharma assembly, teaching and transforming sentient beings, will emit an energy of great spiritual power. Nowadays, people call it a magnetic field; this magnetic field can shake the world of three thousand great thousand, can disturb the palaces of demons, hence the Bodhisattva has the title Mahāsthāmaprāpta.

“The Sutra again says: This Bodhisattva,” refers to Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, “when practicing the path,” here practicing means practicing the path, and practicing the path means teaching. Here, he teaches the sutras and expounds the Dharma to the beings there, regardless of short or long periods of time. This teaching covers: short periods, about two or three days; long periods can extend to many years, not fixed. This is called the time of practicing the path. When practicing the path, practicing the path is synonymous with teaching, expounding the Dharma, and guiding sentient beings.

"All ten directions of the world are shaken," here we must pay attention to the two words "all." When Bodhisattvas teach and transform sentient beings, it is like a stimulus; sentient beings react upon hearing it. Some beings attain enlightenment, achieving great and complete awakening; others realize to a lesser degree; some attain concentration and meditation; others clearly see their own wrongdoings and therefore correct themselves, abandoning evil and doing good. All are reactions, which is called shaking. If they were not moved by the sound of the Dharma, how could they repent and renew themselves? How could they abandon evil and do good? All changes are brought about by the sound of the Dharma.

"When that land trembles, there are fifty trillion flowers and treasures," the land there shakes. The words spoken by the Tathagata, the words spoken by the Bodhisattvas mean the words spoken by the Tathagata. The Dharma-body of the great being all originates from its own nature, so the grass, flowers, leaves, mountains, rivers, forests, and seas all vibrate. The true nature of this matter we can understand today, there is nothing to doubt, science has proven this to the Buddha. That is phenomena; material phenomena and mental phenomena are two aspects of a problem, inseparable, this is exactly what Bodhisattva Maitreya said: "Every thought transforms into matter, matter carries consciousness within it," the sentenceWhat was said above is the clearest evidence.

Where does material phenomena come from? Form itself is a material phenomenon, that color and shape is a material phenomenon. Material phenomena originate from ideas, “each thought becomes form, each unit of matter has consciousness within it”; each material phenomenon has a mental phenomenon. Consciousness here refers to form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; when combined together, they form the five aggregates: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Where do the five aggregates come from? From ideas. This matter is very important; this is the true nature of phenomena. If one truly realizes it, the issue will be resolved; if one has not realized it, the issue cannot yet be resolved.

Not resolved yet? We see that we still have scattered thoughts; within those thoughts, there is self-centeredness, within those thoughts, there is discrimination, attachment, affliction, habitual tendencies, and wanting to stop them but being unable to do so. According to Buddhist terms, this is called ignorance; ignorance is afflictive delusion. What is ignorance? Not understanding the true nature clearly, not recognizing the true nature, is called ignorance. If one clearly recognizes the true nature, sees the true nature, the problem is resolved, not only is there no longer suffering and happiness, but even defilement and purity cease; suffering and happiness, defilement and purity all arise from a mistaken thought, that mistaken awareness is wrong view. Clearly seeing this is called right view, right knowledge, rightThe difference between right and wrong lies in that.

Nowadays, are we practicing the wrong path or the righteous path? Honestly, many people are practicing the wrong path; very few are practicing the righteous path. To give a simple example, being selfish and self-serving is practicing the wrong path, while not being selfish and self-serving, acting with great altruism without self-interest, is the righteous path. Try to see if there is anyone who is not selfish and self-serving? We don't even need to talk about worldly matters; just look among those who practice Buddhism, is there anyone who is not selfish and self-serving? Is there anyone who does not have attachment and discrimination? If there is still selfishness and self-interest, if there is still a trace of attachment and discrimination, that person is practicing the wrong path, not a disciple of the Buddha.

Where should a true disciple of the Buddha begin? From what point should one start? In the Hinayana, the stage of Stream-entry (Sotapanna). In the Mahayana, the Avatamsaka Sutra talks about the stage of Initial Faith in the Ten Faiths; this is the proper meaning of a disciple of the Buddha, a person who practices the righteous path and does not follow the wrong path. Why? Because they have broken the four appearances as the Diamond Sutra states: the appearance of no self, the appearance of no person, the appearance of no sentient being, the appearance of no recipient. This is the first level of elementary study—the First Fruition Stream-entry of the Hinayana. Have we reached that? Not yet; we ourselves understand better than anyone else.

Nowadays we are very fortunate. After studying for several decades, what have we gained? Enlightenment. We understand all these things clearly, everything. We have adjusted our way of seeing things but still have not let go, which means we have not realized enlightenment, we have enlightenment but have not truly realized it. If we had truly realized it, we would be at ease, genuinely free from suffering and joyful,...

The compassion of the Bodhisattva manifests in each of the six realms, appearing in countless, limitless forms in each realm. As long as sentient beings return to tranquility, they will be taught immediately. The only concern is when anger is too intense, or greed is too strong, then there is no way to save them. Even the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas cannot help, because they refuse to listen, they do not accept it, they are too confused, and they are immersed in the five passions and desires. At that time, the Bodhisattva does not intervene; they only observe from afar, waiting for the moment when the beings feel remorse, recognize their mistakes, realize that through countless kalpas they have been reincarnating in the cycle of birth and death as if it were a game, and now dare not return again. That single thought is enlightenment.

When you awaken, the Buddha and Bodhisattvas come to save you immediately. It cannot be said that this is luck; you have encountered many virtuous teachers. I was not as fortunate as you. In reality, it is not like that, but due to each person's karmic conditions; it is because your mind is not sincere. All dharmas arise from the mind; it is due to resonance. If we follow and practice the teachings, the Buddha and Bodhisattvas will come immediately. They will manifest as virtuous teachers to help us. They will be our instructors, fellow students, close friends... to assist and encourage us.

If the heart is not upright, there will also be people who come to help, but when demons and evil spirits come, what do they come to help with? They help us grow desire, anger, ignorance, and arrogance. At that time, we feel very excited, very proud, because they are helping us get rich, helping us compete for power and profit, but the end result is in the realm of hungry ghosts, hell, and animals. It seems very fine at present, but the future will have problems.

On the contrary, when truly good friends help you, although it may seem difficult at first, why? They obstruct fame and gain, firmly preventing us from getting involved with those things. They help us deeply study the scriptures, help us uphold precepts and practice meditation, and help us open our wisdom. Ultimately, at the very least, we are born into the heavenly realms; when born into the heavens, the best result is rebirth in the Pure Land. Rebirth in the Pure Land is equivalent to attaining Buddhahood in this very life, all within a single thought.

Great Wisdom Power Bodhisattva and Avalokiteshvara manifested for us, can we not give thanks? The wisdom, true faith, and complete understanding of Great Wisdom Power Bodhisattva thoroughly comprehend, perfectly and completely, the true nature of all phenomena, truly illuminating them.

The compassion of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara is such that, even if you scold the Bodhisattva all day long, even if you treat the statue as a worthless piece of stone, the Bodhisattva still saves you, still helps you. It is absolutely not because you have behaved badly that the Bodhisattva scolds you, saying: I will send demons to catch you; it is never like that. If it were so, that would not be Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, it would be the action of evil spirits, not the deed of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. Therefore, we must clearly understand why the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are so compassionate; they know that we and they are one entity, and this relationship is how intimately connected!

If we liken this body to the entire universe, all things are the different organs of the body. On the outside are the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and body; on the inside are the six internal organs, and they are diverse, not the same. Yet you must understand that all of them are made from one type of matter, which is the five aggregates. The five aggregates: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, consciousness, are matter, fundamental matter, and they include five types of phenomena. Today, scientists call these subatomic particles, or photons, quanta. Buddhist scriptures call them the smallest of the small (Extremely Minute), the fundamental forms that make up this body; the entire universe is also formed by these fundamental forms.

The Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, full of wisdom, sees that the five aggregates are empty. The five aggregates exist, but they are illusory, not real. What is their essence? Their essence is self-nature; self-nature is not material, yet it can manifest as material; self-nature is not mind, yet it can manifest as mind. Therefore, all these phenomena, whether they are material phenomena, mental phenomena, or natural phenomena, all belong to their own true nature, which is emptiness, and are ultimately impossible to attain.

Form is empty, realization cannot be attained, so the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas still manifest to teach. They must appear, according to conditions and wondrous functions, with proper conduct, gentle and sincere in nature, enduring suffering in place of sentient beings. This is called great compassion, called Avalokiteshvara. Where does Avalokiteshvara come from? From the nature itself manifesting. All the wisdom, supernatural powers, relief from suffering, and saving from danger of Avalokiteshvara are all the inherent virtues of the true nature, not anything else. Avalokiteshvara is one with us, Amitabha is one with us, all sentient beings in the ten directions of the world are one with us. We must understand this oneness, for example, like a single cell, each particle, each tiny photon in the bodyour body.

I am talking about an example sentence from the ancients, a saying from the bottom of the heart, 100% accurate, without any deceit. What did the ancients call it? A treasure in the heart, one's own innermost being, one's internal organs, how could I not cherish it? How could I not cherish it?

All material phenomena, mental phenomena, natural phenomena in the void throughout the dharma realm, all are my treasures. If I understand this issue, recognize the true nature of reality, then I must acknowledge that I am united with all as one. Congratulations, you have become a Buddha; becoming a Buddha is exactly like this.

Truly, the entire universe together forms a unity with me; that is called becoming a Buddha, that is called the Bodhisattva Dharmakaya. Blending into a unity but not yet reaching ultimate perfection, that is the Bodhisattva Dharmakaya. Reaching ultimate perfection is called becoming a Buddha; the matter of becoming a Buddha or Bodhisattva is like that. You see, there is no Buddha or Bodhisattva who does not love sentient beings; there has never been a Buddha who despises sentient beings, certainly not.

Truly practicing the Bodhisattva path, even if people treat you with ill will, they still maintain goodwill toward you. If they retaliated with malicious intent, they would no longer be Bodhisattvas; they would be ordinary people like you. If they are genuinely followers of the Buddha, they will certainly treat you with kindness. Why? Out of gratitude, they will repay kindness. What virtues have you brought to them? If you harm them, what virtue is there? Harming them—what virtue is that? To kill or harm like that is to have sent them to the Pure Land. That is the kind of virtue they must repay, for they have transcended the cycle of birth and death. Birth and death pertain to this physical body, a material phenomenon, but the spirit endures forever.

When one realizes the mind and comprehends their true nature, the great master Huệ Năng once said: “Unexpectedly, the self-nature is originally unborn and undying.” This is the true self; ordinary beings and saints are not two, not different. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are unborn and undying, and all ordinary beings are also unborn and undying. Why? Because all originate from self-nature. Even the land, mountains, rivers, grass, trees, flowers, and leaves are unborn and undying; birth and death are just external matters, outer forms, while the inner mental phenomena remain unborn and undying.

In Buddhist scriptures, mental phenomena in animals are called Buddha-nature, in plants and minerals are called Dharma-nature. Buddha-nature and Dharma-nature are of one essence, not two nor different, both are one Nature, a nature that does not arise nor cease, capable of arising and manifesting. It is necessary to clearly understand these points in Buddhist teachings to comprehend the ideas the ancients wanted to convey: Human nature is inherently good. In early lessons of the past, children at the age of five or six began learning the opening lines of the Three Character Classic: "At the beginning of human life, the nature is originally good." Having grasped these moral principles, what is the aim of education? It is to return to the inherent goodness, that is the purpose ofeducation.

All our unwholesome deeds today are not inherently wholesome; inherent wholesomeness is eternal and has never changed. The current mistaken thoughts and deviant actions are called tendencies, which today we refer to as habits. We have become bad due to the influence of external circumstances, and this is because of unwholesome tendencies.

The purpose of education is to influence you from habitual tendencies back to your true nature; this is called education, the education of sages. That is the way of education of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas, not modern education. Modern education has neglected all these matters. Nowadays, what does education teach? It teaches people how to make money, how to compete for power and benefits, how to benefit oneself at the expense of others, teaching people those things. If everyone learns to benefit themselves while harming others, can there be no conflicts? Can there be no wars? That is why it creates turmoil throughout society, causing continuous disasters onthe earth, all these negative things originate from there.

If we immediately awaken and turn back, we can abandon evil and do good, just as the American Bo Lai Deng said: Abandon evil and do good, correct faults and return to virtue, with a straight and honest mind, any misfortune can be resolved. Although he is not a Buddhist, has never been exposed to Buddhism, and is a scientific researcher, everything he stated is completely in accordance with Buddhist teachings.

It is not that there are no methods to solve all the problems of society; the accidents on earth are not serious issues, all of them can be resolved. The optimal solution is the mind, which is also what the Buddha taught: "All phenomena arise from the mind." Whatever we think, that is what it will become. Thinking good thoughts makes it the Pure Land, thinking wrongly makes it a polluted land, thinking virtuous thoughts makes it a heavenly realm, thinking evil makes everything become hells and hungry ghost realms; all of these arise from the mind, these products do not exist inherently. In inherent nature, there is also no Western Pure Land; the Western Pure Land is a productThe quality of the mind, is manifested from the 48 vows of Amitabha Buddha. Our explanation is very clear.

48 vows are the cause of affinity; what, then, is the cause? The cause is the virtuous mark of wisdom inherent in one's own nature; that is the cause. When one meets such a good affinity, if the cause encounters the affinity, the result will immediately arrive. The result is the adornment of the Pure Land world, manifesting naturally. There is no need for design, no need for planning, no need for construction; it forms naturally. The Pure Land world is like that; all realms of the Buddhas throughout the universes in all the Dharma realms are no different. Practitioners of Pure Land cannot be unaware of this issue.

We have seen Amitabha Buddha, and we pay our respects before his statue. What do these things signify? They represent the marks of Prajñā wisdom that are inherent in our true nature. They represent the 48 vows and five lifetimes of practice. When we see the statue, we immediately think of these things; it is the fulfillment of his vows that brings about the Pure Land. We must learn from this, imitate it, and look at the two attendants beside him: the wisdom of Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta and the compassion of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. We must immediately learn from them and apply it in our daily lives, especially in our interactions with others,...

* In summary, according to our understanding, when using ultimate concentration of mind, the limitation is minimized, and the lowest rank is the Bodhisattva of the Eighth Stage. The Eighth Stage, Ninth Stage, Tenth Stage, Equal Enlightenment, and Wonderful Enlightenment—among these five ranks, four Bodhisattvas hold the highest positions, and lastly is the Buddha. They thoroughly comprehend the true nature of all dharmas, with no remaining obstacles.

Therefore, how should we practice in our daily life? Practice what? The ancient sages tell us: "Do not fear the arising of thoughts, only fear slow awakening," this is the highest guiding principle. What is "the arising of thoughts"? The arising of thoughts refers to an ordinary person; when you have a stirring of the mind, whether it is attachment or anger, what lies in your heart? The seven emotions and five desires, the habitual tendencies of afflictions. As soon as these arise, we immediately become vigilant of the mistakes; this is called "not fearing the arising of thoughts." Because you have awakened, after awakening, you immediately correct it; this is called cultivation or practice.

How does a person who recites Buddha's name adjust themselves? They change it into the phrase 'Amitabha Buddha'; this is called knowing how to recite Buddha's name. A person who does not know how to recite Buddha's name recites 'Amitabha Buddha, Amitabha Buddha' all day long but still wanders in thought, gaining no benefit at all. A person who knows how to recite Buddha's name, in each recitation, can subdue one kind of affliction, leveling all habitual afflictions. Their realm is elevated greatly; this is what is called knowing how to recite. Especially practicing in work and with others is the fastest, the quickest place to train.

What is a person like? Some people like, and in that liking there is attachment and desire to possess; we should trim that away, as these are not good qualities. Some people dislike, dislike, or hate, and that is also a mistake; we must also trim and smooth it away, and then an equanimous mind will appear.

Therefore, the content of the five words on the title of the sutra is very profound. What do we practice? Precisely practicing purity, equality, and enlightenment. Using what method? Pure Land Buddhism uses one phrase: Amitabha Buddha, one phrase: Amitabha Buddha. In daily life, we practice purity, equality, and enlightenment. At work, we generate purity, equality, and enlightenment. In interacting with everyone, dealing with things produces purity, equality, and enlightenment. Treating everyone with gentleness and ease, like the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Do Buddhas and Bodhisattvas consider anyone an enemy? No, everyone is like oneself; that is truly a Buddha. Why? Oneself and the whole emptiness, the entire dharma realm, are one entity.

Hoan Nguyen Quan said: A self-nature that is pure and fully luminous, the universe also originates from here, all things also arise from there, and I also arise from there, a single entity! In a single entity, there is only mutual affection, how could there be enmity within a single entity? Regarding the things one loves, does one’s mind strongly love them, or hate, despise them? Is there such a thing? Of course not. With all beings in the path of goodness or evil, with heavenly beings, hungry ghosts, hell beings, animals, all are treated as if they were your own cherished treasures. Accept the improper treatment of others but do not allow yourself to treat others improperly.other people.

Why? Because they are deluded, and I am enlightened. If I am deluded, then am I like them? Currently, I am enlightened, so I am not like them; I must be like the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, not equal to ordinary people. Every day we recite sutras, chant Buddha's name, and every day we pay respects to Amitabha Buddha, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva. Have you ever thought about these things? If you haven't thought about them, then our daily recitation and worship is considered wasted. I do not know what Amitabha Buddha, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, and Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva teach me; in that case, it is superstition. Society considers people learning Buddhism like us to be superstitious; do we admit that? It is impossible.Do not deny it, we are truly superstitious. If you share those issues with them, they will understand immediately. That is not superstition. This is very useful,...

* We continue to examine the final passage: “These two Bodhisattvas, practicing the Bodhisattva path in the Saha world, when they are reborn in that land, always stand on either side of Amitabha Buddha. Those who wish to go to the Buddhas of the ten directions, and to infinite Buddhas, arrive according to their mind. They currently reside in this world to perform great acts of benefit and happiness. Good men and good women of the world, if facing sudden disaster or terror, even to the point of giving up their lives, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will in no way fail to obtain liberation.” (These two Bodhisattvas practice the Bodhisattva path in the Land of Saha, and when reborn in that land, always stand on both sides of Amitabha Buddha. Those who wish to go to the Buddhas of the ten directions, as they wish, they will arrive. They are currently in this world to do great beneficial acts, both good men and good women,If there are frightening events or dangerous accidents, simply calling upon Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara will allow anyone to be liberated.

This is a very important sutra for the present age. Elder Nian has annotated it as follows: “These two Bodhisattvas are both in the Sahā world,” meaning the world we are living in, this is the world where Shakyamuni Buddha teaches, and its scope is quite extensive. How large is the Sahā world? One world encompasses three thousand great thousand worlds.

Nian Lao tells us that, in the Buddhist scriptures, a world unit is mentioned, which is like a galaxy system in our modern terms. One galaxy system is a world unit, a thousand world units make a minor thousand-world system, a thousand minor thousand-world systems make a middle thousand-world system, and a thousand middle thousand-world systems make a great thousand-world system, which is the Sahā World. A galaxy system equals 1000 multiplied by 1000 multiplied by 1000; how many galaxy systems are there in the Sahā World? One billion galaxy systems; that is the area of teaching and cultivation of Buddha Śākyamuni. That is the area where he currently teaches. Our Earth is one of those billion galaxy systems, notnot different from a small island, it is an extremely small island.

The scope of Buddhist propagation is so vast, and the Buddha lands are the same. Each Buddha land has at least ten billion galaxies. Some lands are even larger, as described in the scriptures. Some areas of the Buddhas' teachings encompass two great thousandfold world systems, three great thousandfold world systems, five great thousandfold world systems, or even more than ten great thousandfold world systems. May the Buddhas in those worlds all be different from one another.

The Buddha Amitabha's realm is vast, it can be said to be like the sky throughout the Dharma realm; every place is a realm. We cannot see it all. What does it mean by cannot see it all? The levels of space are not the same. For example, in many religions, there is often talk about the relationship between humans and spirits, humans living together with spirits, coexisting. But humans cannot see spirits, and spirits cannot see humans; sometimes they even share the same room, yet the levels of space are not the same.

Sukhavati is the world with the highest level of space; they can see us, but we cannot see them. We have discussed this issue before. The divine eyes and divine ears of Bodhisattvas in the world of Sukhavati can thoroughly see all sentient beings in the empty countries throughout the Dharma realm. They see everything clearly, hear everything, and understand the intentions and thoughts of everyone.

These two Bodhisattvas both reside in the Trāyastriṃśa world, assisting Buddha Shakyamuni in practicing the Bodhisattva path. 'Practice' means to promote, to encourage action. The Bodhisattva path includes the Ten Virtues, the Six Harmonies, the Six Paramitas, and the Ten Vows of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. These two Bodhisattvas help Buddha Shakyamuni, promoting the teaching of sentient beings in this world so that they may be reborn in the Pure Land. Both of these Bodhisattvas are from the Pure Land; they assist Amitabha Buddha in the Pure Land.

In the previous part we studied, both of them have been Buddhas for a very long time; they are people who have a special karmic connection with the Pure Land and the Saha World. Therefore, when Sakyamuni Buddha attained Buddhahood, and Amitabha Buddha attained Buddhahood, they sailed back to assist Buddha Amitabha in the capacity of a Bodhisattva. They helped Sakyamuni Buddha, urged the education of Buddhism, and promoted Mahayana education.

"Be a shining example for the people in all ten directions," set an example, be a good model, demonstrate, so that everyone in the world can learn from the Bodhisattva, learn compassion from the Bodhisattva, learn wisdom from the Bodhisattva.

Our karmic affinity today is very auspicious, having encountered such a good book, this is considered a stroke of luck. Because this is a great compilation of five types of original translations, it can be said that this commentary is a great compilation annotated by the venerable ancestors of the past. When annotating this sutra, Master Hoang Nien thought about it—it's really hard to come by, something we all never considered. All of this is due to supreme affinity, what supreme affinity? Supreme affinity during the great Cultural Revolution, very hard to obtain! I believe, if it weren't for the great Cultural Revolution, Elder Niem certainly would not have thought of this.

Certainly, in the past, when listening to Hạ Liên Cư lecture on the sutras, he wrote many notes. If all those were arranged, they could constitute a different commentary, not the current one. All his materials disappeared during the Great Cultural Revolution and were completely burned.

This commentary was carried out under the teacher's orders; if not carried out, how could one face the teacher? But to carry it out, how should it be done? Therefore, he came up with this method, truly wonderful! It is entirely the scriptures spoken by the great virtuous patriarchs throughout history. If anyone questions it, saying it is not so, these are the words of Bành Tế Thanh, those are the words of some great master, not my own, truly wise! He compiled the comprehensive annotations of past commentaries, with each phrase having someone responsible, truly intelligent. This is precisely the wisdom of Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta, the compassion of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, this issomething no one has thought of!,...

Therefore, "The Bodhisattva serves as a model for all beings in the ten directions of the world." How do they serve as a model? By aspiring to be reborn in the Pure Land. Observe, the wish for all beings to be reborn in the Pure Land—why is this? When reborn in the Pure Land, all problems are resolved, and it is guaranteed that you will attain Buddhahood in this very life.

“Currently in this world,” these two Bodhisattvas are presently in the Saha world. “The world here is the Saha world because there is a deep karmic connection with the sentient beings in this realm.” The sentient beings in our world here greatly cherish Bodhisattvas Avalokiteshvara (Quan Âm) and Mahasthamaprapta (Thế Chí), especially Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. Those who know their names must place them first; in every home in China, there are images of Amitabha Buddha and Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. No one in Chinese society does not know Amitabha and Avalokiteshvara. Those who practice Pure Land Buddhism also know Mahasthamaprapta; it is not that people who do not practice Pure Land are unaware of Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta, but they know of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara.

Therefore, in this world, doing deeds of great benefit, the great benefits referred to here are: “Taking care of all beings who recite the Buddha’s name, helping them to stay away from the three lower realms, attain supreme power, and be born in Ultimate Bliss.” Such is the great benefit, and the special objects of this are those beings who recite the Buddha’s name. By practicing diligently and propagating Pure Land teachings, one will surely receive the blessings of Amitabha Buddha, as well as the blessings of Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta. As long as you truly generate the resolve, any difficulty can be overcome, especially through the compassion of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara.

Final passage: “If there is a fearful accident,” just say: “Homage to Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara” and no one will not escape the accident. Here only one example is taken from the thirty-two manifestations of the “Universal Gate” chapter. In history, in cases of encountering accidents, those who prayed to Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara were all responded to; these cases were all recorded very specifically.

Nowadays, accidents are always lurking on the Earth we live on. Many people ask, if an accident happens, how should we respond? The essence of this concept is that when an accident occurs, we should maintain a stable mindset to cope, not be terrified, and not panic. Because when panicking and trembling in fear, even before the accident arrives, you have already suffered from it. Like cancer, the number of people who actually die from this disease is not many; most die from the fear of the disease. I have witnessed that not less than 90% is due to fear; before the accident or disease comes, you have already died from fear. Is this not unfair to you?

How should we respond when it comes? Haven't we already been taught here? Buddha Shakyamuni told us to recite the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, and Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara will immediately come to save us, it is true. If recited sincerely, there will definitely be a response. Why can Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara resolve accidents, have you thought about this issue? How does Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara resolve accidents? It is based on the compassion cultivated over countless eons; that power is immense! The compassion cultivated by Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara surely surpasses all forty-eight vows in the five lifetimes of practice of Amitabha Buddha. The forty-eight vows canThe achievements after years of spiritual cultivation—could it be that the compassion of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara cannot help prevent disasters? That could never happen!

When praying to Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, we should evoke our compassion so that it aligns with the mind and corresponds with the vow of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara; only then will the effect come quickly. When praying to be reborn in the Pure Land, we should do the same. We must have a mind in harmony, vows in harmony, virtue in harmony, and conduct in harmony with Amitabha Buddha; only then is it unavoidable. Why? Because we only resonate with the Pure Land, not with other worlds. Therefore, when understanding this, we realize that this matter is not unrealistic; only then do we truly have faith. IfWithout faith, with doubt, even the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are affected.

What is doubt? Doubt will destroy all trust; only when trust is steadfast can we have health, and the environment around us will not be disrupted or experience accidents. Why? Because the Earth is solid; if the Earth is solid, floods and droughts will not occur, and if the Earth is firm, earthquakes cannot happen. But it will be very problematic if there is suspicion; not believing means suspicion. When doubtful, our body's immune system weakens; when infected, the body cannot resist, and you will fall ill—that is because you lack faith. When faith is gone, mountains, rivers, forests, and seas will soften.no longer stable, mountains collapse, the ground sinks, such scenes will occur, such phenomena are very common nowadays.

What the Buddha teaches us is not superstition. Where do water-related disasters come from? From greed; a greedy mind will lead to water-related disasters. An angry mind will bring about fire-related disasters, droughts are related to fire, and global warming also belongs to fire. What is the cause? It is anger; human anger in the world is very terrible, and it will affect all these disasters.

Foolishness will lead to wind and storm accidents, pride will lead to earthquakes. We do not want earthquakes, so what should we do? Learn humility, learn how to be respectful, and avoid arrogance; those troubles will be immediately extinguished. Arrogance means not willing to yield, while when we should treat others with equality, earthquakes will never happen; everything stems from doubt.

We should build faith, trust ourselves, trust our ancestors, trust traditional culture, trust Buddhist scriptures, and follow medical teachings; then accidents will not happen. When you do not believe, there is no way to resolve anything.

My grandmother said that when she was a child, during idle farming times, she would roll incense (as a side job). She never added any chemicals to the incense, to show respect, because it is an offering item....

--------

Perhaps thanks to making incense with a pure sincere heart, when she was over 30 years old and seriously ill, she was saved by a Bodhisattva (on the street she met an old Buddhist nun who helped heal her illness).

This old lady prepared medicine to cure my grandmother. After taking the medicine, my grandmother recovered from her illness, but since then her spiritual eye also opened; whether it was day or night, she could see another realm that our ordinary eyes could not perceive.

I used to completely disbelieve in theories about the third eye or the yin-yang eye because she always saw things that I could not see, so I always told her: You are mentally ill! And I considered her old-fashioned, feudal, and superstitious…

Later, since I had the good fortune to hear the Dharma and then generated the aspiration to enter the path, I began to understand and appreciate what her yin-yang eyes had seen, because this helped increase my faith considerably.

I would like to recount the reason why I practice Buddhism.

A few years ago, while I was walking on the street, I encountered an eel seller. Seeing them remove the bones and skin of the eels, I felt so distressed... so I decided to buy all the live eels in the basin and release them into the pond in the nearby park.

Since I was little, I have been afraid of snakes, so I am afraid of species that look like them. Therefore, I did not dare to catch the eels in the bag and had to invite my younger sister to come with me to the park, asking her to catch them and release them into the pond for me. Because I was too scared, I only stood back at a distance and watched. Result: After the eels were released into the water, many of them swam close to me, looking healthy, and more than half of them lifted their heads above the water, gathering around me, constantly nodding, respectfully expressing gratitude. I clearly understood their intention, and oddly enough, they did not cluster around my sister even though she was very close to them, but instead swam to surround me and kept bowing.Hello, it took them a really long time to finally leave.

Witnessing this strange scene, at that very moment I was extremely surprised and moved, so moved that tears ran down my face, and I understood what it means: All beings are equal, and objects and humans inherently share the same spiritual nature!

I used to be someone who loved eating meat and always opposed vegetarianism. If there was no meat or fish at a meal, I would firmly refuse to pick up my chopsticks. But after releasing eels, when I returned home, my mind had changed; I was no longer interested in eating meat. I began studying Buddhist scriptures to better understand the wonders of life and quietly thanked those eels for leading me to Buddhism.

At first, I read the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, and from then on, on the ten vegetarian days each month (the 1st, 8th, 14th, 15th, 18th, 23rd, 24th, 28th, 29th, and 30th), I would recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra.

My grandmother was illiterate and knew nothing about these ten-day retreats, but every time the ten-day retreat came, after I came home from work, she would always ask me: Is today the day you will chant the Kṣitigarbha Sutra?

I asked in surprise:

- How do you know?

She answered:

- How could I not know! I could see that the beings of the ghost realm had gathered in the house since the afternoon, so many that they couldn’t even be counted! They came to listen to you chant the sutra!

There were days when it was already very late and I was still working, she came close and said:

- Stop working, focus on reciting the Kṣitigarbha Sutra! You shouldn’t make those sentient beings kneel and wait for long, it is very sinful and not good!

Moreover, she also vividly described the scene: The ghosts only gathered exactly on the ten fasting days, which were the days I chose to recite the sutra. She saw that among them there were both animals and humans, and the spirits of the deceased wore the clothing belonging to their dynasties.

I used to be obsessed with eating meat and did not like vegetarian food, which caused my grandmother to suffer because she had to kill many animals and create many bad karmas on my behalf.

During the time I was chanting the Earth Store Sutra, all the beings that had been killed for food came to listen to the sutra, including pigs, shrimp, chickens, crabs, fish, etc.

In particular, there was one time when a group of crabs came, waving their big claws, as if to indicate that my family had eaten crabs, and they listened to the sutra with great joy.

Now I no longer recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra; my main practice schedule is the Diamond Sutra, Heart Sutra, Shurangama Mantra, etc… Naturally, there are always beings from other realms gathering to listen.

Studying Buddhism is fundamentally about giving up attachments, yet many people become more attached the more they practice. They cling to grievances with enemies and spirits, fearing that these spirits and enemies will obstruct them, so they want to give up and not continue their practice.

🙏 Master Yin Guang once taught: Don't you know that ghosts and humans always coexist in confusion? There is no place without ghosts! Even if we do not invite ghosts, every home has ghosts. In fact, they are present in numbers hundreds of thousands of times greater than humans. If a person is afraid of ghosts, they should accumulate virtue and do good deeds, and surely the ghosts will develop respect and protect them.

If a person engages in shady deeds, the ghosts will compete to ridicule them, making it difficult to live peacefully.

🙏 If one already knows this clearly, then even when alone in a dark house, one should not harbor any wicked thoughts or evil intentions, let alone commit wrongful deeds…

If a ghost is a benevolent one, it will give way when a person approaches, and only after the person leaves will it occupy the land.

If a malicious ghost (evil spirit) appears, it certainly foretells a great misfortune.

🙏One must know that in front of everyone there are always many (good ghosts or evil ghosts). If you want not to fear ghosts, you should: have a good heart, speak good words, do good deeds; if you achieve that, the ghosts present will turn into guardians for you.

The only concern is: the number of ghosts we can make respect us might not be many, if there are many, that's even better; why fear?

🙏🙏🙏Now I would like to talk about the practice of transmitting sutras and treatises orally. Fortunately, I have come to know of this merit. If possible, you should arrange a place in your building for recitation (promoting the Sutras); by doing so, the surrounding environment will be thoroughly transformed and will have the full capacity to guide people's hearts. It is like the pure land of Mount Putuo of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara…🌸🌸🌸

🙏🙏🙏 The great benefit obtained is: Right in the area where the mantra is pronounced, not only humans, but also insects, all sentient beings there, are exempt from falling into the three evil paths, and can be reborn in the heavens, as humans, or in the Pure Land of the Buddhas.

Because the evenings are very busy, I changed it: I chant the sutras every morning. In my house, I have two devices for continuously playing sutras: a DVD player specifically for playing sutras and mantras, which I place in the Buddha hall, and a player for the “Mantra of Manjushri” which I place on the desk in the study room. I hope it can help sentient beings who come to listen to the sutras to benefit at all times.

When I played the DVD of the sutra, it attracted many sentient beings with karmic affinity to come and listen, among them was a dragon. The first time my grandmother saw its gigantic form, she was horrified and screamed: Oh my! How scary this snake is!

She also described it as lying outside the terrace of the Buddha altar. It even circled back and forth outside the yard as if guarding against thieves. I advised her not to be afraid but to look closely: Does the gigantic 'snake' you described have claws or not? She looked carefully and replied that it did. I explained: That is not a snake, but a Dragon (it is the Dharma-protecting Dragon deity!).

This year, that dragon manifests again; this time it is floating in the air, where the Mantra of Manjushri emanates.

In Buddhist scriptures, it often mentions the Eight Classes of Divinities and Dragons, the Dragon and Deva Protectors, etc., yet people do not understand this meaning.

Before entering parinirvana, Shakyamuni Buddha instructed the Dragon Kings and the deities, reminding them to protect the Dharma. Since more than two thousand years have passed, many still consider this a mythical tale, unbelievable and unrealistic.

I sincerely thank the virtuous wise ones for guiding me on the path of practicing the Dharma, and I also feel grateful for her yin-yang eyes, grateful for the manifestation of the Dragon Heavenly Protector… which has given me full faith in the Buddha’s teachings.

The story I am telling is entirely true; if you don’t believe it, just consider it a myth. As for me, I firmly believe that: This world really does have beings that the human eye cannot see.

🙏🙏🙏There are deities just a few feet above our heads, so we must always observe and examine every arising thought and mental intention of ours.

May the merit of this practice be dedicated to all sentient beings throughout the empty space and the entire Dharma realm; may all fellow practitioners attain enlightenment.

HT. THÍCH TRÍ QUẢNG

According to the Birth Story Sutra, after the celestial horse Kanthaka carried Prince Siddhartha to leave the palace and renounce the world, flying over the Anoma River to another country, he dismounted, cut his hair, and was brought back by Chandaka.

Alone in the forest, the prince suddenly saw a Samana wearing a bow and arrows. The prince hurriedly took off his luxurious silk garment to exchange it for the Samana's robe of the hunter who was pretending to be a monk. But to the Bodhisattva's eyes, he saw that this was Indra appearing to offer the robe to the prince and also to warn the prince that from now on he must be cautious with those wearing the monk's robe on the path in search of truth.

On the path of seeking guidance and learning the Dharma, after attaining the Four Absorptions and the Eight Concentrations from the two ascetics Kamala and Uddālaka Rāmaputta, the prince continued his journey in search of the truth. He practiced asceticism to the point of exhaustion, when miraculously, the girl Sujātā arrived just in time to offer milk, helping him restore his health.

Then, the crown prince went down to the Ni Lien River to bathe and wash the piece of cloth used to wrap the corpse that He had picked up nearby. The cloth covering the body of the young girl, who had died so young, made Him contemplate the four elements of a human body subject to the law of impermanence; while alive, she was so beautiful, but as a corpse, she was terrifying. Yet, once born and destined to die, everyone must end their life under the scythe of death, regardless of age, status…

Contemplating the limited lifespan of humans made the prince increasingly weary of the temporary body that exists today and is gone tomorrow. Moreover, when he donned the robe that he had made himself from pieces of cloth covering corpses, it further deepened the prince's awareness that his life along the path of an ordinary being had truly come to an end.

The prince returned to the Bodhi tree and spent 49 days deeply immersed in meditation. He suddenly attained great enlightenment, clearly recognizing the face of the builder of the house of the five aggregates, understanding what created this world, and the existence of all beings.

With the wisdom to see the truth of the three worlds, Prince Siddhartha attained the state of Buddhahood, realizing the knowledge of past lives, the divine eye, and the knowledge of the end of suffering; that is, He accurately perceived the interconnected and coexisting relationships of Himself and sentient beings of all kinds from beginningless time to the present life and into countless future lives.

Therefore, for the Buddha, there is nothing to be sad about, nothing to suffer, fear, or worry over, because He has seen that there is no birth, aging, sickness, or death. The past, present, and future are also "Self," meaning the immortal true mind of humans.

Indeed, according to Buddhism, death is merely the end of the temporary human life in this world, because the conditions that created that existence have reached the time to deteriorate. And death only temporarily ends life, it is not the permanent end of life, as that temporary life will be transformed into another life, taking another form, in another realm, depending on the karma that guides it. And so, living-dying, dying-living of sentient beings from hell, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, gods, and humans continues to revolve according to the chain links of the cycle of rebirth across the six realms of existence. An easy example is, death is like changing into another set of clothes tocontinue performing another play on the stage of the cycle of birth and death.

The original Buddhist sutras also speak of the principle of cause and condition, stating that nothing in this world exists independently. All things and phenomena arise due to causes and conditions, and when these causes and conditions disperse, they cease to exist. From the principle of cause and condition, the Mahayana sutras develop the teachings through which the Buddha discovered the eternal and immortal reality of human beings.

With the understanding of dependent origination according to the ten suchness, the Buddha saw from time without beginning, in the nothingness there still existed being. Therefore, through the practice over countless kalpas, the Buddha gradually transformed body and mind, and often recounted the stories of His past lives. The Buddha said He had been wind, cloud, rock, moss, grass, trees, even animals, and finally He took human form and practiced to attain enlightenment to become the Buddha. That is the process in which He practiced the Bodhisattva path, completely transforming body and mind, and developing perfect wisdom, thereby seeing all dharmas as they truly are and transforming them into His own body, which is the eternal Dharma body.immortal.

And from the realm of great meditation, having attained the state of Supreme Buddhahood, the Buddha returned to human life to teach and save sentient beings.

The girl Su Dà Ta was extremely joyful when she saw the Buddha's solemn and radiant appearance, entirely different from Prince Siddhartha who had previously practiced austerities, thin and emaciated. She could not bear to see the supreme Dharma King wear a robe made from the piece of her servant's funeral cloth. Su Dà Ta hurriedly sewed a new robe to offer to the Buddha. It was truly great merit for her to be the first person to offer a robe to the Buddha right after He attained Supreme Perfect Enlightenment.

And from the Bodhisattva's perspective, Su Dà Ta is precisely the incarnation of the deities descending to the human world to offer robes to the Buddha from the very first step of His journey of teaching and saving beings. This clearly shows that offering robes to the Buddha is closely and intimately connected with the Buddha's extremely noble work of spreading the Dharma and benefiting sentient beings.

Wearing the offering robe made from the sincere and pure devotion of a female lay follower, the Buddha bid farewell to those with affinity for Him at Bodh Gaya to go to the Deer Park to save the five brothers of the Kinh Tran Nhu family. The Buddha, radiant in the robe of liberation, enveloped His majestic and virtuous appearance and the serene, perfected demeanor of the Great Awakener, which caused the five brothers of Kinh Tran Nhu to quickly prostrate before Him, even though just minutes earlier, they had harbored delusive thoughts and did not bother to look at Him.

With boundless compassion and infinite wisdom, the Buddha nurtured these five disciples. And the extremely powerful pure energy along with the Buddha's supreme wisdom profoundly influenced the minds of the five Kieu Tran Nhu brothers, helping them all attain the Arhat fruit within just three months.

Since then, although the garden only had six masters and disciples, the radiance of the six Arhats shone so brightly that the 50 young men of the Da Xa sect were so impressed that they immediately aspired to ordain as monks under the Buddha. And miraculously, living in a field filled with the energy of compassion and wisdom, it wasn't long before all 50 young men of the Da Xa sect also attained the fruit of Arahantship. One day, their parents reunited with their children and, seeing their children now adorned with serene and distinguished appearances completely different from before ordination, they also asked the Buddha for permission to ordain. But the Buddha said that it was not yet their time to ordain, so it would be better to be lay followers at home, supporting the Dharma.

With the guidance of 50 disciples who had attained the Thánh quả, their parents offered robes to the Buddha and the assembly. This was the second time the Buddha received robes from lay followers' offerings. And the Buddha instructed 55 arahants (50 from the Dasa lineage and 5 brothers from the Kiều Trần Như lineage), each to go in different directions to propagate the Dharma and help beings.

Donning the robes of liberation offered by devoted lay followers, the venerable arahants, with purity of body and mind, began their journey in spreading the Dharma—a sacred task closely connected to the life of the Shakya monks.

After converting the five brothers Kiều Trần Như, the Buddha went back to the village of Ưu Lầu Tần Loa to convert the three powerful brothers Ca Diếp, who were influential in the heretical sects of that time.

In just one night, the supreme loving-kindness and wisdom of the Buddha transformed the malicious minds intent on killing Him of the three brothers Ca Diếp and their 1,000 disciples. All of them were converted by the Buddha and became His disciples. The next morning, everyone was extremely surprised to see Ma Kiệt Đà suddenly shining brightly, with nearly 1,000 monks in the Buddha’s robes of liberation solemnly and purely walking step by step on the alms round.

The next step in propagating the Dharma, the Buddha went to instruct Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana along with their 200 disciples, at which time the Buddha's assembly had up to 1,250 monks with body and mind adorned, wearing the robe of liberation of the World-Honored One.

From then on, the region of Five Rivers in India bore the footprints of 1,250 Arhats propagating the Dharma on behalf of the Buddha to save sentient beings. Wherever there is the robe of liberation worn by the Buddha's disciples, there resounds the blissful and happy Dharma sound for all people. Robe and Dharma were intimately linked in such a true and proper sense.

According to the Tripitaka, Māyā, the mother of the Buddha, offered the Buddha a robe made of precious silk that she herself had woven. The Buddha refused to accept the robe and told her to offer it to the monks, because the monastic community is a field of merit, and offering to the monks is also offering to the Buddha. Māyā then offered this robe to the Venerable Maitreya.

And three months before the Buddha entered Nirvana, the scriptures also record that a merchant named Fukosha offered a robe to the Buddha. This merchant had previously been the incarnation of the Deva Śakra, who, as a monk, offered the first robe to the Buddha when He was still a prince who had just left Kapilavastu to live in the forest. At the time when the Buddha was about to pass away, this deity once again manifested as a wealthy merchant to offer a robe to the Buddha at the end of His life in spreading the Dharma and saving sentient beings.

On the path of the Buddha's propagation, certainly there were many devotees who made merit by offering robes to the Buddha and the Sangha. But we only briefly mention a few special cases which, according to Mahayana interpretation, the acts of offering robes to the Buddha, or more generally, all events in the life of the Buddha, were prearranged. Sometimes they manifested as Devas, sometimes as gods, kings, officials, wealthy individuals, ordinary people, children, even as murderers like Angulimala, or as menial people collecting dung like Sunita. All such invisible arrangements were made to support Śākyamuni Buddha in proclaiming the Dharma for the benefit of all beings.

The style of the Buddha's robe and that of His contemporaneous disciples worn during their monastic life and in spreading the Dharma to save beings has continued to adorn the body and mind of all monastics who live a virtuous life following the Buddha's footsteps across the five continents and four seas.

Over time, the style and color of the Buddhist robe have changed depending on the country or region where the venerable masters propagated the Dharma, adapting to the culture and daily life of each place. However, in general, those who have gone forth and wear the monastic robes are determined to live a life of pure moral conduct following the model taught by the Buddha, striving day by day to transform their body and mind toward holiness, to cultivate merit and wisdom, to propagate the Dharma everywhere, and to bring joy and liberation to all beings.

Therefore, the robe of the monastic who carries the Dharma passed down by the Buddha is very precious, and the practitioner always cherishes and preserves it to cultivate their moral conduct, body, wisdom, and life.

For lay Buddhists, seeing monastics in the robes of liberation inspires them to think of those with great aspirations seeking Buddhahood, always abiding in the Buddha's teachings and working on behalf of the Buddha to guide and teach others, helping people let go of afflictions, cultivate compassion, joy, and equanimity, abandon evil deeds, and diligently engage in good deeds. With this understanding, lay Buddhists often generate the intention to offer robes to the monks and nuns during the Vu Lan filial piety season as a way to dedicate the merit to their relatives.

Offering robes is very good, but it must be done according to proper practice. The venerable monks, after three months of the Rains Retreat, diligently cultivating the three higher trainings without defilements, with pure body and mind, receive the robes to propagate the Dharma and benefit sentient beings. Lay Buddhists offer robes with pure faith, sincerely directed toward the Triple Gem. Combining the virtue of true practitioners with the pure mind of the devotees, the offering of robes will then accomplish merit.
