Entering His living room, you feel very peaceful and comfortable; you will have that feeling, and you will not want to leave. Although He does not say a single word, you still want to sit a few more minutes, enjoying His energy field. This is exactly the radiant body that Buddhism mentions; in Qigong it is called an energy field, having this field allows you to feel it.

The physical appearance of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is truly a field of benefit for all sentient beings. This field also transforms. As mentioned earlier, differences in individuals, time, place, and circumstances all make you experience wonderfulness, countless wonderfulnesses. This is a natural matter, capable of embracing and nourishing all sentient beings.

If there are sentient beings who recite and contemplate; Recitation means to pronounce the name, like when we recite the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, recite Namo Amitabha Buddha, recite Namo Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva, Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, that is called recitation. To 'think' (niệm) means to remember, not to vocalize, but to think in the mind, to contemplate the Buddha in the mind. Chapter Viên Thông states that remembering the Buddha and contemplating the Buddha means surely seeing the Buddha in the present and future. Remembering and contemplating truly exist in the mind.

Contemplation, contemplation is to have the form of the Buddha or Bodhisattva, either in general form or particular form. The general form is to see the full body of the Buddha or Bodhisattva, the particular form is to see only a part, or to see the fleshly marks, the invisible crown marks, the invisible crown marks on the fleshly marks, or to see the white hair mark, between the eyebrows there are two strands of white hair intertwined, like a pearl. Or to contemplate the hand gestures of the Buddha or Bodhisattva, that is to see the particular form.

There is no need to ask about the Buddha of the present or the past. At present, it refers to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who are living in the world. In the past, we could create statues of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, or paint images of them. Nowadays, the most convenient way is to take photographs. When we see statues of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas very solemnly, our hearts will feel happy. We can take photos, bring them home for worship, and bring images of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas from the temple back home to offer reverence.

They can all eliminate the four grave and five heinous sins of sentient beings. What does that mean? It means that all dharmas arising from the mind can transform your unwholesome thoughts. The four grave refer to the precepts, the four grave precepts: killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, the four grave precepts; committing these four grave sins leads to hell. The five heinous refer to the Avīci Hell sins, the five heinous sins: killing one’s father, killing one’s mother, killing an Arahant, one cannot kill the Buddha because His merit is vast, but causing the Buddha to bleed in His body, that is Devadatta. When he was alive, he wanted to harm the Buddha Shakyamuni, and he knew that every day the Buddha went out for alms, He had to pass through the side of this mountain; he thenA very large rock was rolled down from above. When the Buddha was passing by, he rolled the rock down, intending to crush the Buddha to death. The Buddha's merit was great, and Bodhisattva Vairocana, the protector, at that time used the Vajra club to block the rock, shattering it. A piece of the rock hit the Buddha's foot and caused bleeding; this is called causing the Buddha's body to bleed. Finally, it is disrupting the harmony of the Sangha, which is also considered a sin of Avīci Hell. Therefore, nowadays, destroying Buddhist images is also considered the sin of disrupting the harmony of the Sangha. Today, we take on the appearance of monastics, living in this society; if we do things that are not according to the Dharma, causing society to criticize Buddhism, vilify Buddhism, and insultBuddhism, we have committed a sin. Therefore, the fourfold assembly of disciples should always respect the face of Buddha Shakyamuni, and not let Buddha Shakyamuni lose face. The ancients taught that we should apply gold to the face of the Buddha; that is a merit. Strictly following the teachings, so that others praise the Buddha and revere the Buddha, that is already like applying gold to the face of the Buddha. If we act improperly, still being selfish and self-serving, still attached to greed, anger, ignorance, and pride, still harming others for our own benefit, then it is like smearing turmeric paste on the face of the Buddha, causing society to harbor resentment toward Buddhism, to have a mind of slandering Buddhism, thus leading to ruin. Therefore, it destroys the image of Buddhism,The five heinous crimes lead to falling into the great hell of Avīci, with very severe retribution. We often see statues of the Buddha; the 32 marks of the Buddha—what do they mean? It is necessary to understand that the 32 marks are karmic results, 32 kinds of meritorious deeds that bring about retribution, which can be looked up in the great Buddhist dictionary. Previously, I gave lectures on the Diamond Sutra; in the 'Commentary on the Diamond Sutra' by layman Jiang Wei Nong, it is explained very clearly: the karmic causes of the 32 marks, each and every one, are described in detail. There are 80 forms of physical beauty; the Buddha's tongue sticks out and can cover the whole face, called the Great Square Tongue Mark. What is the retribution? It is not speaking falsely for countless lifetimes. The Buddha explained in the sutra that if a person can refrain from false speech for three lifetimes, the tongue...can lick the tip of the nose, sticking out the tongue to lick the tip of the nose is three lifetimes without false speech. The Buddha in every lifetime did not speak falsely, therefore His tongue is very thin, and when stuck out it can cover the entire face. Good appearance is achieved through cultivation; the Buddha manifested 32 excellent physical marks and 80 beauties, teaching us that we must cultivate good deeds, and if the deeds are good, there will be good results. A person with a good heart will have a good appearance, good actions will make the body healthy, the body and mind are the representatives of our cultivation. Whether you truly practice, and how you practice, can be seen through your appearance and your body; there is no need to ask anything, just look and you will know. Your practice is reflected on your face, in the placeYour behavior, how could you deceive others? Therefore, people often recite and contemplate the image of the Buddha. What does that mean? It means the 16 contemplations mentioned in the Sutra of Contemplation on Infinite Life. You can truly practice; truly practicing means admiring the Buddha, respecting the Buddha, cherishing the Buddha, and learning from the Buddha. You must be like him; then your four heavy offenses and five grave offenses will be resolved, and you will be freed from the three evil paths, never to fall into them again.

According to one's desire, one can often be reborn in the Pure Land until attaining Buddhahood. This refers to benefits; depending on one's wish, if I want to go to the Western Pure Land, I will certainly be fulfilled. Being often reborn in the Pure Land until the day of becoming a Buddha is the benefit of the bodily actions of a Buddha.

* Continuing with the third type, the third type is the benefit of karma. Third, advising the father to practice the Samadhi of Buddha Recitation. That is to advise all sentient beings to practice the method of Buddha Recitation, using what method to advise? He advised his father, the father-son relationship being very close, the father and son having a close bond, he advised his own father to practice this method, surely it is the supreme method. The supreme, excellent method, offering to parents, using which method to offer to parents? The method of Buddha Recitation, he did not advise practicing any other method, but to practice the Samadhi of Buddha Recitation, setting an example for us to observe, therefore, the Buddha appeared in this world, there are three types of benefits.of body, speech, and mind.

Below is the explanation; The King asked the Buddha, the Buddha said, the fruit and virtue of the Buddha, as the true nature, the first meaning of emptiness, why do we not see the disciples act in this way?

This is the true accomplishment of the Tathāgata's fruit ground, why does the teacher not instruct his students to practice it?

The Buddha told the King, the fruits and virtues of the Buddhas have countless profound realms, supernatural abilities, and liberation, which are not realms that ordinary people can achieve, therefore he advised the King to practice the samadhi of Buddha mindfulness.

This is something we cannot be unaware of: the true suchness, the ultimate meaning of emptiness; understood. Who can realize this state? The dharmakaya of a bodhisattva can realize it. Why is that? Because they have abandoned all deluded thoughts, attachments, and even habitual tendencies of clinging; what remains is only the beginningless ignorance that has not yet been eradicated. Their practice is precisely the true suchness, the ultimate meaning of emptiness. Where is it? It is in the adornment of the true reward, not in the Ten Dharma Realms, and certainly not in the six paths. That is why the Buddha spoke very well to his father: The fruition of the virtues of the Buddhas, with countless profound realms, supernatural powers, and liberations, all manifest inRetribution manifests, where does it appear? It manifests where sentient beings have perception, where Buddhas and Bodhisattvas respond; these are all the Dharmakaya of Bodhisattvas, manifesting and transforming in the boundless dharma realm, in the space realm, in the ten dharma realms within the Buddha-nations, for the sentient beings of the ten dharma realms, bringing the three kinds of benefits as previously explained: helping sentient beings eliminate sins, helping sentient beings obtain merit, helping sentient beings dispel delusion and awaken to enlightenment, helping sentient beings return to their own nature; this is not the realm of ordinary people. The ten dharma realms, the four noble dharma realms, are also considered ordinary, they are beyond the mundane, they have not yet accomplished it, let alone the six realms within the mundane. Therefore, the Buddha advised the king to practice the Samadhi of Buddha recitation. Why is that? Because recitationBuddha samadhi is firm, skillful, swift, easy to practice, and its attainment is unparalleled. If the habitual afflictions are not yet eradicated, as long as at the moment of death you truly subdue them, the afflictions will temporarily not take effect, then one can be reborn in the Pure Land. One mind subdued, ten minds subdued, this person will be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Being born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, the habitual afflictions will never recur, which is very difficult. Moreover, in the Western Pure Land, whether ordinary or holy, those reborn in the lower grade enjoy the benefits of the Abhijñā wisdom. Truly inconceivable, the Master has offered this unsurpassable supreme Dharma.Parents, advise parents to practice cultivation. Also, advise all sentient beings who have affinity; what is called having affinity? They are willing to believe, willing to make vows, willing to act, that is called a person with affinity. A person with affinity is certain to be saved in this lifetime.

Again, the Buddha instructed the father that all sentient beings in the midst of birth and death, if they practice the mind of recollecting the Buddha, will also be thus subdued by it, and their recollection can be connected without interruption, assuring rebirth before the Buddha. Once they attain rebirth, they can immediately transform all evils into great compassion.

This passage is mentioned in the Sutra of Observing the Buddha Samadhi. The Buddha spoke to his father that all sentient beings in the cycle of the six realms of rebirth, birth and death here refer to the cycle of the six realms. The mind that recollects the Buddha is also like this; sentient beings are within the cycle of birth and death. The revolving mind creates the karmic cycle, and the core of the revolving mind is the attachment to self. In the scriptures of the Dharma Character school, it is explained very clearly that the Manas consciousness (Mātṛkā) is a firmly attached part of the Ālaya consciousness, Ālaya. This deluded mind is very large, attaching to a part, considering that part's form as self, giving rise to the view of self. After this mindfulness arises, it firmly clings without cessation.To endure letting go. In Buddhism, it is said that the day one is able to let go, one has truly turned back, is able to return to one's true nature, and can achieve Buddhahood; but if one does not turn back, one cannot. This sentence is easy to say but very difficult to practice. Why is that? Because without clearly understanding the true reality, one cannot turn back. Only by clearly and distinctly understanding the true reality, and truly letting go, can one then immediately enter into one's true nature. In the Theravada tradition, one may attain the fruit of Sotapanna; in the Mahayana, among the 51 stages of a Bodhisattva, a person may attain the stage of Stream-entry. Stream-entry, although very low, certainly progresses step by step without any regression. Why is that? Because Stream-entry is the attainment of the position of non-retrogression.In other words, this person only progresses, with the speed of progress varying. This is related to diligence; if one is vigorous and diligent, progress will be fast, whereas if one is negligent, progress will be a bit slower, but there will certainly be no regression. Beings in the cycle of birth and death are like this.

The clinging to self is strong, and greed, anger, and delusion arise simultaneously with self-clinging. Firm attachment is called self-view, and self-attachment will arise according to self-view. This self-attachment is greed, self-pride is anger, partly anger, and finally delusion; observe self-attachment, self-pride, and delusion. The three poisons of affliction—greed, anger, and delusion—arise simultaneously with self-view, so the Manas consciousness often follows the four great afflictions. We cannot deny that as long as consciousness has not been transformed into wisdom, the four great afflictions still remain. Until when do they remain? They still exist in the Buddha realm within the ten realms. This issue is very serious and cannot be transformed by any means.okay.

Tathagata has skillful means; this section refers to our effective use of skillful means. What is the Dharma of skillful means? It is precisely a six-syllable name mantra, a truly powerful practice, where continuously reciting the name for 24 hours without interruption allows a person to replace self-views, self-attachment, self-pride, and self-ignorance with a single name. In Vajrayana, a six-syllable great bright mantra is used instead. The practice of Master Zhang Jia is precisely the six-syllable great bright mantra, recited continuously for 24 hours without interruption. When receiving guests, we study Buddhism with him in the same way; when he received me, it often lasted for two hours. Master Vajra perseveres,We saw His mouth moving but there was no sound, He was reciting a mantra, what mantra was He reciting? Om Mani Padme Hum. He recited the mantra with His mouth, made mudras with His hands, and visualized in His mind. He also passed this mantra on to me, telling me to recite it often. I asked Him, what is the meaning of this mantra? He taught me. 'Om' represents the body, 'Mani' is the lotus; we also see in the scriptures it is translated, 'Mani' is lotus, 'Mani' means preservation, this is the preservation in Tibetan, 'Hum,' the final syllable, means mind. Put together, body - lotus - preservation - mind, this is Indian grammatical structure, according to Chinese grammar it is preservation of body and mind, mind isThe mind is like a lotus. The lotus grows out of the mud but is not tainted; the mud represents the six realms, and being tainted means being defiled. The lotus blooms above the water, while the stem is in the water; the water symbolizes the four noble realms, and the Pure Land is precisely the Method of Surpassing With Remainder. The lotus blooms on the top, free from both defilement and purity, which is the Realm of True Reward Adornment. Look at the mud; the lotus roots grow in the mud, which symbolizes the six realms—defilement. The stem grows in the water; it is not in the mud, but in the water, which symbolizes purity. The flower blooms on the water surface, signifying the Ultimate Truth Realm. I just understood how profound the meaning of this mantra is! The mind does not leave the mouth, and the mouth does not leave the mind; every thought is considered.Our body and mind are like a lotus flower, not only are they not contaminated by the Six Realms, but even the Four Holy Beings of the Dharma Realm are not contaminated. Think about how wonderful this meaning is, contemplate it in your mind. In our Pure Land school, we use 'Namo Amitabha Buddha.' This single phrase also consists of six syllables. What do these six syllables mean? 'Namo' means to take refuge, meaning to submit your life, 'A' means infinite, 'Di' means measure, 'Buddha' means awakened. 'Infinite Awakening' is the True Suchness of your own self. 'Amitabha Buddha' is the True Suchness of your own self, taking refuge in Infinite Awakening, submitting your life to Infinite Awakening. You see, the meaning is like that, so you must understand this meaning. Infinite Awakening is your original possession, not something to seek externally.Outside. In the 'Khởi Tín Luận', Master Mã Minh spoke very well: 'Fundamental enlightenment is inherently present; non-enlightenment is inherently absent.' What is non-enlightenment? The Ālaya-consciousness is non-enlightenment. Ālaya is the master that creates the ten dharma realms; the ten dharma realms arise from it and manifest from it. The ability to manifest is illusory, so what is manifested does not truly exist. Therefore, 'All phenomena are illusory.' The faculties are illusory; the true is the self-nature. Infinite Enlightenment is the true, eternal, and unchanging. We should turn back, should turn back and rely on Infinite Enlightenment; turning back is originally Infinite Enlightenment itself. Therefore, this phrase means teaching us to abandon the cyclical mind of samsara, and to generate the thought of Buddha; using the thought of Buddha to replace the mind engaged in the cycle of birth and death.The six paths, that is correct. We have been studying Buddhism for many years, and we basically understand this principle: 'all dharmas arise from the mind and thoughts'; we just need to transform that mind. Therefore, all dharmas are determined by the state of mind. We should not rely on others; we must trust ourselves. Buddhism talks about Faith, which is completely different from other religions. Other religions, first you must believe in the true god, believe in the true master; this is the first unconditional point. In Buddhism, the first unconditional point is to believe in yourself. Master Ngau Ich's lecture in the Essentials Explanation is very good: first is to believe in yourself, second is to believe in the Other, but what is this 'Other'?People here only point to the Buddha. We practice Pure Land, believe in Amitabha Buddha, believe in Shakyamuni Buddha. First, we must believe in ourselves; if we do not believe in ourselves, believing in the Buddha is useless, the Buddha cannot help. In Mahayana teachings, the Buddha teaches us a lot, so we must be certain that we are originally Buddhas ourselves; the ancestors also taught us this. We must believe in our original nature, which is fundamentally good. All unwholesome things are habitual traits; unwholesomeness is the cyclic mind, while original goodness is the Buddha mind. You are originally a Buddha. The reason you are in this predicament today is because you are deluded and have lost your self-nature; it is not a true loss, just delusion. You do not know that you have original goodness.not knowing that one is originally a Buddha. These words are all things that the Buddha taught us in the Mahayana scriptures, we must truly understand them clearly and transparently.

You look at what the Buddha teaches us in the passage below: “đản năng hệ niệm bất chỉ, định sanh Phật tiền,” this refers to those who practice the Pure Land method. What does hệ mean? It means to record in the heart, we call it remembering, in the mind do not think of anything else, thinking of other things leads to the cycle of six realms; if you are mistaken, you should remember Amitabha Buddha, then you are doing it correctly. This concentrated remembrance in the mind must not be interrupted; for 24 hours, truly have the Buddha in your heart, truly have Amitabha Buddha. Daily practice, prostrating to Amitabha Buddha, at least 300 bows each day, this is also a very good form of exercise; recite Amitabha Buddha with the mouth, there is concentrated recitation, there is scattered recitation. Concentrated recitation is the practiceMorning and evening practice, the morning practice should at least involve reciting 3,000 Buddha names; not too many. If you have more time, not much work, not busy, it would be best to be able to recite 10,000 Buddha names. Before reciting the Buddha names, it is best to read the Infinite Life Sutra once, or you can read the Amitabha Sutra, both are fine. If there is a lot of time, read the Infinite Life Sutra. Have firm faith, without the slightest doubt, and a sincere aspiration to be reborn in the Pure Land. The time spent reading the sutra can be shortened; reading the Amitabha Sutra is enough, the Infinite Life Sutra is too long. If our understanding of the Western Pure Land is still unclear and incompleteMany people still cannot completely eliminate enchantment, so they should read the Infinite Life Sutra. In the Infinite Life Sutra, the Buddha speaks very clearly; reading it gradually over a long period will help you understand the principle here. When you really have no doubt at all, then read the Amitabha Sutra, no need to read the Infinite Life Sutra anymore. Why is that? Upholding the Buddha's name is the main practice, and you should understand this. Apart from the two daily sessions of morning and evening practice, the other times are called scattered periods; when you think, it is considered recitation. There will come a day when throughout the full 24 hours, the Buddha's name naturally does not stop. Congratulations, your practice has become stable, your afflictions in thinking and perception are gone, and having reached this level of practice, you are certainly no longer controlled.By controlling mental afflictions, although they are not completely eliminated, they do not arise in effect; when your practice reaches this level, you will attain peaceful rebirth. Whenever you wish to depart, Amitabha Buddha will come to take you, and you will feel that beings in this world are very pitiful, facing too many calamities, making you want to stay in this world to help them. Alright! Nothing to worry about. The calamities of this world are many, and even if calamities are right in front of you, you will still be safe and unharmed. Why is that? Because of differing collective karma. People with collective karma face disasters, but you do not have this collective karma, so Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will bless you, the Dharma-protecting spirits will protect you, enabling you to help everyone. The cause and condition for assistance.When all sentient beings are gone, your work is done, you will go to the Pure Land world.

Before being born as a Buddha, look at these words, they are used to affirm so strongly, so that you no longer have any doubt at all.

Once one attains rebirth in the Pure Land, even though it is the lower grade of birth to dwell with both ordinary beings and sages, one can still transform all evil into Great Compassion. It thoroughly cuts off evil and cultivates goodness, thoroughly transforms delusion into enlightenment. When does this happen? When one is born into the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, even though it is the lower grade of birth to dwell with both ordinary beings and sages, it is still the same. Truly, it is beyond comprehension! Achieving Great Compassion indicates that it is not the Lesser Vehicle; the Lesser Vehicle does not possess Great Compassion. From this, it shows that the Western Pure Land is Mahayana. Śrāvaka and Arhat, when born into the Pure Land, also achieve great compassion, the minds of these beings immediately open up, expressing unconditional great compassion, and the same essence as great benevolence.

arises naturally from its own nature, that is the majestic vow power of Amitabha Buddha's blessings.

The venerable elder teaches us that above, the Greatly Compassionate and Filial Worthy Buddha advised his father, only encouraging the practice of Buddha recitation. This idea is very profound; this section requires us to comprehend it deeply. Look at how Shakyamuni Buddha saved his father, not mentioning other practices, only advising him to recite the Buddha's name. This shows that among countless Dharma practices, none are not outstanding, but ordinary beings cannot cultivate them; the Mahayana practices are truly unsurpassed. Why did the World-Honored One not let his father practice other methods, not advise him to meditate, not advise him to recite mantras, not advise him to study the teachings, but only advise him to recite?Buddha. We should consider this. Only the Dharma practice of solely focusing on Buddha recitation is the most suitable, and relying on the practice of Buddha recitation, one can surely attain rebirth. Being reborn in the Western Pure Land is precisely becoming a Buddha; even if one has not yet attained Buddhahood in common practices, or has not yet attained it in expedient practices, one will certainly attain Buddhahood in this lifetime, achieving infinite longevity, with a long lifespan, surely fulfilled. Moreover, due to deep-rooted virtuous causes and karma, upon reaching the Western Pure Land, one does not change to any other Dharma practice, nor wishes to practice any other method, but only recites the name to the end, quickly becoming a Buddha! Why is this? This person has attained the Samadhi of Buddha recitation. The Buddha taughtIt is taught very extensively in Mahayana doctrine: “Calling the Buddha in Samadhi, Samadhi at the center of the king,” do you still remember this phrase? Samadhi is meditation. Calling the Buddha in Samadhi is the king among Samadhis, nothing is more superior, gaining Samadhi, Samadhi can give birth to wisdom; the king of Samadhis is the one who has wisdom, surely the wisdom of Prajñā is perfectly fulfilled. Once there is wisdom, all Buddhas of the ten directions and three times have already spoken countless and limitless Dharma gates, hasn't this person understood them all? The spiritual power of the Buddhas Tathāgata, limitless virtues and capabilities, isn't it fully present at the same time? This is truly the shortcut to become a Buddha. Where else would one find this Dharma gate?Although in China it is very popular and there are many people who recite the Buddha's name, how many truly understand this principle and genuinely aspire to cultivate? Truly aspiring to cultivate means being able to let go of all attachments, only then is it called genuine aspiration. Your mind is truly purified, truly wondrous in function; after it becomes wondrous in function, next comes benefiting others, helping other people. If you have not been able to let go, regarding the principle of ultimate truth, you still have not fully comprehended it, and therefore cannot let go. Truly comprehending, truly understanding clearly, knowing that all the scriptures and teachings ultimately come down to a single Buddha's name; one only needs to recite this name until it is fully understood. Fully understood to what extent? Fully understood to the Self-Nature.All scriptures, worldly and transcendental dharmas, there is not a single dharma that you do not understand.

When one attains rebirth in the Pure Land, one can then transform evil into good. Above, it was mentioned that one can change all evil into great compassion; in this passage, it again says that one can transform evil into good. The wondrous and skillful means of Buddha recitation are manifestly limitless. Master Yin Guang taught people to paste the character 'death' on their foreheads. This sentence emphasizes that one should think constantly of their own death. I often teach people to regard today as the last day of their life in this world; if so, what could there be that one cannot let go of? If one still has tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next year, or years to come, then the burdens and entanglements will continue to be numerous, the mattersThis entanglement brings you no benefit whatsoever. Why is that? Because it is an entanglement in birth and death. If we knew today was our last day, then let's think about what we should do today. Besides reciting the Buddha's name, I would do nothing else. Think about it, isn't it so? Wholeheartedly aspire to be reborn in the Pure Land. I have a compassionate heart, I have a sympathetic mind; seeing sentient beings suffer in this world, including my own relatives, I truly wish to help them. But now I cannot, my power does not follow my will. After I go to the Western Pure Land and see Amitabha Buddha, I can become the Bodhisattva Achyutya.With wisdom and being blessed by Amitabha Buddha, can one be reborn immediately? Yes! You can return immediately, and when you return, you will be like the Buddha, possessing wisdom, spiritual powers, dharma force, and skillful means. Then you can go help everyone. If you do not return, you cannot help at all. By truly understanding the reality of this principle, you will not let the Buddha's name leave your mouth, and your mind will no longer be entangled with trivial matters. Every thought will be Amitabha Buddha. It is truly beyond comprehension; only then can one truly penetrate the wondrous efficacy of reciting the Buddha's name.

Let's continue with the following passage. Throughout the process of ascending the capitals, the World-Honored One advised his father to practice mindful recitation of the Buddha's name, knowing that all sentient beings are caught in the cycle of birth and death, and the mind concentrated on chanting the Buddha's name does not waver. The Buddha's intended meaning regarding the practice of mindful recitation of the Buddha's name refers specifically to the maintenance of the Buddha's name among the four types of recitation.

These are four ways of chanting the Buddha's name in the Pure Land Buddhist scriptures. The four ways of chanting the Buddha's name are not the same. Which way is the most convenient? Which way is the most certain? Which way is the fastest? Surely, those who chant the Buddha's name will ask like this. Which way should we choose? The Small Amitabha Sutra and the Infinite Life Sutra both mention reciting the Buddha's name. Therefore, below, it is said that there are four ways to chant the Buddha's name. The first is reciting the Buddha's name, the second is contemplating the Buddha's image while chanting, the third is visualizing while chanting the Buddha's name, and the fourth is reciting the Buddha's name by realizing its true nature. The order arranged here, in many other scriptures, places reciting the Buddha's true nature first and reciting the Buddha's name last. Here, Elder HoangLaypeople recite the Buddha's name at number 1. Why is that? Because of the teachings of the original sutra.

Below we explain the four ways of reciting the Buddha's name. The first is chanting the Buddha's name, which is the main principle of this sutra, reciting the name of Amitabha Buddha. Sōng, or principle, here means practice, direction, goal, the main outline. What is the main practice of this method? Our main practice is a six-syllable great name, wholeheartedly chanting "Namo Amitabha Buddha." "Chanting" means uttering the sounds with the mouth. What about "reciting"? Reciting refers to the thought, the contemplation in the mind. Chanting is reading with the mouth, reciting is reading with the mind, mind and mouth as one, external and internal are unified; this is called true mindfulness of Buddha. Below is a citation of the teaching of Master Shandao.Master Thien Dao teaches that there is only the path of practice by reciting Amitabha Buddha. The path here is a close path, the closest path, the nearest path for ordinary beings to become Buddhas, the shortest in time, the most effective, which is to focus solely on reciting Amitabha Buddha. 'Focus' here means single-mindedly reciting, without any distracting thoughts, called single-minded recitation. If there are other distracting thoughts, it is wrong. Bodhisattva Giac Minh Dieu Han, in the book 'Xac Chi of the Western Land,' teaches us how we should recite Buddha: without doubt, without distracting thoughts, without interruption. The teachings of this Bodhisattva and that of Bodhisattva Dai The Chi, given in the Lăng Nghiêm Dharma assembly, are completely the same.Chí is the assistant teacher of Amitabha Buddha in the Western Pure Land, and Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta are the assistants and senior disciples of the Bodhisattvas in the Western realm, similar to our class leader today. They teach us the method of Buddha recitation. “To fully gather the six faculties, maintain pure and continuous mindfulness,” these are the two lines of eight characters. What does 'fully gather the six faculties' mean? In modern language, fully gathering the six faculties means letting go of worldly attachments. Letting go of everything: the eyes do not see, the ears do not hear, the nose does not smell, the tongue does not taste—this also means the six faculties let go of the six sense objects, without contact. To fully gather the six faculties, the six faculties turn inward and no longer reach out to external worldly matters. Only after that can you achievebe able to continuously practice wholesome mindfulness. Wholesome mindfulness is pure mindfulness; if you have a doubtful mind, your mind is not pure, if your mind has distractions, it also cannot be pure. You can understand the word 'pure' as meaning without doubt, without distractions. 'Continuously' means without interruption, similar in meaning to Bodhisattva Enlightened Bright and Wonderful Virtue. It is very difficult for us to achieve—not doubting, not distracted, not interrupted—which is really not easy to practice. Why is that? Because we cannot bring our minds under control. To be a scholar, to practice diligently, the prerequisite is to be able to bring our own mind under control. Mencius said, as Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta once taught. Mencius said: 'The way of learning and knowledge is selfless, seeking…'“To cultivate the mind and be joyful,” means that being a scholar involves nothing else, just restraining the mind so that it doesn't project outward anymore is enough. Consider this: the eyes see forms, the ears hear sounds, all are conditions directed outward. Now, if they no longer direct outward, the ears do not hear sounds, the eyes do not see forms. Restrain it, restrain it, then your mind becomes pure; that is called restraint. One must understand restraining the mind; it does not mean not seeing, not hearing. You can see, you can hear, but the mind is not entangled. True practice, the ancients gave a very good example: “seeing but not seeing, hearing but not hearing.” Think about what that means. I see,See clearly and transparently, so why say that you do not see? Because you see without attachment, this practice has nothing to criticize, it is the utmost supreme practice. You see, you hear, but you do not discriminate, you do not cling, that means you have subdued your mind. Seeing is discrimination, is clinging; hearing is discrimination, is clinging; your mind is completely oriented outward, you attach to the six external sense objects, what does attaching to the six external sense objects mean? That is the mind of birth and death, that is the mind of samsara. Without being attached to external objects, turning inward to illuminate the fundamental nature, that is the method of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. How does Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva practice?Success? It is precisely reflecting on the true nature of written words; the nature becomes the supreme path. Bodhisattvas use the ear faculty; the ear faculty does not turn outward toward external conditions, but inward. Inward? Inward is the self-nature, and self-nature is pure. Using the ear faculty is better than using the eye faculty; why is that? Because with the eye faculty you can only see three directions, you cannot see behind, you cannot see above or below; if we say six directions, it can only see three directions. The ear faculty is very good; the ear faculty can hear six directions, front, back, left, right, up, and down. Therefore, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva uses the ear faculty. Regarding worldly sounds, what is practiced? No discrimination, no attachment, no arising of mind, no disturbance.Recitation, that is called true cultivation, this is very difficult, not easy at all. Pure Land Buddhism has taught us the method, everything returns to Amitabha Buddha, the six senses in the realms of the six dusts, all are transformed into Amitabha Buddha, this is easy, very easy, besides Amitabha Buddha there is nothing else, that is the practice that has become established, going deeper leads to single-minded concentration without distraction. Therefore, Master Thien Dao's teaching is very good, Master Thien Dao is the reincarnation of Amitabha Buddha, his teachings are precisely the teachings of Amitabha Buddha, truly the near path, really quick, among the eighty-four thousand methods, no method can compare, Avatamsaka, Lotus, Zen, Tantric all cannot match. In the book Pure LandIn the Records of the Sages, also seen in the Accounts of Rebirth, there are indeed many people who have practiced and experimented with us, serving as models for us, achieving success in three years. Reciting the Buddha's name until the third year, they know the time to depart; the Buddha comes to guide them, without any illness, standing at rebirth, sitting at rebirth, departing freely and at ease in this way, a shortcut path of practice. Ordinary beings in the six realms are truly profoundly deluded, long-term deluded. Saying that one can be reborn in three years, after three years one might die; this Dharma method cannot be practiced, practicing means dying early, people are very afraid, afraid to practice anymore. Why is that? It is because they completely do not understand the teachings, nor the true nature of reality. In this world, even if you live to be 100 years old, you still have todie, can't you die? Being reborn in the Western Pure Land really does not mean dying, you should understand this; you go to the Western Pure Land while still alive, not after death. Can a dead person still speak? That doesn't exist. Look, when a person is about to pass away, they tell you, tell their loved ones, that they have seen Amitabha Buddha coming to greet them, now they will follow the Buddha, very clearly and plainly. This person has gone, no longer needing this physical body, so being reborn in the Western Pure Land does not mean dying, it's rebirth while still alive; there is no such thing as dying and then being reborn. In reality, even in death, one can be reborn. The Dharma of Buddha AAmitabha not only saves humans, but also saves animals, hungry ghosts, and beings in hell, universally saving all sentient beings. If it only saves humans, and cannot save animals, hungry ghosts, or beings in hell, then it cannot be called a skillful means. Beings in the nine realms, as long as you have the affinity to meet them, will be saved, it's just that easy.

Below is an example that says: “Other doors of cultivation lead to liberation from the three realms.” “Other doors” here refer to the eighty-four thousand dharma doors, referring to countless dharma doors, that is, apart from the Pure Land school, or if you take a step further, apart from reciting the Buddha’s name. What is meant by “liberation from the three realms”? “Like an insect born inside a bamboo, it is difficult to get out.” A bamboo has segments, and if the insect wants to go out along a straight path, it must pierce through each segment to be able to crawl out, continuing until it reaches the top and emerges. The word “difficult” here refers to a “difficult path to undertake.” “Reciting the Buddha’s name is like an insect going horizontally out of the bamboo, differing in ease of passing through; this is the horizontal liberation from the three realms.”‘Claiming to practice the way unusually.’ This insect does not need to bore through each segment of the bamboo; it can just bore through the side of the bamboo to get out. It does not need to use the complicated way mentioned above. This is just an example: which way is easy, which way is difficult, this example is very clear. It illustrates the shortcut because it goes straight through, achieving success quickly. Especially by only reciting the name, the shortcut in nearby paths is easy, goes straight, without detours, hence it quickly achieves success. The Amitabha Sutra teaches us that: whether in one day or two days up to seven days, you can see how fast it is. We can see in the book 'The Record of the Holy and Wise in the Pure Land,' during the Song dynasty, Dharma Master Doanh Kha, from the timeHe came into contact with the Pure Land, and after reading the Story of Rebirth, he was very moved. He truly made the resolve to recite the Buddha's name until the end. For three days and three nights he did not sleep, even forgetting to eat. Amitabha Buddha came, and Amitabha Buddha told him that he still had ten more years to live, advising him to diligently recite the Buddha's name. When he passed away, Amitabha Buddha came to guide him. He negotiated with Amitabha Buddha, saying that he did not need the ten more years of life and wanted to follow him immediately. Why? Because his karmic obstacles were too severe, and his afflictions and habitual tendencies were deeply rooted. He feared that if he lived ten more years, he would create countless negative karma and might not be able to be reborn in the Pure Land.Even though you have ten more years of life, you no longer need it, and you will go with me now. Amitabha Buddha has promised. Very well, in three days I will come to pick you up. This is a symbolic act; why didn’t Amitabha Buddha take you right at that moment? Why must it be delayed for three days? I am asking you to tell the assembly in the temple. This is a monk who has broken the precepts, does not observe the monastic rules, and in this temple has a notorious reputation; everyone knows the evil deeds he has done. He chants the Buddha’s name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land because he fears falling into hell in the future. According to his actions, as recorded in the Vinaya, he is completely destined to fall into Avici Hell. He is extremely terrified and asks his friends if there is any way not to be doomed to hell. Is there?someone gifted him the book 'Stories of Rebirth in the Pure Land.' You see, these people who recite Buddha’s name and are reborn do not fall into hell; he generated such a mind, therefore it is said that he feared the suffering of hell, developed the Bodhi mind, and aspired to be reborn in the Pure Land. This mind of generating the aspiration to be reborn in the Pure Land, in the book 'Essential Explanations' by Master Ngau-Ich, it is taught that this is precisely the great Bodhi mind. He did not understand anything; he did not know what is called the Bodhi mind, but he only wholeheartedly aspired to be reborn in the Pure Land. Reflect on this, if the mind aspiring to be reborn in the Pure Land is not sincere, not pure, not equal-minded, can one be reborn? One cannot be reborn! That mind must be the true mind, not the deluded mind. The true mind is the mindBodhi, sincere heart. In the book *Yếu Giải Ngẫu Ích*, the master speaks very well; examples of this kind we can see a lot in the book *Vãng Sanh Truyện*. Among the fellow practitioners present here, there are also some, and if we just pay a little attention, we can recognize it; it is the truth, not false. In recent years, I have lived in Hong Kong more. Hong Kong is very close to Shenzhen; in Shenzhen there is a lay practitioner named Hoàng Trung Xướng, he is 30 years old. After hearing about this Dharma practice, he aspired to experiment for everyone, trying it out himself. He entered retreat for 3 years; in the retreat, he read one set of the Infinite Life Sutra (Kinh Vô Lượng Thọ) every day, and apart from that, he constantly recited Amitabha Buddha's name day and night without interruption. When tired, he would rest.After recovering, he continued reciting; for two years and ten months, he realized it was time to go. Amitabha Buddha came to guide him. It was just two more months to complete three years; he truly departed, without illness, still very young, with an exceptionally good appearance. After cremation, the relics were kept, and now I have enshrined them in a small temple in Shenzhen. People built a stupa for him, and the inscriptions on the stupa were written by me. He listened to my Dharma talks for several years, made a vow to perform experiments, and succeeded. I tell you, this is the truth, not deception. Rebirth in the Pure Land is not difficult; the issue is whether you are willing to do it, whether you are willing to let go. The key really lies here: are you willing to let go?Is it possible to let go or not? Letting go is not worrying about anything anymore, it can be good, it can be bad, all the things in this world are let go. Living in this world, living for a day, really remembering a day, every day thinking that this is my last day.

tieu_de: THE IMPORTANCE OF DAILY RECITATION OF MANTRAS OF BUDDHAS AND BODHISATTVAS, METHODS TO BREAK SPELLS, AND FAMILY PRACTICES
tom_tat: 1. Why nowadays is it necessary in practice and study to recite and meditate on additional mantras? **Why is it called 'Trì'?** TRÌ means to keep continuously (to hold) without letting it be lost, without letting it be forgotten, that is, to thoroughly master it.
noi_dung:
THE IMPORTANCE OF DAILY CHANTING THE MANTRAS OF BUDDHAS AND BODHISATTVAS, THE METHOD TO BREAK SPELLS, AND HOW TO CONSECRATE

1. Why nowadays is it necessary in practice to recite and chant additional mantras?

Why is it called 'Trì'? 'TRÌ' means to keep continuously (to hold) so that it is not lost, not forgotten, which means to be thoroughly familiar with it.

**Why is it called Chú?** CHÚ, in full, is Thần Chú, which is a secret phrase. For convenience, it is simply called “Chú”. Some people do not understand and say: Thần Chú is created by the way of the gods. That is incorrect, it is a mistake. The word THẦN here means “magical power, spiritual insight, transformation”. The word CHÚ is also referred to as CHÂN NGÔN. The Thần Chú verses spoken by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have unimaginable power and merit. We should distinguish between TRÌ Chú (reciting Chú) and NIỆM Chú (mindful chanting of Chú).

**Recitation of Mantras: **That is, a mantra must be repeated continuously and fluently to be called recitation. Holding a book or paper to read it aloud is called reading or chanting, not recitation.

**Reciting a Dharani or Chanting a Mantra:** It means just glancing over it once. For example, the “Shurangama Ten Dharmas” in the morning can be recited just once, without a second or third recitation. The Sanskrit term for a mantra is Dhārani (Đà ra ni, Đà la ni), in Chinese it is translated as Zong Chi, and in English it is called Mantra. Because it encompasses countless dharmas, it is called “Zong” (comprehensive). Because it holds countless meanings, it is called “Chi” (to hold). A mantra carries a meaning that encompasses (comprehensive) all dharmas and preserves (holds) noble thoughts from the countless wonderful meanings of the mind. The phrase “Mantra” represents the entire “mind and intention” of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas toward sentient beings. The meaning of a mantra is extremely secret.No one can understand it, except for the deity (the owner) of that Mantra and the Buddhas who know it.

**The Mantra of the Buddha is different from that of the heretical paths**: The Buddha's mantra has the power to destroy falsehood and establish righteousness, eliminate evil karma, dispel wrong and disturbing thoughts, generate wisdom, increase merit and virtuous foundations, prevent sins, save oneself and help others escape demonic calamities, especially to save spirits to attain liberation in a marvelous and rare way, swiftly leading people from the mundane realm to the sacred realm, closely connecting and resonating spiritually with the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, Holy Spirits, and achieving spiritual fruition. On the other hand, the mantra of the heretical paths only harms people and beings, brings disasters to people, and causes one to fall into the three evil realms after death. Although mantras cannot be explained in words, if one sincerelyIf the mind sincerely and respectfully upholds it, it will achieve miraculous effects beyond reckoning. It's similar to when someone drinks water – only that person can feel whether it is warm or cold; others cannot know, understand, or believe it. The efficacy of reciting a Mantra is the same way; only the person who diligently recites the Mantra can truly know how effective it is! Usually, a single Mantra can encompass an entire Sutra. This is enough to understand that the power and merit of the Mantra spoken by the Buddha are beyond comprehension.

Why must one recite and chant mantras: chanting the Buddha's name and sutras tends to bring inconceivable merit, while reciting mantras tends to bring inconceivable spiritual power. Some mantras include merit, spiritual power, and can dispel karmic obstacles, for example, the Great Compassion Mantra and the Shurangama Mantra. If someone regularly practices these mantras without doubt, they will be protected in body and mind and can dispel karmic obstacles, leading to peace in this life. Highly accomplished monks in Vietnam or China in the past, in their practice besides the effort in Buddha recitation and sutra chanting, also recited additional mantras, for example, Venerable Thich Thien Tam, Venerable Tuyen Hoa, Venerable Quang Kham....

Nowadays is the time of the degenerate Dharma. We are all ordinary people with deep karmic obstacles. If one recites the Buddha's name but does not achieve single-minded concentration, is confused, or has not truly practiced continuously, one will not yet receive the blessings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. This is not to mention that today various kinds of demons, spirits, ghosts, and sorcerers are all waiting to absorb vital energy. Not to mention that because of deep karmic obstacles and vengeful spirits, life becomes chaotic and very difficult for cultivation. If one does not additionally recite mantras but only recites sutras and the Buddha's name, it is very difficult to achieve success; it is very easy to be disrupted, allowing evil energies to rise, and the defilements of the world to awaken bad minds such as anger, lust, greed, and selfishness. ThereforeIt is necessary to chant the mantra to protect the body and mind, eliminate karmic obstacles, and attain peace in this life... In addition, another use of the mantra is to break all kinds of spells and charms. Let us read the following story to understand clearly how to neutralize spells and charms; this story was shared by an anonymous member:

DISSIPATE LOVE SPELLS WITH THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA

"....In the 1960s in Phu Dinh village, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, at that time there were still many fields, houses were still sparse and not developed like now, there was a Buddhist follower, she has now gone to the U.S. She recently said that: that year there was a very famous sorcerer, but he was a sorcerer of a heterodox sect, not from Buddhism. This man practiced very diligently and had magical powers, more than 50 years of cultivation. He came from another village to this one, wanting to show off his powers so that people would respect and make offerings to him. One day, the villagers were performing a ceremony at a small shrine, this shrine was very small but very sacred, so this man came and told everyone"He said: “Is there a temple bigger than this nearby so that I can move the big temple over here for everyone to worship?” When the villagers heard him say this, they all thought he was lying and didn't believe him, but they still showed him a large temple nearby. In the middle of that night, everyone heard a very strong shaking, like an earthquake, and in the morning they naturally saw that the large temple had returned to the exact position of the small temple from the day before. Since then, the villagers greatly respected him and regarded him as a deity. One day, he saw everyone harvesting rice, and he said, “You all go home, don’t harvest here anymore. Tonight, I will harvest it for you.” That night, the villagers again heard the sound of rice being cut, and then in the morning...Every household had rice and grain stored in their own yard, and from then on, this man's fame spread even further. Although he had such supernatural powers, because he did not follow the righteous path, he was still full of lust, anger,.... One day, he passed by a small temple and saw a Buddhist female devotee doing work by sweeping at the temple (she is the one telling this story). Because she was somewhat attractive, the master felt lustful. He went home and used a spell to hypnotize her. At that time, she was sweeping the temple, when suddenly she froze, pulled by a force, and found herself at the house of this sorcerer master, who was sitting on a chair, looking at her and smiling with very lustful eyes. Then,The sorcerer had just gone off to take a bath, and at that moment the spell he had cast weakened for a while, and also due to the merits from the Three Jewels of the Buddhist laywoman, in an instant she suddenly regained her composure, and she was very frightened. Every day, she regularly recites the Great Compassion Mantra. Knowing she was cursed, she found a glass of water nearby, then sincerely, urgently, and wholeheartedly empowered the mantra three times, visualizing the image of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva radiating light into the glass of water (and she could see it). After that, she immediately drank it, and the spell lost its effect, so she returned home. The next day, this sorcerer came to the temple where she was volunteering, knelt down, crying and said to her, 'Miss, who helped you?'Breaking the spell from yesterday, so who is your teacher? Let me meet that teacher, I am very remorseful now, please let me meet that teacher so I can regain my abilities. Over 50 years of cultivation, all the powers I had were lost yesterday. I promise I will not do such things again...” The Buddhist nun then said: “Yesterday, no one helped me remove it, I was only focused on reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva and chanting the Great Compassion Mantra...” The teacher heard this and felt very sad, and he then left that village. From that time on, he completely lost his supernatural powers; over 50 years of cultivation, now all was gone...

Through this story, we can see that a highly skilled master who has practiced for a long time, with just three repetitions of the Great Compassion Mantra, could completely nullify the spell and help the Buddhist devotee escape this peril. This is incomparable to the mediocre masters of today.

So, how to use the Great Compassion Mantra to dispel spells and heal illnesses? There are two methods:

2. METHOD OF BREAKING HARMFUL SPELLS, HEALING ILLNESSES, AND OPENING WISDOM THROUGH MANTRAS

The first method: For those who have already received the empowerment blessings, they can use mudras (I will not go into detail about this in tantric practice). As for regular Buddhists or laypersons who have not received empowerment, they can place a glass of water in front of the image of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva (on the Buddha altar; if there is no Buddha altar, just sincerely practice and recite), then recite the Great Compassion Mantra or the Six-Syllable Seed Syllable Mantra, or keep chanting the Bodhisattva's name (the more recitation, the more effective). While doing so, gaze at the water and visualize the image of the Bodhisattva appearing in the glass, clearly visualizing all details from the limbs to the face, the aura, untilclearly see, then use this glass of water to pour into another glass and respectfully hold it with both hands to drink. While drinking, imagine that this water is ambrosia, drinking it will cure illness, open wisdom...

Method two: If you feel that visualizing in the first method is too difficult, you can visualize as if Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva is standing in front of you, or in front of his image, with a golden halo radiating from between his eyebrows into the water you are sanctifying, while simultaneously reciting the Great Compassion Mantra (or the Six-Syllable Great Brightness Mantra, or the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva). After seeing this, pour another cup of water and respectfully bring it up to drink. As you drink, visualize it as amrita; by drinking it, you will be free from illness and have your wisdom opened...

The method of mantra practice described above is applied to those who already know the mantra; if one does not know the mantra, it is impossible to visualize! Besides breaking spells and curing diseases, it also serves to create protective boundaries, open wisdom, expel demons... If one is ill, taking medicine while practicing the mantra as described will help the illness recover faster (if a monk has high virtue and skill, they may even perform this practice for the patient so that the patient recovers after taking it, without needing to take medicine at all!), and if one is under a spell, practicing the mantra as described will cause the spell to break and rebound to the person who cast it. However, the important thing is to have deep faith in the mantra; if there is a single doubt such asWhether drinking it will completely cure the illness or not, it will not succeed unless you believe that after drinking it, you will definitely be cured. If the illness persists, it is because your karma is still heavy and you need to do more. Then check whether you have maintained moral precepts and practiced the ten wholesome actions. Just examine this way, and with diligence, the illness will gradually disappear. If you want to set up a protective barrier or exorcise demons, just follow the two methods above, the only difference being that instead of drinking, you sprinkle water around the house; wherever you want the barrier to extend, sprinkle the empowered water there. In this protected area, spirits and demons will not be able to enter. Normally, a highly virtuous monk, after blessing the mantra, can perform three empowerments on water, allowing a barrier to be established for one month.up to 1 year, 2 years, ... depending on the virtue and practice of that monk. However, since we are ordinary beings, with weak concentration and not strictly observing the precepts, the power of blessing is still weak, requiring more recitations, and making it difficult to clearly visualize. We may only be able to maintain a protective boundary for 1 to 2 days, so in order to ensure that the boundary remains, it needs to be done regularly.

Those who chant sutras or recite Buddha's name but often experience sleep paralysis lack concentration power, do not have protective deities, or possibly live in places with many spirits or demons, causing restless sleep or continuous disturbing dreams, sometimes even inappropriate dreams... Some people say, I have been chanting Buddha's name and reciting sutras for years, yet my intellect remains dull, and I still have disturbing dreams at night. If a person has strong concentration power, they sleep without disturbing dreams, sleep very well, have good memory, and understand the scriptures as they read... Reciting Buddha's name or chanting sutras without focusing the mind, without sincere respect, and letting the mind be full of distractions, even if recited 1,000 or 10,000 times, is the same. Therefore, it is necessary to perform the Dharma protection ceremony at home.My sleeping place is as above to be at peace in body and mind.

So does that mean it is only by reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara, the Great Compassion Mantra, or the Six-Syllable Great Bright Mantra that one can achieve the above? In fact, it is not only by reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara, the Great Compassion Mantra, or the Six-Syllable Great Bright Mantra that one can achieve the above; if you recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, you can do the same. In the Mahāyāna Mahāsaṃnipāta Kṣitigarbha Ten Revolutions Sutra, it is said that anyone who frequently recites the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, when encountering dangerous calamities, as described in the Universal Gate Sutra, by reciting his name, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will also save them just like Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. You can also use the extermination and concentration mantra.Recite the sacred words or the mind mantra of Kṣitigarbha, and then visualize Kṣitigarbha as described in the two methods above. Or, if you have an affinity with Medicine Buddha, you can recite the name of Medicine Buddha, or recite the Medicine Buddha mantra and do the same, only differing in that you visualize the image of Medicine Buddha. This applies to any tutelary deity or the mantra of any tutelary deity of yours; as long as during recitation you visualize sincerely and see it clearly, it will be effective.

The method of empowering a mantra into a glass of water, besides breaking spells, curing illnesses, and creating protective boundaries, can also be used daily for close ones to drink in order to open their wisdom, eliminate karmic obstacles that hinder their practice, foster connections with the Buddha's path for them, or if your garden or house has many harmful insects and you want them to leave without killing them, you can empower the mantra into water and then spray it on the plants or the animals, gradually they will all leave. Additionally, you can also plant the seed of Buddhahood in them... there are many other benefits, but here we only briefly mention the effects of the mantra, as listing them all would take too long.

then talking about it forever still wouldn't be enough.

**Question: Because of the power of the mantra, at cemeteries or funerals, should one chant the mantra, or should one only recite Buddha's name and chant sutras to give the Dharma as alms?**

Demons are afraid of Buddha recitation and sutra chanting, but not as much as they fear mantra chanting, because reciting sutras and chanting Buddha's name tends toward accumulating merit, while chanting mantras leans toward spiritual power. "...In the past, when Master Tang Sanzang (Tang Xuanzang) went to Western Regions (India) to obtain sutras, historically he actually traveled alone. On the journey, there were many monsters and demons... wanting to absorb his vital essence (not to eat him :3) because he was an adolescent and practiced strict precepts. When he passed through a desert area, demons gathered in groups, surrounded him, and then howled... At this time, Master Xuanzang was very afraid and clasped his hands, loudly reciting the name of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara."then even those demons and ghosts are not afraid, so he calmed his mind and recited the Heart Sutra, focusing on remembering the last mantra, he only recited it once, opened his eyes, and saw no ghosts or demons anymore....” Sometimes when we chant Buddha's name or sutras, we feel a chill in our spine because spirits come close to listen, whereas when chanting mantras, this feeling rarely occurs because the spirits are also afraid, so they only dare to stay outside to listen. If these spirits try to disturb a practitioner, due to the power of the mantra, they will suffer headaches and pain, not daring to come near. At funerals or cemeteries, if one recites a mantra following strict precepts and with powerful chanting, the ghosts and demons are very afraid.Dare to come close; if the chanting monk does not uphold the precepts, even ghosts and demons standing nearby will not be afraid. Therefore, regardless of which practice one follows, strictly maintaining the precepts is very important. Thus, if anyone has a compassionate heart and wishes to offer the Dharma in a cemetery or in a garden, in an abandoned house... it is advisable to play the slow-reading version of the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows Sutra, because spirits, ghosts, and wandering souls really like to listen to this sutra. Additionally, to both deeply penetrate the teachings of the sutra and accumulate merit to dissolve karmic obstacles, one should play the slow-reading version. If one plays the fast chanting version from the monks, spirits also gain merit, but it is difficult to deeply penetrate the teaching and the profound meaning of the sutra, which is why we haveto put the mp3 link of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra reading here so that you can download it and make merit by giving the Dharma

tieu_de: CHANTING: GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA
tom_tat: Dedicate merits, resolve karma, purify mind. Notes before recitation:
noi_dung:
CHANT: GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA

Dedication, clearing karma, purifying the mind

Notes before chanting:

READ THE SUTRA WITH SINCERITY

A novice should have the following attitude when reading the sutra: the three actions of body, speech, and mind must be pure. When the three actions above are calm, merits and wisdom are fully attained.

1. One should sit upright as if sitting before the Buddha. That is the purification of bodily action.

2. Do not speak false words, do not joke around. That is the purification of verbal karma.

3. The mind does not scatter, completely eliminating attachment to objects. That is the purification of mental karma.

When the mind is calm and peaceful, the external environment becomes serene; this is the concordant realization of the mind's source, subtly entering the principle of dharma. When the water is clear, the luster of jade naturally shines; when the clouds disperse, the moon reveals itself. The fulfillment of great vows is like entering the ocean of wondrous meaning. Thorough understanding of the sutra's intention is precisely reaching the high peak of wisdom. If a practitioner wishes to easily achieve success, one must plant Great Vows. When both mind and dharma are forgotten, oneself and all beings in the dharma realm equally enjoy benefit and happiness. Only in this way can one hope to repay the deep kindness of the Buddhas.

PART EXPLANATION

(EXPLANATION OF VERSES)

Until now, many people have extensively preached about the Great Compassion Mantra Sutra, but no one has explained the Great Compassion Mantra itself. Indeed, it is very difficult to explain the Great Compassion Mantra because the sacred text of this mantra belongs to the system of esoteric true words. Now, to explain this mantra, I first present a verse to illustrate the meaning of the mantra:

Great compassion, great mantra reaching heaven and earth

Hundreds, thousands, ten kings rejoice

Great mercy, great compassion can cure illness

With utmost reverence, one beam spreads through the profound heights.

Meaning:

The Great Compassion Mantra has the power to reach both heaven and hell. Anyone who often recites this mantra 108 times a day, doing so for a thousand days, can make the Ten Kings of Brightness rejoice.

The power of Mercy and Compassion in the mantra can heal all kinds of diseases and make the mirror of karma shine brightly.

*The Great Compassion Mantra connects heaven and earth

When you recite this mantra, heaven and earth will tremble, and the entire dharma realm will shake. It reaches the heavens above and penetrates all realms of hell below. Throughout all realms of gods and humans, everyone will feel the resonance and praise the merits.

*One hundred one thousand ten kings rejoice

If you recite this mantra 108 times every day, and continue this practice for a thousand days, which is about 3 years, reciting this mantra continuously for 3 years without interruption, not skipping a single day, no matter how busy you are, then it can make the ten kings who manage affairs in the underworld feel joyful. This means that from King Yama governing the 10th court, along with all sentient beings suffering punishment in the 10 hells, will all feel happy.

*Great compassion can eliminate illness

The power of Compassion and Mercy in this mantra can heal all kinds of illnesses. Why is it called the Great Compassion Mantra? It is because: "Compassion has the power to eliminate suffering." This means that Compassion has the function of removing all the sufferings of sentient beings. As for "Mercy brings happiness," a merciful heart often brings joy to sentient beings. Since this mantra has the ability to reduce suffering and bring joy to all sentient beings, it is called the Great Compassion Mantra. Its primary function is to heal all illnesses. No matter what illness you have, if you recite the Great Compassion Mantra, all suffering and disease will be eliminated.

Some people may wonder: "I have already recited the Great Compassion Mantra, so why am I not healed?"

You have not recovered from illness because you have not fully devoted yourself when reciting. With sincere devotion, you will definitely receive a response when chanting the mantra.

*The most respectful light spreads profoundly and mysteriously

When you recite the Great Compassion Mantra 108 times each day, and continue this for 1,000 days, the Ten Bright Kings will be pleased and all illnesses will be eradicated. Throughout these 1,000 days, that is, these 3 years, you will have accomplished quite a lot of merit. Because during these 3 years, each day you sincerely recite the mantra, leaving no opportunity to generate negative karma. You do not drink alcohol, do not eat meat, and do not consume pungent spices.

In hell, there is a mirror platform that records sins called the 'mirror of retribution.' If you commit an evil deed, that deed will appear clearly in the mirror. It is similar to an image appearing on a movie screen. For example, if a person commits murder in this life, the mirror of retribution will show the scene of that person killing someone. If the person commits theft, the mirror will show them stealing. If the person commits arson against someone else's house, the mirror will clearly display the act of setting the house on fire.

And if you do not create any evil karma at all? Then nothing will appear in that mirror. Therefore, if you recite the Great Compassion Mantra for 3 years, when the mirror of karma reflects, your retribution will be cleansed. In that hell, a plaque will be hung stating: "This person has recited the Great Compassion Mantra, and all of their retribution has been completely resolved."

All the demons and spirits in hell bow and worship this person who recites the mantra with reverence, just as they would respectfully bow to the Buddhas of the past, present, and future. At the same time, those demons and spirits will protect the person who recites the mantra, just as they normally attend to the Buddhas, and all the demons and spirits inform each other not to disturb the person who recites the mantra. The spiritual power of the Great Compassion Mantra is truly inconceivable.

(Rewritten according to the teachings of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua)
