tieu_de: The Intermediate State and Rebirth in the Western Paradise - The Miraculousness of Buddhist Dharma.
tom_tat: The Amitabha Pure Land Buddhist temple “Master Tinh Khong Amitabha” in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia, usually holds Buddha chanting sessions on Saturdays and Sundays. Religious associations practice together.
noi_dung:
The Intermediate State and Rebirth in the Western Pure Land - The Miraculousness of Buddhist Teachings.

The Amitabha Pure Land Buddhist center in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia, often conducts Buddha recitations on Saturdays and Sundays. Associations practice together for a day and a night with more than 2,000 people, practicing very diligently, solemnly, and peacefully.

On February 17, 2012, an elderly Taiwanese laywoman – Ms. Lam Tan Nhuan, who is ethnically Chinese, born in Malaysia, and immigrated to Australia, was practicing recitation of Buddha's name and often practiced at the Pure Land Learning Association. That night, she dreamed she saw the spirit of a young man, emaciated, hollow-eyed, very distressed, who said to her: "Grandma, I have been looking for you for a long time! Today there is a good opportunity, you can save me, I am in such suffering. Please have mercy and save me. I am in so much suffering!"

She asked the young man:

– What's your name? Where are you from? And how come you're in trouble, needing me to help?

The young man answered:

– I am Korean, named Kim Thiện Nhật, 36 years old.

I was taken hostage and then beheaded in Iraq. It was so painful, thank you for saving me.

– Oh, then I know you've suffered a lot, died unjustly, very miserable, I understand. Now I can help you, but you have to chant Buddha’s name, then I can help you. If you do not chant Buddha’s name, you will not be saved.

The young man nodded, and then the old lady taught the young man to chant Buddha’s name. She chanted “Namo Amitabha Buddha” three times, and he also chanted along with her three times. She was startled to see the clock—it was already 2 a.m.; she carried the string of beads to the living room and sat chanting Buddha’s name bead by bead.

Late at night, the son went to the bathroom and discovered his mother sitting and chanting Buddha's name in the living room with the lights on, so he asked:

– Mom, do you know what time it is? It's two o'clock in the morning, why are you awake? You're already old, staying up like this isn't good for your health.

She then said:

– I just had that dream, my child. And this dream is very strange. I saw someone from Korea, named Kim Thien Nhat, being taken hostage and then beheaded in Iraq.

The child said to the mother:

– Mother, you are a practitioner of the Pure Land Buddhist Association. In the Pure Land Buddhist Association, three things are forbidden: Do not listen to the phone, Do not read newspapers, and Do not watch TV. So how did you know about that?

She replied:

– No, I don’t answer the phone, don’t read the newspaper, and don’t watch TV. I only lie in my dreams, my child.

As soon as she said that, her child ran into his room, took out the newspaper, and read the full article with a photo of Kim Thiện Nhật for her to hear.

After hearing it, she said:

– Oh, the picture of this person is very similar to the person I saw in my dream, it’s the same person, my child. It’s in the newspaper, but I don’t read the newspaper.

Hearing his mother say that, the son recorded her dream noting that the news about Kim Thien Nhat was true, not just any dream at all.

Then she prayed to Kim Thien Nhat, saying: “Tomorrow my child will take me to the Tinh Tong Buddhist Association for two days. You can go there to chant Buddha’s name; the energy from the pure field of the congregation together with chanting Buddha will be tremendous. Going there will be very good for you, helping you a lot. If I chant alone, the energy won’t be much. You should go there to chant Buddha’s name…”.

The next morning, her son took her to the Pure Land Buddhist Association to chant Buddha's name for two days on Saturday and Sunday. When she arrived at the practice hall, she recounted that strange dream and asked everyone there to chant Buddha's name together and dedicate the merit to Kim Thien Nhat. As for herself, every day at 2 a.m., her mind would urge her to wake up and chant Buddha's name. She chanted earnestly and sincerely in hopes of saving that young man.

She sincerely recited Buddha's name and dedicated the merits in this way until the 13th day, when she dreamed of Kim Thiện Nhật sitting on a blue lotus, folding his hands, smiling in gratitude, and promising to meet her in the Western Pure Land. She also smiled and folded her hands to recite Buddha's name three times to say goodbye.

Then she told this story to everyone at the Pure Land Buddhist practice group. Everyone was happy because their Buddha recitation and repentance had achieved results. This story was passed on by the venerable monks and lay Buddhists in the Pure Land tradition and shared with Buddhists everywhere. Later, layperson Tịnh Hải included this story and a picture of Kim Thiện Nhật in the book "Reciting Buddha for Rebirth in the Pure Land." Thanks to this, Buddhists both domestically and abroad became aware of this rare story. Truly marvelous! The power of the Buddha is beyond discussion.

CASE 2: REBIRTH IN THE INTERMEDIATE STATE (AS RECOUNTED BY VENERABLE TỊNH KHÔNG)

Laywoman Hồ, the chief staff of our Buddhist group, has been studying Buddhism for seventeen years, but her mother has not studied Buddhism. Her mother is a very kind-hearted person, but has never known about the Dharma. When she saw her daughter studying Buddhism, she considered it superstition.

When she fell ill with a serious disease, some of her daughter's fellow Buddhists came to the hospital to assist her with prayers. She also recited along, but with half belief and half doubt. She often asked: Is it really true? … Is it really so? …

Therefore, assisting in creating spiritual conditions is very important. Having a Dharma Master who often gives her guidance and reminds her to recite the Buddha's name together with everyone is what allows her to move forward.

Her funeral was held at Huo Lin Institute in Taiwan, which is a Pure Land Buddhist practice center of ours. There, a Buddha retreat was held for her, with the Three Periods of Reciting the Buddha's Name practiced continuously for seven weeks, forty-nine days. It can also be considered that she had good spiritual affinity, with more than three hundred fellow practitioners reciting the Buddha's name continuously day and night for forty-nine days without interruption.

Her mother's casket was placed in the room next to the Buddhist chanting hall. She met an aunt. Her mother had entered that aunt's body, entered her aunt's body and conveyed that she also knew she had passed away, she also said that:

"Why are you being so good to me?"… She was very astonished!… "Is it because of my daughter? Why are you being so good to me?"…

This is the first time she reported the news; we all advised her to recite Buddha's name and encouraged her to aspire to be reborn in the Pure Land. At present, she is in the bardo state. After hearing this, she was extremely grateful. After expressing her gratitude, she asked about Buddhist teachings.

“What is a Buddha? Why should one recite the Buddha's name? Is there any benefit in reciting the Buddha's name?”

We had a young Dharma master explain to her, she asked many questions, and after hearing the answers, she was very joyful and said:

“Great! Then it’s good, I will listen to the sutras.”

She wanted to listen to sutras, so her family played them for her on the TV. The TV was placed next to the coffin, playing the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. Moreover, she personally requested that the disc be changed every night. After finishing it, they had to switch to another one. The person changing the disc found it very exhausting, so she instructed her daughter to find a karaoke machine that could play four hundred pages of songs. And indeed, they found one. It contained four hundred pages. The Kṣitigarbha Sutra was played for her continuously day and night without interruption, and afterward, she was no longer seen communing with spirits. It seems she was not seen communing with spirits for more than two weeks.

More than two weeks later, she went into trance again, and I asked where she had gone. She said:

“I didn't go anywhere, just listened to the scriptures.”

After listening to the scriptures day and night, about ten days later she went into trance again and said:

“Now there is no need to listen to the scriptures anymore, I need to recite Buddha's name. I said I want to be reborn in the Pure Land, so why hasn’t Amitabha Buddha come to take me yet?”…

During the final period, she recited Buddha's name until the day of the Three Periods of Collective Mindfulness. On the forty-ninth day, she went into trance again and said:

“Thank you very much everyone for giving her this superior karmic connection, really thank you. She has been reborn in the Pure Land.”

Everyone asked at what rank she was?…

“Lower Middle Birth”

How could someone who had never known about the Dharma be like this? It is because her bardo body was guided to liberation; she is the first person that we personally witnessed.

Why, within such a short time of her bardo body being exposed to the Dharma, was she able to be reborn in the Pure Land?

Because in a past life, she had practiced this Dharma method, but had not succeeded, so in this life, at the time of dying, hearing it again caused the virtuous roots from her previous life to arise, vigorously striving to let go of all attachments without any lingering, therefore she quickly attained accomplishment.

An even rarer occurrence is that she did not believe in the Buddha while alive, nor did she believe in the Buddha after death. When she died, her bardo body heard the Dharma, she clearly recognized it, followed the instructions for recitation and assistance; she was no longer in a human body, but in a bardo body, and by following the guidance for recitation she was also able to be reborn in the Pure Land.

The cause is all due to the virtue from past lives; in this life, there is no prior affinity to hear the Dharma. As soon as they hear it, they immediately awaken. This is similar to a person whose will and faith are so firm. The field of influence of Mara does not affect them; as soon as they generate a thought, Amitabha Buddha immediately radiates light, and they receive benefits. As long as one just generates a thought, one is blessed. Therefore, the response and influence cannot be fully expressed in words.

Namo Amitabha Buddha!

(Diệu Âm Lệ Hiếu compiled from the lectures of HT Thích Giác Hạnh and HT Tịnh Không – 2014)

noi_dung:
GODS EXIST AND LIVE IN A DIFFERENT DIMENSION FROM US.

They do indeed exist and also have the form of life; in this regard, currently scientists can all prove their existence. Therefore, we must be vigilant toward ghosts and deities. It is because, Zengzi once warned: The gentleman is always cautious when alone (even when we are alone, we are still in the situation: “Ten eyes see, ten hands point”). One must understand, every action of ours is seen by ghosts and deities! Those who clearly understand this, how can they not be cautious and fearful? How can one, when alone, dare to behave carelessly?

Beside us, there really are many lives that ordinary eyes cannot see. The sages have said: Like attracts like. In our daily activities, we all know and can clearly see: Across the five continents and four seas, when looking at people from different countries or regions, in terms of appearance, character, and culture, there are already differences: Differences in geography, customs, etc., which corresponds to the saying 'like attracts like.' In Buddhism, this is called shared karma, meaning: A gentleman likes to associate with virtuous people, while a scoundrel prefers to befriend foul dogs. This is exactly the principle!

That is why the sages often taught: Just by looking at someone's friends, you can know what kind of person they are. Because of shared karmic attraction, similar beings naturally seek each other out. Therefore, a person who practices good deeds throughout their life, after death, will ascend to heaven, while a person who does evil will descend into hell, become a hungry ghost, or an animal. This is absolutely not controlled by any deity; it is due to the consciousness of beings being drawn there by the force of their own karma. This is not superstition at all, but rather very reasonable.

Then the demons and spirits interacting with me are similar; as mentioned in the scriptures: Those who commit evil deeds will inevitably experience the phenomenon of "evil spirits residing in the house." These evil spirits are attracted to you due to past-life grudges and karmic enemies, drawn by your malicious thoughts and actions. Naturally, if you could see beings in this different dimension, you would find that throughout the house, above and below, these terrifying evil spirits fill every corner. As long as one commits evil, one forms a bond with evil spirits, known as being in harmony and resonance with them. Therefore, one can imagine the fate and destiny of those who commit evil deeds.Career is not smooth, family is disharmonious, grandchildren are unfilial…

Actually, this is entirely due to the bad karma you have attracted, leading to…

Therefore, nowadays in many entertainment venues, they belong to the so-called "Area of Lustful Spirits." Because these areas always ensure there are "demons residing at the gate," their numbers are too numerous to count. The reason is that the people's hearts in that locality are all unrighteous, hence they attract these demons to come and dwell (lying in wait here). From this, it can be inferred that the directors of nightclubs, bars, discos… those who have tendencies to develop businesses involving: drugs, sex, deviant desires, licentiousness, indulgence… will all attract the outcome: their future careers will increasingly become disadvantageous, not to mention that accidents such as fires, explosions, and killings may occur.v… means sudden calamities that often occur causing death or injury…

The reason is: At decadent and wasteful entertainment venues, such behavior will greatly diminish one's personal blessings. Moreover, such places are also environments that attract many evil spirits, which causes a decline in fortune.

On the contrary, those who specialize in doing good, live virtuously, and have a bright and righteous heart will surely attract benevolent spirits and gods. When mentioning spirits and gods, people should not be afraid; although they are called spirits and gods, in fact, they are just beings living in a different dimension from us. As mentioned, these benevolent spirits and gods all enjoy doing good deeds and helping people achieve perfection.

Because you live righteously, you have moved them, attracting them to come and dwell in your home, making your fortune even better and more harmonious. They will assist you in growing your own virtue. Therefore, in daily work activities, you will experience smooth and satisfactory outcomes. Of course, spirits are only supportive; it is your own virtue that moves your family, and it will also positively affect your colleagues, subordinates, employees, or superiors… toward you. As a result, your family lives in harmony, work goes smoothly, and interpersonal relationships will continually improve. Your words and behavior will also influence the spirits.

kind and virtuous, when they see your kind thoughts and actions, they will be very delighted… Therefore, if they see you speak well but act badly, with inconsistent words and behavior, they will be disappointed and discouraged, distance themselves, and give up on you. Instead, you will attract evil spirits to come, and of course, they will cause disharmony in your family and ruin your career…

Of course, demons are only secondary causes, while your own bad habits and evil tendencies are the main reasons for destroying your blessings! Moreover, karmic enemies can affect the local energy field, disturb your brain waves, cause confusion and delirium, increase worries, or make you irritable and foolish, prone to many illnesses, and encounter all sorts of unfortunate events... In addition, if an individual's thoughts are not virtuous, if their mind is full of selfishness, vanity, material desire, and full of greed, anger, and delusion... then their interpersonal relationships will certainly not be good, family harmony will be disrupted, and with those demons fanning the flames, thenThe scene doesn't need description to know that danger surrounds on all sides, storms whirl around…

Therefore, after studying Buddhism and understanding the path, one must eliminate all bad habits and negative traits from the root. Whether life is good or not depends on you. In reality, the most important thing in life is: You should not let time pass in vain, because the past has gone, and the future has not yet come. Only the present moment is the most important; seize this moment well, which means you can change your destiny. Remember clearly: Everything is created by each present moment!

(Excerpt from BÁO ỨNG HIỆN ĐỜI 7 - Author: Quả Khanh cư sĩ - Translated by Hạnh Đoan)

tieu_de: ASTONISHED BY THE CANCER HEALING ABILITY OF THE DEPARTED MONK.
tom_tat: Ms. Hà Thị Dém, born in 1945, residing in Phú Mỹ Hamlet, Phú Hòa Đông Commune, Củ Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, in 2017, felt unwell and went for a medical check-up. After thorough tests, the doctor informed her of a shocking piece of news
noi_dung:
ASTONISHED BY THE CANCER HEALING ABILITY OF THE VISITING MASTER.

Ms. Hà Thị Dém, born in 1945, residing in Phú Mỹ Hamlet, Phú Hòa Đông Commune, Củ Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, felt unwell in 2017 and went for a medical check-up. After thorough examinations, the doctor gave her devastating news: she had cervical cancer and needed to be sent to the Oncology Hospital for treatment.

After being transferred to the Oncology Hospital, he began to go through months of suffering. He had no spouse or children, living alone until now at the age of 76. Old age and frailty, not being very well-off either, and now with this disease, having to undergo long-term treatment at the Oncology Hospital, it is truly extremely painful.

Anyone who has gone through the process of receiving treatment or caring for patients here clearly understands the misery of this earthly hell. Everywhere are the groans of pain from the patients, the heavy sighs of the relatives, and faces filled with suffering and despair.

Everything is overloaded; patients not only fill the hospital beds, but they are also scattered under the beds, in the hallways, under the stairs, at the toilet doors… Those who are already sick and can afford to pay suffer enough, but the poor sick suffer even more, sometimes not even having rice to eat, having to rely on charity meals and bowls of porridge…

The doctor had to spend a sum of over ten million dong to hire someone to take care of him during his time in the hospital. Misfortunes never come singly; that person took the money, and after just a few days, ran away, leaving the doctor alone in his miserable sickness.

In the following days, I had to undergo treatment, from surgery to radiation therapy, but my body didn't seem to get any better, still tormented by pain and extreme fatigue. My whole body was pale and weak.

One day, feeling sad about aging, illness, and being alone to fight on my own, I slowly walked out to the gate of the Oncology Hospital, and saw me along with others distributing vegetarian meals and giving out books.

I asked for one, and we were given a copy of "Returned by the Hospital, Saved by the Dharma."

Holding the book in his hands, he gave a faint smile and thought to himself: "With all the advanced machines in the hospital and professional doctors like here, if they can't cure it, what Buddhist teachings could possibly heal this illness?"

Then he shoved the book somewhere, not even bothering to read it.

Nearly three months of miserable hospitalization (from January 19 to April 6, 2018), taking medicine then surgery, surgery then radiation therapy, day after day drifting through pain and exhaustion in the Oncology Hospital. Luckily, some benefactors helped with additional hospital fees, but he still didn't feel any better.

Witnessing so many people here go bankrupt because of surgery, chemotherapy, radiation... and then die anyway. In the same surgery batch with you, there were 24 people, almost all have died. Some were even relatives of doctors, with plenty of money, not afraid of expenses, yet still could not escape the hand of death. So what hope do you have, and you are the most severe case among them, which makes it even more miserable.

Desperate, you decided to stop treatment, asked to be discharged home, praying to your ancestors to let you pass away gently without pain would already be very good.

Back home, neighbors came to visit, and everyone looked at him with sympathy. Illness had ravaged his body, making him pale and weak, unable to eat properly. He was alone, with no one to care for him; at most, only a few acquaintances would come to check on him briefly before leaving.

After a few days, feeling sad, distressed, and hopeless with nothing to do, he suddenly saw the book "Discharged from the Hospital, Saved by the Dharma." He took it out to read to pass the time, without any real expectation. Unexpectedly, the book was so good that he finished reading it in just a few hours.

In the book, you see many cases, some even more critical than yours, such as a baby who was sent home by the doctor to await a funeral, and thanks to people coming to chant Buddha's name, eventually recovered, much to the hospital's astonishment. The names and addresses are very clear, not fabricated and unverifiable stories.

That made him reconsider; the methods in the guidebook, mainly reciting Buddha's name, chanting mantras, and repentance... didn't cost anything at all. It's just a matter of putting one's heart and effort into chanting sincerely. At this point, I have nothing left to lose, and there’s no other way out that needs pondering. So, I might as well just practice and see what happens.

He began to recite Buddha's name, bow to the Buddha, and chant following the Great Compassion Mantra printed in the book, reading it three times a day. Especially with the Rebirth Mantra, whenever he had free time he would read it, because the mantra is very short and easy to memorize; soon he had it by heart. The Rebirth Mantra is a mantra excerpted from the Sutra of the Perfection of Mindfulness of the Buddha, the original text in the sutra is as follows:

"At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra addressed the Buddha, saying:

– Venerable One, out of compassion for sentient beings in the age of the Dharma's decline, when lifespans decrease, merit diminishes, defilements increase, and genuine practitioners are very few, I will grant this Dharani of Buddha Recitation to people, so they can protect body and mind, eradicate karma completely at the root, eliminate all afflictions, and quickly be reborn in the Pure Land. It is called the Dharani for Eradicating All Fundamental Karmic Hindrances and Attaining Rebirth in the Pure Land. The Master then recited the Dharani:

NAMO AMITABHA BUDDHA,

DHATHA DA DHA DA,

DA DHI DHA THA,

A DI RI DO BA TY,

A DI RI DA TAT DAM BA TY,

A DI RI DA TY CA LAN DE,

A DI RI DA TY CA LAN DA,

tom_tat: Ta bà ha (Soa ha, xoa ha). In Chinese translation, it has six meanings. Whenever this word appears in any mantra, it carries all six of these meanings. The first meaning is 'achievement'. When reciting this mantra, all requests and wishes of
noi_dung:
THE MEANING OF THE MANTRA AT THE END OF THE MANTRAS: TA BÀ HA ( SOA HA, XOA HA

Ta bà ha (Soa ha, xoa ha). In Chinese translation, it has six meanings. Whenever this word appears in any mantra, it encompasses all six meanings.

The first meaning is "fulfillment." When reciting this mantra, all the desires and wishes of the practitioner will be fulfilled. If you have not yet experienced any response during practice, it is because the mind has not reached true sincerity. If you have wholehearted sincerity and strong faith, you will certainly achieve fulfillment. However, even a slight thought of disbelief in this mantra will prevent fulfillment from ever occurring.

The second meaning is "Auspicious." When a practitioner recites this mantra, all misfortunes will turn into good fortune as desired. However, you must have sincere faith. If you have sincere faith or are half-believing and half-doubting while reciting this mantra, all Bodhisattvas will clearly know. Therefore, if you want everything to be fulfilled, you must first have true faith. For example, if your father is ill and you want him to recover, you must be completely sincere and have correct faith. Only by reciting this mantra in this way will there be efficacy.

Or when you think: “I haven't seen my close friend for a long time. Now I really want to meet him.” If you sincerely recite this mantra, you will immediately meet your friend. Or you think: “I don't have any friends and want to have a good friend.” If you recite this mantra sincerely and continuously, you will obtain a good friend, even encounter a virtuous friend.

The third meaning is “passing away”.

When the monks relinquish their physical bodies or enter Nirvana, it is called "complete cessation." However, here, the word "complete cessation" does not mean death. It is not that reciting the mantra Ta Bà Ha is to seek complete cessation. So what is the use of this mantra?

"Complete cessation" means "virtue without imperfection." It is the merit of a practitioner being completely perfect; "virtue without cessation" is the morality of a practitioner reaching the utmost pinnacle. Only Buddhas and Bodhisattvas can know this perfect and complete practice, while ordinary beings cannot comprehend it.

The fourth meaning is "eliminating calamities," which means all misfortunes are removed.

The fifth meaning is "increasing benefits," which refers to the growth of the practitioner's merits. When reciting the phrase Ta bà ha, all virtuous deeds are amplified, and the practitioner will attain a place of benefit and joy.

The sixth meaning of this phrase, I think, few of you know. Because I have never spoken about it before.

Ta bà ha means "non-abiding." This meaning of "non-abiding" lies within the significance of the phrase "should generate the mind without dwelling anywhere" in the Diamond Sutra.

“Non-attachment” means not clinging to, not being entangled with, or not holding on to anything.

A mind that is non-attached does not hold any preconceived notions or attachments to anything. Non-attachment means the mind is in harmony with everything, seeing all things as good. This is precisely the case of: “Non-doing yet nothing is undone” (no intention or volition arises, yet everything is accomplished). Non-attachment is exactly non-doing in the above sense, and non-doing is precisely non-attachment.

When you have just initiated a thought, do not cling to anything, that is the sixth meaning of Ta ba ha. You should not dwell on thoughts of greed, anger, delusion, pride, or doubt. If you have all these thoughts, you must quickly subdue them, transform them so that your mind no longer dwells on any thought. Subduing and transforming these sentient beings' thoughts is called non-abiding. What should be used to conquer them? Use this Vajra sword mudra to subdue. You say that your mind is filled with thoughts dominated by greed. I will use this Vajra sword to cut them all away. If your mind is full of demonic afflictions, I will also use this Vajra sword.

drive them away completely. If your mind is possessed by deluded demons, I will use this sword of wisdom to cut them into pieces.

I will cut off all those demons with this Vajra King Sword, that is, using the Sword of Wisdom to subdue them. If you want to subdue the heavenly demons and heretics, you must first transform all your own delusions. When you can transform the delusions in your mind, then the heavenly demons and heretics are also subdued; even if they want to come to cause trouble, they will find no way to harm you.

Above are the six meanings of Ta Ba Ha. Any mantra that contains the words Ta Ba Ha carries all six of these meanings.

(Explanation of the Great Compassion Mantra - Venerable Tuyen Hoa)

tom_tat: Question: Every day I recite the Buddha's name, but I feel a headache, discomfort in my body, and at night I have bad dreams... I am really very worried and don’t know what to do. Answer: In the Sutra of Contemplating Amitabha Buddha, it teaches, truly t
noi_dung:
CHANTING BUDDHA, EXPERIENCING HEADACHE, DISCOMFORT IN THE BODY, AND HAVING NIGHTMARES AT NIGHT—WHAT DOES IT MEAN?

Question: Every day I recite the Buddha's name, but I feel a headache, discomfort in my body, and at night I have nightmares... I am really worried and don't know what to do?

Answer: In the Sutra of Contemplating the Buddha of Infinite Life, it is taught that sincerely reciting one Buddha's name can eliminate up to 8 billion kalpas of karmic obstacles and severe sins of birth and death. Those who sincerely recite the Buddha's name will have their karmic obstacles completely dissipated.

A person who practices Buddha recitation and experiences headaches is due to the fact that their karmic obstacles are too great. Therefore, when encountering this Amitabha medicine, it is too strong—it breaks the suffering karma, resulting in headaches. It's like taking medicine; if the medicine is potent or the effect is strong, the first few times you take it, you often feel uncomfortable. But if you continue taking it, it will soon pass.

So, continue reciting Buddha, with wholehearted trust in the blessings of the Buddha, and do not let your spirit waver.

Reciting the Buddha's name requires three things to be firmly maintained: Faith, Vow, and Practice. One must have faith, make a vow to be reborn in the Pure Land, and sincerely recite the Buddha's name continuously. Remember, making a vow means wishing to be reborn in the Pure Land, not wishing to get rid of all illnesses. The vow to be reborn should be heartfelt, not perfunctory. If you genuinely wish to be reborn in the Pure Land, then a few minor headaches are nothing to worry about!

If a person reciting the Buddha's name has a headache and keeps worrying about it, the headache will only get worse. Why is that? Because there is no faith, no deep desire for rebirth, making the recitation of the Buddha's name neither sincere nor wholehearted!

Faith-Vow-Conduct are three yet one, one yet three; lacking one means losing all three, and that is why chanting the Buddha's name does not correspond. This is also caused by karmic obstructions.

What should be done now?

1) Sincerely repent karmic obstructions. How? Bow to the Buddha and chant the Buddha's name extensively, sincerely repenting while bowing and chanting.

2) Determined to let go of all attachments. How to let go? Does it mean abandoning husband and children? Not at all. Letting go means having a relaxed mind, without worry, without stubbornness, without greed, without anger, without fear of headaches, and without random thoughts. Even mistakes from the past should be forgotten. Concentrate on Buddha Recitation so that at the end of life one can be reborn in the Pure Land.

3) If you have a headache, just frankly tell yourself: "That's right, who told me to make mistakes in the past! Who told me to practice too late! Who told me to kill so much!...".

All the current karmic obstructions result in consequences that must be accepted; now one must focus on reciting Buddha's name to go to the Western Paradise so as to no longer be troubled by karma. In the Western Paradise, one attains enlightenment to resolve karmic consequences.

Think that with your own karmic obstructions, you should actually bear far heavier consequences than this, not just this little; in fact, you should be suffering a hundred times more pain.

If one sincerely and courageously repents, then naturally one will no longer feel pain. That is, one will be joyful.

Those who have complete Faith, Vows, and Practice naturally recover from headaches. (If it doesn’t go away, just take a few pills to ease it a bit, then focus on reciting Buddha’s name—what’s there to worry about). All phenomena are empty. Ultimately, even headaches are empty. No problem!

People with terminal cancer who are close to death can be healed just by reciting Buddha’s name, let alone a headache. Do you know how much pain someone with terminal cancer suffers? The pain feels like flesh being cut, yet reciting Buddha’s name can relieve it. So, what is there to worry about a headache!

Do you know how much pain a chicken feels when you hold a knife to cut its throat? Yet, I do not empathize with its pain, so now just having a little headache is nothing to complain about!

Think about the suffering of all beings, and your own suffering will naturally disappear. If you keep worrying about your own suffering, you create additional suffering, called 'Suffering-Suffering'! This is what repentance is. Complaining to heaven or blaming the earth only adds karma on top of karma, certainly leading to more suffering.

If you do not strive and do not have faith, how can you escape from karmic retribution?

*) As for having nightmares, this is probably because the mind has too many delusions, too much worry, too much fear, too much anger, too much sadness, too much restlessness, too much concern about right and wrong... Conversely, if one does not maintain a peaceful mind, is not relaxed, not comfortable, not happy, does not see life as an illusion, and clings too much to greed, hatred, delusion, and pride... in general, if the mind is too restless and impure, it leads to dreaming. Honestly examine yourself, have you violated any of these things?

All phenomena are empty, so nightmares are unreal! Therefore, when experiencing a nightmare, simply arise the thought of reciting Buddha's name, and it will immediately end. Certainly. If reciting Buddha's name does not end it, beware that it may be because the recitation is not sincere, only spoken with the mouth but not believed in the heart. Such recitation is useless!

The world often says: "When the mind is impure, one neither sees nor hears, and truly does not know their position." That is so. Well, just let go of everything, regard worldly matters as light as a feather, to allow your mind to be at ease. That is, one must be joyful, without any worries, then naturally nothing will trouble you.

Remember, those who sincerely recite the Buddha's name have the radiance of the Buddha’s family protection, are supported by 25 Bodhisattvas, and are protected by the devas, dragons, and eight classes of beings... When you are immersed in such a strong force of compassion, what is there to fear that would cause nightmares? Even if nightmares occur, just let them be, focus on reciting the Buddha’s name instead of being worried and unable to sleep!

Do you believe it? If you believe, that’s enough. If you don’t believe, then it’s your loss!

Besides that, one must understand the value of doing good and avoiding evil. Practice releasing living beings for their benefit, sincerely repent past karmic offenses, and in practicing Buddha recitation always dedicate the merit to:

1) All sentient beings in the Dharma realm;

2) One's grandparents, parents, and ancestors;

3) Enemies and karmic creditors from many lifetimes;

4) Dedicate merit toward the Western Pure Land, praying for rebirth and enlightenment to save all sentient beings.

Repentance is also reciting the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land. Sincerely reciting the Buddha's name brings spiritual efficacy; reciting without sincerity does not bring great benefit.

Do not do evil,

Must do good,

A relaxed soul,

Naturally no longer sick.

(A-Di-Đà Buddha - Elder Layman Diệu Âm - (20/10/2008)

tieu_de: EASY-GOING MALE-FEMALE RELATIONSHIPS WHEN YOUNG WILL GREATLY REDUCE BLESSINGS FOR FUTURE LIFE - PEOPLE
tom_tat: 1- Is a person who has many people wronged. 2- Is a person who has many people hating them.
noi_dung:
EASY-GOING MALE-FEMALE RELATIONSHIPS IN YOUTH WILL GREATLY REDUCE BLESSINGS FOR FUTURE LIFE - PEOPLE

1- Is a person who has many people wronged by them.

2- Is a person who has many enemies.

3- Is a person who is poor and deprived.

4- Is a person who does not sleep peacefully.

5- Is a person who does not rest peacefully while awake.

6- Is a person who cannot avoid the 4 evil realms (hell, asura, hungry ghost, animal).

7- Is a person who loves men and women (neither man nor woman).

8- Is a person who is quick-tempered.

9- Is a person born into a lowly family, a lowly type of person.

10- Is a person who is not transparent, often hiding their faults.

11- Is a person with a disabled or ugly body.

12- Is a person with a sorrowful, distressed facial expression.

13- Is a person despised and distrusted by everyone.

14- Is a person with disabilities: blind, deaf-mute, ...

15- Born as a woman (previous life as a man).

16- Is a person with many dreadful illnesses.

17- Is a person who never knows contentment, lives in hardship.

18- Is a person who cannot find peace wherever they live.

19- Is a person who encounters many calamities, injustices from everyone.

20- Is a person who lives far from loved ones, often being abandoned.

Conversely, those who are righteous, live sincerely, and kindly will certainly encounter much luck.

Tú is my schoolmate. He is of average height, has an ordinary appearance, comes from a poor family, and is shy and easily embarrassed. He is similar to me in that he likes browsing the internet for fun and studies in a relaxed manner. We are both studying Literature and are currently in our fourth year.

At this time, every student dreams of finding a good job with satisfactory income after graduation. Therefore, everyone tries their best, hoping for luck and to have good opportunities.

During high school, Tú already had a girlfriend. Later, each of them was admitted to separate universities in different cities, but they still maintained an intimate relationship.

That day, the female student friend came to visit and even proactively wanted to give herself to him. At that time, Tú already had his own rented place, but at the most crucial moment, he still insisted on keeping himself pure, firmly using reason to overcome desire, refusing to cross moral boundaries before marriage.

Before his absolute refusal, the girl friend became angry out of embarrassment, and after leaving, she decisively broke up with him. I asked him:

- Do you regret your conservative, outdated attitude?

He replied: - Absolutely not!

And he explained that it was the golden standard that the saints and sages had always reminded him of, which he himself was compelled to respect and follow, regardless of friends laughing and mocking:

- Doing that is unmanly, not “manly” enough!

They mischievously acted suspicious, saying: - Maybe you are… gay?

He remained calm, paying no attention, and always seriously kept himself, faithful to the principle “never cross the boundary before marriage.” Therefore, he never acted casually with anyone.

Constant ridicule does not move him, so we turn to admire his upright character. However, we still often tease him as the 'rare animal' remaining in this world. Because if he encounters us, any girl willing to give herself to him… we will enthusiastically participate immediately.

Near graduation, the students were both studying and worrying about finding a job after leaving school. Everyone was busy, except for Tú, who was leisurely and calm; he didn't show any sign of worry, and we even said to him: “If you don’t think ahead, being unemployed after graduation is inevitable…” But Tú didn’t pay attention. The result was that after graduation, he really did become unemployed, so he had to go to Shen Zhen to look for a job….

But no one could have expected that, not long after, Tú was quickly helped by a benefactor and advanced straight into working at a television station, a very famous place – with very strict recruitment standards – a position that was extremely good and that most of us dreamed of but not everyone could reach.

Tú made all his friends gape in surprise, because the top students who wanted to work at the station still couldn't get in, while a mediocre recent graduate like Tú got recruited easily. It must be said that this is an exceptionally rare stroke of luck, really fortunate!

This luck is just as the ancients taught: "Whoever possesses extraordinary luck must certainly have virtues that astonish the spirits!" Indeed, that virtue is uprightness and integrity, refusing to do anything hidden or deceitful. Because at the very moment your girlfriend leapt into his arms, offering herself, he still had enough lucidity to stop in time, without committing lewd acts, without destroying his own morality. He did not indulge in lust, even though he loved his girlfriend dearly, he still resolutely rejected the improper act.... Determinationand this virtue has made many people admire.

Hearing stories from the feudal times, there were also many scholars who, thanks to strictly avoiding immoral sexual behavior and not engaging in theft with women, received great rewards. These stories are indeed true, not false, because the story of my friend Tu is a vivid proof even in modern times.

Throughout four years of university, Tu and I shared living arrangements, meals, and daily activities... in the same way. We were both fun-loving, playful, and liked leisure, so our academic performance was relatively average. However, unlike Tu, my personality was quite different from his, completely lustful! I was very passionate about sex. As a result, my career path was always bumpy and troubled, making it hard to find a good job like his.

He and I are close friends, but we have two contrasting lifestyles in terms of virtue. Isn't this contrast a reminder of the age-old principle: "Keeping chastity brings blessings, indulging in sexual desires brings misfortune"? Of course, besides maintaining chastity, one must also cultivate many other virtues.

After so many painful experiences, I have gathered many hard-earned lessons and recalled two teachings of the sages: "Those destined for wealth, due to lust, will have their luck taken away from the jade tower. Those destined for honor, due to indulgence, will have their fame erased from the golden register."

By 2010, I sadly self-reflected and read works that advised renouncing sexual misconduct, studied Buddhism, and discovered that “the reason I encountered so many misfortunes in life was due to the habit of sexual misconduct.” After that, I studied Buddhist practices, applied them, and continuously repented, determined to abandon all evil, and focused on cultivating virtue and doing good deeds. I began to completely stop unhealthy influences such as pornographic films, obscene books and newspapers, or indecent games. Thanks to the protection of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, gradually I was able to overcome the bad habit of masturbation.

After much effort in cultivating and rectifying my body and mind, I finally passed the exam and was admitted into a prestigious research institute to my satisfaction, and received a government-sponsored scholarship.

Previously, when I took exams, my parents went everywhere consulting fortune-tellers, drawing lots, seeking destiny predictions from masters…. Almost everyone said I was talented and destined to succeed in exams, but the results always disappointed my parents. Now, thinking back, the main issue was with myself. I realized two things:

1. Lust consumes merit and blessings very greatly and quickly.

2. Fate, blessings… are all created by yourself, not by anyone else.

Since I decided to cultivate virtue and uphold chastity, joy has appeared, and I passed the exam, ranking at the top of the list. As soon as the exam began, I already felt something wonderfully inexplicable. Later, I gained even more firm belief when I realized that Cause and Effect are real and not deceptive. Everyone says that this year my fortune has come, so my official luck has improved. I just smiled, because I have realized what is called “Luck” – it does not fall from the sky, but entirely lies in our own hands; that fortune lies in “Eliminating depravity, avoiding evil, and practicing good deeds.” If one knows to completely removeMaster of lust, you will become a person with abundant vitality, a flexible mind, and constant good luck.

In society, intelligence ranks at the top as it does today, so lewd behavior will lower physical and mental abilities, causing one to fall to the lowest, inferior class in society, becoming an ordinary, incompetent person, living with regret for a lifetime.

I discovered that the medicine that can help me completely end immoral desires is none other than the Dharma. The more I cultivate, refine, and maintain my virtues, the more everything comes to me smoothly and favorably, my career advances well, and it brings great joy to my parents – fulfilling my filial duty completely. I would like to share my story so that young people of the same generation and situation can gain experience and improve their fate.

(Vo Tri – Excerpt from Báo Ứng Hiện Đời, Volume 7 – translated by Hạnh Đoan)

tieu_de: THE SUFFERING OF THE EVIL WORLD: 5 GREAT EVILS OF THE WORLD
tom_tat: The Buddha said to Maitreya Bodhisattva: 'Those of you born in this lifetime, whose minds are upright and who do not commit evil, possess great virtue.' Why is that? In the ten directions of the Buddha's worlds, where goodness is abundant and evil is scarce, it is very easy to enlighten beings. Only
noi_dung:
THE SUFFERING OF GREAT EVIL: 5 GREAT EVILS OF THE WORLD

The Buddha said to Maitreya Bodhisattva: “Those of you born in this life, with upright minds and not doing evil, that is having great virtue.” Why is that so?

In the ten directions of the worlds of the Buddhas, where good is abundant and evil is scarce, it is very easy to enlighten. Only in this world of the five evils is it extremely painful. Now I have attained Buddhahood here to teach beings to abandon the five evils, end the five sufferings, free themselves from the five burnings, and regulate their minds to do the five good deeds, so that merit may be fulfilled.

What are the five?

The first point: Beings in the world like to commit evil, the strong oppress the weak, crush each other, kill and harm, devour one another, not knowing how to do good to bear the consequences. Therefore, some suffer together, are lonely, mute, deaf, blind, or foolishly wicked due to not believing in morality and not practicing good deeds in previous lives. Those who are noble, wealthy, wise, esteemed, and talented are so because they knew compassion, filial piety, practiced goodness, and accumulated virtue in previous lives.

When you were born with money, you did wrong, after your life went into a dark place and your body was reborn in the paths, there should be hells, animals – for example, in prison in the world there is a dramatic torture – the divine consciousness depends on the sin that has been created, but the life span is long and short, and the retribution is not over, and the crime is not over, and it is very difficult to liberate from it, and the suffering cannot be said all! The evil path circulates naturally, although there is no immediate retribution, but the good and evil are still subject to retribution

.

The second point: Worldly humanity does not follow the law, indulges excessively in lust, allowing themselves to act recklessly; those in high positions are not wise, those in power are unjust, causing wrongful harm, damaging loyal hearts, speaking differently than they feel, scheming in many ways, lying both inside and outside, foolishly getting angry, wanting benefits for themselves, being insatiably greedy, concerned with gain and loss, turning resentment into enmity, leading to broken homes and lost lives, not considering before and after, being rich yet stingy, unwilling to give alms, hoarding possessions, exhausting the mind and suffering physically, and when life ends, taking nothing along. Good and evil, misfortune and blessing, follow karma, being born either into happiness or into suffering. Seeing others doing good, yet still slandering them.tends to imitate, often thinks of stealing, lurking to seize others' possessions, spending everything and then going to seek more. Death leads to the three evil paths, suffering countless torments, revolving through many lives with great difficulty to escape, experiencing immense pain.

The third point: People rely on each other to survive in the world, yet life is not long. Those with unprincipled hearts and dishonest intentions, who harbor evil thoughts, constantly indulge in lust, overflowing with troubles, with false and loose attitudes, wasting their wealth, committing illegal acts, and refusing all requests, moreover gathering factions, raising armies, waging war, committing robbery and murder, seizing and oppressing, providing for wives and children while enjoying pleasure, causing others to despise them, worry, and suffer hardship, creating many sins, die to suffer immeasurable torment in hell, go through many lifetimes, and find it hard to attain liberation, experiencing extreme pain.

The fourth point: In life, people who do not practice virtue, lie, speak harshly, speak maliciously, gossip, envy the good, harm the virtuous, are unfilial to their parents, disrespect their teachers, fail to be sincere with friends, are arrogant and self-important, think they are right, rely on their status, oppress others hoping to be respected, feel no shame, harbor pride, are difficult to educate. Relying on a little merit from past lives, in this life they commit evil and lose all merit, their lifespan ends, evil surrounds them, resentment leads them, and there is no way to avoid it, only advancing into the cauldron of fire, their bodies torn apart, minds and spirits in torment, and by the time they think to repent, it is already too late!

Fifth: People who are indulgent and lazy, unwilling to improve or cultivate their body and mind; when parents advise them, they resist as if dealing with enemies, betray kindness without any repayment, live recklessly, indulge in alcohol and hedonism, are foolish and stubborn, have no sense of propriety, cannot be admonished, communicate with relatives without any affection, do not remember parents' kindness, do not value mentors or friends, only care for themselves, have not done a single good deed, do not trust in Buddhist teachings, do not believe in life, death, or moral consequences, wish harm upon the virtuous, destroy Buddhist teachings, are ignorant while considering themselves clever, do not know where they came from, where they will go after death, and are inhumane.On the other hand, one wants longevity. Feeling compassion and giving advice is met with refusal to listen; dry sighs and hoarse voices are also in vain. A stubborn mind refuses to understand. As the end of life approaches, regretting not having practiced goodness, when closing one's eyes in repentance, is it still in time!

In the universe, five paths are distinct, and the retribution of good and evil, blessings and calamities are clear; one must bear them oneself, no one can take their place. A good person who does good will move from a happy environment to a realm of happiness, from light to light. An evil person who does evil will move from a suffering environment to a realm of suffering, from darkness to darkness. Who can truly know this? Only the Buddha knows clearly, revealing and teaching; very few people follow. Therefore, birth and death never cease, and the evil paths are never ended. People in the world create evil in such ways, naturally resulting in the three evil paths, enduring countless sufferings, turning through many lives without a limit to escape, making it difficult to attain liberation, with indescribable pain. Thus, there exist the five evils, five sufferings, five burnings, like a great fire burning the human body.

If one wholeheartedly maintains their mind, keeps their body pure and mindful, aligns words with actions, sincerely does good deeds and refrains from doing evil, then one will attain salvation, full merit, and longevity leading to the Bodhi path. These are the five great virtues.

The Buddha told Maitreya Bodhisattva: “The five evils, five pains, and five burnings follow one another in succession; if one commits these sins, they are certain to enter the evil realms. In this life, they will suffer illness and calamities, wishing to live will be impossible, wishing to die will not succeed, making people witness such retribution. At the end of their life, they will fall into the three evil paths, endure extreme suffering, burn themselves, and cultivate mutual hatred and destruction.”

Creating a small sin that grows into a great one, being attached to wealth and beauty without willing to give, seeking personal pleasure without self-reflection, evil desire urging one to compete for personal gain, enjoying temporary wealth and glory without tolerance, not sincerely practicing goodness, soon one's power will accordingly perish, karma naturally arranges retribution, and even if one worries or panics, one must descend into the three evil paths; it has always been so. How much suffering!

You are taught by the teachings of the Buddhas to think carefully, remember diligently, and never be lazy throughout your life.

Respecting the Buddha and honoring the virtuous, kind, and compassionate, seeking liberation from the three realms, completely eradicating the root of birth and death, and entirely leaving behind fear and suffering of the three lower realms.

What is called the highest form of good deeds?

One must purify the mind and properly discipline the body, ensuring that the ears, eyes, nose, and mouth act correctly. The body and mind should be clean and aligned with goodness. Do not follow desires, do not commit evil, use harmonious speech and expressions, be diligent in bodily conduct, act with calmness and patience; rushing without careful consideration will lead to ruin and future regret, wasting a lifetime.

(Excerpt from "THE SUTRA OF IMMEASURABLE LIFE, ADORNING PURE TRANQUILITY EQUALLY AWAKENING")

tieu_de: THE REPERcussions OF DRESSING REVEALINGLY AND LIVING PROMISCUOUSLY.
tom_tat: (Buddhist disciple Ngoc Nhi – Hoang Phap Pagoda) “I pray to the wronged spirits and enemies to release me. I wish to be reborn in the Pure Land and escape this suffering.”
noi_dung:
THE CONSEQUENCES OF DRESSING IMMODERATELY AND LIVING A LICENTIOUS, IMMORAL LIFE.

(Buddhist devotee Ngoc Nhi – Hoang Phap Pagoda)

"I pray that all my resentful foes will let me go. I wish to be reborn in the Pure Land, escaping this suffering."

My name is Nguyễn Thị Ngọc Nhi, born in 1992. I am currently suffering from stage 3 breast cancer and also have syphilis. I am writing these lines to advise people not to make the same mistakes as I did, especially the young ones today. Do not live recklessly or follow the trend of showing off your body online. I pray that if I can accrue any merit, it may help eliminate my bad karma soon.

I am an orphan, grew up in An Giang, and my family was poor, so I lived with my grandmother. In my youth, I loved having fun and was led astray by friends. In 9th grade, I dropped out of school and ran away to Saigon to work as a waitress at a café in Gò Vấp.

I am someone who is very passionate about sexuality. I have been working at the shop for four months, and I met a 34-year-old man who was already married with two sons. I also slept with him when I was only 16 years old; but he had no feelings for me at all.

By the time I was six weeks pregnant, he stopped coming to the café. The café where I worked – to be more precise, a brothel – the café was just a disguise, mainly it was to entertain clients and extort money from men. When I became pregnant, the madam of the place forced me to have an abortion; I was beaten so many times that I miscarried. At that moment, I thought I wouldn’t survive this crisis; I lay in bed like that for nearly four days, and eventually, it passed on its own, I recovered on my own.

I worked there for nearly two years and then ran away. Whenever I earned eighty thousand, seventy thousand would be taken away, and I was tricked into signing a paper selling myself to them. Until now, I do not dare to return to Saigon, I am afraid of encountering them again. The trauma has haunted me for the past two years; even if I die, I cannot forget the beatings, and to this day my body is still covered with scars.

After leaving Go Vap, I rented a place in Binh Duong, worked as a sewing worker for three months, and then, unable to endure the hardship, I quit that job and became a sex worker.

I myself like to wear cool clothes, shorts with one sleeve, 2-strap shirts, deep cutouts, most of my breasts out, the purpose of stimulating sexuality for men, I don't wear underwear all day. Now lying on the chemotherapy bed, I think again because of Cause and Effect, the crime of sexual stimulation that harms people, so I have breast cancer.

Back then, to serve to find customers, I created a yahoo nick and phone number on websites, whoever needed me would take pictures of private parts, chat with webcams so that they could see their bodies, and they would go.

I also often go on Facebook and Zalo to live stream. I often join 18+ groups, engage in sexual chats to show off, averaging three to four clients per night.

During my years of working, I had more than four abortions, and the only time I carried a baby to term was because my health was too weak, so the doctor did not agree to allow an abortion.

Therefore, after giving birth, I abandoned the baby in the hospital. Out of ignorance, I only thought it was just blood and did not realize it was already a life. I, as a person, have become emotionally hardened, lacking love and familial affection for my children; now, it is already too late for regret.

I myself am very sexually infected, I go to the hospital, but the next morning, I don't know how to get tired, I go online to look for porn movies, to watch and masturbate. I masturbate two to three times a day, and in the evening I still go to the guest as usual. Thanks to the experience from watching porn movies, I have learned many sex positions to serve customers, so many patrons like me.

In September 2016, during a bath while scrubbing my body, I discovered a hard lump in my chest. Combined with frequent pain and weight loss, I went to the hospital for an examination, blood tests, and all sorts of tests. The results showed that I had breast cancer and syphilis.

My life has almost come to an end. One afternoon, after returning from a check-up, I went straight to the university village's stone pond to commit suicide and end my life. Luckily, a few students having a nearby party saved me.

The years spent in the hospital undergoing chemotherapy, without medication, were days of torment in suffering. Every time I closed my eyes and fell asleep, I saw cries, screams, and bloody images of the children whom I had aborted in the past.

Fortunately, with the help of a Buddhist laywoman who assisted with medicine expenses, I was given the good fortune to learn about Hoang Phap Pagoda, to know the Buddha, and the compassionate Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara who saves from suffering. I began to eat vegetarian and recite the Buddha's name.

I write these lines, praying that everyone abandons evil and does good, and never should have an abortion for any reason, because I myself have had many abortions and therefore have to suffer pain in my private parts as I do today.

Everyone, do not dress immodestly or show off your body, do not watch pornographic movies, or live stream sex chats. Previously, out of ignorance, I only thought that my body was mine and I could do whatever I wanted, but now, after learning about Buddhism, I realize it is a sin.

The body is created by our parents, and not knowing how to cherish it is unfilial; flaunting a naked, vulgar body is spreading bad habits, planting lustful thoughts that harm everyone's mind.

One should not masturbate; dressing provocatively is oneself burning away one's own blessings.

When I was a young girl, I was very beautiful, but since falling into licentiousness, indulging in carnal desires, my body has withered like a starving ghost, and now everyone is afraid when they see me. I used to weigh 50 kg, now only 36 kg. I know that I have committed many sins.

I pray that those to whom I owe money, or who harmed me in the past, can forgive me. Now, my body has nothing left, and I only hope to rely on these remaining energies to recite Buddha's name to escape suffering.

My life is evidence that the law of cause and effect is real. I sincerely ask everyone not to commit evil and to distance themselves from bad habits, or they may suffer as I have. I urgently ask the temple to share my life story to warn everyone.

My final wish in life is to go back to visit my grandmother. She is now over 80 years old, yet I have not been home for 5–7 years. I miss my grandmother very much; she is the only family I have, but I have not been able to take care of her. I sincerely repent.

Namo Amitabha Buddha!!!

May everyone who has the opportunity to read this article please spread it and share it with today's youth as much as possible regarding a moral way of life. And please join in reciting Buddha's name to guide the Buddhist female follower Ngoc Nhi along with the karmic enemies of hers – If her lifespan remains, may her negative karma and illness be resolved. If her lifespan ends, may she soon be embraced by Buddha Amitabha's light and guided to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, where she will never suffer again and be free from the cycle of birth and death.

Namo Amitabha Buddha – please recite often!

tieu_de: THE ORIGIN OF THE 'VERSE TO BREAK HELL' OR 'HUAYEN HALF VERSE SUTRA' THAT WE OFTEN READ WHEN OFFERING FOOD TO THE DEAD.
tom_tat: In the Huayan Sutra Stories of National Master Hien Thu of the Tang Dynasty, there is an account of the spiritual insight of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, originally written: “In the first year of Wenming (684 - Tang Yungzong), a person from the capital, surname Vuon
noi_dung:
THE ORIGIN OF THE "DAMNA-HELL LITANY" OR "HUAYAN HALF-LITANY SUTRA" THAT WE OFTEN READ WHEN OFFERING FOOD TO THE DEAD.

In the Record of the Avatamsaka Sutra by State Preceptor Hiền Thủ of the Tang dynasty, there is an account of the spiritual insight of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, verbatim:

“In the first year of the Wenming era (684 - Tang Emperor Zong), a person from the capital, surnamed Wang, whose given name is unknown, had neither precepts nor practiced virtue. Dying from illness, he saw two people leading him to the gates of hell, where he saw a monk, called Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, who instructed Wang to recite the following verse on a single practice:

If anyone wishes to know

All Buddhas of the three times

Should be contemplated in this way

The mind creates the Tathagatas.

After the Bodhisattva finished teaching the scripture, he said: 'Reciting this verse will open the gates of hell.' Vương exerted himself to recite it and immediately entered inside to meet King Yama. The king asked what merit this person had. [The attendant] replied: He only upheld a four-line verse as mentioned above. The king then released him. While Vương recited the verse, wherever the recitation echoed, those who were suffering there were all liberated.

Three days later, Mr. Vương regained consciousness, remembered that verse clearly, and recounted it to the monks. Upon examining the verse, it was found that it was exactly the verse contained in the chapter 'The Assembly of Countless Bodhisattvas in the Heaven of Da Ma Teaching the Dharma' from the twelfth scroll of the Avatamsaka Sutra, translated during the Jin dynasty (9). Mr. Vương personally recounted this story in detail to the Dharma Master Tăng Ðịnh at Không Quán Pagoda.

*Commentary: In the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows Sutra, it is said that if anyone, at the time of death, can recite even one Buddha's name, or a Pratyekabuddha, Bodhisattva, or even one four-line verse from the Mahayana Sutras, all sins except the five heinous sins and the sin of killing will be absolved. Thus, we understand that the Buddhas never speak falsely; if we find that our practice does not yield the results described in the Sutra, it means that we are doing it incorrectly, not properly, or not sincerely enough.... If someone genuinely practices according to the Sutra's teachings, they will surely receive immense benefits, even while still living, without having to wait until death to gain them 🙏

tieu_de: Reciting the Great Compassion Mantra leads to rebirth in the Ultimate Bliss
tom_tat: The first story: During the Song Dynasty, Master Huệ Tài, a native of Lạc Thanh district, Vĩnh Gia land, became a monk when he was still a child. After receiving the full ordination, he went to study in many places but was unable to understand. He blamed himself for his karma.
noi_dung:
RECITING THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA LEADS TO REBIRTH IN THE LAND OF SUPREME BLISS

The first story

In the life of the Song Dynasty, Hue Tai, a shaman, from Lac Thanh County, Yongjia Land, ordained as a child, after receiving the great vows, he went to many places to study without understanding. Hating himself for his deep karma, the shaman often recited the Great Compassion Mantra to pray for wisdom. After practicing for a long time, he suddenly dreamed that one night he saw a monk who raised a few staffs and took off his robe and put it on him. After waking up, the shaman saw that his mind was enlightened, the sutras he had heard so far, and at the same time, he remembered clearly and clearly.

Later, he sought the teachings of Master Từ Vân Sám, always serving closely nearby, where his understanding became increasingly profound. In the first year of the Trị Bình era, he resided at Pháp Huệ Bảo Pavilion and was granted the title Quảng Từ by the king. Before long, the Dharma master returned to live by the Lôi Phong stupa, diligently practicing the Pure Land teachings. He often stood on one leg reciting the Great Compassion Mantra 108 times, making it his regular practice.

In the first year of the Nguyên Phong era in spring, he, for thousands of lay followers, transmitted precepts at Lôi Phong. Just as he had begun the ritual of giving monastic robes, a bright light suddenly shone from the statue of Avalokiteshvara at the pinnacle, and the lamps and the sunlight all dimmed in comparison. Master Thủ Nhất of Tịnh Từ Temple composed the poem Giới Quang Ký because of this...

On the 21st day of the 5th month in the sixth year of the Nguyên Phong era, the Dharma master bathed, changed his robes, and ascended the preaching platform, writing a verse in praise of the Buddha, then said to the assembly: "I am certain of being reborn in the Pure Land." After speaking, he sat in silence and passed away at the age of 86.

(Excerpt from the Chronological Record of Buddhist Patriarchs)

Story Number 2

During the Republic of China era, in Taizhou, there was a monk named Thích Kim Trược, who ordained at Diên Thọ Temple at the age of 8 and at 20 received the higher precepts at Quốc Thanh Temple. On the path of practice, his master only advised reciting the Great Compassion Mantra and chanting the name of Avalokiteshvara. Following this instruction, the monk recited the mantra 48 times a day. He was often very effective in treating people’s illnesses. Many people asked him to teach the method, but he said: "I only recite the Great Compassion Mantra and chant the name of Avalokiteshvara."

In the year of Mau Thin (Republic era), the monk resided in a small hermitage, and at night was attacked by robbers attempting to steal money. After searching the entire hermitage and finding nothing, they became furious and stabbed him once in the right hand and twice in the temple. Although the injuries were severe, the monk did not die. The stab wounds gradually healed, leaving three large deep scars. This is also the result of negative karma accumulated over many lifetimes, and due to the merit of reciting prayers, the severe karmic retribution was transformed into a lighter one in this life.

In the summer of the year of Kỷ Tị, the master went to Ningbo to settle at A Dục Vương Temple, but because the number of disciples was already sufficient, his multiple requests to join were not accepted. Unsure of where to go, the master sat in meditation for half a day, without any words of resentment or a face of grievance. The supervising monk saw this and led the master to temporarily stay at the Dưỡng Tâm Hall. At the end of summer, the hall's managing monk, following the rules, did not allow him to stay. The master said: "Soon I will be reborn in the Western Paradise; please compassionately allow me to stay a little longer." The monks thought these words were boastful and showed disbelief. On the 21st, before noon, the master put on his robe and paid respects to the Buddha in the main hall, then went before the hall's managing monk.The master said, 'After noon, I will pass away.' At that time, everyone thought it was a lie. At noon, the master and the assembly had their midday meal, eating two full bowls as usual, without reduction. He then told a fellow monk, 'According to the monastery's rules, when someone dies, the body is carried into the deep mountains, requiring four men for transport. Now I have nothing, only a pair of sandals, which I humbly offer; I ask you to take care of this matter.'

Indeed, after 1 PM, the monk sat facing the West, peacefully passing away.

(Excerpt from Du Huệ Úc Sao Collection)

tieu_de: LUST IS THE ROOT OF PHYSICAL HARM
tom_tat: There are many causes of stroke, and using the perspective of modern medicine today, they come down to two types: cerebral hemorrhage and cerebral infarction due to blood vessel blockage. According to the conclusions of ancient physicians, it is considered a stroke, but
noi_dung:
SEXUAL IMMORALITY IS THE ROOT OF PHYSICAL DAMAGE

The causes of stroke are numerous; from the perspective of modern medicine, they mainly fall into two types: cerebral hemorrhage and cerebral infarction caused by vascular blockage. According to the conclusions of ancient physicians, it was considered as wind strike, but in reality, it is caused by the accumulation of fire energy ascending to the brain, leading to disorder in the upper burner. From the perspective of ancient Traditional Chinese Medicine theory, another important cause is the "decline of kidney energy."

In 2006, when I was still a resident doctor, I once saw off three patients in one night due to strokes. They all died from exhausted organ energy, and their ages were 38, 40, and 42, respectively. When writing the death certificates, I wondered why strokes appear at such a young age. If we recall the 1960s-70s, those who had strokes back then were 60-70 years old, even up to 80 years old. But why nowadays do so many people in their early 30s suffer fatal strokes?

The reasons could be that people consume too much animal food, causing fat to accumulate in the body. However, there are still many people who eat a lot but do not suffer from strokes. Another cause is “kidney qi deficiency,” which leads to kidney failure as a result of excessive sexual activity. I would like to share a case with you. A friend of mine is an entrepreneur in the printing and publishing industry, only 32 years old but already had a stroke. When he met me, he confidently said: “Doctor Bành, I am very wealthy now and I change mistresses three times a year.” He considered this a very proud achievement.

I answered: "Then an accident will not be far from you." Why? Because for a person with kidney qi deficiency, it can lead to a series of misfortunes affecting the body, mind, career, and family. This person is also educated and came to me for help in taking care of his health. His symptoms include very small legs, weak steps, and a feeling of faltering when walking. People with very small legs fall into the category of weak kidneys (kidney qi deficiency). When I examined his kidney pulse, the kidneys were very weak. He also showed signs of frequent urination, going about 9-10 times each night.

This is a sign of very serious kidney damage. He wanted me to help treat his frequent urination because it greatly affected his work. I replied: 'Okay, but during the time you take the medicine, you must abstain from sexual activity.' After prescribing the medicine for him, two weeks later he no longer had frequent urination. Afterwards, he asked me about the next maintenance plan for his body. I replied: 'You must abstain from sexual activity (celibacy) for one year or more.'

Because this person has suffered serious kidney damage, as a doctor I cannot speak falsely. I see many doctors compromise with the desires of their patients, but this is an extreme destruction to their health. Therefore, I told him that he must abstain from sexual activity for at least a year or more and absolutely have no improper behavior with a mistress. Because these things will cause legitimate harm to his body.

When I said this, he was very surprised, because whenever he met business partners, he usually went with them to karaoke bars or brothels to satisfy the clients' desires. This not only puts himself into the fire pit but also others into the fire pit. I told him, “If you do not restrain yourself, your health will be seriously damaged.” But he did not listen. Then I met him for the second time, and when I took his pulse, I discovered that his sensitive pulse reached the large intestine meridian point, signaling that he was about to have a stroke.

But he didn't listen and said: “I am still so young, how could I have this disease, don't scare me anymore.” I then replied: “Then just wait and see the natural laws, because what I am saying comes from the words of ancient famous doctors compiled from long ago. These are all natural laws verified by history. If you don't want to follow them, then just let your own body be the experiment.” Yet he continued doing what he wanted to do.

Half a year later, I met him again. He displayed a phenomenon of extreme excitement to the point of being unable to sleep. He was accompanied by a very provocative girl. For provocative girls, they cause three types of harm to men: first, they attract men and deplete all of a man's vital essence.

The second harm will cause a career to collapse; many dynasties of kings have been destroyed because of one or two women, let alone just one person. I told him: “This girl will hurt you very badly, you must quickly stay away from her, otherwise disaster will not be far from you. If you do not listen to me, then we will see how the truth unfolds.”

So he continued his degenerate lifestyle, and six months later, retribution appeared. He suffered from a crooked mouth and eyes, paralysis on one side of his body, and could not maintain his balance while walking. His mouth was twisted to one side, and his eyes were droopy.

This is a typical symptom of a stroke. Moreover, if a normal person suffers a stroke that is not of the “kidney qi deficiency” type, recovery can take from six months to a year, and walking no longer results in imbalance. As for strokes caused by kidney deficiency, recovery is not possible even after three years. He has not recovered for the past three years, and speaking is still very difficult. This is exactly the harmful consequence caused by kidney damage.

When he met me, the first sentence he said was: “I deeply regret not listening to the doctor, which led to my current condition.” He is the experiment before our eyes. In the past, he worked in publishing and had a very successful career, but since he had a stroke, his career has collapsed. The girls who were involved with him before have all left, leaving him alone in the hospital. Every day, the nurse helps him down from the bed, pushes a wheelchair to let him bask in the sun, and he speaks with great difficulty.

I call this "immorality." "Immorality" refers to evil deeds, and "licentiousness" refers to unprincipled debauchery. The consequences of immorality on the body are indeed very serious. Immorality can damage a person's kidney energy, causing many diseases in the body. A person with kidney damage often has a volatile mood, is easily angered, has a chaotic mind, and is prone to making wrong decisions...

Anyone who has these states is about to encounter an accident. Their family and career will also face disaster. That is why the ancients said, "Of all evils, sexual immorality is the foremost." If a person is the king of a dynasty and is promiscuous, then that person and the dynasty will not be far from destruction.

Severe Harm of Masturbation & Sexual Addiction
