tieu_de: SEARCHING FOR PAST LIVES TO RESOLVE CURRENT GRUDGES
tom_tat: I am not happy. Because we rushed into marriage before our love had matured, my husband and I live together like two strangers in the same house. The only thing keeping us in this bleak marriage
noi_dung:
SEARCHING FOR PAST LIVES TO RESOLVE CURRENT GRUDGES

I am not happy. Because we rushed into marriage before our love matured, my husband and I live together like two strangers in the same house. The only thing that binds us to remain in this bleak marriage is our children.

I know, to become each other's spouse, there must be some special destiny between us. Why did I marry this man, and not anyone else? Whenever I feel sad and lonely because of a life lacking love, I often ask myself that question.

My name is Chúc Quyên, I grew up in a poor farming family in Nam Định, and since childhood I have admired Buddhism, immediately enjoying reading Buddhist sutras whenever I encountered them.

When I grew up and got married, I followed my husband to live with his parents in Hanoi. I always tried to fully honor my duties as a daughter-in-law, paying great attention to my words, speech, and actions in front of my grandparents, never daring to raise my voice or argue back. But for some reason, the more I tried to please my parents-in-law, the more they pushed me away, even scolding me and saying things that insulted my family.

Everything I do has become an eyesore to my parents-in-law. They oppose my chanting and recitation of Buddhist scriptures, being strict and nitpicking me over the smallest things. I am very distressed, not understanding what I did wrong to deserve such a situation.

The frustrations in marriage and clashes with my parents-in-law have left me withered, leaving me only with seeking refuge in the Buddhist path. But whenever they see me chanting, they forbid me, calling it foolish, so I only dare to chant the scriptures silently in my heart.

Especially my father-in-law, he treats me like an enemy. He finds every reason to scold me, and as a daughter-in-law, I can only endure it silently. Basically, he looks for excuses to scold, so there is no need for any reasoning about right or wrong. There was even a time when he threatened to hit me, but did not because the neighbors intervened. Sometimes, I feel like I am being imprisoned, trapped with no way out.

One evening, after chanting sutras, I silently prayed to the Buddha, hoping He would help me understand the karmic relationship between my husband and me, so I could release the burden that has been weighing on me for so long. After praying, I went to sleep.

That night, I had a very special dream, vivid and strangely lifelike. I saw a village. There, a large number of villagers, led by a sorcerer, were holding weapons and clubs, chasing a horde of demons. Somehow, they captured and sealed them inside cages that looked like glass cabinets.

They lit torches, stood around, sealed the cages, and then left.

In fear, I turned my head to the side and what caught my eyes was a demon with a bluish face, pale, sallow skin like a zombie. I was stunned to realize that I myself was also a demon trapped inside it.

My chest felt as heavy as if a boulder were pressing down on it. I was still conscious, but unable to move, my mouth rigid and unable to speak.

Desperate, I prayed for someone to come and save me. When I was still free out there, I had never harmed anyone. I kept praying like that continuously for three days. On the third day, I prayed that if someone came to save me, I would be grateful for life.

Suddenly, right after that, someone appeared, tore the seal, and freed me. And I realized that person was my current husband.

Passing through another dream. I saw myself as a concubine in the royal palace. My husband at that time was a prince, the king's son, but he was not favored by the king. On top of that, the prince was slandered and falsely accused by other concubines behind his back. Because in my past life I owed him gratitude for saving my life (he was the one who broke the seal and released me – that is, the demon), at that time, I devoted myself to protecting him, standing up to explain and defend the prince.

Upon waking, I realized why I should be married to this man. It turned out that in a previous life, I owed him a debt of gratitude for saving my life, so over many lifetimes, fate led me to meet him and do everything to repay him.

I continued to persistently chant sutras every day. Not long after, another dream came.

In the dream, I saw myself as a fairly well-off woman, with plenty to eat and own, and I had servants in the house. At that time, I was very fierce, often scolding and berating a young male servant. Sometimes I even threatened to hit him, but had not yet acted.

I realized that boy is actually my father-in-law in this life. It's truly fair; insulting others will lead to being insulted in return. I am being treated by my father-in-law exactly the same way I treated that boy in the previous life.

It turns out that the suffering I experience in my life with my husband and his family all has its root cause from the karmic debts I owe them from a past life.

If it were not for my persistence in chanting sutras and wholeheartedly directing my mind towards the Buddha, and being blessed by the Buddha to know, perhaps I would still be confused and trapped, blaming circumstances and immersed in suffering without a way out.

So, how did I have the affinity to come to know the Dharma and learn to chant sutras and recite the Buddha's name early on?

One night, I had a dream from a past life, and received an answer.

In that life, during the feudal era of kings, a long, long time ago, I was a monk who had left home to practice at a temple in a secluded mountain. Because of diligent cultivation, I had some spiritual power, yet my competitive nature was something I could not control.

One day, when the abbot was away, the brothers in the temple gathered to chat. One of them, in high spirits, challenged the others, organizing a contest to see who was the most talented, by summoning incarnations of the Arhats.

At that time, I immediately volunteered to be the first. For about an hour, I wholeheartedly prayed, asking the Arhats to come. Indeed, in the end, the Arhats appeared, each manifesting on a large tree, with 18 of them having 18 different appearances.

I won that contest. But in my spiritual life during that incarnation, I failed miserably. That was because I practiced while my mind was still full of craving for victory. After the time I invited the incarnations of the Arhats, my merit and virtue seriously declined. Not only did I not achieve anything in that lifetime, at the end of that life, I was even reborn as a ghost, which was the life my husband saved me from.

Fortune, the good affinity with the Buddha's Dharma is very firm; even if one falls into decline, after many lifetimes, when bad karma has been repaid, the affinity for cultivation will rise again. That is why, in this lifetime, from a young age, I have had a heart of reverence for the Buddha's Dharma. At only 9-10 years old, I already knew to cultivate the intention to eat vegetarian, to release crabs and snails, and whenever encountering Buddhist scriptures, I would immediately enjoy reading and chanting them.

Recently, around January 2020, I confided the blockages in my life to a Buddhist lay brother. He advised me to dedicate the merit from reciting sutras and chanting Buddha's name to my husband and parents-in-law. That is the fastest way to repay debts; once the debts are fully paid, they will no longer trouble me, and I will regain my peace.

I applied that method, reciting scriptures more and more diligently. I recited the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, the Ten Thousand Buddhas Sutra, the Ullambana Sutra, the Amitābha Sutra, the Great Compassion Mantra, and the Repentance Sutra, about 4 hours a day, for several months, dedicating the merit to my husband and parents-in-law. In addition, I also dedicated it to all hostile spirits and sentient beings throughout the Dharma realm.

Indeed, after a while, my family became truly peaceful, and I was less often scolded by my parents-in-law as before. Only on the days I stopped eating vegetarian and switched to eating meat, troubles would arise, but otherwise, everything was calm.

Before I had a herniated disc, I often suffered from back pain, which was terribly intense. After diligently chanting sutras and dedicating the merit, the pain naturally disappeared, and my children also did not get minor illnesses. The power of Buddhist scriptures is truly incredibly miraculous.

Through the times I learned about my past lives, I have come to deeply understand the fairness and strength of the law of cause and effect. There is nothing unreasonable or unfair in this world; it is simply because people do not know what seeds they planted in the past. They suffer, yet do not know why they suffer, constantly blaming heaven or others, or seeking all sorts of superstitions in hopes of escaping suffering. This is the current situation of many people, including myself in the past.

Fortunately for those who are karmically connected to the Dharma, they believe in cause and effect, and know how to follow the methods taught by the Buddha to resolve their karmic obstacles. Not only do they find peace and joy in the present, but they also enjoy immeasurable wholesome merits in the future, when they have attained Buddhahood. May more and more people and beings receive this wonderful auspicious affinity.

( Quang Tử - Hoàng Anh, rewritten from the account of Chúc Quyên )

tieu_de: WITH A LUSTFUL THOUGHT, THE HEAVENLY MAIDEN IS IMMEDIATELY FALLEN
tom_tat: (Excerpt from 'Causality Explanation Lương Hoàng Sám 2 – Quả Khanh') In 1990, in Nanjing, a female director came to ask Quả Lâm like this:
noi_dung:
HAVING A LUSTFUL THOUGHT, THE HEAVENLY MAIDEN IMMEDIATELY FALLS

(Excerpt from “Supplementary Karma Explanation of Lương Hoàng Sám 2 – Quả Khanh)

In 1990, in Nanjing, a female director came to ask Quả Lâm like this:

- My mother is 70 years old this year, has had heart disease for two years, and also suffers from severe asthma.

Quả Lâm said:

- Is your mother intelligent, skillful with her hands, and very fond of embroidery?

As soon as she was asked, her face lit up, and she hurriedly boasted that this is a naturally gifted genius. When she was twelve, her mother had already become famous for her beautiful embroidery all over near and far. Currently, although she has been ill and bedridden for two years, she refuses to do nothing, even embroidering pillowcases and garments for her grandsons and granddaughters… so that later, when they get married, they will have them to use. All the grandchildren admire her. Because the heart disease treatment costs a lot of money and is not curable, she is very worried about her mother. She told this while shedding tears.

Mr. Lam said:

- Don't be overly sad; as humans, we must experience birth, aging, sickness, and death. Hospitals cannot cure all patients. Your mother in her previous life was a celestial maiden in the Weaving Palace, belonging to the Dao Li Heaven. Because beings in the Desire Realm still have worldly desires, when she observed the human world with her heavenly eye, she immediately developed feelings of attachment (also because she had karmic connections with your father in a past life, she was bound by this karmic desire, which led to misguidance...), and therefore she was immediately fallen and reincarnated into the human world.

Time in the heavens is so brief that it is like… taking a sip of water, yet on earth, more than ten years have already passed! Therefore, when the celestial beings discovered that their friend was absent, they immediately bowed their heads to look down upon the human world to search… and saw that her mother already had a house full of children and grandchildren. Because when she took a heavenly form she harbored impure thoughts, her mother suffered the karmic consequence of developing a heart disease.

You can repent on behalf of your mother before the Buddha, and recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for her in front of a Buddha statue. The more you recite, the greater the merit. Because the merit of reciting the sutra is divided into seven parts, and your mother will only receive one part (You should let your mother clearly know her own situation so that her own act of repentance will be more effective).

According to popular beliefs (including arguments as well as movies, books…), most people often gather to romanticize love, weaving elaborate decorations around it, always beautifying and praising romantic love in every way… Completely unaware that: even if it is proper sexual conduct, it is still not perfect and complete as they imagine. On this point, please refer to the Sutra on the Ten Wholesome Precepts to see clearly. Therefore, in the Shurangama Sutra, the Buddha declares: "If the lustful mind is not eliminated, the defilements cannot be transcended"…

Moreover, when your mother lies down, having her head tilted to the left is wrong. I see two things that she should not use. First: next to her is a cloth bag containing only white objects; I can see them but cannot clearly identify what they are. Second: on the wall opposite your mother's bed, a painting is hanging. The two items I just mentioned do not belong to your household. Therefore, they will emit depressing negative energy, making your mother short of breath and uncomfortable.

The female director was astonished and stunned, quickly saying:

- My younger sister is the head nurse at the hospital. Since my mother has a lot of phlegm, she often brings some gauze from the hospital's stock to save for my mother to spit and wipe her mouth. My sister said, "Anyone working at the hospital can take some for personal use." As for the painting on the wall, it was given to the hospital by a patient upon discharge as a token of gratitude, and the hospital shared it with the staff to take home. And yet, is that still not allowed?

Lâm asked:

- Taking gauze (which is property of the hospital) home for personal use is considered stealing. Caring for your mother is good, but using stolen public property is bad! Because creating mixed good and bad karma like this, once the result comes: joy will be accompanied by suffering! The painting is a token of gratitude from patients to the hospital, thus it belongs to the hospital's property. If, upon receiving or using it, everyone paid a certain amount to contribute to the public fund, perhaps it wouldn’t be a problem! The act of distributing the painting to civil servants is an action of "taking public resources for private gain"; anyone who accepts it brings bad energy into their own home, and the karmic consequences they have to bear will be even greater...

This is the experience I have drawn from my path of learning Buddhism; in fact, there are many such stories. Suddenly, I remembered a small story, and I would like to share it as a gift to you.

In his commentaries, Master Tuyen Hoa often talked about the situation of the Devas in the Six Desire Heavens, from the First Jhana downwards (such as: Four Heavenly Kings, Trayastrimsha, Yama, Tusita, Nimmānarati, and Paranimmita Vasavatti) stating that Devas and humans in our world have similar forms and also marry, only that the higher the rank, the lighter the expression of desire.

Master Hsuan Hua explained the desires in the heavenly realms as follows:

Four Heavenly Kings, Trayastrimsha, desire: Embracing each other

Yama: Holding hands, Tusita: Smiling.

Nirmanarati: Just a glance is enough.

These are the sensual pleasures of the six heavenly realms.

If a diligent practitioner cultivates, one day when heavenly wisdom is opened, one will clearly see all the situations of the devas in the three realms.

We ordinary people, because we do not understand the Buddha's teachings, consider that every thought and motion of the mind is a sin and a cause of karma. We often reason: "Being near the front veranda allows one to enjoy viewing the moon," so we tend to exploit our official duties and crave to use public property as if it were our own. Some even think, "That is because I am fortunate." They completely fail to realize that this is a deluded greed, anger, and ignorance, which is very pitiable.

A person who behaves in such a way is driven by greed; if they want to atone for their mistakes, they should spend some money on supporting education, helping the poor, or entrusting it to charitable organizations, or assisting in printing moral books, scriptures, etc., which can also help eliminate karmic offenses.

We ourselves have bought many volumes of Master Hsuan Hua's "Enlightenment" to give to others, in order to atone for our own greed. Because this book teaches us to understand cause and effect clearly, and know how we should behave as human beings.

We should not underestimate ourselves; it is certainly not the case that this is the first life in which we have started studying Buddhism. If that were so, we would not be able to participate in the Bowing Repentance of the Precious, or listen to the Dharma Sutras… Venerable Hsuan Hua explained: Whoever can listen to the Shurangama Sutra, read the Shurangama Sutra, or recite the Shurangama Mantra already has deeply planted karmic affinities with the Buddha. Therefore, we must surely generate the supreme Bodhi resolve, cultivate a courageous mind, repent past mistakes, awaken immediately, practice 'Tathagata meditation, perfectly fulfill the Six Paramitas and myriad virtuous practices, making the world everywhere a Dharma assembly; by upholding precepts, concentration and wisdom will manifest in the present.'

-------------------------------------------

*Commentary: The realms of the heavens are not the kind of realms that ordinary people like us can discuss. Without the heavenly eye, spiritual insight, it is difficult for you to see or reach them! Nowadays, we all believe that science has developed and discovered planets, but why can’t we see the heavenly realms, and thus assume that they don’t exist? It is because they exist in a different dimension. If we try to use science to explain Buddhism, it is impossible to fully explain it. Buddhism is the truth of the universe, not only on our Earth but also on countless other planets throughout the universe, and even in the heavenly realms it is revered. Buddhism differs from heterodox paths in thatEven if one does not believe in the Buddha but performs good deeds, one will still enjoy merit and be born in the heavens; conversely, if one believes in the Buddha but does evil deeds, one will still fall into hell as usual. We are like ants; how could ants know that there are great and beautiful civilized cities in the world, or like worms enjoying the pile of dung they are crawling in, thinking it is pleasure, without knowing that there are countless better worlds outside! Even so, the heavenly realm is not the realm to aspire to, because it has not yet transcended the three realms; when merit runs out, one still falls as usual. Nowadays, as we come to know the Buddha's teachings, we should aspire to be reborn in the Ultimate.Be joyous because this is the shortcut path taught by the Buddha through which we can become Buddhas in one lifetime! Today, we are truly extremely fortunate to know the practice of Buddha recitation. If we do not diligently practice, it is like going to a mountain of gold and returning empty-handed! You should very much take note of this!

卍 Homage to the Original Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha 卍

卍 Homage to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva 卍

卍 Homage to the Western Pure Land

The Great Compassionate World

Guiding Master Amitabha Buddha 卍

卍 Homage to Amitabha Buddha 卍

May the merit and virtue be dedicated to all disciples and sentient beings so that they all completely achieve Buddhahood, repaying the four great debts above and relieving the sufferings of the three realms below. If anyone sees or hears this, may they generate the Bodhi mind, and at the end of this life, be born together in the Pure Land.

AFTER 2 CLINICAL DEATHS,

FINALLY, MY MOTHER HAS ATTAINED SUPREME BLISS.

I grew up in a family that has practiced Buddhism for three generations in Bến Lức, Long An. Since I was little, I followed my mother to the temple, ate vegetarian food, and recited Buddha's name; that was truly a great blessing. My dharma name is Diệu Hòa. My mother's name is Nguyễn Thị Ba, with the dharma name Diệu Tịnh.

Since I was little, my mother has had a deep faith in Amitabha Buddha and Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. She lived a kind and virtuous life, always diligently practicing Buddha recitation, as well as helping those who were unfortunate and in distress. And she also taught her children to follow that way of life as they grew up into good people.

However, although she often recited the Buddha's name, because she had no one to guide her, she still did not know about making the vow for rebirth. The essence of Pure Land Buddhism in seeking birth in the Ultimate Bliss consists of three things: Faith – Vow – Practice; lacking any one of these, one cannot achieve rebirth.

Faith is a firm belief in the truthfulness of Amitabha Buddha and the Pure Land.

Vow is a prayer, wishing that after death, when worldly attachments have ended, Amitabha Buddha will shine his light to guide one to the Pure Land, never again to suffer from the pains of this world.

Practice refers to the merits accumulated through reciting the Buddha's name, chanting sutras, giving alms, releasing living beings, helping others, etc. All good deeds are dedicated to the aspiration of being reborn in the Pure Land.

Regarding Tin and Hanh, my mother had accomplished it, but because she had no virtuous teachers to enlighten and guide her, she did not know how to make a vow at all.

Suddenly one day, my mother fell seriously ill, her tongue retracted, her eyes stared blankly, and she stopped breathing. Everyone started worrying about the funeral, and my mother was also quite old, so her passing was not something surprising at all.

But for some reason, I still firmly believed one thing: my mother could not die. At that time, I knelt before the Three Jewels, asking to reduce my own lifespan to share with my mother. Then I disregarded everything else, focusing solely on being with her, sincerely chanting Buddha's name in the hope that she would come back to life. I seemed to forget all about time and space, constantly reciting "Namo Amitabha Buddha," dedicating the merit to my mother. And yet a miracle happened: after 15 hours of clinical death, my mother truly came back to life.

Everyone and I were overjoyed, surrounding my mother and asking how she was. From the moment she came back to life, she completely gave up meat and fish, eating purely 100% vegetarian.

By 2016, once again, my mother fell gravely ill and was clinically dead for 15 hours. Having had the experience before, I went to the Three Jewels to offer my own lifespan to my mother, then sincerely chanted Buddha's name. And the miracle happened once more; after 15 hours, my mother woke up, much to the joy of everyone, without any medicine or medical, hospital intervention.

In the following period, I was fortunate to come into contact with many pure Land practitioners and read many Buddhist scriptures, which allowed me to understand more deeply the teachings of the Buddha. And I also didn’t forget to share it with my mother.

The most crucial point was that I guided my mother to make a vow for rebirth, that when this life comes to an end, she would wish to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha. And to dedicate the merits accumulated throughout her life to that wish. After hearing this, she immediately followed, and every day she became more diligent in chanting the Buddha's name than before.

One day, I dreamed that Amitabha Buddha lowered a lotus into our house. Upon waking, I guessed that my mother was probably about to pass away. Therefore, I made a vow to recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for 49 consecutive days, dedicating the merit to my mother, praying for her karmic obstacles to be removed, for her blessings to grow, and for her to be reborn in the Pure Land.

When the 49 days of reciting the Kṣitigarbha Sutra were almost complete, my mother informed me and everyone else that in a few days, on the 19th day of the 9th lunar month, Amitabha Buddha would welcome her to be reborn in the Pure Land.

On the 19th day of the 9th lunar month in 2017, exactly on the day of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara's temple, because my mother had forewarned me, I invited my fellow devotees to my house, and everyone together chanted the Universal Gate Sutra, anxiously waiting...

Sure enough, after chanting for 15 minutes, while her mind was still clear, my mother passed away peacefully with a satisfied expression on her face.

A few hours later, when everyone checked the body, they found that only the top of the head was warm. On the day of the burial, at night I dreamed that my mother appeared, wearing a bright yellow outfit. She waved at me and said that she had gone to the Western Pure Land.

During the 49 days that followed, my family strictly refrained from killing any living beings, and even the funeral only had vegetarian food. Moreover, a large number of monks also chanted prayers to dedicate merit for her.

On the 20th night after my mother passed away, I dreamt of her appearing again. She told me, "The path to Ultimate Bliss is traveled by very few, while the path down (to the evil realms) is crowded. Because although many people recite the Buddha's name, they wish for various things in the world, and they recite superficially, not with single-minded devotion."

My mother also explained further that during the two times she was clinically dead, because I sincerely recited Buddha's name, asking to share my lifespan with her, combined with the fact that since childhood my mother often ate vegetarian and recited Buddha's name, although she had not yet made a vow to be reborn in the Pure Land, the Buddha allowed her to remain. By the third time, thanks to hearing my guidance, she was able to let go of her attachment to this temporary worldly life, made a vow for rebirth in the Pure Land, and with complete faith, vows, and practice, she was able to return to the Buddha in this way.

And thus, the greatest wish of my life, hoping for my mother to return to the realm of Amitabha Buddha, has been fulfilled. I hope that each of us children, while fulfilling our filial duties, in addition to caring for and supporting our parents, will prepare provisions for our parents to have sufficient Faith, Morality, and Vows to return to Amitabha Buddha in the Pure Land, because that is the best thing we can do for our parents. As for myself, I vow to live my entire life in the True Dharma with a heart of service and gratitude, and I vow to use Compassion, Wisdom, and Courage to study, practice diligently, and hope that myself and all sentient beings, at the end of this life, will be reborn in the Pure Land.

(Quang Tử - Thu Thủy, rewritten from the account of Diệu Hòa)

Source: nhanqua.com.vn

HOW TO ATTAIN REBIRTH IN THE PURE LAND?

Bùi Thị Loan:

– Quang Tử, lately I increasingly realize that life is full of suffering, so I want to pray for rebirth in the Pure Land rather than cure all my illnesses, hoping that the Buddha will guide me to rebirth as soon as possible.

So what do I need to do? Thank you very much.

Quang Tu:

– Dear friend, the Pure Land is a very popular practice nowadays, and it is one of the three largest sects in Buddhism. It cannot be understood superficially, so you need to seriously study and learn a lot before entering into deep practice. Quang Tu will only briefly explain the basic part, then introduce you to the necessary sutras and books.

The Pure Land practice has 3 necessary and sufficient conditions for Rebirth:

1. FAITH (Belief)

You need to have a deep and firm faith in the Pure Land. Be certain that Amitabha Buddha exists, that there is the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and that it is possible to practice in order to be reborn there.

2. VOW (Making a vow)

You need to generate a strong intention, VOW to be reborn in the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha. The following is one of many ways to make a vow for rebirth:

Making a vow for rebirth

“Namo Great Compassionate and Merciful Guide Master Amitabha Buddha! I sincerely devote my whole heart with the vow to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha! I pray for the Buddha's compassionate guidance!”

3. MERIT (Virtue)

You need to recite “Namo Amitabha Buddha” and genuinely perform many meritorious deeds and accumulate blessings, whether by reciting the Buddha’s name, the Bodhisattva’s name, giving alms, observing precepts, chanting sutras, sealing and transmitting, releasing life, or any other virtuous acts, and then dedicate the merits to request rebirth in the Pure Land.

Specifically, every day you recite the Buddha's name a lot, or perform other wholesome deeds… there are many ways to create merit in Buddhism: reciting the Buddha's name, bowing to the Buddha, chanting sutras, reciting mantras, repentance, making vows, releasing animals, distributing scriptures, doing good deeds, giving alms, helping people, building temples, casting statues, etc… though different in method, all are taught by the Buddha and all generate merit.

Because each person's circumstances are different, their fundamental capacities are different, and their preferences are different, there are many different methods, so that each person can choose the method that suits them best to apply.

All the merit that is accumulated should be dedicated to be reborn in the Pure Land with Amitabha Buddha.

Many people mechanically think that only by reciting 'Namo Amitabha Buddha' can one be reborn in the Pure Land. In fact, this is not the case; besides reciting 'Namo Amitabha Buddha,' all types of merit can be dedicated for rebirth in the Pure Land.

In the Avatamsaka Sutra, Bodhisattva Samantabhadra teaches that by making the Ten Great Vows of Samantabhadra, one can also be reborn in the Pure Land.

In the Great Compassion Mantra Sutra, Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara teaches that reciting the Great Compassion Mantra also leads to rebirth in the Pure Land, not only being born into the Sukhavati of Amitabha Buddha, but also one can be born into the Pure Land of any Buddha.

In the Infinite Life Sutra, Chapter 24 – The Three Levels of Rebirth, the Buddha teaches:

"O Ananda! The devas and humans in the ten directions who sincerely wish to be reborn in that land fall into three categories:

The superior beings are those who have renounced worldly desires to become monks, have set their minds on Bodhi, focus on chanting Amitabha Buddha, PERFORM MERITORIOUS DEEDS, AND VOW TO BE REBORN IN THAT LAND.

These sentient beings, at the time of death, are met by Amitabha Buddha along with the Holy Assembly, and immediately follow the Buddha to be reborn in that land, naturally manifesting in seven-jewel lotus flowers, with powerful wisdom and unhindered spiritual abilities.

The middle rank consists of those who, although not monks, PERFORM MANY MERITFUL DEEDS, aspire to Supreme Bodhi, and concentrate on reciting Amitabha Buddha. Although they have performed many meritorious deeds, kept precepts, built stupas and statues, made offerings, hung banners, lit lamps, and offered flowers and incense… ALL MUST BE DEDICATED WITH THE VOW TO BE REBORN IN Sukhavati. At the time of death, the emanation of Amitabha Buddha appears with complete auspicious marks and radiance, just like the Buddha himself, along with the assembly of great beings surrounding and attending to the person, guiding them. They then go with the emanated Buddha to be reborn in the Pure Land, at the stage of Non-retrogressing Supreme Bodhi, with virtues and wisdom matching the higher level of excellence.

The lower grade refers to those who, hypothetically, do not often perform meritorious deeds, but have generated the aspiration for Supreme Bodhi, focus wholeheartedly on reciting Amitabha Buddha’s name, rejoice in deep faith without a hint of doubt, and sincerely wish to be born in the Pure Land. When such a person passes away, they see the Buddha in a dream and are able to be reborn there, with merit and wisdom corresponding to the middle level…”

Thus, we see that the Buddha did not say, “Only by reciting Namo Amitabha Buddha can one be reborn.” He only said that “those who focus wholeheartedly on reciting Amitabha Buddha, rejoice in deep faith without a hint of doubt, and sincerely wish to be born in the Pure Land” belong to the lower grade.

For the Middle to Superior levels, besides chanting Buddha's name, one must also DO MANY MERITORIOUS DEEDS and DEDICATE MERIT WISHING TO BE REBORN IN THE PURE LAND.

And another point to note is that for all three levels – Superior, Middle, and Inferior – the Buddha mentioned that one must GENERATE THE SUPREME BODHICITTA.

So what is the Supreme Bodhicitta? It is to vow to become a Buddha above, and vow to save all sentient beings below.

Finally, dedicate all the merit from chanting Buddha’s name, generating the Supreme Bodhicitta, and other merits to WISH FOR REBIRTH IN THE PURE LAND.

Below is one of the many ways to dedicate merit for rebirth:

“I dedicate the merit of … to seek that I soon eliminate all karmic ties with the mundane world, quickly be reborn in the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha, swiftly attain the Supreme Perfect Enlightenment, and extensively save all sentient beings from the sea of suffering of birth and death.”

_________________

The above is just a basic general introduction; for specifics, you need to study a lot more. At the very least, you should go through the Infinite Life Sutra and also study many teachings on the Pure Land practice (such as the book 'Hometown of Ultimate Bliss' by Venerable Tuyen Hoa...) to gain deeper understanding, because only with deep understanding can one diligently and strongly practice.

tieu_de: QUANG SAID 'TRULY PRACTICING' DOES NOT ONLY MEAN RECITING BUDDHA'S NAME! For ordinary people who generate the intention to learn Buddhism, their actions
tom_tat: If you want to educate people, you must truly act yourself, and others will gain confidence. Quang said that 'truly acting' does not only mean reciting the Buddha's name! Generally, when someone generates the intention to learn Buddhism, their actions must be elevated.
noi_dung:
QUANG SAYS “TRULY DOING” DOESN'T JUST MEAN CHANTING BUDDHA'S NAME! For ordinary people who generate the mind to learn Buddhism, their actions

If you want to educate others, you yourself must truly act, and people will be confident. Quang said “truly act” does not only mean reciting Buddha's name! Any person who aspires to learn Buddhism must have deeds that surpass ordinary people. Saying “surpass” means putting all effort into maintaining the proper moral standards, fulfilling all duties, with a kind father and filial child being things that should be done. At all times, in all situations, one must carefully maintain sincerity; whenever the mind stirs to do anything, it must be “avoid doing evil deeds, be willing to do good deeds.” If someone is deluded and doesn’t have faith, one must use true sincerity toSpeak about the laws of cause and effect that you know. If you do not know, you should not force yourself to speak. Sentient beings are deluded, as if born blind; they are confused but originally have a home. To return, they must rely on a guide to avoid bumping into walls or falling into pits. Those being guided must completely follow the words of the guide, without generating any opposition. If they go against it, not only can they not reach home, but they may also lose their life. The Pure Land teachings as spoken by the Buddha are precisely the guiding teacher for all sentient beings in the three realms. Sentient beings who follow the Buddha's teachings in practice will certainly reach the Western Pure Land, which is their original home, where they can enjoy bliss.peace. Just because using worldly desires does not understand the holy intellect, one then considers oneself clever, and ends up being confused, questioning, and nitpicking, truly pitiable!

- Excerpt from Master An Quang's Dharma Writings, Compiled by Tăng Quảng Chánh, Volume 02.

tieu_de: FINALLY I UNDERSTAND: WHAT IS CALLED 'REPENTANCE'.
tom_tat: - Doctor: Nguyen Trong Hung - When I was young, I had a younger sibling who was 5 years younger and very frail. Feeling sorry for my sibling, I only wished for rain to go catch and behead him, skin him to feed him, wishing him to grow tall like his peers. As a result, until
noi_dung:
FINALLY I UNDERSTAND: WHAT IS CALLED "REPENTANCE".

- Doctor: Nguyễn Trọng Hùng -

When I was little, I had a younger sibling who was 5 years younger and very underdeveloped. Feeling sorry for my sibling, I only wished for rain so I could go catch and skin frogs to feed my sibling, hoping my sibling would grow tall like other kids and friends. As a result, even at 40 years old, my sibling was still only 1.4m tall. (Everyone needs to think about this when buying "golden frogs to make tea flowers").

A whole life of illness and extreme suffering. When it came time to depart, the circumstances were tragic, falling from the 8th floor and no one knew why. Was it someone who threw her down, or did she take her own life to relieve her mother of suffering, having to worry for her child all her life, and also to free herself?

I myself have also been through ups and downs, rising and falling many times. My abilities have never been inferior to anyone's, yet I keep facing endless hardships.

As people say: "Humans can clearly see the faults of others, but how many can see their own faults?"

I often perform rituals for many people, for the karmic enemies and debtors of past lives who have struggled, those who, because of killing or cruelty, encounter one disaster after another, even bedridden, unable to walk for many days.

One day, while I was performing a ritual for the peace of everyone, praying for their karmic enemies and debtors to be liberated, to eliminate hatred, and for their minds to be light and transcend without tormenting the householders anymore, I suddenly heard a voice:

"Master, why don't you pray for yourself? Around you, so many injustices are crying out for revenge, blood is flowing, heads are falling, scattered everywhere."

If it were in the past, I would certainly argue to the end, but this time I remained silent, reflecting deeply, and could not understand. Perhaps it is time to be liberated. I suddenly recalled in my mind (or perhaps they allowed me to see) the scene of so many frogs, and other animals, being decapitated and skinned, writhing in a basin, blood and viscera oozing...

I even saw my younger brother, emaciated, with a water-soaked face in a very horrifying scene.

My younger sibling said:

"I am the one who benefited from countless acts of killing, so I must bear the karma, repay the resentment, and be tormented for decades; now I have to enter this place, not knowing for how long? Although you do not eat, you are also being tormented. Please save me and save yourself."

Everything became clear; now I understand: all the years of hardship and misery caused by the sins I committed were not from a past life but from this life. I began to 'REPENT' and atone for those past evil deeds through good and virtuous actions...

You may not believe it, but for me, since then everything has flowed more smoothly than before. It's still the same people, the same house, in the family, but now it is more peaceful and happier.

Money also comes in a bit more easily than before. Especially the patients and the people I offer to and help all show their affection and respect for me. This hardly existed before, even though I had saved their lives and relieved them from all their difficulties.

Now I understand that "REPENTANCE" is not something to be read many times, memorized, or chanted melodiously. It is simply: "to check whether our unintentional or intentional actions have harmed humans or other living beings for any reason, and then sincerely ask for 'REPENTANCE'.

tieu_de: A METHOD OF CHANTING BUDDHA'S NAME TAUGHT BY MASTER AN QUANG
tom_tat: How to recite Buddha's name for those who have many troubles (reciting Buddha's name while the mind wanders), difficult to concentrate according to Master Yin Guang: These days, Teacher Hu Xiaolin from Beijing came here to visit me. He told me 4 t
noi_dung:
A METHOD OF CHANTING THE BUDDHA'S NAME TAUGHT BY MASTER AN QUANG

The method of chanting the Buddha's name for those who have many vexations (chanting the Buddha's name while the mind wanders), which is difficult to concentrate on according to Master Yin Guang:

These past few days, teacher Ho Tieu Lam from Beijing has come here to visit me. He told me that for the past 4 months he has been chanting Buddha's name. Previously, his Buddha chanting practice was not strong, so chanting was extremely arduous. After reading the works of Master Yin Guang, he truly understood the 10 methods of chanting that Master Yin Guang taught. He studied and practiced diligently for 4 months, and the results were wonderful. I invited him to give a report at our study meeting to share with everyone, because this matter is extremely important. We probably all know Master Yin Guang's words, but fail to implement them. One must count with the mind. The Buddha chanting must arise from the heart.Say it out loud, recite it with your mouth, so that your ears can hear it, everything must be very clear. The mind becomes clear, the mouth recites clearly, the ears hear clearly. Also add counting from 1 to 10. At the beginning, it is best to recite slowly, do not be quick, because being quick will make it difficult to remember. Using chaining of recitations will cause distraction: Amitabha, Amitabha, Amitabha. Do it sentence by sentence like that. Every sentence must be clear, and count in your head which number of Buddha recitation this sentence is. Count from 1 to 10, but counting from 1 to 10 is not easy, you will forget, and if you forget, you have to start counting from the beginning. There really is no other way, so the Great Master taught us to divide it into two parts: remember very carefully from 1 to 5, then remember carefully from 6 to 10. Using this method is not1, 2, 3, 4, 5, then 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, still making 10 counts. Before the first 5 counts are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; after the 5 counts are 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. You have to count like that. After completing 10 counts, go back to the first count, the second count, the third count, and so on. Very focused. Because when reciting the Buddha's name with many distractions, the wandering thoughts are chaotic. Using this method, you can restrain wandering thoughts. This is precisely “controlling the six faculties” as Great Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta spoke. This method has 3 clear aspects. The word “A Di Đà Phật” is clear. When heard clearly, it is recited clearly. When heard clearly, it is counted clearly. Whenever there is difficulty, you can use the 3, 3, 4 counting method. The first section is 3 counts: 1, 2, 3. The second section is 3 counts: 4, 5, 6. The third section is 4 counts: 7, 8, 9, 10. You can use the methodThis method is called 'grasping the six faculties through meditation, continuous pure mindfulness,' taught by Great Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta. You can try and see for yourself. When Hồ Tiểu Lâm reported it, Hồ Cư Sĩ, standing nearby, caught on. She tried it for several days and told me that it was very effective. Indeed, it is not the same; a joyful mind arises. Of course, the most important factor, the method is just a supportive condition; the most important factor is that you can let go, truly let go. That is the real cause. When you let go, you will be free, happy just like those in the Pure Land! What is different about the people there compared to us? It is precisely that they have let go. As for us, we refuse to let go of anything. Truly, once everything is let go, then nothingWhat is the difference compared to the people in the Pure Land? They are extremely happy, we are also extremely happy. The important thing is to let go. To let go, you must see through it, know that this world is all temporary and false, nothing is real, then you will be able to let go completely. If you cannot let go, it is because you see it as real, which is a mistake.

Excerpt from: The Great Treatise on the Pure Land, Volume 381

A Di Da Buddha

Venerable Master Tinh Khong

tieu_de: WHY DID THE BUDDHA ENTRUST THE RESPONSIBILITY OF TEACHING AND TRANSFORMING BEINGS TO BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA INSTEAD OF ASSIGNING IT TO OTHER GREAT BODHISATTVAS
tom_tat: Teaching this section of the scripture made us feel very deeply. After the Buddha passed away, before the next Buddha, Maitreya, appeared in the world, this period of time was extremely long, in 'K
noi_dung:
WHY BUDDHA ENTRUSTED THE RESPONSIBILITY OF EDUCATING SENTIENT BEINGS TO BODHISATTVA KĪRTIMATIYA RATHER THAN TO THE GREAT BODHISATTVAS

Teaching this section of the sutra evokes very deep feelings in us. After the passing away of the Buddha, before the next Buddha, Maitreya, appears in the world, this period of time is extremely long. In the 'Sutra of Maitreya's Descending', the Buddha tells us that, using our worldly calculation, it is about more than fifty-six hundred million years (over 560,000,000 years). During this long period, no Buddha appears in the world, no one teaches beings, beings cannot hear the good Dharma, and they will follow their own greed, hatred, ignorance, and pride to create countless, boundless sins, receivingBear suffering and karmic retribution, the suffering is indescribable. The World-Honored One, in great compassion and mercy, entrusted the responsibility of guiding sentient beings to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. In other words, when the Buddha is no longer in the world, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha takes the place of the Buddha, and the position of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is not like that of other Bodhisattvas. As the earth deity Kiên Lao mentioned earlier, great Bodhisattvas such as Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, and Avalokiteśvara are also immensely compassionate in guiding sentient beings, yet the World-Honored One did not rely on them but specially entrusted this important responsibility to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. Let us try to think about the reason. We can understand it.

In localities where there is no Buddhist teaching, sentient beings are accustomed to committing karma. How can we save these sentient beings from falling into the three evil paths? Everyone should think about what method should be used to teach them. There is no method better than 'filial piety and respect'; [you use 'filial piety and respect'] to advise those sentient beings who are creating karma, so that they may be able to accept it.

Help everyone establish from the heart, the character Địa represents the heart-mind, the character Tạng means the true wisdom and virtue contained in the heart-mind; that is the treasure stored within the heart-mind. Therefore, this dharma method is the most suitable for sentient beings in this period of fifty-six hundred million years. Thus, if we want to help sentient beings, save sentient beings from falling into evil paths, this sutra is a life-saving sutra, teaching us to stand firm in the human and heavenly realms, not to lose our human body, not to fall into evil paths. The supreme merit and benefit of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra lie in this. Using this sutra as a foundation, along with the Infinite Life Sutra and othersThe Amitabha sutra of rebirth helps us transcend the six paths of reincarnation and the ten dharma realms, allowing one to become a Buddha or Patriarch in a single lifetime. This is a non-dual practice for Buddhas to save sentient beings in the era of the declining Dharma. However, the era of the declining Dharma lasts only nine thousand years. After nine thousand years, this sutra will no longer exist, and sentient beings will suffer greatly, entirely relying on Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva to manifest. This is not that the Buddha preaches the Kṣitigarbha sutra; Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva must help all sentient beings. We can imagine that Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will surely help sentient beings abandon ten evils, practice ten virtues, be filial to parents, and respect teachers. In this way, one can avoid falling into evil paths. Therefore, the Kṣitigarbha practiceTHE STOREHOUSE OF ORIGINAL VOWS IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT AND EXTREMELY DEAR TO ANYONE, WE MUST ARISE WITH AN ENTHUSIASTIC INTENTION TO STUDY AND ENTHUSIASTICALLY PRAISE IT.

Excerpt from the Record of Lectures on the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Original Vows Sutra - Volume 41 - Lectured by Venerable Master Jingkong.
