tieu_de: THE SECRET OF 'ADJUSTING YOUR APPEARANCE' – TRANSFORMING YOUR FATE
tom_tat: A person's appearance has a special connection to their destiny, so the ancients established a whole system of 'physiognomy,' complexly predicting fate based on appearance, facial features, and complexion.
noi_dung:
SECRET TO “ALTERING YOUR PHYSIQUE” – TRANSFORMING FATE

A person's appearance has a special connection to their destiny, so the ancients established a whole complex system of "physiognomy," which accurately predicts each person's fate based on their appearance, facial features, and complexion.

Unfortunately, this study of "physiognomy" can only predict but does not know how to alter one's destiny. This causes many people to spend a lot of money to have their fortune read, yet in reality, it does not help them at all, because knowing one's fate in advance does not solve any problems, it only adds to their worries.

The good news is that even though "physiognomy" is powerless when it comes to changing fate, the study of "karma" can address this thoroughly.

_____________

During the reign of Emperor Jing of Han in China, there was a man known as a divine general. He only needed a brief glance to know all about a person's character, fate, and life's destiny. The accuracy of his predictions was astonishing, never wrong even once in a hundred times.

One day, while he was walking on the street, he suddenly saw a young man with a peculiar feature: two lines running from his chin to the corners of his mouth. He approached and said to him:

_ Young man, your face bears the mark of starvation. Within ten years, this misfortune will befall you.

That young man was named Bùi Độ, a poor oil seller. Because the fame of the old general was so great, Bùi Độ could not even dare to doubt him. He went home sorrowfully with the death sentence hanging invisibly over him. He no longer cared about anything, spending his days in gloom and melancholy.

One day, on the way, he saw a girl who was crying pitifully and about to jump into a deep well. Bùi Độ stopped her and asked, and learned that her name was Ngọc Hà, who was on her way to use gold to atone for her father's crime, but on the way, she accidentally dropped the bag of gold into the well.

People said that there was a very fierce and dangerous python under the well, and if one went down, it would surely mean death, so no one dared to help. Yet the girl kept determinedly jumping down, intending that if she could not get the gold, she would die right there.

Suddenly, Bùi Độ's eyes lit up, thinking to himself: “That's right, since I'm going to die anyway, why not use my death to do a righteous deed? Wouldn't that be better?”

Think and act. Even though his heart was racing and his hands and feet were trembling, he still risked climbing down. For some reason, he was not eaten by the python. After diving for a long time, he managed to retrieve the bag of gold and brought it up to Ngọc Hà. Thanks to that, Ngọc Hà survived, her father was exonerated, and their honor and power were restored.

Grateful for Bùi Độ's life-saving act, Ngọc Hà took him home to let him study properly. Later, she asked her father for permission to follow him and 'assist him throughout life.' The wedding was held shortly after, in the joy of all the relatives and villagers.

Then, Bùi Độ's father-in-law asked an influential acquaintance to recommend him for an official position in another region. From there, he continued to rise in rank and position.

His life is now filled with happiness, wealth, and honor; his homes and servants lack nothing. But he still carries the fear that he is about to die.

Until one day, he accidentally met the general deity again. After a sharp glance, the deity's eyes revealed surprise because the starved fate on his face was no longer there.

_ Hey young man – the guardian spirit said – the premature death on your face has vanished, I wonder if recently you have done any virtuous deeds?

The young man recounted everything. The guardian spirit nodded, and said farewell after blessing him.

He returned home with immense joy. He had narrowly escaped the cruel hand of fate. From now on, he could rest assured and do as he pleased.

And he really did it! From then on, he began to live in decadent indulgence, with wild and excessive pleasures. Holding power in his hands, he turned into a cruel eunuch. He plundered from the people, forced the daughters of good families, and the cries of resentment reached the heavens.

Days and months passed, and the injustice continued. Until one day, for the third time, he encountered the general deity again.

The general deity squinted at him. With his sharp and profound eyes, he immediately understood everything, and also saw that the starving official had returned. The general deity spoke sternly:

_ You immoral person, you once escaped death because you knew how to risk your life to save others. Now, instead of cultivating yourself and accumulating virtue more deeply, you become corrupt, degenerate, ruinous, arrogant, doing vile and cruel deeds. The hungry general has appeared again, so worry about arranging your afterlife.

The official Bùi Độ, angered, walked away. Having been accustomed to arrogance, he no longer cares whether the gods or generals are present. He just continues living a sinful life without any remorse. His conscience has now been devoured by fame, fortune, and lust.

Sure enough, not long after that, the people filed a lawsuit with the court. The appointed official was sent to investigate and then arrested him to be tried in the capital. On the way to be escorted, he escaped and got away into the forest. Some time later, people found his body starved to death next to a rock outcrop. This time, death had caught him with a tragic sentence: starvation – just as the divine general had said.

__________________

The fate of Bùi Độ was changed twice by his own hands. Thus, we see that fate is not something fixed or predestined by heaven. Because if it were fixed, nothing could change.

Fate is determined by the good and evil deeds we do for this world according to the law of Cause and Effect.

When Bùi Độ risked his life to save a person he had never met, his fate immediately changed. The starving general disappeared at once. He became wealthy and happy immediately, because the good deed he did was immense, especially when he saved someone despite the danger to himself.

But once again, he changed his fate in the opposite direction. Through brutality and arrogance, through immoral acts, persecuting innocent people, disregarding his conscience.

Those sins directly caused the Karma to change. And Karma rearranged Bùi Độ's fate back to a tragic ending, with the starving corpse returning, he had to die and rot in the forest.

SO HOW TO CHANGE FATE?

In summary, three things need to be done:

Do not create more unwholesome actions, so as not to add more negative karma into our storehouse. If this step is overlooked, the outcome will be like Bui Do; no matter how much good one does over time, it will all be erased. The appearance will revert to its original state, fate will remain the same, and karmic obstacles will still strike.

Regularly repent for the sins committed, and vow not to commit them again. Because a regretful heart and sincere repentance have the ability to eliminate negative karma.

Create many virtuous deeds, accumulate a lot of merit. I want to emphasize a lot, because if it is too little, it will not be enough to compensate for the evil deeds we have committed. You will not see any significant change.

There are many ways to do good deeds and create merit taught in Buddhism, such as reciting Buddha's name, chanting sutras, practicing mantras, repenting, making vows, releasing animals, printing and distributing texts, doing good deeds, giving alms, donating blood, saving people, building temples, casting statues, etc. Although they differ in form, all of them are taught by the Buddha, all create merit, all can eliminate karmic obstacles, all bring luck, and all can change destiny.

Because everyone's circumstances are different, their foundational capacities are different, and their preferences are different, there are many different methods, so that each person can choose the method that suits them best to apply.

After completing it, if you only want to adjust your own misfortune (without any grand or magnificent ideals), you can dedicate the merits like this: "I dedicate this merit, wishing to eliminate my karmic obstacles, resolve all adversities, have a fortunate life, encounter good causes and conditions, increase the Bodhi mind, promptly accomplish Buddhahood, and extensively save sentient beings."

If we have the financial means, we can choose to release animals (buy tens of kilograms of snails, eels, softshell turtles… and release them into rivers or lakes, for example) or give alms to the poor, or make offerings, build-cast-carve Buddha statues, build bridges and roads, etc…

If you do not have a lot of money to do things like giving alms, releasing animals, etc., it's okay. You can choose methods that only require effort and time, such as helping others, doing volunteer work at temples, donating blood, and so on. In particular, you should recite sutras (such as the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, the Infinite Life Sutra, the Universal Gate Sutra, etc.) – and chant mantras (such as the Great Compassion Mantra, the Rebirth Mantra, or the Karma-Eliminating Mantra “OM PA RA MA NI DA NI SO HA” – only 9 short syllables but extremely powerful effects, etc.).

If you don't know where to find sutras or mantras, or find it too difficult or complicated, that's okay. You can choose to recite the Buddha's name; every day you can recite a few thousand times “Namo Amitabha Buddha”, or “Namo Shakyamuni Buddha, the Original Teacher”, or “Namo Great Compassion Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva”, or “Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva of Great Vows”, etc. You can recite the name of any of these, all are good.

Advising others that “you should only recite this name, not the name of another” due to this or that is a mistaken belief; in the Buddha's sutras, it is never taught like that.

The Buddha also taught many different Buddha recitation phrases for each person to choose freely. In the Medicine Buddha Sutra, he taught reciting the name of the Medicine Buddha; in the Infinite Life Sutra, in the “Contemplation of Infinite Life” Sutra, the Buddha taught to recite “Namo Amitabha Buddha.” In the Lotus Sutra, in the Universal Gate chapter, the Buddha taught to recite “Namo Great Compassion Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva,” and so on… Why is that? Why did the Buddha not teach just one name, just one sutra for all sentient beings to recite with single-minded devotion, without the concern of mixing practices?

Because each person's karmic connection with the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in past lives is different. Whoever has a karmic connection with a particular being and recites that being's name will feel more concentrated, more respectful, more sincere, maintain the practice longer, and experience more spiritual response. "Destiny cannot be forced," so the Buddha taught many names and many methods so that each person could choose according to their own affinity; that is the wisdom of the Buddha.

In any method, you still have to strive to do it as much as possible. Many people often focus only on looking for a method that is effective quickly and requires little effort, but then can only practice for a few days before giving up.

Nowadays, learning a subject, after just a few days, if nothing is immediately seen, people go off to look for another way. All year round, this is the pattern: "standing on this mountain, looking at that mountain," hoping to do little, spend little, and gain a lot. Feeling a bit tired, seeing it takes time, or costs a bit, they give up immediately. Such an attitude, whether in life or in spiritual practice, will only result in "half-baked rice, burnt emptiness".

Let me remind you: Do as much as possible to the fullest, and determine to continue until there is a result, without any limit for stopping. Because each person's past karma is different, some people create merit and practice for a short time, and their lives quickly change. But there are others with heavier karma, who repent and practice for a very, very long time before changes occur.

It is hard to know how much past karma one has, so it is best to prepare patience. If there is no change in a month, then in a year; if there is no change in a year, then in ten years... one should not give up midway just because there is no noticeable change in life after a short period of practice.

Even when resolving similar karmic obstructions, one person may see results after accumulating merit for a few days, while another may only see results after a year. This is common because past karma and each person's cultivation ability are different.

Just like the same journey from Saigon to Hanoi, a plane only takes 2 hours, a car takes 2 days, and walking takes 2 months... that's normal. A walker shouldn't expect to finish in 2 hours or 2 days; if they don't see the destination, it doesn't mean they are on the wrong path, it simply means they haven't gone far enough and need to persist.

With methods like those above, combined with persistent effort, whether fast or slow, surely your karmic obstacles will be eliminated.

Once karmic obstacles are eliminated, your destiny will have to change accordingly. When your destiny changes, your appearance will also change, and the ultimate result is that your life will improve, with much less misfortune and suffering, and much more luck, happiness, and peace.

The rule – the method is like that, whereas success or not depends on your own decisions and efforts.

(Quang Tử)

tieu_de: The Consequences of Promoting Unhealthy Cultural Films
tom_tat: The retribution for making movies, producing violent films, writing scripts portraying robbery, murder, sexual acts, or sharing bad images, words, or obscene writings online… which affect the morality of many generations
noi_dung:
The Consequences of Promoting Unhealthy Cultural Films

The retribution for making violent movies, filming, writing scripts depicting scenes of robbery, murder, lust, or sharing harmful images, words, or obscene writings online that affect the morality of many generations of young people: the future is hell. Viewers who praise or admire evil also inadvertently create this karma. Everyone is earnestly urged to be vigilant!

When we watch erotic romantic movies or read sexual stories, most of us also get stirred up emotionally, our thoughts follow along, not to mention some people even imitate what they see in the movies. Books like "The Great Dao Thief Jiang Yang," "Divine Thief," or American movies like "Death Race," etc., will have a negative influence: Among the audience, there will certainly be some who form the intention to imitate the behavior of thieves, robbers, or murderers. In the future, over several lifetimes, that intention becomes the cause leading to action, meaning they will act out the same methods of killing or robbery as shown in the movies. Thus, the sin becomes immensely great.

In reality, there have been many incidents reported in the press as evidence. Violent and sexual films depict robbery, sexual acts… to attract more viewers. The more 'sold-out' the tickets are, the greater the karma created. Thus, the entire crew producing such obscene films, from the writers, directors, and actors… will in the future have to enter hell with little chance of leaving. Because the time they endure the consequences in hell is calculated based on the total time that the audience affected negatively by the film—committed sin—endure the consequences… until all the sins of those viewers are exhausted, only then will the film crew be able to leave hell. The actors performingThe more vividly these scenes are immersive, the greater the sin.

In the film industry, actors who win Oscars, for the most part, often do not understand why their families frequently lose happiness or break apart in strange ways. For example, among the eight film beauties who recently won Oscars, six of them ended up in situations of having to divorce or separate from their partners. Westerners completely do not understand that this is because they once performed too well in villainous roles: pornographic, thieving... which caused their families to lose happiness. This is the result of karma from their past evil deeds.

We can see violent works and films spreading negative influences everywhere. For example, when John Hinckley attempted to assassinate U.S. President Reagan, his motivation for the attack stemmed from his obsessive admiration for actress Jodie Foster in the film Taxi Driver (1976). The film tells the story of a plot to assassinate the U.S. president, and he imitated it. On March 30, 1981, Hinckley carried a gun and lay in ambush outside the hotel where President Reagan was attending a conference. At 2:25 PM (Washington time), as Reagan stepped outside, John fired continuously at him and the bodyguards. The U.S. president was seriously injured (due to the bullet being lodgedinto the chest so had to go to the hospital for emergency surgery) but fortunately survived the critical condition and escaped death.

On April 16, 2007, a tragic murder case occurred at Virginia Tech in Blacksburg, USA, carried out by the perpetrator Cho Seung Hui (a Korean who was also a student at the University of Virginia), who killed 32 people and injured many others. Looking at the photo of him holding two handguns aggressively, this is clearly the influence of the violent Korean film "Old Boys," as the perpetrator was very fond of and idolized this movie.

Therefore, creators, screenwriters, and directors in the world need to produce films that guide people towards goodness. By doing so, they not only create immeasurable merit, but also leave deep blessings for their children and grandchildren. The longer these tapes and discs are circulated, the more their blessings increase.

🔜 ONE MUST REALIZE THAT BOOKS, STORIES, AND MOVIES HAVE EXTREMELY GREAT INFLUENCE.

Evidence in the book “Thọ Khang Bảo Giám” clearly records: Thi Nại Am wrote the work Water Margin, which became famously renowned, in which the book entirely praises evil, encourages rebellion, and shows disrespect... it depicts killing – theft – lust – and deceit in detail, and even highly glorifies them. In reality, he himself suffered the consequences of his actions: his descendants were mute for three generations. In his old age, he was imprisoned in the heavenly prison, endured extreme suffering, was tormented by numerous illnesses affecting his body, and later was exiled, lived a life of hardship, and died from hemoptysis.

Specifically, the great literatus Kim Thanh Than (a figure at the end of the Ming and the beginning of the Qing dynasties) was a person skilled in literature and poetry but often distorted Buddhist scriptures. Because he sowed the seeds of criticism through commentaries, praising works like Shuihu, Xiyou Ji, etc.—books that teach lust, robbery, and glorify rebellion… he later faced retribution and was sentenced to be beheaded. This was all due to ignorance of Buddhist teachings, which allowed disaster to arise from the mind. It is regrettable for a talented person with a full mastery of literature like Kim Thanh Than, who, by choosing the wrong path, harmed himself and caused lasting repercussions for future generations.

In the book “Duet Vi Hieu Duong But Ki,” Kỳ Hiểu Phong was described as follows: In the spring of the year Mậu Tí (1768), Kỳ Hiểu Phong, upon seeing his friend’s hunting painting "Phan Ky Shoots the Cat," was inspired to compose a poem praising it and expressed the sheer pleasure he felt in drinking the blood of the prey on a snow-covered yard.

Unexpectedly, in August of that year, he was dismissed from his military post and exiled to Ô Lỗ Mộc Tề for service (for composing poems that praised hunting, drinking fresh blood, and writing with the purpose of beautifying and glorifying killing), even though he did not personally kill, he still had to face retribution, because these very lines of poetry had encouraged and incited many others to develop misguided murderous intentions.

This reminds us: “Do not commit small evils, the cause and effect of retribution is real and not deceitful.” Writing books and arguing can influence for a hundred years. Therefore, in writing or speaking, our statements must be absolutely cautious.

In today's society, morality is increasingly declining; most books, newspapers, and films are based on content that arouses sex, violence, and murder… without knowing that these actions will bring extremely heavy karmic consequences. For example, the American magazine Playboy, founded by Flint, in 1978 was suddenly shot by someone; although he survived, he became paralyzed from that point on (in fact, that was only the beginning of countless further karmic consequences).

In China, there was a person who wrote obscene sexual novels. Right after publishing, he fell from a building, broke his spine, became paralyzed, and was in a coma for 25 days. After waking up, he recounted that he was in a deep, dark tunnel with no end in sight. This happened because he wrote books promoting immoral ideas, so in this life, he received preliminary karmic retribution (preliminary karmic retribution refers to minor punishments that appear before the main, severe ones) for writing articles inciting lust and robbery. But the real retribution in the afterlife will be unimaginably severe.

🔜 THERE ARE SOME POINTS THAT YOU SHOULD BE ALERT TO:

You should absolutely not introduce someone to places for eating and drinking, and not just to spots for enjoying chicken, duck, seafood, or only to restaurants and eateries famous for salty dishes... Also, do not recommend places that sell good alcohol or quality tobacco, because this is sowing the seeds of teaching others to commit bad deeds. Beings suffer because they have companions who misguide them, helping them to do wrong, so they must endure all kinds of karmic retribution. Therefore, you will certainly find it difficult to avoid the strict law of cause and effect, and the consequences can be even more serious than if you yourself had done the wrong deed.

Everyone probably still remembers the Marlboro scented cigarettes produced since 1950, which were advertised very lively in the United States and were voted as a highly influential brand because they attracted countless people (including teenagers) to rush into smoking. Because it was so profitable, this cigarette manufacturing company expanded enormously (their expansion was due to past fortune, and only when that fortune ended would consequences arise). The advertising team helped the Marlboro brand become the best-selling brand in the world. Marlboro's sales increased from 5 billion USD (in 1955) to 20 billion USD (in 1957).

🔜 WHAT ABOUT THE ADVERTISERS THEMSELVES?

In 1976, British television interviewed six famous advertising figures. They were still relatively young, but all suffered from lung cancer, bronchiectasis, and in the following years, they died one after another in the pain of their illnesses.

Because they advertised looking very majestic, handsome, and stylish, young people admired them at first sight and wanted to follow them to be as impressive and elegant, mistakenly thinking that smoking is a good and modern thing. In the end, the entire advertising group suffered health consequences, getting all kinds of serious lung diseases. Encouraging smoking is a harmful behavior, so how could they possibly maintain their own health?

According to current scientific research, tobacco is a toxic substance that causes a range of diseases, including cancer, and contributes to shortening a person's lifespan. Because tobacco is deadly, anyone who smokes is gradually killing themselves, not to mention those around them who suffer seriously when inhaling the smoke (because they are more heavily poisoned).

Therefore, teaching people to commit the ten evils, praising the ten evils, this mistake is very grave. In today's society, there are still many famous figures who blatantly praise and declare: "One-night stands are reasonable." They accept the practice of "wife-swapping, spouse-swapping" and even advocate, calling for the "legalization" of these immoral acts. Not only do they severely corrupt social morals, but they also poison thoughts, causing limitless harm to countless sentient beings.

Then when they face retribution, it will be: Holding a red-hot copper pillar, dying and coming back to life countless times in a very miserable way. These are precisely the unfortunate people that the Buddha refers to.

Below is a clear illustration of the consequences of making films that negatively influence the audience: "Poltergeist" is a movie listed among the 100 most "thrilling" films in the U.S. and was once nominated for three Oscars. However, what made "Poltergeist" even more famous was the fact that the actors involved sequentially died tragically in mysterious ways.

The movie “Poltergeist” is a horror story revolving around the Freeling family, consisting of five members living a peaceful life in the suburbs. Here, they continuously encounter inexplicable supernatural phenomena, from strange sounds to the movement of objects in the house. The plot intensifies when the youngest daughter, Carol Anne, is harassed and kidnapped by evil spirits.

“Poltergeist” immediately after its premiere haunted viewers. In fact, many people said that when they watched Poltergeist, they could not sleep for many weeks and even to this day, they still dare not watch any horror movies again.

However, what really frightens many people is the fact that 4 of the actors involved died during and after the completion of the 3 parts of the "Poltergeist" series. This led the public to suspect that "Poltergeist" was under some terrible curse, but few understand that it was actually the consequence of making a film that psychologically harms the audience.

The first tragedy to strike the film crew involved 22-year-old actress Dominique Dunne, who played the eldest daughter Dana among the three children of the Freeling family, and was strangled to death by her boyfriend on November 4, 1982, just a few weeks after the film was released.

The next case is 60-year-old actor Julian Beck (who played Father Henry Kane in Part 2 of Poltergeist), who passed away on September 14, 1985, from stomach cancer before the second part of the film was released in theaters. In 1987, actor Will Sampson (who played Shaman Taylor in Part 2) also passed away from kidney disease at the age of 53. In 2009, 67-year-old actor Lou Perryman (who played a supporting character named Pugsley in Part 1) was murdered at his home.

However, what shocked the audience the most was the death of the child actress Heather O’Rourke, 12 years old, who played the role of the demon-possessed girl Carol Anne. Accordingly, she became suddenly ill and died on the operating table in 1988, before the third part of the film was released. Doctors determined that Heather had a gastrointestinal infection and died due to complications.

[Excerpt from “Nhân Quả Phụ Giải Lương Hoàng Sám”] Quang Tử st

Translated by Hạnh Đoan

Education of Cause and Effect

tieu_de: THE CONSEQUENCES OF KILLING AND WAYS TO RESOLVE THEM
tom_tat: 🙏Ms. Dinh Gia Le: Master, do you think that spraying pesticides or burning land to reclaim it can be considered killing? 🏵️Venerable Master Tinh Khong: It is considered killing, especially burning land to reclaim it.
noi_dung:
THE REPERKUSSIONS OF KILLING AND WAYS TO RESOLVE THEM

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: Teacher, do you think spraying pesticides or burning fields for land reclamation is considered killing living beings?

🏵️Venerable Master Tịnh Không: It is considered killing living beings, especially burning fields for land reclamation, which is truly unimaginable!

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: Is that so, Teacher? But now all farmers burn fields for land reclamation.

🏵️Venerable Master Tịnh Không: Setting fire to clear land is a very serious sin. You must understand that a single fire you start can kill countless sentient beings! It is no different from waging a war.

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: Yes, Master! It is truly terrifying!

🏵️Venerable Master Tịnh Không: That's right. Setting fire to clear land is equivalent to starting a war. You kill countless sentient beings, which is a hellish sin and must not be done. However, many people do not clearly understand the law of cause and effect, and many people commit this act!

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: Very many, Master!

🏵️Venerable Master Tịnh Không: I did not know this before I studied Buddhism. After studying Buddhism, I realized this, and it is truly frightening.

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: There could be over a hundred thousand worms burned to death.

🏵️Venerable Master Tịnh Không: It's not just a hundred thousand worms.

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: Not just a hundred thousand worms?

🏵️Venerable Master Tinh Khong: That is several million, tens of millions, invisible to the naked eye, all the animals on the ground would die. If you only count the ants, how many would that be! So the more you think about it, the more terrifying it becomes.

🙏Ms. Dinh Gia Le: Master, it is indeed very terrifying!

🏵️ Venerable Master Tịnh Không: When you kill an animal, it hates you. Setting fire to clear land is even more serious than draining water to catch fish. When a pond is completely emptied, an entire net catches all the fish. The catastrophe that befell the family of Buddha Shakyamuni during the reign of King Lully was due to fishing, as the Buddha explained. In many previous lifetimes, the Shakya lineage were fishermen; they drained the pond, catching every single fish without leaving any behind. When Buddha Shakyamuni was alive in that lifetime, those fish had transformed into humans, became rulers, and destroyed the Shakya family. The Blessed One understood karma and retribution but could not prevent it, he could only advise everyoneThe person fleeing tried their best to escape. Venerable Maudgalyayana used his supernatural powers to place a person from the Shakya family into a bowl.

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: "Teacher, what does 'Bát' mean?"

🏵️Venerable Master Tịnh Không: A rice bowl.

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: You mean the bowl for eating rice?

🏵️Master Tinh Khong: Yes, the rice bowl of a monk. He had supernatural powers, could fit five hundred people into it, and then took them to heaven to escape this disaster. As a result, Buddha Shakyamuni said, 'Go and see for yourself.' When he looked into the bowl, it was all a bowl of blood. This is called a disaster that cannot be escaped; no one can save you, karma is created by yourself. These are people from the lineage of Buddha Shakyamuni, according to what Buddha said. A few people managed to escape, fleeing to Tibet, then Eastern Tibet, and later never returned. Therefore, the later generations of the Shakyamuni lineage are in Eastern Tibet - China; this was told by the Great Master Zhangjia.I know.

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: Dear Master, the karma that we create, we ourselves must bear this karma; this is our own cause and effect.

🏵️Venerable Master Tinh Khong: Yes, that's exactly right.

🙏Ms. Đinh Gia Lệ: Our own cause and effect.

🏵️Venerable Master Tịnh Không: If we now cannot encounter the Pure Land practice, then you have no other way. It is good if you can encounter the Pure Land practice; only Amitabha Buddha can help people resolve this matter. You must sincerely and wholeheartedly recite His name, and you must dedicate the merit to your enemies and wrongdoers.

tieu_de: MASTURBATION IS LIKE SUICIDE. A DISEASE OF STUDENTS, UNIVERSITY STUDENTS TODAY!
tom_tat: He said that in the past five or six years, since graduating, he has been suffering from debilitating joint diseases, almost half of his body feels dead. Could it be because [back when he was still in school] friends would gather together, reading novels together[1] until
noi_dung:
MASTURBATION IS LIKE SUICIDE. THE DISEASE OF STUDENTS, CURRENT UNIVERSITY STUDENTS!

He said that over the past five or six years, since graduating, he suffered from debilitating bone and joint disease, almost half of his body seemingly dead. Could it be because [back in their school days] friends would gather, reading novels together[1] to the point of losing vitality, masturbating continuously, thus causing such a phenomenon? That is precisely the common illness among students nowadays; out of ten, eight or nine are afflicted. Since parents, teachers, and friends all refuse to mention it, those suffering from the disease are increasingly numerous, and it cannot be stopped! Because of this matter, Quang immediately had eight hundred copies of the Tho Khang Bao Giam printed. WheneverWhenever young people met Quang, Quang would clearly explain the pros and cons to them, advising them to take care of their bodies and not to transgress. Whether it was masturbation or illicit sexual relations, they had to seriously abstain and avoid committing them; even husbands and wives when being intimate with each other must exercise moderation and know what to avoid, so as not to end up losing their lives unjustly! If not, even the very good person could die because of this matter. They would gather to blame fate, not realizing that they had already forfeited their own lives!

He is still very young and already ill, so he should often read that book, just as Đức Chánh is often instructed to read. Both sides remind each other, so that the children who have been born, like Quân Tốn, etc., will all be plump, grow up well, have gentle and kind natures, and that he and his wife will live happily to old age, together being reborn in the Western Paradise.

[1] The term “novel” here refers to those novels considered to be “erotic books” that provoke inappropriate romantic feelings between men and women.

(Excerpted from the Collected Writings of Master Ấn Quang)

Link to the Thọ Khang Bảo Giám book:

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IwGtsP0laHozlgwkZDPU3h21pxmjeu8Q/view?usp=drivesdk

Commentary:

Master An Quang is the Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta reincarnated; his teachings should never be taken lightly. Why is it that many of us see good people yet they often suffer misfortune, premature death, while wicked people seem to live in abundance and happiness? Whatever we do, we need to deeply consider cause and effect. Everything that happens to us in this life is our own fault; we must not blame anyone else, because the law of cause and effect spans not just one lifetime but many lifetimes. When good people encounter misfortune, one must examine whether they have committed the sins of killing and sexual misconduct; if not, and they have strictly observed the precepts taught by the Buddha, yet still face misfortune, thenIt should be understood that one is experiencing karma; the bad results should have only been endured many lifetimes later, but now, because of practicing cultivation and repentance, all the bad results from many past lifetimes come out at once. Heavy karma turns into lighter karma, light karma disappears, and when the karma is exhausted, one will receive blessings. As for wicked people who live long and happily, it is due to the blessings they created in many past lifetimes, which should have only been enjoyed many lifetimes later. But now, because they do evil, any small good results also emerge; when their blessings are exhausted, they will endure the consequences all at once, which is truly unimaginable! Cause and effect never err even by the tiniest fraction; everyone needs to be very careful 🙏

A DI ĐÀ PHẬT

PLEASE REGULARLY RECITE

tieu_de: EVER-PRESENT GREAT EARTHQUAKE (Reincarnated Archenemy as a Daughter, Chanting Kṣitigarbha Sutra to Pray for the Liberation of Parents' Souls)
tom_tat: My whole life, I have deeply believed in two things: 1. The cause and effect taught by Buddha is true and not deceptive; people really do experience the consequences of their actions.
noi_dung:
FREQUENT EARTHQUAKES (Enemies Reincarnated as Daughters, Chanting Kṣitigarbha Sutra to Pray for Parents' Peace)

I have deeply believed in two things all my life:

1. The karma that the Buddha teaches is truthful and not deceptive; people truly experience the consequences of karma.

2. There are scenes that sentient beings with physical eyes cannot perceive, yet they still exist, and genuine Buddhist practice can change one’s destiny.

What I want to say is: Nothing happens without cause. Take my husband and daughter, for example; the karmic affinity was very bad. Even though I have studied Buddhism for many years, it is still difficult to let go and sever these ties.

In my recent dream, I dreamt that in a past life I was a poor scholar, already married, but I wanted to take a concubine and abandoned my first wife. My current daughter, in that past life, was a young girl who was forced by me. She angrily said: 'I will hate you for all eternity, and vow to destroy you completely...'

Upon waking, I thought carefully and saw that it was indeed true. In this life, I am female, and after taking care of my husband’s house, we separated. Currently, my husband and daughter treat me coldly like a stranger; they only contact me when they need money, aside from that, they do not care about me.

The things that happened to me personally are real. Today, I share them only in the hope that those who are destined to read this article will be vigilant, sincerely and wholeheartedly repent and practice, follow the Buddha's teachings, choose a meditation method suitable to their own capacity, and practice thoroughly to achieve liberation and be free from suffering. As for myself, I practice the method of chanting the Buddha's name.

I only learned about the Dharma after my parents passed away. At their company, my parents were always praised by everyone as gentle, honest, and kind.

But my mother died of esophageal cancer at the age of 57, and my father, at 63, suffered a broken leg that led to paralysis and then passed away. My parents both died in the same year, only three months apart.

After my parents passed away, it left me with a lot of trauma. It made me feel almost as if living was worse than dying; there was a time when I really wanted to die along with them.

In a state of mental collapse like that, I happened to come across Buddhism (truly a gratitude). At that time, my senior monk brother advised me to recite the Earth Store Sutra; I wholeheartedly practiced it, without any distracting thoughts while chanting the sutra.

When reciting the part where Madame Guang Mu saved her mother, I was moved by her great vow, and tears streamed down… at the same time, my heart felt like it was being cut with a knife, when thinking of the family. The pain was so intense that I did not want to live. After that, I dreamed that Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara told me:

– Don’t be too sad, your parents’ sudden death from severe illness is due to the karma they have attracted…

Suddenly I realized: My parents committed too much killing. My mother liked to kill chickens, while my father liked to catch fish and shoot birds. The Kṣitigarbha Sutra has described in detail the forms and karmic consequences of individuals, including my parents. Before I knew the Buddhist teachings, I had personally witnessed it. At that time, I thought perhaps it was due to being bedridden for a long time and receiving so many injections that I developed hallucinations. But in fact, it was not like that. Later, when I chanted the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and saw the depiction of vengeful spirits and owners of grievances pretending to be the deceased's relatives, leading people away… then my mind suddenly became enlightened and I understood. I even recalled all the things from my childhood clearly (likeas if watching a film reel projected on the big screen).

Chanting the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for the third day, I dreamed again that Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara told me:

– Your father has reached the Western Paradise, but your mother still appears in form: the upper body is human, but the lower body has one leg of a goat, one leg of a cow…

Originally, when my mother was alive in the world, she loved eating beef and goat meat, and also often killed chickens… She had an esophageal tumor that required surgery, and it seemed that the way she had killed chickens was reflected in the surgery: her neck was cut 10 cm, her abdomen was also operated on… it was so tragic that one could hardly bear to look.

When my father was alive, he liked to catch birds and tie their legs. One day, he fell from a height to the ground (only about one meter), yet he broke his leg, which led to brain paralysis, suffering beyond words. The reason I am elaborating at length is to let everyone understand clearly: Whoever hears the Buddha's teachings is very fortunate, so please devote your heart sincerely: Make vows, believe, practice... and with a heart of gratitude, recognize your faults, repent, and sincerely practice mindfulness.

There is one more thing: before the night when Van Xuyen experienced the great earthquake, I had a dream, which was very terrifying: A celestial being, full of anger, said:

– You all commit the crimes of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and every kind of evil. Even those who study Buddhism but whose mind and speech are not in harmony must be allowed to taste the evil fruits of their own actions!

After speaking, one of the celestial being’s legs kicked many people to death and collapsed many houses. His giant foot intended to advance and trample me. I panicked, quickly holding a white iron armor piece above my head, continuously chanting 'Namo Amitabha Buddha' and narrowly escaping disaster. Upon waking, covered in sweat, I heard a dog barking fiercely across the street. I immediately sat up and recited the phrase: 'All forms are illusory'… to reassure myself.

Little did I expect that the next noon, an 'earthquake' occurred in Van Xuyen.

The third thing is, when I was studying Buddhism, there was a period when I often ran around in all directions. Regarding the practice and the method of reciting Amitabha Buddha's name, I often felt discouraged… so there were times when I wanted to give up everything and stop practicing. Unexpectedly, that night I dreamed that I saw Shakyamuni Buddha say:

– You must be steadfast! In the Western Pure Land, there is Ultimate Bliss, there is Amitabha Buddha! After saying this, He raised His hand to point… and I immediately saw Amitabha Buddha radiating dazzling golden light shining upon me, and in the midst of the sky appeared large golden characters, with a few words written: In the Western Pure Land, there is Ultimate Bliss! In the Western Pure Land, there is Amitabha Buddha!

Through this, I want to say: Cause and effect do not deceive. The Diamond Sutra once recorded: The words of the Tathagata are true words, real words, and not different from the words! – Indeed, that is correct.

Today I tell these stories; according to Buddhist teachings, they should not be spoken, but because I see many beings studying Buddhism only focusing on form without actual practice, my heart is very saddened.

The Dharma is not easy to encounter, nor is it easy to hear; being born as a human is also difficult. Those who get to hear and know the Dharma… it can be said that in many past lives they have cultivated ripe virtuous roots, which is why they are able to encounter the Dharma. Once encountered, one should practice well to repay the Buddha's grace…

May the merit of this practice be dedicated to all, praying that all wronged spirits and harmed beings in this life have their hearts of hatred extinguished, may their blessings and wisdom increase, and may they soon be reborn in the good path.

Layperson Viên Chiêu

The poet Viên Chiểu reciting the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra achieved results very quickly because she did not harbor distracting thoughts. When reciting the part where Guangmu saves her mother, she was deeply moved by the great vows of Guangmu, tears streaming down, feeling as if her heart were being cut when thinking of her own parents (This reflects her filial piety and empathy with Guangmu's feelings). Because of this, she attracted the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, who appeared in a dream and clearly described the current situation of her parents. This is why some people experience effects after reciting only a few sets, while others see nothing—it solely depends on whether one has sincere heart or not.

The interesting point is that the Kṣitigarbha Sutra praises Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and clearly explains his merits and vows, but this time the Bodhisattva who conveys the dream is not Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, but Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, demonstrating that the Bodhisattvas always mutually support and connect with each other, without distinction or passing on responsibility... like ordinary humans.

The Buddha entrusts sentient beings in the Sahā world to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and requests that he must save them so that they do not fall into evil paths until Maitreya Bodhisattva (the future Buddha) descends to the human realm. This is an extremely difficult responsibility. Yet Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha still promises...

The Buddha once confirmed: He and the Bodhisattvas have incarnated hundreds, thousands, billions of times... in the Saha world to save sentient beings. Surely, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva must continue to save sentient beings as promised to the Buddha, and the best way to help beings not fall into evil realms is to help them understand karma so they practice the true Dharma correctly and know how to protect themselves.

However, when we come into contact with the incarnations of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, we often do not realize it or recognize them. Yet, it is also very easy to recognize a Bodhisattva, because anyone who meets him (or even receives his teachings from afar) shares one thing in common:

The force of intense awakening, diligent practice, and courageous determination to abandon evil and practice good, to give up meat and eat vegetarian, strictly observe precepts, stopping the path of descending into evil realms right in this life.

Source: Di Da Fruits

tieu_de: IF YOU ALWAYS THINK THAT YOU NEVER MAKE MISTAKES, THAT ALL MISTAKES ARE ON OTHERS, THEN YOU IN THIS LIFE
tom_tat: When an enlightened person encounters all things not going as they wish, we should not blame them, but turn back and reflect: have we truly not done well enough, have we caused them dissatisfaction? Improve yourself, and do not complain.
noi_dung:
IF YOU ALWAYS THINK THAT YOU NEVER MAKE MISTAKES, THAT ALL MISTAKES ARE ALWAYS ON OTHERS, THEN IN THIS LIFE YOU

When an enlightened person encounters all things not to their satisfaction, one should not blame them, but instead turn back and introspect: have I truly not done well enough, have I acted in a way that displeased them? One should improve oneself and decisively not blame others.

Buddhists have a saying: "Turning back is the shore." What does turning back mean? One should not see the faults of others but must see the faults of oneself; one should not blame others but must blame oneself. Only in this way can one be saved, only in this way can one be delivered. If one always believes that oneself has no mistakes and that all faults lie in others, then in this life there is no hope of rebirth in the Pure Land; in this life, one is certainly still trapped in the six realms of samsara. Reciting the Buddha's name may be done better, but it merely connects one’s affinity with Amitabha Buddha, planting the seed of Buddha in the Alaya Consciousness. Although this seed is a vajra seed, eternally...Far from imperishable, yet the old layman Lý Bỉnh Nam, in the notes of the "Sutra of Infinite Life," wrote very well: "It is difficult to avoid many lifetimes of reincarnation." This is true, not false. We must definitely have a highly vigilant mind.

Excerpt from the Buddha's Teaching of the Mahayana Infinite Life Sutra, Adorned, Pure, Equal Enlightenment (Volume 182)

Lectured by Venerable Elder Tinh Khong

Amitabha Buddha _()_

tieu_de: . WHEN INFATUATED WITH MONEY, IT IS JUST MONEY. ONCE ENLIGHTENED, ONE REALIZES THAT IN MONEY THERE IS HEART (Our Merit and Blessings in Practice Do Not Depend On It)
tom_tat: Speaking of doing good deeds, many people believe that the more valuable the item they give away, the greater the merit they will receive in return, corresponding to the value of what they have offered. Is this true or false? Truly
noi_dung:
. WHEN OBSESSED WITH MONEY, IT'S JUST MONEY. ONLY AFTER ENLIGHTENMENT DO WE REALIZE THAT WITHIN MONEY LIES INTENTION (The Blessings We Receive from Our Practice Do Not Depend)

When it comes to doing good deeds, many people think that the more valuable the thing they give away, the greater the merit they will receive in return, corresponding to the value of what they have donated. Is this right or wrong? In fact, this arises merely from people's varying degrees of discrimination, and it is not how the law of Cause and Effect works. If we pay close attention to life around us, we will easily notice that some people donate only a single coin, yet the merit they receive is extremely great. On the other hand, there are those who donate tens of millions, but the merit they receive...is still extremely small. This indicates that the merit we gain from practicing does not depend on the amount of money we give in alms. So what does it depend on? It depends on the mind when performing the act of giving.

If when practicing charity our mind is too narrow, merely doing it for formality, to be seen by others, or to gain as much merit as possible, the result is that the merit we receive is extremely small. Why? Because it corresponds to the narrow mind from which our act of giving arises.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who begged and went to the temple to worship Buddha. She offered 2 coins, which was all the money she had begged for that day. Unexpectedly, the abbot personally came out to dedicate the merit to her. Later, thanks to the merit of offering those 2 coins, she was selected to serve in the palace as a noble consort. After achieving a life of wealth and glory, she remembered the temple from years ago, so she sent attendants with 2000 taels of silver to offer to the temple. This time, however, the abbot did not personally come out to dedicate the merit to her, but only sent his disciples to do it on his behalf.

She was very surprised and asked:

_ "Last time I only offered 2 coins, and you personally dedicated the merit for me. This time I offered up to 2000 taels of silver, but you did not personally dedicate the merit for me. I wonder what the cause is?"

The abbot replied:

_ "In the past, although my offerings were few, they were made with utmost sincerity; if the master did not personally dedicate the merit to me, I would fear that it would not be worthy of this sincere heart. Now, my offerings are many, but not as sincere as before, so it is enough for the master to have someone else dedicate the merit on my behalf."

Therefore, even giving only 2 coins can be considered a complete virtuous act, while giving 2000 taels of silver can still be considered a partial virtuous act. Why is it called partial? Because there is only money without heart; the mind is too narrow.

Buddhists often say:

_ "The mind encompasses vast emptiness, the heart measures the boundaries of vermilion."

If, when doing good deeds, one's mind can expand to cover the entire void, then the merit one receives will be as immense as the void. This is considered a perfect good deed. Why? Because mind and action are in harmony.

During the Han dynasty, the Taoist master Zhong Li passed down his alchemical methods to Lü Dongxin, which could refine elixirs into gold to help the poor.

Lü Dongxin then asked Zhong Li:

_ "Form changes into gold, may I ask how long until it changes back into form?"

Chúng Ly replied:

_ "After 500 years it will change back into form."

Lã Đồng Tân said:

_ "Then it will harm people 500 years later. I do not want to do this."

Chung Ly taught Lã Động Tân how to refine gold simply to test Lã Động Tân’s heart. Therefore, when he heard Lã Động Tân speak like that, he realized that he had a truly kind heart and said:

_ "To cultivate immortality, one must accumulate 3,000 merits. Now that you have spoken these words, the 3,000 merits can be considered complete."

Why is it that with just one sentence, the merits are already complete? Because Lã Động Tân has a genuinely kind heart; he sincerely cares for the well-being of everyone. Hence, even with just one sentence, his merits are fully complete.

People in this world have very narrow minds; apart from self-interest and personal gain, their hearts cannot hold even a single thing or a single person. So how can they seek blessings for themselves? It should be understood that whether it is worldly law or Buddhist law, it is all within the mind, all essentially valued in the intention of the mind, not in external form.

When we clearly understand this principle, then when practicing good deeds and cultivating merit, we will know how to cultivate merit and perform good deeds correctly. Only by having a vast mind can one let go of all personal self-interest to seek abundant blessings for oneself.

The ancients said:

_ "When confused by money, it is just money.

Only upon enlightenment do we realize that within money there is mind."

Amitabha Buddha!

_ Reference: Dharma sayings of Master Ting Kong, The Four Instructions of Lieu Pham_

tieu_de: THE ENLIGHTENMENT of player CÔNG VINH through the assistance of singer THỦY TIÊN: After practicing for nearly 8 years,
tom_tat: "In the past, at the end of every year, Mr. Vinh would slaughter a pig to give to the villagers. We had only known each other for 2 months, and the first thing I did was forbid him from doing that. He could use that money to give gifts or buy rice for everyone."
noi_dung:
THE ENLIGHTENMENT of football player CÔNG VINH through the assistance of singer THỦY TIÊN: After nearly 8 years of practicing,

“In the past, at the end of each year, Mr. Vinh’s family would slaughter pigs to give to the villagers. We had only known each other for 2 months, yet the first thing I did was forbid him from doing that. He could use that money to give gifts or buy rice for people to eat, but he could not kill animals. Using this suffering to compensate for happiness is completely meaningless. He will bear the consequences” – Thuy Tien shared.

-------------------0o0---------------------

Please check out the interview with the "golden couple" CÔNG VINH-THỦY TIÊN in the Vietnamese entertainment-sports world:

- What led you two to practice spiritual cultivation?

- Thủy Tiên: My family has been practicing Buddhism for a long time. My mother has been vegetarian since she was 14 and met my father in a temple. While she was pregnant with me, she chanted sutras all the time. She had to complete the entire set of sutras before going into labor. My childhood memory of sutras was stronger than that of school lessons.

The greatest luck of my life is being born as my mother's child. Although there are many times when our thoughts do not align, without my mother, I think my life would be very miserable.

It is also thanks to my mother that I came to know Buddhism. I feel happy to become a Buddhist, to be a child of the Buddha.

- How have the teachings of the Buddha changed your perspective on life?

- Thuy Tien: In Buddhism, there is a very meaningful philosophy called the law of Cause and Effect. If we encounter a great misfortune and cannot rise above it, it is due to the karma from previous lives that we have caused for others.

It is like planting a chili tree; it can never produce sweet fruit. We must accept those bitter things. Hatred or resentment cannot change it, because it will create a different cause and effect. By facing the problem calmly and patiently, we can overcome it in a very happy way.

If one does not understand the law of cause and effect, one might blame life or others. Complaining about why one is suffering, why heaven does not show mercy. But such things will only bring bad energy to humans, it can never be good.

Interview with Công Vinh – Thủy Tiên: “10 years ago, my wife persuaded me but I felt the timing wasn’t right, now I spend 1 hour every day practicing” - Photo 2.

The photo of the whole family shared by Thủy Tiên on her fanpage: "Sunday morning at my house...".

- As for Mr. Vinh, is your reason rooted in "consideration for your wife"?

- Cong Vinh: (Laughs loudly) No. About 10 years ago, Tien kept talking, persuading me all the time, but I just said, if you haven't had the destiny, how can you get in? Until I met my master, the Venerable Minling Khenchen Rinpoche – the Ninth Incarnation of Hong Quan Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva in India. Being transformed by Him, I have been practicing since then.

After practicing for nearly 8 years now, with about 1 hour each day or more, I feel that my mind has been transformed.

- Specifically, how so, sir?

- Công Vinh: I think many people have never thought about death, not even once has the idea crossed their mind. But there are times when walking on the street, I suddenly realize that I will die. I deeply understand that: "Ah, money is not that important to me." Of course, it is still needed for life but it is not everything. Fame and everything I have are just ephemeral.

I live today, but tomorrow I may not wake up anymore. Why not live to the fullest, live as a father, a husband and a son, and live a useful life for society. If I can love and help someone, I always have to be ready. Because after I die, there is no chance to do it.

We should think that being alive now is a privilege. Live in a way that is useful and complete to be happy, so that the people around us can also be happy. Life is as it is now because we planted a virtue in a previous life. And whatever is done in this life will also affect the next life.

Interview with Công Vinh – Thủy Tiên: “10 years ago, my wife persuaded me but I felt the timing wasn’t right, now I spend 1 hour every day practicing” - Photo 3.

- In the beginning, when you couldn’t convince your husband, how did you feel?

- Thủy Tiên: Previously, Vinh would still do charity and good deeds, but for him to think deeply about practicing spiritual cultivation was difficult. I started by talking gradually about impermanent things. Since my father passed away when I was only 9, I understood how terrible it is to lose a loved one. But no one can escape death. At that time, Vinh said that living while constantly thinking about dying would be too sad, so he decided not to think about it anymore. After some time, due to some kind of fate, he changed, voluntarily oriented himself towards it, and felt that it was the right thing to do.

In the past, at the end of every year, Mr. Vinh would slaughter a pig to give to the villagers. We had only known each other for 2 months, and the first thing I did was forbid him from doing that. He could use that money to give gifts or buy rice for people, but he could not take lives. Using this suffering to compensate for that happiness is completely meaningless. He will be the one who bears the karma.

Since I was little, even ants, my mother would not allow me to kill. She taught me to love and share. The money I saved as a child was also to help the poor, not to spend on myself. This deeply influenced my life and many of my decisions later on.

Interview with Công Vinh – Thủy Tiên: “10 years ago, my wife persuaded me but I felt the timing wasn’t right, now I spend 1 hour each day practicing” - Photo 4.

- How is your current life?”

- Công Vinh: Thủy Tiên’s work is probably like that of many other women in a family. In the morning, she wakes up and prepares breakfast for her husband, then talks with him before having lunch. In the afternoon, she exercises, and in the evening, she drinks tea and chats with each other before going to sleep (laughs).

- What about you?

- Thủy Tiên: Vinh is the kind of person like he’s on a boat, even if tomorrow is the end of the world, tonight he still has to lie down and sleep, then deal with it tomorrow. Very relaxed, doesn’t worry about anything at all.

- Công Vinh: Actually, I think that what I have achieved at this moment is beyond imagination. I still tell Tiên that I am used to living a hard life, as long as I have rice and vegetables, I can live day by day.

I don't care about money because I don't deal with money, whatever there is my wife keeps. I just need a happy family, a place to eat when I come home, a bed to sleep in, and to see my wife and children happy.

- Which adjective would describe most accurately the state of both of them right now?

- Công Vinh: Happy. I feel that my life is exactly like that. In a week, I have time to do what I like, time to work, and I can balance family and life. More importantly, I have a very strong support system and don’t worry when facing any problems. Everything is taken care of by my wife, I just play, so it’s really enjoyable (laughs).

I am someone who stays optimistic in any situation. I have experienced all kinds of happiness and hardship. Now I have nothing to worry about, I have food at home, and at night I can lay down and sleep without having to think about anything.

Interview with Công Vinh – Thủy Tiên: “10 years ago, my wife persuaded me but I felt the timing wasn’t right, now I spend 1 hour a day practicing” - Photo 5.

- How long did you two prepare to have such leisurely days?

- Công Vinh: After I stopped playing football. Having passed half of my life, I think I understand the true value of life. Now is the most beautiful age, still healthy enough to enjoy life. I see many people at 60 or 70 still having to do this or that, buried in work. They don’t have a moment to enjoy life or to be at peace, and they don’t even have time to travel.

- Thủy Tiên: Actually, whether you feel at ease or not depends on yourself. There are people for whom building the biggest possible career is essential. They may have one company, but they start 3 or 4 more to form a conglomerate. When they become chairman, they feel very satisfied. The wealth they have built is enormous, yet they don’t know when death will knock on their door. If that day comes unexpectedly, everything they have built becomes meaningless. They can’t enjoy anything except waking up in the morning, signing contracts, paying employees, attending meetings, and burying themselves in work. Living like that, what is it for?

- People will say, now I only have 2 million, 2 billion, but when will I have 200 billion, I will be like Công Vinh and Thủy Tiên…

- Công Vinh: No, when they have 200 billion, they will wish for 2,000 billion. I think money is never enough.

- Thuy Tien: A long time ago, there was a time I went to Australia to perform. The time difference and the fact that artists have to rush around meant hardly any sleep. I arrived in the morning, performed in the evening until about 2 or 3 a.m., and then by 4 or 5 a.m. I had to rush to the airport to continue. At the airport, I didn't dare to sleep for fear of missing the plane. This went on for 3 or 4 days. I thought: "Why am I working so hard like an ox? What am I a slave to?"

I am very sleepy but cannot sleep because I have to go earn money, yet in truth, am I lacking so much that I have to do this? Many artists, after a trip to the U.S., come back with a lot of money but their faces are gray and exhausted. Suddenly, I thought that perhaps I am becoming a slave to money. Then I changed my perspective on life, even changing the mindset that I must work to save for my children in the future.

Interview with Công Vinh – Thủy Tiên: “10 years ago, my wife persuaded me but I felt it wasn’t the right time, now I spend 1 hour each day practicing” - Photo 6.

- Why is that?

- Thuy Tien: Leaving assets for your child that they don't have the blessing to enjoy will only ruin everything. The most important thing is to leave virtue for your child.

We still tell little Gao (the nickname of Cong Vinh and Thuy Tien's daughter – PV) that this is her parents' property. When you grow up, work, and earn money, that will be your property. Parents' money belongs to parents, not to you. Parents won't give it to you, so you have to learn and work on your own.

- Công Vinh: Many people say that making money should be to secure your children's future and earn money for your children. I think that is not everything. Of course, I will have enough finances to support my children, but it doesn't mean I will leave assets to my children so that they become dependent on them. My parents didn't leave any assets for me in the past.

Interview with Công Vinh – Thủy Tiên: “10 years ago, my wife persuaded me but I felt the timing wasn't right, now I dedicate 1 hour each day to practice” - Photo 7.

- Currently, where does your largest income come from?

- Thuy Tien: I still go singing and doing advertisements. As for Vinh, he mainly earns from running a sports center business and the CV9 football academy. In addition, there is real estate investment and some other products.

- What advantages and disadvantages does business bring to celebrities like you two?

Interview with Cong Vinh – Thuy Tien: “10 years ago, my wife persuaded me but I felt it wasn't the right time, now I spend 1 hour a day practicing spirituality” - Photo 8.

- Thủy Tiên: There are no disadvantages. As for the advantages, like in investing in a football academy, we find it very beneficial. First, the kids have a professional place to play and interact with coaches who are former professional national players, dedicated to teaching them. Second, it helps colleagues.

Many people, after retiring, do not know what they will continue to do. If they continue working with a professional football team, they have to be separated from their wives and children, while their children are growing and need their father's presence.

If working at the academy, the salary is good, less strenuous, the international environment is civilized and professional, and it is also close to family, wife, and children. As a result, the more we develop, the more useful we will be to colleagues, friends, and even to the students.

- Did both of you anticipate the risks when taking your savings out to invest?

- Công Vinh: We only do what we truly understand. Because the money we earn is made with "sweat and tears." When using it, we have to be considerate. Tiên and I share the same views on this matter. I feel that what I am investing in and doing is completely right.

I have a special love for young children. Regardless of their age, whether 5 or 17, I can connect with them. I can tell what problems the child is having on that day, whether they are happy or sad. I will always listen so that the children can open up about everything, and I will always have words or things to encourage them to overcome it. I believe that children will get better and better each day.

- Thủy Tiên: Every business matter of ours has to be useful. At the academy, there are many children with hyperactivity, autism, who cannot integrate with the community. Mr. Vinh had to be persistent for many months, and now, they smile very happily. As for families in difficult circumstances, he will provide support with tuition fees.

He remembers the names of every child among the hundreds of students at the Academy. He loves them as if they were his own children. If they feel a little pain, he will comfort them. He is happiest after returning home from teaching the children.

- How does following Buddhism and practicing it affect your business perspective?

- Công Vinh: Of course, it is very important. If I do it, I have to do it with the right mind and honesty.

Interview with Công Vinh – Thủy Tiên: "10 years ago, my wife persuaded me but I felt the time wasn’t right, now I spend 1 hour every day practicing" - Photo 9.

- Does that affect your profit?
