tieu_de: WHEN I STUDY BUDDHISM, WHILE READING THE Kṣitigarbha SUTRA I WAS STARTLED, THE SUTRA DESCRIBES SOMETHING VERY SIMILAR TO MY FATHER'S CASE, FROM
tom_tat: The classics of saints and sages, from a young age, around before ten years old, were almost all memorized and never forgotten throughout life. When needed, they would quote the scriptures immediately, because they all remembered them. Good habits all come from a young age.
noi_dung:
WHEN I STUDIED BUDDHISM, I WAS STARTLED WHILE READING THE Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, IT SPOKE VERY SIMILARLY TO MY FATHER'S CASE, FROM

The writings of the saints and sages, from a young age, around before they are ten years old, are almost all memorized and never forgotten throughout their lives. When needed, they quote from the scriptures immediately, because they all remember them.

Good habits are cultivated from a young age. Not killing living beings nurtures what in them? Compassion; compassion needs to be cultivated by not eating the flesh of living beings. Why is that? Not being cruel. Here, we are not talking about cause and effect, just simply about compassion. If people understand cause and effect, they dare not eat the flesh of living beings. People with compassionate hearts are not cruel enough to eat the flesh of living beings. If people have compassion, they are not cruel in harming others, in causing harm to others. Why is that? Lack of morality. If one understands cause and effect, they dare not eat the flesh of living beings, and dare not harm others. Why is that? Because there are consequences. A wholesome mind manifests with good consequences, while evil thoughts...Evil deeds have evil consequences, cause and effect do not fail in the slightest. In the previous chapter, we learned a lot; the previous chapter specifically talked about the reward of good deeds, and it is completely true.

I had been studying Buddhism for half a year when I became a vegetarian. Why? I don't understand much about the theory, but I fear karma. I witnessed this karma with my own eyes—I saw my father's karma when he died. My father was a good person, but he accumulated heavy karma. What was his sin? He liked hunting. During the resistance war, he was a soldier, managing the military arsenal. What did he manage? Weapons, so guns and ammunition were very easy to get. I remember I was about 15 or 16 years old then. At home, there were eight rifles and handguns because he managed the weapons. As for ammunition, he would bring it home in boxes to use for hunting. Every day we would wake up very early, before dawn, he would call me and my younger brother to get up and go.hunting with him. My younger sibling was still very small, so did not dare to shoot, while I was fifteen or sixteen years old, so I could do it. I went hunting with my father, hunting for three years straight. Every day at least ten bullets were fired, so I practiced how to shoot, does it require precise aiming? No, almost every shot hit the target, I also trained this skill. Practicing every day, hunting every day.

After studying Buddhism and reflecting, when my father passed away, it was exactly like what is described in the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. Seeing a mountain, he ran toward it; a man thin as a stick, yet very strong, several people could not catch him. Seeing water, he dived in, extremely pitiful—what is that? It is the karmic retribution for killing, hunting in the mountains, catching fish in ponds—how is the fish caught? Using explosives, throwing a bomb into a pond, many fish would be caught. After throwing a bomb, thousands of fish would die, completely unaware. Therefore, life during the years of war was extremely hard; in my household, we had wild game meat to eat every day. But afterwhen the victory also lasted only five years, my father encountered this suffering, and left like that.

When I studied Buddhism and read the Earth Store Sutra, I was startled because it closely resembled my father's situation, so I no longer dared to eat meat. Therefore, Master Chương Gia taught me to practice charity, and the first thing I learned was liberation of animals. Since I personally did not have the conditions to do this, whenever the community performed animal liberation, I would gladly contribute money and effort and participate in the liberation with them.

Creating such heavy negative karma is serious. The Lankavatara Sutra says very well: “A person dies and becomes a goat; a goat dies and becomes a person.” If you eat half a kilogram of it, in your next life you must repay it with eight taels; this is talking about the law of karma and cause and effect. A life debt must be repaid with a life debt, a monetary debt must be repaid with money.

In recent years, it seems as if the entire universe, the whole world, has undergone a general reckoning. Many people who practice Buddhism, whether lay or monastic, have had vengeful spirits or patrons come to claim their lives or debts; this has happened. This is not superstition, not fake.

Recently, about three months ago, there was a person who practiced Buddhism at home. He had suffered from asthma for many years, but it could not be cured. He secluded himself to contemplate the Buddha for one month and discovered that his asthma was caused by a vengeful spirit in his body, which was making him suffer this illness. Upon discovering this, he sincerely repented and said: the Bodhisattva Su-xuen_called this vengeful spirit, asking them not to trouble him so that he could recite sutras well and chant the Buddha’s name properly, hoping that this vengeful spirit could cultivate together with him. He dedicated the merit of his cultivation to them, praying for rebirth in the Pure Land. As soon as this intention arose, his asthma indeed disappeared. This asthmaIs it still there? Yes, beside him, a month later, the creditor told him: Amitabha Buddha has received them into the Western Pure Land, his asthma is gone, no treatment is needed and it is already cured. Later, he thought about it, his face looked very unpleasant, and he thought: Could it be that another resentful creditor has come to find him? Indeed, he was right, it was a resentful creditor. His face really looked very unpleasant, like he was drunk, he called this a drunken person. Using this method to beseech Amitabha Buddha, Amitabha Buddha indeed showed compassion, guiding him to the Western Pure Land. He had suffered from these two illnesses for many years, both untreatable, causing immense suffering, and now the problem has been resolved.

Therefore, it makes us reflect that when our body hurts here and is ill there, it is certainly because resentful spirits and enemies are troubling our body. People who do not study Buddhism do not understand this and have to endure torment and receive retribution. People who study Buddhism understand this, dedicate merit to them, worship them, and help them transcend. They rejoice, depart, and the illness is then healed. Thus, both oneself and one’s family benefit.

(Excerpt from: Explanation of the Great Sutra of Pure Land, volume 542)

tieu_de: Retribution for Killing Living Beings
tom_tat: The greatest enmity in the world is none other than 'killing.' Therefore, it is said: 'Kill a person to repay life, owe a debt to pay money.' If you kill someone's father or brother, they will kill your father or brother. Keep
noi_dung:
CONSEQUENCES OF KILLING LIVING BEINGS

The greatest enmity in the world is nothing other than "killing living beings." Therefore, it is said: "Kill a person, repay with a life; incur a debt, repay with money." If you kill someone's father or brother, they will kill your father or brother. This way, people massacre each other, never ending. Because of too much killing of living beings, the consequences come very quickly, called: "present-world retribution," meaning the retribution appears in the present life.

Why do people nowadays often develop so many strange illnesses? To summarize in one sentence, it comes from killing living beings. If you take the lives of sentient beings, those beings will come to you to claim your life. For such peculiar diseases, even doctors are helpless. So what should you do? That means you need to sincerely repent, correct your mistakes to become a new person, and do many meritorious deeds that benefit sentient beings; only then can the sins accumulated from the past be eliminated. If you do not do this, it is feared that you will not easily recover from illness. This is the truth, not superstition.

1. Boils on the Face of People in the Present Time

Today I will tell two cases about the matter of killing living beings. Around the year 1945, there was Venerable Master Dai Ming, the abbot of Thua Thien Temple, in Suzhou Province, China. Although this Venerable Master was a Buddhist, he believed in non-Buddhist practices, and in the temple also worshipped the Fox Immortal. As a result, the fox freely came and went in the temple without being driven away by anyone, and it was not afraid of people either. People and the fox lived together peacefully.

At that time, the Venerable Master was in seclusion at this temple to read through the Tripitaka. The fox also came to the Venerable Master's room to practice with him. While the Venerable Master was reading the scriptures, it slept on the cushion for worship that the Venerable Master used. When the Venerable Master wanted to perform prostrations, he said to it: "I want to bow to the Buddha, you go outside!" At that time, the fox obediently stepped out of the room. After the Venerable Master finished his prostrations, it came back in and continued to sleep on the cushion for worship. Every day was like this, over a long period, and the two became like fellow practitioners.

One day, the Venerable Master was a little hot-tempered. When it was time to pay respects to the Buddha, the Venerable Master said to it: “If you don’t go out right now, I will beat you to death!” The fox glared as if it didn’t care about the Venerable Master, then it closed its eyes and continued sleeping. Perhaps it thought something like: After all, a monk has aspirations of compassion and uses skillful means as a gateway. So it did not go.

At that moment, the Venerable Master got angry and said, “How could this be! So the guest wants to overpower the host as well! I will beat you to death!” After saying that, the Venerable Master took out his stick to threaten it to leave. But the fox still did not bother to pay attention. In a fit of anger, the Venerable Master swung the stick in one strike. Unexpectedly, he missed his target and hit the fox's head, causing blood to flow and stain the entire Buddha altar cushion red. Indeed, the Venerable Master had killed it. Because he had committed the sin of killing, the Venerable Master felt deep remorse in his heart and did not know how to settle it properly. How could he absolve this karmic sin? Thinking over and over, he also ponderedthere was no way out. Suddenly, the Venerable Master’s spiritual intelligence recalled that someone had said: if one kills a fox and gives its meat to others to eat, the karmic debt of killing will be resolved. So the Venerable Master skinned the fox and gave the meat to some workers to eat - thinking that this would settle the matter.

Unexpectedly, seven days later, the fox spirit came to tell the Monk: "I have gone to the King of Hell to accuse you, you must pay with your life!" The Monk, who was in the middle of meditation, was extremely terrified upon hearing this. So the Monk began to recite the Great Compassion Mantra. Thanks to the power of the mantra, the fox spirit could not come near the Monk, so it could not harm him. But it also refused to leave, and it constantly came to disturb him. Seven days later, realizing that it could not take revenge on its own, the fox spirit went to seek reinforcements. Can you guess which reinforcements it sought? It was the spirits of Japanese soldiers who had died in battleDuring the Japanese invasion of China, the fox gathered a large number of troops, and then they used cannons to fire at the Monk. But although they bombarded for many days, they still could not hit the Monk. Why? Because the Monk focused all his mind on chanting the Great Compassion Mantra, not leaving his seat, so the cannonballs missed and just fell around the Monk.

After many days of not eating or drinking, the Venerable Monk was truly exhausted. In an instant, he felt his mind in a state of panic and dizziness, and unfortunately, his right knee was hit by a shell. Immediately, the Japanese spiritual soldiers withdrew. The Venerable Monk escaped the shelling threat, so he felt extremely relieved, thinking the ordeal was over. Just as he thought so, he felt pain in the spot where he had been hit by the shell. When the Venerable Monk looked down, he saw a pustule on his right knee that resembled a human face, complete with a mouth and teeth. The wound was swollen and painful, and no medicine could heal it.gone.

One day, someone said to the Venerable Monk: “Applying fatty meat on the sore will relieve the pain.” The Venerable Monk tried it, and indeed it worked. But when the piece of fatty meat was completely eaten up by the sore, the Venerable Monk began to feel pain again. And so the Venerable Monk was continually tormented by sores, enduring indescribable suffering. After many days of pain, the Venerable Monk suddenly realized that only by eliminating all karmic obstacles could one be free from suffering. Thus, the Venerable Monk wholeheartedly devoted himself to cultivation and no longer paid attention to the pain. He persevered through intense suffering and single-mindedly performed Buddha worship and repented for the karma of killing. After threeNext year, the Venerable Monk will recover from the illness.

This Venerable Monk is a true practitioner. He often traveled to consult and learn from virtuous teachers and also visited the four famous sacred mountains (Mount Wutai, Mount Emei, Mount Jiuhua, Mount Putuo) and the eight large and small mountains in China. The Venerable Monk possesses great spiritual virtue. Although he accidentally killed a fox, he still had to repent and perform Buddha worship to eliminate the karmic obstacles. Therefore, we should understand that the karmic consequence of killing is the worst. Please pay attention! Do not kill living beings but instead engage in many acts of merit by releasing them. If you kill at will, you will suffer from various strange illnesses that cannot be cured.or else you will become disabled, and then regret it for the rest of your life!

2. Pustules on the Face of People in the Past

During the reign of Emperor Yizong of the Tang dynasty, there was a National Teacher named Zen Master Wu Da. When the Zen Master was at Cu An Temple in Chang'an province giving sermons, Emperor Yizong personally came to listen to the Dharma and specially gifted the Zen Master a throne made of agarwood. At that time, the Zen Master developed arrogance in his heart, considering himself the greatest monk of his era, unparalleled by anyone. Unexpectedly, as soon as such delusions arose in his mind, the Dharma Protector immediately abandoned the Zen Master. Consequently, a longstanding enemy who had followed the Zen Master for ten lifetimes took this opportunity for revenge and struck a blow to the Zen Master's groin. From then on, a boil shaped like a human face appeared on the Zen Master's knee, havingeyelashes, has eyes, has a mouth, has teeth. Every day it must eat meat and drink wine. If it is not given meat and wine, the boils will cause painful aches, suffering indescribable. No matter how many doctors, they are helpless, with no way to cure it.

At the time when Zen Master Ngộ Đạt had not yet attained the prestigious position of National Teacher, there was a year at a temple in Chang'an when the Zen Master encountered a monk suffering from the growth of malignant boils. The pimples oozed fluid and bled, looking extremely filthy, and emitted a foul stench that made people feel like vomiting. No one dared to go near the ailing monk. At that time, Zen Master Ngộ Đạt was in the next room, and day by day he took care of the sick monk. The Zen Master wholeheartedly served, offering meals and washing the monk's wounds, without any concern for the foul and filthy odor. Time passed without notice; summer ended and autumn arrived. By the time the season...Afterwards, it became cool, and the sores of the monk gradually healed. When it was time to part, the sick monk said to Zen Master Ngộ Đạt: 'Thank you for taking care of me. If you ever encounter any difficulties in the future, come to Mông Sơn in Sichuan to find me. On the mountain, there are two giant pine trees as a landmark. My name is Ca Nặc.'

Zen Master Ngộ Đạt recalled past events and then went up to Mông Sơn to find the monk who had previously suffered from a poisonous tumor.

From afar, looking up at the mid-mountain, the Zen master saw two towering pine trees reaching into the clouds. When he arrived in front of the two pine trees, the Zen master discovered a temple made of dazzling gold. Just as he was about to search for it, he saw the monk standing at the temple entrance, smiling, and then led Zen Master Ngộ Đạt inside. After paying respects to the monk, Zen Master Ngộ Đạt then explained in detail his suffering. The monk told the Zen master to go down to the rock at the stream the next morning to cleanse his wound, as this would heal his illness.

On Monday morning, the novice monk led the Zen master to a rock by the stream. Just as he was about to wash the wound, the pustule on the person’s face suddenly spoke: “Wait before washing! There is still unresolved hatred between us. You are a venerable monk, having read many scriptures, you must have read the history of the Western Han. So do you know the story of Yuan An slicing across Zhao Hu’s back? Yuan An is you now, and Zhao Hu was me in the past. You have been a monk for ten generations, practicing diligently, so I could never find the opportunity for revenge. It was only because you became arrogant that I had the chance to sneak in. Today, thanks to the compassionate Venerable Kanak,“Wanting to reconcile the enmity between us, You used the samadhi water practice to cleanse me, so from now on, I will no longer resent You.”

After National Teacher Ngộ Đạt heard the story, his soul floated up to the ninth heaven. He hurriedly scooped water to wash the poisonous sore, but felt a sharp pain down to his bones, then collapsed into a coma. After a long time, when he suddenly woke up and looked down at his knees, there was no trace of the poisonous sore anymore. It was then that National Teacher realized that the monk was a holy sage. National Teacher intended to return to the temple to pay respects and worship the monk, but when he turned his head back, he could not see the temple anywhere. So National Teacher gathered grass and built a hut at that place, and morning and evening devoted himself to ceremonies and chanting. National Teacher is the author of the Sám Pháp prayer, as we know it today.The book "Compassion Samadhi Water Repentance" consists of three volumes.

Through the two stories above, although there are slight differences, as most parts are similar, they both serve to warn people that the law of cause and effect is truly without the slightest error.

The first story is about retribution that happens in this very life, while the second story is about retribution that occurs ten generations later. In short, when karma matures, our time has also come, and ultimately we must face the consequences. Today I am talking about these two cases to help everyone clearly understand that killing is harmful, and it should not be treated like a child's game. Nowadays, as science progresses, weapons that kill will also become even more terrible. All the causes and effects they have created—how can they be eliminated?

Currently, the world is in a dark state full of obstacles; even a slight trigger could cause a great war to break out. The vengeful demons will use this as an excuse to take revenge. But karmic retribution for wrongful deeds, how long will it ever end? Unless one refrains from killing; otherwise, we will never have a day of peace.

Lecture on April 15, 1984

30. What Is Called the Six Great Principles?

Look! Nowadays, most people in the world are almost going crazy, looking like they have mental illnesses. This world is about to turn into a mad world. Regardless of male or female, old or young, they all fail to recognize the basic conditions of being human. That’s why there is the scene of one person competing, another seizing. In order to achieve personal goals, people resort to all kinds of tricks, forget morality for profit, and betray friends. How terrifying! So what are the basic conditions of being human? They are the Six Great Principles of the Vạn Phật Holy City. If everyone were to follow them, the world would be peaceful.bottle.

The Six Great Principles are:

1- Do not compete: Do not compete with anyone. Keep what you should have and should not have things you do not need. Absolutely do not get angry.

2- Do not be greedy: Regarding material things, as long as you have enough to use, it is sufficient, and do not be greedy for anything. The things I have, if you need them, I will give them to you. We should not be stingy or covetous.

3- Non-attachment: Not seeking external things, called: “A person with virtue seeks nothing,” someone who does not seek is a person of noble character. Generally, a person of character is content with little desire and knows sufficiency. Whoever does not crave wealth, does not crave beauty, does not crave fame, does not crave food, does not crave sleep will have a mind filled with much peace and their heart will feel no fear at all.

4- Do not be selfish or self-centered: Anything that belongs to the public for everyone's convenience should not be kept for oneself. You can give alms, which means you do not have selfishness or self-centeredness, and it is called: "Consider all the elderly as your own parents, love all children as if they were your own." This is the manifestation of a person without selfishness. The establishment of universities, high schools, elementary schools, and nursing homes at the Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery also stems from this mindset.

5- Not seeking personal gain: It is to dedicate oneself for others. Whatever is beneficial, we let others do it. On the contrary, whatever is not beneficial, we take it upon ourselves to do. Absolutely never being greedy for fame, profit, or material gain, seeking reputation or recognition, because those are selfish and self-serving thoughts.

6- No false speech: The mouth has four evils, which are: false speech, lying speech, harsh speech, and double-tongued speech. A person who commits any of these evils will in the future be condemned to hell, where their tongue will be cut off. False speech is one of the Five Precepts. Those who study Buddhist teachings should strictly observe the Five Precepts. What is false speech? It is to speak falsely, which means: to say you see what you do not see; to say you do not see what you see; to say you hear what you do not hear; to say you do not hear what you hear; to say you understand what you do not understand; to say you do not understand what you understand; to say you know what you do not know; to say you do not know what you know. That is false speech.

Why do people in the world go crazy, go mad like this? Because they have a mind of strife, a mind of greed, a mind of craving, a selfish mind, a self-benefiting mind, and a mind of false speech. Therefore, all day long they go around crazily without being at ease. This is a very serious problem; we should not regard it as mere speculation but should quickly improve social habits, otherwise we will face unimaginable consequences.

HT Lecture on April 16, 1984

31. The Descendants of the Demon King

The Buddha used his concentration power to overcome the magical powers of the demon king during their contest. At that time, the demon king said to the Buddha: "Now I have no way to defeat you, but in the future, when your disciples lack sufficient concentration and their understanding is incorrect, I will sneak into your house through a broken door, wear your clothes, eat your food, and afterwards even urinate in your bowl. Let us see what you will do then!" The Buddha Shakyamuni calmly replied: "Then I have no way either."

Clearly, nowadays, there are people who have openly become monks and say that the Amitabha Sutra is fake, with the reason being that there are some sentences in the sutra that have no basis for verification, such as: “From here, going westward, passing through ten thousand billion Buddha realms, there is a world named Ultimate Bliss.” He asks: “Which local official measured that? Measuring the distance of ten thousand billion Buddha realms might be a bit more, or it might be a bit less. So can we be sure it is ten thousand billion Buddha realms?” Indeed, these are foolish and absurd arguments, only serving to make a laughingstock of themselves before the world!

Recently, a monastic declared to everyone that the Śūraṅgama Sūtra is a forgery and should not be believed. Based on the passage: “On the day of the king father's death anniversary, King Pasenadi held a feast to invite the Buddha into the palace. The king personally welcomed the Tathāgata and arranged a table full of precious food,” that person argued that this passage did not align with Indian customs at the time—because in India, filial piety was not taught. Therefore, he decisively concluded that the Śūraṅgama Sūtra is a forgery and not taught by the Buddha. This is precisely the act of destroying the sutras and slandering the Buddha, and the karmic retribution for this destruction is unimaginable. The thought of this monk is trulySo childish! As for the mind, where it is, you can figure it out for yourselves!

In the Dharma Scripture on Complete Extinction, it is said: “In the future, when the era of the Decline of the Law arrives, the Shurangama Sutra will be the first to be destroyed.” This is because the Shurangama Sutra represents the era of True Dharma. Without the Shurangama Sutra, it means there is no True Dharma. Currently, there are many mountain demons and water monsters, and they assert that the Shurangama Sutra was not spoken by the Buddha and want people not to believe it. If one does not believe in the Shurangama Sutra, then all other scriptures could also be dismissed and disbelieved, right? Why? Because there would be no basis! Therefore, you can see that the mind of the demon king is truly extremely vicious!

This is also because the Lankavatara Sutra speaks the truth very clearly. Meanwhile, the demon king cannot maintain the Four Pure Repentances, which are the four pure precepts, nor can he practice the Universal Dharma Method of the twenty-five sages, and he dare not read about the realms of the Fifty Types of Pretas. Because he fears that his true form will be exposed, revealing his real face to people, he seeks to destroy the Lankavatara Sutra. The destruction here does not mean burning the scriptures, but destroying the sutra from the minds of sentient beings, causing everyone to lose faith in the Lankavatara Sutra.

The stories of life are just that wonderful. Very few people truly recognize them. It's like the trade business: those who sell fake medicine make great sales, while those who sell real medicine have no buyers. Why? Because no genuine person can recognize its value. Therefore, I say, the truth is not recognized by anyone, while the fake captivates everyone. It's a very easy-to-understand principle!

Currently, it is the period of Dharma Decline, and many people slander and do not believe in the genuine teachers practicing Buddhist Dharma. But the false teachers, because they preach the Dharma in a very lively manner, draw many listeners, to the point that there is no space left in the lecture hall; people are crowded together like sardines, struggling to breathe. Yet there are monastics who advocate the slogan of not eating vegetarian. This teacher tells everyone: "Anyone who eats vegetarian food is greedy; only those who do not eat vegetarian food are not greedy." Such reasoning is truly laughable to the world, it blinds people, causing them confusion - confusion over and over, continuously confused.until going down to hell, never escaping forever.

Therefore, when studying the Dharma, we need to have the Dharma-discerning eye, the eye that knows how to choose the Dharma, so that we can clearly distinguish right from wrong, correct from incorrect, and good from evil. Otherwise, we are no different from blind people feeling an elephant, unable to grasp the true principle. People say something, and we repeat it exactly the same, echoing what we hear. People say the elephant is like a wall, and we also say the elephant is like a wall. People say the elephant is like a pillar, and we echo by saying the elephant is like a pillar. In the end, what is the elephant really like? We do not know. When studying the Dharma, we must truly understand it.morality, rather than following blindly. Everyone should pay special attention to this point!

Dharma Talk on April 17, 1984

According to Khaithī - Dharma Master Tuyên Hóa

tieu_de: FOUR PRINCIPAL CLEAR AND PURE REPENTANCES (Both Laypeople and Monastics Should Recite Morning and Evening Practice, Like a Steel Shield)
tom_tat: Ah Nan! The master often hears in the Vinaya circles that the Tathagata once proclaimed the three decisive meanings of practice, which are: Controlling the mind is called MORAL CONDUCT, from MORAL CONDUCT arises CONCENTRATION, and from CONCENTRATION arises WISDOM; this is called the 'three practices'.
noi_dung:
FOUR TYPES OF PURE AND BRIGHT REPENTANCE (Both Laypeople and Monastics Should Practice Morning and Evening, Like a Steel Shield)

Ananda! The teacher often hears in the monastic community that the Tathagata has declared three decisive meanings of practice, which are: Controlling the mind is called MORAL DISCIPLINE, from Moral Discipline arises CONCENTRATION, from Concentration arises WISDOM; these are called "three non-defiled trainings."

Teacher Ananda! Why is controlling the mind called "Moral Discipline"?

Beings in the six realms across all worlds, if their minds are free from lust, will no longer continue to wander in samsara. A monk practices the dhyana meditation mainly to escape from worldly suffering, and if the mind does not eradicate lust, one cannot escape worldly suffering. Even if one has great wisdom and experiences meditation, if the mind does not completely cut off lust, he will definitely fall into demonic paths:

•Those of high rank will become demon kings.

•Those of medium rank will become demon subjects.

•Those of low rank will become female demons.

The various kinds of demons also have their followers, and all claim themselves to have attained supreme enlightenment! After the Tathāgata passed into nirvana, in the era of the degenerate Dharma, these demons became extremely numerous, their influence renowned in the world, full of lustful behaviors, yet pretending to be good spiritual teachers, causing sentient beings to fall into the pit of sensual desire, losing the path of bodhi.

Teachers instruct people to practice the method of proper concentration, and first of all, one must abandon the mind of lust. That is the clear, pure, and decisive primary teaching of the Tathāgata and all past Buddhas.

Therefore, Ananda! One who practices meditation but does not eradicate lust is like trying to cook sand and rocks into rice; even after hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, it will still be nothing but hot sand and rocks. Why is that? Because its root nature is sand and rocks, not rice. Using a lustful body to seek the profound fruit of Buddhahood, even if one attains enlightenment after many lifetimes of practice, it is still rooted in lust. If the root is lust, it will inevitably wander through the three evil paths, unable to escape; is there any path to attaining the nirvana of the Buddhas? Surely, one must put an end to the source that triggers lust, both in mind and body.all are eliminated; until even the very nature of elimination no longer exists, then one can hope to attain the Bodhi fruit of the Buddha. Just as the Tathagata said, that is the word of the Buddha; if it is not true according to this saying, it is the word of the Mara of Asura.

Again, Ananda! Sentient beings in the six realms across all worlds, if their minds do not refrain from killing, they will not cease to wander in birth and death. Monks who practice the dhyana samadhi do so to escape the troubles of the world; if the mind that kills is not eliminated, they cannot escape worldly troubles. Even with much wisdom and present meditation, if the mind of killing is not eradicated, they will certainly fall into the path of ghosts:

•Those of high level will become great-powerful demons. •Those of medium level will become air-traveling yakshas or ghost generals.

•Those of low level will become rakshasas that walk on the ground.

Those types of demons and spirits also have their followers, and all claim themselves to have attained supreme enlightenment! After the Tathagata passed into nirvana, in the degenerate age of the Dharma, these demons and spirits became extremely numerous and their prestige was renowned throughout the world. They claim that even by eating meat, one can achieve the path of bodhi.

Hey Ananda! The Tathagata tells the monks to eat five kinds of pure meat; that meat is all born from the Tathagata's divine power and originally has no life element. In the land of Brahmins, the terrain is mostly hot and humid, with much sand and rocks, so vegetables cannot grow. The Tathagata uses the power of great compassion and, out of the human heart's great benevolence, calls it meat, and the revered monks also experience that "meat-like" taste. How, after the Tathagata's Parinirvana, can those who truly eat sentient beings call themselves Buddhists! Revere monks should know, those who eat meat, even if their minds are enlightened, are only somewhat like having right concentration; in reality, they are all great killers, after the karmic retribution ends.That body will certainly be submerged in the sea of suffering of birth and death; it is not a disciple of the Buddha. People like that, who kill each other and eat each other without end, how can they escape the three realms!

The teacher instructs people in the practice of proper meditation, first of all one must abandon the mind of lust; next is to abandon the mind of killing. That is a clear, pure teaching, the second determination of the Tathagata and the Buddhas of the past.

Therefore, A Nan! A person who practices meditation but does not give up the mind of killing is like someone who covers their own ears, shouting loudly yet hoping others won't hear; this is called the more one wants to hide, the more exposed one becomes. The pure monks and Bodhisattvas, even when walking on a path, do not step on young grass, let alone take it by hand! How can a person with great compassion use the flesh and blood of sentient beings as food? If the monks do not wear fabrics made of silk, do not use shoes made of leather or garments made of fur from the East, and also do not consume milk, butter, or cheese, those monks are truly detached from the world.liberated, having paid off all the injustices of past lives, will no longer return in the three realms. Why is that? Using the body parts of sentient beings means one must form karmic connections with them; just as humans eat hundreds of types of grains taken from the earth, so the feet are never separate from the earth. Those who resolutely make both their body and mind abstain from eating things made from the flesh of sentient beings, not using things made from the body parts of sentient beings, the Tathagata says these are truly liberated people. Just as the Tathagata says, that is the word of the Buddha; if it is not as this, then it is the word of the Mara Ba-thuân.

Again, Ananda! Beings in the six realms throughout the worlds, if their minds do not steal, then they will no longer continue to wander in samsara. A practitioner of the samadhi method aims to escape the suffering of the world; if the mind's habit of stealing is not eliminated, one cannot escape the suffering of the world. Even if one has much wisdom and present meditation, if the mind's habit of stealing is not ended, one will surely fall into the wrong path:

• The higher ones become spirits. • The middle ones become demons.

• The lower ones become evil humans, who are possessed and deceived by demons.

Those heretical beings also have their followers, and all claim themselves to have attained supreme enlightenment! After the Tathāgata's parinirvāṇa, in the age of the decline of the Dharma, these heretical beings become extremely numerous, their influence renowned throughout the world, secretly deceiving, claiming to be good teachers, asserting themselves as ones who have attained the profound Dharma, deceiving the ignorant, frightening people so that they lose right faith, and serving them to the point that homes are depleted.

The Tathagata taught the bhikkhus to practice almsround in order to gradually eliminate greed and attain Bodhi. The bhikkhus do not cook for themselves, sending their transient lives to rely temporarily on the three realms, appearing only once and returning no more. How could those bandits use the Tathagata's attire to trade the Tathagata, committing all kinds of karmic offenses while claiming it is the Dharma of the Buddha! They also slander genuine monastics who strictly observe the bhikkhu precepts, saying it is the Lesser Vehicle! Because of this slander, countless beings are deluded, and therefore they must descend into the Avici Hell.

After the Tathagata passes into nirvana, if a monk generates the resolve to practice the method of dhyana concentration like an illusion, he can, in front of the image of the Tathagata, use his body to light a lamp, burn a fingertip, or burn an incense stick on his body. The Tathagata says that the monk, the karmic consequences from beginningless past, in just one moment, have been completely repaid, permanently abandoning the world, freeing himself from all defilements. Although he has not yet clearly seen the path to supreme enlightenment immediately, he has made a firm resolve towards the Buddha Dharma. If one cannot perform such a small act of self-sacrifice, even if one attains the path of non-action, one must be reborn as a human to repay old debts, like the story of eating horse fodder ofTathagata, not different at all.

The teacher instructs people to practice the dharma of right concentration; after having abandoned the mind of lust and the mind of killing, one must also abandon the mind of stealing. This is the clear, pure teaching, the third decisive principle of the Tathāgata and past Buddhas.

Therefore, dear Ananda! A person who practices meditation but does not abandon the mind of stealing is like someone pouring water into a bowl with a hole in the bottom and expecting it to fill; no matter how many lifetimes pass, that bowl will never be full. If monks possess nothing beyond their three robes and one bowl, even the slightest thing should not be kept; if there is a surplus from alms, it should be given to starving beings; when arriving at the assembly, they should join hands in salutation; if anyone scolds or insults them, they should rejoice and treat it as praise; both body and mind must be fully let go, regarding the physical body as a common possession of all beings; and they should not use the teachings as means for their own benefit.taking the Tathagata as the basis for one's own understanding, causing beginners to go astray; then those individuals will be certified by the Tathagata as truly having attained genuine samadhi. Just as the Tathagata says, this is the word of the Buddha; not in accordance with this saying, it is the word of the demon Bhātuân.

Hey Ananda! Beings in the six realms throughout the worlds, even if both body and mind have completely ceased actions of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, if they still commit the great fault of lying, their right meditation is still not pure, becoming a deluded attachment and losing the seed of Buddhahood. These are people who claim to have attained what they have not, claim to have realized what they have not; or there are those who want to be honored by everyone as the foremost in the world, and then they say:

“I have now attained the fruit of Stream-Entry, the fruit of Once-Returner, the fruit of Non-Returner, the fruit of Arahant, the fruit of Pratyekabuddha, the fruit of Bodhisattva on the Ground or the Upper Ground,” saying so with the hope that people will worship and offer alms. These are those who destroy wholesome roots, annihilate the seeds of Buddhahood; like someone cutting down a banyan tree with a knife. The Tathagata said that this person has completely lost the good roots, no longer possesses right view, and is forever sinking in the ocean of suffering, never achieving right concentration.

The Tathagata told the Bodhisattvas and Arhats, that after the Tathagata passes away, they should manifest in various forms, being born in the age of the decline of the Dharma to guide sentient beings who are immersed; sometimes as monks, sometimes as laypeople, kings, officials, male companions, female companions, even collaborating with immoral women, widows, deceitful people, thieves, butchers, merchants, in order to praise the Buddha's teachings, so that their body and mind may enter the stage of the third bhūmi. However, while doing so, they must absolutely not say:

“I truly am a Bodhisattva, I truly am an Arhat.” One must not carelessly reveal the secret teachings of the Tathagata to those who have not yet practiced Buddhism; only at the moment of death may one silently entrust them. How could those who crave illusory views deceive living beings and incur the great sin of false speech!

The teacher instructs people in the practice of right concentration; after abandoning desires, the mind of killing, and the mind of stealing, one must also abandon the mind of great false speech. This is the clear, pure, and decisive fourth teaching of the Tathagata and past Buddhas.

Therefore, Ananda! If the mind's great false speech is not eradicated, it is like taking human excrement and molding it into the shape of incense wood, then hoping it will have the fragrance of incense wood; it will never happen.

The Tathagata taught the monks: Direct mind is the seat of the path. In all actions—walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—one must maintain a straight and upright mind, without a trace of deceit. How could one then proudly proclaim to have attained the profound Dharma of the superior beings? Ordinary people, even in their ignorance, who claim to be kings, bring upon themselves ruin; let alone the position of Dharma King—how could one dare to falsely claim it? If the person is not sincere, the result will surely be crooked. A person like that, seeking the Bodhi fruit of the Buddha, is like trying to bite one's own navel with the mouth; how could it ever be bitten!

If the monks' minds are like tense strings of a musical instrument, all their conduct will be genuine, and they will surely directly enter the meditative absorption, never being disturbed by demonic influences; and the Tathāgata will seal confirmation for them, accomplishing the Supreme Knowledge of the Bodhisattvas. As the Tathāgata said, this is the word of the Buddha; if it is not as this statement, it is the word of the demon Pātūn.

Hey Ananda! The teacher asked about how to concentrate the mind, and the Tathagata just spoke: Those who wish to enter samadhi, practice the wondrous Dharma, and seek the Bodhisattva path, must first uphold the four fundamental precepts, pure as a crystal or as dew; then naturally, all branches like the three faults of thought and the four faults of speech will have no cause to arise. Ananda! If one strictly observes these four major precepts, the mind of that person will not be inclined toward the sense objects of form, smell, taste, touch, let alone all demonic matters—how could they arise! If the karmic habits from past lives cannot be eradicated, the teacher should instruct that person to wholeheartedly recite the supreme mantra "Maha Tat."“Đát Đa Bát Đát Ra” (Lăng Nghiêm Mantra), by the virtuous transformed Buddha sitting on the jeweled lotus throne, appearing from the light in the fleshly tuft on the top of the Tathagata's head, was proclaimed while the Tathagata entered samadhi.

As for you, in many previous lives, you have shared karmic ties with Ma Đăng Già, and your romantic intimacy had become a habit, not just in this one life. Yet, with just one instance of the Tathāgata proclaiming the mantra, Ma Đăng Già instantly and permanently freed herself from the mind of lust and attained Arhatship. When she was still a lustful woman, she had no intention of cultivating, only relying on the unimaginable divine power of the mantra to quickly achieve the stage of the Non-Learner! Moreover, since you, venerable master, are among the Śrāvakas in the assembly, directing your mind toward the Supreme Vehicle, you are certain to attain Buddhahood, like dust being carried along the wind—with no difficulty at all!

tieu_de: MERIT IN CREATING BUDDHA STATUES
tom_tat: The Lotus Sutra – The Expedient Means Chapter – Chapter 2 Briefly Explained by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua
noi_dung:
MERIT OF CREATING BUDDHA STATUES

Lotus Sutra – The Expedient Means Chapter – Chapter 2

Venerable Tuyen Hoa's brief commentary

Sutra text:

If a person, for the sake of the Buddha,

Builds images,

Carves them into forms,

They have already attained the Buddha Way.

Or uses the Seven Treasures to make

Bowls, white copper, red copper

Aluminum along with lead and zinc

Iron, wood, or clay

Or using adhesive cloth,

Devoutly making Buddha statues

People like that

Have all attained the Buddhist path

Brief explanation:

If people create statues for the sake of the Buddha, those who made statues to offer to the Buddha, by carving into forms, all the subtle characteristics of the Buddhas of the ten directions, have all attained the Buddha Way. They have attained the Buddha Way.

Or they use the seven treasures; gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, mother-of-pearl, red pearls, agate, or bronze, copper, copper alloy; aluminum along with lead and zinc; iron, wood, or clay; or use lacquered fabric; these are adorned to make Buddha statues. Those people; have all attained the Buddha Way. Making Buddha statues has eleven kinds of merit:

1. For countless lives, you have eyes that clearly see.

2. You are not born into evil places. Friends and neighbors are all good people. You will not encounter wicked people or wild beasts.

3. You are always born into wealthy families. Being born into a rich family earns respect.

4. Your body is golden in color.

5. You are abundantly wealthy.

6. You are born into a virtuous family.

7. You could be born as a king. Today there is no Emperor, but you could become President. That is the same. Or if you insist on becoming an Emperor, you could find a monarchy and be born in that country.

8. You could become a Wheel-Turning King. Being a Wheel-Turning King is even higher than being a President. When you are a Wheel-Turning King, if you practice, you could become a Buddha.

9. You could be born in the heaven of Brahma and live for a long time, up to one lifespan. You could become the king of celestial beings.

10. You will not fall into the evil path. Those who make Buddha statues will not fall into hell, the animal realm, or the hungry ghost realm.

11. In all future lives and cycles of existence, you will respect the Triple Gem, take refuge in the Triple Gem, and will not fall into downfall.

Hearing about the eleven merits of making Buddha statues, if we are capable, we should make even more Buddha statues. If you make Buddha statues, your appearance will be very perfect. Why is the Buddha's appearance so perfect? Because over three great eons of Asamkhyeya kalpas, He created countless Buddha statues. In the first Asamkhyeya kalpa, the Buddha encountered more than 75,000 Buddhas; in the second Asamkhyeya kalpa, He encountered more than 76,000 Buddhas; in the third Asamkhyeya kalpa, He encountered more than 77,000 Buddhas. Having met so many Buddhas, naturally, He must have created even more Buddha statues than that number. Who can know how many Buddha statues He created? Therefore, His appearanceExtraordinarily perfect. But when creating a Buddha statue, we should not think: “I will make a Buddha statue and then I will be beautiful, and everyone will love me.” That is not a proper motivation. We should cultivate merit and wisdom to become Buddhas in the future. All those who create Buddha statues have already become Buddhas.

Sutra text:

Drawing a radiant Buddha statue

A hundred features of auspicious merit

Whether done by oneself or instructing others

All have already accomplished the Buddha path.

Even children playing

Using grass or brushes

Or using their own fingernails

To draw a Buddha statue

Such people

Gradually accumulate merit.

Full of great compassion

All have attained the Buddha path

Only teaching the Bodhisattvas

To save countless beings.

Brief explanation:

Although the above scripture mentions using fabric and glue to create Buddha statues, the monastic code does not advocate using glued fabric to make Buddha statues because the glue has a certain unpleasant smell. The monastic code also states that if the statue is a standing Buddha, we, as Buddhist practitioners, should not sit in front of a standing Buddha statue. If it is a seated Buddha, we should not lie down in front of a seated Buddha statue.

Painting Buddha statues brilliantly, with a hundred auspicious marks, is adorned with the blessings of the Buddha. Buddha statues are honored with the virtuous marks of the Buddha. Whether done by oneself or commissioned from others, it has already accomplished the path to Buddhahood. These people have all attained Buddhahood.

Even children play, using grass or pens. Or using grass, or using a branch to draw a Buddha statue, or using colored pens to draw a Buddha statue. Or using their own fingernails, or while playing in the mud, children use their fingernails to draw a Buddha statue. And they draw a Buddha statue.

Long ago, in Sichuan, there was a person who specialized in chanting the Diamond Sutra, and when chanting, he would use his hand to write the Diamond Sutra in the air. Every day, he stood in the same spot and used his hand to "write" in the air. Later, whenever it rained, no rain would fall around the place where he wrote the Diamond Sutra; this happened every time it rained. Only those who had opened their Buddha eyes could see that although he used his hand to write the Diamond Sutra in the air, the celestial dragons and eightfold beings also came to protect this Sutra, preventing the rainwater from falling there. Therefore, later a temple was built at this location. Hence, you mayseeing that he only used his hand to write in the void but had such a great influence. This story is recorded in the book "Kim Cang Kinh Linh Di Ky."

Those kinds of people, the people mentioned above, are the ones who make Buddha statues. Gradually accumulating merit, full of great compassion, they have all attained the path of Buddhahood. These people have all realized supreme enlightenment and become Buddhas.

They only teach Bodhisattvas, liberating countless beings.

Buddhas propagate the teachings to Bodhisattvas, and guide the Śrāvakas from the Lesser Vehicle towards the Greater Vehicle, practicing the Bodhisattva path, and later redirect them towards Buddhahood, liberating countless, innumerable sentient beings.

tieu_de: RESPECT BUDDHA, BE COMPASSIONATE, HUMBLE. VIRTUE STRENGTHENS THE PATH OF PRACTICE.
tom_tat: 1. When you succeed at anything, do not be proud, because according to cause and effect, being proud of something will result in losing it later. For example, being proud of being beautiful or talented, after some time, the beauty or talent will fade.
noi_dung:
HONOR THE BUDDHA, BE COMPASSIONATE, HUMBLE. MERIT SOLIDIFY THE PATH OF PRACTICE.

1. When we succeed in anything, we should not be proud, because according to cause and effect, being proud of something will lead to losing it afterward.

For example, being proud of being beautiful or talented, after a certain period of time, beauty and talent will fade.

2. When succeeding in something, do not arise with arrogance, secretly thinking you are more talented than others; this is an act of burning your own Merit.

Therefore, to preserve blessings, do not be arrogant or look down on others. A person who has a heart that despises or belittles others is someone who brings about failure in life.

3. For those who practice (spiritual cultivation), it is to always control their mind to correct and overcome their own mistakes, so that when viewed externally, there are no wrong words or gestures, living harmoniously and friendly with everyone, receiving much praise and admiration from many people… one should be cautious of the compliments from others.

Everyone's praise is good; accept the praise, thank the praise sincerely, but do not be delighted by that praise. Instead, let it go, do not hold on to the praise to secretly rejoice.

Because:

When the mind becomes joyful at the praise of others, the ego will grow, depleting the merit of practice, and the path of cultivation will be blocked.

For those who do not practice, who do not know Buddhist teachings, when overly delighted by praise, it also increases the self, increases arrogance, and will extremely reduce merit.

For intelligent people, they do not like praise, they do not like showing off for that reason.

A discreet and quiet life will give people more strength to succeed in the path of life!

Homage to the Original Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha!

BUDDHIST MASTER QUANG

Homage to Amitabha Buddha
