tieu_de: THE JUDGE SERIOUSLY RESPONDED: "THE KING OF THE UNDERWORLD SEES THAT THE YANG WORLD HAS RELEASED EVIL ENERGY AND CAN NO LONGER BE TOLERATED"
tom_tat: Thankful to the Buddhas for their blessings! I almost couldn't write today. These past few days, there have been many obstacles preventing A Ngọc from going to hell; indeed, this round hasn't ended yet, and another one comes. First of all,
noi_dung:
SERIOUS JUDGE REPLIED: "THE KING OF THE UNDERWORLD SAW THAT THE HUMAN WORLD HAS RELEASED EVIL ENERGY AND CAN NO LONGER BE BEARED"

Thank you, Buddhas, for your blessings! I almost couldn’t write today. In the past few days, many obstacles have come to prevent A Ngọc from going to hell; indeed, one difficulty ends only to be followed by another. First, the computer malfunctioned and I couldn’t type, then some inhuman beings took advantage of the fact that I was sleeping to disturb me and drain my energy. At this moment, A Ngọc began to feel feverish and have a headache, very exhausted.

This morning, I had already come down with a cold. Whenever I catch a cold, I diligently recite mantras, it usually takes at least 7 days to recover, otherwise it would take half a month. Earlier, I used my power of recitation to tell myself that today I absolutely must not fall ill, that I must go to hell, that I must write, and I believed that I would certainly succeed. So I sat down and began reciting the Peacock Mantra. Roughly after 30 minutes, the fever was gone, my nose no longer ran, my throat started to feel better, my head no longer hurt, and the cold began to lighten. I am infinitely grateful for the blessings of the Peacock Bright King andAll Buddhas of the ten directions. A Ngoc is determined to do his best in this sacred work to repay the Buddha's grace! Otherwise, he will betray the protection of the Buddhas!

Sitting in the white lotus, Judge A Di Đà Phật!

Today, the Judge takes me to visit a hell of Sexual Immorality, the Hell of Soul Sword Flower.

I ask the Judge:

"Why is it called the Hell of Soul Sword Flower?".

The Judge seriously answers:

"This hell is meant for sentient beings whose natural lifespan is not yet over, who in the human world indulge in masturbation and immoral sexual conduct; men who daily or frequently deliberately change girlfriends or lovers while feeling proud of themselves, women who daily or frequently deliberately change boyfriends or lovers while thinking it is clever. Those who violate sexual morality in this way, indulging in lust, severely disrupt the balance of righteous energy and the yin-yang harmony of heaven and earth. Every time they commit masturbation, the thoughts of sentient beings emit a large amount of lustful and immoral energy; this type of negative energy attracts various demons, spirits, etc., which quietly harm the person performing the act."without knowing. When this type of evil energy becomes too abundant and too strong, forming an extremely powerful force, countless types of disasters will inevitably occur in the human world to restore balance. Humanity severely violates the natural laws of the universe, and because there is no law to handle it in the human world, some Western countries even legally approve cohabitation, etc. Those who enact such laws must endure immeasurable hellish retribution, and the karma of hell will only end when such laws are completely abolished in the human world. As the saying goes, 'Bodhisattvas fear causes, sentient beings fear effects'; we need to make everything in accordance withCause and effect every day, be careful to sow a little good cause so as not to suffer bad retribution in the next life. King Minh of the Underworld saw that the mortal world had released so much evil energy that it could no longer be tolerated, most of which was caused by young people who had not yet reached adulthood creating evil karma. Therefore, I, King Minh, had to build many more hells to punish those beings who violated precepts but have not yet completed their mortal lifespan, hoping to use the act of capturing the souls of the living from the human world into hell as a warning to people, eliminate their karmic sins, and also slightly reduce the time they have to endure punishment in hell after death.

Many thanks to Judge because A Ngoc explained in detail, and I also learned a lot, truly must thank Judge!

When I went to the Hell of Soul Sword Flowers, I saw that this prison was very vast. It turned out that there were many small children in the prison, especially from Western countries, all being punished together—indeed, there were so many! There were children from England, America, France, and China, generally speaking, all types of people from different nationalities were there. At that moment, I saw many spirits of little boys being dragged out by demons and struck in their genitals with a tool shaped like a flower made of iron. They suffered in pain and cried out loudly, fresh blood gushing out—it looked truly horrifying. As for the girls, a red-hot iron flower was inserted into their lower parts, causing pain so intense that they rolled on the ground, screamingwail and cry.

Here, there are too many prisoners, the cries echo to the heavens, I hear them very uncomfortably, after watching for a while I immediately withdrew, feeling very uncomfortable; if it were not for advising people with all my might, A Ngoc absolutely would not want to come here!

Beings in the human world who undergo this punishment feel as if they have a fever, lying on their bed in a hazy, dreamlike coma, because the three souls of their body are taken to hell. Therefore, such people cannot live a normal life. Some think they are having a nightmare but it is more painful than a nightmare; most can feel the suffering in the physical body, especially in the lower part, which is extremely painful and uncomfortable; a few people, after enduring the punishment of hell, are awakened by the physical pain and change.

The Judge said:

"The King of Hell in the underworld attaches great importance to this social issue; punishment is to prevent immoral practices from continuing to spread, aiming to avoid serious accidents in the human world."

A Ngoc respectfully asks the judge:

"Why are the punishments in the lustful hells so modernized, with devices like computers, ice-reflecting mirrors, etc...?"

The Judge said:

"Hell is a reflection of the human world; as long as beings in the human world violate the rules with modern things, hell immediately creates corresponding forms of punishment to punish them. Currently, reconstructive techniques in the human world are very advanced; with just a little money, one can change from head to toe at any time without anyone knowing. In the human world, one can hide and escape, but in terms of the Law of the Underworld, not to mention changing the head or face, even if one reincarnates many times, they will be immediately brought back by me, the King of Light, to endure punishment. Ah Ngoc, go back and try to advise beings in the human world; they must follow the law."Law, filial piety towards parents, adherence to Benevolence, Righteousness, Propriety, Wisdom, and Trustworthiness; do not say that this is an antique with no meaning but it is very important for balancing the rules for the constant operation of heaven and earth. Whoever does not comply will naturally be eliminated and receive punishment. Alright! Today, this is enough, you may go home, and we will continue next time.

A Ngọc respectfully bows farewell to the Judge!

(Excerpt from The Heartless Sound Law)

tieu_de: Chanting Buddha's Name to Treat Dengue Fever and Amitabha Buddha Arriving
tom_tat: Amitabha Fruit, before I was a tantric practitioner. I was very close to Avalokiteshvara. Every day I recite Om Mani Padme Hum. The mind is extremely peaceful and cool. The power of the mantra makes me very compassionate.
noi_dung:
CHANTING BUDDHA TO TREAT HEMORRHAGIC FEVER AND AMITABHA BUDDHA COMES

Amitabha Fruit, I was previously a tantric practitioner. I was very close to Avalokiteshvara. Every day I recited Om Mani Padme Hum. My heart was extremely peaceful and cool. The power of the mantra made me very compassionate. Even an ant, I cared for. That is thanks to the power of Avalokiteshvara.

One light rainy day, on the mountain, I was reciting a mantra. I went to the scripture cabinet and accidentally read the book "Essentials of Nianfo" by Dharma Nhiên Shàng Rén. He is Xālībhāra, the Great Arhat, the Dharma Master General. He also said he is a person of Sukhāvatī. He manifested again as the founder of the Pure Land school in Japan. From that moment, I realized the supreme nature of the Pure Land and determined to recite the Buddha's name to be reborn in the Pure Land.

I continuously recite Buddha's name, and my mind becomes cool, peaceful, and relaxed in a way that's hard to describe. Every night, I look at the edge of the forest, listening to a girl reciting mantras, and watch the river, feeling immense happiness and peace. I pray that everyone in the world can be as peaceful as I am. I have reached the stage of initial effortless recitation (During the times of chores and earning a living, as an ordinary person with heavy karma, I have already lost the stage of initial effortless recitation). I just sit quietly, listening intently and looking up at the sky. The master asks, 'Which level of heaven have you reached?' We just smile.

I had dengue fever; my senior brother, who studied at a pharmaceutical college, looked at my skin and diagnosed that I had dengue fever. Even while writhing in fever, I still did not leave the Buddha's title. My senior brother and family asked me to go to the hospital. I refused and said that the Buddha is the Great Physician. My senior brother gave me a fever-reducing effervescent tablet and scolded me for being stubborn.

I recited Buddha's name and fell asleep. In the middle of the night, I woke up and looked at the Tripitaka cabinet and then toward the window; the moonlight came in, spreading across the floor very beautifully and mysteriously. If I remember correctly, it was around 2:15 a.m. I sighed and continued reciting, wishing for Amitabha Buddha to heal my illness. After reciting for about ten minutes, suddenly my mind became extremely peaceful as a cool sensation started at the top of my head and gradually spread down my entire body, like a cool blanket slowly covering me from head to toe, and I could clearly feel the coolness wherever it reached. Feeling comfortable, I thought:

"Amitabha Buddha has come, He has come. He has come to cure the illness." I chanted until I fell asleep. The next day I was 100% cured, jumped out of bed to have breakfast, strong as an ox. My senior monk brother was shocked when he heard me tell the story. And to see that yesterday I was a frail old lady lying in high fever, suffering, and today I was a lively young man. The master had no comment. I wholeheartedly believe in Buddha and chant Buddha’s name, relying on Amitabha Buddha to cure dengue fever like that.

A DI ĐÀ PHẬT, Buddha is the Great Healing King. If you are suffering from illness and pain, sincerely recite Buddha’s name without doubt. Be certain that Amitabha Buddha will come to heal you. He will surely come, so vow to entrust your life entirely to Amitabha Buddha. If your life is not yet finished, your illness will certainly be cured. I had dengue fever and only took two effervescent fever pills, that’s all. Why did I have a rapid response in just one day and night? Because at that time my faith was extremely full. I only recited Buddha’s name, and recited Buddha’s name, entrusting this life entirely to Buddha. I had strong faith, He would come, and indeed He did. Cancer? Modern medical science hasCannot be cured? Then why not take the medicine of Amitabha Buddha, sell your life to Amitabha Buddha. Sell your virtue as well, no longer care about the world. Single-mindedly recite the holy name. He will come and you will be cured. If your life has reached its end, you will be reborn in Ultimate Bliss and attain the stage of Bodhisattva of the Eight Grounds in one lifetime.

TC

tieu_de: ANYONE WHO EXPERIENCES SLEEP PARALYSIS IS CAUSED BY GHOST OCCULTISM.
tom_tat: Anyone who experiences sleep paralysis is caused by a demon. Demon enchantment is also one of the eight types of demons and gods we often see in the Sutras. The eight types of demons and gods include: Deva, Dragon, Yaksha, Gandharva, Asura, Garuda
noi_dung:
ANYONE WHO EXPERIENCES SLEEP PARALYSIS IS CAUSED BY EVIL SPIRITS.

Anyone who experiences sleep paralysis is caused by demon suppression. Demon suppression is also one of the eight groups of demons and deities commonly seen in the Scriptures. The eight groups of demons and deities include: Devas, Dragons, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Asuras, Kauravas, Kinnaras, and Mahoragas. When a person experiences sleep paralysis, their mind is fully aware, but the whole body cannot move, wanting to escape but being unable to do so. This is because the house they live in is not clean, in other words, there are demons in the house. Why are there demons in the house? Because the thoughts and actions of the people in the house are not righteous, hence attracting them.These demons come. These demons wait at home for the opportunity; when they see someone in the house whose fortune is not good, meaning their fortune is declining, they immediately take action to cause trouble and to intimidate that person.

When experiencing sleep paralysis, more than half of the time it is because one's fortune is in decline, so these spirits come to disturb. If one's fortune is flourishing, these spirits would not dare to come and disturb. Especially for those sincerely practicing cultivation, these spirits not only do not dare to disturb but are also scared and stay away. Therefore, when experiencing sleep paralysis, we must understand that our current fortune is not good, which is why spirits come to oppress us. Why is our fortune not good? It is because we do not practice according to the proper method, so our cultivation practice is ineffective, and various karmic obstacles arise one after another, causing our fortuneour [fortune] declines. Therefore, quickly turn back and follow what is taught in the Buddha’s scriptures to strive in practice; only then can your own fortune prosper.

It can be said that almost everyone in life more or less encounters this phenomenon. However, for those who sincerely practice Buddhism, after studying Buddhism, these phenomena will gradually decrease. Generally, during the first 10 years of studying Buddhism, they still occasionally occur, but after the first 10 years, this phenomenon will disappear. Therefore, in Buddhist practice, if you want to know whether your practice is genuine or whether your practice is effective, just compare it with the phenomena you experienced before studying Buddhism or when you first began studying Buddhism, and you will immediately know.

How should one compare this? Previously, whenever I went to sleep, I often experienced sleep paralysis, or in dreams I would encounter nightmares such as walking on dangerous paths, or being assaulted by deceased people, or being chased and killed by unknown individuals, or seeing myself wandering with demons and spirits... however, in these dream scenes, my mind was very scattered, very fearful, and uncontrollable. After a period of diligent practice, although I still dream, I am very clear-headed in the dreams, and all activities are just like in daily life, no longer encountering nightmares. This indicates that my practice has made significant progress. And if one often dreams of the Buddha,A Bodhisattva, or seeing oneself engaged in Buddhist activities, or practicing cultivation, these are all good matters resulting from the effective practice of cultivation that one has attracted.

Amitabha Buddha!

_ Dharma Master Jingkong_

tieu_de: HUSBAND AND WIFE ALONG WITH THEIR PHILANDERING WIFE ARE REBORN IN THE PURE LAND. (Amitabha Buddha. So good!
tom_tat: Trần Tánh Lương, courtesy name Tích Châu, was from Vô Vi district, Anhui province. He was a person engaged in the commercial class, and in middle age, he finally had a son named Thiện Thọ, who was naturally quite intelligent.
noi_dung:
HUSBAND AND WIFE, ALONG WITH THEIR CHILD, TOGETHER REBORN IN THE LAND OF SUPREME BLISS. (Amitabha Buddha. So great!)

Tran Tanh Luong, styled Tich Chau, was from Vo Vi district, Anhui province. He belonged to the merchant class, and in middle age, he had a son named Thien Tho, who was naturally quite intelligent, but unfortunately passed away at the age of fourteen. Tanh Luong thought to himself that he had always maintained a benevolent heart and often performed virtuous deeds, so why was his lineage cut off? Consequently, he completely disbelieved in the law of cause and effect. His second wife, Mrs. Ho, was gentle by nature and very devoted to Buddhism. Knowing her husband's attachment could not be explained, she merely endeavored to practice quietly, reciting the holy name of Avalokiteshvara.She used a sound to pray for a child. It wasn't long before she became pregnant, but when she was about to give birth, a sudden disaster struck. For twenty-nine days, she could neither eat nor speak or move; her body was burning hot like fire, and she was as thin as dry wood. Doctors from both Chinese and Western traditions were at a loss, and there was absolutely no hope of saving her life.

One night, Ms. Hồ Thị dreamed of an old woman holding a long-stemmed lotus flower, waving it from head to toe, saying: “It is due to your past karma that you have fallen severely ill, but fortunately you knew how to practice sincere mindfulness. Now I will sweep away your karmic obstacles and give you a good child!” At that moment, she felt her body and mind refreshed, strangely joyful, and suddenly woke up; her illness seemed to have vanished, and she got out of bed and moved around as usual. The next morning, she gave birth to a healthy, heavy baby boy with a handsome and fine appearance. This extraordinary event greatly astonished Tánh Lương! But after inquiring and hearing his wife recount all the details, he finally believed in the principle of cause and effect across three lifetimes.Truth is not nothingness. Deep in his heart, he was very grateful for the great compassion of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. From there, the husband and wife, along with the monastic community, recited the Buddha's name, resolutely practiced cultivation, helped the poor and suffering, built vegetarian monasteries for the monks, and tried their best in all good deeds. Knowing that Mrs. Hồ’s illness was cured and she gave birth due to the salvation of Avalokitesvara, Tánh Lương often went to Mount Putuo monastery to pay respects to the Great Master. Both husband and wife took refuge with Master Ấn Quang; Trần Tánh Lương's Dharma name was Liu Viên, and Mrs. Hồ’s Dharma name was Liu Thường. Around the first year of the Republic, all the monasteries on Mount Putuo were lacking food, and the entire area was requisitioned by the government for German residents. Tánh Lương hurriedHe relied on friends in the bureaucracy to help intervene, so in the end he avoided misfortune. The layperson then personally funded the restoration of the Da Bao pagoda and carried out various Buddhist activities to rebuild his monastery in order to repay the Three Jewels.

In the ninth year of the Republic era, a couple and their five children all received Bodhisattva precepts at Phap Nguyen Pagoda in Beijing. Three years later, Liu Thuong suddenly fell ill. On February 28, while she was reciting Buddha's name, she suddenly saw two acolytes holding a fan with four characters: "Western Land Reception." Knowing it was a sign of imminent rebirth, she asked her husband to invite four monks to their home to help with repentance and Buddha recitation. By the twenty-eighth of the next month, her illness had peacefully subsided. But in the first ten days of the fourth month, Liu Thuong again felt unwell, realizing that her time was near, and wholeheartedly recited Buddha's name, praying for early rebirth. On the fifth day, Tinh Luong invited the monksUpon arriving at the house, he instructed the household members to take turns assisting in chanting so that the sound of Buddha was continuous day and night. Liu Chang also silently recited along.

On the morning of the sixth day, she asked her family to heat water for her to bathe and change clothes. Then she tried to reach the altar to chant, make incense offerings, and perform prayers, after which she requested a bed to be prepared so she could lie on her right side facing the West. After lying quietly, she focused on chanting Buddha’s name until the hour of Hoi (9-11 p.m.), when suddenly she sat up, clasped her hands, and said: “The Three Saints of the Western Paradise have arrived!” She also said: “I still have three thousand Buddha recitations left; once I finish, I will go!” At that moment, more than thirty monks and laypeople loudly chanted the sacred name. Liu Thuong also chanted aloud for a while, her face showing a radiant smile as she passed away. At that time, a strange fragrance wafted through the house. At noon the next day, during the encoffining, incense offerings...Her head was still hot, her hands and feet soft, and her scent remained.

When Thiên Thọ, his firstborn son who died young, urgently needed an heir, Tánh Lương married another concubine, Sa, who was only seventeen. After a few years in her husband's house, thanks to proper guidance, she developed sincere faith and took refuge with Master Ấn Quang, receiving the Dharma name Liu Từ. From then on, Sa strictly observed the Five Precepts, practiced celibacy, and recited Buddha's name. Later, Liu Từ suffered from a persistent illness that would not heal, lying in bed for two years. Yet her faith and vows remained firm, and she never abandoned reciting the Buddha's name.

On the 15th day of the second month of the 19th year of the Republic, on the occasion of the Buddha's Parinirvana, the whole family invited the monks to gather at home to practice the Great Compassion Repentance. Just after the noon ceremony was over, the daughter brought a bowl of water, saying that she saw it ripple and emit light. Tánh Lương, standing nearby, quickly helped hold the bowl. At that moment, she said she saw him holding a lotus flower, fearing that the time of passing had come. Upon hearing this, Tánh Lương immediately went outside to invite the monks into the room to assist in chanting. Liu Từ suddenly knelt by the bed, bowing and saying: "The Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara radiates light from the Pure Land to shine throughout my entire body." Tánh Lương advised her to let go of allAll with a single mind sincerely praying for the Great Being to guide. Liu Từ, following the instruction, joined his hands in prayer: “I have endured much suffering from illness, praying that people in the world may soon be liberated and free from suffering. May the Bodhisattva have compassion and guide me to the Pure Land!” Around two o’clock in the afternoon, she said: “The Bodhisattva has appeared! Please ask the monks to step outside, so I can wash myself and change clothes.” But just as she was changing, she said again: “Amitabha Buddha has come from afar, extending His hand to radiate light and guide, accompanied by the Vajra attendants. Please quickly invite the monks back to assist in prayer!” At that moment, Liu Từ, without time to put on the robe, hurriedly sat cross-legged, joined his hands, and repeatedly chanted Amitabha Buddha’s name, then said: “I am going now!” Afterwards, she closed her eyes quietly.When passing away and being reborn in the Pure Land, both hands were still held together at the chest. At that time, everyone in the house smelled a fragrant scent. By noon the next day, her forehead was still warm, and her complexion was fresher and more radiant than when she was alive.

Tánh Lương watched over his wife, and because she recited the Buddha’s name, she received auspicious signs and actually experienced rebirth in the Pure Land, which further strengthened his faith. After that, he renovated the front hall for worship, making it as solemn as a temple or hermitage, and put up a signboard reading 'Lay Buddhists’ Practice Hall for Reciting the Buddha’s Name,' often gathering fellow practitioners together to cultivate and encourage one another. In the winter of the Tân Mùi year, the layman fell ill, and he prepared offerings to invite the monks from Thiên Phước Temple to stay at the Lay Buddhists’ Practice Hall, reciting the Buddha’s name daily in order to constantly hear the Buddha’s name and fulfill right mindfulness. On the eleventh day of the third month in the Nhâm Thân year (1932), at noon, Tánh Lương said: "I see the appearance of the Buddha and the Bodhisattvas.Good, solemn, and the lotus was very large and beautiful! The monks and his family knew that the moment of his Western return had come, so they all gathered in the room, loudly chanting Buddha's name. The laypeople also sat and counted their prayer beads, chanting along, and by past noon at two o'clock, he peacefully passed away.

That afternoon, lay practitioner Từ Huất Như, a close friend of Tánh Lương and also the abbot of Lâm, upon hearing the death announcement, hurriedly invited a group of friends to offer condolences. When the delegation arrived, it was already eight o’clock in the evening. All the friends saw that Tánh Lương was still sitting cross-legged upright, holding a rosary in his hands, his face fresh as if alive. Upon feeling, his crown was still warm, and his hands and feet were soft and gentle.

(Excerpt from Several Pure Lotus Tunes - CS B Bành Tế Thanh - Translated by the late Venerable Thích Thiền Tâm)

tieu_de: PLANTS ALSO HAVE LIFE, ISN'T EATING VEGETARIAN ALSO KILLING?
tom_tat: Question: The Buddha said all phenomena are equal, animals and plants both have life, eating meat is equivalent to killing. Similarly, vegetables and fruits also have life. Why is it not considered killing when we cut them to eat?
noi_dung:
PLANTS ALSO HAVE LIFE, ISN'T EATING VEGETARIAN ALSO KILLING?

Question: The Buddha said that all phenomena are equal, animals and plants all have life, and eating meat is the same as the act of killing. Similarly, vegetables and fruits also have life; we cut them to eat, so why is this not considered killing?

Venerable Master Tinh Khong answered: Your question is very good, very profound. Can a person go without eating? Yes. If you look at Shakyamuni Buddha in the past, while still in the world, he ate only one meal a day, as we often see in the Sutras. Arhats in this world eat once a week, while the Pratyekabuddhas eat once every half month. In the Heavenly Realm of the Form, celestial beings no longer need to eat; those in the Form Realm who have attained Samadhi and reached the First Dhyana have no attachment to wealth, beauty, or fame—this is considered cultivation. As for us in this world, it is called karma; you are obliged to eat, otherwise...When it comes to eating and drinking, you cannot survive; if you cannot survive, you also cannot escape the Six Realms of Samsara. In the Six Realms of Samsara, ultimately it is the law of retribution, this principle is very profound, and even explaining it to you for two weeks would not suffice. If you are forced to eat, then think about it: is it better for you to eat human flesh or animal flesh? This involves making a choice. Is it better to eat your parents' flesh or the flesh of other people? You would not eat your parents' flesh, but you would eat the flesh of others. If you compare humans with animals, you would eat animals rather than humans. If you compare animals with plants, you would leave animals and eat plants. You compare each level.that way it will be clearly understood, it cannot be the same.

Plants are living beings, yet they do not have emotions, meaning they have no sense of revenge or hatred. But if you eat animals, animals have revenge and hatred. What will that lead to? In the next life, things may not go as you wish—this is a serious matter. Plants are not like that; after they grow, they even seem to hope that you eat them. Why is that? They cultivate merit and also know how to accumulate blessings. We grow vegetables ourselves in Australia; our vegetables are not fertilized with chemicals, nor are they sprayed with pesticides, yet they are just as good as vegetables from other regular farms. We let the vegetables hear the chanting of Buddha's name and listen to Dharma talks.

Kinh, using a tape recorder to play for them to listen, took care of them very attentively. The fellow cultivator who managed the vegetable garden one night dreamed that a gourd came to him, saying that the gourd was very old, and he should quickly go harvest it as it was too old. He felt very strange, and the next day he went to that place to look, and indeed he found it. The gourd was hidden behind the leaves and had been accidentally overlooked. It really was old, how old? It was no longer edible, so he left it to use as seed. Observe plants, flowers, and trees; all understand human nature. If we show kindness to them, they also repay our kindness. They repay our kindness precisely in this way, by offering to the assembly.You need to study these matters well, and you will truly understand all phenomena in the universe and human life.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

BUDDHISM ENCOURAGES PEOPLE TO EAT VEGETARIANALLY; DOESN'T PLANT LIFE HAVE A SOUL? IF THEY HAVE NO SOUL, THEN cutting them, cooking them, would they not feel pain?

Question: A disciple has a friend who has not yet entered the Buddhist path and once asked the disciple: "Buddhists advise people to be vegetarian, eating meat is killing, so do plants not have life?" The disciple answered: "Because plants do not have a soul, cutting them, cooking them, they will not suffer," the disciple answered like that, is it correct?

Venerable Master Ting Kong replied: Your answer is only half correct and cannot be considered entirely correct. Why is that? You are right in saying that plants do not have souls, but there is a problem in saying that they do not feel pain. Regarding this matter, the experiments of Dr. Jiang Bunthang over the past years have already provided an answer. This phenomenon can only be thoroughly and clearly explained by Mahayana Buddhism. Outside of Mahayana Buddhism, it is difficult to fully explain this matter because it pertains to very profound knowledge. We can only say that plants do not have attachment, do not discriminate, because they do not haveAttachment and discrimination should not give rise to a mind of revenge or anger; it can only be explained this way. Plants that we eat, in fact, have sacrificed and devoted themselves, and we should have a sense of gratitude towards them, not waste them at will. Wasting is a sin. Why do we need to eat today? It is because of karmic obstacles. When we eat, we must generate a sense of shame and have a heart of gratitude toward the plants; only then is it proper.

Wealth, beauty, fame, and sensual pleasures are collectively called the Five Desires, and this is known by fellow Buddhist practitioners. In which realm do the Five Desires exist? They exist in the Desire Realm. When considering elevation to a higher state, one is born into the Form Realm. People in the Form Realm do not need to eat, they do not need to sleep, and they have no sexual desires; wealth, beauty, fame, and sensual pleasures are nonexistent there. That is the Form Realm. Currently, we still rely on these things, and when seeing those in the Form Realm, we immediately feel shame. We are so far inferior to them that they can exist without these things, which is something we need to understand. We must continuously elevate our own state of being.Eating should be as simple as possible, as little as possible. Therefore, in the past, the Blessed One ate one meal a day, in the middle of the day, and slept under a tree at night. Each of His meals came from going out with a begging bowl to receive alms; whatever anyone gave Him, he ate that, without any sense of discrimination. The meaning within is very profound: surely there is no discrimination, surely there is no attachment. Today, when we receive offerings from plants, we must also be worthy of them, practice diligently, cultivate our own virtue, accomplish our own knowledge, and make great contributions to society and sentient beings. In this way, the plants that you consume in this life also share in merit.Virtue, in reality, is all beneficial; they achieve success for you, while you achieve more good qualities and good deeds yourself, both sides benefit. If we create karma of wrongdoing, we make mistakes, then they also have faults; this principle needs to be clearly understood.

Venerable Thích Không

tieu_de: SHOULD RECITING BUDDHA'S NAME BE ACCOMPANIED BY ADDITIONAL MANTRAS? WHY SHOULD WE PRAY TO BE REBORN IN THE WESTERN PURE LAND?
tom_tat: 1. OVERVIEW OF MANTRAS. What is a Mantra? Why is it called Trì? TRÌ means to keep continuously (trì giữ), not to lose, not to forget. Why is it called Chú? To explain fully, CHÚ is a Mantra, a secret word. Now, in order to
noi_dung:
SHOULD CHANTING BUDDHA NAMES BE ACCOMPANIED BY MANTRAS? WHY SHOULD WE WISH TO BE REBORN IN THE WESTERN PURE LAND

1. OVERVIEW OF MANTRAS.

What is Trì Chú? Why is it called Trì? TRÌ means to hold continuously (trì giữ), not letting it be lost, not letting it be forgotten. Why is it called Chú? CHÚ, when fully expressed, is Thần Chú, a secret word. Now, for convenience, it is shortened to “Chú.” Some people do not understand and say: Thần Chú is created by the Taoist sect. That is incorrect, it is a mistake. The word THẦN here means "supernatural, spiritually powerful, transformative." The word CHÚ can also be called CHÂN NGÔN. The Thần Chú verses spoken by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have inexplicable power and merit. We should distinguish between TRÌ Chú and NIỆM Chú.

Reciting a Mantra: This means a mantra must be repeated continuously many times in order to be memorized thoroughly; only then is it called recitation. Simply reciting 3 or 7 times is considered chanting, not recitation. Chanting or reciting a mantra: This means just going through it once. For example, the “Ten Śūraṅgama Mantras” in the morning are chanted once, without a second or third time. The Sanskrit word for a sacred mantra is Dhārani, Chinese translation is Zong Chi, and in English it is called Mantra. It is called “Zong” because it encompasses countless dharmas, and “Chi” because it contains immeasurable meanings.

The Mantra carries an all-encompassing (total) meaning of all Dharma, preserving (sustaining) noble thoughts from the infinite wondrous significance of the inner mind. The phrase “Mantra” is the entire “Mind-Intention” of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas towards sentient beings. The meaning of the Mantra is extremely secret, no one can understand it, except for the deity (the master) of that Mantra and the Buddhas alone.

The Buddha's Mantra is different from that of the demonic path. The Buddha's mantra has the power to destroy evil and establish righteousness, eliminate bad karma, dispel false and harmful thoughts, generate wisdom, cultivate blessings and virtuous roots, prevent sins, save oneself and others from calamities caused by demons, especially to save the souls so they can be released in an extraordinary and rare way, leading people from the mortal realm to the holy realm quickly, closely connecting and resonating spiritually with the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, Saints, and achieving spiritual attainment. On the other hand, the mantra of the demonic path only harms people and things, brings disasters to people, and leads one to the three evil realms upon death. Although the mantra cannot be explained,With a devoted heart and sincere recitation, one will obtain miraculous and inconceivable effects. It is like drinking water; whether it feels warm or cold is only known to the person drinking it—others cannot know, nor can they understand or believe it. The efficacy of reciting a Mantra is the same; only those who are devoted to reciting the Mantra know clearly how effective it is—this is the 'secret'! Usually, a single Mantra can encompass an entire Sutra. This alone is enough to understand the power and merit of the Mantra that the Buddha spoke, which is beyond conception.

So why in this life is it necessary to pray for rebirth in the Western Pure Land? Why not stay in the world of Saha and practice until attaining Buddhahood?

From countless beginningless eons until now, we have drifted in birth and death through innumerable lifetimes. In many of these lives, we once generated the courageous bodhicitta, determined to diligently practice to definitely escape from birth and death. But after a period, from the first life to the subsequent lives, being defiled by the worldly dust, we backslide in bodhicitta, committing many evil karmas. From the realms of Devas, Spirits, Humans, Pretas, Animals, to Hell, we have all experienced them, only that we do not remember. Following the stream of karma, we continue in cyclic existence. Thus, after countless lifetimes, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, we still have not escaped from birth and death. The truth is, if we have the thought ofPracticing in this world to attain Arhatship (the Saintly fruit, liberation from the cycle of birth and death), or even the First Stage of Stream-Entered (the first fruit among the Four Saintly Fruits, guaranteeing Arhatship in the future), is extremely difficult, very, very hard; it can be said that even if one practices in this world for 1,000,000 lifetimes, one may still not attain it.

Why is that?

Because our realm is a corrupt world, it is possible that in this life we practice cultivation and vegetarianism, accumulate many virtuous deeds, and in the next life be born into a wealthy family, only to forget the initial bodhi mind and joyfully indulge in the five desires. Due to having merits, it is very easy to create bad karma, so after death one may fall into hell, and then in the following life practice goodness again. Even a single thought of pride, lust, or anger at the time of death can lead to downfall... and so on, when creating good karma one enjoys blessings, creating bad karma results in suffering... making it very difficult to attain enlightenment. Today, we learn about the practice of Buddha recitation, and as long as you have deep and firm faith inThe Western Pure Land, about Amitabha Buddha; those who courageously practice, observe vegetarianism, keep the precepts, make vows, and recite the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land can be reborn there. If one is reborn in the Middle Level of the Medium Birth, after 7 days the lotus will bloom, and upon hearing Amitabha Buddha expound the Dharma, one will attain the initial fruit of Stream-Enterer. After half a kalpa, approximately 8 million years, one attains Arhatship and then continues practicing to become a Buddha. Or, if reborn in the Upper Level of the Medium Birth, as soon as the lotus unfolds, one hears sounds praising the Four Noble Truths and immediately attains Arhatship (according to the Infinite Life Sutra), then continues practicing until becoming a Buddha.

We see that if in this lifetime one makes an effort to practice, then after rebirth one can be assured of liberation even if born into the lower grades of the lower realms. This practice method can carry karma for rebirth (that is, bring karma along for rebirth) and is very suitable for sentient beings in the latter days of Dharma today. It only requires that at the time of death, if one can recite the name of Amitābha Buddha ten times and aspire to be reborn in that realm, Amitābha Buddha will come to receive you. Even if one is currently still an ordinary being full of evil thoughts, at the moment of death, if one diligently recites the Buddha's name and lets go of all attachments, one will surely be reborn there. This is due to His 18th Great Vow, and we canthanks to His saving power, [one] attains rebirth.

Try to think about it: compared to drifting through hundreds of millions of lifetimes in reincarnation, which is easier? Therefore, in this life, knowing about the practice of Buddha recitation, we absolutely cannot neglect or overlook it!

If one recites mantras, can they attain rebirth in the Pure Land? Or is it only by exclusively reciting the Buddha's name that one can attain rebirth?

Reciting mantras can lead to rebirth in the Pure Land, but with the condition that one must recite the mantra to the state of either 'non-thought to spontaneous thought' or 'single-minded chaos' (these two states are very difficult for ordinary people who do not specialize in practice to achieve); otherwise, it is very difficult to be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Therefore, if one wishes to attain rebirth in the Western Pure Land, besides having complete Faith, Vow, and Practice, one should use the practice of reciting mantras as an auxiliary practice and the practice of reciting the Buddha's name (Amitabha) as the main practice if one wishes to be reborn. The time spent reciting mantras should only equal or be less than half the time spent reciting the Buddha's name. Why? Because in the 18th great vow of Amitabha Buddha, he vowed, '...Suppose when I attain Buddhahood,'Sentient beings in the ten directions wholeheartedly believe and wish to be born in my land, persevering in ten thoughts; if they cannot be born there, I will not attain supreme enlightenment...” On ordinary days, if one does not diligently practice cultivation, when facing death, the mind will disperse, making it very difficult to recite even a complete mantra. That is why we must nurture the seeds of mind through more recitations of the Buddha's name than through mantras. At the time of death, if you can recite the name of Amitābha Buddha ten times, Amitābha Buddha will come to take you to the Pure Land. Even if there are a few scattered thoughts, it doesn’t matter, as long as you have strong faith in the Pure Land, let go of all worldly attachments, and vow to be born there, you will surely attain rebirth! This is easy.much more than you recite to reach non-thinking, self-thought, or single-minded distraction! Because this is thanks to the other-power of our Buddha Amitabha, we should pay great attention to this!

So why should one recite mantras? Can one just chant the Buddha's name? Chanting the Buddha's name and reciting Sutras tends to lean towards inconceivable merit, while reciting mantras leans towards inconceivable spiritual power. Some mantras encompass merit, spiritual power, and the ability to eliminate karmic forces... for example, the Great Compassion Mantra (Chú Đại Bi) and the Śūraṅgama Mantra (Chú Thủ Lăng Nghiêm). Those who regularly practice these mantras without developing doubt will be protected in body and mind, can dissolve karmic forces, and experience peace in this life. High monks in Vietnam and China in the past, during their practice, besides chanting the Buddha's name and reciting Sutras, also recited various mantras, for example, Venerable Thích Thiền Tâm and the Great Master Ấn.Quang, HT. Tuyen Hoa....

Nowadays is the age of the decline of the Dharma, we are all ordinary beings with deep karmic obstacles. If we recite the Buddha's name without single-minded focus, confusion, and without genuine and continuous practice, we will not yet receive the blessings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. That is not to mention that today various types of demons, spirits, ghosts, and enchantments are all waiting to drain vital energy. Additionally, due to deep karmic obstacles and grudges, life becomes chaotic and makes it very difficult to cultivate. If one does not also recite mantras and only recites sutras and the Buddha’s name, it is very difficult to attain accomplishment, and it is easy to be disrupted, causing evil spirits to rise and worldly defilements to awaken negative minds such as anger, lust, greed, selfishness... ThusSo some people initially generate courageous aspirations to practice, but after a while, they lose their bodhicitta, become contaminated by worldly defilements, and even commit evil deeds! Therefore, it is necessary to recite mantras to protect the body and mind, eliminate karmic obstacles, and ensure peace in this life... Otherwise, it will be very difficult to practice (especially for lay practitioners who aspire to be reborn in the Western Pure Land). For this reason, it is necessary to combine both practices (mantra recitation and Buddha recollection), which will greatly increase the achievement. The 'powerful' mind leading to the Pure Land will be swift and peaceful, without obstacles. In addition, everyone should try to memorize one type of mantra, preferably the Great Compassion Mantra, so that when traveling, one can recite this mantra (with the possibility to omitThrough rituals in which the mantra is recited aloud or silently, with the aim of planting connections with the Buddha's path for sentient beings, both visible and invisible, along the way who hear it, then the merit of you is truly unimaginable!

(Excerpt from the "Foreword" in the book "Special Spells" compiled by the An Si Toan Thu Admin group)

tom_tat: How should one practice? First of all, one must eliminate desires and cut off attachments. One should neither stay too far from others nor get too close. Being too distant will lose the good affinity with people. Being too close will cause attachment.
noi_dung:
The character for 'busy' in Chinese consists of the characters Heart and Forget combined. It is also similar to the character for forgetfulness,

How should one practice? First of all, one must eliminate desires and cut off attachments. One should not stay too distant from others, nor should one be too close. Being too distant will lose the good connection with people. Being too close will let emotions control reason, making it impossible to practice.

When practicing, one should not wear a mask, pretend, or act for others to see. Practice relies entirely on one's own effort. Only then will there be results. Wherever there is a portion of sincerity, there will be a corresponding response. Everything depends on earnestness, truthfulness, and being genuine without falsehood. One should not deceive oneself or others.

If you want to save the world, you cannot use atomic bombs, gas bombs, or lasers, because they are inherently things that destroy the world. Only by using the eight virtues: filial piety, benevolence, loyalty, trustworthiness, propriety, righteousness, integrity, and honor. These eight virtues are the elixir that saves the souls of sentient beings, and also the miraculous medicine that most effectively saves human lives.

The incurable disease of the world is: The bankruptcy of education.

Venerable Master TUYÊN HÓA

tieu_de: WHY DO GOOD PEOPLE STILL ENCOUNTER MISFORTUNE?
tom_tat: - Source: Nhanqua.com.vn - Many people sometimes do good deeds to help others but still encounter quite a lot of misfortune and unhappiness... Could it be that heaven is blind? Let's read the story below to understand the reason.
noi_dung:
WHY DO PEOPLE WHO DO GOOD DEEDS STILL ENCOUNTER BAD LUCK?

- Source: Nhanqua.com.vn -

Many people sometimes do good deeds to help others but end up facing quite a lot of misfortune and unhappiness... Could it be that heaven is blind? Let's read the story below to understand the reason for this:

"In the final years of Emperor Kangxi's reign, there was a man named Liu Heng who lived by the riverside.

That year, there was a heavy rainstorm that lasted for several consecutive days without stopping, causing the river water to rise high, with waves surging endlessly toward the sky. The light boats, unable to withstand the strong waves and wind, often capsized and met with disaster.

On that day, right during the heavy rain, Lưu Hoành suddenly saw a pregnant woman in the river, struggling to hold onto a paddle that had a large piece broken off by the waves, thrashing about and crying out for help...

At that time, although there were many people on the riverbank witnessing the scene, no one dared to risk jumping into the rushing water to save her because of the strong waves and winds.

Lưu Hoành, feeling very anxious, said:

- Are you all really true men? How can you watch someone die without helping?

As soon as he finished speaking, Liu Heng, without a moment's hesitation, pulled the small boat down to the river and went along the current, about three or four miles away from the shore. Because of the high waves, Liu Heng's boat nearly capsized several times. Finally, he reached the woman and rescued her onto the shore.

In the following days, this woman gave birth to a baby boy. A month later, Liu Heng suddenly fell seriously ill, unable to walk or eat, suffering greatly. He instructed his wife and child to prepare for his funeral arrangements.

Seeing this, everyone felt pity for Lưu Hoành and blamed heaven and earth, saying:

“Why do good people meet with misfortune while those standing on the riverbank who did not save that woman are all living healthily? Heaven truly has no eyes!”

Lưu Hoành then sighed and said to everyone:

- Everyone, do not be quick to blame! On the very night I saved that woman, I had a dream. In that dream, I was extremely frightened.

In a moment of panic, I was brought before the entrance of the official's office. A kind demon led me in to meet an official who was opening a ledger. The official pointed at me and said:

- You have accumulated all kinds of evil deeds in your lifetime, and this year you were destined to die and be reborn as a pig. After five lifetimes as a pig, being slaughtered each time, you would only then have a chance to be reborn as a human. But fortunately, you just saved two lives, thereby generating great virtuous merit.

According to the regulations of the Underworld, you should have your lifespan extended by 24 years. But this extended 24-year lifespan will offset the evil deeds you have committed, so this year you still have to die; however, the lives of those reincarnated as pigs and slaughtered will be exempted.

Currently, your time of death has arrived. I fear that the world does not understand the truth and may doubt, saying that someone who has done great good still dies early. Therefore, I summon you here today to make it clear to you, so you can seize the time to tell others to understand. Your cause and effect in this life is considered concluded; in your next life, reborn as a human, strive to do good and accumulate virtue!

After I woke up, I felt that this dream was unfortunate, so I did not tell anyone early. Now that the time to die has arrived, I indeed suffer from a severe illness, so I believe in that dream!

Not long after, Lưu Hoành truly passed away...

From this story, it can be seen that the reward and punishment for those who do good or evil deeds is very clear, not at all obscure. The fate of a person, whether good or bad, always depends on that person's actions over many lifetimes.

One should not base their belief on certain events and think that Heaven has no eyes, that there is no Heavenly Dao. Cause and effect is not mistaken in the slightest; doing evil does not mean there will be no retribution, it just means the time has not yet come!

The profound law of cause and effect is difficult to know and understand, yet it is the most important rule, governing the entire life of every person and every sentient being. Being born as a human is already difficult, and to have enough wisdom to comprehend the deep law of cause and effect is truly extremely hard.

Congratulations to those who believe in and understand karma, fear doing evil, desire to do good, and cultivate themselves in the True Dharma. May everyone in the world be like that.

NĀM MÔ A – DI – ĐÀ PHẬT! PLEASE CONTINUE TO REPEATEDLY REMEMBER__()__

tieu_de: METHODS TO BREAK LOVE SPELLS, CURE DISEASES, AND OPEN WISDOM THROUGH MANTRAS.
tom_tat: The first method: Place a glass of water in front of the statue of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva holding it with both hands in front of the face; if not available, then fold your hands and place them on the table while reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, or the Six-Syllable Great Brightness Mantra.
noi_dung:
METHODS TO BREAK LOVE CHARMS, CURE ILLNESSES, AND OPEN WISDOM THROUGH MANTRAS.

Method one: Place a glass of water in front of the image of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, holding it with both hands in front of your face. If there is no image, then put your hands together on the table and recite the Great Compassion Mantra or the Six-Syllable Great Brightness Mantra, while also chanting the Bodhisattva's name (the more you recite, the more effective it is). Look at the glass of water while visualizing the Bodhisattva appearing in it, clearly imagining all the details from hands and feet to the face, the halo, until you can see it clearly. Then pour this water into another glass (to show respect) and reverently lift it with both hands to drink, while maintaining the visualization.This water is ambrosial water, drinking it you will be cured, it opens wisdom...

Second method: If you find visualizing in the first way too difficult, you can imagine Avalokiteshvara standing in front of you, or in front of His image, with a golden radiance shining from between His eyebrows onto the water you are consecrating, while simultaneously visualizing and reciting the Great Compassion Mantra (or the Six-Syllable Great Brightness, the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva). After seeing this, pour another cup of water and respectfully lift it to drink. While drinking, visualize that this water is the nectar of immortality; drinking it will cure illness and open wisdom...

➖ NOTE: Before visualization, choose a picture of Avalokiteshvara that you like the most, then look at it carefully, remember every detail in your mind, and then begin the visualization as clearly as possible.

Also, you should use a consecrated glass of water (this glass should not be drunk directly to show respect) and pour it into another glass before drinking. If it is impossible to find another glass of water in an urgent situation, you can use the same glass; you should not be overly rigid as long as you are sincere.

In addition, prolonged illness is mostly due to karma reaching its fruition or karmic creditors coming to collect debts. Therefore, besides empowering water with mantras to cure diseases, one must sincerely start by repenting for past sins, then repent for karmic obstacles (one can recite the Liang Huang Repentance Sutra), and repent to karmic creditors (according to the ritual here https://nhanqua.com.vn/http-nhanqua-com-vn-nghi-thuc-sam-hoi-oan-gia-trai-chu) in order to completely address the root cause of the illness. One should not harbor the arrogant mindset of "I already have this mantra, so even if there are karmic creditors, they cannot harm me!" and become complacent and self-satisfied, butOne must cultivate a mind of equal compassion and mercy towards them, because in countless past lives we have harmed them. Now that we know how to practice Buddhism, we need to repent and pray for their liberation (according to the ritual above). That is truly the moral path of someone practicing mantras, and a genuine Buddhist. Doing so will truly be in harmony with the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and they will certainly bless you. The empowerment method above applies to those who already know the mantra; if one does not know the mantra, one cannot visualize it! Besides breaking spells and healing, it also has the functions of creating protective boundaries, opening wisdom, and warding off demons... If you are ill, taking medicine while performing empowerment as described above will help you recover faster (if a monk is morally upright).Virtuous practice, when done with high skill, can even allow this method to cure the patient after drinking it, without the need to take any medicine at all! If affected by a curse, the empowerment as above will also break the curse and return it to the one who cast it.

However, it is important to have deep faith in the mantra and strictly observe the precepts (one of the precepts, if you have taken any precepts, you must strictly keep them: the Five Precepts, the Ten Wholesome Deeds, the Sāmaṇera precepts, the Bhiksu precepts, the Bodhisattva precepts, etc.). If there is even a single thought of doubt, such as whether drinking it will actually cure the illness, whether your prayers will be fulfilled, or if it doesn’t work, it will not succeed. You must trust that after drinking it, you will surely be cured, that your prayers will surely be answered; if they are not fulfilled, it is because your karma is still heavy and you need to practice more. Then, examine whether you have strictly kept the precepts, whether you have carried out the Ten Wholesome Deeds, and so on...

Just keep examining like that, diligently and persistently, then gradually the illness will go away, and whatever you wish will come true!

Those who recite mantras or chant Buddha's name but frequently experience sleep paralysis do so because they lack concentration, lack spiritual protection, or possibly because their living place has many wandering spirits, causing restless sleep or continuous dreams, sometimes even inappropriate dreams... Some people say that they have been reciting Buddha's name or mantras for years but their wisdom remains dull, and at night they often have disturbing dreams. For those with strong concentration, sleep is dreamless and very peaceful, memory is good, and they understand whatever they read in the scriptures...

Reciting Buddha's name and chanting mantras without focusing the mind, without sincerity and reverence, and allowing the mind to be full of distractions, then even reciting 1,000 or 10,000 times is the same. Therefore, when chanting, one must concentrate and be respectful. And one must practice regularly without missing any day, so that when the time comes to use it, it will be effective! Otherwise, if you do not practice normally, when you really need it, it will be very difficult to achieve a response. Moreover, if the mouth recites mantras while the body commits theft, sexual misconduct, killing, and the mouth tells lies... and one relies on the power of the mantra to erase all karma to freely commit evil, then chanting the mantra will not only be ineffective but will also anger the protecting deities, thus causing...Harming yourself, you really should be very careful about this!

➖ So does that mean only reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara, the Great Compassion Mantra, or the Six-Syllable Great Brightness Mantra can achieve the above? In fact, it is not only by reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara, the Great Compassion Mantra, or the Six-Syllable Great Brightness Mantra that one can achieve this; you can also recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and achieve the same results. In the Mahāyāna Mahāsaṃnipāta Kṣitigarbha Ten Wheels Sutra, it is said that whoever regularly recites the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, when encountering dangerous situations, will be rescued just as described in the Universal Gate Chapter by reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. You can also use the extermination mantraEstablish the vow through the true words or the heart mantra of Kṣitigarbha, then visualize Kṣitigarbha as in the two methods mentioned above. Or, if you have a connection with Medicine Buddha, you can recite the name of Medicine Buddha, or chant the Medicine Buddha mantra and do it in exactly the same way, the only difference being that you visualize the image of Medicine Buddha. This applies to any yidam or the mantra of any yidam you follow; as long as when reciting and visualizing, you do so with true sincerity and clearly see it, it is acceptable.

The method of empowering a mantra into a glass of water, besides breaking curses, healing illnesses, creating protective fences, ... you can also empower it daily for your relatives to drink in order to open their wisdom, eliminate karma that obstructs their practice, plant the seeds of connection to the Buddhist path for them, or if your garden or house has many harmful insects that you want to drive away without harming them, you can empower the mantra into water and then use a mist spray to spray it on the plants or on those creatures, making sure not to kill them by spraying too much water; gradually, they will leave. In addition, you also plant the seed of the Buddha in them... speaking of its effectsThere are still many other uses, here we only briefly talk about the uses of the mantra; if we were to cover them all, it would be endless.

With the wish that fellow Buddhists and believers across the country who have supported the An Sĩ Toàn Thư Page over the past time can remain steadfast on the path of practice, especially for lay practitioners at home, and also to create a means to assist everyone in seeking rebirth in the Western Pure Land smoothly and easily, ensuring a stable life in this world, eliminating karmic obstacles, and protecting the body and mind from being disturbed by spirits, ghosts, illusions, etc., the An Sĩ Toàn Thư Team has compiled this book to help readers have an additional resource as a companion on the path of practice toward liberation, ensuring rebirth in the Pure Land in this life! Wishing you diligence and effort!

(Excerpt from the Foreword in the book "Special Mantras" compiled by the Admins of the An Si Toan Thu group)

tieu_de: VENERABLE THICH GIAC KHANG - A MENDICANT MONK WHO PASSED AWAY AT 3:30 PM ON MARCH 30.
tom_tat: 🌼🌼🌼NAMO AMITABHA BUDDHA🌼🌼🌼 Venerable Giác Khang is the abbot at Ngọc Vân Monastery in Trà Vinh. He was trained as a monk following the lineage of Venerable Minh Đăng Quang. He is a very respected monk and observes the precepts very strictly.
noi_dung:
VENERABLE THÍCH GIÁC KHANG - THE MONK OF THE MENDICANT SCHOOL WHO ATTAINED BIRTH IN THE PURE LAND AT 3:30 PM ON MARCH 30.

🌼🌼🌼NAMO AMITABHA BUDDHA🌼🌼🌼

Monk Giac Khang is the abbot at Ngoc Van Monastery in Tra Vinh. He comes from a monastic lineage following Monk Minh Dang Quang. A highly respected monk, he upholds the monastic precepts very rigorously.

When he ordained, he made a vow: "If I have not attained Arhatship, I will not accept disciples."

The monk recounted that after decades of practicing meditation, he did not believe in the Pure Land teachings, even saying: "The Pure Land teachings are lies; there is no world with form and appearance." Later, he studied Yogācāra (Consciousness-Only School), and alas, he saw the Pure Land world clearly as if it were in the palm of his hand, with no need to debate believing or not believing anymore.

And the monk chose the path to the Western Pure Land for himself. Nevertheless, he still maintained traditional practice. He walked barefoot for alms, ate one meal a day before noon, accepted only one portion of food, and absolutely did not accept anything extra.

The monk does not lie on high beds, soft mattresses, sofas, or hammocks... The monk gives dharma talks outdoors, under the shade of a tree, and meditates once a day for about 8 hours.

When beginning to teach the Pure Land practice, the monk also encountered some difficulties because the disciples of the mendicant tradition did not accept it. So when giving dharma talks at temples of other sects, he taught in a different style, while at Pure Land temples, he taught about the Pure Land. The monk said that there were many times he wanted to retreat and pass away immediately, but seeing that the lay practitioners were too weak, he tried to stay to continue giving dharma talks.

I WOULD LIKE TO SHARE AGAIN THE PROCESS OF THE MASTER'S PASSING AS FOLLOWS:

1. The Master had known about his departure for a long time. Before passing away, the Master, along with close Buddhists, went to visit the land of the Buddha. His intention was to leave his body there, but the Buddhists wished him to return. The Master said he did not want any fuss or expensive arrangements, and it would be more convenient for him to go there. But the Buddhists earnestly requested the Master to return to Vietnam.

2. More than ten days before passing away, the Master arranged and entrusted tasks to his disciples regarding land, temples, and so on...

3. On the morning of March 30, the Master met with the Buddhist followers and gave many instructions. Then he asked what time it was; at that moment, it was past 10 a.m. The Master announced the time of rebirth before the assembly and said to the followers: "IF YOU LOVE ME, RESPECT ME, THEN YOU MUST RECITE Buddha's name with a single mind to be reborn in the presence of Amitabha Buddha, THAT IS TRUE LOVE AND RESPECT. NOT BEG ME TO STAY SO YOU CAN RELY ON ME AND NOT PRACTICE DILIGENTLY."

The Master also shared many other precious teachings.

4. The monk had been ill for many years, yet before passing away, He did not show any sign of pain or illness. The monk lay down, smiling, and departed very peacefully, as if going to sleep. And exactly at the time He had foretold - 3:30 PM on March 30, 2013.

5. Strange phenomena appeared three times in a row: lights and a halo in the sky, each lasting for more than an hour. The halo shone brightly over a corner of the sky, clouds gathered and changed colors... Ms. Thi Gia recounted that when the clouds in the sky changed colors, her clothes on the ground would also change color, sometimes yellow, sometimes green. The sun spun rapidly like a top, one could look directly at it without being dazzled, and it was bright red. During the midnight tea-offering ceremony, the halo also appeared very frequently.

6. When cremated, the Master left behind many relics, more than 60 large relics, over 100 medium-sized ones, and countless small ones; there were also relics of different colors: gold, green, white, red...

We respectfully invite those fellow practitioners with affinity to visit YouTube to watch the Dharma talks on the Pure Land Buddhist practice of mindfulness of Amitabha that the Master gave, which are clear and easy to understand to increase faith on the path back to the homeland - the Western Pure Land...

Namo Amitabha Buddha.

tieu_de: GOOD SPIRIT GUARDS THE ONE WHO MAINTAINS PRECEPTS.
tom_tat: (Excerpt from Báo Ứng Hiện Đời 4 - Quả Hồng) In today's society, natural and man-made disasters such as earthquakes, tsunamis, floods and fires, epidemics, wars, traffic accidents... always occur. What should we do to t
noi_dung:
THE GOOD SPIRIT WHO PROTECTS THOSE WHO KEEP THE PRECEPTS.

(Excerpt from "Report on Manifested Life 4 - Persimmon Fruit")

In today's society, natural and man-made disasters such as earthquakes, tsunamis, floods and fires, epidemics, wars, traffic accidents... constantly arise. How should we act to stay away from accidents? In the Sutra of Observing the Apex, the Buddha teaches:

If we take refuge in the Three Jewels, there will be 36 guardian deities protecting us. Those who observe the Five Precepts will have five guardian deities for each precept, totaling 25 deities. These deities also have countless attendants, all of whom support practitioners.

The Buddhist Scripture on the Four Heavenly Kings also records the same.

Aunt Tran is a devout Buddhist, 72 years old this year, with a rosy, radiant face, and a vigorous spirit. Everyone who meets her praises her for being both youthful and beautiful. It is impossible to guess that she is a woman over 70.

But about 10 years ago, Aunt Trần's spirit was very different from now. At that time, she was a person whose whole body was in pain, suffering from many internal diseases, taking medicine all year round because of old age and frailty.

Every time she went to the hospital, my aunt was very worried, afraid that the check-up would reveal yet another illness, and inwardly she was always afraid of death. Every day she lived in anxious suspense. Until one day, she went to the temple to worship Buddha and requested a book called "Karma Revealed in This Life." When she got home and read it, she suddenly had a great enlightenment: it turns out that in this world, there is Buddhist teaching, a wonderful medicine that can cure many ailments. Not only does it skillfully heal the body and mind, but it also benefits all sentient beings.

From then on, Aunt Trần began studying Buddhism, eating vegetarian, repenting for past karma, chanting, making offerings, printing sutras, and releasing animals... Practicing in this way for many years, her health gradually improved. By the second year of following the Buddhist path, something unexpected happened.

That afternoon, she was taking a walk in the park with her niece. Just as they reached a turn, suddenly a person riding a bicycle appeared from behind and collided directly with Aunt Trần. The strange thing was that after hitting her, the bike bounced back, shot out several meters, and with a loud 'BANG,' both the bike and the person caused the accident to fall straight into the lake on the left side opposite them.

At that moment, the niece was startled and quickly asked:

- Oh my! Aunt, are you okay? That was a pretty hard hit!

- No, I’m fine! - Aunt Trần smiled and replied.

- How can that be? I clearly saw the car hit you so hard that it threw you straight into the pond! Let me take you to the hospital for a check-up!

- I’m fine! No need to do that.

Just as the two of them were talking, the person who had fallen into the pond while riding his bike managed to crawl to the shore, and he rushed forward in a fury. Even from a distance, he hastily pointed at Aunt Tran and shouted:

- That old hag, how dare she crash into your 'dad's' bike!?

- Oh my god! This man is truly arrogant! Clearly, he was the one who hit my aunt and then 'flew' straight into the pond, everyone here saw it!

The crowd gathered around also started clamoring, scolding the cyclist. He was shouted at until he was speechless and had no choice but to sneak over to the pond to pull out his bike.

Everyone hurriedly advised Aunt Trần:

-You must go to the hospital for a check-up immediately. We saw the car hit you very hard; just get examined to be safe, to prevent any risks...

So Aunt Trần went to the hospital for a check-up, and the result was that, except for a slight injury on her back, everything else was normal, with no issues at all. Therefore, the nephew beside her felt very strange.

After that, Aunt Trần recounted to me (that is, Quả Hồng):

-At the moment of being hit by the bicycle, aunt felt as if there was a metal plate protecting her back, thanks to which she didn't feel pain and didn't even have time to realize what had happened.

I said:

-Thanks to your strict observance of precepts and your diligent practice of the Dharma, Bodhisattva Amitabha came to help you resolve the accident and manifested the metal plate to stop the bicycle, preventing you from getting hurt...

The power of the Dharma is truly unimaginable; those who strictly uphold the precepts, in moments of danger, will bear less than deserved and turn calamities into blessings.

Further explanation: Why do some people diligently practice Buddhism yet still encounter accidents? It is because before studying Buddhism, in this life, they have already created negative karma through killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, etc., and even the negative karma accumulated from beginningless past lives has now ripened, resulting in immediate consequences. (When the karmic results have fully ripened, even the guardian deities cannot prevent them)

Once one practices Buddhism, if one knows how to sincerely repent with a united heart, abandon evil and follow good, never commit wrongdoings again, use keeping precepts as the foundation, and diligently cultivate, one can transform misfortunes or reduce severe karmic consequences... When receiving retribution or calamities, one must understand that it is the resolution of past karma. In the Diamond Sutra, there is a passage: “Those virtuous men and faithful women who uphold and recite this sutra, if they are despised by others, it is due to the karma of their past lives that deserved to fall into the evil path, and through being despised in this life, the karma of their past life will surely be eradicated...”
