tieu_de: PLEASE DO NOT EAT FROG MEAT
tom_tat: There was one time I went to the market to buy release animals, when I arrived I saw people killing frogs... the frogs had their heads cut off and their skin completely removed. Even though their heads were cut off and their skin peeled, the frogs were still folding their two hands in a gesture of respect - their muscles twitching, all
noi_dung:
PLEASE DO NOT EAT FROG MEAT

Once, I went to the market to buy animals for release. When I arrived, I saw people already killing frogs… their heads had been cut off and their skins completely removed. Even after being decapitated and skinned, the frogs still clasped their two hands together in a gesture, their muscles twitching, and their whole bodies continued to move on the tray as if trying to regain life 😥

That image made my heart ache. I hurriedly bought all the remaining frogs and, unable to control my emotions, ran to a spot to cry. Tears kept falling, sorrowful for the suffering of sentient beings 😥

When a frog is killed by humans, it must endure the sufferings of eight small hells:

1. At the moment the frog is killed, first the head is chopped off: The first hell "chopping the head"

2. After chopping, the frog is immediately skinned: The second hell "skinning"

3. Next, the four legs are cut off: The third hell "cutting the legs"

4. Then the intestines are gutted and the liver removed: The fourth hell "gutting"

5. Finished, put into the pot and cook on high heat "Fifth Hell," oil boiling "

6. Season the pot: Sixth Hell "just add salt"

7. Put in the mouth and chew thoroughly: Seventh Hell "crushed stone"

8. Swallow into the intestines along with impurities: Eighth Hell "filth"

PLEASE DO NOT EAT FROG MEAT 🙏🙏🙏

Source: Hương Nguyễn

tieu_de: PRAYING FOR WEALTH AND PROSPERITY
tom_tat: (Collection of Tales of Servant to Bodhisattva Dizang S1) During the Song Dynasty, in Tran Luu district, there was a young poor maiden who worked for others to make a living, leading a hard life. She then adopted vegetarianism and recited the Holy Name of Di
noi_dung:
PRAYING FOR BLESSINGS TO BE WEALTHY AND PROSPEROUS

(Collection of Stories About Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva S1)

During the Song Dynasty, in Tran Luu district, there was a young poor girl who worked as a hired help to make a living, leading a hard life. She then ate vegetarian food, chanted the holy name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, and prayed to Him to bestow wealth and honor. Considering her heavy past karma, she did not know if she could achieve her wish.

On the leap day of February 24, in the fifth year of Khai Bảo, the young lady saw ants crawling all over the house and did not dare to enter for fear of stepping on them. Then she saw the ants gradually turn yellow, which frightened her. The neighbors, seeing this, also thought it strange. After a whole day and night, she finally entered the house and saw that the ants had disappeared, and the mat was full of gold, just enough to make three dâu. The young woman sold it and became wealthy. Afterwards, her faith in the Bodhisattva strengthened, and she renovated the house into a temple, worshipping and offering there. Later, a widowed district chief married the young woman as his wife and pampered her in every way.

Translated by Dịch Lớn Chẳng Lo

During the Tang Dynasty, in Lu Chau, there was an imperial censor named Khang Cu Thong, who was a person of utmost sincerity. For many years, he had been devoted to worshipping the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and was very earnest in painting images of the Bodhisattva. He was always respectful. He had not neglected any of the images, which radiated light clearly—all due to this faith. By chance, two mounted officers came to chase him, and he was very frightened. The two officers suddenly dismounted and said: “We were mistaken! Kṣitigarbha’s altar is at fault, but it is hard to assign blame,” and after saying this, they disappeared. Upon waking, he became even more sincere.

During the first year of the Guangyuan era in the reign of Emperor Hytong, a plague broke out in the country, demons ran rampant, and people died in heaps. He dreamed of hundreds of thousands of demons passing by his house, saying: "This house is the seventh chamber of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, we are your servants, be careful not to enter this house." Because of this, the entire family was spared from disaster. In the Zhonghua year, he had to travel far and got lost in a snowfield, hastily praying to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. Suddenly, a warbler flew down into the snowfield; finding it strange, he chased it and arrived at the main road. When he reached Guangqi, he fell ill and sincerely prayed hoping to recover. He dreamed that the Master said: "You killed the bluebird"of ours, a sin worthy of going to hell. Now must pay for that karma, endure suffering for two days before being reborn in the Pure Land.” After hearing this, he joyfully paid respects, was immediately cured of his illness, and passed away after two days.

tieu_de: Change House Into Temple
tom_tat: (Collection of Miracles of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva S2) During the Tang Dynasty in Jianzhou, Jinshui County, there was a Gentleman Officer surnamed Dang, who had long been a devout follower of Buddhism. One day, he saw a staff with the image of a deity carved on the top.
noi_dung:
Turning the House into a Temple

(Collection of Miraculous Responses of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva S2)

During the Tang Dynasty in Jianzhou, Jingshui County, there was a Deputy Minister surnamed Deng, who had long been devoted to Buddhism. One day, he saw a staff with a carved image of a Master on its top, so he took it home and placed it against the wall. Two or three years later, he suddenly fell ill and died, but his chest was still warm, so his family, though suspicious, had not yet laid him out. The next night, he regained consciousness, crying with tears streaming down, and recounted: “When I had just died, two people rode horses and led me to the gate of a large city. In the main hall, I saw many people being chained. The King was angry and was about to question me. At that moment, a monk with an ugly appearance entered the hall. The King quicklyHe respectfully stood up, clasped his hands and knelt, saying: “Great Sage, why have you come here?” The monk said: “This court attendant is my subordinate; Your Majesty should pardon him.” The king said: “Now the decision has been made, his fate is sealed, his allotted life is finished, it is difficult to forgive.” The monk said: “In the past, I was in the Hall of Good Dharma in the 33rd heaven, and the Buddha told me that I could save those with destined sins. All along, moreover, this court attendant has not committed a grievous sin, so why would I not be able to save him?” The king said: “The Great Vow of the Great Sage is as steadfast and immovable as a diamond mountain; I shall follow the instructions and pardon him to return to the human world.”

The monk was very happy to take my hand and lead me to the path of life. As I was about to leave, I asked, "You who saved me are my great benefactor, may I know your dharma name to remember your kindness?" The monk replied, "I am Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Long ago, Thị Lang found a staff along the road with my image carved on it. Although he did not understand it at the time, he brought it home and placed it on the wall. For the joy of children, he carved the image on the top of the staff. He had only carved halfway, so the top of the staff was still incomplete and looked ugly. Thị Lang, do you still remember?" After saying this, he disappeared.

Thi Lang woke up and saw that the staff planted on the wall had only its top remaining, so he hired a craftsman to carve a five-inch-tall figure out of sandalwood. The statue often emitted light that illuminated the entire room. Thi Lang then carved an even larger statue, turned his house into a temple called Dia Tang Dai, and enshrined the smaller statue inside for devout men and women from near and far to admire.

Thanks to Bodhisattva Kshitigarbha, escaping the tiger's attack

During the Tang Dynasty, in Hua Prefecture, Huệ Nhựt Monastery had a master named Phap Thuong. At the age of thirty-seven, he became a monk. When he was still at home, he often went hunting. One day, he saw a light shining in the bushes, which made him curious, so he dismounted and went to see, only to find a rotted piece of wood more than a foot long, which he brought home. Later, while hunting again, he saw that piece of wood glowing, which surprised him, so he picked up the piece of wood to place it on a branch. On the way back, he encountered a tiger, so he spurred his horse to chase. The bowstring broke, leaving him weaponless. The tiger, startled, ran away, and in fright, he fell off the horse. He thought to himself that he would surely be caught by the tiger and could not avoid it. At that moment of panicI saw a Master with an ugly appearance come to drive away the Tiger. I asked the Master who he was. He said: 'I am Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva; that rotten log in that bush is my body. In the past, your great grandfather once used this tree to build a temple and create my statue. Now the temple has deteriorated, and my statue has also decayed. Only the core of the tree remains, and you see my light, so I came to save you.'

After waking up, I only heard the sound of horses neighing and no longer saw the tiger, feeling extremely regretful. I then built a Pure Land Temple in the place that emitted light, carved a statue of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha from a decayed log, and continued to offer incense and respect, which is called Tue Nhat Temple. On February 24, at the age of 78, Phap Thuong said to his friends: "Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha came to my house and said: 'You were present at the Dharma assembly of Từ Thị Buddha preaching three times. In the second preaching, you were an enlightened one, and today, after giving up your mortal life, you will be born in the Deva Realm.'" I reported to the Great Master: 'In the heavens, there are the realms of the five desires, very pleasurable, and without Bodhi, it is difficult to encounter the Buddha. Now...“I wish to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, the world of Bliss.” The Bodhisattva replied: “According to your wish, if you want to be reborn in the Pure Land, you must recite Amitabha Buddha day and night, focusing your mind on recitation to be reborn there.” With the Bodhisattva's blessing, since yesterday until now, my Dharma Master has been focusing on reciting Amitabha Buddha. Now, having attained rebirth, he spoke and then clasped his hands toward the West and passed away.

tieu_de: DON'T BE AFRAID OF LOSING, LOSING IS A BLESSING.
tom_tat: Whether in favorable or adverse circumstances, with good or bad conditions, one should not be swayed, maintaining one’s own 'purity, equanimity, and awareness,' always keeping a heart of gratitude and a heart of repayment, that is correct. Do not
noi_dung:
DON'T BE AFRAID OF LOSING, LOSING IS A BLESSING.

Regardless of whether in favorable or adverse circumstances, good or bad causes and conditions, one should not be disturbed, but instead maintain one’s own "purity, equanimity, and enlightenment," and forever keep a heart of gratitude and a heart of repaying kindness. That is correct. Do not fear being at a disadvantage. Being at a disadvantage is a blessing; do not seize the convenience of others. Seizing convenience brings harm, is a disaster, and knowing that being at a disadvantage is a blessing, as the ancient sages and immortals said, is not wrong!

All those who slander, envy, insult, and harm me, I thank them. Why? They all come to test me to see whether I truly study Buddhism or pretend to. If we have resentment toward such adverse circumstances and evil people, it proves that our study of Buddhism has been in vain! What the Buddha taught, we have completely forgotten!

You see Śākyamuni Buddha, while practicing virtue and the Perfection of Patience, encountered King Kaṇḍu, was tortured and sentenced to death, yet the Bodhisattva harbored not a trace of resentment, and thus perfected the Perfection of Patience. If He had not faced that situation, He would not have yet fully realized the Perfection of Patience. In that final, great test, He successfully endured, overcame it, held no grudge against King Kaṇḍu, and even expressed gratitude to the king. As He was about to die, He told King Kaṇḍu: "In the future, when I become a Buddha, I will save you first." That is repaying kindness; this is truly what it means to be a disciple of the Buddha, and we should learn from this. Truly understanding and learning, one neither abides in non-action nor in action.

(Old Master Jingkong)

How to eliminate karmic obstacles? Recite Amitabha Buddha and the karmic obstacles will be eliminated!

Amitabha Buddha _()_

Source Facebook: Adi da Phat

tieu_de: Save Sentient Beings from Hell
tom_tat: (Collection of miraculous stories about Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, part 3) Author: Thùy Hương – member of the group 'Cause and Effect - Reincarnation'
noi_dung:
Save Living Beings from Hell

(Collection of miraculous stories about Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, part 3)

Author: Thùy Hương – a member of the group ‘Cause and Effect - Reincarnation’

Dear fellow practitioners, I am very grateful because after sharing my personal repentance stories (the articles ‘Repenting to the Snail’, ‘Repenting to the Pig’), many friends sincerely joined me in repenting for the mistakes they have caused

Today, on the occasion of the holy day of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, July 30th, I would like to offer the community another story of miraculous response when reciting the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, something I myself never thought I could accomplish. As mentioned in the previous two articles, I usually recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra during my free time throughout the day. In the early years when I first began reciting the sutra, one evening, as usual, I was deeply focused on the sutra when I was suddenly startled by a very loud 'clang, clank' sound. Listening carefully, it was clearly the sound of chains clashing together. Because I knew my practice was still weak, I always reminded myself that I had toAware of the scenes happening around me, I ignored them and continued to focus on the unfinished sutra. But the 'clinking' sound still echoed in my ears, this time accompanied by a noise like fingernails scratching the ground. At this moment, I felt extremely annoyed with myself for not focusing on reciting the sutra and instead letting my mind wander, making myself uneasy.

To calm my mind, I immediately closed my eyes, took a deep breath, and after a while, I heard a very loud scream: "Help me, please help me.."

I curiously looked around and was horrified. I saw two people that folk often call "ox-head, horse-face," very tall. They were truly terrifyingly large; in the universe, there really are beings different from us. They were both wearing a hard armor outside, like iron, with rough but solid skin, their feet in animal leather shoes, walking slightly hunched because of their half-human, half-animal form, each holding a long chain that dragged on the ground. So that was where the clinking sound came from.

The two of them were dragging a woman by her legs; she was far too small for the two jailers, her entire body probably only reaching their knees. The woman was wearing a white shirt, bleeding heavily, her hair soaked with sweat. Because she was being dragged face down by the 'ox-headed, horse-faced' figures, she tried her best to press her ten fingers into the ground, producing a horrifying sound. In fact, she did not understand that she was being taken to hell, she was just terrified of the two large figures, human in body but beast-faced.

It seemed that realizing I was looking in that direction, she shouted even louder: "Help me, please help me..., please save me..."

Originally just an inexperienced lay practitioner, I could only stare, not knowing what to do. I was scared, truly scared that one day I might also be dragged like her. What should I do, what must I do?

While feeling panicked, suddenly the two of them turned their heads back. Oh Buddha! I just wanted to faint to avoid seeing this scene. They bared their teeth, and just looking at them made my limbs go weak; to be honest, at that moment I was so scared that I thought if I got bitten even once, my body would be split in two. Not knowing what to do, I just sat there as if planted to the ground, watching her being dragged further and further away… Then, suddenly she screamed very loudly: "Recite Buddha's name, recite Buddha’s name for me." Instinctively, I immediately hurried to recite Buddha's name: "Namo Amitabha Buddha, Namo Great Vow Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva…" I recited continuously, sitting upright with my legs crossed neatly. Both hands clasped in front of my chest. At this point, the entireMy body and mind wholeheartedly only want to save her.

Please constantly recite the Buddha's name, and recite it anytime, anywhere, so as to cultivate the habit into your subconscious, because if you have not often recited the Buddha's name before, during critical moments you will not be able to utter the prayer. I recited a few phrases, and a very strange thing happened: the two 'ox-headed, horse-faced' beings suddenly stopped. They seemed surprised that even in such a desperate moment, that girl still knew to ask me to recite the Buddha's name. I heard a 'thud' as they let her legs down and stopped pulling. Suddenly, everything sank back into emptiness. I remained sitting there, but it was utterly silent.

As if waking from a trance, I hurriedly continued the interrupted sutra recital. This time, besides repenting to the grievances and debts to others, I also dedicated the merit and resolved to do some good deeds, hoping she could escape from hell. Normally, every time I recite the sutra, it only takes about half an hour (completing one-third of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra). But that day, from the moment I began the sutra, observing that event and continuing the recitation took a full 3 hours. Perhaps, the process of my observation of the incident I just described took about 2 hours.

Normally, I am also very lazy in reciting sutras. But after seeing that scene, I became very diligent in daily recitation. In fact, I wanted to save that girl more than to repent for myself because I thought that if I was not diligent and sincere in saving her, she would forever descend into hell, and the chance to return to a human life would be very difficult. So I always took advantage of my free time during the day to recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, sometimes reciting an entire volume three times a day. Thinking back, I feel really ashamed because I was so inadequate and not diligent at all. Day after day, I regularly dedicated the merit to her. In my heart, I silently hoped that even though she fell into hell, one day she would still be able to returnto atone. I never dared to think that I would have the chance to meet that girl again.

About half a year later, one night, after finishing chanting, I suddenly felt sleepy. Thinking that working during the day and practicing diligently at night had made my body tired, I went to bed. In a drowsy state, I saw a woman wearing a long dress that covered her body, in a greenish-white color, and she seemed to be smiling at me. Oh, this was the woman I had seen being dragged away by the 'buffalo-head-horse-face' before, but now she looked very peaceful, not frightened like she had been that time.

I tried to raise my eyes, to get up, but I could not. The distance she stood from me was very close, and for some reason, when I looked at her, a feeling of love, an indescribable closeness, welled up in my heart.

She looked at me with a gentle smile, nodding slightly as if to send her thanks. Then that image gradually faded into nothingness. I don’t have to say it; you can surely guess that the girl had been freed from the gate of hell, right, esteemed virtuous ones? I felt the same way; at that moment I was very happy, at least I had saved a sentient being from hell. Later, upon further reflection, I understood one thing. If I don't diligently practice, I too will be pulled in the same way, with no exceptions.

Because my reverence for Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is very deep, I naturally receive good responses myself. I sincerely hope that all of you will join me in striving to reform our body and mind, do good deeds, and avoid evil. Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva saves all beings, both living and deceased, for us every day. As long as we have a moment of thought and take refuge in Him, no matter how great the difficulties, even if the fires of hell burn our bodies, He will provide support to help us return to the shore of enlightenment. Once again, I wish to recite, 'Namo Da Yuan Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva!!!'. I vow to be His disciple for countless lifetimes, without ever turning away.

tieu_de: AS YOU SOW, SO SHALL YOU REAP (Cause and Effect, Karma, Symptoms of Untreatable Dizziness, Ways to Eliminate Rats and Insects)
tom_tat: My neighbor is Mr. Truong, who likes to practice Qigong and also uses Qigong to treat people. But he cannot cure others, and he himself is also plagued by illness. He has been dizzy for 3-4 years.
noi_dung:
AS YOU SOW, SO SHALL YOU REAP (Karmic Retribution, Treating Incurable Dizziness, Methods to Eliminate Rats and Insects)

My neighbor is Mr. Truong, who likes practicing Qigong and also uses Qigong to heal people. However, he could not cure others and he himself was tormented by a disease. He has been dizzy for 3-4 years. No matter what medicine or therapy he tried, it didn’t work.

He said:

– My head feels dizzy as if I just drank two bottles of wine!

Due to a fortunate encounter, he met Venerable Thich Dieu Phap and begged him to use Qigong to treat his illness.

The master smiled and said:

– I cannot use qi Gong to cure illness; every person who falls ill has a cause. I can clearly explain the reason why you feel dizzy. Whether the illness goes away or not depends on you. This is also the principle that the Buddha taught: "Fate is established by oneself." – For example, if you act wrongly out of ignorance, causing suffering and distress for yourself and others. If you encounter a virtuous teacher who explains and points out the cause, once you clearly understand and recognize your mistake, and make an effort to correct it, then suffering and distress will disappear. Because the Dharma is not meant for those who are superstitious about the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, or any eminent monk.but so that each person can attain wisdom. Transform your own destiny by yourself!

Mr. Truong thought for a moment and then nodded his head.

The monk continued:

– You are dizzy because 3-4 years ago you once harmed a nest of small mice. Is that true?

Mr. Truong recalled and said:

– Yes, there is something. Master! You truly possess great supernatural powers! About three years ago, one day I entered the storage room and discovered a nest of newborn mice, about 6-7 of them. I’m very timid and didn’t know how to kill them, so I put them in a cage and shook it as hard as I could. After shaking for a long time, I thought they were dead and threw them into the trash. Oh! Could such a thing be related to my dizziness?

– That’s right, the nest of mice wasn’t killed by your shaking; they were only made dizzy by you. That’s karma. This is the reason why you feel dizzy.

Mantra Truong mumbled to himself:

– You are absolutely right. Ever since then, I started feeling dizzy. Luckily, the rats are still alive; if they had died, I don't even know how severe the consequences I would have faced.

– That's correct, taking life shortens one's lifespan; otherwise, even in this life, one would encounter accidents and misfortunes. The reason animals can be killed is because in their past lives they once sowed the seeds of taking life, so in this life they experience the corresponding retribution.

As for us, in this life, killing them means we are borrowing lives, and thus karma circulates, injustice is repaid with injustice, never ending. Therefore, we ordinary people continue to reincarnate in the six realms with no day of escape. Only by understanding the Buddha's teachings, deeply trusting karma, ceasing evil and doing good, can one be freed from the sea of suffering in birth and death. So, from now on, do you still wish to kill?

Mantra Truong, sitting there, was terrified and bewildered. Hearing the monk’s question, he hurriedly replied:

– From now on, I will never dare to kill again.

After saying this, he happily reported:

– Master Bach, my head suddenly feels clear, not dizzy at all.

Everyone around laughed.

Mantra Truong asked further:

– But, rats are harmful, eating crops, gnawing on household items, and even spreading plague… if we don’t kill them, what if they reproduce and spread in the future?

– The entirety of the cosmos, from the vast universe to the tiniest speck, including all types of living beings… all have their own laws of operation and periods of existence. If humans have “birth, aging, sickness, death,” then things have “formation, duration, destruction, emptiness”… whether mountains, rivers, seas, air, flowers, grass, or dewdrops… As long as something “forms, it will decay!” However, the process of decay or this “cycle of life and death” has its own rules! If we disregard these laws and recklessly destroy according to our theories and preferences, we will naturally bring upon ourselves unimaginable evil consequences!

For example, if we, for immediate benefits, allow deforestation and blasting of rocks, causing forests to be destroyed, mountains to collapse, and animals in the forest to be harmed… all these thoughtless actions of ours will lead to the earth being flooded, climate change, and floods occurring… Don't you see that the number of trees being cut down and animals hunted and killed is so extensive that some become extinct or disappear. Even rats have natural enemies such as snakes, cats, hawks, eagles, owls, etc… It is possible that these natural enemies are also killed by humans for meat or have their skins used for clothing and jewelry. Hence, there is a saying: “Natural disasters are mainly due tohuman depiction formation”

The Venerable Master paused for a moment and then said:

– I will show you a method that can eliminate the rat problem, would you like to try it out?

Everyone looked intently at the Venerable Master, and He smiled as He explained:

– First, you must understand that mice are also living beings with feelings; they are born from mothers and are nurtured. They are similar to buffaloes, horses, cats, and dogs, and some can even understand human speech. Once you clearly understand the principle of not killing, you can daily prepare leftover food for them, place it where mice usually appear, and quietly say: 'In the past, I did not understand the Dharma, so I killed many mice. Now that I understand the principle, from now on I will definitely not kill any living being. I will chant sutras to pray for the mice I have killed. I hope the mice will not damage items in people's homes'... As long as you are sincere and earnestDoing so, you will definitely see results. Even one day, the mice will move their nest and leave.

The master's talk caused our eyes and ears to feel renewed. Afterwards, this method was successively tested, with very good results. Even someone at home who had many ants applied this method and said it was very effective.

Don't believe it? Then try experimenting yourself!

tieu_de: At the end of the dynasty, people who want to practice the Pure Land school of Buddhism should first take refuge and pay respects to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.
tom_tat: Master Hoằng Nhất, this time I meet you all here in Vĩnh Xuân because there are many extraordinary affinities. Last summer, layperson Vương Mộng Tinh sent a letter, and before that I had also promised some laypersons, ...
noi_dung:
IN THE LATE PERIOD, THE FRENCH WANT TO PRACTICE THE PURE LAND SCHOOL FIRST, SO THEY TAKE REFUGE AND WORSHIP BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA

Master Hoằng Nhất

This time I meet with all of you here in Vinh Xuan, due to many profound and rare causes. Last summer, layperson Vuong Mong Tinh sent a letter, and before that, I had also promised some laypeople, such as Lam Tu Kien… that the Pho Te pagoda would host sutra lectures. I came once at the end of autumn to give a three-day lecture on the main idea of the Diamond Sutra; by July I closed my room to cultivate meditation and did not go down the mountain anymore. Yesterday, layperson Mong Tinh along with several others came up the mountain to pay respects; it rained, so they stayed at the pagoda overnight. This morning, exactly on the Sacred Birthday of Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha, taking advantage of this rare cause, I will briefly outline the key point: 'Those practicing Pure Land should recite the sutras.'"Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vow", to commemorate His Birthday.

The practice method for those who follow the Pure Land Dharma is primarily based on the three sutras that speak about the Pure Land. I think that, in addition to these three sutras, it is advisable for fellow practitioners to also recite the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Original Vows Sutra as an auxiliary practice. Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha has a particularly profound connection with sentient beings in this world, and the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Original Vows Sutra is uniquely suited to people of all capacities and social classes, so I dare to recommend that fellow practitioners also recite this sutra. Now I will only briefly mention it, hoping that you all can make an enlightened choice:

First, since ancient times, Bodhisattva Dizang has had an extremely profound connection with the Pure Land. For example, the 8th Patriarch, Master Lian Chi, wrote the preface for the Sutra of Bodhisattva Dizang's Original Vows, praising and encouraging its transmission. The 9th Patriarch, Master Ngau Yik, devoted his entire life to serving Bodhisattva Dizang, praising and propagating His boundless merits. The master stayed on Mount Jiuhua for a long time, calling himself a "disciple of the Bodhisattva," practicing repentance rites according to the Dizang Repentance Ritual, regularly reciting the true mantra of Dizang, praying for the elimination of karma obstacles and rebirth in the Pure Land. Likewise, the contemporary polar star of the Pure Land school—Master Yin Guang—extensively propagated the Sutra of Dizang.The Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Fundamental Vows, the master printed tens of thousands of copies to help people who practice pure conduct earnestly read and recite them, and follow the teachings. Now, based on the mind and conduct of past patriarchs, I encourage all fellow practitioners to recite the Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Fundamental Vows more and to practice the methods of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. By combining many excellent causes and conditions, achieving the fruition of the Way is only a matter of time.

Secondly, the Kṣitigarbha practice focuses on three main sutras, which are: the Sutra of the Original Vows of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, the Ten Wheels Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, and the Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Observing the Recompense of Good and Evil Deeds. The Sutra of the Original Vows of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva does not clearly explain the meaning of rebirth in the Pure Land, but the other two sutras do mention it. The Ten Wheels Sutra states: “Rebirth in the Buddha’s land, together with the teachers.” The Observing Sutra states: “Whoever wishes to be reborn in the Pure Land should be single-minded and undistracted, focusing on reciting the sacred name of that Buddha (Amitābha); whoever practices this will certainly be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.” Therefore, the ninth patriarch of the Lotus Sect, Master Ngẫu Ích,Every time performing rituals to venerate Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and reciting repentance, one makes the vow: 'I vow that when leaving this body, I will be reborn before the Buddha, behold Amitabha Buddha and other Buddhas, receive their empowerment, and then return to the human world to save all sentient beings, together being born in the Land of Bliss.' From this, it can be seen that the Kṣitigarbha practice has a very close relationship with the Pure Land practice. So why not practice both simultaneously and integrate them together?

Thirdly, in the Sutra on Contemplation of Infinite Life, practicing the three merits is regarded as the fundamental cause for pure karma. The first merit among the three is "filial piety towards one's parents." In the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra of Original Vows, there are many past life causes in which Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha showed filial devotion to his parents. This is why the ancient sages revered the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra of Original Vows as the "Sutra of Filial Piety in Buddhism," with very practical benefits. Generally, all virtuous friends, and in particular, family members, should wholeheartedly recite the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra of Original Vows, to assist in the spirit of filial piety advocated by the Sutra on Contemplation of Infinite Life. By practicing both, one upholds the way of filial piety and repays kindness.deep gratitude, while also cultivating superior merit.

Fourth, the contemporary Pure Land master - Yin Guang - taught that for those who recite the Buddha's holy name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, they must first deeply believe in cause and effect, avoid doing evil deeds, diligently do good deeds, and finally he said: "Rely on the compassionate power of the benevolent father Amitabha, and one can be reborn while still burdened with karmic obstacles." The Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Original Vow Sutra also speaks extensively and very clearly about cause and effect, explaining it thoroughly. Virtuous friends should frequently read and recite the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Original Vow Sutra, practice accordingly, and prepare pure karmic provisions. Those who do not deeply believe in cause and effect will certainly not pay attention to the practical aspects of ethics and morality.Virtue. This person should not expect to be reborn in the Pure Land, because the three evil paths are already waiting. I sincerely think that everyone should deeply believe in cause and effect, constantly reflect, and review the things they do every day. Sincerely repent, strive to renew oneself. Then practice the Five Moral Principles, the Ten Virtuous Deeds…, to support the practice of Buddha recitation and contribute to the karmic store for rebirth.

Fifth, a practitioner of the Pure Land method, if they do not have the ability to let go of all pleasure and suffering, whether favorable or unfavorable, will not be able to perceive the realm of liberation. If one has enough capability to rely on suffering to eliminate self-view (one of the five views), and use adverse conditions to firm up one's vow for the Pure Land, then the superior realm will appear right before their eyes. However, truly achieving this is very rare—among tens of thousands, only one or two can do it. This is because most of us are still in the position of ordinary beings; although we know to cultivate purity according to our basic capacities and efforts, if we have not yet reached a level of clearly understanding the body, mind, and the external world, it is not sufficient.the ability to disregard eating, clothing, living conditions…; the mind is not yet calm in the face of disasters such as natural calamities, fire, war, famine…; this harsh and difficult circumstance is the greatest obstacle for practitioners in general and for those practicing pure conduct in particular. Now, if one can return to rely on and venerate Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, there will no longer be concern about these matters. According to the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Original Vows, the Bodhisattva has the ability to ensure that sentient beings have sufficient clothing and food, remain free from illness, have peaceful homes, have all their wishes fulfilled, enjoy longevity, be accompanied by divine protection in and out, and be free from all calamities. The ancients said: 'Body at peace, path grows.'This is exactly this idea. Therefore, I advise all fellow friends to follow the essential teachings of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.

The above is a summary of the general meaning of reciting the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Original Vow Sutra. Although the meaning may not be fully clear, this general outline is relatively complete. I hope everyone can understand this point and encourage people to wholeheartedly recite the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Original Vow Sutra together, in order to attain boundless benefits.

tieu_de: ANNIVERSARY OF THE CELEBRATION DAY OF VENERABLE LUU LY QUANG VUONG BUDDHA  April 28 LUNAR CALENDAR
tom_tat: The Eastern religious leader makes twelve vows to propagate
noi_dung:
ANNIVERSARY OF THE DAY OF VENERATION OF BUDDHA LUU LY QUANG VUONG, 28TH DAY OF THE 4TH LUNAR MONTH

The Eastern spiritual master

Twelve vows to propagate widely

To save all beings from suffering

To expound the true Dharma

Forty-nine days of incense lamps,

Dignified throughout the temple,

Chanting the name and bowing respectfully

Eliminate calamities, attain long life.

All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas manifest in the world out of compassion to save sentient beings who are immersed in the sea of suffering and the cycle of birth and death. Because sentient beings are countless and limitless, Buddhas also manifest in countless forms, constructing their lands and making great vows according to the karma and dispositions of sentient beings to teach, guiding them to escape from affliction and suffering, and to have a life of peace and freedom. Medicine Buddha is one among countless Buddhas, each with their own realm and vows.

The Medicine Master Buddha is called in Sanskrit: Bhaisajya-guru Vaidurya-prabharajyah, fully named the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light King Tathagata, and abbreviated as Medicine Master Buddha. According to the Sutra of the Original Vows of the Medicine Master Tathagata: to the east, about 10 countless Buddhas' degrees away from the world of Saha, there is a Buddha land called Pure Lapis Lazuli, and the name of that Buddha is Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light Tathagata.

Why is it called the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light Tathagata? According to the Sutra of the Medicine Master Tathagata's Original Vows and Meritorious Deeds, it is because while cultivating the Bodhisattva path, He made 12 great vows to eliminate all diseases and sufferings for sentient beings, allowing them to be full of wholesome roots and to aspire to liberation. Therefore, upon attaining Buddhahood, He resides in the Pure Lapis Lazuli world, adorned like the Land of Ultimate Bliss, along with two great Bodhisattvas, Sunlight Permeating All Directions and Moonlight Permeating All Directions, as His retinue to teach and transform sentient beings.

The original vow of the Medicine Buddha is to cure all serious illnesses and mental afflictions of sentient beings, and to save them from the suffering of birth and death. Because the Medicine Buddha has such a pure vow, a completely pure and transparent light (Lapis Lazuli Light) manifests unobstructedly on His body, and His Pure Land is the same, which is why He is called the Medicine Buddha of Lapis Lazuli Light.

Like the Buddhas of the ten directions, the Medicine Buddha possesses all the ten titles of Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaiḍūrya Prabha Tathāgata: Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened, Radiant Virtuous Happiness, Good Vows, Worldly Understanding, Supreme Sage, Controlled Expert, Teacher of Gods and Humans, and World-Honored One.

According to Buddhist scriptures, the Medicine Buddha has an additional six Manifest Bodies to collectively transform and save the seven worlds, hence he is honored as the Seven Medicine Buddhas. The names of these seven Tathāgatas are:

1) The Tathāgata of Good Name and Auspiciousness, who transforms and saves the Glorious World in the East

2) Moon-Protecting, Dignified and Bright Sound, Tathāgata, who transforms and saves the Wonderful Treasure Kingdom in the East

3) Golden Radiant Treasure, Perfectly Virtuous Tathāgata, who transforms and saves the Perfectly Complete Fragrant Accumulation Kingdom in the East

4) Utterly Worry-Free, Supreme, Auspicious Tathāgata, who transforms and saves the Worry-Free Kingdom in the East

5) Dharma Sea Thunder Sound Tathāgata, who transforms and saves the Dharma Assembly Kingdom in the East

6) Dharma Sea Victor Wisdom Recreational Supernatural Tathāgata, who transforms and saves the Good Abiding Treasure Sea Kingdom in the East

7) Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light Tathagata, who transforms and saves the Pure Lapis Lazuli World in the East

SINGLE-MINDEDLY BOW AND WORSHIP: Namo Eastern Teacher, Dispeller of Calamities, Longevity Giver, Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light King Buddha 🙏 🙏 🙏

Source: Nguyễn Tuý Minh - Duyên Giác

tieu_de: Lust and Intelligence
tom_tat: Lust is inversely proportional to a person's intelligence. Because lust leans too much toward emotion, when there is too much emotion, intelligence fades away. Precisely because of a lack of intelligence, there are no innovations, no cleverness.
noi_dung:
SEXUALITY AND INTELLIGENCE

Lust is inversely proportional to a person's intelligence. Because lust leans too much on emotion, when emotion is excessive, intellect dissipates. Precisely due to a lack of intelligence, there is no initiative, no memory, no focus, so life gradually becomes miserable, unhappy, and full of suffering. Behind an addiction lies a dark life. Sexual desire, alcohol, gambling, drug use... are all like that. They all drive people into misery and deadlock. From this, we understand that the more lustful a person is, the less valuable they are in life, and the more easily they become a burden to others.also intelligence gradually declines, work is no longer productive, actions are no longer proper, thoughts are no longer sharp.

On the contrary, whoever controls desire will see their intelligence begin to grow. Gradually, their focus on study and work increases, and because of this increased focus, memory also develops. Once memory develops, the ability to handle work and life becomes increasingly profound, subtle, and correct. With desire subdued, the mind is not disturbed, not pressured or uncomfortable, not burdened by longing or sorrow, therefore wisdom shines and understands everything.

Youth entering puberty with excessive sexual desire will very easily fail in the next stage. They keep struggling in confusion without knowing why. Because they lack the wisdom to make the right decisions for their lives. A restless mind prevents us from thinking through anything thoroughly or completely. Only with a stable, firm inner self can one have enough strength to make accurate decisions instantly.

Let us reflect on our lives; most failures bear traces of desire in them. Failure in career, failure in education, failure in morality, failure in health, failure in reputation... all have desire contributing to them. Reflect on this and be startled.

Watching pornography, masturbating, thinking naughty thoughts... also harms brain cells, causes brain atrophy, thereby losing a person's intelligence. Because the mind and body are a tightly connected whole and cannot be separated. A dark mind will make the body weak. A healthy body will make the mind healthy too. Therefore, nurturing the body and nurturing the mind are equally necessary.

Therefore, to preserve intelligence, the prerequisite is to break free from indulgence in pleasures, strong sensations such as sex, alcohol, in order to protect a pure mind and an agile brain that has sufficient willpower, courage, perseverance, and wisdom to face and handle everything in life accurately. In addition, intelligence also comes from the practical application of knowledge. If one only studies, if one only knows theory but cannot apply it in practice, it is merely a waste of knowledge. It is precisely when we practice that we develop reasoning and thinking, thereby increasing intelligence.

Intelligence also comes from love and kindness in life. The person whose heart is deeply loving and kind in behavior is also more intelligent and perceptive. Why is that? Because when we love, we want to put ourselves in others' shoes to understand them; when we are kind, we turn our own desires into benefits and happiness for others. Therefore, we will understand others and life much more.

Intelligence also comes from facing difficulties and finding ways to handle them in order to draw lessons and experiences for oneself and others. Only those who have gone through failure, poverty, and loneliness, and then risen above it, can become truly wealthy and resilient people. Because they have deeply understood life.

Intelligence also comes from correct thinking in life. If you don't think foolishly, everyone will gradually become more intelligent over the years. This is the general formula for intellectual progress. Positive, optimistic, loving, and kind thoughts... will nurture creativity, nurture memory, nurture dreams, and nurture the clarity of the soul.

Intelligence also comes from a pure inner mind. A person who is light in desires is already intelligent, but a person who is pure and clean is even more sensitive and creative by ten thousand times. Therefore, keeping the mind pure and clean through the method of meditation and chanting Buddha's name is also a way to enhance intelligence in life....

Let us together choose a clean lifestyle, free from desires, to find more lasting and genuine happiness.

CONTROL DESIRES

NAMO AMITABHA BUDDHA

tieu_de: IF YOU ARE FOND OF SUPERNATURAL POWERS AND LIKE SENSATIONS, YOU CAN EASILY BE DECEIVED BY DEMONS AND MONSTERS
tom_tat: How does Buddhism transform sentient beings? By teaching according to their appearances. We all know that in the scriptures we have read, the eight signs of attaining enlightenment are a form of teaching. I would like to explain more clearly, in a slightly easier way, that it is currently
noi_dung:
IF YOU ARE FOND OF SUPERNATURAL POWERS AND ENJOY SENSATIONS, YOU CAN EASILY BE DECEIVED BY DEMONS AND EVIL SPIRITS

How does Buddhism transform sentient beings? By manifesting appearances as a means of teaching. We all know, in the sutras we have read about eight signs of attaining enlightenment, which are forms of teaching. I would like to explain more clearly, a little more understandably, that it is like acting in a play, performing, showing it to us, so that the people among us see it every day. Seeing it for a long time will suddenly lead to great awakening, enabling one to see the path, and thus you can benefit from it. The Buddha first manifests appearances, and then delivers the Dharma. If we do not have any good appearances, then we ourselves cannot attain accomplishment. A good appearance comes fromA sincere heart naturally achieves, it is not fake. If it is fake, it is not Buddha, then who is it? It is a demon.

In the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, it is mentioned that there are 50 kinds of deceptive spirits, all of which are illusory. Their appearances manifest, and if you are careless and inattentive, you will regard them as Buddhas or Bodhisattvas, seemingly no different from Buddhas or Bodhisattvas, with dignified and beautiful appearances. It appears that they also have good intentions, good conduct, and virtuous speech. How can one distinguish that they are not genuine? For novices like us, in reality, we do not have the ability to discern. Previously, Master Lý taught us to distinguish between demons and Buddhas. A Buddha is purely pure and purely good; a demon can also be good and pure, but not purely so. They also teach sentient beings; for example, if they teach you 100 things, 99 of them are similarAs the Buddha said, but in it there is a sentence different from what the Buddha said. That sentence is poisonous; it is the root of hell, so distinguishing between a demon and the Buddha is truly not easy.

People who practice Buddhism easily encounter demonic obstacles; we have encountered too many already. Anyone who encounters demonic obstacles is always very dedicated, very diligent, very hardworking, very assiduous. If you are pretending to practice, demons will not come to find you. Why is that? Because demons can see very clearly that you will not achieve attainment; you are destined to remain in the six realms of samsara, still enduring the three evil paths. Demons particularly enjoy those who are trapped in the evil paths, so they do not come to bother you. If you truly practice and can genuinely transcend the three realms, demons become fearful and will come to create difficulties for you. In recent years, we have observed that many people genuinely encounter demonic obstacles.is a person who is very diligent, very hardworking, seeing this person as extremely good, having studied Buddhism for only a few years, then suffers from demonic interference. Ordinary people in the world, when we get schizophrenia, in the end, we all have to be taken to a psychiatric hospital, and the future of an entire life has been ruined, which is truly regrettable.

Moreover, many people have very high academic degrees; I have met many of them, and their relatives came to ask me: Is there any way to save them? The first question I asked them was: Does he really like supernatural powers? Does he really enjoy psychic phenomena? That's right, the trouble comes from this. Loving supernatural powers, loving psychic experiences, leads to being deceived by demons and evil spirits. Do Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have supernatural powers? Yes. However, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas definitely do not use supernatural powers for Buddhist work; the main work of Buddhism is teaching, and they absolutely do not use supernatural powers to educate sentient beings. Why is that? Because Buddhas and Bodhisattvas use supernatural powers to educate sentient beings.It's also like loving demons and ghosts. We have no way to distinguish who is a Buddha and who is a demon. Therefore, the Buddha uses the method of teaching, while demons and ghosts do not know how to preach the Sutras or teach; they only know how to display magical powers. So the Buddha does not use this method; the Buddha demonstrates using things that demons cannot do. We cannot be unaware of this.

(Excerpt: The Sutra of Infinite Life, 10th lecture, volume 314)

tieu_de: .1. First aspiration: To honor all Buddhas!
tom_tat: Filial piety towards parents and service to one's teacher is filial respect; filial respect that reaches complete perfection is the reverence of all Buddhas. In the Mahayana Precepts Sutra, the Buddha clearly instructs: 'Being filial and obedient to parents and monks, being filial and obedient...
noi_dung:
.1. First Vow: Respectfully paying homage to the Buddhas!

Filial piety towards parents and service to teachers is filial respect; filial respect to the ultimate fulfillment is the veneration of all Buddhas. In the Mahayana Precepts Sutra, the Buddha clearly revealed: "Filial to parents, to monastic teachers, filial to all sentient beings. Filial is called Precept." The Mahayana precepts are established on the foundation of filial piety. The word Hiếu (filial piety) is a compound ideogram: the top part is the character Lão (elder), and the bottom part is the character Tử (child), together forming the character Hiếu. In the character Hiếu, generations are interconnected; the generation of Lão and a subsequent generation are of the same essence. One generation above (Lão) also has a generation above it, extending into the infinite past; the generation below has one below it as well, yetLai vô chung. Lai vô chung is an integrated whole. Viewed vertically, ancestors and future descendants form one entity; viewed horizontally, it includes brothers, relatives, and friends; the brothers of brothers, the relatives of relatives, the friends of friends, spreading everywhere in all ten directions. Vertically throughout three generations, horizontally across all ten directions, this constitutes the entirety of the Dharma Realm. The character Filial Piety is a symbolic emblem representing the entirety of the Dharma Realm. Only by becoming a Buddha can one perfectly fulfill the path of Filial Piety.

Why do we have to study Buddhism? Because we want to perfectly fulfill the utmost filial duty, knowing that throughout the entire universe, everything is just ourselves! Therefore, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva himself said: To "pay respect to all Buddhas," one must be reborn in the Western Pure Land world to fully accomplish that aspiration. Samantabhadra Bodhisattva represents those who are reborn in the Western Pure Land world among the ten directions of the universe. If Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is like that, how much more so for us? If we want to perfectly fulfill the utmost filial duty, the only way is to follow Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; without following him, attempting to become a Buddha is hopeless!

In Buddhist teachings, from the Initial Aspiration to become a Buddha until attaining Buddhahood spans three great Asamkhyeya kalpas. In the past, we have practiced for countless Asamkhyeya kalpas; why haven't we become Buddhas? It is because our afflictions have not been eradicated, and we continue to be reborn in the six realms through endless cycles. Understanding the Pure Land from the Avatamsaka Sutra, we know that the Avatamsaka Sutra ultimately leads to reciting the Buddha's name to be reborn in the Western Pure Land. Therefore, I die single-mindedly insisting on reciting the Buddha's name to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, and Bodhisattva Samantabhadra saves us in this way.

The ceremony to venerate Buddhas, who are the Buddhas? The Buddha clearly teaches: “All sentient beings are originally Buddhas”; all phenomena arise from the combination of causes and conditions, and these are called “sentient beings.” Let us consider: Are there any dharmas that do not arise from the combination of causes and conditions? Only space is not produced by the combination of causes and conditions. Our bodies, towels, lecture halls are all produced by the combination of causes and conditions and are all called sentient beings. The Avatamsaka Sutra has a very important sentence as follows: “Sentient and insentient, all share the same nature of wisdom.” Sentient refers to sentient beings, specifically animals, sentient beings within the ten dharma realms. Insentient refers to the insentient.Sentient beings, only plants, minerals. 'All-encompassing wisdom' is becoming Buddha. Sentient beings can practice, can recite the Buddha's name, can become Buddha; but how can insentient beings become Buddha? Towels, tables, chairs, when will they become Buddha?

Now, thanks to this Virtue and Vow, we finally understand: sentient beings are Buddhas, and insentient beings are also Buddhas. When do insentient beings become Buddhas? When the conditioned body transforms according to the true body. The day we become Buddhas, we immediately perceive that mountains and great lands, all grass and trees, even dust particles, all become Buddhas; that is the phenomenon of Buddhahood. If one day you see yourself as a Buddha but see that others have not yet become Buddhas, then honestly speaking, you are dreaming, you are generating deluded thoughts, and it is certainly not Buddhahood. What the Avatamsaka Sutra teaches are entirely the realms and actual experiences of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, things that they have seen with their own eyes.see, hear with one's own ears, it is completely the true reality, not the realm of ordinary people.

How should one study this dharma practice? That dharma practice is the practice of the Dharma Body of the great masters; we are ordinary beings, with a single affliction not yet eliminated—can we practice it? Of course! Textbooks belong to the doctoral level within Buddhism, yet even we as kindergarten students can apply them; it is truly miraculous! Buddhist scriptures are beyond mere thought—they are complete and harmonious scriptures. Textbooks for beginners are precisely the scriptures for attaining Buddhahood; the dharma practice begins with learning reverence. Using a sincere mind, a pure mind, an equal mind, and a respectful mind toward everyone—that is paying respect to the Buddhas. We regard the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with reverence.Extraordinary respect, but for someone slightly inferior, it is not the practice of Samantabhadra. The practice of Samantabhadra is the practice of equality.

In each morning sutra session, we use the most sincere and respectful heart to pay homage to the Buddha. Afterwards, we use that same heart to interact with others. Whether dealing with parents, family members, relatives, friends, colleagues, or all people in society, both good and evil, we should approach them with a sincere, pure, equal, and respectful heart; that is the practice of Samantabhadra. Beyond humans, we must also use a sincere, pure, equal, and respectful heart to interact with all things. A towel represents the Buddhas; after using the towel, do not crumple it and throw it around. It should be thoroughly cleaned, dried, and neatly arranged; this demonstrates respect towards it. TableThe chair is also a Buddha, it must be cleaned thoroughly and arranged neatly; that is showing reverence towards it. Regarding work, any task we are responsible for must be done wholeheartedly and diligently to completion; that is showing respect for the task. It should not be done carelessly, nor should the responsibility be pushed onto others.

This Dharma practice is difficult, not easy to cultivate; it is originally the practice of the Enlightenment-level Bodhisattva. We are in kindergarten, so we must try our best even if we cannot achieve perfection. Learning a part brings a part of the benefit; the great benefit is beyond imagination. For example: If one can use a sincere, pure, equal, and respectful mind to treat people and things, one will never generate afflictions, and will experience incomparable mental pleasure, immediately attaining happiness and joy. Why are you not happy and joyful at present? It is because in your mind you distinguish this person as good, that person as bad, making judgments all day from morning to night,Clinging and mental afflictions, incessant delusions—how can you be truly happy and joyful? If you want to cultivate happiness and joy, the practice of Samantabhadra is the quickest and most effective. Just try to broaden your heart. As long as you sincerely generate the aspiration, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva will bless you. The sutra teaches: 'Through the power of Samantabhadra's vows, deeply believing and understanding, as if facing them directly.' With the divine power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's blessings, if we make a little effort, try a little, we can also achieve some results.

“All use pure body, speech, and mind to cultivate respect and reverence constantly”: Respect refers to ceremony and propriety. Not only should one show respect to people, but one should also show respect to things. If the mind is sincere and reverent, the outward expressions will conform to propriety. A pure mind is the true mind; in a pure mind there is no concern for right or wrong, self or others, discrimination, or attachment. Bodhisattvas use a pure mind to cultivate respect and reverence without interruption. Success or failure in practicing the Buddha’s teachings depends on patience. Many people, when first generating aspiring thoughts, feel very courageous, but after a few days they lose heart. If one can maintain the initial mind without regression, there is no one who will not become a Buddha.

only in one lifetime. Here, Bodhisattva Samantabhadra sets an example, encouraging us to preserve our original mind. He said: 'Only when the boundary of space is exhausted will my respect be exhausted.' The boundary of space cannot be exhausted, and if we vow to practice the great conduct of Samantabhadra, we also cannot regress. He also said: 'Only when the beings' boundaries are exhausted, their karma is exhausted, and their afflictions are exhausted, will my respect be exhausted.' The population of the world continues to grow, so the boundaries of beings are not exhausted. The afflictions of beings also increase day by day. Only by diligently learning Buddhism can afflictions be reduced. When afflictions decrease, wisdom grows. The afflictions of beings cannot be exhausted, so we mustBy venerating Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, of course, there is no end day.

Bodhisattva Samantabhadra also advised us: “Moment after moment, without interruption.” That is the secret of practice. Those who recite the Buddha’s name and accomplish these two phrases within a period of three months to half a year will have vigorous progress in their practice of Buddha recitation, and will definitely achieve mastery in their practice. These two phrases have a meaning completely equivalent to the phrase “to fully gather the six senses, maintaining pure and continuous mindfulness” of Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta in the Lankavatara Assembly.

"The body, speech, and mind in practice never get tired": The body must act; we see that everyone must be respected; speech must be considered carefully, the mind must be sincerely pure, equal, and respectful. Bodhisattva Samantabhadra uses a pure mind, therefore there is no fatigue, no distress. We use a discriminating mind, a defiled mind, so over a long period we become tired. In daily work, if we use a pure mind, a joyful mind, a mind aiming to benefit sentient beings, even if the work is heavy and numerous, we will not feel tired or discouraged. That is part of the benefit from practicing the Samantabhadra conduct.

The realm of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is vast, and that is precisely what differentiates his practice from that of other Bodhisattvas. Samantabhadra's practice is the practice in accordance with inherent nature. The intrinsic nature of Suchness is extraordinarily vast; the Buddha often said: “The mind encompasses the universe, its measure is as countless as the grains of sand” (the mind spreads throughout space, encompassing all worlds as numerous as sand). Each vow and practice of Samantabhadra corresponds to its own inherent nature; therefore, each vow and practice encompasses the entire dharma realm. Not only is the mind of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva sincere, pure, equal, and compassionate, but it is also boundlessly vast. Using such a mind to cultivate is what makes that practice truly called the Practice of Samantabhadra!

CHAPTER OF BODHISATTVA SAMBHI BUFFICIENT VOWS

tieu_de: LEARNING ABOUT THE DRAGON GOD PROTECTOR
tom_tat: _Excerpt from “Cause and Effect Explained, Luong Hoang Sam 2 - Qua Khanh”_ ⚘ The dragon is a mysterious creature, often considered by people as a product of imagination. But in reality, this is not the case; those with the third eye
noi_dung:
LEARNING ABOUT THE DRAGON GOD OF PROTECTION

_Excerpt “Cause and Effect Commentary on Lương Hoàng Sám 2 - Quả Khanh”_

⚘ Dragons are mysterious creatures, often considered by people to be the product of imagination. But in fact, that is not the case; people with the divine eye, such as the Buddha, saints, or practitioners who have opened the divine eye in the modern era, can see and interact with dragons.

In particular, those true cultivators often have dragons as Protectors.

********************************

The Dharma-protecting dragon is not yet a Buddha, Bodhisattva, or sage, so it still possesses desires, anger, and ignorance... and is very judgmental and attached to appearances. If it sees someone practicing incorrectly, it will become furious, develop anger, and take action to punish.

In 2002, I (Quả Khanh - a layperson with clairvoyance and divine eye knowledge) along with some fellow practitioners visited a temple in Hà Nam. We heard from people at the temple:

The small attic at the back of the temple, meant for traveling monks to stay, is often disturbed by ghosts or spirits. Many people who stayed there would frequently hear knocking on the door in the middle of the night, startling them awake. When they went out to open it, no one was there… Moreover, while lying in bed, they would be carried down… which terrified them, so they didn’t dare stay there…

Some people say that this is caused by deceased monks! The temple has held grand ceremonies to pray for their souls, but these disturbances still continue as before…

We immediately went there to observe and discovered: it turned out that the protective dragon deities were inside.

I asked:

- Are you the ones disturbing them?

The deity replied:

- Yes! I am very angry!... The ones I target are entirely those who receive offerings but do not practice cultivation!

We are very angry and don't want to act as their protector anymore! Without going too far, try asking them: Yesterday, June 19th, was the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara's day of commemoration, so what did they do, how did they practice? It was all done superficially, living chaotically and recklessly, without any proper discipline at all!

I said:

- What use is anger? Could it be that you scare all the monks into fleeing, leaving the temple empty, and think that solves the problem? From now on, do not destroy things like this anymore!..

Although the Dragon Guardian Deity responded to the request, and there was no longer any disturbance in the temple, my mind suddenly became heavy and sorrowful...

Nowadays, in the age of the decline of the Dharma, we, as disciples of the Buddha, should not hope to request wealth for Buddhist activities, but should rather wish for ourselves: to observe precepts strictly, conduct ourselves with dignity, and maintain standards. If we do so, it will naturally make both heaven and humans delighted, and the Dragon Deities will happily protect us. If not, we will be looked down upon with disdain by ghosts, deities, and the Dragon Guardian Deities!

Whether it is a Benevolent Dragon or an Evil Dragon, they all have more or less anger in their hearts. Right at the entrance of the Tien Duong River, every year, there is often a rising tide that sweeps away the lives of many people.

Recalling in 1993, there was an incident where a crowd watching the waves was swept away by the tide, and only one person survived, being washed ashore by the waves.

At that time, Qua Lam (daughter of Qua Khanh, who also has the ability of fate insight and heavenly vision) observed: She saw the consciousness of those who had just died staying in the Dragon Palace and being tied down on the ground. Qua Lam asked the Dragon King:

- Why arrest them?

The Dragon King replied angrily:

- Let them live to propagate and promote the killing and eating of my aquatic people? They have already eaten countless species of my aquatic people!

Quả Lâm asked:

- But why did the Dragon King allow one person to live and create waves to bring them ashore?

- Because this person only likes to gather in lively crowds to watch the waves and have fun, but he himself does not commit acts of killing. The reason accidents, tsunamis, etc., occur on Earth is all related to indulging in killing, caused by those who have accumulated heavy karmic debt from killing. How someone lives, what they do, can be noticed at a glance!

In the Kinh Chánh Pháp Niệm Xứ, the Buddha warned and reminded us that: Supporting the world is the Good Dragon. As for whether the weather is mild, the winds favorable, and the rain harmonious, it depends on the Evil Dragon! They hold the authority to manage this! Therefore, whenever storms, hail, tornadoes, or unusual floods occur, the main cause is due to the intentions and actions of humans living wickedly that attract such consequences...

If we have clearly seen this, then each of us needs to strictly observe the precepts and diligently practice so that the Good Dragon can gain more power, making it easier and more convenient to protect humanity. We should not commit sins allowing the Evil Dragon to gain advantage, because whenever given the opportunity, they will unleash widespread disasters upon humans (this is similar to the human world: whenever hoodlums, gangs, thieves, and evil people run rampant… the criminal organizations gain more power, expanding... taking the opportunity to wreak havoc and harm the people).

Dragons that cultivate often like to act as deities protecting the Dharma, greatly admiring the Buddha's teachings; therefore, the Dragon Palace contains countless Buddhist scriptures, seemingly even more than in the human world.

If a person truly observes precepts and cultivates, they will certainly be protected by the Dragon King and the Eight Legions of divine beings.

When Venerable Hsuan Hua was in the Northeast, he once took ten dragons as disciples. Prior to that, because his disciple, Quả Thuấn, built a place of practice (near the Dragon King's temple), on the day of its inauguration they invited the Great Master to come.

That day, 10 dragons appeared in human form to request refuge. At that time, the Northeast was experiencing a drought, so Master Xuanhua set a condition: If the dragons agreed to make rain, he would accept their refuge. Sure enough, the next day, rain fell and ended the drought. On the third day, the 10 dragons were officially accepted as disciples, all receiving the Dharma name "Cấp Tu".

From then on, wherever Master Xuanhua went, the dragons in his retinue would always provide him with sufficient water, never letting him lack and never leaving his side.
