tieu_de: BE CAREFUL WITH WORDS - PIERCING ACTIONS, SOWING DIVISION.
tom_tat: (Excerpt from "Buddhist Tales") - Collected by: Thích Minh Chiếu -
noi_dung:
BE CAREFUL WITH SHARP WORDS - ACTIONS THAT PIERCINGLY SEPARATE.

(Excerpt from "Buddhist Folktales")

- Collected by: Thich Minh Chieu -

Once there was a monk named Kondaahana. Since the time he was ordained, wherever he went, a woman would follow behind him. The monk himself did not know this, but everyone else could see it.

When going on alms rounds, donors would offer two spoonfuls of rice into his alms bowl. For the first spoonful, they would say:

- This spoon is for the Teacher, and the second spoon is for the Teacher's female friend.

The monks, seeing this, were convinced that the Teacher had violated the rule of not cohabiting and went to speak with the householder Cāpaka and requested him to expel the monk Kondaahana from the monastery.

The householder did not dare, and when the monks informed the female devotee Visakha, she also did not dare.

The monks then went to appear before King Bimbisāra and narrated the event. The king agreed.

In the afternoon, returning to the temple, the king ordered the soldiers to surround the main hall, while he went up to the hall. Master Kondaahana, hearing the commotion, came out to see, and the king saw a woman behind the Master; as for the Master, he knew the king had arrived and immediately went back inside.

When meeting the Master, the king did not pay respects, but at this moment the king no longer saw the image of the woman who had been outside.

The king searched the corners and under the bed but did not find her, then asked:

- Master, I just saw a woman here, where has she gone?

- Your Majesty, I do not see it.

- I myself see a woman standing behind the Master.

The monk still insisted firmly.

- I do not know and do not see it.

The king thought:

"How strange this matter is!"

The king then said:

- Then please, Master, go outside.

When the Master left, immediately a woman followed behind. The king saw it clearly, and then invited the Master in.

When the Master entered, the king watched the figure of that woman, but suddenly she disappeared. The king was surprised and asked:

- Master, where is that woman?

- Your Majesty, this humble monk does not see any woman at all.

- Please, Master, speak honestly to me clearly.

- Your Majesty, everyone says that there is a woman walking behind me, but I cannot see her.

The king thought that this was just an illusion, but still doubtful, he said:

- Then please go away from this place once more.

When the Master went outside, the image of the woman appeared again, standing behind him. The king asked, but the Master answered as before. The king then thought: “Indeed, it is an illusion,” and he said:

- Venerable Teacher, once there is something impure like this, no one can offer alms to you in purity; therefore, from now on, please go into the inner palace, and I will offer you the necessary items.

The monks then whispered among themselves:

- Esteemed Teacher, think about it, the king is excessively obstinate; we invited him in to observe the situation, yet he refuses to expel the monk who has broken the precepts, and even invites him into the palace to offer alms.

Then the monks spoke to Venerable Kondaahana:

- Hey, breaker of precepts! The king is also a coward like you.”

Before, the monk had no proof to respond, but now that the king had witnessed it, he immediately replied:

- You are the breakers of precepts, you are the ones who lead girls away.

The monks then reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One called the monk and asked:

- Did you scold those monks?

The monk replied:

- Blessed One, it is because those teachers spoke to the disciple.

The Blessed One asked those teachers:

- Why did you scold this monk?

- Blessed One, it is because we saw a woman following behind this monk.

Then the Blessed One addressed the monk Kondaahana and asked:

- These monks saw a woman following behind you, so why did you not see her and got into a quarrel with these monks? This result is also due to the karma of your past life, so why now do you still not abandon that bad habit?

At that time, the monks collectively said to the Buddha:

- World-Honored One, what kind of karma did Venerable Kondaahana perform in the past?

The Buddha then taught that:

- During the time of Buddha Kassapa, there were two monks who loved each other as if they were siblings from the same parents. At that time, every year the monks would gather once to perform the Pat Luu ceremony. As the Pat Luu day approached, the two monks invited each other to go to the place where the ceremony would be held.

On their way, a deity from the Tavatimsa heaven saw the two monks loving each other and thought:

“These two monks love each other very much, can I separate them?”.

While thinking of a plan to separate them, one of the two monks said:

- Please wait for me a moment, sir, I need to go to the river.

The deity waited for that monk to finish going to the river. When emerging from the bushes, he immediately transformed into a woman, holding up her skirt with one hand and lifting her hair with the other, as if she had just been intimate with that monk. The deity deliberately waited for the monk to see before disappearing.

Therefore, when this monk arrived, the deity said:

- You are a rule-breaker.

- No, sir, I'm not!

Just now I saw a girl walking behind the Master.

- Master, this matter is really not me.

The two Masters argued, and in the end, they went their separate ways, never able to get along, because they did not agree to perform the Taming Ceremony together.

The Deity, seeing such a disastrous outcome, thought:

“I have committed a great offense already,” and immediately appeared down to say:

- The virtue of this monk is still pure; this is merely because I wanted to test the two of you. Please, both of you perform the Patimokkha ceremony together.

Then, the two monks agreed to listen and gladly performed the Patimokkha ceremony together.

Because of that karma, after death, that Deva was condemned to the Avici hell for many lifetimes, and has now been reborn as Kondaahana.

After recounting the past lives of Venerable Kondaahana, the Buddha then said:

- You have these extraordinary events today because of that vile karma. Yet you still hold on to that vile nature. You should not speak any words to the monks. You must remain silent like a mute person; only when you can do that can you hope to end your karma and attain the fruit of enlightenment...

Therefore, in our daily lives, we should refrain from all slanderous words. Whatever we hear, we should not repeat it to cause discord between people.

The wise reconcile those who are divided, binding the ties of affection between those who share the same mind and purpose.

The wise take the harmony of others as their own delight, considering it their work and their pleasure.

A person only speaks words that promote harmony among people.

Namo Bhagavā Sakyamuni Buddha __()__

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahāsattva __()__

tieu_de: IF YOU HAPPEN TO BE CAUGHT BY YOUR FAMILY EATING PORK, THEN WHEN YOU CUT IT, REMEMBER THAT EACH SLICE OF THE KNIFE IS A RECITATION OF 'A DI DA PHAT'. OR AT
tom_tat: We are not monastics. Monastics live in temples, so they are not obstructed by the chaos of society. Because they have little work, they do not generate chaos. It is very difficult for us laypeople to do the same, all ...
noi_dung:
IF SOMEONE IN THE FAMILY HAPPENS TO BUTCHER MEAT, THEN EVERY TIME YOU CUT, remember that each knife stroke is a phrase 'A DI DA PHAT'. OR IN

We are not monastics. Monastics live in temples, so they are not obstructed by the chaos of society. Because they have little to do, they do not stir up disorder.

For us laypeople, it is very difficult to do the same, as we are always concerned with worldly matters. For example, when it comes to commonly seen things related to the seven emotions: everyone calculates money. Once calculating money, we think: who should give me how much money, to whom should I give how much, and how much profit is gained. Because of that small profit, we then plan this, calculate that.

That is the mind of greed! So what should one do?

Listen to me say a few sentences: When paying money, do not harbor bad intentions, do not try to think of ways to harm others. If you have to give money to someone, just count one, two, three, four bills... that amount, and once counted, do not fixate on it. One, two, three, four are just numbers for counting, neither good nor evil. Once you have finished counting, let it go completely, after the task is done, release it, and do not think about it anymore. "Letting go" is very essential; here I only take the act of counting money as an example.

It is similar to practicing at home: if you are practicing, but your family members are not, and they go to the market to buy meat and ask you to cut it or slaughter an animal, what should you do? At that time, do not panic. If you cannot prevent them from doing it, then you have to do it; but while doing it, never forget to recite 'Amitabha Buddha'. That meat, because they have not studied Buddhism and have created negative karma, has become a pig, a goat, or meat, to be cut and divided by others. When you cut it, with each stroke of the knife, recite 'Amitabha Buddha', and that knife will become a means for Amitabha Buddha to absolve your sins. Using this method of contemplation to transform your mind is sufficient.

Even in places like the toilet, in unclean areas, even if one does not recite the Buddha's name aloud, one can think: “In the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, there is no such thing, no defecation or urination. The Sahā world is so dirty, and we create all sorts of karma that force us to be born here; the mind is not pure, yet we live in an unclean place.” At that moment, keep a heart of repentance, and in your heart, pray to Amitābha Buddha to soon allow you to embrace His feet.

No matter what you do, never forget Amitābha Buddha, and there is no need to recite aloud. Keep the Buddha in your mind to transform your state. That is precisely “thinking of the Buddha.”

COLLECTION OF MASTER LI BINGNAM'S PURE LAND TEACHINGS

A collection of writings on the Pure Land by layman Li Bingnam.

PLEASE REGULARLY RECITE THE BUDDHA'S NAME & BOW TO THE BUDDHA:

NAMO AMITABHA BUDDHA 🙏🙏🙏

tieu_de: WHEN DEDICATING MERIT TO SOMEONE, ONE MUST STATE THEIR NAME AND AT THE SAME TIME THINK OF THAT PERSON
tom_tat: I watched a CD, last time a fellow practitioner from the north gave me two CDs, I watched them, about the matter of possession. Two generals from the Sino-Japanese period possessed other people, one general
noi_dung:
WHEN DEDICATING MERIT TO SOMEONE, YOU MUST STATE THEIR NAME AND AT THE SAME TIME THINK OF THAT PERSON

I watched a CD; last time, someone practicing cultivation in the north gave me two CDs. I watched them, and they were about spirit possession. Two generals during the Sino-Japanese period possessed others: one Chinese general and one Japanese general. They prayed for rebirth. They said to the people performing the prayers: When you dedicate the merit, you must read their names, visualize them, and think of them; just reading without thinking of them is useless, they cannot be liberated. You must definitely think of them; this information is very good. Nowadays, most people just read according to the text without visualizing, reading in this way.just a waste of effort. Reading it must definitely make you think.

When thinking of the Original Teacher, Shakyamuni Buddha, one must think of Him in the mind; only then will there be a response. Just reciting without thinking will not generate a response. When thinking of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, one must think of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. Whatever you are reciting, you must think of that; only then will it be effective.

PS. TỊNH KHÔNG

tieu_de: WHY PEOPLE OFTEN GET HURT AND SUFFER IN RELATIONSHIPS (Cause and Effect Are Naturally Very Fair, Reincarnation Leads to Meeting Each Other and Causing Suffering)
tom_tat: On the afternoon of December 24, 2006, a reader wrote a letter to me as follows: – Hello Ms. Diệu Liên! I often go online to see you answer questions about karma, and reading it makes me feel sad, tears streaming down. I know myself
noi_dung:
WHY WE OFTEN GET HURT BY RELATIONSHIPS (Karma Is Originally Very Fair, Reincarnation Leads Us to Encounter and Cause Suffering to Each Other)

On the afternoon of December 24, 2006, a reader wrote a letter to me as follows:

– Hello, Sister Diệu Liên! I often go online to see you explain about karma, and reading it makes me feel poignant, with tears streaming down. I know I have deep sins, perhaps because in past lives I created boundless negative karma, so in this life I experience all kinds of suffering and hardships. Three times being harshly mistreated in love have made me want to commit suicide many times. Since I began studying Buddhism, I have bravely done repentance and self-correction; although it may still be insufficient, everything is now improving. I understand that this is thanks to the blessings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and I silently give thanks, only knowing to vow to diligently cultivate myself before helping others, hoping to repay the Buddha's kindness.

However, in moments of quiet contemplation, I vaguely see many past-life images related to twisted fate. I feel this very clearly but do not yet have the ability to fully understand or see the reasons. Here is my story, I hope you can take the time to read it:

I was born and six months later my parents argued and then separated. When I was 3 years old, my parents divorced, and I went to live with my grandmother in my hometown A for 10 years, then because of school I had to move to city B, but still lived with my grandmother. In 1996 I passed the university entrance exam, and in 2000 I graduated and started working in city C.

Then, because I changed jobs, I had to go to different streets, and now I have returned to city B.

Back in 1994, I was studying in high school, majoring in Literature, when I got to know Mr. Bằng. In 1995, feelings developed, and by 2002, I was living with Bằng on street D. In March 2003, we broke up, making it over 8 years of being in a relationship. Although we had broken up, I still had lingering feelings. In August, Bằng came to city D to see me again, and initially, because Bằng agreed, I allowed myself to become pregnant.

But unexpectedly, after Tet 2005, Bằng suddenly disappeared without a trace. After that, I had an abortion. In total, we had been in love for 10 years, and until now, we have not met again.

At the end of November 2003, I went to City E, striving to work with a leader named Minh. My career flourished and both sides were successful. Because of this, I also fell into an attachment that was hard to escape. Since only I loved passionately, it became hopeless, because at the end of 2004, Minh was transferred to City C and no longer kept in touch with me. I clearly knew that he did not need me, but I was helpless in letting go of this feeling, so I clung to boundless sorrow.

On March 15, I met Bân. Because we had similar work experience and social background, we easily empathized with and understood each other. From the moment we met, we were passionately in love, unable to escape, our closeness seemingly inseparable. Yet, in the blink of an eye, the relationship quickly ended. On May 8, his wife appeared, and he disappeared, never seeking to meet me again. Until now, we have never met again. It can be considered that the ending was similar to a first love.

Above, I only recounted the deep loves that brought me intense suffering. As for trivial affairs of the heart, it is not worth mentioning. One can see that in this life I have seriously transgressed in matters of love, committing sins of immeasurable depth; just a single word, love, has caused me hardships and sorrow for half of my life.

Sister! As I tell this, I cannot stop the streams of tears from flowing. Perhaps you also look down upon me, not knowing what karmic sins I created in a past life that make me suffer so much in this one. Besides repentance and spiritual practice, I do not know what else I should do. Please explain to me what I should understand, and I respectfully bow and thank you.

– Kim Khanh!

On December 29, 2006, I explained to Kim Khanh the cause and effect of her past actions as follows:

– Regarding the love affair with the young man named Bang, in a past life, Khanh was Count An, while Bang was a young lady who loved Khanh passionately. Just like in this life, their feelings were deeply attached for 10 years, then the Count suddenly changed, no longer caring or thinking about the young lady. It was because he sought a new love, so he became cold and harsh toward his former beloved, causing the girl immense suffering.

– About the romance with the leader named Minh, in a past life, both were mice: Kim Khánh was the female mouse, Minh was the male mouse. The male mouse loved the clever and cute appearance of the female mouse very much, so he always tried to please her. Whenever he found a delicious treat, he would bring it to her, but the female mouse only had the intention of taking advantage to enjoy it. After finishing all the offerings, she treated the male mouse very badly. Although she secretly liked the male mouse constantly being by her side, she always ignored him, pretending not to see or hear, acting arrogantly, without even glancing at the male mouse.

– Regarding the past connection with the young man named Bân, in a previous life, Kim Khánh was a general leading an army. After a battle, he stayed at the small estate of a local magnate. In that life, Bân was a woman, the daughter of that magnate. When they first saw each other, both harbored the same resentment in their hearts and regretted meeting each other too late, because at that time the general already had a wife back home. However, the general and the young woman were still intoxicated with love, unable to break away, spending every day clinging to each other. But soon, the army had to depart, and this love became hopeless, with no result.

After telling the story, I concluded that in many past lives, Khánh often served as a general, had met and mingled with countless beautiful women, and it was considered that they could hardly escape Khánh's experienced and charming hands. In this life, with all karmic conditions met and guided by the laws of karma, Khánh always has to taste again the emotional wounds he once caused, piling up suffering for others across many previous lives.

Through this story, I would like to advise everyone that in life, one must create good karmic connections with all beings instead of forming bad ones. One must understand that cause and effect follow like a shadow follows a form. A thousand, ten thousand times, you should be careful; you should not be careless, playful with emotions, or create evil deeds. When the time comes to receive the consequences and you regret it, it will be too late.

Diệu Liên.

according to: Bát Khách website

tieu_de: Bodhisattva Manjushri asked the Buddha: Among all actions, which action is the gravest?
tom_tat: The Buddha answered: Among all actions, killing and taking life, eating the flesh of sentient beings is the gravest sin. Why is that? Because for every cut there must be a cut in return, for every life taken there must be a life repaid. For thousands and millions of lifetimes, beings devour each other.
noi_dung:
Bodhisattva Manjushri asked the Buddha: Among all actions, which karma is the heaviest?

The Buddha answered: Among all karmic deeds, killing living beings and eating their flesh is the gravest sin. Why is that? Because a cut requires to repay a cut, a life must be repaid for a life. For countless lifetimes, beings continue to devour each other endlessly. Therefore, if a Bodhisattva wants to escape the cycle of rebirth, first he must practice compassion, not eating meat and not killing living beings.

Second is theft, damaging the wealth of others; little capital, much talk; therefore, for thousands of lifetimes one must repay old debts. Why is that? Because things belonging to others, if not given but taken by oneself, whether money or grains of rice, must be returned. Therefore, a person practicing the Bodhisattva path, wanting to have much wealth, to be rich as desired, must first practice generosity; how could one then steal or deceive others?

Third is committing sexual misconduct; bonds of desire last for thousands of lifetimes, impossible to be liberated. Why is that? Because sexual desire is the formal seed of birth and death (cycle of reincarnation), one must first eliminate lust.

The fourth is committing the crime of false speech, verbal misconduct, slander against each other, leading to endless generations of right and wrong opposing each other and quarreling. Why is that? Because injustice begets injustice, generation after generation people want to devour each other with words. Therefore, if a Bodhisattva wants to attain the path, first he must be honest and eradicate deceit.

The fifth is committing the crime of drinking alcohol. Alcohol clouds the true nature, and for countless kalpas the mind becomes darkened. Why is that? Because alcohol has the power to make the mind dull, causing ignorance for generations, filthy bodies, and staggering drunkenness. Therefore, if a Bodhisattva wants the mind to be calm and wisdom to be clear, he must give up the karma of drinking alcohol.

These five karmas are very great and very heavy. If a person preserves them completely, they become a Saint; if not fully preserved, they wander in suffering for many lifetimes, and once the human body is lost, it is difficult to regain for countless lifetimes.

(Mahayana Diamond Sutra Commentary)

tieu_de: HARMFUL EFFECTS OF SEXUAL LUST
tom_tat: People who are lustful are often also people who are easily dishonored. We can observe this very clearly in ourselves. If we engage in sexual misconduct secretly in places where no one knows, our minds are filled with dark and obscene desires and s
noi_dung:
HARMFUL EFFECTS OF SEXUAL IMMORALITY

A person with strong lustfulness is often also someone prone to losing their honor. We can clearly observe this in ourselves. If we frequently indulge in sexual acts secretly where no one knows, with a mind full of dark lust, and then interact with people around us, we are more likely to be criticized, scolded, humiliated, or mocked in very strange ways. Because when we are heavy with lust, our intellect and intelligence decrease, making everything we do go wrong, fail, or lead nowhere, which causes great discomfort to those around us.

Muddy mind

Being overly lustful also makes our mind dull, sluggish, no longer able to respond wisely and handle everything skillfully. Moreover, when we are overly lustful, our body loses some virtue, and people naturally respect us less without knowing why. Not to mention, those who are overly lustful always emit an invisible malicious aura surrounding them, making their presence cause others to become easily angry or uncomfortable. One often becomes a thorn in people's eyes, eliciting their contempt.

Lack of confidence in communication

Excessive sexual desire also makes us lack confidence in communication. It's strange. Why? Because only those who are mentally stable and healthy have confidence. People with excessive sexual desire, who are psychologically unsettled and mentally weak, lose their confidence. They are timid, hesitant, and overly anxious in whatever they do. This scene is very similar to those addicted to drugs who prefer to find a secluded place alone rather than interacting with others. From there, wealth, fame, and social status gradually disappear in life.

Rude

Excessive lust also makes us become rude and degraded in our behavior without us realizing it. For example, someone who used to live very cleanly and tidily. After several years of excessive lust, we will see them becoming foul-smelling, corrupt, and losing all decorum. Or a student who used to study very well may, after becoming addicted to sex, see their academic performance decline, lose interest in studying, and no longer have the motivation to strive... And these are all signs of the degeneration of one's character as a human being. If one remains excessively lustful, eventually that person will enjoy doing actions similar to animals and may degrade into the animalistic world. This happens very often.

Increasing Malice

Excessive lust also gradually makes us more malicious. People who are not angry, when addicted to lust, will become irritable and cruel. A filial child, due to being infatuated with lust, will turn into a ruthless, unfilial person. A person living a pure life, when sullied by lust, will become restless and anxious. A kind-hearted person, when consumed by lust, no longer recognizes their own faults and keeps making mistakes… And the outcome is receiving only extreme disdain from society.

Destroying All Merit

Excessive lust burns away all glory, wealth, and luck in our lives, turning them into pleasure for us to enjoy. Because lust is secretive and its consequences come more slowly than drugs, many times we do not realize it. Anyone addicted to lust ends up with a decayed body, madness, failure, suffering, and ignorance. Therefore, to avoid becoming a burden to others, to avoid becoming something for others to despise, we should awaken and eliminate desire.

Loss of willpower

Being overly lustful will cause a loss of willpower. Willpower can only arise within a strong inner self. If our mind is full of lust, then the mind is very weak, fragile, easily sad, easily suffering, easily broken. Therefore, to protect the will to live, the will to work, the will to practice, the will to contribute… one should completely quit lust.

Control Lust - Live Purely

Namo Amitabha Buddha

tieu_de: THE BAD CONSEQUENCES FOR PEOPLE WHO KEEP BIRDS
tom_tat: Nowadays I see that keeping birds has become very popular. When they have free time and don't know what to do, people have come up with many entertainment activities.
noi_dung:
THE BAD CONSEQUENCES OF BIRD KEEPERS

Nowadays I see that keeping birds has become extremely common.

When people have free time and don’t know what to do, they come up with many forms of entertainment and amusement.

Among them are keeping birds, doves, fish, fighting roosters, etc...

I used to think this was normal, but little did I know that those who keep them are actually creating very terrible, horrific repercussions that they themselves don’t realize.

Today I will list the retributions of people who keep birds:

1. Sowing the cause to be imprisoned:

Because birds are freely flying, yet we confine them in cages.

This is essentially making them imprisoned without reason.

When this retribution manifests, the bird keeper will have to endure imprisonment in the future.

In many cases, people who are imprisoned, even if they are imprisoned due to injustice,.... But actually, in terms of karma, that person in the past had planted the karma of imprisoning beings without reason.

So now they are experiencing the karmic result of being imprisoned, and it is not unjust at all.

2. In life, many instances of bad luck and misfortune will appear:

These types of karmic results come from the grief and suffering of the birds, so that person has to endure similar karmic consequences.

3. Mental fatigue and exhaustion will appear in the lives of these people:

I saw a case where a family raised a lot of birds.

After some time of raising them, the mother became possessed, acting crazy and mad.

As a result, the whole family had to live in suffering and sorrow.

Truly immediate karma, yet which sentient beings would know.

4. The legs will be weaker than normal, and may tremble:

Because the birds are confined in the cage for too long, their legs become stiff, reducing the strength of their legs.

Therefore, the keeper will have to bear the repercussions of this karma.

5. Thoughts such as feeling bored with life, pessimism, despair, wanting to commit suicide.... will always appear in the keeper's mind:

This is because when they keep birds, the birds feel trapped and bored in their hearts, flying frantically in the cage, and sometimes they also want to end their lives to feel relief, due to feelings of loneliness and sadness.

Above are the five basic karmic consequences for bird keepers.

Therefore, you should not keep birds; you should let them fly away so that your soul feels light and at peace.

And not only should we not keep them, but if we see someone else keeping them, we should buy them back and let them fly away, or advise the person not to keep them.

Many birds that are close to humans, sometimes in their previous lives, were actually people who were also our relatives.

Such as parents, siblings, relatives, or aunts and uncles from both sides of our family,.... Because they lived wrongly, when they died they were reborn as birds.

So today, when we raise birds, be careful, as we might be keeping our own relatives imprisoned.

Therefore, remember to never raise birds, to avoid the bad consequences as mentioned above.

Namo Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva.

tieu_de: TODAY, APRIL 4TH LUNAR CALENDAR IS THE DAY OF WORSHIP OF BODHISATTVA MANJUSHRI
tom_tat: Bodhisattva Manjusri is also called Man Thu That Ly, which means Wonderful Virtue, Wonderful Auspiciousness. Wonderful Virtue is understood as having all virtues complete. In ancient times, he was the third son of King Vo Trach Nhiem, named
noi_dung:
TODAY, THE 4TH OF THE LUNAR CALENDAR, IS THE HOLY DAY OF BODHISATTVA MANJUSHRI

The Bodhisattva Manjushri is also called Manju Shili, meaning Wonderful Virtue, Wonderful Auspiciousness. Wonderful Virtue is understood as all virtues being complete. In ancient times, he was the third son of King Votracnh Nhiem, named Prince Vuong Chung. He offered to Buddha Bảo Tạng and made a vow to save sentient beings, thus he was titled Manjushri. After Buddha Bảo Tạng predicted that he would, in countless eons, become a Buddha in the pure world of Vô Cấu Bảo Chi in the south, he would be named Buddha Manjushri. Bodhisattva Manjushri appears in almost all scriptures.The importance of Mahayana Buddhism: Avatamsaka, Shurangama, Lotus Sutra, Vimalakirti… as one of the closest figures to Gautama Buddha.

At times, He officially represents the Blessed One to expound the True Dharma, while at other times, He plays the role of program director to introduce to the listeners an important Dharma session of the Blessed Teacher. He comprehends Buddha-nature, which includes the three virtues: Dharmakaya, Prajna, and Liberation, therefore among the Bodhisattvas, He is the foremost. As a representative Bodhisattva of wisdom, Manjushri Bodhisattva is often depicted with a youthful appearance sitting cross-legged on a lotus cushion. His distinctive symbol is a sword flaming in His right hand, raised above His head. It implies that it is precisely the golden sword of wisdom.This will break all the chains of ignorance and affliction that have bound humans to the suffering and misery of the endless cycle of birth and death and lead humans to perfect wisdom.

Meanwhile, His left hand is holding the Prajnaparamita sutra in a posture as if embracing it close to the heart. This symbolizes mindfulness and enlightenment. Sometimes, we also see His left hand holding a blue lotus, representing virtue. This means using wisdom to completely eliminate all defilements and desires, like a lotus in the mud that does not absorb the smell of the mud. In other words, a Bodhisattva is not someone who hides in remote mountains or lives in a serene, leisurely setting, but is someone who mingles with the public, rolling in the dust of the world to save sentient beings, so at times they may become kings, at times ministers, and sometimes even commoners.cursed with poverty… Although living amidst abundant pleasures, the Bodhisattva still maintains a pure mind, not defiled like ordinary people. This is thanks to the wisdom that completely eradicates desire, achieving perfect moral cessation.

The armor He wears is called the armor of patience. Thanks to it, pointed arrows of criticism cannot penetrate the body. It can protect Him to maintain complete compassion, so that the enemies of hatred and resentment cannot shake the Bodhisattva's vows. The Bodhisattva never parts from the armor of patience because without it they cannot carry out the Bodhi mind. Regarding Asian Buddhism, Mount Wutai in China is considered the residence of Manjushri Bodhisattva. Mount Wutai is located in Shanxi Province and has five mountains grouped together: East Peak, West Peak, South Peak, North Peak, and Central Peak. The scenery is verygraceful with sparkling lakes, clear winding rivers along with wondrous natural landscapes like ink wash paintings, it has long been regarded as a fairyland, the dwelling place of immortals according to Chinese legend. The Flower Adornment Sutra says:

Manjushri Bodhisattva resides on Mount Qingliang in the northeast and is currently preaching to the Bodhisattvas. This Mount Qingliang later came to be referred to as Mount Wutai. Therefore, during the Tang Dynasty (736 AD), a Chan master named Dao Yi, a high-ranking monk, made a pilgrimage to Mount Wutai. The master encountered an old monk riding a white elephant on the opposite side. The old monk said that tomorrow he would meet Manjushri Bodhisattva, and after speaking, the old monk disappeared. The master was extremely joyful and spent the night reflecting on Qingliang Temple, the center of Mount Wutai. The next morning, at dawn, the master awoke and set out alone.Head west up the mountain. The monk met the person riding the white elephant from yesterday and the monk encouraged him to continue going up the mountain.

When the monk went northwest, crossing a bridge, he saw a majestic and solemn mansion like a monastery, all made of gold. Then he met the old monk again and no longer had any doubt; he was certain that the old monk was a manifestation of Bodhisattva Manjushri. The monk was so overjoyed that he was dazed and it took him a while to regain his composure. Taking this opportunity, he asked about the confusions in Buddhist teachings, and the Bodhisattva also kindly inquired about the state of Buddhism in the monk's homeland. After bidding farewell to the Bodhisattva and walking about a hundred steps, the monk looked back, and everything had disappeared. Monk Dao Nhat reported all the things he had witnessed.Emperor Tang Xuanzong. The emperor was very attracted by this story and therefore ordered the establishment of the Golden Sand Temple. This is a grand temple built according to the model that the monk remembered, completed at the end of the 8th century.

Another Japanese monk named Ennin also made a pilgrimage to Mount Wutai in 840 AD. He stayed there for more than two months and recorded what he witnessed as follows: “Around dawn, we, a group of about ten monks, suddenly saw a magical lamp appear in the eastern sky of the valley. At first, the light was only about the size of a vase, but then it gradually grew to the size of a house. We were truly shaken by this sight, hurriedly knelt down to bow and loudly recited the name of Bodhisattva Manjusri. Then another lamp appeared even closer to us.”

The role of praising the Wonderful Dharma of Bodhisattva Manjushri can be found in the sutra: "Manjushri speaks about the Inconceivable Realm of the Buddha." This is a declaration of the bodhisattva ideal made by a great bodhisattva representing wisdom. The goal and ideal of the bodhisattva path is not merely to transcend the cycle of birth and death and reach the state of Nirvana, but to accomplish Buddhahood in order to save sentient beings.

Especially, His role in praising the wondrous Dharma was exceptionally highlighted in the "Vimalakīrti Sūtra." Venerable Vimalakīrti was a lay practitioner, yet he practiced and attained realization, possessing profound secret conduct that even the great disciples of the Buddha could not match. Desiring to save sentient beings, He manifested in the city of Vaiśālī, using boundless wealth to guide the poor, maintaining pure precepts to guide those who break them, practicing patience to guide the angry, and applying great diligence to guide the lazy. Even though He appeared in white robes while maintaining the pure precepts of a monk, and though living as a layperson, He was not attached to worldly life, manifestHe currently has a wife and children, yet he often practices pure and tranquil conduct. Even though he wears precious clothes, he adorns himself with a noble demeanor. Though he eats and drinks in accordance with worldly ways, he takes Zen delight as his flavor. Or when he goes to places of gambling and singing, he adapts according to circumstances. Everyone he meets shows respect and offers homage. One day, wishing to create an opportunity to propagate the Dharma and benefit sentient beings, he took the pretext of being ill to find a chance to expound the teachings to sentient beings. The Buddha, knowing clearly the true 'illness' of him, successively requested the great disciples to visit Venerable Vimalakirti on his behalf. However, all of the Buddha’s great disciples of the past had been questioned by the wealthy householder Vimalakirti about the mind's Dharma and their knowledge, yet not a single one was able to answer.His words flowed smoothly before the profound Buddhist knowledge and flawless eloquence of Mr., so all were fearful and declined. Some typical examples include:

One day, Ananda took a bowl to the house of a Brahmin to request milk for the World-Honored One when He was sick. At that time, Vimalakirti came and asked him:

- O Ananda! Why are you holding a bowl and standing here so early? Ananda replied:

- Respected layman! The World-Honored One is slightly ill and needs cow's milk, so I came here.

Layman Vimalakirti said:

- Stop, stop! Ananda, do not speak like that. The Tathagata's body is a diamond body, all evil has been completely eradicated, all goodness is complete, there are no more illnesses, no more suffering. Ananda, be silent about this. Do not slander the Tathagata, do not let others hear these words. Ananda, the Wheel-Turning Sage King has only a little merit but still does not get sick, let alone the Tathagata who has limitless cultivated merit, superior in every way. Ananda, if outsiders hear this, they will think: How can we call the Buddha a Teacher? Unable to cure one’s own sickness but able to cure others’ sickness? Ananda, know that the Tathagata’s body is the Dharma body, not a body of flesh and desire. The Buddha is the World-Honored One who transcends the threerealm. The Buddha's body is free from defilements, all defilements have been cleansed, the Buddha's body is beyond action, not subject to numerical counting. If the Buddha's body is like this, what sickness could there be? Ananda remained silent and went home.

Another day, the wealthy layman Vimalakīrti met Ananda. He asked:

- Dear Ananda! You are a son of the Buddha, having given up your royal position to renounce the world for the Dharma. What are the benefits of such renunciation? Ananda replied:

- The benefits of renunciation are exactly in accordance with the Dharma. The wealthy layman Vimalakīrti added:

- Hey Rahula! You should not speak of the benefits of the merit of ordination. Why? It is without benefit, without merit, that one truly ordains. When seen from the perspective of conditioned phenomena, one might speak of benefits and merit. But ordination belongs to the realm of unconditioned phenomena, and in the unconditioned there is no benefit or merit. Rahula! Ordination does not involve comparisons, it is free from the sixty-two views. In Nirvana, it is the enjoyment of the wise, the practice of the saints, it subdues evil beings, delivers the five paths, purifies the five senses, attains the five powers, establishes the five faculties, causes no trouble to others, avoids all kinds of evil, overcomes the non-Buddhists, transcends false fame, escapes the mire of the world, and is not subject to attachment,selflessness and self-possessions, having nothing to receive, a mind undisturbed, wishing to protect and remember all sentient beings, according with meditation, free from sins. Only if it is like this can one truly be a monk.

Finally, only Manjushri Bodhisattva represented the Buddha in visiting the sick householder Vimalakirti. Accompanying Manjushri were 8,000 Bodhisattvas, 500 Śrāvakas, and hundreds of thousands of heavenly beings to witness a debate on the Dharma between these two outstanding figures.

Vimalakirti asked: What is the seed of the Tathagata? Manjushri Bodhisattva replied:

- Having the nature of a Tathāgata seed, ignorance and sensual desire are seeds, greed, hatred, and delusion are seeds, the four inversionisms are seeds, the six sense bases are seeds, the seven consciousnesses are seeds, the eight wrong dharmas are seeds, the nine afflictions are seeds, the eighteen good paths are seeds. In short, the sixty-two views and all afflictions are all seeds of Buddhahood.

Vimalakīrti asked: Why?

Mañjuśrī replied:

- If one who sees the impermanence in its true aspect enters the proper position, they can no longer generate the mind of supreme enlightenment. It is like a high mound where a lotus cannot grow, but in the low, muddy ground, the lotus can grow. Similarly, one who sees the impermanent dharmas in the proper position can no longer give rise to Buddhadharma; it is only in the mud of afflictions that sentient beings give rise to Buddhadharma. Therefore, be aware that all afflictions are the seeds of the Tathagata; just as if one does not descend into the great ocean, one cannot obtain the priceless jewel.

Likewise, without entering the ocean of afflictions, one cannot attain the jewel of All-Encompassing Wisdom.

We worship Manjushri Bodhisattva to turn toward the innate wisdom within us. Ignorance and desire have caused us to dive into the cycle of birth and death, enduring countless layers of suffering. Let us awaken to return to our inherent wisdom and use the sword of wisdom to cut through the net of craving and rise above the deep sea of suffering. Yes, only wisdom has the power to save us from the cycle of karmic retribution. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva is a shining example of altruism; we must use this sword of wisdom to liberate all beings from the enemy of afflictions, from the poisonous snake of greed, anger, and ignorance. Only by practicing in this way can weworthy of worship is the Bodhisattva Manjushri, holding a sword, wearing armor, sitting on the back of a lion.

Merit in its intrinsic nature is not obtained through giving or offering. Therefore, it is said that fortune is not equal to merit, and giving alms cannot compare with reciting sutras.

tieu_de: KARMA - WHERE DOES KILLING LIFE LEAD TO?
tom_tat: One of the basic ethical principles of Buddhists is not to harm or kill living beings. Members of the Buddhist Family youth groups, when they first enter the temple, have memorized the phrase 'I care for people and animals.'
noi_dung:
KARMA – WHERE DOES TAKING LIFE LEAD?

One of the fundamental ethical principles of Buddhists is not to harm or kill living beings. Members of the Buddhist Family Youth Group, when they first enter the temple, have memorized the phrase “I love people and animals.” Not only do they refrain from killing, but Buddhists also cultivate a compassionate heart and always practice releasing life to save beings.

If someone creates the karma of killing many living beings, they will certainly suffer the retribution of bodily weakness, many illnesses, a short lifespan, and both people and animals will avoid them because they constantly emit dangerous, cold murderous energy. According to the wisdom of the World-Honored One, those who commit much killing, especially those engaged in hunting, butchering, or selling meat, not only lack blessings in health and longevity but also endure the retribution of poverty and misery.

"Once, the Buddha was in the kingdom of Sāvatthī, in the Jīvaka forest, at the Cāpāla Grove. At that time, the World-Honored One said to the monks:

- Do you teachers see anyone who kills a buffalo because of creating this karma later being able to ride a cart, horse, or mighty elephant?

The monks replied:

- No, World-Honored One!

The World-Honored One said:

- Excellent! Monks! I have also not seen, nor heard of anyone who slaughters a cow, and then rides in a chariot, on a horse, or on an elephant. This is because I have not seen anyone who slaughters a cow obtain wealth and then ride in a chariot, on a horse, or on an elephant; there is no such reason. What do you think, monks! Have you seen anyone who kills goats, kills pigs, hunts deer, and after committing such evil deeds, acquires wealth and then rides in a chariot, on a horse, or on an elephant?

The monks replied:

- No, World-Honored One!

The World-Honored One said:

- How wonderful! Monks! I also have not seen, nor heard of anyone who kills goats or slaughters living beings, and then earns the right to ride a chariot, horse, or large elephant—this is completely unreasonable. Monks! If you see someone who kills oxen and rides a chariot or horse, know that this is a merit from a previous life, not merit from this life, all of it being the result of deeds from the past life. Monks, if you see someone who kills goats and is able to ride a chariot or horse, know that this person is reaping the fruit of merit sown in a previous life. Why is that? Because the killing mind does not diminish. Why so? If someone associates with evil people, delights in killing living beings, and accumulates hellish karma, then if they are reborn as a human, their lifespan will be very short. If there is someone who delights in stealing and sowsThe hellish crime is like that of the butcher who buys cheap and sells dear, deceiving people, not following the Right Dharma. The person who kills the ox is also the same, because of a killing mind causing this sin; they are not allowed to ride carts, horses, or large elephants. Therefore, the monks should cultivate loving-kindness towards all sentient beings. In this way, monks should learn this.

At that time, the monks, having heard the Buddha's teaching, were glad and gladly complied.

(Saṃyutta Nikāya A-hàm, Volume II, Chapter 36, Listening to the Dharma)

Observing the lives of hunters, butchers, and meat sellers, we can clearly see the teachings that the Buddha gave above. Due to the heavy karma of killing, over time their careers quickly deteriorate, they suffer from continuous illness and accidents, their families collapse—in general, they lose everything. But that’s not all; many people, before dying, also exhibit severe near-death karma, writhing, screaming, convulsing, covered in blood, with their souls scattered, like the animals they had previously killed.

In this Dharma talk, a noteworthy point is that, besides those who carry heavy karma from killing and then immediately face the consequences, some people experience retribution a bit later, so they remain wealthy. Our ordinary human perception cannot fully understand this, leading to doubts about cause and effect. They still commit evil acts, yet seem unharmed! Some even consider trying to follow their path to become rich quickly. In reality, these people are able to be stable and prosperous despite doing evil because they are relying on remaining leftover merit from past blessings. When that old merit is completely exhausted and the karmic results of their crimes manifest, they will immediately fall into misfortune.

Karma is a very complex process, with three times: immediate result, next life result, and distant result. Becoming wealthy by doing evil, according to the World-Honored One, is "absolutely impossible." A Buddhist disciple, deeply believing in karma, always cultivates a heart of loving-kindness, never harms living beings, and thereby accumulates merit, increasing both fortune and longevity.

(Quang Tan)

tieu_de: MARRIAGE LIKE HELL (Reincarnation Is Really Scary, Previous Life Was a Wolf, This Life Is a Wife, Please Read Through, Determined
tom_tat: One time, about a dozen of us laypeople wanted to go to Wutai Mountain to pay respects to Venerable Dhyana Dharma. Brother Kim, the director of the printing house, volunteered to drive us there. Although he did not believe in Buddhism, he was the type
noi_dung:
MARRIAGE LIKE HELL (Reincarnation Is Truly Frightening, Last Life Was a Wolf, This Life Is a Wife, Please Read Through, Determined

One time, more than ten laypeople and I wanted to go to Mount Ngũ Đài to pay respects to Venerable Diệu Pháp. Mr. Kim, the printing house director, volunteered to drive us there. Although he did not believe in Buddhism, he was the type of person who was wholeheartedly devoted to his friends. He drove his new, luxurious car himself, taking us on the long journey. Moreover, there were three reasons that made him enthusiastic:

• First, he wanted to help his friends.

• Second, he had heard rumors of miraculous things about Venerable Diệu Pháp, so he was also curious.

• At that time, I had never been to the scenic spot of Wudang Mountain, so I also wanted to go and see it clearly.

Unfortunately, on the first day when we accompanied the Venerable to seek teachings, Kim perhaps was too tired from driving and went to sleep completely.

The next morning, a few laypersons once again approached the Venerable Master to inquire about the causes of their illnesses. The Master patiently explained, telling them which animals they had killed before, even how they had killed them, how they had eaten them, down to what they had stolen in the past, how much they had used, and how much remained and where it was kept... each detail was recounted very clearly. Witnessing this truth, Mr. Kim was completely shocked. He kept staring with wide eyes, mouth agape, attentively observing. He appeared extremely excited and anxious, and several times he wanted to say something but refrained.

In the afternoon, he came to find me, expressing his wish to go alone that evening to the Venerable Master's ceremony to ask a few questions. Being hesitant, he asked me to seek permission in advance on his behalf. With the Master's approval, at seven o'clock in the evening, I led him to the guest room.

I only saw Mr. Kim respectfully kneel before the Venerable Master, clasp his hands together, and solemnly bow three times in ceremony. It seemed that he had been convinced by the Master and sincerely believed in the Buddhist teachings. (Yesterday, when we met the Master and performed the ritual with Him, he only stood outside watching.)

After sitting down, Mr. Kim, with a sorrowful face, recounted in a mournful manner:

My wife, Xiao Jie, and I have been married for 12 years and have a 10-year-old son. Before marrying Xiao Jie, I had feelings for a childhood friend and neighbor named Xiao Li. We were childhood sweethearts and had planned to marry each other. At that time, I met Xiao Jie. In terms of looks, job, and family background, Xiao Jie was far inferior to Xiao Li, yet I don’t understand what spell or charm I was under; I fell in love with Xiao Jie at first sight. Despite the opposition of friends and relatives, I stubbornly insisted on marrying Xiao Jie.

Just three days after getting married, there were still guests visiting the house, and my parents were busy helping to entertain them.

At this moment, two friends came in, greeting and congratulating me with hands clasped, while laughingly saying:

"Kim, I feel really bad, you got married without telling us, were you afraid we’d drink too much congratulatory alcohol?"

I hurriedly stepped forward to welcome them and replied with a smile:

"I am really sorry! Because the marriage was arranged suddenly, and I was busy, I couldn't inform you in time. I hope you can forgive me!"

At this moment, Tiểu Khiết brought out some water to offer. The friends joked:

"Wow! Mantra Kim! I have to scold you for not giving us a heads-up! Turned out your aunt is so beautiful, were you afraid we… might take her away?"

She laughed heartily and said:

"Beautiful? What beauty! She’s so ugly! I’m even regretting it right now!"

Before I could finish speaking, Xiao Jie suddenly turned around, her eyes wide open, red with fury, and a fierce glare; she slapped me twice. At that moment, I saw sparks in my eyes, everyone in the house stood frozen, and the newlywed wife was both crying and making a scene, causing a big commotion, absolutely refusing to let it go. I was slapped so hard that I felt dizzy, anger welled up, and I just wanted to tear her apart. But as I raised my hand, I lowered it, reason reminding me: "I shouldn’t do this and make the neighbors around laugh at me, I shouldn’t upset my parents."

Because the two friends felt guilty and apologized, and everyone gathered to give advice, I had to suppress my anger and force a smile to look cheerful.

For the past 12 years, we have constantly argued and fought, made a fuss, and demanded divorce six times, including two times when Tiểu Khiết packed her things and left. But whenever we were about to go through the divorce procedures, relatives would gather to intervene, making the divorce fail. This made my heart always painful. Both of us want a divorce, but we always encounter situations where parting is unsuccessful. Isn't that strange? I ask Master to kindly instruct me.”

While Mr. Kim was speaking, Venerable Thich Dieu Phap gently closed his eyes as if listening, yet also as if thinking.

Now he looked at Mr. Kim and asked:

Did you take your son to the zoo, and enjoy watching the peacocks very much?

Yes, that's right. He thought the peacock spreading its tail was very beautiful.

The Venerable smiled and said:

“Three generations ago, he was born in a small village at the foot of a mountain, a manly man. He often went up the mountain to chop wood and became acquainted with a peacock on the mountain. Every time they met, he would often give it something to eat; the peacock would play with him, he loved the peacock very much and the peacock was also attached to him. There is affection and there is feeling!

In the next life (the second life), he was still born as a man, but his spouse was reincarnated as a woman, and because of feelings from the previous life, they became husband and wife. However, since the wife had just been reborn from an animal life, although she had a human appearance, her animal instincts remained, so the couple often quarreled loudly. When he became enraged, he could not avoid hitting his wife; she was a woman and could not resist him, of course harboring resentment in her heart.

In a later life, he was reincarnated as a man, dressed like a martial artist. One day, he was pushing a wooden-wheeled cart up a mountain when he suddenly encountered a wolf. He immediately used a metal chain to strike it, and soon the wolf was defeated. He quickly tied its neck with the chain, tightening it with all his strength; the wolf struggled for a while before becoming motionless. He left the wolf lying there and pushed the cart away.

Later, the wolf woke up, but due to its injuries, its nerves were damaged, leaving its limbs paralyzed. It howled, calling other wolves to drag it back to its den, and gradually it died.”

Venerable Thien Su Dieu Phap, having finished telling the story, noticed Mr. Kim's skeptical face and immediately asked:

On your wife's neck, there are faint white lines, the scars are scattered without any order, right?

Hearing that, Mr. Kim was shocked, his face changed color, and he replied:

Yes! That's right!

The Venerable, seeing his pale face, spoke gently:

Don't be so tense. Every person's physical form, five senses, appearance, even fingerprints and moles... are carried from the time in the womb, including habits, character, beauty, ugliness, white, black... all are related to the karma created in previous lives.

Because he is normally kind-hearted and likes to do good deeds to help others, even though he himself does not believe in Buddha, this time he still wants to volunteer to help people go up the mountain to worship Buddha and listen to the Dharma. Thanks to this, today he has the opportunity to hear me explain how to resolve karma. When I say 'resolve,' it means there is a method to neutralize it. He should not keep insisting that the person sleeping next to him is a wolf. Because his wife is truly a human being now!

Each of us has been reincarnated in the six realms since time without beginning; is there a realm we haven't passed through? In the past, even the Buddha manifested as a stag. I want to ask you another thing: will you help the girls buy tickets to visit the temple? (In Mainland China, visitors to famous scenic spots have to buy entrance tickets, and the fees are managed by the government).

Director Kim looked very surprised and said:

Yes, yes. Those are some unemployed female workers who wanted to enter the temple to worship Buddha but didn't have enough money to buy tickets. Luckily, I happened to pass by at that time, saw it, and helped. How could Master know about this trivial matter?

If you want others not to know! Unless you don't do it. Whether doing good or evil, the principle is the same.

So… anything bad I did… You know everything?

All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Heaven, Earth, Ghosts, and Spirits… know and see everything! That is why the Buddha advises us not to do evil, but to do only good deeds.

So… does that mean later Xiao Jie will take my life?

The monk spoke slowly:

"Wait until you are over 40 years old, one night, you come home, because of a trivial matter, you have a loud argument with your wife and you will hit her. Then you go to sleep. After a while of crying, the wife's wolfish heart will erupt. So she goes to find an electric cable, folds it in half, then wraps one end around your neck, threads the other end through the loop around your neck, and ties it to the bed leg. Then she grips the electric cable firmly with both hands, uses her foot to push on the bed post, and pulls hard, tightening it around your neck. You struggle for a while and then become motionless. The wife will loosen her grip to rest for a bit, then continue, pulling and tightening the cord while scolding you… unexpectedly, you wake up, open your eyes… but from your neck downward"fell unconscious, since then he has been paralyzed”…

Hearing this, Kim's face turned pale with not a trace of blood. He quickly knelt before Master Dieu Phap, panic-stricken, and said:

Master, please save me! About 5-6 years ago, I once went to Bách Hóa company. On the way back, as I reached the main gate, I saw someone pushing a wheelchair toward the gate. I was extremely shocked to discover that the person sitting in the wheelchair… was me (but older), looking around 40 years old! I quickly tried to calm myself and looked again, only to see that it wasn’t me. Then I looked again, and it was me! This strange phenomenon made me think for several days. At that time, I thought: "Could it be that I am seeing a premonition that when I am over 40, I will become paralyzed?"

At that time, I racked my brains but couldn't understand. Now, after hearing Master tell this story, I understand and believe—it seems I really was experiencing that disaster. Please, Master, please save me, take me as your disciple! From now on, I want to be a follower of the Buddha. Otherwise, even if I earn a lot of money, what use would it be?

Venerable Diệu Pháp smiled and said:

Stand up. The matter of taking refuge can wait until it is announced at the temple. As for helping you overcome this disaster, the key lies within yourself.

First, you must repent for the karma of quarrelling, beating people in the previous life, and the fault of having killed a wolf. Now you can go to the main hall to worship the Buddha and repent.

After returning home, you must set up a Buddha hall right in your house. If it is not convenient, it is also okay not to set one up, because Buddha is in the heart. But the important thing is that every day, when you have free time, try to spare some time to recite a sutra, "The Universal Gate of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva", which takes about more than half an hour to complete one cycle. Depending on your own time, you can recite a few cycles each day. During recitation, you must purify your mind, focus fully, and sincerely dedicate merits to the "wolf of a past life" whom you harmed, helping it increase blessings, connect with the Buddha’s path, and eliminate the wolf’s heart and the heart of anger and resentment towards you.

Gradually you will see your wife change, becoming more loving and kind towards you; the family will be harmonious, and the tragedies that were bound to happen will no longer occur.

This is called "the scene changes according to the mind," meaning that your mind can change the situation, causing the family's atmosphere to be transformed for the better. You must cultivate and purify your mind, maintain purity in body, speech, and thought to transform negative energy into benign energy, transform afflictions into Bodhi, because "all phenomena are created by the mind."

After you leave this place, from now on you should often keep close company with virtuous friends. With your friends, you can use your personal experiences and your own practice to teach the Dharma, guiding them toward the right path. When free, you should read the Buddhist scriptures, study deeply to understand thoroughly, and open your own mind.

Normally, wherever you go, whether walking or driving, or when you have free time, you should frequently recite the name of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara.

In a society filled with riots and struggles like today, one should not scheme to gain excessive benefits, nor pursue unjust wealth. One must know that "harming others is harming oneself."

From now on, definitely do not do anything wrong that offends your conscience. When working and interacting, be honest. Taxes should be paid on time, and only actions that benefit the country and the people should be undertaken. If this is done, your factory will surely remain stable and not fail in the business world.

Since you want me to be your Master, I transmit the Buddha's teachings to you. You must respectfully observe and follow them to be a true disciple of the Buddha; by doing so, you will receive protection from the Heavenly Dragons and blessings from all the Bodhisattvas.

If you are negligent and refuse to uphold the precepts, then you are not a disciple of the Buddha, even if you have a certificate of having taken refuge. At present, it will be difficult to receive the Buddha's blessings, and in the future, you will fall into the evil realms. I have explained all this; do you understand everything I have said?

Kim respectfully listened attentively and hurriedly said:

Master Bach! I understand everything clearly. I have never smoked or drunk alcohol, and I don’t even use tea. From today onwards, I swear to strictly observe the precepts and completely abstain from eating meat….

I think there is no need to continue telling the rest of the story. Currently, Director Kim's family is harmonious, the factory work is thriving and extremely busy, and the brand has become trusted and very famous.

(Excerpt from Báo Ứng Hiện Đời)

His 48 great vows are similar to the 48 great vows of Amitabha Buddha, and he made an additional 49th vow (quoted verbatim): 'For all who have ever seen my face, heard my teachings, or even heard my name, I must help them attain the Western Paradise.
