tieu_de: WHERE DOES THE GLOBAL ATMOSPHERE OF DARKNESS COME FROM?
tom_tat: When sentient beings have great merit, the true Dharma is strong and Mara is weak. When sentient beings have little merit, Mara is strong and the true Dharma is weak. Wherever there are people who practice sincerely, there the disasters are fewer and smaller. If there are many people
noi_dung:
WHERE DOES THE WORLD'S DARK ATMOSPHERE COME FROM?

When sentient beings have great merit, the right Dharma is strong, and evil is weak. When sentient beings have little merit, evil is strong, and the right Dharma is weak.

Wherever there are people sincerely practicing cultivation, there the disasters are fewer and smaller. If many people practice cultivation together in one place, their collective strength can transform negative energy into auspicious energy.

The Sages of the past always reprimanded themselves. Unlike people today, who never admit their own mistakes and always look for faults in others.

For those who have just developed the aspiration to practice, the biggest obstacle to diligent practice is: the desire of lust, boys being attached to girls, girls being attached to boys. This is the most fundamental issue.

A practitioner who fears solitude cannot practice.

If one does not eliminate lust, then even if one renounces the world and practices for eighty-four thousand great eons, one cannot achieve success. Therefore, this point is very crucial.

When observing a person practicing the Tao, where do you look? You look at whether they uphold precepts or not. If they do not uphold the precepts, they are definitely a demon. If they uphold the precepts, especially strictly, then they truly are a disciple of the Buddha.

If you want to know whether that realm is real or fake, whether the person is a Bodhisattva or a demon, you can look from this point: You look to see whether they have lustful desires. If they do have lust, then they are indeed a demon. If they do not have it, then they truly are a Bodhisattva.

If one does not eliminate passionate desire and ignorance, ultimately one cannot escape the sea of desire and birth-and-death.

To practice cultivation, one must cultivate with a heart like a newborn baby: The mind is free from any attachments. One must be like a child, returning from old to young (returning to the original source), meaning your mind should be like that of a child, naturally innocent and lively, without any laziness, slackness, desire for competition, or sense of self versus others. It is also like: If there has never been anything there before, then worldly dust has nothing to cling to.

In life, if we do something wrong, it is like living in hell. Doing things that are not morally right, having selfish intentions for personal gain, is already being in hell. Always finding joy in this thing and that, getting angry over this and that, always using emotions to solve problems, is also like being in hell.

If you are full of benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom, your face will show a kind of virtuous appearance, a kind of merit.

Good people have a bright white aura. Evil people have a dark black aura. Therefore, doing good or evil naturally appears in one’s appearance. You can deceive people, but you cannot deceive Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, or spirits.

You must definitely memorize the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. Not only can you transcend birth and death, but you can also avoid demonic calamities, disasters, and save sentient beings.

Homosexuality is an evil desire, contrary to natural disposition, morals, and physiology.

Romance and love affairs are sources of misfortune. If one can cut off desires, eliminating the karma of romantic attachment will bring relief. When love is deep, karma is also very heavy. Hence the saying: When karma is gone, love is not; that is the true Buddha. When karma is heavy and attachment intense, that is the ordinary person.

Because of lustful desires, evil deeds arise in the world. If you can perform good deeds, purify yourself, and refrain from lewd actions, that is in fact practicing virtuous conduct.

Where do troubles in life come from? They come from the fact that people are all a little selfish. Where does selfishness originate? It starts from the place of desire and thoughts (the intention to crave and lust).

When practicing the path, never be greedy for anything. Do not be greedy for good things, and even less for bad things. Take a calm mind as your place of practice. Always remain calm, desiring nothing. Whenever there is greed, it is a mistake.

If you sincerely read and chant the scriptures, there will often be celestial beings scattering flowers, pleasant fragrances spreading everywhere, and ghosts and spirits respectfully offering homage.

Most of the education nowadays, although teaching students, in fact focuses on selling books (collecting tuition fees) to make a profit. They teach how to obtain high positions, earn a lot of money, become a famous person or the best in the world. That is, they do not teach children the basic ethics of being human. Instead, they keep teaching children to compete for fame and gain. This is putting the branch before the root, going against morality. Acting against morality is truly an enormous mistake.

If you do not listen to lectures or teachings of the Dharma and only bury yourself in practice, that is called blind and disorderly cultivation. Even if you practice for countless lifetimes, you still cannot succeed.

Because the mind is not peaceful, we need external music to help harmonize our inner state. If your mind is always calm and peaceful, filled with an atmosphere of harmonious serenity, then that is true music.

If all day long you do not waste words, do not think of trivial matters; you regulate your mind to be serene and natural, without binding, without strangeness, without self-interest, without right and wrong, then isn't that music?

Dharma Words of Venerable Thien Master Tuyen Hoa

Namo Amitabha Buddha

Source: An Si Complete Book

tieu_de: A TRUE KARMIC STORY ABOUT THE VENDETTA OF SNAKES
tom_tat: A story from Quang Tu's friend respectfully shared with you to further strengthen faith in karma and the Buddha's teachings .... ------------------------------
noi_dung:
A TRUE KARMIC STORY ABOUT THE REVENGE OF SNAKES

The story from Quang Tu's friend respectfully shares with everyone to increase faith in karma and the Buddha's teachings....

------------------------------

.......Dear fellow practitioners!

My name is Hue Van, I have known about Buddhism and have been a vegetarian for over 3 years. Today I would like to tell a true story that happened in my family in the past time!

PART 1: KILLING A SNAKE 🐍

That day was April 10, 2020. My mother was working in the garden and accidentally saw a snake's 🐍 nest. She was very scared, afraid that it was a venomous snake, so she panicked and ran out to call the neighbor. He came to catch it, and then saw that it was a snake that was incubating eggs. He caught it (it seems he killed it), and when my mother was using a sickle to clear the weeds, not knowing, she accidentally cut two eggs (inside, there were already baby snakes forming).

Stories that happen like that are considered normal by everyone, very normal in everyday life, nothing special! So my mother also did not tell me about it and I knew nothing about that matter!

Yet, that night I dreamt, I saw a woman with the appearance of my mother standing by the neighbor's house, then turning back to our house, scolding me, cursing the kids. The little ones were huddled together playing in the yard. In the dream, my mother scolded fiercely, her face was frowning with anger, her teeth clenched tightly, spitting while swearing profusely. She cursed many terrible things, including something like, 'If you guys walk around staring, I’ll kill you all…' I was standing there playing with the kids and couldn’t understand why my mother was suddenly scolding? Why was she standing by the neighbor’s house looking over?

Does our family curse like that???

Then the kids were playing with each other, suddenly I didn't see the second child anywhere (she's less than 2 years old now). At this moment, her mother had also returned to the yard at some point, no longer standing near the other house, looking as calm as usual, as if completely unrelated to the scolding incident just now!!?!?!?! So my mother and I looked around for the child and saw that she had fallen into the pond and drowned sometime ago. Her naked body was lying motionless under the edge of the pond as if sleeping (the water was so clear that it was easy to see). I was so scared that I immediately regained consciousness! 😳

This morning, I was performing my Buddhist rituals as usual, and in my heart, there was a bit of unease and worry about last night's dream, when my mother came in to sit and also bowed to Buddha mumbling something. Then she told me, “Yesterday when I was working in the garden, there was a snake, and I was so scared I called the neighbor to catch it. He probably took it home to kill it. And as for the eggs in the nest, I accidentally hit one or two with the sickle while cutting the grass. Normally, I wouldn’t think anything of it or see anything, but since yesterday until now, every time I think about that incident, my mother gets completely horrified, with goosebumps all over her body.In the past, if there was killing, my mom never felt this way (proving that this mother snake had very high intuition)...my mom said that you, a Buddhist practitioner, should perform the rite of liberation for the snake to help my mom!

I am extremely scared because since the day I learned the Buddha's teachings, I do not dare to kill even a mosquito, while snakes are known to hold grudges for a long time. I told my mother to take the snake eggs back to their old place, and then I kept mumbling day and night to apologize to them. I become even more frightened when I think about last night's dream...

PART 2: NIGHTMARES 🙀

Since knowing about the snake incident and linking the dreams together, I felt that they must be related. It's bad, because my mother comes from a family of scattered snakes, I don't know what to do about this!

Recalling the dreams that lasted a week, each dream was a few days apart:

1- On that very night, I dreamed that the second child drowned, and the woman with a spitting mouth and gnashing teeth was indeed a terrifying image, harboring hatred for snakes.

2- A few days later, my mother was half-awake, half dreaming, feeling that the gate was locked but kept being pulled outside by a ghost, unable to lock the gate even though she couldn't see anyone. At that time, I hadn't slept yet and saw my mother mumbling in her sleep, so I called her awake, and she told me this.

3- A few days later, I had another dream about the whole family going out and the older child getting lost. I couldn't find them in the tourist amusement area. In the distance, there was the sea with roaring waves, and many people were swimming and diving. I went to look for the child and entered the management building of that tourist area, where I saw a police chief sitting and making a record, questioning a male criminal. I asked him that I wanted to find my lost child, but he just looked at me without speaking because he was busy dealing with that male criminal. I went into an inner room where another police officer was sitting inside, guarding the door and controlling the engine, in front of the door.I wanted to step into that room which had a kind of engine shaped like this ⚙️ but looked scarier, with sparser and sharper teeth. It was spinning, and if I wanted to go in, the security guard had to let me stop it, otherwise I would be pulled into it and fall down below. When I stepped onto the part with the engine, the security guard immediately made me stop. I told the guard that I wanted to go inside to find my child. The guard said through the glass door that there was nothing in there and asked me to go out so I wouldn't get caught in the engine. So I went back outside to continue searching. In my dream, I still saw a woman.The child tried to plot to harm me, but somehow I knew about that intention, so I quietly went somewhere else.

4- One other day, I dreamed of a woman with a very sinister, menacing face, wandering around aimlessly, throwing some clumps onto the table (maybe eggs???) and then leaving in a way that seemed like she wanted to lure me into something I didn’t agree to. That person schemed to harm me, grabbed my legs and scratched, causing a long wound that bled like the image of a long snake. Does it mean that the snake in my dream represents an injury from being bitten or scratched?!!!

Partly worried, partly because that child has a very strong conscience, feeling pity for the snake's mother, which is very difficult, being peaceful and then suddenly witnessing the slaughter like that, imagining if it were me, it would also be very heartbreaking, experiencing through two dreams of myself losing two children, one drowned and one lost! I have been contemplating for several days, asking myself what should I do?!?!?!!!

I want to pray for the Snake and ask for forgiveness for my mother!

But I think my own practice is still weak, so what ability do I have to perform a liberation ceremony??? Well, just sincerely do it! As far as I can go, that's fine, and it also somewhat eases my inner remorse! I just hope the Snake Family can return to a peaceful realm.

🙏 PART 3: LIBERATION CEREMONY FOR THE SNAKE AND THE UNEXPECTED MIRACLE OF THE DHARMA PLATFORM

April 23, 2020 (more than 10 days after the mother snake was killed).

I prepared fruits, flowers, and offerings for Buddha, bought an animal for the release ceremony to transfer merits, and recited the Amitabha Sutra to pray for my mother Rắn's soul. It's called a ritual ceremony, but it was just like my daily remembrance practice. However, that day I prepared the incense and offerings more meticulously and fully; with sincere devotion, my heart was heavy with guilt, carrying sorrow and compassion for Rắn's family. I felt as if it were entirely my fault—sincerely asking Rắn to forgive my mother. I spoke to my mother to sit and participate in the ritual together, with wholehearted dedication.repent and apologize to the Snake.

When I was reading the sutra, reciting Buddha's name, and bowing in repentance… near the end of the session, I saw my mother spinning around, nodding her head, and her mouth was reciting NAM MÔ A DI ĐÀ PHẬT, NAM MÔ A DI ĐÀ PHẬT… after a few breaths, she seemed tired. I realized someone had possessed her. I continued reading the sutra, repenting, performing the dedication of merit, and then I turned to ask who had possessed my mother! Actually, seeing the spirit enter so suddenly made me very surprised and worried because I've heard that spirits are not to be taken lightly; they say nonsensical things and can overwhelm both my mother’s and my body! But now I don’t really know what to do, so I just kept asking.So! Let's see who the spirit is, see what they need! After all, the Spirit was once a person too, so at this point, let's just talk normally and see how it goes!

At that time, my mother had a raised face, gritted her teeth, and said, just like in a dream, I guessed that perhaps it was the Snake Spirit possessing you!

I often heard that spirits are easily persuaded (difficult to handle like a ghost), so I "flattered" it by praising the Spirit for knowing how to chant Buddha, chanting Bodhisattvas skillfully, to ease the tension and also to make the spirit more devoted and skilled in chanting Buddha, seeing the spirit nod in response and appear more agreeable!

- I said: Spirit, concentrate fully on chanting Buddha, alright? Are you the Snake Spirit, mother?

- Vong nodded and smiled lightly: Yes, that's right!

The mother snake said, "Actually, I hate your mother, hate your family very much. I knew that you practiced and recited the Buddha’s name but didn’t inform others, and you called someone to kill me. Your mother’s strike hit two of my eggs... but anyway, I also know your mother didn’t do it intentionally. Because your mother was too scared, she called a neighbor to catch me!” (Meanwhile, the snake said that its child also revealed this and apologized because the mother inadvertently caused this situation out of fear and confusion, asking the snake for forgiveness. This is also due to the karma from a past life: the mother snake also had a human body but carried too much deep-seated anger and hatred, so she was reborn as a snake. Now she hopes the snake...let go of everything, wholeheartedly recite Buddha's name so that He may take you to a peaceful realm…)

The mother snake said, "You foolishly cut the grass and accidentally hit my eggs, but you also knew how to cover them up so that the old place could allow them to hatch safely instead of throwing them away. Thanks to your family, my children were able to hear the scriptures, know how to recite Buddha's name, and know how to repent; therefore, I understand that it is due to my life's predestined karma, so I forgive your family. Oh, in that place (the garden where the French cemetery is established) there are many karmic enemies and spirits who listen carefully, and because of that, many can be saved because they understand Cause and Effect! We are very grateful to your family, so I forgive the wrongdoing."

Mother... oh, today the memorial ceremony was performed for many wronged spirits and many souls, so many… I recite Namo Amitabha Buddha, asking Buddha to save us, to let us go to the Western Pure Land…

🙏 I would like to tell more about the Buddhist altar I placed in the garden at the cemetery👣

My family has a small garden plot right in the old cemetery area. I heard from my grandparents and parents that place used to be a shooting range; many people, including the enemy soldiers, our army, and civilians fleeing died there, so the people established it as a cemetery since that time. With a sincere heart, I wish to offer long-life offerings, offering to the spirits there to hear the Dharma, understand Cause and Effect, and ultimately sincerely chant Buddha's name to be reborn in a good realm to relieve suffering. The spirits and demons in the realms are very miserable, beyond description! So, in November of the yearIn 2019, I bought a Dharma lecture machine powered by solar energy and copied the Earth Treasury Sutra, Amitabha Sutra, Ten Good Deeds Sutra, and recited the Buddha! These 4 files play 24/24, all day and night without stopping!

Today I write down this true story of mine, hoping everyone will believe even more deeply in KARMA, believing that the spiritual world is real! We should not foolishly think that just because we cannot see the spiritual world, it does not exist. Everyone should stop killing living beings; the karma of killing manifests in many forms such as an unstable life, encountering misfortune, family discord, illness, and pain... all arise from the cause of killing living beings.

🙏NAMO AMITABHA BUDDHA🙇

The content of the dharma practice should revolve around texts such as: Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra of Original Vows, Amitabha Sutra, Ten Wholesome Karma Sutra, Buddha Recitation... as in the link I uploaded above, you can download it.

🦉 It is advisable to place the Dharma altar in places with a lot of spiritual energy such as: cemeteries, the graves of loved ones, places with high concentrations of spirits... Because in such areas, many ancestral spirits may come to listen, bringing great benefits to them.

🐌 If chanted at home, it is mostly only heard by the people living in the house and the hostile spirits of the household. If one does not use a repentant mind until they do not know how to advise them, they may chant again in a voice that they do not like to hear. (Some spirits often do not accept listening to chants with a meditative tone, and may even have a stronger adverse reaction in the case where the Master chanting does not possess virtue, wisdom...) In cases where the spirits like to hear the chant, it is very good; if not, it is of no benefit at all.

🌳 Therefore, it is best to choose readings that are easy to listen to, familiar, with slow and moderate sounds... so that spirits can easily receive them.

🍁 If practicing at home, it is recommended to have a separate room or a private area, then use that room as a meditation and chanting room. If that area has spirits who want to practice and listen, they will concentrate in that room to listen and practice. If there is no separate room but you want to practice in the living room, there are two situations:

1. Any spirit (practicing ascetic) that wants to enter the house, if allowed, will focus on the living room area, creating a mix of yin and yang energies in the house.

2. If in the house, there are individuals who practice well or perform a lot of good deeds and have protective deities or house guardians, usually spirits will not be able to enter, thus bringing no benefit whatsoever.

I dedicate this merit to the Rắn family along with the spirits of the Nine Generations Ancestors, parents of many generations, and all souls throughout the Dharma realm, wherever they may be, so that they may be influenced, cultivate faith, and aspire to the practice of Buddha for rebirth in the Pure Land.

tieu_de: The Karma Forecast
tom_tat: In the country of Kế Tân, there was an arahant named Ly Viet, who went deep into the mountains to practice meditation. One day, someone who had lost a buffalo went searching, and followed the tracks to that place. At that time, Venerable Ly Viet was boiling grass to dye his robe, when suddenly the robe turned bi-colored.
noi_dung:
FORECAST OF KARMIC ACCUSATIONS

In the country of Kế Tân, there was an arahant named Ly Viet, who entered the deep mountains to practice meditation. One day, someone who had lost a buffalo came looking for it, following the tracks until reaching that place. At that moment, Ly Viet was boiling grass to dye his robe, and suddenly the robe turned into buffalo hide, the dye water turned into buffalo blood, the boiled grass turned into buffalo meat, and the alms bowl he was holding turned into a buffalo head. The owner of the lost buffalo saw this and immediately had him taken to the local authorities, imprisoned in a cell, where for 12 years he had to take care of the horses and clean up horse manure.

When his karmic connection was about to end, Ly Viet's disciple from afar used his divine eye to see his teacher imprisoned in the jail of the Kingdom of Kexin, and immediately went to speak to the king of that country. Upon hearing this, the king said that if any monk wants to leave the prison, he may do so. As soon as Ly Viet heard this, his hair and beard fell out, his entire body soared into the air, displaying all 18 transformations. The king, seeing this, felt ashamed and knelt to repent for the crime of imprisoning an Arhat.

Venerable Ly Viet then taught: “The king is not at fault; it is due to the karmic causes from my previous lives. In a past life, I once lost an ox, which led me to wrongly suspect and falsely accuse an Arahant, insulting him throughout an entire day and night. Because of that sin, I fell into the three evil realms, suffering countless torments. The misfortune has not yet ended, so even though I have attained the Arahant fruition, I am still falsely accused and slandered.”

*****************

An arahant is a practitioner who has ended rebirth and escaped samsara, yet still cannot escape the residual results of karma, because their opposing enemies still remain. However, it should be understood that the karmic consequence an arahant experiences is entirely different from the karmic consequence that ordinary people experience. Just as containers of food for the devas may look the same, the food inside can be purified or coarse and bad in different ways. Similarly, like an elephant, a horse, and a rabbit all swimming across a river, each animal experiences the depth of the river differently. Therefore, events cannot be interpreted in the same way for everyone.

tieu_de: THE BUDDHA IS NO MORE, KṢITIGARBHA BODHISATTVA REPLACES THE BUDDHA. HE IS VERY EXHAUSTED, IN FIVE HUNDRED SEVENTY BILLION SIX THOUSAND YEARS
tom_tat: Time in this world is very long without the Buddha! The teachings of Shakyamuni Buddha have declined, nowadays studying Doctrine is the same, studying Meditation is the same, studying Esoteric teachings is also the same, it is truly extremely difficult. Old layman
noi_dung:
BUDDHA IS NO LONGER, BODHISATTVA KŪZANG REPLACES THE BUDDHA. HE IS VERY TIRED, IN FIVE HUNDRED SEVENTY-SIX THOUSAND YEARS

Time in this world without the Buddha is very long! The Dharma of Śākyamuni Buddha has declined, and nowadays studying the Teachings is the same, studying Zen is the same, studying Esoteric Buddhism is the same, truly extremely difficult. Elder layman Hoàng Niệm Tổ told me this; he personally practiced Zen, practiced Zen with the old monk Hư Vân, and studied Esoteric Buddhism with the elder Cống Cát. He told me that in his lifetime, there was no one who reached enlightenment through studying Zen; only a few attained Concentration, not many, attaining Zen Concentration but not yet able to reach enlightenment. He stated that those studying Esoteric Buddhism, from the time China was newly established up to the present,There are only six people who have achievements in Mainland China, which is far too few! The elder himself recited Buddha's name to be reborn; at that time, he told me that every day he recited Buddha's name fourteen hundred thousand times, departing in a very excellent way, truly reciting Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land. We should not be ignorant of these facts.

In the future, Maitreya Buddha will descend to become a Buddha, holding the “three Lotus Flower Assemblies, saving countless beings” (three Lotus Flower Assemblies, saving countless beings). He differs from Shakyamuni Buddha; Shakyamuni Buddha spent his entire life preaching in over three hundred assemblies, while in the future, Maitreya Bodhisattva will only have three assemblies. His assemblies are very large, with a great number of people. Shakyamuni Buddha's assemblies were not large; some small assemblies had only two or three people, yet they were still considered an assembly. One day, when someone approached him to ask for teachings, he would then give a dharma talk to them, and [the words of that sermon] were also recorded in the Āgama Sutras. You can see the sutra text is very short, two or three hundred words, constituting one assembly. A great assembly could sometimes last for several years,completely different, varying in length, and the places are also different. The Long Hoa three assemblies are three grand dharma assemblies at the same place, bringing about countless rebirths, as stated in the scriptures.

Currently, we are in the era of Shakyamuni Buddha. Those who study Buddhism but have not yet attained liberation have planted seeds of virtue. In the future, after fifty-seven thousand six hundred million years, during that time, we will have undergone countless cycles of reincarnation in this world. The Buddha will no longer be present; it is very rare for someone to take the Buddha's place. Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will take the Buddha's place. Therefore, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva works very hard! For fifty-seven thousand six hundred million years, all Buddhist teachings will be led by Kṣitigarbha. He will be here to teach sentient beings, cultivate seeds of virtue, and when Maitreya Buddha descends, he will participate in the Lotus Assembly. If we wish to do so...Is that good or not? Doing it this way is also fine, but it takes a very long time. If you want to become a Buddha a little faster, recite the Buddha’s name to go to the Pure Land and meet Amitabha Buddha; that way, it will be very quick. By the time Maitreya Bodhisattva descends to become a Buddha, you will descend again from the Pure Land to help Him, just like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana were such people. You will take a vow to come again, help Maitreya Buddha teach sentient beings, and become a great disciple in His assembly. I reveal this news to you, and how to do it is up to yourself to decide. Today, our time is up, and we will stop learning here.

- Venerable Thích Không, Explanation and Meaning of the Great Sutra of Pure Land 11, Volume 92.

tieu_de: Commentary on the Original Vows of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra
tom_tat: (Venerable Thuan Hoa teaching at the Ten Thousand Buddhas Sacred City) Part 2: Supernatural Powers in the Heaven of Tāvatiṃsa (Lesson 3)
noi_dung:
EXPOSITION OF THE ORIGINAL VOWS OF BODHISATTVA KṢITI**GARBHA** SUTRA

(Venerable Thien Hoa giving a lecture at Van Phat Holy City)

Part 2: Supernatural Powers in the Heaven of Trayastrimsa (Lecture 3)

(continued)

The word Santi Paramita. Among the six Paramitas, I have finished explaining two, so there are four more. Therefore, the third Paramita is "Santi"; this is also a Sanskrit word (Ksanti); in Chinese it is translated as "patience."

"Patience" includes Patience with Birth, Patience with Dharma, and Patience with Non-Birth Dharma. Patience with Non-Birth Dharma is a profoundly deep and subtle realm, always overflowing with the joy of Dharma. Only by attaining Patience with Non-Birth Dharma can one truly taste the flavor of the Buddha's teachings, and truly understand the subtlety and inconceivableness of the Dharma.

One must be able to practice patience in order to aspire to achieve the "Paramita"; without patience, it is impossible to attain the "Paramita" — and one cannot reach the "other shore"!

The practice of Tý Ly Da Bà La Mật. "Tý Ly Da" is also a Sanskrit term (Virya); in Chinese it is translated as "diligence"; and this is the fourth of the Six Paramitas. Some people misunderstand this virtue of diligence as diligence directed towards non-Buddhist paths; but in fact, a sincere person who truly understands diligence must direct their diligence towards the Buddha’s Dharma. If one directs diligence towards non-Buddhist paths, it is merely practicing asceticism in vain.

In India, there are many heretical sects. Some heretical sects advocate not eating rice but only eating grass, imitating the behaviors of oxen, and observing the "ox precepts". Some heretical sects promote learning the behaviors and movements of dogs and observing the "dog precepts"—whatever dogs do not do, they will not do; whatever food dogs do not eat, they will not touch; they will only eat what dogs are willing to eat. This is called the "ox-dog precepts".

There are also heretical sects that advocate sleeping in piles of ashes. The human body is already not clean, so what about them? They even smear ashes all over their bodies to make themselves dirtier, burying themselves in ashes and dust and claiming that this is practicing cultivation!!!

In addition, there are heretical sects that put forward the doctrine that cultivation must involve enduring suffering - enduring suffering in what way? One must lie and sleep on a bed of nails to prove that they have the capacity to withstand physical pain, and can practice all forms of asceticism.

Above are a few typical examples among countless acts of asceticism where people of heterodox schools irrationally and uselessly torment their bodies. They consider themselves very diligent in their practice; in reality, it is merely a diligence arising from wrong view and wrong knowledge, not from right view and right knowledge, so such diligence is of no benefit at all!

We should be diligent in wholesome practices, not diligent in unwholesome practices. If you apply diligence to unwholesome practices, that is going against the Dharma, turning your back on the Dharma.

Regarding wholesome practices, diligence means diligently prostrating to the Buddha, reciting sutras, performing repentance ceremonies, and chanting the Buddha's name — this refers to "bodily diligence" (the diligence of the body). Next is "mental diligence" (the diligence of the mind); what is called "mental diligence"? It means constantly keeping in mind the practice of cultivation, never forgetting to diligently engage in wholesome practices, always enthusiastically practicing the Perfection of Diligence, without regard for fatigue.

If you sincerely practice Buddhist Dharma, you will not feel tired, nor will you feel hungry or thirsty, and you will not have to endure unwanted disturbances. Why is that? Because whenever you are diligent, you will no longer feel that sluggish, discouraged sensation. If you are lazy and lack diligence, it is very easy to develop many bad habits, often feel tired, lose spirit, and just want to sleep to rest your body! Diligence is the main measure to see how you are. Therefore, in every place and at all times, we must diligently practice good deeds; that is what is called "Paramita of Diligence."

During the summer retreat last year, while teaching the Surangama Sutra, I mentioned four verses that those who renounce the world must engrave in their hearts. When the Buddha was still alive, his monastic disciples recited these verses daily, and were absolutely not allowed to neglect them; therefore, during last year’s summer retreat, I particularly brought them up for you to hear. I even realized that those intending to renounce the world also need to memorize these four verses by heart, let alone those who have already renounced the world - you must not forget them! The four verses are as follows:

Guard your speech and restrain your thoughts, and your body will not commit faults,

Even if all sentient beings are everywhere,

It is useless for ascetic practices to strive for detachment,

Thus the practitioner can save the world.

(Guard words and intentions, the body should not violate,

Do not cause suffering or harm living beings,

Useless ascetic practices should be avoided,

The practitioner thus skillfully saves the world.)

"Thủ khẩu nhiếp ý thân mạc phạm" (guard your words, restrain your thoughts, and avoid transgressing with your body). "Thủ khẩu" means not speaking recklessly, not freely judging right or wrong, saying this is good, calling that bad, praising one thing as delicious, criticizing another as inferior...; instead, one must "guard the mouth," be careful with every word spoken.

"Nhiếp ý" means to gather and restrain the mind, not letting it run here and there, not indulging in idle or far-fetched thoughts, not engaging in restless thinking.

"Thân mạc phạm" means not allowing the body to transgress the Precepts.

Every moment, we must always remind ourselves that we are monastics and must absolutely not violate the Precepts and rules - this is called "guarding the mouth, restraining the mind, avoiding bodily transgressions."

"Mạc não nhất thiết chư hữu tình" (do not cause distress to sentient beings.) We should not disturb or upset sentient beings. Not only toward humans, but even toward an animal, if you make it angry, then you are in the wrong. All monastics should not cause distress to any sentient beings.

"Useless austerities should be avoided" (useless austerities need to be kept away from). Regarding the twelve ascetic practices, we should practice them; but for austerities that are useless and not in accordance with the Buddha's teachings, we need to stay away from them and not follow them. Even if some heretical sects claim to have a method of becoming a Buddha in this lifetime, you should not follow them! We should only practice according to the Buddha's teachings, rather than chasing after those who practice "ox-dog austerities," imitating the lifestyle of oxen and dogs. How did the phenomenon of "ox-dog austerities" arise?

Heterodox practitioners practice asceticism, physically torment themselves, and do very arduous things, and some of them also attain the Divine Eye. After obtaining the Divine Eye, they happened to see a dog being reborn into the heavenly realm. Immediately, they concluded that if dogs can ascend to heaven, then if they emulate dogs, they too will be able to ascend in the same way; therefore, they observe the "dog discipline," imitating the way of life of dogs.

There are also other heretics who possess the Heavenly Eye, and thus see an ox, after death, being reborn in the heavenly realm; therefore, they follow the way of the ox, observing the "ox precepts."

These heretics, because they lack wisdom, although they arduously practice various forms of asceticism, gain no benefit at all; hence it is said, "ascetic practices are futile and should be abandoned."

"As a practitioner acts, one can skillfully relieve the world" (thus, a practitioner skillfully saves the world). One who practices the Way must be like this—guarding speech, controlling the mind, observing precepts, not disturbing sentient beings, not practicing austerities uselessly—only then can they save the world and teach sentient beings.

"Diligence," in reality, does not inherently exist. The reason it is said there is diligence is simply to explain the Dharma to ordinary beings like us; fundamentally, there is nothing called "diligence." Therefore, it can be said that all six perfections in the Six Paramitas are Diligence, and at the same time, are not Diligence.

Generosity, Observance of Precepts, and Patience belong to the diligence of the body; whereas Meditation and Prajñā (Wisdom) belong to the diligence of the mind. Therefore, diligence does not exist independently, because it has already merged with the other five perfections and transformed into something else. For example, if you diligently practice generosity, that is the diligence of Generosity; if you strictly observe the Precepts, that is the diligence of Observance of Precepts; if you persist in enduring and showing patience, that is the diligence of Patience. If you further diligently cultivate, that is the diligence of Diligence itself, meaning the very nature of diligence diligently striving and making effort. Moreover, if you diligently sitMeditation, without rest, without regard for fatigue, that is the diligence of Meditation; if you diligently practice Prajñā Wisdom, that is the diligence of Wisdom; if you study the Prajñā method, that is the diligence of Prajñā.

Therefore, diligence itself does not truly exist, because it is transformed into a kind of 'effort without attachment'—though arduous, it does not rely on effort. Thus, you should not cling to the idea that you possess diligence, because only then can it be called true diligence! If you stubbornly insist that you are diligent in this way or that, that your diligence is boundless, that you are very diligent in practicing the Six Paramitas—then it can be said that you are not diligent at all! For in doing so, there is a 'diligence' blocking your heart and obstructing your liberated thoughts, causing you not to have true diligencesteadfast step.

Once one truly understands the Buddha-Dharma, you will see that all things do not inherently exist. Before fully comprehending it, you may still perceive something called "diligence," but when you truly understand, you will no longer see it! Upon hearing this, some people might say: "Currently, I see nothing at all, so I don't need to be diligent!" Indeed, if you are not diligent, diligence also does not manifest, but there is still a difference here. That is, if you truly understand the Buddha-Dharma, true diligence also does not manifest! Why? Because at that time, you no longer cling! On the other hand, if you do not understand the Buddha-Dharma,If there is still an attachment to one's own diligence, then that cannot be called diligence. It is precisely because you truly do not understand the Buddha's Dharma, and completely do not know what diligence is, that you certainly cannot claim that you are diligent!

Regarding the Dharma, it is because you have not understood that you do not know; but once you understand, you must even let go of the Dharma itself; otherwise, it means you still do not understand the Dharma! We must abandon all forms, and should not cling to anything; for as long as there is attachment or clinging, it means the Dharma is not yet understood!

The language of Prajñā Meditation. "Thiền" is a Sanskrit word, a short form of "Thiền Na" (Dhyana); in Chinese it is translated as "contemplative practice," and also as "tranquil reflection." Regarding meditation, there are the Four Absorptions, the Eight Concentrations, and also the Ninth-Level Concentration. In addition, meditation is further divided into Worldly Meditation, Transcendental Meditation, and Supreme Transcendental Meditation.

Ordinary people practice Worldly Zen; this includes the Four Immeasurables of the mind and the Four Formless Absorptions. Regarding these realms, I do not explain in detail, because as long as you diligently practice and meditate, you will naturally understand everything. So what is Transcendental Zen? Transcendental Zen includes the Four Jhānas of Eightfold Concentration, the Eight Superior States, and the Eight Grounds of Equanimity.

Now, even if I explain these famous meditation masters clearly, it will only make you more confused! Because, for example, if I say that a dish is delicious, but if you don't try it, you ultimately won't know how tasty it really is! Therefore, now you know that there are many different things like Worldly Zen, Transcendental Zen, Supreme Transcendental Zen, Tathagata Zen, Patriarch Zen...; you just need to be diligent in your practice, and later you will certainly know the "flavor" of these things.

The Prajñā Pāramitā. "Prajñā" is a Sanskrit word; in Chinese, it is translated as "wisdom." Wisdom is further divided into worldly wisdom and transcendent wisdom.

Worldly wisdom is also called Thorough Understanding of the World. The advancements in science, philosophy, and all knowledge today are considered worldly learning. The ability to reason intelligently and be astutely perceptive about worldly matters, even being able to justify the unjustifiable, is called Thorough Understanding of the World.

Transcendental Wisdom refers to the wisdom of the transcendental world. Diligently seeking the Buddha's Path, studying Buddhist teachings without ever resting, even thinking about Buddhist teachings while asleep, dreaming about Buddhist teachings, and even when sick or in pain, thinking about Buddhist teachings at all times — that is truly practicing transcendental wisdom.

So then, worldly wisdom and transcendental wisdom, in the end, are they the same or two different things? They are essentially the same, but it depends on how you use them - if used for worldly matters, it is worldly wisdom; if used in Buddhism for transcendence, it is transcendental wisdom.

Wisdom is not divided into two; it is only distinguished for the purpose of explanation. Initially, when you study worldly matters, you realize that everything in this world is suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self. Then, if you use the understanding gained from worldly matters to study transcendental knowledge, that is also transcendental wisdom. Therefore, Worldly Wisdom and Transcendental Wisdom are not actually two separate things.

Most people only possess worldly wisdom, not transcendent wisdom; yet there are some who have transcendent wisdom but lack worldly wisdom. Why is it like this? Many people are very intelligent but spend their efforts on trivial matters—putting all their energy into unnecessary things—while paying little attention to, or showing no interest in, important issues such as life and death. Moreover, some people study transcendent matters but understand nothing of worldly affairs. We need to clearly understand both worldly and transcendent principles:

"Enter the world, yet transcend the world,

Signifying leaving the world yet entering the world."

Entering the world while leaving the world, leaving the world while entering the world – the act of entering and leaving the world must be understood without obstruction. If you understand clearly, then entering the world is precisely leaving the world; however, if you do not understand, even leaving the world will become entering the world!

The ancients have a saying:

Wisdom is also hidden,

The hidden guides to the path of wisdom,

Without trusting the hidden, one cannot use wisdom,

Cleverness can be countered by cleverness.

(Cleverness and intelligence come from hidden virtue,

Hidden virtue guides the way to cleverness,

Cleverness without faith in hidden virtue,

That cleverness backfires, cleverness harms itself)

"Intelligence comes from hidden virtue" (intelligence and cleverness arise from moral merit). How do we acquire intelligence? It is thanks to our predecessors performing many "hidden virtuous deeds." What are "hidden virtuous deeds"? These are acts of kindness carried out quietly with genuine goodwill, not for the purpose of showing off or being noticed by others. For example, if there is a person who lives alone and dies without a coffin, and if you feel compassion and buy a coffin for them, then take care of the burial properly; although performing a good and praiseworthy deed, you do not boast about it.generous, not revealing to anyone - that is having hidden virtue.

In summary, if you secretly help or do things that benefit others without boasting or letting anyone know, that is called 'hidden kindness.' If in a previous life one performed many acts of hidden kindness, then in this life one becomes intelligent; if in a previous life one read many Buddhist texts and recited numerous Buddhist scriptures, such as chanting the Diamond Sutra Prajnaparamita tens of thousands of times, then in this life one also becomes intelligent and wise. Additionally, if in a previous life one read extensively and diligently studied books to learn, then in this life one also has a sharp mind. Thus, intelligence essentially comes from hidden kindness—resulting from cultivating virtue and accumulating merit in past lives.having accumulated much virtue, so in this life one is more intelligent and talented than others.

"Subtle virtue leads to intelligence" (virtue guides the way to intelligence). Thanks to having virtue, you are able to be intelligent; therefore, it can be said that virtue has guided you to the path of intelligence.

"Cleverness without faith in unseen virtue leads to trouble,/ Cleverness used cleverly can backfire" (if cleverness does not trust in unseen virtue, that cleverness will backfire and harm itself). If in this life you are blessed with cleverness, but due to negligence you do not follow the right path, do not believe in unseen virtue, and do not do good deeds, instead relying solely on your own intelligence to plot evil, then precisely that intelligence of yours will harm you. Why? Because if you were not intelligent, you would not be able to do many bad things! It is precisely because of your sharp cleverness that you know things that others could never suspect; therefore, even if you actIf there is something shady or harming others, then with cleverness, you still will not be suspected or discovered by anyone. Therefore, using intelligence without believing in having hidden virtue, that intelligence will become an obstacle, and is what is called 'harmful intelligence'!

During the Three Kingdoms period (China), Cao Cao was originally a very intelligent person, one could even say he was smarter than both demons and gods. He also had a few achievements thanks to his intelligence and cunning. However, the harms caused by his sly intelligence were also not few!

Those who like to be clever, after hearing the above verse, should strive to do good deeds that are beneficial to humanity, rather than scheming to harm others.

To supplement the lecture on "The Perfection of Moral Discipline,” I will tell you a Zen story. In the time when Buddha Shakyamuni was still alive, there were two monks who went together to pay respects to the Buddha. After a long journey, they ran out of water, and both monks were exhausted from thirst. In a moment of despair, when it seemed they were about to die of thirst, one monk suddenly saw a human skull containing a little water. He joyfully exclaimed, "There is water! We are so thirsty, so let's drink the water in this skull!"

That monk objected: "We shouldn't! There are insects in that water, we can't drink it!"

The first monk tried to persuade his companion: "We are so thirsty that our throats are dry like this, if we drink this water, we might survive and be able to continue on to the place of the Buddha. Otherwise, the two of us would have to die here, unable to meet the Buddha!"

That monk remained resolute: "I would rather die for keeping the Precepts! Although I may not meet the Buddha, I will surely follow His teachings, and even if I die, I will not regret it!"

The first monk then drank up the stagnant water in that skull, and continued the journey alone; as for the other monk, because he refused to drink, he indeed died of thirst.

Then, the monk drank water and made his way to the place where the Buddha was staying. He went to pay respects to the Buddha and spoke: "Venerable World-Honored One! There were two of us traveling together, and halfway through the journey we were unbearably thirsty; upon seeing a little water collected in a human skull, I drank it so that I would not die of thirst, hoping to be able to meet the World-Honored One. As for the monk traveling with me, he was too stubborn, insisting rather to die than to drink this water; because there were insects in the water, he said that drinking it would violate the Precepts. In the end, I survived by drinking this water and was able to have an audience with the World-Honored One; as for him who refused to drink, perhaps by now he hasdied of thirst already!"

Buddha Shakyamuni said: "Do you think that monk died of thirst? That monk, thanks to observing the Precepts, was able to come to meet Me first; now he is here listening to My Dharma teaching. Observing the Precepts is indeed very difficult, but if one is sincere, I will truly understand and empathize. You have met Me, yet your mind is not sincere because you do not keep the Precepts strictly. Therefore, that monk has now enlightened and attained the fruit, while you still need to continue your practice!"

Through this koan, we can see that the six Perfections - Observing Morality, Patience, Generosity, Diligence, Meditation, Wisdom - need to be practiced sincerely and seriously. If one is not wholehearted and does things perfunctorily, it will certainly not be in harmony with the Dharma of the Buddha. Therefore, those who have renounced the world must constantly remember and follow these four verses in their practice:

Guard the speech, restrain the mind, abstain from bodily offenses,

Do not harm any sentient beings,

Avoid arduous practices that are futile and remain distant from them,

Thus, the practitioner is able to help the world.

(Guarding words and thoughts, the body should not transgress,

Do not create suffering or harm sentient beings,

Avoid useless ascetic practices that are necessary to shun,

Such a practitioner skillfully helps the world.)

Observing precepts is extremely important; do not mistakenly think that simply following the rules in general is sufficient, because even a slight lapse can lead us astray by a thousand miles. Therefore, practicing must be done properly and seriously, diligently and carefully; whatever we do must be honest and thorough, not careless.

The sound of Compassion. The heart of 'loving-kindness' gives joy, the heart of 'compassion' relieves suffering – all beings who hear this sound from the Buddha Shakyamuni can move from suffering to joy, escaping the cycle of birth and death.

The Joyful Generosity. "Joy" is delight, happiness; "generosity" is giving. Therefore, "joyful generosity" is to give with delight. Loving-kindness, Compassion, Joy, and Equanimity are collectively referred to as the Four Immeasurables, meaning the four vast and boundless minds – the Boundless Loving-kindness, the Boundless Compassion, the Boundless Joy, and the Boundless Equanimity. To practice the virtue of giving, one needs to cultivate a joyful mind – to joyfully let go, happily practice the act of giving. One should not feel regretful or reluctant in the heart after letting go and giving; for that would mean the joyful mind has not yet arisen.

Shakyamuni Buddha emitted the sound of Joyful Forgiveness, causing all sentient beings who heard this sound to develop a joyful mind of giving.

The Sound of Liberation. "Liberation" means attaining true freedom, completely unbound and unimpeded. So, what does "liberation" mean to be free from? It is freedom from the suffering and distress of birth and death within the six realms of reincarnation.

In the past, a monk went to seek guidance from a renowned senior monk and asked: "May I ask Venerable Sir, how can one attain liberation?"

The venerable monk asked again: "Who is binding you?"

Upon hearing this, the monk immediately attained enlightenment: "- ! So it turns out that no one is binding me; it's just that I am binding myself! If I no longer bind myself, I will naturally be liberated."

What is meant by "binding oneself"? Everyone should pay attention to this point - because we do not have clear insight and cannot completely let go of everything, we become constrained and restricted, unable to achieve freedom; and not achieving freedom is also not achieving liberation! If you can see through matters, understand everything, and be able to let go of all, it means you have untied yourself and will attain true freedom; being free is also being liberated. Then, you will experience serenity and ease, unrestrained and unbound, "without fear or dread, forever apart from suffering"."deluded fantasies" (Heart Sutra). Truly letting go of everything will lead to liberation; if one cannot let go, one cannot achieve liberation.

Buddha Shakyamuni has spoken this language of Liberation, so now we should also liberate ourselves, not tie ourselves up, and also not imprison ourselves, so that we are forever denied freedom. Why say that one imprisons oneself? If you are not being imprisoned, it means you have been liberated; but if liberation has not yet been achieved, it is no different from being in prison, not free to follow your own will—north, south, east, west, wherever you want to go, you are not free at all!

The "freedom" that we are talking about is not the freedom of this "stinky leather bag", but the freedom of nature. If this nature is free, then you want to live as long as you live, and if you want to die, you can die at any time. And you don't need to have any illness to die, you just sit and die – that is true freedom. This is called:

Birth and death due to self, non-divinity.

(Life and death are due to me, not heaven.)

At that time, if you want to live, you live; if you want to die, you die. You can choose to live to a hundred years old, a thousand years old, or ten thousand years old... it's all possible. If you no longer wish to live, you can return to your "original homeland" at any time. If you like staying in this "place," you can stay; if you no longer like staying, you can "move" away at any time, as you wish.

The freedom of one's true nature consists of two things: the freedom of the consciousness and the freedom of inherent Buddhahood:

1) Freedom of the spirit. The spirit belongs to the yin and can travel anywhere; for example, from the city of Old Kim Son, the spirit can go to New York, Europe, Asia... Although the spirit can clearly know the situation of the place it goes to, it cannot grasp objects - the spirit cannot buy gifts in New York and then bring them back to Old Kim Son; why is that? Because the spirit inherently belongs to the yin. The spirit can only observe the scenery of New York, but cannot do anything there.

2) Freedom of the inherent Buddha-nature. Buddha-nature belongs to the yang, it is the entire great function, with vast and infinite capabilities. Achieving this kind of freedom, even if you are in the city of Old Kim Mountain, if you need something from New York, you just need to reach out and you can get it immediately. Do you see how miraculous this is? Is that not supernatural power? In reality, it is the realm of liberation, without bondage or restraint, free and unimpeded. In this realm, the entire three-thousand great-thousand world system is like being in a single room; you can move freely throughout it and do whatever you wish.

So, if we are liberated, if we are free, then we will be able to experience such realms. However, we are not allowed to display our abilities carelessly or recklessly. We must not say: 'You like that thing from Germany, so I will go to Germany to get it for you. I just need to perform my supernatural power and it will be done immediately!' We absolutely must not abuse supernatural powers to do such things!

When approaching Nirvana, the Buddha instructed all disciples not to use supernatural powers; otherwise, if they used supernatural powers, they must depart quickly and not remain in this world any longer! Ordinary people do not possess supernatural powers, so if you use supernatural powers, it will inevitably cause everyone to feel fear towards you!

In summary, you can act freely according to your will to complete a task, which belongs to the Yang; if unable to accomplish it, it belongs to the Yin, and is the effect of consciousness - everyone needs to understand this clearly.

The Pure (Faultless) Mind. "Faultless" means what? It means no longer having ignorance. No longer having ignorance means being faultless. Even if you only have a small portion of ignorance left, you still do not achieve faultlessness. Therefore, ignorance is exactly the source of afflictions – wherever there is ignorance, there are all kinds of afflictions; without ignorance, there are no afflictions.

Why do you have a mind of craving? Because you have ignorance.

Why do you have a mind of anger? Because you have ignorance.

Why do you have a mind of delusion? Because you have ignorance.

Why do you have lustful thoughts? It is also because you have ignorance!

Exactly because from the very beginning you did not understand clearly, you created karmic obstacles. However, if you hear the sound of the Non-Defiled, you will no longer be ignorant. Therefore, Shakyamuni Buddha emitted countless types of sounds so that all sentient beings could hear and thereby awaken to the Way. There is a saying:

This is the essence of the true teaching,

Purely found in sound and text.

(This place of true teaching essence,

Use pure sound.)

In the Saha world, the essence of Buddhism is sound – using sound for Buddhist practices, hence there are types of sound that praise, extol, and articulate...



Scripture:

... the sound of Wisdom, the sound of Great Wisdom, the Lion's Roar, the Great Lion's Roar, the sound of Thunderclouds, the sound of Great Thunderclouds. When the Buddha emitted such unspeakable, ineffable sounds,...

Brief Commentary:

Wisdom. "What is 'wisdom'? Wisdom "eradicates" ignorance – if there is wisdom, there is no ignorance; if there is ignorance, there is no wisdom – these two cannot exist together. Now I will let you know one more thing that is relatively easier to understand; that is: "Wisdom is ignorance, ignorance is wisdom!"

Some people say: "I am ignorant now, which means I have wisdom; so I can just indulge my ignorance!" If you can be extremely ignorant, ignorance to the utmost extreme, then that is true wisdom!

Some people also say: "Master! The reasoning you just presented is really hard to accept! You say that wisdom is foolishness and foolishness is wisdom; yet I notice that foolish people do only reckless things, while wise people do things that are just and sensible."

That's right, you are very correct, but I am not correct! Why is that? Because ignorance can turn into wisdom, so I say "ignorance itself is wisdom"; yet wisdom can also turn into ignorance, so I say "wisdom itself is ignorance." A few days ago, when giving a lecture on the verse "cleverness and intelligence thanks to virtuous conduct," I already explained this; now I am merely restating it.

A wise person is someone who attains true freedom and also genuinely achieves liberation. Why is this said? A wise person does not act recklessly; whereas a foolish person does only reckless things, not wise ones. In addition, a foolish person does not gain freedom and is entirely in a "passive" state. Meanwhile, a wise person is the opposite, never having to be in a "passive" state; because they possess true mastery, true wisdom, and no matter what happens to them, they are aware of the good and bad aspects of the matter - do the good, avoid the bad. In general, they haveauthentic judgment and the authentic Dharma-eye (the eye that selects the Dharma).

Foolish people are not like that - they clearly know it is wrong but still do it. For example, we all know gambling is not good, but foolish people think it is a rare opportunity, and if they win, they will become very rich! It is because of a moment of ignorant greed, wanting to gain this 'ignorant wealth,' that all their assets vanish without a trace! Even after losing everything, they still do not wake up, and they plan: 'I have to try my luck one more time, who knows, maybe this time I will win and become very rich!'

It's like someone buying lottery numbers; one dong can buy eight numbers, and if they win they get more than a thousand dong, but unfortunately they get one number wrong and don't win any money; that person then thinks that if they buy again, they will surely win! Think about it, isn't that foolish? If all gamblers won, then the person who invented gambling for red and black would never be able to get rich!

And then there are those addicted to opium: Everyone acknowledges that smoking opium is harmful, but the foolish say: "Let me try!" Trying once is not satisfying, so they try a second time, then a third, a fourth..., and so on, "trying" again and again. Just one "try" can lead to addiction; if they don't "try" again, they can't bear it. Tell me, isn't that foolish?

A normal person is decent and polite, but when addicted, influenced by opium, oh dear, tears and runny nose hang down, the whole body is restless and uneasy, truly extremely miserable, and they must hurriedly find money to buy that drug to use to "lift" their spirits. This is all caused by ignorance, which deprives them of freedom. Why are they not free? People who smoke opium think that smoking opium is a kind of freedom, immersing themselves in it for pleasure; however, when the time comes for withdrawal and there is no drug to smoke, can they still be free?

So, whatever you do that you should not do is all foolish, without wisdom. If you had wisdom, you would not be deluded, you would not do the things that you should not do!

Great Wisdom. A person with great wisdom can see the key point of a matter at a glance, without having to wait until the situation unfolds to discover it. Because of possessing great wisdom, they can anticipate what should not be done and what the result would be if done, allowing them to avoid reckless actions. What is great wisdom? Studying the Dharma is great wisdom. One must study the Dharma to truly attain freedom, therefore this is great wisdom.

The Roar of the Lion. The lion is the king of all beasts. Whenever they hear the lion roar, all kinds of animals tremble so much that they are "caught off guard" — unable to stand steadily or run properly. Even fierce and powerful wild beasts like tigers, leopards, wolves... are all afraid to the point of having no reaction at all! When the animals hear the lion's roar, they feel as if their minds might explode from fear, becoming so terrified that they turn stupid!

The Roar of the Great Lion. The roar of a regular lion is already formidable; the roar of the great lion is even louder, heard clearly from both near and far.

The Sound of Thunderclouds. This sound resembles the thunder that explodes from within a cloud.

The Sound of Great Thunderclouds. This thunder sounds louder than regular thunder. Here it implies that Buddha's Dharma is like a huge cloud in the sky, shining across the continent and covering the entire world. Once this thunder resonates, it can be heard everywhere, indicating that Buddha's Dharma reaches all sentient beings.

Where there are clouds and thunder, there will be rain. "Rain" symbolizes the Buddha's Dharma nourishing the innate nature of all beings, allowing all beings to experience the "taste" of the rain of Dharma (Dharma rain). Rain pours water over the entire world; large trees absorb more water, smaller trees absorb slightly less; flowers and grass absorb an amount of rainwater appropriate to their type. Buddhist Dharma is similar - all beings are imbued with the rain of Dharma according to their capacity; as a result, the Dharma body and wisdom life increase, and great wisdom is opened.

When the Buddha emitted sounds that are ineffable and beyond description, ... "Ineffable" refers to a very large number, indescribable in quantity. So, after Śākyamuni Buddha emitted countless types of sounds, so numerous that they cannot be fully enumerated, what happens next?

Scripture text:

... from the world of Ta Bà and other realms of water, countless billions of Devas, Dragons, Ghosts, and Spirits also gathered at the Dao Li Heavenly Palace. These are the celestial beings from the Four Heavenly Kings, Dao Li Heaven, Tu Diem Ma Heaven, Dau Suat Da Heaven, Hoa Lac Heaven, Tha Hoa Tu Tai Heaven, Pham Chung Heaven, Pham Phu Heaven, Dai Pham Heaven, Thieu Quang Heaven, Vo Luong Quang Heaven, Quang Am Heaven, Thieu Tinh Heaven, Vo Luong Tinh Heaven, Bien Tinh Heaven...

Brief explanation:

First, the Buddha emitted countless large bright clouds, then He also released innumerable kinds of Dharma sounds, causing sentient beings to leave delusion and follow enlightenment, abandoning falsehood and returning to righteousness. At that time, from the world of Saha and other realms in different directions...

"Saha" is the Sanskrit term; in Chinese it is translated as "forbearance," and it also means "extreme suffering." Compared to the Western Pure Land, our Saha world here is indeed a world of "Extreme Suffering"!

Why is it called "forbearance"? Because beings in this world can be patient and endure suffering.

"Other realms" refers to the realms belonging to other worlds, not to our Saha world.

At that time, countless billions of Devas, Dragons, Ghosts, and Spirits from all places also gathered at the Trayastrimsha Heaven Palace, that is, the Thirty-Three Heaven.

These are the celestial beings in the realm of the Four Heavenly Kings. The Four Heavenly Kings are also called the World-Protecting Four Kings, meaning the four heavenly kings who protect the world. The Heavenly King of the Heavenly realm resides midway up Mount Tu Di; while the Dao Li Heavenly King is at the summit of this mountain.

The Four Heavenly Kings are the four great heavenly kings guarding the four directions - the Eastern Heavenly King, the Southern Heavenly King, the Western Heavenly King, and the Northern Heavenly King. The Heavenly King in the east is Chí Quốc Heavenly King, in the south is Tăng Trưởng Heavenly King, in the west is Quảng Mục Heavenly King, and in the north is Đa Văn Heavenly King.

In the heavenly realm where the four Great Heavenly Kings reside, the lifespan of the heavenly beings is five hundred years; and one day and night in this Heaven of the Four Kings is fifty years in the human world.

The Heaven of the Four Kings is the heavenly realm closest to our world. In the human world, anyone who does good or evil is judged by the Heaven of the Four Kings; because the heavenly beings there oversee the deeds of humans. That is what is said about the Heaven of the Four Great Kings.

Heaven of Đao Lợi. In the previous section, I have already explained - "Đao Lợi" (Trayastrimsa) is Sanskrit; in Chinese it is translated as "thirty-three," that is, the Heaven of Thirty-Three. The ruler of this heaven is also called Năng Thiên Tử.

Heaven of Tu Diệm Ma. This is a place where neither sunlight nor moonlight can reach. So would that place be very dark? Not necessarily! Because the celestial beings in the Dạ Ma Heaven have radiance shining from their bodies, so they do not need the light of the sun and moon.

Why is this heaven called "Dạ Ma"? "Dạ Ma" (Suyama) is a Sanskrit word; in Chinese it is translated as "thiện thời phân" (skillful division of time). Why is it called "thiện thời phân"? Because this heaven is located at such a high place that the light of the sun and the moon cannot reach it; therefore, the celestial beings here use the opening of lotus flowers to distinguish day and night - when the flower opens it is daytime, when it closes it is nighttime.

In the Heaven of the Four Kings, the celestial beings are half a mile (li) tall.

In Dao Loi Heaven, the celestial beings are one mile (li) tall and have a lifespan of a thousand years. One day and night in this heaven equals a hundred years in the human world.

What about in Da Ma Heaven? The celestial beings here are one and a half miles (li) tall and have a lifespan of one thousand five hundred years. One day and night in this heaven equals a hundred years in the human world.

For each higher heaven, the lifespan increases by five hundred years, and the height increases by half a mile (li); therefore, the higher the heaven, the taller the celestial beings become, and the longer their lifespan.

Tusita Heaven. "Tusita" is a Sanskrit term; in Chinese, it is translated as "zhi zu" (knowing sufficiency); therefore, it is also called "Heaven of Knowing Sufficiency." Tusita Heaven consists of an inner court and an outer court. Maitreya Bodhisattva currently resides in the inner court, while the celestial beings stay in the outer court.

The Three Calamities (three types of disasters - fire, flood, storm) cannot spread to the Inner Court of Tusita, but they can still destroy the Outer Court of Tusita.

Trời Hóa Lạc (Transformation Heaven of Bliss). The joy in this heavenly scene is transformative in nature, because that extraordinary pleasure is created by the deities residing there.

Trời Tha Hóa Tự Tại (Heaven of Freedom through Transformation of Others). The joy in the Heaven of Freedom through Transformation of Others originally comes from other heavenly realms; since the deities here possess supernatural powers, they can transfer the pleasures from other heavens to their own realm. The Heaven of Freedom through Transformation of Others is the abode of celestial demons, not of true deities or immortals.

The six heavens mentioned above – Four Great Kings Heaven, Deva of Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, Yama Heaven, Tushita Heaven, Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven – are collectively called the Six Desire Heavens. Why are they called the "Six Desire Heavens"? Because the devas there, although born in the heavenly realms, still have desires and still hold impure thoughts. During the past summer retreat, when I was teaching the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, I had already lectured on the Six Desire Heavens, but I am certain that after listening, everyone did not wish to keep it for themselves and "gave" it all to me; therefore, now I am teaching it again to "personally give" it to you once more!

The gods in the Six Desire Heavens still possess lust. The sexual activities of the deities in the Four Heavenly Kings Heaven and the Trayastrimsha Heaven are just like those of humans in the mortal world. Why is that? Because they all have physical forms. The celestial beings in the Four Heavenly Kings Heaven also marry like worldly people; and even the beings in the Trayastrimsha Heaven are the same, as they all have spouses and children, no different from humans in the earthly realm.

What are newborns like in the Tứ Vương Heaven? In this heaven, children at birth are already as big as five-year-old children in the human world. How about in the Ðao Lợi Heaven? Newborns in Ðao Lợi Heaven are about the size of seven-year-old children in the human world; and in Dạ Ma Heaven, newborns are about the size of ten-year-old children in the human world. Newborns are already this big, sitting on the laps of celestial beings; and shortly after, they are fed with "heavenly dew," a kind of cam-lộ that naturally manifests in this heaven. Soon after eating, the child suddenly grows tall like other celestial beings—half a lý in height, and has a lifespan of five hundred years. That is to sayabout the Four Heavenly Kings.

There is a verse about the realm of sensual pleasures of the deities in the Six Desire Heavens as follows:

Four Kings, Dao Li embrace in desire,

Demon Ma holds hands, Do Suat smiles,

Transforming Bliss looks long, Others glance briefly,

This is the sensual pleasure of the Six Heavens.

(Four Kings, Dao Li still embrace,

Demon Ma holds hands, Do Suat smiles,

Transforming Bliss looks long, Others glance briefly,

This is the sensual pleasure of the Six Heavens)

"The Four Kings, Daoli engage in sexual activity" (The Four Kings, Daoli still embrace). The celestial beings in the heavens of the Four Heavenly Kings and the Daoli also engage in sexual behavior like humans in the world.

"Yama holds hands, Dausuo laughs" (Yama holds hands, Dausuo laughs). The sexual behavior of celestial beings in Yama Heaven is holding hands.

In this heaven, male and female celestial beings express sexual relations by holding hands, similar to the way Westerners shake hands.

What about in the Heaven of Supreme Joy? In the Heaven of Supreme Joy, when the men and women of heaven smile at each other, they are already considered husband and wife; this is because the heavenly beings there do not smile in ordinary times! Why? Because their desires are very light, almost nonexistent. In the Six Desires Heavens, each level one ascends reduces one's desires by one degree.

Why, in our human world, do those who practice the Tao need to "eliminate desire and sever attachment," to sweep away all lustful thoughts? Because if desire and lust are abundant, ignorance and delusion also increase; the more desire is reduced, the more wisdom and clarity grow. Desire belongs to the realm of the Five Defilements of the Evil World - what is called "defilement"? That is desire! Desire is the most impure, the filthiest thing.

The sexual desire of the celestial beings in the Heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings is similar to that of humans; while the lustful thoughts of the celestial beings in the Heaven of the Thirty-Three Gods are somewhat milder compared to those in the Heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings.

The sexual behavior of the celestial beings in the Heaven of Yama involves holding hands, while in the Heaven of Tuṣita, it involves smiling at each other. Do not think that smiling is good—humans often consider smiling to be good, without knowing that smiling also has an effect on emotions and sexuality.

The deities in the Yama Heaven all enjoy practicing cultivation, so it is very rare for hand-holding to happen.

"Hóa Lạc stares, Tha glances." "Stare" means to look a little longer, about a minute, two minutes, or five minutes. The male and female deities in Hóa Lạc Heaven, if they gaze at each other for a few minutes, it becomes lust; whereas in Tha Hóa Tự Tại Heaven, just a brief glance is enough, no need to look for a long time.

"Try the pleasure of the Six Heavens" (that is the pleasure of the Six Heavens). The sexual behavior of the male and female deities in the Six Desire Heavens is like this—each time they ascend one level higher, their desires diminish by one level. Those with heavy desire cannot be born in the heavens, which is why those who are born in heaven have very little desire. The previous verse talked about the pleasures in the Six Desire Heavens.

Heaven of the Brahma Assembly, Heaven of Brahma’s Sons, and Great Brahma Heaven. These are three levels of heaven in the First Jhana realm, also called the Three Heavens of the First Jhana. Additionally, there are the Second Jhana and Third Jhana realms, and in each realm, there are also three levels of heaven.

Heaven of Purity. "Purity" means being pure. The desires of heavenly beings in the Realm of First Meditation Heaven are even lighter compared to those in the Six Desire Heavens, hence it is called "purity." All heavenly beings residing in this heaven are pure and all are citizens of the entire Realm of Pure Heaven.

Heaven of Assisting Purity. The gods in this place are pure administrators, serving as officials in heaven. "Assisting" means to assist; and here it means assisting the King of the Great Pure Heaven.

What about the Great Brahma Heaven? This is the residence of the Great Brahma Heavenly King. He was a person who diligently practiced the Way, but he only cultivated heavenly blessings to enjoy the happiness of the heavenly realm and had not yet reached the level of enlightenment or attained a fruit position; therefore, he was born into the heavenly realm and became the king of the Great Brahma Heaven. This Great Brahma Heavenly King is supported by deities from the Brahma Assembly and Brahma Father heavens.

The First Jhāna of the Three Heavens is also called the Realm of Detachment, Joy, and Bliss, which is the state far removed from the arising of afflictions, and is extremely delightful. Ordinary people, when they diligently practice and reach the state of the First Jhāna, can also access the First Heaven to meet the Great Brahma Heavenly King, his assisting ministers, and the inhabitants who dwell there.

The Heaven of Dim Light, the Heaven of Infinite Light, the Heaven of Light and Sound. These are three layers of heaven belonging to the realm of the Second Dhyana, also called the Three Heavens of the Second Dhyana. How can one be born into this heaven of the Second Dhyana? One must "eliminate desire and cut off attachment," completely purging the mind of sexual lust! If there is still a desire for sensual pleasure, it is impossible to be born into this heaven. Each layer of heaven here differs by a "rank"; why? Because the deities in this place no longer have desires, and as one ascends to higher layers, desire decreases, gradually diminishing.

The Lesser Light Heaven. The bodies of the devas in this heaven radiate a luminous aura; and this aura is much greater than the aura of devas in the Yama Heaven. However, among the three heavens belonging to the Second Dhyana’s Third Heaven, the aura of devas in the Lesser Light Heaven is somewhat inferior to that of the other two heavens.

Why do these celestial beings have an aura? It is because when they were still practicing in the human world, they focused on strictly observing the Precepts, maintaining them very purely. The deities in the Brahma Heaven and Brahma Support also observe the Precepts, but not as strictly as the deities in the Tranquil Light Heaven, so while they are pure, they do not emit an aura. The celestial beings of the Tranquil Light Heaven not only keep the Precepts rigorously but also generate an aura, which is why they are born into this heaven.

The Heaven of Infinite Light. The previous heaven was the Heaven of Slight Light — with little radiance; so how is this heaven? It has infinite, boundless radiance, impossible to count.
