Bright Sound Heaven. The heaven located above the Immeasurable Light Heaven is Bright Sound Heaven. How do the deities in Bright Sound Heaven communicate with each other? Through radiant light! Similar to how electric light is used to create images on a television, the deities here use light as a representation of speech. The celestial beings in Bright Sound Heaven do not speak aloud; this does not mean they do not know how to speak; it is simply that they use radiant light to communicate instead of language.

Some people criticize, saying that the deities in the Bright Sound Heaven cannot speak, have no language, have no writing; and the reason they use radiance instead of language and writing is because they simply do not know how to speak! That is not true! If they did not know how to speak, then is the entire Bright Sound Heaven filled with 'mute' celestial beings? In that case, how would they be any better than people who can speak in the human realm? If it is said that the deities in the Bright Sound Heaven use radiance to represent speech because they are all mute, then what benefit is there in being born into this heaven???

Therefore, I say that they also have a language, it's just that they do not use language. In our human world, we have writing and we use writing to represent language; we do not merely use writing and abandon language. The aura used in the Quang Am heaven is similar to the writing of our human world - the deities there use aura to write, and its nature is akin to our fax machines. This is definitely the case; it is not that they have no language, they can only communicate through aura!

Therefore, regarding the Dharma of the Buddha, you can take the Buddha's teachings and worldly dharmas to mutually compare and reason, and you will immediately understand. You should not follow others in hastily assuming that the Bright Sound Heaven has no language and that all the deities there are mute! Those people certainly have not clearly understood the issue!!!

Just now, we spoke about the three levels of the Second Meditation Heaven. Those who practice meditation and attain the concentration power of the Second Meditation Heaven reach the realm of the Earth of Bliss Born from Concentration, from which a kind of joy and bliss arises within concentration.

However, even those who reach the state of the Second Jhāna cannot say that their cultivation practice has reached the pinnacle, the highest level. It is not like that! Ladies and gentlemen, those of you practicing, now ask yourselves whether you have reached this level or not? Is it really true that your heartbeat has stopped? Is it really true that your breathing has been interrupted? Is it that whenever you sit in meditation, your breathing immediately ceases? Is it not? If not, then continue practicing; if you do not practice, it is impossible to stop the cycle of birth and death. Even if you achieve the state of the First Jhāna or the Second Jhāna, the cycle of birth and deathyour own has not yet ended.

We practice diligently not to see some small realms, not to see Bodhisattvas manifesting as protectors, or to catch a glimpse of someone... When we meditate, if we do see a halo, we must understand that it is merely a trivial realm, and we should not develop attachment or cling to that realm.

There are cases where, while meditating, the body suddenly starts to sway — you do not want to move, but the body keeps rocking back and forth, and even if you want to stop, you cannot. This is the effect of the six types of vibrations on the six sense organs, manifesting in six ways of the earth's vibration. However, this is still not true practice; you still need to strive forward with greater effort.

If you have not yet reached the stage of First and Second Jhānas, you need to make greater effort and not be lazy. If you are lazy, you will not be able to break free from the cycle of birth and death; and if you cannot break free from birth and death, it will be very dangerous for your future; therefore, becoming a monk and practicing is not an easy matter. Laziness is like paving the way for yourself to fall into hell. If you do not want to descend into hell, you must be diligent, hardworking, and dedicated in your practice.

Some people complain: "- Whenever I exert effort, I feel uncomfortable in my body, not well." Then, when you are condemned to hell, you will see that it is even more uncomfortable and painful there! If you want to be comfortable and happy in the present, the future will not be "pleasant"; but if you are willing to diligently put in effort right now, the future will surely be very "pleasant." Therefore, please consider this carefully! Once condemned to hell, there is no knowing how long you will have to endure the torment; because if you are sent to the Avīci Hell, you will never get out, and you will have to endure it all year round.sin, to endure punishment. Because after ordaining to study the Way, one is still lazy and negligent, unwilling to make effort, not studying Buddhist teachings, only wanting "freedom and ease" according to one's own will, one must therefore bear the sin in hell. That is exactly "freedom and ease" into hell!

The Trời Thiểu Tịnh, Trời Vô Lượng Tịnh, and Trời Biến Tịnh. These are the three heaven levels belonging to the realm of the Third Meditation (Tam Thiền).

The First Meditation realm is also called the Land of Rejoicing Free from Birth, the Second Meditation is the Land of Rejoicing Born of Concentration, and the Third Meditation is the Land of Wonderful Rejoicing Free from Delight.

In the First Meditation Heaven - the Brahma Heaven of Assemblies, the Brahma Heaven of Fathers, and the Great Brahma Heaven - all celestial beings are pure, yet there is no halo. In fact, it is not entirely absent - they also have halos, but they are extremely weak and faint. Celestial beings in the Second Meditation Heavens have bright halos and are also purer.

Here we can give a very simple analogy, comparing the sequence of the heavens with the process of cleaning a floor. First, the floor needs to be swept thoroughly - this represents the Pure Abodes, Brahma’s Abode, and the Great Brahma’s Abode (belonging to the First Jhāna Heaven).

Although the floor has been swept clean, it has not yet been waxed, so it does not look bright and shiny. After waxing, the floor shines - this represents the Radiant, Infinite Light, and Radiant Sound heavens of the Second Jhāna Heaven.

After waxing, we still need to clean further for the floor to be completely shiny and glossy. Because after waxing, there is still some dust or a few bristles left on the floor, so although the floor looks brighter, it is not entirely clean. When it is carefully cleaned, with not a single speck of dust left, the floor becomes both bright and clean—this is an analogy for the Heavenly Realms of Minimal Purity, Infinite Purity, and Transformational Purity of the Three Meditative Heavens. Those who wish to fully understand the realm of these heavens should meditate further on this analogy.

When you meditate and reach the state of the Third Jhana, all thoughts cease, and all mental fabrications stop. In the First Jhana, thoughts still exist, and you are still thinking. In the Second Jhana, this stream of thoughts has not yet ended; but when you reach the Third Jhana, all thoughts are completely ended—there is no longer a situation where one thought arises after another.

In a single moment there are ninety cycles of birth and death, and in each cycle of birth and death there are nine hundred thoughts; therefore, even in an extremely brief instant, we have generated countless thoughts. But when one reaches the state of the Third Meditation, all thoughts cease. At this time, not a single thought arises, there is no prior thought nor subsequent thought - everything is silent. That is the state of the Third Meditation.

At that time, not only the breath and pulse stop, but even thoughts cease, no longer arising. Those who practice Zen to this level can meditate for an entire month without realizing that a month has passed, or meditate for a whole year without noticing that a year has gone by. Although they no longer have a sense of time and space, this is a state of entering deep meditation, not death; therefore, if they wish, they can still return. "Wanting to return"? But aren't all thoughts already halted? When they suddenly think, "Why am I meditating here?" the stream of thought immediatelyreborn and they return.

Thus, in the realm of the Third Jhāna, even thoughts do not exist, so it is called "pure" (clean). If there are still thoughts, it is like still being covered with dust, not yet completely pure and clean. Therefore, the heavens belonging to the Third Jhāna are named Slightly Pure, Immeasurably Pure, and Fully Pure.

The Third Dhyana Heaven is also called the Realm of Delight in Freedom, a state far removed from pleasure. As human beings, whenever we feel joy, we consider it a good thing, but even this "good thing" must be abandoned; we should not cling to or become attached to pleasure. By doing so, miraculous effects will arise.

Scriptural text:

...the heaven of Blessed Birth, the heaven of Blessed Love, the heaven of Extensive Fruit, the heaven of No Thought, the heaven of No Troubles, the heaven of No Heat, the heaven of Good Seeing, the heaven of Good Appearance, the heaven of Ultimate Form, the heaven of Mahesvara, up to the heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception. All the celestial beings, Dragon beings, along with all Ghosts and Spirits, come together to convene.

Brief explanation:

1) Heaven of Blessed Birth. Why is it called the heaven of Blessed Birth? Because the deities in this heaven are all "those who have exhausted suffering and abide in extraordinary bliss" - they no longer experience pain, nor do they cling to sensual pleasures anymore.

What is meant by "all suffering is exhausted, and pleasure is not permanent"? The deities in the First Jhāna heaven still experience a kind of suffering that even in the Second and Third Jhāna heavens, this suffering still exists and is not completely eradicated. It is only in the Fourth Jhāna heaven, in this Brahma-loka of Bliss, that it can truly be said "all suffering is exhausted" — the seeds that cause suffering no longer exist, and all potential causes of suffering are destroyed. Does the absence of suffering mean there will be happiness? At that time, they also do not cling to pleasure, hence it is said "pleasure is not permanent."

So, what is the cause of suffering? The cause of suffering is "desire" - "desire" is precisely the factor that leads to all suffering. What is "desire"? It is "craving," or "lust," which means the longing; in English, it is called desire! This character "desire" is exactly the cause, the seed of suffering; without "desire," there would be no suffering. Without a lustful mind, there would be no cause creating so many other troubles.

Devas in the Four Jhāna Heavens no longer have sexual desire; because they have eliminated lustful intentions, it is said that "all desires are destroyed"—all cravings and desires have been completely eradicated, no longer existing. All gross forms are destroyed, all forms that have shape and are very coarse are eliminated. Once the gross forms are destroyed, they immediately attain a kind of very pure merit, hence it is called the Heaven of Birth in Merit—a place where pure merit arises. This is the first heaven belonging to the Four Jhāna Heavens.

Many people only vaguely know that heaven exists; do you know how many heavenly realms there are? According to Buddhist scriptures, there are six heavens of the Sensual Realm (Six Heavens of the Sense Realm), three heavens of the First Jhāna (Three Heavens of the First Jhāna), three heavens of the Second Jhāna (Three Heavens of the Second Jhāna), three heavens of the Third Jhāna (Three Heavens of the Third Jhāna); and what about the Fourth Jhāna? The Fourth Jhāna realm has up to nine heavens, and the Heaven of Great Merit is the first heaven belonging to the Fourth Jhāna Heavens. Because of the arising and presence of pure merit in this heaven, it is therefore called the "Heaven of Great Merit."

2) The Heaven of Blessed Love. This is the second heaven belonging to the Four Rupa Heavens. "Phước ái" means love—love what? Love of merit—cherishing merit, liking merit. "Phước Ái Thiên" means the heaven that loves and values virtuous merit.

The deities in this heaven are:

The deities in this heaven are:

Generous and accommodating in heart,

Pure and superior in understanding,

Attaining subtle compliance with the way,

Separate from both suffering and pleasure.

(A mind of complete generosity,

Conquered and peaceful,

In accordance with wonderful compliance.

Both suffering and joy are distant.)

"A mind of complete generosity." The giving heart of the deities in this heavenly realm has reached a state of perfect and unobstructed generosity – that which cannot be given away is given away, and that which can be given away is also given away; that which cannot be let go is let go, and that which can be let go must be let go. This is what is called "a mind of complete generosity."

"Supreme purification attainment." They have achieved a very pure and superior liberation. "Supreme," in English, is called supreme. "Supreme purification attainment" – their merit is immensely great, it can be said that this merit surpasses heaven and earth, nothing can obscure it.

"Attaining marvelous compliance." They have reached the state of "mind following desire," getting whatever they wish. This is an extremely marvelous compliance, whatever they want they get, always fulfilling their heart's desires.

"Suffering and bliss separated." At that time, there was neither suffering nor joy—they had abandoned the feeling of suffering and pleasure. However, the deities here still had another kind of desire, another kind of hope. What was it? Their hope was the two heavens just above the Heaven of Blessed Affection; which two heavens were these? They were the Heaven of Extensive Fruit and the Heaven of Non-Perception—they hoped to reach the realm of these two heavens.

The Heaven of Abundance (Quảng Quả) is one of the heavens belonging to the Four Meditative Heavens, while the Heaven of Non-Perception (Vô Tưởng) is the dwelling place of non-Buddhists. From the Heaven of Blessing and Love (Phước Ái), the deities can go to the Heaven of Abundance, and they can also go to the Heaven of Non-Perception; going to the Heaven of Non-Perception means entering the realm of non-Buddhists. Therefore, it is like encountering a fork in the road here - it is very easy to go the wrong way. Thus, even though one is born into the heavenly realm, it is also easy to be lost into the heaven of non-Buddhists.

3) The Heaven of Quick Fruition. What is called the Heaven of Quick Fruition? The Heaven of Quick Fruition is the fruit position of ordinary beings. The six levels of the Desire Realm heavens (Six Desire Heavens) are all considered the realm of ordinary beings - the fruit that ordinary beings can achieve does not go beyond the Heaven of Quick Fruition, it cannot surpass the level of the Heaven of Quick Fruition.

The Heaven of Extensive Fruits is completely free from all defilements and troubles of the lower heavens. In the Heaven of Extensive Fruits, the deities live in boundless bliss and their supernatural powers are exceedingly marvelous; therefore, being reborn in the Heaven of Extensive Fruits is not an easy matter. In the Heaven of Extensive Fruits, the 'marvelous compliance' is even deeper than in the Heaven of Blissful Love—not just 'compliance,' but 'extensive marvelous compliance,' a vast and wondrous form of compliance! 'Compliance' means acting according to one's heart and will, where the deities in this place attain the fruition they have been cultivating, in accordance with what they desire. That is the Heaven of Extensive Fruits.

Sky.

4) The Realm of Infinite Thoughtlessness. What is called the Realm of Infinite Thoughtlessness? The deities in the Realm of Infinite Thoughtlessness have ceased their thoughts, yet this is not permanent cessation; they have only ceased for five hundred lifetimes. Their lifespan is five hundred lifetimes, so throughout one of their lifetimes, thoughts do not arise—they do not think, there are no thoughts. However, among these five hundred lifetimes, four hundred ninety-nine (499) lifetimes are without thought, and there is one lifetime with thoughts. In this lifetime, during the first half of the lifetime, thought is extinguished and does not arise; by the last half of the lifetime, thought arises again. Therefore, "thoughtlessness" here meansfor a lifetime, very rarely giving rise to thoughts.

The entire heaven is the dwelling place of non-Buddhists. Here, non-Buddhists consider themselves to be in the highest heaven and firmly believe that at this moment they can attain Nirvana. Therefore, they stay here to practice; yet, although they practice, they still fall into suffering as usual! Thus, this heaven is the residence of non-Buddhists.

5) Heaven of No Affliction. "Affliction" means mental defilements. Deities in this heaven no longer have "afflictions stemming from perception and thought," as they have completely eradicated these afflictions. What are "afflictions stemming from perception and thought"?

"Seeing" is the act of perceiving; when facing a scene, it immediately gives rise to desire and attachment, which is called "seeing affliction" – the affliction of perception. "Thinking" is contemplation; regarding the principles of the Way, because of a lack of clear understanding, it gives rise to discriminatory thoughts, which is called "thinking affliction" or "thought delusion" – the affliction of ideas.

The devas in the Heaven of Infinite Bliss no longer have the two afflictions of view or thought, so they do not endure the affliction of mental agitation; nor do they experience suffering or pleasure - both pleasure and suffering have vanished. In this realm of "pleasure and suffering both gone," they have no struggling mind. Because there is no struggling mind, there is also no mental affliction; with the absence of affliction comes coolness (refreshment).

6) Heaven of No Heat. "Heat" refers to mental agitation. This heaven is very cool and tranquil, no longer possessing the "heat" of affliction.

7) The Heaven of Good Vision. Why is it called the Heaven of Good Vision? The deities in this heaven have an extraordinarily broad vision; they can see very far.

8) The Heaven of Blissful Manifestation. In this heaven, there is a most wondrous transformation – the deities here can manifest all realms of bliss.

9) The Heaven of Ultimate Form. The Heaven of Ultimate Form is the last heaven among the heavens in the Form Realm.

10) The Heaven of Ma He Thu La. "Ma He Thu La" is Sanskrit; in Chinese, it is translated as "Great Freedom." The Great Freedom Heavenly King has eight arms, three heads, rides a large white ox; and He considers Himself very leisurely and at ease.

Among the ten heavenly realms mentioned above, except for the Heaven of Infinite Emptiness, which is the dwelling place of celestial demons and heretics, all the remaining nine heavens - the Heaven of Blessing Birth, the Heaven of Loving Blessings, the Heaven of Extensive Merit, the Heaven of No Anxiety, the Heaven of No Heat, the Heaven of Good Vision, the Heaven of Good Manifestation, the Heaven of Form's Ultimate, and the Heaven of Ma He Thu La - all belong to the realm of the Four Meditative Heavens.

The Fourth Jhāna is also called the Realm of Purity of Mindfulness (Xả Niệm Thanh Tịnh Ðịa). In the stage of the First Jhāna, breathing becomes irregular; by the Second Jhāna, the heartbeat stops; in the Third Jhāna, thoughts cease entirely; and in the Fourth Jhāna? It is "mindfulness release," discarding all thoughts, leaving nothing behind.

This continues up to the realm of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception (Phi Tưởng Phi Phi Tưởng Xứ). Additionally, there are gods from the realms of Infinite Space (Không Vô Biên Xứ), Infinite Consciousness (Thức Vô Biên Xứ), Nothingness (Vô Sở Hữu Xứ), and Neither Perception nor Non-Perception (Phi Phi Tưởng Xứ) as well, who also go to the Tāvatiṃsa heaven (Ðao Lợi) to participate in the Dharma Assembly.

Because even the "consciousness" no longer exists, it should not be called "non-thought"; but this "non-thought" is not completely without "thought," there is still a little, therefore it is called "non-non-thought" - it is not that there is no thinking. That is the Place of Non-Thought Non-Non-Thought of the Devas.

All the celestial beings, dragons, along with the assemblies of ghosts and gods, come together to participate in the Dharma Assembly at the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.

(To be continued....)

tieu_de: THE WONDROUS CAUSE AND EFFECT OF FOUR BROTHERS (THE SACRED POWER AND MERIT OF THE EARTH STORE SUTRA AND THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA).
tom_tat: I (lay practitioner Quả Khanh) know of a certain family, in which there are four brothers: the eldest, before the age of 40, specialized in killing and eating meat, in terms of the severity of the ten evils, he violated them all, there is no evil that he did not commit
noi_dung:
THE WONDERFUL KARMIC RESULTS OF 4 BROTHERS (THE POWER AND MERIT OF Kṣitigarbha SUTRA AND GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA).

I (lay practitioner Quả Khanh) know a certain family, in which there are four brothers: the eldest brother, before the age of 40, specialized in killing and eating meat; considering all ten severe evils, he violated them all, committing no evil that he did not do. By the age of 40, thanks to reading the Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch, he developed the aspiration to cultivate, and up to now it has been 20 years. Although he underwent all kinds of hardships, he never wavered in his resolve. He recounted to his fellow practitioners: due to many years of diligent practice, I have recalled previous lives; in many former lives, I was a disciple of the Buddha, but because my lustful desires were not eradicated, I was reborn as a dragon. In this life, encountering the Buddha’s teachings once again, thanks to the BodhisBodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, out of compassion, saves beings and knows the way 'home'.

If it weren't for studying and practicing according to the Buddha's teachings, surely in this life you would enter the womb of cows and goats (because you eat beef and goat meat too much, so if you knew you were dead, you would certainly become a cow or goat). It is feared that you would have to endure being skinned and cut into pieces hundreds of times, then next become a pig to repay debts, then a fish, shrimp, ant, worm, mosquito, etc... meaning you would have to be countless animals over many lifetimes to repay the debt of killing. In that case, who knows when you would have a human body again? The calculations would be endless. Thanks to your cultivation practice, you have opened the knowledge of past lives and can see through all these lifetimes.

He told about his second younger brother (his sibling) who at 30 years old had died from a brain tumor. He realized that his younger brother originally came from the pig kind, and now he had reincarnated as a pig again, namely the big-headed white pig being raised in the house. Knowing this, out of love for his brother, he set up a small altar, sincerely performed Buddhist rituals kneeling while chanting "Great Compassion Mantra" 108 times to pray for his brother. After that, he observed and saw the big-headed white pig suddenly die unexpectedly and be reborn in heaven. He clearly saw his brother now sweeping the flower garden in the heavenly realm. He silently said: “Being in heaven, even just sweeping the flower garden, is still better than being in the hellish realms (hell, hungry ghosts,beast), I hope my second brother, under the blessings of the "Great Compassion Mantra," will in the future come to the human world to practice, learn Buddhism, transcend the three realms, and perfectly attain Buddhahood…

Uncles three and four, from a young age, did not like playing together, and as they grew up, they often fought over small matters, so they were scolded by their parents many times. After they started their own families, they continued to quarrel over land, clashing with each other for decades. The eldest brother tried every way to educate them, and although uncle four believed in Buddhism, it would be harder than going to heaven to make him give up the disputes!

The eldest brother recounted: these two younger brothers in their previous lives were animals with spiritual awareness, and in that life, they also were not harmonious, constantly causing fights until they were reincarnated into the human realm (in this life, if they do not resolve their grudges, then surely because of the evil deeds they created, they will descend into hell. Then from hell, they will be reborn as animals, continuing to struggle endlessly). The eldest brother confided: I have been advising them for more than twenty years to no avail; this is due to the severe evil karma they have accumulated over many lifetimes, and their lack of reverence and faith in the Buddha's teachings.

A family gathering together is due to good karma or bad karma; without karma, they wouldn't gather, or it happens because of owing or repaying debts; without debts, they wouldn't come.

Later, the eldest brother recited 108 sets of the "Kṣitigarbha Sutra" for the sake of our parents and two younger siblings. Two months later, our mother was the first to start changing, followed by the third and fourth uncles, who decided to let go of old grudges and no longer fought noisily with each other.

Although this is only the beginning, a grudge that lasted more than thirty years was transformed in one day. This cannot fail to praise the miraculous virtue of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra.

I share this true story in the hope that the disciples of the Buddha will soon let go of all personal grudges and no longer hesitate. Because once impermanence arrives, these unresolved grudges will turn into strong obstacles preventing you from leaving the three realms.

(Excerpt from “Causal Explanations of Lương Hoàng Sám” - Quả Khanh)

tieu_de: WHAT CONSTITUTES THE CRIME OF IMMORALITY? THE CONSEQUENCES OF IMMORALITY
tom_tat: Many people suffer from illness, broken families, or even ruined reputations just because they commit sexual misconduct, yet they do not wake up or repent because they do not believe that doing good deeds can partially resolve their sins.
noi_dung:
WHAT IS THE CRIME OF LUST? THE CONSEQUENCES OF LUST

Many people suffer from illness, broken families, or even destruction of reputation and career simply because they committed sexual misconduct, yet they do not awaken or repent because they do not believe that doing good deeds can partially atone for their sins.

Those who do not have spiritual faith are easily led astray when they pursue their desires regardless of moral principles. They do not know that even when a lustful thought arises, even before any action occurs, it has already created significant karma for themselves and their children.

What is considered the crime of sexual misconduct

In Buddhism, suffering caused by desire and attachment is recognized, because they are among the three very dangerous poisons that can corrupt, destroy morality, and kill a person's spiritual life not only in the present life but also across future lives. Therefore, the issue here is to extinguish the suffering of each individual. Among them, desire is the most important milestone, and it is driven by the hand of ignorance.

In the five precepts for lay Buddhists, the Blessed One only established the precept against sexual misconduct. Sexual misconduct refers to engaging in sexual activity, having sexual relations with someone who is not one's spouse. That is, not cohabiting with someone who is not one's wife or husband.

If a man and a woman are husband and wife, according to customs and traditions, recognized by both families and relatives, approved by the authorities according to the law, and acknowledged by everyone… then sexual activity between husband and wife is not considered immoral, because it is a normal act of people living a domestic life, and it is not criticized by others. The marital bond – transcending life and death to find each other – should not be betrayed; do not betray your spouse out of lust or desire.

Even one's own wife or husband, if sexual communication occurs at the wrong time, such as on full moon days, the first day of the month, sacred Buddhist days, and in the wrong place (only allowed in the bedroom), and without moderation, and not appropriately timed, it is also considered adultery. In summary, any sexual relations between men and women that are not recognized by law and customary law are regarded as adultery.

More delicately, we should not indulge in lust, engage in improper thoughts, or behave flirtatiously. In addition, masturbation and watching obscene sexual films or stories are also considered sexual immorality. Avoiding sexual immorality is a condition to ensure family happiness, safety, and social stability.

There is nothing more unfortunate than having to live in a family with an illegitimate relationship. Illegitimate actions within the relationship of one of the spouses will lead to arguments, jealousy, beating, and quarrels; destroy family happiness; lead to divorce; cause children to lose the love of their father if they live with their mother, and lose the love of their mother if they live with their father. Furthermore, children are more likely to fall into depravity, lacking the education of either the father or the mother, and then indulge in social evils. In addition, relatives neglect them; the village criticizes them, friends distance themselves, their reputation is tarnished, and their virtue fades...

The Blessed One advises us not to commit sexual misconduct as a way of respecting justice and happiness. Everyone wants to have a warm and joyful family. If everyone upheld this precept, society would not have people who destroy families, disgrace their lineage, or lead others into sexual immorality and depravity.

As we see in reality, there is no hatred more intense than the hatred caused by deceit or betrayal driven by love. Murders occur every day for various reasons, yet most are the result of licentiousness. Therefore, for lay practitioners, the Blessed One skillfully taught a happy and harmonious family life.

The doctrinal purpose of Buddhism tends to lead all sentient beings, especially humans, out of suffering; and the main cause of that suffering is desire. Therefore, Buddhism teaches people to distance themselves from desire as early as possible and constantly praises those who have, are, and will have the inclination to distance themselves from desire.

Specifically for those who have renounced worldly life, the Buddha teaches to abstain from sexual desire. Because sexual desire is the cause that leads to downfall, suffering, and reincarnation in the cycle of birth and death. The stronger the craving, the tighter the bondage, and thus the increasing suffering. The motive of craving is ignorance, relying on the root of delusion and selfishness to love. Therefore, attachment only causes suffering to oneself and others, not only in the present life but also in being trapped in the cycle of endless rebirth. If love is obstructed or rejected, love transforms into hatred. If love is satisfied, it becomes more indulgent and blind.

CAUSE AND EFFECT OF REAPING THE CONSEQUENCES OF LUSTFUL SINS

Anyone who commits evil deeds of lust with another person's wife, husband, or child; if the sin is severe, after that person dies, the evil karma of lust will bear fruit in the next reincarnation in the four evil realms (hell, asura, hungry ghost, animal), suffering the consequences of that evil deed until the results of that karma are exhausted before escaping the evil realms.

After escaping from the hell realm, if some other good karma bears fruit during the next rebirth as a human; and in the case where someone commits evil karma of sexual misconduct with a minor sin, after that person dies, that sexual misconduct karma does not have the ability to bear fruit in the next rebirth, but some other good karma bears fruit during the next rebirth as a human; then in both cases, that person will still have to endure the bad result of the sexual misconduct karma from a past life.

In the past, some people had the ability to see that the retribution for the sin of sexual misconduct is the most severe.

For example, committing adultery with someone else's wife, or defiling someone else's daughter will result in being tormented in hell for 500 years. After that, he may have to live as an ox or horse for another 500 years before being reincarnated as a human. Even as a human, he may have to work as a prostitute.

If someone schemes to commit adultery with a widow or a nun, corrupting human morals, that person will suffer in hell for 800 years. After that, he may be reincarnated as a pig or a goat to be slaughtered for meat for the next 800 years. When he is finally born as a human again, he may suffer from disabilities.

Seducing someone of high status or a child, corrupting the moral order, will cause that person to suffer in hell for 1,500 years. When he is born as a human again, he may die in the womb or be stillborn, meaning he has an extremely short life.

Of course, these retributions are not exhaustive and may vary depending on the situation. However, this shows the severity of the sin of adultery.

Many people, due to momentary pleasure and indulgence in the secular world, receive extremely serious retribution for the sin of adultery. The suffering in hell is indescribable. Once entering Avici Hell, there is no way out.

In the Dhammapada, the Blessed One teaches as follows:

"Adultery, taking another's wife by force

Four misfortunes

come at their time to befall:

First is to suffer calamities and disasters

Second is difficulty sleeping

with a heart often anxious

Third, a life spat upon all over

Fourth, to be cast into hell,

pierced with skewers, bound in bundles!" (Golden Words Scripture, line 309).

Full of sins, must bear, must carry

Misfortunes chase after,

Bend your back and crawl!

Pleasure as delicate as silk thread

Then panic, then fear

Joy is nothing in comparison!

The king's severe law drags you away!

Harvesting fierce consequences

for being involved with someone else's wife!" (Golden Words, lines 309 & 310).

DOING GOOD WORKS TO CANCEL SEXUAL SIN

Karmic desire has the power to strongly influence and affect personal life; if not transformed and leading to a loss of control, it can result in countless sins. Most importantly, practicing meditation is essential to master the mind (because the mind leads all phenomena), transforming sexual energy, and creating balance and tranquility for body and mind. Additionally, attention should be given to physical exercise, labor, and other social activities to release excess energy as well as to relieve general psychophysiological inhibitions.

The story about how doing good deeds can absolve the sin of adultery is recounted as follows: A man from Kim Hoa named Tề Vượng, at the age of 50, still did not have children. A physiognomist said, "There is an evil aura on your face, you must have done things against your conscience." Tề Vượng replied, "When I was young, I secretly had an affair with another man's wife."

The physiognomist said: "Committing this kind of sin will lead to the extinction of your descendants! The sin of adultery is the hardest to repent for; you must accumulate many good deeds to be able to restore it!"

Tề Vượng therefore decided to repent. In the first year, when others did good deeds, he was very happy to donate money to them. The fortune teller said, "What you have done is still not enough!" So, the following year, no matter what good deeds he encountered, Tề Vượng was always the first to contribute money, and the amount he donated was always more than half. The fortune teller said, "What you have done is still not enough." In the third year, without anyone telling him, Tề Vượng went to do good deeds on his own. The fortune teller said, "The merit from your good deeds has already appeared on your face, you no longer need to worry about having children."

Later on, Tề Vượng indeed had a son.

When Tề Vượng reached the age of 70, his body was still healthy, and he could still play with his children and grandchildren!

tieu_de: Heaven, earth, demons, and spirits have many officials responsible for supervising all sentient beings regarding the arising of thoughts and intentions, and the actions they create
tom_tat: Not only do they see, but they also keep records. Every sentient being has an extremely complete set of documentary files. This is not to deceive people, it is not false. The realistic society of ours, the system of ma
noi_dung:
Heaven, earth, ghosts, and gods have many officials in charge of supervising all sentient beings regarding the arising of thoughts and intentions, and the actions they create

Not only do they see, but they also have records. Every sentient being has a perfectly complete set of data files. This is not deceiving people, it is not false.

Our realistic society, the machinery of state agencies, every person from birth to death has their own records, because they have the responsibility to manage this locality. Why must these angels and demons also retain a complete part of the records? Because this area of ours also falls under their management. The City God manages this district, and they have records. Their records are even more complete compared to the records of our earthly government. The angel of this area of ours is also within the scope of their governance. In the Buddhist scriptures, it is told to us that the Great Brahma Heavenly King, Ma He Shula Heavenly King, the scope theyManagement is the entire world of Ta Bà. Or in other words, we are sentient beings in the six realms, and there are many managers over us, but we do not know. Just like in the society before our eyes, if we are in this area, there is a village chief or hamlet chief managing us; above that, there is a commune chief, a township chief; higher up, there is a district chief; even higher, there is a provincial chief managing us; above that, there is central management. There are too many who manage us. Spirits and angels manage us, the situation is even more complicated and numerous than this, so is there any way? Who causes us to fall into the three realms?

In the three realms, those whom angels and demons cannot control are Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Buddhas. They cannot be controlled. Why can't they be controlled? Because these people are selfless. In other words, those who "have a self" can be controlled by them; those who are "selfless" cannot be controlled by them. Those whose "bodies are outside the three realms and not within the five elements" are respected by all angels and demons. The Buddha is honored as the teacher of humans and gods, and this is the principle behind it.

tieu_de: the benevolent deity who protects the Five Precepts
tom_tat: In the Sutra of Observing the Precepts and the Treatise on the Jewel Forest of Dharma, the names of 25 Precept Deities are recorded. Each precept has 5 benevolent deities. Whoever upholds all five precepts will always have the 25 benevolent deities accompanying and supporting their body. FIVE DEITIES T
noi_dung:
The benevolent deity protecting the FIVE PRECEPTS

In the Quán Đỉnh sutra and the Luận Pháp Uyển Châu Lâm text, the names of 25 Precept Deities are recorded. Each precept has 5 benevolent deities. Those who fully observe all five precepts usually have 25 benevolent deities always accompanying and supporting their body.

FIVE DEITIES PROTECTING THE PRECEPT OF NOT KILLING

1. Sái-xô-tỳ Dũ-xá-ni removes harmful and evil influences.

2. Du-da-lợi Du-dà-ni guards the six senses to remain completely intact.

3. Tỳ-lâu-già-na-ba governs the harmony of the five organs (heart, lungs, liver, spleen, and kidneys).

4. Ādālongmada to make the blood vessels circulate, to smooth flow.

5. Hoan-ni-hoaba protects the fingernails, fingers, toenails, toes to be beautiful.

FIVE DEITIES PROTECTING AGAINST THEFT

1. Demaatybada blesses us to go in and out peacefully.

2. Atulunbalada blesses eating and drinking to be pleasurable.

3. Balama Danhungthu supports good sleep when we sleep or dream.

4. The Brahman Địa-bệ-đá eliminates poisonous creatures harmful to us.

5. Na-ma-hu Đa-gia-ná removes fogs contaminated that harm the body.

FIVE DEITIES PROTECTING AGAINST IMMORALITY

1. Phật-đà-tiên Đà-lâu-đá protects the mouth from being harmed.

2. Bệ-xà-gia Tầu-đa-xa removes evils brought by epidemics.

3. Nát-để-hê-đa-da-đa-già removes harms caused by traveling.

4. A-la-đa Lại-độ-gia guards the house.

5. Balana Buddha pacifies the eight spirits in the house.

FIVE GUARDIAN DEITIES WHO DO NOT TELL LIES

1. Adepham Giassanlia eliminates demons and wandering spirits in graves and cemeteries that cause harm.

2. Nhandailani Andailah protects the doorways.

3. Agialam Thibada removes harmful external spirits.

4. Phutdamghi Madada averts fire disasters.

5. Alai-xoa Tamsatda repels thieves and robbers.

FIVE GODS WHO PROTECT THE HOUSE AND DO NOT DRINK ALCOHOL

1. Amala Tư-đầu-hy wards off tigers, wolves, and other harmful wild animals.

2. Nala-môn Xà-đâu-đế wards off death deities that bring harm and disease.

3. Tát-bệ-ni Càn-na-ba wards off disturbing cries of birds and owls.

4. Đề-bệ Xà-tỳ Xá-ni-la wards off invading dogs and rats.

5. Già-ma Tỳ-na Xá-ni-khư protects against harmful powerful people.

These protective deities guard day and night, bestowing blessings so that practitioners can be peaceful and stable in their six-times-a-day practice. Therefore, the precepts are a precious gem, a protective armor. We must always remain vigilant and uphold them.

tieu_de: THANKS TO CASTING THE GUANYIN STATUE - ONE SHOULD BE ABLE TO SEE AMITABHA BUDDHA - REBORN TO THE LAND OF BLISS!
tom_tat: Monk Thích Tự Giác is from Vọng Đô, Bác Lăng. At the age of ten, he became a disciple of Master Trí Khâm at Khai Nguyên Pagoda, where the district where he lived was located. The Master saw that he had greater determination than others, so he named him Tự Giác. On that occasion, the Master said
noi_dung:
PRAY TO THE GUANYIN STATUE - YOU MAY SEE AMITABHA BUDDHA - AND BE REBORN IN THE PURE LAND!

Monk Thich Tu Giac, from Vong Do, Bac Lang. At the age of ten, he became a disciple of Master Tri Kham at Khai Nguyen Pagoda, where he resided. The Master saw that he had an extraordinary will, so he named him Tu Giac.

Then, the Master jokingly said:

– The name is full of meaning, could it bring any benefit?

The Monk replied:

– The Buddha seed arises due to predestined conditions, I could never forget my teacher’s teachings!

In the second year of the Zhidu era (757) during the Tang Dynasty, the Master received full ordination. Later, he went to the Chan Fa Temple in Linh Tho to study the scriptures and vinaya of both the Theravada and Mahayana traditions; the Master analyzed and explained them clearly.

After some time, the Master thought:

– Life is full of countless matters, growing more each day. If I could have a straw hut on a rock at Mount Tai, that would already be enough!

In the first year of the Dali era (766), the Master went to the Chong Lam institute in the west of Binh Son district and said:

– The mountain is deserted, no people are there; no affliction arises. Doesn't the absence of affliction correspond to the Buddha's teaching of non-verbal instruction?

There were already ghosts and spirits here before, so for three years the Master expounded the Dharma to them.

In the fifth year of the Dali reign (770), there was a drought, bandits arose like swarms of bees, and the mountains and forests were dense, filled with tigers and wolves. The Master gathered forest fruits and ate only one meal a day. Governor Zhang Zhao in Hengyang, noticing the great drought, knew that the Master lived in austerity and diligence and often had signs of auspiciousness, so he personally went into the mountains to report:

– Truong Chieu does not have the talent to govern the country and has brought disaster to the people; it has been three years of drought, not a drop of rain. I blame myself for not being able to help the people at all!

He then said:

– I heard that the Dragon King and his relatives have been listening to you teach the Dharma and have forgotten to make rain. I hope that you, Master, will compassionately pity everyone so that Truong Chieu will no longer be anxious!

The Master immediately burned incense and, looking toward the distant pond, offered prayers:

– May the Dragon King make the rain permeate. If not, what virtue would the Dragon King have?

In an instant, dark clouds arose from all directions, and the sky poured heavy rain. That year, the people of Hằng Dương had a bountiful harvest.

Since he became a monk until that time, there was a time the Master made forty-nine vows. The first vow was to rely on the great compassion of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara so that he might meet Amitabha Buddha.

Therefore, the Monk raised donations to cast a Forty-Nine-Foot statue of the Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara and built a temple to enshrine it. When the temple was completed, the Buddhist work was accomplished, the Monk went before the Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara statue, bowed his head and wept, praying:

– The sacred statue has been cast, the temple has been completed, I vow to rely on the sacred power to attain Peaceful Rest soon!

At the third watch of that night, the Monk suddenly saw two beams of virtuous light, and between the golden beams appeared Amitabha Buddha descending on a cloud, accompanied by the Bodhisattvas Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta. Buddha extended his golden arm to stroke the Monk’s head and said:

Maintain a firm original vow

Putting the benefit of sentient beings first,

The treasure pond is the place of rebirth

May everyone achieve their wishes!

In an instant, the light disappeared, and the cloud completely dissolved without a trace.

On the full moon day of the seventh month in the eleventh year of the Đại Lịch era (776), the Master saw a person appearing half-body on a cloud, shaped like Tì-sa-môn. That person bowed down and said to the Master:

– It is time for you to go to An Dưỡng!

On that very day, the Master recounted the matter, and at the same time advised the disciples to diligently practice, to be courageous in the teachings of the Tathagata, and not to develop a lazy mind.

Afterwards, the Master went before the statue of Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara, sat in full lotus, and passed away. The disciples wanted to place the Master's body in a coffin and return it to the old mountain, but everyone in this district earnestly requested to keep it here, so a stupa for the Master was built to the south of Dai Bi Pagoda.

Excerpt from Four Assembly on Rebirth

Source: Cause and Effect - Reincarnation

tieu_de: BODHISATTVA Kṣitigarbha INCARNATES TO CREATE MERIT FOR SENTIENT BEINGS (Transforming and Saving Sentient Beings, Studying Buddhism and Reciting Buddha to Rebirth)
tom_tat: During the resistance period, I studied in Guizhou. At that time, it was the National Third High School, now it is the Dong Ren First High School of Guizhou, which is our old school. The principal's wife was Chu Bang Đ
noi_dung:
BODHISATTVA KȘITIGARBHA INCARNATES TO CREATE MERIT FOR SENTIENT BEINGS (Transforming and Saving Sentient Beings, Learning Buddhism, and Reciting Buddha to Rebirth in the Pure Land)

During the resistance period, I studied in Guizhou. At that time, it was the National Third High School, currently known as Dongren First High School of Guizhou, our old school. The principal's wife, Zhu Bangdao, our foster mother, after the victory of the resistance, when the school was dissolved and handed over to Guizhou Province, the local government took responsibility. We all left the school and returned home; we were all displaced students. The principal's family lived in Nanjing, and I visited the teacher's house in Nanjing. The garden was very large, truly a serene courtyard. Passing through the main gate was the garden, Through the second door is the skylight, like a quadrangle courtyard, a skylight. Through the third door you finally reach the teacher's residence, having to go through three layers of doors, walking a very long path. The nun told us that one day, while she was at home, a monk came to the house for almsgiving. She asked him where he came from. 'From Mount Jiuhua,' he replied. She asked what he needed. 'I need five catties of fragrant oil.' She did not give it, as at that time she had not yet believed in Buddha!

The abbess is a very kind, compassionate person, full of love, who cares for her students more than her own children. Having been at the school for many years, she takes very thorough care of the students. Her own children do not receive as much attention; the students come first. Therefore, we students regard the abbess as if she were our mother. We regard the principal as if he were our father, with very deep affection.

The abbess did not offer the monk five pounds of fragrant oil, and the monk then left. After the monk left, she suddenly remembered and said it was truly strange, how did the monk get in? This house has three layers of doors; the main door was not opened, and when he left, the doors were not opened either, so why didn't anyone see him? For many years, she could not resolve this doubt.

After arriving in Taiwan, all stayed in Taichung. Master Li taught the sutras in Taichung, and that is how they became acquainted. She sought guidance from Master Li and recounted this story. Master Li said that the monk was an incarnation of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha; she deeply regretted not offering five catties of fragrant oil to him, as this was an incarnation.

You see, this manifestation told me that when coming and going, there are no traces and no knocking on your door. When coming to three layers of doors that do not open, how did he arrive? When leaving and all three layers of doors remain closed, how did he go out? And when meeting and talking, the time is quite long, absolutely not an illusion. The manifestation of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha had not yet arrived for even half an hour. Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is a Samyaksambuddha Bodhisattva, naturally residing in the true, splendid realm, and has a karmic connection with Master Chu's wife, so he responds accordingly. From then on, every day she recited a set of Kṣitigarbha Sutra, her mind calm, wholeheartedly focusing on Buddha's name.

The lady who recites the Great Compassion Mantra water is very responsive; in Taiwan, many people know about it. Her Great Compassion water can heal illnesses. She recited Buddha's name to be reborn in the Pure Land, and after passing away, the cremation produced more than 300 relics. She was a laywoman, truly unimaginable! At that time, we had not encountered Buddhism and did not believe it; hearing her story was like hearing a myth. But we knew that both the teacher and the master's mother were genuine people, absolutely not deceitful. We just felt that this was very rare, inexplicable, and could not be explained. There truly was such a thing, it could not be explained, and only later, after studying Buddhism, did we understand.

Commentary on the Great Sutra of the Pure Land, Volume 275 – Venerable Thich Ting Khong

Source: Buddha of Infinite Life

Namo Great Vows Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

tieu_de: LIFE SUDDENLY BECAME BETTER SINCE I DISCOVERED BUDDHISM.
tom_tat: - Author: Vo Van Lan - - Source: Buddhist Flower Garden -
noi_dung:
LIFE THAT WAS STUCK SUDDENLY BECAME MORE BEAUTIFUL SINCE I DISCOVERED BUDDHIST TEACHINGS.

- Author: Võ Văn Lân -

- Source: Buddhist Flower Garden -

My hometown is a poor rural area; at that time, the village did not have a school, so few children in the village were able to go to school. I was quite old when I first asked to go to school. Every day I went to class alone because the third grade class was held at the village communal house while the other kids from my neighborhood attended school.

After finishing primary school, most children dropped out to stay home and work on the farm or go to vocational training; I was one of the few who managed to get into the public secondary school for boys, the only one in the city of Hue at that time.

In the classroom, alongside most children from well-off city families, neatly dressed, many of them good students, I felt lonely and often embarrassed because of my many lacks.

I still vividly remember the French reading lesson with Mr. Ne. Before the lesson, he would write the text on the board. First, he would erase one word from each sentence and call one or two students to read it aloud. Then he would gradually erase two, three, four words from each sentence until the entire text was erased. In this way, he would call each student in turn to read the whole lesson. If you were lucky enough to be called when only a few words at the beginning were erased, it was still easy to remember and read, but by the fifth or sixth turn, when half of the words on the board were gone and you were called, there was nothing you could do but stand at attention like during a flag ceremony.

I sat holding my breath, trying to shrink myself like a faint shadow, but I couldn't avoid it! And every time I was called on, I would freeze in place. Strangely, many others would stand up and read smoothly. It turned out later that I found out they had memorized the books beforehand...

I was determined not to give up, working hard every day... Every day after school, I would stop by the Tan Hoa bookstore on Tran Hung Dao Street, or the Binh Minh bookstore near the foot of Truong Tien Bridge, secretly opening books, copying lessons, and taking them home to study. Often, when I was caught, the shop assistants would chase me away as if I were a ghost, but I took the risk...

Then, due to the circumstances, I gave up studying to take the entrance exam for the teacher training college. Getting into the teacher training college wasn’t easy when it was one against twenty. In a group with many people of different ages and levels, some were four years older than me. I tried my best to study so as not to be looked down upon and to be able to teach near home after graduation. But life is full of twists and turns; although I graduated with fairly high marks, I had to teach in a distant province. Arriving in unfamiliar Quang Nam, after years traveling through mountains and villages. Such hardship! Is it fate or is it the heavens being unfair? I pondered, asking myself, but the answer still lies ahead...

The Tet Offensive (1968) pushed many young people into the battlefield. I was also drafted and only returned to the education sector after two years. Then after 1975, life was difficult, filled with constant fear day and night… I continuously strived to teach and work well in order to continue my teaching career and ensure my children could go to school. Working excessively took a toll on my body, causing all kinds of illnesses. Life was truly hard! I turned to Eastern and Western philosophy to try to find the cause, but the answer remained elusive...

Like many teachers at that time who were retained, I was transferred to teach literacy to the elderly, raise the educational level for young people and officials, including a few monks and nuns studying at the temple who came to ask for lessons.

Fate led my life to take a turn, bringing me closer to the teachings of Buddhism. The words of the Buddha opened my mind to find answers to the questions that had long troubled me. It turns out that each person's happiness or suffering is not determined by fate or any heavenly power, but by the karma they have created in the past. Actions, thoughts, words, and deeds, whether good or bad, form long-standing habits of virtue or vice that accumulate over countless lifetimes and create the karmic force that influences each person's happy or unhappy life. I live according to the Buddha's teachings, abandoning evil and practicing good, with compassion, joy, and forgiveness, so I feel more at ease, my family and children gradually stabilize, and my health has been restored.

Life has so many mysteries that it is impossible to fully express! Turning to seek refuge in the Three Jewels has brought me unexpected benefits. I have recorded a few experiences from practicing the teachings of the Buddha in the hope of sharing them with friends and descendants. If anyone feels a sense of empathy, it is also a karmic encounter. I bow my head in silent gratitude to the Buddha and the Bodhisattvas!

tieu_de: A TRUE STORY ABOUT THE SOULS OF MISCARRIED FETUSES
tom_tat: When a fetus dies, it often becomes a restless spirit, because the children have waited a long time for a chance to become human but were deprived of the right to live by their own parents, resulting in resentment in their hearts. If it is a good child th
noi_dung:
A TRUE STORY ABOUT THE SOULS OF MISCARRIED FETUSES

When a fetus dies, it often becomes a restless spirit, because the children waited so long for the chance to be born but were deprived of the right to live by their parents, leading to resentment. If the child is virtuous, nothing will happen, but if not, it can cause trouble. In particular, red infant spirits, if not cared for by their parents (through rituals), are very resentful and often harm their parents in various ways. Below is a true story about the souls of wasted fetal children.

"Six years ago, I received a request from an acquaintance. She asked me to help write a letter to her daughter (Ms. H), who had passed away a year earlier due to leukemia. While writing this special letter, I put myself in Ms. T's position, sending messages of love to her daughter and hoping she would find peace soon. The letter was cremated on the first anniversary of her passing."

Ms. T's daughter was originally the most well-behaved child in the family. Although born into a family of free trade business, with quite affluent economic conditions, Ms. H never indulged in showiness or extravagant spending. From a young age, Ms. H was a gentle and obedient child, fond of literature, growing up with certificates of merit, various literary achievements, earning royalties as early as 10 years old. Furthermore, Ms. H was particularly beautiful, sang well, and was very affectionate towards her parents... All of these made her the greatest pride of both sides of the family and also the greatest sorrow when she passed away at such a young age, that year shejust turned 23 years old.

But there is a story behind this loss... Once, after the funeral of Ms. H, I met the spirit of a boy. He was a 7-month-old fetus that Ms. T had aborted.

But what surprised me even more was that he led along 11 of his other siblings, all of whom had been abandoned by Ms. T when they were only a few months old. He clearly stated the exact day, year, and method each one was abandoned. Some were aborted, some were too large and had their bodies dismembered part by part, some had their heads crushed, and some were still gasping for breath when picked out before dying... Each word he spoke was a scene passing through my mind, making me truly sorrowful and haunted.

I asked him why he made sister H suffer; she hadn’t committed any crime. He replied, “We just happened to have baby H, who has been a good and talented child since birth, and then one fine day, we suddenly took her life so that Mrs. T would know what it means to have a life taken in revenge. Ask her how it feels to watch her daughter die, to see her deteriorate day by day and take her last breath, whether it feels as light as when she killed us, whether she cries out as we did when we died. Killing her isn’t enough; she must suffer for her entire life. Everything isn’t over yet, still...That D guy too (Ms. T's second son), don't worry, I won't let him die, but let's take our time and then we'll decide, we have this many kids anyway.

To be honest, I do not dare to recount all the words I heard from that little red boy, just briefly summarizing so that she understands she has created very great karma. I also learned that, after the day she heard me speak, she went to meet many spiritual masters, performed many small and large ceremonial offerings, and participated in numerous memorial services for the deceased, to repent and hope to partially resolve her karmic obstacles.

After a few years, the last time I met Ms. T was at the end of 2018. She told me that her son had lost a leg in an unfortunate traffic accident, and at the same time, he suffered from severe kidney failure, requiring weekly dialysis for the past two years. Currently, only she lives with her son. She and her husband divorced because he frequently changed his temperament, caused disputes, and physically abused her, which she could not endure. Now, she only hopes to have enough health to take care of her life and care for her son... What made me think even more was when she lifted her shirt to show me the burn on her left arm from an accident. Although the burn had dried, it still appearedclearly shows an image of a fetus curled up....

The soul of a fetus is inherently the most pitiable soul, because they have cultivated for a long time, enduring many hardships, just to return to human life, yet their life is coldly taken away by their own parents. Therefore, they are also the deepest, most terrifying vengeful souls, with many souls developing the consciousness of seeking revenge against their parents. That anger is very intense, and it cannot be resolved by just a few measures of mortals, especially in the case of Ms. T. I dare not talk about an overly negative future, but with the existence of those 12 souls full of resentment, her life will still have to facewhat other misfortunes, perhaps only they have the answer....

I hope that, with the events that Ms. T has gone through, the 12 "little red ones" have also lessened their hatred, so that from here she can have a path to live, and it is also for themselves a chance to reach a better realm.

Through this story, you surely have a clearer view of the existence of fetal spirits. I hope this article will be widely shared so that our small community can further spread the message to help reduce the current rampant abortion situation, so that lives are no longer left unfinished from before their form is even shaped, and so that those who remain are no longer surrounded by karmic consequences, hatred, and further suffering...

Amitabha Buddha!

tieu_de: MAKE A VOW TO BUY A HOUSE NEAR THE TEMPLE & LAKE TO RELEASE ANIMALS AND THE SURPRISE BEHIND.
tom_tat: - Source: Pure Land Lotus Group - - Author: Diệu Bích -
noi_dung:
VOW TO BUY A HOUSE NEAR THE TEMPLE & LAKE TO RELEASE ANIMALS AND THE SURPRISE BEHIND.

- Source: Lotus Pure Land Group -

- Author: Diệu Bích -

Diệu Bích would like to share a miraculous story about the act of releasing life that happened to herself. The story has no other purpose; if there is any merit in it, please take it as faith and encouragement for everyone to practice the release of life, for every household to practice the release of life, and to avoid killing animals.

With a heartfelt wish to save as many animals as possible day and night, Diệu Bích only hoped that in the future her house would be near a lake for the convenience of releasing animals, and close to a temple so she could go and recite Buddhist prayers.

The process of looking for land to build a house was truly difficult when land prices in Hanoi were extremely expensive and money was limited, especially for a plot near a lake, which Diệu Bích did not dare to dream of. Therefore, despite her wish, when searching for land to buy, Diệu Bích no longer dared to pay attention to finding land near a lake; any plot would do.

There have been too many moments of disappointment. On one morning during the usual ceremony, after finishing the dedication and taking refuge, Diệu Bích prayed to the Buddhas:

"I have never dared to ask for anything for myself; my prayers are always for the benefit of sentient beings. But there is one thing that has troubled me for several months. I ask the Buddhas to help me find a piece of land near a lake so that I can carry out the practice of releasing animals, and near a temple so that I can practice reciting the Buddha's name. I also vow to spend 2.5 million VND to perform these animal releases."

Unexpectedly, that very evening, Diệu Bích's husband suggested going to see a piece of land...

(The strange thing is that until now, Diệu Bích's husband had never supported buying land; every time Diệu Bích suggested looking for land, he would get annoyed).

Even though it was almost 8 p.m., the couple made the effort to go see the land because if they didn't go immediately, Diệu Bích's husband would be on a business trip for more than a month the next day.

Unexpectedly, the land was near three large lakes; from the piece of land, one could go straight to the three lakes to freely release animals, and it was also close to a pagoda, just as Diệu Bích had wished.

Moreover, it is only a few kilometers from the city center; from the center, it only takes 5 minutes by motorbike to get there.

Another strange thing is that the person taking them to buy the land was a broker, and he said the price was many times higher. But after inspecting the land, Diệu Bích's motorbike suddenly wouldn't start at all.

The broker didn’t know that the couple's vehicle had broken down, so he went ahead. After fumbling for a while, a neighbor came out and asked:

- You want to buy land? I’ll give you the owner’s phone number to ask; why go through a broker? They charge very high prices!

If I could get the landlord's phone number, the car could also start, Diệu Bích called, and to my surprise, the land price was too cheap compared to the current land market.

The next day, the two of us went to make the deposit. Meeting the landlord, who was a good person I had never met before, knowing that Diệu Bích's husband would be on a business trip for a month, he agreed to let us pay a month later, and even allowed delayed payment.

Another strange thing was that when making the deposit, the land payment was still significantly lacking. But surprisingly, on that very same day, Diệu Bích was asked by a colleague, for some unknown reason, if she wanted to borrow money. And indeed, Diệu Bích had not asked anyone about this matter. In the end, this money was fully repaid.

Another miraculous thing was that the land was priced extremely low compared to the land rates at that time. Diệu Bích even suspected a planning issue and went to the ward office to inquire.

The cadastral officers in the ward, after asking Diệu Bích how much she bought that plot for, couldn’t believe their ears, because they said how could there be a plot so cheap without any planning, in a high-income residential area, close to schools, an ecological lake, a market, a cultural house, a swimming pool, tennis courts, parking lot...

A week after buying the land, someone offered double the price, and up to now, the price has nearly tripled. Furthermore, when measuring the land again, the plot turned out to be more than 10 square meters larger than the payable area (on the red book, it only shows 55.8 m², but in reality, nearly 70 m² can be built on).

Every time someone asks to buy back the land, even offering a lot of money, Diệu Bích just smiles, remembering her own vow.

There is one thing Diệu Bích wants everyone to understand: when releasing animals, we must start from the bottom of our hearts with the intention of freeing the animals, not releasing them to seek personal gain.

Releasing animals brings mutual benefits. For the person performing the release, the act helps develop a compassionate mind. For the animals, it allows them to avoid being killed, be liberated, and gain freedom. More deeply, by hearing the chanting of Buddha's name and taking refuge in the Triple Gem, when they die, their negative karma is reduced and they may be reborn in a good realm. Later, they will have the opportunity to practice and escape from being birds, fish, or other animals. This is the true meaning of animal release.

The article is a bit disorganized; if there is any merit, may it be dedicated to the animals, with the hope that through this article, everyone will be encouraged to practice the vow of releasing animals.

The Sutra of the Buddha's Teaching on Ten Rebirths in the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha.

🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏

🙏BENEFITS OF CHANTING THE BUDDHA'S NAME

The sutra says:

The ocean of love is boundless

The sea of suffering is countless and vast

One desires to escape the suffering of samsara

Instantly contemplate Amitabha.

Temporary translation:

The river of love stretches a thousand measures

The sea of suffering has countless waves

To escape the suffering of samsara

Hurry to contemplate Amitabha.

🙏 The benefits of reciting Buddha have 7 supreme advantages 🙏

Cam Lo So says:

1. Few words, making it easy to practice: Because one only needs to say the phrase 'Amitabha Buddha', everyone can recite it.

2. Meditating on causes according to the Buddha's form: Because one concentrates wholeheartedly on the causes in the Buddha's beautiful appearance, using the pure land as the scene.

3. Being free from calamities brings peace: Because one receives blessings from the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, a person who recites the Buddha's name will not encounter misfortunes and will experience joy and goodness.

4. Reciting the name eradicates sin: Because reciting the Buddha's name once eliminates the heavy sins accumulated over 8 billion eons of birth and death.

5. Maintaining recitation brings merit: Because reciting one Buddha's name brings more merit than the seven kinds of treasures offered to the Buddha and Arhats in the four heavenly oceans.

6. The karmic result of feeling the Buddha: Because living beings recite the Buddha's name, they will definitely see the Buddha.

7. The Buddha personally welcomes the rebirth: The transformation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas emit light to welcome practitioners to be reborn in the Buddha's realm.

🙏 The sutra says:

Whoever sincerely upholds the Buddha's name in this life will receive 10 benefits:

1. Day and night, they are constantly supported by all heavenly beings with great power, divine manifestations, and countless attendants appearing in hidden forms.

2. Usually accompanied by 25 Great Bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteshvara, and many Bodhisattvas according to their guardianship.

3. Always protected by Buddhas day and night. Amitabha Buddha often emits light to receive that person.

4. All evil spirits such as yakshas and rakshasas cannot harm them; all poisonous dragons, poisonous snakes, and poisons cannot invade.

5. Not affected by disasters such as: floods, fire, enemies, swords and arrows, chains, prisons, sudden death.

6. Previous evil deeds are gradually eliminated, and lives that were wronged by oneself are liberated from vengeance through the merit of reciting Buddha's name.

7. Sleeping at night is peaceful, or one may dream of auspicious signs or see the wondrous form of Amitabha Buddha.

8. The mind is often joyful, the complexion is bright and smooth, physical strength is sufficient, and work yields good results.

9. Often respected and helped by others, or happily receive worship just as one venerates the Buddha.

10. At the time of death, the mind is free of fear, mindfulness arises, seeing Amitabha Buddha and the Saints holding golden lotus platforms to lead the rebirth to the Pure Land, enjoying profound bliss even in future lifetimes.

The Treatise on Mindfulness of the Buddha by the Second Patriarch Master Thien Dao says:

The sutras on mindfulness of the Buddha and rebirth say: Mindfulness of the Buddha has 30 benefits across the three times: Past - Present - Future:

🙏 PAST:

Eliminating sins; reciting one Buddha name eradicates 8 billion eons of heavy sins of birth and death (Sutra on Contemplating Immeasurable Life).

🙏 CURRENTLY:

1. Eliminate sins: Reciting a single Buddha's name eradicates 8 billion kalpas of severe birth-and-death sins.

2. Infinite merit: Reciting a single Buddha's name brings 8 billion kalpas of wonderful merit.

3. Attain the supreme Dharma of the Buddhas.

4. The Buddhas witness together.

5. The Buddhas collectively support the recitation.

6. The Buddhas of the ten directions all encourage faith in recitation.

7. If there is calamity, reciting the Buddha's name immediately removes it.

8. At the time of death, the mind does not become disturbed (Sutra of Praising and Extolling the Buddha of Pure Land).

9. Reciting the Buddha's name as one practice encompasses many practices.

10. The Pure Land Dharma Gate includes: 5 sects, 8 teachings; a single phrase "Amitabha Buddha" recited proficiently encompasses the three baskets and 12 divisions of the sutras, containing all the ultimate teachings. 1,700 cases and methods for the path of enlightenment are included. 3,000 etiquettes, 80,000 meritorious deeds, and the three gatherings of precepts for purity are also included.

11. At the time of death, the Buddha Himself comes to welcome (Sutra of Praising and Extolling the Buddha of Pure Land).

12. Using a small amount of merit can quickly be reborn in the Pure Land (Ancient Dharma Sutra).

13. Long life, increasing blessings and longevity, the Buddha's name is the elixir of immortality of the Great Enlightened One.

🙏 FUTURE (Coming):

14. Being born in a lotus pedestal, body golden yellow. The sutra says the nine grades of lotus are one's parents.

15. Live long without dying, live until the day of attaining Buddhahood.

16. Body emits light.

17. Possess all 32 marks.

18. Attain the six supernatural powers (divine eye, divine ear, knowledge of past lives, divine recollection, mind-reading, extinction of all defilements).

19. Attain patience in regard to the unborn dharma.

20. Often see the Buddhas.

21. Befriend Bodhisattvas. The sutra says: "Bodhisattvas are companions on the path."

22. Offer incense, flowers, and music six times.

23. Food and clothing naturally remain sufficient for many lifetimes.

24. Freely progress on the path directly toward Bodhi.

25. Often youthful, without the appearance of old age.

26. Often healthy, free from illness.

27. Not condemned to the three evil paths.

28. Rebirth is attained freely.

29. Day and night, in the six periods, often listen to much Dharma.

30. In an unshakable position.

🙏The Treatise on the Pure Land by Great Master Hoai Cam states:

Those born in the Western Direction have 30 benefits as follows:

1. Rebirth in the Buddha's realm.

2. Attaining the great joy of the Dharma.

3. Being close to the Buddhas.

4. Offering to Buddhas in all ten directions.
