Lecturer: Elder Teacher VENERABLE TINH KHONG

*********************************************

DHARMA GATE “REPEATING THE BUDDHA’S NAME”

I) Teachings of the Buddha and Patriarchs on the Dharma Gate of Buddha Recitation:

1. “In the era of the Decline of the Dharma, countless practitioners exist, but few attain enlightenment, only relying on the practice of Buddha Recitation to escape the cycle of birth and death.” (Great Collection Sutra)

2. “Truly for birth and death, generate the Bodhi mind, and use deep faith and vows to uphold the Buddha's name.” (Master Triet Ngo)

3. “The reason the Tathagata manifested in the world is only to speak of Amitābha’s original vow ocean.” (Master Thien Dao)

4. “Whether one attains rebirth in the Pure Land or not depends entirely on whether there is faith and vow. One’s rank, high or low, depends entirely on the depth of practice.” (Master Ngau Ich)

5. In the Treatise on the Degrees of Wisdom, Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna revealed: “The practice of the Buddha-recitation samadhi can eliminate all afflictions and karmic obstacles of this life and previous lives. Other samadhis may have methods to eliminate sexual karma, but cannot eliminate anger karma. Some may eliminate anger karma, but cannot eliminate delusion karma. Some may eliminate anger and delusion karma, but cannot eliminate greed and sexual karma. Some may eliminate greed, anger, and delusion, but cannot remove karmic offenses from previous lives. The Buddha-recitation samadhi vows to completely eradicate greed, anger, delusion, and all worldly afflictions and karmic offenses from previous lives.”

Moreover, reciting the Buddha's name in samadhi often generates great wisdom and vast merit, which can save sentient beings. If Bodhisattvas wish to save beings but practice other forms of samadhi, the results are very slow and inferior. This is because other forms of samadhi do not match the merit of reciting the Buddha's name in samadhi. Why is that? Because the Buddha is the Dharma King, whose merit and wisdom are complete, so the practitioner’s boundless merit and wisdom must grow and be accomplished quickly from the Buddha. Furthermore, because

one constantly recites the Buddha's name, the mind does not leave the Buddha, hence the practitioner frequently encounters the Buddhas…

6. “Only by maintaining the name [of the Buddha] can one realize the True Aspect; there is no need for visualization to see the Western Pure Land” - Master Yin Guang praised the Pure Land practice: “Beings in the nine realms, without this practice, cannot perfect Buddhahood; all Buddhas of the ten directions, without this practice, cannot benefit all kinds of beings.”

7. The path to entering the Pure Land School is that the first step for a practitioner is to maintain purity in “Body - Speech - Mind” (Ten Wholesome Deeds Sutra). The principle of the Pure Land School is “Deep Faith, Aspiration, and Upholding the Name of the Buddha” (Amitabha Sutra).

II) Some Important Experiences in Practicing the Method of Buddha Recitation:

1. There are four methods of Buddha recitation: "Reciting Buddha with True Nature - Contemplating Buddha's Image - Visualizing Buddha in Thought - Reciting Buddha's Name." The method of reciting Buddha's name is uniquely the most superior.

The "Reciting Buddha's Name" method has 10 ways of recitation as follows:

Reciting the name of the Buddha; 2. Châu's Method of Reciting Names, 3. Tùy Tức Method of Reciting Names, 4. Truy Đảnh Method of Reciting Names, 5. Giác Chiếu Method of Reciting Names, 6. Rituals and Bowing Method of Reciting Names, 7. Ten-Number Method of Reciting Names, 8. Lotus Method of Reciting Names, 9. Quang Trung Method of Reciting Names, 10. Observing the Buddha Method of Reciting Names (Ten Essentials of Buddha Recitation – Venerable Thích Thiền Tâm, page 136)

Among the 10 methods of reciting the Buddha's name, only the "Ten-Number Method of Reciting Names" is considered superior, because this method cures two common ailments of practitioners: the ailment of "Drowsiness" (sleepiness) and the ailment of "Distraction" (wandering thoughts, lack of focus).

2. “Counting Ten Numbers of the Name” means that you recite “Namo Amitabha Buddha,” with your mind counting number 1, then continue reciting “Namo Amitabha Buddha” with your mind counting number 2, and continue reciting the Buddha’s name up to number 10. If someone has long breaths, they use 2 breaths (1-5; 6-10 recitations of the Buddha’s name), and if someone has short breaths, they use 3 breaths (1-3; 4-6; 7-10 recitations of the Buddha’s name).

Note that when reciting 10 times “Namo Amitabha Buddha,” you will move one bead of the mala. If while reciting any of the “Namo Amitabha Buddha” the mind is distracted or wandering, you do not move that bead and must recite 10 times “Namo Amitabha Buddha” again, ensuring it is done properly before moving that bead.

3. True Buddha Recitation has 2 important elements:

a) The recitation of the Buddha's name must be clear and distinct, either spoken aloud (in a solemn place) or recited silently (in a non-solemn place), with the ear listening to the sound of the Buddha's name to bring the Buddha's name into the seed of consciousness.

b) The mind and mouth reciting the Buddha's name are united as one (single-minded Buddha recitation).

Thich Dao Thong

(Excerpt from Sutra, and compiled during the 2018 Rain Retreat)

tieu_de: METHOD TO ATONE FOR HEAVY KARMIC OFFENSES, QUICKLY AND EASY TO PRACTICE IN ABOUT 15 MINUTES EACH DAY.
tom_tat: (Every day, you only need to spend 15 minutes practicing with sincere mind and reverence, and there will be no heavy karma or serious sins that cannot be eradicated. Especially for those who are often sick, encounter misfortune, and have accumulated heavy sins)
noi_dung:
METHOD OF REPENTANCE FOR HEAVY KARMIC DEBTS, QUICK AND EASY TO PRACTICE ABOUT 15 MINUTES EVERY DAY.

(Spending just 15 minutes a day practicing with sincere and respectful intention can eliminate even the heaviest karma and grave sins. Especially for those who are often ill, face disasters, have accumulated heavy sins, live in a messy house, have unstable work, possess many bad habits, or suffer from addiction or infidelity, it is even more necessary to repent to eliminate sins. Once sins and negative karma are reduced, it is like clearing away dark clouds, and destiny will naturally become smooth.)

Before performing the repentance ritual, one should take a bath, brush and rinse the mouth, and wear clean, respectful clothing.

This repentance practice mainly includes the mantra of the Seven Buddhas for Eradicating Sins, which is very short, taking only 5-7 seconds to recite, but its power to eradicate sins is extremely formidable, and the names of the 7 Buddhas who expounded this mantra are as follows.

LY BA LY BA DE

CAU HA CAU HA DE

DA RA NI DE

NI HA RA DE

TY LE NE DE

MA HA GIA DE

CHAN LANG CAN DE

TA BA HA

Should be studied; this mantra should be recited together with repentance, or during bowing repentance—recite it once per bow. This mantra is short, so recite it for about 7 seconds, stand up, recite the mantra once, and then bow again. With sincere repentance, hundreds of thousands or countless karmic offenses will be eradicated, including the five heinous crimes which are:

Killing one's father

Killing one's mother

Causing the Buddha to bleed

Killing an arahant

Disrupting the harmony of the Sangha (using various means to cause division and discord among monks, destroying the monastic community)

These 5 offenses are extremely serious; repentance cannot remove them, yet it can also possibly eliminate them. One should not see the Chinese characters or the short prayer and lightly regard it without reverence, as the elimination of karma cannot be underestimated.

Furthermore, this prayer, when recited during the act of releasing animals, to pray for these animals' karmas to be resolved, is also very effective. Everyone should observe it.

And kneel and bow by standing up and kneeling down, five parts of the body touching the ground.

BEGIN:

WITH ONE MIND, BOW AND PAY RESPECT TO NAMO ALL BUDDHAS OF TEN DIRECTIONS IN THE THREE TIMES

(3 bows)

Each bow is accompanied by one recitation of the Seven Buddhas’ Mantra for Eradicating Sins. (In total, three bows equal three recitations)

With one mind, I bow to all the Dharma treasures of the ten directions across the three lifetimes.

(3 bows)

"Each bow is accompanied by one recitation of the Seven Buddhas’ Mantra for Eradicating Sins"

With one mind, I bow to all the virtuous saints, the great Bodhisattvas, and the holy monks of the ten directions across the three lifetimes. (3 bows)

"For each bow, recite once the Seven Buddhas’ Mantra for Eradicating Sins"

WHOLEHEARTEDLY BOW AND PAY RESPECT TO NAMO BHAIJA THI NHU LAI (3 bows)

"For each bow, recite the Seven Buddha Expiation Mantra once"

WHOLEHEARTEDLY BOW AND PAY RESPECT TO NAMO THI KHI NHU LAI (3 bows)

"For each bow, recite the Seven Buddha Expiation Mantra once"

WHOLEHEARTEDLY BOW AND PAY RESPECT TO NAMO TISHA PHU NHU LAI (3 bows)

"For each bow, recite the Seven Buddha Expiation Mantra once"

WHOLEHEARTEDLY BOW AND PAY RESPECT TO NAMO CAU LUU TON NHU LAI (3 bows)

"For each prostration, recite the Seven Buddha Repentance Mantra once"

Wholeheartedly prostrate, Namo Caṇabhūmi Maṇi Tathāgata (3 prostrations)

"For each prostration, recite the Seven Buddha Repentance Mantra once"

Wholeheartedly prostrate, Namo Kāśyapa Tathāgata (3 prostrations)

"For each prostration, recite the Seven Buddha Repentance Mantra once"

Wholeheartedly prostrate, Namo Original Teacher Śākyamuni Tathāgata (3 prostrations)

"With each prostration, recite the Seven Buddha Expiation Mantra once"

Your disciple's name is... age... Dharma name... Today, I sincerely and respectfully repent for my sins (declare the sins that I have committed in this life, for example, committing adultery with someone, killing some creatures, stealing from someone... etc.), then I continue to declare

"I sincerely beseech the Buddhas, the Dharma, the Sangha, and all the Wise, Holy, Great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions to witness my repentance. I repent for in countless past eons and in this very life, due to ignorance, I have been led by greed, hatred, and delusion to commit countless sins, such as killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, speaking harshly, speaking dupliciously, speaking vulgar or lustful words....etc., which cannot encompass the countless offenses. Now I sincerely repent, vow to reform, and not commit them again, and to regularly uphold the Five Precepts and follow the teachings of the Buddha, which are:

1. Do not kill

2. Do not steal

3. Do not commit sexual misconduct

4. Do not lie

5. Do not use addictive substances or drink alcohol" (Read the passage from "Kính mong" to "do not use addictive substances or drink alcohol" 3 times).

I sincerely pray to the Ten Directions Triple Gem, the Seven Buddhas of the past, and all the great Bodhisattvas to witness and bless me so that my karmic obstacles are quickly removed, my body and mind are at peace, healthy, everything goes as wished, practice diligently, open wisdom, benefit myself and others, and everything is safe and as desired.

Then bow to the Triple Gem and step back.

So in total, there are 30 bows and 30 recitations of the mantra altogether. But because this mantra is very short, anyone who wants to eliminate more sins can recite 3 mantras for each bow. For example, a total of 30 bows and 90 recitations.

✅ And the most important thing is that when bowing to the Buddha, if each bow is done with a heart of reverence, it will destroy countless heavy sins accumulated over hundreds of thousands of lifetimes. Even just one bow can bring immeasurable merit.

And if one prostrates many times but the mind is elsewhere, or cannot arouse a sense of reverence, it is still not equal to one sincere prostration.

Quality over quantity.

Those who are old, weak, or sick and cannot kneel may sit and bow.

Every day, dear practitioners, please take 15 minutes to repent and you will see miraculous results.

It is hoped that those who are busy but wish to practice repentance will save this message and uphold it daily.

tieu_de: VENERABLE LANG NGHIEM - DIVERSE SENSATIONS
tom_tat: Hanh Doan recruits translators. My name is Thong Dong, disciple of Master Pho Quang! There are many spiritual inspirations about the Lingyan Mantra! Now I would like to recount a few experiences that I personally went through:
noi_dung:
CHU LANG NGHIEM - DIVERSE SENSATIONS

Compiled and translated by Hạnh Đoan

My name is Thông Đông, a disciple of Master Phổ Quang! There are many experiences related to the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra! Now I will excerpt a few experiences that I personally went through:

1. The first time I heard a lecture on the virtue of the Great Lăng Nghiêm Chant, I wanted to give up immediately, but when I started reciting, because I was not familiar with the characters, I could only recite a few lines. I found the wording too hard to remember, and the chant too long, so I didn’t have enough patience to finish reciting it! One night, before going to bed, I made a firm decision: “I must finish reciting one round of the Great Lăng Nghiêm Chant! If not, it will not do.”

But there were too many words I didn't know, so I had to open YouTube and recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra online at Vạn Phật Thành (at that time I had not taken refuge with Venerable Phổ Quang at Chung Nam Mountain, but I was more familiar with Master Tuyên Hóa). I put on headphones and followed along with the video. It was very difficult, but I managed to complete one round of chanting.

Then I went to sleep. And then a strange dream happened that has shaken me to this day!

I remember that after dozing off, I dreamed of seeing a large Buddha, about the height of several floors, sitting on a lion (unfortunately I could not see the lion clearly because the place where the lion sat was not very visible). To the left of this great Buddha in midair, there was a tall Bodhisattva holding a wish-fulfilling jewel (looking like Bodhisattva Samantabhadra). The Great Buddha and the Bodhisattva were entirely white! I saw that on the rooftop of a building, suddenly a storm with swirling rain appeared, the sky and earth whirled, and the building I was standing on was about to collapse! I was extremely terrified! Suddenly, from the Buddha, countless sparkling rays of golden light appeared, then the building did notshaking a lot, and there was a large ring emitting a golden light appearing below the building (in my dream I saw it very clearly, but when I woke up I had forgotten).

There is a circle of words “Nam Mô Di Lặc Tôn Phật”, Nam Mô Vi Đà Bồ Tát” very large, appearing above the building, the line “Nam Mô Di Lặc Tôn Phật” also swirling above the building, while the words “Nam Mô Vi Đà Bồ Tát” appear in the middle, all of the words are very large radiating brilliant golden light. After waking up I forgot a lot, I don't remember clearly, but the line “Vi Đà Bồ Tát” I still remember clearly and have a deep impression! In my dream, I also saw countless beings sitting on planes of strange shapes, flying densely into the sky! Truly unimaginable! After waking up, my whole body was sweating, feeling verygentle, comfortable, and moving.

This is the first time I read the Lăng Nghiêm mantra and experienced a strange dream.

2. At that time, I often watched videos of Master Lăng Nghiêm from Vạn Phật Thành and listened to Master Tuyên Hóa giving lectures. I was very happy, but the Lăng Nghiêm mantra was too difficult to memorize. Later, when the conditions were just right, I went up to Chung Nam Mountain to spend seven days reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. Back then, the rules at Chung Nam Mountain were not too strict. After reciting the mantra for about 6-9 minutes, you could stay on the mountain to participate in retreat sessions. I remember one day I was too sleepy and did not wash my hands, hastily going up to the hall to hold the book of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra and open it to read, and as a result, a large bee (I don’t know what kind of bee it was! It was a very large black wild bee) fell in front of my chest because I was not careful with my hands.I touched it and got stung. At that moment, I was in a lot of pain. After a while, my finger swelled up! I tried to endure the pain while chanting during a break, and I told Master Pho Quang that I had been stung by a bee. He laughed and said, "Spit a little saliva on the painful spot and it will be gone!" I did as he said, and soon the pain disappeared and the swelling was reduced by more than half! It's really amazing! I thought it couldn't be just my saliva, it must be due to the Master's blessing! Normally, if stung by a bee this large (this bee is about 2.5 cm long), it would take at least two to three days to heal! Right now, I would like to thank Master! Namo Thang Pho.Venerable Hạ Quang Hòa!

At Chung Nam Mountain, after practicing the seven-day meditation retreat, I gained a lot of benefits and also understood the way more.

On the mountain, I dreamed that I was a technology instructor at my company. As a result, after completing the seven-day retreat, not long after returning, I was made a technology professor (at that time, I had just joined the company, my skills and technical background were lacking, yet I was promoted. Truly unbelievable).

My master also said that I was about to get rich! After that, my salary increased! There were also many other bonuses! The Śūraṅgama Mantra really can save one from poverty! The Buddha's words are truly accurate and not deceitful. (I used to be very poor, always short of spending money and had a bad job.)

2. Master Phổ Quang is very formidable! Chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra more than 100 times, his whole body is like indestructible diamond! Any disciple who has a thought, Master knows it all. Many times, when Master gives teachings, what he says are exactly the thoughts that everyone has in their hearts. I personally have experienced this many times. When Master gives teachings, others may not know, but only those involved, the one who has made a mistake, will deeply understand. Master said: We were sent to Chung Nam Mountain by Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara and Bodhisattva Veda, and I also firmly believe this. I think there is also the blessing of Master Xuan Hua. My entering the Buddhist path is due to this influence.benefit of Master Xuan Hua. After attending the meditation retreat at Zhongnan Mountain, I came down the mountain. Within about a month, I had memorized the Lankavatara Sutra! Because during the retreat, the Lankavatara Sutra was easy to read, I memorized it quickly.

Therefore, fellow practitioners who want to memorize the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra must participate in the Dharma assembly reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra; it will be much easier than chanting at home! And it is best to chant the version of the mantra of Venerable Phổ Quang, which is said to have been transmitted by the Vajra Bodhisattva in a dream.

3. Practicing the Lăng Nghiêm mantra requires diligence. The more repetitions, the better. Even a single recitation is incredibly powerful. Master Hsuan Hua said that reciting the mantra once in the morning (reciting it once protects you throughout the day, and reciting it again before going to sleep protects you at night) and persistently reciting it every day, even if just once, has immense and marvelous power! There are also lay practitioners who are psychically sensitive (mediums) who say that reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra seven times brings forth a green lotus at your feet. OF COURSE, reciting 50 repetitions daily, or 108 repetitions is best. Master Phổ Quang said that reciting 36,000 times is sufficient to basically ensure rebirth in the Pure Land.

Translator's note:

Because I am too busy, I only translated a short section to share with you. If you feel it is enough and don't need to read more, I will stop translating to save time... for practicing cultivation 😂

If you recite 108 repetitions of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra per day, it will take about one year to complete 36,000 repetitions.

If you recite 40 repetitions per day, it will take about three years to complete 36,000.

Master Phổ Quang is in the high mountains of Chung Nam in Hubei Province, Mainland China; you do not need to go there to seek him. Especially during the epidemic and with inconvenient travel, plus the language barrier. Therefore, once you have the dharma, you can practice anywhere, as long as your heart is sincere.

Due to the urgent situation, I am posting quickly so that you can read it immediately, so errors are hard to avoid. I hope you can understand and forgive 🙏🏻

Hạnh Đoan

Source: Kỳ Liên

tieu_de: THE STORY OF CLAMS
tom_tat: 🍁THE MIRACULOUS EFFICACY OF LIFE RELEASE _Hạnh Đoan's narrative_
noi_dung:
THE STORY OF CLAMS

🍁THE MIRACULOUS RESPONSE OF RELEASING ANIMALS

_Narrated by Hạnh Đoan_

The story happened a long time ago: One afternoon, my great-grandparents were given a basket of clams by local fishermen. Fearing that if they boiled and ate them at night their grandchildren might get a stomachache, my great-grandfather told my great-grandmother: Let’s soak the clams in water for now and boil them to eat tomorrow morning!

That night, my great-grandmother dreamed of a kind-faced old woman who came and told her:

- My nephews and nieces went out to play and got lost, they haven't come back yet. I heard someone say they went into your house, did you see them?

Ba Co woke up with a start, and in the morning told her husband about it, her husband said:

- Dreams and hallucinations, why bother believing or worrying about them and exhausting your mind?

Before Bo Co boiled the clams, in the morning she went to the market and told her acquaintances about it. Everyone said:

- Oh, just let the clams go, lady. Having such a dream and still trying to boil and eat them might bring bad luck. Even if we were to meet them, we wouldn't dare to eat!

She went home to tell her husband. He said:

- In that case, let's release all the clams!

That night, she dreamed that the old lady from yesterday appeared again, this time with a beaming smile, saying:

My grandchildren have returned home. Thank you for letting them go.

After some time, their fifth daughter fell ill, additionally suffering from chronic insomnia, and her health gradually deteriorated, with no treatment seeming to work.

One night, the grandmother dreamt of an old lady from the past, holding a basket of lotus seeds, who said:

- These lotus seeds are very good, give them to your daughter to eat, and she will gradually recover.

Upon waking, she discussed it with her husband and decided, since they had no other options, to try it out…

The couple went to pick lotus seeds for their daughter to eat. After eating them, their fifth daughter gradually became healthier, and after a while, she fully recovered.

Grandparents realized that it was thanks to me releasing the clams that they received blessings.

(Written according to the thoughts of a reader, based on the story told by My Su)

🌲COMMENTARY:

☘ After reading this story, do you believe it? I have read many stories about releasing life, seeing turtles or tortoises appearing in dreams to thank the person who released them. These stories are from a long time ago, so it is hard for me to believe. Even though I am a strict vegetarian, even though I occasionally release life (it’s just that I happen to see fish being killed, I feel guilty so I purchase them to release; this is called an unexpected release... to save their lives in time, not intentionally going to the market to buy life to release). Even though I have released many, I have never dreamed of a single fish thanking me.

However, after finishing, the mind often feels joyful, with a sensation as if floating on clouds, unexpectedly happy, and sleeping very well at night.

I've just been telling others' stories, whether you believe them or not is not certain, but when I see something interesting or strange, I share it with my FB followers, that's all.

☘ Now I will tell my story: I have a friend who follows Christianity, gentle, generous, kind, and likable; the only thing is that she believes in "food nourishes people," so she kills animals heavily, plus she is talented in cooking and seasoning well, so everyone likes her, everyone is fond of her. Therefore, whenever a family has a party for memorial services, weddings, etc., they all rush to hire her to cook.

My friend was just fifty years old, and suddenly she got severe diabetes, and before long she passed away.

I was puzzled, wondering constantly, silently thinking: My friend is gentle, so good-natured, why was her life so short?

That night, I dreamed I heard faintly in my ear the explanation: My friend, because of killing many living beings, had his lifespan reduced by two 'ky'!

I was startled. In the morning, I calculated: One 'ky' is twelve years, so reducing two 'ky' means losing twenty-four years! Thus, my friend would have actually lived to 74 years, but due to killing too many living beings, he had a premature death, only living to fifty.

I felt sorrowful… quietly sad. Very sad! Even if I speak of this, surely none of his relatives would believe it, and my esteemed readers, how many of you would believe it?

☘ I suddenly remembered my translations. Phung Phung is a person with a third eye, who once encountered a wandering spirit. He saw that this spirit had a good nature and should have lived to 80, but because he ate a lot of meat and spent his whole life indulging in eating, enjoying animal flesh too much, he developed diabetes and died at only in his fifties.

🍁 BENEFITS OF EATING VEGETARIAN:

I remember Master Xuan Hua also once said a sentence with the general meaning as follows: “When living, eating vegetarian seems like a loss, but after death, it brings benefits. When living, eating meat feels like happiness, but after death, one must endure suffering.”

Eating vegetarian brings great benefits to us: It prevents untimely death, extends lifespan, reduces illness, and even if accidents occur, one is protected and misfortune is transformed into safety. If vegetarianism is accompanied by strict observance of precepts, it is like a tiger with wings, a dragon meeting clouds; everything goes smoothly, mantras become effective, and all aspirations are easily fulfilled.

If you see someone living righteously and eating vegetarian but meets an untimely death or a violent end… it is because in the past they created evil karma and now must repay it. If you firmly believe in cause and effect, just sow good causes, and you will surely reap good results.

This story is written so that readers may benefit. Therefore, whether you believe it or not, and how you choose to live, is up to you.

Hanh Doan - Written on 29/6/2019 7:34

tieu_de: CONFESSIONS OF AN ANGEL
tom_tat: In Mahayana scriptures, the Buddha often reminds that on the days: the 1st, 8th, 14th, 15th, 24th, 28th, 29th, 30th… people should practice vegetarianism and cultivation to increase merit and wisdom, because on these days angels go on inspection.
noi_dung:
CONFESSIONS OF AN ANGEL

In Mahayana scriptures, the Buddha often reminds that on the days: the 1st, 8th, 14th, 15th, 24th, 28th, 29th, 30th... people should practice vegetarianism to cultivate virtue, because on these days, celestial beings go on inspection (roughly, on the 1st and 15th, the Four Heavenly Kings patrol; on the 14th and 28th, the Prince patrols; and on the other days, the Celestial Generals patrol).

If people observe the Ten Wholesome Deeds and eat vegetarian on these days when celestial beings inspect, they will attract favorable weather and increase great blessings.

Although we do not know much about these patrol Angels, there are indeed many gods, each holding a position and responsible for specific duties, each minding their own task. Those in the world with extremely pure hearts can also interact with them.

The following is the sharing of a Buddhist disciple, who strictly observes precepts, has opened the heavenly eye, and has the ability to communicate with the gods. Every sentence told is truthful and sincere. It is hoped that those with affinity, upon reading, can abandon bad habits and cultivate good ones, strive to calm the mind, and widely spread this to awaken others, thereby accruing immeasurable merit:

"Yesterday was the day of Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta's celebration. In the evening, I was meditating as usual, when suddenly I saw a deity approaching me, who said:

I am a celestial general responsible for overseeing the beings of the ghost realm in the human world, yet I often witness scenes of men being seduced by demons. Sometimes I see in places of vibrant entertainment, illuminated by colorful lights, many pairs of men and women sitting together, drinking wine, and having fun.

Although I clearly see that these people are all being hoisted on the backs of little blue-faced, white-toothed demons, with their necks clamped, why do they not feel anything at all?

There was a time when I saw a man sneaking after a girl he had just met, his brain was filled with lewd and pleasurable thoughts, and I saw that he was very stupid, because he didn't know that the beautiful woman walking beside him had been controlled by the devil, leading him to fall into depravity. As soon as they were making love and making love, the demon cubs, the demons and grandchildren of this female demon stood by their sides, watching them lustfully waiting for the moment to suck their essence. Even more dangerous was that they could eat the original flesh and blood of men. But the other man didn't know it, because he was immersed in lust. I saw these men, their spirits constantly circulating, their bodiesThey became worse and worse, but they still showed no remorse, and eventually: They died in debauchery and lust!

When Thien Tuong spoke up to this point, his face looked sad, he bowed his head and sighed, showing a very sorrowful expression.

I asked:

– These demons are so arrogant, why don't you in heaven control them?

He said:

– It's not that we don't control them, but because we only have the authority to punish those demons who roam around harming people indiscriminately. As for anyone who harbors lustful minds or evil intentions, they have voluntarily followed them, which means they are actually inviting and beckoning them. Therefore, no matter how much we want to, we cannot save them!

Most of them are wise and intelligent, worldly, considering themselves intellectuals with profound education, only believing in science, not believing in ghosts, gods, or karma and reincarnation. But unfortunately, they live too indulgently and freely: their lust and evil desires are too great, they refuse to listen to anyone's advice, as if they are driving themselves toward death.

They had no idea that their own strong lust would attract the demon species that feed on essence, lying in wait behind, waiting for the moments when these men and women who were not husband and wife to become immersed in their sexual frenzy, so that the demons could freely drain their essence and spiritual energy… making the men feel dizzy, their minds like they had taken a sedative, no longer alert, engaging in pleasures all night without rest, leaving the young demons and demon children thoroughly satisfied.

In the morning, when they woke up feeling very weak, they went home to rest, but as soon as they lay down, they suddenly felt their heart hurting. Once their eyes closed, if their fortune, luck... had run out, they would immediately turn into a lifeless body. According to medical diagnosis, they were suffering from: "Heart pain and sudden death."

Minh Nhan

LND: After translating these stories, I hesitated a lot, but in the end, I decided to release them. I only hope to contribute to warning and reminding you to live a pure life. The soul-sucking demons mentioned in Buddhist scriptures are often brought up and explained. You have the right to believe or not… but I hope you will wisely choose the best way to live, which benefits yourself!

Karma in This Life

Translated by Hạnh Đoan

tieu_de: PRACTICING TO TRANSFORM THE TEN BASIC KARMIC OBSTRUCTIONS
tom_tat: I will briefly talk about the karmic obstacles we created in past lives so that we know how to practice transformation. The ten karmas are as follows:
noi_dung:
PRACTICING TO TRANSFORM THE TEN BASIC KARMIC OBSTACLES

I will briefly talk about the karmic obstacles we created in previous lives so that we know how to practice transformation.

The ten types of karma are as follows:

1. Karma that causes frequent illness:

Constantly sick, while others are healthy, nothing wrong with them.

The causes of illness karma are:

Often killing living beings, being a deceitful pharmacist selling fake medicine, selling expired food,......

2. Karma related to slow intellect, dullness, slow mental calculation:

Traits such as being infatuated with women or men, addicted to alcohol,

burning books, stepping on books or scriptures, being lazy in studying, disrespectful to teachers, etc.

3. Karma causing difficulties in love life:

Being unfaithful oneself, deceiving others in love, sabotaging those who are already married, ...

4. Karma leading to infertility, difficulty conceiving:

Cursing people as "to be exterminated," being an abortion doctor, liking to eat animals while they are still in eggs or unborn, hating children, .......

5. Karma of being mute or deaf:

Being mute:

Caused by:

Forbidding others to speak the truth, or often cursing people as

"shut your mouth",....

Being deaf:

Preventing others from hearing good things, hearing the truth, such as forbidding others from listening to Buddhist sutra teachings.

Or being overly curious about many things or liking to hear things that are not worth hearing, useless things, evil things,.....

6. Karma leading to poverty :

Causes such as :

A stingy and miserly heart, rarely doing good deeds, seldom helping others, destroying wealth, misusing assets, wasting food, burning crops,....

7. Karma of being orphaned at a young age :

Causes :

Having parents but not loving them, being unfilial, abandoning them.

Having children but not loving them, not raising them, giving birth and then abandoning them at the banyan tree, temple gate,....

Isolating animals when they are newborns like chicks, young birds, puppies,.....

8. Karma of illiteracy, little education :

The causes such as :

Despising books, being lazy to study.

Preventing others from studying, hating teachers,....

9. Karma of ungrateful and disobedient children :

The following causes :

Having parents but not knowing how to care for and nurture them.

Laughing at others, criticizing others when seeing their children being unfilial, ...

10. Karma from working in a foul, polluted environment:

The following causes:

In past lives, worked in polluted environments, did not know how to create a clean and beautiful environment, did not protect the environment, ...

The common point among all methods of practice is:

One must accept that they have once committed evil deeds and made mistakes.

Therefore, repentance is a very effective practice that you must apply.

You must see clearly what causes have created the current results you are receiving.

You must find the right key in order to unlock the lock.

Every day, you should sit in meditation in front of the Buddha altar to acknowledge your faults, and bow to the Buddha to repent.

Then, chant the mantra of seven Buddhas for erasing sins (the more, the better):

Ly ba ly ba de, cau ha cau ha de, da la ni de, ni ha ra de, ty le ne de, ma ha gia de, chon lang can de, ta ba ha.

After repenting, one must be determined to change oneself.

One must transform from a bad person into a good person.

Combine this with daily practice of virtuous deeds such as charity, offering, providing food, releasing living beings, practicing vegetarianism.... to increase merit.

Being persistent and diligent in this way over time, karmic obstacles will gradually diminish and can be transformed.

Wishing you diligent progress in your practice

Namo Amitabha Buddha 🙏🙏🙏

tieu_de: WHY DOES REAPING WHAT YOU SOW COME QUICKLY SOMETIMES, AND SLOWLY OTHER TIMES?
tom_tat: Aquarius: – Quang Tu, please let me, and I hope to receive an answer so that I can be clear.
noi_dung:
WHY DOES RECOMPENSE COME QUICKLY SOMETIMES, AND SLOWLY OTHER TIMES?

Aquarius:

– Master Quang, please give me your insight, and I hope to receive an answer so that I can understand clearly.

For example, friend A and friend B both commit the same mistake, the same sin. But A quickly receives the consequences and stops. Meanwhile, B never seems to suffer any repercussions and continues carelessly making mistakes, committing sins. Such situations are very common in life. Why has B not yet received the consequences and stopped doing evil like A? I hope Master Quang can help me clarify this. Thank you very much.

Master Quang:

– Hello!

Dear friend, the time from creating karma to receiving the retribution varies for each person due to many factors:

1. People in the past create many merits, and in the next life commit sins; the retribution does not come immediately because one must wait until that person has used up their previous merits. For example, some people create such great merits that it is predetermined they will never get sick, starve, or encounter accidents for ten lifetimes. So during those ten lifetimes, even if they kill people and commit all sorts of severe sins, they still do not experience retribution. Only after ten lifetimes, when the old merits run out, the accumulated sins will result in extremely terrible retribution. This is the most common reason why those who create karma are not immediately punished. At the end of the article, Quang Tử will include two stories as illustrative examples.picture for this.

2. On the other hand, for those in the past who created little merit, because they do not have merit to protect them, even a little wrongdoing will quickly result in bad luck and retribution, causing suffering. This is both a disadvantage, because that person will experience a life full of pain, and at the same time a kind of luck, because it makes him quickly awaken and realize to stop creating negative actions.

3. Some people are blessed by the Buddhas – Bodhisattvas, or deities, or spirits in the invisible world..., so when they create any karma, they will be warned with small disasters, like “a word of caution,” to help the person awaken and know to stop.

There are people who plan to take a machete to attack someone, but as soon as they step outside, they fall off their vehicle. Some people enter a temple arrogantly, showing disrespect before the Buddha statue, and that night they have a nightmare where demons chase and beat them, and the next day they fall ill, so from then on they refrain and dare not do it anymore, and so on... This is not yet the official karmic retribution, but only a reminder from the invisible world, to help the person quickly turn around and correct their ways.

4. In special cases, if someone has far-sighted intelligence and fears that in many future lives they might fall into wrongdoing and create negative karma, they will have to endure long-lasting suffering as a result. That person makes a vow to prevent themselves from committing evil deeds in the future, roughly as follows:

"I vow for countless future lifetimes that whenever an unwholesome thought arises in my mind, whenever I intend to speak an unwholesome word, or intend to perform an unwholesome action contrary to the precepts taught by the Buddha, my body will immediately feel pain and suffering, until I can let go of those unwholesome body–speech–mind actions, no longer arise nor act upon them, only then will my body return to peace."

If one recites that vow many times, in future lives, according to the vow, whenever one engages in evil or unwholesome actions, the body will feel pain, forcing one to stop creating bad karma. This is not immediate retribution, but rather the POWER OF THE VOW from one's previous life, locking oneself from falling into unwholesome deeds.

Quang Tu once knew people who, from a very young age, whenever their parents fed them savory food containing the blood and flesh of sentient beings, would vomit violently, writhe, scream, and cry… forcing their parents and family to feed them vegetarian food.

This is not retribution, but surely due to the vow made by the child in a previous life. And so, without any effort, that child will by default be a lifelong vegetarian and may never commit the sin of killing living beings.

In Buddhist scriptures, some cases are recorded where a person, due to a vow in a past life, never approached women to commit sexual misconduct. In subsequent lives, when reborn, whenever the mother or wet nurse tries to breastfeed, the child cries loudly, refuses, and can only take milk indirectly placed in a cup or glass.

While so many monks practice, trying to uphold precepts like not killing, not committing sexual misconduct… struggling tirelessly but still breaking them, those children are born already keeping the precepts, showing us that vows are truly powerful!

___________________

EXAMPLE OF CREATING KARMA WITHOUT YET SEEING THE RESULTS

First story:

THRILLING: A PERSON COMMITS SUICIDE AND DESCENDS TO HELL – TO SEE WHETHER CAUSE AND EFFECT ARE FAIR.

During the Shunzhi period of the Qing Dynasty, in Shunyi County, Beijing, there was a wealthy Gong family, owning hundreds of acres of farmland and a herd of horses. In middle age, they had a son and named him Khánh Hữu for the birth ceremony.

At this time, Mr. Li, who worked as the steward managing the tenant farmers for the Gong family, also had a son and named him Li Phuc.

When Cung Khánh turned 7 years old, Mr. Cung invited a tutor to teach his son. The steward Lý saw that his master's son Cung was receiving education, so he begged Mr. Cung to allow his own son to study together with Cung Khánh, and Mr. Cung agreed.

Time passed quickly, and when Lý Phúc turned 14, he stayed at the academy together with Cung Khánh, meaning they studied together during the day and slept together at night.

One night, while Lý Phúc was sleeping, he dreamed that a large gate opened in the sky, and two deities descended from the heavens, landing right in the academy. One of the deities pointed a finger at Cung Khánh Hữu, while the other deity said:

– How is he?

The other deity said:

– He is a person full of blessings, passed the secondary school exam at 17, passed the bachelor's degree at 19, will be promoted to the second rank in the future, and will enjoy honor, wealth, and prosperity throughout his life.

The deity then pointed to Ly Phuc and asked the other deity:

– What about him?

The other deity said:

– This person has a life of suffering, no fame, and will remain poor all his life.

After speaking, the two gods flew back to heaven. After the two gods went through the heaven's gate, the gate closed again as before. Lý Phúc woke up, feeling strange, and recounted the entire dream to his parents and others.

When Khánh Hữu turned 17, he indeed passed the provincial examination. At that time, Lý Phúc no longer studied. The family had farmland, and although Lý Phúc farmed, he always paid attention to Khánh Hữu's behavior. He saw that Khánh Hữu was domineering, always did evil, was cruel and violent, and did not perform good deeds.

After Khánh Hữu passed the baccalaureate exam and continued to advance, he indeed was promoted to a high-ranking official of the second grade. However, Khánh Hữu, as an official, was corrupt, cruel to the people, and beat loyal subjects.

The behavior of Khánh Hữu was considered a crime in Lý Phúc's heart, feeling that Khánh Hữu would eventually face retribution. Who would have thought, Khánh Hữu lived to 71 years old, still wealthy, healthy, with many children and grandchildren.

Not only that, Khanh Huu could also know when he would die; before his death, he told his son how to arrange his funeral. But Ly Phuc's behavior was completely different from Khanh Huu's. Ly Phuc lived frugally, treated people very properly, moved toward goodness, and did not commit evil deeds.

For evil people like Khanh Huu, they enjoyed blessings throughout their life and even knew the day of their death in advance. In his heart, he felt unfair, feeling that even in the underworld there was bribery and corruption, and he was determined to go with Khanh Huu to the Netherworld to seek the truth.

So he told his son that he would die on that date, and to prepare for his funeral. Mr. Lý Phúc wanted to go with Khánh Hữu to the underworld to see how it was, insisting on seeing it clearly. Lý Phúc told his son when he would die, not because he knew the time of his death, but because he had purchased a package of poison in advance.

If Khánh Hữu truly died on the day he said, he would take the poison to die along with Khánh Hữu to go down to the underworld to meet King Yama.

Unexpectedly, Khánh Hữu really died on that day, and Mr. Lý Phúc also drank poison and died along with him.

Down in the Underworld, King Yama finished dealing with Khánh Hữu's affairs before coming to meet Lý Phúc, and said:

– Why have you come as well?

Lý Phúc replied:

– I came down here because of Khánh Hữu. In the human world, people fear power and respect wealth; is it possible that the King of Hell in the underworld also has to fear in the same way? I thought that Khánh Hữu lived on the human world, cruel and evil, committing countless wrongdoings; when he was alive, he did not suffer any retribution, so coming to the underworld, he should face punishment. I didn't expect that the human world and the underworld are actually the same.

The King of Hell said:

– Wait a moment and you will understand.

Yama ordered the judge to open the book of birth and death, good and evil, to take a look. On the name of Cung Khánh Hữu, there was a line of writing. Yama said:

– Because in the previous life Khánh Hữu did many great good deeds, in this life, although committing evil, he has consumed quite a bit of the good merit from the previous life. But there is still a lot of remaining blessings from the great good deeds of the past life.

Therefore, when transitioning to the next life, he will still enjoy blessings, but not as great as those in the previous life.

For the evil deeds he has done, the time for retribution has not yet ripened. Your Lý Phúc, because in a past life he was not diligent in doing good deeds, must suffer in this life.

But because he became enlightened and wholeheartedly did good deeds, although he does not enjoy blessings in this life, he lacks nothing in clothing or food, and when he moves to the next life, he will enjoy great blessings.

Lý Phúc prayed to King Yama that when he reincarnates he not be given Meng Po's soup, so that in the next life he can witness the results of Khánh Hữu's actions. King Yama granted Lý Phúc's request.

Lý Phúc followed Khánh Hữu to reincarnate. Because he had not drunk Mạnh Bà's soup, he knew everything, and he realized that Khánh Hữu was reincarnated into a wealthy family. He, on the other hand, was reincarnated into an average family, still practicing and maintaining virtue.

Khánh Hữu, when he grew up, became a county magistrate, still cruel to the people, without any remorse at all, relying on his power to be corrupt and harm the innocent.

Because he forced confessions, he gouged out a person's two eyes; because of a wrongful case, he cut off another person's legs. Khanh Huu lived to be over seventy, fell ill, and passed away. Ly Phuc had the intelligence to cultivate to a high level. After many years of hard cultivation, he reached a stage where he could leave his body and descend into the underworld.

Knowing that Khanh Huu had died, Ly Phuc sat in meditation and entered a trance, his soul leaving his body to follow Khanh Huu to meet King Yan. This time, unlike before, King Yan dealt with Ly Phuc first and only then attended to Khanh Huu.

When seeing under Khanh Huu's name in the book, the merit had been completely exhausted.

When serving as an official, poking out people's eyes and cutting off others' legs, these two actions can only be repaid with one's own body. It was judged that Khanh Huu in the next life would be born into a poor family, blind, with disabled legs, begging on the streets every day, suffering immensely.

When Ly Phuc saw the cause and effect of Khanh Huu across three lifetimes, each one had its reason and was extremely fair. Moreover, he realized something even more important, which is that the cycle of birth and death over many lifetimes is actually very frightening.

In this life, being a good person and generating much merit does not guarantee that one will be good in the next life. On the contrary, when blessings come, indulging in them can change a person’s nature, making them greedier, more cruel, and then commit many sinful acts. Thus, in the following life, they will endure terrible retribution...

Fearing the loss of his true nature and having to undergo the cycle of reincarnation, he persevered in cultivation, generating a courageous intention to save himself and others, determined to diligently practice until his merits were complete, permanently escaping this cycle of birth, death, and suffering.

(Excerpt from Ngọc Lịch Bửu Phiêu)

KILL A GOAT AND BE REBORN IN HEAVEN?! – MISCONCEPTIONS ABOUT CAUSE AND EFFECT

By Admin Team - August 20, 2019

In the time of the Buddha, there was a butcher who went to meet King Ajatashatru to request a favor. The king asked:

– What do you wish to request?

He replied:

– When you hold your sacrificial ceremonies that require the slaughter of animals, if Your Majesty permits, I will devote myself to that work.

The king said:

– Slaughtering is a job few like; why do you wish to do it?

He replied:

– In my past life, I was originally a poor person, working as a goat butcher to make a living. Because of that work, after death I was born into the heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings. When my lifespan in heaven ended, I was reborn as a human, continuing the work of goat butchering. When I died again, I was born into heaven for the second time. In this way, I spent six lifetimes on earth as a goat butcher, and because of that, I was reborn into heaven six times, receiving blessings beyond measure. For that reason, I have come here to ask the king to let me continue this work of butchering.

The king said:

– You are setting up such a lie, but how could you possibly know this?

He said:

– I know about the previous life.

The king, unable to believe, thought he was lying, and pondered: "How can such a lowly person know about a past life?"

Later, the king met the Buddha and immediately reported the matter to inquire.

The Buddha taught:

–Truly as he said, not a lie. In a previous life, this person had encountered the Bích-chi Buddha. He saw the Bích-chi Buddha with delight in his heart, sincerely observed carefully, contemplated from head to toe, and then generated wholesome thoughts. Due to that karmic connection, he was blessed to be reborn in heaven six times, return to the human world six times, and know his own past life karma.

Because his virtues were well-practiced, it was not yet time for him to experience the results of suffering. When this life ends, he will fall into hell to atone for the sin of having killed a goat. Once the sin in hell is exhausted, he will have to be reborn as a goat multiple times to complete his lifespan. That butcher only knows a little about past lives, seeing six times being born in heaven but not knowing the seventh life: When experiencing a human body, the merits accumulated previously explain why he mistakenly thinks: "By killing goats, one can be born in heaven." In this way, only knowing the previous life, he is neither possessing supernatural powers nor is he a wise person!

Therefore, when a practitioner creates merit, they must make a vow and not be negligent, so that the result is clear. Use this example to reflect upon it.

(Excerpt: COLLECTION OF VARIOUS SUTRAS AND EXAMPLES)

Compiled by: Bhikkhu Dao Luoc.

Chinese translation: During the Yao-Qin dynasty, Tripitaka Master Xu-ma-la-thap.)

_________________

Further discussion:

Karma and reincarnation is an extremely profound issue, requiring the wisdom of the Buddha to fully understand, because He comprehends the infinite, countless lifetimes of all sentient beings.

There are occasionally some people who have the ability to see a few past lives, or even beings like the Demon King Bātzūn can know thousands of lifetimes of sentient beings, yet that is still not enough to grasp the entirety of the Truth, as they still harbor many misconceptions.

If one clings to knowing a few past lives and then makes this judgment or that conclusion, it will be really one-sided and dangerous. Like in the story above, the butcher could only see six past lives, in each life he killed goats and in each life he was reborn in the heavenly realm, and he hastily concluded "killing goats will lead to being reborn in the heavenly realm," without knowing about the life seven incarnations ago, when he respectfully served a Bích Chi Buddha, and that was why he was reborn in the heavenly realm, not because of killing goats!

Nowadays, occasionally there are some people who, in some way, can see past lives, but they do not see countless lifetimes like the Buddha, only a few lives, or a few dozen lives at most. Based on that, they also draw various conclusions, contrary to the Buddha's teachings, like the butcher above, which is extremely harmful to those who follow them, leading them into wrong views and accumulating sin. Both the person spreading the wrong views and those who follow will have to face terrible consequences.

Therefore, a wise person should not place their trust easily, but should follow the teachings of the Buddha, for only the Buddha possesses the wisdom to thoroughly understand the endless, countless cycles of reincarnation, while also comprehending all the principles within them.

tom_tat: In the CD about the life of the Late Venerable Thich Thien Tam, a venerable master who promoted the practice of both esoteric and Pure Land Buddhism in Dai Ninh, Vietnam, author Bao Dang mentioned layperson Minh Thien in the Pagoda Management Board.
noi_dung:
REAL MIRACULOUS STORIES ABOUT RELEASE PRACTICES

In the CD about the life of the Late Venerable Thich Thien Tam, a master who promotes the dual practice of esoteric and Pure Land Buddhism in Dai Ninh, Vietnam, the author Bao Dang mentions layperson Minh Thien in the Administration Board of Phat Quang Pagoda in Ben Tre Province.

The fellow Minh Thien made a living trading fish from Tonle Sap to sell to the fish markets in the South. Around 1967, one morning at 11 a.m. while working in his office, Minh Thien suddenly felt sleepy. As he dozed off, he saw a group of more than 20 people, young and old, men and women, wearing blue clothes speckled with yellow, with red hats on their heads, looking distressed and weak, helping each other to walk into the office and kneel down, begging him to save their lives.

Minh Thiện, surprised, asked who they were, then was shocked to suddenly realize and stepped out the door following the direction in which the strangers had just left. When he reached the place where the workers were pouring fish onto the boat, he saw more than 20 blue fish speckled with yellow, the largest as big as a two-year-old child, the smallest as big as a calf, and each fish had a red mark on its mouth as big as a hand, looking like a pointed hat, with eyes as if asking him for help. Minh Thiện felt a chill down his spine, got goosebumps, and broke out in sweat; he suddenly thought that these were the people who had come to ask him for help, so he ordered someone to release them into the river. From then on, he quit the fish trading business and moved to Da Lat to trade vegetables and fruits.

🍁The Ancestors often taught: “In the ultimate reality, not a single speck of dust is retained; in the skillful means of the teachings, not a single practice is abandoned.”

(In the true and ultimate realm, all false and differing views are completely ended, so that not even a speck of dust clings. But when practicing or engaging in Buddhist activities, do not neglect a single good deed.)

🍁According to the teachings of Venerable Tuyen Hoa, Buddhism has up to 84,000 methods, and each method helps practitioners transform afflictions and attain liberation and enlightenment. Life release is one of these superior methods, so it should not be underestimated.

(Nguyen Thanh)

_________________________________

During the Early Tang period, the Prefect of Do Cam O, one day suddenly fell seriously ill, and the physician mistakenly gave him the wrong medicine, so his life was nearly at an end. He then made a vow:

“I vow to dedicate myself to helping people and benefiting the world to atone for my wrongs; besides that, I am no longer attached to anything else.”

Then, one day he dreamed that the Venerable Avalokiteshvara came and said:

“In your previous life, you served as an official in the State of Chu. When handling official matters, you were overly strict, which harmed your benevolence. However, since you had no personal motives, only your salary was reduced. Moreover, because you often killed living beings, you suffered the retribution of a short life. Fortunately, during a serious illness, you made firm vows, with each vow set on saving lives and benefiting others, without any trace of resentment. Therefore, the underworld used your merits to offset it, thereby benefiting you. Only the virtuous deed of 'releasing lives' can increase your own lifespan and also enhance your position and fortune. You must be careful and make continual efforts to continue this practice."

implement”.

After waking up, he told his family not to kill living beings and even spent money to buy animals for release, so during that winter he was promoted and received orders to be transferred to serve as the Prefect of Jiujiang.

By the spring of the second year, he was completely healthy.

The prefect felt grateful for the greatness of the act of releasing life in Buddhist teachings, so he took altruistic benefit as his great vow, taught others to release life, not to kill, to follow a simple vegetarian diet, treat people with extreme kindness, be fair but not strict. Later, he enjoyed a fairly long life and passed away without illness.

(Excerpt from “True Stories of Miraculous Outcomes from Releasing Lives”).

🍁 MERIT OF RELEASING LIVES:

Releasing lives: is a very common way to cultivate merit, bringing great virtue along with many miraculous results. To perform releasing lives, you need to find and buy animals that are about to be killed, which can easily be found in the market, buy them, and then release them into a safe environment. Some notes you need to remember when releasing lives:

•Choose healthy animals, because many weak animals, even if released back into the wild, will quickly die. Prioritize releasing long-living species such as eels, snails, catfish…

•Choose a suitable and safe environment for release; otherwise, they will also die or be caught again.

•There is no need to release according to any fixed schedule; any day is good for release.

• Avoid buying 'released birds' sold at the temple gate, because they are naturally free; they are only caught because people buy them to release. Buying them only encourages people to catch more, causing more harm than good.

tieu_de: WHAT DOES 'BUDDHA-MOUTH, SNAKE-HEART' MEAN?
tom_tat: I am a retired Major General – Nguyen Chu Phat, I have a friend who has position and power. Seeing that he also often studies, I would like to repeat that it is 'studying' Buddhism and giving some praise. He often encourages
noi_dung:
WHAT IS "BUDDHA'S MOUTH, SERPENT'S HEART"?

I am a retired major general – Nguyễn Chu Phát, and I have a friend who has rank and power. Seeing that he also likes to study, I would like to reiterate that by "study" I mean study of Buddhism, and I have praised him a few words. He often advises me to read the sutras "Địa Tạng" and "Heart Sutra of Prajñāpāramitā".

Almost every time he meets me, he boasts that he follows Buddhism and only wants to do good deeds to bring blessings to his descendants in the future.

He said our ancestors had a saying:

"Doing good in a lifetime, goodness is never enough!"

"Nhất nhật hành ác, ác tụ hữu dư."

(Rough translation:

A lifetime of doing good deeds is still not enough!

One day of committing evil, and the evil is already abundant.)

Therefore, I have to try to follow it to accumulate goodness for my children and grandchildren in the future. A little while later, he came to see me with a complaint form against a senior official and asked me to sign it with him. He said:

- Now he keeps rising through the ranks rapidly, money comes in like water, while I just lag behind, only holding empty titles.

In the denunciation letter, he mentioned three crimes:

+ Improper sexual relations.

+ Corruption.

+ Authoritarianism and despotism.

The denunciation letter for all three crimes contains forged signatures, fake addresses, and identification, but they are all vague, and no one can verify them. The denunciation letter for all three crimes contains forged signatures, fake addresses, and identification, but they are all vague, and no one can verify them.

I said:

- He is a good person, he doesn't have the three crimes you listed.

My friend laughed and replied:

- You're slow, writing like that makes the crime heavier, that's what you call denunciation. Besides, once it's called an anonymous letter, you can fabricate it however you want.

I said:

- You follow Buddha but do evil things, make up stories, fabricate, and slander others like this, how can that be acceptable? Too evil!

It was only then that I was startled and noticed, my friend curled his lips into a malicious smile, and said casually:

- I asked to probe which side you are on. As for this petition or similar ones, I have already sent four or five of them. Each petition I wrote differently, in a different style.

I was so surprised, I could only exclaim:

- What an evil gathering there is!

He turned to argue:

- I read Buddhist scriptures just to know about them! 'Cause and effect' and 'Revenge'—I don't believe in any of that! Besides, nowadays such things are so common, just accuse anyone in office and it sticks; how can anyone know the extent of the crime? They must be taught a lesson...

His demeanor at this moment was very arrogant, and his actions were wicked because he relied on having protection.

The complaint he sent never made any impact? Because those above found out it was an anonymous report, they didn't bother to look into it...

After a period of time, he came to see me, his face noticeably aged, gaunt, haggard... He spoke to me, both distressed and panicked, seeking help:

- I received news that my only son, who is in the United States, had an accident and is in the hospital. His friend called back, unclear whether he is alive or dead? I was preparing to go there when the security agency called to warn: "You have a denunciation letter claiming participation in an organization against the State, listed online"! I was so shocked that I shouted: "It's all fabricated!"

Explanation and correction still could not convince the security agency, they even said: "If you do not admit and repent, handcuffs number eight are waiting!"

After telling me, he collapsed and exclaimed:

- Oh my God!!! How can some child invent such cruel things???

I felt my hands and feet go numb, my gut burning like fire, cold sweat pouring down, perhaps:

"I must follow Buddha and relearn the law of cause and effect!"

(Excerpt from “Collection of Cause and Effect Stories” by Lieutenant General Doctor Nguyễn Chu Phác)

_________________________________

Discussion:

The moral principles left by the sages for humanity are not few, but not everyone in the world has the fortune to read them. Some people, when they encounter the teachings of Buddhist Dharma that are both profound and close to life, feel very pleased; this is a fortunate thing because they have passed through the first gate.

Oh, but the happiness didn't last long… then the second barrier suddenly came. That is, reading and liking the principles is already difficult, applying those principles to life, forcing yourself to act according to them is truly a thousand times harder than just reading. And many people who study Buddhist teachings have fallen at this second barrier.

They can talk endlessly about morals, pointing out what person A did wrong in this matter, nitpicking that person B did not follow the Path in that matter, but themselves… they cannot live according to those morals; the greed, anger, and ignorance in their hearts remain uncorrected, their own mistakes go unrecognized, and because of that… their hands and mouths continue creating karma without rest. All their moral teachings stop at "empty words," merely theoretical.

So how can one escape cause and effect? When karma falls upon us, empty theories are of no use, are they?

It's really unfortunate, because they are like people who have found a treasure but cannot sell it for money to use, standing in the middle of treasure yet having to starve to death.

If you are fortunate enough to read this line, please remember, the Buddhist teachings are meant for each person to take them to correct themselves, to create a new path for themselves to reach a brighter future. And that can only happen when we control our own hands and our own mouth, and must follow the Dharma!

MOM HAS PASSED AWAY AND CAME BACK TO TELL ABOUT THE AFTERLIFE

Today I am sharing these things, and they are 100% true, as my mother told me.

My mother, who passed away due to an accident, was also comforted first.

Last night around 11 PM, my siblings and I were sitting talking in the house when my mother came back (possessed) into my younger brother, then cried and spoke to us.

Mother recounted how she passed away and arrived in the underworld:

Two days before my mother passed away, Mr. Nam Tao reported to Mr. Thanh Hoang Lang (who manages all the souls of this village) that my mother's time was up and came to tell her to go, saying that if she owed anyone or had anything unfinished, she should take care of it (as people who are about to die often have omens or unusual signs).

Exactly 2 days after my mother passed away in an accident, she said that for the first 3 days she had to complete the procedure of cutting the household registration in the living world, and after 3 days she entered the registration in the underworld. During the 49 days after death, she had to report to the underworld officials, who judged her karma and merit from when she was alive in the human world. When going there, she passed through 7 prison gates and saw many people who had committed crimes being executed (I often read the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra, so when I heard my mother speak, I immediately believed her, everything she said was exactly as in the Sutra).

Passing through the 7 prison gates, there were 3 bridges.

The first bridge: is for the celestial beings and the human realm (in the scriptures it is called the Heaven realm) (the 'human realm', when reincarnated as a human, drinks the Meng Po soup and then forgets everything to proceed with reincarnation)

The second bridge: is for hungry ghosts

The third bridge: is for animals

I asked my mother: in the past few months, I have done virtuous deeds and dedicated the merits to you. Do you know, can you receive them?

Mother said: Yes, the officials called mother over and said that thanks to the virtue of her daughter, mother would also receive a portion, but it still wasn’t enough to be liberated; the time to be reborn could also be shortened.

Mother said: Because of that, mother is also happy; every time the officials call mother to report, they smile at her (just hearing that, I already feel very joyful and happy).

Mother advised: You children in life must absolutely not do evil deeds, live with virtue and accumulate merits; if I do not benefit, my children will benefit (living a life full of virtue is more than enough to prosper).

Mother continued: going down there (the underworld), I saw many people who had committed evil deeds while alive being tortured and beaten.

People who were married but had improper relationships with others were tied to bronze pillars and then hacked apart.

Thieves had each of their finger joints cut off.

Those unfilial to their parents were thrown into vats of boiling oil...

When we die, we only take with us the karma and consequences we created in this life.

Hell is real, cause and effect, retribution is real; hopefully everyone will know not to do evil deeds so as not to suffer.

(Source: FB Tran Hoang)

noi_dung:
TODAY TRANSMITTING THE TRUE DHARMA THROUGH INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY IS THE PATH TO OVERCOME LIMITLESS MERIT

☘In this life, encountering the Buddha's teachings, I realized that the Dharma is supremely excellent beyond comparison and can change one's own destiny. In past lives, I was negligent in practicing merit, so in this life I am poor, sickly, and lacking wisdom. Encountering the Dharma affirms that fate can change greatly. In Buddhism, there is a saying "whoever asks will receive," and no one is abandoned at the Buddha's gate. The reason you do not receive what you ask for is that you are not asking correctly or in accordance with the Dharma. What does it mean to ask correctly and according to the Dharma? It is practicing generosity. Giving the Dharma leads to intelligence and wisdom, fearlessness in giving leads to health and longevity, and giving wealth leads to prosperity. But among the typesGiving alms, giving the Dharma is the most excellent, because it includes both material giving and fearless giving. Therefore, I realize that if I want to change my own fate and make up for the merits lacking in the past, this life has no other way but to give the Dharma. A person without merit certainly cannot hear the Buddha's teachings, because the Buddha is perfect in both merit and wisdom, so people honor him as the 'One Perfect in Both.' Learning from the Buddha is learning perfect wisdom and perfect merit, so those without merit cannot hear, understand, or fully realize the Buddha's teachings; they simply do not have merit. I want to become a Buddha, perfect in both merit and wisdom, so I must cultivate merit.

tieu_de: LISTENING TO SCOLDING IS A WAY TO PURGE BAD KARMA
tom_tat: (Excerpt from 'Cause and Effect' attached to 'Lương Hoàng Sám' - Quả Khanh) In 'Lương Hoàng Sám' there is a passage that says:
noi_dung:
HEARING CURSING IS A WAY OF ACCUMULATING BAD KARMA

(Excerpt from 'Cause and Effect Supplement Explaining Lương Hoàng Sám' - Quả Khanh)

In Lương Hoàng Sám, there is a passage that says:

The Prajñāpāramitā Sutra teaches that: “If anyone recites this sutra and is despised by others, it is because that person committed a grave sin in a previous life, deserving to fall into the path of evil. Nowadays, being despised by others helps to eliminate the sins of the past life.”

Explanation:

In the "Diamond Sutra," it is also taught: if a person upholds precepts and practices cultivation, constantly abandoning evil and doing good, but is looked down upon by those around them, it is because if this person in this life does not approach the Buddha's teachings and does not believe in the Buddha, then it is due to extremely bad karma from a previous life; after death, they will be reborn in a lower realm. By encountering the Buddha's teachings, learning cultivation, and strictly upholding precepts, the karma that should have caused them to be reborn in a lower realm is now eliminated thanks to being scorned, humiliated, and slandered by others. Therefore, those who insult them and look down on them are actually helping them eliminate karma.

If you clearly understand the principle 'instead of paying a heavy karmic debt, you can transform it into a lighter payment through cultivation,' then you should thank the Buddha and be grateful to those who are insulting and despising you.

THE IGNORANT MOTHER

There was a female scholar in Taiwan who, when she was young in her hometown, gave birth to a baby girl. Because that year was the Year of the Goat, she believed that giving birth to a girl was inauspicious, so she pressed her daughter into a water barrel and drowned her to death.

Since then, for many years she suffered the karmic retribution, her entire body in constant pain. Later, at a dharma assembly I attended, she was seen by Layman Chu sitting next to me (who had also opened his divine eye) regarding her past. Without fear, he spoke a sentence that exposed the whole matter. Immediately, the mother who had cruelly killed her child was surrounded and scolded by hundreds of people present.

Half an hour later, suddenly her painful illness disappeared completely. She was extremely grateful to Layman Chu, believing that it was because he revealed her guilt that her karma was eliminated. Layman Chu said to her:

- You must be grateful to those who have just insulted you; they are the ones helping you eliminate your karmic debt.

Therefore, when dealing with people who insult us, we should not harbor anger, but should instead use a mindful heart to feel gratitude and appreciation.

Because it may be precisely thanks to those who scold us (to our face) or slander us (behind our back), that our sufferings and afflictions can be quickly eradicated.

(Enduring physical pain or being scolded and insulted are all karma repayment; ultimately, however it is, physical pain is still more uncomfortable than being scolded in the ear. Because, after all, scolding is just "words blown by the wind," and it can even help us escape the pain of illness or the torment of the body. Isn't that a profit for us? Therefore, if we are scolded by others, we should tell ourselves, "Lucky, being scolded by them means I might escape illness or some disaster in the future; what a good opportunity" - QT)

There are many people who, before believing in Buddha, were fine, but after worshiping Buddha, observing precepts, and chanting sutras, they develop serious illnesses. This is exactly: "Future retribution turns into present retribution," meaning the karmic consequences of future lives manifest early in this life, and "Heavy retribution is turning into light retribution," thanks to their worship of Buddha and recitation of Buddha's name, which helps to eliminate their karma.

If one, because of falling ill, starts to have doubts about Buddha, it is like entering a treasure mountain but not seeing the jewels, and returning empty-handed; truly a great pity!
