tieu_de: The Beauty in the Phoenix Dress
tom_tat: (Excerpt from The Report on Present Life, Volume 6 - Quả Khanh) Introduction by the Buddhist Association:
noi_dung:
BEAUTY IN PHOENIX DRESS

Introduction of the Buddhist Society:

This is an article by Lay Master Zhi Ngo, a member who recalled and told about his past life, which shocked the reader

.

The author has an excellent memory and can remember even the time when wearing diapers, and also remembers in the previous life going to hell and the punishment endured. Before going to hell, the author was a girl with a mesmerizingly beautiful face, who, having been deceived in love and money, hanged herself. Because she died with intense anger, she was immediately sent to hell and suffered many torments.

Now, please listen to the author tell the story:

"When I was a child, I had a very good memory. Even from the time I was in the cradle, I already knew and remembered everything that happened: for example, when I was lying in the cradle, I saw my mother suffer from asthma, my father giving her medicine… then when I was learning to walk, how I was chased by a flock of geese… to this day, I still remember it all very clearly. Sometimes, some very strange images would appear in my mind, such as the scene of a prostitute being condemned to hell. Occasionally, when I told my parents about these things, they always chuckled and affectionately said it was because I was still small, so my thoughts were absurd and nonsensical!"

My family practiced a non-Buddhist faith, worshipping deities instead of Buddha. When I was about five or six years old, my maternal grandmother took me to a deity altar to participate in a ritual called the "Opening of the Heavenly Eye": I drank wine infused with hand blood, wrote talismans, and then burned them. From that moment, the door connecting to past life memories opened, allowing me to see through my previous life, with every scene and image vividly clear!

It turned out that in my past life, I was a courtesan, wearing graceful Phoenix robes, fond of watching "ca tử hí" (7) but I do not know which era that belonged to.

Because my family was poor since I was young, I had to work in the kitchen for a wealthy house. Due to my beauty, the owner lusted after me and raped me. After that, I went into a brothel to become an entertainer. The brothel owners were very loving and extremely kind to me.

At that time, I was a young, charming beauty, so I took advantage of my looks to deceive countless people for love and money... In the end, I was deceived by another young master, which caused me to lose all my money and love. I was extremely angry, always wanting revenge, and unable to endure the suffering, so I hanged myself to commit suicide.

I saw the corpse of my own body that had died, but the soul went to a vast place, with blazing fire. Here, there were men, women, old and young… everyone's faces were gloomy and sorrowful, as if we had all entered a predetermined path, an invisible force pulling everyone straight into it.

After walking for a while, we came to a fork in the road, and everyone scattered in all directions. I, along with a group of people, went to the place with a single-log bridge spanning a deep ravine, commonly called Nại Hà Bridge. It was dark, cold, and damp there, with screams, cries, and wails echoing around, and waves of foul, bloody stench hit my nose. Many people on that wet, dark, and slippery bridge fell down below.

I did not want to continue, but I had no right to decide, so I had to step onto the bridge. After walking for a short while, I also slipped and fell down.

Below is a bottomless chasm wider than the sea because no borders or shores can be seen. Inside it are all kinds of snakes, large and small… baring their fangs to tear us apart. These snakes are countless, ferociously attacking me. Later I realized: In this sea of blood, there are many people but their heads cannot be seen, because everyone, like me, quickly sinks into the sea of snakes. These snakes continuously bite and tear our bodies, making our bones crumble and blood flow endlessly. My body feels like it is being shattered by bombs and bullets, a sensation of ultimate suffering, yet in an instant, my flesh and skin recover to their original state.then being bitten, torn, tortured into pieces again and again, that scene of suffering kept repeating. Only then did I realize this was hell.

Karmic retribution now presents mountains of swords and seas of fire, pillars of bronze, cauldrons of oil, torturing crimes…

I just want to get out of this fetid, bloody sea, while the swarming venomous snakes attack; I vaguely hear the weak cries of many people suffering. Having endured enough misery, I finally leave this place of torment and reach the shore. But climbing onto the shore is still not the end of suffering in hell.

Just after leaving the sea of snakes, as I crawled onto the shore, I was terrified when I saw a 'God.' I can only call him 'God' because he looked very tall, wearing a dark gray robe, with an extremely solemn appearance, unlike the Gods worshiped in the human world. He did not utter a word, communicating only through 'spiritual connection,' meaning no language was spoken here (similar to transmitting thoughts mentally).

Suddenly I realized: Because I have no religious belief at all, the figure appearing before me does not take any religious form. Since I do not believe in God or Buddha, rebel against my parents, live a life full of deceit, and practice the immoral profession of a courtesan in brothels, I use my beauty to harm men to the point of death… having committed all these sins, I have come to this place to suffer.

The "Deity" advised me: After receiving punishment, I must make efforts to cultivate and practice virtue.

At that time, I didn't have the slightest bit of shame and repentance, I always felt innocent, I was innocent, I was depressed and angry, when I thought: "Because the deceiver made me hang myself, and yet I died here and was bitten by a poisonous serpent"... so I was furious... the god immediately disappeared.

Mr. Thần disappeared, and I was driven away by a few yellow-skinned demons (like liver pain) to run up a high mountain. The path was rugged and precarious, causing me to stumble and fall… It was at the moment of falling that I realized there was a whole forest of sharp knives, in all shapes and sizes: short, long, big, small, protruding from the ground. No matter where I went, as soon as I fell, these sharp points would automatically "attack," like a "bed of spikes" or "sword traps," continuously slicing our bodies, causing bones to break, flesh to be torn, and blood to flow endlessly, the pain almost making me faint from death. Then the body would restore to its original state, and I would continue to endure this extreme torment, unrelenting suffering without pause.

The scenes of punishment were just as described in the Buddhist scriptures, I only understood this after studying Buddhism later. Because in the "Liang Huang Sorrow" it is written:

After countless lifetimes in hell, one is fortunate to encounter a Good Knowledgeable Person, to hear the Bodhisattvas admonish and advise: "One must repent and reform, vow to practice to escape suffering."

But because I was too violent, stubborn, and obstinate, I had to endure torture there for a very long time.

Even now when I recall it, the feeling of that incessant suffering is still vivid, as if it has just happened to my body. Hell is truly as the Buddhist scriptures describe:

From the upper floor, descending to the lower floor, being barked at by hunting dogs and gnawed on bones swallowing marrow. The Lassa prison guards stabbed a trident into the head… the criminal was burned all over his body, iron nets showered down with blades. The blades pierced the body through the pores.

When I got out of the mountain of knives, I was thrown into a huge, terrifying mill, indescribably large! Watching it move with a roaring sound, I was very afraid of being crushed, but unable to find a place to hide, I had no choice but to run around on the surface of the mill, yet soon my body was ground to pieces, the pain was immense… then my body recovered completely, only to be ground again. I heard the continuous screams and wails of the sinners; they ran, stood, lay down, and sat… in chaos, all being pulverized.

Escaping the mill, I was tied to a blazing red copper pillar, flames burning all around, my flesh scorched, my consciousness hazy.

Once my body was burned to ashes, it would return to its original state. Next, I was tied to another large copper pillar, and demons used sharp hooks to pull out my tongue until it was severed, blood gushing, this is the punishment for the sins of speech, cursing, stabbing, and weaving lies.

Then I was thrown into a pot of oil, my body like a pig being fried, continuously rolling, swelling, feeling as if my body was ripped apart by some kind of bomb, extremely painful, enduring ultimate suffering. But then my body would recover as before, as soon as I just raised my head out of the pot, the demon would immediately use a spear to push me back into the oil, forcing me to continue experiencing being fried. Thus, I was neither fully alive nor fully dead… this punishment repeated over and over, suffering beyond description. Because I created too much evil karma, even when working in the kitchen I once fried, chopped, and pounded… living creatures, so this is just tasting again what I have sown myself.

Having gotten out of the oil pan, the crowd and I went to a dry patch of land, where we had to roll the soil into round balls (some big, some small, with varying shapes and numbers), and once completed, we threw them into our gourds. This scene resembled forced labor; some people, due to the dryness of the soil, could not shape it properly.

Since descending into hell, we haven't eaten anything, so everyone is tired and hungry. After shaping the soil, we went to an area resembling a fire zone. Everyone handed out gourds and each person received a bowl full of white pus that was both smelly and bitter! Perhaps due to karmic connections from past lives being deeply ingrained, I found eating like this too strange, so I didn't bother to eat!

Reincarnation

Then, I was brought before an enforcement officer (Judge). He had thick eyebrows and large eyes; he didn't look fierce but was very authoritative. Just like the deity I met before the serpent sea, he used the method of "spiritual communion" to tell me that I would be reincarnated into the world as a girl. He advised me: "A thousand times, you must not create evil karma, you must not deceive people anymore, and you should do good deeds to accumulate virtue and practice diligently."

After hearing him speak, I was extremely dissatisfied and immediately complained to the law enforcer! Using the excuse that I have endured too much suffering, I am unwilling to remain a woman and want to become a man to take revenge!

Hearing me express that, the law enforcement official looked very surprised; he didn’t understand why I had endured all the tortures without becoming insane or forgetting everything, but on the contrary, remembered the old matters very clearly. Yet he still called me to line up and issued each person a card with a number and a color. I received a pink card, and after everyone received their cards, they went to line up in front of a gate according to the color of the card in their hands, waiting to be reincarnated.

At that moment, I heard some demons gossiping noisily:

- Pink is for being reborn as a female, blue is for being reborn as a male, green is for being reborn as a duck, purple is for being reborn as…

As soon as I heard that, I quickly slipped to the next line because I didn’t want to be a female, so taking advantage of the moment when no one was paying attention, I snatched the blue card from the other person and handed them my pink card.

Seeing the demon rushing towards me, I quickly ran away, blending into the forest of people with green cards. Fearing the demon would stop me, I ran to an area with many houses. It was night, and I saw that some houses had lights on while others did not. I based myself on the number recorded on my card to locate the door number, immediately entered, and thus was reincarnated as the male I am today.

Fated enemies meet again in narrow alleys

In this life, when I entered medical university, I met a girl who turned out to be the fair-faced gentleman who had deceived me in my past life. The first time we met, both of us felt extremely familiar with each other, as if we had known each other for a very long time. Gradually, the influence of past life events became increasingly clear. Eventually, due to parental opposition, and also because I did not want to continue the previous karmic relationship, we broke up (fortunately, I no longer had the desire for revenge).

As for the couple who owned the old brothel before, in this life they are my biological parents. The young man whom I deceived and caused to die, in this life has become my wife. When we first met, I felt very familiar with her but our lives were not compatible, because in the previous life I never loved her, so in this life my inner feelings toward her often generated dislike for no reason. Therefore, she always harbored resentment toward me and treated my family very coldly. Both sides often used the cold war to torment each other. Although I earned a lot of money and brought it to her, repaying the deceitful money from before, she never showed any satisfaction.

In a previous life, there was a man who often helped me resolve many injustices; now he is my close friend.

Repenting past sins serves as a warning to the world to cultivate virtue.

After studying Buddhism, I understand that everything arises from cause and effect. Reflecting on myself, I realize that everything comes from attachment and clinging. In this life, old habits have not yet disappeared. But in this life, I will no longer foolishly commit evil, I will not compete for wealth, and I will not use tricks to seize anything… if I keep chasing bottomless desire, I will suffer forever.

My first girlfriend and I broke up early, and each of us has our own marriage now, but if I look at it honestly, I still find it hard to forget her. Deep down in my heart, I realize that I still have strong feelings for her. But I know this is just karma and an illusory delusion, so I don't pursue it.

Because in a past life I hanged myself, in this life I dare not wear clothes with collars, as I am very afraid of recreating the painful sensation in my throat.

Also, in a past life I worked as a cook, so in this life my culinary skills are excellent.

Because I have experienced the feeling of being fried in hot oil, I am especially afraid of heat, not cold. In this life, whenever I see a moving millstone, I immediately become terrified, my whole body covered in goosebumps.

In short, the habits and memories from past lives have not disappeared at all.

Looking back at the sufferings I have gone through, the rare teachings of the Deity and the Law Officer here have helped my mind become enlightened. I clearly understand: Being human requires valuing trust, not deceiving, not harming others, and not doing anything against one’s conscience.

I also know that life is mostly determined by karma, “you reap what you sow,” we have to taste the fruits we plant ourselves. Those who harm me do not necessarily intend to harm me; my suffering is due to paying the consequences according to the law of cause and effect. Therefore, towards others, I should be tolerant and forgiving, and must not harbor anger.

Having tasted and clearly understood the suffering of hell, do you think I would still be indulged in the five desires, burying myself in committing evil?

Although in my past life I was a great evildoer, irreligious, in this life I have come to seek the Dharma, following the teachings of the Buddhas because the hell described in the sutras is exactly like what I have experienced.

Now I only want to practice, diligently practice until liberation and have no attachment to this world. I very much wish to go to the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha, practice to attain enlightenment, and then return to help sentient beings suffering here.

Through this experience, I sincerely repent for all the mistakes I have committed in the past, praying to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to bless me, so that I may eliminate karmic obstacles, cultivate virtuous roots, be reborn in the Pure Land, and escape the cycle of rebirth.

In fact, all of us have been to hell, because our minds are full of evil thoughts. But due to ignorance, we simply do not remember. Some people are even regular visitors of hell; this is called "just escaped, but seeking to enter again." Hell is originally nonexistent; it manifests because we create evil karma.

The three realms are not peaceful, like walking inside a house of fire, there is nothing to be attached to! I dare not speak of others, only using my own experiences as proof: all the torturous punishments I endured in hell were due to evil deeds of body, speech, and mind (killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, etc... I committed them all). I was once a skilled cook, specializing in killing living beings, stewing, roasting, barbecuing, frying... so I also tasted the pain of being chopped by axes, fried in hot oil; my mouth spoke evil, my tongue committed many sins, so it was gouged out and cut... for the sin of sexual misconduct, I was burned and bound to a bronze pillar.

If in this life I do not know how to repent, do not awaken to correct myself, and continue to commit evil, then it is certain that I will descend into hell.

If we admit that this Earth exists, then we cannot deny the existence of hell and the Pure Land! Infinite karma, infinite worlds, infinite sentient beings… Only the Buddha's teachings are the path that helps us escape the three realms and relieve suffering. Regarding this, I believe firmly without doubt, and my heart only wishes to forever leave the realm of suffering and be reborn in the Buddha's land to practice. Whether you believe the story I tell or not depends on your own blessings and merits.

Please take my story as an example and avoid creating evil karma. I hope everyone diligently listens to the Buddha's teachings, strictly observes the precepts, and diligently practices to transcend the three realms; one should never plant the seeds that lead to hell a thousand or ten thousand times over.

Layperson Triet Ngo

Translator's note:

I translated this story two years ago, but because of my hesitation, I only released it now. One very interesting thing is that right when I started translating, I didn’t know whether the narrator was male or female. In the end, I found out…! When I got to the part discussing the green card, pink card… I also suspected that with that personality, the person might swap them, but how could they actually swap them? I have read many confessions from people who have gone through hell. Basically, they are similar, but in minute details, they differ, no one is exactly alike. I think the person being able to swap the cards was also a kind of "arrangement" by the Judge; maybe he knew in advance that the person would do so. Actually, what identity or genderIt also requires corresponding blessings; it cannot be obtained through deceit. I have tried to translate this story fully, without omitting a single detail, hoping that you can better understand hell.

The most precious thing is that the person who narrates has awakened; although he currently walks among the mundane world, his mind surpasses the mundane world!

tieu_de: HOW IS MERIT DIFFERENT FROM VIRTUE?
tom_tat: Merit (immaculate blessing) and virtue (non-immaculate blessing) are different, we need to clearly recognize this. Merit is practice effort; one must have genuine practice effort in study. The harvest of practice effort is called
noi_dung:
WHERE DOES MERIT DIFFER FROM VIRTUE?

Merit (immeasurable blessing) and virtue (measurable blessing) are different, and we need to clearly recognize this. Merit is effort; one must genuinely practice diligently. The harvest obtained from diligent practice is called virtue. For example, keeping precepts is effort, meditation is virtue. If you keep precepts and achieve concentration, that is called merit. If you keep precepts very well but cannot achieve concentration, does your keeping of precepts bring any benefit? Yes! But that keeping of precepts is not called merit, it is called virtue. If you keep precepts very well and very strictly, you receive the fruit of virtue ofMerit leads to blessings in future lives, it is not the same as virtue. Virtue can eliminate afflictions and can help attain Buddhahood, whereas blessings cannot. Blessings cannot eliminate afflictions, nor can they lead to Buddhahood, they can only bring you good fortune. We must clearly distinguish between virtue and blessings. Practicing concentration brings merit, and wisdom will then arise. The awakening of wisdom is virtue. If one practices concentration but cannot awaken wisdom, then that concentration is a blessing, not virtue. This type of blessing is enjoyed in the heavenly realms of the Four Absorptions; it cannot eliminate afflictions of view and thought, nor transcend the three realms and six paths. Therefore, the difference between virtue and blessing is very great, and we should know this.

How should one practice to have merit? Merit never leaves blessing. Practicing blessings without attachment is precisely merit. Practicing blessings with attachment is exactly blessing. If you practice giving wealth hoping to be rich in the future, it then transforms into blessing. But if you practice giving wealth with "three non-attachments," without any desire, it then transforms into merit. Although you have no desire, in your daily life, you lack nothing, because within merit there is blessing, but within blessing there is no merit. Therefore, regardless of how we practice blessings, understandingIt is often said that there are three types of giving: giving of wealth, giving of Dharma, and giving without fear. Giving can be completely pure, but the key is that the mind must be pure, not attached to the appearance of giving, and one should not often think of the merits one has for others, or of all the good deeds done for them. One should not have these notions. If such notions arise, they immediately transform into karmic rewards, and your mind cannot be stabilized. What is concentration (samadhi)? Concentration is a pure mind. Giving, if absolutely not accepting any reward, makes the mind pure. When the mind is pure, how vast is that merit? It extends to the entire Dharma realm throughout space as the place where we enjoy merit. Not only do you give right here, you enjoy merit right here, but irrespective of where you...Wherever you go, in the ten directions of infinite and boundless lands, wherever you go, you will receive blessings. Why is that? Your heart is vast, without obstacles, therefore your blessings are great, and those blessings pervade the entire space and dharma realm. These important principles are in the Mahayana Sutras, and we should understand them.

If you practice virtue but often get attached to thoughts like, "I have formed connections with people in this area, I have accumulated this many merits," then in the future you will have to be reborn in this place to enjoy those merits; if you are reborn elsewhere, people in that place have no connection with you, and you have not formed this bond with them, so you will not receive the merit. Although you practice the same way, the merits received are not the same. Why do you insist on doing this foolish thing? Why don't you broaden your mind? Any merit you cultivate, no matter how small, spreads throughout space and the entire realm of phenomena; everywhere benefits from it. In the Mahayana scriptures, this point iswe definitely cannot underestimate. Therefore, we must know that merit and blessings are not the same.

(Excerpt from the Amitabha Sutra, 10th recitation, 1998, volume 14 - Dharma Master Jingkong lectured)

*Additional notes:

Normally, if you make offerings, give alms, release animals, observe precepts… do all good deeds, but do not dedicate the merit to all sentient beings in the Dharma realm, what you receive will be merit, and if your mind is still attached to the merit, it will generate merit. This reward is actually very small, much smaller compared to the virtuous deeds, because all phenomena are created by the mind. A small mind produces small merit; if the mind is for the sake of all sentient beings in the Dharma realm, the merit will cover all of space. And the merit accumulated, the merit with defilements can only be used within the human and heavenly realms, meaning it can make one a king, minister, high official, a wealthy and powerful person, or have a beautiful physical body…or become the king of the heavens, the deities……however, no matter how great one's merits are, there will come a day when they are exhausted, and during the process of enjoying those merits, one may inadvertently create a lot of karma, making it very easy to fall into hell. In the past, when Quang Tu first embarked on the path of studying Buddhist teachings, he was very selfish and greedy, always wanting to do many meritorious deeds to become wealthy, beautiful, and fulfilled, such as printing sutras, publishing virtuous books, carving Buddha statues… but his mind was still too attached to the rewards of merit, so greed, anger, and delusion never decreased, wisdom did not increase, which was truly very dangerous. Therefore, even as a disciple of the Buddha, he still indulged in sexual desires, lies, anger…… and nowadays the partMany Buddhists easily fall into this

Merit (immaculate virtue) is what enables us to let go of greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, selfishness, hatred, lust, and so on… It helps us attain the stages of: Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, Arhat, Pratyekabuddha… and allows us to be permanently liberated from the cycle of rebirth. When we practice acts of offering, chanting, cultivation, releasing animals… even to a small good deed like a grain of sand, if we dedicate that merit to all sentient beings, it will generate merit. Whenever we do good deeds without clinging to the reward and dedicate them to all sentient beings, merit is generated, and that merit is immensely great, multiplied hundreds of thousands of times compared to the original, according to the Sutras.Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's original vow is that Kṣitigarbha wholeheartedly advises sentient beings to cultivate merit, all should practice giving and dedicating the merit to sentient beings, which is why one invites the Buddha regarding this matter! Because within merit there is also blessing, even if enjoyed for 100,000 lifetimes, it does not run out. Therefore, after performing good deeds, offerings, or releasing life…, everyone should dedicate the merit like this:

My name is….. Dharma name…… today I release animals/recite sutras/carve statues……. I wish that all the merits I have accumulated be dedicated to all sentient beings throughout the vast emptiness and the entire Dharma realm, so that they may rely on these merits to eliminate karmic obstacles, leave suffering and attain happiness, be reborn in peaceful realms, practice according to the Buddha's teachings, and ultimately attain the supreme enlightenment of Buddhahood!

If it is like this, then this merit is infinitely boundless and even in future lives it will not be fully enjoyed; at the same time, over time, your compassion and wisdom will gradually grow, and your path of practice will advance very quickly!

tieu_de: Back then, poor but sincere and respectful, with a heart that sought nothing, so received great blessings. Now rich.
tom_tat: We see in Liễu Phàm Tứ Huấn a small story about a little girl born in the countryside, whose family was extremely poor. One day, she went to the temple with only two coins on her, which were two old coins.
noi_dung:
THOSE DAYS, POOR BUT SINCERE AND RESPECTFUL, WITH NO DESIRES IN THE HEART, THEREFORE RECEIVED GREAT BLESSINGS. NOW RICH

We see in Liễu Phàm Tứ Huấn a small story about a little girl born in the countryside, whose family was extremely poor. One day, she went to a temple, having only two coins with her, which were old copper coins. Her heart was sincere and reverent as she offered those two coins to the Three Jewels.

The abbot of that temple saw that the girl was very sincere, so he dedicated merit to her. The little girl left, and later she was selected to enter the imperial harem, becoming a concubine of the emperor, in other words, the empress. Many years passed, remembering the year she went to the temple to offer two coins, this time to repay the Buddha's kindness, she received such great merit that she became the empress. She then brought a thousand taels of gold to the temple to offer to the Three Jewels. After the offering was completed, the old abbot was still alive. The old abbot instructed a disciple to dedicate merit to her. The empress was very annoyed: "More than ten years ago, I offered two coins here, and the old abbot personally dedicated merit to me.

Today we bring so much gold, silver, and wealth to offer, so why does he only send one disciple [to quickly dedicate merit] just to get it over with?" Therefore, she questioned the old monk. The old monk told her: "In the past, when you were a child, you offered those two coins with a sincere heart, which is why you attained the position you have today, becoming the imperial consort. Now, although you bring many things to offer like this, the merit is not as great as before; your merit is very small!" You can see the prideful mind, without any humility or virtuous modesty!

She was still quite good, still able to accept, which is why she truly repented and confessed her sins. Therefore, whether one receives much or little merit from giving does not depend on the amount of offerings, but on the sincerity and respect of the giver. At that time, with sincerity and respect, without expecting anything in the heart, one receives such great merit. Thus, regarding the matter of offering to the Three Jewels, we need to understand [this].

Commentary on the Larger Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra - Volume 108

Dharma Master Tịnh Không

tieu_de: Buddha's Crown Radiance Great Bodhisattva Dat Da Bat Dat La Supreme
tom_tat: Today, due to good fortune, I would like to seek the blessing of the Dharma Body of all Buddhas in ten directions, and the Bodhisattvas, so that I may complete writing this entire piece. - As for the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, when I hear it, I feel that it is nothing special,
noi_dung:
Buddha's Radiant Light Great Bodhisattva Dada Batdatra Supreme

Today, due to good karma, I would like to rely on the blessings of the Dharmakaya of Buddhas of the ten directions, Bodhisattvas, to be allowed to write this entire article.

- With the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, when I listened to it, I felt it wasn’t particularly special, not loud, not majestic like other Dharani mantras. I only noticed one peculiar thing that everyone would hesitate or shake their head at when looking at it: why is it so long? Why couldn’t it be shorter so that I could learn it faster? On second thought, it makes sense; the length must have its own reason, encompassing all 5 sections of the Dharma teachings. Consider this: chanting the Great Compassion Mantra once takes 3 minutes, so multiplying that, chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra once takes 30 minutes. Chanting it twice takes a full hour, yet the mind doesn’t feel tired, nor does it feel boring.

- The Dharma Body of the Tathagata is omnipresent, as vast and equal to the void (read the Surangama Sutra to see), so fulfilling one's wishes is not difficult. The only concern is being lazy and not reciting, causing demons and spirits to dislike it, and if karma is heavy, how can one expect miraculous responses? And why recite for miracles? Does it bring freedom? It is better to recite in the hope of attaining the threefold concentration and skillful means to benefit sentient beings; this is more proper. Being pleased by the Buddhas of the ten directions and regarded as a relative by the Bodhisattvas, one will quickly succeed the Tathagata, which is certainly better.

- The benefit of this mantra is that it produces results very quickly; without much concentration, chanting it once already brings fulfillment immediately. There is no long wait, no need to wait, because chanting it once is equivalent to reciting the Great Compassion Mantra eight times without any distracting thoughts, or chanting the Cundi Mantra 250 times according to the number of syllables.

- Furthermore, this mantra does not require setting up an altar, does not require entering a random Buddhist hall, and does not require practicing rituals. Simply chanting this mantra, the merit is equivalent to that obtained through altar offerings and ritual practice, with no difference.

- Each sentence in the mantras has innumerable meanings; when ghosts, spirits, and other beings hear them, countless seeds of bodhi arise. This mantra has more than 3,000 words, which is indeed a considerable number.

- The mantra includes full dedication of merit for practitioners, lacking nothing whatsoever.

-1. Protection from Harm (Dharma for eliminating misfortune). Once we recite the Shurangama Mantra, all misfortunes are removed.

2. Subduing Method (The method subdues). No matter what kind of demonic or heretical forces the opponent possesses, once we recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, the spiritual power of these demons will be destroyed, and they will be easily subdued.

3. Beneficial Method (The method helps to increase benefits). For example, if we practice the path, the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra will help us grow in wisdom, develop the Bodhi mind, and strengthen our vows—everything will increase. That is the method that enhances benefit.

4. Achievement of Dharma (Dharma helps to achieve accomplishment). If we recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, then no matter which practice method we follow, this mantra will also help us achieve accomplishment.

- There is no need to recite a lot; reciting once a day for ten days without purification is certainly not right. But first, this sutra must be read, for there is a reason why the BUDDHA taught the sutra before recording any commentaries.

- A passage in the sutra is as follows:

- Ananda! These wondrous, secret phrases of "Buddha's Radiant Crown, purely white and untainted" give birth to all Buddhas:

- The Tathagatas of the ten directions, by this mind mantra, attain Supreme Perfect Enlightenment.

- The Tathagatas of the ten directions, by upholding this mind mantra, subdue evil spirits and restrain heretics.

- The Tathagatas of the ten directions, by practicing this mind mantra, sit on jeweled lotus seats and appear in countless realms.

- The Tathagatas of the ten directions, by using this mind mantra, in countless realms, turn the great Dharma wheel.

- The Tathagatas of the ten directions, holding to this mantra, often confer empowerment and initiation to Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and even to those who have not yet attained any level of realization. - The Tathagatas of the ten directions, relying on this mantra, often rescue beings from sufferings such as: hells, hungry ghosts, animals, the blind, the deaf, the stammering, the mute, and the eight kinds of suffering; simultaneously liberating them from major and minor calamities; calamities such as bandits, soldiers, kings, imprisonment, storms, floods, fire, water, and even hunger, thirst, and poverty, are immediately dispelled.

- The Tathagatas of the ten directions, when practicing with this heart mantra, are able to receive those with karmic affinity from all ten directions, causing the Śrāvakayāna to hear secret teachings without generating fear of the sutras.

- The Tathagatas of the ten directions recite this heart mantra, attain Supreme Enlightenment, sit under the Bodhi tree, and enter Great Nirvana.

- The Tathagatas of the ten directions transmit this heart mantra; after passing away, they entrust the Buddha-dharma, uphold it until the end, maintain the discipline pure and solemn, and all is completely clean.

- As we explain the mantra "The Light of the Buddha’s Crown is unstained," from morning until night, the chanting continues without stopping. Within it, the words and phrases do not repeat; if one realizes and comprehends from this, they will understand that all sentient and non-sentient beings also constantly recite this mantra, which is why it is called the "Crown of the Tathagata."

- Those of you who are in the stages of learning and have not yet transcended the cycle of existence, if you genuinely aspire to cultivate and attain the Arhat fruit, without reciting this mantra while sitting in the meditation hall, and wish to distance your body and mind from the influence of demons, there is no proper method.

- Ananda! If there are sentient beings in the worlds, depending on the materials available in the country, whether leaves, paper, or white cloth to write this mantra, and place it in a small pouch, if the person is ignorant and cannot recite it from memory, they should wear it on their body or keep it in their house; know that this person will not suffer from harmful poisons throughout their life.

- Ananda! Now I teach this mantra for you, helping the world attain great fearlessness and accomplish transcendental wisdom for sentient beings.

- After I attain Buddhahood, sentient beings in the degenerate age of the Dharma, if they know how to recite this mantra themselves, or teach others to recite it, should know that such sentient beings who recite it cannot be burned by fire, cannot be drowned by water, cannot be harmed by poison, and even all evil mantras of the Devas, Dragons, ghosts, spirits, demons, and magic cannot cling to them. Their mind receives correct longevity, all charms, incantations, poisons of gold and silver, herbs, plants, insects, snakes, and all types of poisonous gases, when entering their mouth, all turn into ambrosia. All evil stars, spirits, even if they harbor harmful intentions toward them, cannot incite evil against them; the evil demon kings Tần Na, Dạ Ca (pig-headed and elephant-nosed) along with their followers,ALL WHO ARE GRATEFUL TO THE BUDDHA, often receive blessings from him.

- Ananda should know! This venerable one usually has eighty-four thousand countless races of Vajra Treasury Bodhisattva Kings, each with their own retinue, protecting day and night. Suppose sentient beings have scattered minds and cannot enter the Three Grounds, but recite orally or mentally in their practice; then these Vajra Kings often support that good man. Especially for a person determined to enter the Bodhi Path, these Vajra Treasury Bodhisattva Kings cause that person to manifest divine consciousness, body and mind diligent, immediately recalling deeds from eighty-four thousand countless kalpas until now, all clearly without doubt. From the first life to the final body, generation after generation, they are never born into the species of Yaksha,Rakshasas, disease demons, stinking demons, sorcery demons, life-force sucking demons, along with types of hungry ghosts with visible and invisible forms, with thoughts and without thoughts, and the realms of wickedness.

- That virtuous friend, whether reading, reciting, writing down, or wearing and offering this dhāraṇī, will never be born into impoverished, lowly places or unsafe situations in any future life.

- These sentient beings, even though they themselves do not perform meritorious deeds, the Tathagatas of the ten directions still bestow merit upon them, thereby in countless kalpas they always coexist in the same place with the Buddhas, possessing immeasurable merit like clusters of evil spirits’ fruits, cultivating together in the same place, never separated. Therefore, this mantra easily allows those who have broken precepts to purify their fundamental precepts, those who have not obtained precepts to gain them, and those who are neither diligent, nor wise, nor pure, nor disciplined in their precepts, to all achieve fulfillment.

- Ananda! That virtuous man, suppose he previously had violated precepts, then after reciting this mantra, all offenses of breaking precepts, regardless of severity, are eradicated. Even if he has drunk alcohol, eaten pungent foods, and other impure things, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, Devas, and spirits will not consider him at fault; even if he wears tattered clothes, whether walking or standing, he is equally pure; even if he does not set up an altar, does not enter the sacred assembly, and does not practice the path, by reciting this mantra, the merit is no different from those who enter the assembly and practice the path.

Explanation: The reason it is so is that, by knowing this mantra, one has already gained much merit. Even the Venerable Wise Master still needs to recite this sutra every morning in order to travel to China. Moreover, the power of the sutra, of the 84,000 infinitely numerous Vajra lineages, causes demons to be terrified, so there is no karma or demonic obstruction that can violate its authority. Reciting this mantra causes the three great heavenly worlds to tremble, prevents demons from harming, and brings comfort even to beings in hell, relieving the three sufferings and thus creating much benefit for others.

- If in the past one committed the grave offenses of the five heinous crimes, the unpardonable crimes, the Four Violations, or the Eight Violations of monks and nuns (equivalent to the death penalty for laypeople), then after reciting this charm, it is like strong wind blows away a pile of sand, all such heavy karmas are completely eliminated, without leaving the slightest trace.

- Ananda! If sentient beings, over countless past lives until now, have accumulated all kinds of heavy and light karmic obstacles, even if they have not had the chance to repent in previous lives, now if they know how to recite and copy this incantation, keep it on themselves or place it in their living space, then the karma accumulated from before will all vanish like ice melting in boiling water, and soon they will attain the patience of non-birth.

- Again, Ananda! If there is a woman who has not yet had children, who earnestly wishes to conceive and sincerely recites this, or wears this charm, she will give birth to sons and daughters who have blessings and wisdom, will live long if she wishes to have longevity, will receive blessings if she wishes for blessings, and even concerning body, life, and strength, all will be as desired. After death, she can be reborn according to her wishes in the pure lands of the ten directions, and certainly will not be born at the borderlands, among lowly people, let alone in mixed or depraved forms!

- Ah Nan! If countries, districts, villages, and hamlets suffer from famine, epidemics; or places are afflicted by disease, turmoil, bandit attacks, and all other disasters, write this mantra and paste it on the four gates of the city, and on small temples or on prayer banners, so that beings in the country follow this mantra, respectfully worship, wholeheartedly make offerings; making every person carry the mantra with them, or place it in their homes, all disasters will be completely eliminated.

- Ananda! If sentient beings in various countries, wherever this charm is present, the celestial dragons rejoice, the weather is favorable for rain and wind, the crops are abundant, and the people are peaceful; all calamities caused by evil spirits everywhere do not arise, people do not die prematurely, and they are not bound by chains, shackles, or fetters, sleeping peacefully day and night, and usually having no nightmares.

- Ananda! In this Saha world, there are eighty-four thousand harmful calamities, ruled by the 28 great evil stars; additionally, there are 8 great evil stars as chiefs, appearing in the world in many forms, often causing strange disasters for sentient beings. As long as there is this mantra, all of them are destroyed, within a range of 12 do (units of distance or time), the fierce calamities simply cannot invade.

- Therefore, the Tathagata expounded this mantra, to protect beginners in future practice, entering the Three Evil Realms (Tri Ma Dia), keeping body and mind at ease, attaining great tranquility, not being harmed by any evil beings, spirits, or enemies, nor by past karmic debts from beginningless time.

- You and those with virtuous qualities among us, along with future practitioners who follow the precepts properly in the monastery, receiving precepts from a pure teacher, and do not harbor doubt about this mantra, then the body born from this person's parents, if not endowed with spiritual understanding, the Buddhas of the ten directions will speak falsely.

Homage to the Amitabha Buddha, the Guide Teacher, of the Western Pure Land, revered by three hundred sixty trillion, one hundred ten thousand, nine thousand five hundred, sharing the same name and title, full of great compassion and great mercy.

Source: Le To Hong

tieu_de: The Buffalo and the Magpie Rise to the Pure Land, Preserving Relics
tom_tat: In 1980, in Fujian, there was a boy herding cattle who said to a cow: 'Tomorrow you will be sold to the butcher.' The cow immediately shed tears and knelt on its two front legs. The boy herding cattle said
noi_dung:
The Buffalo and the Parrot's Rebirth Leaving Relics

In 1980, in Fujian, a boy herding buffalo told the buffalo, "Tomorrow you will be sold to a butcher." The buffalo immediately burst into tears and knelt down on its front legs. The boy told his parents and local officials to come and see it, and then the buffalo knelt down and asked for his life. Everyone took pity on him, donated some money to buy the buffalo and took it to a monastery to be released. After the buffalo came to the monastery, the buffalo enjoyed listening to the sutras and bowing to the Buddha. At the endLife, the buffalo knew beforehand the time of its death, it slowly walked out to the field and lay down. After half a day, the buffalo passed away. That was on the 13th day of the 10th lunar month in 1993. The buffalo was buried at the place where it died.

---000---

In 1987, a blue-feathered parrot with a red beak from Lushan, Sichuan Province was brought to Baodou Temple in Inner Mongolia. Because this parrot was foolish, could not speak human language, and would peck at people who tried to train it, it was not very well liked. Eventually, the parrot was given to the elderly layman Wang to raise. Everyone in Wang's family were devout Buddhists who liked all kinds of animals and small creatures. They kept many dogs, cats, goats, and pigeons that had been abandoned by people. After the parrot came to this family, it listened to tapes chanting the name of Amitabha Buddha and Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva all day long, and its temperament becamegentler. Many months later, the parrot that previously could not learn to speak at all began to recite the name of the Buddha! It recited 'Namo Amitabha Buddha! Amitabha Buddha, Buddha, Buddha! Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva! Avalokiteshvara Buddha!' etc… Its voice was very clear and pleasant to hear. Usually it would also say, 'Recite the Buddha quickly! Brother, recite the Buddha! (Brother is its proper name), ah, recite the Buddha!'

Every day, when its owner chants morning and evening prayers, the parrot usually follows. Whenever someone chants or recites Buddha’s name in the Wang family's Buddhist hall, it participates. Even when its owner silently recites in his mind, the parrot knows and recites as long as the owner does. The most remarkable thing is that besides chanting Buddha’s name, no one can teach it to say anything else. The Wang family receives many visitors at home for gatherings, and there are many conversations in the house daily. However, the parrot never learns ordinary phrases like “How are you? Please have a seat.” These are the sentences people try to teach it. It only says"Chant Buddha! Namo Amitabha Buddha!"

One day in May 1998, the parrot was frightened by something and then stopped eating. It had continuous diarrhea until the next day. Near the end of its life, it chanted the Buddha's name with its owner, and a faint voice of "Namo Amitabha Buddha" could be heard from its throat. After passing away, its body remained soft and its feathers still shiny as if it were alive. Layperson Mr. Wang and his entire family chanted for it for 12 hours. They invited an elderly Dharma master from Wutai Mountain to preside over the cremation ceremony, and more than a hundred laypersons who knew about it came to attend. It was a solemn ceremony. After the cremation, people foundseeing the parrot's tongue still intact and more than 20 white relics like pearls with tiny red spots, along with dozens of relic seeds.

This story, along with many other stories about animals in Buddhism, shows that from the wisest creature to the most foolish one, all can benefit from reciting the Buddha's name. This story also shows that all sentient beings have Buddha-nature and can become Buddhas.

Namo Amitabha Buddha 🙏

(Collected)

tieu_de: Chanting the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra for nearly two years, the gray hair turned black
tom_tat: _Hạnh Đoan recruitment translation_ (posted according to the request of... 30 people who need to read)
noi_dung:
CHANTING THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA FOR NEARLY TWO YEARS, WHITE HAIR TURNED BLACK

_Translated by Hạnh Đoan_

(posted according to the request of... 30 people who need to read)

For the past two days, a female layperson in her sixties has shared her joy with us (those at Phat Thanh Tu)

She said: I chant the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and my gray hair has turned black!

The first time we heard the news "chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra turns gray hair into black," we were very surprised and asked her:

- How did that happen?

The thing is, that day she ran her hand through her hair and suddenly discovered many new hair strands growing in, all black, which made her extremely surprised and delighted, so she shared the news with us.

When she was 50, her hair was already very gray, "more salt than pepper," but since last year, she has been diligently reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra 7 times a day. This year, she increased it to 21 recitations a day. Unexpectedly, in less than two years, both her spirit and demeanor have improved. The most remarkable phenomenon this year is: although she is now 60 years old, all the newly grown hairs are completely black.

The next day she cut her hair; since her new hair roots were all black, she had a new (very short) head of jet-black hair, making her look youthful and healthier, much more vibrant than before!

She also shared with us another joy: her son started to diligently practice acts of kindness and charity, which made her very delighted and happy.

Her son opened a food company on his own and has always been eager to sponsor impoverished children.

She said: When my son sent me a live video of the scene of virtuous deeds for me to watch, witnessing my son change and enjoy doing good deeds, my heart was very happy.

She had been reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra for less than two years, and not only did she personally gain benefits, but she also influenced her son to turn his heart in a positive direction.

As an elderly female lay practitioner practicing at home, she persisted in reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra without interruption, and every year the number of mantras did not decrease but increased; this diligence commands respect from people.

Master Xuan Hua said: I met a person who, no matter how busy he was, read the Lankavatara mantra seven times every day. Because of this, in his life he often experienced great spiritual responses, and these subtle responses are indescribable.

Those of you studying Buddhism should diligently practice the Lankavatara mantra. If you can memorize and recite the Lankavatara mantra, then your entire life as a person can be considered not wasted.

If you cannot learn or recite the Lankavatara mantra, it is like entering a treasure mountain only to return empty-handed.

The Lăng Nghiêm mantra originates from the true nature of the heart and contains everything. Those who can recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra are people with incomparable blessings; all their desires will also be fulfilled as wished.

🍁 EFFECTS OF PLAYING THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA

Regularly playing the Lăng Nghiêm mantra at home can transform the family's feng shui and purify the energy field.

When the sound of reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra spreads, it has the power to ward off evil and eliminate disasters. Reciting it once is equivalent to ten thousand merits!

Opening the practice of the Five Great Heart Mantras is similar. The Lankavatara Mantra is the king of all mantras, while the Five Great Heart Mantras are the most revered and extremely beneficial mantras.

In the Dharma's declining age, if you do not recite the Lankavatara Mantra but wish to attain realization, it is impossible.

🍁 THE VENERABLE MASTER XUAN HUA, BEFORE PASSING AWAY, ADMITTED THAT HE WAS THE REINCARNATION OF BODHISATTVA GUANYIN

Before the Master entered final nirvana, Sư Hằng Thật once asked Master Xuan Hua:

-Master Bach, many people say that you are the reincarnation of Amitabha Buddha, the reincarnation of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the reincarnation of Patriarch Bodhidharma. So who exactly are you, Master?

The elder replied:

-I am Ancient Avalokiteshvara. Ancient Avalokiteshvara is Avalokiteshvara! Avalokiteshvara is the True Dharma Bright Tathagata.

_Respectfully recorded by lay disciple Quả Huệ_

NAM MÔ GREAT MERCIFUL GREAT COMPASSIONATE GUANSHIYIN BODHISATTVA

tieu_de: ABSORBING DEMON
tom_tat: Author: Quả Chân (Ứng Hiện ĐỜi Newspaper 6) Edited by: Quang Từ
noi_dung:
ABSORBING DEMON'S ESSENCE

Author: Quả Chân (Ứng Hiện ĐỜi Newspaper 6)

Edited by: Quang Từ

------------------------------------------------

Among the demons mentioned by Buddhism, there is a type called spirit-sucking demons. So how do they operate?

When men and women indulge in lust, commit adultery, have extramarital affairs outside of a legal marriage, engage in secret sexual relations, live promiscuously, or practice immoral sexual behavior, the spirit-sucking demons will appear.

I have a friend who, at first, was very opposed to sex or porn websites, considering them immoral, decadent… but over time, he thought: Even if I accidentally see them, it’s okay. Unexpectedly, after being curious and checking them out, he kept looking back and forth, and gradually he became addicted.

Suddenly one day he confided:

Sex movies, stories, and discs… with sexually arousing content should not be watched; I must say, they should absolutely not be watched. I was shocked to see ghostly figures appearing in the sexual scenes. It was really terrifying.

It turned out that he went online to watch sex (6), and suddenly discovered a strange phenomenon in the scene: Just as the prostitute was receiving customers, the back of her bed clearly showed the figure of the demon dressed there, the upper half of the demon's body clearly showed a white face, black eye sockets, and long shaggy hair that looked like a human face but looked very scary. The demon that was currently behind her was staring at the prostitute, controlling her to act dirty tricks, her eyes were full of eroticism, delusion, and no longer sober

.

This completely shocked my friend, and since then he has never watched pornographic films again. He emotionally said:

- No wonder the ancients said: Relationships that are not between husband and wife are filled with demons, possessed by demons!

And indeed, there are demons infiltrating and hiding within. Those possessed by demons gradually have their essence, energy, and spirit drained, becoming increasingly corrupted and more foolish, bewildered, and confused.

Another friend of mine, although he doesn't like to go out promiscuously, loves to watch sex online or on tape or disc. Sometimes he also watches pornography, nudity or "Artistic sex". After watching it for a long time, he said: Suddenly he felt like a cold air from behind his back entered his body, causing his body to become weakened, lose self-control and keep breaking out in a cold sweat...

He realized that this phenomenon was not a good thing, so he immediately stopped and did not watch it anymore. Occasionally, whenever out of habit he thought about sex, he would control himself and not allow the thought to continue. Gradually, this state occurred less and less, to the point that when he opened the computer, he no longer wanted to view sexual content or pornographic films, but hurriedly switched to another page.

A Buddhist practitioner with supernatural abilities who had opened the heavenly eye once exclaimed to me:

- How can humans do such inhumane things?

tieu_de: Early and late sessions, even snakes come to listen
tom_tat: Once, Ms. Chơn went out for some business, and on the way home, she saw a man catching snakes, carrying two cloth bags on his shoulders, which contained two snakes. As soon as Ms. Chơn saw him, she asked him where he caught the snakes.
noi_dung:
Early and Late Sessions, Even the Snakes Come to Listen

Once Ms. Chon went out to have a job, on the way home she saw a person catching snakes, carrying two cloth bags on her shoulders, containing two snakes. Ms. Chon saw it and asked him where he caught it, he caught the snake and replied to Ms. Chon, it turned out that it was caught near Ms. Chon's house. Ms. Chon said, "These two snakes are mine, you have to pay me". How could the person who caught that snake pay, he said: "Strange! I've been catching snakes for decades, since I haven't heard of anyone in the mountains raising snakes, what do you raise snakes for?" Ms. Chon said to him: "We went to the ceremony in the morning and eveningOh my, both of these snakes came to listen. If there is rice, they get to eat the rice. It's been like that for years. Well, now I'll give you 30 dong, quickly let them go,” the snake catcher still refused, saying: “No! No, what can 30 dong be used for? How much is the skin of these two snakes worth? Their two livers are also worth several tens of dong, and snake meat is a dish people compete to buy!”

At that moment, Ms. Chơn loudly said: “A Di Đà Phật, A Di Đà Phật, how pitiful!” Unexpectedly, at that very time, the two snakes in the cloth bag, hearing Ms. Chơn's chanting of Buddha's name, began to thrash in the bag continuously, using all their strength to try to break free. The young man carrying the snakes could no longer continue to take them!... He then accepted 30 đồng from Ms. Chơn and asked where she wanted them released. Ms. Chơn said he could release them right there. He opened the bag, and the two snakes happily slithered toward the mountain. All animals inherently have a fear of death; after experiencing this fright, the two snakes during the day...no longer dare to crawl out. The truth is exactly this proof: snakes, people are very afraid but also know they like to hear people chanting, thereby being saved, from fatal accidents, from being skinned and having their tendons pulled out, blood spilling and flesh torn!

CHANTING AMITABHA BUDDHA BRINGS EXPERIENCES SEEN WITH THE EYES AND HEARD WITH THE EARS.

Source: Amitabha Buddha.

tieu_de: Demon Disguise Scene
tom_tat: As mentioned above, those who recite the Buddha's name may sometimes see forms that actually are demonic illusions; this refers only to the case of incongruent cause and effect. For example, a person who is contemplating the form of the Buddha might suddenly see the form of a beautiful woman.
noi_dung:
FINISHED HOAX

As mentioned above, a person who recites the Buddha's name may sometimes see forms that actually turn out to be demonic visions; this refers to cases where cause and effect do not correspond. For example, someone contemplating the form of the Buddha may suddenly see the form of a beautiful woman. A person who diligently recites the Buddha's name hoping to see the splendid scenery of the Western Paradise may instead suddenly see a cluttered area of houses, with men and women mingling with beasts, running about in confusion. Someone expecting to see a precious lotus flower may suddenly see a small cart. Because the cause and effect are not compatible in such cases, one recognizes them as demonic visions. There are five situations to distinguish whether a vision is demonic or real as follows:

1. The karmic cause-and-effect scenes are inappropriate; while perceiving one appearance, one sees another, seeking one scene but another appears, as mentioned above. Moreover, the scenes that appear do not match those described in the sutras, all are demonic scenes.

2. The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have a pure compassionate mind, so even if ghostly or divine forms appear to test, I still feel calm and tranquil. On the contrary, the inherent nature of demons is vexatious and evil, so even if the form of a Buddha appears to teach, I feel agitated, restless, and uneasy.

3. The light of the Buddha makes us feel gentle and cool, without shadows and without dazzling the eyes. The light of demons makes our eyes hurt, makes us restless and uneasy, and has shadows. Therefore, the Lankavatara Sutra says:

The Buddha's land is supremely excellent

Pure, adorned with splendor

Radiant like blazing fire

Its light reaches everywhere

Brilliant without harming the eyes

Circulating to save the three realms.

4. The Dharma words of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas align with the sutras and follow the truth. The words of demons contradict the truth and do not conform to the teachings of the Buddha.

5. When auspicious signs appear and one wants to test them, the practitioner should focus the mind to recite the Heart Sutra of Prajñā, or concentrate on mantra practice while remembering the Buddha. If it is a holy manifestation, the more one recites, the clearer it becomes, for real gold fears no fire. If it is a demonic manifestation, after reciting or practicing for a while, it will immediately vanish, as falsehood cannot overpower truth.

* One must consider all five points mentioned above for examination; it is not possible to only consider one or two. Because there are certain celestial demons or deities from external sects who wish to lead us toward their ways, they may disguise themselves as Buddhas or Bodhisattvas to teach the Dharma. Although their practices are not the ultimate path of liberation, they may have virtuous karma or relatively high meditative power, so the aura they emit can make us feel cool and calm. Additionally, their way of teaching Dharma sometimes also encourages doing good deeds, keeping precepts, eating vegetarian food, and reciting Buddha's name, but there are a few aspects that differ from Buddhist scriptures, and one must carefully discern and understand the teachings to know. For example, they alsoThey advise eating vegetarian and chanting Buddha’s name, but then teach that one must circulate the Buddha’s name throughout the body, called 'turning the Dharma wheel,' to open the Ren and Du meridians, and to open the Neihan Palace. This is the way of preaching of heretical demons. Or some demons appear in the form of high monks saying: 'Bronze Buddha, cement Buddha cannot save from water, because if you go into water you have to sink; Buddha statues, wooden Buddha cannot save from fire, because when encountering fire they will burn; only the Buddha mind cannot be destroyed by anything. If one cultivates a pure Buddha mind, there is no need to cultivate the body and speech; therefore, even eating meat, drinking alcohol, having a wife and children is harmless. The cultivation of body and speech, like keeping precepts, eating vegetarian, reciting sutras, chanting mantras, and chanting Buddha’s name, are all forms of hardship.'"Happiness tied up is useless." This is the sermon of those who have long been deluded, or the kinds of demons who love desires. There are those non-Buddhist demons with relatively high practice abilities, who can use the power of meditative concentration to help practitioners achieve mental and physical stability for seven days, or twenty-one days. However, their method of preaching does not lead to liberation; in the end, it remains only within self-attachment.

* The ancients said: "If you see ghosts and spirits, but they are not truly ghosts, they will destroy themselves; if you see monsters and strange beings, but they are not truly monsters, they will collapse on their own." This means: if you see ghosts or strange beings without your mind being disturbed by fear, keeping mindfulness steady, or sincerely reciting Buddha's name, those ghosts or strange beings can do nothing and will leave on their own. Not only should one act like this when seeing ghosts and strange beings, but even when achieving some results in practice or seeing victorious signs, one should not be overly sentimental, shocked, or elated. For example, if we drop a pearl to the bottom of a pond, due to the muddy water, searching for it continuously will still yield nothing. Now, when the water clears, the pearl can be found again; the pearl was always there, what is the need to change anything?Amazed, joyful? If a practitioner’s mind is not calm, overly sorrowful, it will be possessed by the species of sorrowful demons, causing endless crying. Likewise, if overly joyful, one can be possessed by the species of joyful demons, causing one to laugh uncontrollably. Moreover, a practitioner reciting the Buddha's name, although hoping to see the sacred realm, should not fantasize or desire too much, because reciting already means one is making a wish. One should maintain a calm state of mind, 'wishing without wishing, not wishing yet wishing,' so as not to be disturbed by desire. Simply sincerely recite the Buddha's name, and over time, the pure power of recitation will harmonize with the Tao, and one will certainly see the sacred realm. If one constantly harbors desires, these are delusions, and demons will take the opportunity to infiltrate and destroy.* Around the late Qing period and the beginning of the Republic era, in China, there was a man named Wei Xifu, who was a meditation companion of the layman Yang Renshan. Wei Xifu practiced meditation for nearly thirty years, and one day he suddenly attained Heavenly Eye Knowledge. At first, he saw things outside the walls; next, he could clearly see events within a few dozen miles as if they were right before his eyes. Realizing that he had gained the Heavenly Eye, he was extremely astonished and delighted! Initially, he could only see, but later he could also hear the sounds of people and animals from afar. This is known as Heavenly Ear Knowledge, corresponding to individual discovery. Gradually, he was able to see and hear things several thousand miles away. Even for events that had not yet been discovered, he could still see them.listen and understand clearly. This is the vision of Predicted Fate Insight. At that time, the faction of Hồng Tú Toàn belonging to the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom had not yet started attacking the Qing dynasty, but Ngụy Tịch Phủ foresaw that the war would eventually occur in Guangxi and move on to Suzhou, with countless people dying. Having witnessed many tragic deaths firsthand, he was deeply moved and, whenever he met anyone, he would mournfully say, "A great turmoil is coming, and the people will suffer tremendous hardships—what can be done?" At that time, everyone who heard him speak this way thought he was mad. Layman Dương Nhân Sơn, who often stayed close to him in the capital, therefore knew this matter clearly. Later, the uprising actually happened. When the chaos was quelledThen, layman Duong Nhan Son met Wei Xi Fu in Yangzhou several times and saw that he was still crying. Later, Nhan Son met layman Dinh Phuoc Bao, recounted the matter, and said: 'That is a scene influenced by ominous spirits. Whenever a practitioner reaches the stage of attaining spiritual power, the Heavenly Eye Clairvoyance may appear unexpectedly, so one should examine one’s own nature and not let worldly desires cause disturbance. One should know that our supernatural abilities are always present, and should not be overly happy or astonished as if it were something extraordinary.'

* In "Trúc Song Tùy Bút Lục," Master Liên Trì recounted the story:

- A Zen master built a hermitage near a stream. One night, while meditating, he heard two demons sitting by the stream talking to each other, saying: "Tomorrow at sunset, someone wearing a steel helmet will cross this stream bridge, and I will drown them to take their place." One demon said: "I am happy that you will be released; I still have to endure the cold waiting until two years later for someone to take my place." The Zen master listened carefully. Around noon the next day, a heavy rain fell, flooding the stream and the bridge. In the late afternoon, the rain continued lightly, and indeed someone wearing an iron pan on their head tried to cross the stream bridge to get home. The master went to intercept them and clearly recounted what he had heard.The person was terrified and turned back. That night, the meditator heard the demon say: "About to be liberated but being sabotaged by this monk, tonight I must take revenge!" Upon hearing this, the monk immediately concentrated and entered a state of right meditation, seeing the demon come in and go around the hermitage several times as if searching for something. Due to the power of right meditation, the demon could not find the meditator no matter how hard it tried, and in the end it became frustrated and left.

Above are two stories, "exorcising ghosts" and "refusing ghosts". Recorded here for fellow practitioners to increase awareness on the path of mindfulness practice.

(Excerpted from TEN ESSENTIALS OF MINDFULNESS OF BUDDHA - Venerable Thien Tam - Second Patriarch of the Pure Land School in Vietnam - He is an incarnation of bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta)

Source: Hieu Dieu Minh

tieu_de: Great Compassion Mantra to Eliminate Accidents
tom_tat: Genuine benefits are often hard to express. Like a person drinking water,
noi_dung:
Great Compassion Mantra to Eliminate Accidents

True benefits are often difficult to express.

Like a person drinking water,

only they themselves know whether it is cold or hot.

Even in extreme heat, if you are not afraid of the heat or the long journey over mountains and rivers, coming here to participate in the meditation hall, then what benefit is there? True benefits are often difficult to express. Like a person drinking water, only they themselves know whether it is cold or hot. Only those with a sincere heart can comprehend its wonder.

How can one reap this benefit? Nothing other than sincerely reciting the name of the Bodhisattva. True mind means concentrated mind. Therefore it is said: "Concentration brings efficacy, division brings failure." That is, if completely focused, it is effective; if divided, it is blocked. When the mind is fully concentrated, it will naturally receive spiritual communion. The experience of spiritual communion is beyond thought. However, one must exert effort oneself; no one else can do it for you, and it certainly cannot be obtained by luck.

It's like "talking about eating rice or counting money for someone else." Some people often mention these kinds of nutritional things, but they don't eat them themselves; so no matter how nutritious the food is, they cannot enjoy it. Therefore, it is said:

Chung nhật sổ tha bảo, tự vô bán tiền phần.

Y pháp bất tu hành, kỳ quá diệc như thị.

Meaning:

Spending all day counting someone else's money, but not having a single penny oneself.

Studying the Dharma without practicing it leads to mistakes as well.

My own practice of Buddha recitation is the same. It is not enough to merely understand or discuss the merits of reciting the Bodhisattva; one must truly recite to the point of a single-minded, undisturbed concentration; even to the extent that when water flows or wind blows, my ears hear only the name of the Bodhisattva. Therefore it is said:

Sentient beings, insentient beings,

All manifest the great mysterious Dharma of Mahā.

Meaning:

Whether sentient beings or insentient beings,

All speak of the Mahayana Dharma.

If one cannot practice so that the mind is single-minded and undisturbed, then whether the wind blows gently or the water flows murmuringly, one will not be able to feel its wonder. Therefore, one must sincerely recite and not let wandering thoughts pull away, only then can one reap the benefits of the Dharma.

When attending a retreat, one must respect the rules of the retreat hall. Because "Without rules, one cannot achieve perfect practice." That is, without rules, one cannot achieve complete practice. The rules of Tây Lạc Viên are to avoid speaking loudly so as not to hinder others' practice.

During these seven days, we also recite the Great Compassion Mantra. The merit of the Great Compassion Mantra is very difficult to comprehend. If a person does not have a good root of virtue, it is hard for them to even hear the three words "Great Compassion Mantra." Now, the assembly not only has heard it but also has received and chanted it, which shows that you all already possess a good root of virtue. If you already have this good root of virtue, you should not take it lightly and should not let this life pass by in waste.

I still remember the first time Tay Lac Vien Pagoda held a retreat; among the ten laypeople, eight or nine could not recite the Great Compassion Mantra. But now, out of ten people, up to eight can recite it. This demonstrates the progress of the laypeople. I will tell you a story to illustrate the merit of the Great Compassion Mantra.

In Manchuria, there was a wealthy landlord who owned many estates. One autumn, this landlord personally followed four or five carts full of sorghum down to the town to sell. Because the distance from the countryside to the town was more than 150 miles, he set off at one o'clock in the morning. Unfortunately, halfway there he encountered bandits. Seeing this, he immediately recited the Great Compassion Mantra. Amazingly! The bandits suddenly seemed blind and didn't see his carts, so he safely passed through the danger. That is one of the miraculous experiences of the Great Compassion Mantra that I personally witnessed.

The Great Compassion Mantra Sutra teaches: "Those who recite the Great Compassion Mantra can eliminate disasters: Fire cannot burn them, water cannot drown them." Therefore, I advise everyone to recite it at least three times a day. If anyone does not yet know how to chant, quickly learn. The merit of reciting the Great Compassion Mantra can not only repel thieves but also eliminate many illnesses and escape the disturbances of demons. Therefore, everyone should sincerely recite it.

Today is the first day of the retreat, and the atmosphere of the Dharma assembly is very joyful and solemn. I hope everyone will exert effort and diligently practice.

Venerable Tuyen Hoa Lectured at noon on June 13, 1958

at Tay Lac Vien, Hong Kong,
