tieu_de: Copying sutras to save parents from hell, hungry ghosts
tom_tat: In Sơn Âm district at Cối Kê, there was a scholar who, seeing that he was ill, vowed to copy the Vimalakirti Sutra. Just after making the vow, he dreamed at night of a celestial maiden stroking his head with her hand, and upon waking, his illness seemed to improve.
noi_dung:
COPY THE SUTRA TO HELP PARENTS ESCAPE HELL, HUNGRY GHOSTS

In Sơn Âm district at Cối Kê, there was a scholar who, noticing he was sick, vowed to copy the Vimalakirti Sutra.

Just after making the vow, he dreamed one night of a celestial maiden stroking his head with her hand, and he woke up seemingly completely cured.

The scholar became even more convinced, copying the sutra over several days to complete one set, and then, seeking to pray for the salvation of his deceased parents, copied another set.

Just as he copied the chapter "Illness", that night the scholar dreamed of a celestial being with a dignified and handsome appearance, who rode on clouds and came to say:

- I am your father. Because of my evil deeds, I was condemned to the Black Am Hell. When you copied the sutra for your parents, suddenly a beam of light shone down, and I was freed from suffering and reborn in the heavenly realm. Now I am at peace and have come here to make things clear to you.

The scholar asked:

- Where is my mother now?

He replied:

- Your mother, due to the karma of greed and stinginess, has fallen into the category of hungry ghosts. When you copy the section 'Buddha's Land,' your mother will be reborn in the Immoveable World of Buddha Akshobhya. Not long after, I too will be reborn in that pure land. So you should diligently complete the copying.

Upon waking, the scholar was moved to tears, sincerely copied the entire sutra, and then conducted a ritual to offer it. That night, he dreamed again of an official in a strange costume, holding a flag, who came and said:

- In Yama King's summons to death, his name was called, and he should have died. But because he copied the Duy-Ma Sutra, he would be reborn in the Buddha land of Kim Túc. The Ming prefecture monk extended his lifespan by another twenty years. Therefore, he should strive to practice and not be lazy or delay.

Twenty years later, at the age of seventy-nine, the scholar passed away. Upon his death, his body radiated a bright golden color. Everyone took it as a sign of rebirth in the Buddha land of Kim Túc.

Source: Quán Tự Tại

tieu_de: AT THE END OF THE CHÁP, EVERYONE SHOULD MEMORIZE THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA!
tom_tat: All those who consider themselves Buddhists with true faith should cultivate a compassionate mind for the whole world and always recite the Śūraṅgama Mantra.
noi_dung:
LATE FRANCE PERIOD, EVERYONE SHOULD MEMORIZE THE LĂNG NGHIÊM CHANT!

All those who consider themselves true Buddhist believers,

should cultivate the mind of great compassion for the whole world and always recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra.

Tạ Quả Chánh

Since 1990, after taking refuge with the Venerable Master, listening to the Venerable Master's recorded teachings and instructions, it was said that He came to the West to propagate the Dharma mainly relying on the power of the Lankavatara Mantra and the Great Compassion Mantra. It is precisely thanks to the power of these two mantras that He was able to penetrate into the 'desert' that belongs to Buddhism. In Western society, where non-Buddhist beliefs prevail, He has established a sacred work of countless eons that will never be destroyed for Buddhism.

Since 1968, Venerable Master Hsuan Hua began propagating the Dharma to Westerners in San Francisco, USA, and He started by giving lectures on the Shraddhā Sūtra of Lankā (including the Lankā Mantra) as an opening step. From this, we can somewhat see the urgent importance of the Lankā Sūtra and the Lankā Mantra for the secular world and human minds—no other Buddhist scriptures can truly compare. In other words, for an era of excessively greedy humans, with morality almost seriously deteriorated, reciting the Lankā Sūtra and the Lankā Mantra is the most timely approach, and also a treasure of Dharma to overcome adversity.the best “beginning.” Because in the end times of the Dharma, an era when “demonic energy flourishes and righteous energy declines,” demons and evil spirits run rampant, causing turmoil everywhere, corrupting human hearts and preventing the world from being peaceful. Yet the ordinary eyes of common people cannot perceive these demons and evil spirits, except for those who have opened the Five Eyes and Six Supernatural Powers.

What these kinds of demons and evil spirits fear most are the Surangama Sutra and the Surangama Mantra, because the principles in the Surangama Sutra are too true, and the power of the Surangama Mantra is strong, making all strange and deformed beings terrified upon hearing them. They become honest and obedient, no longer daring to act recklessly. The monk once said:

“You have just chanted the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, so why do demons and ghosts no longer dare to appear? Because the divine power of the Mantra is too strong, too great; throughout the entire cosmos and all realms, there is no place not covered by this auspicious light. Therefore, when someone chants the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, it is equivalent to supplementing the righteous energy that heaven and earth lack.”

On the mountain gate of the Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery in the state of California, USA, there is a couplet carved that was written by the Venerable Master, with the right side (upper line) reading:

“Floral Adornment Dharma Assembly, Lăng Nghiêm Altar,”

"Forty-Two Hand Seals to Stabilize Heaven and Earth."

It can be seen that the Venerable Master primarily relied on the Forty-Two Hand Seals, the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Surangama Sutra and Surangama Mantra, and also the Great Compassion Mantra, to stabilize heaven and earth, silently using the power of the Buddha Dharma to seek peace for the world. Among them, the Surangama Sutra and Surangama Mantra were particularly revered by the master, who always earnestly instructed that, in this degenerate age of the Dharma, as Buddhist believers, everyone should memorize the Surangama Sutra and the Surangama Mantra; only then can one be considered a "true Buddhist disciple." He once said:

“The Mantra of Leng Nhiem is related to the entire rise and fall of Buddhism, it is a sacred text that helps the world avoid the apocalypse!”

“As long as there is even one person in the world who knows how to recite the Mantra of Leng Nhiem, this world will not be destroyed!”

In the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, it is clearly stated that as long as one can recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, no matter encountering famine, epidemics, wars, chaos and plundering, or any other misfortunes, everyone can "turn misfortune into fortune," transform danger into safety, and moreover, all prayers will be answered, especially with miraculous effectiveness.

I remember in 1994, while I was working in Los Angeles, one day I drove my two 13-year-old nephews to Long Beach Temple to attend a Dharma assembly. On the way home, the two nephews were sitting in the back seat, playing and making a ruckus. I couldn’t stop them, there was nothing I could do, so I had no choice but to stop paying attention to them. I put on a recording of the Lankavatara Sutra that I had recorded at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas and chanted along. About five or six minutes later, I suddenly felt an unusual silence from the back, so I looked in the rearview mirror and saw both of them closing their eyes, as if in a deep sleep that wasn’t sleep, like two "motionless worms," their heads resting against the side.

The seat in the back row. In my heart, I suddenly thought, isn't it the power of Master Lăng Nghiêm that caused this? In just a few short minutes, it made the 'stubborn ghost' in the two children's bodies run away? This was the first time I accidentally experienced the wonderful effect of Master Lăng Nghiêm.

The master once expounded on the miraculous efficacy and merits of reciting the Shurangama Mantra, which are truly beyond imagination and cannot be fully described even in the distant future. Everything mentioned in the Shurangama Mantra serves to subdue celestial demons and restrain heretical paths. From the opening line to the final line, every sentence embodies the profound teachings of the Buddhas, each sentence carries a specific intention, and every word holds the subtle profundity of its meaning, all full of unparalleled spiritual power. Even reciting just one word, one sentence, one section, or the entire mantra causes cosmic upheaval, which is why it is said:

“Heaven and earth are terrified, gods and spirits weep,

Evil spirits keep away, demons hide.”

After that, because I had developed the habit of reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra while driving, my car was unconsciously filled entirely with the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, and I gradually observed all the people who had ever sat in my car. Normally, they liked noise and commotion, but as soon as they sat in my car, if they didn’t become “dazed,” they would be much quieter, and they could easily sleep well. I believe this is also the silent influence of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra!

In addition, there is a matter worth mentioning about my parents. Ever since I was little, I noticed that my parents often quarreled with each other. Although they went through a period of trying to develop the habit of full vegetarianism, my father's habit of nagging and being irritable still could not be corrected or reduced; on the contrary, it increased with age and became more intense! I racked my brains in thought and still could not understand, because I often heard people say that being vegetarian makes a person's temperament relatively gentle and kind, but in my father's case, this did not happen! Perhaps this is a common problem for manyOlder people, perhaps? It could also be that my father's karma is relatively heavy, and the 'spirit of anger' often plays tricks on him. In short, being a child like me feels like being stuck in the middle; the feeling of having to listen to my parents quarrel is really unpleasant!

Since I memorized the Leng Yan Mantra, I thought perhaps I could try using it. The Venerable once said: "Regularly reciting the Leng Yan Mantra can eliminate the karmic obstacles from past lives; all sins and karmic obstacles from past lives can be eradicated!" "Regardless of whether the sin is minor or major, even the four grave unpardonable sins, the five heinous acts, the four deadly acts, the eight serious offenses, as long as you recite the Leng Yan Mantra, no matter how severe the sins are, all will be eliminated, not even a hair's worth will remain." It can also be said that reciting the Leng Yan Mantra is one of the methods to eliminate karma.fastest, most thoroughly.

Therefore, from that time onward, I would recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra while driving to work; I did the same after leaving the office. After that, I dedicated this merit to my parents, praying that they could improve their temperaments. The results were very promising—I quickly noticed that the tension between my parents gradually reduced significantly, arguments decreased greatly, and sometimes when I arrived home, I would see my father sitting alone watching TV like an obedient "sheep." Seeing him sitting on the sofa, it looked like he wanted to get angry but could not. It seemed that the "spirit of anger" that often controlled him had been subdued by the Bodhisattva KimThe treasury of scriptures or the demon kings in the Shurangama Mantra control it, making it obedient, submissive, and no longer daring to act wildly. But I also deeply understand that, unless my own father also generates the aspiration to study Buddhism and diligently cultivates, otherwise, if he only relies on the external power of the Shurangama Mantra, it can merely temporarily amend the situation, but cannot eliminate the root cause of that evil temperament.

I have also tried using the method of confession to help my father eliminate his karmic obstacles, hoping that one day he would awaken and begin studying Buddhist teachings. But up until now, my virtue has still not been able to influence my father to take refuge in Buddhism. I pray to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas for compassionate blessings, so that my father may soon take refuge, sincerely practice, correct himself, and abandon his bad habits. If this can be achieved, I will be very happy, for that would mean that my life has not been wasted!

The Venerable once said: "The best practitioner of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is one who can generate a vast aspiration, reciting it for the whole world, dedicating all merits to the entire world."

One of the eighteen great vows of the Venerable is:

"May all sentient beings, whether they just see my face or merely hear my name,

all develop the Bodhi mind and quickly attain Buddhahood."

How vast this aspiration is! Therefore, at present, I also follow the Venerable Monk in generating this resolve. Every day after reciting the Lankavatara Mantra, I vow to dedicate this merit not only to my parents or close friends, but even to all colleagues at my workplace and their relatives, to everyone I meet today, everyone I call on the phone, and even to all sentient and insentient beings in the Dharma Realm, wishing that all may swiftly attain Buddhahood. Since doing so, I feel that in terms of dealing with people and handling affairs, not only have many obstacles been resolved, butThere are also often many things that are 'done for fun but yield real results,' with surprising effectiveness. Currently, being asked not to recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra for a day is really difficult for me, because that practice has integrated into my life, and I often try to apply it to all layers surrounding my life. At the same time, I have gradually realized its wonderful effects. I also hope that with this vow, for the future, lifetime after lifetime, I will support the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, so that the True Dharma will remain forever in the world, and the world will become better and better.

Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra also has another distinctive feature that attracts people's attention, which is the particularly outstanding merit of those who recite it. The Venerable Monk once said that if you can memorize the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, achieve the Samadhi of Mantra Recitation, recite it as smoothly as flowing water, continuously without stopping, "at the very least, you can be wealthy for seven lifetimes, like the oil king of the United States, being rich for seven generations, possessing abundant silver and money"! Although maintaining the recitation of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra can bring such great blessings, the Venerable Monk also reminded everyone not to become attached to such trivial realms, "seven lifetimesBeing wealthy is, at most, a period that passes in the blink of an eye. So what should we hope for when reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra? We must hope to ultimately become a Buddha, to attain Supreme Perfect Enlightenment. In reality, those who practice the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra are incarnations of the Buddha. Not only are they incarnations of the Buddha, but they are also "Buddha transforming on the Buddha's crown, Buddha transforming within Buddha's transformation." "If you can uphold the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, you will definitely become a Buddha in the future!" This is the guarantee that the Venerable Monk has written for us.

This is also a method that is “extremely rare and difficult to encounter for many countless lifetimes.” It can be said that throughout world Buddhism, the miraculous efficacy and principles of the Shurangama Mantra can be fully realized seemingly only in the Ten Thousand Buddhas Holy City, and only a venerable and highly virtuous monk like Master Hsuan Hua could expound such a profound and inconceivable dharma. Because the Shurangama Mantra is related to the rise and fall of all Buddhism and the world, it is shameful to be a member of the Buddhist community yet not have reason to cherish, support, and widely spread it!

Because the practice of reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Dharani is particularly responsive, especially quick, and the power and merit of the dharani are particularly great, the practitioner must keep a pure mind, speak and act with clarity and integrity, and observe precepts in order to attain results. As the Venerable Master has advised, we must at least uphold the Five Precepts and practice the Ten Wholesome Actions; otherwise, not only will there be no response, but we may instead bring trouble upon ourselves. When some people hear this, they dare not rashly study the Lăng Nghiêm Dharani; in truth, those who study Buddhism must rigorously observe the precepts, if withinIf the mind is still full of greed, anger, and delusion, then regardless of whether you recite sutras, chant mantras, or meditate, you will not be able to achieve any accomplishment. Even if you accidentally cause some minor troubles, it is still a warning, a trial, making us restrain our body and mind, forcing you to follow the rules and not violate precepts again.

After going to Taiwan to work, whenever I had the opportunity, I also introduced the miraculous effects of reciting the Lankavatara Mantra to colleagues who were interested. The feedback I often received was: “I heard that the Lankavatara Mantra can only be recited in the morning, and it is not allowed to be recited at other times; otherwise, it will not be good for oneself!” Why is it that in Taiwan, there are so many monasteries where the masters teach people that the Lankavatara Mantra can only be recited early in the morning, while at other times of the day they must “yield to others”? The Buddha is compassionate and also equal, and would not hold prejudice toward this mantra; it can only be said that it is merelypeople just “misheard and spread rumors”!

Evil spirits and heretics, because they want to destroy the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra which they fear the most, their demon kings and demon descendants have created these rumors, hoping that people will recite this mantra less, so they can achieve their goals, do mischief, and cause more bad things in this world. The Buddha also said that in this degenerate age, the Buddhist Dharma that will be destroyed first is the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra and the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, because the demon kings and their followers use every trick possible to try to destroy these scriptures and mantra. And many ignorant people follow these whims blindly; avoiding them is probably too late, and even friendsI know someone who has been studying Buddhism for more than ten years, yet has never heard of what is called the 'Śūraṅgama Mantra.' This is truly a great loss and extremely painful for Buddhism.

Someone asked Venerable Master Hsuan Hua: “I heard that the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra should only be recited at five o’clock in the morning; at other times, it should not be recited?” The Venerable Master replied: “You can recite it any time, that time is always five o’clock in the morning! Five o’clock here is evening in America, how do you calculate that? Reciting sutras and mantras should not cling to forms!” “Reciting the mantra at any time will have the same effect.” In this life, we never imagined that we would be fortunate enough to meet a great wise teacher with profound insight like Venerable Master Hsuan Hua to guide us! His words are like the morning bell and evening drum, giving hopecan awaken as many lost people as possible. The master once said:

“When the Lăng Nghiêm thrives, Buddhism thrives.

When the Lăng Nghiêm declines, Buddhism declines!”

Encountering an era in which morality is in decline and corruption is worsening every day, not only in Taiwan but indeed across the entire world, advancing gradually toward a dangerous moment, on the brink of destruction as it is now, all Buddhists who consider themselves to have true faith should cultivate a great heart, continuously recite the Lengyan Mantra, and dedicate the merit to the entire world, in order to salvage the decay and collapse, to uphold righteous energy, and to ensure that the Dharma lasts forever in the world. This is the proper attitude toward learning Buddhism that modern Buddhist followers should possess!

Commentary:

The benefit of the Ling Nguom spell is that it works very quickly; you don't need to concentrate much, and just reciting it once, you can immediately see your wishes fulfilled. You don't have to wait, because when we recite it once, it is equivalent to reciting the Great Compassion Mantra 8 times without a single distracting thought, or reciting the Chuan De (Cundi) mantra 250 times when counted by the number of characters.

- Again, this master does not need to set up an altar, does not enter any random dharma assembly, nor does he need to practice the path, but just reciting this mantra, his merit is equal to setting up an altar and practicing the path, with no difference. This is very rare when practicing the esoteric Tong teachings, therefore in this degenerate age, encountering the radiant mantra is like finding a treasure, but if you do not recite the mantra, it is as if you return empty-handed.

- Again, in the Lankavatara Sutra, Volume 7, there is a passage: "…That virtuous friend, whether reading, reciting, transcribing, wearing, or offering this mantra with the mind, will not be born in poverty, lowliness, or unsafe places for countless lifetimes. These sentient beings, even if they themselves do not perform meritorious deeds, will receive merit from the Buddhas of the ten directions, thereby, over countless lifetimes, always being born together with the Buddhas in one place, accumulating immeasurable merit like a cluster of aksha fruits, practicing together without separation. Therefore, this mantra often enables those who have broken precepts to purify their precept roots, those who have not yet attained precepts to attain them, and those who are not diligent, not…"Wisdom, not pure, not celibate, all can be fulfilled. Ananda! If that good man previously violated the precepts, then after reciting the mantra, all offenses of breaking the precepts, regardless of severity, are eliminated. Even if he has drunk alcohol, eaten pungent foods, and other impure things, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, and spirits do not consider it a fault; even if wearing tattered clothes, whether walking or standing, it is like being pure; even if not establishing an altar, not entering the Dharma assembly, and not practicing the way, by reciting this mantra, the merit is no different from entering an altar and practicing the way…” Therefore, everyone can recite this mantra; one cannot blame circumstances by saying, 'I have not been able to focus on reciting it.'Venerable Lăng Nghiêm says that as long as you have enough faith, sincerity, and perseverance in reciting the mantra, you will certainly receive great spiritual responses. Besides clearing karma, dispelling harm, and protecting oneself, the mantra can also help practitioners achieve all their wishes: if you pray to recover from illness, you will recover; if you pray for wealth, you will become wealthy; even if you pray for rebirth, you will ultimately achieve what you desire. As long as you have enough faith, perseverance, and respect for the mantra, you will gain the benefits you wish for!

- Venerable Tuyen Hoa once said that each sentence in the Shurangama Mantra contains countless meanings; when ghosts, spirits, and other beings hear it, innumerable bodhi seeds arise. This mantra has more than 3,000 words, truly a considerable amount. The mantra contains sufficient dedication of merit for practitioners, leaving nothing lacking.

-1. Eliminating Calamities through Dharma (Dharma to remove misfortunes). Once we recite the Shurangama Mantra, all calamities are removed.

2. Subduing Method (Method to subdue). No matter what kind of demonic or heretical beings the opponent is, once we recite the Samantabhadra Mantra, the spiritual power of these demons will be broken, and they will be easily subdued.

3. Beneficial Method (Method to increase benefits). For example, if we practice the Path, the Samantabhadra Mantra will help us grow in wisdom, grow in bodhicitta, grow in vow power—everything will increase. This is the method that enhances benefits.

4. Achievement of Dharma (Dharma helps one achieve attainment). If we recite the Shurangama Mantra, then no matter which practice method we follow, this mantra will also help us achieve attainment.

- It is not necessary to recite many times; reciting once a day for 10 days without purification certainly indicates it is not right. But first, one must read the Shurangama Sutra; there is a reason why the BUDDHA preached the sutra before recording the commentary.

THE SUPERIOR PERSON XUAN HUA, BEFORE PASSING AWAY, ALREADY ADMITTED HIMSELF AS THE REINCARNATION OF BODHISATTVA GUAN YIN

Before the Master passed away, Venerable Heng Truth once asked Master Xuan Hua:

-Venerable Master, many people say that you are the rebirth of Amitabha Buddha, the rebirth of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the rebirth of Patriarch Bodhidharma. So, who exactly are you, Master?

The venerable replied:

-I am the Ancient Avalokiteshvara. The Ancient Avalokiteshvara is Avalokiteshvara! Avalokiteshvara is the True Dharma Light Tathagata.

tieu_de: HAVING WEALTH BUT NOT WILLING TO GIVE ALMS MAKES DEMONS WATCH WITH ENVY. YOU HAVE MONEY BUT ARE UNWILLING TO GIVE ALMS (SELFISH,
tom_tat: The seventeenth deity, 'Master of Wealth and Underworld King', is called the God of Wealth by the world. The Master of Wealth and Underworld King is the God of Wealth. The explanation in the book 'Chu Giai' is very good: In the residence of
noi_dung:
IF YOU HAVE WEALTH BUT REFUSE TO GIVE ALMS, EVEN DEMONS WATCH WITH ENVY. IF YOU HAVE MONEY BUT REFUSE TO GIVE ALMS (SELFISH,

The seventeenth position is the 'Master of Wealth and Ghost King,' commonly known as the God of Wealth. The Master of Wealth and Ghost King is essentially the God of Wealth. An explanation in the book *Chu Giai* is very good: In the mansion of the Eastern Music Emperor, the Master of the Wealth Court is the person responsible for managing finances. The Music Mansion only refers to the Eastern Music Emperor; in reality, the Five Music is the great ghost king, whose status is only lower than the Diem La King, the Diem La King is like the king of a country. The area managed by the Five Music is very large, overseeing many provinces, higher in rank than local positions.of the provincial governor. It seems that Dong Nhac Dai De managed six or seven provinces; he had such a large area under his control.

In the past, Chương Thái Viêm once served as a judge for the Eastern Music Emperor, a very high-ranking judicial position, equivalent to our ministerial secretary position. Therefore, regarding matters in the spirit realm, he spoke to people very much and in great detail. Under him (that is, the Eastern Music Emperor) there was the spirit king in charge of finances, in the Eastern Music mansion referred to as the Master of Financial Affairs. The Master of Financial Affairs refers to the Spirit King of Financial Affairs, known in the mortal world as the God of Wealth. This God of Wealth exists in both large and small forms.

Here are two sentences we must remember: 'Having possessions but not willing to share them invites the gaze and jealousy of demons.' If you have money but do not offer alms, even demons will envy you, and this trouble will be very serious! Demons will often seek you out, causing problems for you. The Supreme Being strictly forbids robbing the belongings of others; this is something we must particularly pay attention to. Stealing the property of others is a very serious, grave offense. If we remain calm and contemplative to observe, there is no need to wait for karmic retribution in the afterlife; even in this life, theyThey will also suffer the consequences, the karmic retribution; in today's society, there are many such cases. Let's look at stocks in the world, what are stocks? Stocks are basically gambling; they are all about seizing the possessions of others. Many people make a lot of money from playing stocks, and when the stock prices drop, they immediately jump off buildings to commit suicide, homes are destroyed, people lose everything, and the karmic retribution is right in front of them. Such things happen very often; this is an unprincipled tactic. What they achieve, as we mentioned earlier, is all what is readily available on the internet, and what is not available online.then absolutely cannot achieve it. Taking away someone else's belongings is also something that exists in the realm, just like enjoying blessings a little earlier, which only harms others and creates bad karma. After enjoying one's blessings earlier, it also creates bad karma. Therefore, we must understand that everything has its owner; unjust assets cannot be taken decisively, and if taken, there will definitely be accidents, and it certainly will not bring any benefit.

(Excerpt: Record of Lectures on the Sutra of the Original Vows of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha - Volume 28 / Page 436)

tieu_de: THE LIFE OF MASTER AN SHIH-KAO - HIGH MONK THIEN TRUC BRINGS BUDDHISM TO CHINA
tom_tat: His name was originally An Tinh, but because he was the crown prince of the Kingdom of An Túc (Parthian), later generations referred to him as An Thế Cao. Regarding the Kingdom of An Túc, the histories of the Former Han and Later Han, during the Three Kingdoms period, the Southern and Northern Dynasties,
noi_dung:
THE LIFE OF AN THẾ CAO - THE HIGH MONK THIÊN TRÚC BRINGING BUDDHIST TEACHINGS TO CHINA

His name was originally An Tinh, but because he was the crown prince of the country of An Túc (Parthian), later generations referred to him as An Thế Cao. Regarding the country of An Túc, the histories of the Former Han and Later Han, the Three Kingdoms period, and the Northern and Southern Dynasties all recorded it clearly. An Túc was the country that founded the nation of Arsakes. In the 16th year of the Yongping era of Emperor Ming of the Han (73), Ban Chao was sent as an envoy to the Western Regions. In the 3rd year of the Yongyuan era of Emperor Huan of the Han (91), Ban Chao was appointed as Cavalry Commander, governing thirty countries in the Western Regions. In the first year of the Zhanghe era of the Eastern Han (87), the country of An Túcsent tribute lions to Zhongtu. Furthermore, in the reign of Yù Nián, the king of An Túc sent envoys bearing tribute to Zhongtu, initiating trade between the two countries. In the thirteenth year of the Vĩnh Nguyên era (101), An Túc regularly brought gifts as tribute to the Eastern Han court. Forty-seven years later, Lord An Thế Cao went to Zhongtu.

For his parents, He was very filial, so he was praised and admired by the people. His natural intelligence was very clear, and he was diligent in studying, so he understood all foreign classics, as well as the seven wonders (the sun, the moon, and the stars), the five elements, medicine, meteorology, and astronomy. By observing a person’s complexion, He could immediately understand their illness and then prepare medicine to treat them. By listening to the sounds of animals and birds, He could understand their intentions. Once, while walking on the road, a flock of swallows suddenly flew by, and He then said to his companions:

- Those swallows said that soon someone would bring food to us.

A little while later, indeed it came true. The people, having heard of this, were extremely amazed and admired Him. Therefore, His reputation from then on spread and reverberated throughout the countries in the West, and He was revered by kings near and far.

When he was at home studying Buddhist teachings, he often strictly observed the precepts very carefully, without any negligence. He frequently gathered people to preach the scriptures and explain the Dharma. When his father passed away, he ascended the throne. At that time, the Kushan dynasty (78-320; established the country of Dayu Zhi) continuously campaigned against the countries to the west and threatened the country of Anxi. Seeing the instability, suffering, emptiness, and impermanence of the world, An Shigao felt extreme aversion and distress toward the throne. Therefore, after arranging his father’s funeral, he immediately ceded the throne to his uncle, then became a monk to study the path, showing no attachment to the royal seat, and devoted himself entirely to diligent practice.Fifty years after His passing, the state of An Túc collapsed due to the ministers fighting over the throne.

After becoming a monk, he reviewed all the sutras and scriptures, among which he was especially fond of the Abhidharma debates. He often recited meditation sutras and thus constantly attained marvelous experiences. Wanting to propagate the Buddha's teaching, he traveled across various countries, becoming very proficient in their languages. Tạ Phu of the Jin dynasty wrote: "Cao Tông is well-versed in foreign customs and proficient in the languages of many countries," meaning that Master An Shigao clearly understood the different customs of each country and was skilled in their languages. Before passing through Central China, while still in Anxi, and until he reached the Western Regions, he had already mastered the Chinese language. By the time of Emperor Huan of Han (147-167),At around the age of thirty, He traveled east to the land of Chang'an. With extraordinary talent and keen insight, He could understand something after just one glance. Upon arrival, He immediately began propagating the Dharma and translated many scriptures, such as the Ān Ban Thủ Ý Sutra, the Yīn Chí Rù, the Great Twelve Gates, the Small Twelve Gates, etc...

In ancient times, there was a Tripitaka master from India named Tống Chúng Hộ, who once compiled and wrote the essential meanings of the scriptures into twenty-seven chapters. Master An Thế Cao based on that earlier work, selected seven chapters, and then translated them into Chinese, which is the scripture 'Đạo Địa' as we know today. In total, he translated more than thirty scriptures. All the meanings were clear and bright, and the texts were very accurate. Although the wording was not ornate, the style was not crude.

Master An Thế Cao often recounted the extraordinary karmic connections of his past lives that others could not understand. He said that in his previous life, he was also a monk. At that time, he had a fellow practitioner friend who had a very hot temper. Whenever they encountered a donor who acted displeasingly, he would immediately become angry. Many times, Master An Thế Cao would advise him, but the temperament of that monk remained unchanged. More than twenty years later, Master An Thế Cao (the first) bid farewell to that monk and then said:

- I must go to Guangzhou to repay a debt from a past life. The master understands the scriptures deeply and is diligent and attentive. However, because he has a temper full of anger, after leaving his corporeal body, he will endure the form of a demonic punishment. If I attain the saintly fruit, I will certainly save him from disaster.

After speaking, Master An The Cao went to Guangzhou. At that time, the region was afflicted by chaos, and robbers rose like bees. On the road, he encountered a young man coming from afar. That young man then drew his sword and said:

- Ah! You have come here to give your life to me!

He said:

- In my previous life, I owed you a life, so I traveled many miles to come here to repay it. The moment you saw me, you immediately felt anger. This is because the grudge has not yet been resolved!

After speaking, he calmly offered his head to be beheaded, without any trace of fear. Without any delay, the young man swung the sword and beheaded him. At that moment, his spirit flew to the An Tức area, and he was reborn as a crown prince, namely An Thế Cao (the second).

During the Han dynasty, eunuchs contended for power. Wars continuously broke out. Therefore, Master An Thế Cao (the second) had to leave Luoyang and go to the Jiangnan region to continue propagating the Dharma. He told himself:

- First, I must go through Lu Mountain to save the Dharma friends who studied in past lives.

When arriving at Lo Son, he resided at Dinh Ho Hermitage. According to Venerable Hue Vien (334-417), in the book 'Lo Son Lueck Ky,' it is recorded as follows: "On the southern mountain peak, below Lam Cung Dinh Lake, there is a temple of a deity. The people, following the name of the lake, named the temple Cung Dinh Ho. The deity at Cung Dinh Ho Temple was influenced by Venerable An The Cao. The legend is still recorded in Tu Son Bac Thien."

It is said that the Cung Dinh Ho Temple is very sacred. Merchants passing through that area must first pray and make offerings, only then will they be safe and unharmed. One man secretly went up the mountain to cut bamboo without paying respects at the temple. As soon as his bamboo-laden boat left the riverbank, it was capsized by the waves. Seeing this, the merchants became even more reverent toward the temple deity.

The other day, Mr. An The Cao, along with more than thirty merchants, boarded a boat to go to that temple. Upon arrival, the merchants entered the temple to worship, while he stayed on the boat. After they offered tributes to pray for peace, the deity in the temple then told them:

- There is a monk on the boat, so invite him here.

The merchants were terrified upon hearing this and hurriedly ran to invite him into the temple. As soon as he stepped in, he heard the deity say:

- In my past life, I once went forth with the Master to practice the Way in the Western Regions. Although I often practiced giving, my temperament was full of anger, which is why I became a deity at this Imperial Lake temple. The temple, which spans a thousand miles, is entirely under my management. Because in my previous life I frequently practiced the virtue of giving, I am now able to receive countless priceless treasures. However, due to my angry mind, I suffer the karmic result of becoming an evil spirit, with a large and hideous body. My life is about to end. When I die, my body will emit a foul odor throughout the rivers and lakes. Therefore, I must go to the streams in the western mountains to die. After death, I will be condemned to hell to endure suffering. I beg the Master, with compassion, to take all the precious objectspromised to make offerings to the Three Jewels on my behalf, to build temples and pagodas, so that my future lives will be reborn in a good realm.

Upon hearing these words, An Thế Cao (the second) said:

- I originally came here to transform and save you. Why not show your true form?

The deity replied:

- I naturally have the appearance of an evil demon. If I show my form, the people will surely be frightened!

- Just showing your form is enough. The people will not be scared!

From inside the temple, a huge canoe appeared, crawling to the side of Anthegao (II). He then preached the Dharma, and recited mantras in Sanskrit. After a while, the canoe was touched and shed tears like rain, and then slowly disappeared. He picked up the jewels and went back to the boat with the merchants. At that time, everyone saw the canoe appearing in its original form on the top of the western mountain, its body was several miles long. At dusk, the boat was gliding on the river when a young man suddenly appeared, and he bowed to him. After his blessing, the young man suddenly disappeared. He said to themerchant:

- That young man was originally the deity of the Cung Dinh Ho temple. Now he has escaped the evil spirits and ascended to the heavenly palace.

Since then, the Cung Dinh Ho temple has no longer been sacred. Later, local people discovered a huge python, several miles long, lying in a stream bed to the west of Lo Son Mountain. Currently, that mountain area is called Xa Thon, Tam Duong District, in Jiangxi.

The Tu Ky Tower records: "Ngoa Quan Temple in Don Duong was established by the monk Hue Lap during the reign of Emperor Ai of Jin. Later, the monk An The Cao brought remaining items from Cung Dinh Ho to repair it."

After repaying part of the karmic debt, He also went to the Guangzhou area, seeking the young man who had killed Him in a previous life, then recounted the past-life connection to release the old grievance, hoping to build a friendship together. Upon meeting, He said to that person:

- I still have a debt that has not been repaid. Now I must go there to make amends.

That person knew that He was not an ordinary person, so they respectfully made offerings. The next day, He and that person went out to the street and happened to see two men fighting with sticks. One of the men accidentally struck His head, causing Him to lose His life. Having witnessed the cause-and-effect of karma twice, that person then resolved to diligently practice the Buddha's teachings and often recounted this true story to others. Whoever hears this story comes to deeply believe in the law of cause and effect across three lifetimes.

Then His spirit returned to become the crown prince of An Tức, namely An Thế Cao (the third). After growing up, He also gave up wealth and honor (as mentioned above) to leave home and practice the Way, then went to Trung Thổ to translate scriptures.

Sanskrit and Chinese are very different. However, the scriptures He translated were easy for everyone to read.

In the collection Tripitaka Chronicles, An Shigao's disciple, Yan Fo Diao, wrote a preface for the book 'Ten Wisdom Chapters of the Sāmaṇera'. The teacher highly praised the merits of his venerable master. Kang Senghui (217-280) commended An Shigao in the preface to the text 'An Ban Shou Yi'. Chen Hui praised An Shigao as the Bodhisattva Universally Perceiving in the preface to the scripture 'Yin Chi Ru'. Dao An (312-385) also highly praised An Shigao in the preface to the text 'An Ban Shou Yi', and often said:

- If one meets An Shigao, it is the same as meeting a sage.

According to Mr. Đạo An, Mr. An Thế Cao continuously translated scriptures for twenty-two years, from the time of Emperor Huan of Han (148) to the time of Emperor Ling of Han (169). In addition, in the prefaces to the Great Twelve Gates Sutra, Đạo Địa, etc., contemporary senior monks all praised the merits of Mr. An Thế Cao.

Nghiêm Phật Điều once wrote: "In all matters of entering and exiting, Mr. An Thế Cao either explained orally or transmitted through writing."

Using the mouth to explain means that He often lectured on the scriptures. Using written words to transmit means that He translated the scriptures from Sanskrit into Chinese.

In ancient times, Buddhism was introduced to the Eastern regions very early. The common people also knew how to venerate and believe in the Dharma. Moreover, there were many monks from the Western regions who came to translate the scriptures, but most did not specify the names of the scriptures, and sometimes the names of the translators were not recorded either. It was not until the era of Emperor Ming of Han that the court officially recognized the translation of scriptures by the two venerables Kātyāyana and Dharmarakṣa. However, in terms of history, An Shigao was actually the first to translate the scriptures.

Two hundred years after Master An Shih Kao passed away, during the Eastern Jin dynasty, Master Dao An (312-385) compiled the catalogue of scriptures. Later people followed that to write the book 'Compilation of Records on the Extraction of the Tripitaka,' dividing sections and recording the names of translators of the past. According to the book 'Compilation of Records on the Extraction of the Tripitaka,' Master An Shih Kao translated thirty-four texts, totaling forty sutra volumes as follows: The Sutra of Anban Shouyi (1 volume), Yinchi Entry (1 volume), One Hundred and Sixty Items (1 volume), The Great Twelve Gates (1 volume), The Small Twelve Gates (1 volume), Great Dao Earth (2 volumes), Original Human Desire To Give Birth (1 volume), The Way and Thought for Developing Conduct (2 volumes), Abhidharma Five Dharmas (1Volumn), Seven Dharmas (1 volume), Five Dharmas (1 volume), Ten Dharmas (2 volumes), Universal Dharma Meaning (1 volume), Dharma Decision Rules (1 volume), Part of Karmic Afflictions (1 volume), Four Noble Truths (1 volume), Seven Bases and Three Contemplations (2 volumes), Nine Dimensions (1 volume), Noble Eightfold Path (1 volume), Miscellaneous Sutras of Forty-Four Heavens (2 volumes), Fifty Teachings Outline (2 volumes), Great Peaceful How-to (1 volume), Reflection (1 volume), Twelve Links of Dependent Origination (1 volume), Five Aggregates Analogies (1 volume), Turning the Dharma Wheel (1 volume), Absorption (1 volume), Dharmas and Non-Dharmas (1 volume), Dharma Inheritance Transmission (1 volume), Fourteen Intentions (1 volume), Fundamental Features and Aspiration (1 volume), Abhidharma Discussion on Nine and Seven Special Points (1 volume), Meditation Practice and Dharma Contemplation (1 volume), Difficult Issue of Kala-Vivêka (1 volume).

The content of the scriptures translated by Ān Thế Cao can generally be divided into two parts: The first is the type of sutras related to meditation and contemplation, such as the Ān Bàn Thủ Ý Sutra, Thiền Hành Hành Pháp Tưởng, etc. The second type follows numerical teachings, such as the Âm Trì Nhập Sutra, Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path, Five Dharmas, Twelve Links of Dependent Origination, etc.

The representative scripture for meditation and contemplation is the Ān Bàn Thủ Ý Sutra. The content of this sutra includes ten points: mindfulness of breathing, following thoughts, stopping, contemplation, completion, purity, and the Four Noble Truths.

1/ Counting breathing (ganana) is counting the breaths. 2/ Following thought (anugama) is following the inhalation and exhalation so that the mind does not scatter. 3/ Concentration (sthana) is stopping the restless thinking mind. 4/ Contemplation (upalaksana) is clearly observing the phenomena. 5/ Completion (vivartana), also called transformation, is reflecting on the mind and clearly knowing that it is not real. 6/ Purity (parisuddhi) is the mind having no basis of attachment, not generating wandering thoughts. Additionally, the Four Noble Truths are suffering, origin, cessation, and path, making a total of ten points for developing wisdom. The An Ban Thu Y Sutra was established based on these ten points of wisdom. However, this sutra is particularly prominent in the first six points. Relying on these six points, later the great master Zhiyi (538-596) of the Tiantai school...Thai established the Six Wonderful Dharma Methods. These six types are entered through breath counting; gradually regulating the respiration and counting the inhalations and exhalations to focus the mind in one place, that is, practicing the Dharma of concentration. By observing, one clearly understands the object being contemplated. By observing the mind, one truly realizes the principle of emptiness, and then attains a state completely free from arising delusions. These six types are called An Ban Thu Y. In the sutras, it is further described as: the Four Foundations of Mindfulness are breath counting; the Four Right Efforts are following thoughts; the Four Bases of Psychic Power are directing the mind; the Five Faculties and Five Powers are contemplation; the Seven Factors of Enlightenment are completion; the Eightfold Path is purity. Among these, there is a detailed explanation of breath counting. Practicing these six methods can also achieve the same accomplishments as taught in the Sutra of the Thirty-Seven Practices. SutraAn Ban Thu Y theorized thoroughly about the governance of these six matters.

The An Ban Thu Y Sutra, a sutra representing the Theravada teachings translated by Aṅguli Saṅghika An Shigao, was very quickly adopted by the Chinese. Daoism used this sutra to establish the practice of 'Tai Xi' (Fetal Breathing).

The meaning of the An Ban Thu Y Sutra [A]

The Buddha said:

- I practiced the technique 'An Ban Thu Y' for ninety days, and my body and mind became at ease. After completing the An Ban Thu Y practice, one can grasp the concepts. 'An' refers to the body. 'Ban' refers to the breath. 'Thu' refers to the path, to restraint, also called not violating precepts. Restraint is also called protection, meaning protecting all precepts without violating them. 'Y' refers to the mind, also the path.

An Ban refers to inhalation and exhalation, which is also the method of breathing. The breathing method, namely Sổ Tức Quán, is the fundamental basis of practicing the Dao. According to this method, one can generate the virtues and features of a Tathagata. 'An Ban' uses the breathing method to establish 'Thủ'. The Four Dhyanas rely on the body to accomplish 'Concentration'. The breathing method has six stages: exhalation, following, stopping, observing, completing, and purification. Practitioners of meditation usually go through four stages of meditative concentration. Master Đạo An pointed out that observing Sổ Tức together with the Four Dhyanas are the distinctive key points of 'An Ban'.

The incorporation of 'An Ban Thu Y' doctrine into the cultural thought of the Chinese is as follows: Humans naturally live according to the nourishing qi of heaven and earth. Therefore, life depends on the presence or absence of breathing. Breathing is the act of inhaling and exhaling, which is the root of life and also the vital force of heaven and earth. If one clearly understands the regular operation of breathing qi, he can harmonize with heaven and earth as one entity. This method aligns with Zhuangzi's philosophy. From ancient times to the present, the human body has always inhaled fresh air and exhaled old air.

The Thai Breathing Method of the Chinese was invented by Taoist priests. In the scriptures translated by An Shigao, such as the Anban Shouyi Sutra and the Yinshi Ru, the 'Anban' method was exploited and adopted by the priests to create the 'Thai Breathing' method.

Later, Master Zhiyi based on the six practices (liu xing) of the Anban Shouyi Sutra to establish the 'Six Mysterious Dharma Gates'. Indeed, the fourth part of the Tiantai Xiao Zhi Guan all discuss breathing methods. The Japanese Zen Master Dogen, when teaching seated meditation methods, also discussed breathing methods.

Therefore, in terms of the doctrinal method of practice, over many generations, the An Ban Thu Y Sutra has had a great influence on meditation practitioners.

It represents the sutra that An The Cao translated as the Am Tri Nhap Sutra. It includes: The Five Aggregates, the Six Elements, the Ten Manifested Forms, the Six Consciousnesses, the Four Noble Truths, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the Four Brahmaviharas, and the Three Realms.

(Excerpt from “Thần Tăng Thiên Trúc”)

tieu_de: EXTERIOR BOUNDARY
tom_tat: The external realm is a scene that does not arise from the inner mind, but comes from the outside. Some practitioners may see the Buddha or Bodhisattvas manifesting to preach the Dharma, encouraging and praising. Or some practitioners, while reciting the Buddha's name, suddenly
noi_dung:
OUTDOOR SURROUNDINGS

The external realm is a scene that does not arise from the inner mind, but comes from outside. Sometimes a practitioner sees the Buddha or Bodhisattvas manifest to teach the Dharma, encourage, and praise. Sometimes a practitioner, while reciting the Buddha's name, suddenly has an opening in the mind and sees the Pure Land immediately. Sometimes a practitioner, while in pure mindfulness, sees deities or immortals coming, joining hands and circumambulating to show respect, or inviting them for a walk. Sometimes a practitioner sees spirits coming to seek refuge. Sometimes a practitioner, when reaching a high level of practice, is tested and disturbed by external demons...

* As in the past, there was a Buddhist devotee of dull nature, yet often respectfully reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara. One night, he dreamed that the Bodhisattva came and said he should frequently study and recite the following verse; over time, he would attain enlightenment:

Great wisdom arises in the mind

Where in the mind can it be found?

It accomplishes all meanings

Neither ancient nor present!

* Like in the recent era of the Republic of China, there was a layman named Giang Am Nam, who in March of the year Nhâm Thân (1932), while he was ill, witnessed the scene of the Pure Land. He painfully forced himself to write a letter to his brother, the layman Giang Diệt Viên, roughly as follows: "I am seriously ill. Around three o'clock in the morning on the twenty-fifth of March, after a thunderstorm with heavy rain, the sky cleared, bright as daytime. In the western direction, suddenly appeared the true scene of the Pure Land, vast and boundlessly bright. I saw the seven treasures adorned, the longevity pagoda, stupas, and countless wondrous appearances. The Buddha sat in the midst of the void, inviting me to come pay homage. But when I reached before the Buddha, the auspicious mark of Amitabha BuddhaTôn gradually drifted away, his voice echoing very faintly, and the surrounding scene completely vanished. It must be because your concentration is still weak, but from now on I am sure that the Western Pure Land is real...

* Also during the Republic of China period, there was a layman named Liu Kai Nan, with the courtesy name Xi Qiao Xiansheng. Before he passed away, the deities invited him to the Underworld to assume an official position; then he saw the celestial beings requesting him to ascend to heaven, but the layman solemnly refused, saying: "Holding office easily creates karma, and heaven's blessings will one day run out. I only wish to be reborn in the Pure Land." A few days later, the layman passed away.

* A Buddhist nun acquainted with the author’s pen, practicing near the Da Lat area. After a period of recitation and meditation, she was sitting in stillness and suddenly saw two messengers, whose demeanor and attire were like immortals, coming respectfully to invite her up the mountain to view the scenery. In her state of concentration, the nun asked: "The mountain is high, I am weak, how can I go?" One messenger replied: "Do not worry, I have a way." He then took a branch resembling a willow twig, gently struck her body, and told her to follow. She suddenly felt her body floating, gliding over the tips of the grass, and moments later ascended the mountain. Upon reaching there, she saw lush forests, branches spreading seeds dancing, and in the distance, a palace with pavilions. Just at that moment, her attendant at the back of the housedropped an object with a loud noise. The nun suddenly became aware, the state of meditation disappeared, and felt her two thighs still sore.

The various states briefly mentioned above are all called external realms. Some people ask: "Seeing the Buddha and seeing the lotus, is that an illusion or a demonic vision?" The answer is: "If the cause and effect are in accordance, it is not a demonic vision. Because the Pure Land School belongs to the 'realm of existence,' a person who recites the Buddha's name, upon initially generating the aspiration, starts from the realm of form and enters, wishing to see the holy realm in the Western Land. When one sees that good form, it is the result responding to the cause; the cause and effect coincide, so it is not a demonic vision. On the contrary, in the Chan (Zen) School, one enters from the 'realm of emptiness.' When generating the aspiration to cultivate, all forms are immediately swept away, even the forms of the Buddha and the Dharma are destroyed. A Chan practitioner does not seekSeeing the Buddha or the lotus, and the form of the Buddha and the lotus appear, that is a cause and effect that does not match. The effect arises without a cause, that is truly the realm of demons. Therefore, those who practice meditation always raise the sword of wisdom, demons come to kill demons, Buddhas come to kill Buddhas, entering the state of true emptiness, not accommodating any form at all.

However, that only applies to practitioners who are just beginning their practice. For those at advanced levels of meditation, they may sometimes see forms but they are not demonic visions. Because those who have practiced meditation for many lifetimes, once their mind is opened, can perceive the realms of evil as well as the heavens, extending to the Pure Lands in all ten directions and the impure realms; for worlds in the ten directions are all within the light of the true mind. And practitioners of Pure Land meditation may sometimes see forms, but these are demonic visions, which will be explained in detail in the following section on Discerning Demonic Visions.

In conclusion, the internal realm and the external realm refer to approximations according to the level of the person still walking the path of practice. As for those who have attained the fruit of enlightenment, the mind is the realm, and the realm is the mind; all things are of the same essence with us, there is no distinction between inside and outside.

Excerpted from the book “Ten Essentials of Mindfulness of Buddha” – Venerable Thich Thien Tam
