tieu_de: Venerable Thích Tuyên Hóa Gives Instruction on the Recitation of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara
tom_tat: (Reciting Avalokiteshvara in an emergency – Words of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua) Today I want to pass on to you a key point. It is a key point to apply in truly urgent moments. When faced with those situations, we should ph
noi_dung:
VENERABLE TUYÊN HÓA EXPLAINS THE PRACTICE OF REMEMBERING BODHISATTVA GUANYIN

(Reciting Avalokiteshvara in urgent situations – Words of Venerable Hsuan Hua)

Today I would like to teach you a key method. This is a key method to apply in truly urgent moments. In such situations, we must remain calm, do not panic, temporarily put aside matters of life and death, and wholeheartedly recite Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. Certainly, danger will transform into good fortune, and we will escape calamity.

In a moment of urgency, let us think: "Either way, we will die, so before dying, let us wholeheartedly recite the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, as perhaps that is the hope." Acting in this way is to encounter luck in the midst of danger.

When flying, if the airplane encounters trouble in the air, about to crash, at that very moment we should recite the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva.

Because Avalokiteshvara is a Bodhisattva dedicated to saving those who suffer and are in danger, a Bodhisattva who responds to prayers; if we do not recite His name, our life is extremely perilous, with no hope left.

At that time, if we sincerely directed our thoughts and responses to His compassion, then all the lives on the plane would be saved. When entering the Guanyin meditation session, we must also arise similar thoughts in order to perform the practice of reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name.

We can also imagine when riding a train, and suppose that the train derails, that is, in that split second, if we do not recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, all the passengers on that train would face fatal disaster.

Reciting and contemplating Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva means calling out for help; when the Bodhisattva hears our cries, even if separated by tens of thousands of rivers and mountains, He will immediately come to rescue us from suffering, with infinite efficacy.

Also, imagine we are on a ship at sea, and unfortunately, the ship is about to sink, the danger of being swallowed by a fish. In a critical moment, if we recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, continuing to recite until the last moment, even to the final second, if done so, it is certain that danger will turn into safety.

Suppose we are sitting in a car speeding down the road, and suddenly the car becomes uncontrollable, flying over the roadside toward a deep ravine, with sheer cliffs. If the car falls to the bottom of the ravine, it will be fatal, bones crushed and flesh torn.

At that very moment, if one recites Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva with complete sincerity, the car will land safely, terrifying but not dangerous. This is precisely the response from the practice of reciting Avalokiteshvara.

In moments of urgent danger, reciting a single phrase of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva is equivalent to hundreds of thousands of recitations under normal circumstances.

Why is that? Because when there is nothing dangerous, our recitation is not earnest enough, our heart is not sincere enough. Therefore, when reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, we must be wholehearted, completely sincere, then that spiritual response will truly be inconceivable.

Just now I told Quả Khiêm: "Nowadays, here at the Ten Thousand Buddhas City, if you recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, just imagine as if you were on a boat sincerely and earnestly praying, there will surely be a spiritual response.

At that time, amid strong waves and fierce winds, with such immense danger, if it weren't for chanting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, there would have been no hope to reach today. Only by chanting Avalokiteshvara could there be some hope, or even a chance to be saved, so by earnestly and wholeheartedly chanting in supplication, ultimately the calamity will be overcome, the wind will calm, the waves will subside, and one will reach the shore.

Now, when I chant Avalokiteshvara, it is even to have time to rest, because I am no longer in a dangerous situation as before.

"In truth:

Each day that passes, life gradually diminishes,

Like a fish without water, what is there to be happy about!

Everyone!

You must be diligent, save yourself.

Think of impermanence, do not be negligent!”

Recite the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, at any place and any time, in other words, walking, standing, lying down, sitting, all can recite. Whether reciting with the mouth or in the mind, the merit is the same, do not create a discriminating mind, always be according to circumstances.

One must remember that waiting until the moment of death to recite prayers is already too late, there will be no more opportunity. That is why there is the saying: 'Think of impermanence, do not be careless.'

tieu_de: A PERSON WHO UPHOLDS THE THREE REFUGEES IS PROTECTED DAY AND NIGHT BY 36 GUARDIAN DEITIES. SO DO WE HAVE GUARDIAN DEITIES PROTECTING US
tom_tat: In the Buddhist Sutras, the Buddha said that when you observe the Three Refuges, there will immediately be 36 Dharma Protectors guarding day and night. And when you observe the Five Precepts but only keep one precept, there will immediately be 5 Precept-Protecting Deities guarding you, if you
noi_dung:
THOSE WHO UPHOLD THE THREE REFUGES ARE PROTECTED DAY AND NIGHT BY 36 GUARDIAN DEITIES. SO DO WE HAVE GUARDIAN DEITIES PROTECTING US?

In the Precepts Sutra, the Buddha said that when you observe the Three Refuges, there will be 36 Dharma Protecting Deities guarding you day and night.

Furthermore, when you observe the Five Precepts but only keep one precept, there will be 5 Precept Protecting Deities guarding you; if you observe all five precepts, there will be 25 Precept Protecting Deities guarding you.

When you practice the Ten Virtues, spirits such as the Earth God, the City Deity, etc., will protect you.

We have all taken the Three Refuges and observed the Five Precepts, and a few have also taken the Bodhisattva Precepts, so is there a Dharma Protector guarding us? We do not see it. Why do we say we do not see it? Because taking the precepts is only in form and not in substance.

What does it mean to be genuine? It means strictly observing precepts. When it comes to taking the Three Refuges, have you truly taken refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha? If you only invite a teacher to preside over the ceremony to confer the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, but in reality you do not turn yourself around nor rely on the Buddha's teachings to practice, and you continue to be deluded and create karma as before, then you have not truly taken refuge in the Triple Gem. The Guardian Deities will certainly not protect you; that is the principle.

Taking refuge in the Buddha, Buddha means Enlightenment; we turn from delusion and confusion to rely on Enlightenment. When we interact with people, events, and objects at all times and in all places with enlightenment rather than confusion, then you truly take refuge in the Buddha.

If at all times and in all places you always give rise to discrimination and attachment, then you are in delusion, not in Enlightenment. Have you accomplished these things yet? Taking refuge in the Dharma means turning away from wrong knowledge and wrong views to rely on right knowledge and right views. Taking refuge in the Sangha means being pure and harmonious with everyone.

Regarding the Three Refuges, whether others observe them or not has nothing to do with oneself, but one must strictly adhere to them. Only by doing so can it be called upholding the Three Refuges, and only then will the 36 Guardian Deities protect you.

The Guardian Deities base their actions on the essence, not on form. They observe daily whether you have truly taken refuge, and if you have genuinely taken refuge, even without external forms, the Guardian Deities will still protect you.

Those who observe the Three Refuges and strictly follow the precepts may seem to outsiders as if they have nothing. However, they are actually very at ease, because in their hearts there is no fear. They know very clearly what is right, what is wrong, what should be done, what should not be done, what should be encouraged, and what should be avoided; this is true freedom.

The precepts of Buddhism may seem very difficult to follow at first glance. But compared to the sufferings of life, what significance do they really have? So why don’t we try to observe the precepts, so that our own life can be free and happy?

Dharma words of Dharma Master Jingkong

NAM MÔ A MI ĐÀ PHẬT

tieu_de: GOOD MALE AND FEMALE DEVOTEES MUST BE CAREFUL WHEN USING ITEMS OF THE TEMPLE:
tom_tat: ♦️FOOD, DRINKS, CAKES, AND FRUITS THAT ARE DEDICATED AND BROUGHT TO THE TEMPLE AS OFFERINGS TO THE BUDDHA BELONG TO THE OWNERSHIP OF THE TRIPLE GEM. YOU MUST NOT TAKE THEM WITHOUT PERMISSION; IF YOU WANT TO TAKE THEM, YOU MUST ASK THE PEOPLE IN THE TEMPLE FOR PERMISSION.
noi_dung:
GOOD MEN AND FAITHFUL WOMEN SHOULD BE CAREFUL WHEN USING ITEMS OF THE "TEMPLE":

♦️FOOD, DRINKS, CAKES, AND FRUITS THAT HAVE BEEN MADE an offering and brought to the temple to present to the Buddha belong to the ownership of the Three Jewels. You are not allowed to take them on your own; if you want to take them, you must ask for permission from those in the temple. Do not think that food you bought yourself and brought to the temple to offer gives you the right to take it back. Thinking this way means you have inadvertently committed the theft of the Three Jewels’ property (many people are unaware of this; we hope everyone reads this article carefully and pays close attention to this matter).

♦️Turning on electricity, making phone calls, using a water faucet, a piece of paper, a needle, a thread... can all constitute the crime of stealing from the Three Jewels. Seeing others do it seems fine, so we do the same. It is only when the retribution manifests that we regret too late.

In the world of thieves, all Buddhist scriptures warn us that taking from the Three Jewels carries the most severe sin.

The owner of the Three Jewels is "Buddha, Dharma, Sangha" throughout the entire empty space and all realms of existence; this theft cannot ever be repaid completely. In the Mahayana Sutras, it is often said that if you commit the five heinous and ten evil deeds, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have ways to save you; however, if you steal from the Three Jewels, from the eternal dwelling, then all Buddhas in the ten directions and three times have no way to save you. Therefore, there is a saying: "In front of the gates of hell, there are many monks," which is extremely meaningful. This statement is true, not false.

The offering items at the Buddha's doorstep are easy to steal, so is it dangerous? When you use them, it is very convenient, but in the future, you may not be able to repay. This principle must be understood. Even a needle, a thread, or a piece of paper that is regularly offered cannot be taken with a stealing mind. But nowadays, people are negligent, seeing others doing the same thing without consequences, and think it's okay to do it too. There may be no immediate consequences, but when karma appears before your eyes, it will be too late for regret.

In this place, the resident monk is usually very compassionate. He photocopied this passage from the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra and posted it everywhere to tell everyone, this is great kindness and great compassion, not something to fear that the resident monk will take away. The resident monk here is very generous; if you want to take something, just take it. In the future, when you receive the karma of your actions, what must you do? Therefore, you must definitely understand this principle. I often say, the current era is not like before; science and technology have developed. When we turn on electric lights, do we have to pay for the electricity? The electricity cost is covered by the resident monk. When we use telephones, we also have to pay for the phone bill. It is unnecessary to waste these energy resources ofpermanent resident, to be a permanent resident one must pay fees, which also belongs to theft.

🌷 There are some lay practitioners who clearly understand the principles, and I admire them very much. They use the abbot's phone, and after using it, they make sure to leave money behind, which is correct. The matter, bit by bit, very small, is exactly what is referred to here: "Even a speck of unwholesomeness." This is not a major unwholesome act; a tiny bit of unwholesomeness mixed in here can destroy all your wholesome deeds, and we must be aware of it.

The closest understanding of theft is what we nowadays call taking someone else's share of benefit, and this scope is very broad. It is not easy to seize someone else's benefit. People may not suffer great loss, but our own loss is truly enormous.

Why is that?

Obstructing one's own karmic path, destroying the purity of one's mind, and missing the opportunity to be reborn in Buddhahood in this life. Think about it, how great is this loss? There is no way to make up for it; we must understand, is it really necessary to do this? If someone takes what is rightfully yours, it's okay, no problem, we don't need to calculate or plan; this is almsgiving and should not be kept in the heart. If we start trying to calculate, then we are wrong again, and we turn into unwholesomeness once more.

We absolutely must not have the notion of taking the benefits of others. If taking the benefits of a single person is not allowed, how could you take the benefits of a collective? Such as those of the local government, the state, or the Triple Gem—it will naturally run out. Be sure to remember this thoroughly; in our lifetime, we will definitely achieve success.

BUDDHA TEACHES THE SUTRA OF TEN GOOD DEEDS - VOLUME 1

LECTURER: MASTER TINH KHONG

🙇‍♂️📿 NAMO AMITABHA BUDDHA 📿🙇‍♀️

tieu_de: TERRIFYING OMINOUS REPORT
tom_tat: This morning, someone from Vietnam brought two children to meet me, saying that their health was not good and hoping that I would help them have everything go smoothly and favorably. These two children have abnormal nerves, I just...
noi_dung:
TERRIFYING WARNING

This morning, someone from Vietnam brought two children to meet me, saying that their health was not good, and hoped that I could help them with everything to be smooth and auspicious.

These two children have abnormal nerves, I could tell immediately just by looking at them, so I asked if they had ever killed any living beings. After their mother listened to my explanation for a while, she understood and told:

In the past, there was a great old tree. When they cut it down, they saw that under the tree there were two snakes, which had crawled into a hole.

At that time, these two children used boiling water to pour into the hole to kill the two snakes.

After that action, their eldest son locked himself in his room, and a few days later when he went outside, he developed a mental illness. The first son was like that, the second one as well, both suffered from mental illness, and the mother hoped I could help them resolve this issue.

This disease is related to killing. Because they act cruelly, without compassion. The two snakes had already crawled into the hole, yet they still poured boiling water to kill them. These two snakes were originally brothers, and because they were burned to death by them, they themselves also develop madness.

The karma of killing brings very severe retribution. One keeps killing and then suffers the consequences: killing each other, repaying each other, this is a very tragic matter in the world. Even if people do not understand or believe that committing the karma of killing will lead to evil retribution, the cycle of vengeance and debt repayment constantly occurs, leading to national wars, resulting in mutual killing karma! The deeper the killing karma, the heavier the sin committed, so the cycle of killing continues endlessly.

In 1980, a director from distant Southeast Asia came to the Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery seeking my help because he was seriously ill with cancer. I led him to the Main Hall and had him perform repentance before the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly in all ten directions to salvage his karmic sins.

He recounted that he had committed many crimes, having eaten countless animal meats such as monkey brains, goose feet, etc.

Then I asked:

- Have you ever killed anyone?

He said: Absolutely not! But I once asked my wife to abort a pregnancy!

I explain:

- So, the reason he developed a terrifying terminal illness is because all these lives came to him, demanding their debts!

I would like to remind everyone: you should not have an abortion and never encourage others to have an abortion, because doing so is also equally guilty of killing!

Those who observe precepts have the merit of observing them; those who break precepts incur the evil consequence of breaking them. According to the law of cause and effect, whether you take and uphold precepts or not, cause and effect always exist and operate! The act of killing (aborting a fetus) is very wrong; according to the law of cause and effect, you will surely suffer retribution.

All acts of killing only increase resentment, attracting strange and evil diseases to the body along with unusual symptoms that are difficult to explain and cannot be cured!

Nowadays, besides cancer, there are other incurable diseases. These diseases initially stem from violating the precepts against sexual misconduct, killing, stealing, lying, and using intoxicants, smoking, or injecting drugs...

When everyone observes the Five Precepts, practices the Ten Virtues, and follows a vegetarian diet, there will be no natural disasters, and they will receive many great blessings; even a pure mind can enable many people to have supernatural abilities and open the 'five eyes'.

Stories of karmic retribution are real, they are manifestations of the Dharma, but worldly people do not believe them. Most still devote themselves to doing evil, not knowing to stop killing or releasing lives… If we want a peaceful world, everyone should observe the five precepts: Do not kill, do not steal, do not commit sexual misconduct, do not lie, do not drink alcohol or use drugs… If you do not create bad karma, the world will be free of natural disasters, suffering, and disease, and people will live happily.

(Venerable Tuyen Hoa)

tieu_de: THE MIRACULOUS BENEFITS OF SEXUAL EDUCATION
tom_tat: I am a 39-year-old woman, working at a factory in city T, have a happy family, am loved by my husband, have obedient and lovely children, and am always cared for by my parents. I must say life
noi_dung:
THE WONDERFUL BENEFITS OF EARTHWORM INTRODUCTION

I am a 39-year-old woman, working at a factory in city T, with a happy family, loved by my husband, having obedient and lovely children, and always cared for by my parents; I must say life is extremely satisfying.

I have only been studying Buddhism for a year. At first, when I saw the two words “sexual misconduct” in the Buddhist precepts, I always thought of myself as a good, kind person, completely faithful to my husband, doing nothing related to sexual misconduct, so I did not pay it any attention.

However, over time, when I deeply studied Buddhism and thoroughly absorbed its teachings, I realized that everything was due to my own ignorance, so I mistakenly thought I was clever, I was right, holding onto wrong views, even committing mistakes without realizing it.

The habit of lustful misconduct is indeed “self-taught without a teacher”; I recall at 17-18 years old, there were times when I was overly excited and gratified my own desires, gradually forming a habit, which persisted even after getting married and having children.

At the beginning of committing this mistake, I often felt remorse, shame, and thought of myself as truly dirty and despicable.

Once, I happened to read an ancient Chinese book that said: Masturbation causes a hundred diseases to arise!

I immediately made up my mind to give it up, but unfortunately, when I went online, I happened to read articles by many experts, seeing them declare: Masturbation enriches marital life, helps release body energy, reduces stress, relieves suppressed sexual desires, is very good for health, this behavior is completely harmless, it is normal, nothing to panic or blame yourself for…

So I clung to these words of encouragement and felt at ease, indulging my habits freely, because I saw that even renowned modern figures considered this behavior reasonable and normal, so I just practiced it. I reassured myself, thinking: Doing this does not betray my husband, and it even enriches our sexual life, therefore I continued to follow the advice of online experts, throwing away all the teachings of ancient sages and saints, without paying attention to them.

Later, as I got older, I developed many gynecological diseases, my vagina became inflamed, etc., but I didn’t pay much attention because I firmly believed: nowadays, which woman doesn’t have these conditions? I thought it was normal; there are a lot of women with gynecological diseases, so why should I be concerned or worried?

It wasn’t until later, when I noticed that my lower body often discharged fluids with a very unpleasant smell, that I realized I needed to maintain better hygiene. However, no matter how many times I bathed a day or how often I changed clothes, this condition still did not improve.

When I started studying Buddhism, I almost fell backward when I clearly understood: Masturbation is sexual misconduct, a highly wrong behavior, very shameful, and must be completely abolished, and the illnesses I was suffering from were the retribution of sexual misconduct; masturbation invited these consequences!

At that moment, it felt as if I had been struck on the head with a stick, my mind was awakened, and from that instant, I knew to deeply repent for the mistakes I had committed in the past.

From that point, I made a firm decision: To thoroughly give up masturbation, and it has now been five months. Although I have only recently stopped and eliminated this bad habit in a short time, strangely, gynecological problems suddenly disappeared completely, and what made me happiest was that my lower body no longer emitted an unpleasant odor.

I never expected that observing chastity would bring such miraculous benefits to both body and mind, filling me with immense joy. Not only that, my appearance has become radiant, and what brings me the most happiness is: I have become a pure woman by observing the Buddha's precepts.

Because I want to express gratitude to the Buddha and hope that everyone benefits from reading this article, I have gathered all my courage to write down my story to share. As a disciple of the Buddha, of course, I do not lie; please believe that the experience I personally went through is completely true.

I sincerely urge sisters not to think that living in modern times allows them to disregard ancient wise teachings and warnings. We must be cautious and prudent when reading articles that encourage indulgent living or allow oneself sexual indulgence online. Please do not believe in the theory: Masturbation is a normal act that brings benefits. It must be clearly understood that: At the very least, masturbation invites three evil consequences:

1. Numerous diseases arise as a result.

2. The body develops a foul odor.

3. Luck is always unlucky.

May all women be free from illness and suffering.

May everyone have a healthy and strong body and a happy family.

Minh Vũ - 20/3/2012

tieu_de: IMMEASURABLE MERIT OF CLEANING PAGODAS AND THE CAUSAL CONNECTION OF ARHAT BA KIET DA LE
tom_tat: The Bodhisattva Bhūmi Sutra records: “In the past, when the Buddha was still in the world, one day He said to five hundred arhats: - You all tell me what merits each of you created in past lives that now you have the karmic condition to meet Me and
noi_dung:
INFINITE MERIT OF CLEANING PAGODAS AND THE KARMIC CONNECTION OF ARAHANT BA KIET DA LE

The Sutra of Bodhisattva's Original Conduct records: "In the past, when the Buddha was still alive, one day He said to five hundred arhats:

- You all tell me what merits each of you accumulated in past lives that have now caused the affinity to meet Me and attain enlightenment!

At that time, the arhat named Bhikshus-kiet-da-le rose from his seat and said:

- O World-Honored One, I remember that in countless previous lifetimes, there was the Buddha Dinh Quang (Calm Light) appearing. After that Buddha entered Nirvana, His relics were divided so that people could build stupas and offer them homage.

In the age of the decline of the Dharma, there was a poor man with no means of livelihood, so he made a living by selling firewood. One day, he went to a pond to gather firewood and saw an extremely grand pagoda, so he went to the pagoda to admire the Buddha statue, feeling happy and paying respects. He saw that this place was only inhabited by wolves, birds, and wild animals; weeds and thorns filled the pagoda, there were no people, no footprints, and no offerings. Seeing this desolate scene, his heart was filled with compassion, so even though he did not understand the great virtue of the Tathāgata, he happily cut down weeds, cleaned the mud and trash, circled the pagoda eight times, paid respects, and then left.

Thanks to that merit, after passing away, that person was reborn in the heaven of Quang Âm, residing in a magnificent palace made of various treasures, with brilliant light, the most beautiful of all the heavens, beyond description. When their lifespan ended, that person returned to be the Wheel-Turning Sage King one hundred times, possessing all seven kinds of treasures, ruling four continents.

Later, when passing away, that person is often born into the households of kings and noble families, wealthy ones, with countless riches, possessing a very beautiful appearance, incomparable to anyone, and anyone who sees them feels happy and respectful. When that person walks, the roads naturally become clean, and flowers of all kinds fall from the sky.

Bakita said: “The poor person in the past is exactly this child today. Thanks to the merit of sweeping the stupa, in one aṭaṅkā and ninety lifetimes, you will not fall into evil paths, and wherever you are born, in heaven or among humans, you will naturally be wealthy, honored, and enjoy immense happiness. This is now the final body, having met the Buddha, you leave behind wealth, become a monk, and attain the state of Arahant, possessing the threefold knowledge, the six superknowledges, and the eight liberations.”

If someone does a good deed, even as small as a single hair, for the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, wherever they are reborn, they will enjoy immense blessings.”

Source: Cause and Effect

tieu_de: A Great Disaster for Humanity!
tom_tat: More than half of humanity will be destroyed, and those who survive are those who know how to cultivate spirituality, those who truly practice, those who know how to recite the Buddha's name, those who know how to chant scriptures, and those who are vegetarian.
noi_dung:
A Great Disaster for Humanity!

MORE THAN HALF OF HUMANITY WILL BE DESTROYED, AND THE SURVIVORS WILL BE THOSE WHO KNOW HOW TO PRACTICE THE WAY, THOSE WHO TRULY PRACTICE, THOSE WHO KNOW HOW TO RECITE BUDDHA'S NAME, THOSE WHO KNOW HOW TO CHANT SUTRAS, AND THOSE WHO FOLLOW A VEGETARIAN DIET – THESE ARE THE ONES WHO CAN SURVIVE

Currently, there are still people researching AIDS and trying to find a cure for this disease. Oh my! It's really like knowing that something cannot be done but still trying to do it. They force to cure this disease, not only failing, but also creating another kind of AIDS, which is pneumonia. This pneumonia is even more terrible than AIDS. Because this new disease can be transmitted through handshakes. The patient just opens their mouth and speaks, and the disease can be transmitted to others. In the past year, not only have patients been unable to recover, but even doctors and nurses, nearly twenty thousand people, have died because of this disease. There is no way to escape, not even by wearing masks or respirators!

As long as skin touches skin, the disease is transmitted. The germs of the disease can spread through the air. This kind of disease is even more dangerous than atomic bombs or even chemical bombs. Therefore, it is a disaster no different from a plague. Now this plague has broken out, and not only men are affected, but women as well. And not only both men and women are affected, even newborns also suffer from pneumonia and this AIDS disease. Look at it! Isn't it truly horrifying?

Now, across the world, if we count the number of people with AIDS and this new pneumonia, the number is not small, because some fetuses have been infected with this pneumonia bacteria while still in the womb. Therefore, around the world, the final hour of humanity has come. The so-called last days of mankind mean that everyone will be destroyed and disappear. More than half of the world's population is infected with this bacteria. When it breaks out, it will be like the Great Flood that no one can stop.

What should humanity do when faced with this calamity? We must sincerely and earnestly recite the Great Compassion Mantra. The Buddha taught that the Great Compassion Mantra can heal eighty-four thousand illnesses in the world. The eighty-four thousand ailments include AIDS and lung inflammation/infection. We must cultivate sincere devotion, regarding the recitation of the mantra as important as eating rice, as necessary as wearing clothes, and as indispensable as sleeping and resting.

What should I do to make the Great Compassion Mantra a part of my daily life? If so, AIDS will be afraid, pneumonia will also hesitate, but the most important thing is that we must be extremely sincere.

More than half of humanity will be destroyed, and the survivors will be those who practice the Way, those who truly cultivate, those who know how to recite Buddha's name, those who know how to chant scriptures, and those who are vegetarian – these are the people who can survive. I am not saying this intentionally to scare you. The time has come when I cannot help but speak loudly: this era is not a time of peace; this is an extremely perilous era. I cannot help but earnestly call out to you that: when you wake up in the morning, there is no certainty that you will be safe until evening; because this disaster can come in a moment that no one can expect.

Venerable Thích Tuyên Hóa gave a lecture on August 16, 1992 at Kim Luân Temple, Los Angeles

Namo Amitabha Buddha 🙏🙏🙏

tieu_de: GOD AVALOKITESHVARA BODHISATTVA AND THE ORIGIN OF THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA
tom_tat: (Lunar June 19, which is Gregorian August 8, 2020, is the day of the deity) Perhaps among each of us Buddhists, we all know Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, a very compassionate Bodhisattva, and when sentient beings have urgent matters, ...
noi_dung:
BODHISATTVA GUAN YIN AND THE ORIGIN OF THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA

(The 19th day of the 6th lunar month, which is August 8, 2020 in the Gregorian calendar, is his festival day)

Perhaps among each of us Buddhists, everyone knows Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, a very compassionate Bodhisattva, who when sentient beings are in urgent distress or suffering and recite his name, he immediately manifests to help, relieving all sorrow and suffering, eliminating all fears. I probably do not need to explain this; those who have a connection with Avalokiteshvara already know 😊. However, regarding his origins when he was still an ordinary being and the source of the great compassion mantra that he gave us to recite daily, perhaps many people are not clear about it.

In the Bi Hoa Sutra, it is said that before he became a monk, in one of his past lives, he was the firstborn son of King Vô Tránh Niệm, named Prince Bất Huyến.

During the period when that king ruled the world, the Tathagata Bảo Tạng was born.

The king saw that people’s hearts increasingly inclined to follow the teachings of the Buddha, and he thought: “If Buddhism were not genuine, would people worship it all over the country like this?”

Then the king developed the intention to prepare all the offerings to make offerings to the Buddha and the Sangha for three months, and also advised the princes and high officials to do the same.

At that time, Prince Abhaya, obeying his father, with wholehearted reverence, prepared all the delicious and precious items and brought his own treasured belongings to offer to the Buddha and the assembly for three months, without neglecting any day and with nothing lacking or inferior.

The great minister Bao Hai, father of Buddha Bao Tang, seeing this, advised: "Your Highness is already willing to cultivate merit by offering to the Buddhas and the Sangha: therefore, please dedicate that merit to the Supreme Enlightenment, and do not seek blessings in the Deva realm or the Brahma realm.

Because those realms, though they are pleasant places, with happy inhabitants, beautiful bodies, long lifespans, granted supernatural powers, free to roam at will, with abundant clothing and food, full access to leisure activities, and enjoying all types of natural pleasures, do not have suffering as in the human world.

The blessings in those realms, though so perfect and beautiful, still belong to the realm of conditioned existence, subject to decay and loss, with no certainty at all; they are impermanent, truly of an indeterminate nature, like a swiftly blowing wind that no power can hold back: when pleasure ends, sorrow arises; when happiness ends, suffering returns. Even living for thousands of years cannot escape the demon of birth and death dragging one into one path or another.

If Your Highness continues to seek those blessings, you surely will not escape the cycle of birth and death: if one cannot escape the cycle, then one cannot be assured of attaining freedom and ease at any time.

It would be better for Your Highness to use that merit to seek the precious and inexhaustible blessing, which does not decay or perish, and to enjoy infinite and endless joy beyond the three realms and four existences, and to dedicate it to the Bodhi path to quickly attain Buddhahood, so as to save sentient beings from the river of delusion and the sea of suffering. Thus, the portion for one’s own benefit is fulfilled, while the virtue of benefiting others is also complete.

When Crown Prince Bat Huyen heard Mr. Bao Hai advise in this way, he responded: “I observe all beings in the hell realm suffering extreme torment: as for humans and heavenly beings, they are full of defilements, numerous worldly troubles, lacking any purity, hence generating karma and consequently experiencing retribution by falling into the three evil paths: hell, hungry ghosts, and animals.”

Crown Prince Bất Huyến responded and then thought to himself: “Because sentient beings in this world do not encounter virtuous and noble people who advise them to avoid evil and do good, guiding them on the path of liberation, but only meet cruel and petty people who deceive each other to make friends, often inciting misconduct, and also corrupt the True Dharma, scorn the Great Vehicle Law, causing the loss of wholesome roots and adding wrong views, therefore obscuring the nature of the mind, not knowing what morality is, so they must endure suffering.”

Crown Prince Bất Huyến pondered for a long time, then said: “Now, before the Buddha and the great assembly, I declare: I vow to dedicate all the merits I have offered to the Three Jewels and all the merits I have cultivated through the wondrous Dharma to the path of Supreme Enlightenment.”

I vow that while I cultivate the virtues of a Bodhisattva and perform deeds beneficial to sentient beings, if I see someone suffering in poverty and misery, in a state of ignorance, not knowing whom to rely on or where to seek help, yet they recite my name, I will immediately use the power of divine hearing to listen and the power of divine vision to observe where the afflicted person is and what he or she prays for, so that I may appear to save them from suffering and bring them joy. If I fail to fulfill this vow, then I will not attain Buddhahood.

Venerable One! Now I make a great vow for the sake of all sentient beings, study the Dharma, and take care of self-interest deeds, may when my father is a Mind Without Avoidance, I will spend all my lives and patience after becoming a Buddha, and I will be called Amitabha Tathagata in the realm of Happiness, the World, and the transformation of sentient beings, and when I enter Nirvana, the Dharma will be passed down, then I will practice Buddhist work. When the Dharma is about to be destroyed, as soon as I destroy the previous one, I will attain the Bodhi Path in the next time.

I sincerely ask the World-Honored One to compassionately give me a prediction of my attainment, and I also wholeheartedly request all the Buddhas currently in the countless worlds in the ten directions to give me such predictions as well.

The Tathagata Bảo Tạng, upon hearing these vows, immediately gave a prediction to the Bodhisattva Bất Huyến, saying: “You observe that sentient beings in the realms of heaven, among humans, and in the three lower realms all experience karmic retribution for their offenses, and you generate great compassion, wishing to end all suffering, eliminate all afflictions, and enable everyone to enjoy peace.”

Because a person has a heart that examines the needs of sentient beings in the world and saves them from suffering in such a way, now I appoint the title: Avalokiteshvara.

While you practice the Bodhisattva path, you will teach countless sentient beings to be free from suffering and accomplish all Buddhist deeds.

After Amitabha Tathagata enters Nirvana, the Pure Land will be renamed: "The Accomplishment of All Treasures," and the manifestation body will be even more beautiful many times over than before.

At that time, during the night, in a moment, whenever all the solemn appearances appear, you will sit on the Diamond Throne under the Bodhi tree and attain Supreme Enlightenment with the title: “Tathagata of the King of Virtuous Light Manifesting All Meritorious Deeds,” complete in fortune and perfect in conduct, glorious in all matters, profoundly lofty in the Dharma, possessing vast supernatural powers, highly honored and revered, incomparable, living up to ninety-six billion eons, and upon passing away, the True Dharma will continue to be propagated for another sixty-three billion eons.

Prince Akṣayasūra, upon hearing the Buddha Bảo Tạng give a prediction, immediately rejoiced and respectfully said: "O World-Honored One! If my vow is truly fulfilled as You have spoken, what a great delight it would be! Now, I prostrate before You and ask what can be done so that all the Buddhas in the countless worlds may also give predictions to me, and so that all the worlds simultaneously resound with music, and all beings hearing this sound may attain purity of body and mind, and be separated from all worldly desires."

When Crown Prince Bat Huyen spoke, bowing his head in worship of the Buddha, immediately the worlds naturally shook and resounded, emitting gentle sounds; anyone who heard them felt joy arise in their hearts, causing all desires to suddenly vanish.

At that time, upon hearing the Buddhas of the ten directions simultaneously predict to Avalokiteshvara: "In the period of the Good Dharma lasting, in the world of Sandelwood, when Buddha Bảo Tạng will be born to teach sentient beings, there will be a son of King Vô Tránh Niệm, named Prince Bất Huyến, who will aspire to offer alms to the Buddha and the Assembly for three months: Due to this merit, he will, over incalculable kalpas, become a Buddha, named: The Tathagata Radiantly Ruling with the Light of All Encompassing Virtue, in the world called All Jewel Accomplishment."

After Prince Bất Huyến received the prediction from the Buddhas, his heart was very joyful.

Until the time of passing away, He was reborn in successive lives, from one lifetime to another, always maintaining His original vow, diligently practicing, seeking the Bodhi path, performing the conduct of a Bodhisattva, and attentively carrying out deeds that benefit sentient beings, never for a moment forgetting the thought of great compassion and great vow.

Originally, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva had already attained the Buddha fruit (True Dharma Bright Tathagata); however, out of the vow to save sentient beings, he manifested as a bodhisattva. Currently, he resides in the Western Pure Land serving Amitabha Buddha, daily guiding sentient beings from the ten directions back to that realm. Moreover, he has 32 emanations appearing in various realms to save sentient beings in distress across the ten directions.

Later, after Amitabha Buddha entered Nirvana, he succeeded the Buddha position to teach and guide sentient beings…

ORIGIN OF THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA

The origin of the Great Compassion Mantra is extracted from the Sutra of Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's Extensive, Complete, Unobstructed Great Compassion Mantra.

In the sutra, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva says to the Buddha: "O Worthy World-Honored One, I have the Great Compassion Mantra, and now I wish to recite it in order to bring joy to all beings, to eliminate all sickness, to grant longevity, to bestow wealth, to destroy all heavy karmic offenses, to be free from obstacles and calamities, to accomplish all virtuous roots, to dispel all fears, and to quickly fulfill all desires. I humbly request the World-Honored One to compassionately grant permission."

After the Bodhisattva finished reciting the mantra, the land shook six times, heavenly flowers and treasures rained down scattered everywhere, all the Buddhas of the ten directions rejoiced, and heaven's demons and externalists were terrified to the point of their hair standing on end. All the assemblies attained fruition.

THE POWER AND MERIT OF THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA

Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara said to the Buddha:

World-Honored One:

If any sentient being, in a single day and night, recites this mantra five times, they will eliminate heavy sins accumulated over hundreds of thousands of millions of eons of birth and death.

If a sentient being infringes upon the wealth and food of those who are constantly abiding, they will incur very heavy karma. Due to the obstructive nature of this evil karma, even if a thousand Buddhas were to appear, they would not be able to atone for it; and even if one tried to atone, it would not be eradicated. If this sin has been committed, one must perform repentance before teachers of the Ten Directions in order to eliminate it. Now, by reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, it can be immediately eradicated. Why is that? Because when the Great Compassion Mantra is recited with a devoted heart, teachers of the Ten Directions come as witnesses, and therefore all offenses and obstacles are completely eliminated.

Any sentient being who recites this mantra, all sins of the ten evil deeds and the five heinous acts, blasphemy, harming others, breaking precepts, committing offenses, destroying temples and stupas, stealing from monks, defiling virtue, all heavy karmic sins will be completely eradicated, except for one thing: if the person reciting the mantra still harbors doubt. If such a mind arises, then even minor sins and light karma cannot be eradicated, let alone heavy sins.

If any sentient being recites the Great Compassion Mantra, yet all their wishes are not fulfilled in the present life, then this mantra cannot be called the Supreme Protector of the Great Compassion Mind—except in cases of unwholesome intent and lack of sincerity.

If a woman is bored with being a female and wishes to become a male, she recites the verses of the Great Compassion Mantra, saying that in future lives she will certainly not transform from a female body into a male body, and she vows that she will not attain perfect enlightenment. Even if there arises a slight sense of doubt, it will not be fulfilled.

Truly, anyone who regularly maintains this mind-mantra is like bathing in rivers, lakes, and seas. If beings within those waters come into contact with the bathing water of that person, all their heavy karmic offenses will be completely destroyed. They will immediately be reborn into a pure land elsewhere, manifesting in a lotus body, no longer taking birth in womb, egg, or lower forms. These beings can achieve this merely through a small influence; how much more so the person who recites and upholds the mantra themselves?

And, just like when a person reciting a mantra walks along the road, and a breeze blows past them, if those beings behind are brushed by that person's breeze passing over their garments, then all their heavy negative karma and obstacles will be completely destroyed, they will no longer fall into the three lower realms, and they will be reborn in front of the Buddhas. Therefore, one must know that the merit and blessings of the person who recites mantras are truly beyond comprehension!

Moreover, the person who recites this Dharani, when they speak any words, whether good or evil, all heavenly demons, heretics, devas, dragons, ghosts, and spirits hear them as the pure sound of the Dharma, and they develop an attitude of respect and reverence toward that person, honoring them as they would a Buddha.

Whoever recites this Dharani should know that they are precisely the Buddha nature, because 9.9 billion countless Buddhas all cherish them. They should know that they are precisely the treasury of light, because the light of all Tathagatas shines upon them. They should know that they are precisely the treasury of compassion, because they often use the Dharani to save sentient beings. They should know that they are precisely the treasury of wondrous dharma, because they encompass all categories of Dharani. They should know that they are precisely the treasury of meditation, because hundreds of thousands of samadhis all manifest before them. They should know that they are precisely the treasury of space, because they often use the wisdom of emptiness to observe sentient beings. They should know that they are precisely the fearless treasury, because heavens, dragons,The benevolent deity often provides protection. One should know that this person is precisely the treasury of wondrous speech, for the sound of 'da ra ni' flows endlessly from their mouth. One should know that this person is precisely the treasury of permanence, for natural disasters and evil lifetimes cannot harm them. One should know that this person is precisely the treasury of liberation, for celestial demons and heretics cannot persecute them. One should know that this person is precisely the treasury of the Medicine King, for they often use 'da ra ni' to cure the ailments of sentient beings. One should know that this person is precisely the treasury of supernatural powers, for they can freely wander in the ten directions of the Buddha realms. The merits of this person are beyond all praise.

All grave evil karmas, such as the ten evil deeds, the five rebellious offenses, insulting others, slandering the Dharma, breaking precepts, destroying monasteries and stupas, stealing from monks, and defiling those who practice pure conduct, will all be extinguished.

Except for one thing: if there arises doubt regarding this mantra, then even minor sins and light karmas cannot be extinguished, let alone grave offenses. Although grave offenses are not immediately eradicated, one can still create the cause and condition to become a Buddha in the future.

Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara then addressed the Buddha:

"O World-Honored One! If beings in the heavens and humans recite the Great Compassion Mantra, they will obtain 15 types of good rebirths and will not suffer 15 types of bad deaths.

Those types of bad deaths are:

1. Not dying from extreme hunger and thirst.

2. Not dying from beatings or imprisonment.

3. Not dying due to enemies or adversaries.

4. Not dying in battles where soldiers kill each other.

5. Not dying from tigers, wolves, or wild beasts.

6. Not dying from poisonous snakes or scorpions.

7. Will not die from water drowning or fire burning.

8. Will not die from being poisoned.

9. Will not die from being harmed by evil herbs.

10. Will not die from going insane or losing one’s mind.

11. Will not die from landslides or falling trees.

12. Will not die from being cursed by wicked people.

13. Will not die from evil spirits or demons.

14. Will not die from serious malignant diseases.

15. Will not die from suicide.

Whoever recites the Great Compassion Mantra will not die from 15 types of evil deaths and will receive 15 types of good births, such as:

1. Wherever born, there is usually a wise ruler.

2. Usually born in a good country.

3. Usually encounter a good era.

4. Usually meet virtuous friends.

5. The faculties are always complete.

6. The path-mindedness is pure and skillful.

7. Do not violate prohibitions.

8. Relatives and followers are grateful and harmonious.

9. Food and wealth are always abundant.

10. Always respected and assisted by others.

11. Their treasures are not taken by thieves.

12. All wishes are fulfilled.

13. Benevolent dragons and spirits often protect.

14. Everywhere one is born, one sees the Buddha hearing the Dharma.

15. Upon hearing the True Dharma, one immediately comprehends the profound meaning.

If someone recites the Great Compassion Mantra, they will attain the 15 types of good lives. All humans and deities should regularly recite it and not be lazy.

Today, June 19, 2020 lunar calendar (corresponding to August 8, 2020 solar calendar), on the occasion of his sacred day, we should eat vegetarian, observe precepts, practice the ten wholesome actions, recite the Great Compassion Mantra, or chant his name to remember his merit in saving sentient beings from suffering in this world ^^

tieu_de: Venerable Thích Không talks about the secrets of the afterlife; before each disaster, a list of people already exists.
tom_tat: Everyone must live very frugally; every sip of water and every bite of food has already been predetermined. Who determines it for oneself? It is oneself, not the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, God, or King Yama who decides. The Buddha said that is
noi_dung:
Venerable Thich Khong did not talk about the secrets of the afterlife; before every disaster, there was already a list of people

Everyone must live very frugally; every sip of water and bite of food has already been predetermined. Who determines this for oneself? It is oneself, not the Buddha, Bodhisattas, God, or King Yama who decides. The Buddha said that it is determined by karma. Even in cases of death due to accidents or war, it is not an unjust death. When I studied Buddhism, Elder Layman Chou Ching-chu helped me a lot. He was the first person to print Buddhist scriptures in Taiwan in the 38th and 39th years of the Republic era. He lived to the age of 96 before passing away. He told me many strange stories he had experienced, notis fake. The old man himself initially followed science and had never believed in ghosts or spirits until now. But his father-in-law, Mr. Trương Thái Viên, was a great master of National Studies in the early Republic era. When he was alive, he once served as a judge for Emperor Dong Nhạc. Every night, two little ghosts would carry him to go to work; at that time, his body lay still on the bed as if he were dead. Early in the morning, when the roosters crowed, he would finish work and be brought back. He told his friends that he saw ghosts who lived longer than humans, encountered people from the Tang and Song dynasties, and even read their literature. The society in the ghost world was similar to our society; there were also foreign ghosts, but the language there was almost completely understandable, and there was also labor.there are also benefits. The Great Music Emperor oversees five provinces, and the life and death cycles of the people in the five provinces are all managed by him.

Great-Grandfather Chau also recounted, on a spring day of the Year of the Pig (Tân Hợi), there was a family with an only son. This son, upon passing the exams, did not want to become an official but stayed at home to farm and take care of his parents. He was very filial and, after getting married, had a child. At noon, he had a feeling as if he were dreaming, suddenly seeing someone knocking on the door holding a card, asking him that our General wants to invite him. Seeing his name correctly, he said, "I have never associated with officials in my life; I do not know your General at all." The person ignored his reasoning and said, "If the name matches, then just come with me and see," insisting.He mounted the horse. After getting on the horse, he felt as if the horse was flying in the sky, with the wind rushing past his ears. When the horse stopped, he saw many people seemingly negotiating a great matter. He asked the people there who the Grand General was, and they answered it was Yue Fei, which stunned him. Yue Fei was from the Song dynasty; why did he come here to find me? I am already dead, aren't I? My parents are old and my child is still very young; I cannot die. A moment later, the Grand General appeared. It turned out he wanted to find him to fight the enemy. The Jin people back then were the Manchus. Yue Fei wanted to suppress the Jin army and invited him to be secretary because he was a scholar. He saw that Yue Fei treated him extremely well.With courtesy, he said: I have parents above me, my wife is still very young, my child is too small, and I am the only son in the house with no siblings, so I feel very embarrassed. Nhạc Phi told him: It's okay, we will not start for another four months, I can take you home to prepare and arrange everything in the house. He felt that following Nhạc Phi was very honorable and glorious, so he gladly accepted. When the little demon took him back, he immediately woke up and told the story to his parents, but no one believed him. He said it was not a dream, it was completely real. In a flash, the appointed time arrived, he informed all acquaintances to come and see him off. Being young and without any illness, everyone crowded together.To see how he would die, Elder Châu also came to watch. When it was time to leave, he told his father: someone is waiting for me at the door. His father could hardly believe it and angrily expressed his refusal. He advised his father that it would be better to let him go, or else instead of drinking celebratory wine, they would end up drinking punitive wine. His father, frustrated, said: fine, you go. After saying this, he immediately passed away, leaving as soon as he was given permission. Then, two or three months later, the Xinhai Revolution succeeded, overthrowing the Qing Dynasty. Therefore, Elder Châu said: before the world becomes chaotic, the spirits and demons have already gone astray, and only when the spirits and demons win their battles do we win ours.

He also recounted that before the resistance war, during the January 28 Incident in Shanghai, three months earlier Mr. Zhou had a friend who worked as a clerk in the underworld handling official documents. The city god of Suzhou was like the provincial governor. In the underworld, Shanghai was considered a district. From Shanghai, a register of births and deaths was sent over, and this friend, while delivering it, secretly opened it to look and was very astonished to see that the names were all four or five characters long, unlike Chinese names. Later, while having a meal with Mr. Zhou and some friends, he recounted this story. No one really understood, and three months later, when the battle in Shanghai broke out, they realized who these people were.Death is the surname of the Japanese. Therefore, if one is destined to die, they must still die; the name was already in the register of life and death three months ago. Elder Châu saw this and said: in this world, when we see someone die unjustly, it is because we see it that way, but in truth, it is karma and reincarnation causing retribution for retribution.

We have to understand that if we truly want to save people and society, besides Buddhism, there is no other way. The law of cause and effect is a truth confirmed many thousands of times. Only Buddhism can save us from the terrifying sufferings of the cycle of birth and death. To be honest, Shakyamuni Buddha clearly told us in the Mahāsaṅgīti Sūtra that in this age of the Final Dharma, we can only rely on the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha, and we can only rely on Amitābha Buddha to peacefully transcend the Three Realms.

tieu_de: THE HONORABLE MONK TẦN, IN LOT A, EVEN THE ARHAT HAS NOT ENTERED NIRVANA AND IS STILL IN THE REALM OF YAMĀ, PLANTING MERIT FIELDS FOR BEINGS
tom_tat: Tan Toulu (賓頭盧) or Tan Tou (賓頭); is the leader among the 16 Arhats. Venerable Tan Toulu has lived a long life, appears with white hair and long eyebrows, and is therefore called the Long-Eyebrow Monk (長眉僧) or Long-Eyebrow Sramana (長眉
noi_dung:
MONK TAN DAU LO OF THE ALAHAN CATEGORY HAS NOT ENTERED NIRVANA AND IS STILL IN THE YAMAPHA PLANE WORKING FIELDS OF MERIT FOR SENTIENT BEINGS

Tán Đầu Lô (賓頭盧) or Tán Đầu (賓頭) is the leader among the 16 Arhats. Venerable Tán Đầu Lô lives a long life, with silver hair and long eyebrows in appearance, hence he is called the Long Eyebrow Monk (長眉僧) or Long Eyebrow Shramana (長眉沙門). The name Tán Đầu Lô roughly translates to Immovable (不動), and his family name Phả La Đọa means Sharp-Witted (利根). He obeyed the Buddha and lived long in the age of the decline of the Dharma to receive the offerings of sentient beings and help them cultivate merit; therefore, he was called the First in the Field of Merit (福田第一). Originally, he was a high minister of King Udayana (s, p: Udayana, 優填). The king saw that he was diligent and earnest, so he advised himbecome a monk with the Buddha. After attaining the Arahant fruit, he returned to his country and preached to the king. Therefore, the king respected him very much and came every morning and evening to inquire about the teachings. At that time, there was a great Brahmin minister of heretical beliefs who did not believe in the Buddha's teachings. When he saw King Uden come for consultation, Tañdālo just sat aside without standing up to welcome the king, and on that occasion, this person used a scheme to create enmity and incite the king. The king then said: 'Tomorrow, when I come for consultation, if he does not stand up to receive me, I will immediately execute him.' The next day, when Tañdālo saw the king approaching from afar, he stood up to receive him and initiated the greeting. Seeing this, the king was surprised and asked the reason why. The Venerable replied:“I did it for that king!” The king asked: “Why for me?” The reply: “In the past, Your Majesty came with a good heart, today You come with an evil heart; if I do not rise to welcome You, You will kill me. Whoever kills a Arhat will descend into Hell. So if I rise to welcome You, You will lose your kingship; but I would rather let You lose your kingship than descend into Hell. That is why today I stand to welcome You.” Hearing this, the king asked: “When will I lose my kingship?” The reply: “In 7 days.” Indeed, 7 days later, the king was captured by the neighboring country and made a prisoner. At that time, there was a wealthy man named Thọ Đề (樹提), who used Sandalwood (旃檀) to make a bowl and placed itOn the top of the tall pole, a loud voice declared: 'No matter who it is, if anyone can take this bowl without using a ladder, this bowl will belong to that person.' At that time, Xin Tou Luo displayed supernatural powers and took the bowl. Upon learning about this, the Blessed One immediately rebuked him, saying: 'Can a Bhikkhu misuse supernatural powers to take an outsider’s bowl?' And he ordered him never to dwell in Jambudvīpa for the rest of his life, so he went to reside in Apara-godhānīya. Later, the disciples, missing the Venerable One, earnestly begged the Buddha to allow him to return to Jambudvīpa. But the Buddha did not permit him to enter Nirvana.but must reside in the world, uphold the True Dharma, and receive offerings from sentient beings during the degenerate age of the Dharma. Therefore, in the dining halls of monasteries, there is often a seat at the front row on the west side, which is the seat of the Chief Abbots (首座, in Zen Buddhism, it is the name given to the one who stands at the head of the assembly), but no one actually sits there. However, at that seat, food, drinks, bowls, and chopsticks, etc., are frequently arranged to offer to the Venerable. When offering the monastic meal, the Venerable will manifest as a Bhikkhu to receive the offering. Therefore, when reciting the dedication for the offering, there is often a phrase: “Namo Xindu Lofa La Duo Zha Venerable, greatly manifest and certify.” It is said that a wealthyThat gentleman made merit by offering alms to 1,000 monks with the purpose of seeking blessings and hoping to have an Arhat come to receive them. He organized a three-day alms-giving ceremony. On the evening of the third day, he dreamt of an old monk wearing tattered robes, with three frightening lumps on his forehead, who appeared and said to the gentleman: “I am Tan Dau Lo!” “Oh, you are Tan Dau Lo? Are you here to attend the alms-giving?” The Venerable replied: “Of course! On the first day, when I arrived, the gatekeeper would not let me in. I said I came to bestow blessings on this homeowner. The gatekeeper did not believe me, saying that since my robes were tattered, how could I have any blessings to give to others? After saying that, he hit me with a stick, causing the lumps on my forehead to...a lump. On the second day, I was hit and got another lump. By the third day, I thought it would be the last day I could enter, but I was hit again.” The wealthy man woke up, learned the truth, and deeply regretted not having the good fortune to receive the Holy Monk. There was also a county magistrate who, having heard that offering food to the monks would surely allow the Holy Monk Tan Dau Lo to come and receive the offerings, arranged a meal offering at Thien Dong Temple (天童寺) in Ningbo (寧波). At the time of the noon meal, he suddenly saw a monk wearing ragged clothes, very old, with drooling and a runny nose, showing no trace of dignity, stumbling as he walked, advancing toward the seating area ofthe position of the Abbot. Usually, this position is always reserved for offering to the Holy Monks. The county magistrate came closer to look and, upon careful inspection, saw that the whole body of that monk from top to bottom was unbearably filthy. He then used his hand to grab the monk's ear and pull him to sit in the last row. After the meal, the magistrate asked Zen Master Thiên Đồng if the Holy Monk had attended today. The Zen Master replied yes. Upon hearing this, the magistrate happily asked who it was. The answer: 'It is the monk whose ear you pulled.' The old county magistrate was astonished, trembling, and exclaimed: 'Truly, I had eyes but no vision. I have humiliated the Holy Monk! Such a grave sin!' According to the Great Song Monastic Records.Sū Lüè (大宋僧史略) Book 3, section Phương Đẳng Giới Đàn (方等戒壇) states that when Vinaya Master Đạo Tuyên (道宣, 596-667) was at Zhongnan Mountain (終南山), he established the Linggan Precept Altar at the monastery in Qingguan Village (清官村). There was a monk whose eyebrows were long enough to reach the front of the Precept Altar, admired. As in the Saṃyukta Āgama (增壹阿含經, Taishō No. 125) Book 3, there is a passage: “Subjugating external heretics and practicing the proper Dharma, the monk Xintoulu is one who subdues external heretics and practices the proper Dharma; that is called the Monk of the Heart of Xintoulu.” Also, in the Saṃyukta Āgama (page 125) Book 44, the Buddha predicts for four Śrāvakas, among whom is Xintoulu, saying: “In the present year, having gradually declined, reaching beyond the age of eighty, now...The Tathāgata has four great Śrāvakas, capable of undertaking teaching and propagation, with limitless wisdom, and possessing complete virtues. Who are the four? They are the Śrāvaka Mahākāśyapa, the Śrāvaka Anuruddha, the Śrāvaka Upāli, and the Śrāvaka Rāhula. These four great Śrāvakas mainly do not enter Nirvana, practicing my teachings to completion, and only then enter Nirvana. The meaning is, 'This year I am already weakened, my age is over eighty, yet now the Tathāgata has four great Śrāvakas, capable of undertaking the work of propagation, possessing limitless wisdom and complete virtues. Who are the four? They are the Śrāvaka Mahākāśyapa, the Śrāvaka Anuruddha, the Śrāvaka Upāli, and the Śrāvaka Rāhula. These four great Śrāvakas primarily do not enter Nirvana until my Dharma has ended.'finished, then only enter Nirvana)..."

tieu_de: MR. THAI VIEM REVEALS ABOUT THE HELL SCENE THAT PEOPLE WITHOUT KARMIC DEBTS WILL SEE NOTHING WHEN THEY COME TO HELL
tom_tat: Among the disciples of Master Hư Vân, there was a person named Chu Kính Trụ (1889-1985), with the dharma name Khoan Kính. He was originally a scholar in finance and economics, and once held the position of Director of Finance of Xikang, Sichuan Province.
noi_dung:
CHAPTER: MR. THAI VIEM REVEALS ABOUT HELL SCENES, PEOPLE WITHOUT KARMIC RECORDS GOING TO HELL WILL SEE NOTHING

Among the disciples of Master Hư Vân, there was a person named Chu Kính Trụ (1889-1985), with the dharma name Khoan Kính. He was originally a scholar of finance and economics, having served as the Director of Finance of Xikang, Sichuan Province, and the head of the Finance Department of Zhejiang Province. In 1949, he went to Taiwan to devote himself to Buddhist practice and to propagate the Dharma. He also established a Buddhist scripture printing workshop in Taiwan to circulate Buddhist texts.

Zhu Jingzhu was the son-in-law of Zhang Taiyan (1869-1936) – a master in the Chinese academic world in the early years of the Republic of China. In 1931, Zhu Jingzhu worked as a director at a bank. During his leisure time, he often invited a few close friends to play mahjong and chat.

In that group of friends, there was one person who was a 'spirit messenger,' who usually went to the Underworld in the evenings for work. That person's position was not very high, just similar to being in charge of delivering official documents, serving as a subordinate to the Tô Châu City God. In the human realm, Tô Châu is a district, and Shanghai is a large city, but in the underworld, the City God of Shanghai is only like a district-level official, under the management of the Tô Châu City God. The 'City God' we talk about also has distinctions in ranks; the 'Ducheng City God' is the highest position, managing an entire province.

As dusk approached, two little demons came to invite him onto a palanquin, then carried the palanquin to his workplace in the Underworld. Because he served as a judge for a relatively long time, he had the opportunity to see the situation under the control of the netherworld officials…

He said, one day the City God of Shanghai brought a "book of life and death" to report to the City God of Suzhou, and he was the one who received it. Out of curiosity, he opened it to see who was listed, and the result left him feeling vaguely puzzled. Most of the names had five or six characters. The next day, while chatting with Zhou Jingzhu, he recounted this story, and no one could figure out the reason. Chinese names are usually at most four characters long; they cannot possibly be as long as five or six characters. Therefore, Zhou Jingzhu's friends, no matter how much they thought, could not make sense of it.

Three months later, on January 28, 1932, Japan launched a war in Shanghai, and the Nationalist army heroically resisted. At that moment, they finally realized that the previously sent "book of life and death" to Shanghai was actually the list of Japanese soldiers who would die in the campaign on that day, January 28. From this, it can be understood that "life and death are predestined," meaning that three months before the war broke out, those who perished already had their names on the list, which had been sent to the place of the Tô Châu City God.

This clearly indicates one thing: those who die unexpectedly in war have actually already been destined by fate. When and where they die has been predetermined; it is truly as if "every morsel of food to eat and drink has been preordained." Those whose fate is not to die, even if they are in a rain of bombs and bullets, will remain unharmed; the person whose time to die has come, even a stray bullet will kill them. This is all the truth.

The elderly layman Chu was the son-in-law of Chương Thái Viêm, and Chương Thái Viêm was a scholarly master, very famous in literary circles. At that time, Viên Thế Khải held power, and Chương Thái Viêm, having offended Viên Thế Khải, was imprisoned. How did he offend him? He said that Viên Thế Khải was not worthy of being scolded by him, meaning that scolding Viên Thế Khải would only dirty his own mouth. When this statement reached Viên, he became very angry and immediately had Chương imprisoned. In reality, it was not a serious crime, so just over a month later he was released.

After Zhang Taiyan passed away, Zhu Jingzhu organized the works left behind by his father-in-law and discovered a strange letter. The letter was written in very respectful language addressed to a "superior," and it recorded how Zhang Taiyan went to the Underworld every day to act as the King of Hell. Later, Zhu Jingzhu used this as a basis to compile an article titled "Yuan Shikai Wants to Be Emperor, Zhang Taiyan Is Afraid of Being King of Hell." The article stated that shortly after being released from prison, in early December 1914, Zhang Taiyan dreamed of two small demons carrying a palanquin, saying that the Great Deity of Mount Dong called for him and invited him to get on the palanquin. The two demonsThis little one went as fast as flying, and before long had arrived at the place of the Eastern Music Emperor.

China has the Five Great Mountains (five major mountains), with Dongyue overseeing five provinces, while the Capital City's god in Jiangsu governs only one province, so it can be seen that the Dongyue Emperor is a great demon king. The Dongyue Great Emperor invited Zhang Taiyan to serve as a judge, inviting him to work there every evening. He recounted that as dusk approached, two little demons would come to invite him onto a sedan chair, then carry the sedan chair to the workplace, and the next early morning, when it was daylight, they would take him back home. Because he served as a judge for a relatively long period, he had the opportunity to observe the situation in the Underworld of Yin Court and Diyu (Hell).

That is the truth! In the underworld, although the races are different, the nations are different, and the languages are different, in the Yin Court, all speech is understood, and both sides can communicate without obstacles and understand each other, which is a miraculous phenomenon. Their eating, drinking, and walking are also similar to those in the human world, except that they cannot see sunlight, so their daytime is eternally dark and gloomy. Emperor Tai Ying served as a judge under the Eastern Yue Great Emperor, holding a very high position, receiving treatment, and also eating and drinking, but he had no place to reside, because he was still among the living.

Once, he realized that in this hell there was a type of punishment called "bào cách," which involved heating a bronze pillar until it was red-hot and then forcing the punished person to embrace it. Emperor Chương Thái Viêm was a Buddhist and a devout follower; he said this form of punishment was too cruel, so he proposed to Great Emperor Dong Yue: "Could it be abolished? If so, wouldn't You have done a truly good deed and gained great merit?"

After hearing this, Emperor Dong Nhac said, “You may go take a look at the crime scene first,” and sent out two little ghosts to lead him to the scene. The little ghost led him through many roads, and when they arrived at the scene, the ghost stood still and said: “We’ve arrived! Please, judge, take a look.” Yet he saw nothing at all. Suddenly, he realized that, according to Buddhist scriptures, hell is manifested by karmic forces, not established by King Yama. Because it is manifested by karmic forces, if you do not have the karmic force, even if it is right in front of you, you cannot see it. This story seems to have been written by the elderly layman Chu in one of his previous works.at the end of life.

In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, it is said that only two kinds of people can see and enter hell: one is the person who created the karma of hell and the person who is undergoing the punishment, who can then see it. Another kind of person is the Bodhisattva, who enters there to teach and transform sentient beings. If you are not one of these two types, you cannot see the realm of hell even if it is right in front of you. Therefore, this is not created by human power, but is manifested by the karmic force of those individuals themselves, as they are there to endure punishment. In reality, even the little demons, ox-headed and horse-faced beings, and enforcers of law in hell are manifestations of human karmic force, humans themselves haveWho can be blamed here? Truly, you reap what you sow, even King Yama has no way.

Since then, every night Mr. Chương would dream of himself as the King of Hell. Later, he became extremely weary and once wrote a letter requesting to resign, but it was not accepted. By the time he wrote this letter, it had already been more than 4 months...

(According to Soundofhope.com, excerpted from a lecture by PS Tịnh Không)

tieu_de: LIVE TWICE
tom_tat: In Ngô District, there was a judicial officer who suddenly collapsed and died. Overnight, he woke up, hurriedly called his family to summon the Prefect along with all his fellow officials and subordinates, then kowtowed deeply.
noi_dung:
TWO TIMES LIVING AGAIN

In Ngo district, a certain magistrate suddenly collapsed and died. After waking up one night, he hurried to call his family to invite the Prefect along with all fellow officials and his subordinates, then he kowtowed and bowed to everyone, saying: “I was taken to the underworld, and I begged for my life. At first, they did not agree, but later they asked me: ‘Can you advise a thousand people not to eat beef? We give you three days to do that.’ Now I am lucky to have come back to life, but if you do not help me advise the people throughout the region, this task cannot be accomplished."

People [did not believe those words were true, so] only pretended to make empty promises [and then no one did anything]. After three days, that judicial official indeed fell down dead. The Prefect was extremely shocked and immediately summoned all the officials in the district, together taking a vow to abstain from eating beef, and also had a register placed at the crossroads, encouraging the people to write their names in it [to vow not to eat beef]. When the number reached one thousand, the register was then burned.

After a moment, the Investigating Magistrate came back to life, recounting: “I was taken by someone to the underworld. The Judge, upon becoming angry, scolded me, when a person dressed in yellow brought a register, saying this is the list of people who have vowed not to eat beef. The Judge glanced through it and became extremely pleased, saying: 'Not only will you be allowed to live again, but your lifespan will also be extended by 6 ji.' The Prefect along with those who [vowed not to eat beef] all received boundless blessings.”

That Investigating Magistrate later lived to be a hundred years old. COMMENTARY

Recently, the local leaders have also issued a ban on killing buffaloes, but there is a lack of implementation methods. Therefore, even though signs banning the killing of buffaloes are hung all over the city, buffalo meat dishes are still found everywhere.

Those who work as buffalo butchers only do it out of greed for profit. If they cannot gain any profit, naturally they will quit the trade. Therefore, the local authorities should take turns to supervise [everywhere]; if they catch someone selling buffalo meat, they should impose a fine and use that money as a reward for the person who caught them. The amount of that reward must be greater than the bribe money that the butchers receive privately. In this way, the authorities will gladly follow the official orders without taking bribes to cover up those who violate the law. If this is not done, once the authorities receive bribes from the slaughterhouses and collude to protect them, how can the local officials know? How could it be detected?

Notes:

1 Each cycle is 12 years, adding 6 cycles equals 72 years.

2 That is, in the time of scholar Zhu Anshi.
