tieu_de: WHEN YOU WANT TO WORK WELL, THE KARMA REVEALS IT.
tom_tat: "WHEN YOU WANT TO BECOME A BUDDHA, DEMONS COME TO CHALLENGE." If you do not want to become a good person, karmic retribution does not appear. The more determined you are to be a good person, the more karmic retribution comes relentlessly. When you want
noi_dung:
WHEN YOU WANT TO DO WELL, KARMA SHOWS ITSELF.

"WHEN YOU WANT TO BECOME A BUDDHA, DEMONS COME TO CHALLENGE."

If one does not want to become a good person, karmic retribution does not appear. The more determined one is to be good, the more karmic retribution comes swiftly. When one wants to become a Buddha, demons come to test.

The greatest flaw of sentient beings is attachment and desire; they live day and night in attachment and desire and cannot let it go. If one can transform a lustful mind into a mind dedicated to studying the Buddha's teachings, being mindful of practice every hour and every minute without neglecting it, one will quickly become a Buddha.

For those who are new to cultivating, the greatest obstacle when practicing is the lustful desire between men and women. This is the most fundamental issue.

Those practicing the Way should pay attention! Do not sow impure attachments with others. This binding rope of impurity will lead us to downfall.

Practicing the Way means following the Middle Path - treating everyone equally, taking compassion as the foundation, but remember to be careful, do not get lost in the nets of love and desire.

Cultivation requires keeping oneself pure, like keeping the eyes free from a single grain of sand.

Practitioners of the Way, wherever they are, must hide and erase traces, and should not reveal themselves.

A virtuous person is not defined by status or age, but in discreet and silent actions, their distinctive character naturally appears, earning the respect of others.

A person who truly knows how to practice will find that every gesture and movement is a form of practice.

In our temple, we must know how to save all items. It is said:

"Cherish the temple's belongings

Like protecting the pupil of the eye.

A true practitioner of the Way must examine all their own actions and movements. Whether walking, standing, lying, or sitting, one must not lose mindfulness. Do not be like a mirror—only knowing how to reflect others' faces without reflecting your own true self.

A monastic must solemnly maintain the four dignified postures of walking, standing, lying, and sitting. It is said: "Walk lightly like the wind, sit firmly like a bell, stand straight like a pine tree, lie like a drawn bow."

A practitioner must cultivate selflessness, practicing to the point where there is no "self". If the "self" no longer exists, one can endure everything, and no matter what realm arises, the mind remains unmoved, seeing oneself as like the void.

If one thoroughly understands the Precepts, one can penetrate the entire realm of Buddha-dharma. If one does not understand the Precepts, it is like clouds drifting in the sky, floating aimlessly, with no fundamental support.

The essence of the Precepts is only one thing, which is not to be selfish.

Diligently observing the Precepts is mainly about doing so in places where no one can see. It is not only about diligently observing the Precepts in front of others, but also when alone, one must always be diligent, diligent, and strictly observe the Precepts.

One must definitely uphold the precepts in a truly strict manner. This is extremely important, of utmost significance.

The Precepts are the lifeblood of a practitioner.

Studying Buddhist teachings means learning not to harm others. Should Buddhists be vegetarian? Because if eating meat means harming the lives of other living beings.

Being vegetarian means having to endure hardships because you cannot enjoy the delicacies of life. But if you do not eat vegetarian and instead eat animal meat, after death you must go to the underworld to settle your debts. I speak honestly with my conscience to let you know: If people do not crave "delicacies" or pleasure, then after death they will not have to appear in court!

Do you think that if you are vegetarian you can still eat eggs? You can! Just wait until you are reincarnated as a chicken, and then you will understand that being a chicken comes from eating chicken eggs.

Many people make vegetarian foods resembling meat, chicken, duck, or fish because they cannot forget the taste of meat. They keep tasting it. They say that eating such fake meat helps to relieve cravings, tricking the palate. In Buddhism, it is necessary to correct this bad habit. If it is not corrected, over a long period of time, there may be no monastics who eat vegetarian food anymore.

I think that if one eats vegetarian, even the name of the dish should not include chicken, duck, or similar references. I hope that every Buddhist follower needs to have the eye of understanding truth (Dharmic discernment). One must understand cause and effect, and not be confused in the process of planting causes and receiving results.

When practicing vegetarianism, eat to purify yourself, do not keep thinking about the taste of meat. Making food in the shape of shrimp or fish (even if artificial) is no different than insulting the Buddha's path. A believer who does not observe carefully and casually assumes it is fine is fundamentally lacking wisdom, without the eye to recognize the truth, not understanding cause and effect, only vaguely and ignorantly confused.

When animals are killed, their hearts are filled with malice, hatred, and a desire for revenge. At the moment of death, their minds are fearful, resentful, and want to take revenge. That malicious and hateful mentality produces toxins, causing the person who eats their meat to ingest those toxins.

The type of meat you eat, over time, your own temperament is entirely shaped by the temperament of those meats: be it the nature of pork, the nature of beef... Your blood is also their blood. Therefore, your meat also becomes their meat. I urge those with wisdom to deeply contemplate this matter.

A bowl of soup full of fish meat (though small), yet contains resentment and hatred as deep as the sea. One cannot fully express that enmity.

Meat contains a kind of impure energy. This is because it originates from impure beings. Therefore, those who eat meat find it difficult to maintain precepts, hard to develop wisdom, and hard to attain samadhi.

Eating meat increases desires and delusions, making it very difficult to enter concentration. Not eating meat lightens desires, brings contentment to the heart, and reduces delusions. This is because one's vital energy is light and not impure.

Killing causes resentment to accumulate, filling the universe and leading to all kinds of accidents. If people do not kill but instead release life, and do not eat the flesh of any beings, then violent and cruel thoughts will be eliminated. Why are some people fierce, aggressive, and ferocious? It is because they eat meat. Eating meat increases desires, increases a hot temper, and leaves no compassion.

From countless kalpas until now, from one life to another, each person creates different karmas, so their delusions are also different. Heavy karma leads to many delusions, light karma leads to few delusions.

A reverent heart can transform a stubborn nature into a gentle, kind nature.

"The one who points out my mistakes is my Teacher." The person who speaks out our faults is our virtuous friend; therefore, we should be grateful, not harbor resentment.

THE DHARMA WORDS OF VENERABLE TUYEN HOA

5. Homage to the Tathagata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened, Ocean of Dharma, Thunder Sound Buddha

6. Homage to the Tathagata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened, Ocean of Dharma, Supreme Wisdom, Marvelous Powers Buddha

7. Homage to the Tathagata, Worthy of Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened, Medicine Buddha, Lapis Lazuli Light King

And all the Buddhas, the World Honored Ones, who eternally dwell in all the worlds of the ten directions. May all the Buddhas, the World Honored Ones, have compassion and remember me.

My name is…. Dharma name…. now I, before the assembly of three directions,

of all Buddhas, sincerely repent for all the karmic sins I have created in this life or previous lives.

From beginningless time until now, I have gone with the flow of the river of crimes, creating karmic obstacles together with sentient beings, bound by greed, anger, and ignorance. When I did not know the Buddha, did not know the Dharma, did not know the Sangha, and did not know good and evil, I committed the five heinous crimes through body, speech, and mind: evil intentions causing the Buddha's body to bleed, blaspheming the Buddha's teachings, destroying the harmony of the Sangha, harming Arahants, and harming father and mother. I committed ten evil deeds through body (three), speech (four), and mind (three) by doing them myself, commanding others to do them, and rejoicing when seeing others do them. Towards virtuous people, I arrogantly blasphemed; I cheated with scales and measures, considered wrong as right, and gave spoiled food to others; and towards parentsFor many lifetimes in the six realms, I have been destructive; regarding the property of the Stupa, of monks from the four directions, and of the present monks, I have stolen, plundered, and freely used; regarding the precepts and the teachings of the World-Honored One, I have not wished to observe or practice them, and I do not follow the instructions of the master; when seeing anyone following the vehicle of the Śrāvaka, the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddha, or the vehicle of the Mahāyāna, I have insulted and disturbed them; when seeing anyone superior to me, I have become jealous and envious, and even regretted giving in charitable deeds, letting ignorance block my understanding, and being deluded by wrong views, I have not cultivated good deeds but rather increased evil actions; I have blasphemed even the World-Honored One, declaring what is the Dharma as non-Dharma, and what is non-Dharma as Dharma. So many transgressions such asThus, venerable Buddhas, with true wisdom, true eye, true realization, true equality, knowing all and seeing all, I today sincerely take refuge and respectfully pay homage. Before the venerable Buddhas, I dare not hide anything. I will not commit unaccomplished sins, and I repent of the sins I have already committed. The karmic obstacles that lead to the six paths and eight sufferings that I have created, and the karmic obstacles I am currently creating, I vow to eliminate them all. I vow that in the future I will not have to endure the results of these karmic obstacles. Just as the great Bodhisattvas of the past, practicing the path of enlightenment, have repented all their karmic obstacles, so too will my karmic obstacles be repented, todayToday I sincerely repent all. I reveal everything, dare not hide anything. The sins I have committed, I vow to eradicate; the sins I have not committed, I vow not to commit them anymore. Just like the great bodhisattvas in the future practicing the Bodhi path, they repent all karmic obstacles, and so does my karma; today I sincerely repent all. I reveal everything, dare not hide anything. The sins I have committed, I vow to completely eradicate; the sins I have not committed, I vow not to commit them anymore. Just like the great bodhisattvas presently practicing the Bodhi path, they have repented all karmic obstacles, and so does my karma; today I sincerely repent all. I reveal everything, dare not hide anything. The sins I have committed, I vow todestroy everything, the crime not yet committed, I vow not to dare to do it again.

In the ten directions of the world, however many sentient beings currently practice charity, observe precepts, meditate, and cultivate wisdom, I now profoundly rejoice in all of them, rejoicing in all the merits of all sentient beings of the past and the future. Moreover, for the Bodhisattvas who have just begun to practice and have generated the bodhi mind, however many merits they possess; for those Bodhisattvas who have practiced the Bodhisattva path over hundreds of lifetimes, however great their merits; for those Bodhisattvas who have attained the patience of the Dharma without birth, who are irreversible, who will be born only once, all such immense accumulations of merit, I wholeheartedly rejoice in and praise them all. For the past and the future, however many merits all Bodhisattvas have, I also rejoice inRejoice and admire like that. Furthermore, in the present ten directions of the world, all the Buddhas, Worthy Ones, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones have realized the subtle wisdom of bodhi; in order to liberate countless sentient beings, they turn the supreme Dharma wheel, practice the unobstructed giving of the Dharma, beat the Dharma drum, blow the Dharma conch, raise the Dharma banner, shower the Dharma water, compassionately teach and guide all beings, making everyone believe and accept; through the grace of the giving of the Dharma, all attain boundless happiness and comfort. The Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas gather merit; beings who do not yet have such merit are granted it. All the merits of the Buddhas and Saints of the present, I joyfully rejoice in them. Past and future Buddhas andO venerable saint, whatever merits there are, I wholeheartedly rejoice in and praise them all.

DEDICATION

Repentance and rejoicing in others' merits surpass all

Dedication increases boundless blessings and wisdom

May all beings throughout the Dharma realm

Soon attain Supreme Bodhi.

Afflictions eliminated, without obstacles

May I increase wisdom

No longer having karmic obstructions in all

Generations, cultivating Bodhisattva practices.

May it be that when I leave this physical body

I am born in the Pure Land in the West

Where lotus blooms, revealing the heart, seeing the Buddha

And unretreating bodhisattvas gather together.

May I dedicate this merit

Towards all directions

My disciples and all sentient beings

All perfectly attain Buddhahood.

tieu_de: Carp Dream Prophecy Thank You
tom_tat: I am an ordinary Buddhist like many other Buddhists, just beginning to step into the path of the Dharma, learning and trying to practice according to the Buddha's teachings, one of which is to cherish the lives of living beings. Therefore, even
noi_dung:
THANKSGIVING PROPHECY CARP

I am an ordinary Buddhist like many other Buddhists, just beginning my journey in the path, learning and trying to practice the Buddha's teachings. One of those teachings is to cherish the lives of all beings. Therefore, even though my financial situation is still not very stable, every Saturday, I try to set aside a little money to release fish and snails to nurture and grow compassion.

About 11-12 days ago, in the afternoon on my way home from work, I stopped by a fish stall. That day, the fish seller happily sold me more than 2 kilograms of perch for 60,000 VND. Looking at the next stall, I saw some carp and immediately bought a very large gourami for 150,000 VND. Afterwards, as usual when releasing the fish, I just briefly spoke a few words to them, something like: "If you are reborn as a human, try to cultivate yourself to help others!" After that, I chanted Buddha's name.

The matter also passed normally, and I did not remember it at all, until last night, while half-asleep, I saw an old man wearing a white outfit, with eyebrows so long they touched the ground, a beard reaching his belly, a smooth, shiny bald head, holding a slightly curved stick in his hand (I do not remember exactly what shape it was because I did not look closely at that time). Behind him were many people standing densely. The old man saw me and immediately thanked me for saving his descendants. I asked, "Who are you?" (because I also release fish and snails every week, so I did not know who he was), he said: "I am the grandfather of the carp you saved the other day, thanks to that..."Our descendants were saved, today I come to thank you!", I was both surprised and happy, increasingly believing in the miracle when releasing to save a living being. Today, I tell this story based on my own personal experience.

May anyone who reads this article develop the aspiration to release life, redeem the lives of living beings; more and more animals are being released to cultivate greater compassion in every person.

Namo Amitabha Buddha.

Thank you to everyone who has contributed merit by sharing my article.

➖ NOTE: Right after my post THANK YOU DREAM CARP was published at 9 a.m. on August 14, 2020, a miraculous thing happened to me. At 12:30 p.m. the same day, after more than 3.5 hours—which is the nap time at the company—I also fell asleep. In a half-conscious, half-dreaming state, I saw that old man in white clothes again (I guess he must be over 1000 years old and is the ancestor of the carp species). This time, he also thanked me for posting the article. Additionally, many people shared it with hundreds, even thousands of viewers, so his family lineage would be saved a very, very large amount. At that moment, I was startled.I woke up (hic, it's a pity I didn't get a chance to say anything before waking up), I still can't believe that I could dream continuously about one person for several hours. Until today, by chance I heard that many people volunteered to release crucian carp, I then realized that he had known in advance and was grateful for this.

On this occasion, I sincerely thank all of you for sharing the article, which contributes to increasing countless merits of perfection (pāramitā), as each share is an opportunity for hundreds of thousands of animals to be released.

I hope that you will always maintain such a compassionate and peaceful heart.

Namo Amitabha Buddha! 🙏🙏🙏

Quoted from the words of Sister Hân Hân

Collected by: Huệ Bình

tieu_de: SUPER ENLIGHTENED MOTHER FROM HELL TO HEAVEN.
tom_tat: Master Quảng Hóa was a disciple of Venerable Từ Hàng (a famous high monk in Taiwan, after passing away he left behind an "incorrupt body"). Before ordaining, Master Quảng Hóa had killed many beings. Like
noi_dung:
SUPER MOM FROM HELL TO HEAVEN.

Monk Guang Hua was a disciple of Venerable Tu Hang (a famous high monk in Taiwan, who left behind an "incorrupt body" after his passing).

Before ordaining, Monk Guang Hua had killed many animals. But after ordaining, by strictly observing precepts and practicing true methods, he opened his heavenly eye, attained many unimaginable benefits, and shared some of his real-life stories.

Below is one of the thrilling stories of Monk Guang Hua:

_____________

“My mother passed away on the Mainland. I immediately dedicated the merit of my monastic practice to her and then witnessed with my own eyes her rebirth in heaven. This is an absolutely true event (this happened at the Seven Treasures Pagoda of Ksitigarbha, at Daijue Temple in Qilong, Taiwan).

After the day my mother passed away, one night, I dreamed that my mother was imprisoned in jail. Then she stepped out of hell, holding onto me, and spoke in a sorrowful voice:

– My child, please quickly save me!

I asked:

– Why are you in here, mother?

My mother told me: How she was imprisoned by people, how miserable it was, and then she urged me to quickly rescue her. I said to my mother:

– Alright, please wait, I will surely save you.

I suddenly woke up, sat up… It was just dawn, and I immediately made a memorial tablet to pray for my mother's liberation.

The way I made the memorial tablet for my mother was as follows: First, I put my hands together, recited a volume of the Amitabha Sutra, and 21 repetitions of the Vãng Sanh Mantra.

After chanting, I wrote the memorial tablet. While writing each stroke, I recited a Buddha’s name for each one. After finishing, I continued to chant an additional 21 repetitions of the Rebirth Mantra, then dedicated the merit and sincerely invited the Bodhisattvas to bless my mother so that she would transcend, leave suffering, and attain bliss.

After that, because I had to go perform the ritual duties immediately, I took the memorial tablet my mother gave me and asked a novice monk to place it on the ancestral altar in the “Merit Hall” for safekeeping, though I wasn’t sure where exactly the novice would place my mother’s tablet.

That night, I dreamed that I was holding tightly and helping my mother escape from hell, then flying straight up into the sky to Taiwan.

I remember that from the sky over Jinmen, in just one step I jumped straight across the Taiwan Strait. When I arrived at Daijiao Temple, I immediately descended in front of the gate of the Nianfo Hall.

Then I led my mother upstairs, inviting her to sit in a corner on the right side of the ancestral altar in the “Gongde Hall,” and said:

– Mother, please sit here and wait for me! I will help you attain liberation!…

After saying this, I woke up.

The next day, because I was too busy with ordination ceremonies, I couldn't find time all day to go see how that young monk had enshrined my mother's spirit tablet.

By the afternoon, when everyone went to have a meal, I was too busy at noon to eat, so I took advantage of this time to go to the "Chanting Hall" and… Oh my!

My mother's spirit tablet was placed exactly in the spot where I had once invited her to sit in my dream.

Facing my mother's spirit tablet, an involuntary feeling of sadness arose; I couldn't hold back and tears streamed down my face.

So I immediately recited a copy of the Amitabha Sutra and 21 Mantras of Rebirth, dedicating merit to my mother, sincerely praying to the Buddha to deliver her.

After finishing the recitation, I went out, feeling bittersweet, not happy. I turned back to look at the Seven Treasures Pagoda. In previous visits, I would just pay my respects and leave, but this time I stepped into the courtyard of the Avalokiteshvara Hall and knelt in worship, with only one thought in my heart: "Praying to the Bodhisattva for compassionate deliverance for my mother."

I continued to go to the Halls of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, Bodhisattva Manjushri, and my Master Shakyamuni Buddha… In each hall, I kneelingly bowed in turn, praying for Buddha's power to bless my mother to quickly attain liberation…

Returning to the Avalokiteshvara Hall, by then it was dark, and I was about to leave, when I suddenly noticed a light in the corner of the opposite wall, and from there a cold, mournful ghostly wind blew out. I felt a shiver and thought: "Could that be the ghostly wind of a restless spirit?"

Because I wanted to know whether it was a vengeful ghost or not, I went closer to take a look, and when I arrived, I loudly asked:

– Hey! Are you some kind of vengeful spirit? If so, come to me, I can help you clear your grievance. (Because I used to work at the Ministry of Justice, and I still have many friends who are Judges and Prosecutors, I can file a petition to help clear your grievance)

After I finished speaking, that eerie feeling disappeared. I bowed my head and looked down, and saw that below was a basement. So I went down, having to take a spiral staircase to get there.

So it turns out this is a memorial altar for ashes, inside which there is a statue of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. As soon as I saw him, I immediately remembered that in the past the Bodhisattva had also helped my mother, so I immediately prayed to the Bodhisattva to deliver my mother.

I prayed:

– I ask for nothing else, because there is a saying: “A child who genuinely ordains and practices can help their nine generations of ancestors and seven generations of forebears ascend.” These are the words of the Buddha, and the Buddha never speaks falsely! Therefore, I earnestly plead to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, tonight please manifest and let me see; I want to witness with my own eyes my mother ascending to heaven. If she does not ascend, I will kneel here forever and never stand up!

After speaking, I knelt before Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, my left hand forming the Vajra mudra against my waist, my right hand performing the Flower Seal, and I chanted the mantra to summon my mother's soul. The Pǔ Zhào Thỉnh mantra is very effective; in the past, whenever I chanted it, I felt a response, so I believed that when I recited the mantra, my mother would come… Then I chanted the Dissolution of Karmic Obstacles Mantra of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. While reciting, I put my hands together and mentally visualized the words of the mantra in Sanskrit.

In this way, I chanted the Mantra of Extinguishing Fixed Karma to eliminate the sins for my mother, then I recited the "Mantra for Extinguishing Karma Obstructions" of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. I made hand mudras, visualizing the Sanskrit characters in my hands emitting light, white in color, wishing for my mother to eliminate karmic obstructions. After finishing the mantra, I addressed the Bodhisattva:

– Revered Bodhisattva! My task is completed, and next I sincerely hope that You will surely save my mother. Until the day my mother is liberated, I will kneel here for one day; if not liberated in two days, I will kneel here for two days; if not liberated in seven days, I will kneel for seven days without standing up… I hope to witness with my own eyes the scene of my mother ascending to heaven, not just seeing it in a dream.

After finishing, I knelt down again and recited: “Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva of Great Vows!”

I prayed earnestly, tears streaming down my face, not knowing how long I had been reciting, when suddenly on the ground, beneath the statue of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, a wisp of blue smoke rose, at first just like a large incense smoke.

– Wow! Smoke appears? Could it be that I have been responded to?

In my heart, thinking this, I intensified my recitation: "Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva!"

At this moment, the blue smoke gradually rose higher, going beyond the roof tiles, forming the shape of a dome and ascending layer by layer, layer by layer, …

When flying to the fourth level, the green smoke transformed into the shape of a lotus; reaching the fifth level, there was a person sitting on the lotus, somewhat resembling my mother at home.

At the sixth level, my mother transformed into a pure, beautiful celestial being. Ascending to the seventh level, she looked even more solemn, tenderly beautiful like the image of the Ancestor Goddess that people often worship. She wore a phoenix crown, dressed in heavenly attire, holding a jewel in her hand.

In the blink of an eye, the lotus tower soared high. I hurriedly turned to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and prayed:

– Bodhisattva! Please let me clearly see and recognize that the one sitting on the lotus throne is my mother!

As soon as I finished speaking, oh my! The person sitting in the lotus immediately turned their head, looked down, and called out:

– Nguyên!

I immediately replied:

– Yes! I hear you, mother!

My mother smiled, looking very joyful, then she transformed into a wisp of blue smoke, flew straight up, and disappeared into the high sky.

I turned back to look at the statue of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, feeling moved to tears, and said:

– Bodhisattva! Thank you for helping my mother to ascend to heaven.

Finally, after my efforts, right here I witnessed my mother ascending to heaven with my own eyes. Indeed, the indescribable joy in my heart at that moment was overwhelming.

Many people might think: Once you become a monk or nun, you can no longer support your parents… But you can use sincere prayers to show filial piety, strictly observe precepts, diligently practice, and dedicate these merits to your parents or ancestors… This act is truly the most valuable, and aligns with the saying:

"A disciple of the Buddha is greatly filial, because they can repay the kindness of parents from many lifetimes. This is the true way to repay the great kindness and virtue of one’s parents."

(Excerpt from 'Reaping Rewards in This Life 7' – Author: Master Quang Hoa – Translated by: Hanh Doan – Edited by: Quang Tu)

tieu_de: A little gain suffers a big loss
tom_tat: A girl about 27-28 years old, her hearing in the ears is sometimes working and sometimes not. She went to the hospital for a check-up, the doctor said she has no illness, but her hearing is still unclear, no one knows why. The master asked:
noi_dung:
GREED FOR SMALL GAINS LEADS TO BIG LOSSES

A girl about 27-28 years old, sometimes her ears work, sometimes they don't. She went to the hospital for a check-up, and the doctor said there was no illness, but her hearing was still unclear, and she didn't know why.

The master asked:

– What kind of work do you do that makes your ears ... full of small change like that?

She was momentarily stunned and confused, unable to respond.

I (Qua Khanh) explained it to her on behalf of the master:

– These small coins do not originally belong to you, but because you were a bit greedy, you took this money for your own use. Your ear therefore became ill, it is not because your ear is full of money! Please check if this really happened?

You immediately replied that you are a cashier at a gas station, and when counting daily settlements, there is often some small change, usually about one or two dimes, left by customers who did not need change. Every day, when commuting to and from work by bus, you found it convenient to take this small change to pay for your bus fare. You believe that this is not embezzlement.

I said:

– This is not corruption, but greed, right?

She seemed embarrassed, awkwardly nodding her head.

Master asked:

– From now on, will you still be greedy for these small sums of money?

She said decisively:

– Then that's good!

As soon as Master finished speaking, she showed a look of surprise and exclaimed:

– My ears can hear very clearly now!

The master smiled and said:

– I no longer see any small change in your ear now, but I still see "sliced ham, fruit, drinks"... what is this about?

She widened her eyes in astonishment and shouted:

– Oh my mother, how can You... see through everything like that?! Sometimes when handling payments, if customers give a few extra coins, we usually use them to buy sliced ham, fruit, drinks, etc., for lunch. Is this also considered a sin?

– You are the cashier, you cannot miscalculate. Money belonging to the public fund should not be used personally, you do not have the right to do so at will, do you?

She nodded repeatedly:

– You are right. From now on, I will not dare do that anymore.

– Once you say it, you have to keep your word!

She joyfully stood up and said:

– Master, my ears are completely clear now, did you "Release power" for me?

I answered on behalf of the master:

– This is the result of the power (you just repented) to swear to overcome material temptations, determined not to make mistakes again! She was very happy and moved on to another question: – For the past few years, my eyes often feel itchy and blurry. When I look closely, I don't see anything, but my eyelids are always red. Could this be retribution related to some wrongdoing? The master answered without thinking: – It's good that you can reflect on yourself like this! We see a lot of detergent on your eyelids!

She shouted:

– Oh! I know! We work at the gas station, so we have to use soap to clean stains, which is why we regularly use detergent to wash our hands every day while working. Since work at the station is not too busy, we girls often take the opportunity to wash our own clothes during free time, and afterwards we even bring clothes and household items to the station and use this soap to wash them too – saving both housework time and detergent and water.

– You girls are being greedy because you have misappropriated and encroached upon national property as well as work time, and that is a mistake, since you took what belonged to the public that you shouldn’t have taken, right?

She nodded:

– Until now, I never thought that doing that was committing a crime. Doesn’t that mean I’ve already become a bad person? – She said with tears in her eyes.

I couldn’t help but interrupt:

– Back when I did not understand the Buddha Dharma, I also behaved just like you. In the “Kṣitigarbha Sutra” it says: “Beings in this realm, whenever they have thoughts and intentions, there is nothing they do not create karma from, nothing they do not commit sin from.” Because those living in this realm of desire, whether much or little, all have tendencies of greed, anger, and ignorance. As for your illness, the cause comes from a greedy mind, a lack of understanding of the Dharma, and not seeing the truth clearly. Once you repent sincerely, the illness will vanish.

The master compassionately added:

– From now on, you must study many scriptures to increase your wisdom. In your work, you need to do many acts of service to atone for the wrong of taking the organization's resources.

When leaving, she felt that her eyes had improved a lot, so her heart was filled with faith and reverence for the Buddha's teachings.

Source: Báo Ứng Hiện Đời

tieu_de: CONSIDER THE DAY OF TAKING REFUGE AS A BIRTHDAY.
tom_tat: THE LIFE OF SPIRITUAL PRACTICE BEGINS FROM THAT. A year has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, winter. That is obvious, everyone knows. But do you know that human life is also divided into four stages: birth, aging, illness, death.
noi_dung:
CONSIDER THE DAY OF TAKING REFUGE AS YOUR BIRTHDAY.

THE LIFE OF PRACTICING SPIRITUALITY STARTS FROM THEN.

A year has four seasons: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter. That is obvious, everyone knows. But do you know that human life is also divided into four stages: Birth, aging, sickness, death. Being a human, everyone dies, so we must consider the future and strive to practice the Way. Spiritual practice also has four stages, namely: learning, practicing, accomplishing, and realization.

From the moment a person is born until the age of twenty is the period of learning the Way. During this time, one must study and learn Buddhist teachings well. It is similar to what is mentioned in the book "The Great Learning": "Establishing virtue in brightness." This means to make the wisdom and virtue shine brightly. This is the time to train one’s character to become increasingly pure. From the age of twenty-one to forty is the period of practicing the Way. This is the time to apply what has been learned; to use one’s previous studies and understanding to benefit sentient beings and support worldly affairs. As written in "The Great Learning": "Regulating the people," which means to renew the lives of the people.From the age of forty-one to sixty is called the period of attaining the Way. In the book of the Great Learning, it is written: "Chỉ ư chí thiện" which means to stop at the highest good. Confucius taught about "chí thiện" but not very thoroughly, because he had not reached the realm of True Emptiness and Nirvana, so it was not the ultimate goal. Therefore, in the final stage, we need to "liễu Ðạo" (realize the Way). After attaining the Way, one returns to the realm of Nirvana. Compared with the three principles of Confucianism: "Enlighten virtue, care for the people, stop at the highest good," Buddhist practice is much more comprehensive.

Some people say: "From childhood until I was twenty, I did not believe in Buddha. Now, to say that I am studying the Way, that period has already passed. How can I still study? Does it mean I don't need to study?" You must understand, when I talk about the four stages, it is only an ideal concept, not something fixed and immutable. Therefore, one can consider the day of taking refuge as a birthday, and from that day onward, time can be counted as the beginning of practicing the path.

Some people say: "I have taken refuge for four years, but why haven't I learned any Buddhist teachings at all?" In reality, although you have taken refuge for four or five years, in terms of Buddhism, you are nothing more than a four- or five-year-old child. Therefore, do not worry that you have not accomplished anything. Buddhist teachings are very profound. As long as, after taking refuge, you make twenty years of effort to study the Dharma and twenty years of effort to practice the Dharma, would you not eventually achieve success?

There was also an old man who sighed deeply and lamented: "Now I am eighty years old, and I fear that I no longer have a chance to gain twenty more years, and then another twenty years to practice skillfully." Indeed. "Time diminishes life," that is, the days go by, and life gradually decreases. There are not many days left, that is true! If one shortens time in calculation, spending two months practicing the Way, two months following the Way in this manner, then as long as one is sincere and determined, even in old age, one can be like a young person—vigorous and strong, step by step, step by step in practice, so why fear not achieving success one day. Make an effort!

(Venerable Thích Tuyên Hóa Lecture on June 15, 1958)

tieu_de: HOW TO IMPROVE YOURSELF IN 3 STEPS
tom_tat: Leviethoa: – Hello Quang Tu. I have been on Facebook and looked into your posts about Buddhism. I want to ask you more about the practice to improve oneself. To help the body and mind be peaceful.
noi_dung:
HOW TO PERFECT YOURSELF IN 3 STEPS

Leviethoa :

– Hello Quang Tu. I have been on Facebook and read your posts about Buddhism. I want to ask you more about the practice to perfect oneself. To help the body and mind be at peace.

Quang Tu:

– Dear friend, according to the sequence taught by the Buddha, practice and study need to follow 3 steps: HEAR → REFLECT → PRACTICE

1. VĂN – in Chinese, it translates to Listen. In ancient times, people mainly learned by listening to the teachings of the masters, so the Buddha used the word Listen. We can understand Văn as LEARNING. This step corresponds to the first part of the Noble Eightfold Path in the Four Noble Truths: RIGHT VIEW.

This learning can be understood as including reading Buddhist scriptures, reading essays, interpretative books, analyses by knowledgeable and virtuous teachers, and also listening to Dharma talks, viewing 'correct Dharma' writings on all media such as Facebook, YouTube, other websites, etc., so that one can understand the teachings of Buddhism, understand the laws governing the universe, and correctly comprehend the path of practice taught by the Buddha.

What it means to understand correctly, what it means to understand incorrectly, we will not discuss here; this issue is very difficult and complicated. Quang Tu has already given a separate talk on this issue, entitled "Understanding Buddhist Teachings: Reject or Trust?"

* Link as follows:

https://nhanqua.com.vn/tim-hieu-phat-phap-bac-bo-hay-ca-tin/

2. TƯ – means Thinking. This step corresponds to the second part of the Noble Eightfold Path: RIGHT THINKING.

After having studied the catechism, we need to spend a lot of time and mental effort to think about and ponder that catechism, because Truth is not something that can be fully understood just by listening; it is necessary to compare and contrast these teachings and see how they are applied in practice.

Each case, each period will have countless variations, impossible to understand mechanically. Then there are many different areas of knowledge, different methods, different paths of practice such as the Shravakayana, the Pratyekabuddhayana, and the Bodhisattvayana... how can one systematize them to understand flexibly without misunderstanding? This is very difficult and also depends on one's intellectual capacity and personal circumstances.

In short, "Tư" means that one must spend a lot of time and effort to carefully think about the things that have been learned, so that those teachings truly penetrate the mind and transform into a system of thought that guides every personal decision in life.

Even when studying the Path without thinking, true wisdom does not actually arise, or one may forget, or only have a vague understanding, and worse, by merely hearing what others say and blindly following without reconsideration, one might luckily encounter the right teaching and follow it correctly, or unfortunately encounter false teachings and follow wrongly (the problem is that the person doing wrong will not realize they are wrong, still believing they are right, which is common). This will certainly lead to misunderstanding and cannot achieve Right Thinking.

3. TU means Practice, which is to start acting according to what has been understood from Learning and previous Thinking about the moral principles. This step corresponds to the last six parts of the Noble Eightfold Path: RIGHT SPEECH – RIGHT ACTION – RIGHT LIVELIHOOD – RIGHT EFFORT – RIGHT MINDFULNESS – RIGHT CONCENTRATION.

And this is exactly the difficult stage of spiritual practice; merit or karmic obstacles are determined here, and whether one makes progress or remains stagnant also depends on this step.

The first two parts, Literature and Thought, are only theory – and understanding the theory correctly. Whether or not one cultivates depends on whether we practice according to the principles or just talk about them and understand them on paper.

When we start practicing, we realize how difficult it is to apply the principles; it is by no means easy to do exactly as the Buddha taught even slightly.

Some people want to learn the Path, so they go to a monk who is renowned for wisdom and virtue, and ask the monk:

– What is the essence of practice?

The monk calmly replied:

– Do not commit evil deeds. Diligently do good deeds.

The other person, hearing this, scoffed and said:

– Saying that like a great master, even a three-year-old child can say it.

The monk replied calmly:

– True. A three-year-old child can indeed say that. Yet, even some ninety-year-old elders may not necessarily be able to follow it.

The Dharma of Buddha is supremely profound and infinite. If it were easy to learn and practice, everyone would have already become a Saint. However, in reality, that is not the case.

When entering the stage of Practice, one must sweat and shed tears to be able to follow the principles correctly, and it is by no means easy or leisurely.

Buddha teaches generosity, we must spend money, feeling pain in our hearts. Buddha teaches patience, we must grit our teeth, even clench our jaws and bear listening to others' insults without reacting. Buddha teaches us to eliminate our own ego, we must turn inward to dig out our mistakes, repent, give them up, and change. In reality, facing the dark side of ourselves is not pleasant at all.

Buddha teaches diligence in learning the True Dharma, we must stretch our eyes to read scriptures that are very difficult to understand and can easily make us sleepy, yet we still must persist in reading them month after month, year after year.

Buddha teaches that one must diligently practice, not chasing after the pleasures of life. We must give up parties, travels, shopping, playing games, watching movies, etc., and use that time to study the Dharma and apply it: observe precepts, refrain from this, refrain from that, recite scriptures, chant mantras, recite the Buddha's name, meditate... Each of these practices is difficult and strenuous, easy to become discouraged, and not at all as attractive or enticing as worldly amusements.

Only through practice do we realize that "Seeing a bowl of traditional Chinese medicine and drinking it are two completely different things." If you only look at it without drinking, you surely cannot cure the illness, and no change will occur at all.

It is only when we experience the extremely bitter taste, inhale the very unpleasant smell, grit our teeth and drink it all without spitting, and persist from one bowl of medicine to another, that we truly see our illness and health being changed.

Practicing according to the Buddha's teachings is similar; it is extremely difficult and arduous, and moreover, it takes a very long time and involves many levels. Only those who overcome all obstacles without giving up can receive the deserved reward, which is a virtuous character, supreme wisdom, the fruit of liberation, and ultimate eternal bliss that never fades.

The three steps of Listening – Reflection – Practice are not linear, from Learning to Thinking to Practicing as an end. No, this is a continuous loop that connects and supports each other across many levels.

When first studying Buddhism, we will engage in Study - Reflect - Practice (Study – Contemplate – Practice) in the basic teachings, which can be roughly understood as the beginner level.

After completing the basic level of practice, we will realize that there are still many issues we do not know how to understand or what is the correct way to act, because the teachings previously learned were not mentioned, or were mentioned but we did not comprehend at the time.

So we continue to study in order to learn the deeper and more advanced parts of the teachings, then we Contemplate and Practice at a higher level than before.

In school, the Ministry of Education divides classes from Kindergarten, to Bud and Leaf, Grade 1, 2, … 12, Vocational, College – University, Graduate, Doctorate – Professor… generally around 20 levels. But in Buddhism, there are billions of levels from low to high, the basic part for ordinary people is different, the advanced part for monks and nuns is different, the high-level part for saints such as Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas is different, the difference between the levels of doctrine can be said to be vast.

As mentioned above, Quang Tu has briefly outlined the process of practicing study according to Buddhist teachings, but it is only a rough and general overview; for each aspect, when explored deeply, it opens up an immense treasure trove of explanations that are endless.

This shows that Buddhist teachings are not as simple as most people mistakenly think—just being good and occasionally going to the temple is not enough. That is only a little initial good fortune; it is merely seeing the starting line of a long journey spanning countless lifetimes.

Wishing you to Learn broadly – Understand deeply – Practice thoroughly the golden teachings of the Tathagata, and soon attain the wholesome fruits on the path of studying Buddhist Dharma.

_________________

tieu_de: Evil and Vicious Demon King
tom_tat: The Multiple Evil Demon Kings Rise, the Demon King Falls Ill
noi_dung:
Evil Demon King

Multiple Evil Demon Kings

Sickly Demon King

Scattering Demon King

Destructive Demon King

Exhausting Demon King, etc., as mentioned in the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra

They are Demon Kings who bring misfortune, disasters, debts, and death

If humans commit evil acts such as

Being unfilial

Slandering the Three Jewels

Killing too heavily

Adultery too severely

Deceiving and harming people, etc.

Wherever they go, they will be watched by the Demon Kings and reported to their followers that

Today there is a person who lives without believing in cause and effect, is wicked, beats his father and mother, curses the Buddha and the Dharma, commits adultery without shame, his karma is too heavy, truly deserving of death, you should push him to break his arms and legs or to die,

Or

Make him lose wealth, accumulate debts, run out of food to the point of death,

Or

Make him suffer from serious, incurable diseases, etc.

But for people who live virtuously, know how to love, share, help, and sincerely practice according to Buddhist teachings,

Wherever they go, they will be respected by both benevolent and malevolent spirits,

They will inform their relatives about these things

Today, if a Bodhisattva passes by you, you must protect them so that all misfortunes come to that person.

From evil demons who specialize in spreading accidents, illness, and suffering to everyone.

But if one abandons evil and does good, focusing sincerely on studying Buddhism, they will become one's followers.

(Excerpted from many lectures by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua)

tieu_de: THE INCOMPARABLE MERIT OF PAINTING IMAGES OF BUDDHAS AND BODHISATTVAS
tom_tat: July Vu Lan – the season of filial piety has arrived! During this sacred month, Buddhist children often make a vow to eat vegetarian, chant the Buddha's name, recite sutras, release animals, and do charitable deeds to dedicate merit to their grandparents and parents.
noi_dung:
THE INEXPRESSIBLE MERIT OF PAINTING THE IMAGES OF BUDDHAS AND BODHISATTVAS

July marks Vu Lan – the season of filial piety! Buddhist devotees during this sacred month often vow to eat vegetarian, chant Buddha's name, recite sutras, release animals, and perform acts of merit to dedicate to their grandparents, parents, and ancestors, which has long become a very cherished traditional beauty of the Vietnamese people. Particularly in this Vu Lan month, there is also the memorial day of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha (30th day of the 7th lunar month) – the great Bodhisattva with a tireless vow to save sentient beings and exemplary filial piety in Buddhism.

This Vu Lan Festival, besides chanting the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and reciting His name, have you ever thought about painting an image of Kṣitigarbha to dedicate your merit? Chanting and copying the Kṣitigarbha Sutra has become very popular and familiar to many people, but coloring His image is something that hardly anyone pays attention to. Are you worried that you don't know how to draw and therefore cannot do it? Don't worry! Even if you don't know how to draw, we can still color His paintings, and the merit and blessings are beyond imagination. The following will specifically guide you through the steps of coloring the paintings, so you can personally offer these beautifully colored paintings in homage and gratitude to Kṣitigarbha.Dedicate and transfer merit to our relatives. But first, let's understand how vast and great the merit of creating images of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas is!

I. MERITS OF PAINTING IMAGES OF BUDDHAS AND BODHISATTVAS

1. In the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, the Buddha teaches about the powerful merits of painting images of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and the great rewards for both the living and the deceased, saying:

“O Phổ Quảng! If there is any virtuous man or virtuous woman who draws an image of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and then once contemplates it, once pays homage, that person will be born into the realm of the Devas of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven a hundred times, no longer needing to fall into the evil paths. (...) Moreover, if any virtuous man or virtuous woman transcribes this sutra themselves or instructs someone to transcribe it, or personally sculpts or paints an image of the Bodhisattva or instructs others to sculpt or paint it, that person will surely receive great benefit when experiencing the results.”

“When someone is near death, their parents and close relatives use the person's property, treasures, clothing, etc., to fund the adornment or painting of a statue of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. They then let the sick person, while still alive, see and hear that their family members are using their property and treasures to paint or decorate the image of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. If the sick person has karmic retribution that would otherwise result in severe illness, this merit can help them recover and prolong their life. If, however, the sick person’s karmic lifespan is already finished and they have accumulated all kinds of heinous karmic offenses that would have sent them to the evil realms, yetBecause of this merit, after death one is immediately born into the heavenly realm or the human realm to enjoy the supreme and wonderful pleasures, and all sins and obstacles are completely eradicated.

"It is like being able to paint the image of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and sincerely listen to His name. Then, by merely witnessing and paying respects once a day or continuously for seven days, without losing the initial resolve, hearing His name and seeing the image to pay homage and make offerings, the deceased relatives of that person who were due to suffer in the lower realms because of their bad karma, inevitably enduring countless lifetimes of suffering, can now, thanks to the merit created from painting the image of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and the homage and offerings made by their children or siblings, immediately attain liberation, be reborn in the heavenly or human realms, and enjoy supreme and wondrous happiness. As for the deceased relatives of that person who were fortunate..."Once virtuous, having been born into the heavenly or human realms to enjoy the supreme and wondrous fruits of joy, one, thanks to this merit, further increases the karmic potential to reach the level of the Saints and enjoy immeasurable fruits of happiness.

2. In the Lotus Sutra, chapter two contains a verse teaching the merit of painting images of the Buddha, whether intentionally or unintentionally, as follows: Painting the Buddha resplendent / With a hundred marks, adorned with blessings / Doing it oneself or asking others / One has already attained the Buddha Way / Even children at play / Using plants or brushes / Or using their own nails / To draw the Buddha image / Such individuals / Gradually accumulate merit / Fully possess the heart of great compassion / Have already attained the Buddha Way / Teach Bodhisattvas / And save countless beings.

3. The divine power of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva makes disease-causing spirits dare not enter the house: this is the story of Imperial Censor Kang Cutong of the Tang Dynasty. Because he worshiped and sincerely drew images of the Bodhisattva, the underworld soldiers did not dare to accuse him. When an epidemic occurred, the disease-causing spirits only passed by and did not dare to enter the house, and the whole family escaped disaster. After passing away, they were reborn in the Pure Land.

4. Turning an early death into a long life: the story of a novice monk whose life was about to end. One night, while sleeping at a certain temple, he saw a painting of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva hanging in the temple, and he used his fingernails to practice drawing the image of the Bodhisattva on the wall. The next morning, he heard a voice whispering in his ear, "fifty, fifty." After that, he was granted an additional 50 years of life, all thanks to a single time of practicing to draw the image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. The merits and blessings of the Bodhisattva are truly beyond comprehension!

5. Master Hsuan Hua lectured on the 11 merits of creating a Buddha image:

First, for many lifetimes, having bright eyes to see clearly.

Second, not being born into evil places. Friends and neighbors are all good people, not encountering evil people or wild beasts.

Third, always being born in wealthy and noble families, being respected.

Fourth, attaining a golden body.

Fifth, living a rich and noble life.

Sixth, being born into virtuous and kind families.

Seventh, having the possibility of being born as a king.

Eight is being able to become a Wheel-Turning King. When one is a Wheel-Turning King, if one cultivates, one can become a Buddha.

Nine is being able to be born in the heaven of Brahma and live for one lifetime.

Ten is not to fall into the evil paths of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals.

Eleven is that in all future lives and lifetimes, one will always respect the Three Jewels, take refuge in the Three Jewels, and not be lost.

Hearing about the eleven merits of creating Buddha statues, if we have the ability, we should create even more Buddha statues. Creating a Buddha statue makes your appearance very perfect. Why is the Buddha’s appearance so perfect? Because over the course of three great Asamkhyeya kalpas, He created countless Buddha statues.

II. INSTRUCTIONS FOR PAINTING THE IMAGE OF BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA

1. The Kṣitigarbha Sutra teaches that if sentient beings cultivate good roots in the Buddha's teachings, even as small as a hair or a thread, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will save them for countless lifetimes until they become Buddhas. Moreover, the Bodhisattva of great compassion loves sentient beings dearly, so there is no need to fear being scolded if the painting is not done beautifully. Do you remember the story of the young temple boy who practiced drawing the image of Kṣitigarbha on the wall with his fingernails, and just by doing that, he gained up to 50 years of lifespan? How could the young boy's drawing be beautiful, yet the karmic reward was so great. The Kṣitigarbha Sutra says that good men and women paint, but in the Lotus Sutra, the venerableThe World-Honored One does not limit the benefits only to good men and women who paint, but any sentient being, even children playing with their nails, grass, or trees... creating images of the Buddha or Bodhisattvas, will 'have already attained the Buddha path.' The skillful means and the compassion of the Buddhas in saving sentient beings are inconceivable and beyond discussion!

2. Points to note when painting images of Buddha and Bodhisattvas:

- You need to buy a new set of coloring tools (colored pencils, crayons, watercolors, etc.) and use them exclusively for painting images of Buddha and Bodhisattvas. Absolutely do not use coloring tools that have previously been used to paint flowers, plants, etc., on Buddha images. The money used to buy the coloring tools must be pure, obtained legally through your own work; you must not use illicit money, embezzled funds, or stolen money to buy brushes or paper for painting Buddha images.

- Before beginning to paint, one needs to bathe and wash clean, wear proper clothing, kneel properly before the image of the Buddha or Bodhisattva, and make the vow: "My name is ... I make the aspiration to paint Your image in order to dedicate the merit of this act to my living and deceased ancestors in countless past lives, as well as to dedicate it for all sentient beings throughout the space of the Dharma realm, especially those suffering in hell, hungry ghosts, animals, Asuras, and beings in the intermediate state. I pray that they may soon be freed from suffering and be reborn in the Pure Land. I ask the Triple Gem to bless me and all sentient beings to eliminate karmic obstacles, open wisdom, cultivate the Bodhi mind, and perpetually for countless lifetimes always ..."Receive refuge in the Three Jewels, listen to the wondrous true Dharma, diligently practice, quickly transcend birth and death, and ultimately perfect the path of Buddhahood.”

Throughout the process of painting the images of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas, one must pay attention to maintaining purity in body, speech, and mind, abstaining from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, avoiding alcohol, and refraining from eating onions and garlic. Husbands and wives should not engage in sexual relations on the days they are painting the Buddha. The more one observes virtuous precepts, the greater the merit and blessings. Partial reverence brings partial benefit; full reverence brings full benefit.

- After painting and dedicating the merit, the artwork should be framed and displayed on the Buddha altar. Daily veneration and respectful worship are in accordance with the teachings prescribed in the scriptures.

In this article, there are many pictures of the Bodhisattva Land Organ for you to choose from, each with a template and a pencil drawing to fill. You can download the pencil drawing and print it on A4 size paper (it is best to print it on drawing paper, if you don't have it, you can print it on paper at a photo shop), then use crayons to fill in the pattern. If you haven't imagined what the finished picture will look like, below there are four pictures of the Land Organ numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4 painted and completed by a female friend, you can see and refer to it! That female friend has done it perfectly, why can't we?

Wishing you a meaningful and peaceful Vu Lan season in the radiance of the Buddhas.

Namo Amitabha Buddha.

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

tieu_de: The Salty Cliff of Despair, Rebirth in the Western Paradise
tom_tat: Layman Chau So Phong, with the courtesy name Dinh Chuong, from the Ming dynasty, was a native of Yunnan province. He was gentle and kind, fond of chanting Buddha's name, and managed his household without counting gains or losses; whatever he had, he would immediately share with the poor. Whenever someone praised him, he would just smile;
noi_dung:
Fasting from Meat, Rebirth in the Western Paradise

Layman Chau So Phong, with the courtesy name Dinh Chuong, lived during the Ming dynasty and was from Yunnan province. He had a gentle and kind nature, liked to recite Buddha's name, managed his household without keeping track of earnings or expenses; whatever he had, he would immediately share with the poor.

When praised, he would only smile; when scolded, insulted, or humiliated, he would also just smile! Every early morning, he chanted the Diamond Sutra, the Amitabha Sutra, and recited the Buddha's name with great joy and delight! He often said:

– I do not abandon my daily work, but I am not attached to desires; I just live like that!

At eighty-nine years old, during the Qingming Festival, he went to visit graves to bid farewell to his ancestors and parents. Returning home, he said to his wife:

– I am about to leave; Amitabha Buddha will welcome me, Guanyin and Dizang Bodhisattva will both come!

He also said:

– Guanyin told me to completely abstain from meat for five days to be able to be reborn in the Western Paradise!

Every day, he ate one meal of porridge and one meal of vegetables. When the time came, he bathed, washed his hair, put on his cap, and had his children and grandchildren chant Buddha's name. After reciting the sutras himself, he sat upright and passed away. His body gave off a fragrant scent, and his face looked just like when he was alive.

Commentary:

Whoever smiles when praised has the purity of joyful conduct. Whoever smiles when scolded has entirely eradicated the poison of anger. Whoever shares all their wealth has exhausted the poison of greed.

When the Buddha and Bodhisattvas come to receive one, they also advise avoiding pungent foods for five days before rebirth, which sufficiently proves that even if one cannot yet lay down the knife, and the mouth still desires delicious flavors, one can still attain rebirth.

Please regard vegetarianism and abstaining from killing as immediate and urgent duties.

Excerpted from the Vajra Precious Spiritual Records

Source: Diệu Thiện

Edited by: Quang Từ

tieu_de: Bodhisattva Reappearing
tom_tat: Venerable Thien Su Dieu Phap recounted that, during the time he went to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to pay respects to Master Xuan Hua, he happened to encounter a lay dharma protector in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas who had a car accident and died. This layperson had not seen his wife and children for several years.
noi_dung:
BODHISATTVA REBIRTH

Venerable Dieu Phap recounted that during the time he went to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to pay respects to Master Xuan Hua, he happened to encounter a lay practitioner protecting the Dharma at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas who had a car accident and died.

This lay practitioner had not met his wife and children for several years and was finally reunited with them at that time. He was driving to pick up his wife and children from the airport, and just as they were about to reach the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, the accident occurred. His wife and children were slightly injured, but he alone passed away.

Someone asked Venerable Dieu Phap:

– This layperson left his family in Taiwan and came alone to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to work as a Dharma protector as well as a teacher for the students there. His heart was very kind, but why did he encounter such a violent death?

Venerable Master Dharma Wonderful answered:

– This person is a Bodhisattva of equal enlightenment reborn, coming here to help Master Xuan Hua! Protecting the Dharma has always been his original vow! His sudden death was due to repaying a grudge from a past life, and at the same time, it serves as a warning to the world about the impermanence of life, urging people to diligently practice cultivation! In a past life, he had harmed a pair of large birds, so when he was returning from the airport, at the moment he had to repay, the two (grudge) birds spread their wings in front of his car windshield, blocking his view, causing him to not see the road, hit a pole, and die!

The abbot asked his wife and children:

– Did your husband urge you both to quickly go to the U.S.?

His wife replied:

– Yes, a few days ago, he kept reminding me on the phone, saying that even if he was no longer present with us, we should still strive to practice well. At that time, I felt annoyed because he kept saying it, but now, looking back, I understand that he had already prepared us in advance…

The monk explained:

– This is because he wanted you both to come to the U.S. to see him one last time, to send him off.

The words of the Venerable made his wife and children feel very comforted, and also encouraged them to increase their faith and practice. They then respectfully bowed to him.

Those present at the scene who believed what the Venerable said also respectfully bowed.

But there were also many who were skeptical and voiced their objections, which reached the ears of the Venerable:

– That layman, what's so special about him? He hasn't made any significant contributions to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, so how can he be called a “sammasambuddha bodhisattva reborn”? If he were a sammasambuddha bodhisattva, then I would be… a Buddha reborn!

In the "Fourfold Pure Repentance" in the "Surangama Sutra," the Buddha explains very clearly: Even "women of loose conduct, widows, thieves, butchers"... can be "reappearing Bodhisattvas or Arhats in manifestation," let alone laypeople and monks?... These reappearing beings, even at the moment of enlightenment, never beat their chests claiming or boasting "I am truly a Bodhisattva or Arhat"... except at the time of death, they may leave subtle final words, or after their passing, a wise person may reveal their identity... As for themselves, they come silently and leave silently. This is all for the sake of guiding people, manifesting the truth of 'impermanence of life,' and all actions are done in accordance with how the Buddha appointed.This matter… wait until you are enlightened, then it will naturally become clear.

As ordinary people, when we are still confused and unclear, we should not recklessly criticize others, to avoid creating bad verbal karma and committing endless mistakes. Master Tỉnh Am passed away at the age of 49, and we should not use our ordinary perspective to comment: "He didn't practice well, so he had a short life!" – Because all the realms before us are tests for practitioners, "if one is truly a genuine practitioner, worldly faults are not seen!"

"Not seeing the faults of the world" does not mean seeing someone do something evil and not criticizing, advising, or correcting them… but rather it means to respond using the perspective of Buddhism.

tieu_de: WHAT WILL WE DO IN THE VU LAN FESTIVAL MONTH

WHAT WE WILL DO DURING VU LAN MONTH

Bow 100 times every day (from now until the end of the month, you will complete 2,600 bows).

👉If all of us wholeheartedly work together to do this, the realm of the dead will rejoice, countless beings will be freed from suffering and have the causes for Bodhi. Therefore, let us all do it together, everyone!
