tieu_de: THE TIMES OF TRIỀU SƠN WITH MR. HƯ VÂN
tom_tat: Translator's note: Venerable Hư Vân was a holy monk of noble speech and conduct. His life had many mystical occurrences; when he visited Kê Túc Mountain, the bells and wooden clappers rang by themselves, and when he went to Cao Đảnh Pagoda, the orchids spread their fragrance.
noi_dung:
THE TIMES OF ASCENDING THE MOUNTAIN WITH MASTER HƯ VÂN

Translator's note:

Master Hu Van was a saintly monk of eminent virtue. His life was filled with many mystical occurrences: when he visited Ke Tuc Mountain, bells rang on their own; when he went to Cao Danh Pagoda, orchids emitted a fragrant aroma; during his sermons, dead trees came back to life, plum trees blossomed, vegetables in the garden flowered, and even all the candles lit in the hall bloomed in the shape of lotus flowers. He could pray for rain and receive rain, pray for snow and receive snow; whatever plans he made were assisted by hidden spiritual powers: moving rocks, filling rivers… When he was forced to cut down ancient trees, the falling trees would inexplicably fall in a direction that would not harm the pagoda. When the Japanese targeted his pagoda with bombs, the bombs fell in vacant spots, causing no fatalities butA Japanese plane crashed and was shattered. The Japanese were so scared that afterward, whenever they had to fly, they would take a detour rather than fly over the Temple. Any animal that received refuge from the Master immediately became vegetarian; their aggressive and combative nature suddenly turned gentle. Cows also came to him for help, tigers knew to come to him for precepts… Heavenly immortals and Dragon kings all transformed into human forms to come and request precepts…

In the beginning, at the age of 43, he resolved to make a pilgrimage to Mount Ngũ Đài, performing three steps and one prostration each time, paying homage to Bodhisattva Manjushri from the south to the north to seek blessings for his mother. It took nearly three years to reach the destination. Notably, along the way he became seriously ill and almost died, causing Bodhisattva Manjushri to "can’t bear it any longer" and descend to the human world in the form of a beggar to save him, carrying supplies, cooking, and assisting him…

Below is a fascinating anecdote about his mountain pilgrimage (at this time he was probably nearly one hundred years old, according to his disciples), which I was fortunate to read, and I would like to share this good fortune with the readers:

TIMES OF ASCENDING THE MOUNTAIN WITH MASTER HU VAN

The other day, at Nhan Si Mountain in Xuyen Bac, we encountered a group of monkeys. Whether they were benevolent or curious, we couldn’t tell, but several climbed trees to pick fruit and threw it down while shouting noisily in our direction. When we moved closer to pick up the fruit, we saw a very large monkey, like the leader of the monkeys, calling out while motioning with its hand towards us. Master Hu Van explained:

Look, it wants us to open the bag to catch them. We hurriedly opened the bag, and the monkeys in the trees immediately picked the fruits and threw them down, carefully selecting only the good ones. When we ate the fruits, they looked down from the trees and called out loudly, showing great delight. The monk Hu Van said: How adorable!

But this was not even the strange part, because afterwards we encountered even more marvelous things throughout the journey with Master Hu Van.

Bridge over the abyss

One day, we were hiking on Vinh Phong Mountain when we got lost and reached a dead end. Ahead was a cliff more than ten meters wide, looking down into a bottomless drop, seemingly impossible to cross to the opposite side. At that moment, as it was getting dark and we had no way to manage the situation, we had no choice but to sit down in meditation, starting our practice schedule, preparing to spend the night there.

Right then, a violent storm arose, and when the wind subsided, we suddenly saw on the other side of the mountain a huge snake patch appeared, nearly half a meter wide, with its mouth open like a basin. The Master said to me:

– Saint An, we can cross the abyss now!

At this moment, I saw the giant python, its mouth wide open, tongue flicking, eyes blinking, head directed towards us nodding, I was terrified, thinking about the scene of it eating me, I turned back and said to Master:

– Are you joking with me, sir? Are you sure it won't eat us?

The monk Hu Van smiled and said:

– Don’t be afraid, it is Bodhisattva who sent it to help us!

My master saw that I was still afraid, so he told me to close my eyes and held my hand to guide me. I peeked and saw the giant python stretching its head over the abyss and crouching like a bridge. Master Hư Vân stepped across first, and I followed right behind, feeling as if I were walking on a large, springy bridge. Finally, we reached the opposite side, and only then did I realize that this python was unbelievably long, as I could not see where its tail was.

After crossing the shore, Master Hư Vân immediately sat down and chanted sutras. A gust of wind arose, and when we opened our eyes, we could no longer see the giant serpent.

Continuing to travel about a thousand miles (one kilometer), we arrived at a village called Tây Tiêu Village, which had eighty households, and we stayed there for three days.

The warmth in the forest

Once again, when we entered the primeval forest, this mountain was called Hổ Khâu Mountain…

Suddenly, the weather changed, dust-laden winds swirled, and it grew darker by the moment. There were no villages ahead, and no shops behind. Only the sound of the rushing wind could be heard. After a while, heavy rain poured down, hailstones fell everywhere, and only after some time did it stop.

The heavy rain had passed, everywhere was damp, the roads were slippery, and the sky was getting darker and darker, so we had no choice but to take shelter here. I went to fetch water and gather some firewood to start a fire to boil water. Since we were all dressed simply and had been caught in a heavy downpour, our whole bodies were wet and cold. As I boiled water and tended the fire, I suddenly heard the loud roar of a tiger. I only heard the sound, without seeing the tiger. But one roar was answered by several other roars, seeming to indicate that it wasn’t just a single tiger!

The master saw my face change color and immediately said:

– Being cowardly again! If our lives aren't over yet, we will live; only when life ends will we become food for tigers. Come closer and lean on me, so you will no longer be afraid!

Since we were too full at noon to eat, now we have no choice but to drink hot water to settle our stomachs and sit leaning against each other.

I was still very young at that time, and because the journey was so tiring, I quickly fell into a deep sleep. Around midnight, I felt increasingly warm, and when I opened my eyes… Oh my God! There were six big tigers surrounding us. To top it off, Master Hư Vân even reached out to stroke the head of the biggest female tiger.

At that moment, my mind was truly confused, because I didn't know whether I was dreaming or awake. Could it be that I was seeing the scene of “Tiger Lying Before the Arhat”? Three times I tried to stand up, but Master stopped me each time, telling me to quickly recite the sutra and focus my mind. After a while, I drifted off again.

When morning came, as I woke up, Master smiled and said:

– Were you very scared last night? It was the Mountain Spirit visiting.

Receiving and seeing off

On Mount Wutai, there is a saying: A bodhisattva, towards those with affinity… “Welcomes from eight hundred miles away, sends off to a thousand miles.” Naturally, within approximately eight hundred miles around Mount Wutai, there are no bandits.

That day we were resting, sitting and chatting, and Venerable Master Huy Van explained to me the events that had occurred. He said: At that time, we were not encountering a python, but actually a dragon. And up on the mountain, the creature we met was not a tiger, but a royal leopard. See, when we get near Mount Wutai, there will be someone to receive us.

That day the sky was full of fog, Master was a bit dizzy, we rested for a while and then went back up the mountain.

Going halfway up the mountain, we suddenly saw a bright light ahead, like an electric glow. Venerable Hu Van immediately told us to quickly kneel down and pay our respects. At that moment, we saw on the mountainside the Bodhisattva Manjusri, holding a fly whisk and waving it, as if trying to say something. This scene lasted for five minutes; indeed, the Bodhisattva Manjusri truly appeared to welcome us. This made us very happy, and our whole bodies felt strengthened. After walking several kilometers all day, we had skipped lunch but did not feel hungry at that moment. By evening, we finally arrived at Ha Phong Pagoda and stayed there for two days.

Then our monkey departed, leaving Wutai about thirty miles behind, and saw the mountainside suddenly glowing with Buddha's light. An old lady came down from above, and from afar she called out to us:

– Are you tired?

It was autumn at that time, and the old lady took a few large almonds from her basket to give to the four of us.

She said: Eating the first fruit would remove hunger, eating the second fruit would remove thirst, eating the third fruit would relieve fatigue, and eating the fourth fruit would make the whole body feel light and the mind relaxed. After receiving the fruits of happiness, when I looked back, I could no longer see the old lady.

It was then that we realized: This must have been Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara helping us. Because it was autumn at that time, how could there be ginkgo fruits? But clearly, we had ginkgo fruits in our hands. After eating these ginkgo fruits, indeed, for several days we felt no thirst, no hunger, and our spirits were extremely good.

These are the rare and unforgettable memories from the times we accompanied Venerable Hư Vân on pilgrimages to the mountains.

Thánh An

Excerpt from Báo Ứng Hiện Đời - Translated by Hạnh Đoan

Edited by: Quang Từ

tieu_de: ABSOLUTELY DO NOT PRAISE YOURSELF - CRITICIZE OTHERS
tom_tat: Even if we practice cultivation very properly, even if our effort has been effective and we have attained the true benefits of the Buddha Dharma, we must not praise ourselves while criticizing others. This is the foundation.
noi_dung:
ABSOLUTELY DO NOT PRAISE YOURSELF - CRITICIZE OTHERS

Even if we practice very properly, even if our cultivation has been effective and we have attained the true benefits of the Buddha's Dharma, we must not praise ourselves and criticize others.

This is a common ailment of everyone, often praising and commending one's own Dharma school, and even saying that one's own practice is very good while others are not as good, which should not be done.

This is also delusion, discrimination, and attachment!

If you say that your practice is very good, how does it compare to an Arhat? How about compared to a Bodhisattva? Far inferior! A little bit of this, what does it matter?

Absolutely do not praise yourself, absolutely do not slander others. This happened in past times, and nowadays it is especially even more frequent, too much, not knowing that this karma is very heavy!

We practice Pure Land Buddhism, reciting Buddha’s name to be reborn in the Western Pure Land. When encountering someone practicing Zen or studying Tantra, it is like encountering an enemy. How can this be!?

Meditation was taught by the Buddha, Tantra was also taught by the Buddha; if you slander these Dharma methods, isn't that slandering the Buddha?

Are you then slandering the Dharma that the Buddha taught?

Many people who follow meditation and Tantra have successfully cultivated; although nowadays there are fewer, there used to be many. In that case, doesn't that mean you have slandered the Sangha?

Therefore, whether we are aware of it or not, we have committed these mistakes, praising ourselves while speaking ill of others, slandering the Three Jewels; this will lead to being condemned to the Avici Hell. From now on, do not do this foolish thing anymore.

What kind of attitude should we have instead?

When we see others practicing meditation or reciting mantras, we must treat them with respect, with joyful reverence, praising them without slandering.

In 1977, when I was in Hong Kong giving a lecture on the Lankavatara Sutra, Master Thanh Nhat came to visit again and attended three more days of the lecture. He was very delighted and even encouraged his followers to come to listen to my lectures.

The Master practiced Zen Buddhism, and one day he invited me to visit his monastery, which I gladly accepted. The Master was the abbot at Bao Lien Temple, located behind Dai Di Mountain. The road up the mountain was very narrow, cars could not go up, and it took about thirty or forty minutes on foot to reach a small temple.

The monk told me that the purpose of not widening the road up the mountain is to create a bit of difficulty when going to the Temple.

If you really don't need to go to the temple to learn, then don't go to the Temple, so the road is not widened; this purpose is very clever!

I went there to visit and was very impressed by them. Until now, I have never seen a Dharma Hall as solemn as that. There are about forty monks in the Temple, and every day they meditate at the incense altar on time.

A Dharma Master invited me to give a teaching at the meditation hall; I could not say that practicing Zen cannot be accomplished and that only reciting Buddha's name can be accomplished.

Wouldn't that be destroying someone else's Dharma assembly? This absolutely cannot be done!

Luckily, I had previously lectured on the Diamond Sutra, the Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch, and the Zen Song of Proof from the Yongjia School; I have lectured a bit on matters in Zen, so even my Kohorta-style Zen is not too bad.

I praised them, admired, and lauded the Dao Trang, praised the Dharma Master, and praised the assembly studying Zen there; all of these are things that must be done.

After leaving, the fellow practitioners who accompanied me to visit the temple asked:

The Dharma Master praises Zen Buddhism like that, so why do they recite Amitabha Buddha?

I then told them that because my temperament is not quick-witted, I cannot compare with those who practice Zen; let alone that I cannot achieve enlightenment, even whether I can enter meditation is uncertain.

As for reciting the Buddha's name, relying on Amitabha Buddha to seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land, I feel more at ease.

What I am saying is all true, therefore the Buddhists say that if you want Buddhism to flourish, it is enough for monks to praise other monks.

By admiring and praising each other, Buddhism can be revitalized and can expand widely. If anyone slanders and criticizes each other, it is not good; all will fall into the Avici Hell.

We must understand this principle: the nature of all beings is not the same, which is why the Buddha opened up countless Dharma doors.

H.T. TỊNH KHÔNG!

(Introduction to Pure Land Buddhism)

Source: Diệu Thanh

Edited by: Quang Từ

tieu_de: SECTION ON PROTECTING THE BUDDHIST DHARMA IN THE LATE DHARMA AGE
tom_tat: More than 2,500 years ago, during his lifetime, the Buddha Shakyamuni left a prophecy for future beings that: In the age of the Degenerate Law, many abnormalities will appear, such as terrorism, epidemics, and great disasters
noi_dung:
SECTION ON PROTECTING THE DHARMA IN THE LATER DHARMA AGE

More than 2,500 years ago, during his lifetime, the Buddha Shakyamuni left a prophecy for future beings stating that: In the period of the Decline of the Dharma, many abnormalities will appear such as terrorism, epidemics, great calamities of disease, natural disasters... and it is also the time when humans no longer have the Dharma mind to restrain morality.

Beings in the degenerate age of the Dharma have chaotic minds, live recklessly, and accumulate deep karmic consequences, like a sky full of dark clouds covering the sun (symbolizing enlightenment). The blockage of the path back to the Buddha-mind causes beings to become ignorant, directionless, and deluded, no longer clear-minded enough to distinguish between the true Dharma of the Buddha and the heretical teachings of the demon king. Without the light of the Buddha's Dharma to guide the way, beings will continue to sink in the three evil realms of samsara without being able to realize it. Alas! Beings stand amidst clear, cool waters yet still lament their thirst.

The Buddha – the fully enlightened one, full of great compassion and loving-kindness – had long understood everything. Before entering Nirvana, He entrusted the task of saving all sentient beings to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha (in the Sutra of the Original Vows of the Bodhisattva). Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha made vows to save even those beings who are obstinate, difficult to teach, hard to reform, and seemingly impossible to save; in particular, he specializes in saving beings in the three evil paths. He does not aim to save just one or two beings but all of them, sparing no one, only then will his vow be fulfilled.

But precisely in this context, some individuals exploit the label of "layperson" to propagate distorted ideas, completely deviating from the true teachings of the Buddha, leading followers onto a path of serious moral decay, and fanning the flames of false views. More dangerously, those laypersons have spoken untruthful words. They wrote on their personal pages that:

- "...after the Buddha entered Parinirvana, he did not entrust the leadership of the Sangha or assign any responsibility over sentient beings to any particular disciple..."

- "…Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is just an imagination, He does not really exist and is only a metaphysical form…"

- "…Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is precisely those true practitioners, who give up their families to become monks following the Buddha, enter temples to study, receive precepts, possess wisdom, compassion, and great vows… then that is Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, no need to search any further…"

How pitiful! They uphold, listen to the sutras, and recite, but they do not understand the profound meaning of the scriptures, so they have mistaken views about a particular Bodhisattva as well as about the path of the true Dharma in general. If one were to follow the opinions of this person, wouldn't that mean all the words of the Buddha are false?

Those believers who are encountering the Buddha's teachings for the first time, if by chance they read these articles, the consequences will be immeasurable. First of all, they will lose the will to practice, turn their backs on the true Dharma, slander the Triple Gem, and the most terrible thing they cannot imagine is that a foot in the Avīci Hell is already waiting.

In this urgent situation, the Protecting the Dharma admin group can no longer remain silent. We are determined to speak out to protect the truth of the true Dharma and publicly warn about the dangerous activities of some individuals posing as lay practitioners who have been and are leading many people along the path of wrong views. The admin group would like to ask the followers whether they agree and support us in doing the work of separating the muddy from the clear here? With the consent of the followers, the admin group will work very decisively, not yielding to any wrongdoing that goes against the true Dharma of the Buddha. Initially, we will warn those opposingthe statue has the actions mentioned above. If they do not amend, we will be forced to publicize their personal information so that everyone can be cautious.

The admin group eagerly looks forward to receiving feedback from believers soon so that we can together pick out the “grains of sand” deliberately put into the “delicious rice pot.”

Finally, we hope that our path of learning Buddhism will grow strongly through the blessings that are carefully nurtured. Thanks to the power of blessings, we can break through the wrong views that obstruct the Dharma, which is the life-saving lifebuoy that helps people avoid sinking through countless lifetimes in the cycle of rebirth.

Namo Shakyamuni Buddha

Buddhism Protection Admin Group

tieu_de: THE AURA OF UNCLE LANG NGHIEM
tom_tat: 💐 Chanting the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra Dreams of Seeing Relatives Being Damned and Encountering Protective Deities _Classical Chinese Version: VÂN NGUYỆT VŨ THƯỜNG
noi_dung:
THE POWER OF UNCLE LANG NGHIEM

💐 RECITING THE LANKA SUTRA AND DREAMING OF A RELATIVE FALLING INTO SUFFERING AND MEETING A PROTECTIVE DEITY

_Chinese Text: VÂN NGUYỆT VŨ THƯỜNG

_Vietnamese Translation: Nun Hạnh Đoan

Many people do not know that besides its power to subdue demons and exorcise evil spirits, the Lanka Sutra also has other miraculous effects!

The Lăng Nghiêm mantra has the ability to dispel sorcery and malevolent spells of heterodox teachings. Conveniently, this mantra does not require secret oral transmission; anyone can recite it and experience very miraculous responses. Therefore, if you suspect that you are being harassed by demons or that someone is using malevolent magical spells to harm you, you only need to diligently and continuously recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra to immediately neutralize it. The Lăng Nghiêm mantra also has another miraculous effect: those who recite it can quickly become averse to meat and easily give up flesh to eat vegetarian! This is truly very useful for those who cannot give up eating meat!

I am a woman working in Shenzhen, a place where most people living here value material things very much, only chasing after desires and satisfying their passions… but I met a girl who also came to Shenzhen to work but is as pure and untainted as a lotus flower. This friend’s surname is Zeng, so I temporarily call her Sister Zeng. From the very first glance, we felt very close even though we hadn’t had a chance to talk yet.

After that, we often went to Hung Phap Pagoda in Shenzhen to print sutras and release animals. We usually discussed and commented together on the valuable points in studying Buddhism, and from research, we moved on to trusting and practicing it.

I started eating vegetarian in February this year, while Sister Tang had been eating it for half a month.

In the evening, she recites the Diamond Sutra, three repetitions of the Heart Sutra, and three repetitions of the Great Compassion Mantra. Every day, whenever she has free time, she practices Buddha chanting. Sister Tăng is very diligent, often reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra and the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, each session lasting several hours. Although she has been reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra for less than half a month, she often experiences spiritual responses!

The reason we chant the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is that one time, Sister Tăng and I went to Hùng Pháp Pagoda to request the Lăng Nghiêm mantra to wear. Afterwards, she asked me what merit the Lăng Nghiêm mantra has. I explained that this mantra is a spiritual script from heaven and earth, possessing unparalleled power; when one chants it, the Buddhas in all ten directions listen, and all demons are terrified by the power of the mantra and dare not move.

So Sister Tăng immediately generated the intention to chant it (at that time, she had not yet given up eating meat). One morning, she took out the Lăng Nghiêm mantra to chant it once; this was the first time she read it.

A miraculous result happened: That afternoon, she had planned to eat meat. But after chanting, just thinking about meat made her feel nauseous, so she had to give up meat and has been vegetarian ever since. It seems that the Lăng Nghiêm mantra helped her quit meat extremely effectively!

After experiencing the first time chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, which made her give up meat and become vegetarian, she strongly believes in the power of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, so she has included it in her daily evening chanting routine.

At this point, I felt really ashamed, because I was not used to chanting the prayer and was lazy, so I only memorized the main part of it. Meanwhile, Sister Tang patiently tried to learn the entire five chapters. After a few days of study, Sister Tang told me that whenever she recited the prayer, she often felt a bright golden light shining above her head, which made her feel very comfortable. I knew that she was chanting it sincerely, so the response arose naturally.

After ten days, she told me that yesterday she had been reciting a long mantra, from the evening until five in the morning and then accidentally fell asleep. She dreamed that her deceased elder sister appeared in her dream: only the upper half of her body remained, while the lower half no longer had a human form; at this point, she woke up. But as soon as she opened her eyes... oh my! She saw two Vajra guardian deities wearing golden armor, looking very majestic, appearing before her, so she hurriedly stood up to bow to the guardian deities.

Remembering my sister, she appeared as a dream-prophesying ghost in my dream, and she quietly reasoned and understood the cause that led my sister to be condemned to the evil realm as follows:

My older sister works for the government and lives with her husband. Counting her parents-in-law and her son… there are a total of five people in the house. Because her husband's family belongs to the wealthy class, as a daughter-in-law she often has to buy turtles, giant softshell turtles, fish, chicken, and various extremely delicious seafood dishes... to cook for the whole family to nourish them. Especially her seven-year-old son, if there is no meat he refuses to eat. To satisfy the culinary demands of all the luxurious salty dishes of her husband's family, my older sister had to kill countless animals. Therefore, she created too much negative karma, bringing misfortune upon herself. She died young and fell into the realm of ghosts.

Knowing this clearly, Ms. Tang immediately said to the Dharma guardian:

- I know my elder sister's karmic debt of killing is too heavy, she has committed great sins. Please give me a few days; I will print sutras and release animals, make offerings to the Three Jewels... to pray for my sister to reduce her sins! After Ms. Tang finished speaking, the Dharma guardian immediately disappeared.

This is the truth, I am not lying. The authority of Master Lang Nhiem is very great. There really is a Dharma guardian protecting!

Of course, if you recite without sincerity, have too many distracting thoughts, or recite without diligence, and depending on many other reasons, you cannot see the scenes that Sister Tang has seen!

Occasionally I recite once but not diligently, and my recitation is not fluent either. Of course, until now I have never had any spiritual response. In fact, because Sister Tang is a fellow female practitioner, a virgin girl, she often sees scenes that ordinary people cannot see.

I am writing these things in the hope that those of you who are chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra will try to be more diligent and diligent. My close friend, Sister Tăng, had only been practicing for more than ten days but already experienced such spiritual responses. We need to make more diligent efforts.

Sister Tăng specializes in worshiping the sacred statue of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. She is very respectful and trusting of him. In addition, she also remembers her past life and many previous lives. I used to not remember past lives either, but this year, after studying Buddhism with Sister Tăng, I have also been able to remember a little bit. I am very grateful to Sister Tăng for inspiring me to practice diligently and to be able to see my own cause and effect in the cycle of rebirth.

🍁 TRANSLATOR'S NOTE:

I am translating this piece not for you to start hoping to see strange scenes or encounter Vajra guardians.

In my opinion, we do not need to dream of anything; it is enough that we recite sincerely, with a happy and peaceful mind, and that our life flows smoothly and well. This is something certain.

You should not hope to know past lives either, because if in the present you have many good qualities, then in past lives you have helped many people; if presently you have many bad qualities, then in past lives you definitely caused harm and suffering to many people.

Therefore, it is important that you cultivate your mind and perfect your character rather than being curious about knowing your past life.

I absolutely do not want to know my past life, whether I was a queen, an empress, or a beggar, it is meaningless. Because everything is in the past, what matters is the present life here.

Even now, there are deep affections and close ones that I want to completely forget to feel carefree and light-hearted, but I still cannot forget them; so recalling past bonds of affection will only make the heart more exhausted.

I translate it as wishing you diligence in practicing more. The Lankavatara Sutra is essentially already like a wish-fulfilling gem. The goal we aim for is liberation, no longer reincarnating through suffering; when we achieve the Lankavatara Samadhi through much concentration, the auxiliary blessings naturally arise without needing to seek them. The most practical thing for a practitioner is that the mind is always at ease and happy.

Wishing you diligence and many benefits from reading this translation.

Hanh Doan

Source Facebook: Nguyen Lan Phuong

tieu_de: GREAT BENEFITS OF WORSHIPPING BODHISATTVA KṢITIṄGA
tom_tat: Dear Public! It has been nearly a week since we entered the lunar month of July. This month is an extremely important and busy month for the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas in general, and Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha in particular.
noi_dung:
GREAT BENEFITS FROM WORSHIPPING BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA

Ladies and Gentlemen! It has been nearly a week since we entered the lunar month of July. This month is extremely important and busy for all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in general, and Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva in particular. During this month, the Underworld reviews and grants pardon to sinners, and relying on the power of salvation of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, many sinners and spirits in the three evil realms are liberated.

Returning to the main issue, what is meant by paying homage to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, and why should one pay homage to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva?

💮 1) The character 'chiêm' here refers to admiring or gazing at the noble face of the Bodhisattva, while the character 'Lễ' means to bow or pay respects to the image of the Bodhisattva. When we stand before His image, clasp our hands and admire, gazing at the noble face of the Bodhisattva, then joyfully and reverently bow to the Bodhisattva, that is precisely the Chiêm Lễ of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, which is mentioned many times in the Sutra of Original Vows.

💮 2) Why should we perform the Chiêm Lễ to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha?

This issue, if anyone frequently reads the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra, can clearly see that it is directly from the Buddha's mouth advising beings of this life and the next to pay homage to him, as well as speaking about many great benefits of making offerings, reciting his name, and paying homage to taking refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. Here is a brief summary:

_In the FIRST chapter, the Buddha tells Manjushri that if anyone paints, carves, sculpts, or paints the image of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and wholeheartedly pays homage, makes offerings, and recites his name, at the end of this life they will be reborn 100 times in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven as a celestial being and will never fall into the three evil paths.

_In the fourth chapter, the Buddha also says that if anyone happens to commit many sinful deeds but then meets noble and wise advisors who guide them, and they wholeheartedly take Refuge, REVERENCE, praise, and respect, then even those previous sins that deserved to be reborn in the three evil realms will be completely eradicated. If they are able to spend their life in service, offering, and REVERENCE, such people in hundreds of thousands of lifetimes often are born in the heavenly realm, enjoying wonderful and supreme happiness. When their heavenly merit is exhausted, they are reborn in the human world as kings or rulers and remember their previous lives.

_In the sixth chapter, the Buddha also said that if anyone hears the name or sees the statue of a Bodhisattva and puts their hands together, praises, reveres, and worships it, they can eliminate the sins and sufferings of 30 lifetimes (🔅This is a great eon, not just one lifetime of several decades as we think, one great eon is about 1.3 billion years).

Furthermore, if anyone can paint the statue of a Bodhisattva and wholeheartedly WORSHIP it, they will be reborn in the Deva realm of the God of Fortune 100 times, never again falling into the three evil paths.

_The Buddha also said that whoever seeks beauty or hopes to be born as a daughter in a royal or noble family in the next life should sincerely WORSHIP the image of the Bodhisattva, for in hundreds of thousands of millions of lifetimes they will be born into noble families, with perfect beauty.

_In the eleventh chapter, the Earth Deity of Hard Work says that if one worships the painting or statue of a Bodhisattva in a clean room in the southern direction and frequently burns incense to WORSHIP, they will receive ten benefits:

• First, the land will be fertile and good,

• Second, the house will remain safe and stable forever,

• Three is that the dead are reborn in heaven, • Four is that those still alive enjoy benefits, • Five is that whatever is wished for will come true, • Six is that there are no disasters from water or fire, • Seven is that all wasting matters are eliminated, • Eight is that nightmares are completely ended, • Nine is that when going out or coming in, there are spirits to protect, • Ten is that one often meets noble Saints.

_In the 12th Chapter, the Buddha reiterates in a succinct verse, mentioning a lot about the importance of WORSHIPING AND TAKING REFUGE in Bodhisattvas, which is summarized as follows:

🔱 "I contemplate the power and authority of Kṣitigarbha,

Eons of countless kalpas are difficult to comprehend on earth,

Seeing and hearing just one thought of reverence and worship,

Benefits for gods and humans are inexhaustible..."

〽️(This passage indicates that WORSHIPPING BODHISATTVAS yields inconceivable and unimaginable benefits.)

"If one wishes to practice supreme Bodhi,"

Hoping to be free from birth and death in the three realms,

This person has developed a great compassionate heart

First should respectfully venerate the image of the Great Sage.

Hearing the name and taking refuge in the completely virtuous one,

Offering with reverence and sincerity,

Karmic obstacles do not hinder,

All wishes are soon fulfilled..."

〽️(This passage, the Buddha says whoever generates the mind to cultivate the way seeking liberation or to be reborn in the Pure Land to escape birth and death, FIRST SHOULD WHOLEHEARTEDLY PROSTRATE AND TAKE REFUGE in the Bodhisattvas, then obstacles and karmic hindrances cannot stop us, and all wishes in Life and the Way will soon be fulfilled without missing any.)

"Beings are poor and sick,

Disaster befalls their homes, people separate,

Sleeping leads to restless dreams, not peaceful slumber,

Seeking fails, desires cannot be achieved at all!"

Wholeheartedly worshiping Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha,

All evil deeds immediately vanish

Even dreams become peaceful,

Spirits protect, wealth is abundant...

〽️(This section is where the Buddha speaks to those who are extremely poor, in debt, dealing with household separations, and continuous accidents. Sleep is restless, plagued by nightmares or sleep paralysis. Praying to quickly escape this situation brings more misfortune the more one prays. The Buddha says if one devotes fully to reverently worshiping the Bodhisattva, many misfortunes will quickly disappear, luck will come, sleep will be peaceful, and deities will protect so that one quickly receives FOOD, CLOTHES, RICE, MONEY as desired.)

"Just as someone hears the name of Kṣitigarbha,

Sees the form and devoutly worships with all sincerity,

Offering incense, flowers, food and drink, and presenting garments,

Hundreds of thousands of beautiful merits reap good fortune...

〽️(This section, the Buddha says that if one wholeheartedly offers and WORSHIPS Bodhisattvas, in this life and countless future lives, hundreds of thousands of good karmic results will arise that one can never fully enjoy.)

_Additionally, in the thirteenth chapter, the Buddha says that anyone who sincerely recites the Earth Treasury Sutra, makes offerings, and WORSHIPS Bodhisattvas will receive 28 benefits:

1. Celestial beings and dragons will often protect and support.

2. Meritorious deeds will grow greater day by day.

3. Contain the supreme spiritual group of the Saints.

4. Never lose the path of Bodhi.

5. Clothing and food are abundant and sufficient.

6. Illness does not come to the body.

7. Free from disasters of water and fire.

8. Not harmed by thieves.

9. Others, upon seeing, develop a feeling of reverence.

10. Demons and spirits follow to protect.

11. In the next life, a female body will transform into a male body.

12. In the next life, one will be born as a daughter of kings or great deities.

13. A beautiful appearance.

14. Mostly born in the heavenly realm.

15. Or become a king or ruler.

16. Possessing bright intelligence and awareness of previous lifetimes.

17. All wishes will come true.

18. Relatives will be happy and peaceful.

19. All sudden misfortunes are completely ended.

20. All karmas leading to evil paths are entirely eliminated.

21. Wherever you go, you will not encounter obstacles.

22. Sleep at night peacefully and joyfully.

23. If deceased relatives had committed sins, they are freed from suffering.

24. If in past lives there were merits, then one is reborn into a realm of happiness.

25. Praised by the Saints.

26. Quick-witted and intelligent.

27. Rich in compassion.

28. Ultimately become a Buddha.

Those who look at the benefits of WORSHIPING Bodhisattvas, the Buddha said this is only a brief mention; in truth, even if explained over hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, it would never be exhausted, and there are still many great benefits like this.

Everyone, I, a sinful person, write this to vow before the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Triple Gem that in the past I was poor, ignorant, ugly in appearance, unlucky in everything I did, and people avoided me... Since I finished reading the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and saw the great benefits of worship, I have since devoted myself daily sincerely to bowing and venerating the Bodhisattva. Now, several years have passed, my life is prosperous—not excessively wealthy, but I have enough money to spend and to generously support Buddhist activities. My appearance looks more pleasant and radiant, my wisdom has grown quickly and keenly, and in everything I do I am always fortunate to receive people's help. I say this before the Buddhas of the ten directions as witnesses.not at all false even for just one sentence.

🙏🏻 Today, I, a humble sinner, earnestly beseech the readers, if anyone comes across this article, please join me in making a vow to bow to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva 3,000 times (100 or 150 times daily). If anyone does not have a statue or picture of Him, you can open a picture on your phone and place it in front of you to bow to, or face SOUTH, the direction where the Bodhisattva resides, and bow. Then, dedicate the merit to the three evil paths of suffering to pray that sentient beings in hellish realms may quickly be liberated and be reborn in peaceful realms. This will bring joy and delight to the Bodhisattva, and likewise, you will eliminate countless sins and quickly receive the blessings of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, making all your wishes in this life come true.May all wishes be fulfilled and practice go as desired.

Homage to the Lord of the Underworld, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.

🙏🙏🙏 RESPECTFULLY

tieu_de: Participate and Receive Longevity
tom_tat: Then what's the need to become a monk? Don't deliberately lie, don't do things like 'covering your ears while stealing a bell.'
noi_dung:
Receiving Blessings

No Need to Become a Monk

Do not intentionally lie, do not do things like "covering your ears while stealing a bell."

(Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa's teaching)

A person who ordains must have a solid foundation in practice. What is a solid foundation? It is strictly observing the precepts. One who ordains must memorize the "Four-Part Treatise," that is, the novice rules, the bhikkhu rules, the bhikkhuni rules, the Brahmajala Sutra, etc., and then study them thoroughly, in order to be qualified to ordain.

If the foundation is not solid, constantly thinking about money and then sexual desires, then "though the body is monastic, the mind does not enter the Way." In this way, they are a hundred thousand miles away from the Way. These monastics in Buddhism engage in corrupt actions and cannot be recognized as true monastics.

Monastics should not go around seeking alms from one place to another, nor should they go alone to stay at a small temple and call laypeople to support them. Receiving offerings alone and behaving in such a manner does not conform to the rules established by the Buddha. If one engages in such behavior, it must be corrected promptly, because:

The alms of the donor, even a single grain of rice, is as weighty as Mount Sumeru.

Without understanding the Way, even a feather can be returned to complete the circle.

Meaning:

The grain of rice offered by the donor is as weighty as Mount Sumeru.

After eating, one does not practice the Way, yet wears horns and dons feathers in return.

In the past, genuine practitioners of the Way lived in straw huts, plowed their own fields, and ate by themselves; they absolutely did not rely on external support. For the purpose of eliminating greed, they practiced in leaf houses. Alternatively, they secluded themselves to firmly establish their knowledge and virtue. If one genuinely practices the Way, one can be alone, but cannot take solitary receipt of lay offerings. Doing so turns the True Dharma into the Degenerate Dharma, and also destroys Buddhism.

Currently, monks prefer to practice alone in the monastery. Why is that? Because if they do not uphold the precepts, no one will see, and if they break the rules, no one will know. They can follow their own desires, do whatever they want, with no one to supervise, free and unrestrained; it can be said that there are no restrictions at all. Or, if there is someone else, they gather a few laypeople in their monastery, claiming to hold this or that dharma meeting, but in reality, they just use the monk's robe and the name of the Buddha to earn a living.

There are monks who, instead of using the offerings of laypeople for Buddhist affairs, exploit that money to buy luxury items, cars, or to benefit themselves. Or they buy a TV and then watch it every day, neglecting the practice of morning and evening chanting. Or they buy a refrigerator to store delicious and exotic foods. In short, they are immersed in enjoyment, craving material things, craving pleasure. The current attitude is precisely like this. They completely transform the ascetic nature of Buddhism, truly disappointing the hardships endured by Shakyamuni Buddha in the past!

Some people say: "Being born in this era, one needs to watch TV, needs to know international news, otherwise one is blind, mute, and deaf, knowing nothing at all." And what good is knowing about the things in the world? Even if you know about worldly matters, can it help you when you die?

Some people say: "Can a person who practices spirituality avoid death?" You practice spirituality, yet when death comes, you must still die; however, before dying, your mind is clear, absolutely free of afflictions, not confused, peacefully dying. If one does not practice spirituality, when death comes, they will also die; but die in a confused, drowsy, ignorant manner. Remembering neither south nor north, the heart impure, dying with resentment. That is the difference, do you understand, dear ones?

For a true practitioner, at the moment of death their mind is very clear, knowing where they came from and where they will go; there is clearly no confusion at all, not forgetting their original face. Those who do not practice are dreamy when they arrive and even more confused when they leave, spending a whole life in delusion. They do not know the reason why they came, nor why they are going. They also do not know where they came from and where they are going. Completely in darkness.

The purpose of ordination is to understand life and escape death, not for enjoyment. Therefore, once you have become a monk or nun, why be greedy for material pleasures? If you have a desire for enjoyment, why ordain at all? I maintain that anyone who wants to live alone in a small temple to seek enjoyment is better off returning to lay life. Why is that? Because returning to lay life is much better than living alone in a small temple, as it does not create the aforementioned karmic offenses. I hope that everyone pays attention to this point.

To say that a solitary monk staying in a small temple does so not to practice but to greedily enjoy the offerings is certainly something many people do not want to hear. I do not care whether you want to hear it or not; I still say it because I think of the future of Buddhism. Therefore, I speak it, even if it makes others uncomfortable. Once again: "Anyone who has left home to enjoy themselves without genuine practice is nothing more than wearing the disguise of a monk." I hope fellow practitioners encourage one another, remind one another, and do not deliberately lie, or do things like "cover your ears while stealing a bell." Using thin cloth to hide from the eyes of a sage.

Lecture on November 11, 1983

Source: Tri Duong

tieu_de: THE VENERABLE STUPA IS MORE PRECIOUS THAN DIAMONDS
tom_tat: The sayings immortalized through history of Master Xuan Hua (briefly translated by Nun Hanh Doan)
noi_dung:
VENERATING MONKS IS MORE PRECIOUS THAN DIAMONDS

The immortal sayings of Master Xuan Hua

(Translated briefly by Venerable Hanh Doan)

1. This lecture on the Shurangama Mantra comes from my heart; it can be said to be like my blood and my sweat. I use my true mind to teach, hoping to help those who have not yet believed to believe, and to encourage those who already believe to become more diligent. I wish for everyone to together generate the aspiration to recite this sacred Shurangama Mantra to help save the world from reaching its end.

2. Only a virtuous person can encounter this Dharma; those who are not virtuous, even if they encounter it, cannot understand it! The Lankavatara Sutra is the king above all samadhis.

3. In our practice, we must use a straightforward mind: Body, speech, and mind must all be pure: The mouth should not speak lies, should not fabricate, should not speak sexually inappropriate words, should not backbite (double-tongued), should not speak harshly. Body: do not kill, do not steal, do not commit sexual misconduct.

Regarding the mind: The thoughts of greed, anger, and ignorance must be completely cleared: If your mind is not indulgent and has no distracting thoughts, the mind becomes pure.

In every second and every minute, we must not forget this dharma; if we can sincerely and devotedly practice it, it will make the Buddha's teaching flourish. This is a marvelous dharma that is difficult to encounter even over hundreds of thousands of aeons, so you should not let this rare opportunity slip away.

4. Whoever recites it mindfully will receive spiritual response, and whoever chants it will be protected by Bodhisattva Vajrasattva!

The Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is the longest mantra, also called the “sacred text,” because this king mantra is extremely sacred and infinitely miraculous.

Therefore, those of you practicing this mantra need to have a sincere and devoted mind, cultivate yourselves… and stay away from all desires. If you can do this, the practice of this mantra will have a great response. You also need to eliminate arrogance and conceit.

The benefits of reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra are countless; if you truly want to recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, you must treat the recitation of this mantra as important and necessary as your eating, dressing, and sleeping, and also do not entertain the delusion that you will receive any special response or miraculous results.

Because as soon as you start thinking like that, it is a delusional thought, it will not be accomplished; thinking this way is like a newborn baby, who hasn't learned to sit yet but wants to run!

The Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is a sacred text, each sentence carries its own power; do not think, "Why do I recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra and see no effect at all?"

It is like if you eat rice just to not be hungry, that is enough; if you want to have one meal and hope to be full forever, that is impossible!

Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is the same; if you diligently recite it every day, your efforts will not be in vain, and over time it will certainly be effective.

Those who recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra often have the Bodhisattva Vajra Treasury accompanying them, always by their side to provide protection, and that is the truth.

However, when reciting the mantra, you must not let your thoughts wander randomly, or the Bodhisattva Vajra Treasury might see it and think: "This person has no determination, no future, and is only wasting my time!" The Dharma-protecting Bodhisattva may become angry and lose their temper, so you must be careful.

5. The most important aspect of reciting the Shurangama Mantra is to strictly observe moral precepts. If you do not keep the precepts, no matter how much you recite it, it will not be efficacious.

If you strictly observe the precepts, are free from jealousy and obstacles, and are not greedy, angry, or deluded, then when reciting the Shurangama Mantra, you will achieve great spiritual response and significant benefits.

6. You must understand that reciting the Shurangama Mantra brings you greater benefits than trading in gold and silver.

Because a Shurangama Mantra that you recite brings value equivalent to tens of thousands of ounces of gold, but you must not use a greedy heart to recite it.

7. Regularly reciting the Shurangama Mantra can eliminate toxic energies in heaven and earth. You only need to recite it, and invisibly, heaven, earth, and all things will provide assistance and response.

8. Regardless of the method of cultivation, the first step is to focus on virtue; if virtue is insufficient, obstacles from demonic forces may arise. If you do not correct bad habits and do not eliminate afflictions, you will not gain the benefits of the practice. A vigorous mind arises easily, but a long-lasting and steady mind is difficult to maintain, so you need to be patient and persist without wavering.

Some people want to practice but, due to heavy selfishness and deep-rooted ego, cannot let go of the "self," and therefore are prone to falling into obstacles from demonic forces.

When one practices, one should not be impatient, wishing to attain enlightenment quickly, achieve success soon, or be eager for rapid accomplishments, or have a curious nature, enjoying boasting about strange abilities, craving to obtain supernatural powers, or longing to reach extraordinary states; such tendencies make it easy to be led astray by demons. If you do not generate any other delusive thoughts, then even if you want to invite demons, there would be no demon to invite, because you have no delusive thoughts, no heretical knowledge or wrong views.

People who get entangled with demonic obstacles do so because of heretical knowledge or wrong views. If your mind is diligent, impartial, without impatience, without desire to excel beyond others, and focused solely on practice, then no demon will appear.

9. IN THIS WORLD, IF THERE IS ONE PERSON WHO KNOWS HOW TO RECITE THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA, THEN THE WORLD WILL NOT BE DESTROYED, AND THE TEACHINGS WILL NOT BE DESTROYED. UNTIL THERE COMES A TIME WHEN NO ONE KNOWS HOW TO RECITE THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA ANYMORE, THEN BUDDHISM WILL HAVE TO PERISH!

Currently, there are some demonic beings from other paths, arrogantly claiming that the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra and the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra are fake, fabricated. They are the descendants of demons sent by those demonic beings from other paths to spread wild heresies, with the aim of making people no longer believe in the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra and the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. Once people no longer trust the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, no one will recite it, and then this world will quickly be destroyed! If we want the world not to be destroyed, everyone should quickly recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra and read the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra.

9. IF YOU CAN RECITE THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA DAILY, THE DANGER OF ATOMIC BOMBS AND GAS BOMBS WILL NOT HAPPEN TO YOU.

Sincere Mind Surely Effective—"Sincere" means having no doubtful mind!

When you chant sutras, recite mantras, and practice all dharmas, it must be done with a sincere heart, observing precepts, bathing, keeping body and mind pure, and eliminating all delusive thoughts. If you are not sincere, no matter how effective the mantra is, it will no longer be effective.

Therefore it is said: "A sincere mind is effective," and "sincere" precisely means having no doubtful mind.

You must truly believe that this mantra has unimaginable power, and there is nothing it cannot achieve. If you genuinely have sincere and unwavering faith, then your practice will bear results.

10. BECAUSE SOME PEOPLE PRACTICE FOR A VERY LONG TIME WITHOUT FEELING ANY EFFECT, THIS IS NOT BECAUSE THE BUDDHIST TEACHINGS, SUTRAS, OR MANTRAS ARE INCAPABLE, BUT BECAUSE YOU ARE NOT SINCERE, merely reciting superficially, doing it carelessly just to get it over with! Therefore, to practice the Shurangama Mantra, one must sincerely and genuinely carry out the practice.

In the Lăng Nghiêm Dhāraṇī, there are many names of demons, gods, and heavenly beings of the eight classes of dragons and deities. Whenever one recites the name of any demon king in the dhāraṇī, all followers of that demon must obediently and faithfully comply, not daring to disobey the rules. THEREFORE, if a monastic recites the Lăng Nghiêm Dhāraṇī daily, it is helping this world to avoid all misfortunes, bringing peace to the world. A monastic who recites the morning session in the early morning and the evening session in the afternoon, unknowingly brings peace and happiness to everyone.

11. WHEN WE RECITE THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA, WE CONTRIBUTE TO MAKING THE WORLD'S POLLUTED ATMOSPHERE PURE. THE MOMENT WE RECITE THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA, IT IMMEDIATELY DESTROYS EPIDEMICS AND INFECTIOUS DISEASES IN THE VOID.

The void inherently contains toxic gases, but if you recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, it instantly neutralizes the toxins, which is a great benefit!

THEREFORE, YOU SHOULD NOT UNDERESTIMATE THE LĂNG NGHIÊM CHANT! IF YOU CAN RECITE THE ENTIRE CHANT, THAT IS BEST, BUT IF YOU CANNOT COMPLETE IT IN FULL AND CAN ONLY VERSE SOME PART OF IT, IT STILL HAS GREAT POWER. Therefore, if you have encountered gold, do not mistake it for brass; if you have studied Buddhism, you cannot avoid reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Chant!

Develop Great Compassion for the Whole World While Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Chant

Every single verse in the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra carries infinite meanings, and each meaning has infinite powers. Those who wish to study the Mantra and recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra should generate a broad-hearted intention: Vow to recite it for the entire world, and dedicate all the merit to the whole world. In this way, the accomplishment of merit is very great, because there is no selfishness and it is not for one’s own sake.

12. You must know that if you persistently recite this Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, in the seven future generations, you will all be wealthy like the oil king of America. But if someone hears this and immediately says: I must quickly learn the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra to be wealthy for seven generations.

If your dream is so petty and trivial, then there is no need to learn the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra at all! Because even if you are wealthy, if you are a billionaire for seven generations, it is still just a fleeting moment, and you will still continue to circulate in the six realms of reincarnation!

13. So what should one seek by reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra? Only the aspiration to become a Buddha, to attain Supreme Perfect Enlightenment, and the Threefold Bodhi of Three Declarations. One should not seek minor realms or ordinary goals.

14. In reality, a person who studies the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is the incarnation of a Buddha, is a transformation of Buddha upon the crown of Buddha, therefore the miraculous power of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is beyond imagination,

IF SOMEONE CAN MAINTAIN THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA, THEN WITHIN THE SCOPE OF FORTY WEEKS, WHEREVER THAT PERSON IS, NO ACCIDENT WILL OCCUR, EVERYTHING WILL BE TRANSFORMED FROM DANGER TO SAFETY!

tieu_de: THE ANIMAL DIED TRAGICALLY
tom_tat: One day, after Lu Cu Si and Tieu Man finished their vegetarian meal, as they stepped out of the shop together, they suddenly saw not far away a white mass in a puddle of water, its shape unclear, so they approached it.
noi_dung:
THE TRAGIC DEAD ANIMAL

One day, Layman Lộ and Tiểu Man had finished their vegetarian meal, and as they stepped out of the shop, they suddenly saw not far away a white mass in a puddle of water, its shape unclear. They immediately walked closer to see… and were startled with fright. It turned out to be the corpse of a pigeon, but the scene of its tragic death was so horrifying that it gave them goosebumps. Except for a few bones on its back and its intact wings, the rest was gone. The two laymen felt deep sorrow, so they wrapped its body in paper, recited a prayer for rebirth, and then buried it in a nearby flower bed. Later, when attending the Dharma assembly, Layman Lộby chance mentioned this matter, everyone said:

– This must be the karma of cause and effect...

That's right, I suddenly saw clearly: such a tragic death was caused by the evil deeds it had sown in a previous life, happening during the Second World War:

“There was a German soldier responsible for burying the bodies of the murdered Jewish people. Among them was a body still barely breathing, with both arms stiffly outstretched. The soldier found it unpleasant, so he thought of a cruel way: pouring gasoline on the firewood to burn the body. In no time, the body was completely burned, leaving only the two hands and the skull, looking very tragic.

Because that German soldier was a cruel person at the time, after he died he fell into the evil path, and in this life he was born as a dove. While searching for food, he was caught and eaten by a wildcat, leaving only his wings. This wildcat was actually a Jew who had been burned to death in the past.

Karma is true and not deceptive. Here, I sincerely advise readers not to create the karma of killing, to keep a kind heart, to pity suffering beings, to adopt a vegetarian diet as soon as possible, practice Buddhism, so that one can quickly leave suffering and attain happiness.

Further explanation: The net of heaven is vast; though sparse, it is hard to escape. Good and evil deeds will eventually be repaid. Do not commit a small evil, and do not neglect a small good.

If many people in the world believe in the Buddha, study Buddhism, and follow the teachings, then human society will greatly reduce accidents and suffering.

(Excerpted from Báo Ứng Hiện Đời - Quả Khanh, translated by Hạnh Đoan)

Edited by: Quang Từ

tieu_de: MERIT & HOW TO MAKE CHU LANG NGHIEM NECKLACES
tom_tat: In Buddhism, there is a special secret taught directly by Shakyamuni Buddha to counter all kinds of disturbances from demons encountered during meditation, various spells and charms, and secret letters due to someone secretly h
noi_dung:
MERIT & HOW TO MAKE CHÚ LĂNG NGHIÊM NECKLACE

In Buddhism, there is a special secret taught by Gautama Buddha himself to counter all disturbances caused by various malevolent spirits encountered during meditation, as well as curses, love charms, secret sabotage, and all kinds of evil and demon magic. This is the legendary Lăng Nghiêm mantra.

It is said that during the time of the Buddha, Ananda was targeted by a woman named Ma Đăng Già who used a love spell to enchant him, causing his mind to be clouded, and he nearly engaged in intimacy with Ma Đăng Già.

May, relying on the Buddha to recite the Śūraṅgama mantra, sent Bodhisattva Manjushri to bring the Śūraṅgama mantra to rescue Ananda.

When the sound of the Śūraṅgama mantra resounded, all the spells of the heretics immediately lost their effect, Ananda awakened, and even Mādang Già eradicated all desires, following Manjushri to see the Buddha, and after listening to the Dharma, attained the stage of Arhat.

Thanks to that karmic connection, the world has since received the Lăng Nghiêm mantra - a priceless dharma treasure, capable of countering all obstacles, spells, sorcery, and magic... Even today, most temples in many countries still maintain a schedule of reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra early in the morning.

As for ordinary people, learning the Lăng Nghiêm mantra by heart is not easy at all, because the mantra is very long. And even maintaining daily recitation is something not everyone can do.

However, we still have another method, which only needs to be done once to receive the protection of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra for a lifetime, and that is to write the mantra and carry it on your person. Specifically, please continue reading the section below:

MERIT OF WRITING – RECITING – CARRYING THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA ON YOUR PERSON

(Buddha Shakyamuni proclaimed in the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, Volume 7)

“… You scholars, who have not yet left the cycle of reincarnation, should wholeheartedly resolve to cultivate and attain the fruit of Arhat. If you sit in the meditation hall without reciting this mantra (the Shurangama Mantra), and wish your body and mind to be free from demonic influences, you will find no correctness in that.

Ananda! If there are sentient beings in various worlds, they may use items in their country, such as leaves, paper, or white cloth, to transcribe this mantra, and keep it in a small pouch. If the person is ignorant and cannot memorize or chant it, they should wear it on themselves or place it in their house, and it should be known that this person will not be harmed by poisons throughout their life.

Ānanda! Today I recite this mantra for you, to help the world achieve great fearlessness, and to accomplish transcendent wisdom for sentient beings.

After I pass into parinirvana, sentient beings in the era of the Dharma's decline, some will know how to maintain and recite it themselves, or teach others to recite this mantra. Therefore, those who recite it, fire cannot burn, water cannot drown, poison cannot harm, and even all evil spells of the Devas, Nāgas, demons, spirits, and ghosts cannot afflict them. Their mind is rightly protected, and all charms, ancient spells, poisonous metals, herbs, plants, insects, snakes, and all kinds of toxic gases, when entering that person's mouth, all turn into ambrosia.

All evil spirits and demons, even if they have malicious intent to harm people, cannot generate evil towards that person; the evil demon kings Qina and Yaga along with their retinues, all receive the Buddha's grace and often protect that person.

A Nan should know! This venerable one usually has eighty-four thousand innumerable kinds of Vajra Treasury Bodhisattvas, each of which has its own retinue, protecting day and night. Suppose there are sentient beings whose minds are scattered and cannot enter the Three Grounds, and they recite or maintain the mantra with their mouths or hearts, then the Vajra Kings often follow to support that virtuous man. How much more so for a person who has the determination to enter the Bodhi path; these Vajra Treasury Bodhisattvas enable that person to manifest spiritual consciousness, with body and mind diligent, and at that moment can recall clearly all matters from eighty-four thousand myriads of eons until now, without any doubt.

From the first life to the final body, generation after generation shall not be reborn among the species of Yakkhas, Rakshasas, disease demons, stinking ghosts, sorcery demons, energy-sucking demons, as well as hungry ghosts with form or without form, with thought or without thought, and in places of cruelty.

That good friend, whether reciting, copying, or keeping and offering this mind-mantra, will, lifetime after lifetime, not be reborn in impoverished or lowly places and in places that are not peaceful.

These beings, even if they themselves do not perform virtuous deeds, the Buddhas of the ten directions also bestow merits upon them, consequently allowing them to be born together with the Buddhas in one place through countless eons, having limitless merits like a cluster of Aksobhya fruits, sharing the same cultivation, entirely without separation.

Therefore, this mantra often enables those who have broken precepts to purify the root of their precepts, those who have not obtained precepts to acquire them, and those who are not diligent, not wise, not pure, and not practicing the precepts, all to be accomplished.

A Nan! That virtuous man, supposing that he previously had violated precepts, after reciting the mantra, all offenses against the precepts, whether major or minor, are eradicated. Even if he has drunk alcohol, eaten pungent foods, or other impure things, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, Devas, and spirits will not consider him at fault; even if he wears tattered clothes, whether standing or walking, he is equally pure; even if he does not set up an altar, does not enter the sacred assembly, or does not practice the path, by reciting this mantra, the merit is no different from those who establish an altar and practice the path.

If in the past one committed grave crimes such as the five heinous offenses, the endless crimes, the Four Defilements, or the Eight Defilements of Bhikkhus and Bhikkhunis, then upon reciting this mantra, it is like strong wind scattering a heap of sand; such heavy karmas are completely eliminated, leaving not the slightest trace.

Ananda! If there are sentient beings who, from countless past lifetimes until now, have accumulated all kinds of heavy and light offenses, and although they did not have the opportunity to repent in previous lives, if they now know how to recite, copy, and keep this mantra on themselves or place it in their dwelling, then all previously accumulated karmas will be dissolved like hot water melting ice and snow, and before long, they will attain the patience of non-arising.

Again, Ānanda! If there is a woman who has not yet had children, who wishes to become pregnant, sincerely prays, or wears this charm, she will give birth to sons and daughters endowed with virtue and wisdom; if she wishes to live long, she will have longevity; if she prays for blessings, she will receive blessings; even if she prays for strength, her life, and vitality, all will be fulfilled. After death, according to her wishes, she will be reborn in the lands of the ten directions and will certainly not be born in marginal regions, among lowly people, let alone in any impure forms!

A Nan! If countries, regions, villages suffer from famine, epidemics; or places afflicted by disease, chaos, bandit attacks, and all other disasters, write this mantra and paste it on the four gates of the city, and in small shrines or on banners, so that beings in the country can reverently uphold this mantra, respectfully worship, and wholeheartedly offer; making the people each carry the mantra on themselves, or place it in their dwellings, then all disasters will be completely eliminated.

A Nan! If sentient beings in all countries, wherever this mantra is present, then the Devas and Dragons rejoice, the rain and wind are timely, the crops have a good harvest, and the people are peaceful; all calamities caused by all evil spirits in every place do not arise, people do not die prematurely, shackles, chains, and fetters do not attach to them, they sleep peacefully day and night, and usually do not have bad dreams.

A Nan! In this world of Ta Bà, there are eighty-four thousand harmful disasters caused by evil stars, led by 28 major evil stars; there are also 8 great evil stars in charge, appearing in the world in many forms, often causing strange disasters for sentient beings. As long as there is this mantra, all of them are destroyed, within a range of 12 do tuần, the fierce calamities cannot intrude at all.

Therefore, the Tathagata explained this mantra, protecting beginners of future practice, entering the Three Evil Places, with body and mind at ease, obtaining great peace without being harmed by all evil spirits, demons, and those enemies, past karmic debts from beginningless past.

You and the assembly of virtuous practitioners, together with those who practice in future generations, if they uphold the precepts according to the rules in the meditation hall, and receive transmission of pure precepts from a teacher without doubts toward this mantra, then the body born of this person's parents, if lacking spiritual insight, will cause the Buddhas of the ten directions to speak falsehoods.

Having said this, countless Vajras simultaneously bowed and paid homage to the Buddha: As the Buddha has taught, we sincerely vow to protect those who cultivate the Bodhi path.

At that time, King Brahma and Indra, along with the Four Heavenly Kings, also simultaneously paid homage to the Buddha, saying: If there is anyone who cultivates in this way, we wholeheartedly vow to protect them, so that in their lifetime their actions may be fulfilled as they wish.

There were also countless Demon Kings who clasped their hands and paid homage to the Buddha, saying: We also vow to support and protect that person, so that their Bodhi mind may quickly reach full completion.

Furthermore, countless celestial beings of the Sun and Moon, Wind Masters, Rain Masters, Cloud Masters, Thunder Masters, along with Palace Masters, Watchers, various Stars, and their attendants, paid homage to the Buddha, saying: We also safeguard the practitioner, helping them establish their practice hall and be free from all fear.

There are countless Mountain Gods, Sea Gods, Wind Gods, the Immaterial Heaven, all the spirits on the earth, under the water, and in the air, who also pay homage to the Buddha: We also protect that practitioner so that they may attain Bodhi, completely free from demonic disturbances.

At that time, the eight hundred forty-thousand myriads of Bodhisattvas Vajra Treasury King present at the assembly rose from their seats and respectfully paid homage to the Buddha:

Although we have cultivated Bodhi for a long time, we have not yet attained the realization of Nirvana. We often follow this directive to help those who truly practice the Three Vehicles in the final age of the Dharma. World-Honored One, those who cultivate the mind to seek right concentration in this way, whether in a temple or while walking in meditation, even when taking leisure walks, my disciples and I often follow to protect them.

Even if the Demon King, the Great Sovereign of Freedom in Heaven, wants to find a way to cause trouble, it is completely impossible. Lesser demons and spirits must stay at least ten worlds away from that person, except when they have already aspired to practice the proper dharma, only then can they draw near to that person. World-Honored One, if those evil spirits or demon followers wish to come and disturb that person, I will smash their heads with the Vajra Club as if they were dust particles, allowing that person's deeds to be fulfilled.
