tieu_de: TODAY, JULY 13TH LUNAR CALENDAR IS THE DAY OF WORSHIP OF GREAT BODHISATTVA MAITREYA
tom_tat: Before ordaining to study the Way, Great Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta was the second son of King Vô Tránh Niệm, named Prince Ni Ma. He obeyed his father's advice and aspired to offer donations to the Buddha Treasure and the assembly.
noi_dung:
TODAY, JULY 13TH IN THE LUNAR CALENDAR IS THE DAY OF VENERATING BODHISATTVA MAITREYA

Before becoming a monk and studying the way, Great Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta was the second son of King Vô Tránh Niệm, named Prince Ni Ma.

He obeyed his father’s advice and made a vow to offer to the Buddha Treasury and the sangha continuously for three months.

The great minister Bảo Hải, seeing this, urged: “Your Highness! In the practice of merit, there are two kinds: one is practicing conditioned merit, and the other is practicing unconditioned merit.

Even great worldly blessings, no matter how immense, their rewards are only enjoyed within the human and celestial realms in pleasures; they do not escape the cycle of birth and death.

As for limitless blessings, their results lie beyond the three realms and four directions, in eternal ease and freedom through countless lifetimes.

Therefore, Your Highness should pray for all sentient beings to attain "All-Encompassing Wisdom" and dedicate that merit to the path of Supreme Bodhi; then the blessings will never be exhausted, and at the same time, the heart’s aspirations will also be fulfilled.

Bt Dai the chi

Prince Ni Ma, upon hearing the High Minister advise him so clearly, immediately clasped his hands and said to the Buddha Báo Tạng: "Venerable World-Honored One! Now I wish to dedicate the merit of offering to the Buddha and the Sangha for three months, and the virtuous practices I have undertaken, as follows:

Three bodily deeds

1- Not killing living beings,

2- Not stealing others' property, and

3- Not committing sexual misconduct

Four verbal deeds.

1- Do not lie rudely

2- Do not speak with exaggeration

3- Do not speak double-tongued

4- Do not speak cruelly or coarsely

And the three karma of the mind

1- Do not be attached to fame, gain, or sensual pleasures

2- Do not harbor anger or resentment

3- Not deluded or ignorant, along with my practices of pure virtuous conduct, I dedicate merit to the Supreme, Perfect, Rightly Enlightened Dharma and pray for a world very solemn and beautiful, like the Buddha Realm of Infinite Manifestations of All Merits, Bright King Tathagata, to whom He had made a prophecy for my elder brother.

When that Buddha attained enlightenment, first I encouraged Him to expound the complete Dharma of the Three Vehicles thoroughly in order to save sentient beings.

Meanwhile, I also practice the Bodhisattva Path, engage in Buddhist activities, teach and guide everyone, and perform deeds beneficial to sentient beings, aiming to quickly fulfill the vows of merit I have made.

When the Buddha, the Tathagata of All-Encompassing Merit and Radiance, passes into parinirvana, I will attain enlightenment, succeed the Buddha in transmitting the True Dharma, and guide sentient beings.

The beautiful solemnities in my country, as well as the period of decline and the initial establishment of my Right Dharma, I vow will be just like the transformative work of the Tathāgata of Inconceivable, All-Pervading Merit and Radiance, Sang Wang Buddha.

Phat Bao Tang, upon hearing the words of Prince Ni Ma's vow, immediately gave his prediction, saying: "According to your wish to accomplish a vast and adorned world, in the future, across countless eons, you will have your prayers completely fulfilled."

Because you have a heart that longs for such a beautiful and vast world, we give you the title "Dak Dai The" (Great Aspiration), which means Great Wisdom Bodhisattva.

After the Buddha Manifesting All Merit and Light, Sang Vuong Tathagata, entered Nirvana, you were assigned to become a Buddha, with the title: Thien Tru Tran Bao Tathagata, then successively appeared in the world to save all sentient beings."

Prince Ni Ma, upon hearing the Buddha Treasure give the prophecy, immediately said: "Venerable World-Honored One! If my prayers are truly fulfilled as You have prophesied, I respectfully pay homage to You and beseech You to make all the worlds resound, and for the vast space to shower many kinds of beautiful fragrant flowers. Also, may the Buddhas of the worlds in the ten directions likewise give me such a prophecy."

Then Prince Ni Ma spoke, and as he bowed to the Buddha, immediately all the worlds in the ten directions, including mountains and rivers, trees, and all tangible objects, shook and resounded with echoes everywhere, while in the midst of space fell various fragrant and beautiful flowers like rain.

The Buddhas of the ten directions all concurred and prophesied: “In the realm of Sandelam, there is a disciple of the Precious Treasury Tathagata named Ni Ma, the second son of King Untroubled Mind, who has sincerely offered to the Buddha and the assembly for three months, dedicating those merits toward the Supreme Bodhi and aspiring to obtain a world adorned with splendor.”

Therefore, after countless kalpas, that person will attain Buddhahood, after the Tathagata of All-Encompassing Merit, the Bright King of Luminous Eyes, has entered Nirvana.

Prince Ni Ma, having received prophetic confirmation from the Buddha Bảo Tạng and the Buddhas of the ten directions, was very joyful, constantly practicing virtuous deeds without fault in order to quickly fulfill his heartfelt wishes.

From then on, Crown Prince Ni Ma passed away and was reborn in another body in another life. In every life, he consistently upheld his original vow, determined to practice, study the Great Vehicle (Mahayana), perform Bodhisattva deeds, expand wisdom for sentient beings, and carry out beneficial actions to guide beings out of the river of delusion and onto the path of enlightenment.

Currently, Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta (that is, Crown Prince Ni Ma) is a Samyak-sambuddha Bodhisattva, serving near Amitabha Buddha in the Pure Land, assisting the Buddha in teaching, guiding sentient beings, and awaiting the time when his fruition will be complete to become a Buddha in the Pure Land.

Today, the 13th day of the lunar calendar is the day of his homage; everyone should make the resolve to eat vegetarian and observe precepts to receive the full merit 🙏

tieu_de: CHANT MANTRAS IN SANSKRIT, TIBETAN, OR VIETNAMESE? WHICH PRONUNCIATION IS CORRECT AND EFFECTIVE?
tom_tat: 1. Efficacy lies in oneself, inefficacy lies in oneself - The Ancestors often said, "efficacy lies in oneself, inefficacy lies in oneself," meaning "effectiveness comes from oneself, inefficacy also comes from oneself".
noi_dung:
CHANTING MANTRAS IN SANSKRIT, TIBETAN, OR VIETNAMESE? WHICH PRONUNCIATION IS CORRECT AND EFFECTIVE?

1. Efficacy is in oneself, inefficacy is in oneself

- The Patriarchs often said “efficacy is in oneself, inefficacy is in oneself,” meaning “efficacy comes from oneself, and lack of efficacy also comes from oneself.”

- It is also said “sincerity creates efficacy,” meaning “if you are sincere, it will be effective.”

2. Faith leads all practices

- The Avatamsaka Sutra says “Faith is the root of the Way, the mother of merit and virtue, nurturing all good roots,” meaning “faith is the origin, the mother of merit; it nurtures all good seeds.”

- Jesus said, "Blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe."

- The story about faith includes the tale "The Magical Dog Tooth" (in the book "The Snow Lion with a Blue Mane") and "The Flying Beans," which are very famous.

3. The Masters who have attained Enlightenment in different places

- Venerable Master Xuan Hua recited the Great Compassion Mantra and the Surangama Mantra in Sino-Sanskrit (translation of the mantra imitating the Sanskrit sound, written in Chinese characters, pronounced in Chinese style) to cure illnesses and subdue demons. Some people asked him how he was able to establish the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas (in the USA), and he said it was all thanks to the Great Compassion Mantra, the Surangama Mantra, and Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva.

- People in China and Taiwan who recite the Great Compassion Mantra in Sino-Sanskrit (Mandarin) also find it very effective (See the book "Stories of Mindful Buddha Recitation: Witnessed Experiences" – Lin Kan Zhi)

- Venerable Monk Thượng Giác Hạ Hạnh recites the Great Compassion Mantra in Sino-Vietnamese pronunciation to save (rescue) spirits from underwater, from dark and gloomy places, or to help them attain liberation (see the clip "Spiritual Stories" by the Venerable Monk on YouTube).

- Venerable Monk Thượng Tịnh Hạ Từ recites the Great Compassion Mantra in Sino-Vietnamese pronunciation, together with many others, with many miraculous results (see the book "The Miracles of Avalokiteshvara - Thích Tịnh Từ").

- Venerable Thien Tam recites the Great Compassion Mantra, the Buddha Praise Mantra, and the Ten Thousand Kalas with Sanskrit pronunciation; although this pronunciation is not entirely accurate compared to the original Sanskrit (there are still differences from the original Sanskrit sounds), it is extremely effective, enabling sentient beings from other realms to return to the Buddha's path (See the book Vô Nhất Đại Sư – Thích Thiền Tâm Một Cao Tăng Cận Đại).

- More recently, Venerable Thượng Phổ Hạ Quang in China has been reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra since childhood. He is now 119 years old. His body and dwelling often emit the scent of sandalwood, and he also recites using a combination of Sanskrit and Chinese pronunciation.

- The masters in Tibet recite the Great Compassion Mantra in Sanskrit-Tibetan pronunciation (different from the original Sanskrit pronunciation).

- The masters in Japan recite the Great Compassion Mantra in Japanese, or in Sanskrit-Japanese pronunciation (different from the original Sanskrit pronunciation).

- The masters in Korea recite the Great Compassion Mantra in Korean (different from the original Sanskrit pronunciation).

- All of them have spiritual efficacy, regardless of which pronunciation is used. The recitation may differ in sound, but it is the same in mind. All are recited with sincere mind, urgent intent, and reverent heart.

4. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas possess infinite spiritual powers

- Buddhas and Bodhisattvas attain the Samadhi of “Understanding All Languages”, so whatever language or sound you think in, they can comprehend. Whatever you say, they understand; just by your intention, they are already able to know.

- Not only Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, but also Ghosts, Spirits, Demons, Deities… all realms can understand your "mind" if you initiate mindfulness. Mindfulness is mindfulness of the mind. Sound is only a manifestation, like an image in a mirror, like the reflection of the moon on water, like the wind passing through a bamboo grove creating echoes, like the collision of elements that can produce sound due to conditions.

- “The heart moves, and demons and gods know,” the moment a thought arises, both demons and gods are aware, and this dharma realm shakes and can all be recorded. The Dhammapada teaches that the mind leads all dharmas and governs all dharmas. Therefore, reciting the Buddha’s name, chanting mantras, and reading sutras all rely on the mind. Form is also important, because form helps the mind to express itself, but the root is in the mind.

The sound of speech is formless, but in fact, it is also a kind of form. The sound of each person's voice can be loud, soft, deep, or high; that is the form. The difference in forms is due to different karma, but ultimately, they all return to the mind. Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Ghosts, Spirits, etc., all have "other minds knowledge," "heavenly ear knowledge," and "heavenly eye knowledge," so whatever you recite, they can hear, understand, and know.

5. Want to sincerely and effectively recite the Bright Mantra

- Master Xuan Hua taught that if you want the Bright Mantra to be effective, you must have "cheng," which means sincerity, reverence, and wholeheartedness. He also said that you must observe precepts, especially "not to lie." You must speak the truth. The Bright Mantra is the "true word" (the truthful speech) of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas; if you want to recite the Bright Mantra effectively, you must always follow the precept of speaking the truth. A person who speaks the truth (a practitioner of the Bright Mantra), reciting the true words (the Bright Mantra) from the Holy Ones who speak the truth (Buddha, Bodhisattvas), will surely have a "spiritual response and connection."

- The Lăng Nghiêm Sutra teaches to avoid the five pungent substances. If one eats scallions, chives, garlic, shallots, etc., these substances diminish the power of the Mantra. Demons and spirits will come to lick one's lips and mouth. The Devas will also stay away from those who consume the five pungent substances. Moreover, eating the five pungent substances can either increase anger or increase lust. Eating the five pungent substances is highly disadvantageous for those who practice Buddhism in general and for those who practice the Mantra in particular.

- To have the Mantra be effective, one must speak cautiously, only saying words that are important and necessary; do not engage in idle talk, meaningless words, or harmful speech. Every word spoken should be truthful, compassionate, and instructive to guide others toward goodness.. Only by doing this can one recite the Mantra. All unwholesome actions of the mouth should be abandoned, and all wholesome actions of the mouth should be practiced. Everything spoken should be words of blessing, praying for the safety and well-being of others.

6. The true Mantra consists of good and beautiful words

- In the Primitive tradition, the Buddha taught the Hộ Chú practices. Compared to Minh Chú, Chân Ngôn, and Mantra in the Mahayana or Vajrayana traditions, Hộ Chú is just a different name but has the same essence.

- Hộ Chú, Minh Chú, Chân Ngôn, and Mantra are basically beautiful prayers, blessings, wishes for peace, and vows.

- Some Minh Chú or Mantra consist of only one or two seed syllables. The seed syllable is the 'root' of the sound, of good karma, and also represents the principal deity. Reciting the seed syllable means reciting the principal deity, entering the true nature of the dharma realm.

- Those who speak truthfully, cultivate their mind and character, and live with compassion and goodness, their words immediately align with the meaning of Buddha and Bodhisattvas, making any Mantra effective.

7. Belief in Mysteries

- Because the mind is limitless, mysteries are also limitless. Believing that the mind can manifest all phenomena leads to the belief that Mantras can also manifest all phenomena.

- Studying Buddhism in general, and learning Mantras in particular, requires faith in the miraculous and mysterious; this goes beyond ordinary human understanding, so one can only believe in it.

- Magic and supernatural powers are both natural manifestations of one's inherent nature; the miraculous comes from the mind itself.

- The stronger the faith, the more effective it is. As stated in the Sutra of Thousand-Hand Thousand-Eye Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's Extensive, Complete, Unhindered Great Compassion Dharani, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva said that nothing cannot be accomplished through the Great Compassion Mantra, except for those who doubt; even a little doubt is like poison that ruins all the wondrous tastes of camellia, and with just a bit of doubt, nothing can be achieved.

- People who believe in evil, wickedness, who believe there is no Heaven, Buddha, Saints, or Gods all have a very strong belief. So strong that they dare to commit all kinds of evil deeds without fear of cause and effect or retribution.

If they can believe in what they are thinking to the extent that there is no evil act they won't commit, then why don't you believe in the unfathomable mystery of the Sacred Mantra, of the Buddha's name to chant, to do good deeds and accumulate merit?

Your faith must be strong and profound. Believe that the words of the Buddha are true and not deceptive, believe in your true nature and true mind, believe that anything can happen. Whatever you want, you can have, as long as you have faith. Masters, sorcerers, other religions, even the law of attraction,... all speak about faith. Without belief, you will gain nothing. Studying Buddhism without faith in the Buddha will not lead to accomplishment.

8. You are the entire dharma realm

- The Flower Ornament Sutra says "All is created by the mind alone," which means everything is a manifestation, an appearance, a creation of your mind.

- The Buddha teaches you to enter the mystery of the mind, so he taught many Dharma teachings suitable to the capacities of each individual. It is said that the teachings are suitable to the capacities of each person, but in essence, they do not go beyond Cause and Effect, the Four Noble Truths, and the Noble Eightfold Path.

- Sound is energy, and energy will create matter through transformation in one way or another. The recitation of the Mantra is using sound to enter the mind, to purify the mind, to transform the mind, and to return to the mind. The sound of the Mantra also creates vibration, and from this vibration, material particles are formed according to your mind, through which your desires can be achieved.

- Speaking of liberation, a person who has passed away in the bardo state can remain there for an indefinite period of time, due to their attachment to self and also because of the influence of karma. Now, when you recite Sutras and Mantras, the liberation comes through the sound of the Sutras and Mantras, allowing your mind to harmonize with the mind of the Buddha, using that strength to affect the vibrations in the mind of the deceased, helping them to awaken and wisely proceed towards the wholesome path.

Whether a spirit can be liberated depends on your precepts, virtue, and sincerity. Enlightened beings have purified their contaminated minds, returning to the pure true nature; when they recite a sutra or a mantra once, they can shake the entire universe of three thousand great thousand worlds and strongly transform the consciousness of the recipient. Reading in the Sutras, when the Buddha or Bodhisattvas recite mantras, they cause the realms to tremble in six ways and elevate the listener to the state of Enlightenment. For example, when Zen Master Pho Am recites the Diamond Sutra once, it can liberate a spirit.

- If your mind is pure, then your worldview and outlook on life are pure. Using the Bright Mantra is meant to cleanse the mind; if the mind is clean, naturally your world will be clean and beautiful. "Thanh" means cool, pleasant. "Tịnh" means calm, gentle. A pure mind is virtuous, cool, and only manifests compassion. A serene scene has no obstructions or conflicts; it is uniformly adorned, beautiful, and in any view, it brings comfort. Therefore, if you practice Buddhism and chant the Bright Mantra but still feel uneasy, increasingly angry, greedy, or uncomfortable, it means you are practicing incorrectly, on the wrong path, wandering into the path of demons, spirits, or ghosts.

- The purpose of the Buddha is to teach you to become a Buddha like Him. The Buddha can master this Dharma realm, also master life and death, master everything in the world. The Buddha transcends all, becoming the teacher of the realms of Devas and humans. Learning Buddhism means making your mind pure like His. The Buddha's mind makes no distinctions; self and others are equal, only containing compassion and wisdom. The Buddha has mastered the mind, so He can master the Dharma realm; if you can master your own mind, then you can also master the Dharma realm.

9. Recite the sounds that you are familiar with

- What is familiar to you is the easiest for your mind to grasp. Original sounds, native language speech are the closest to you and also the most proficient, so if you are accustomed to reciting the Mantra in Sino-Vietnamese, just continue reciting it.

- In many past lives, you have studied Buddhism, you might also have practiced reciting in Sanskrit, Tibetan, etc., so if those sounds feel closer to you in this life, now you recite in Sanskrit or Tibetan.

- The mind method of practice is:

* "Pure" means consistent from beginning to end.

** "Sincerity" means being wholehearted, reverent, giving one’s entire heart and soul.

*** "Faith" means having deep and firm belief, like being united as one.

**** "Diligence" means practicing earnestly, making progress every day.

***** "Purity" means practicing with calmness and cleanliness of body, speech, and mind. Observing precepts helps purify body, speech, and mind.

****** "Goodness" means practicing for the sake of all beings, cultivating with a bodhi mind. Every action brings benefit to oneself and others.

Purity, Accomplishment, Faith, Progress, Tranquility, Goodness—these six words starting with “T” are what I can speak to you from my own understanding, and also what the Buddha and Bodhisattvas have taught me. They can be considered as a small guideline for you to practice.

- I study Sanskrit, Tibetan, English, Chinese, Pali; I can recite many Sutras in different languages. But I always chant “Namo Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva,” because this chant is closest to me, arises most quickly in my mind, and is also my familiar mother tongue.

10. Any chant is efficacious

- Through all the above-mentioned points, you can have more confidence in chanting Sutras, in the Mantras, regardless of which sound you use to chant. The translators of the scriptures are not ordinary; they translated under the silent blessing of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas. When they translated the Sutras and transcribed the Mantras, they were very careful; you can follow, chant, and practice after having understood and developed faith.

- The six words in section 9 are the foundation, the guiding principles for your practice.

- When reciting sutras, depending on where one lives, the localities, and languages, there will be differences in pronunciation, but the mind itself is one, naturally unified and unchanging. Reciting sutras with the mind transcends language. Each sound naturally has a different effect on form, but enlightenment is only one; purifying karmic obstacles to achieve various accomplishments is the same.

- Wishing that you can recite "Namo Amitabha Buddha" and the Rebirth Mantra, so that in the future we can meet in the Western Pure Land.

- This article comes from a connection with a friend who wanted me to transcribe the Sanskrit version of the Rebirth Mantra. Before I transcribe and compare the different versions of the Rebirth Mantra, I want to write this article to say that, even if you are chanting the Sino-Vietnamese version, it is still effective, still miraculous, still mysterious, and is indeed the Buddha and Bodhisattvas proclaiming it. Of course, as promised, I will soon provide the Sanskrit version that I use to chant the Rebirth Mantra. But until then, if you find chanting the Sino-Vietnamese pronunciation easier or more familiar, just continue in that way, because you will surely attain rebirth with that Mantra of Illumination.

Source: Lam Son Trang,

22/07/2020

tieu_de: THE OX SOUL BEGS FOR LIFE THANKS TO BUDDHIST DHARMA RESOLUTION
tom_tat: Namdu County, Sichuan Province had a layman named Liu Xingmi. In his house, there was a maid with the surname Niep; in her previous life, she made a living as a butcher and had killed 96 oxen. After these oxen died, they all transformed.
noi_dung:
THE OX'S SOUL DEMANDS LIFE, RESOLVED THROUGH BUDDHIST TEACHINGS

Nam Du County, Sichuan Province had a layperson named Liu Xingmi. In his house, there was a maid named Niep; in her previous life, she made a living as a butcher and had killed 96 oxen. These oxen, after dying, all turned into demons and followed her to seek revenge.

Niep was also from Sichuan, and since returning after marriage, she was often tormented by demons. Several times a year, she would fall ill, and each time she became ill, she had to endure unspeakable suffering.

One February, one year, Miss Nhiếp came to the house of Scholar Lưu Tịnh Mật to work as a servant. One day, suddenly she fell seriously ill, her whole body covered with red spots like a rash, causing both pain and extreme itchiness. Unable to bear it, she intended to jump into the river to commit suicide, but people discovered and stopped her. She would always scratch the ground and howl like a mad dog, and even sing a song about killing a buffalo, singing it with rhythm and rhyme; the content of the song described the sufferings of the buffalo about to die. She wandered everywhere, singing loudly and continuously.

Scholar Lưu Tịnh Mật visited her. As soon as she saw him, she said:

- Master! I am not Miss Nhiếp, we are the souls of the oxen. In our previous lives, Miss Nhiếp in Van District killed us, all 96 lives were taken, today we have come here to demand our lives back, please do not interfere in our matter.

Layman Luu Tinh Mat looked straight at Miss Nhiếp and spoke to the souls of the 96 oxen:

- You are truly foolish, refusing to seek the reason why in your past life, Ms. Nhiếp killed you. Since you had once killed her, you were reincarnated to become oxen to be killed by her; otherwise, why did she only kill 96 lives and not more, nor fewer? Everything has its reason. Today, you do not remember that you had once killed her, but only remember that she killed you, which is why you return as ghosts to take revenge; if grievances are returned upon grievances like this, when will it ever end? In the end, it only keeps revolving in samsara to repay debts to each other. Think about it, today you killed herMe, then in the future she will kill you again, so what will happen?

The soul of the 96 buffaloes said:

- What you say makes a lot of sense; indeed, we have been too reckless. But the blood on our necks has not yet dried, the pain has not yet subsided. It is because of the agony that has taken over us, that we now have thoughts of revenge.

Layman Lưu Tịnh Mật then said: - This matter is not difficult to resolve.

After speaking, he immediately sent a servant to bring half a glass of water, then chanted the Cam Lộ mantra three times, and then invited those restless spirits to drink. All these spirits were formerly oxen; when they became demons, they had the ability to walk like humans, but their heads remained ox heads, their front legs transformed into hands, but were twisted like the front limbs of a dinosaur, making it impossible to hold a glass to drink. They immediately said:

- How can we hold the glass without hands?

Layman Liu immediately instructed his servant to bring a cup of water to Nhiếp's lips, and thanks to that, they were able to drink. Unexpectedly, as soon as they finished drinking, all of them joyfully exclaimed: "This water is truly miraculous! We feel incredibly healthy. Our necks are completely healed. All our nails have fallen off, and our horns are gone." After saying that, they jumped around in delight.

Layman Liu then praised the realm of the Western Pure Land and taught them to chant Buddha's name. After praising, Layman Liu asked them:

- If you are able to be reborn into the Pure Land, never again suffering the torment of samsara, would you like to go there?

The restless spirits immediately responded:

- The Pure Land is truly as beautiful as you say, why wouldn't we want to go there? But our karma is too heavy; we are afraid we cannot go.

- If you vow to recite the Buddha's name, wholeheartedly wishing to go to the Pure Land, I will invite Amitabha Buddha to come to lead you. Do you agree?

- Very good! Very good! But we have been hungry for a long time, please kindly give us some food.

Layman Luu nodded in agreement. He took a cup of water, rice, and recited the true mantra seven times, then poured it into the bamboo bush. Shortly after, the vengeful spirits said: “We have eaten until we are very full, thank you! Thank you!”.

Layperson Liu Xingmu stood by the window, took three incense sticks and turned them toward the West, respectfully invited Amitabha Buddha, and also recited the Rebirth Mantra, the Great Compassion Mantra, the Heart Sutra of Prajñā, and the holy names of the Bodhisattvas, inviting them to come and guide all these ox souls to be reborn in the Pure Land. Suddenly, one of the oxen spoke loudly:

- Hurry up, friends! The master just invited, and Amitabha Buddha has arrived. He is standing outside the window waiting for us. Look, Buddha is so solemn, his entire body is golden, so beautiful, so beautiful. Let’s quickly go with Amitabha Buddha to the Pure Land.

At that time, Mr. Lưu's wife was standing beside him and asked:

- Did you see the Western Pure Land? What is it like?

Mr. Lưu replied: - I have seen it. The Western Pure Land is solemn and much more beautiful than described in the scriptures.

Before, those restless souls, upon being reborn in the Pure Land, clasped their hands to thank Mr. Lưu, saying:

- We are extremely grateful to you for helping us, allowing the enmity of many past lives to be completely dissolved. For many years, we have followed Miss Nhiếp to harm her, causing her constant suffering. We were truly foolish, thinking that doing so would avenge ourselves, would satisfy our anger, but little did we know that by doing so, we ourselves also suffered. Today, relying on the power of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, we aspire to be reborn in the Pure Land. We hope that you can compassionately encourage Miss Nhiếp to recite the Buddha’s name, so that in the future she may also be reborn in the Western Pure Land. When the master and madam are reborn, we will follow Amitabha Buddha to go and receive you. Saidfinished, then go immediately.

An hour later, Ms. Nhiếp woke up. Mr. Lưu asked her, and she replied:

- Just now, while I was sleeping, I had a dream. I saw a herd of very fierce buffaloes charging straight at me, their heads covered in blood, extremely frightening. In that critical moment, I suddenly heard the old master's voice, and the scene before my eyes instantly changed: the ground was flat, the trees were lush and healthy, pleasing to anyone who saw them. After that, I heard the buffaloes praising the delicious rice, saw all of them eating happily, even jumping with joy. What happened after that I am not sure of…

After this incident, Miss Nhiếp was no longer haunted by ghosts, and she also began to vow to practice vegetarianism and recite Buddha's name.

In the spring, two years later, layman Lưu Tịnh Mật took the resolve to become a monk in Tây Khang, with the Dharma name Tuệ Định. This is a true story he recorded before ordination.

Source: Cause and Effect

tieu_de: THE DANGER OF LUST IS REALLY SCARY!
tom_tat: REINCARNATION IS ALSO BECAUSE OF THIS MIND. Mount Putuo in the South China Sea, during the Qing dynasty, there was a monk named Liu Ting. When he was still a layperson, he was a young man who believed in Buddhism, and every day he would recite a copy of the Diamond Sutra.
noi_dung:
THE DANGER OF LUST IS TRULY TERRIFYING!

REINCARNATION ALSO HAPPENS BECAUSE OF THIS MIND

Mount Putuo in the South Sea, during the Qing dynasty there was a monk named Liu Ting. When he was still a layperson, he was a young man who believed in Buddhism, and every day he would recite a copy of the Diamond Sutra. No matter how busy or late it was, he always made sure to finish reciting it before going to sleep. He practiced very diligently; he could go without food during the day, but he could never skip reciting the sutra.

One night, while sleeping, the teacher dreamed that his house had a horse-drawn carriage, on which there were six girls, each very lovely; their beauty made "birds fall and fish dive," like celestial maidens descending to the mortal world.

The girls approached and asked: "Dear sir! Come here! Dear sir, come here! There is still plenty of space on the carriage, we have saved a spot for you!" At that time, Liễu Tình was a young man, just like many other young men, who could hardly resist such stunning beauty, combined with sweet invitations and "deadly" smiles... he felt enticed and immediately got on the carriage.

After the car had been going for a while, it stopped, and the six girls got out; he also got out. He saw a door ahead, but the door was very small. After the six girls went inside, he also intended to follow. But strangely, the six girls didn't walk in but crawled in, and he did the same as them.

After they finished crawling in, it was your turn. You saw a Vajra deity, similar to Bodhisattva Amitabha holding a Vajra club. As soon as he saw you, he stopped you: “You cannot enter here, go out quickly, go out!” But you insisted on going in. The Vajra deity shouted: “I already told you not to enter, yet you stubbornly want to go in. Those who recite the Vajra sutra are not allowed to enter this place. I told you to go out, but you refuse!” Then he struck your head with the Vajra club, causing intense pain, and you immediately fainted. When you woke up, you found yourself lying on the bed. You said: “Ah, so it was just a dream!” But strangely, you felt that there was a very foul smell somewhere.

It's like the smell of pig manure, a smell that has never been in your house before, and you have never smelled it before. Oh my! You are also extremely tired, your stomach is restless, and sweat soaks your whole body.

You looked carefully and noticed that it was already past midnight, and you couldn't go back to sleep, so you got up to chant the Diamond Sutra and sat until morning. In the morning, you decided to find the place you had dreamt of last night, going to nearby locations to see what it was, wondering what that small door could be.

Oh! There it is! You still remember that small door vividly; it was the water channel outside the pigsty (where a channel is dug to let the pig's waste and urine flow out), the exact place you saw yourself entering in last night's dream. At that moment, you felt a chill down your spine and immediately went to find the owner to ask what was really going on.

You asked:

- Sir! May I ask a little question. Did anyone come here last night?

The owner replied:

- Nobody came, who would come at midnight.

You asked:

- Last night I dreamed of seven people going in there by this small path. I wonder if anything happened inside?

The owner laughed and replied:

- Ah! There is such a matter. My family raises sows, last night the mother pig gave birth to seven piglets, six females and one male, but the male died right after birth.

- Where did you put the dead pig? Can you take me to see it?

- Why not? I put it by the fence, come with me!

As soon as he saw the male pig, he immediately knew it was himself. At that moment, he felt his ears ringing, unable to hear any sound, the world turned dark, dizzy, chaotic, his limbs trembling, unable to speak. He tried to run back as fast as he could, stammering: “Da… da… da… danger… danger… too… too!” If last night the Vajra deity hadn’t shouted at him, “Those who chant the Vajra Sutra are not allowed to enter this place,” and hadn’t struck his head with the mallet, he would have surely become a pig by now. After regaining his composure, he went to Mount Putuo to request to become a monk. The abbot of Mount Putuo asked him:

- Why do you want to become a monk?

He then told the abbot about everything. After hearing it, the abbot said:

- In that case, you are a person with very good karmic roots.

On that occasion, the abbot gave him the Dharma name "Liu Tinh". Therefore, the teacher is called "Venerable Liu Tinh".

● Dreaming is very dangerous and should not be taken lightly. When dreaming, the sixth consciousness (mind) cannot control one’s own “spiritual perception”; it always chases after the scenes in the dream, which is truly dangerous!

Everyone needs to pay special attention when dreaming, especially young people; even if a young woman invites you, do not go. You can respond: “I am not going anywhere! I have my own path!”. To achieve such a firm-mindedness, it is necessary to practice reciting Buddha’s name in dreams. If in the dream you are unable to recite Buddha’s name and are instead being pulled by the dream, it is really dangerous!

If we do not practice reciting the Buddha's name regularly, do not have mindful recitation, then our consciousness will become vague and always follow dreams. "Who knows what will happen tomorrow." Falling asleep like Master Lieu Tinh is truly dangerous; if it weren't for the Vajra spirit striking, one would surely not return!

Namo Amitabha Buddha 🙏🙏🙏

(Excerpt from The Measure of a Practicer of Pure Land. Dharma Master Hoi Tinh - Translator: Dao Quang)

After reading this story, I was also surprised because the world has many similar occurrences.

My great-grandmother told that great-grandfather was a teacher, skilled in reciting incantations for people to “go on a journey” to visit hell.

There was a man who requested to go on such a journey, and great-grandfather recited the incantation so he could descend into hell, but when it was time to summon him back, his soul did not return to re-enter his body.

Great-grandfather examined and realized that the man had been reborn as a pig in the neighboring village. His relatives had to buy that male pig and slaughter it for him to be able to come back.

When he woke up, he said he went downstairs and saw five beautiful girls walking, so he chased after them; as a result, they all entered the pig's belly. The neighbor's pig gave birth to five piglets, a female and a male, and finally, he was one of them.

My nun grandmother did not lie; she even boasted that she knew the incantation to send someone to hell but did not know the one to bring someone back up.

At that time, I was 17-18 years old. Hearing the story, I was curious and wanted to know the incantation, but I thought: "Not knowing the one to bring them back is like sending someone to their death." So, I did not ask.

In fact, we do not have to wait until dreaming; at any moment, we must focus our mind to maintain pure thoughts. Because we can leave our body at any time, we can die at any moment, a clear mind without wrong thoughts will lead us to a good realm. This is the reason why Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Holy Masters always advise us to practice at all times.

Hanh Doan

Source: Huu Duyen Thi Gap

tieu_de: THE HORRIFIC TRUTH BEHIND DISEASES CAUSED BY KARMA
tom_tat: 🍁 At a Dharma Q&A session hosted by Quả Khanh (a monk with clairvoyant abilities, able to see the karma and fate of everyone), there was a woman who asked
noi_dung:
THE TERRIFYING TRUTH BEHIND DISEASES CAUSED BY KARMIC CONSEQUENCES

🍁 At a Dharma Q&A session hosted by Quả Khanh (a lay practitioner with a clear mind, who can see people's karma and destiny), a woman asked a question:

- My son is in 4th grade, but he still can't even do simple addition and subtraction. What is the cause?

Quả Khanh replied:

- During pregnancy, women often eat seafood, chicken, duck, etc., which can harm the baby's brain, making the child less intelligent. To prevent this and to help the child become bright-minded, parents should chant Buddha's name, eat vegetarian, and recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for the child. Every day, they should recite from 7 to 10 times the Great Compassion Mantra, dissolve it in water, and give it to the child to drink. The child should also, every day before going to school, perform three Buddha worship rituals, offer incense and flowers to the Buddha, and gradually will become intelligent again.

🍁 May I ask:

- Why is it that some people get sick even if they only eat one chicken or a small piece of meat? While others eat hundreds and still remain healthy without any issues, and some have never fallen ill—what is the reason behind this?

🍁Answer:

- A person who eats chicken and becomes slightly ill is due to the fact that in the past they had no resentment towards chickens. Therefore, eating just one piece makes them sick. Meanwhile, a person who eats hundreds of chickens without any problem is because in the past they had killed and eaten hundreds of chickens or other animals, so in this life they eat back those chickens (which are the beings they once ate, now reincarnated as chickens and must repay the life debt they previously took). One must understand, the law of cause and effect always responds correctly, even if it appears minor.

We should often stay alert, not make mistakes, always control ourselves, and not let our mind run wild. We must skillfully use the mind to change circumstances, not let circumstances change the mind.

🍁Someone often suffers from headaches. What is the cause?

Khanh answers:

- Because you are unfilial to your parents, always causing them to worry. As a result, you feel the consequences yourself as a headache. Whenever others suffer, you also experience the same.

A girl asked:

- My parents don't believe in Buddha, what should I do?

Khanh replied:

- My mother also doesn't believe in Buddha. Last year she was ill, I knelt and recited 100 sets of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra praying for my mother and guiding her to a very high state of being. If your parents still do not believe in Buddha by the time you are grown up, then sincerely recite sutras and Buddha's name for the sake of your parents.

A woman has had vitiligo for more than 20 years, and the left cheek also has a large red rash. She asked for the cause.

Answer:

- Besides the cause due to killing and eating meat, she also committed faults such as speaking ill of and spreading the shortcomings of others, causing others discomfort, so she herself received unbearable retribution.

🍁Incidentally, let's talk about the causes of other diseases. Stomach pain is often related to the frequent killing and eating of meat, and intestinal diseases are the same. Mr. Tuyên Hóa once said: People with bowel tumors are due to often eating meat.

Regarding Gynecological Diseases, apart from a few caused by other factors, most are due to moral faults. Therefore, women who suffer from such diseases should reflect and examine themselves: Have I committed any moral wrongs? The same goes for men! If you have symptoms of Prostatitis, quickly examine your faults and repent...

As for asthma and coughs… they are usually caused by eating seafood. Here is an example: Teresa Teng was a very famous female singer (from Taiwan), once acclaimed as: “The number one female singer in Asia.” In 1995, she traveled to Chiang Mai (Thailand), and on May 8, she had an asthma attack, wheezing… and then suddenly passed away at a hotel in Chiang Mai.

The passing of Đặng Lệ Quân caused many fans to grieve and sparked waves of suspicion and doubt surrounding her death. To explain this matter, Quả Lâm observed and clearly saw the following: In Đặng Lệ Quân's lungs were filled with all kinds of seafood…!

You must understand that: When we eat reptiles and seafood, because the spirits of living beings no longer have a place to reside, they immediately cling to the lungs of the person consuming them, harming them… little accumulates at first, over time it becomes much, and when the time is ripe, the evil consequences appear…

🍁But there is a real story we witnessed, about a patient with lung disease, having great difficulty breathing, staying at Hospital 108. For a whole month, professors and doctors conducted all sorts of tests, scans... but could not detect any cause of the illness. In the last days of life, the patient realized that the fate was caused by himself, during a period while performing duties... he had let many people fall into deep wells and they died from lack of oxygen. I would like not to mention names for ethical reasons. But that isreality.

Whether these stories are true or not is everyone's right to speculate.

But it is best to always maintain self-discipline and especially to strictly observe the limits if one is a disciple of Buddha.

Source: Facebook, Dr. Quách Văn Mích

tieu_de: Please tell another story recorded by Thích Quán Bổn, a disciple of Master Hư Vân:
tom_tat: WHITE FERRET Year 25 of the Republic, Bính Tý. After Nam Hoa had opened the Great Precept Platform and completed the transmission of the three platforms, just as the precepts were about to be concluded, Lam Quoc Canh – Commander of the 16th Division stationed at Tao Khe – came to visit, hand
noi_dung:
Please tell an additional story recorded by Master Hư Vân's disciple, Thích Quán Bổn:

THE WHITE WEASEL

Year 25 of the Republic, the year of Bính Tý. After Nam Hoa had held the Great Precept Assembly and transmitted three ordinations, just as the assembly was about to conclude, Lam Quoc Canh – the commander of the 16th Division stationed at Tao Khe – came to visit, carrying a cage that contained an animal, entirely snow-white with small black spots, smooth fur, a pointed snout, and a long tail, which was unmistakably a weasel. The commander said:

- This animal has a very adventurous history. Initially, it was captured by hunters in Baiyun Mountain – Guangzhou. People say that when the walls of Guangzhou were broken to open the main road, it jumped out from inside the city and was caught.

My friend bought it for 40 yuan, planning to take it home for a nutritious and tasty meal. But seeing its lively, sparkling eyes, which seemed to understand human intentions, he couldn't bear to kill it. So he confined it and sold it to Guangzhou Zoo. Later, he was suddenly arrested and thrown in prison without knowing the cause or charge, and the case remained unresolved without anyone settling it.

By chance, his wife attended a spirit-writing session. Before she could even ask a question, the divination already appeared, accurately addressing what she was wondering in her heart and explaining that her husband was currently imprisoned due to the karmic repercussions of selling the marten to the zoo. It also instructed her that there was a high-ranking monk currently leading Dharma propagation at Nam Hoa Temple, and she should quickly bring the marten there to release it, so that her husband would be saved from danger.

The wife was startled and hurriedly paid the ransom to redeem the civet. Since Captain Lam was her husband's close friend and happened to be stationed at Tao Khe, she asked him to take the civet to the temple for release on her behalf.

Master Hư Vân, upon hearing the story, immediately took in the marten. He taught it the Three Refuges and Five Precepts and then released it into the dense forest behind the temple. Every day, it would come into the temple to be fed by the monks. Since receiving the precepts, it refused to eat meat, only ate vegetarian food, and greatly enjoyed eating fruit. The temple builders wanted to tease it, so they stuffed meat into a banana and offered it to it. When the marten realized it had eaten the wrong thing, it spit it out. It scratched at the food with its front claws, inspected it several times, looked around, glared at the workers, showing anger and indignation because they had deceived it. After that, it left straight away and did not return for several days.

One day, being chased by villagers, it climbed up a towering tree almost dozens of trượng high, clinging to a branch and crying. The novice monk saw this and reported it to the Abbot. Venerable Hư Vân immediately went outside to the base of the tree and looked up. As soon as it saw Him, the marten quickly slid down, clinging to His sleeve, looking very happy. The monk took it home. Fearing that it would be caught by people, He built a cage for it. Afterwards, when released into the forest, it only roamed around the temple, no longer going into the forest.

One day, Chiang Kai-shek went with ten attendants to visit the temple without prior notice. As they arrived at Cao Khe gate, they saw a ferret. The guards intended to shoot it, but Chiang stopped them. The ferret shook its head, wagged its tail, and led Chiang inside. When they reached the main hall, it ran like lightning into the Abbot's quarters, bit the monk's robe, and pulled him down the stairs to meet Chiang. When people heard the story, everyone laughed.

Whenever the Abbot was meditating, the ferret would often lie under the meditation platform. Seeing the Abbot closing his eyes for too long, it would start to fidget, tugging at his beard playfully. The Abbot opened his eyes, looked at it, and said:

- You have a sensitive nature, do not enter the forest, do not go outside the mountain gate or come near people's houses where the children might bother you!

One day, for some reason, it went somewhere and was run over by a vehicle, seriously injured, lying there, unable to get up. Seeing the Venerable Hòa Thượng come to visit, it tried to show its wounds to Him. The Venerable knew it could not be saved and, feeling pity for its pain, began to teach: "This leather bag is no longer worth being attached to! Do not cling to it, let go, and repent for all past karmic actions. If a wrong thought arises, one must descend into suffering, endure the bad consequences, and suffer greatly. Now, the fruit of past karma has ended, I hope you wholeheartedly recite the Buddha's name, so that you may attain liberation soon."

The weasel understood, nodded its head, made a few sounds, and then passed away. Its body remained unchanged even after two days. The monk remembered the story of Master Baizhang helping a wild weasel and thus organized its funeral as that of a monk, burying it on the southern side of the mountain.

This may seem strange, but the reason such things happen in life is the same as what is described in the repentance texts.

We are ordinary mortals, often reasoning that raising birds and fish is an extremely enjoyable pastime. Most also hold the ignorant belief that once they have gained some wealth, they have the right to go out for entertainment and indulgence by buying flowers, hiring women, and they argue that brothels are places to buy fun, for their amusement and leisure. They do not realize that enjoying blessings in this way actually brings misfortune, unaware that such indulgent behavior inadvertently creates bad karma, causing them to fall into endless hell. When retribution manifests on their body and impermanence strikes, it will be too late to repent!

CAUSE AND EFFECT COMMENTARY ON LIANG HUANG SAM

LAY BUDDHIST QUẢ KHANH

VIETNAMESE TRANSLATION: NUN HẠNH ĐOAN
