tieu_de: CAUSE AND EFFECT THROUGH MANY LIVES IS FAIR
tom_tat: <Excerpt from Ngọc Lịch Bửu Phiêu> Why are there people in this world who do evil yet live happily, while others who do good live in misery? Many people see this and feel an inner sense of injustice.
noi_dung:
CAUSE AND EFFECT THROUGH MANY LIFETIMES IS FAIR

< Excerpt from Ngoc Lich Buu Phieu >

Why is it that in this world some people who do evil live happily, while others who do good live in suffering? Many people see this and feel injustice in their hearts, believing that Heaven and Earth are not fair. In fact, all of these things have their reasons. The following small story will help us understand this to some extent.

During the Qing Dynasty (1644 – 1661), in Shunyi County, Beijing, there was a very wealthy family with the surname Gong. The family's assets included hundreds of acres of land and herds of donkeys and horses. The Gong family had a son named Gong Khanh Huu. The year Gong Khanh Huu was born, the husband and wife of a family servant named Li Dai also had a son. The couple named their son Li Phuc.

When Gong Khanh Huu was 7 years old, the Gong family invited a good teacher to teach the boy. Seeing that the young master was receiving education, Li Dai immediately pleaded to have his own son study alongside him.

The two boys, Công Hữu and Lý Phúc, grew up together, studying together by day and sleeping together by night, and fourteen years passed in the blink of an eye.

One night, Lý Phúc was sleeping very deeply and had a dream. He dreamed that a large door in the sky opened, and two deities appeared one after another. Both deities walked into the study where Lý Phúc and Công Hữu were still sitting and studying.

Then one deity pointed at Công Hữu and asked the other deity: “What kind of boy is this?”

The deity said: "This person is extremely wealthy and noble, at the age of 17 he will pass the regional examination, at 19 he will pass the national examination, and in the future, he will hold a second-rank official position, enjoying a lifetime of honor and wealth!"

The deity then pointed at Ly Phuc and asked: "What about this boy?"

The deity replied: "This is a poor person, who will live in poverty all his life and will have no official or scholarly accomplishments whatsoever!"

After saying this, the two deities gradually flew into the inner gates of heaven, and the heavenly gate closed again as it had at the beginning.

Lý Phúc suddenly woke up and felt very strange. He immediately recounted the things he had witnessed in his dream to his parents and everyone else.

When Cống Hữu was 17 years old, he indeed passed the tertiary examination. At that time, Lý Phúc had already stopped studying and stayed at home to work in the fields. Although Lý Phúc worked in the fields at home, he still always paid attention to Cống Hữu in his heart.

Ly Phuc clearly knew that Cong Huu had a cruel and vicious nature and committed many evil deeds. Yet, since passing the provincial exam, Cong Huu's career continued to rise. He even became a high-ranking official. After becoming a high-ranking official, he accepted bribes, disrupted order and discipline, and treated the people brutally.

In his heart, Ly Phuc always thought: “Surely, Cong Huu will face retribution in this life!”

But unexpectedly, Cống Hữu lived to the age of 71 and was still healthy, with many children and grandchildren. Moreover, he even predicted the time of his own death. He also informed his descendants in advance about the day of his death so that the family could prepare for the funeral.

Ly Phuc, on the other hand, was very diligent in his work, treated everyone kindly, and often helped others. In Ly Phuc's heart, he always thought: "I should be the one to receive blessings, while Cong Huu should suffer retribution." But in reality, everything turned out completely the opposite, so he felt very resentful and believed that the underworld was biased. So, he was determined to follow Cong Huu to the end to understand the full cause and reason.

Ly Phuc also informed his children about the day he would die so that the family could arrange the funeral. But in reality, he did not know when he would die; instead, he planned to commit suicide by poison on the day Cong Huu died so that he could go with Cong Huu to meet King of Hell. Unexpectedly, Cong Huu died exactly on the day he had planned, and Ly Phuc also drank the poison and died along with him.

As soon as Ly Phuc arrived in hell, he met the King of Hell coming out to welcome Cong Huu. After reviewing all of Cong Huu’s matters, the King of Hell then allowed Ly Phuc to enter. The King of Hell said:

- Why have you also come here?

Ly Phuc answered:

- I came because I wanted to follow Cong Khanh Huu. People in the living world fear power and show respect to the wealthy. Why would the King of Hell in the underworld also fear power and the rich? That Cong Khanh Huu was cruel and vicious in the living world, committing many evil deeds. I thought that if he didn’t receive retribution on earth, he would surely suffer severe punishments in the underworld. But I never expected that the underworld and the living world are of the same kind.

- Wait a moment, I will explain it to you clearly.

Then, the King of Hell ordered a judge to bring a notebook recording life and death, good and evil. After that, the King of Hell opened the notebook and looked for the page recording about Cống Hữu and then said:

- The reason is that in his previous life, Cong Huu did many good deeds, but in this life, he committed many evil acts, causing a considerable consumption of his meritorious deeds. However, Cong Huu still has a lot of merit left, so in the next life, he will still enjoy blessings, just not as blissful as in the previous life. As for you, Ly Phuc, in your previous life you did not perform good deeds, so in this life you must endure suffering. However, because in this life, you have wholeheartedly done good deeds, you are able to have a life with enough food and clothing, which can be considered not suffering any loss. In the next life, you will enjoy blessings for the good deeds done in this life.

Ly Phuc knelt down and pleaded with King Yama:

- I beg you to allow me not to drink the 'anesthetic potion' in my next reincarnation.

King Yama agreed to his request.

Lý Phúc was reincarnated together with Cống Khánh Hữu. Because he did not have to take anesthesia, he witnessed the entire life of Cống Hữu. In his next life, Cống Hữu was reincarnated into a wealthy family, while Lý Phúc was reincarnated into a fairly well-off family. Later, when Cống Hữu grew up, he became an official, reaching the position of county magistrate, but he still treated the people cruelly without mercy. He took bribes, falsely accused honest people of theft, and gouged out the eyes of innocent people because of tortured confessions… In another case, he even cut off the legs of a villager. Cống Khánh Hữu lived to over 70 years old and then fell illdead.

Ly Phuc, because of his wholehearted goodness and his practice, had his soul become capable of freely leaving his body and entering the underworld. At that moment, he saw Cong Huu had died, so he immediately sat upright to let his soul follow Cong Huu down to meet King Yama. Ly Phuc was very surprised, because it was very different from before; this time, King Yama came to meet Ly Phuc first, and only afterward asked about Cong Huu's crimes.

King of Hell examined and saw that Cong Huu had already enjoyed all the good merits of his previous life. Moreover, in this life, while serving as an official, he gouged out the eyes and chopped off the legs of innocent people. These two evil deeds could not be compensated by any good, so he had to repay them with his body. Thus, the King of Hell decreed that Cong Huu be reincarnated into a poor family, blind in both eyes and crippled in both legs. Every day, Cong Huu had to crawl along the road to beg for food, enduring indescribable suffering.

As for Ly Phuc, seeing that Cong Huu had received the karmic consequences of three lifetimes, he became even more afraid of losing his moral direction and falling into the cycle of reincarnation, so he persisted in practicing virtue, both for his own salvation and that of others.

tieu_de: THE LATE REPENTANCE OF A FEMALE BUTCHER
tom_tat: (Excerpt from the reportage collection "Cause and Effect and the Miraculous Dharma," Volume 1 - Writers' Association Publishing House _author: journalist Hoàng Anh Sướng) Throughout the journey from the North to the South meeting, interviewing, and collecting materials for t
noi_dung:
THE BELATED REPENTANCE OF A FEMALE BUTCHER

(Excerpt from the reportage collection "Karma and the Miraculous Dharma" Volume 1 - Publishing House of Writers _author: journalist Hoang Anh Suong)

Throughout the journey from the North to the South, meeting, interviewing, and collecting materials for this special feature report, I have heard and witnessed too many horrifying, haunting stories about karma and retribution. I realized that: although each person creates karma in different ways—killing, abortion, grave-robbing, destroying temples, breaking Buddhist statues, slaughtering livestock...—the consequences vary for each person, yet the suffering, pain, repentance, regret, and torment of the survivors are all the same. There are many stories that haunt me so much that, when I sit down to write these lines to share with you, my hair still stands on end.standing, goosebumps all over my arms. The story I am about to tell is an example.

🍁Money is a magical potion:

She is Hồ Thị K., born in a poor rural area of Trà Vinh Province. Her parents were farmers. They worked all year long but remained poor. At 17, her parents forced her to marry. Her husband is Trần Văn Th., from the same village, also from a poor family. The day after moving into her husband's house, her parents-in-law made the couple live separately. The assets given by her parents included 2 pots, 1 pan, 10kg of rice, and 200,000 VND. Borrowing additionally from relatives, she bought a used Wave motorcycle and started a pig trading business. After pinching pennies for a few years, they paid off all debts and saved a considerable amount of money. The couple decided to expand their business: trading pigs and slaughtering. From then on, their businessHer family's fortune improved. She immediately opened a slaughterhouse at home. Part of the meat was supplied wholesale to agents, and part was sold retail at the market. She said that each night she slaughtered about 4-5 pigs. During the wedding season or the days leading up to Tet, due to the high demand for pigs for Tet storage, she slaughtered many, sometimes reaching several dozen a day. Early in the morning, she would pull each pig out of the pen to slaughter it; the pigs screamed pitifully, their four legs splayed, clinging tightly to the ground. It seemed they knew their impending death. Her husband gritted his teeth, holding a sharp hook, squinting, stabbing at the pig's throat and then straining his back to drag it away. Some weighed nearly two quintals, strong as buffaloes, yet still stubbornly clung on.All four legs on the ground. Her husband went mad, grabbed a big heavy hammer, and swung it straight at the head. The pig squealed once and fell over. The couple dragged the pig onto the cement porch. The shiny, sharp knife stabbed straight into the throat. Blood gushed into the basin. Sometimes, when bleeding too much, one pig would not be dead yet before another was already being bled. The pig ran around for a while before dying. Blood splattered all over the floor. For any pig that hadn’t bled out completely, her husband would stomp on the belly to get all the blood out.

During her first pregnancy, she suddenly discovered a lump on her neck. At first, it was only as big as a finger, then grew to the size of a chicken egg. A few months later, it became as large as a small bowl, making her neck tilt to one side. She was very worried, but the work of slaughtering, cutting meat, measuring, and counting money kept spinning from morning to night, so she had no time to see a doctor. One day, her best friend met her at the market and said, "K.! The lump on your neck looks terrible. Do you want to die lying on a pile of money? Listen to me, go to the hospital and get checked. Go tomorrow."

Following a friend's advice, early the next morning, she took a bus to Saigon Hospital. After undergoing a bunch of tests, the doctor said, “Go home and roast a chicken to celebrate. The tumor is benign. After surgery, you can be discharged in about ten days.” But three days after the surgery, with the wound not yet healed, she persistently asked the doctor to allow her to be discharged. Back home, the next day, she was already clanging a meat cleaver. “Money is like a magical medicine. Just seeing money makes me immediately feel better,” she said, laughing.

During her second pregnancy, she still worked tirelessly from morning till night. With her huge pregnant belly, she continued to chop and cut. Until the time she experienced premature water breaking at the market. Her husband hurriedly took her to the hospital. The doctor examined her and found that the amniotic fluid was gone and the baby's head was nearly at the cervix, so scissors had to be used to separate the uterine muscles. Unfortunately, the scissors pierced the baby's head, causing a 3cm long, 0.5mm deep wound, with blood gushing out. The baby boy cried inconsolably day and night. Occasionally, he had epileptic seizures. His limbs would convulse, foam would come from his mouth, and his eyes would roll back entirely showing the whites like a boiled pig's eye. Because of this, although she gave birth to a son, she was heartbroken. Every time he had a seizure, shetears welled up again. Many nights, staying awake holding her child, she thought, “Could it be that killing animals brings divine retribution upon me?” Yet she reassured herself, “But there are plenty of people in the slaughtering profession like me whose children are still healthy, and whose families are still rich and prosperous, right? Besides, if everyone who kills animals were to face retribution, then who would dare to slaughter pigs or kill chickens for people to consume every day? Humanity would starve to death.”

🍁The husband acts up:

Staying up at night taking care of the child, feeling sad and worried, her health deteriorated. She was thin, her skin pale and greasy, frequently suffering from headaches and dizziness. One time, while sitting on the bed holding down her son's arms and legs during a seizure, blood poured from her body, soaking the sheets. Dark red blood spread everywhere. She turned pale and collapsed. Her family rushed her to the emergency room. The doctor concluded that she had postpartum hemorrhage and an ovarian cyst, so they carried out methods to stop the bleeding and provided intensive resuscitation, fluid transfusion, and blood transfusion. After stabilizing her, the doctor proceeded to remove the entire ovary because the tumor was large and malignant. Her husband was visibly sad. GiaMy family has been without a male heir for three generations. In my village, the idea of 'valuing men over women' is still very strong. Not having a son to continue the family line is very shameful. The whole village mocks: 'That family is wicked, so God and Buddha punish them by only giving birth to women.' When attending wedding feasts or village events, they have to sit at the lower table, not the upper table. Because of this, her husband always longs to have another son. This boy is sick all the time, and if he has 3-4 epileptic seizures a week, what hope is there.

Since then, he changed his habits and behavior, becoming a completely different person. He threw himself into drinking, gambling, smoking, womanizing, and men... Whenever he drank, he got drunk. When drunk, he would smash everything, hit his sister, and curse her, calling her "immoral, which is why she is infertile." He had all sorts of gambling tricks: Tổ Tôm, dice, lottery, billiards. He always lost. When he lost, he would come home causing trouble, forcing his sister to give him money to continue playing to recover his losses. If she didn’t give it, he would grab her hair, drag her roughly to the pond in front of the house, where she worked long hours cleaning pigs, and push her head into the water until she gave him the money he demanded. Many times, he would take the butcher’s knife and chase her all over the yard and out to the street,He threatened to cut off my ear, to draw my blood. Witnessing that horrifying violence, my mother-in-law could only call out to heaven, call the village and the local authorities to come rescue me. Many times she told me: 'K.! I think maybe Th. is being possessed by a demon or haunted by a ghost. Only ghosts and demons would torment and beat their wife like that. He is naturally gentle, loves his wife and cares for his children. You should invite a shaman to our house to perform an exorcism for him. Otherwise, if this continues, one day he might kill you.' Hearing my mother say that, I could only cover my face and cry. In this world, there are no ghosts or demons. There's only drunkenness, gambling addiction, mother.

Her husband neglected household chores. The burden of the family fell entirely on her shoulders. Slaughtering, cutting meat, buying and selling—all were handled by her alone. Feeling sympathy for her hardworking daughter-in-law, the mother-in-law, over 70 years old, would still fumble into the kitchen early in the morning to boil a pot of water and clean the slaughterhouse to assist her. Until one time, around 4 a.m., half-awake, she stepped into the kitchen. In the thick steam rising from the boiling water, she screamed when she saw the elderly mother with her head submerged in the boiling water. Grabbing her hair to lift her head, her hand felt empty. A chunk of hair came off from the head. Her head was pale white. She fell to the ground, fainting. The mother-in-law's death caused a stir in the entire village. People said: "Those who practice‘The butcher, sooner or later, will also be reaped.’ Hearing that, she was very upset. Her mother-in-law was virtuous, working hard all her life for her husband and children, never stepping out of the village bamboo fence—how could Heaven possibly punish her?

At my mother’s funeral, my sister slaughtered five pigs in a row to offer to our mother and to host a feast for the neighbors who came to help. In the afternoon, she went to the village pagoda, inviting the nun to our house to perform the ceremony and recite sutras. Seeing the five pig heads lined up on the altar, the nun called my sister over and explained: "When someone dies, everyone hopes their soul will be liberated to the realm of the Buddhas. Slaughtering so many pigs like this will create additional negative karma. The deceased will suffer greatly from being reborn as an animal to repay debts, and the living will also face severe karmic consequences." For some reason, as soon as my sister heard the nun say this, her hands and legs became weak. A stream of energy ran from her feet up toThe top of her head made her shiver, giving her goosebumps. She burst into tears out of regret. Her mother-in-law had worked hard all her life. Now that she had passed away, she killed up to five pigs to show her final filial respect, not realizing it would be considered unfilial. She immediately asked a nun to organize a memorial ceremony to dedicate merit to her mother. For 49 days, every day she went to the temple to chant sutras for her mother and listen to the teachings of Buddha. She took refuge in the Triple Gem with the Dharma name Diệu Minh. However, due to making a living, she still has not given up the slaughtering profession. Every day, she still has to use a knife and chopping board to slaughter and chop.

🍁A terrible disaster struck the son :

One night at the end of 2005, she dreamed that her husband was dragging a piglet onto the table to slaughter it. Throwing it down, looking closely, it turned out to be her son. Startled, she woke up drenched in sweat. She was extremely anxious, confused, not knowing what the horrific dream could signify. She fretted all week. Until one afternoon. She was bathing her 5-year-old son, who often suffered seizures and epilepsy. Her husband stumbled home from somewhere, swaying as he approached her, his voice slurred, reeking of alcohol: "Give me some money. I’m going to get it." She angrily retorted: "What money? You spend every month drinking with your friends."tea, prostitution, gambling. I rush back and forth to make a living to support this household. Having enough food to fill my mouth is a blessing. Where would I get money to supply to the addicts?” As soon as she finished speaking, she suddenly saw a bright flash of a knife being swung. She quickly dodged. “Thuk.” The knife stabbed her son's neck. Blood spurted like a fountain. A few minutes later, he died. She fainted. Her husband collapsed face down onto their son's blood-soaked chest, coughing up harshly.

The death of our child helped her husband come to his senses. He quit drinking, gambling, and visiting prostitutes, and stayed at home to take care of the family. The peaceful life lasted about a year. One day, while going out, Ms. K. noticed blood. The abdominal pains were like someone was cutting through her intestines and liver. Some days she went 3-4 times. The severity of the abdominal pain increased day by day. The bleeding became heavier. She became very thin. Mr. Th. took her to Cho Ray Hospital for examination. The doctor concluded that she had rectal cancer. Emergency surgery and chemotherapy for some time were needed. Ms. K. recounted: “Those were the most terrible days of my life. I had done manual labor since I was little, had good health, yet during the chemotherapy...Chemicals, I can't eat or sleep. Every time I eat, I vomit, my body is weak like jelly. In the scorching heat of mid-summer, I still have to wrap myself in blankets, my body always curled up from the cold. Mouth sore and dry with bitterness, hands and feet limp, darkened. My body is nothing but skin and bones. No medicine can knock a person down as quickly and brutally as this. Many people with cancer, after undergoing chemotherapy once or twice, ask to refuse further treatment and go home to die because they cannot bear the side effects of the chemicals. Once, I had severe chemical poisoning. I also wanted to give up and not go to the hospital for chemotherapy because I was so scared. But thinking of my little child, I forced myself to endure.

The doctor suggested that she undergo four cycles of chemotherapy, but by the second cycle, her health was exhausted, and she was severely anemic, so the doctor sent her home to rest for a week. That night, she tossed and turned, unable to sleep. Near dawn, too tired, she dozed off. In her fitful sleep, she dreamed that she was walking to the pigpen behind the house. She suddenly heard a voice calling: "Dear, pour some water for me again, the mosquitoes bite me so badly." She clearly recognized it as her mother-in-law's voice. But she had already passed away. Looking around, there was no one there. She only saw a large white pig, with a few black spots on its back. Feeling uneasy, she stepped closer. The pig then spoke:"Put the mosquito repellent on me, dear. Right now there's no repellent, the mosquitoes are biting me too much, child. I'm already like a pig." She woke up with a start, scared.

Early in the morning, she forced herself to walk out to the backyard, where the pigpen was. She was startled. A pig weighing more than 100 kilograms, white with black spots, was lying in the pen just like in her dream. She suddenly thought of the village nun's words at her mother's funeral: "Killing a pig for such an offering, the person who dies will have to be reincarnated as a pig to repay the debt." She then went closer, stroked the pig, and chanted Buddha's name while tears fell. That evening, while sitting and chanting the Medicine Buddha Sutra, her daughter reported that the pig had stopped eating and had died. She burst into tears. Abandoning the rest of the sutra chanting, she asked her husband to drive the motorbike to meet the nun at the temple. Hearing her recount the dreamA white pig with black spots, the nun said: Buddhist teachings hold that after death, if a person has unfinished karma, they will be reincarnated back into the mortal world. According to the law of cause and effect, if in life one does many good deeds, they will be reincarnated as a human in a place of happiness. If one has sins, they will be reincarnated as animals, including pigs. In the Buddhist world, there have been many suspected cases of people reincarnated as pigs. The most famous story, clearly documented, about a person being reincarnated as a pig is the story that took place in Taixing County, Jiangbei, China. The story goes: in Taixing County, there was a man named Thi Khánh Chung, unemployed, with a violent temperament, who often bullied the common people, causingThe local people were fearful and kept their distance. In 1923, Thi Khanh Chung suddenly fell gravely ill and had to lie bedridden, his life flickering like an oil lamp in the wind. At that time, a monk named Van Thuy passed through Thai Hung district. Hearing the local people’s account, the monk understood Thi Khanh Chung’s situation, felt compassion, approached him, and said: 'All the bad things you usually didn’t avoid doing have accumulated as sins, and now the time for retribution is near. It would be best for you to repent quickly to make amends for the sins you have committed. If not, after death, you will surely be reincarnated as a pig.'

Thi Khánh Chung knew that his illness was incurable and that he would not live much longer. Hearing this from the monk, he was extremely terrified. The evil deeds he had committed, even if he regretted them now, were already too late, but thinking about being reincarnated as a pig in the next life, Thi Khánh Chung felt unwilling to accept it, so he reluctantly clasped his left hand over his chest, pretending to be remorseful. The monk standing beside him saw this and sighed, saying: “What a pity! What a pity! You only worship the Buddha with one hand, making it difficult to avoid the fate of being reborn as a pig. This is the result of karma. Even so, your left hand may be exempt, not having to become a pig in the next life, and additionally, you can avoid the karma of beingkill.”

A few days later, Thi Khánh Chung passed away. The people in Thái Hưng were all rejoiced because the wicked person who had been tormenting them was dead. Seven days after Thi Khánh Chung's death, the neighboring household, Thái Đại Trụ, had a litter of pigs, among which there was a very unusual one. The front left leg of this pig was shaped and sized exactly like a human left hand, complete with fingers and even fingernails. When this pig walks, its left leg does not touch the ground but is always held in a praying position. When people saw this pig, they immediately thought of the words of the monk Vân Thủy. Thus, the news about the pig being a reincarnation from a past life, ThiKhanh Chung became the hot topic of discussion among the people of Thai Hung District. Khanh Chung’s family, feeling pity, spent a large sum of money to buy this pig and then brought it to Bao Hoa Pagoda in Shanghai to release it. The strange thing was that every time someone came to visit the pagoda garden, this pig would hide in the middle of the other pigs, as if it didn’t want to be seen by anyone. This strange phenomenon made people believe even more that the pig was the reincarnation of Thi Khanh Chung. Many people came to take photos of the pig and hung them everywhere as a reminder of karma, to advise people to live well and do useful deeds for life.

Repentance

The story of the nun haunted Ms. K. endlessly. She went to Saigon for further treatment. One day, instead of staying in the patient ward, she went out to wander the streets. She wandered aimlessly. Her feet suddenly stopped in front of a temple in District 10. She went in to worship Buddha, and unexpectedly, she met the abbot. Somehow, she recounted her entire life to the monk. He said: “Have you seen that what you sow, you reap? Only when you have cancer, are cut open, and suffer in pain do you realize the daily suffering of sentient beings that you torment and kill. When karmic retribution comes, no one can be blamed; you are responsible for yourself.”I endure it, causing suffering to the children, affecting the family's happiness. When a child kills an animal, it is extremely painful. The child is afraid of dying, and it is also afraid of dying. It is full of resentment, and its spirit keeps lingering around the child waiting for revenge. Only by practicing cultivation, reciting Buddha's name, eating vegetarian, and releasing life back to the sentient beings can perhaps there be some benefit.

Listening to the teacher's lecture, she began to clearly understand the reason why she had cancer, why her mother-in-law and her son died painfully and tragically, and why her family was not happy. She began to accept the karmic retribution. Instead of wailing in grief like the other patients in the ward, she diligently recited the Buddha's name, even though every time she underwent chemotherapy, her body felt hot, restless, very painful, and miserable. The fellow patients in the same ward, seeing that she was devoted to Buddhism, gave her a book titled 'The Law of Cause and Effect Across Three Lifetimes.' She read up to page 26, which described the story of pigs telling a monk about how, when people tied them up and slaughtered them, it caused them pain and resentment.Hating, moaning, begging in every way, she cried bitterly. Then she read it to her husband. She prayed to Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva to help her, giving her the chance to return to being a good person, not killing or harming living beings, sincerely cultivating, using merit to dedicate for the sentient beings she had once killed. From that point, she decided to become a lifelong vegetarian, give up the profession of pig killing, diligently practice and recite Buddha’s name. Her mind was no longer fearful or confused, and she no longer had nightmares at night.

Every day, reading the book “Buddha Transforms Cancer Cells” by Venerable Dao Chung, she increasingly believes in the miraculous power of Buddhism. Venerable Dao Chung was once a famous doctor (Dr. Quach Hue Tran) specializing in treating cancer, but later, the venerable also contracted this deadly disease. Through the miraculous practice of chanting sutras and reciting the Buddha's name, the Venerable escaped the hands of death and has helped many people overcome it. The book “Reciting the Buddha’s Name to Transform Cancer Cells” contains invaluable teachings and wonderful experiences for defeating cancer by the Venerable, including four articles sharing the heartfelt experiences of professors and doctors, all of whom are people withexperience of overcoming illness, all of them are cancer patients... Practicing according to those teachings, every time she recited the sutras, she lightly rubbed her lower abdomen, the location of the removed rectal tumor. And strangely, her pain gradually lessened. Her skin became rosy, her hair grew back, she ate well and slept soundly. This miraculous Buddhist practice transformed her entire family. Her husband now also took refuge in the Three Jewels, practiced Buddhist mindfulness, with a peaceful mind and body, and a stable life.

Through me, she wants to send a message to those who still practice killing animals daily: "Sincerely repent for the sins you have committed against sentient beings. Please change your profession, do not harm or kill sentient beings, as it harms not only yourself but also those around you. Cause and effect never fail, you all." From the painful lesson of her life, she also wants to send a message to the readers of Tuoi Tre newspaper and Life:

🍁“Try to eat vegetarian. Meat-eaters, when eating, how can they know how much boundless resentment from the animals is in the piece of meat they are eating. Each piece of meat is filled with fear and resentment throughout its cells. Illness also comes from here. If we eat the flesh of sentient beings, the karmic retribution of disease torments the body painfully. Try to release life, repent for karmic obstacles by chanting sutras, reciting Buddha’s name, bowing to Buddha to create blessings. No matter how wealthy one’s money is, if one keeps killing and eating meat, illnesses will be endless, and life will not have any happiness.”

Thanks to the source from Facebook of journalist Hoàng Anh Sướng

tieu_de: THE GOLDEN AND JEWEL TEACHINGS OF THE ANCESTORS
tom_tat: * MASTER AN QUANG teaches: A practitioner who does not vow to be reborn in the Pure Land, no matter how skillful their practice is, in this era cannot escape the cycle of birth and death. * MASTER TĨNH AM teaches: Those who are concerned with lower practices
noi_dung:
THE GOLDEN AND JEWELLED TEACHINGS OF THE ANCESTORS

* MASTER AN QUANG teaches: A practitioner who does not aspire for rebirth in the Pure Land, no matter how skilled in cultivation, in today's era cannot escape the cycle of birth and death.

* MASTER TINH AM teaches: A person who focuses on cultivating virtue and performing good deeds, no matter how great the merit, cannot achieve liberation from birth and death. He said: The greater the good deeds, the heavier the burden of birth and death; at the moment of death, if a thought of attachment arises, one will surely be trapped in the cycle of reincarnation for countless kalpas.

* VENERABLE GREAT MASTER THIEN DAO taught: Reciting the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, if ten thousand people practice, ten thousand people will be reborn, which is called ten thousand people practice and ten thousand people attain. He said, even if one’s Buddha recitation has not yet reached single-minded concentration, if the Vigil Practice is organized carefully, anyone can be reborn.

* VENERABLE Zen Master TRUNG PHONG taught: A person who recites the Buddha's name without aspiring for rebirth, no matter how advanced their practice is, it is only illusory, because it goes against the Buddha's teachings.

* MASTER LIEN TRI teaches: The three baskets of sutras and the twelve divisions of teachings—whoever wishes to study them to attain enlightenment may study them; the eighty-four thousand methods—whoever wishes to practice them may practice them. As for me, I only recite a single Buddha name, Amitabha Buddha, to be reborn in the Pure Land.

* MASTER QUAN DINH teaches: In this degenerate age of the Dharma, all sutras and repentance rituals no longer have the ability to save sentient beings; only the Buddha name, Amitabha Buddha, can accomplish it.

* MASTER LY BINH NAM teaches: People of this time, if they do not recite the Buddha’s name to be reborn in the Pure Land, then if they are not foolish, they are reckless and deluded!

* VENERABLE TỊNH KHÔNG said: In this era, anyone who does not recite the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, if not foolish, is also deluded! But ultimately, delusion is also foolishness...

It is because of a lack of wisdom that one doubts the Buddha's words. It is because of arrogance that one acts against the Buddha's words. How can a person who does not follow the Buddha's teachings be worthy of the name of a Buddhist? If one does not wish to attain enlightenment in this lifetime, then they can say whatever they want, do whatever they want, and fall into any hell they wish, and there is nothing to prevent it! In His practice centers, apart from chanting Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, He does not allow diverse forms of practice. Over the past years, many people have chanted Buddha's name to attain rebirth everywhere, and ultimately, all have practiced according to His dharma teachings.

All the Patriarchs teach sentient beings in this degenerate age to recite the Buddha’s name and aspire to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, in order to attain Buddhahood in a single lifetime. We should sincerely follow the teachings of the Patriarchs in practice, as this is the most secure way.

In fact, it is not only the Patriarchs who teach this; Shakyamuni Buddha also teaches this extensively in the scriptures.

•• The Amitabha Sutra records that the Buddha taught four times that one must generate the aspiration to be reborn in the Western Pure Land. Whoever hears him speak of the Western Land and believes it, then vows to be reborn there, and thereafter sincerely recites the name of Amitabha Buddha for one to seven days with focused devotion, at the moment of death Amitabha Buddha and the assembly of saints will appear to guide them to the Western Pure Land.

The Buddha clearly taught this; why do his disciples not have faith? The Buddha never speaks falsely, so why do those who study Buddhism doubt the Buddha's teachings?

•• In the Infinite Life Sutra, the Buddha said countless times that sentient beings must wholeheartedly recite the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land. If anyone truly believes, vows to be reborn, and single-mindedly recites the Buddha's name, then even if they only recite ten times (before the moment of death) and do not attain rebirth, Amitabha Buddha would vow not to become a Buddha. So why do we not follow the teachings to achieve rebirth and Buddhahood, but instead heed what worldly people say?

•• The Great Collection Sutra teaches that in this Last Dharma Age, even though countless people practice, it is difficult to find a person who attains realization (meaning it is hard to transcend the cycle of birth and death). But the Buddha said that only those who recite the Buddha’s name and seek birth in the Pure Land will be liberated from the cycle of rebirth.

•• In the Avatamsaka Sutra, the virtuous child Sudhana attained the Dharma Body, and his fundamental teacher, Bodhisattva Manjushri, taught him to recite the Buddha's name. The virtuous friends he sought guidance from—first, it was Master Duc Van who taught him to recite the Buddha's name, and the last was Bodhisattva Samantabhadra who taught the ten great vows and to aspire to be reborn in the Western Pure Land (meaning also to recite the Buddha’s name to seek rebirth). If a Bodhisattva who is wise and has realized the nature of mind still needs to recite the Buddha’s name, why shouldn’t we recite the Buddha’s name? Namo Amitabha Buddha

tieu_de: ‍♀️  OVERVIEW OF TYPES OF "GHOSTS" AND THE REALMS OF GHOSTS ACCORDING TO PRACTITIONERS 🧟‍
tom_tat: 👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇 (very meaningful, should read through)
noi_dung:
‍♀️ OVERVIEW OF TYPES OF "GHOSTS" AND THE REALMS OF GHOSTS COMMONLY ENCOUNTERED BY PRACTITIONERS 🧟‍

👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇

(very meaningful, should read)

👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇

"Ma" in Sanskrit is called Mara, in Chinese it is translated as Sha, because it often robs merit, and kills the life of wisdom of practitioners. "Ma" also refers to the conditions that cause destruction, making practitioners falter in their path, become frantic and lose mindfulness, or generate wrong views, commit evil deeds, and ultimately fall into degeneration. Actions that generate wisdom and merit, leading sentient beings to Nirvana, are called Buddha's work. Conditions that destroy good roots, causing beings to suffer and descend in the cycle of birth and death, are Ma's work. The longer one practices, the higher one's path, the more clearly one sees how fierce and strong Ma's influence is.

There are many drugs, but basically they are of three types: Affliction Demon, External Demon, and Heavenly Demon.

Affliction Spirits indicate afflictions such as attachment, anger, ignorance, arrogance, doubt, ill will ... up to various kinds of spirits: the five aggregates, the six sense bases, the twelve sense fields, the eighteen elements. This type of spirit is also called Internal Spirit, arising from a confused and deluded mind, thus it must be dispelled by a sincere, clear, and enlightened mind. Ordinary people already have their own karma, and together with the collective karma living in the environment, most people around them have malicious natures and severe karmic obstacles, making it easy to trigger afflictions. Some cannot withstand the allure of the five sensory objects, thus falling into downfall. Some, due to adverse circumstances, experience sorrow and grief, making their aspiration to advance...eliminate and disappear. These occurrences cause practitioners to feel mild sadness and resentment, which can lead to pain and illness; in severe cases, they may become disheartened and abandon the path, or despair and end their own life; even more dangerously, they inevitably lead to losing all good sentiments toward both monastics and laypeople, causing avoidance and dislike, generating contempt, division, and criticism, disbelieving in cause and effect, committing evil deeds and consequently falling into the three lower realms.

To counter this kind of demon, a practitioner must contemplate that afflictions are illusory, agitating, oppressive, binding, dark, and only cause suffering for oneself and others. By ending afflictions, we return to the true mind, free, liberated, cool, clear, and joyfully mysterious. One should contemplate attachment from the five aggregates up to the eighteen senses in the same way. In the Lotus Sutra, the Buddha says: "Do not be infatuated with coarse forms, sounds, smells, tastes, touch, or dharmas. If one becomes attached and greedy, one will surely be burned by it." Long ago, Bodhisattva Manjushri asked a celestial maiden: "How do you regard the eighteen senses?" The celestial maiden replied: "As if seeing the world being burned by a conflagration!"

"These are words of warning to destroy the type of disturbing demons."

Afflictive spirits or Internal demons, if not subdued, will inevitably attract External demons from outside to cause harm. An old saying goes: "If there are petty people inside the house, petty people will come from outside. If there are noble people inside, noble people will come from outside." Similarly, when a thief tries to break in, if the homeowner remains calm and admonishes, the thief will surely be frightened and leave. If the homeowner panics and pleads, that behavior is essentially inviting the thief into the house.

Foreign Demons are enchanting demonic creatures from the outside. When practitioners have a little skill, they are tested and disturbed by them. This type can be divided into three categories: Bo Ma, Ai Ma, and Nao Ma.

👉 Bố Ma is a type of ghost that likes to terrorize, causing people to be fearful. This kind of ghost often takes the form of tigers, wolves, snakes, centipedes, or other strange ferocious animals, or terrifying demon-like figures to scare practitioners. These appearances can be extremely illusory, such as being headless, having multiple heads, multiple arms, multiple eyes; or having a human body with an animal head, or an animal body with a human head, or wielding weapons, or spewing red fire. If a practitioner becomes frightened, they can immediately have their mindfulness disrupted and often descend into madness. In such situations, one should consider that all these appearances are false, that the ghost can only destroy the illusory body but cannot harm the true mind. After contemplating this, one can remain calm without fear of death, at peace.If you focus on chanting Buddha's name or reciting mantras, it will withdraw by itself.

👉 2. Aima is a type of demon that agitates lust to the point of intoxicating the mind with the five sensory objects. They take the form of beautiful naked men or women; or the appearance of parents, siblings, or close relatives; even the body of the Buddha or Bodhisattva with dignified features to entice. If someone likes delicious food, they transform into sumptuous dishes with fragrant aromas to offer; if someone favors treasures, they appear as strange animals holding jewels to present. Depending on what the practitioner desires, they immediately manifest that. They can use their demonic powers to make people attain wrong meditative states, wrong wisdom, eloquence, and supernatural powers to know the past and future. Those who do not understand may think they have attained enlightenment, allall believed and obeyed; but in truth, that person was mentally disturbed, specializing in using demonic magic to deceive the world.

- There was a Vietnamese monk practicing at Bang Long Pagoda in Laos. While meditating, he saw a group of naked beautiful women holding hands and dancing. The monk could not calm his mind, so he sincerely recited the Buddha's name, and the vision disappeared.

- In the past, at Chung Nam Mountain Temple in China, there was a monk practicing meditation. One day, when he felt cold and hungry, a sudden thought of wanting to eat arose, and he suddenly saw a young woman bringing food as an offering. The young woman knelt and poured the food into the bowl, urging the monk to eat immediately before it got cold and lost its taste. The monk, feeling hungry, wanted to partake at once, but thinking it was not yet mealtime, patiently told her to set it aside and wait until the proper time to eat. The young woman, hearing this, seemed offended and left. After a while, at the proper hour, the monk opened the bowl and saw it was full of wriggling maggots. Only then did he realize that by giving in to a fleeting desire, he had invited a demonic illusion; fortunately, he had some measure of mental discipline.stop eating dirty food and committing the offense of killing.

- Another monk who also practiced meditation in the mountains felt lonely and longed for some company. One day, an old woman came with two beautiful young girls, saying their home was in the village at the foot of the mountain, and they sought the monk's instruction in Dharma. Initially, the monk had no suspicions and began teaching them. This continued for some time until one day the old woman requested that the two girls be allowed to serve as attendants, taking care of chores and meals to ease the monk's burden. The monk, upon hearing this, felt a suspicious thought briefly arise and sternly refused. The three of them seemed ashamed and left. The monk secretly followed them around a bend but suddenly lost sight of them. Upon looking further, the path was blocked, and there was no house.Not a single door in sight, only three ancient tree trunks, one large and two small. He thought that these were tree spirits causing trouble; he wanted to strike them with his hammer or set them on fire to prevent future trouble. Just as he was thinking this, he suddenly saw three people appear, begging for forgiveness and asking for their lives.

Therefore, one should know, when the mind is peaceful and the environment is calm, delusions arise and demons manifest; practitioners must remember this.

👉 3. Não Ma is a type of demon that specializes in disturbing and confusing meditators. Each species has its own subtle traits and appears according to its own hour; roughly, there are three species per hour, making thirty-six types of spirits in twelve hours. For example, at the hour of Tiger (Dần), there are tigers, leopards, bears; at the hour of Cat (Mão), there are cats, rabbits, foxes; at the hour of Dragon (Thìn), there are dragons, fish, eels... In the meditation manual called Tọa Thiền Chỉ Quán, there is mention of a type of demon called Du Lạp Kiết Chi, which the Chinese call Dôi Dịch, having a head and face like a pipa instrument, four eyes, two mouths, and often likes to stir up and disturb meditators. They wait for the practitioner to chant or recite, then transform into worms or insects, either crawling over the entire face and head; or slipping into the mouth, nostrils, eyes, or ears; orThey crawl into the armpits and stomach of the practitioner to bite and sting. Sometimes they cry loudly into the ears, creating a noisy, headache-inducing sound; or suddenly embrace the person, reaching out to find them but not touching. They can also transform into the five sensory phenomena, either in accordance, contrary, or neither accordance nor contrary, creating unpredictable illusions, making the practitioner restless and unable to perceive properly, easily losing concentration. To counter the thirty-six types of spirits and beasts, simply call their names according to the hour and reprimand them.

For the Demon Duo, one should recite the Three Refuges and Five Precepts or the basic precepts, because they are the kinds of spirits that violate precepts. By doing so, they will immediately disappear. Alternatively, a general method of countering them is to focus the mind on proper meditation, or to concentrate strictly on reciting mantras and mindful remembrance of the Buddha, and they will dissolve.

When encountering many obstructive spirits, the ancients also had a method of buying two mirrors, then retreating to seclusion for forty-nine days, focusing on chanting the Great Compassion Mantra or the Chuẩn Đề Mantra to empower the mirrors. Afterwards, hang the two mirrors high, tilted down to the place where one usually sits to practice chanting, one in front and one behind. If spirits come, they are immediately captured and appear in the mirror, at which point the practitioner can choose to expel or punish them as desired. This magical mirror should occasionally be cleaned with a clean cloth and empowered with the mantra again. Doing so not only reminds one of the purity of the mind but also enhances its efficacy. This is the way to use mirrors.to combat internal demons and external demons according to the experience of the predecessors.

To elaborate further, External spirits are also spirits associated with heterodox paths. According to the observations of the author and many fellow practitioners, those who in previous or current lives practiced heterodox teachings later returned to Buddhism; or those who merely rely on the Three Jewels, but whose ancestors all followed heterodox paths, are often disturbed by external spirits. The practice of heterodox paths never escapes defilements, and remains in the cycle of self-conceit, attachment to fame and power, so adherents of heterodox paths often form factions and do not want those connected to their group to practice another faith. The author has a monastic friend, gentle and kind-hearted, but in their practiceBeing constantly disturbed by external demons. It is regrettable because this friend still retains seeds of external heresy and does not sincerely use Buddhist teachings to counteract demonic practices. In moments of being trapped by the demons, he went to many places seeking salvation from followers of heterodox schools. As a result, he completely fell into heresy; outwardly, he maintained the appearance of monastic life, but inwardly, he devoted himself to esoteric practices, rejecting the worship of the Buddha and the chanting of sutras, considering them to be attachment to forms.

There was also a female Buddhist practitioner, very kind by nature, but she often encountered disturbances from external demons. One day, while she was practicing, she was disrupted by heterodox spirits and heard a voice: "Your ancestors all practiced our Five Elements sect, why do you not return to your original roots, instead of following Buddhism?" Terrified, she sincerely recited the Buddha's name, and with each recitation she saw a ray of light emanate to cover her body, preventing the demons from harming her. They angrily warned: "Do not be arrogant because of the Buddha's powers; there will be our superior coming here to teach you a lesson." After saying this, they withdrew. At that moment, she suddenly heard the voice of a venerable masterThe benevolent spirit said: "They are jealous because you have taken refuge in the Three Jewels, instead of following the ancestral way and worshiping them. Right now, you should make the Vajra Fist mudra with both hands, press your thumbs against the base joint of your ring fingers, and clench them tightly. Keep it like that and sincerely recite mantras or the Buddha's name continuously, because soon some of their elders will come here, using the five-thunder spells to attack and capture your soul. Their forces are numerous, and I can only assist to a certain extent, since on your own, you can't drive them away. Your strength is limited, and over a long period, it may become unbearable to resist, so it is better to enter a temple to cultivate in order to avoid disaster." She immediately followed the instructions, clenching her hands into the Vajra Fist mudra andreciting the Great Compassion Mantra. Suddenly, she heard a loud tumult, then a flash of lightning struck down heavily like a hammer, burning painfully across her head. She immediately let go of all thoughts, devotedly and desperately recited the mantra, no longer aware of the outside world. After a while, she heard the surroundings fall silent, and her body and mind returned to a calm, normal state.

After that, the young lady entered the temple, but because her elderly mother was often sick and there was no one to take care of her, she was forced to return home to handle livelihood matters to provide for her. After a period of separation, the author heard news that she often spoke of mystical matters and realized she could not resist, thus becoming possessed by spirits, which caused silent pity! Therefore, those who previously had connections with foreign sects but later returned to practice Buddhism should look at this example and be cautious.

👉 3. The Celestial Demon is a type of demon in the Heaven of Transforming Freedom, belonging to the sixth layer of the Desire Realm. This type of demon has merits and enjoys the supreme mystical pleasures of the five senses, considering them as absolute bliss, holding power over sensual desires, and not wanting anyone to escape their domain. When a practitioner reaches a fairly high level of cultivation, their mind-light manifests, and the light penetrates the Heaven of Transforming, causing the demon palaces to tremble. They immediately become aware and, fearing that someone might be liberated and that their kin would be reduced, they try to sabotage.

They appear in many forms, either to threaten, to entice, or to assist in corrupting one’s determination, mind, and spiritual powers in order to deceive practitioners; they also take turns lurking constantly, never leaving, waiting for a convenient opportunity. If a practitioner has even a moment of negligence, they immediately invade, urging one to commit actions against morality, and the life of practice is considered ruined.

In the Treatise on the Awakening of Faith, Great Master Ma Ming once advised:

"When a practitioner cultivates in purity, they are often disturbed by celestial demons, heterodox beings, or ghosts and spirits. They appear in terrifying forms to frighten, or in beautiful male or female forms to seduce. Sometimes they manifest as Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, or Devas with all kinds of virtuous and solemn appearances; or speak of Dharani practices, or the practices of charity, precepts, patience, diligence, meditation, and wisdom; or talk about the principles of equality, emptiness, formlessness, and desirelessness, praising the state of having no hatred, no attachment, no cause, no result, an ultimate void and silence, claiming this to be true Nirvana... Or they cause the practitioner to know their past lives and see the future."(clairvoyance), perceiving clearly the thoughts of everyone (telepathy), up to having unhindered skill in debate. They cause practitioners to become attached to worldly fame and profit, have unstable temperament, easily get angry or laugh, like to sleep, have many illnesses, be prone to emotional sensitivity, sometimes be very diligent, other times be lazy and negligent. Or they incite practitioners to have doubtful minds and disbelief, worry a lot, abandon basic practices and return to following miscellaneous rites, become immersed in deceitful worldly matters. Or they make practitioners experience a partial resemblance to Samadhi, able to remain in meditative absorption from one day up to seven days, with body and mind at peace, unaware of hunger or thirst; yet this is due to the power of heretical attainment granted by external teachers, notYou must truly be in Samadhi. Otherwise, it may cause the practitioner to eat and drink irregularly, sometimes more, sometimes less, with their complexion constantly changing. When encountering such situations, the practitioner must use wisdom to observe, strive to maintain mindfulness, and not develop attachment that leads them into the net of evil. Only by persisting in this way can one be free from demonic obstacles.

👉 In conclusion, to be more specific, there are only Internal demons and External demons; Heavenly demons also fall under the category of External demons. However, the reason for establishing Heavenly demons as a separate category is to make practitioners aware of their subtle and dangerous destructive nature. Besides Affliction demons, External demons, and Heavenly demons as mentioned above, the sutras also mention Illness demons and Death demons. Because illness often diminishes a practitioner’s progress, and dying before achieving realization can cause one to lose the fruit of the path, they are called "demons." However, Illness demons and Death demons generally refer to the obstacles of illness and death related to the four elements body on the spiritual path, and do not have a destructive or disruptive nature.to kill the spiritual mind in the true sense of 'demon.' Therefore, this is briefly omitted and not mentioned.

The cultivation strength of people nowadays is mostly disrupted by afflictive demons or external demons and is not enough to provoke the Heavenly demons. This type of demon only approaches those with high levels of cultivation. If the Heavenly demons are determined to destroy, those with ordinary cultivation levels have little hope of escaping. In the Shurangama Sutra, out of concern for the many perils on the path of practice, the Buddha advised meditators to also recite secret mantras, so that they could rely on divine power for protection, escape from demonic dangers, and achieve correct concentration. Master Yin Guang taught: "At first glance, it seems that the Shurangama Sutra has a different view from the Pure Land, but upon deep reflection, one can see that this sutra implicitly praises and supports the Pure Land."

Why is that? Because a practitioner who has attained the third stage of sainthood, Anāgāmi, can still be led astray by demonic visions, the practice of reciting the Buddha's name to be reborn in the Pure Land becomes even more crucial, as under the protective light of Amitābha Buddha, there is no longer the danger of demons.

Therefore, considering the path of practicing the Way, before being reborn in the Pure Land, practicing Pure Land Buddhism can also encounter demonic obstacles. However, most of this is due to the practitioner not understanding the teachings or not skillfully regulating the mind, allowing inner demons to arise and thereby attracting external demons to cause disruption. If one maintains a focused mind, then by the power and merit of reciting the Buddha's name, external demons cannot do anything, and afflictions will gradually be eliminated. Therefore, for those practicing Pure Land Buddhism, encounters with demonic visions are rare. In contrast, for those practicing meditation, demonic visions appear more frequently because they rely solely on their own effort.

A meditation practitioner must meet the following five conditions in order to hope for success on the path:

- First, strict moral discipline;

- Second, a quick and clear intellect;

- Third, a thorough understanding of the Dharma, skillfully distinguishing between right and wrong appearances, truth and illusion;

- Fourth, a strong and steadfast will;

- And fifth, relying on a virtuous teacher who is well-versed in the scriptures and has many years of meditation experience, for guidance.

If any of those five conditions are missing, one is easily afflicted by spiritual calamities. The ancients taught: "Khô mộc đường tiền thác lộ đa!" This phrase means: in the foundation of meditation, there are many binding obstacles. Therefore, to practice meditation successfully, one must be a person of sharp wisdom and superior disposition. The venerable masters of the Zen tradition, when transmitting the Dharma, also advised: "Those of the highest superior disposition only; do not easily promise acceptance." (Phi thượng thượng căn. Thận vật khinh hứa). These words are enough to prove the above observation.

In the Treatise on Awakening Faith, after combining a general overview of the essence of Mahayana teachings and presenting the method of practice, Master Paramārtha then said: "The Saha world is full of strong afflictions, true faith is difficult to sustain, and it is rarely that one meets a Buddha to hear the Dharma; the practice path is fraught with many dangers and obstacles. Therefore, one should know that the Tathagata possesses supreme expedient means, teaching the way to aspire for birth in the Pure Land elsewhere. As stated in the sutra: if one concentrates on reciting Buddha Amitābha, dedicates the merits accumulated from practice, and aspires to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, one will attain the blissful world of Ultimate Happiness, always seeing the Buddha and hearing the Dharma, without regressing. If a practitioner follows this method of practice, they will surely attain it."enter the concentration aggregation.

As mentioned above, we see that focusing on reciting the Buddha's name is a miraculous method to escape from demonic troubles and quickly achieve right concentration.

Ten Essentials of Buddha Recitation

(Venerable Thich Thien Tam)

tieu_de: THE PARADOX OF THE UNDERWORLD - THE OVERWORLD
tom_tat: During the Qing dynasty, in Ly village, there was a woman who was a daughter-in-law in a farming family. Every morning and noon, she often brought meals to the fields for the workers in the house to eat. During that period
noi_dung:
THE PARADOX OF THE YIN WORLD - THE YANG WORLD

During the Qing dynasty, in Ly village, there was a woman who became a daughter-in-law in a farming family. Every morning and noon, she often carried meals to the fields for the workers in her household.

During that time, whenever she went or returned with meals, she always caught glimpses of a woman following her—sometimes on her right, sometimes on her left, sometimes hidden, sometimes visible. Suspicious, she asked the fellow villagers who were going or returning alongside her whether they saw that woman. They all replied that they saw nothing. Hearing this, she was very frightened, for she realized it was a ghost.

Later, when she was at home, she also saw that woman either appearing in the garden or near the edge of the wall, but not entering the house. A few times she tried to strike and get closer to look clearly, the woman would run away to a distance, and when she went into the house, the woman returned to her original spot.

She had no choice but to use her mind from afar to ask the woman:

– Who are you? Why do you keep following me like this?

The spirit answered (mind to mind):

– In a previous life, you and I both worked as concubines for a famous wealthy man. You were jealous that he favored me, so you falsely accused me of having an affair with another man. Because of that, I was killed by him in a hidden place full of hatred. Therefore, in this life, I sought you out to take revenge, but ironically, in this life, you are a dutiful daughter-in-law often protected by many benevolent spirits, so I cannot get close to take my revenge.

Therefore, every day I followed her to look for good opportunities. But with the protection of such a benevolent deity, I would probably never be able to take revenge. So, I suggested to her, let us sincerely recite the name of Buddha Amitabha ten thousand times, dedicating the merit to me, to both resolve my resentment and help me attain liberation.

She was very pleased upon hearing this and immediately made the vow to recite Buddha's name. Every time she recited one phrase, she saw the spirit of that woman bow once, and after completing ten thousand recitations, the woman was no longer seen! This event, she recounted in her old age.

(Excerpt from “Duyệt Vi Thảo Đường Bút Ký” - Kỉ Hiểu Lam, Qing Dynasty)

WHERE IS THE CONTRADICTION?

Without long-windedness, I will say it directly:

We living humans have physical bodies, so we are obstructed from seeing invisible beings, cannot see the deities, gods, spirits, souls, or ghosts... thus there are many things we do not know. Compared to the soul of a deceased person, human understanding is very limited.

But on the contrary, because humans have a physical body, they can do things that spirits, and even some deities or celestial beings, cannot do, or if they can, the effectiveness is far inferior; that is the ability to cultivate.

Only when having a physical body can one recite the Buddha's name, chant sutras, practice mantras, give alms, do charitable deeds, release lives, perform rituals, observe precepts, or engage in other meritorious acts, that the resulting blessings can truly be long-lasting and transcendent.

This is a mocking paradox. For example, as mentioned above, a departed soul that knows the mantra “Namo Amitabha Buddha!” has great merit and may, because of that, attain liberation, but cannot recite it by itself to achieve liberation.

As for living people, chanting Buddha's name is not a difficult task, yet they often do not realize how miraculous this mantra is. Many people go to temples, practice various methods, and keep chanting Buddha's name endlessly, but their bodies remain stiff and unchanged significantly, so many people look down on it.

Who would have thought that those who follow the Buddha’s teachings and pray for rebirth, spending their whole lives reciting "Namo Amitabha Buddha," accumulating countless merits, upon leaving this body will be born into a peaceful world, enjoying eternal happiness.

That only happens when one dies, becoming spirits; only then do people see, know, and believe, but by then it is already too late, and one can only regret, saying, "If I had known this earlier while still alive, I would have competed less with life, to save more time and effort for cultivating myself, even just a little; now I have already reached a certain realm."

If you have read this far, understood the issue, and realized that human life is truly precious, it is not because humans can trade for a living, accumulate wealth, nor because being human allows one to marry and have children, nor because having a physical body allows one to fully enjoy pleasures like parties, travel, shopping...

No, all of those things vanish in an instant upon death; even before death, they may have already fallen apart, completely lost.

A precious human life is valuable because being human comes with a physical body, and having a physical body makes cultivation effective. Every good deed done brings immense merit, incomparable to anything else, even compared to those practicing in the Western Pure Land; cultivation in our world allows one to advance 36,500 times faster.

The Buddha taught in the Infinite Life Sutra:

“...Practicing for one day and one night in the Saha world surpasses doing good deeds in the Land of Infinite Life for a hundred years.

Why is that?”

The Buddha's realm is all about practicing goodness and accumulating virtue, without a trace of evil. Practicing goodness in the Sahā world for ten days and nights is better than doing good for a thousand years in other Buddha realms.

Why is that?

Because in other Buddha realms, merit and virtue naturally exist, and there is no condition to commit evil. Only in this Sahā world is goodness scarce and evil abundant, filled entirely with endless suffering…”

If you have understood this paradox, then congratulations! You have acquired a very precious compass to guide you on where to go, while most of humanity is still wandering in a maze of competitive fame and fortune with no escape.

Devote your effort, time, and make the most use of whatever you have to diligently practice, accumulate merit, so that one day, inevitably, when your eyes close, your hands fall, and when your life's blessings and karma come to an end, the outcome will be determined, you can smile with satisfaction, knowing that you have not wasted a single human life.

(Quang Tu)

tieu_de: THE STRUGGLES AND SUFFERINGS OF AN EEL TRYING TO PRACTICE TO BECOME HUMAN
tom_tat: (Lesson on cherishing the human body and life) Teacher Thich Tue Minh
noi_dung:
THE TRIALS AND SUFFERINGS OF AN EEL STRIVING TO PRACTICE TO OBTAIN A HUMAN BODY

(A lesson on cherishing human life and existence)

Venerable Thich Tue Minh

Today I want to tell everyone a story that truly exists in life, a story that I was fortunate to encounter in this lifetime,

Some people might consider it fictional or fabricated, and some might be skeptical! But I recount this story not for those two types of people, but for those who have sincere faith and the complete affinity with the true Dharma!

Many years ago, in the mountainous area where I practiced, there was a stream that wound its way to a cave. Since this was the end of the stream, the water accumulated into a very large pond. Water hyacinths and wild plants grew on the surface of the pond, forming a thick layer several palms deep! It was also at this place that, once while searching for medicinal herbs, I encountered a rare event in life: the moment of transformation of an Aquatic Tribe, longing and yearning to have a human body, how much they desired it!

That day, while endlessly searching for medicinal herbs to help a person suffering from pus-filled skin disease, I followed the stream to the very end of the pond when a heavy rain suddenly fell. The evening was twilight, and with the rain, it made the daytime seem as dark as night! I hurried into a nearby mountain cave to shelter from the rain. As soon as I stepped into the cave, a strong, foul, fishy smell rose up, like the scent of a corpse. I quickly placed my basket of herbs on a rock and looked around to see what animal had died, and a horrifying scene was unfolding before my eyes.

A golden animal was sluggishly crawling slowly toward a small rock crevice, where a viper was lying still, waiting for the moment to enjoy its favorite meal of the day.

At first glance, I could guess that the viper was preparing to eat the eel (if anyone from the Southern region has probably seen this scene in the countryside, no matter how small the viper is, no matter how big and strong the eel is, it cannot escape on its own but obediently crawls back to be eaten by the snake as if hypnotized and completely losing its self-control!)

It is believed that the trun snake secretes a hypnotic fragrance for eels, and when they smell it, they can be commanded at will like a slave!

The only difference is that today, this eel is unusually large, about the size of a newborn baby, golden, shiny, and wavy, with ears already grown, protruding above its head, a nose also grown, its front limbs developed, and the back limbs like two small flesh buds, wriggling while trying to push its head into the mouth of the trun snake, even though its body is 3-4 times smaller than it.

I quickly pulled the eel out, and the snake also wriggled quickly into a nearby stream crevice! I scooped water to clean the eel and then released it back into the pond!

If it were just that, there would be nothing to tell. But that night, while meditating, I saw a person standing outside the cave door, peeking in, wearing a bright yellow robe. Thinking it might be a fellow practitioner passing by visiting this place, I immediately invited them in. The person then stepped inside, clasped their hands to bow and greet me, and after greeting, knelt in front of me and sobbed uncontrollably.

Before I could ask what was going on, the other person spoke, their voice fragmented, loud and unpleasant like that of an ethnic person who was not yet fluent in Vietnamese:

- Master Bach, I am the eel whose life you saved this afternoon. If not for your kindness and virtue, I would probably have become a ghost in that snake's belly by now!

I was surprised and asked again:

- How long have you practiced in order to be able to take human form and stand here talking to me? How could you be so easily captured and eaten by that snake?

The other person continued speaking:

- Master Bach, I have been practicing here for over 500 years. You may not know me, but I know you clearly from the day you first came here to cultivate. I was supposed to be transforming into a Ferret, but before I could complete it, I encountered this calamity. During the transformation, I no longer had the ability to use supernatural powers, and because of that, I fell under the control of the scent of that snake and nearly lost my life. Fortunately, thanks to the great blessing of meeting you and being saved, I am here today to express my immense gratitude to you!

I asked next:

- So after transforming into a weasel, how much longer must one practice?

The other person replied:

- Master, perhaps it will take over 700 years for a weasel to absorb yang energy and manifest a human form. From the moment one attains a human form and continues to cultivate, it will take more than 300 years to hope to perfect one’s virtue and become a junior immortal. During that time, if one unfortunately dies, it would be as if a thousand years of effort were lost to the rivers and seas.

So that's how it is, no wonder humans never encounter ascetic animals, because they are extremely fearful. If by any chance humans kill them, a century of effort would be completely lost. That's why humans are truly frightening, not those demons; they fear us even more than we fear them by many times!

I recount this story to remind everyone that having a human body is an invaluable asset, as the World-Honored One once taught: Having a human body is like a blind turtle stuck in a bamboo tube, something extremely rare over a thousand years. So many other beings, animals, and hungry ghosts out there long for and wish to have a human body. Just like the eel I mentioned above, it takes over a thousand years, going through countless dangers, ups and downs, as well as pain and sacrifice, just to obtain a human body to practice in.

Yet today, there are quite a few people who neglect their own bodies, destroying them with various poisons, neglecting to cultivate their mind and body to escape suffering early, and instead chasing after the illusions of life. When they fail or feel regret, they turn to death themselves, destroying their own lives,

It is truly as I have said before: we humans only know to value something after we have lost it, only know fear after it has happened, and only know regret when it is already too late!

------------

tieu_de: Escaping disaster by doing good deeds
tom_tat: There was a Buddhist woman in Hai Phong, and since she embraced the faith, she actively did good deeds, built roads, and constructed bridges... Then one day she was walking on the road, collided with a car, and was caught under the vehicle. The driver heard the sound of the collision with the vehicle.
noi_dung:
ESCAPE DISASTER THROUGH GOOD DEEDS

There is a Buddhist nun in Hai Phong, since she learned Buddhism, she actively does good deeds, builds roads, constructs bridges...

Then one day she was on the road, collided with a car and got caught under the vehicle. The driver, hearing the sound of the collision, thought he had run someone over and would go to prison. But he calmly got out of the car with others to help her, intending to take her to the hospital for emergency treatment, but she waved her hands, meaning 'let me lie still.' She lay still for a while, then sat up and recounted that:

When she hit her head on the wheel, the wheel did not crush her head, her head hurt, but she kept hearing the Master's voice saying: When the head is injured, the brain is injured, just lie still to let the brain recover on its own, so she tried to wave her hands to tell everyone to let her lie still, and she silently recited Buddha's name.

Later, she went to the hospital, had an X-ray, and there was nothing wrong, only an external impact.

Afterwards, she went to see the Master and told him about it, and the Master said:

She was supposed to pay a heavy karma and be run over by a car, but because she had accumulated a lot of merit, she escaped the danger, though the karma still came and she only suffered lightly.

According to the law of cause and effect, once karma is created, at some point when the conditions are right, it must be repaid, but for those with much merit, the punishment is much lighter.

She said that since then, her husband has greatly believed in Buddha and goes to the temple with her.
