tieu_de: Karmic Story 2: Overcoming Lust
tom_tat: Ngọc is an office employee at a foreign company. But because of her appearance and diligence, she gets a lot of attention from her superiors. Although she has a lot of work, she still arranges time to go to the temple, do good deeds, and practice her spiritual discipline.
noi_dung:
Karmic Story 2: Overcoming Lust

Ngoc is an office worker at a foreign company. But due to her appearance and diligence, she is very noticed by her superiors. Although she has a lot of work, she still arranges time to go to the temple, work regularly, and practice regularly.

But unfortunately for her, adversity comes to the challenge.

Today, after the shift early, the director invited her to eat. During the meal, he said that he had feelings for her and wanted to provide her with money if she would be his little wife. Hearing this, Ngoc left silently.

That night she could not sleep. She knew he already had a wife and two children. And this action was an adulterous act. Although she wanted to quit her job to avoid him, there was something in her heart that stirred, making her hesitant and unable to be decisive.

The next day she met him and said that everything should end here; if they continued to sink deeper, both would lose all their honor. But the director still insisted that he truly loved Ngoc.

Ngoc was once again feeling sad because she deeply respected her boss. Since he often cared for and helped her with work, she seemed to feel that she owed him.

A month later, her boss's attention became even more special, coupled with many intimate gestures, making her even more worried. Ngoc understood that if she didn’t find a way to end this improper relationship, she herself would create karma and have to face terrible consequences in future lives.

One day, she accidentally read the story "the retribution for adultery," which said that those who commit adultery would descend into the hell of lust. Ngoc suddenly remembered the venerable Zen master at the temple she often visited to do volunteer work and learn about spiritual teachings.

A week later, she arranged her work and went to visit the Zen master.

When she met the master, tears fell from her eyes. She confessed to him that she still had feelings for that director but did not dare to accept his proposal for an affair because she knew the retribution would be very painful.

After listening to Ngọc’s story, the Zen master looked at her with eyes full of compassion mixed with sorrow.

He began to explain:

- Worldly love is actually not real. It is only influenced by karma. Perhaps in a previous life you helped your current boss, so in this life when you meet him again, he feels very favorable toward you. But since this realm is the realm of desire, sentient beings easily develop emotions and consider them love. Not knowing the Dharma, sentient beings do not know how to restrain themselves and eliminate desire. They even think it is a normal instinct and indulge in pleasure, thereby creating countless karmic obstructions.

Ngoc knelt down, sincerely asking the Zen master to teach the way to cut off karmic lust with her boss.

The compassionate Zen master teaches:

- I have been fortunate to know the Dharma and recognize my mistakes, which led me to seek out the teacher. This is also the result of deep virtuous roots cultivated over many past lives with the Buddhist teachings. Now I should go home to sincerely bow to the Buddha and wholeheartedly repent for the sins of desire, arrogance, and clinging to personal achievements accumulated over countless lifetimes. Especially, I should repent for my current boss as well, so that they may gradually lighten the karmic burden of desire. Since I am also indebted to my boss, in this life my heart still holds feelings towards him. I should repay him with morality, with Buddhist principles, rather than with the body or romantic involvement, because the more I repay in that way, the more karma I create. Otherwise, I will be trapped in the cycle of birth and death.

Hearing this, Ngoc suddenly woke up like a dazed person. She paid respects to the Zen master and left.

In the following days, Ngoc bowed to Buddha every night to repent of his karma of lust, adultery and arrogance from countless lifetimes. Not only that, she also directed her thoughts towards the other director, hoping that he would be relieved and free from his feelings for her.

Since the day she bowed to the Buddha and repented, she looked at him calmly, without the previous emotional disturbance. Similarly, the director looked at her coldly, no longer with the affectionate and caring gaze full of special attention as before. At this moment, she was brave enough to refuse and explain the consequences of adultery to him to make him understand. At the same time, she submitted her resignation and got a better job.

This time, she deeply felt the Buddha's teachings more than ever. Indeed, romantic relationships are not real and are very transient. Everything is governed by fate and karma. When the fate and karma end, there is no more affection between each other. Therefore, we should treat each other with compassion, as the Buddha taught.

ST

tieu_de: Namo Amitāyus, the Supreme Auspicious Tathāgata
tom_tat: NAMA SANS WORRY SUPREME VICTORIOUS AUSPICIOUS TATHAGATA ...Again, O Man Thu That Loi! In the East, more than seven ganjisa away from the Buddha realm, there is a world called Wu You, where the Buddha named Wu You Supreme Victorious Auspicious Tathagata resides.
noi_dung:
NAMO UPAI SUPREME VICTORIOUS AUSPICIOUS TATHAGATA

NAM MÔ WORSHIP THE ULTIMATELY SUPREME EVER-PROSPEROUS BUDDHA

..."Moreover, O Man Thu That Loi! In the East, more than seven gan-jas-buddha realms away, there is a world called Vô Ưu, where the Buddha named Vô Ưu Tối Thắng Cát Tường Như Lai Ứng Chánh Ðẳng Giác is currently teaching the Dharma to the great assembly. The Buddha’s realm is vast, solemn, and pure, the land is as flat as a hand, made entirely of fine, soft jewels, constantly fragrant, free from sounds of suffering, and devoid of afflictions. There are no ferocious animals or female beings. Everywhere there are bathing ponds made entirely of gold plates at the bottom. The fragrant water overflows, rows of precious trees stand straight, fruits are abundant, and the exquisite music sounds without being played… like the palacethe solemn virtue of the Land of Infinite Life in the Western world.

O Man Thu That Loi! When the World-Honored Buddha practiced the Bodhisattva path, He made four great vows, which are:

- The first great vow: I vow that in future life – when I attain the supreme Bodhi – if there are any sentient beings who are often bound by suffering and affliction, if they hear my name and sincerely recite it, by this power, all their distress and suffering will be eliminated, allowing them to live long and peacefully, until they achieve Bodhi.

- The second great vow: I vow that in the future life – when I attain Supreme Bodhi – if there are any sentient beings who commit evil karma, born in the darkest, uninterrupted hells, enduring suffering and torment, due to having heard my name in a past life, I at that time will personally emit light, shining upon those who are suffering. By this power, when they see the light, their karmic obstacles will be completely destroyed, they will be freed from all suffering, be reborn among humans or devas, enjoy whatever happiness they wish, up until attaining Bodhi.

- The third great vow: I vow that in future lives – when I attain Supreme Enlightenment – if there are sentient beings who commit evil deeds such as killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, they should immediately suffer in their present life from pain caused by knives and sticks, descend into evil paths, and if they happen to take human form, they will experience many illnesses, die young, be born into poor, low, and deprived families, frequently endure suffering from hunger and thirst, cold and heat; their appearance will not be radiant, and their relatives and kin will be fierce; if they hear my name, sincerely recite it, then through this power, according to their wishes, they will receive sufficient food and clothing, their bodily appearance will resemble that of deities, shining, attractive, and their relativesAll the followers are virtuous, up to attaining Bodhi.

- The fourth great vow: I vow that in future lifetimes – when I attain supreme enlightenment – if there are any sentient beings who are often harassed and troubled by Yakshas, or other malevolent spirits, losing their souls and enduring sufferings, if they hear my name and sincerely recite it, by this power all such Yakshas, etc., will retreat and all beings will generate a mind of compassion, be freed from suffering, and eventually attain Buddhahood.

Once again, O Man Thu That Loi! These are the four great and wondrous vows of the Tathagata, the Perfectly Enlightened One, that have been made. If any living being hears the name of that Buddha and day and night, in the six periods of time, recites the name, bows, shows reverence, wholeheartedly makes offerings, and generates a mind of compassion to care for all beings, then their karmic obstacles will be eliminated, they will be freed from sorrow, will be free from illness, live a long life, attain the wisdom of a long lifespan, be reborn in a lotus flower in that Buddha's realm, and will always be protected by the heavenly beings.

Hey Man Thu That Loi! Reciting the name of that Buddha often brings countless merits, but the vow power and supreme virtuous adornment of that Buddha cannot be known by the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, only by the Tathāgata, the Perfectly Enlightened One, can it be known.

Namo Amitāyus, the Supreme, Auspicious King Buddha (among the seven Medicine Buddhas) in the Sukhāvatī World

tieu_de: LITTLE-KNOWN TRUTH ABOUT HELL
tom_tat: My name is Trần Tuyết Trinh, currently living on Kha Vạn Cân Street, Thủ Đức, Ho Chi Minh City. I have a female colleague, working together at the same company in the high-tech park, District 9, Ho Chi Minh City. Her full name is: Hứa Ngọc Thủy , sin
noi_dung:
LITTLE-KNOWN TRUTH ABOUT HELL

My name is Trần Tuyết Trinh, currently living on Kha Vạn Cân street, Thủ Đức, Ho Chi Minh City. I have a female colleague, working together in the same company in the high-tech zone, District 9, Ho Chi Minh City.

Her full name is Hứa Ngọc Thủy, born in 1960. That year I was 21 years old, and she was already 50. Technically, I should call her 'aunt,' but she still looks very young, and since we work in the same company, we call each other sister and brother for closeness. She has a petite figure and fair skin. Her face is full of kindness with a beauty mark on her forehead.

She took refuge in Buddhism when she was only 10 years old, and she has been vegetarian since she was 20. She is very knowledgeable about Buddhist teachings. Her name is Thuy, Dharma name Dieu Ki, and she is from An Giang, right at Chau Doc market, where the Chau Doc River flows through.

She shared that because her parents died in an accident, she became an orphan at the age of 9 and had to be independent in everything. At the age of 10, due to hardship, she went to a temple to ask for food, and it was through that connection that she came to know Buddhist teachings.

After a while, she met the abbot and confessed to him that she wanted to shave her head, but he didn’t allow it. He said that she had the potential for practice, but her worldly defilements were not yet gone, so she could not become a monk.

Because she had the potential for practice from many past lives, the abbot gave her special attention, performing the Refuge ceremony for her alone without waiting for many people.

One day, when I visited her boarding room, she cooked a very delicious vegetarian meal for me. After a while, she suddenly asked me:

– Do you believe in the spirit world?

I replied:

– I believe, but I haven't witnessed it yet.

– So do you believe what I say?

– Of course I do, sister, because thanks to you I know a lot about Buddhist teachings, I know how to read mantras, and I feel the coolness in my soul when reciting them.

– Then, dear, I will tell you a story about hell, do you want to hear it?

I smiled, thinking she is good at joking, how could she know a story about hell. She continued:

– I will tell anyone who wants to hear, and this is completely true, you have the destiny so you need to hear it even more

And she began to tell, her voice slow and steady:

– You know, back when I was 18, I had a car accident that almost killed me, but fortunately I only had severe injuries to my arms and legs, I was just heavily impacted by the vehicle and unconscious for 7 days straight.

I asked:

– So who took care of you in the hospital?

– It was the nun and the abbot, because I had an accident near where I lived. During that time, I wandered into a dark space, with a faint light where I saw my parents, and then I saw Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha as well. Normally, I often recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and am extremely respectful of Him, so when I met Him, I was so happy that at that moment I didn't know how many times I had prostrated to Him, then ran to hug my parents. I asked Him where this place was, and He replied that this was Hell, which made me extremely terrified.

Then Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva said to me:

– You have accumulated much virtue from three generations, so I save you from the cycle of hell, sparing you from an untimely death. I save you for the benefit of mankind; this is a parting bridge – He pointed to a bridge – you must bid farewell to your parents so that they may be reincarnated, and you should return to where you came from. Do not look back; hell lies behind you.

She immediately knelt down and bowed to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, feeling immense gratitude for his grace. He continued to speak:

– In your previous life, you practiced Buddhism, but you killed a young life to save others, so you had to endure the consequence of an untimely death. Fortunately, because you dedicated merit to that being to help it attain liberation, and in this life you sincerely practice under the Buddha without doubt, you have escaped danger; I am showing you this.

– Yes, Venerable Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, please, with your great compassion, save all sentient beings, and let me see the state of hell so that my mind may grow firmer. Namo Amitabha Buddha!

– Because you planted a great seed of virtue in a previous life, I will take you there. When you see the terrifying scene, bite this pill in your mouth and press your hands together in a mudra.

She immediately followed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's instructions. The two huge iron gates opened, and above the door was a depiction of a dog's head with its mouth wide open, staring fiercely.

The gate had just partially opened when immediately there surged a sound of lamentation, the moaning of very—very many people combined, resonating into a terrifying cascade of noise. The ground here was covered with a veil of gloomy smoke, above which a red and green light spread widely, creating a very ghostly appearance. Layer upon layer of people followed one another in dense succession, exceedingly numerous, and behind them countless demons stood on both sides. She and Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha were flying above those people in the void.

She asked Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, but she asked with her mind rather than with words:

– Yes, Bodhisattva, may I ask, what are these people like?

– The ones going in are people going to meet the Judge, the ones going out are people going to another realm.

– Yes, may I ask, Bodhisattva, in my ignorance, why does no one bow to You, but only focus on going?

– They, due to ignorance, do not see me, just as they do not see you, because I have placed a sealing bead in your mouth already.

She passed by a palace like a royal palace, but it looked gloomy rather than bright, then she and the Bodhisattva flew through a rock wall, similar to stalactites, and what struck her eyes immediately was a scene of fierce battle, with flesh and blood scattered everywhere, a horrifying scene: people fiercely attacking and slashing each other without mercy.

Here and there there are also animals like buffaloes and cows, using their horns to charge fiercely. She focused on watching a man below, seeing him cut to death, his body covered in gore, dead and then revived, only to be chopped again, not knowing how many times this scene of slashing and killing would repeat.

Blood and flesh flew everywhere, screams of extreme pain, clashing sounds of swords, all combined into a horrifying scene that would make anyone who witnessed it tremble with fear.

She asked the Bodhisattva why these people were stabbing and slashing at each other like that. The Bodhisattva said that it was the fire of anger and delusion burning their consciousness; if they do not wish to be free, even He cannot save them. These people are all either meat and fish merchants, or fishing, setting nets, capturing living creatures, or hired killers...

They suffer the consequences of their own actions and cannot be saved because they are veiled by ignorance. Next, she and the Bodhisattva passed through a place like the mouth of a volcano with scorching lava. She felt the heat burning her, even though she was very high up; this was the second hell.

Thousands upon thousands, tens of thousands of people, even without anyone urging them, naturally threw themselves into the sea of fire, and then they were pierced by thousands of arrows, their screams and cries horrifying enough to tear apart the eardrums and the souls of those who heard them. Truly, no matter how hard words try, they cannot describe the terrifying sounds and scenes of hell. This is only an account of a tiny fraction of what I witnessed. At that moment, I asked the Bodhisattva:

– Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, why are those people burned by fire, die and come back to life, and even pierced through by a thousand arrows? Why does the Bodhisattva not save them?

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha answered:

– These people, due to their greedy and stingy minds, some take money from the poor, others use deceit and mislead people to seize the wealth of the masses, are blocked by ignorance, and do not see Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha before them. Even if they want to be saved, it is not possible. If they knew how to recite the Buddha's name, their suffering would be eased.

After passing through those two prisons, she and Lord Kṣitigarbha passed through another partition resembling white five-colored stone, whose veins had very horrifying shapes.

Then she saw iron spikes, then countless iron pillars, all of which were heated red-hot, only hotter and never cooling down.

People from all classes had to sit on those iron spikes, which were about more than 10 cm long. Of course, it was impossible to sit still; many sharp spikes pierced the flesh, causing excruciating pain. The sinners kept crawling up and sliding down, with bones and flesh protruding, blood flowing like rain.

On top of that, filth and saliva from various animals poured down. They were bathing in both blood and excrement, enduring relentless torment without rest.

But that was not all; from the sky, thunder and lightning struck loudly, burning the sinful souls. Here and there, large, round, scorching-hot stones rolled over people, bringing countless pains all at once. The level of horror here, she dares to assert, no talented or experienced writer could describe in words what she witnessed.

Those who have light sins in this prison must hold onto a copper pillar, sometimes as hot as molten lava, sometimes as cold as ice. Before she could ask, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva said:

– This hell is for those who are unfilial, unforgiven by heaven and relentless by earth; sins differ, so the punishments vary in severity.

What you see above is only a small part of this hell, the whole hell is horrifyingly vast. Imagine the smallest part is already thousands of kilometers in size.

I said :

– So the smallest hell must be the size of our country, Vietnam, right?

– You are right, each hell is very vast, countless sentient beings inside, densely packed. The next hell you visit, though not as horrifying as the three hells you just mentioned, is disgusting, spine-chilling, causing bumps all over, this hell contains vats of leftover rice wriggling with maggots, along with fleas, ants … all kinds of repulsive insects. Those who are punished must stay in that vat, forced to eat the leftover food that was wasted when they were alive.

There are also the dung pits of various animals, where the sinful souls must stay in the pits to “enjoy” all that foul, pungent dung, especially with one pit per person, each pit only as big as a five-story building. The dung diminishes and then automatically rises again, and only when a person has “suffered through” an entire pit can they be reincarnated.

And she also has another special pit, a pit that contains nothing but corpses, rotten and disgusting, and guilty souls have to swallow that flesh alive because when they were alive they killed living creatures, slaughtered pigs and cows, sold dog meat, etc. Having seen that pit with her own eyes, she was terrified, and that is why she made the decision to be vegetarian until now, whenever she has money she releases animals and prays to atone for past sins.

Poor sentient beings there, if they sincerely recite the Buddha's name, the Bodhisattva can save them, but if they are ignorant and cannot recite, then the Bodhisattva has to endure. The Bodhisattva is compassionate, always pitying those who are lost and stumbling, naturally wanting to rescue them, but if they do not generate the intention to recite the Buddha's name, even Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will be defeated.

You were led by Him to another prison. This prison you found very special because it was full of gold, silver, jewels, diamonds, and piles of money, sparkling beautifully, but you know, they have to eat and swallow those things.

The sinful souls are surrounded by gold and silver, each chunk falling like hail, striking anyone and smashing their heads and brains, blood flowing like rain; some people are crushed, others have gold and silver shot through their bodies, or it falls into blocked ears or mouths, or if gold and silver enter the stomach, it expands bigger than the bellies of pregnant women, both heavy and painful. Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva said: this is the punishment for those greedy for money, selfish and stingy, cheating in trade for profit, corrupt officials, and so on...

In another place, she saw driverless cars crushing souls to pieces, splattering brains, exposing bones, and someone had to pick up the fragments of flesh and bones of others to reassemble them, restoring them to life, continuously in turn.

The most horrifying part is the scene of reattaching arms and legs, heart and lungs; if they aren't reattached, the person suffers terribly. Each person relives this tragedy repeatedly throughout the day, being hit by a car, reduced to pieces of flesh and bone, then stitched back together, dying and coming back to life a thousand times. This is the retribution for drivers who deliberately kill someone or cause an accident and then flee.

In another place, there is a huge machine that crushes people into tiny pieces; as the flesh spills out, flies and insects swarm over it, and then it is ground again until it becomes like powder. After that, one regains consciousness and begins to be ground from the start. The souls of the guilty are executed this way until their karmic debt is paid, then they are transferred to other prisons to endure the punishment for other sins. This is also the last hell that she visited.

The hells that she witnessed were only a small corner of the thousands of prisons here. Everywhere was the peak of suffering, demons wailing and wolves howling pitifully, everywhere was shattered bones and broken flesh, dying and coming back to life endlessly. How sad it is that humans, while alive, create evil and thus receive such immense pain? How much pleasure in human life can compare to these extreme, endless sufferings?

After that, she was led by Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva back to the human world, to the place where her motionless body lay.

The Bodhisattva said that she should swallow the jewel that the Bodhisattva had given her earlier, which she had been holding in her mouth while visiting the scenes of hell.

She swallowed it slowly, and saw the Bodhisattva chanting something; her soul immediately returned to her body. She woke up, looked in the direction where the Bodhisattva had been standing, but could not see the Bodhisattva anymore. However, she still heard His voice faintly in her mind:

– You should practice the Buddha's teachings more diligently, then you will see other scenes, and help benefit sentient beings when they seek to learn the Dharma.

She sat up, as if she had completely healed, knelt down and worshiped the Bodhisattva, worshiping tirelessly, crying non-stop like rain, and then everyone rushed to her side…

***

It has been a long time since I lost contact with her, truly regrettable. I hope that if fate allows, she reads this article, and we, as sisters, will have the opportunity to meet again.

(Trần Tuyết Trinh's self-narration – fb: bạch tuệ ngọc)

tieu_de: THE WAY TO TAKE REFUGE AND MAKE VOWS WITH BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA.
tom_tat: Dear everyone! Today is the last day of the 7th lunar month, which is also the feast day of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. Because it is noticed that the article (The Benefits of Worshiping Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha) is of interest to many people and also
noi_dung:
HOW TO TAKE REFUGE AND MAKE VOWS WITH BODHISATTVA KṢITIṄGA.

Dear everyone! Today is the last day of the seventh lunar month, which is also the day to honor Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. Noticing that the article (The Benefits of Worshiping Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha) has attracted the interest of many people who have vowed to bow to the Bodhisattva three thousand times, many have already completed their bows and have reported feeling great peace as well as receiving many benefits both in life and in Dharma, and have asked about the way to take refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.

Therefore, I humbly take the liberty to write a few words to share the way to make vows as well as the method to take refuge in the Bodhisattva according to the proper Dharma.

〽️ First, we should understand what the two words 'Quy Y' mean. Why should one take refuge in the Bodhisattva?

➖ The word 'Quy' means TO RETURN. The word 'Y' means TO DEPEND ON. Taking refuge in the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha means returning to depend on Him, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. So how do we return to depend on Him?

It is that we MUST ABANDON EVIL AND PRACTICE GOOD, ABANDON WRONG AND RETURN TO RIGHT.

In the past, before we took refuge in You, we all had no place to rely on. The Bodhisattva teaches us to abandon evil and do good, to strive to eat vegetarian meals either regularly, periodically, or strictly, to observe precepts, and to practice cultivation.

Now that we vow to take refuge in the Bodhisattva, we must first follow His teachings, and only then turn to rely on Him.

It cannot be said that, in the Sutras, taking refuge in the Bodhisattva has truly many merits and benefits, yet merely reciting the Refuge and Vow without practice while still maintaining the same faults, still committing evil deeds, still keeping an evil mind, that is not truly called Taking Refuge but only adds to the worry of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha in having to save those beings.

〽️ So how should we take refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and make vows?

💮 TAKING REFUGE IN BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA:

My name is..., Dharma Name..., Today I listen to the Kṣitigarbha Buddha Sutra being preached, lectured on the inconceivable matters of the Buddha, which deeply moves me and sincerely, wholeheartedly, before the Great Saint Kṣitigarbha, I wish to make this vow:

"From today onward, I vow for my entire life and all future lives, until the day I become a Buddha, I vow to forever take refuge in and rely on Him."

I vow that until the end of future lives, until the day I become a Buddha, life after life, I will use countless means to guide and encourage all sentient beings to know and take refuge in You, so that all beings may receive great benefit.

Great Holy Kṣitigarbha! I sincerely hope that You, with great compassion and mercy, will witness my taking refuge and this vow of mine, so that I may never forget it in all my lives.

Currently, I am an ignorant and foolish ordinary person with deep karmic obstacles. I earnestly hope that the Great Sage, out of compassion, will have mercy on me and all sentient beings, and bless me and all creatures to attain peace, to have all things go as desired, to expand wisdom, to eliminate all karmic obstacles, to quickly achieve the purity of my original mind, and ultimately to swiftly transcend birth and death and attain Buddhahood.

❗️If you cannot memorize it, you can take a piece of paper and rewrite it. Each day, face the statue of the Bodhisattva, join your hands, remember the Bodhisattva, and make a vow.

If someone has not yet had the缘 (opportunity) to have a Bodhisattva statue, they should face south and make a vow (not missing a single day, at least for one year).

The way of making such a vow must be sincere. If it is truly from the heart, the benefits are beyond imagination. Tệ Nhân himself and many other fellow practitioners have relied on taking refuge and making this vow to achieve wondrous things that are hard to imagine, and all their wishes were fulfilled... etc.

Such events of villainy truly cannot be fully recounted, I only wish that whoever practices accordingly will find as much as they eat is sufficient, and know the warmth or coldness of the water they drink; it will definitely not be entirely false or exaggerated beyond the truth.

The Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra and the Kṣitigarbha Ten Foolish Karmas Sutra state very clearly and advise all sentient beings to cultivate the mind of taking refuge and offering to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, thereby attaining boundless and inconceivable benefits. If such great benefits as spoken in the Sutras were false, then all the Buddhas of the Ten Directions and Buddha Śākyamuni would also be speaking falsehoods, except for those who are insincere or do not have true hearts.

Today, this unworthy person sincerely hopes that at least each of us, the Buddhists, should follow the teachings, practice respectfully, and rely on refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, as per the instructions in the bequeathal of Shakyamuni Buddha, who entrusted Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha up to three times before the Buddha entered Nirvana. That is:

"All sentient beings—Devas, Humans, the eight classes of beings, etc.—in future lives, now I carefully bequeath them to you."

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva..... Remember to think of me and entrust yourself to my care earnestly, striving to save beings in the Saha world, so that when Maitreya Buddha appears, they may all be liberated from suffering. Meeting the Buddha, they will receive the Buddha’s prophecy.

🙏🏻 Each of us, as Buddhists, should take the vow to take refuge in the Bodhisattva and then should generate the aspiration to prostrate before the Bodhisattva 3,000 times to show our sincere respect. By doing so, it is certain that over time, you will gradually feel positive changes in your daily life.

(Actually, 3000 prostrations are very easy. Doing 100 prostrations a day finishes in 1 month; if doing 50 prostrations a day, it finishes in 2 months. We should complete them within at most three months from the time of making the vow to take refuge with the Bodhisattva.)

Praying that all beings are safe and quickly fulfill all their wishes as desired.

Respectfully 🙏

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, Lord of the Underworld Realm.

tieu_de: KING YAMA TEACHES THE WAY OF BEING HUMAN
tom_tat: (Excerpt from Hồi Dương Nhân Quả. In the past, Mr. Lâm Tự Kỳ was mistakenly captured by a ghost, and after coming back to life, he recounted the things he heard and saw in the underworld. Nhứt Điện Vương tried 43 cases and thanks to taking the Phát Huệ medicine, he only remembered them after coming back to life)
noi_dung:
KING YAMA TEACHES MORALITY

(Excerpted from Reaping the Results of Virtue. In the past, Mr. Lam Tu Ky was mistakenly captured by ghosts, and upon returning to life, he recounted what he heard and saw in the underworld. The First King Dian judged 43 cases, and thanks to taking the Enlightening Medicine, he was able to remember and recount them after coming back to life)

The judge reported: 'The twenty-three evil acts have violated a total of 42 handled cases. As for the virtuous scholar Lam Tu Ky, who was mistakenly arrested, what should be done now?' King Tan Quang summoned the soul of Tu Ky back and decreed: 'Now I am sending your soul back; you must diligently cultivate with sincerity. I have just handled those cases; do you understand them all?' Tu Ky reported: 'I believe I understand.' The king said: 'The officials will escort the virtuous scholar's soul to King Dong Nhac to receive approval and then return, so that the virtuous scholar may recount to the world the cases I have adjudicated.' Tu Ky said: 'I am quite ignorant and cannot recall the cases clearly.' The king looked at the judge and declared: 'Give the virtuous scholar a potion to awaken his wisdom to hold in the mouth while returning.'Yang, then remembered everything without omission. ‘Tự Kỳ, after receiving the medicine, reported:’ I thank the prince for allowing me to live again. From now on, I am determined to practice cultivation, but I do not yet know the way to cultivate morality. Which step should I take first to practice correctly?’

King Tan Quang said: The Way is the Five Relationships: ruler-subject, parent-child, husband-wife, siblings, friends; these are also within the five levels of relationships, with nothing unusual. How does one speak of the ruler-subject relationship: For officials, they must first be loyal to the ruler and care for the people; whether serving in the court or governing regions outside, they must act according to the law appropriate to their position, wholeheartedly and devotedly with justice, forgetting personal interests, focusing on state affairs and neglecting family matters; this is in accordance with their role. As for the people, they should fulfill their tax obligations without breaking the law, perform their duties obediently and honestly, firmly maintaining righteousness in family life through benevolence. Advising the simple villagers and preserving customs is practicing the ruler-subject relationship.As for a father, if one is a father raising a child, one must teach and, to love the child, must provide for them. Either teach the scriptures to understand moral principles, or teach farming, trading, or occupational skills for livelihood; one should not spoil them, allowing them to indulge in wine, lust, debauchery, or gambling. As for a child, one should care for, nurture, and respect their parents; in important matters, one should strive to study and achieve success to bring honor to the parents, and live honestly and uprightly so that parents receive praise. Furthermore, one must do their utmost to support their parents, dressing and eating suitably according to one’s means, whether rich or poor; if wealthy, provide delicious tastes and pampering to make parents happy, ensuring they are never displeased, fulfilling filial piety; if poor, even with simple foods like salted dishes, one should still care for their parents properly.One should wholeheartedly devote oneself with the courage of a buffalo or horse to repay benefits. Even in poverty, one must be entirely respectful to parents; do not think that mere support exempts one from respect and propriety. One must also understand that this body is made of the flesh and bones given by the parents, so one must protect it, not dare to harm it, and also not dare to act wrongly to bring disgrace to the body given by the parents, which is true filial piety. This is the way of father and child. As for the husband-wife relationship, they must be distinct: the husband takes care of matters outside, the wife takes care of matters inside, appropriately. The husband holds authority over the wife, but they must treat each other with propriety and rites, not abandoning manners to be bossy or servile. If the husband abuses his authority to oppress the wife, or the wife is disrespectful to insult the husband, it is wrong. The husband values the wife for her virtue, and should not be captivated by mere beauty, the wife respects the husband.Just as worshiping God requires adhering to His way, harmony between husband and wife also requires proper conduct. The husband instructs the wife to be gentle and respect her parents-in-law, so the daughter-in-law will follow suit. Harmony between sisters-in-law ensures no misunderstandings arise in the family. A wife must heed her husband's righteous guidance, which is called fully practicing marital duty. This is the duty of husband and wife. As for siblings, they come from the same origin, of the same blood and flesh like hand and foot, with branches growing from the same root; if one suffers, the other feels the pain, and they are considered one body. Whether in fortune or misfortune, joy or sorrow, they share it together as one entity.

If parents are still alive and siblings are harmonious and love each other, the parents will be very happy. Even if the parents have passed away, seeing siblings is like seeing the parents, loving siblings is like loving parents. Therefore, even if siblings are not harmonious, it does not matter; if outsiders attack your siblings, you will strongly defend them. Reflecting on this, siblings are very important. In short: your parents and siblings are determined by heaven and cannot be changed. Spouses and children come afterward, determined by other circumstances, so they can change. Therefore, do not overly prioritize your spouse and children while neglecting your siblings. You should place the duty to siblings before personal feelings, then you are fulfilling your responsibility toward your siblings. As for friends, how come they are considered on the same level as human ethics? MyselfNot having done anything wrong yet, thanks to you for admonishing me, I have stopped. Matters that should be harmful, one must contend with themselves; sometimes parents and children cannot speak out because they feel reluctant, but you dare to speak. The matters of one's heart and blessings, sometimes parents and children cannot speak out, but you dare to speak. In urgent situations, parents and children cannot save, but you worry and are able to save. Therefore, a person should not be without loyal friends. Therefore, in making friends, one must speak firmly and consider words carefully: over time, one will not forget each other. Be concerned for your friends, help and rescue your friends. By being loyal to friends, naturally friends will be beneficial to you. By cultivating the way of friendship, five levels of human relations are perfected. I urge good people to strive to advance a level. Yes.These are my simple, rustic words, meant to teach people; listen and understand quickly, then diligently practice. To put it briefly, for those who cultivate themselves, it doesn't matter whether one leaves home or stays at home, whether male or female, young or old, nor whether one is noble or humble, rich or poor, or drifting through hardships. There is no person who cannot cultivate, no place where one cannot cultivate, no time when one cannot cultivate. One should follow their duty and find peace in their heart. If you have more than enough, consider it still insufficient; do not develop arrogance or waste it excessively. If you lack, consider it still sufficient; do not give rise to greed or dreams beyond reason. When living with others, adhere to a single word: TOLERANCE; when managing your household, remember the hundred-fold rule of PATIENCE.

If someone behaves wrongly in any matter, one sincerely seeks out what is right for that person. In matters where one is mostly correct, one endeavors to consider and discover any missing points of correctness. Being diligent and frugal is the principle of creating reason, maintaining filial piety and respect for elders is the root of self-cultivation. Additionally, giving charity to help the world and doing good without tiring. If one can do this throughout life; observing vegetarianism is good, even if not, it’s still good; reciting Buddha’s name is effective, even if not reciting, it’s still effective. Ziqi said: ‘You must have possessions to give in charity, if you are poor, what can you do?’ It is answered: The act of giving in charity does not require possessing wealth; giving possessions is charity for those in extreme poverty. If one does not have surplus, but gives a bowl of rice to the hungry, a bowl of water to the thirsty, it is also considered charity. Still remainingMany ways of giving without spending money. For example, when someone is afraid, you use gentle words to help them overcome their fear, which is called fearless giving.

As for those who are infatuated and do not know repentance, if I advise them to wake up from all mistakes, it is called charitable giving through the Dharma. If there is something convenient for life, I put in effort; if there is something inconvenient, I worry for them, which is called skillful means of giving. If people argue or litigate, and I prefer to mediate, it is called giving to resolve conflicts. Feeling compassion or love for others in the heart is called giving with a compassionate mind. The things mentioned are giving through words and deeds, and they must accompany the gift of money. Zi Qi said: “According to what the monk said, one must be vegetarian and recite Buddha’s name to truly practice.” He replied: “Being vegetarian and reciting Buddha’s name is forcing the body and correcting the mind. Do not think that being vegetarian benefits the Buddha at all. As for recitingWhat benefit does Buddhism bring to life? As long as one practices the ten good deeds and avoids the ten bad deeds, that is sufficient. If one is vegetarian and chants Buddha's name but does not abandon the ten bad deeds and does not practice the ten good deeds, not only will there be no merit or virtue, but there will also be many sins and faults. So, those eleven or so monks from before, who also practiced vegetarianism and chanted Buddha's name, were still sent to hell; that is not true cultivation. If it is true cultivation, correcting oneself and observing the precepts is the first priority, giving alms and practicing vegetarianism is the second. The value of each lies in the intention: giving alms is difficult due to the humane heart, not because of external conditions; practicing vegetarianism is difficult because of the correct intention, not because of avoiding words or food. Therefore, for a poor household to give one đồng in alms, it is as valuable as a thousand đồng from a rich family. For a rich household to have one vegetarian meal, it is also as good as a meal of vegetarian practice.A month in a poor household is to take a little hardship as a way to accumulate merit; if one diligently endures much hardship, one can truly practice sincerely.' Tự Kỳ asked: 'Why is it said that in the Diamond Sutra there are four valuable verses?' The answer: 'This meaning is profound, I record it clearly, virtuous people should remember it well. The Diamond Sutra has 32 sections, the fifth section:'

The Buddha told Subhuti: 'All forms are illusory and deceptive; if one sees that all forms are not forms, then one sees the Tathagata.'

Meaning: Buddha Shakyamuni taught Subhuti that anything that has a form is illusory and deceptive. If one perceives a form as not being a form, that is seeing the Tathagata. Because the Buddha does not assume forms, does not establish a hall, one should not mistakenly regard them as precious.

(Excerpt from the final part of Hoi Duong Nhan Qua - Lam Tu Ky)

tom_tat: In ancient times in China, during the Tang dynasty, there was a monk whose dharma name was Du Thuan. He often lectured on the scriptures and gave dharma talks, and he also taught meditation. Sometimes he would teach people to chant the Buddha's name. He used every method
noi_dung:
THE PEOPLE AROUND US CAN ALL BE BODHISATTVAS

In ancient China, during the Tang dynasty, there was a monk named Đỗ Thuận. He often gave sermons and taught the Dharma, and he also taught meditation. Sometimes he taught people to chant the Buddha's name. He used all methods to educate and guide people. He had a disciple who had been practicing under him for over 10 years. On ordinary days, this disciple paid great attention to the merits and conduct of his master. He tried to understand who his master was, meaning, whether his master was a Bodhisattva, an Arhat, or sometimes a Buddha. Finally, after 10 years, he came to the conclusion that his master, Dharma Master Đỗ Thuận, was an ordinary person, having noThere is nothing unusual about my teacher. He eats like everyone else. He dresses like everyone else. He sleeps like everyone else. He does not have anything more than anyone else. Therefore, the disciple firmly understands that his teacher is not a Buddha, nor a Bodhisattva, nor an Arhat. Thus, the disciple goes to his teacher to pay respect, ask for permission, and leave him.

What is your intention?

I intend to go up to Mount Wutai to pay homage to Bodhisattva Manjushri.

The young man intended to seek wisdom from Bodhisattva Manjushri in the hope of attaining enlightenment. He said, “Master, I have been with you for over 10 years, and I feel that I have not learned anything. I understand nothing; I am truly ignorant, and I have decided to go pay respects to Bodhisattva Manjushri in the hope that I will gain wisdom.” “Alright!” the master said, “If you want to pilgrimage to Mount Wutai, then go ahead. I have two letters for you to deliver on your way. One is for Miss Thanh Luong and the other is for Old Madam Zhu.”

When the disciple arrived at the address written on the envelope for Ms. Thanh Lương, she had become a prostitute. The disciple was extremely surprised, "Why would my master write a letter to a prostitute?" He wondered, "Or maybe she is my master's lover, and my master asked me to be the intermediary?" But he handed over the letter and said, "My master, Đỗ Thuận, sent you a letter." Ms. Thanh Lương took the letter, read it, then sat down and said, "Good! He is leaving. I will go too."

Then she died right in her seat. She had entered nirvana. The disciple saw the entire event as very strange, and he picked up the letter to read. He then realized that Ms. Thanh Luong was actually the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, because the letter said, “Avalokiteshvara, I have finished my work here and will depart. You should come with me.” The disciple sighed with regret, “If I had known that was the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, I would have knelt before him, I would not have stood up until he entered nirvana, so that I could have gained wisdom and enlightenment. How wonderful that would have been. But now I have missed the opportunity.”

That is truly in line with the meaning of the phrase: In front of him. Still not recognizing him as Guanyin. He held the letter and headed towards Madame Zhu's residence.

But when he arrived at the address in the letter, no one knew about this person. As he passed by a pigsty, an old sow asked him, "Why are you looking for Madame Zhu?" The disciple was surprised and didn't know what kind of creature he was encountering. He quickly replied, "My master told me to deliver a letter to Madame Zhu." The old sow said, "Oh! Good. I am Madame Zhu. You can give the letter to me."

The old sow received the letter and read it. It was really hard to understand how she could know what was written in the letter. However, after reading it, she sat down and said, “Oh! His work is done. I shall go as well.” And she died. When the young disciple read the letter, he realized that she was the incarnation of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. “Could it be that Bodhisattva Samantabhadra truly is that pig?” The disciple still struggled with doubts. He paid no attention to what work his master had completed, as mentioned in the letter. He went up Mount Wutai. There, he met a very old monk, who asked him, “Why have you come here?” “I have come to pay homage to Bodhisattva Manjushri and hopeto attain the wisdom of enlightenment.”

“This young man!” the old monk said, “You came here to pay respects to Bodhisattva Manjushri, but paying respects to your master is even better by a thousand times.” The bald disciple asked, “Why?”

“Your master, Venerable Tho Thuận, is actually Amitabha Buddha incarnated. He manifests in the human world to teach and guide sentient beings. You have been his disciple for more than 10 years. How could you not recognize that?” “Oh! My master is Amitabha Buddha!” the disciple said, “He doesn’t look anything like Buddha at all!” When the disciple looked back, the old monk had disappeared.

Then he saw a short letter saying: “Bodhisattva Manjushri tells you to return immediately to your teacher, Venerable Do Thuan, for he is Amitabha Buddha.” In the end, the disciple believed it. He met Bodhisattva Manjushri in the flesh, and he instructed him to return to his teacher.

He hurriedly returned; Venerable Master Do Thuan passed away yesterday. Once again, he missed the opportunity. He had been a disciple of Amitabha Buddha for 10 years without recognizing it. He missed what was within his reach in order to seek what was too far away, only to find one thing: that he should return to his master. Now, who is there left to meet?

VENERABLE TUYEN HOA

tieu_de: THE STORY OF SUTRA WRITING INSPIRED BY BODHISATTVA KṢITI GARBHA
tom_tat: (A shared article by a male Buddhist). - I would like to take the liberty to confess my own story about my spiritual connection with Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. May the Buddhas bless those who are karmically connected.
noi_dung:
THE STORY OF COPYING SUTRAS INSPIRED BY BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA

(A shared article by a male Buddhist).

- I would like to respectfully share my personal story about experiencing the spiritual influence of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. I pray that the Buddhas will bless those who are karmically connected.

- Today is 2020. I, through fate, came to know His title. When I heard His vow, "I will not become a Buddha if hell is not empty," I naturally felt extreme admiration and made the resolve to uphold the Kṣitigarbha Sutra without a moment of hesitation. In the past, I was still unclear about the true Dharma, even though I had been a lay Buddhist since childhood. Due to quite stressful work, I chant one chapter of the sutra each day, and on days when I have more energy, I chant more.

- The first inspiring story: BODHISATTVA LEADS ME TO FIND A DEPARTED RELATIVE

I have an older brother, who suffered a stroke and passed away in 2012 when he was still very young, leaving behind a wife and young child. Time quietly passed by; although the person from the past is gone, those who remain still hold immeasurable love and remembrance that cannot fade. I don't know where he is now, in heaven or in hell??? That question keeps lingering in my heart, day after day. Some aunts and uncles said they dreamed that he ascended to heaven, and I was glad to hear that, but I didn't quite believe it—maybe they said that just to comfort me and ease my sadness?

Eight years passed by in a flash, like eight afternoon naps....

When I first recited the complete Kṣitigarbha Sutra, I knew that the Sutra mentioned if any virtuous men or faithful women sincerely wish to know the whereabouts of their deceased relatives and sincerely pray to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, they would receive his assistance. I believed in this, but it felt too far-fetched, so I did not dare to ask him. That noon, lying down, I kept feeling attached and restless, wishing to be guided by Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha to my brother's place, which would be truly wonderful.

I just dozed off for a little while and quickly fell into a deep sleep. In my dream, I felt like I was being swept into a whirlwind, carried into another space, surrounded by an illusory scene; my whole body tumbled like an astronaut in a spacecraft, and then it took me to a vast, infinitely open place, everywhere drifting clouds, with many pleasant and soothing colors. (Later I guessed it was the Realm of the Four Heavenly Kings). Suddenly, I saw far above, my older brother sitting in meditation there. Suddenly, a deep, resonant sound echoed through the sky: "look, look, your older brother"that"

Waking up, I felt both happy and disappointed (because I couldn't talk to you). I know that Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha responded and came to comfort me. Since then, I have begun to diligently recite the Sutra of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha's Original Vows, dedicating the merit to all sentient beings, wishing them to soon leave suffering and attain happiness.

Namo Amitabha Buddha.

Namo Great-Vow Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha

- The second story of spiritual response: RECITING THE KṢITIGARBHA SUTRA TO HELP MY GRANDFATHER'S LIBERATION

My maternal grandfather was from Duy Xuyen, Quang Nam. He passed away in 2013, and now, in 2020, it has been 7 years. Nothing would have been particularly noteworthy if, in June 2020 (when I made the decision to recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra), I hadn't started dreaming about him. In the dream, I saw him walking weakly, his body frail and emaciated, coughing and heaving blood, extremely pitiful, with three or four people on each side supporting him as he staggered along (but I couldn't clearly see their faces)....

In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, it is said that if a virtuous man or woman sees a deceased relative appear in a dream, it is because that person is suffering in the three evil paths, enduring continuous torment, and does not know where to turn for help. Seeing that their descendants uphold the Buddha's sutras, they look towards them in hope of finding a way to be liberated.

Upon waking, I felt a deep affection for my grandfather. I resolved to save him at all costs. From then on, I recited the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and copied it, wishing to dedicate the merit to him and to his adversaries and karmic creditors.

Up until now, it is September 2020, and last night I dreamed of my grandfather once again. But in the dream, he appeared very healthy, rosy, smiling joyfully, with a divine aura,.... he was standing lighting incense in front of a tray of offerings, bowing in thanks around to express gratitude as he prepared to transcend to another realm.

Upon waking, my heart was extremely joyful.

The majesty of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is truly beyond comprehension. I sincerely feel grateful for the response and the compassion toward sentient beings of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. His love for all living beings is immense, profound, boundless, limitless, and beyond any words to express.

His response cannot be seen by our mortal eyes; it can only be felt with the heart.

Namo Amitābha Buddha.

Namo Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva

(Author: Phạm Hữu Đức. Address: Cẩm Lệ, Đà Nẵng, September 2020_lunar calendar: 29.7 - the day of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva)
