tieu_de: FATHER PRAYING FOR SUPERIOR REBIRTH
tom_tat: There was a doctor with the surname Hoang who had a very strange illness; when it got dark, his eyes would roll back, he wouldn't speak or sleep, and he would also punch with his hands and kick with his feet... but as soon as it became daylight, he returned to normal. It is said
noi_dung:
FATHER OF THE SUPERIOR PRAYER RITE

There was a doctor with the surname Hoang who had a very strange illness; when night fell, his eyes would roll back, he wouldn't speak, he wouldn't sleep, and he would even punch and kick… but as soon as morning came, he would return to normal.

It is said that since the onset of the illness, six specialist doctors have examined him, but all were at a loss. His wife also tried treatment through contemporary qigong, but Dr. Hoang did not believe in it and basically refused to go.

Then, Dr. Hoang's wife was enthusiastically introduced by Professor Ly, so she intended to go to seek Master Hoa's help to look at the illness for her husband.

Mrs. Hoang said that her husband did not even believe in qigong, so he probably could not go for Master Hoa to examine him because her husband always thought that "everything is superstition!"

Later, when she got home, Mrs. Hoang told this story to test her husband's opinion. Unexpectedly, Dr. Hoang's eyes lit up, and he anxiously asked:

– What is the name of that Master Hoa?

When he heard the words: "Venerable Master Diệu Pháp," he became so anxious that he could not wait and insisted on contacting Professor Lý at any cost, even expressing his desire to take the Venerable Master as his teacher.

A few days later, Professor Lý, Dr. Hoàng and his wife, and I got into a car to go to Mount Ngũ Đài to pay respects to the Venerable Master before sunset. Since I suggested calling ahead, the Master had already made preparations.

The Master asked Dr. Hoàng.

– Is your father still alive?

Mrs. Hoang answered on behalf of her husband: – Yes, he passed away nearly two years ago...

The master said:

– You still have two older brothers, but your father loved you the most?

At this moment, since it was already dark, Doctor Hoang's eyes started trembling, and he kept silent.

His wife continued to speak on his behalf:

– Master, you are absolutely right, the two brothers are in their hometown, while my husband is in the city. Since childhood, my father-in-law loved him the most.

The monk explained:

– His father, when alive, had committed relatively severe karmic offenses, so after death he had to suffer in the hells. He knew his son had an affinity with Buddha and could help rescue him, so he once sent him dreams. But his son didn’t believe him. Therefore, to escape suffering, he had no choice but to resort to the lower method of 'relying on his son's body' to force him to come to the Buddha for help. You see, now his eye spirit has returned to normal, hasn’t it?

At this moment, everyone turned to look at Dr. Hoang; his face had become rosy and lively. His eyes had regained their usual liveliness.

The master continued speaking:

– Wait a moment, first lead him to the main hall to pay respects to the Buddha.

Tomorrow, a memorial tablet will be set up to pray for his father's soul at the "Ksitigarbha Hall", relying on the power of the monks' sutra chanting, his father will be freed from suffering and attain peace.

Suddenly, Doctor Hoang knelt at the feet of the Venerable Master, with a determined expression, pleading:

– Master, I want to take you as my teacher! Please accept me!

Hearing this, Mrs. Hoang showed a worried, tense expression, not knowing what to do.

I only saw the Venerable smile and say:

– Alright, you may become a lay disciple of the Buddha's teachings!

When I explained to Mrs. Hoang what “lay disciple” meant, she finally breathed a sigh of relief; all this time she had been worried, mistakenly thinking that her husband wanted to… become a monk!

We also paid respects to our Master and brought offerings to the main hall, then together we bowed to the Buddha.

That night, we stayed in the guest room outside the temple. After more than half a year of turmoil, Dr. Hoang finally slept peacefully.

Currently, Dr. Hoang is practicing Buddhism very diligently and industriously. He has always been naturally quiet, but when he hears people praising him, his face lights up, and he cheerfully says:

– This is thanks to me turning a "misfortune" into a "blessing"!

The experienced doctor, who was once a victim and directly suffered from a strange illness that medicine could not cure, was able to have his karmic debts alleviated through the help of an accomplished monk. This enabled him to develop a deep affinity with Buddhism today.

-----------------------------------

THE FETUS LIKES TO LISTEN TO KINH DIA TANG

Ms. Trần, a female neighbor of mine, recently confided: "My daughter is more than seven months pregnant, and recently the fetus in her womb often kicks and punches, causing her immense pain."

I told her, according to Buddhist teachings, the child in the womb is a karmic connection coming to claim its debt and cause suffering. It could also be due to the karma of killing animals for meat. From now on, it is best for the pregnant woman to stop eating meat (that is, stop eating savory food and eat completely vegetarian). She told me to have the fetus recite a set of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra to see. As long as it is recited with utmost sincerity and respect, it will have good effects.

I also added:

– If the pregnant woman is determined to persist in reciting the seven volumes of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and dedicating the merit to her child, it will eliminate the enmity between mother and child; but if she recites the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and it has no effect, then I will let her daughter be eaten again…

Next, I gave her a copy of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra to take home for her daughter to recite.

The next day, Ms. Trần happily thanked me. She said:

– Last night, I went home and told my daughter what the scholar had said. After hearing it, she immediately took a bath and began chanting the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. After finishing the chant, she saw that the fetus stopped being restless and aggressive. Finally, last night, my daughter was able to sleep peacefully. This is a miraculous event that has never happened in the past few months.

At the same time, my daughter also gave up the habit of eating salty food. Madame Trần praised and said:

– The Dharma is truly miraculous. If only my daughter had been guided a little earlier and knew how to chant the sutras regularly, she wouldn't have had to suffer like this, right?

Soon, the daughter of the female scholar Trần gave birth to a lovely baby boy. The childbirth was almost painless. During the month of confinement, every day the child recited a set of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. Previously, the mother preferred salty foods, but strangely, now she hated meat whenever she heard about it. The female scholar Trần asked me the reason why.

I said that disliking the smell of meat is due to the merits gained from reciting sutras, which cleanse the body and mind. This makes the inherent Buddha nature reveal itself, and she no longer desires to consume the flesh of sentient beings. Now her daughter only needs to eat plenty of vegetarian food and fruits, and her body will surely be better than before.

----------------------------------------

THE DISEASE OF SPEECH

If you want to avoid disease

Your mind must be pure

All living beings have feelings

Value life, one must protect it

Ms. Ly from Taiwan came to respectfully ask Venerable Master Diệu Pháp:

– Your mother-in-law is physically healthy, she has no illness, it's just that whenever she goes out, after less than a hundred meters, both of her ankles feel very painful, and she has to sit and rest for a while before she can continue walking. Therefore, she has gone to many hospitals in Taiwan and the United States for examination but they could not find any illness. Please, Master, give some guidance.

– Your mother likes to eat stewed pork leg, doesn't she?

– Yes, Master. How did you know? My mother asks for pork leg every day, and if she cannot eat it, she cannot sleep that night – Ms. Li said with a trembling voice, her eyes brimming with tears, her face full of emotion.

– Go home and tell your mother that from now on she must not eat pig's trotter anymore. If she can repent, practice vegetarianism, and recite Buddha's name, her illness will gradually heal.

The female scholar asked:

– Why can't she eat pig's trotter?

The master explained:

– As you sow, so shall you reap! People who like to eat fish eyes often suffer from eye problems, those who enjoy chewing chicken necks will have issues with their neck bones. People obsessed with eating pork intestines will have stomach aches… Don’t be foolishly gullible by believing in the theory “eating a certain organ of an animal nourishes the corresponding organ in your own body”; if you keep thinking that consuming these things will benefit certain parts, it is completely mistaken! Besides harming others for your own benefit, in the end, the result is self-harm. You will certainly face retribution and have to repay the debt.

Excerpt from "Báo Ứng Hiện Đời" - Translated by Hạnh Đoan

Proofread by: Quang Từ

tieu_de: This is the ritual of offering to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva
tom_tat: The first sutra that Venerable Tuyen Hoa read was the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, the first sutra he gave a lecture on was the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, and the first sutra he practiced by prostrating and reciting was the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. This is a Bodhisattva in the Dharma-body form.
noi_dung:
This is the ritual of offering to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha

"The first sutra Master Hsuan Hua read was the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, the first sutra he lectured on was the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, the first sutra he practiced and chanted on his knees was the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. This is a Bodhisattva of the Dharmakaya, a great being, who returned to this Saha world to teach sentient beings, but he also particularly followed this sutra.

"When Master Hsuan Hua went abroad to propagate the Dharma, he also often spoke about the Kṣitigarbha Sutra.

"Master Xuan Hua said: those who want to change their life's destiny, those who want to follow me through aesthetic practice at the Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery, under my guidance, but currently are not yet qualified or capable. If you study the Ksitigarbha Sutra, Master Ksitigarbha will bless you, and you will be able to follow me. Those who want to change their lives, memorize the Ksitigarbha Sutra; this is a way to offer respect to Master Ksitigarbha.

"Advising people to follow Master Ksitigarbha is a way to offer respect to Master Ksitigarbha.

"Offering the Dharma is greater than offering material gifts; it is countless times beyond comparison.

"Studying one chapter of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra is also a Dharma offering to Kṣitigarbha; copying the Kṣitigarbha Sutra is also a Dharma offering to Kṣitigarbha.

"Chapters 2, 6, 11, 12, 13 are very important. These chapters talk about the benefits of Kṣitigarbha, the benefits of memorizing the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, or a single chapter, or a story in the Kṣitigarbha Sutra; the merits are beyond discussion."

"When going down to Hell, the King of Hell interrogates a person's crimes. If that person has ever memorized the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, even a single chapter or a single story from the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will come and say: This person has once studied a chapter or a story from the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. The King of Hell will release them and not hold them accountable; this person will not be condemned to the three evil paths.

"Kṣitigarbha Sutra, Chapter 12: Those who sincerely take refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, from this life onward, will never fall into the three evil paths; Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will protect them."

"The Kṣitigarbha Sutra, Chapter 2: The Buddha Shakyamuni instructed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. If sentient beings only bring benefits as tiny as a hair or a strand to Kṣitigarbha, he will save them. How much more so if one takes refuge in him; it is inconceivable that one would fall into the three evil realms, as this principle naturally does not exist.

"If we cannot attain rebirth in the Pure Land through merely reciting the Buddha's name, we also will not fall into the three evil realms for countless lifetimes. This is because we have the practice of making offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva."

"When practicing, being influenced by Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, the path of cultivation will not be obstructed; worries about food, clothing, money, husband and children, wife and children, and work will be protected by Him. Do you want rebirth in the Pure Land, right? I will assist you so that you can have a single-minded, undisturbed mind to be reborn. If you want to attain enlightenment, I will support you to quickly achieve it. If you are pulled by your predestined karma, I will take your place so that you can practice in peace. If you fall into evil ways, I will save you. That is why all Buddhas of the ten directions specially praise Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and say that He is like the most precious mani jewel of the Buddhas in the ten directions."

"The mani jewel is unique, and very precious. In the Kṣitigarbha Ten Orbits Sutra, the Buddhas of the ten directions say that Kṣitigarbha is the mani jewel of the Buddha." "Most ghosts and spirits are disciples of Kṣitigarbha in great numbers. If one respectfully offers worship to Kṣitigarbha, one will be protected by Dharmapālas. Ordinary recitation of mantras may not necessarily gain the support of these Dharmapālas, especially if one is not sincerely practicing or observing precepts."

"Sutra of Kṣitigarbha, Chapter 6: Ghosts and spirits rejoice with those who are truly sincere in their cultivation. Regarding the Buddha Dharma, if there is even a single thought of reverence, they will offer protection. Moreover, since we follow Lord Kṣitigarbha, wouldn't they provide their blessings? Lord Kṣitigarbha will send beings in that area to protect us.

"Source: Complete An Si Records.

"Namo Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-Sattva 🙏🙏🙏❤️❤️❤️🌹🌹🌹.

"Namo Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-Sattva 🙏🙏🙏❤️❤️❤️🌹🌹🌹.

"Namo Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva 🙏🙏🙏❤️❤️❤️🌹🌹🌹.

tieu_de: CHANTING MANTRAS - BASIC CONCEPTS FOR BEGINNERS
tom_tat: (Quang Tử) Reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, reciting the Rebirth Mantra, or the Six-Syllable Great Bright Mantra ... these are not unfamiliar things to most people who practice the Buddhist Dharma.
noi_dung:
CHANTING MANTRAS - BASIC CONCEPTS FOR BEGINNERS

(Quang Tử)

Reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, the Rebirth Mantra, or the Six-Syllable Great Brightness Mantra... these are not unfamiliar to most people who practice Buddhism.

However, many people, even after reciting for many years and experiencing some miraculous responses, still remain vague when asked questions such as "What is a mantra?", "Why does reciting a mantra work even when we don't understand it?", "What merits are gained from reciting a mantra?"

In this article, Quang Tu will try to explain in the easiest way possible, so that everyone can clearly understand.

1. WHAT IS A MANTRA?

A mantra, also called a sacred word, or Dharani (or Da Ra Ni), simply put, is a mysterious code that contains the truth and the essence energy of the Universe, used by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who concentrate their wisdom into condensed sounds and concise words, creating mantras or mantra texts.

Because it is condensed and concentrated, the meaning in each line of the mantra is complex and profound, beyond the comprehension of ordinary thinking; only the wisdom of Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas can fully and correctly understand the meaning of the mantra.

Therefore, mantras are not translated; those who recite them only need to read with faith without understanding the meaning, yet they can still manifest the power of the mantra. This is different from the practice of reciting sutras, which requires understanding the meaning clearly in order to practice.

Reading with faith without understanding the meaning is like when we are sick, we go to a pharmacist, buy medicine, and take it to get cured.

Experts, professors, doctors, pharmacists… with high professional knowledge in medicine, use their understanding to formulate medicinal ingredients with precise proportions, along with complex preparation processes to create pills.

Patients who want to get well only need to take the medicine in the appropriate dosage, and they will be cured even if they do not understand what the ingredients of the pills are or how they are made.

It's not that medical professors with PhDs don't want patients to understand the ingredients and preparation methods of medicine before taking it. It's just that doing so is too difficult for the patients' level of understanding.

It requires many years, even several decades of dedicated study and research to be qualified enough to fully understand the components, preparation methods, and mechanisms of a pill. If one had to wait that long to understand it before taking the medicine, the patient would have already passed away.

Therefore, the patient only has one option: to trust the doctor and the pharmaceutical company, take the medicine as directed without needing to understand anything, and still be able to recover.

This is similar to using a key to open a locked treasure chest. The person given the key does not need to know how the inside of the lock is constructed, how the pins or grooves are arranged, they just need to insert the key into the lock, turn it once, and the treasure chest opens, allowing them to take the gold, silver, and jewels to spend.

Similarly, those who are destined and decide to choose the practice of reciting mantras for cultivation only need to trust in the wisdom and abilities of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, who have compiled these mantras; by reciting accordingly, they will achieve miraculous results.

If one does not believe, then it is best to choose another practice. The Dharma has many different practices for us to choose from; if one method does not suit, we can choose another, and that is perfectly fine.

It should also be added that mantras are not exclusive to Buddhism; other religions and popular beliefs also have mantras, notably including the mantras of Taoism that Taoist priests often use to exorcise spirits, as well as the mantras of shamans and folk magic masters.

The difference of mantras in Buddhism is that they always bring good things to those who recite them, without fear of side effects, and they always contain the seeds of Bodhi, containing the potential of Buddhahood, enabling the reciters to continually increase their good karmic connections, until sometime in the distant future they may become Buddhas.

– So how are Buddhist mantras transmitted nowadays?

Originally, during the time of the Buddha, either Buddha Shakyamuni himself or great Bodhisattvas would expound mantras. After Buddha Shakyamuni entered Nirvana, Ananda compiled these mantras into the scriptures, which not only contained the mantras but also clearly described the circumstances in which the Buddha or the Bodhisattvas expounded the mantras, along with their efficacy, methods of practice… those mantras that were publicly taught are called universal mantras, and anyone who is inclined to recite them can do so.

For example, the Great Compassion Mantra, spoken by Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara in the Great Compassion Heart Dharani Sutra; the Surangama Mantra, spoken by Buddha Shakyamuni in the Surangama Sutra; the Precious Seal Dharani, spoken by Buddha Shakyamuni in the Sutra of the Secret Heart of All Tathagatas' Complete Body Relic Dharani; the Rebirth Mantra, spoken by Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in the Sutra of the Perfection of Mindfulness of the Buddha… along with thousands of other mantras that have been publicly transmitted in many other scriptures.

If we want to know clearly, we should spend a lot of time studying the scriptures left by the Buddha; without studying, knowing everything is like picking stars from the sky.

However, there are many mantras with special characteristics, not everyone is allowed to recite them. The Buddha and the Bodhisattvas only transmit them to those with sufficient affinity, level, and virtue, passing them down secretly from generation to generation, which are called secret mantras. Since they are secret, we do not need to explore them deeply; thousands of common mantras are already more than enough for everyone to practice.

2. MERITS AND BENEFITS OF READING MANTRAS

Each mantra contains its own specific powers and unique characteristics, yet generally shares the following attributes:

1. Eliminating karmic obstructions

As a result, the reader can avoid misfortunes, disasters, illnesses, and suffering...

2. Increasing blessings

Thus, the reader can encounter more luck, gain wisdom and virtue, and reap many good things...

3. Creating the specific functions of a mantra

For example, the Lăng Nghiêm mantra has the function of exorcising evil spirits and breaking strong obstacles; the Vãng Sinh mantra helps the reader eliminate karma and be reborn early into the Pure Land. The Biến Thực mantra has the function of transforming provisions into abundance, the Đại Bi mantra is all-powerful, capable of curing illnesses, enhancing wisdom, performing supernatural feats, and quickly attaining enlightenment.

To clearly understand the function of each mantra, the only way is to carefully read it in the scripture where that mantra is described.

4. Invoking the blessing of the Buddha or Bodhisattva who expounded that mantra.

This is a marvelous thing that not every Dharma practice possesses. Most Dharma practices in Buddhism require the practitioner to rely on their own effort, called self-power. The more effort one exerts in practice, the more accomplishment one attains.

There are specifically two practices, reciting mantras and chanting the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, through which one receives additional other-power. What is other-power like?

When reciting a certain mantra, or chanting the name of a particular Buddha or Bodhisattva, besides the merit gained from the effort of recitation, the practitioner also receives special blessings from the Buddha or Bodhisattva – the principal deity who revealed that mantra – along with the support of many benevolent deities and Dharma protectors to help achieve results quickly, which is called external force (thā lực).

Having both the merit from one's own effort and the additional external force from the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, practitioners following these two methods often quickly encounter marvelous spiritual responses.

5. Cultivating the Bodhicitta

Simply put, Bodhicitta is the initial seed that allows one to become a Buddha. Once planted, this seed never deteriorates, but slowly germinates and gradually grows.

Through countless lifetimes, even if one reincarnates many times without remembering anything, whether as a human, or having to be an animal, a hungry ghost, or entering hell, Bodhicitta does not disappear. It silently guides us toward goodness, toward the Dharma, to practice and accumulate merit gradually until one becomes a Buddha.

The first four characteristics (reducing negative karma, increasing merit, special abilities, protection) can be observed in the present, more or less depending on each person, while the fifth characteristic (planting the Bodhi seed) can only be seen after countless future lifetimes.

The first four characteristics require meeting quite a few conditions during practice to be achieved, and violating prohibitions will cause them to be lost (details will be explained in a later article), whereas the fifth characteristic, once read, certainly plants the Bodhi Seed Mind and is never lost.

For those with limited intellect, who like results to come immediately, they will consider the first four qualities more important than the fifth quality.

But for those with far-sighted intelligence, seeing far beyond countless eons, understanding the impermanence of gains and losses of all things, they will realize that the fifth quality – sowing the Bodhi seed to possibly become a Buddha in the future – is truly the most important.

(Quang Tu)

________________

In the next lesson, we will learn about the factors that increase or decrease merit when reciting mantras.

Source: Quang Tử

tieu_de: Repentance of Kṣitigarbha
tom_tat: Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva made many great vows, Having gone through countless changes and transformations,
noi_dung:
Kṣitigarbha Repentance

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva made many great vows,

Having gone through countless transformations,

He manifests himself everywhere as he wanders,

Determined to save beings from being trapped in suffering.

If there are still those in the midst of anguish,

He would not rest in attaining Bodhi,

In the ten fearful gates of hell,

He still sees imprisonment never empty.

He vowed not to seek Buddhahood,

True compassion is wide and deep,

Hoping beings reach high levels,

Deeply understanding the whole path, the merit of practice.

By then fame and profit are wiped away,

Everywhere is pure, serene, and peaceful,

As the Tathagata speaks in the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra,

The heavens of Trāyastriṃśa, His cultivated deeds.

Countless kalpas, there is one kind-hearted,

Through many lifetimes, only aiming to cultivate virtue,

Whether as man, woman, king, or commoner,

In every life, He is always compassionate and beneficial to others.

In one life, transforming into a Brahmin woman,

Wholeheartedly persuading her elderly mother,

After death, descending to hell,

Feeling pity, she prays to the Buddha named Enlightened Flower.

A sincere heart also resonates with the Buddha,

Thus guiding the way to rescue and save from sin,

Quang Muc, the wealthy layman incarnation,

In every life, You always uphold filial piety.

During the Jin dynasty, the people lived in peace,

With the title Vinh Huy, You passed away and were reborn,

In the palaces of Silla,

Your name was Kieu Giac, with the family name Kim.

At the age of twenty-four, You resolved to seek the Great Way,

Meditating in seclusion on Mount Cuu Hoa to cultivate Yourself,

For seventy-five years, You avoided worldly dust,

Just ninety-nine years old, he attained the high fruit of realization.

At that time, Cat Hao of the Min family,

Every year held a single Buddhist lay assembly,

At the time of offering to Buddha for peace,

He would carefully prepare the rituals to invite the Buddha.

Descending to certify the lay assembly of bright monks,

Performing miraculous methods to save sentient beings,

Min Gong had a virtuous son,

Dao Minh, whose name manifested in accordance with the Master.

Twenty years without sparing effort,

So one quickly clearly understands the mysterious path,

Taking refuge first for the child, then for the parent,

Both attain the fruit, following on both sides.

In the last life, as previously mentioned,

Truly glorious for those who practice,

One hundred and nineteen enjoy life,

Pass away at thirty, in a good and healthy month of autumn.

Because long lives of diligent practice finally bear fruit,

You attained the holy path and manifested enlightenment,

Bestowed the great title of Saint Kṣitigarbha,

Sovereign of the Dark Realm, guiding and saving sentient beings.

In the hells, the dark realm became a realm,

Thanks to your virtue, beings are relieved from extreme suffering,

Countless imprisoned sentient beings,

Repent, recite sutras, and cultivate practice.

The Tāvatiṃsa Heaven proclaims Kṣitigarbha's name,

The Tathāgata expounded teachings for you,

By the time of the statue era, the world is full of suffering,

Replaces holding the true Dharma to arrange salvation for beings.

Waiting for the time of Maitreya's descent,

That is the day of successful fulfillment,

Truly manifest and miraculous,

The incarnations roam transforming through the ten realms.

If there are those who think of the heavens and recite Buddha's name,

According to their good causes, the Lord secretly guides them,

Helping them cross the river of delusion,

Arrive at the shore of free and peaceful enlightenment.

Hand holding the golden staff.

Cave opens prison doors, saving all beings.

Sincerely think of the name.

Manifestation responds, prison is completely dissolved.

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, King of Light, Great Vow to Save Suffering 🙏🙏🙏

Collection of repentance texts by Thích Quảng Tịnh

Source: Dũng Louis

tieu_de: BY OPENING THE KṢITIGARBHA SUTRA AT HOME AND OFFERING IT TO THE BEINGS OF THE DHARMA REALM, IT HELPS RESOLVE KARMIC HATREDS FROM MANY LIVES.
tom_tat: Dear fellow practitioners, I am Nguyễn Thị Hiền, Dharma name Minh Hoà, Facebook name Hoa Ưu Đàm. People often call me Ưu Đàm. I would like to share a miraculous aspect of Buddhist Dharma, which is opening the Kṣitigarbha Sutra.
noi_dung:
ASKING TO OPEN THE EARTH KŌZANG IN THE HOUSE TO OFFER TO SENTIENT BEINGS IN ORDER TO HELP RESOLVE KARMIC OBJECTIONS FROM MANY LIVES.

Dear fellow practitioners, I am Nguyễn Thị Hiền, Dharma name Minh Hoà, Facebook name Hoa Ưu Đàm. People often call me Ưu Đàm. I would like to share a miraculous aspect of Buddhist Dharma, which is to open the Kṣitigarbha Sutra continuously day and night to offer it to beings in the invisible realm:

My family knows about Buddha but does not practice following Buddha. So from a young age, I was very ignorant and often caught fish, snails, and so on to eat. Our family raised cows, so when I went to herd them, I often caught my friends—dragonflies, grasshoppers, locusts, snails, and so on—to make toys. For some friends, I would break their wings; for some, I would twist their legs; for some, I would tear them in half; for others, I would squash them... and countless friends died miserably at my hands. Yet I still did not realize that this was extremely heavy evil karma.

Growing up and getting married, not understanding cause and effect, not knowing Buddhist teachings. So I worked in raising pigs for meat. Although I didn't kill the pigs with my own hands, raising them for people to eat their meat is also creating a great karmic debt. Then I also had several abortions. Karma upon karma.

I thought life would go smoothly without problems until 2014. Karma began to manifest. I lost a few front teeth right at the door, just like when I pulled out the teeth of some grasshoppers, and I also had very painful cavities. Before the suffering from my teeth ended, I got rectal prolapse, with blood and foul-smelling pus continuously oozing from the area around my anus, making me lose the will to live. Then I also got gallstones, with excruciating pain that made me sweat profusely. It was really just like when I used to torment the grasshoppers... Back then, I became so thin from the pain, I didn't want to live anymore. Through that fate, I came to know the Great Compassion Mantra and later the Earth Store Sutra.

After that, I chanted the Great Compassion Mantra and went to release animals. My illness required me to go to the hospital, and the doctor said I had to remove a tumor in the anus. However, strangely, after one week of reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, the tumor gradually diminished and disappeared. From then on, I began to study Buddhist teachings. Subsequently, I came to know the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra. Then I read in the Sutra and felt a horrifying fear because of the evil deeds I had committed.

From then on, I vowed to propagate the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra throughout my life. In 2018, I began to conduct the Kṣitigarbha Sutra continuously day and night, offering it to all beings in the Dharma realm. And truly, the benefits are beyond imagination.

In July 2020. When I was chanting Buddha's name, I saw countless beings. Friends were killed by me, babies were aborted by me... and some deities came. They looked at me and said in unison: "Thank you, Ưu Đàm, for opening the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for us. We came to pay respect to Ưu Đàm, now we are leaving." After saying that, they slowly departed.

Truly, the greatest luck of my life is knowing the Dharma of the Buddha. I just want to tell my fellow practitioners: "Any evil karma we create, whether unintentional or intentional, will inevitably result in immense consequences." Therefore, I hope that my fellow practitioners will think carefully before doing anything.

These are a few words I have written here. I hope my fellow practitioners can take them as an example. The Buddha's Dharma is miraculous and beyond comprehension. I hope that if you have come to know the Dharma, you will cherish it. Do not let it go to waste, for it may take countless lifetimes before one has the chance to encounter the Dharma again.

I vow to connect the karmic merit with all sentient beings throughout the entire void, throughout the entire dharma realm. I vow to recite Amitabha Buddha with all sentient beings to be reborn in the Pure Land. So that when leaving this body, we can simultaneously be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss under the door of Amitabha Buddha.

I vow to dedicate this merit

To adorn the Buddha's Pure Land

Above, to repay the four great debts of gratitude

Below, to save the suffering of the three realms

If anyone sees or hears this

May they all generate the bodhi mind

Finishing a body of karmic retribution

Rebirth together in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Namo Repentant Bodhisattva

Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva

Namo Amitabha Buddha

Source: Hoa Uu Dam

tieu_de: An earthquake that the U Minh realm had to carefully plan for 50 years?
tom_tat: He was an honest and upright official, a whole life without shame in his heart. Yet when the earthquake occurred, all his children died, and he himself was injured in the leg, causing him to lament: Must be ch
noi_dung:
An earthquake that the U Minh realm had to painstakingly plan for 50 years?

He was an honest and upright official, living a life without shame in his heart. Yet when the earthquake occurred, all his children died, and he himself was injured in the leg, causing him to sigh: Could it be that Heaven's justice is so unfair?

Ngưu Thụ Mai (1791-1875), courtesy name Tuyết Tiều, pen name Tỉnh Trai, was a native of Thông Vị, Gansu Province. He passed the doctoral examination in the 21st year of the Daoguang era, and in the 28th year of Daoguang, he was appointed Prefect of a region in Xiang Prefecture, Ningyuan County, Sichuan Province.

According to records, on the night of the 7th day of the 8th month in the 30th year of the Daoguang era (i.e., September 12, 1850), a major earthquake struck the Xichang region. The entire city shook, houses collapsed, and everywhere was filled with cries of grief and lamentation. The night was accompanied by heavy rain and strong winds, making rescue efforts difficult in many places. When morning came, the city was nothing but a heap of ruined rubble, and countless people were crushed to death by wood and stones. Prefect Niu Shumai was also trapped under the debris and injured in the leg; he was fortunate to survive while all of his children perished.

Witnessing the entire city being leveled to the ground, people losing their homes, and the populace suffering, Niu Thu Mai painfully wrote an essay questioning the City God: Why do You enjoy the incense offerings of the people but fail to protect them, causing countless beings in this region to die unjustly? Are they all evil people? Moreover, I have lived my life as an honest official, diligent and cautious, with a clear conscience. Why must my innocent children die? Doesn't this mean the gods oversee in ignorance, and that Heaven's justice is unfair?

At night, Niu Shu Mai dreamt that he went to the City God’s mansion. The City God performed the rituals for host and guest with him, saying: "Sir, your eloquent words wrote a piece to reprimand me, which is because you do not understand the supervisory way of the Deities. Therefore, I especially invite you here to clear all the grievances and doubts in your heart!"

“All major disasters do not arise randomly, but are the result of accumulated evil deeds. Because of this earthquake, the Underworld had to investigate and record for 50 years. Anyone who should not suffer the disaster was moved to another place early on. As for those who have recently added new sins, it causes them to return. Perhaps at that time there will be some inconsistency, but the Underworld already has clear records and investigations, and will absolutely not allow innocent people to die unjustly.”

Ngưu Thụ Mai said: “If that is the case, could it be that there is not a single good person in the entire city? What is the reason that I and my children are also punished by Heaven in this way?”

The City Deity said: “In the city, there are three households, indeed it is difficult to move them in such a short time, but currently all are safe and unharmed. First, there is a widow living on a certain street, she has been widowed for three generations and is now raising a young grandchild. Second, there is a doctor, who has never sold fake medicine; when people invite him to treat illnesses, even in the late night during rain and wind, with muddy and difficult roads, he immediately goes and treats them wholeheartedly. There is also a family of a grandmother who sells fried cakes, who also did not encounter any misfortune.”

"If you don't believe it, then investigate and inquire; you will surely find out. As for your children, because in their past life they accumulated deep sins, in this life they cannot easily avoid calamities. This is also taking advantage of this opportunity to repay their karmic debts. You yourself in this life are also subject to fate, but because you are an honest official, you are shown leniency, and only your leg was injured. In short, the rewards and punishments of Heaven are extremely careful and absolutely do not favor any individual. Understanding this law of cause and effect, I hope you strive to do even better; in the future, your position will surely be promoted to that of an inspector.”

Ngưu Thụ Mai, upon hearing this, suddenly woke up to clarity, feeling guilty in his heart, and then bid farewell and returned. After waking up, he inquired everywhere, and indeed found the person's temple caretaker and herbal doctor that Thần Thành Hoàng mentioned, and they were truly safe and sound. As for the old woman selling pancakes, after several inquiries, he also found her in a small corner supported by a few wooden beams of the house.

The old lady recounted that on normal days she would sell fried cakes here, and anyone who was disabled, elderly, young, or poor and could not pay she would welcome, sometimes even giving them for free. One or two days before the earthquake occurred, there were suddenly more buyers than usual, so she took her grandchild to make cakes all night. That day, an earthquake suddenly happened, and the two of them were trapped under the collapsed roof with no way to escape. Fortunately, they had a lot of fried cakes to eat, so the two of them were luckily able to survive.

Nguu Thu Mai could not help but be astonished; he blamed himself for his own lack of virtue, feeling unable to protect the people. He resolved to take the suffering of the people as his responsibility, helping them rebuild their homes, while also donating 1,500 taels of silver to properly support those affected by the disaster. From then on, Nguu Thu Mai increasingly believed in karma, continuously cultivating himself, promoting goodness, following righteousness, and ensuring that the people would not suffer unjustly. The people lived in peace and were immensely grateful, and everyone called him Nguu Thanh Thien. Later, he was indeed promoted to the position of Inspector of Sichuan.

Ngưu Thụ Mai's official record was illustrious, and he was praised by the court as "the foremost in following principles," loving the people like his own children. In the 13th year of the Tongzhi reign, Ngưu Thụ Mai returned to his hometown, devoted himself to reading and writing, and his works include "Tỉnh Trai Complete Collection," "Văn Thiện Lục," "Ngưu Family Sayings," and so on.

At Xuan Ngu beach, Nam Quan, Thanh Duc Xuong district, Sichuan province, the villagers spontaneously raised money to build a three-arch gate engraved with the words "Ngưu Thụ Mai Đức Chính Phường." During the "Destroy the Four Olds" campaign of the Cultural Revolution, the three-arch gate was at risk of being demolished. At that time, people from the county cultural palace covered the gate with a layer of cement and then added a layer of white powder to write the words "Quotations from Chairman Mao." Thanks to this, the three-arch gate fortunately escaped destruction and has remained until today.

All things in the world have a cause. From the perspective of modern science, earthquakes are a phenomenon of geological change, but the fundamental cause is the karmic force of sentient beings that leads to it. Natural disasters among humans are actually also consequences caused by human immorality.

All natural disasters are related to the karma accumulated from life to life. The profound and mysterious law of cause and effect is not something that humans can arrogantly add reasoning to based on experience or knowledge. The world may seem chaotic and disorderly at first glance, but in reality, everything has already been arranged.

Because of an earthquake in the human world, the U Minh realm has carefully calculated for 50 years. In an accident, if one wants to turn danger into safety, one must follow the way of heaven, self-reflect, and value virtue and practice goodness; this is the effective method to help us find peace.

tieu_de: SPEND TIME ON SPIRITUAL LIFE
tom_tat: Source: Facebook Ái Liên Master SPENDS TIME FOR SPIRITUAL LIFE
noi_dung:
SPENDING TIME ON SPIRITUAL LIFE

Source: Facebook Ái Liên Sư Cô

DEDICATE TIME TO SPIRITUAL LIFE

As a child of Buddha, every day one should spend at least about 15 to 30 minutes practicing the Dharma.

Meditating, chanting sutras, reciting the Buddha’s name, reciting mantras, walking meditation, counting the breath… any practice convenient for the Buddhist practitioner is acceptable. The time for practicing the Dharma should be valued and prioritized most in a day. Consider this as a precious time, as if we are roofing a Dharma house or building a Dharma temple. Perhaps we do not need it now, but in the dark night alone in the wind and rain, has anyone thought about it yet?

Many Buddhist followers here might say they don't have enough time, but that's not really the case. We have time to watch TV, time to listen to music, time to sleep, so if we take a little time from each of these activities, it is still enough for us to practice the Dharma.

Life consists of a part of material life and a part of spiritual life; the precious thing is that we know how to balance each a little. Because if our mind is not strong, even if 'everything is going normally,' we will still feel insecure inside.

The benefits of practicing Buddhism are not something we have to wait for in a future life; we can enjoy them right in this life. This is the priceless comfort that Buddhists receive when practicing the Dharma.

A few words to share, wishing everyone peace in the teachings of the Buddha.

*********

- Many, a hundred years in one lifetime

Everyone must leave eventually!

Live in a way that is full of meaning

So that the pass-away moment sees a smiling face..

Như Nhiên

tieu_de: FOUR THINGS THAT DAMAGE MERIT
tom_tat: 👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇 Merit accumulates quickly but is also easily lost. What does it mean to lose merit?
noi_dung:
FOUR THINGS THAT DAMAGE MERIT

👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇

Merit accumulates quickly but can also be lost easily. What does it mean to lose merit?

👉 First, the Buddha taught that if one does good deeds but boasts about the merit just gained, that merit is immediately lost. For example, boasting right after doing charity is a very quick way to lose merit.

👉 The second thing that diminishes merit is instead of rejoicing when others do good deeds, feeling jealousy; in this way, one loses an amount of merit equal to the merit they have just done. For example, when hearing that a friend has just received an award or done something good, if one thinks "how ridiculous," then one immediately loses a lot of merit. Therefore, when seeing someone do something good, it is best to rejoice, or at the very least, not feel uncomfortable when they do good deeds.

👉 The third thing that destroys merit is regretting doing good. For example, if today you just helped someone, and when you return home you hear a few words from your wife and feel regret for helping them, then all the merit you earned disappears.

👉 The fourth thing that destroys merit is anger. There is a saying that one moment of anger can burn down an entire forest of merit. Anger is very dangerous because all the merit accumulated will be lost when we get angry.

👉 These are four things that harm merit: 'Boasting, Envy, Regretting Good Deeds, and Anger.' If we only build a little, accumulate little merit, but destroy a lot, doing many actions that harm merit, then we will lose a lot of merit.

🙏 Namo Fundamental Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha

One share or one comment from you can help many people access this article more.

Please don't hesitate to put in a little more effort to join hands in bringing wholesome practices, bringing the Dharma of Cause and Effect taught by the Buddha to many people, reducing a bit the darkness of ignorance in life, and increasing a bit the light of Buddha's Teachings, with boundless merit!

🙏 Welcome to share

tieu_de: Reciting Buddha's name can change karma
tom_tat: Her name is Lee..., over 40 years old, living in the United States. She recently learned about Buddhism and exchanged thoughts on Buddhism with me back in May 2014, by chance, when looking into the law of cause and effect. She initially...
noi_dung:
CHANTING BUDDHA'S NAME CAN TRANSFORM KARMA

Her name is Lee…, over 40 years old, living in the United States. She recently learned about Buddhism and came to discuss Buddhism with me back in May 2014, by chance, to look into the cause-and-effect mirror.

At first, she studied Buddhism but did not believe in it; later, the more she practiced, the more she felt the support of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas. Especially after several near-accidents while driving, it seemed as though she was protected, and both she and her vehicle came out unharmed. There was one time when the palms of her hands became itchy, developed blisters, and then were cut as if by a razor from one finger to another, all ten fingers were fine again, then cut again, and after cutting they healed, then peeled off… very painful and burning while working. She had visited many doctors, finished taking medication, and applied ointments (more than a dozen types of creams) but the condition did not resolve, causing severe pain that madeShe moaned incessantly. Changing medicines many times still didn't improve her condition; the doctor admitted defeat and said that this disease was incurable. At that moment, she felt very pained and miserable, so she kept asking herself how to make it end now.

I asked her if she could recall whether she had ever harmed any animals before. She paused for a moment and then suddenly remembered that nine years ago, she had caught fish one by one, put them into a strainer to clean their scales, and ate them without realizing the pain and suffering they experienced. She ate a lot, moving from one bowl to another because at that time she was pregnant and had heard that eating small fish would make giving birth easier. Now, she thinks perhaps karma has begun to take effect, causing her hands to be unable to do anything, constantly aching as if being cut, slashed, and torn.

I said, if you know the cause, you need to sincerely repent for your mistakes. Every day, you should strive to pray, chant the Buddha, and accumulate virtue through charitable deeds to dedicate merit to all those adversaries, as well as the various animals you have once killed, harming their lives, helping them to be reborn in a better realm. Next, gently and lightly stroke your hands while chanting Amitabha Buddha as a way to soothe and resolve karma with these beings. Believe and follow this method; every day practice repentance, chant the Buddha, dedicate merit, and gently stroke your hands.

hands that recite Buddha's name.

Living in an overly civilized country, seeing the material world as paradise, most people only believe in science (things that are tangible and visible) and do not believe in cause and effect, karma, or the spiritual world. When your colleagues see you doing this, they say that you are superstitious, gullible, and trusting in things that are not real, not existing.

Unexpected results, two or three weeks later, her hands healed on their own, the skin became increasingly smooth and no longer showed any trace of that strange disease. She was joyful and moved to tears, her family was surprised, her colleagues stared in astonishment, and even when she went for a check-up and tests at the hospital, the doctors widened their eyes looking at her intensely and then looked down at her hands repeatedly, "Oh, how strange! I had given so much medicine and it still didn’t get cured." She just smiled slightly—it really was completely cured. It was destiny.Then one must know that only sincere repentance is effective. Therefore, if it is a karmic illness, the only way is to wholeheartedly and sincerely repent, then maybe the illness can be treated. Seeing a doctor and spending any amount of money is useless, as it will keep recurring endlessly or turn into another illness.

Colleagues have witnessed from the time she contracted this illness until she fully recovered, it's hard not to believe. Everyone no longer criticizes or blames her but instead asks how she did it and whether she can guide them as well.

A Di Da Buddha, indeed, the repentance and mindfulness of Buddha's name are so miraculous that they can transform karma in a wondrous way! That is the truth, so why don't you do it?

I hope you try to firmly believe in cause and effect; her lesson is also a lesson for us – You reap what you sow – Try to sow good seeds, so that you may have the ability to change your circumstances, change your destiny, and your karmic consequences will improve.

Wishing you diligence and peace.

Namo Amitabha Buddha

Diệu Âm Lệ Hiếu (10/2014)

tieu_de: STRANGE STORY 100% TRUE
tom_tat: Topic: THE TALKING SNAIL.. This whole week, the weather has been pouring rain, so the young people in the upper hamlet, being unemployed, can't go to work. The rainy scene is gloomy and not knowing what to do, so Mr. T invited three more people to go catch snails.
noi_dung:
100% TRUE STRANGE STORY

Topic: THE TALKING SNAIL..

It had been raining heavily all week, so the young men in the neighborhood were unemployed and couldn't go to work. The rainy, gloomy weather and having nothing to do led Mr. T to invite three more people to catch snails to drink, so they all went together. After catching the snails, of the four participants, Mr. H was busy with an urgent matter, and Mr. D went home to pick up his child, so they hadn't started preparing the snails to drink. Mr. T brought the snails home, poured them into a tub to soak, planning to deal with them later. Suddenly, Mr. T felt unwell and went to lie down in his room. A little while later, Mr. T's wife came back, saw the motorbike still at home, didn't know where Mr. T had gone, and went into the room to find him lying unconscious with his whole body turning blue. Mr. T's wife panicked and ran out.The street was filled with shouting so that neighbors could come to help. People gathered and ran into Mr. T's house. At that moment, Mr. T was lying down, shouting loudly and saying, 'If you caught me somewhere, take me back there, or don't blame me.' Among those neighbors was Mr. H. Mr. H suddenly remembered that he had participated in catching snails with Mr. T, so he carried a box of snails to the pond where the four of them had caught snails. After emptying the box of snails, Mr. T at home returned to his usual healthy state as if nothing had happened.

Through the incident that happened, everyone in the neighborhood got goosebumps; the story about a talking snail is true. Upon investigating the matter, it turns out that many people often bring fish and snails there to release them. From this true story, Binh also hopes that everyone should not kill living beings and always dedicate the merit so that troubles can be avoided. On the weekend, I wish the whole family good health and success in life.

tieu_de: PRAYER FOR CENTRAL VIETNAM
tom_tat: Ladies and gentlemen! No further introduction is needed, we all are surely following and turning our hearts to our compatriots in Central Vietnam who are struggling against the floods - the floods
noi_dung:
PRAYER FOR CENTRAL VIETNAM

Dear ladies and gentlemen!

No need for further introduction, surely all of us are following closely, and turning our hearts towards the people of Central Vietnam who are struggling against the floods - floods of historic proportions, with stormy and relentless destructive power.

All over from North to South, the government, organizations, individuals, and I believe including you - the person reading this article, have been, are, and will continue to support in every possible way, whether by contributing effort or resources to help fellow citizens facing natural disasters.

Those acts of help, no matter in what form, are all extremely precious and worthy of appreciation.

And besides material assistance, there is a valuable thing that the community of Buddhist followers can offer to the people of Central Vietnam, which is the merit obtained from each person's practice.

Merit and blessings are invisible, but for those who truly understand the workings of the law of Cause and Effect (Karma), we all know that the people to whom we dedicate the merit of our practice will surely receive it. Thanks to this merit, invisibly, the law of Cause and Effect will quietly be adjusted, greatly reducing damage, sorrow, and loss.

Therefore, Quang Tu humbly requests that you, the readers of this article, please dedicate the precious merit of your practice - at least one hour - to pray for the people of Central Vietnam to be relieved from calamities and dangers.

You can choose to prostrate to the Buddha, recite the Buddha's name, recite the Bodhisattva's name, or choose to chant sutras, recite mantras, etc... any practice you usually follow, because all these practices are taught by the Buddha and all generate great and supreme merit.

If someone does not know which practice to follow, they can simply choose to recite "Namo Amitabha Buddha!" - or "Namo Great Compassion Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva!" to dedicate the merit.

We also do not need to be picky about the formality; kneeling before the Buddha altar is very good, but if not possible, you can walk, drive, or sit somewhere... as long as your attire is proper, you can still chant and recite.

After finishing the practice (try to spend at least 1 hour, the more the better), you should dedicate the merit as follows:

"I vow to dedicate the merit of my practice ... to the people in Central Vietnam who are suffering due to natural disasters, storms, and floods, so that through this merit they may eliminate karmic obstructions and safely overcome these calamities. I also dedicate this merit to the souls of fellow citizens and soldiers, as well as all sentient beings who perished due to natural disasters in recent days, praying that they soon attain peaceful liberation, quickly be reborn in the Pure Land, swiftly achieve Buddhahood, and widely save all sentient beings."

Sincerely grateful for the merit of your contributions and support!

___________________

P.S.: After dedicating the merit, you can comment below the post, not to show off, but just to motivate others to join in. And please share so that the message can spread. Thank you!

tieu_de: THE GOLDEN WORDS OF GRAND ELDER VENERABLE THICH TRI TINH
tom_tat: 1 - Be merciful in forgiveness, do good when you know it, let things happen as they may. 2 - In life, if you want to be leisurely and carefree, do not get involved in interests.
noi_dung:
GOLDEN WORDS OF THE GREAT ELDER VENERABLE THÍCH TRÍ TỊNH

1 - Be merciful in forgiveness, do good when you know it, and go as far as you can.

2 - In life, if you want to be at ease and free, do not get involved in personal gains.

3 - Work when conditions are favorable; if not, be skillful and patient to overcome it.

4 - Eat vegetarian, love people, love animals, chant sutras.

5 - Avoid committing evil deeds. Do good deeds whenever possible.

6 - Love people and also love animals, recite Buddha's name and practice meditation.

7 - Mindfulness starts with the three recollections: Recollection of the Buddha, recollection of the Dharma, recollection of the Sangha.

8 - "Eating the flesh of sentient beings every day while hoping for liberation, that will never happen."

9 - Make time to practice, do not skip it; when busy, do your work; when free, focus your mind: recite Buddha's name, recollect the Dharma, recollect the Sangha.

10 - Being intelligent and knowledgeable is no match for old men and women who are vegetarian and recite Buddha's name.

Source: Collected

tieu_de: I used to be a kind of beast
tom_tat: Because I live near the temple, I know Buddha's teachings: Being a human comes from karma.
noi_dung:
I Used to Be a Beast

Because I am near the temple, I know the Buddha's family

Being a person is born from karma

In this life, I know how to chant sutras and pray

I pray to be free from greed and anger

Ignorance and darkness, afraid of not returning

I join my hands and vow that

Above, I seek the Buddha's path; below, I seek rebirth

How pitiable it is during the practice

Ignorance arises in a turbulent heart

If in past lives one had been human

Would the obstacles in the path of practice be less?

Why then do they rise repeatedly?

Already lacking diligence, still sowing sorrowful karma

I always wish to escape the six realms

Wanting always to practice by observing the mind itself

Fearful that when karma turns in cycles

Being reborn as an animal, how could one practice Dharma.

Pray upon the Three Jewels for rebirth

In the future, may wisdom cut through the veil of delusion.

In this life, simply seek the path directly

Awakening within one's true nature to compassion and benefiting others.

Recognize evil and wrongdoing

Bringing the mind to unite with the Buddha's mind.

Standing above, looking down at the vastness

Feeling compassion for sentient beings who do not practice diligently.

Crying out in lament and sorrow

Going West (the West) does not get buried by the passes and checkpoints.

What a waste of a life as a human.

Without cultivation, one cannot escape the cycle of birth and death.

How long until one can return

Being a human to practice and escape through the six paths.

tieu_de: BEING FATED TO TAKE REFUGE IN BODHISATTVA Ksitigarbha
tom_tat: and met Thien Tri Thuc - My Master is Dieu Thanh. This year I am 33 years old. Two years ago, my family experienced an incident in which two of my relatives passed away only
noi_dung:
THE CAUSE AND CONDITION OF TAKING REFUGE IN KSI.RO BODHISATTVA

and met Thien Tri Thuc - Master

I am Dieu Thanh, 33 years old this year. Two years ago, my family experienced a tragedy when two of my relatives passed away just 10 days apart. The pain was so great, and at that time I did not know about Ksitigarbha (Dia Tang) and did not understand much about Buddhism.

When two of my relatives passed away, I was heavily stressed and had a period of being immersed in negative thoughts and often thinking about the idea of death.

During the 49 days, my mother and I went to the temple near our house to offer prayers and accumulate merit for my father and my sibling. At the temple, there were statues of Bodhisattvas and Kṣitigarbha, but the only one I knew by name was Avalokiteśvara. At that time, I was extremely tired and wished I could find a teacher who could help me escape from negative thoughts and the sins I had committed; I wished I could confess my sins to someone and be helped. During that time, I prayed in my heart like that andI think no one could have enough virtue, intelligence, and compassion to help me.

I am telling a story that probably many people will not believe, but it is true.

My family consists of my husband and two children, renting a separate house one month before that sad event happened.

After being there for 4 or 5 months, my older son, while sitting and studying, suddenly shouted. 'Mom, there is someone's shadow.' At that moment, I thought my child must have seen his own shadow on the wall, so I said it was just the shadow of the ball, not anyone else. My child said no, it was the black shadow of a tall man, so small like him. At that moment, I also got goosebumps but tried to reassure my child that it was nothing. On the second day, my child shouted again while playing in the room with me. He looked into the corner of the wall and said, 'That person again, Mom, he's a man.' At that point, I began to feel scared but still tried to reassure my child. On the third day...My three children saw it again and said they clearly saw that it was the shadow of a tall man. I started to feel scared. That evening, I was cooking. Then I clearly heard next to my ear a man's voice saying: I am the grandfather of the landlady's husband whose house you rent. I ask you to help me with one thing. Send me to the temple to take refuge. Help me and I will not harm your family at all. I will give you many good things.

At that time, I began to realize that she had a connection with me.

I texted and told the monk at my temple to come to that ceremony. The monk said that she had a predestined relationship with the son and the child. So I should do what he said. At that moment, I sincerely believed and promised to do my best for her and to bring her to the temple to take refuge.

After a few months, I invited the monk to my house to perform a ceremony and also invited him to go to the pagoda. I went along and brought 500,000 VND to give to the monk as an offering to the Three Jewels. At that time, the monk put the 500k into the merit box of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. And at that moment, I bowed and prayed in front of the statue. It was then that I realized it was Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Perhaps this was the beginning of my karmic connection with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva!

A few months later, I accidentally came across a Facebook page sharing some quite good Buddhist teachings and credited the source: Quang Tu, along with two other women. At that time, out of the three people, I immediately searched for Quang Tu and found their personal page, even though they weren’t a mutual friend of anyone. I started reading for two consecutive nights about many interesting posts on karma, retribution, and saw there were sins that could lead one down an evil path, and surely I was among them. I was scared and proactively sent a message sharing my thoughts with Quang Tu, hoping to learn Buddhist teachings. ImmediatelyAfter texting Quang, I was shared by him about Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and advised me to take refuge in Him. I immediately decided to switch to a vegetarian diet after just one night without going through a transition period, and until now I still don't understand how I could go from eating meat for 33 years to a vegetarian diet, and at this point, after 7 months, I don't crave any meat, fish, or seafood at all. I don't crave it and don't want to eat it. I eat vegetarian food with joy and comfort, without forcing myself, and I don't crave meat at all; even the smell of beef is very unpleasant to me!

After a few weeks, Quang Tu allowed me to meet the Teacher - the person I had wished to see a year ago, a wish to have someone virtuous, wise, who would save me from stress and negative obsessions!

Since then, my life has changed. I have been guided to practice morality and repent for my sins.

Since then, although the karmic obscurations were deep and the defilements were thick, my devotion and love for Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva increased intensely, and I made a vow to be devoted to Kṣitigarbha and to be the disciple of my Master for countless lifetimes.

I began to be guided by my Master to practice dedicating merits and guiding the spirits of my deceased relatives. The dedication of merits benefits sentient beings in the three evil paths.

And in the seventh lunar month, I met Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva in a dream.

That was on July 15, lunar calendar. My mother arranged a small ceremony in the courtyard of our house to invite the spirits. I stood in front of the ceremony, reciting the name of the Lord and praying for His mercy to save those beings from the three evil paths.

That night, I dreamed that my mother and I were standing right at the beginning of the alley. I picked up a small statue of Kṣitigarbha that had been broken and fallen to the ground. I held it up and carefully reassembled it with immense compassion. A little while later, my mother and I saw that the statue had transformed into the real body of the Master. He was wearing a red kasaya and did not wear a hat (exactly like the Master’s image in the painting where I daily offer prayers and repentance).

He walked with someone who was wearing the same clothes as him (I think he was his disciple). He walked along the road in front of my mother's house during the memorial ceremony for the deceased at 3 PM. He walked slowly, putting his hands together and smiling kindly (I will never forget his face at that time, even though I was standing at the end of the alley). He walked slowly and young and old, male and female, surrounded him.

That was my first dream about You, and I think perhaps my prayers asking You to help the souls in front of my house have been answered by You.

Then there was this thing, which when I think about it again, I also find truly miraculous.

I was practicing kung fu when suddenly an image appeared of my child and my grandchild (5 years old) playing in the room and getting injured, bleeding from a glass object or a sharp object. That image kept appearing continuously, and I suddenly felt anxious. I stopped practicing kung fu and went into the room to see what the two little ones were playing with. I looked into the room and saw the two of them playing happily on the bed.

I continued doing my meticulous work, then just sat down and heard my little boy say to my nephew, "Be careful not to get hurt," and I suddenly felt a pang in my stomach. When I went in, I saw my child holding a sharp piece. At that moment, I didn't think it was glass, I thought it was like a piece of sharp plastic. I threw it into the sink and heard a clinking sound. I realized it was glass, so I ran in and asked the two kids what it was. Both pointed to the thermometer case. It turned out it had broken, and they had hidden the remaining piece in the cabinet. I panicked and looked down at the floor, and oh my, the glass was everywhere.and a piece of broken glass lying right under my feet. But somehow I walked in and didn't step on it, and the two little ones didn't step on it either. At that moment, I got goosebumps thinking about the scene where I was shown and warned about that danger while practicing. Otherwise, the two little ones would have surely stepped on the broken glass and extremely poisonous mercury.

(rewritten according to the account of Ms. Diệu Thanh.)

tieu_de: WHAT EXACTLY IS PRACTICING BUDDHISM???
tom_tat: WHAT IS A BUDDHIST DISCIPLE? What is a Good Man - Good Woman?
noi_dung:
WHAT EXACTLY IS PRACTICING SPIRITUAL DISCIPLINE???

WHAT IS A BUDDHA DISCIPLE?

What does it mean to be a Good Man - Good Woman?

Dear everyone, today this worthless person would like to share a little about this dharma talk, hoping those with affinity can share together.

Writing these words makes me truly ashamed.

Why? Because this worthless person has poor virtue and thin merit, what right do I have to wave my hands and move my feet? But this worthless person also has a few words of experience in practice over the past 10 years, now shared for your reference.

Speaking of true cultivation, this evil person feels a thousandfold ashamed: greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, jealousy, rivalry... all still abound.

The mouth recites Sutras - chants Buddha's name, but the heart cannot let go, still discriminating, clinging to right and wrong, etc...

I secretly think, what does the word 'cultivate' mean? Cultivation is precisely 'TO CORRECT'.

Correct what? To correct this ordinary mind of ours! That is the meaning of the word CULTIVATE.

If we want to study Buddhism, we should first learn how to be a human. If we cannot be a good human, can we truly become a Buddha?

So, how are we living as humans nowadays?

When we open our eyes, is it only about worrying over food, clothing, money, fame, competition, benefits, family, and children?

Can we take these things with us when we die? Yet, these are our habitual tendencies.

When we say we practice cultivation, it means cultivating based on these very things, correcting ourselves right on these very things; you cannot just say prayers or recite scriptures while your mind remains exactly the same without change—this is not the meaning of the word CULTIVATE.

If that is not CULTIVATION, then what is it called? That is precisely selfishness!

Why do we say it is selfish?

Think about it: every day, when you recite scriptures or chant the Buddha's name, is it not usually that you are praying for your family, for health, wealth, children, and so on?

Have you ever chanted Sutras or recited Buddha's name praying for everyone in this world to be happy, healthy, and so on?

Or do you pray for yourself to attain enlightenment and true wisdom?

Instead, do we always follow that old habit of being selfish for ourselves and our family in these impermanent things?

If you chant Sutras or recite Buddha's name and gain no benefit, would you continue? Do you say PRACTICING is to cultivate your mind, or is it to seek something?

Those here daily discuss and learn according to the Buddhist teachings, reading without missing the everyday stories of Cause and Effect... so what are they actually learning?

It is precisely the great compassion that forgets oneself for the sake of others of the Bodhisattvas.

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, in principle, would have become a Buddha countless eons ago and entered Nirvana countless eons ago. But for the sake of these evil beings and all beings, He still endures extreme suffering in the realm of darkness, going throughout the ten directions day and night to find ways to help beings attain liberation and transform their hearts and minds.

If you cannot do this and only engage in empty discussions while your mind is full of uncorrected worldly habits, then it truly disappoints them.

So how shall we correct ourselves?

The ancients said, "Rivers and mountains are easy to change, but human nature is hard to alter."

We cannot correct ourselves by mere words.

Among us here, who claims to be a Buddhist? Who has already taken refuge?

Do you keep the Five Precepts daily or not? If someone has taken Refuge but cannot uphold the Five Precepts, then they are not worthy of being called a Buddhist, and it is not proper to call them as having taken Refuge in the Buddha.

We take Refuge because we want to practice according to the Buddha and observe the Five Precepts, and thereby transform our mind and character. Is it that after taking them, the Precepts belong to the precepts and I belong to myself? Is taking Refuge only to have a Dharma name or just a certificate of refuge?

Precepts are very important, Precepts come first.

All Buddhas of the ten directions achieved enlightenment by keeping the Precepts.

This immoral person, reading in the Tripitaka, has not seen any Buddha who attains enlightenment without observing precepts.

When the Buddha was about to enter Nirvana, Ananda asked:

- O World-Honored One, while You are in the world, we rely on You; now that You have entered Nirvana, whom should we respect as our teacher?

- The Buddha replied: TAKE THE PRECEPTS AS YOUR TEACHER.

If we want to change our mind and nature and wish to be Buddhists, we must observe the precepts.

There is no principle that says: "I practice at the Mind".

May I ask, where is your Mind that you claim to practice at the Mind? Can you show this to a vile person like me?

So, if we just go on lying, being lustful, competing, arrogant... and then claim that we practice at the Mind?

The state of your Mind is reflected in your speech and actions.

So, what does the FIVE PRECEPTS consist of?

Here, if explained in detail, it would be long, so this vile person will give a brief summary:

1. DO NOT KILL: Not even an ant or a mosquito should be killed. Why? Because they all have Buddha-nature and can be reborn as humans and cultivate to become Buddhas.

The word 'sanh' in 'sát sanh' refers to sentient beings, life. An ant or a mosquito is also a sentient being.

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha vowed that as long as there is a single sentient being whom he has not saved to become a Buddha, he will not attain Bodhi.

Why do we take this precept?

Because it is to cultivate compassion and avoid causing more resentment with hostile spirits or wronged souls.

2. DO NOT STEAL: All things that do not belong to you must absolutely not be taken, whether it is a blade of grass, a tree, a needle, whether it is at an office or in the home of family members.

Why do we uphold this precept?

To help us reduce our greed.

3. NO IMMORAL SEX: Within the marital relationship, sexual activity is proper; extramarital affairs are considered immoral sex. Additionally, if spouses watch obscene films together or engage in sexual acts on inappropriate days (Buddha or Bodhisattva days, full moon, the first day of the month, etc.),

or have sexual activity in inappropriate places (outdoors, other areas such as the kitchen, etc.), or engage in masturbation, etc., all are considered immoral sex.

Why must we observe this precept?

The ancients said: Among all evils - SEXUAL IMMORALITY RANKS FIRST.

We really cannot ignore this precept, if you do not want your merit and even your own lifespan to be harmed. Sexual misconduct causes the decline of wisdom, deterioration of health, and makes people despise and look down on you.... If indulged, the consequences are immeasurable: deities and protectors will despise you and leave, hungry ghosts will cling to you, everything will go wrong, your career will decline, nothing you practice will be accomplished, and at the end of this lifetime you may fall into hell. Not to mention that lust and desire also make oneself more arrogant and selfish.... How sorrowful it is, to endure too much evil karma for just a little fleeting pleasure! You definitely muststrictly observe this precept!

4. DO NOT LIE: Meaning all words that are false and untrue, with the purpose of elevating oneself, belittling others, or even deceiving others for personal gain...

If your mind is crooked, your words will be crooked. With such a mind and words, how can one dare to recite Buddha's name - chant mantras - or practice the sutras? Who would attain enlightenment?

5. DO NOT DRINK ALCOHOL OR USE ADDICTIVE SUBSTANCES:

Why must one observe this precept?

If we drink alcohol, the mind will surely go mad, losing self-control and violating all the other four precepts. That is why the Buddha established this precept, also wishing that sentient beings would not be driven to madness, wasting money on things that harm themselves and others.

How many murder cases have been caused by alcohol, leading to ruined families during drunkenness?

How many lives, how much life, how much money... has been wasted?

This wicked person has spoken too much, only hoping that everyone can first learn to become a complete, socially useful human being before learning Buddhism.

Only in this way can we hope that one day the Dharma will be widely spread and truly applied in life, benefiting oneself first and then others.

Respectfully wishing everyone diligent practice and much peace and joy.

NAMO Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva 🙏🏻

tieu_de: DON'T BOAST AND DESTROY YOUR OWN BLESSINGS
tom_tat: 👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇 In what situations do people often destroy their own merits?
noi_dung:
DON'T BOAST AND DESTROY YOUR OWN BLESSINGS

👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇👇

In what situations do people often destroy their own merits?

That is, being proud of one's own merit, being proud of one's own good deeds, boasting about oneself. Whatever you boast about, you must be careful, lest in the future you lose exactly that! When good deeds are hastily shown to others so they know, told to make others happy when they praise you, the merit and blessings are immediately reduced by half, and the more people know, the more the blessings are gone. Often generate a sense of shame, repent. Silently, often practice the perfection of generosity (Bodhisattva practice). Do not cling to the giver, the gift, or the recipient.

For example, if you have a precious gem, you show it off everywhere you go for others to see. In this way, demons will very much want to destroy your gem. Without diligent practice and stabilizing the mind with wisdom, the mind will be unsettled. Consequently, they will take advantage and lead you to accomplish their own intentions.

When working for sentient beings, if the mind sincerely cares for them, do not think of personal gain or benefit, not even in your thoughts. Forget your own benefit for the sake of sentient beings. Truly performing virtuous deeds cannot be measured or fully comprehended.

It is not necessary to show it to the Deities, because every single action of yours, they understand as clearly as in daylight.

Do not use donations or relief funds for personal gain, embezzlement, or misappropriation... The future will fall into the THREE EVIL PATHS. Hell is full of suffering in many forms, whereas if you sincerely use your Heart to truly give Gifts to the Deities, the Happiness received is indescribable.

🙇🏼‍♀️I SINCERELY REPENT

MY SINS PILE UP LIKE MOUNTAINS

GREED, ANGER, IGNORANCE, PRIDE, AND DOUBT ARE ALL PRESENT.

TODAY I SINCERELY REPENT🙇

🙏 Namo Amitabha Buddha

🙏 Namo Repentance Bodhisattva 🙏
