tom_tat: I didn't intend to post this, but since someone mentioned the car accident, I'll explain: Do you know why spirits are restless? Spirits usually linger where they died. If a person normally doesn't know how to practice, kh
noi_dung:
THE STORY OF THE XÔ GHOST

I didn't intend to post this, but since someone mentioned the car accident, I’ll explain:

Do you know why ghosts push people? Spirits who die somewhere usually linger there. If they didn’t practice cultivation or accumulate merit, they suffer greatly and go hungry.

They can gather in groups, waiting for people to pass by so they can push them to death or cause injuries, making people in the human world see that accidents frequently happen there and have to build shrines to feed them to ease their hunger. That is the purpose behind them pushing and causing accidents.

The targets they attack are: heavy drinkers, people with little merit, those whose fate is running out, and those with bad luck. With a disturbed mind, full of greed, anger, and delusion, and having accumulated much evil karma, taking action will easily lead to success.

Therefore, those who travel with strong willpower, abundant good karma, or who frequently recite Buddha's name or practice mantras, they cannot be pushed over.

Many people have confided in me: between 11 PM-12 AM, or 5-6 PM, while driving, suddenly the steering wheel becomes stiff and uncontrollable, as if wanting to plunge into a pit or river; they have to recite Avalokiteshvara's name, or perform mantras, in order to steer according to their will.

That is why I advise you, when walking on the path, to focus your mind on mindfulness.

* The merit of sharing the Dharma is immensely endless; it can eliminate karmic obstacles, change destiny, and increase auspicious causes.

Please be brave in sharing Dharma articles, helping more and more people access the teachings, honoring the Buddha above, and saving countless beings below! Namo Amitabha Buddha!

Author: Venerable Nun Hanh Doan

Source: Nho Phat Niem Phat

tieu_de: SHELF PRAISING BODHISATTVA KṢITI
tom_tat: Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha in the southern land
noi_dung:
PRAISE KÔNG OF Kṣitigarbha

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha

In the southern realm

Flowers and incense swirl with clouds

Good and beautiful, a solemn scene

The Buddhas praise Kṣitigarbha

Bodhisattvas of ten directions have faith

Kṣitigarbha's virtue is immeasurable

Compassion houses virtuous deeds

Saving sentient beings over countless lifetimes

Hands ready holding a golden staff

Saving sentient beings from hell

Holding a bright round jewel in hand

Radiance spreads throughout the Great Heavens

Helping all sentient beings

Perfectly attaining the supreme path.

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha

Advises all sentient beings

Morality, concentration, and wisdom strictly

Taking refuge in the Three Jewels

Practicing the Bodhisattva mind

Offering to parents

Being filial to grandparents

Always keeping precepts

Helping people in trouble

Peaceful and at ease

Refusing invitations

Lowly desires

The merits already made

Dedicate to everywhere

May all beings be liberated.

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha

Admonishing sentient beings

Practicing the Kṣitigarbha conduct

Obtain twenty-eight benefits

Receive the protection of the Buddhas

Gain blessings and good fruit

Attain the stage of Stream-entry

Develop the Bodhi mind

Have sufficient food

Enjoy health and longevity

Avoid accidents

Being protected from theft and robbery

Being respected by sentient beings

Being supported by Bodhisattvas

Being healthy

Being engaged in a good profession

Having a good physical appearance

Being reborn in the heavenly realm

Becoming a noble king

Having perfect wisdom

Having all things as wished

Blessed with a happy family

Freed from calamities

Completely free from evil karma

Safe in walking and standing

Having joyful dreams

Loved ones freed from suffering

Born in a comfortable place

Praised by Bodhisattvas

Clever and intelligent

Wise and compassionate

Attaining ultimate Nirvana.

In the Daoli heaven realm

The World-Honored One speaks the wondrous Dharma

Kṣitigarbha's conduct is profound

His teachings reach thousands of generations

Heavenly beings and humans are freed from suffering.

Now I make a broad vow

To practice Kṣitigarbha's virtuous conduct

Above, to repay the four great debts of gratitude

Below, to help people reduce suffering

If there are people who hear it

All will generate the Bodhi mind

Forsaking illusions caused by karma

Rebirth into the realm of Nirvana. (CCC)

tieu_de: LOVE BODHISATTVAS THE WAY YOU HAVE LOVED A PERSON
tom_tat: TAKING REFUGE IN BODHISATTVAS SHOULD BE PRACTICED DAILY In the past few days, there have been many questions related to taking refuge in the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. I feel that there needs to be an article to clearly explain this for all of you here. Front
noi_dung:
LOVE THE BODHISATTVA THE WAY YOU HAVE LOVED A PERSON

TAKING REFUGE IN BODHISATTVAS SHOULD BE PRACTICED DAILY

In the past few days, there have been many questions related to taking refuge in BODHISATTVA Kṣitigarbha. I feel that it is necessary to have an article to clearly answer for everyone here. This is to prevent people from messaging me and seeing a delayed response.

#question1/ If I have already taken refuge in the Three Jewels, can I also take refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha? Is it disrespectful or might it offend others?

The answer is: you can take refuge in infinite Buddhas as well as infinite Bodhisattvas. After taking refuge in the Triple Gem, taking refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is like giving wings to a tiger. In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, the Buddha praises Kṣitigarbha profusely and encourages all beings to rely on him and take refuge in him. Therefore, taking refuge in him is most in accordance with the wishes of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is a bodhisattva whose merit cannot be matched by anyone, so merely respectfully clasping your hands and reciting his name already brings infinite merit, let alone wanting to take refuge in him yourself and follow the teachings he instructs.

Secondly, Buddhas and bodhisattvas do not hold attachments or jealousy, so they are extremely joyful when they see that you take refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. No Buddha or bodhisattva feels sad because you take refuge in another Bodhisattva or Buddha in front of them. A bodhisattva is only saddened if you take refuge in demons or evil spirits.

We are ordinary people who always think that Buddhas and bodhisattvas are like us. That is truly a mistake.

#question2/ Should one take refuge EVERY DAY or is ONCE ENOUGH

Dieu Nhi answers as follows: YOU SHOULD TAKE REFUGE IN BODHISATTVAS EVERY DAY

WHY IS THAT: Reciting the refuge prayer regularly will help strengthen the bond between you and the Bodhisattva. It's like making a phone call. Right now, if you don't know a friend's number, you just randomly dial among billions of people, making it really hard to find the correct number. But the phone number of BODHISATTVA Kṣitigarbha has already been given to you today. If you want to meet him and want him to see that you love, care, and protect yourself, then you need to maintain regular connection with him.

For example, if we have a friend, a teacher, a parent, but we only call them once in our lifetime, how can our feelings really become close? A path not traveled will be overgrown with weeds; people who do not interact will become strangers. You manage to call the Bodhisattva once and then think, 'Ah, the Bodhisattva answered, ha ha, that's good,' and then you don't call again. Later, overwhelmed with the hustle and bustle of life, you forget about practice and remembering him. So, is there a connection?

The more diligently and sincerely you practice and genuinely make changes, the faster you will be protected by him. Please believe this.

Not only does Nhi take refuge in Him every day, but every day Nhi also spends a lot of time thinking of Him with infinite gratitude and sincere, loving respect as for a real teacher. Nhi also likes to look at His statues and pictures. Every time seeing Him, Nhi feels happy and joyful, smiling. Every day, whether something sad or happy happens, Nhi shares feelings with Him. Or perhaps writes letters to Him... etc. Once, Nhi was so sad that she didn’t want to complain on Facebook, so she wrote a tearful letter to Him, and in her dream, she immediately saw Him coming to comfort her. Friends, you should do the same. It’s miraculous. Love the Bodhisattva just like this.You passionately love someone. You feel pain when they are in pain. You feel sad when they are sad. You feel affection when they are struggling. You want to help, want to be there, want to care, want to protect... then gradually you will gain that person's heart.

Respectfully.

Source: Dieu Nhi

tieu_de: AVOID 6 BEHAVIORS
tom_tat: CAUSING DAMAGE TO MERIT AND FUTURE KARMA                            🌸🌸🌸🍀🌸🌸🌸 Listen to the Buddha's teachings to know and stay away from these 6 behaviors that damage merit. Only then will life be smooth,
noi_dung:
AVOID 6 BEHAVIORS

CAUSING HARM TO MERIT AND FUTURE KARMA 🌸🌸🌸🍀🌸🌸🌸

Listen to the Buddha's teachings to know and avoid these 6 actions that harm your merit. Only then can life be smooth, prosperous, and avoid future karmic consequences.

In this life, everyone wishes to have luck and smoothness in their work. So, if you want to stay away from trouble, scandals, and the loss of merit, follow the Buddha's teachings and avoid these actions. 🍀🍀🍀🍀🍀

🍂1. Complaining, Causing Disputes, Envy, and Jealousy

These are actions that should be avoided as much as possible, because they not only affect harmony between people, but also harm the harmony of heaven and earth.

According to spirituality, if one frequently engages in these actions, their fortune will decline. Even if the ancestors' blessings are abundant, over time, they will eventually diminish. People will find it difficult to accomplish anything, encountering obstacles and even poverty. Speaking ill, slandering others, and discussing disputes—surely, in the future, one will have to face similar situations themselves.

🐠2. Frequently Killing Living Beings

According to the Buddha's teachings, killing is the foremost act that harms one's merit. If one frequently kills, the blessings of their children will be affected, and future generations will have to bear the sinful consequences caused by their parents.

However, in daily life, completely avoiding killing is impossible, for example, when we accidentally step on a worm, an ant, or kill insects that harm us. Therefore, if possible, we should minimize killing as much as we can. We should be aware of the Buddha's teaching on the 7 cases in which one should not kill to avoid harm. If possible, we should avoid work that requires killing, and if it must be done, we should regularly practice good deeds, accumulate merit, and sincerely turn towards the Buddha.

🌊4. Boasting, Arrogance

No one can be proficient in everything; some people are strong in this area, while others are strong in another. If fortunate enough to have ability in a certain field, one should not become arrogant, condescending, or point fingers at others. It is very possible that we are better than others in this area, but when facing issues in another field, others may become our teachers.

People need to know how to be humble and learn; humility helps us progress, while excessive boastfulness and arrogance not only cause us to lag behind, but also affect our future blessings.

🙅🏻5. Conflicts, Frictions With Parents and Superiors

Frequently having conflicts, being rebellious, and arguing with parents and superiors will also affect your blessings. Even if you desire to achieve something, it will not succeed. Filial impiety - Evil deeds will bear the greatest retribution.

Parents are the ones who gave birth and raised their children, and no matter how many times children try to repay them, it will never be enough. Therefore, the duty of children is to obey their parents, not to let their parents feel sad, to be filial, and to use all their strength to repay their parents' kindness. Anyone who can do this will have a happy life, easily achieve their desires, have a smoother path in life, and receive the protection of both celestial beings and spirits. Those who are unfilial and stingy with their parents will encounter difficulties and obstacles in both career and relationships, endure public criticism, and their life will not be joyful. According to the law of cause and effect, conflict, contradiction, and unfilial behavior towards parents...then in the future, the children will also be indifferent, not respecting you.

🍂 6. Lustful, Licentious

Those who are licentious and lustful have an unhealthy mind. This behavior not only harms their own virtue and health but also causes harm to others and violates societal ethics.

According to the teachings of the Buddha, those who engage in this behavior, if their conscience feels guilty, will live in constant unease; if their conscience does not feel guilty, they will face severe karmic repercussions.

🧐 7. Giving Alms Unwillingly or Stingily, Rarely Doing Good Deeds

Generosity must come from one's own heart. When giving to the poor and less fortunate than oneself, one must give sincerely, voluntarily, without using a domineering attitude, condescension, or harming the pride of others just to satisfy personal ego.

If giving alms is done incorrectly, not only will we not receive gratitude, but we may also be hated and resented by others. Giving alms correctly brings joy when practicing Buddhism. Along with that, if our life is full of wealth and material possessions but we still have a single-minded desire to hoard, to enrich ourselves, and are unwilling to share with anyone, our merit will be affected. Money is an external object; we cannot take it with us when we die. It is better to live happily in the present, without greedily hoarding wealth, and when we see ourselves more fortunate than others, to be ready to give alms. In this way, life becomes happy, and good fortune more easily comes to us.

🙏NĀM MÔ AMITĀBHA BUDDHA🙇

tieu_de: OUT OF DANGER
tom_tat: Here it is again, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva! In future lives, if there are any good men and women, whether because of business dealings, personal affairs, birth and death matters, or urgent matters requiring entering the forest
noi_dung:
OUT OF DANGER

Once again, O Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva! In future lives, if there are any good men and women, whether regarding business affairs, personal matters, matters of birth and death, or urgent matters that require entering forests and mountains, or crossing rivers and seas, or encountering great floods, or traveling along dangerous paths.

Before leaving, one should recite the name of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha ten thousand times. By doing so, wherever one goes, there will be spirits protecting them, whether walking, standing, lying, or sitting, they will always be safe and happy, even when encountering wolves... but all harmful things cannot harm that person.

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara: "Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha has a great affinity with the realm of hell. When it comes to the benefits that sentient beings gain by seeing the form or hearing the name of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, even if spoken over hundreds of thousands of aeons, it would not be enough.

O Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara! Therefore, you should use your spiritual power to propagate this Sutra so that sentient beings in the Saha world may enjoy lasting peace for hundreds of thousands of eons.

Excerpt from Chapter 12 of the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Original Vows Sutra

"SEEING AND HEARING THE BENEFITS".

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva 🙏🏻

tieu_de: HOW TO DEDICATE MERIT TO THE SICK (Your Merit and Good Deeds Will Help Relatives, the Living, and the Person)
tom_tat: The best way to dedicate merit for a patient's quick recovery: - Take any valuable items they own and offer them to the Triple Gem or convert them into money to do things like printing sutras, releasing animals, casting statues, helping
noi_dung:
HOW TO DEDICATE MERIT FOR THE SICK (Your Merit and Virtue Will Help Relatives, the Living, and Others)

The best way to dedicate merit for a sick person's swift recovery:

- Take an item of value that they own and offer it to the Three Jewels, or convert it into money to do things like printing scriptures, releasing animals, casting statues, helping the needy...

- Then read the sick person's name and say that you are doing it on their behalf, dedicating this merit to them so they will fully receive it. If they have passed away, they will only receive a part of the merit, and the person doing it will receive six parts.

- At the same time, you should SINCERELY read the Ksitigarbha Sutra and dedicate the merits to their Enemies and Debt Holders. To repay the debts for the sick person.

🍀All these methods are in the middle volumes of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra, originating from Tathagata:

Sixth Chapter:

• Eliminating karmic obstacles:

"Again, O Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara! In the next life, if any man or woman lies paralyzed on a bed, whether they wish to live or die, they will not be able to do so. Or at night, if they dream and see demons, whether toward loved ones in the house, or while walking on dangerous roads, or being oppressed by shadows, or accompanied by spirits and demons."

After many months and years, one becomes afflicted with tuberculosis, with paralysis... In sleep, cries wail, lamenting in deep sorrow. These are all caught up in karmic consequences yet to be determined as light or heavy, so either they are hard to die from, or hard to heal.

The vulgar eyes of the man, the woman cannot clearly discern this, and must only face the images of Buddha and Bodhisattvas, loudly reciting this sutra once.

Or take the personal belongings of an ordinary patient that they treasure, such as clothing, precious items, house, garden, etc., and in front of the patient loudly declare:

“We, [their names], now because this patient, in front of the image of veneration, brings these items to offer or dedicate to the image of veneration, or to create a statue of Buddha or Bodhisattva, or to build a temple or tower, or to buy oil lamps to light in offering, or offer them to the usual temple hall.”

Go down like that three times so that the patient can know. Suppose the consciousness of the patient has dispersed to the point that breathing has stopped, time is sometimes one day, two days, three days, up to seven days, keep loudly saying bạch like above and loudly reciting this sutra.

After that patient dies, at the same time, if in the past there were serious sins up to five offenses of Vo Gian, they can also be completely freed, and wherever they are born, they usually remember the affairs of their past life....

The steps are as follows :

My name is... Today is the date of...

I, with a sincere heart, read sutras (or have done some good deeds to mention...) and dedicate these merits to the sick person named... aged... at house number...

(You should also express all your heartfelt wishes for how you hope they will be.)

After completing the chanting of sutras or Buddha recitation, you then dedicate these merits to the Resentful Spirits and Owners of Grudges.

You say... (I dedicate the merit to the resentful spirits who have grievances against the sick person named... may you let go of hatred and accept my sincerity, and forgive the sick person named...) and then you also dedicate to all sentient beings in the universe for their common benefit. You must do this for at least 1 week or until the person recovers. If they do not recover, it seems that you have helped them avoid falling into hell if they have committed any severe karmic offenses.

This is a simple, easy way to dedicate merit for those who are busy and don't have much time but still want to help their relatives. If you don't have much time, you can recite the Buddha's name and make offerings such as sutras, giving alms, and releasing animals. If you have more time, you can read the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for them, one or half a volume each day. The key point is sincerity.

Of course, you still gain merit if you sincerely help sentient beings.

A MI DA PHAT! Please recite it often.

Source: Namo Buddha

tieu_de: BUDDHA TEACHES ABOUT THE FOUR GREAT GRATITUDES
tom_tat: The Four Gratitudes, or the Four Profound Gratitudes, are the four significant debts that a Buddhist must strive to repay fully. They are: 1) The gratitude to Parents:
noi_dung:
BUDDHA TEACHES ABOUT THE FOUR GREAT GRATITUDES

The Four Gratitudes, or the Four Heavy Gratitudes, are four significant debts that a Buddhist must strive to repay fully. They are:

1) Gratitude to Parents:

Nine months of carrying, giving birth, and nurturing. Parents always worry about their children, often losing sleep and food, toiling hard throughout life, enduring all kinds of mental and physical hardships, even willing to sacrifice everything, to raise and educate their children to become virtuous people. This gratitude is truly as immense as the vast sea and sky.

2) Gratitude to Teachers:

In Quy Son it is said: “Those who give birth to me are my parents, those who educate me are my teachers.” The main idea of this sentence is that our bodies are given to us by our parents and we have what we have today thanks to our teachers. None of us can understand by ourselves without learning, so the gratitude to teachers is very great.

3) Gratitude to the Nation and People:

We live in a country, and thanks to the protection of the law, education from schools, care from hospitals, the army fighting enemies, etc., we are able to live safely and happily. Therefore, we should show gratitude to our nation by being good citizens and contributing our efforts to make the country prosperous and the people strong.

4. Gratitude to all beings:

All beings are all causes and conditions, everything outside of us. Without the support of everything outside, we ourselves could not exist. Isn't that so?

How could we exist without people planting, processing, and cooking food and drinks to nourish our bodies? The same goes for fabrics, vehicles, houses, and everything else, etc... In short, we all depend on each other to live. Therefore, we must be grateful to them.

✅ Repaying the Four Great Graces are the four largest, most important debts in a person's life that no one can ever forget.

tieu_de: Everywhere has gods in charge, people without the heavenly eye cannot see them.
tom_tat: (HT TUYEN HOA EXPLAINS THE GREAT BODHISATTVA HEART SUTRA DHARANI) "Thuan-Nha-Da" is the name of the Space Deity; Thuan-Nha-Da is a Space Deity. I have lectured a lot about "Thuan Nha Da," do you remember? That is t
noi_dung:
EVERYWHERE THERE ARE RULING GODS, PEOPLE WITHOUT CELESTIAL EYES CANNOT SEE THEM

(HT TUYÊN HOÁ PREACHING THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA)

"Thuấn-Nhã-Ða" is the name of the Void Deity; Thuấn-Nhã-Ða is a Void Deity. I have preached a lot about "Thuấn Nhã Ða," do you all remember? That is the Void Deity! You all listen to the sutra but pay no attention! After listening, you return everything back to me! You truly have no attachment; not even the Dharma do you wish to keep for yourselves anymore!!! Surely you have reached the realm of "no self, no Dharma"!

River and Sea Gods. In large rivers and the sea, there are River Gods and Sea Gods who govern them.

Spring Gods. Springs also have gods who are the lords of the springs.

Lake and Small River Gods. In small rivers and ponds, there are also gods who take care of them.

Herbal Gods. All kinds of medicinal herbs have gods who govern them.

Forest Gods. In the forest, there is also a god who governs the forest.

House Gods. Even houses have House Gods who govern them.

Along with the Water God, Fire God, Earth God, and Wind God. Earth, water, fire, wind—all four elements have gods who govern them. The Earth God was originally a goddess; she used to be very arrogant, believing that she alone was the Earth God and that there were no other gods. When she met the Buddha, He preached to her and explained that besides the Earth God, there are three other gods who are also gods of the Four Great Elements: the Water God, Fire God, and Wind God. At first, she refused to believe, but after the Buddha used countless analogies to explain, she understood and accepted. Therefore, what is described above is about the four gods of the Four Great Elements.

Earth God, Mountain God. The land and mountains are all governed by the God of Earth and the God of Mountains. According to legend, tigers are actually Mountain Gods, the lords of the forest, which is why on the mountains people often worship this "Mountain God."

Stone God. Moreover, even rocks are all managed by the God of Stones.

Divine Palaces, etc., all gather together. The gods guarding the palaces and many other gods also assemble together to participate in the Dharma assembly.

Usually, every river has a guardian deity; it's just that mortals cannot see or recognize it. Those who attain Heavenly Eye Knowledge will understand that there are divine beings everywhere—at all places, at all times, there is a god standing by to manage things.

The Buddha had a disciple named Kaludadi, who attained the Arahantship. Whenever he needed to cross a river, the Master would often call the River Spirit and say: "Oh little servant! Stop flowing!" "Servant" means a maid, a woman who works as a servant for someone. Therefore, "little servant" refers to a small servant or a minor attendant, not a major servant! Why did the Master ask the water to stop flowing? Because only when the water stopped rushing could the Master cross the river. (Usually, those who have attained Arahantship, when going anywhere with water, can freely command the water to stop flowing so they can wade across.)

Then over and over again, whenever he wanted to cross the river, Master Ca-Luu-Da-Di would always call it that way. The River Spirit was displeased and went to complain to the Buddha: "O Blessed One! You have a disciple who speaks without any tact. Whenever he sees me, he is not only impolite but also calls me 'little servant'! He should not call me that! Why does he call me 'little servant'?"

The Buddha Shakyamuni replied: "Alright, when he returns, I will tell him to come and apologize to you."

When Master Kaludadi returned to the monastery, the Buddha then reproached him: "Why, every time you cross the river, do you call the River Spirit 'little servant'? You shouldn't be so tactless! You need to speak thoughtfully and with a bit more courtesy!"

Then the Buddha taught: "Kaludadi! Go to meet the River Spirit and admit your fault; personally apologize to him immediately!"

Master Kaludadi obeyed, joyfully went to meet the River Spirit, and said: "Little servant! Please do not be angry with me anymore! I am truly at fault!"

The River Spirit originally did not want to be called a "little servant," yet the Master still loudly said: "Hey, little servant! Don’t be annoyed with me anymore!" At that time, Buddha Shakyamuni and the Great Arahants, upon learning of this, all burst out laughing. Why did they laugh? Because calling the River Spirit a "little servant" made the spirit unhappy, so Master Kaludadi had to go apologize; yet when he met the River Spirit to express his apology, he accidentally blurted out: "Hey, little servant..."

Knowing it is wrong, one should correct it, calling it "River Spirit," or "Lord Spirit," or any title that sounds "pleasant" would also be fine; yet Master Ca-Luu-Da-Di still keeps calling it "little servant" as before! Why, having already come to admit the mistake, does Master still call the River Spirit "little servant"?

That is because in five hundred past lifetimes, this River Deity was always a servant of Master Ca-Luu-Da-Di's family, so the Master got used to calling him "little servant." In this life, even though he has attained the Arahant fruit, the Master still retains old habits, so whenever he meets the River Deity, he naturally calls him "little servant." This is also a matter of cause and effect!

The above event proves that gods exist everywhere; however, we cannot see or meet these gods like we do with mortals. If you have opened the Third Eye of Wisdom and attained the Six Abilities, then you will be able to see the gods; if you have not opened the Third Eye, not attained the Six Abilities, then even if you see them, you will not recognize them and will not know who they are!

tieu_de: I WOULD LIKE TO SHARE THE MIRACULOUS RESPONSE OF THE KSKSA SUTRA (Kṣitigarbha Appeared IN A DREAM, Maternal Grandparents Benefited From Merit)
tom_tat: I have handwritten the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and sent it to Địa Tạng Phi Lai Temple in Hà Nam. After finishing it, I made a vow to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva that I wish to recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra three times to help liberate the spirits and sentient beings.
noi_dung:
I WOULD LIKE TO SHARE THE MIRACLES OF KSI Kṣitigarbha SUTRA (Kṣitigarbha Appeared IN A DREAM, Maternal Grandparents Thanks to Virtue)

I have hand-copied the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and sent it to the Kṣitigarbha Phi Lai Temple in Ha Nam. After finishing the copying, I made a vow to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva that I would read the Kṣitigarbha Sutra three times to help liberate the souls, those sentient beings who are suffering around me, for the souls of my ancestors, including my paternal grandparents. For all sentient beings throughout the Dharma realm.

Just as the Kṣitigarbha Sutra states, after reciting three times or up to seven times, one will be liberated.

After sending the sutra, I started chanting, and after completing the third transformation, I dreamed of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva along with another Bodhisattva, both radiating a golden light even more beautiful than in the picture above, flying in the sky with smiles. I looked up at the sky, following them, unable to take my eyes off. In my heart, I felt immense peace. I had never dreamed a dream in which the image of Kṣitigarbha was so clear before. In the dream, I also saw my father and mother. My mother was also copying the sutra. I said to her: The merit of copying the sutra is beyond imagination, mother...

There are still many dreams, but I remembered the 2 details that are most important. Upon waking, my heart was extremely happy, knowing that my paternal grandparents had ascended to Heaven to enjoy the supreme and wonderful joy. I lay there recalling the dream. Tears kept flowing and I silently recited NAM MÔ ĐẠI NGUYỆN ĐỊA TẠNG VƯƠNG BỒ TÁT. NAM MÔ A DI ĐÀ PHẬT continuously without stopping. Silently thanking Him for His great compassion and mercy, always loving sentient beings in the realm of suffering and making many plans to save sentient beings.

I can no longer sleep, so I woke up to write this article, sharing with everyone more faith on the path of practicing Buddhism. Coming to Buddhism to practice, to see, to be peaceful, and to attain liberation... The Buddha's teachings are true a thousand times over.

I know that from now on I will regularly recite this to help liberate sentient beings throughout the entire realm of existence, so they may soon leave suffering and attain happiness. This Sutra is like a treasure in my hands, it cannot be separated from those who practice Buddhism with great filial piety as their foundation before wishing to learn or advance further on the path of liberation practice.

Namo Amitabha Buddha 🙏🙇

Namo Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva 🙏🙇

Source: Sương Quỳnh

tieu_de: RELEASING LIVING BEINGS AVOIDS GREAT CALAMITIES, ESCAPES SERIOUS ILLNESSES, AND BRINGS GREAT MERIT
tom_tat: If you want longevity, remember to release life. In the chapter “Releasing Life Discourse” it says: “If you want to extend your life, listen to my words, everything must be carefully sought for yourself, wanting to prolong life
noi_dung:
RELEASING LIVES TO AVOID DISASTERS, RECOVER FROM SERIOUS ILLNESSES, AND RECEIVE GREAT BLESSINGS

If you want longevity, remember to release life. In the chapter 'Life Release Praise' it is said:

“If you want to extend your life, listen to me, everything must be approached with awareness and you must rely on yourself. To extend life, you must practice life release. This is the true principle of karma. When creatures are about to die and you save them, when you are about to die, heaven will save you. If you want to extend your life, there is no other way except to abandon the karma of killing and practice life release.”

The Bodhisattva Maitreya Sutra also says:

“Advise people to diligently perform acts of merit and release living beings; ultimately, it leads to longevity, and if one develops the Bodhi mind, the great calamities of heaven will surely be averted.”

In the Buddhist scriptures, it is said that there are 7 blessings of heaven and humans:

⚘ Noble lineage.

⚘ Dignified appearance.

⚘ Longevity.

⚘ Freedom from disease.

⚘ Good relationships and fate.

⚘ Full wealth.

⚘ Great wisdom.

The root of "longevity" and "being free from illness" lies in the merit of life release; life release also serves as a supporting cause for the other five blessings.

Vasubandhu, the scholar, said:

"Abandoning the karma of killing is like bestowing life, eliminating the killing of sentient beings, thereby receiving long life; a nurse or doctor giving medicine without harming sentient beings thus attains a body free from disease."

There are some patients who, due to the karmic retribution of killing in a previous life or this life, doctors are powerless to treat. If they immediately practice life release, their illness will be completely cured. In Hangzhou, there was a person who, because of the evil karma of shooting birds, suddenly developed sores on their back. Doctors were also unable to help. At this point, he realized this was the karmic consequence of killing in this life, so he vowed to give up the karma of killing and do meritorious deeds by practicing life release. After that, the treatment began to take effect and he gradually recovered.

There are many patients whom doctors diagnose as terminal, certain to die, and beyond cure. If their family members know how to practice merit-making by releasing living beings and reciting sutras, there will definitely be hope for gradually restoring the patient's life. Especially in the case of abnormal illnesses that doctors cannot diagnose, these are all considered to be the immediate manifestations of karma from killing living beings in this life or a past life. At such times, the only beneficial practice is making merit through releasing living beings. The Buddhist sutras also state that releasing life can extend longevity.

There is a story told in the Sutra of Merit and Virtue as follows:

"Once upon a time, there was a novice who followed his master to study the Dharma. One day, the master entered meditation and realized that the novice's karma allowed him to live only for about seven more days. After coming out of meditation, the master wanted the novice to meet his parents, so he said:

– You have studied under me for a long time. Now you may go visit your family, and return here after a week.

The novice monk was allowed by his teacher to visit home, and he happily bowed and set off. On the way back, heavy rain poured, and water flowed everywhere. By the roadside, an anthill was flooded, and the ants clung to each other in panic and were about to be swept away.

Seeing this, the novice monk thought:

"As a disciple of the Buddha, I must have a compassionate heart and do my best to save all beings." Then he built a small earth embankment to protect the anthill and moved the ants to a dry place. After that, he returned home, and seven days passed without any incident.

By the early morning of the eighth day, the novice returned to the temple. The teacher was extremely surprised, not knowing by what cause the novice had managed to overcome his past karma. Then the teacher entered a meditative state to observe and saw that the novice's act of saving an army of ants had brought him blessings of peace, transformed his life-shortening karma, and even increased his lifespan.

When the novice arrived to pay respects and knelt to one side, the teacher said:

– You have accomplished a deed of great merit, do you realize it yourself?

– Teacher, over the past seven days, I have just stayed at home and haven’t performed any virtuous deeds at all.

The teacher said:

– It is because you saved the ants from death that you escaped a short life destiny; not only that, your lifespan has also been increased.

The novice monk listened to the teacher and felt very joyful and firmly believed in the merit and karmic reward of saving living beings. From then on, he always diligently practiced, loved, and protected the life of all creatures, and later attained the fruit of Arhat.

Excerpt from 'Merit of Releasing Life'

✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿✿

Extensively saving living beings is an offering to enlightenment.

If you don't have money, then eat vegetarian. Eating vegetarian is releasing life.

Namo Amitabha Buddha 🙏🙏🙏

Source: Amitabha Buddha

tieu_de: Is there any problem with lying down while chanting sutras?
tom_tat: Question - Mr. Quang Tu, may I ask you this question? There is an instruction on how to recite the 'Killing Karma' mantra, and you emphasize that one should not lie down while reciting the mantra unless they are sick.
noi_dung:
IS IT HARMFUL TO LIE DOWN WHILE CHANTING SUTRAS?

Question

-Brother Quang Tu, may I ask you a question? There is a guide on how to recite the Diệt Định Nghiệp mantra where you emphasize that one should not lie down while reciting the mantra unless sick.

But sometimes it's late and I go to bed, and I want to recite the mantra but think that if I lie down while reciting, it's not allowed. So is that correct? Is there any sin in lying down while reciting the mantra? I heard somewhere that reciting sutras lying down will result in the karmic retribution of being reborn as a snake, is that right?

Answer :

- Quang Tu once had a thorough discussion with a Vajrayana master and consulted the opinions of many other spiritual teachers. Everyone agreed that, regarding SCRIPTURES - MANTRAS spoken by the Buddha (writings and teachings on Buddhist topics not spoken by the Buddha are not considered scriptures and are not included here), along with reciting the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, then:

- DO NOT LIE DOWN AND READ OUT LOUD (doing so is disrespectful to the Dharma), similarly in cases such as going to the WC, wearing improper clothing… you should not chant aloud, or there will be karmic retribution. Looking deeply into the mind, the retribution mainly arises from a mind that disrespects the Dharma Treasure, not just from outer posture; that is the key point.

- However, if chanting is done silently, without making a sound, you can still lie down while reciting, including reciting the Buddha's name - chanting sutras and mantras, as well as in situations that are not ceremonious like going to the WC, being nude, changing clothes, men taking off their shirts and wearing shorts, women wearing short skirts or camisoles...

Except for the moments when men and women are intimate, it is COMPLETELY NOT ALLOWED.

Once the key point is understood, we can open up many other flexible interpretations:

1. A bedridden patient, unable to sit, can they still chant sutras and recite Buddha's name in that position? Yes! Volunteers who assist people nearing death, the person is usually lying down while reciting Buddha's name, because how could they sit when about to die.

Their mind does not despise the Dharma treasure. This is different from a healthy person who could sit up but refuses, because they regard the sutras as equal to other types of things.

So, instead of only considering the external posture, or only considering the inner mind, we need to consider both. Because body and mind are inherently connected.

We cannot say "I do not care about external appearances, I only value the inner mind, I worship Buddha in my heart" and then carelessly do whatever we want. Because the mind will manifest itself in external form.

Here, I will give the following example:

Normally, when close friends are casual with each other, or with people who are not special in any way, like neighborhood kids coming over to play, we just treat them comfortably, going shirtless and in shorts freely, lying down and talking to avoid getting tired, as usual. Why? Because in our eyes, we consider them as equals, or lower, just with affection, without attaching any significant respect.

So now, if a relatively unfamiliar guest comes to visit, even if they are on the same level, would you dare to take off your shirt, wear shorts, lie down with your legs crossed, and receive the guest like that? Usually, the answer would be no. Why? Because receiving guests in that manner is rude and impolite.

Now, for example, if a boss comes to visit your house, or an old teacher who taught you for many years stops by, or even the President comes to encourage and check on you… just imagine if you would dare to be shirtless, lying down, swinging your legs while receiving them?

Certainly not. Why? Because we respect them very much; dressing properly and sitting to welcome distinguished guests is turning kindness into action.

In other words, it's seeing the heart through actions. Unless due to illness or other exceptional, unavoidable circumstances, this cannot be done; only then can it be overlooked. The guest will understand, otherwise... it’s very tiring.

Thus, every time we face the Triple Gem, the Dharma scriptures, or the image of the Buddha, and then we look back at our posture and demeanor to see whether they are inappropriate or not, we also understand how much our mind reveres the Triple Gem. It is not mechanical that whenever we are in front of a Buddha statue we must continuously bow; at the very least, we must maintain a certain level of decorum to show respect, rather than behaving casually as we would with a neighbor's child visiting.

On the other hand, there is no need to be overly concerned with the external form and then consider that as everything, without examining the core within the mind, as it will become empty and mechanical. In this way, one will not understand the essence and will not be able to apply it flexibly in special cases.

If we break it down, we will have a series of different cases, with merits and sins also continuously changing according to the level during reading sutras – chanting sutras, worshiping, and reciting the Buddha's name:

Case 1: Reciting sutras or mantras to ridicule, attack, defame, or deliberately mislead – the sin is damnation to hell, whether lying down or sitting. This case may seem strange, but it exists. Some elements who seek to undermine Buddhism often do this. Here, we can see that even if a person is not lying down, but sitting upright, dignified, and extremely solemn, the outcome is still the creation of enormous negative karma, with hell difficult to avoid.

Case 2: Disdain. Because they think Buddhist scriptures – mantras are ordinary, they can do whatever they want. So they lie down while reading, even though they could sit, and they don't bother to check whether their attire is proper or not. Here, we see that in their minds, they regard the Dharma treasures as ordinary items, so this mindset is to disdain the Three Jewels, which will have karmic consequences.

It is not necessary to become a snake 100%, one being can generate many different types of karmic results. Besides becoming a snake in the next life, it can transform into many other forms of retribution: such as foolishness, being bedridden with illness, and so on. A person who already has great blessings may lose blessings, lose their position, or be looked down upon by everyone...

Case 3: The mind maintains reverence, but the circumstances do not allow for proper solemnity. For example, a beggar respects the Buddha. If he has no clothes, wearing only pants, can he take off his shirt in front of the Buddha statue, bow to the Buddha, and recite sutras and mantras?

Who says it’s not allowed? Forbidding someone from begging, beware it is that very person who might face retribution.

In the time of the Buddha, men of the poor class were completely shirtless. There was a man named Ni De who was impoverished, working as a dung collector for the wealthy; his body was covered in filth and smelled of excrement, so he was hesitant to approach the Buddha despite great reverence. And what did the Buddha do?

The Buddha came and took his hand, treating him with respect, equally as with disciples from royal families, encouraging him to become a monk, and later, through his practice, he attained the Arhat fruit.

So through the story above, do you still think that being bare-chested – meaning wearing improper attire in front of a Buddha statue – will always 100% create disrespectful karma?

Anyone who stubbornly holds a one-sided understanding and says: definitely 100% creates karma, no exceptions. Be careful, that statement itself is verbal karma, because it misleads people in life.

Case 4: Both body and mind maintain proper standards, externally solemn, and inwardly respectful, then when this person chants, they will have greater merit.

Case 5: Some people push their inner reverence to the extreme. For example, they go to the temple to worship and chant sutras like others; outwardly, no one notices any difference, but inwardly, this person reveres the Three Jewels to the point of crying when thinking of the Buddha, seeing a Buddha statue as if seeing the real Buddha, or being willing to sacrifice their life for the Three Jewels without hesitation.

This matter is a secret known only to that person and the Buddha; outsiders cannot understand it. Furthermore, it must be known that each prostration to the Buddha by this person, each recitation they make, carries immense and countless merits, which cannot be equated with those of others, even if outwardly they appear the same.

Case 6: Opposite to the type of person mentioned above, there are some people who, although their inner devotion is relatively superficial, due to certain ceremonial circumstances, they emphasize the external level of elaboration. For them, the rules must be kept in this way, attire must be properly arranged in that manner, prostrations must be in this posture, chanting must be intoned in that style, and ritual instruments like bells and wooden fish must not be missing ... and many more.

Considering cause and effect, this person certainly has merit, quite a lot. Because they have to go through so many procedures and still manage to maintain them, regardless of how sincere they are inside, it is still very commendable. No one dares to say that what they do is wrong; they must have blessings and merit.

However, is it more than someone who pushes their inner sincerity to the utmost? No, certainly not! The mind inside is much more important, so the merit is much greater; a person who focuses on outer appearance cannot compare.

In addition, placing too much emphasis on form can - and often does - have consequences for others. It creates a barrier for those who do not understand much about Buddhist teachings. Every time they plan to practice, they become confused, wondering whether what they are doing is sinful or not. Since no one provides a satisfactory answer, they decide to give up practicing for peace of mind.

So, this is precisely the deadly danger of emphasizing form over substance, then imposing it on everyone to follow, causing difficulties that make people discouraged and withdraw. The act of abandoning practice is truly a disaster, both for the person who quits and for the one who applies pressure that makes others hesitate and abandon their practice.

Case 7: both the reverent heart within and the external forms of ritual are pushed to the utmost. Internally, there is a passionate devotion to Buddha, being ready to sacrifice one's life for the Dharma without hesitation; externally, whenever going to the temple or the Buddha's shrine, everything is meticulously prepared, offering incense, flowers, candles in a solemn manner, bathing and cleaning oneself thoroughly, wearing the most appropriate attire possible, and bowing with utmost respect. (Particularly, some sects such as Tantric Buddhism stipulate that in certain special cases, practitioners need to prepare very elaborate rituals that not everyone can fulfill)

Without needing analysis, anyone can know that such a person has immensely great merits and is the best in all cases. If in the future they do not become Buddha, then it is hard to know who will.

Above are 7 cases briefly mentioned, but in reality, there can be divided into thousands and one other different cases. Merit and sin transform in such a complex way that it is extremely difficult to fully explain each case.

Therefore, if someone asks questions like whether something is allowed or not, we should not foolishly give a one-sided answer: either definitely 100% yes, or definitely 100% no. Simply stating an absolute answer for every case is surely wrong. Quang Tử has spoken excessively up to this point, do you understand the issue now?

__________________

Buddhism is profound and subtle but so vast that you don’t know where to start?

Or you have studied a lot yet still feel you haven’t grasped the key points to apply, what are those points?

Therefore, Quang Tử has condensed key writings that contain teachings with high practical applicability, which many people are interested in during this era, and which anyone needs to understand thoroughly as a fundamental foundation to apply in resolving all of life's suffering.

The 21 articles and videos on this Facebook fanpage cover 21 different topics. Although they are nothing compared to the vast ocean of Buddhist knowledge, it is hoped that they will help you satisfy your desire to learn and grasp the essential key points. Click on the link below and explore each article one by one:

21 KEY LESSONS

tieu_de: PERSUADING OTHERS TO PRACTICE BUDDHISM
tom_tat: Hao Nguyen: – Quang Tu, may I ask how to make my relatives, who do not understand karma, who still enjoy killing karma, still kill too much, and who still like raising livestock and brewing alcohol, change their thoughts, attitudes
noi_dung:
PERSUADING OTHERS TO PRACTICE BUDDHISM

Hao Nguyen :

– Quang Tu, may I ask how one can make their relatives, who do not understand karma, who still enjoy committing harmful deeds, who still kill too much, who like raising animals and making alcohol, change their thinking and mindset, to follow the Dharma and think and do good deeds?

Quang Tu :

– Convincing others to follow the principles of the Way has always been an age-old issue that both lay and ordained Buddhist disciples continuously worry about.

The first essential factor in persuading others with moral principles is that one must practice the Buddha's teachings oneself, not just speak empty words; one must become a living example of the teachings. Every action and gesture, in body, speech, and mind, should follow the Buddha's teachings, carried out in the most sincere manner.

If it is not genuine, and only done to create a flashy facade, people will soon see through it and nickname the person "Chanting Nam Mô with a dagger in the heart," which only makes others turn away from the Dharma.

It's also easy to understand; we cannot give others what we do not have ourselves. A person who pretends to have moral principles on their lips, but truly does not have Dharma in their heart, how can they impart it to others?

You can deceive the gullible, but not the discerning. And even if you deceive the trusting, it can only be for a short time, not forever.

If one sincerely practices the teachings according to the Buddha's instructions, after a period of a few years, the person will naturally radiate an attraction, a silent persuasive power, drawing others who wish to follow. Depending on each individual's cultivation practice, the strength of this attraction varies.

At that time, every word that person spoke, even if not polished, very simple, even clumsy and rough… still strongly influenced others, because those words were crystallized from the arduous practice, they had the power that emanated from the inner self. For those with profound cultivation, a single word spoken not only moves the listeners, but also resonates throughout the world for demons and gods to follow.

People have long heard stories about spiritual teachers guiding disciples and educating the public, often focusing only on what the teacher says to persuade others. In fact, the main issue lies in the teacher's prior practice process.

The second factor is DESTINY AND KARMIC CONNECTIONS.

Besides the attraction of the inner self, there is another formidable force that closely governs the ability to persuade others to follow, which is DESTINY AND KARMIC CONNECTIONS.

This is the law of cause and effect; if in this life or a past life, we owe someone a debt of gratitude, then whatever that person says, we will follow, regardless of right or wrong, whether reasonable or unreasonable. Only when the debt is fully repaid will we stop being swept along.

So when is a DEBT created?

When we receive help from someone else, whether it is giving money, gifts, helping with effort, saving a life, or providing guidance and useful teaching (leading someone astray obviously does not count), whether the help is material or spiritual, etc., AS LONG AS IT BRINGS BENEFIT TO US, we will be in DEBT to that person.

How strong is this law of KARMIC DEBT? Let me say it is absolute.

Once we are indebted to someone, especially deep debts, we will feel extremely pleased with whatever that person says and want to keep listening. Most importantly, whatever they ask of us, we will want to comply and follow.

Regardless of right or wrong, their words are rationalized by our hearts, and they exert a tremendous power over us, a power that comes from emotions rather than reason.

The majority of human actions, or more precisely the actions of all beings, are primarily governed by emotions rather than reason. When reason and emotion conflict, our mind will generate all kinds of arguments to deceive its own clear intellect, closing its eyes to follow the guidance of KARMIC CONNECTIONS.

Mothers who irrationally spoil their children, lovers who recklessly pursue their passions, followers of heretical beliefs... are the clearest examples.

You see, once there is DEBT, even the words of a child can command adults, let alone the words of people who are educated, experienced, reputable, or have supernatural powers… Therefore, the false teachers of all kinds of beliefs from ancient times to future times can still persuade many people to follow them, even willing to give their lives, like extremist Muslim followers, for example; for them, a suicide bomber, killing themselves and many other innocent people, is still considered right according to their sense of justice.

Anyone standing outside can easily see that they are wrong. But they themselves always have countless arguments to consider themselves right, and even when they are at a loss for words and can't argue anymore, they simply close their eyes and stop thinking, just following their heart regardless of everything. At that point, no matter how much the world tries to convince them, it is all in vain; the power of KARMIC CONNECTION so strongly governs emotions in such a way.

Fortunately for those who have karmic affinity with the Noble Wise, at that time, the words of the Noble Wise will captivate both the reason and emotions of the person, completely devoted to practicing accordingly, even if they do not understand the principles very well, they still follow them very enthusiastically.

So who are the Good Knowing Ones? All those who guide others to follow the True Truth, benefiting both the present and the distant future, are Good Knowing Ones. The most standard and greatest Good Knowing Ones are the Buddhas; below them are the Bodhisattvas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas; below them are those with wisdom who understand the Dharma correctly. Regardless of any religion or non-religion, they are all Good Knowing Ones.

Unlike harmful suggestions, erroneous teachings, and heresies, the words of a Wise and Virtuous Person are TRUE REALITY, and anyone who practices according to the TRUE REALITY will achieve increasingly better results. You can use this point as a measure to distinguish between right and wrong, clearly separating TRUE REALITY from heresy. That is, observe the results; if it is true REALITY, the more you practice according to it, the more positive results you will obtain.

This result must be tested over a long period of time, not just a few years or months, to draw a conclusion, because from Cause to Effect it may span many lifetimes. To verify the TRUTH, we need to carefully consider many things collected from various sources from East to West, from past to present, observe the progression over a long period, and even find a way to pierce through the veil of multiple lifetimes to clearly see from Cause to Effect, only then can we see where the TRUTH lies.

Returning to the matter of the Wise Ones’ teachings, those who listen and follow the guidance in accordance with the Truth of the Wise Ones and practice accordingly, over time, will achieve good results. This is called Merit.

For example, if a Good Knowledgeable Person advises someone to release life, to save the lives of animals about to be killed, and that person follows this advice, after some time, which could take many future lifetimes, that person will enjoy many blessings from this act of releasing life, including abundant health, wealth, honor, and academic success... This means that because they previously had a debt to the Good Knowledgeable Person, they followed the guidance, and then they additionally receive blessings by practicing what was advised, meaning debt stacks upon debt, and the person feels even more inclined to follow the words of the Good Knowledgeable Person and act accordingly.

But if it is not a Good Knowledgeable Master, and instead is an evil teacher who teaches wrongly, it will bring terrible results to those who have debts, and the debts will thus be resolved.

In this way, the Enlightened Ones clearly understood this law. Before wanting to bring the teachings to sentient beings, they always sowed great kindness and gratitude among them. Sometimes they helped one person, sometimes they saved another, sometimes they gave alms, sometimes they saved lives, sometimes they treated illnesses, sometimes they showed directions, sometimes they taught skills… countless ways to sow debts of gratitude. The Buddha summarized these into four methods called the Four Means of Attaining Others: Giving, Kind Speech, Benefit Action, and Cooperation, to establish good connections with sentient beings.

When the bond of fate ripens, sentient beings follow, and only then is the Dharma explained to them, guiding them step by step from this life to the next.

The third necessary element to use the Dharma to persuade others.

That is SKILLFUL METHOD.

We can employ many other means to persuade, not just the way of using words to advise.

Like bringing moral stories and stories of cause and effect to tell people so they can understand by themselves. Or bringing books, videos, lectures... finding a skillful way so people want to be spiritually guided. Or using technology such as Facebook, Zalo... to appropriately share moral and cause-and-effect articles.

There are countless methods; each person has a different situation and level, so we must flexibly find the most suitable way. The important point is to clearly understand the mentality and viewpoint of the person you want to guide spiritually, and gradually provide suitable guidance, not too abruptly.

Just as with people in the past who have always revered science, if we keep telling mysterious, unverifiable stories, how could people accept them? At that time, we need to find concrete, clear evidence, arguments with strict logic, step by step to make them believe and understand.

Or psychologically speaking, if you want to advise a person with a prideful nature to stop killing and practice vegetarianism, using preachy admonitions, like a teacher criticizing others' bad habits and telling them what they must or must not do, will only make them resist more. With such people, it is necessary to use a gentle approach, guiding them softly and praising each small step of progress to achieve results.

There are countless types of people with different psychologies and levels, so there must be countless different ways of persuading them. This is the skill of leading people's hearts, which requires learning a lot about psychology, methods of explanation, ways of presentation, etc., and cannot be fully explained in one article. Each person must study and train for many years, even many lifetimes, to achieve mastery.

In summary, we need to closely combine all three factors to achieve the highest persuading effectiveness (if all three are not sufficient, the effectiveness decreases, but there will still be some certain effect).

– 1. By living rightly according to moral principles yourself and setting an example, that example can persuade both those who have affinity and those who do not to follow.

– 2. Giving alms – helping, creating many karmic connections with everyone and all beings, and at the same time, when creating these connections and helping them, always have the intention to guide them to follow the Right Dharma of the Buddha.

For example, when buying medicine to cure someone, one vows: “May the patient follow me in practice until the day of attaining Buddhahood.”

Even when pouring a glass of water for someone, giving them directions, or saying a word, etc., my mind always wishes for them in the future to follow the true Dharma in their practice until they attain Buddhahood.

Over time, depending on the amount of KARMIC DEBT, they will follow more or less. However, because I vow to guide them to the complete attainment of Buddhahood, this karmic connection will continue for countless eons, becoming increasingly profound, until that person truly becomes a Buddha as I initially wished, then this connection will stop.

– 3. Regularly learn and study psychology, different methods of persuasion and explanation to apply, supporting the guidance of others in practicing according to the Buddha's teachings.

Wishing you successful application, bringing the light of the Dharma to help many people escape from ignorance and the suffering of samsara!

(Quang Tu)

tieu_de: Husband and wife are formed because of恩怨 (grudge/revenge).
tom_tat: HOW TO RESOLVE IT? Husbands and wives being together in this life is entirely due to fate and karma. If the two often have conflicts and do not treat each other well, it may be because their past grievances have not yet been resolved.
noi_dung:
A HUSBAND AND WIFE FORMED OUT OF GRUDGE.

HOW TO RESOLVE IT?

Husband and wife coming together in this life is all due to fate and karma. If two people frequently have conflicts and treat each other poorly, it may be because of unresolved grudges from past lives.

There was a woman who worked in trade in a small town in the North. She had a husband whom she loved and cared for deeply, sacrificing everything without hesitation to serve him.

A few years ago, she fell seriously ill and eventually became paralyzed on one side of her body. During this time, the relationship between her and her husband became very bad.

Especially after she became bedridden due to her illness, her husband treated her even more indifferently.

She was puzzled and could not understand the reason why. The question always appeared in her mind: "Why do I always treat him well, yet he treats me so cruelly?"

The more she thought about it, the sadder and more confused she felt inside.

After being treated coldly for a long time, she felt very miserable. Then one day, lying on her bed, she complained: “Oh God! How can my husband treat me so badly?”.

After saying that, she fell asleep without realizing it.

Then, in that half-asleep dream, she saw some events related to her past life. She saw that in previous lives, there was a lifetime when she was a practitioner. In that life, she still had a female body like in this life and followed a master with profound virtue, practicing in the Buddhist path.

One day, her master took her to a place with a very large wooden door, covered with a roof above. The master said to her, "Climb up here immediately. Remember, no matter what happens below, do not come down. Remember my words carefully!"

After climbing onto the roof, two men appeared below. The two men fought with her master; they were determined to kill this master.

Unable to leave her master in danger, possessing martial skills, she angrily jumped down, grabbed a sharp iron rod, and then ran behind the two men to stab them.

As a result, both of these men were stabbed to death by her. The incident greatly frightened her master, who hurriedly pulled her away to escape...

She suddenly woke up and thought, “I wonder if this is really true?” Then she lay down and continued to sleep, and a little later, she dreamed the same dream again as before.

Later, she remembered that on her husband's back there was a very large white birthmark, exactly at the spot where she had stabbed one of the two people in her dream.

Upon careful reflection, she realized that her husband was one of the two people she had stabbed to death, and that birthmark was the remaining trace of the wound she had inflicted with the iron rod in past lives.

It was at this moment that she realized that she was paying the debt for what she had caused her husband in a past life. It is not by chance that people come together as husband and wife; all are debts of fate from past lives. In her case, it was a blood debt.

Because of that debt, karma directed her thoughts to love and pamper her husband to the fullest. The love in her heart was merely a tool of the law of karma to restore justice.

Since that day, her heart has felt completely relieved, no longer resenting her husband as before, and she even promised herself that she would treat him better.

_______________________

IF YOU ENCOUNTER THAT SITUATION, WHAT WOULD YOU DO?

Paying off the debt changes everything. Either the two parties will no longer have to meet, or if they do, their mindset will change, and they will treat each other better.

This is not only true for husband and wife, but for all human relationships, relationships between humans and animals, humans and spirits, as well, the same principle applies: whenever someone causes you distress or suffering, such as scolding, beating, harming, betraying, making demands... in various ways, and you cannot break away, there is certainly some debt involved.

But repaying debt by enduring torment, or by mutually pampering each other, takes a very long time, perhaps even a lifetime. Do you want that?

If not, then read on, read very carefully:

In short, all types of debt: blood debt, life debt, money debt, love debt, gratitude debt, etc., between husband and wife, as well as all other relationships in society: father and son, mother and child, siblings, lovers, friends, neighbors, colleagues, leaders - employees, etc., even accidental encounters on the street that lead to conflicts, and even animals that disturb us, and even spirits that trouble us, can all be repaid with the following secret:

1 - Create a lot of good deeds and merit

2 - Dedicate that merit and good deeds to the creditor - the very person who is causing you suffering.

3 - Persist in doing as above until the person no longer torments you, which means the debt is cleared. If they still torment, it means there is still debt, and you must continue, regardless of how much merit needs to be cultivated.

There are many ways to create merit in Buddhism, such as chanting the Buddha's name, reciting sutras, practicing mantras, repentance, making vows, releasing animals, printing and distributing scriptures, doing good deeds, giving alms, donating blood, saving lives, building temples, casting statues, etc. Even though these are different, all are taught by the Buddha, all generate merit, all can help eliminate karma, all bring good fortune, and all can be dedicated to the creditor.

Because each person's circumstances are different, their foundations are different, and their preferences are different, there are many different ways, so that each person can choose the method that suits them best to apply.

If we have the financial means, we can choose to perform acts of life-release (buying tens or hundreds of kilograms of snails, eels, soft-shelled turtles, etc., to release into rivers or lakes, for example) or give alms to the poor, or offer donations, build-cast-carve Buddha statues, build bridges or roads, etc...

If you don't have a lot of money, to do things like giving alms, releasing animals, etc., it's okay, you can choose methods that only require effort and time, such as helping others, volunteering at the temple, donating blood, etc.

In particular, you should recite sutras, such as the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the Infinite Life Sutra, the Universal Gate Sutra, etc. Or chant mantras, such as the Great Compassion Mantra, the Rebirth Mantra, or the Karma Destruction Mantra "OM PRA MA NI DA NI XOA HA", etc., which have boundless merit.

Some people like copying sutras rather than reading them, and that's even better. You just need to get a beautiful notebook and copy the entire sutra into it. The merit is similar to reciting the sutra but greater because it takes more effort and time. (Note: after finishing copying, the sutra should be placed in a respectful location)

If you don't know where to find sutras or mantras, or find it too difficult or complicated, it's okay. You can choose to chant the Buddha's name; every day you can recite a few thousand times “Namo Amitabha Buddha,” or “Namo Shakyamuni Buddha,” or “Namo Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva,” or “Namo Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva”… you can recite the name of any of them, it's all good.

You can choose one method or multiple methods simultaneously. Do as much as you can (at least it won't be harmful), and make a determination to continue until you get results, as there is no limit to stop.

Because past debts are different for each person, some creditors require only a small amount of merit to resolve, while others demand a very large amount of merit, and it takes a long time before there is any change.

How little or how much, we do not have the foresight to know exactly. Just need to know the rule: when the debt is paid off, naturally cause and effect will be rearranged, the situation will improve, freeing you from the debt.

So you must be persistent, and should not give up halfway just because you don't see any changes after doing it for a while.

In resolving a similar matter, one person may accumulate merit for a few days and see results, while another may take a whole year to see results. This is common, because the debts vary in size, and also because each person's spiritual capacity is different.

After each time you create merit, you dedicate it as follows:

“I dedicate this merit, praying for… (the name of the debtor, or roughly him, her, that animal…) to eliminate karmic obstacles, have body and mind peace, increase favorable conditions in the Dharma, be reborn in the Pure Land soon, attain Buddhahood quickly, and widely save sentient beings.”

___________________

* To help you visualize, let me continue with the following story, which successfully applied the above secret:

THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA SAVES A TRAGIC MARRIAGE

Mrs. Trần Mộng Cầm is 83 years old this year, living at Huệ Viên Lầu, Hong Kong. She sincerely and kindly wishes to pass on Shaolin skills to everyone, while also teaching them to chant the Great Compassion Mantra, advising them to practice good deeds, cultivate their character, and help guide those with destiny.

Not only did she teach Shaolin martial arts, but she also cared about the daily lives of each of her disciples. Her Bodhisattva heart was like the sun shining everywhere, and the students often confided in her about all the issues in life, revealing all their worries for her to help resolve.

Among her disciples, there was a young woman with the surname Đặng. Last year, Ms. Đặng was beaten by her husband and broke her arm. Normally, this husband frequently hit his wife with his hands and kicked her with his feet, leaving her body covered in bruises. Each time he finished beating her, he would even threaten to throw her off the roof onto the street.

Miss Đặng, after hearing her grandmother teach Shaolin Kung Fu, went to apprentice with a master, hoping that after becoming skilled, she could defeat her "enemies" and defend herself well so she would no longer be bullied by her husband.

Mrs. Trần understood Miss Đặng's intention, and just smiled and said:

- I teach this kung fu with the purpose of helping you strengthen your body and health, not to use violence to fight. Furthermore, resentments should be resolved, not accumulated; using violence in retaliation is a poor strategy. Then she taught Miss Đặng to recite the Great Compassion Mantra, dedicating the merit to her husband to repay all past debts and grievances, aiming to neutralize her husband's violent behavior.

Miss Đặng listened earnestly to Mrs. Trần's heartfelt advice, so she obediently followed it. From then on, she sincerely chanted the Great Mantra every morning and evening, without missing a single day. Because she was illiterate, Mrs. Trần had to patiently teach her, each day helping her memorize one line.

After a year, a miraculous change occurred: her husband completely transformed into a different person. He treated her very gently, asked about her, showed care in every way, even helped her with the housework, and completely quit smoking. He had completely changed, no longer being an abusive and violent husband.

Even whenever Ms. Dang fell a little ill, her husband would hastily take her to the hospital for a check-up, tenderly whispering: "You must not die before me. If you leave me in this world, what meaning would life have?"

Now Ms. Dang is very happy; she emotionally confided in Mrs. Tran, expressing immense gratitude to Bodhisattva Quan Yin for responding to her prayers.

The Great Compassion Mantra truly works in miraculous ways, unimaginable, as it saved her tragic marriage and helped her family achieve perfect happiness.
