Source: Amitayus Buddha

tieu_de: THE TRUTH OF CAUSE AND EFFECT.
tom_tat: (Author: Thich Huyen Dieu). In this world, happiness and suffering; war and peace; wealth and poverty… if we make a little effort to practice and keep our mind truly calm, we will discover many things
noi_dung:
THE TRUTH OF CAUSE AND EFFECT.

(Author: Thich Huyen Dieu).

In this world, happiness and suffering; war and peace; rich and poor... If we work a little hard and keep our minds calm, we will discover a lot of wonderful things. There are many people who have the same soil, the same seed, but those who have good results and others who do not?

Some people are born into wealthy families, inheriting a large fortune left by their grandparents and parents, but why do they become poor after a while? Some people are intelligent and resourceful in every aspect while alive, yet they use every trick to deceive others in various forms to acquire a huge fortune, but in the end, they cannot enjoy their food, cannot sleep peacefully, and then have their wealth taken away by others, dying tragically?!

Many people have the highest authority on this earth, inherited from father to son for hundreds of years, wherever they go there are hundreds of thousands of people cheering 'long live'; but in just a short time, their power and status vanish like smoke?!

Some people, while alive, amass treasures and wealth to fill barns, but when they die, they do not even have a coffin to be buried in?!

I am a person who has been trained in a scientific environment, living and working in various countries for nearly 50 years. I have paid attention to observing and studying the issue of karma. I observe, investigate, and study thoroughly in an objective scientific spirit without bias or narrow-mindedness, regardless of the circumstances. Sometimes, I even use my own life as an experiment to test the truth of karma. I find it extremely accurate. My experiments, repeated many times in different situations and circumstances, all clearly reveal that the truth of karma is very precise, very scientific, and fair, and no one can escape it.

Those who commit crimes, break the laws of a country, or those of their organization, may try to flee to another country, bribe their way out, or hire many skilled lawyers to escape prison. But I have observed very closely, they cannot escape the law of cause and effect.

This small book is not a memoir, reportage, or fairy tale, but a compilation of research and life experiences of many individuals who wrote and recounted the truths. The creation of this small book is not intended to defame or criticize any individual or organization, but to share experiences together to live and work better, to have joy and happiness in this life. Dear readers are also encouraged to observe and participate in studying this truth of cause and effect. Please observe carefully those around you; they may have a lot of wealth, power, fame… but they do not believe in cause and effect.specialized in fraud, exploiting others in many different forms. Dear friends, please observe their appearance and life very carefully; they seldom have happiness and often encounter many obstacles. They and their families often experience many accidents, or sometimes they have to wait nearly until the end of their life before they face severe karmic retribution.

In daily life, if we are fortunate enough to meet a teacher or a friend who believes in karma, I think that is a great blessing, because a teacher who believes in karma will teach students all the good things and truths without ever guiding them onto the wrong path. A friend who believes in karma is the same; because they believe in karma, they will never dare to do anything wrong that causes suffering to others. If we are fortunate enough to be friends with someone who believes in karma, that is a great blessing, because they will never make us suffer, they will never create difficulties. When we are lacking or in need of something, they are willing to share and help.help us. If we have money to invest in business with people who believe in karma, if they make a profit they will also share it with us, they would not dare to cheat us. And if by chance they encounter difficulties and obstacles, they would only cheat us twenty percent or half at most, the rest we can still survive, but if a person does not believe in karma, they will certainly cheat us 100 percent.

I believe that if everyone in this world believes in karma, is determined to stay away from evil, and vows to do good, then this world will have peace, joy, and happiness.

Our society today is called advanced and civilized, science develops more and more every day, which is very beneficial for humans, but people are increasingly suffering, more confused about many things, more hatred, more disputes and schemes to oppress and exploit each other in many forms, hence many accidents, natural disasters such as earthquakes, storms, and floods in many countries around the world, as well as wars, hatred, disputes, and struggles for all kinds of matters everywhere. Hundreds of thousands of other acts of greed and selfishness also occur due to disbelief in cause and effect.

The law of cause and effect has been proven for thousands of years, very accurate and fair, but because humans are ignorant and their greed is bottomless, they have done all sorts of reckless things, so they must suffer in many different cases.

I tried to collect materials and then wrote this small book with a sincere wish that everyone on this earth should develop faith in cause and effect, respect one another, and vow never to harm living beings, including respecting the environment. When eating fruit, one should remember the person who planted the tree; when drinking water, one should remember its source. Trees give us the air to breathe and live, so we must absolutely respect the environment. If everyone believes in cause and effect and respects one another as mentioned above, I believe that peace, joy, and happiness will certainly come to everyone.

Below are true stories about cause and effect, with clear evidence from both the writer and the storyteller. We sincerely hope that readers will finish reading and share them with others. People together can develop a belief in cause and effect, which is a practical way you are contributing to the peace and happiness of your family and your country. We hope you can share many other true stories related to the truth of cause and effect, so that subsequent works can continue to be richer. Belief in cause and effect is truly the secret method leading to peace, success, and happiness for individuals and society, and so I boldly share it with you, dear readers and friends, in this book.this small one.

Sincerely grateful to you!

(Vietnam Buddha Kingdom Temple - Lumbini, Buddhist year 2554 - Full moon day of the fourth month, Year of the Cat).

________________________________________

1. FIRING GUNS AT THE TEMPLE.

This matter was recounted by Mr. Nguyen, deputy director of Tay Nguyen University and General University, on the rooftop of Vietnam Buddha Kingdom Temple - India, while the group was having tea at 4:30 PM on November 12, 2010.

In the years 1977-1978, the Central Highlands was still not completely peaceful because the Fulro front and some revolutionary soldiers were still active. After the war period, some soldiers on patrol, whenever passing by temples and shrines, would often randomly shoot into these sacred places, partly for amusement and partly out of fear that someone might be hiding there. Some commanding officers with conscience advised that they should not shoot in these spiritually sacred places. When advised, the young soldiers would obediently say yes… but when their superiors were not present, they would still shoot at temples and shrines, laughing and joking afterwards, considering those places of Buddhist and divine worship to be superstitious and irrational.

After the Fulro front in the Central Highlands completely collapsed, these soldiers returned to civilian life; some were promoted, and some were assigned to various government offices. About 10 years later, Mr. Nguyen remembered his comrades and went to visit them. Alas, one by one, they had died in tragic, unforeseen accidents, which is very heartbreaking to mention. The elders used to teach that you reap what you sow; if you sow the wind, you will face the storm.

_______________________________________________

2. TEMPLE, PAGODA, AND SHRINES SUFFER TRAGIC DEATHS.

This story was told while having tea and watching the sunset with a delegation from various countries at Viet Nam Phat Quoc Tu - India at 10 o'clock on November 12, 2010.

Anh Hung was born and raised in Hanoi, he witnessed many historical events in this thousand-year-old land of Thang Long. After Hanoi was liberated, some people brazenly destroyed temples and other sacred places of worship, and they even took temple land as their own. Then, as time passed, Anh Hung carefully observed the people who had once participated in destroying temples, and all of them died in truly terrible accidents. The accidents happened in such strange ways that no one could have expected.

It was as if someone walked across the bridge and then it broke, and they were pierced to death by a sharp tree, like a fish being stabbed to be grilled. Every day, hundreds of people pass across this bridge without anyone dying, but only this man walked across and such a terrible accident happened.

As for those who occupied temple land and sold it to others to make a lot of money, their lives became wealthy and luxurious. Then one day, as usual, they went out for exercise, strolling on the sidewalk. For some unknown reason, a truck lost control and ran onto the sidewalk, crushing the two elderly people, decapitating them, though their bodies remained intact and unharmed. This family had to endure yet another tragedy. Before the parents’ funeral was completed, their children fought violently over the inheritance while the coffins had not yet been buried. Local residents believed they had to face retribution in this life without needing any further intervention."In future lives, because they create too many karmic results, especially the act of seizing temple land and then selling it.

(S.t: Liu Thiện Như).

tieu_de: YOU, THIS MORNING YOU JUST GOT ANGRY, THEN YOUR MERIT IS NOTHING MORE THAN A FEW HOURS! A FEW DOZENS OF YEARS AGO
tom_tat: In the Buddha's temple, we often talk about burning an entire forest of merit. What is merit? You must know. Merit is a pure mind. If we use the Buddhist doctrinal term to explain, then merit
noi_dung:
YOU, IF YOU JUST GOT ANGRY THIS MORNING, THEN YOUR MERIT IS ONLY A FEW HOURS AT MOST! A FEW DECADES AGO

In Buddhism, we often say 'burning a forest of merits.' What is merit? You must know. Merit is a pure mind. If we use the terminology of Buddhist dharmas, then merit is concentration and wisdom. You see, the moment anger arises in the mind, concentration and wisdom immediately vanish, thus burning the forest of merits.

From that, it shows that you need to try thinking about how much merit you have cultivated. You have studied Buddhism for many years, so how much merit have you gained? If you calmly reflect and think about when you last did not get angry, your merit is equivalent to that much. If, for example, you just got angry this morning, then your merit is only a few hours at most. All the decades of practice before are burnt away, not counted, no longer existing. If you study Buddhism your whole life, and at the moment close to death you suddenly have a fit of anger, it is all gone; all your merit is lost in that one incident. This is very frightening. This is all true, it is all true.

Therefore, the Buddha advises us to accumulate merit, and to accumulate merit, one must practice patience (Perfection of Patience), only then can your merit truly be accumulated. Accumulating merit is very difficult, very difficult; it is not just about outwardly not getting angry while inwardly feeling a bit of displeasure. If there is even a slight feeling of displeasure in the heart, the merit is gone. This merit is difficult, extremely difficult, extremely difficult to cultivate.

But you must know, I have done a lot of good deeds, good deeds are blessings, and the blessings still remain. Blessings are not obstructed by anger. You get angry every day, yet the blessings from your practice still remain. The Buddha in the scriptures tells us that asuras have great blessings. How do asuras cultivate? It is all through practicing blessings in the Buddha’s path. Like some of us today, every day we are cultivating blessings, the blessings from our practice are very great, anger is very great, arrogance is very great, and we do not want to lose to anyone in anything.

Even lighting incense, they want to light it before others, they refuse to be after others. When offering donations, if you contribute 10,000 and I contribute 15,000, I must be greater than you, like a competition. What kind of karmic retribution will such people face in the future? King Asura. When they do this, they receive great blessings, receive great blessings, great blessings in the human realm.

What about merit? If there is no merit, the blessing is still very great. Blessings cannot transcend the three realms. Only merit can end birth and death and escape the three realms. We must understand this clearly and profoundly. Therefore, cultivating blessings is easy, within the Buddha's gate it is easy to cultivate blessings. Merit, however, is extremely vast and not easy. Even a slight displeasure in the mind can negate all merit.

(Excerpted from the Diamond Sutra Commentary, Volume 104)

Venerable Master Jingkong

tieu_de: Chanting to Help the Dying Escape the Three Evil Paths
tom_tat: NAM MO AMI DA PHAT Nhân has never participated in funeral chanting before. But three months ago, Nhân's father-in-law passed away, so Nhân went to offer guidance to him and to his karmic enemies and chanted Buddha's name for about an hour.
noi_dung:
CHANTING TO HELP THE DEAD ESCAPE THE THREE EVIL PATHS

NAMO AMIDA BUDDHA

Nhan has never participated in a deathbed chanting session before. But three months ago, Nhan's father-in-law passed away, so Nhan returned to enlighten him along with his grievances and chanted Buddha's name for about an hour.

It was about 4 hours after he passed away that Nhan got back home.

In Nhân's wife's rural hometown, his mother-in-law didn't believe in Buddhism, so she still hired drums and trumpets and slaughtered animals for the funeral. When Nhân gave a Dharma talk to him and chanted Buddha's name to assist with the funeral rites, it was during a funeral with loud, miserable cries and noisy instruments. Nhân knew that no matter how much he tried to advise his family, they wouldn't listen and would instead severely curse... so Nhân did not obstruct or oppose the way the funeral was conducted. He quietly approached the coffin, looked directly at him, gave the Dharma talk, and then chanted Buddha's name.

Before the recitation of the sutras, his face was dark and pale, then after Nhân gave his instruction and completed the Buddha recitation, his complexion became rosy and bright. Of course, Nhân did not need to touch his body or examine it to know that his facial features had softened.

Nhân's father-in-law, when he was alive, committed all kinds of evil deeds, including the five grave offenses, and he had a great fondness for killing and harming lives and enjoyed eating living things... When he died, his enemies and those he wronged gathered to guide his spirit into the Three Evil Paths. At this time, his soul was extremely terrified, with no refuge, unable to resist karma, completely powerless, and in immense suffering.

When Nhan returned, his face was dark and sallow, also because the resentment and suffering surrounding him were closing in. At that time, Nhan used a compassionate heart for all beings to teach karmic consequences to his adversaries and to enlighten him.

Nhan used a gentle, compassionate heart towards both him and his adversaries and said:

A MI DA PHAT, do not be afraid!

Oh, vengeful spirits who are enemies of Mr. Chiến (Nhân's father-in-law named Chiến). Look, this person, while still alive, was already transformed by you into aggressive cells causing cancer, making him suffer extreme pain, living worse than dying. Now that he has already died, are you satisfied? Do you feel happy and gleeful? I see that you have taken your revenge and settled your grudges. Now you are transforming into his relatives and creating scenarios he enjoys to push him into hell, and then you enter hell with him. Are you now feeling fulfilled and gleeful?Not yet, are you satisfied? Today I am fortunate to meet you all, so I have come here also to give you all an opportunity to escape the three evil paths right now. Whoever has enough affinity will be reborn into the Western Pure Land; whoever does not yet have enough affinity will be reborn into the realm of Heaven, humans, to continue their practice until the day of rebirth into the Western Pure Land. This is a once-in-a-thousand-years moment. If you still refuse to let go of hatred, you will descend into hell together with this person. The satisfaction of revenge is temporary, but the suffering of countless rebirths is truly not worth it. Please let go of all attachments and recite Buddha's name with me, seeking rebirth in the Western Pure Land. You must.One must believe in Buddha; you all just need to let go of all attachments, and a single thought of non-arising transcends the Three Realms. Anyway, the person has already died, the vengeance has already been carried out, so you should let go of all hatred to free yourselves. In this way, you also accumulate a little merit to seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land or to be reborn into one of the three good paths. Now, everyone, please recite Buddha's name with me, and I will assist in guiding you in your recitation.

After giving the above instruction, I recited A MI ĐÀ PHẬT. After reciting the Buddha's name for a few minutes, the sky, which had been hot and sunny, began to rain. The rain under the sunny sky made the atmosphere cool. This was the response of countless sentient beings who, in different times, suffering immensely, encountered the true Dharma and were reborn in a good realm. At that funeral, everyone said they had never attended a funeral that felt so warm; usually, funerals feel very cold and desolate... this was the perception shared by everyone.

As for my grandfather, he was reborn in the heavenly realms as a celestial maiden.

So whether this practice of assisting someone in chanting is beneficial or not depends on the mind of the person who is assisting. I tell you that when I recite the Buddha's name, my mind pervades the entire space of the Dharma realm without distinguishing between kinship or familial relationships, without distinguishing enemies or adversaries; all sentient beings in suffering and distress are loved by me as my own children.

So, when I recite the Buddha's name, are there any delusive thoughts?

I do not know whether I have delusional thoughts or not, but each thought I have is a true thought because beings suffer. Even if my bones are broken and flesh is torn, even if I must enter hell to endure pain, I vow to recite the Buddha’s name, seeking the Buddha’s power to radiate light and save all suffering beings who are trapped in the dark realms, allowing them to transcend the darkness and be reborn in blissful realms.

This is my mind when I recite the Buddha’s name to assist in recitation for my mother-in-law.

Lay Practitioner Do Nhan

tieu_de: The Law of Cause and Effect Arranges Your Life
tom_tat: (Excerpt from *An Sĩ toàn thư* _ Author: Chu An Sĩ) Cause and effect are profound and difficult to know, difficult to understand, yet they are the most important law, governing the entire life of every person, every sentient being; therefore, understanding v
noi_dung:
how THE LAW OF CAUSE AND EFFECT ARRANGES YOUR LIFE

(Excerpt from An Sĩ Complete Works _ Author: Chu An Sĩ)

The cause and effect are profound and difficult to understand, but they are the most important law, governing the entire life of every person and every sentient being. Therefore, understanding cause and effect is the thing most worthy of learning in each person's life. It is not as simple as people think, "Plant melons and you get melons, plant beans and you get beans," but the law of cause and effect has an extremely subtle and miraculous transformation.

The following article by Mr. Chu An Si, although only a small part of the countless ways karma manifests, will help us somewhat better understand the transformation of the law of cause and effect - both fair and extremely flexible.

__________________

**1 *GOOD KARMIC REWARDS BUT CANNOT BE ENJOYED**

Some people, although they have silks and brocades filling their chests, only wear a few pieces of coarse, poor-quality cloth on their bodies; they have gold, gems, and treasures full in their cabinets, but their daily meals are just slightly better than those of the poor, considering this as comfort; they also enjoy extremely hard labor, seeing it as pleasure and delight.

People like that are seen to worry and be distressed all day long, clearly having good fortune but unable to enjoy it like others.

That is because in a previous life, although one practiced giving charity, they did not cultivate a sincere, joyful heart; they only gave reluctantly due to encouragement or persuasion from others. Another reason is that after giving, they may feel regret or remorse for what they have done.

**2 *RECEIVING ENJOYMENT BUT WITHOUT GOOD KARMIC RESULTS**

Some people come from poor households, yet they often live in the large and luxurious homes of others; meals at their own homes may be meager vegetable soups, but they frequently get to enjoy lavish delicacies served by others.

Such a person enjoys pleasures but it cannot be said that they have merits. That is because in a past life, they did not practice giving themselves, only knew how to advise and encourage others to do charitable deeds; or when seeing others give, they would immediately feel joy and praise them.

**3 *RICH BEFORE, POOR LATER**

The Sutra on Diversified Consequences teaches: "If there is any sentient being who, upon hearing the advice of others, performs acts of charity, but later generates a feeling of regret; due to such causes and conditions, that person in the next life will be wealthy for a period, but afterward must endure poverty."

4 *POOR FIRST, RICH LATER*

The Sutra also teaches: "Furthermore, if there is any sentient being who, by hearing the advice of others, performs a small act of charity, but after giving, feels joy. That person, in the next life as a human, will initially endure poverty but later will become wealthy."

5 *RICH BUT MUST WORK HARD*

Being rich comes from sowing the seeds of wealth; but having to toil and labor also comes from sowing the seeds of hardship. As the scripture teaches: “Those who offer alms to the monks will surely gain unlimited wealth, that is natural. However, if someone invites the monks to their house to offer alms, causing the monks to exert themselves and struggle to come, and only then offers food, that person in the next life, though still gaining unlimited wealth, will have to labor and undergo hardship.”

6 *IDLE AND STILL RICH*

If someone generates the aspiration to offer alms to the monks, bringing food directly to monasteries and temples, enabling the monks to enjoy it at ease, that person will receive blessings in the next life, being born in the realms of humans or gods, naturally enjoying all pleasures.

**7 *POVERTY BUT STILL CAN GIVE**

The scripture also teaches: "If there is any sentient being who, in the past, practiced giving but did not encounter those who are the fields of merit in the world, they will continue to wander in the cycle of birth and death.

Those beings, when born as humans, because they did not encounter a field of merit, the act of giving only brings very small benefits, sometimes present, sometimes absent, not lasting long. However, since they had previously practiced the habit of giving, when born, even living in poverty, they could often perform acts of giving.

**8 *WEALTHY BUT NOT GENEROUS**

There are also beings who are not accustomed to giving; upon meeting a good spiritual friend who advises them, they may temporarily give once, and by chance also encounter a highly virtuous and respected field of merit.

Thanks to the merit of offering to exalted benefactors, future generations are born wealthy and prosperous. However, because they are not accustomed to the practice of giving, even though they live in affluence, their hearts are often stingy and they do not engage in acts of charity.

**9 *GIVING MUCH, RECEIVING LITTLE BLESSING**

The Bodhisattva Path Sutra teaches: “If there are sentient beings who give alms but not wholeheartedly, or offer gifts without reverence; or when giving alms or making offerings without joy in their heart; or when giving alms, they cultivate arrogance, pride, and self-importance; or give alms and offerings to those who follow heretical and deluded views.

Such giving of alms and offerings is like a person who comes across barren and unproductive land: even though they sow many seeds, they harvest very little.”

**10 *GIVING A LITTLE, RECEIVING MUCH BLESSING**

In this sutra, it is also taught: “If at the time of practicing giving, one can arouse a joyful mind, a respectful mind, a pure mind, without expecting any reward, or offering to Bodhisattvas, holy monks.

Giving and offering in this way is like a person encountering a good field; even if they sow few seeds, they will still harvest much.”

**11 *SADNESS IS ALIKE, BUT RESULTS ARE DIFFERENT**

The book Pháp Uyển Châu Lâm says: "For example, there are two people, one poor and one rich. Someone comes to ask for help, both of these people feel sorrow. The rich person, with much wealth, feels sorrow because they fear the other person's pleas will cost them their money.

The poor person feels sorrow because they want very much to help but have no money to do so. Later, the poor person is reborn in the heavenly realm, while the rich person falls into the realm of hungry ghosts. Although both people felt sorrow, they receive different karmic results."

**12 *DIFFERENT LIFESPANS, SAME MERIT**

For example, if a person lives during a time when the lifespan is up to a thousand years, spends their life observing the Five Precepts and practicing the Ten Good Deeds, compared to a person who lives during a time when the lifespan is only ten years, but also spends their life observing the Five Precepts and practicing the Ten Good Deeds, the merit of both people is the same, no different.

**13 *EVIL DEEDS AT THE END OF LIFE LEAD TO GOOD RESULTS**

For example, if someone commits evil deeds but at the end of their life enjoys good results, it is because the consequences of the evil deeds done in this life have not yet ripened, while the consequences of the good deeds performed in a past life have ripened earlier.

During the time of the Buddha, there was a butcher who went to see King Ajatashatru to ask for a favor. The king said:

– What do you wish to ask?

He replied:

– When you hold a sacrificial ceremony that requires the slaughter of animals, if Your Majesty allows, I will wholeheartedly perform this task.

The king said:

– Slaughtering is something few people like, so why do you want to do it?

Responded:

– In my past life, I was originally a poor person, working as a goat butcher to make a living. Because of that work, after death I was born into the heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings. When my lifespan in heaven ended, I was born again as a human, continuing the work of goat butchering. When I died again, I was born into heaven for the second time. In this way, after six lifetimes on earth working as a goat butcher, I was born into heaven six times, gaining unimaginable blessings. For this reason, I have come here to ask the king to let me continue that butchering work.

The king said:

– You are spreading such lies, how could you possibly know that?

He said:

– I know about the previous life.

The king, unable to believe, thought he was lying, and pondered: "How can such a lowly person know about a past life?"

Later, the king met the Buddha and immediately reported the matter to inquire.

The Buddha said:

–Truly as he said, not a lie. In a previous life, this person had encountered the Bich-chi Buddha. He saw the Bich-chi Buddha with delight in his heart, sincerely observed carefully, contemplated from head to toe, and then generated wholesome thoughts. Due to that karmic connection, he was blessed to be born six times in the heavenly realm, six times returned to the human world, and personally knew his past karma.

Because his virtues were mature, it was not yet time for him to receive the fruit of suffering. When this body ends, he will fall into hell to pay for the sin of having killed goats. When his time in hell is over, he will have to be reborn as a goat many times to live out his lifespan. That butcher only knew a little about his past lives, saw six times being reborn into heaven, but did not know the seventh life: When he took human form, the merits he had previously created were already in place, so he mistakenly thought: "By killing goats, I am able to be reborn into heaven." Thus, he only knew about the past life, which is neither supernatural power nor the wisdom of a clear-sighted person!

Therefore, when a practitioner creates merit, they must make a vow and should not be negligent, so that the result is not unclear. Take this example as a matter for contemplation.

(Excerpt: Selected Discourses on Giving)

Generally, when observing that some people commit evil deeds yet receive blessings, one should understand it as such.

**14 *DOING GOOD DEEDS IN LIFE BUT SUFFERING EVIL CONSEQUENCES AT THE END**

Some people spend their whole lives doing good deeds, but at the end of their lives they suffer tragic outcomes. This is because the karmic results of the good deeds done in this life have not yet ripened, while the karmic results of the evil deeds done in previous lives ripen first.

Moreover, even though it seems like they are suffering bad consequences, in reality it is not truly bad. For example, long ago there was a young boy herding cattle who, one day, picked flowers to offer to the Buddha. On his way back, he was gored to death by a bull, and his consciousness immediately was reborn in the realm of the Devas of the Tavatimsa heaven.

Again, there was a monkey that, upon seeing a monk, felt joyful and went near to borrow the monk's robe to try it on. At that moment, it unexpectedly slipped and fell into a deep ravine, dying, and its consciousness immediately arose in the heavenly realm.

In summary, even if one loses their life while doing good deeds, it does not necessarily mean they do not receive a good result; it is just that, for a moment, the physical eyes of ordinary people cannot perceive it.

**15 *THE BODY IS HAPPY, THE MIND IS NOT HAPPY**

Ordinary people cultivate blessings; in this life, everything goes as desired, which can be called having a peaceful body. However, without learning the transcendent Dharma, one has not yet escaped the cycle of rebirth, and ultimately the mind still cannot avoid the worry of falling into the three evil paths.

**16 *PEACEFUL MIND, UNPEACEFUL BODY**

An Arahant, having attained the fruit, has ended the need for rebirth, can be regarded as having permanently escaped the three evil paths, and has gone beyond the six realms of samsara, which can be called having a peaceful mind. Yet, if one did not regularly cultivate blessings in the past, one would not receive offerings as desired.

**17 *GREAT CHARITY, SMALL MERIT**

The Prajñāpāramitā Sutra teaches: “If a Bodhisattva only gives away precious treasures but does not generate the aspiration to attain Buddhahood to save all sentient beings, even if they practice over many lifetimes as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they will receive very little merit.”

Here, merit is actually not little, but the point is that compared to a Bodhisattva who has generated the bodhicitta (the aspiration to attain Buddhahood to save all sentient beings), this person's merit is small.

**18 *SMALL CHARITY, GREAT MERIT**

The Prajñāpāramitā Sutra also teaches: "If a Bodhisattva, while practicing generosity, can dedicate the merit for the attainment of unsurpassed Bodhi for the sake of saving all beings in the ten directions, then even if the act of giving is small, it will still accrue immeasurable merit."

For this Bodhisattva, from the moment of arousing the intention until the attainment of Buddhahood, neither the mind nor the field of merit increases, because it is already complete. Encountering favorable circumstances is precisely the time to practice merit."

When encountering favorable circumstances, one should think like this: “Our family is wealthy today; it must be because in past lives we often practiced generosity, so in this life we should rescue people and help beings even more. My body is free of illness; it must be because in past lives I frequently practiced compassion, so in this life I should avoid killing and engage in acts of life preservation even more.” It is similar to when a lamp has been lit, one must continue to add oil in order to maintain the light.

19 *EVEN WHEN FACING ADVERSITY, ONE CAN STILL ACCUMULATE MERIT*

When encountering adverse circumstances, one should think like this: “Today I face this miserable and calamitous situation, it is all caused by the karma caused by past lives, if I willingly accept it, surely I can repay all past debts.”

It is not only about that; if I encounter extreme poverty, I often wish that everyone would be wealthy and prosperous; if I suffer from many illnesses, I often wish that everyone would be healthy and well; if I frequently face struggles and conflicts, I often wish that everyone would be harmonious and joyful; if I am ignorant and dull, I often vow that everyone would have clear and wise intellect; if I myself lack perfect senses, I often wish that everyone would possess good physical form.

Whenever encountering a difficult or dangerous situation, one vows in future lives to save those who are in such distress. Isn't this transforming poison into nectar, revealing Bodhi right in the midst of affliction? If a person does not know how to cultivate merit, it will certainly be the opposite.

**20 *WHEN OTHERS DO GOOD DEEDS, I CAN GAIN MERIT**

When others perform good deeds but have not yet completed them, and one follows along to encourage and motivate them, that is called gaining merit through encouragement. When others have already completed good deeds, and one follows along with joy and delight, that is called gaining merit through rejoicing in others' merits.

Frequently praising and commending good actions, encouraging others to imitate them, that is called gaining merit through praise. Ultimately, throughout heaven and earth, from ancient times to the present, all good deeds in the world can bring merit to us. Therefore, when Bodhisattva Samantabhadra makes ten great vows, the fifth vow is specifically to 'rejoice in the merits of others'.

On the countless merits accumulated over many lives by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; down to even a small act of virtue by any sentient being in the six realms of samsara, when one becomes aware of it, he or she generates a mind of praise and rejoicing in all of them.

Once one can do this, then all the merits throughout the infinite space, pervading the Dharma realm, anywhere, can become one’s own merit, and oneself can also be like Bodhisattva Samantabhadra without difference.

**21 *WHEN OTHERS DO EVIL, I CAN RECEIVE MERIT**

When someone else is about to do evil but has not yet succeeded, and you make an effort to persuade them to stop, you will surely receive blessings.

When someone else has already done evil, and seeing it causes you sorrow and worry, without joy, you will also receive blessings. When the evil has not yet spread, if you try every method to stop and prevent it, you will surely receive blessings.

If the evil has already spread, it should be taken as a lesson to warn yourself, stay vigilant, and avoid committing it yourself, you will also receive blessings. If harmful actions affect you and you can bear them patiently, you will surely receive blessings.

If evil deeds harm others and one can advise them to endure patiently, one will certainly receive blessings.

HOW MUCH MERIT IS THERE IN CREATING A BUDDHA STATUE?

These things were explained by the Buddha himself to Maitreya Bodhisattva, analyzing the benefits and merits of those who create Buddha statues, whether as large as a mountain or as small as a thumb, whether ugly or beautiful, all attain supreme merit. If we do not read the GREAT MAHĀYĀNA SUTRA ON THE MERIT OF CREATING BUDDHA STATUES, we cannot fully imagine it. Here are a few excerpts:

“ ... At that time, Indra – the ruler of the Tāvatiṃsa heaven – addressed the Buddha:

– Venerable World-Honored One! Are there any people in the world today who, in previous lifetimes, created Buddha statues?”

The Buddha said to Lord Indra:

– Those who have created statues of the Buddha in the past have all been liberated. Among the beings in the heavens, there is none left, let alone elsewhere. Except for one son of a Brahmin in the north, named Nali Saba, who once created a Bodhisattva statue in the past, due to this merit he later became a king, named Tansa Sala. Moreover, because he encountered me, he is now born in a heaven with great power, completely free from the evil realms.

The monks Upali, Kassapa, and Ananda, in their past lives, used to maintain temples and venerate Buddha statues; because of that karmic connection, they attained eternal liberation.

In his past life, Mr. Kieu Pham Bade was a buffalo. While looking for grass and water around the temple, he ate grass in the bamboo bushes. Seeing the appearance of the Buddha statue, he felt joyful and, due to that merit, he is now liberated.

Venerable Thi Ty La once held a precious parasol to offer to the Buddha statue. Venerable Nau Lau Da lit a lamp also to offer to the Buddha statue. Venerable Du Be Ma once swept the floor under the Buddha statue. Venerable A Ba Ma Na lit lamps in front of the Buddha statue to help illuminate it. Bhikkhu Nan Da, out of respect and reverence, used fragrant water to wash the Buddha statue, etc… There are countless such Arhats, all of whom once offered humble gifts before the Buddha statue.

Even those of the lowest rank, like Venerable Na Gia Ba La, in front of the Buddha statue, used a little red and gold to paint the body of a statue for the purpose of making an offering… Due to this merit, they all completely departed from suffering and attained liberation.

The Buddha continued to say:

– O Indra! If there is anyone who, during my Dharma period that has not yet ended, makes a statue of the Buddha, he will attain liberation at the first assembly of Maitreya Buddha.

If any sentient being, not for their own sake, but seeking to be free in order to attain unsurpassed Bodhi, creates a statue of the Buddha, you should know that this is the very cause of the thirty-two marks, which can swiftly lead that person to Buddhahood.”

THE MAHAYANA SUTRA ON THE MERIT OF CREATING BUDDHA STATUES is particularly very good, not difficult to understand, and also contains many passages where the Buddha analyzes the cause and effect for people who create statues, embroider, or paint images of the Buddha, explaining the karmic reasons for being born as a woman, or as a homosexual, including bisexual people… and the ways to resolve them. I hope everyone takes some time to read the entire sutra to gain a deeper understanding of karma and accumulate limitless merit (the sutra is a bit long, you might want to share it on a wall to read gradually).
