THE MAHAYANA SUTRA ON THE MERIT OF CREATING BUDDHA STATUES

I heard as follows: Once, the Buddha was staying in the Trayastrimsa heaven, under the Bali Chatura tree (Note: the lord of the trees in heaven), together with countless great monks, countless great Bodhisattvas gathered, and the Great Bodhisattva Maitreya was the foremost among them.

At that time, the Blessed One stayed in that heaven for three months, teaching the Dharma to his mother, which brought many benefits to the deities, countless deities were freed from suffering and attained liberation. Countless deities absorbed the Dharma and received great blessings. Then, among the deities, there was a heavenly being whose lifespan was about to end, showing the five signs of decline (Note: Wilted flowers on the head – Dirty and stained clothes – Armpit sweating – Foul body odor – Dislike of sitting on the throne). By the power of hearing the Dharma, after passing away, he was reborn in this heaven, completely leaving the path of evil.

At that time, in Yama's realm there was no Buddha. It was like a dark night, full of stars but without the moon, like water without a king, like a house without a master; all pleasures and entertainments were completely suspended.

Then sentient beings seemed lonely without a place to rely on. Regarding the Buddha, everyone's hearts carried a grieving attachment as if they had lost their parents, like an arrow shot into the heart, and they went together to the places where the Buddha once stayed, but only saw empty gardens, forests, and courtyards; everywhere was vacant without the Buddha, and people felt increasingly sorrowful and unable to stop yearning.

At that time, King Udāyi, who was staying in the palace, often carried sorrow, was always emotional, and longed for the Buddha. The king paid no attention to the main queen, princesses, or entertainments. He thought: “If I keep worrying like this, I will soon die! How can I, before my life ends, see the Buddha?”

Then the king thought: “If someone loves another but cannot meet them, perhaps seeing the place where that person has been, or meeting someone who looks exactly like them, might lessen some of the sadness.”

The king pondered further: "Now, if I go to the place where the Buddha has been before and do not see the Buddha, surely I would grieve and lament, my emotions so intense that I might perish! In my life, I see no one whose appearance, merit, and wisdom could equal that of the Tathagata; how could I meet someone like that to lessen my sorrow?"

Having this thought, the king reflected again: "Now I should make an image – a statue of the Buddha, and worship and offer sacrifices." But the king considered: "If I make a statue that does not resemble the Buddha, I fear that I would incur boundless sins."

Then the king thought further: “Suppose all the wise people in the world continually praise the virtues of the Buddha, it still would not be enough. If someone praises according to their capacity, that person will still receive boundless merit. I shall do likewise, so I will create a statue according to my own ability.”

The king immediately ordered all the skilled craftsmen in the country to gather together. Once everyone assembled, the king said to them:

– Whoever can create an image – a statue of the Buddha – for me, I will reward that person with jewels and give them recognition.

The skilled craftsmen reported to the king that:

– Today the king has issued an order, which is truly a difficult task. The virtuous and miraculous features of the Tathagata, there is no one in this world who can match them. How then can we create an image of the Buddha? Even if the heavenly being Vishvakarman were to create a statue, it could not resemble the Tathagata. If we were to accept the king's request to make an image of the Buddha, perhaps we could only imitate a little of the hair curls and the white tuft, but as for the other beautiful, radiant, and majestic features full of dignity, who could possibly create them? When the Buddha descends from the heavens to the human world, if the statue has any errors, our reputation will be ruined. We secretly think we cannot dare to undertake this.do.

King Uttāyī then said again:

– My mind is made up, do not refuse! Like a person who is thirsty and wants to drink river water, would they not drink just because they cannot empty the river?

The skilled craftsmen, hearing the king say this, all knelt before him and said:

– We will obey the order, but we request that Your Majesty allow us to think tonight and come to work tomorrow morning.

They further added:

– Today the king wants to make a statue, so it should be made entirely of Chenandan wood (Note: a precious wood with a strong fragrance, unmatched by any other scent, found in India). Its texture is fine, its substance very durable. As for the form – should the Buddha statue be seated or standing, and what should be its height?

The king brought this question back to his ministers. One knowledgeable minister respectfully told the king:

– The king should create a statue of the Buddha sitting. Why is that? Because all Buddhas attain great Bodhi, turn the wheel of Dharma, manifest great supernatural powers, subdue non-Buddhists, and accomplish great Buddha deeds… All of this is in the sitting posture. Therefore, one should make a statue of the Buddha sitting cross-legged on a lion throne.

At that very moment, the heavenly being Tỳ Thủ Yết Ma (Note: he is a minister of the god Indra, capable of transformations and creating various objects and extraordinary crafts, overseeing architecture) saw this from afar, and knowing the king's intention to create a Buddha statue, he thought that night: "When it comes to knowledge of the body, I am a genius; in the whole world, no one is like me. If I create a statue for the king, it might somewhat resemble the Buddha."

He immediately transformed himself into a carpenter, holding sharp tools. At dawn, he went and stood by the gate of the king’s palace, telling the gatekeeper to clearly inform the king: “Today I wish to create a statue for the king. No one can match my skill, so I humbly ask the king not to assign anyone else.”

The king, upon hearing these words, was very pleased and ordered him to be brought in. Observing his appearance and gestures, he realized he was a skilled craftsman, and thought to himself: “How is it possible that such a person exists in the world? Could it be the angel By Thu Yet Ma or a disciple of His arriving here?”

Immediately, the king took off the string of pearls he was wearing, held it in his own hands, and placed it around the neck of the deity Tỳ Thủ Yết Ma. The king also promised to reward with precious gems for his merits.

At once, the king, together with the treasury official, went into the storehouse to select fragrant wood, with the king personally shouldering and carrying it, and handed it to the celestial craftsman, saying to the craftsman:

– Very good, Your Majesty! Use this wood, for I am making a statue, so that it resembles the image of the Buddha.

At that moment, the celestial craftsman said to the king:

– Although my skills are top-notch, when it comes to shaping or sculpting the Buddha, it is impossible to do it perfectly. For example, if someone uses charcoal to draw the sun and claims it looks exactly like the sun, it is truly unreasonable. Even if one uses pure gold to create a Buddha statue, it would be the same.

There are heretics who often claim: "King Phạm can create the world" but cannot create all the good forms in the Buddha's figure. Only my skill is supreme in this life, therefore today I work for the king. This morning is the eighth day of the month, while the Phat Sa star and Ty Ha De star appear. When the Buddha was newly born, this sign of spiritual response also appeared. Today is auspicious, so it is proper to begin the work."

The Deva Tīṣya Yētama spoke those words, then took a hammer to carve wood. The carving sound echoed to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, reaching the Buddha. By the Buddha's power, wherever the sound of the carving reached, sentient beings who heard it had their sins, defilements, and afflictions eliminated.

At that time, the Tathāgata smiled in many ways, praised the merits of the king, and even from afar foretold the king's attainment of the Supreme, Perfect, Complete Enlightenment.

Then, Indra – the ruler of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, addressed the Buddha saying:

– Venerable World-Honored One! Are there any people in the present world who, in past lives, have created statues of the Buddha?

The Buddha said to Lord Indra:

– Those who have created statues of the Buddha in past times have all been liberated. Among the celestial beings here, there is not a single one left, let alone elsewhere. Except for a son of a Brahmin in the North, named Nalī Sāba, who in the past once made a statue of a Bodhisattva; due to this merit, he later became a king named Caṇḍa Bāśa. Moreover, having encountered me, he is now born as a powerful Deva, completely freed from the evil paths.

Monks Ānanda, Kassapa, and Nadika, in their past lives, used to maintain temples and honor Buddha statues, and because of that connection, they attained permanent liberation. In a past life, Kiều Phạm Ba Đề was a buffalo, and while searching for grass and water around the temple, he ate grass in the bamboo groves; upon seeing the image of the Buddha, he felt joyful and inspired. Thanks to that merit, he has now attained liberation. In the past, Thi Tỳ La once held a jeweled parasol to offer to the Buddha statue.

Mr. Nậu Lâu Đà lit a lamp to make offerings to the Buddha statue. Mr. Du Bệ Ma once swept the floor beneath the Buddha statue. Mr. A Bà Ma Na lit lamps in front of the Buddha statue to provide light, and the monk Nan Đà respected and honored it, thus washing the Buddha statue with fragrant water, etc… there are countless arahants like that, all of whom once offered humble gifts in front of the Buddha statue. Even the lowest, such as Mr. Na Già Ba La, in front of the Buddha throne, used a little red and gold to draw the body of a statue to make offerings… Due to this merit, they all completely freed themselves from suffering and attained liberation.

The Buddha said further:

– O Śakra Deva! If there is anyone who, while my teaching is not yet completely extinct, creates a Buddha statue, they will be liberated at the first assembly of Maitreya Buddha.

If any sentient being, not for their own benefit, seeks liberation in order to attain the Supreme Enlightenment and creates a Buddha statue, know that this is the primary cause of the thirty-two marks, which can help that person quickly become a Buddha.

At that time, King Udāyī, thinking to himself: “How can I make the statue I am creating be completed quickly?” After thinking this, he spoke to the celestial craftsmen:

– You make every effort to help the work be completed quickly, so that I may soon admire and pay homage.

At that time, the heavenly craftsman Tỳ Thủ Yết Ma displayed all his skill, focusing without delay, and in less than a day the statue was completed. The statue sat in the lotus position, seven feet tall in wood, with its face, hands, and feet all golden purple in color.

King Uda-Diên saw the statue completed, with an elegant and dignified appearance, and his heart developed pure faith, attaining the state of 'Compliance and Forbearance.' Once he achieved this, the king became even more joyful, as all his karmic obstacles and worries vanished, like mist dissipating at sunrise, leaving only one remaining karmic consequence that he was experiencing in his present life, which was due to having once spoken ill of the Sage. At that time, the king offered all kinds of precious jewels and rare items as rewards to the divine craftsman, but the craftsman said to the king:

– Today the king has made a statue according to my heart's wish, and I wish to cultivate this merit together with the king. Now that the king has bestowed it, I dare not accept it. If it is necessary to give to each other, please wait for another auspicious day.

After speaking, the deity immediately returned to the heavenly realm that very night. Right after that, the kings of great countries, such as King Ajātaśatru and so on… these kings all held a deep admiration for the Buddha. Upon hearing that King Udāyī had successfully crafted the exquisite statue, they were all delighted, and together they went to King Udāyī's place. Each king brought a large amount of flowers, incense, and music to offer to the Buddha statue, and also presented precious jewels to King Udāyī. All the kings said:

-Your action is truly rare, being able to take out the poisonous arrow of sorrow that affects us all.

At that moment in the heavens, Indra, the Buddha spoke the Dharma on behalf of His mother, and all the celestial beings rejoiced and benefited. Things worthy of being done, the Buddha had completed. The Buddha then told the celestial assembly:

– O kings of gods! All Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have an eternal body (Note: eternal, here refers to the Dharmakaya of the Buddha). If among sentient beings, there is anyone worthy of being saved, the Buddhas immediately manifest to teach them, speaking the Dharma to them. Once the Buddha's work is completed and there is no one left to receive the teachings, the Tathagata then ceases to appear. Those without wisdom may think that the Buddha has truly passed away. The body of all Tathagatas is indeed the Dharmakaya, an eternal body, and truly does not perish.

O kings of gods! The Dharma of all Buddhas is like this: they manifest, or do not manifest, for the sake of teaching sentient beings.

Then the Buddha continued to teach, saying:

– You should know! These gods, those worthy of my guidance, I have already guided. Now I am about to descend to the human realm, gods, if you think of me, be diligent and do not slack off.

Why is that? It is also because of the sin of negligence, which prevents you from attaining the Supreme Enlightenment of the Holy Way. Yet because in ancient times you planted good roots, you now enjoy the pleasures of Heaven here, only to become negligent, indulged in pleasures, and fail to cultivate merits and virtues. These pleasures, according to impermanence, once fall away, will forever drift in evil paths.

Once again, celestial beings! You are heavily afflicted with vexation; when you see someone better than yourself, you become jealous, without ever thinking that: which heaven is happier is due to accumulating a lot of merit, and if we diligently practice, we can achieve it too. Now you have radiant complexions, like the sun rising at dawn, but if you cling to feelings of jealousy and envy, you will become dark like ashes, and will have to fall into a dark prison, to the extent of not being able to see your own hands, and later will even have to be a ghost eating filthy food.

Once again, heavenly beings! Enjoying the blessings of a pure and dignified body, with mighty and powerful authority, due to jealousy, one will suffer a female form, completely losing the heroic strength and might of a great man.

– O rulers of heaven! I remember in the past countless kings, because of your own jealousy, were harmed in an unreasonable way.

O Sovereigns! Once there was an Asura king (Note: non-deva, a type of deity with great merit, but not a god) named O La, who practiced severe asceticism with pure morality. The gods sent an angel named O Ba Thi to enchant the king’s mind, causing him to lose his virtue. That king became infatuated, so his power and virtue declined, and he was killed by the god Nala Diena, along with countless Asura subjects being destroyed at the same time. After the god Nala Diena killed this Asura king, he also annihilated the Asura army and returned the angel O Ba Thi to the heavenly palace.

There was again an Asura king named Na Ha Thọ. The deities used deceptive words on him and also helped other celestial beings attack the Asura. Then the deities turned back to harm him.

Furthermore, deities! Because of Lady Xá Chỉ (Note: she was originally an Asura princess and later became Indra's wife), a jealous mind arose. Xá Chỉ incited the Asura king to act aggressively, causing a celestial named A Già Bà to be unjustly suspected and utter a poisonous curse.

Again, the gods deceived King E Tra, telling him: “The place of the fairies has a lot of pure gold.” King E Tra believed these words and forced the fairies to hand it over. Because of this, the hearts of the fairies became angry, and immediately the fairy king was burned by a strong fire.

In the past, there was also a heavenly king named De Ba, who often held grand assemblies to make offerings. Due to this merit and virtue, he had supreme power and freely ascended to heaven to enjoy heavenly pleasures. The gods, feeling jealous, plotted against him, causing De Ba to fall from Daoli Heaven to the human world. All his former power was destroyed, like the moon losing its light, like a river running dry.

O rulers of the heavens! In life, many people possess serene virtue. Some attain supernatural powers, and some accomplish the four divine abilities… yet if a single thought of jealousy arises, such merits vanish in an instant, like Devadatta, for example, who, in deep ignorance, harbored jealousy toward me, immediately lost the five types of supernatural powers.

At that moment, the Heavenly King spoke to the Buddha:

– Respectfully, O World-Honored One! Today I have a question I wish to ask: What exactly is jealousy?

The Heavenly King continued to ask:

– Venerable World-Honored One! If a being sees someone better than themselves and thinks: 'How can I gain what that person has obtained?', is that mind jealousy?

The Buddha replied:

– No! That is greed, not jealousy. O Indra! Jealousy means wanting fame and gain for oneself and not wanting others to have it; seeing what others possess and feeling hatred, that is jealousy.

At that time, all the celestial beings rose from their seats, bowed their heads to the ground, clasped their hands toward the Buddha, and spoke these words:

– As the Buddha teaches, we, the celestial beings, will all comply. We bow to the Venerable Buddha in this world, who is our Father, our Lord, the most revered one, the Supreme Victor. Towards us, with great Compassion, coming here so that all celestial beings may benefit. Our wish has not yet been fulfilled, and we wish to once more request one thing from the Buddha:

Homage to the Blessed One, the World-Honored One! People in the world look down upon the devas and us. Why? Because Buddhas are born among humans and attain Perfect Enlightenment in the human realm. Among humans, there are those arahants who have realized the fruit of enlightenment. The solitary realizers, with great spiritual power, also appear in the midst of humankind.

Today, if the Tathagata does not remain here and descends to the realm of Yama, then the people of the world will all think: Our deities do not know that the Tathagata possesses great virtue, worthy of being properly offered to by the deities. They will also think: We do not know how to offer to the noble Tathagatas of the past. We hope that the Tathagata will stay a little longer, accepting our humble offerings, so that the people of the world will know that the deities have offered to the Buddha.

At that time, the Buddha silently accepted the request. Then, the Buddha said to the venerable Mahamaudgalyayana:

– You should go to the underworld of Yama first, visit the four groups of beings, and say the following words: "All those who remember and think of me should gather at the Sangha assembly at Tisa, and in seven days they will see me."

Maudgalyayana bowed at the Buddha's feet, and after bowing, in the blink of an eye he arrived at the Yama realm and conveyed the Buddha's message to the four groups. King Udāyī and everyone who heard the Buddha's message felt joy in both body and mind, all their sorrow was removed, and they felt completely at ease.

At that time, the four groups—monks and nuns, laymen and laywomen—wished to travel to the country of Sangha Chì. First, they gathered in the city of Vương Xá and discussed among themselves:

– The Buddha, the revered one of the world, is about to descend to the human realm. Whoever can respectfully pay homage to the Buddha first shall be the leader during the period before the Dharma is completely extinct.

Venerable Maha Kassapa, having heard those words, felt no joy in his heart, fearing that the nuns would become the senior leaders. Why was that? Among all the nuns, there were Uppalavanna and Rupa. These two bhikkhunis could thoroughly understand the scriptures of the Buddhas and attain supernatural powers, second only to Venerable Maudgalyayana; no one else could surpass them. Thinking this way, Venerable Kassapa found every means to admonish the bhikkhunis.

At that time, Bhikkhuni Rupa told the nuns that:

– We women living in the midst of the secular world are often honored, even if our lineage is humble, we are still respected by men and provided for in every way. Moreover, nuns in the Buddha’s Dharma, their parents and relatives, for the most part, belong to royal or noble families. Our nun community is diligent, observes precepts, does not violate etiquette, and possesses all virtuous qualities, yet we still have to pay respects to monks to receive the higher ordination. Now, Venerable Kassapa has many reproaches… I will teach the nuns various methods, so that Bhikkhunis may excel more than him.

Having said this, she then went together with the four groups to attend the assembly at the Sangharama.

At that time, King Bát Tư Nặc, King A Xà Thế, and King Nghiêm Xí of the Vệ Xá Ly kingdom… Each king led four strong military units (Note: infantry, cavalry, chariots, elephants) to accompany the king, holding great power. The elephants and horses ridden were adorned with precious decorations. Flags, banners, incense, flowers, music, majestic demeanor, and general appearance resembled heavenly beings, and they all arrived at the city of Tăng Già Thi.

King Uttadīna at that time was solemn, with a four-soldier guard serving as his attendants. The king rode a white elephant adorned with beads and jewels and personally carried the statue of the Buddha that had been created. Flowers were scattered, banners held (Note: now called banners), and musicians played music in procession offering homage, from the king's country heading towards the city of Saṅghāṭhī.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Angel Ty Thu Yet Ma, along with the assembly of devas, knew that the Buddha was about to descend to the Hell realm, and thus created three pathways with noble steps from the city of Tăng Già Thi to the Deva Heaven of Tavatimsa. The steps of the middle path were made of lapis lazuli, while the steps on both sides were made of gold, and the landing spots were paved with silver, interspersed with seven kinds of heavenly jewels.

The Deva Lord Indra sent divine messengers to the heavens of Yama, Tusita, Nirmana, Paranimmitavasavartin, and to the heavens of Brahma, to announce the news: "The Buddha is about to descend to the realm of Hell, intending to offer and wish to descend here."

He again sent a messenger to the Four Heavenly Kings, the Dragon King of the great sea, King Gandharva, King Kinnara, and the Yakshas, telling them: "Now the World-Honored One is about to descend to Jambudvipa; you may bring offerings here to make offerings."

At that time, the Devas, Dragons, and Spirits, etc., upon hearing the message, all gathered at Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.

At that time, the World-Honored One was on the summit of Mount Sumeru, together with a multitude of Devas from the various heavenly realms about to descend. All the Devas, front and back, filled the sky, their virtues magnificent, their radiance shining like the full moon in the midst of the sky, countless stars scattered, like the sun just appearing, dazzlingly bright. The Buddha and the assembly at that moment were also likened to this state.

At that very moment, due to the Buddha's spiritual power, there were five rare phenomena in Jambudvipa:

First, it caused those Devas not to see any unclean things in the human world.

Second, make women see the Heavenly men without arousing sexual desire.

Third, make men see the Heavenly women without generating lustful thoughts.

Fourth, allow mortals from afar to clearly see the offerings of the Heavenly beings.

Fifth, the bodies of the Heavenly beings are bright, pure, and beautiful, normally invisible to humans, but by the power of the Buddha, humans can see them clearly.

At that moment, when the Buddha descended from the heavenly palace and set foot on the central jeweled terrace, King Brahma stood on the right side, holding a white parasol, and Indra stood on the left, holding a white fly whisk. In addition, all the other Devas relied on the sky to descend with the Buddha, while all kinds of music arose simultaneously.

The Devas held fans and banners, and scattered flowers as offerings. The celestial beings of the Pure Abode heavens filled the sky, with countless hundreds of thousands of Devas and heavenly maidens wearing strings of jewels, together praising the Buddha's holy virtues.

There were also deities in the midst of the void, scattering fragrant incense and flowers. The Dragon Gods showered gentle fragrant rain. At that time, the sky was without clouds, and the soft sound of thunder brought joy to the hearts of listeners. The deity Gandharva and the deity Kinnara performed an incredibly wonderful musical piece called Devadatta, praising the past deeds of the Tathagata.

At that time, in Yama-Purabhi, kings, officials, common people, and the four assemblies filled the entire city of Tăng Già Thi, some scattering fragrant flowers, some holding fans and canopies, blowing conch shells, beating drums, and playing various kinds of music, all directed towards the sky to show their offering. They raised their hands, clasped them, and revered the Buddha.

Fragrant flowers renowned in the realms of heaven and earth fell intermingled from above and below, covering up to the knees. Seeing the above scene, the followers of other teachings all generated the mind of taking refuge and paying respect.

When the World-Honored One set His true foot on the jeweled steps and began descending, halfway down, the Four Heavenly Kings at their respective places arranged offerings to honor the Buddha. This offering was exceedingly skillful and extraordinary, something humanity had never seen since ancient times.

The World-Honored One accepted the offerings of the Four Heavenly Kings, and then, together with the assembly, descended all the steps. Upon reaching the last step, as the Buddha was about to place His foot on the ground, the Bhikkhuni Lotus Color immediately transformed herself into a Wheel-Turning King, took command of the four armies and seven kinds of treasures, and hurriedly came down from the sky to approach the Buddha first.

The kings all wondered, “Where did this Wheel-Turning King come from?”

At that time, Venerable Subhūti was in the room, and upon knowing that the Buddha had arrived, he adjusted his robes respectfully (Note: at that time, Venerable Subhūti welcomed the Buddha using the contemplation of emptiness). The nun Nīlottama returned the form of the Wheel King and quickly paid homage at the feet of the World-Honored One.

Then, the Buddha reproached the nun and said to her:

– Don't you know? Tu Bồ Đề paid respects to Me first. Who told you to become the Wheel-Turning King? You have entered the ranks of monastics and received the full precepts excessively. Your mind is petty, and your deceit is boundless; even if you repay kindness with compassion, it is only like a drop of morning dew. How could you possibly become a Supreme Leader in My Dharma?

Ni Liên Hoa Sắc, upon hearing the Buddha's admonition, felt deeply ashamed and immediately said to the Buddha:

– Homage to the Blessed One! Now I realize that my own faults are many. From this day forward, I will no longer manifest supernatural powers.

At that time in the Yama Heaven, the kings, officials, and the four assemblies all brought offerings and presented them to the Buddha.

King Udāyīna brought a statue of the Buddha on his head along with the most precious and unusual offerings to the Tathāgata and presented them. The Buddha's body, with its perfect and majestic features, shone brilliantly among the deities, like the full moon emerging from behind clouds. As for the carved statue of the Buddha, compared to the real Buddha, it was no different than a mound compared to Mount Sumeru; it could not be properly compared. Only the curled hair and the noble features slightly resembled the Buddha, to let the four assemblies know that it was a statue of the Buddha.

King Udāyin respectfully spoke to the Buddha:

– Revered World-Honored One! In the past, the Tathāgata, in the cycle of birth and death, sought the Bodhi path, practicing countless, infinite, extremely difficult, and arduous virtuous deeds, enduring unimaginable hardships. As a result, attaining a most wondrous body unparalleled by anyone. The statue I made does not resemble the Buddha; I secretly think it is very sinful.

The World-Honored One told King Udāyin:

– You are not guilty! Today you have done immeasurable good, incomparable to anyone else. Now you are within my teachings, being the first exemplary person. Due to this cause, countless beings in future lives will be born with very deep faith. Today you have received immeasurable merit and vast wholesome roots.

At that time, the heavenly king Indra said to King Udāyī:

– Today, O King, do not be afraid. When the Buddha was formerly in the heavens and in the human world, He praised the merit of the King’s making of statues, and the assembly of Devas greatly rejoiced. Those with faith in future lives will, because of the King, create Buddha statues to gain blessings. Now, O King, you should be happy and rejoice yourself.

At that time, the Buddha sat on the Lion Throne, at the Suṅgha Ground of the Tăng Già Thi kingdom. The minds of the four assemblies all thought: “We hope to hear the Buddha expound on the merit of making statues. Whoever creates them, how great is the blessing?”

At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Maitreya understood that thought, immediately rose from his seat, adjusted his robe to expose his right shoulder, knelt upright with hands clasped, and respectfully addressed the Buddha:

– Respectfully, World-Honored One! King Udayana created images – Buddha statues, if the Buddha is still alive or has already entered Nirvana, a person with faith, making Buddha images according to their means, what kind of merit will that person attain? I earnestly hope the World-Honored One will explain this fully.

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Maitreya:

– Maitreya! Listen carefully and consider attentively, I will speak for you.

If there are any virtuous men or women whose faith is pure, who focus their minds on binding their thoughts to the merit of the Buddha, who often examine the Tathāgata's self-existent power and abundant virtues, the Ten Powers, the Four Fearlessnesses, the Eighteen Special Dharmas, great compassion, great loving-kindness, the knowledge of all seeds, the thirty-two marks of the great hero, and the eighty secondary marks. Each pore contains countless lights of different colors, creating a hundred thousand billion superior merits and adornments, limitless wisdom that is clear and thorough, infinite samādhis, infinite supernatural powers... All these kinds of merit are limitless, free from faults, and incomparable to anyone.

Whoever contemplates and then develops deep faith and preference, creating an image of the Buddha according to good characteristics, the merit of that person is vast and boundless, beyond calculation.

Maitreya! If anyone uses threads to embroider images of the Buddha, or casts them using gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, zinc… Or carves with fragrant Chen tree wood, or engraves using pearls, shells, brocade, woven fabrics, red clay, plaster, clay, or various kinds of wood, etc. (Note: nowadays technology has developed, we have many sophisticated ways to draw, sculpt, and create Buddha statues, such as Photoshop, 3D printing… the merit is the same as mentioned above). Using those materials according to one’s ability to create Buddha images—even as small as a thumb—can make others recognize it as a sacred image, and the person will receive merit.here I will say:

Maitreya! Such people, although still wandering in the cycle of birth and death, will not be born into poor families, nor into lowly lineages, nor will they be born alone, isolated on distant frontiers. Nor will they be born into households of wrong views, merchants, meat-sellers, nor into lowly families, impure courtesans, or households of heterodox teachings or ascetic wrong views… except due to the power of vows of Compassion, otherwise they will not be born into such families.

This person is often born in a family of the Chakravartin dynasty with great power. Or born into a Brahmin family with pure conduct, or a wealthy family that does not commit serious sins. Wherever they are born, they often encounter the Buddha and respectfully offer devotion. They may become a king who upholds the Dharma, spreading the teachings without violating the path. Or become a mighty Chakravartin Holy King, possessing the seven treasures, having a thousand children, flying in the air to spread teachings across the four continents, living a life of freedom, wealth, and happiness.

Or become the Deva King of the Ao Li Heaven, the Deva King of the Yama Heaven, the Deva King of the Tusita Heaven, the Deva King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Deva King of the Parinirmitavaśavartin Heaven… enjoying the pleasures of both gods and humans, with nothing left unexperienced, the merit and blessings continue endlessly. Wherever born, one is always a man, not taking a female body, nor taking a homosexual body, and vile bisexuality (Note: bisexuality refers to being emotionally, romantically, and sexually attracted to both people of the same gender and different genders from oneself).

The body is born without ugliness, the eyes are not blind, the ears are not deaf, the nose is neither crooked nor broken, the mouth is not twisted, the lips do not droop nor wrinkle, the teeth are not sparse, black, or yellow, the tongue is not short or retracted, the neck has no swelling or sores, the body is not hunchbacked, the skin has no blotches, the hands are not stubby, the legs are not deformed or crippled, it is neither too thin nor too fat, neither too long nor too short… All undesirable features are absent.

That person's body is upright and dignified, with a full face. The hair is black, soft, and clean. The lips are red like lipstick, the eyes like green lotuses, and the tongue broad and long. The teeth are white and even, speaking words that are pleasant and skillful, making everyone who hears feel happy and delighted. The elbows are just right. The hands are flat, the back is full, the shoulders and chest broad, the arms and legs gentle as if they were cotton, all features complete without deficiency, with strong sinews, as if like the Nāra Deva (Note: a great strongman of the heavenly realm).

Maitreya! If someone falls into a cesspool and then manages to get out, scrapes off the filth, washes themselves with water, anoints their body with perfume, and wears clean, new clothes... How does such a person compare to someone who is still in the cesspool and has not gotten out, in terms of filth and fragrance? How far apart are they?

– Homage to the World-Honored One! The two are separated by countless degrees!

– Maitreya! If there is anyone still in the cycle of birth and death, who cultivates faith and creates a Buddha statue – compared to the time before they created it, the distance is also the same. It should be known that he, in each life, eliminates all karmic obstacles, all kinds of skillful means, without seeing but understanding. Although born as a human, the senses are considered like those of the heavenly realm. If born in heaven, then far surpassing many celestial beings. Wherever born, there are no deformities, no leprosy, no cancer, not possessed by demons. Not afflicted by diseases of madness, wasting, jaundice, malaria, bladder stones, severe scabies, deep scars, uncontrollable dysentery, indigestion, or aching limbs.paralysis of half the body…Such diseases, even up to four hundred and four ailments, none exist.

Also, not harmed by poisons, weapons, sticks, tigers, wolves, lions, water, fire, thieves, robbers… such unexpected adverse conditions do not cause damage. Usually not fearful, does not commit offenses.

Maitreya Bodhisattva! If sentient beings have previously committed evil karma, they must endure all kinds of suffering, such as being restrained, handcuffed, fettered, beaten, scolded, burned, pricked, skinned, having hair pulled out, hung upside down, or even having their insides cut open… If they develop faith and create images – statues of the Buddha, then all such sufferings will not be experienced. They will not be born into places of war and disturbance, collapsed fortresses, disasters caused by evil stars, hunger, or epidemics… They will not be born into such places; if it is claimed otherwise, that is false speech.

At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha:

– Homage to the World-Honored One! The Tathagata often says, 'Both wholesome and unwholesome karma are never lost.' If there are sentient beings who commit heavy karma, must they be born into lowly, impoverished, disabled families with short lifespans? After developing faith and creating a statue – an image of the Buddha, must these karmic retributions still be endured or not?

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya:

– Listen carefully, I will speak for you. If any sentient being has committed crimes, then generates the intention to create statues and pray for repentance, determined to eliminate them, and vows not to commit them again, all the sins they have committed will be destroyed. Now I will expound this matter for you.

Maitreya! Suppose in a previous life someone was miserly, and because of that condition suffered poverty, had no wealth, lacked provisions, and suddenly encountered a monk who had just emerged from meditation; that person immediately offers food and drink as a donation. Once the offering is made, the person will be free from poverty, and whatever they wish for will be fulfilled. Maitreya! Will the evil karma from the past life and the place of retribution for that poor person still exist now?

Maitreya replied:

– Homage to the World-Honored One! Through offering food, all past evil karma is completely eradicated, poverty is removed, and one attains wealth and abundant possessions.

The Buddha said:

– Bodhisattva Maitreya! Just as you say, know that others are the same. By creating statues, the old evil karma completely ceases, and one does not undergo the retribution one deserves.

Maitreya! Karma has three types. First, retribution is experienced in the present life. Second, retribution is experienced in the next life. Third, retribution is experienced many lifetimes later… Among the three types of karma mentioned above, each type has definite and indefinite. A person with faith in creating statues of the Buddha will only have definite karma in the present life and will still undergo a small portion, but will not experience other types of karma.

At that time, Bodhisattva Maitreya asked:

– Reverently I ask, World-Honored One! The Tathagata often says: There are five very serious karmas that will certainly lead to the Avici Hell (Note: the most terrible type of hell, with continuous extreme punishments). These are the crimes of: killing one's father, killing one's mother, killing an Arhat, malignantly causing the Buddha's body to bleed, and disrupting the harmony of the Sangha. If a being has previously committed these crimes, but later develops faith in the Buddha and makes images – Buddha statues, will that person still fall into hell, or will they not?

The Buddha replied to Bodhisattva Maitreya:

– Today I will give you another example: Suppose there is a person, holding a strong bow in the middle of a forest, aiming upward to shoot at the leaves, the arrow flies through without any obstacle. If there is a being who has committed a grave sin, later creates a Buddha statue, sincerely repents, even if their faith is not very strong, their sins will be alleviated, so even if they go to hell, they will soon be released, just like the arrow that flies through without stopping; this person's case is similar…

Likewise, a monk, having attained supernatural powers, can cross from this shore to the other, and the seas surrounding the four continents cannot impede him. Similarly, someone who has committed sins may temporarily descend into hell, but later be liberated; past karma cannot obstruct this.

Bodhisattva Maitreya then respectfully asked further:

– Revered World-Honored One! All Buddhas Tathagata have the nature of the Dharma body; they are not bodies composed of form and shape. If one takes form and shape as the body of the Buddha, then Venerable Nanda and the Wheel-turning King should be considered Buddhas, because they both possess all good marks. If there are sentient beings who destroy the Buddha's Dharma body, what is Dharma is spoken of as non-Dharma, and what is non-Dharma is spoken of as Dharma, then subsequently develop faith and create Buddha images, will this grave offense be completely eradicated, or will it not be eradicated?

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Maitreya:

– If a sentient being speaks what is Dharma as non-Dharma, and non-Dharma as Dharma, only using the mouth to speak without breaking views, and after birth has faith and likes to create forms – Buddha statues, then the previous evil karma will result in only slight retribution in the current body, not falling into evil paths, yet will still not be liberated from birth and death immediately.

Bodhisattva Maitreya then asked further:

– Homage to the World-Honored One! If someone steals items from the Buddha's stupa, steals items from the monastery, steals items from monks in all directions, steals items from the monks present, uses them for themselves, or gives them to others to use, considering them as their own, the World-Honored One often said: “Using items stolen from the Buddha's stupa or from the monks, that sin is very grave.” So, for sentient beings who have committed that sin but sincerely feel remorse, generate pure faith, and create a Buddha image, are those people's sins then extinguished?

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Maitreya:

– If any sentient being has ever used that object, then later, upon self-reflection, feels ashamed and remorseful, compensates for what was taken, and vows not to commit it again, today I will give one example for you: Suppose there is a poor person who once had many debts and suddenly comes across a buried treasure of countless gold and jewels. After paying off all the debts, there is still a large remainder. Similarly, the one who has committed a sin, after making restitution, then creates a Buddha statue, will be free from suffering and will enjoy lasting happiness.

At that time, the great Bodhisattva Maitreya respectfully asked the Buddha:

– Homage to the World-Honored One! As the Buddha once taught, "To commit a grave offense while in the Dharma of the Buddha is not called living." (Note: Grave offenses are the types of offenses for monastics; monks have 4 types, nuns have 8 types.) If someone commits such an offense and then resolves to remember the merits of the Buddhas and creates statues, can they "live" again according to the Buddha's teachings? Moreover, in this life, or the second, third, or fourth life, can they attain the Dharma?

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Maitreya:

– For example, if a loved one is tied up, their hands, feet, and neck bound, if the bindings are removed, it would be like a bird freed from a net, able to fly away freely; the same applies to that person. If one develops faith and reflects on the merits of the Buddha and the making of Buddha images, then all karmic obstacles will be eliminated, one will swiftly be freed from the cycle of birth and death, without hindrance. Maitreya should know, there are three Vehicle teachings: the Śrāvaka Vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, and the Great Buddha Vehicle. Depending on the Vehicle, when one makes Buddha images with a wishful mind, one will attain liberation according to that Vehicle. If one creates them solely to attain Buddhahood, without seeking any other rewards, then even if the karmic obstacles are heavy, they will still be swiftly overcome.eradicate, although subjected to birth and death, yet without suffering, until attaining Supreme Bodhi, gaining a pure realm; possessing all good marks, enjoying an endlessly long lifespan.

At that time in the assembly, there were those who had not yet awakened to the Great Vehicle, who all harbored doubts and thought like this: “In the past, did the Tathagata create Buddha images or not? If He did create them, why is His realm filled with filth and not pure?”

King Basyu Nag, relying on the power of the Buddha, immediately rose from his seat, stood up, pressed his palms together, and respectfully knelt to address the Buddha:

– Revered World-Honored One! I see that the Tathagata’s marks and all his family traits are unsurpassed, and my mind is firmly resolved without a trace of doubt. Yet, World-Honored One, there was a time when the khandala tree pierced Your foot. There was another time when Devadatta rolled a stone that hit You, causing Your foot to bleed. Previously, there was a time when You said You were ill, so You had the physician prepare good medicine. There was also a time when You experienced back pain. You instructed Elder Mahākāśyapa to recite the 'Seven Methods of Enlightenment,' and the pain was alleviated. There was another time when You suffered from aches and sent Ananda to the house of a Brahmin to request cow’s milk. Previously, there was a time in the village of Tāla, during the three-month rains retreat, when You ate only horse fodder.Once again, went on alms but received nothing, the bowl did not return.

Honorable World-Honored One! As the World-Honored One said: “If anyone creates images – Buddha statues, all karmic obstacles will be eliminated, they will be free from suffering, and will not have diseases.” So, in past lives, did the World-Honored One ever create statues or not? If in the past He did create statues, what were the causes and circumstances for those deeds?

The Buddha said to King Pasenadi:

– Listen! Listen carefully and remember well, I will clearly explain to Your Majesty.

O Great King, in my past life, for the sake of seeking Bodhi, I used precious jewels, fragrant Chiên đàn wood, and paint to create images of the Buddha—more than all the beings of gods and humans present here today. Due to this merit, even though I am still caught in the cycle of birth and death and delusion, my body is as durable as diamond, incapable of being destroyed.

Oh Great King! I have memories of countless past eons. Even during my cycles of birth and death, I created Buddha statues. At that time, I was still greedy, angry, and deluded… countless afflictions corresponded with my mind, yet I never, even for a moment, faced disruption of the four elements due to karma, nor was I possessed by spirits, nor did I suffer from any minor disease. Everything I needed was always complete. How much more so now, since I have attained Bodhi enlightenment, is there still something "unsatisfactory"?

Great King! If in the past I have created Buddha statues, and now I have karmic consequences to endure as a result, how can I become the one 'Fearless in Speech' and then say that 'Creating statues can definitely eliminate all bad karma'?

Great King! In the past, I generously provided countless foods and drinks, wealth and treasures; how is it that in this life I cannot receive alms and must eat horse grain? If, as today, that is the case, how can I in countless sutras, in many ways, praise the perfection of giving and speak of generosity without any falsehood or deception?

Great King! I am a person who speaks the truth, one who does not speak lies. If I were to lie, whom could I save?

Great King! For a long time, I have abandoned all evil deeds, given up what is hard to abandon, done what is difficult to do, even letting go of hundreds of thousands of lives, have created countless forms – images of Buddhas, repented countless evil deeds, would I be subject to injury, illness, or suffering, eating the grain of horses, or hunger and thirst? If I had once gained superior results, but now they are lost, how could I be encouraged to cultivate those merits again?

O Great King! All Buddhas Tathagatas have an eternal body, a Dharma-nature body, and manifest these activities for the sake of guiding sentient beings; they are not truly like that. Getting injured in the foot, back pain, asking for milk, taking medicine, and so on… until entering Parinirvana, leaving relics, distributing them to various places, building stupas, and so on… All are skillful means of the Buddha, making sentient beings see such appearances.

Great King! I manifest in this world such sickness and suffering with the purpose of allowing sentient beings to clearly understand that karma does not disappear, so that they may feel fear to abandon sin, practice wholesome deeds, and thereafter, know the eternal body, understand the body of the Dharma-nature, have infinite lifespan, and dwell in a pure land.

Great King! All Buddhas, Tathagatas, are never deceitful, purely embody great compassion, skillful wisdom, and therefore are able to manifest in all these various ways.

At that time, King Basyanaga, upon hearing these words, rejoiced greatly, and together with countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, all generated the mind for Supreme Bodhi.

At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Maitreya continued to ask the Buddha:

– Reverently, World-Honored One! There are women with narrow-minded intentions, who harbor much jealousy, anger, contempt, deceit, hold grudges without letting go, and do not repay kindness. Even though they seek Bodhi, few maintain a steadfast mind, often wishing to deceive everyone, yet are also deceived in return.

O World-Honored One! If this woman creates images – Buddha statues, will such karmas be eradicated? Will she become a grateful person, able to repay kindness? Will she attain sufficient wisdom and great compassion? Will she be free from the cycle of birth and death or dislike departure? Except by making a vow, will she have to endure being born as a female again? Will she be like Lady Kṣitigarbha’s mother and the Buddha’s mother, Lady Māyā?

The Buddha answered Bodhisattva Maitreya:

– If a woman frequently makes Buddha statues, she will certainly not be reborn as a woman again. If she does take a female body, she will be the most noble and eminent among women. Compared to women who possess the five virtues, what a woman gains from creating statues surpasses that of those women. What are the five virtues?

First: Bearing children.

Second: Noble lineage.

Third: Innate chastity.

Fourth: Physical beauty and appearance.

Fifth: Perfect demeanor.

Maitreya! All women have eight karmic causes, therefore they often endure being female for many lifetimes. What are the eight?

One: Loving and treasuring the female body.

Two: Being attached to the lustful pleasures of a woman.

Three: The mouth often praises the physical appearance of women.

Four: The heart is not upright, hiding wrongful deeds.

Five: Feeling weary or dissatisfied with one's husband.

Six: The mind is heavily burdened with thoughts of others.

Seven is: Knowing that someone has done you a favor but you betray them.

Eight is: Adorning oneself, wearing false attire to make others feel enchanted or attached.

If one can completely abandon such eight things, in making images or statues of the Buddha, even until becoming a Buddha, they are usually male. Taking a female form is unreasonable.

Maitreya! There are four causes that make men take a female body. What are the four?

First: Pretending to use a woman's voice, scornfully laughing and calling the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, and other Saints.

Second: For those who observe precepts, harboring criticism and saying that they have violated the precepts.

Third: Enjoy flattering and deceiving others.

Fourth: Feeling jealousy when seeing someone better than oneself.

If any man does the four above things, after death he will certainly be reborn as a female and endure countless sufferings in the hells. If he develops deep faith, repents for past actions, and makes a Buddha statue, all the above offenses will be eliminated, and ultimately he will no longer have to be reborn as a female.

Maitreya! There are four causes that lead men to engage in homosexual acts. What are the four?

First: harming the bodies of humans and animals.

Second: being angry at, mocking, or disparaging monks who observe purity rules.

Third: being lustful, greedy, and deliberately violating precepts.

Fourth: being close to someone who violates precepts and advising them to do so.

If any man previously did this, later generates faith and creates – Buddha statues, even until becoming a Buddha, does not report it, often becomes a man with complete faculties.

Maitreya! There are four types of karma that often make men endure a dual-gender inclination, the lowest among all people. What are the four?

First: Lewd and obscene sexual acts in sacred places.

Second: Being corruptly infatuated with a male body.

Third: Committing sexual acts oneself on one's own body.

The fourth is: Buying and selling women's beauty to others.

If any sentient being engages in these actions, they will deeply blame themselves for their mistakes, regret their past offenses, arouse a pure faith and create Buddha images, and even until they become a Buddha, they will not assume that body.

Maitreya! There are also four causes that make men often generate sexual desire for women, enjoying sexual acts with men. What are the four?

First: Either doubting or mocking and insulting others.

Second: Loving the way women dress and decorate themselves.

Three is: committing sexual misconduct, being impure with female relatives.

Four is: truly lacking virtuous qualities, yet falsely accepting reverence from others.

Due to these causes and conditions, men give rise to different kinds of afflictions. If one repents for mistakes committed, refrains from creating new faults, and the mind generates faith in making images – of the Buddha, that sin is already destroyed, and that mind is also ended.

Maitreya! There are five types of stinginess or harming sentient beings. What are the five?

First: Being stingy and possessive with the village and the nearby place where one lives (Note: This means wanting only oneself to be in this place, not accommodating others). Because of this, one will end up in desolate, empty places.

Second: Being stingy and possessive with the house, the porch, and roof for living (Note: This means only allowing oneself to enter and leave this house, not permitting others to do so), will lead to chronic illness, often in places that are dirty and confined.

Third: Being stingy and possessive with one's beauty and appearance (Note: This means wanting only oneself to enjoy beauty, not wanting others to enjoy it), will result in an unattractive appearance contrary to one’s desires.

The fourth is: Being stingy with wealth (Note: meaning only wanting to have wealth for oneself, not allowing others to have it), will result in poverty and lack of basic necessities.

The fifth is: Being stingy in sharing the Dharma already known (Note: meaning only oneself knows the profound meaning, not letting others know), will incur the karmic consequences of being a lower being and becoming dull-witted.

If one repents for one’s previous karma and creates

Buddha statues, one will abandon the previous stingy mind and will not suffer the results as mentioned above.

Maitreya! There are five conditions that cause sentient beings to be born in barbarian regions, in borderlands, or in times when there is no Buddha Dharma. What are those five?

First: Not generating a pure faith in the field of merit of the Three Jewels.

Second: Acting contrary to truth, deviating from right principles, while falsely teaching the precepts (Note: teaching precepts is the duty of ordained practitioners).

Third: Not adhering to true doctrine yet teaching it to others.

Fourth: Breaking the harmony of the Sangha, causing it to split into two factions.

The fifth is: At least causing two monks to not get along.

Completely ending the above karma and making a Buddha statue will result in frequently encountering the Buddha and often hearing fundamental dharma.

Maitreya! Beings also have five types of causes and conditions that often make many people dislike and avoid them, even their close relatives do not like to meet them. What are the five?

First: Speaking double-tongued words (Note: that is, saying bad things about one person to another, and vice versa)

Second: Speaking cruel words.

Three is: Many disputes.

Four is: Much resentment.

Five is: Skilled in using flattering words to criticize others.

Later, if one aspires to create images of the Buddha – repents past karma and vows not to commit it again, that person's sins will all be eradicated, and they will be respected and approached by everyone. Why is that? Because the Buddhas possess immeasurable and boundless superior merits, immeasurable and boundless vast wisdom, immeasurable and boundless Samadhi of liberation, and complete rare Dharma-nature virtues.

Virtuous men! Suppose someone were to take three thousand great thousand world systems (Note: equivalent to 1 billion solar systems) and grind them into fine dust, then take that dust and, for each particle, grind it into many tiny particles, in number equal to the dust particles in one great thousand world system; how countless would be the total number of ground particles.

Suppose someone takes the number of ground dust particles and, using supernatural power, travels eastward. That person travels for a long time, many lifetimes, as numerous as the ground dust particles. In each moment, that person passes through a number of worlds as countless as the dust of a great heaven that has been ground into pieces. After passing through all of those worlds, they drop one dust particle.

That person then continues to travel east beyond that number of worlds and drops the second dust particle.

Upon reaching the third dust particle, they go even farther than before, and so on, multiplying each time, until all the ground dust particles have been dropped.

The East is like that, and the South, West, and North are the same. In the places the person has passed in the four directions, they crushed the entire world there to dust.

All sentient beings together could still count these dust particles, but the merits in each hair on the body of the Tathagata cannot be known. Why is that?

The merits that the Buddhas have are limitless and inconceivable.

Virtuous men! Suppose the number of people is as many as the tiny dust just mentioned, their wisdom equaling that of Śāriputra, how many of their wisdoms would not equal a single thought of the Thus-come-one?
