tieu_de: ONCE YOU SEE HELL, YOU WON'T DARE TO HAVE A SINGLE EVIL THOUGHT (An American Escaping the Viet Minh, Practicing to Attain Enlightenment)
tom_tat: The time I gave a Dharma lecture in Miami, USA, there was an American. During World War II, he worked in intelligence for the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and he was a pilot who participated in the war.
noi_dung:
SEEING HELL ALREADY, ONE DOES NOT DARE TO COMMIT A SINGLE EVIL THOUGHT (An American Escaping the Viet Minh, Practicing to Realize)

The time I gave a Dharma talk in Miami, USA, there was an American among us. During World War II, he worked in intelligence for the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and he was an aviator who participated in the Vietnam War. When his plane was shot down, he parachuted out and was then chased by the Viet Minh.

He ran into a temple; the elderly monk in the temple was very compassionate, so he took him in and hid him in the temple for a year. This elderly monk practiced meditation and taught him to meditate. He stayed there practicing for a year and attained the divine eye. He acquired it from meditating.

First, he said that when his third eye opened, his head felt very heavy, extremely painful, and incredibly uncomfortable. This lasted for about two or three months. One day, he suddenly felt refreshed. After that, he saw many extremely terrifying strange things. Gradually, he became accustomed and things returned to normal. Things that the physical eyes could not see, he could see.

On his body, there are still more than ten bullets that he doesn't dare to remove, fearing touching the nerves. So when there is a thunderstorm with rain, his whole body aches painfully. In the past, he himself killed too many people, and today he must endure the consequences of that. He said he is very resigned!

He stated that he had once seen hell. He said that the situation in hell, the suffering there, is truly something that no evil thought dares to touch. Not only does one not dare to commit evil deeds, but even a single evil thought is not dared to move. Anyone who truly possesses divine eye (heavenly vision) is like that.

He is not an ordinary fortune teller, boasting and deceiving people. He does not use magic to fool others. Every night he comes to listen to my sutra lectures. There is a layperson who translates English for him.

A person who truly sees hell decides not to entertain even a single evil thought. Because creating karma that leads to hell is too easy. Once fallen there, the suffering is immense. Wanting to leave hell is by no means an easy task!

In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, this matter is explained very clearly. Indeed, the words of the Buddha all have meaning. Bodhisattvas fear the causes, sentient beings fear the consequences. By the time sentient beings face the fruition of their actions, it is too late to be afraid. Bodhisattvas understand how terrifying the consequences are, so they are extremely cautious when creating causes.

From the moment the mind arises, the language and actions are made, there is nothing done without careful attention. They absolutely dare not create bad causes. To seek a little profit now and suffer the consequences later is unimaginable.

These are some foreigners talking privately with me that are worth our caution.

H.T. DO NOT PURIFY!

tieu_de: THE MIRACULOUSNESS OF UNCLE LANG NGHIEM
tom_tat: Below is a compilation of a few small stories about the miraculous interventions of Reverend Lang Nghiem that some people commented on the YouTube page! Hue Van has summarized them for everyone to read 💐 🍀 From Ka Ri
noi_dung:
THE MIRACULOUS POWER OF UNCLE LANG NGHIEM

Below is a compilation of some small stories about the miraculous responses of Monk Lăng Nghiem that some people commented on the YouTube page! Hue Van has summarized them for everyone to read 💐

🍀 From Ka Ri Viu:

I want to share a true story about this child! In our case, our family had a child who suffered a very frightening possession when going out at night and going to an unclean place, specifically the restroom. When returning home, the child would cry uncontrollably, with tears streaming, which was very scary. Especially as it got darker, the crying and groaning were even more terrifying, as if something frightening was following the child. Our family tried every method, from wearing charms, taking the child to the temple, and performing rituals 2-3 times, but there was still no result.

Our family was lucky to have someone introduce us to this Kinh Lăng Nghiêm. I went on YouTube and typed 'Chú Lăng Nghiêm' in Sanskrit, and at that moment, my baby, who was crying, suddenly calmed down and peacefully fell asleep on my shoulder.

This is a 100% true sharing to prove to you, as well as to myself, who previously thought that Buddhist scriptures were just teachings and advice, praying to gods was no different than ordinary ideologies. Many things I could not understand, only explained based on my own understanding; only when you experience it yourself can you truly understand the miraculous nature of this set of scriptures!

🍀 From Long Lân:

The Śūraṅgama Mantra is an uncle who will disappear first before the French are defeated, but anyone in this life who hears him should cherish it because later on, they will no longer hear him. The sayings are very difficult to understand, but the mental discipline is very great. Rejoice when hearing him!

🍀 From friend Vu Ho:

Anyone who has the fate to hear this Thủ Lăng Nghiêm mantra is a person with great blessings accumulated over many lives and many past incarnations. This mantra has unparalleled power, transforming bad karma into good karma, suffering into peace, and poverty into prosperity. It strongly assists people who diligently practice learning and cultivation.

🍀 From friend Hien Le:

Every time I am oppressed by fear, I always open up to listen at any moment. At first, I was scared, but gradually it became an indispensable habit for me. Once, while in the hospital, I dreamt that a man was teasing the oppressive entity, which made me unable to fully awaken; I just woke up vaguely. I woke up and opened up to Master Đại Bi, but still continued to be affected. By chance, I went on YouTube and found Master Lăng Nghiêm, and I opened up. Since then, I have a feeling that the spirits no longer disturb me; it is truly very effective. I want more people to know about Master Lăng Nghiêm.Thank you to the person who created this video. A Di Da Phat...

🍀 From friend Dai Loi Ngo:

This story happened quite a long time ago... I went out with friends to Turtle Lake and other places in Saigon. When I returned, it was already midnight, and at that time I was staying at the house of a nun I knew (I was a third-year student at HUFLIT at that time). I was arranging things and happened to look out the window (what they call the ventilation column of a multi-story house). I saw a black form creeping from outside into my room. I thought I was hallucinating, but no, the truth is I was being followed by a spirit. The next night, when I slept...I saw a woman pressing down on me (I am male). At that moment, I couldn't do anything, I just recited the phrase 'Nam Mô A Di Đà Phật,' and everything started to gradually ease, and I was able to sleep again. After that, I called my family, and they advised me to read the Great Compassion Mantra. I did read it, and things improved somewhat, but after a few meals, it happened again. When I sleep, I always have the feeling that someone is watching or following me. In my dream, I met a woman wearing a very beautiful gray robe; she talked to me and said that if there is anything I need or want, she will help. ButI knew that it was a spirit following me. After that, I looked for a master to resolve it, and it turned out that there really was a spirit following me. Later, when I happened to return to Saigon, the lady owner knew about it and introduced me to this monk Lang Nghiem! I spent an hour that night reading, and this monk is truly very effective! He is really powerful and very effective, everyone!

🍀 From my friend Vi Nguyen:

Mantra Lang Nghiem is truly miraculous. There was a time when I thought I had long fallen into evil influences, but fortunately, I came to know Mantra Lang Nghiem, and he genuinely dispelled everything for me. I sincerely praise him with all my heart, and truly, I have experienced an incredible miracle! At first, I even felt fear, but now I feel extremely peaceful; all my fears vanish when I hear him. It is truly unimaginable, moreover, my illusions have also significantly diminished. RespectfullyI hope that all Buddhist followers, near and far, have the opportunity to hear and recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra! Namo Shakyamuni Buddha!

🍀 From my friend Lan Linh:

This mantra has very great power. Wherever this mantra is recited, the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, Dharma Protectors... as many as the sands of the Ganges River come to protect it. The power is immense!

🙏🙏🙏 Venerable Tuyen Hoa explains:

The Lankavatara Mantra is the longest mantra, also called the "spiritual mantra" because it is very efficacious and wondrous, beyond what words can describe.

Therefore, one must pay attention, the most important thing when reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is to strictly observe the precepts; if one does not maintain the precepts, no matter how one recites the mantra, it will not be effective. If one can uphold the precepts, without blameworthy intentions, without greed, anger, or delusion, then reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra will have a greater impact and greater benefits. I tell those who recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra that they can earn even more money than trading gold; reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra once has a value equivalent to tens of thousands of ounces of gold."but should not use greed to recite. If early in the morning you recite the Mantra of Śūraṅgama once, then recite the Heart of Śūraṅgama Mantra 108 times, you will receive boundless, immeasurable blessings. Therefore, it is said that if you recite the Śūraṅgama Mantra, in the next life you will obtain wealth and prosperity for seven lifetimes. This means that if you want to pray for blessings from heaven and humans, if you do not want to pray, then naturally it is not necessary. If you want to pray for karmic rewards to manifest in the world, then you will achieve your goal.

I also do not want to say what benefits Master Lăng Nghiêm ultimately has, because if I say it, people who recite will develop greed. Reciting Master Lăng Nghiêm with the desire for benefit is not truly yearning to recite Master Lăng Nghiêm.

📜 The Mind Mantra is: ''Đát diệt tha. Án a na lệ tì xá đề, bệ ra bật xà ra đa rị, bàn đa bàn đa nể, bật xà ra bàng ni, phấn hổ hồng đổ lô ung, phấn ta bà ha.''

If in this world, no one recites the Diamond Sutra, then the Demon King will appear. If there is even one person who recites it, then the heavenly demons Ba Tuan will not dare to show up. Because their greatest fear is the Diamond Sutra. What they want to destroy the most is the Diamond Sutra. When the law begins to be eradicated, the Diamond Sutra will be affected first, including the Sutra Scriptures. At that time, the heavenly demons Ba Tuan will appear, wreaking havoc everywhere. At that moment there will be no heaven or earth, no Buddha; they will have absolutely no fear of anything. SoTherefore, I advise every Buddhist (both lay and monastic) to memorize the Śūraṅgama Mantra and recite it daily; this is the Dharma-protection method, and it ensures the Dharma endures for a long time. Do not underestimate it as meaningless or irrelevant. Currently, here, only a few dozen people listen to lectures on the Śūraṅgama Mantra. But it is precisely these few dozen listeners who have held back the forces of demons, causing them to panic when this Mantra is mentioned.

🙏NAMO BUDDHA SHAKYAMUNI 🙇

🌸🙏NAMO AMITABHA BUDDHA 🙇🙇🏻‍♀️

tieu_de: MY FEELINGS WHEN CHANTING THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA
tom_tat: I have been studying Buddhism for several years now. Since learning about the extraordinary power of mantras in Buddhism, I have grown even more devoted in my practice. The more I practice, the more I see the efficacy of the Great Compassion Mantra and the Lăng Nghiê Mantra.
noi_dung:
MY FEELINGS WHEN CHANTING THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA

I have been studying Buddhism for several years now. Since realizing the mighty power of mantras in Buddhism, I have become even more devoted to practice. The more I practice, the more I see the great efficacy of the Great Compassion Mantra and the Surangama Mantra very clearly.

Like the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, I have copied the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra many times. When copying it myself, if I maintain a sincere and calm mind, I can feel as if there is light shining down on the top of my head. At that moment, I feel very pleasant and peaceful, as if the light shining down purifies both my body and mind.

Although the number of recitations is not very many, I usually chant in the morning. Up to now, I have done it more than 400 times. Even with just that amount, I find that my body and mind become increasingly light and peaceful, which is very miraculous.

I often think that merely reciting is not enough; I should also study more of the theoretical reasoning in the sutras. After studying the scriptures, I realized that in the past I had done many wrong things, and there were many things I was not good at. Thinking this way, I feel as if a cool stream is flowing from within my heart, sweeping away all the accumulated impurities from before.

I find the chanting voice of Master Tuyen Hoa extremely solemn. I often listen to Master Tuyen Hoa recite sutras, and after repeatedly hearing him chant, I immediately followed his way of pronunciation. The strange thing is that after learning his pronunciation, when I chant the Mantra, I feel my entire chest trembling, and my breath and energy gradually improve.

Namo Amitabha Buddha, we can still feel the spirit of Venerable Tuyên Hóa in his recordings; his voice makes listeners feel a kind of heavenly authority and earth-establishing dignity, solemn and fearless. From then on, when reciting the sutra, I noticed that my mind and character gradually improved. Namo Homage and Refuge to Venerable Tuyên Hóa.

Translation Source: Mật Hỷ

Source: Bồ Đề Tâm

tieu_de: THOSE WHO STUDY BUDDHISM, AT NIGHT DO NOT SLEEP NAKED, MUST WEAR A SHIRT AND SHORTS, THE MIND SHOULD BE USUALLY AS IF IN FRONT OF THE BUDDHA. DELICIOUS RICE
tom_tat: Buddhist practitioners should maintain a kind heart, speak kind words, and do kind deeds. 'Maintaining a kind heart' means not allowing any evil thoughts that go against heaven and reason, that harm others for one's own benefit, to arise. If they arise
noi_dung:
BUDDHIST PRACTITIONERS, AT NIGHT DO NOT SLEEP NAKED, MUST WEAR A SHIRT AND SHORTS, HEART SHOULD BE AS IF FACING THE BUDDHA. DELICIOUS RICE

Those who study Buddhism should maintain a kind heart, speak kind words, and do good deeds. "Maintaining a kind heart" means never allowing evil thoughts that go against heaven and reason, harm others to benefit oneself, to arise. If such thoughts do arise, one should immediately feel shame and repent, causing them to be immediately destroyed. All minds inclined towards filial piety, respect, loyalty, trust, propriety, righteousness, honesty, honor, benefiting others, and benefiting things should always be preserved, and whenever possible, one should earnestly act on them. If one cannot act, the mind should still frequently think of these matters.

“Speaking kind words” means saying words that are beneficial to people and things; it is not merely saying words that make others feel happy and calling them kind! For example, teaching children and advising people to do good, advising people to refrain from evil, advising people to uphold moral principles, advising people to practice merits, etc. “Doing good deeds” is actively engaging in acts of filial piety toward parents, respecting elders, living harmoniously with relatives, and improving customs [for the better].

Whenever reciting sutras, performing Buddhist rituals, chanting Buddha's name, making repentance, or engaging in any Buddhist activities, one must do so with respect in both body and mind!

A Buddhist practitioner should not sleep naked at night; they must wear a shirt and shorts, keeping the mind as if in front of the Buddha. When eating rice, one should not overeat. No matter how delicious the rice is, only eat up to eight or nine parts [at most]. Eating ten parts brings no benefit; eating more than ten parts will certainly harm the internal organs. Regularly eating like this will certainly shorten life. Eating too much leads to a dull mind, a tired body, slow digestion, and inevitably results in passing gas. Passing gas is the worst matter, and it causes the greatest sin.

In places like the Buddha hall or the monk's quarters, one must be respectful; for example, lighting incense is merely to express one's heart, but ultimately, there is no type that can truly be considered incense! If one eats too much and passes gas, it is extremely foul, causing the stench to permeate the Three Jewels, and in the future, one may be reborn as maggots in a dung pit. If one does not overeat, one will not pass gas excessively! If one consumes cold substances and feels unwell, simply go to an open space to relieve yourself and wait until the smell dissipates before returning to the room. If there is a situation where one cannot go outside, one should use strength to restrain it; in less than a moment, it will dissipate in the stomach. Some people say that not releasing it will cause illness; this statement is stillHeavier in sin than the act of passing gas publicly, by all means do not follow. The Buddha's precepts did not mention this matter; perhaps in ancient times, people were healthy, not greedy for food, and did not have this problem, so it was not mentioned.

If there were any, surely the Buddha would have spoken. Do not say that the Buddha does not forbid it, so you can just act freely; that is precisely inviting your own downfall, and even the Buddha would find it hard to save you! Confucius, in the capacity of a sage meeting a sovereign (the ruler of a country), though an ordinary person, when about to enter the palace, on the steps below, did not even dare to breathe strongly, let alone when entering the palace to meet the king! Therefore, the Analects record: “Nhiếp tề thăng đường, cúc cung như dã. Bình khí tự bất tức dã” (Lifting the hem of the robe to ascend the hall, bending the body like this, holding breath as if not breathing) (Nhiếp 攝: to lift. Tề 齊, pronounced like Tư 咨12, meaning the hem of the robe. Cúc 鞠: to bend. Bình 屏: to conceal. Tức 息: breath from the nose. Confucius meeting the king, whenAbout to ascend to the throne, first bow your body. Because of bowing, the front flap of the robe is longer, so you must lift both edges of the robe about a meter above the ground to avoid stepping on the robe, tripping, and being disrespectful. Utterly serious, so the breath in the nose seems not to escape. Try to see to what extent He is cautious? People nowadays are far inferior to Confucius, and the king then was even far inferior to the Buddha! Letting out wind is even more different from exhaling. Silent contemplation, how is it different from the vast earth having no place to lodge? Is it not extreme attention?)

We are ordinary beings with karmic retribution in the Buddha's hall of the Holy of the Holy, the Heaven of the Heavens (the saint of saints, the heaven of heavens), where the Three Jewels are fully present; how dare we not restrain ourselves and indulge in farting at will? That sin is the greatest beyond compare! Many people, because they have not studied much of the ancient teachings before, think that the ancients did not mention it. They do not know that the ancients spoke very skillfully, calling it “lower release of air” (gas escaping from below). They also do not understand what that phrase means and do not care to pay attention. Thirty, forty years ago, Quang often talked about this matter, and later, when asked again, people did not know what it was about! Therefore, it is best to speak directly:"farting." In traditional opera, whenever someone insults another and says 'careless performance,' they would say: 'Your words are like letting out a fart.' Whenever there is something frightening, one dare not breathe heavily, so how could one even fart? Because in careless performance there is no restraint, that’s why one can fart! Do not say 'talking about farting is unpleasant to hear,' in fact, I want to create a way to save people from being ripped apart by maggots in a cesspit! Upon waking up and after defecating or urinating, one must wash their hands. Whenever touching the body or feeling down to the feet, one must wash their hands.

During the summer months, pants should not be worn loose; they must be tied up. Carelessly spitting phlegm or blowing your nose is a great loss of merit! In the pure land of Buddha, not only is it forbidden to spit or blow your nose inside the halls, but even on the clean grounds outside the halls, one should not spit or blow their nose. Spitting on clean ground creates a dirty appearance! Some people are careless and unrestrained, spitting anywhere on the ground or on the walls inside the room! A beautiful room ends up with the ground and walls covered in phlegm. Such a person spits to show arrogance, and over time it becomes a habit; they spit every day, and the essence of the food and drink they consume turns entirely into phlegm. If one endures swallowing the phlegmSwallow it, and over time the phlegm will no longer appear. That is the best way to use phlegm to eliminate phlegm. If you cannot swallow it, you should take a handkerchief to wipe the phlegm into your sleeve, spit onto it, and then put it back into your sleeve. This method is both tiring and unclean, not as good as swallowing it, which is neither tiring nor unclean and will permanently prevent phlegm-related illness. This is the best way to treat phlegm-related disease.

A Buddhist practitioner must be mindful in every action and movement. When reciting the Buddha's name, one must be sincere. Whenever feelings of sorrow arise in the mind, that is actually a sign of good roots manifesting, but one should not let it happen frequently. Otherwise, one could be influenced by evil forces. Whatever brings pleasure, one should not be overly delighted. Otherwise, one will surely be affected by demonic joy. While reciting the Buddha's name, the eyelids should be lowered, and one should not strain the mind excessively to the point that the mind becomes agitated; this can easily cause symptoms like itchy scalp, headache, etc., which need to be properly regulated. When chanting aloud, one should not exert too much effort to the point of illness. Using prayer beads while reciting can help prevent this.laziness, but when sitting in meditation, unable to use the rosary; whenever using the rosary, the fingers move so the mind cannot be still, and over time it is bound to become a sickness.

When reading sutras and various books, one should not rush. They must be read many times; reading in a hurry will not allow for stillness, making it difficult to grasp the intended meaning. Young scholars who are somewhat intelligent often encounter a set of scriptures and then forget to eat or sleep while reading, thinking that reading it once is enough. By the second time, they are no longer interested. Even if they read again, it is like being absent-minded or dazed. Such people cannot achieve anything; one should do their best to prevent this! Su Dongpo said: “Old books, read a hundred times, one never grows tired; read carefully and think deeply, and one will naturally understand” (An old book is never dull after a hundred readings; read deeply and reflect, and one will naturally know).

WRITINGS OF DHARMA MASTER AN QUANG

PLEASE REGULARLY CHANT AMITABHA BUDDHA

tieu_de: IN TODAY'S AGE, NOTHING WASTES BLESSINGS AND LIFESPAN MORE THAN LUST

noi_dung:
IN THE PRESENT AGE, NOTHING WASTES FORTUNE AND LIFESPAN LIKE SEXUAL DESIRE

In the present era as well, nothing consumes merit and lifespan like lust. A person's career, reputation, and lifespan, which could have been wealth, long life, and successful descendants, are ruined simply by committing sexual misconduct, such as: 'illicit sexual relations before marriage or adultery after marriage, promiscuity with widows, defilement with prostitutes, masturbation, committing sexual acts on taboo days (refer to the book Thọ Khang Bảo Giám on Taboo Days), viewing pornographic books and films, and then being taken over by soul-hungry demons, mischievous spirits, snake spirits, fox spirits... who cling to the body freely.'Sucking the vital essence makes the spirit confused and the body weak, the mind filled only with thoughts of lust.

Engaging in sexual misconduct causes the merits from our past or present life to be instantly burned away, and gods and spirits despise us. Then, at home, our children and spouse may suffer consequences in repayment. Parents feel ashamed. It is the sin of unfilial conduct.

Before committing evil, please think of your loved ones. "If I now commit adultery with someone else's wife or child, it is certain that someday a wicked person will also commit adultery with my wife or children. This is absolutely 100% certain without doubt." If thinking about this can cool one's heart, it is truly a great blessing.

- Master Ấn Quang's Instruction.

Namo Amitabha Buddha

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva

tieu_de: SHOCKING SCENES THAT THE GIRL SAW WHEN LISTENING TO THE RIGOROUS LITANY. - Translated by Hạnh Đoan
tom_tat: After practicing the Lăng Nghiêm mantra for several years, my body has undergone many unimaginable changes, and my health has also improved significantly. The purity of the mind allows me to experience a state of dharmic joy.
noi_dung:
SHOCKING SCENES SEEN BY THE LITTLE GIRL WHEN LISTENING TO THE LANGOING MANTRA. - Translated by Hạnh Đoan

After reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra for several years, my body has undergone many unimaginable changes, and my health has also improved significantly. The purity of mind allows me to enjoy a state of abundant spiritual joy, my distracting thoughts are purified, and my concentration has increased; there are so many good things that cannot be fully described.

A few years ago, I lived and worked in Saudi Arabia, a country that follows Islam and is highly discriminatory against other religions. But here, I still diligently recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra every day.

Once, I carelessly was captured by some ruffians and locked in a room, forced to pay them money, and they even threatened to kill me.

In that moment of despair, I cried and continuously chanted the name of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. Because of that, the opponents relented, they released me and let me live. This incident made me even more faithful and respectful to the Triple Gem.

One evening, on my way home from work, I passed through a deserted street in the Middle East and got hit by a car, but miraculously, I was unharmed because at that time I was walking while chanting the Lingyin mantra. When the accident happened, I had just finished chanting the Third Assembly.

Last summer, while in my homeland, my hometown experienced a heavy midnight rain, a terrifying rain so severe that everyone was too scared to sleep, fearing that this dreadful rain would bring disaster to the local residents.

I sincerely got out of bed and respectfully recited the Lăng Nghiêm mantra ten times, praying to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and heavenly protectors to shield and support me, hoping that the storm would lessen and stop. I recited the Lăng Nghiêm mantra until the seventh repetition, and the sound of the rain began to weaken. After finishing all ten repetitions, the rain stopped. Because of this, I quietly felt the miraculous and inconceivable power of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra.

Every day I diligently recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and everything around me quietly changes for the better.

Although I read the Lăng Nghiêm mantra daily, I do not understand the meaning contained within these incantations. For many practitioners who recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, if they do not clearly see the results of the mantra, they can easily lose faith and become disheartened.

However, just as Master Phổ Quang taught us, when chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, you only need to focus your mind, because every word and phrase in the Lăng Nghiêm mantra teaches us to become Buddhas, and the Lăng Nghiêm mantra has the ability to eliminate all disasters.

Now I would like to share the story of an 8-year-old girl who saw a scene while reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. In fact, for the scenes she saw, they were nothing more than flowers in a mirror, the moon in the water... But I hope that those who are just beginning to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, when reading this text and hearing what I report, will increase their faith and diligently recite the mantra. However, please do not cling to these strange visions, because the Diamond Sutra says: "All forms are illusory; if you see forms as no-forms, then you see the Tathagata"…

In July of last year, I had just attended a retreat at Chung Nam Mountain and returned home. At that time, whenever I was about to go abroad, I often visited seniors and close relatives.

When I visited my foster mother, I told her about the benefits and positive experiences of my recent Buddhist vegetarian practice. I praised the merit of reciting the Leng Yan mantra and cheerfully shared with my foster mother the good things I had witnessed and heard at the Quan Am Co Dong at Chung Nam Mountain. I also showed her a picture of Master Pho Quang.

At that time, my foster mother looked at the photo of the Master and asked with suspicion: Is it true that this Master is 115 years old? He looks so young!

I said that the Master had just left seclusion, and all his life he specialized in reciting the Lankavatara Mantra, which is why the miraculous power of the Lankavatara Mantra is beyond comprehension.

My foster mother, upon hearing this, immediately said that she also wanted to learn the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, as she was familiar with the Đại Bi mantra. However, the Lăng Nghiêm mantra was indeed too long, with many words she did not know. Since she was already 60 years old, she was concerned that learning the mantra would be difficult and exhausting. I talked with her for a while, and then she asked me to recite a few rounds of the Đại Bi and Lăng Nghiêm mantras to help create positive energy for her family.

Right afterward, I sat cross-legged on the sofa in the living room. At that time, her two grandchildren were present: a girl about 8 years old in second grade, and a boy about 5 years old attending kindergarten.

Seeing me sitting cross-legged on the sofa in their house, the children's natural curiosity arose, making them come up to me and ask questions continuously for the whole morning. The two children asked me:

- What are you doing, Mantra Ba?

I said that Mantra Ba was about to chant the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. Hearing this, my niece immediately boasted: - I know the Đại Bi mantra because I often hear my grandmother recite it. She also teaches me every morning to remember to recite “Nam mô Quan Thế Âm Bồ tát,” so that I will be intelligent and do well in school.

I felt very happy hearing my grandchildren speak. It turns out my foster mother also knows how to teach them to chant Buddha's name. Even though they are so young, knowing to chant Buddha's name early is also planting deep roots of good karma.

To ensure that while I recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, the two children would not play around and make noise, I encouraged them to sit cross-legged on the sofa, put their hands together, and quietly listen as I chanted. Although the two children did not yet understand much, they obediently followed my instructions.

First, I recited the Great Compassion Mantra seven times, and after chanting, I asked the two children if they felt anything.

The grandson said: I didn't understand anything, Mantra Ba, but my sister expressed:

- Mantra Ba! As soon as you recited the Great Compassion Mantra, I saw a Bodhisattva appear; every time you recited a line, one appeared. When you recited quickly, the Bodhisattvas appeared quickly as well, changing very fast. I also saw a Bodhisattva sitting on a large flower, holding a vase and a branch of willow.

The child didn't say what kind of flower it was, because he didn't know the name, but he seemed moved and reached out to point at the lotus flower decorated on the glass door of his house, then said: The flower looks like this.

I immediately explained: That is a lotus flower.

The little girl then said: I see the flower like this, but pink, very big and beautiful. As I listened to her description, I was silently shocked; it turns out children can see scenes that we cannot see.

At the same time, it also proves that the compassion of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas is real. Previously, I had read articles on the Internet about the Great Compassion Mantra: Recite one verse and a Bodhisattva appears… but this little girl had never read those articles, yet she described it exactly in the same way.

Hearing my grandchild speak, I was also very curious, secretly wanting to know what the child could see when I recited the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. Therefore, when reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, I focused deeply and completely followed the version of Master Phổ Quang. For example, in the First Assembly, where it talks about repaying the kindness of seven generations of mothers and fathers… and the sections in the Five Great Heart Mantras… I solemnly read them repeatedly three times. When I finished reciting, I asked my granddaughter: What did you see?

The little girl said: Mantra Ba, when you just chanted this incantation, I saw many Buddhas appearing, shaped like those worshiped in temples. There were so many, so many that I couldn't count them all, and all around them in all directions, golden light radiated. It was entirely golden aura.

When Ba Ut recited this incantation, countless Buddhas appeared in rows and layers, neatly arranged. For every three recitations, many Buddhas would appear; the more he recited, the more Buddhas appeared. They appeared surrounding him, looking like a square formation, standing solemnly and neatly. Many Buddhas sat on large lotus flowers. These flowers were white, red, purple, pink, blue, etc. Some other Buddhas rode on dragons.

In addition, there were also many dragons—golden dragons, white dragons—and many people posed on the flowers.

As soon as I heard my niece speak, I was very excited; it turned out that the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is wonderfully unpredictable. After that, I specifically recited the Five Great Heart Mantras “SẤT ĐÀ NỄ, A CA RA, MẬT RỊ TRỤ, BÁT RỊ ĐÁT RA DA, NÃNH YẾT RỊ” 21 times.

After I finished chanting the Five Great Heart Mantras, the little girl described:

When the youngest third uncle read this sentence, I saw a great Buddha seated in the center and four Buddhas surrounding him. Gradually, many Buddhas gathered around those Buddhas, and they took turns circling to form a ring that increasingly expanded outward, countless Buddhas appeared in a very orderly manner, and I could not count them.

After that, I also separately recited a few times the Lăng Nghiêm Bạch Tán mantra: "TẤT ĐÁT ĐA BÁT ĐÁT LA"

When I finished reciting, I asked the little girl what she saw?

Child respectfully says: I saw a stream of white aura, radiant and brilliant, forming a very beautiful, very large circle, very big! Inside, there were many shapes that looked like dragons, and they also emitted a very fragrant scent.

What the child described shocked me immensely. At the same time, I quietly felt the astonishing power of Master Lăng Nghiêm.

Previously, Master Phổ Quang had once given teachings about the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, mentioning 3000 Buddhas—now isn’t it already very clear?

Later, after many times of listening to the Master expound, I thought I understood very well, but it turned out that the three thousand Buddhas that Master Phổ Quang often mentioned are actually the Buddhas who, out of respect for the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, are represented by three thousand Buddhas, divided into five directions. So when we recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, it is no different from reciting the Buddhas.

When my niece described the scene that appeared while I was reciting the Five Great Heart Mantras, I understood even more clearly the words that Master Pu Guang often emphasized: Reciting the Five Great Heart Mantras is especially important. He said that the Five Great Heart Mantras are the king of the 54 great deities, a major mantra in Buddhism, the Tathagata's heart treasury, and the most important and effective spiritual mantra.

Therefore, Venerable Master Xuan Hua and Master Pu Guang repeatedly emphasized and continuously told us that:

- You must know to cherish, respect, and wholeheartedly value the Lankavatara Mantra.

Below is an important teaching from Master Phổ Quang about the Lăng Nghiêm mantra:

The Lăng Nghiêm mantra is the true syllable, the genuine word, spoken from the Great Buddha's crown of the Tathagata. This mantra has not a trace of falsehood – it is truly the true syllable, the genuine word, absolutely free from deceitful speech, not a single word of madness, capable of helping the Dharma endure in the world, being a great sacred mantra that helps the world live in harmony and the nation be peaceful. It is a sacred script between heaven and earth, a savior for all sentient beings.

The Lăng Nghiêm mantra is the arising cause of all Buddhas and the path to Buddhahood. Once this mantra is mastered, the mind can be focused without distraction, the mind will not be disturbed, and when the mind is free of even a trace of defilement, one will reach the highest state of realization. At that time, the crown of your head may emit light, your mouth radiates brightness. The whole body emits radiant light, which can eliminate all accidents, remove all suffering, destroy all sins, and you will become a Buddha.

On June 6, 2016, at Quan Âm Cổ Động, Chung Nam Mountain

(This article only represents the author's viewpoint)

tieu_de: Making a vow to memorize the Kṣitigarbha Sutra can immediately resolve karmic ties, and also help to liberate resentments toward the master body voluntarily.
tom_tat: The other day, Nhan encouraged all the brothers and sisters in the VÔ TẬN ĐĂNG Dharma Hall to make vows for all the four debts in three realms, for ancestors and family members, for past and present enemies, and for all beings in the Dharma realm.
noi_dung:
PRAYING TO MEMORIZE THE SUTRA OF KSHITI GIVES THE ABILITY TO RESOLVE ANCESTRAL CONNECTIONS AND VOLUNTARILY TRANSFORM THE REPAYMENTS OF GRUDGE ON ONESELF

The other day, Nhân encouraged all the brothers and sisters in the VÔ TẬN ĐĂNG Dharma Hall to vow to learn by heart the Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows for the sake of all four kinds of gratitude in the three realms, ancestors and relatives, past and present resentful beings, as well as all sentient beings in the Dharma realm who are suffering.

A few days later, a resentful entity (past karmic connection) from a previous life of a sister practitioner in the Dharma hall came to meet Nhân and said:

I have loved this person since a past life. During the recent Dharma assembly in Quang Tri, the Buddha sent down a lotus to guide me, but I did not go. I want that later, when this person attains rebirth in the Western Pure Land, I will go with them. I still do not want to be apart from this woman, but now this person sincerely vows to learn the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for the sake of sentient beings suffering, so I have no way to get close to that woman anymore... now I do not know what to do. I also want to be reborn now and do not want to endure suffering here for another day. I hope the teacher will help me by chanting the Buddha’s name for my sake.

Upon hearing that person speak, I rejoiced for them while chanting Buddha's name, and they also peacefully attained rebirth in the Pure Land.

That resentful person happily let go of all attachments and was no longer bound by desires, and they could also develop the Bodhi mind, all because that elder sister sincerely made a vow for the sake of her enemies and, without fear of difficulty, memorized the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, thus immediately transforming resentment. The resentful person also attained rebirth in the Pure Land right there.

And on that same day, many invisible beings came to meet me and said to me: 'Greetings, master!'

We had just escaped from hell and immediately came to see the master. It was also thanks to this woman making a vow for all four kinds of gratitude, ancestors and relatives, resentful beings and past and present debts, as well as suffering beings in the Dharma realm, and learning the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. Because of their sincere hearts and vows, and because they diligently studied the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, we were able to rely on that and escape from hell. We are all relatives of that woman from many generations.

This is a rare occurrence. The Kṣitigarbha Sutra is a sutra of gratitude, meaning it can best transform enmity. Whoever faithfully receives and practices the Kṣitigarbha Sutra will certainly never fall into the three evil realms. In all future lives, wherever they are born, they will know the true Dharma to rely on for practice, cultivating diligently and steadfastly without regression.

Those who can faithfully receive and practice the Kṣitigarbha Sutra will certainly attain an unwavering Bodhi mind and never fall into the three evil realms.

Also, because of this miraculous karmic connection, [Master] encourages all the assembly to make vows for all four debts in the three realms, for ancestors and relatives, for past and present enemies and debtors, and for all sentient beings in the Dharma realm who are suffering, to learn and memorize the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra.
