tieu_de: CHICKEN IN THE OFFERING PLATE
tom_tat: - SHOCKED WHEN LEARNING THE TRUTH BEHIND (Compiled by Diệu Âm Lệ Hiếu from the lecture of Nun Thích Nữ Như Lan)
noi_dung:
THE CHICKEN IN THE OFFERING PLATE

- SHOCKED WHEN LEARNING THE TRUTH BEHIND

(Dieu Am Le Hieu compiled from the lecture of Nun Thich Nu Nhu Lan)

This spine-chilling story was told by a nun named Dieu Thanh in Da Lat, recounting an incident that happened within her own family.

Her parents, commonly called Mr. and Mrs. Mười, had opposite personalities. Her mother was gentle and liked to go to the temple to study, following the Buddhist principle of respecting life. Her father, on the other hand, was different; he enjoyed killing animals. He had a habit of inviting friends over, then killing animals to entertain them. Her mother often advised him to eat vegetarian food and recite Buddhist prayers, but he did not listen.

Once, during summer vacation, Mr. and Mrs. Mười, along with their grandchild named Hòa, went to Vũng Tàu for a holiday. In Vũng Tàu, there was the house of a relative’s child named Bê, who called her aunt "dì".

That night, while sleeping at the hotel, Mrs. Muoi dreamed that Mr. Be came to invite the couple to his house to attend his mother's memorial anniversary. In the dream, she saw the two of them arrive at Mr. Be's house for the meal, and at that moment, Mr. Be brought out a bowl of water with a flower pattern and said:

– Aunt and uncle, rinse your mouths first and then join us at the table for the meal. Today is my mother's memorial.

Mrs. Muoi looked behind the kitchen and then said:

– What did you cook today to offer for your mother's memorial?

As soon as she looked back, she saw that Mr. Be's mother had her throat cut horizontally and had one arm cut off, and one arm was hanging from the crossbar. Mrs. Muoi just shouted in panic:

– Oh my God, why did you kill your mother to sacrifice your mother?

After speaking, she shouted in a low voice. Dream came here, because she was too scared, she woke up. When she woke up, she told her husband the whole dream:

– Grandpa, why did I have such a strange dream? I saw Be inviting our couple to a memorial meal. He brought a bowl of water with a lotus flower pattern for me to rinse my mouth. I went to the kitchen and saw his wife cutting her mother’s neck for the memorial, only one hand was left, the other hand his wife tore up for salad...

Grandpa Muoi said:

– It's just a dream, not real. Once you wake up, it'll be over, nothing to be afraid of. You always have such nonsense dreams every day.

Mrs. Muoi kept talking even though her husband didn’t listen, so she called her grandchild to tell them to relieve some stress and find an ally.

Unexpectedly, at 7 a.m. the next morning, Bé came to the hotel and said:

– Aunt Ten, Mantra Ten, today is my mother's death anniversary. I invite you to my house for the memorial meal.

Aunt Ten was startled upon hearing this, thinking how eerily similar it was to a dream. Meanwhile, the couple had just happened to go to Vung Tau for a summer vacation with their grandchild, and they had no idea it was Bé's mother's death anniversary. She immediately pulled her husband aside and said:

– There, see, didn’t I tell you, didn’t I, wasn’t my dream accurate...?

Mr. Mười turned to poke Mrs. Mười:

– Come on, you, keep your mouth shut for a bit, don’t say silly things. People are poor, it’s the day of their mother’s death anniversary. If they have the heart to invite, we should think about taking a little time to attend, otherwise if we refuse, they will feel hurt.

He turned to speak to nephew Bê:

– It’s okay, son, you can go home. Around 9-10 o’clock aunty and uncle will drop by to attend the memorial.

By more than 9 o’clock in the morning, Mr. Mười pulled Mrs. Mười to go to nephew Bê’s house, and she said:

– I'm really scared, I clearly saw that it was Mantra Be's mother's death anniversary, they killed his mother to offer her for the death anniversary. I'm really scared, I won't go anywhere, you go alone.

Mr. Muoi said:

– A dream is just a dream, it's not real, so why are you worried? Go ahead, I'm here, don't be afraid of anything.

Finally, he managed to take Mrs. Muoi along with their grandchild to visit Mantra Be's house for the death anniversary. As soon as they arrived and sat down, Mantra Be poured water into two cups:

– Kids invite aunt and uncle to have a sip of mouthwash and then come to the table to eat with us.

Looking at the cup, indeed there was a water lily printed on it. Mrs. Muoi spoke up:

– See that, I told you the other day, it's exactly like that.

Mr. Muoi nudged lightly:

– Please, keep your mouth shut for me.

Being repeatedly spoken to by her husband, she was annoyed:

– Then let me go to the back and see what they are doing to make offerings for their mother?

When she went out to the back of the kitchen, she saw hanging from the kitchen beam a chicken that had been slaughtered, only one wing remaining. The other wing had been torn apart by Mr. Be's wife to make salad. She was so scared that she shouted:

– Oh Mr. Muoi, that's right, this chicken only has one wing left. In my dream, I saw clearly that it had killed its mother and then hung by its neck on the beam, with only one wing remaining; the other wing had been torn by Be's wife to make salad. And now, it's exactly happening just like that.

She hurriedly recounted the entire situation from her dream to this young man Bê's family. As soon as he heard it, he shivered and broke into cold sweat, stopping everything, neither eating nor drinking anything at all.

He only scooped up three bowls of plain rice to offer to his mother, leaving all the chicken meat behind. From that day on, young man Bê also practiced vegetarianism and chanted Buddha's name, because he never expected that he had actually "killed his mother to offer a funeral meal to her."

Later, even Mr. Mười also made the resolution to practice vegetarianism and chant Buddha's name.

Another true story in Ho Chi Minh City, equally chilling, was recounted by nun Thích Nữ Như Lan.

MOTHER PREGNANT WITH A DUCK, KILLED BY HER CHILD

On Duong Ba Trach Street, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, around the 1970s, there was a person who specialized in selling duck porridge, named Miss Hai. Her duck porridge restaurant was very popular, known throughout the area as "Miss Hai Duck Porridge." So many customers came that in one afternoon she could sell 20 ducks.

Fearing that buying pre-prepared ducks from outside wouldn't be delicious, Miss Hai always personally went to the market to select each live duck to slaughter herself.

With many years of experience, Mrs. Hai only needed to hold a duck to know which one had more skin, which one had more fat, which one had tough meat, and which one had tender meat... Then she would take it home and personally cut each one's neck to prepare the meat.

During about 20 years of selling duck porridge in this way, the number of ducks she slaughtered was indeed a number that makes one sweat, over 140,000 ducks.

One day, after slaughtering dozens of ducks, she felt a headache, so she left the work to her children to continue, while she went inside the house to take a nap.

In the dream, she saw her mother (who had died several decades ago) come back looking for her. The astonishing thing was that her neck had been cut by someone unknown, her head was not completely severed but dangled on her neck, blood was gushing, looking very horrifying.

She angrily stepped forward to grab Hai's head, her voice low, and complained:

- I raised you to grow up, to mature... and now you cut my throat!

Hai immediately said:

- When did you slit my throat that you say such things? I'm dead, I've been dead for decades, and now you say I slit your throat? I died from illness, so why blame it on you slitting my throat?

The mother immediately grabbed her daughter's head and slammed it onto the bed, shouting:

- It's because you don't understand, so you say that. You just slit my throat, you know how much it hurt. Now that I'm back, I will take revenge on you.

At that moment, Hai jumped awake, terrified, and sat down to recall, and then remembered. Indeed, at noon, among the dozens of ducks she had killed, there was one duck that, after she had slit its throat, due to her slightly excessive force with the knife, its head was nearly severed, hanging loosely on its neck. Yet this duck did not die immediately; it struggled, managed to run a bit before finally collapsing and dying. Now, recalling it, she realizes that the duck's neck had hung just like her mother's neck in the dream.

Piecing the events together, Ms. Hai horrifyingly realized that her mother had been reincarnated as that duck, and it was her own hands, no one else's, that had cut her mother's throat.

Recognizing that this cycle of reincarnation was truly unjust and cruel, and that the karmic killing was terrifying, she subsequently quit the duck porridge business. The brand “Ms. Hai Duck Porridge” gradually faded into oblivion, but the evil karma she had caused, along with the grudges and revenge of the animals she had killed in past lives, would follow her, with no end in sight.

Master Tinh Am said in the essay Encouraging the Mind to Bodhi:

“Deceiving someone until they bleed or the tragedy of my mother

Leading the pig into the furnace, unaware of my father's suffering.”

These two lines of poetry are an exclamation from the Master based on two true stories in China. The first story:

Long ago in Nanjing, there was a family with a tradition of raising donkeys, passed down from father to son. Then the father passed away, leaving the mother and child to live in hardship. The mother raised the child until grown, then also passed away, and the child continued the tradition of raising donkeys.

After a while, the child raised a female donkey. For 18 long years, the donkey devoted all its strength to carrying loads for its owner without regard for hardship.

But when it became too old, each time it carried heavy goods to the market to sell, it was not as agile as before, so the child often used a whip to hit the donkey's back very hard to make it go faster.

Every time it was beaten like that, the donkey's eyes would stream tears in two rows. In reality, because of old age, the donkey did not have the strength to pull. The owner thought that this donkey was just lazy after eating and beat it to scare it. One day, this child dreamed of the mother who had long passed standing by the bedside saying:

– In the past, the debts of gratitude and resentment between child and mother had already been fully settled, but later, the mother stole 18 gold coins from her child, so she had to be reincarnated as a donkey to repay her child’s debt for 18 years. Do you know how much suffering your mother endured throughout those 18 years? Every time you struck the donkey with a rod, it pierced her to the bone. Even more painful was that it was her own biological child cruelly beating her, yet she could not tell you.

Now mother has paid off her debt to you. Tomorrow she will depart. Before leaving, she came to give you a dream. She advised you that from now on you should stop, do not cruelly kill animals because who knows, they might be your parents in many lifetimes. It was your own mother reincarnated, but you had no idea, yet you cruelly beat her for 18 years.

Startled awake, the child did not know what was real or not. He ran out to the donkey pen only to find that the old donkey had already died. Afterwards, he sold all the donkeys and went to become a monk.

The second story:

There was a butcher who daily led pigs to the slaughterhouse, killing at least three pigs each day. One day, he woke up late, and on his way to lead a pig to the slaughterhouse, the pig suddenly stopped and refused to move. He beat it cruelly, but the pig still would not move. A passerby happened to walk by, saw the scene, and said:

– Just leave it there, I know a way to get it to move. Then this person called out: "Ly Dau, Ly Dau! Come here!"

Immediately, the pig approached the passerby. The owner was surprised and asked:

– Do you know who Lý Đẩu is that you call it that? Lý Đẩu is the name of my late father. You are not from this area, so how do you know and call the pig by the name Lý Đẩu?

The guest said:

– Lý Đẩu is this pig, and is also your father. Because your father in the previous life killed too many living beings, now he has been reincarnated as a pig to pay for his karma.

The astonished butcher looked at the pig, tongue-tied and unable to say anything, just standing there dumbfounded. When he turned back, the guest had disappeared; it turned out that the guest was the Bodhisattva in disguise, meant to reveal causality and give guidance to the butcher.

There is an important truth that 99% of people today do not believe or know. That is, anyone, after death, will have to be reborn and transmigrate through the six realms: the realm of Heaven – the realm of Asura – the realm of humans, the realm of animals, the realm of hungry ghosts, and hell. If one has a fair amount of merit, they will be reborn as a human; less merit, they become a hungry ghost; if karma is heavy and merit is low, they are reborn as an animal, which is also normal.

And unfortunately, if one is reborn as an animal, one will not go far, but will often be reborn around close family members, friends, or those with karmic ties to oneself, such as children, relatives, friends, etc., or those to whom one owed debts that were not fully repaid during one's lifetime.

This means that the animals around us, such as dogs, cats, buffaloes, cows, chickens, ducks, etc., raised in the house, are often relatives or friends from many previous lives who had great merits and heavy karma, and thus were reborn as animals. Because of the karmic connection, they are born in our house, or in one way or another, are brought by us to be raised.

Even without raising them at home, we can go to the market to choose and buy those animals for slaughter. Due to predestined connections, we will also end up selecting animals that have karmic ties with us from previous lives. If there is no connection, we would not encounter them.

And as in the stories you have seen above, slaughtering those animals for food, for sale, for entertaining guests, or even for memorial ceremonies, is essentially killing relatives or kin from many of our past lives. This is a deeply painful truth that not everyone is aware of.

Because the vast majority of animals do not have the ability to send dreams as described in the story above. Only very few animals in past lives who had accumulated a small amount of merit are capable enough spiritually to send dreams.

For this reason, Buddhism always chooses non-violence as the first precept that every disciple must uphold. It also consistently encourages everyone to follow a vegetarian diet, in order to prevent heavy karmic consequences, to avoid the tragic cycle of revenge, and to prevent the killing among kin and family in the cycle of reincarnation.

Hopefully, in time more people will understand this and stop creating karma, give up killing, avoid spreading suffering to sentient beings, which is also for themselves.

tieu_de: DIALOGUE WITH THE GOD WHO SPECIALIZES IN RECORDING HUMAN GOOD DEEDS
tom_tat: This morning, Nhân was conversing with a deity but did not know who it was, so Nhân asked: Who are you? That deity replied: Beside the Earth God, there are the Left Officer and the Right Officer.
noi_dung:
CONVERSING WITH THE GOD WHO SPECIALIZES IN RECORDING PEOPLE'S GOOD DEEDS

This morning, Nhan discussed philosophy with a divine being but did not know who it was, so Nhan asked: Who are you?

The being replied: Beside the Earth Deity, there are the Left and Right Officers.

I am the Left Officer, specifically recording the good deeds of humans in the mortal world.

Nhan: A MI DA PHAT. Thank you for your reminder!

The Earth Deity, then, each place has a different Earth Deity, right?

Master: Yes! But we also do not consume meat, only vegetarian food, so we only accept vegetarian offerings given by the people and then distribute them to the homeless there and help people sow more merit fields.

Disciple: Is there a way to offer to sentient beings without being defiled, without being disturbed by them?

If there is, please show me so I can promote it to help sentient beings be well-nourished.

Master: What do you want to offer to the sentient beings?

Disciple: Rice, porridge, rice, salt.

As for me, many times I want to give alms but fear being influenced by bad spirits, so I don't dare to give alms.

Commentary: Offering a meal or several meals to sentient beings is not as good as offering the Dharma to them.

When you provide them with lunch, by evening they are hungry again; they will come to you and look forward to your offerings.

When this act becomes a habit, if you are busy and cannot offer, they develop feelings of resentment and avoidance, so it is better to offer the Dharma to them.

Offering rice is only a temporary method to relieve hunger.

Offering the Dharma is truly the ultimate method to help sentient beings know the Buddha, rely on the teachings of the Buddha, and from that, they repent and atone for their mistakes!

Even if they are suffering in the Avici Hell, when they understand the Dharma, repent for their karmic sins, and can recite the name of a Buddha, Bodhisattva, or Pratyekabuddha, they can immediately be freed from hell and ascend to the heavenly realms.

Moreover, because they have a connection with the Buddha due to the seeds of affinity that I sowed, they may continue to propagate the Dharma, helping others to escape suffering.

In this way, both you and they attain immeasurable merit.

Making offerings to the Dharma by: reciting Buddha's name - reading the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and dedicating the merit to all, this is the practice of the pāramitā of giving, it is great giving.

Even humans, if they are sick or hungry, it is due to past evil deeds. If we have wealth to give, we should rejoice and help; if not, we should only guide them according to circumstances to rely on the Buddha's teachings and joyfully repay their karma.

Nowadays, countless people take advantage of poverty or sickness to seek improper benefits; we, as ordinary beings, have eyes like deafness and blindness, unable to see through their minds.

Therefore, only giving the Dharma according to conditions is the great generosity, is the great merit, not fearing mistakes and not fearing truth or falsehood, right or wrong.

For example, if we have money but give it in the wrong place, and the person receiving the money does wrongful deeds, even if they descend into hell, we will not be free from consequences.

Therefore, giving the Dharma to those with affinity is not afraid of loss, not afraid of mistakes.

Namo Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Source: Layperson Do Nhan discussing with Quan Ta, recording good deeds.

tieu_de: EATING PURE VEGETARIAN MEALS ABSOLUTELY DOES NOT INCLUDE THE FIVE SPICES AND DOES NOT EAT EGGS (eggs without a yolk or not)
tom_tat: Vegetarians who recite sutras, chant mantras, or meditate on the Buddha should absolutely not use the Five Pungent Spices, which are: shallots, chives, garlic, onion shoots, pickled onions, and the coriandrum plant (the coriandrum plant also belongs to the onion family and is also included in the Five Pungent Spices).
noi_dung:
EATING PURE VEGETARIAN MEALS SHOULD ABSOLUTELY NOT CONTAIN THE FIVE SPICES AND SHOULD NOT EAT EGGS (eggs without yolk or without...

Vegetarians who chant sutras, recite mantras, or practice Buddha mindfulness should absolutely not use the Five Pungent Spices, which are: scallions, chives, garlic, shallots, onions, and asafoetida (asafoetida also belongs to the onion family and is included in the Five Pungent Spices). Eating these raw causes anger and irritability; if cooked, they arouse sexual desire. Consuming these causes good spirits, celestial beings, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas to stay away, while demons and evil spirits take the opportunity to approach.

1• In the Shurangama Sutra, the Buddha teaches that:

"Ananda! The twelve types of beings in the world cannot live on their own; they must rely on four ways of eating for nourishment, which are: eating by chewing and tearing like humans; eating by smelling the aroma like ghosts and spirits; eating by mental recollection like the beings in the Four Jhānas; and eating by consciousness like the beings in the Four Formless Realms. Therefore, the Buddha said that all beings exist by means of eating.

- Ananda! All sentient beings, if they eat sweet, they live; if they eat poison, they die. Therefore, sentient beings who seek the Three Martial Grounds should abandon the five pungent substances of the world. These five pungent substances, when cooked, arouse lust; when raw, they increase anger. Those who consume the five pungent substances, even if they understand the teachings of the twelve collections of sutras, the devas of the ten directions all avoid because of the foul smell; the demons, taking advantage of the person while they are eating the five pungent substances, lick their lips. Such a person often dwells with demons, and their merits gradually diminish, gaining no benefit.

NĀMŌ BŎN SƯ THÍCH CA MÂU NI PHẬT

2• Quoted in the second letter responding to layperson La Trí Thanh (An Quang Dharma Master's Collected Letters, Volume 1), Great Master An Quang (the 13th Patriarch of the Pure Conduct School, who is the incarnation of Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva) recorded that:

“Vegetarians should not eat chicken eggs because they contain life potential. Even if they do not have life potential, they still should not be eaten because they contain toxins. Some people say, 'In places without hens, eggs will not contain life potential,' but in this place, such eggs are very rare. In the past, there was a person who liked eating chicken eggs; over time, the toxins accumulated in his stomach, producing many eggs and chicks. Traditional healers did not understand this illness. Truong Trong Canh said that if you eat garlic, you will immediately vomit out many chicks along with chickens that already had feathers.”Don't be foolish. Mr. Truong told the patient to never eat chicken eggs again for life; if they eat them, there will be no way to treat it. It's enough to know that chicken eggs cause great calamity!

Considering, the disciples of the Phước Châu Buddhist temple who eat vegetarian food often fear nutritional deficiency, so the monastery has the saying "eggs without yolk, none of these sprouts can be eaten," which has become a customary practice, causing confusion for those who do not understand and almost crossing boundaries. Therefore, the disciples earnestly request the master to explain this article. It should be widely published to alert others. Disciple La Tri Thanh respectfully records this note.

3• Or quoted in Lá Thư Tịnh Độ in response to layperson Chân Tịnh, Master Ấn Quang wrote: “Can chicken eggs be eaten or not? The debate has been carried out thoroughly for a long time! But those who truly understand the principle never think that eating chicken eggs is right. Those who like to eat cleverly argue, but in fact, they enjoy folly! Why is that? Some say that eggs with embryos, meaning they have a living germ, cannot be eaten, but eggs without embryos that cannot hatch into chicks can be eaten! If said this way, then living creatures would never be able to be eaten.So when an animal dies, it can be eaten, maybe that’s right? Intelligent people often point out that ant, not knowing it is just satisfying their appetite while wasting their own intellect, to the point of being pitied by those who understand the reasoning! Monk Chi Dao Lam, during his lifetime, was well-educated, skillful in reasoning and debating with his teacher about whether eggs could be eaten or not; because he was good at refuting arguments, the teacher couldn’t make Dao Lam concede. That teacher has passed away, appearing in front of him, holding a chicken egg and smashing it on the ground, the chick.quickly crawled out. Dao Lam shyly expressed his gratitude, the monk and the chicken egg both disappeared. That was the decisive word of the Tang era.”

4• Venerable Thuyen Hoa was a senior monk of the modern era (1918 – 1995). He was considered an incarnation of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva and also had taught: “Do you think that being vegetarian means you can eat eggs too? Yes, you can! But wait until you are reborn as a chicken; then you will understand that being a chicken is exactly because of eating eggs.” Here is an excerpt from Venerable Thuyen Hoa's response when a Buddhist disciple asked about this:

Question: As a Buddhist disciple, is it permissible to eat eggs?

Answer: "If you want to eat those nutritious things, then why do you need to ask me?"

Question: Why can't vegetarians eat eggs?

Answer: “There is no such thing as a male chicken, yet a female chicken can still incubate eggs that hatch into chicks as usual. In the past, people did not understand this, so they said that if an egg has no male chicken inside, it cannot hatch into a chick. However, this way of talking has no evidence. Why do people reason like this about eating eggs? That is because they want to eat the egg. Regardless of whether an egg has a male chicken or not, it can still produce a chick; it is not that it cannot. In the Lankavatara Sutra it says 'Noan duy tưởng sanh,' meaning that eggsimagination that is born.

• (Digression: If you eat vegetarian for health, for healing, or because you are tired of salty food, then whether you want to eat eggs or not is up to you.

However, if you are like me – a Buddhist disciple, we are all mere mundane beings full of worries and karma, so we should strictly follow the teachings and instructions of our Patriarchs; we should eat vegetarian and definitely should not eat eggs.)

NAM MÔ A DI ĐÀ PHẬT

Namo Shakyamuni Buddha

tieu_de: RITUAL - REPENTANCE FOR ENEMIES AND OPPOSERS
tom_tat: The souls of the deceased always exist around us. Unlike the living, spirits are often hungry, sad, and suffering for many reasons, such as having a mind still attached to something.
noi_dung:
RITUAL - REPENTANCE TO AVENGE WRONGED ENEMIES

The spirits of the deceased always exist around us. Unlike the living, spirits often suffer from hunger, despair, and misery for many reasons, such as because their minds are still attached to something in the mortal world, longing for possessions, wives and children, relatives… unable to let go, while others are due to hatred toward someone they have not yet avenged, and it is very difficult for them to free themselves from these attachments. Therefore, there are spirits that have wandered for hundreds, even thousands of years, unable to be liberated or reincarnate anywhere, simply because they could not let go ofcling in the heart.

Among them, the most terrifying are the spirits of wronged enemies. They are the souls of humans, animals, and even demons, who in this life and countless past lives have held deep grudges against us. Sometimes they were animals that we captured and killed for food, sometimes they were humans whom we beat, tortured, robbed, deceived, or killed…. At times, they are fetuses destroyed by their parents… creating countless tangled grudges and resentments.

When the wronged spirits find the person who harmed them, what naturally happens is that they will follow and seek revenge. So how do they take revenge?

Spirits have a certain amount of supernatural power, whether a lot or a little. And they are also very intelligent, coming up with many ways to take revenge. Many methods, such as causing us to become ill, severe cases like cancer, mild cases like aches and pains, all kinds of diseases. Or causing family turmoil, arguments, tormenting each other. Or "ghosts lead the way, spirits guide the path" causing us to fail in business, and they might even push us, deceive our vision while we are driving, causing accidents, injuries, or even death, etc...

Not all disasters and suffering in life are caused by grudges from spirits, because many times they are simply the result of Karma causing pain, with no presence of any ghost. However, the revenge of grudging spirits causing illness and disasters also accounts for a very large proportion; in essence, this too is a kind of karmic retribution and does not lie outside of Cause and Effect.

So how can one dissolve the resentment of those hostile spirits and wronged masters? Only by repentance and compensating for mistakes by dedicating merits to them. Until they are willing to let go, we can only be free. And that is the purpose of the "Ritual of Repentance for Hostile Spirits and Wronged Masters."

Many people have recovered quickly after repenting to the hostile spirits and wronged masters. It's simple: the illness was caused by them (the hostile spirits); now that they are willing to let go, the illness will disappear. Some people who are very unlucky will also find their misfortune vanish just by repenting to the hostile spirits and wronged masters.

Quang Tử had a friend, she complained about why, despite practicing all the disciplines, bowing to Buddha very often, offering alms, and releasing animals... her life was still difficult and she could never get a job. Quang Tử immediately sent her the ritual text "Ritual to Repent for Hostile Spirits and Grievance Holders," and she practiced it right away. She performed the ritual on Monday, and by Friday she got a very good job.

There is another female friend of Quang Tu, who often went to the temple together. She faced various problems in life: unexplained illnesses, unstable mental state, constant marital conflicts and arguments, and a life so miserable that at times she even thought about suicide.

After Quang Tu introduced her to the "Rite of Confession for Resolving Grievances from Past Karma," she offered it continuously for 21 days, once a day (actually, it didn't have to be continuous like that). Indeed, after that, everything changed clearly and quickly. Her health and mental state stabilized. The family became more peaceful, and life seemed to turn a new page.

This is nothing strange, like when we are riding a bicycle on the road, and the wheel gets caught by a plastic bag or debris, stopping it completely. At this moment, no matter how hard we pedal, the bike just stays in one place. But as soon as we get off and remove the debris from the wheel, the bike runs normally again.

Honestly, anyone present in this world, most always have vengeful spirits of those they have wronged following them for revenge. Most people have killed this animal or that animal, and even if they haven't killed directly, they have consumed the flesh or blood of many lives, thus creating karmic debt.

But if someone insists that they have been completely innocent since childhood, there are always many wronged spirits from many past lives who come seeking them.

Like Ngộ Đạt Quốc Sư – the person who compiled the famous book Compassionate Water Repentance. In a past life, he had falsely harmed someone, causing that person to die unjustly, executed by a horizontal beheading. That spirit followed Ngộ Đạt Quốc Sư for 10 consecutive lifetimes without being able to take revenge, because during all 10 lifetimes, Ngộ Đạt Quốc Sư diligently practiced cultivation, and the Dharma protectors guarded him closely, preventing any approach.

By the 10th life, when he had reached the position of National Preceptor, because he had become prideful, the Dharma Protector left, and the vengeful spirit took the opportunity to enter him, causing him to suffer from a terrible disease: a boil in the shape of a human face on his knee. In modern terms, it would be malignant cancer, extremely painful and incurable by all royal physicians.

So, if even a highly virtuous monk like Ngộ Đạt Quốc Sư, who has completed 10 lifetimes of proper cultivation, can still be wronged by enemies seeking revenge, then ordinary people like us should not think that we have no enemies at all. It’s just that the time for them to take revenge has not yet come. And if you have understood the purpose of this Ritual, please proceed to the content of the Ritual of Repentance to Enemies.

THINGS TO NOTE BEFORE CONDUCTING THE RITUAL OF SUPPLICATION FOR THE DEPARTED

1. LOCATION

"Repentance Ritual – Praying for Redemption of Ancestral Spirits and Hostile Ghosts" can be conducted right in the house of the person who needs to repent, and that is the best place, because the hostile spirits are already there, and it is easy for them to receive the repentance and be liberated.

If it is not convenient, we can, depending on the circumstances, find another place, such as a relative's house, or a quiet place where no one will disturb.

As for temples, shrines, and even Martyrs' cemeteries, there are usually Dharma Protector deities, and sometimes spirits are allowed in, sometimes they cannot enter. If choosing to organize at a temple, it is best to get the approval of the abbot and ask the Dharma Protector to allow the spirits to enter.

As for organizing at home, if there is a Buddha altar in the house, we proceed in front of the Buddha altar (preparing offerings for restless spirits or for unborn children on a separate table, placed to the left or right of the Buddha altar).

If not, then we arrange a clean place (including the bedroom) where no one or nothing will disturb the ceremony.

2. TIME

The best time to conduct it is in the evening, when the sun has set, as spirits can easily attend the ceremony. Even during the day, some spirits can still move around, but not all spirits can do so.

In the seventh month, spirits from the Underworld are free to move to the living world, so performing rituals for salvation in the seventh month draws the most spirits to attend the ceremony.

On other ordinary days of the year, it is still possible to perform the liberation rites without being particular about choosing any specific day. Doing good deeds, any day is a good day. Doing bad deeds, any day is a bad day. Depending on the circumstances, we just arrange to perform them on whichever day is convenient.

3. NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS

Everyone can organize the Ritual of Repenting to Grievances, whether at home or in a monastic setting, whether Buddhist or not. If possible, inviting more people to support in chanting would be ideal; if not, one can completely carry it out alone.

In repenting to grievances, oneself—the "person who needs to repent"—is the most important. Because every grievance has a beginning, and every debt has an owner, the sincere repentance of the one at fault is what the spirits most want to hear—it is the key factor that makes aggrieved spirits, as well as unborn souls, agree to forgive, let go of hatred, and accept prayers for liberation.

4. THINGS TO PREPARE

When we prepare the offering tray, regardless of the ritual, we must use vegetarian items and must not offer meat, fish, salty foods, or alcohol... It is not necessary to have an elaborate tray or lots of offerings, nor is paper money required, because the sound of chanting sutras and reciting Buddha's name is infinitely more precious than all worldly offerings.

This is something that psychic Nguyen Van Nha, along with a series of famous psychics in Vietnam, all witnessed at Truong Son Cemetery. At that time, psychic Nguyen Van Nha stood in the middle of the cemetery, clasped his hands respectfully, and chanted “Nam Mo A Di Da Phat” 108 times, and immediately the spirits of the martyrs, regardless of whether they had a religion in life or not, all clasped their hands and sincerely chanted along.

And the spirits of the martyrs responded to Mr. Nguyen Van Nha and the psychics present there that it is precisely the chanting of sutras and Buddha’s name that is the most precious thing that the living can send to them.

Therefore, the amount of offerings can be more or less depending on the host's intention; there is no need to be overly meticulous. If there are limited conditions, a few fruits, some cakes, a bit of porridge, a glass of water, and an incense stick… are sufficient.

In any case, during the ceremony, we will recite the miraculous mantras of the Buddhas such as the Transformation of Food Mantra, the Amrita Mantra, the As-You-Wish Precious Wheel King Mantra, which have the power to invisibly multiply the offerings, ensuring that all are abundantly fulfilled.

During the Ritual, if there are bells or gongs, that is good, but it is also okay if there are none. If it is possible to kneel throughout the session, that is very good, but if not, changing to a standing or sitting position is also acceptable.

In the Rituals, the words in parentheses (…) are instructions; we do not read them, only pay attention to following those instructions correctly. However, in some circumstances where it is not possible to follow them, it is permissible to skip them flexibly, without being rigid.

Form is merely a supporting factor, while the core element that determines the success of a memorial ceremony is sincerity. That is why many people spend a lot of money inviting shamans, monks, and priests to perform extravagant, extremely costly memorial rituals, burning gold paper to the sky, yet feel little spiritual response and see no changes in their lives. This is because the spiritual realm values sincerity above form.

A shaman who comes only for money, no matter how professional they may appear, will have a heart full of greed, selfishness, and self-interest... how could there be sincerity for the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to bless? How could there be the power to help the deceased attain salvation? It is better for the host to prepare a simple vegetarian offering themselves, praying for the deceased with sincerity, which is a thousand times more effective.

In "Ritual of Confession – Praying for the Salvation of Aggrieved Spirits and Deceased Adversaries," sincerity is truly being remorseful and regretful for the wrongdoings and sins one has caused to aggrieved spirits, deceased adversaries, and aborted fetuses.

Reading each repentance sentence makes the heart feel anguish, shame, wanting to express an apology from the bottom of the heart, to the point that some people have to burst into tears, wanting to make amends for them, help them attain liberation, be reborn in the Pure Land, that is sincerity.

While reading teachings or scriptures, focus your mind on understanding the meaning, following the principles therein to inspire your intentions. While chanting mantras, it is not necessary to understand their meaning (because the meaning of mantras—dhāraṇīs such as the Great Compassion Mantra, the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Wheel King Mantra, the Rebirth Mantra… ordinary people cannot comprehend), but it is enough to strongly believe in the miraculous power of the sounds of those mantras transforming the spirits in the unseen realm.

While reciting the Buddha's name, the mouth recites, the mind arises with reverence for the Buddha, the eyes do not see, but the mind always envisions, as if invisibly, Amitabha Buddha along with the Bodhisattvas appear according to one’s heartfelt recitation to welcome the souls of the departed to rebirth; that is true sincerity.

When the heart is sincere, there will be a response. Even if the offering tray is simple, without bells or gongs, without chanting… if the mind earnestly recites, it still has the powerful effect of relieving suffering and granting joy, far surpassing elaborate external ceremonies with an empty heart.

REPENTANCE WITH ENEMIES AND OPPOSERS

(Only the officiant recites)

From endless past ages until now, due to my ignorance and foolishness, not understanding the Dharma, being deluded and not following the words of the Buddha, lacking conscience, through my body, speech, and mind, I have sown so much pain and suffering, horror upon you, causing you to hold resentment reaching the sky; the guilt is truly infinitely deserving of death. (1 prostration)

Or for one's own meal, the meal of relatives, of guests, etc., mercilessly taking the lives of you, or instructing others to kill, or paying for someone to kill, or buying to eat, etc., without caring about your suffering, or that of your relatives. Now that I know the Dharma, I am extremely ashamed, sincerely repent, and before the sacred Triple Gem, I bow my head to apologize to you. (1 prostration)

Or out of malice, wolfish heart, cruel tactics, torture and beatings, torment in many ways, causing you either physical pain, or mental anguish, or unjust death, etc... without thinking about your suffering, or that of your relatives. Now that I know the Way, I am extremely ashamed, sincerely repent, and before the sacred Triple Gem, I bow my head to apologize to you. (1 prostration)

Or using scheming and sinister tricks, deceit and fraud, treachery and untrustworthiness, wizardry and sorcery, poisonous drugs and anesthetics, machinery and other means… sophisticated tactics, diverse methods that harm you by causing loss of property, loss of honor, loss of family, loss of chastity… even leading to death in resentment, without thinking of your pain, or of your family's pain. Nowadays, having known the Path, I am extremely ashamed, sincerely repentant, and remorseful, and before the sacred Triple Gem, I bow my head to ask forgiveness from you. (1 prostration)

Or being cold and indifferent, unfaithful in love and loyalty, treacherous to those who were kind, severing familial bonds, causing your hearts to break, harming your body and mind, generating immense resentment, driving you to either unwillingly face death, suffer from depression and illness, or take your own life, etc., without considering your pain, or that of your relatives. Now that I know the Dharma, I am extremely ashamed, sincerely repentant, and humbly apologize before the sacred Triple Gem, asking to bow my head in atonement to you. (1 prostration)

Or relying on power, influence, money, or strength, forming cliques, partisan factions, using the strong to oppress the weak, acting arbitrarily and recklessly, etc., causing you to lose property, honor, family, chastity, virtue, etc., even your life in anger, without considering your pain or that of your relatives. Now that I know the Way, I am extremely ashamed, sincerely repentant, and remorseful, before the sacred Triple Gem, I kowtow to apologize to you. (1 kowtow)

Whether accidentally, intentionally, directly doing it yourself, indirectly standing behind, inciting, instructing, or merely guiding, crafting... creating conditions that cause others to act, or encouraging, enjoying when others act, or heedlessly neglecting, etc., in every possible way, in this life or previous lives, causing you to lose your wealth, your honor, your family, your chastity and virtue, etc., even leading to death in anger, with body and mind in suffering, grief, resentment to the bone, unconcerned about your pain or that of your family. Today, having known the Way, I am extremely ashamed, sincerely repentant, and remorseful, towardBefore the sacred Three Jewels, I bow my head to apologize to you. (1 prostration)

Dear wronged and offended spirits, the sins I have committed against you are countless, and my words cannot convey it, my regrets are meaningless compared to the suffering you have endured. But I ask you to open your hearts with tolerance and forgive the foolish sins I have caused you, because "grudges should be untied, not bound." Holding onto hatred, seeking revenge... will not bring you any benefit, but only increase your torment. Accumulated resentment can easily lead you to fall into paths of suffering, unable to transcend to a peaceful realm.

Today I respectfully request (asking the assembly) to recite sutras and chant the Buddha's name, dedicating the merit to pray for everyone to eliminate karmic obstacles, let go of resentment, have peace of body and mind, cultivate the Bodhi mind, and rely on the Buddha's power to be reborn in the Pure Land, forever escaping all the suffering of this world.

Thus, I invite all hostile spirits and wrongdoers, together with the assembly, to chant aloud the Great Compassion Mantra of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, which has the power to eliminate karmic obstacles, bringing peace and comfort to body and mind, and distancing from all suffering.

GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA

(Chant at least 7 times)

Namo Great Compassion Assembly of Supreme Buddha Bodhisattvas (3 times).

Thousand Hands Thousand Eyes, Unimpeded Great Compassion Heart Dharani.

Namo Hā rā dā nā da rā dā da.

Namo ā rì dā bà lu yè dì, shù bā rá dā, bodhi tà duó bà dá, ma hā tà duó bà dá, ma hā kā lu ní kā dá. Ān tà bàn rá phạt duệ, shù dá nā dá zuò.

Namo tất kiết lì duó, y mòng ā rì dā, bà lu kiết dì, thất Buddha rá lăng dá bà.

Namo Naracandri Heri, Maha Banda Samé, Tat Bha Atadu Du Bang, A The Dung, Tat Bha Tat Da, Nama Baji, Ma Phat Dat Dau, Dat Diet Tha. GENERAL REPENTANCE

(Excerpted from the Sutra of Golden Light, Chapter on Eliminating Karmic Obstacles – Shakyamuni Buddha illustrates the method of repentance)

“…I respectfully and devotedly surrender to the Buddhas of the present in all ten directions, those who have attained Supreme Buddhahood, turning the wheel of the wondrous Dharma, the radiant Dharma wheel, showering the Great Dharma, sounding the Great Dharma drum, blowing the Great Dharma conch, erecting the Great Dharma banner, holding the Great Dharma torch, for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings, always practicing the giving of Dharma, teaching those who are deluded to advance, enabling them to attain great fruition, and always be happy.

O World Honored Ones, like that, I prostrate with body, speech, and mind to pay homage and respectfully venerate. O World Honored Ones, like that, with true wisdom, true eyes, true realization, true equality, you know everything, see everything, the wholesome and unwholesome actions of sentient beings.

From beginningless time until now, I have followed the river of sin and, together with sentient beings, created karmic obstacles, bound by greed, anger, and ignorance. When I did not know the Buddha, when I did not know the Dharma, when I did not know the Sangha, when I did not know good and evil, I committed through body, speech, and mind the five grave offenses: it is evil intention that caused the Buddha’s body to bleed, slandered the Buddha and Dharma, disrupted the harmony of the Sangha, harmed the Arhats, and harmed my father and mother.

A child with three bodily evils (killing, stealing, sexual misconduct), four verbal evils (lying, exaggerating, double-tongued speech, harsh speech), and three mental evils (greed, hatred, delusion) commits ten unwholesome actions by doing them oneself, instructing others to do them, or rejoicing when seeing others do them.

For the virtuous, the child is arrogantly slandering; for measuring tools, he is deceitful; he calls evil good, gives bad food to others; towards parents of many generations in the six paths, the child causes harm; towards the wealth of the Stupa, of the monks in the four directions, or of the present monks, the child steals, freely uses it; towards the precepts and teachings of the Blessed One, the child does not wish to observe or practice them, does not comply with the instructions of the master, and when seeing anyone following the vehicle of the Śrāvaka, the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddha, or the vehicle of the Mahāyāna, he insults and disrupts them.

When seeing someone better than myself, I immediately feel jealous; concerning giving Dharma or wealth, I regret it, letting ignorance obscure me, being confused by wrong views, I do not cultivate wholesome deeds but instead increase unwholesome deeds. I even slander the Buddhas, calling what is Dharma not Dharma, and what is not Dharma as Dharma, etc...

With so many offenses, the Buddhas, with true wisdom, true eyes, true realization, and true equality, know everything and see everything, so today I sincerely take refuge and pay homage. Before the Buddhas, I do not dare to hide anything.

For sins not yet committed, I dare not commit them; for sins already committed, I sincerely repent. The karmic obstacles that lead to the six realms and eight sufferings which I have caused, and the karmic obstacles I am currently causing, I vow to eliminate completely. I vow that in the future, I will not have to bear the retribution of these karmic obstacles.

Just as the great Bodhisattvas of the past, who practiced the path of Bodhi, have repented all karmic obstacles, so too with my karmic obstacles, today I sincerely repent of them all. I reveal everything, daring not to hide anything. For sins already committed, I vow to eliminate them; for sins not yet committed, I vow to dare not commit them again.

Just like the future Great Bodhisattvas who practice the Bodhi path, all karmic obstacles are confessed; my karmic obstacles are the same, today I sincerely confess them all. I reveal everything, not daring to hide anything. The sins I have committed, I vow to eradicate entirely; the sins I have not committed, I vow not to commit them anymore.

Just like the present Great Bodhisattvas who practice the Bodhi path, all karmic obstacles have been confessed; my karmic obstacles are the same, today I sincerely confess them all. I reveal everything, not daring to hide anything. The sins I have committed, I vow to eradicate entirely; the sins I have not committed, I vow not to commit them anymore…”

Those who wish to be born into that world only need to wholeheartedly and continuously recite "Namo Amitabha Buddha!" and vow to be born into the Western Pure Land. When their human life ends, the Great Compassionate Amitabha Buddha will manifest to receive them into His world.

My body is flesh and blood, my lifespan is not yet finished, I cannot yet see Amitabha Buddha, but you are a metaphysical being; as long as you sincerely recite "Namo Amitabha Buddha" and wish to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, you will immediately see Amitabha Buddha radiating light to welcome you.

tieu_de: Basically, there are 7 disparities in the world
tom_tat: 1. LIFESPAN - Short lifespan is due to:
noi_dung:
Basically, there are 7 inequalities in the world

1. LIFESPAN

- A short lifespan is due to:

Oppressing others to death, killing living beings, trading, imprisoning people and animals

- A long lifespan is due to:

Loving all beings, releasing lives to save people and animals, living a pure life to accumulate merit.

2. ILLNESSES

- A body with many illnesses is due to:

Harming sentient beings, not helping the sick and suffering, becoming wealthy from the illnesses of others

- Having a body with few illnesses is due to:

Living a moderate life, not harming people and animals, providing medicine to the sick and suffering.

3. APPEARANCE

- Having an ugly body shape or appearance is due to: often feeling anger and having conflicts with others; covering up or blocking the light of the Buddha's teachings from reaching people; laughing at the unattractive appearance of others.

- A graceful and beautiful body and appearance are due to: often cultivating patience and gentleness; practicing and creating images of the Buddhas; giving food to others.

4. AUTHORITY TOWARDS OTHERS:

- Not having authority over others is due to: feeling jealousy and envy towards others' possessions; not often accumulating merit.

- Having authority over others is due to: not harboring jealousy or envy towards others; always maintaining sincerity and not deceiving people.

5. NOBLE OR LOWLY STATUS:

- Being born into a lowly status, despised by others, is due to: arrogance, insulting others; owing money or property to others without repaying; despising or not respecting religious practitioners and saints.

- Being born into a noble status, respected by others, is due to: assisting others in achieving success, rejoicing in the success of others, knowing how to respect and serve the Triple Gem; regularly striving to do good deeds; treating everyone with humility and kindness.

6. POSSESSION OF WEALTH

- Suffering from extreme poverty is due to: being miserly, stingy, not practicing the virtue of giving; stealing, robbing, or deceiving others' property.

- Enjoying wealth and prosperity is due to: often having a kind heart and giving to others; rejoicing in the good deeds of others and not owing anything to anyone.

7. GOOD AND BAD KNOWLEDGE

- Evil, wrong knowledge is due to: associating with evil people; praising, glorifying bad and evil conduct; being dishonest, not sharing, not teaching the Dharma to others.

- Noble and virtuous knowledge is obtained by: regularly cultivating right wisdom, associating with ascetics, receiving and practicing the True Dharma.

REFLECTION:

- In this world, everything has its cause; do not think that things happen naturally as they are. Merit, sin, beauty, ugliness, wealth, poverty, success, and failure all originate from the arising of the mind.

A wise person often observes each arising thought and intention to take control of their own life and future karma.

A foolish person acts without thinking, following instincts regardless of consequences, and when the retribution ripens... 'there is no escaping fate.' Seeing the evil retribution they face today, we feel pity for them, but looking at the causes they once sowed, we can only sigh. Once retribution ripens, even heaven cannot save them. It's regrettable that previously, when others advised avoiding evil and doing good, they ignored it and paid no attention.

Nhu Thi

Namo Buddhaya

tieu_de: THE USE OF WEARING A MYSTIC AMULET
tom_tat: Author: Tưởng Quả Quân Hạnh Đoan abridged translation
noi_dung:
THE BENEFITS OF WEARING A LAM ENGRAVED CHARM

Author: Tuong Qua Quan

Briefly translated by Hanh Doan

I see in the Lingyan Sutra a description of the power of the Lingyan Mantra when we wear it on our person. In the Buddhist sutras, it is clearly stated:

If we wear the mantra on our body or hang it on the wall of the house, thanks to the protection of the mantra, all harmful things cannot harm us throughout our lives.

IF ONE RESPECTFULLY recites, or respectfully transcribes, carries on their person, or worships in the village, homestead, or residence... the accumulated karmic obstacles from many lifetimes will melt away like snow meeting boiling water. With karmic obstacles eliminated and right concentration present, before long, one will attain the Dharma of Non-Arising.

If one has committed the Five Offenses, thanks to the power of the mantra, all serious sins will also be destroyed. One will not be harmed by all kinds of demons and ghosts, including enemies, unexpected disasters, old karmic debts, misfortunes, debts from past lives until now, etc. One will also gain immunity to vegetables contaminated with pesticides, various viruses, and so on.

The clearest proof is that after I continuously and devotedly practiced the mantra, my body became healthier than before, I no longer caught colds, and I felt calm and at ease.

Unfortunately, I have to write concisely, so I cannot recount all the details thoroughly. If you want to know everything clearly, you should refer to the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, where you will understand the full, extraordinary superiority of this.

Since I have understood many wonderful and precious things about this "king mantra," that morning, I copied the mantra to hang it on the walls inside the house as well as in the yard, to further enhance protection and peace. I also had my family members wear the mantra and felt great benefits. At all times, the mind feels firm, fearless, and is no longer anxious as before.

Recalling the time before practicing mantra, I always felt anxious, panicked, and restless. Now I realize that: It is not only by sitting in meditation that one attains calm, BUT THE BUDDHA'S TRANQUILITY IS EXACTLY IN WALKING, STANDING, LYING DOWN, AND SITTING… ALWAYS IN STILLNESS, GREAT STILLNESS, and THE MEDITATIVE POWER INHERENT IN THE LANKAVATARAVYUH SUTRA is truly profound and supremely victorious!

The Lankavatara Sutra says: “WHETHER READING, OR CHANTING, OR COPYING, OR WEARING, OR KEEPING, ALL FORMS OF OFFERINGS WILL NOT BE BORN IN POVERTY, LOWLINESS, OR UNEASE.”

I remember the day of my father's funeral, I photocopied the hand-copied "Chú Lăng Nghiêm" for the family to wear. At the funeral home, they also gave each guest a talisman drawn on red paper. My youngest sister, in her rush, could not find the pouch for my hand-copied "Chú Lăng Nghiêm," so she just wore the talisman provided by the funeral home.

Unexpectedly, after returning home from the crematorium, my sister could not get out of bed the next morning, as her whole body ached, she had headaches, back pain...

At that time, I thought that all you needed was to take a nap and you would get better, but unexpectedly, by the third day of sleeping, your illness became increasingly severe.

I felt something strange, so I took the Lăng Nghiêm Charm I was wearing and put it on my younger sibling. Unexpectedly, beyond my imagination, they immediately felt better and could sit up! Later, I found a place that printed a tiny, very exquisite Lăng Nghiêm Charm, so I brought it home and offered it to my sibling in exchange (because this printed version of the Lăng Nghiêm Charm was compact and lightweight, much more convenient than my handwritten version which was several thick, heavy pages and very inconvenient), but they firmly refused to exchange it; I had to explain to them that the contents were exactly the same before they felt comfortable exchanging it, which shows how much they trusted the charm they were already wearing!

In March 1985, my eldest daughter went to South Africa for a tour with her friends, visiting many famous scenic spots, and when she returned home it was already late at night.

I was sleeping when she woke me up to tell me: She had dreamed of many frightening scenes, so terrified that she couldn't continue sleeping.

I said: Why aren't you wearing the Ling Nghiêm amulet on your neck?

So I hurried to search, fortunately there was one left, and I immediately put it on my daughter.

My child went back to their room and then slept peacefully until morning, no longer seeking me out, as if they were completely safe and unharmed.

In early October 1986, after my youngest daughter witnessed the death of a white person in the church next to the school, she felt dizzy when she returned home… feeling very strange inside.

I investigated and found out it was because she was not wearing the Zen Lăng pendant. She said: The school has rules that prohibit wearing jewelry such as necklaces or anything else...

So I used a safety pin to attach the Lăng Nghiêm Talisman inside my child's collar. As soon as he wore it, he felt a cool and soothing sensation in his head, his whole body felt comfortable again, and now my youngest child absolutely does not dare to forget to wear it anymore.

In April 1984, my eldest son fell seriously ill. For three months, he had a high fever of 41 degrees. I wrote the Lăng Nghiêm Talisman by hand for him, but since his mind was heavily obstructed, he firmly refused to wear it. I had no choice but to respect his wishes, as it was not right to force him to wear it.

By July 1984, my son passed away. I continuously recited the sacred name of Amitabha Buddha, and after he had been gone for about nine hours, his whole body was completely cold, yet his head remained warm, while his forehead, just a little distance away, was as cold as ice; to have such a difference so close together was astonishing. His face still bore a hint of a smile, showing a calm and auspicious expression.

This is my family's experience of reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and I would like to share it. I hope everyone can uphold the Buddhist scriptures, sow the seeds of becoming a Buddha – practice the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra and the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, cultivate perfectly, and soon attain Buddhahood!

PERMISSION TO QUOTE ACCOMPANYING TEXT ANSWERING QUESTIONS ABOUT WEARING THE MANTRA:

Question: I am currently wearing the Lăng Nghiêm mantra on me. I heard some people say that when wearing this mantra, you must take it off before entering the toilet or bathroom. But others say that you only need to take it off when taking a bath, while you can keep it on when using the toilet. Please help me clarify this issue - QUẢNG PHÚ

Answer: Dear Quảng Phú!

Currently, Buddhists often wear the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, which is folded small and encased in hard plastic, commonly in two forms: one is the full text of all five sections of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and the other is the phrase “Nam-mô Đại Phật đảnh ma-ha-tất-đát-đa-bát-đát-ra” (image), which is the essence or the pinnacle of the five sections of this mantra.

We think that the advice to remove the talisman when taking a bath is simply to avoid it getting wet or soaked (because the talisman is laminated, so it is not very durable). As for the recommendation to remove the talisman when entering the restroom, this is due to the fear that the sacred text (or Buddha statue) may become 'defiled,' which would be disrespectful to the Triple Gem.

As followers of Buddha, respecting the Three Jewels is essential. However, having to remove a mantra (or Buddha statue) from oneself every time one goes to the toilet is truly inconvenient, and almost no one can practice it perfectly in daily life. Moreover, upon calm observation, it is unnecessary to wait until entering the toilet to be “impure,” because wearing a mantra on the body is considered “impure” regardless of how clean one is, since the Buddha taught that the body is a leather bag containing impure objects inside.

Therefore, I think that, unless one with an evil mind intentionally defiles the mantra and the Buddha statue, one will not incur a sin. In daily life, with the spirit of skillful means, a Buddhist can wear the mantra and Buddha statue on their person at all times and in all places.

Master Quang Tanh

Wishing you diligence!

Source: Nguyen Tuy Minh

The method of writing the mantra you can see here. Here: https://m.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=2053286991470348&id=1641986395933745

tieu_de: VENERABLE PHO QUANG TEACHES ABOUT VENERABLE LANG NGHIEM
tom_tat: Recently, thanks to the translation by Venerable Hanh Doan, many friends have come to know Master Pho Quang (in China), and from that point on, have also practiced the Lingyan Mantra more. Currently on Facebook, the post d
noi_dung:
Venerable Pho Quang Teaching About Master Lang Nghiem

Recently, thanks to the translation by Nun Hanh Doan, many people have come to know about Elder Master Pho Quang (in China), and from that, have also practiced the Lankavatara Mantra more.

Currently on Facebook, the translation about Elder Master Pho Quang contains the following main contents:

1. Talks about His life biography.

2. Talks about the Five Major Heart Mantras in the Lankavatara Mantra.

3. Talks about the short mantras for repaying the kindness of one's parents for seven generations.

You all should take the effort to search for the keyword "Phổ Quang Hòa Thượng" to read, because here Lam will translate more about Him, so the previous content will not be repeated. When there is more time, it will be translated or rewritten for you later.

By reading about His biography, you will know how formidable the Elder Venerable is.

This article contains the teachings of Elder Venerable Phổ Quang on practicing the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra.

The photos you see with light in them are lit naturally using a camera. All of these images are naturally taken without editing.

Below are some short teachings of Venerable Master Phổ Quang on the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra:

1. When you recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, the energy field of your body will change. The more you recite, the more the pure energy increases and the impure energy decreases, transforming your body into another form - described as a crystal-like body.

2. If you chant once, the Buddha and Bodhisattvas will focus their minds on you and grant you all merits (this is mentioned in the Surangama Sutra about the Tathagatas from the ten directions granting merits to those who chant the Surangama Mantra).

3. People with weak energy fields should diligently chant the Surangama Mantra, and you will see changes.

4. The magnetic field on high mountains is very good because it is close to the Universe, close to the Heavenly realms, and close to all four directions. The magnetic field there flows down directly, and humans easily harmonize with nature.

5. The meditation halls on the mountains are very good. Wherever there has been an accomplished spiritual practitioner, the energy field there is extremely strong.

6. The light of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas is gentle, very pleasant, giving a comfortable and relieved feeling to the soul, similar to the feeling of a child who has been lost and hungry for many years finally being rescued by their biological mother.

Spirits and souls illuminated by the light of the Buddha immediately change their appearance - becoming tall, with a bright and beautiful complexion, and may even sit on a lotus throne.

The Buddha said in the Lankavatara Sutra that the Lankavatara mantra has extremely transcendent effects, extraordinary and incomparable. The Lankavatara mantra is entirely the light of the Buddha, a perfect form of light, because this light illuminates by itself, and the light emanates from the crown of each Buddha, called "Buddha Crown Light Accumulation." Therefore, the more it is chanted, the more beneficial it is for all sentient beings.

Therefore, saying that chanting the Lankavatara Mantra causes fear or drives away spirits is not correct. [You can chant the Lankavatara Mantra for liberation.]

7. Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra without missing a single word, thirty-six thousand times (36,000), a lotus will appear beneath your body. When you walk, there will truly be lotuses supporting you in the air.

8. Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra thirty-six thousand times not only saves your parents of seven generations, but also includes parents from many other lifetimes.

9. At the end of life, if the Shurangama Mantra is too long to recite completely, it is enough to recite the six syllables "Tàt Da Ta, Bát Da La" (悉怛多钵怛啰 - Xī dá duō bō dá luō). The entire Shurangama Mantra contains several special mantra verses within it, among which is the verse "Tàt Da Ta, Bát Da La"; this is the name of the Buddha Shakyamuni, also known as "Great White Umbrella" (The Large White Umbrella), representing a diligent mind covered by a great umbrella, and supreme skill.

If you do not have time (when near death), keep these six words and the five main Mantras of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra (Sattada Ne, A Ca Ra, Mat Ri Tru, Bat Ri Dac Ra Da, Nanh Yet Ri).

10. Be sure to start with "Great Buddha Lăng Nghiêm Mantra", otherwise you are reciting the Mantra without a beginning.

(Here it is only written this way without explanation; according to the translator's view (Lam), one needs to recite "Namo Lăng Nghiêm Hội Thượng Phật Bồ Tát" and "Namo Đại Phật Đảnh Thủ Lăng Nghiêm Thần Chú" each three times before chanting the mantra, so that it will be complete).

11. Eating eggs is more sinful than eating meat, because eggs represent an entire life. Precepts are very useful for the Mantra verses.

(In this teaching, it means that if you can practice vegetarianism, it is better than not being vegetarian, and if you are strictly vegan without eggs, it is better than being vegetarian but still eating eggs. And practicing any Dharma—especially reciting the Bright Mantra—requires keeping the precepts).

12. Reciting "Xá Kê Dã Mẫu Na Duệ" is to repay the kindness of mothers in seven generations. Reciting "Lặc Đát Na Kê Đô Ra Xà Da" is to repay the kindness of fathers in seven generations.

Translated and edited by Lam Son Trang,

01/04/2021

tieu_de: The daughter sincerely chants solemn mantras, repents on behalf of her mother to eliminate the insane karmic grudges.
tom_tat: Ms. Muổi has a mother named Sâm who suddenly developed a mental illness. She is very small and skinny, but whenever she has a fit of madness, her strength is unimaginable; she can suddenly lift a very heavy wooden cupboard that holds dishes.
noi_dung:
A DAUGHTER SINCERELY CHANTS TO THE RELICS, REPENTS FOR HER MOTHER TO ELIMINATE CRAZY KARMIC GRUDGES

Muổi's mother, named Sâm, suddenly went crazy. She was very small and skinny, but whenever she had a fit of madness, her strength was unimaginable. She could lift a heavy wooden cabinet for dishes, and even the neighbor's three-wheeled cart placed against the fence, Mrs. Sâm could lift it as well.

The neighbors guessed that Mrs. Sâm had been possessed by a spirit, so they invited some shamans to perform rituals for her, but it didn't help; in fact, Mrs. Sâm's condition kept getting worse.

In the summer, Mrs. Sam often yelled, talked to herself incoherently, tore her own clothes, wandered away from home with her hair messy, and her family had to tie her up in the house.

Neighbors advised taking Mrs. Sam to the city's mental hospital for treatment.

Ms. Muỏi also quit her job and took Mrs. Sâm to the city's mental hospital for a check-up. The doctor prescribed medicine for the family to buy, but after nearly two years, Mrs. Sâm's condition still did not improve. Ms. Muỏi's family was very sad and distressed. Whoever suggested a method, they tried to follow, hoping their mother would be cured of insanity.

Then someone in the village told Ms. Muỏi that there was an elderly monk named Tịnh Thông, at a rural temple in the South, who could cure mental illness, neurological diseases, spirit possession, and ghost attachment...

Ms. Muoi asked for leave, packed her belongings, and brought her mother to this temple.

After a difficult journey and a long road, Ms. Muoi's mother and daughter also found the temple. Meeting the monk Ching Tong as they have pointed out, after listening to Ms. Muoi explain her mother's illness, the monk Ching Thong pondered, he said that he had no magic or power, he could only instruct Ms. Muoi and her family to read the Mausoleum, the Dharma Sutra and other sutras every day, read the Repentance and dedicate to Ms. Sam's name, age, address, and hometown. Ms. Muoi agreed to follow the teacher's instructions, because she didn't know what else to do.

Monk Tinh Thong arranged for Muoi's mother and child to stay in a small room in the temple, behind the bamboo garden.

Every day, Venerable Tinh Thong and a young disciple guide Muoi's mother and child to the main hall, respectfully light incense in front of the Ksitigarbha statue made of beautiful sandstone, and look at the statue with joy. Every early morning, they recite the Leng Yan mantra, read one chapter of the Lotus Sutra each morning, and in the afternoon, they recite the Compassionate Water Repentance. They bow to the great names of the Buddhas, recite the Ten Thousand Buddhas Sutra, recite the Leng Yan mantra once more in the afternoon, and recite this mantra again in the evening. In other words, they recite the Leng Yan mantra three times a day.

Almost Ms. Muoi sincerely followed the monk's instructions, while Mrs. Sam had a blank, lifeless expression.

Every day, the mother and daughter ate vegetarian meals at the temple.

On the ninth day, suddenly Mrs. Sam cried loudly and violently, saying: "I am Mrs. Y, who died 7 years ago, and I have a grave buried near the village road.

Every day, when Mrs. Sam went to the market past the grave, she would point to my image on the tomb and tease the other women in the village coming back from the market: 'This lady looked beautiful, but it was such a waste that she died.'

Then occasionally, Mrs. Sâm would get tired on the way back from the market and even sit to rest on my grave, but her attitude was not respectful, seemingly mocking, and sometimes after eating snacks she had just bought at the market, Mrs. Sâm would even push the garbage around my grave. So I (Mrs. Y) entered Mrs. Sâm to make her go insane."

Master Tinh Thong calmly and gently spoke to Mrs. Y's spirit: "You also don't be angry or punish Mrs. Sam anymore; she is pitiful, and you would also accumulate more sins. Now Mrs. Sam has realized her mistakes and sincerely repented. You also have had the chance to hear Buddhist scriptures, the Buddha's mantras, and by learning from the Buddha you can attain liberation, and in future lives, become a disciple of the Buddha."

As soon as Master Tinh Thong finished speaking, Mrs. Sam fell to the floor of the main hall. After a while, Mrs. Sam regained consciousness, sighed with fatigue, then clasped her hands to bow to the master and asked to become his disciple.

Mother and daughter Muoi thank monk Tinh Thong for helping their family overcome suffering and promise to offer a Buddha statue to this temple, along with the sutras that the temple needs.

Mother and daughter Muoi also resolve to follow a vegetarian diet and vow to recite the Lang Nghiem mantra, read the Lotus Sutra, and pay homage to the Buddha's holy name every day at home. Meanwhile, monk Tinh Thong gives mother and daughter Muoi a beautiful and glossy Ksitigarbha statue made of green cypress wood, about 25 cm tall, so that the family can worship the statue daily.

Since then, Ms. Muổi went back and told the neighbors in the village and invited them to diligently read scriptures, recite mantras, chant the Buddha's name, and read confessions to escape suffering.

Collected.

Source: Lee Phan

tieu_de: The Great Freedom Dharani Mantra of Instantly Attaining Whatever One Wishes
tom_tat: --- The Great Mantra in Sanskrit is Mahā-Pratisāra-Vidya-Dhāraṇī
noi_dung:
The Dharani Mantra of Great Freedom, Instantly Accomplishing Whatever is Desired

--- The Great Mantra's Sanskrit name is Mahā-Pratisāra-Vidya-Dhāraṇī --- The Great Wish-fulfilling Bodhisattva's Sanskrit name is Mahā-Pratisāraḥ, phonetically rendered as Ma Ha Bát La Để Tát Lạc, that is, the Great Wish-fulfilling Bodhisattva, briefly called the Wish-fulfilling Bodhisattva.

He is an Incarnation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and is a Deity in the Avalokiteshvara Institute within the Garbha-Dhātu-Maṇḍala of Tantric Buddhism. Because this Deity has very profound Vows, he often fulfills the wishes of sentient beings, eliminates uninterrupted sins, averts disasters from water, fire, weapons, poison, grants rain or stops storms, bestows children, and facilitates rebirth in the Pure Land, he is therefore named the Great Fulfiller of Wishes and is a Bodhisattva worshipped in the faith during the Latter Days of the Law.

---

The Da La Ni Mantra was compiled by the Master by combining 8 Mantras into one sentence and transmitted to disciples as follows:

OṂ _ VAJRA PARAŚŪ PĀŚA KHAḌGA CAKRA TRIŚŪLA CINTÀMAṆI MAHĀ-VIDYA-DHĀRAṆI SVĀHĀ

In addition, the Canon also records another Mantra of the Great Wish-Fulfilling Bodhisattva as:

OṂ _ MAṆI-DHĀRI VAJRIṆI MAHĀ-PRATISĀRI SVĀHĀ

or

OṂ _ MAṆI-DHĀRI VAJRIṆI MAHĀ-PRATISĀRE HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ

or specifically the full eight Mudras and Mantras are as follows:

1. OṂ VAJRĀYA SVĀHĀ (Five Ancient Vajra Words)

2. OṂ PRAŚŪ SVĀHĀ (Vietnamese Cover)

3. OṂ PĀŚA SVĀHĀ (Seduction - Auspicious Knot)

4. OṂ KHAḌGA SVĀHĀ (Treasure Sword)

5. OṂ CAKRA SVĀHĀ (Dharma Wheel)

6. OṂ TRIŚŪLA SVĀHĀ (Three Ancient Rakes - Vajra Trident)

7. OṂ CINTĀMAṆI SVĀHĀ (Wish-fulfilling Jewel)

8. OṂ MAHĀ-VIDYA-DHĀRAṆI SVĀHĀ (Ruang Sanskrit Scripture - Sanskrit Dharani)

---

These eight sacred mantras represent the Wisdom. The eighth seal (Sanskrit Dharani Seal) harmonizes the Five Wisdoms of the Two Vehicles. All Buddhas of the Dharmakāya use the Five Wisdoms as a foundation. The Five Wisdoms of the Two Vehicles combined represent a Great Dharmadhātu, within which all eighty thousand Dharmas are encompassed.

---

The Buddha said in the Sutra of 'Immediately Attaining Great Freedom Upon Request Dharani Mantra' that the merit of this Great Request Bodhisattva Mantra is recorded as follows:

This Great Request is the Great Freedom Dharani Mantra that grants all beings the highest happiness, protecting them from all Yakshas, Rakshasas, mental illnesses, hungry ghosts, Tsaqgyan ghosts, and harmful spirits; also safeguarding them from ailments caused by heat and cold.

The dwelling place is always auspicious, free from invasions stemming from war and enmity, and able to shatter enemies; malicious spells and curses cannot harm. Past karmic sins are eradicated, poisons cannot harm, fire cannot burn, swords cannot injure, water cannot drown, and one is protected from lightning, evil winds, and storm damage.

If someone upholds this Mantra, their residence is often favorable. If one can write down the Mantra and then wear it around the neck or tie it on the arm, that person will often achieve all supreme pure deeds. They are usually supported by the Devas and Dragon Kings. Furthermore, they are protected by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Vajra Secret Seal, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Indra, the Great Brahma King, the Tiṇṇa Gods, the Great Freedom Heavenly, the Kumbhāla Lords, Tīna Dāka, the Great Black Deva, Nandī Kāśyapa Deva, etc., day and night often follow to support the one who upholds this mantra.

If this Mantra is worn on the body or hands, the Ghost Child Parent, Thần Ma Ni Bạt Đà, Lực Thiên, Đại Lực Thiên, Thần Thắng Khí Ni, Thần Câu Tra Đàn Để, Công Đức Thiên, Đại Biện Thiên, etc., will always accompany and support.

If any woman practices this Mantra, she will have great power and often give birth to noble children. During pregnancy, the fetus will be safe and stable; during childbirth, she will be happy, without diseases, all sins will be eliminated, and there will be no doubt.

Due to the power of virtue and blessings, wealth and grain will increase. Words spoken that are believed by others will often receive respect in all matters, so one must remain pure and calm. If any man or woman, young or old, recites this mantra, they will experience peace, be free from illness, have all sins eradicated, possess beautiful and healthy appearance, achieve complete auspiciousness, and have their virtue and blessings increased.

The person who wears this amulet, even before entering the altar, will immediately achieve fulfillment. One who has entered all altars, sharing merit with those who have entered the altars, will not suffer from nightmares, and heavy sins will be eliminated. If someone harbors ill intentions towards them, they will not be able to harm the person who recites this amulet. All desires and pleasures wished for will be accomplished.

--

Compiled by Tam Dang. Ancestor Hue Dang from Song Lam Huong Tich -
