*Because sentient beings revolve in samsara for many lifetimes, creating impure karma many times, purification will occur many times. Even if one experiences blessings, one should not become arrogant or self-satisfied. One must continue to diligently practice, and regard it as praise from the Triple Gem, encouraging practice so that one has more faith on the path of learning Buddhism.

*As the Esoteric Buddhism texts also say, "Now there are monks and Confucian scholars who briefly study meditation principles, and upon seeing those signs, consider them strange. This not only disparages the supreme vehicle teachings, but also offends wrong views, discards forms, and clings to essence; yet they do not realize that those forms originally are the essence."

Source: Compiled.

tieu_de: WHY ONE SHOULD TAKE REFUGE IN Kṣitigarbha BODHISATTVA
tom_tat: 1. The Twelfth Chapter of the Sutra of Kṣitigarbha states: Anyone who sincerely takes refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will, from this lifetime onward, never again fall into the three paths (Hell, Hungry Ghosts, and Animals) because they are protected by Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.
noi_dung:
WHY ONE SHOULD TAKE REFUGE IN BODHISATTVA KṢITI GARBHA

1. The 12th chapter of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra states: Any person who sincerely takes refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will, from this life onward, never again fall into the three realms (hell, hungry ghosts, and animals) because they are protected by Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.

2. In the 2nd chapter of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, Shakyamuni Buddha advised: "Sentient beings only need to create merit as small as the weight of a hair or a single strand of hair, and Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will save them. How much more so for those who have taken refuge in Kṣitigarbha—how could they fall into the three evil paths?"

May he guide me so that I can hear and encounter many good things, thereby developing diligence in practice according to the Buddha's teachings, doing good and avoiding evil.

3. If our chanting of the Buddha's name does not yet have sufficient affinity to be reborn in the Pure Land, then now taking refuge in Kṣitigarbha, we will be guided by him for lifetimes, never falling into the three lower realms, because we have the practice of offering to Kṣitigarbha.

4. Practicing and receiving blessings from Kṣitigarbha, the path of study and cultivation will not be obstructed, karmic hindrances will be swiftly eradicated, no more obstacles will remain, and necessities such as food and clothing will be sufficient, family members will be safe, … all will be protected by him.

+ If you want to be reborn in the Pure Land, He will help us to be single-minded and undisturbed in order to attain rebirth.

+ If you want to quickly attain enlightenment, He will help you quickly attain enlightenment.

+ If you are pulled by predestined karma, He will take your life for you so that you can practice with peace of mind.

+ Falling into evil paths? He will rescue you.

That is why Buddhas of the ten directions particularly love Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, and liken Him to a very precious Mani jewel (only one in existence) among the Buddhas of the ten directions.

5. The Sutra of Kṣitigarbha, Chapter 6: Demons and spirits are very delighted with those who sincerely practice the teachings; with just a single thought of reverence toward the Dharma, they will protect that person. Most demons and spirits are disciples of Kṣitigarbha and are very numerous. If one takes refuge in him, makes offerings, and respects him, protective deities will follow and guard them. And Kṣitigarbha will appoint beings in that area to bless us.

6. Benefits of Taking Refuge in Kṣitigarbha

As taught in the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, the benefits are inconceivable when hearing the name, contemplating, bowing to, praising, and offering to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. And the benefits of taking refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha are even more inconceivable, as it can greatly change your life. There are many stories where, thanks to their ancestors taking refuge in Him, descendants were saved from calamities. Therefore, if one sincerely makes a vow, the benefits are beyond words.

7. How to take refuge:

Read the content of taking refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha at:

√ Every day, face south and remember to think of Bodhisattva making vows (should not skip any day)

√ In front of the statue or image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva

√ Before reading or copying the Sutra, look at His image

tieu_de: PIERCING MEAT INTO THE BODHISATTVA'S MOUTH, RECEIVED RETRIBUTION AND DIED IMMEDIATELY
tom_tat: Mocking the Dharma early leads to misfortune in Māgama
noi_dung:
PICKING UP MEAT AND STUFFING IT INTO A BODHISATTVA'S MOUTH, GETTING THE CONSEQUENCE OF DYING IMMEDIATELY

EARLY MOCKERY OF BUDDHISM BRINGS MISFORTUNE

In Ma city

there were two people who had passed the civil service exam, one fully

believed in Buddha, while the other mocked and blasphemed. One day, both

were reading books in the hall of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, when suddenly a

person brought dog meat to offer. The one who believed in Buddha immediately waved his hand, telling

them to go elsewhere, not to enter the hall, and hastily ran away to avoid

went outside the door.

The Buddhist layman saw this and immediately said: "I follow the teachings of

Confucianism, I do not know anything about Buddhism or Taoism

at all." Then he climbed up the high platform, mocking as he tried to feed meat into

the Bodhisattva's mouth. But just as he lifted the chopsticks, he felt a force

pushing on him through the air, causing him

to fall to the ground and die immediately.

A moment later, the graduate who had stayed outside the door also collapsed

and died. At that moment, he saw the person who blasphemed Buddha

undergoing hundreds of types of punishments, wearing a red-hot collar around his neck,

and his entire body being scorched by fierce flames.

Yama, the King of Hell, said to the believer: “You have faith, so you shouldn’t have come to this place. I brought you here

to let you witness that person suffering torment, so that you

"to tell people so they can know." Having said this, he ordered to return to the living world, and he immediately came back to life.

COMMENTARY

The Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, in this Saha world, has made the great vow: "If there is a sentient being who has not yet been liberated, I consider it as if I have pushed them into a pit myself."

When the World Honored One was preaching in the Deva Heaven of the Tāvatiṃsa, he

praising Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, saying: "Even if the Buddhas of the ten directions were to praise his merits, a thousand myriad kalpas would not exhaust them." The Buddha further taught: "Suppose there are sentient beings in the heavenly realms who have exhausted all their merits, showing the five signs of decline, about to fall into the evil realms such as hell, hungry ghosts, or animal births; if they are able to see the image of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha

then wholeheartedly admire and worship, one can avoid falling into suffering

and even gain more blessings in the heavenly realms.

The Buddha also taught: "If there are beings who devote themselves

sincerely to worship Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, without faltering throughout their life,

then in future lives they will often be born

in the heavenly realms, enjoying happiness and blessings. When the heavenly blessings

are exhausted, and they are born among humans, for hundreds of thousands of eons they will still

become a sovereign king.

Alas, the Great Sage possesses unimaginable divine power,

his name shakes countless worlds, his awe-inspiring aura

encompasses myriad heavens, all beings who hear

his name or see his form are blessed with unparalleled fortune, yet a mundane, ignorant, filthy person, with

shallow and petty understanding, dares to slander him, as if taking the light

A firefly in the morning compared to the blazing sun, using a fly's wing

to cover the entire sky, really not knowing one's own limits!

tieu_de: WHY INDIA IS SUFFERING DISASTERS LIKE TODAY
tom_tat: 📖 According to the news reported on An ninh thủ đô, the religious ceremony lasts for 2 days on November 28 and 29 every year, taking place at the Gadhimai goddess temple in Bariyarpur, Nepal, near the Indian border. By offering sacrifices
noi_dung:
WHY INDIA HAS DISASTERS LIKE TODAY

📖 According to news reported by An ninh thủ đô, the religious ritual lasts for 2 days, on November 28 and 29 every year, taking place at the Gadhimai Goddess Temple in Bariyarpur, Nepal, near the Indian border. By sacrificing thousands of buffaloes, pigeons, and goats, devotees believe that the Goddess Gadhimai will bring strength, luck, and prosperity to the people.

The festival begins at dawn on the first day with a ritual called “Pancha bali”, which involves killing 5 animals: a mouse, a goat, a rooster, a pig, and a pigeon.

Next, more than 200 professional slaughterers will use knives to chop off the heads of the animals confined on a large piece of land. About 6,000 buffaloes and nearly 100,000 goats and poultry, such as pigeons and chickens, were killed as offerings to the Goddess on the first day, November 28. More than 100,000 other animals will also be slaughtered when the festival ends on November 29.

The heads of the animals will be buried in a large pit as an offering to the Goddess, while the skins will be sold to pre-contracted traders. At the 2009 festival, 300,000 animals were slaughtered, while in 2014, the number rose to 500,000.

———————————————

“All along in a single bowl of soup

Resentment as deep as the sea, hatred as high as the mountains

Wanting to know the origins of weaponry

Listen to the slaughterhouse’s scream in the quiet night.”

One might wonder why India suffers such calamities today. The Buddha taught that accidents, epidemics, and warfare all arise from killing and eating meat. If one wants to eliminate misfortune, nothing is better than vegetarianism and releasing life to resolve profound enmity with sentient beings.

No matter who you are or which country you come from, please eat vegetarian to save the Earth, or in other words, to save yourself. Stop the acts of killing for sacrificial meat offerings, as they completely go against the principle of reverence for life in heaven and earth.

Namo Amitabha Buddha 🙏🙇

tieu_de: DEMON KING MAKES A VOW OF GOOD DEEDS
tom_tat: 🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿 At that time, the Evil Poison Demon King joined his hands respectfully and said to the Buddha:
noi_dung:
KING OF DEMONS MAKES ALTRUISTIC VOWS

🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿

At that time, the Evil Poison Demon King clasped his hands respectfully and addressed the Buddha:

"Respectful World-Honored One! We are a large number of demon kings in the realm of Yama, some of us benefit others, and some harm others; each one is different from the other.

But because of karmic retribution, our relatives pass through the world, doing much evil and little good. Passing by someone's yard, or a town, village, garden, or house, if there is a young man or woman who can accumulate a little merit, even by a hair or a strand of hair, by hanging a ceremonial fan, a valuable item, offering a little incense, a little flower to the Buddha statue or Bodhisattva statue, or by reciting the sutras, burning incense while making offerings with a verse, a line of scripture, etc.

We, the ghost kings, respectfully perform the rituals for that person as if reverently worshiping the Buddhas of the past, present, and future.

We transmit to the lesser demons with great power and those responsible for the land, that they must assist in guarding and not allow any evil acts or sudden illnesses, or any disasters, even up to matters that are displeasing near the households of these people, let alone entering their homes.

The Buddha praised the king of demons, saying: "Wonderful! Excellent! You, together with King Yama, can support good men and good women in this way! I also command the heavenly king Brahma and Indra to protect you!"

🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿

Excerpt: Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Fundamental Vows, Chapter 8.

🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱

🍁🍁🍁Diệu Nhi also has a small true story like this to share with everyone🍁🍁🍁

Last year, Ms. Diệu An’s household had a sister-in-law who was about to give birth. In the family, only Ms. Diệu An knew how to practice, so she personally bought fish to release and also advised the soon-to-be parents of her sister-in-law to contribute a few dozen coins so that she and Diệu Nhi could carry out the release of the fish.

The two sisters went releasing animals for several days in a row, then one day, about 2 or 3 days before the birth. The younger brother, Diệu An (that is, the husband of the woman giving birth), continuously dreamed of Táo Công (wearing an official's robe and a winged hat like in the movie about Guan Yu) standing in front of the couple's room.

My younger brother found it strange, so he asked me. He didn't know what phenomenon it was. Diệu Nhi then remembered that in the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, there is a passage that roughly says: "During childbirth, countless kinds of demons and spirits that crave blood come seeking to harm the mother and the baby. The local earth deity does everything to help keep the mother and baby safe. Therefore, performing good deeds and avoiding evil brings benefit to both mother and child. However, if during childbirth, the family gathers to kill living beings for food, play music with bamboo flutes, the mother and the baby will both suffer harm."

Here, the family of the younger sibling, thanks to the fortunate elder Diệu An performing charitable deeds on their behalf and dedicating the merit, made the Land Deity extremely joyful, manifesting to protect them, and also allowing the family members to see this, in order to increase their faith and diligence without turning back. This shows that practicing according to the teachings of the Sutra truly brings immense benefit. YOU SHOULD NOT UNDERESTIMATE IT.

🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱

Feel free to copy and share.

Source: elder Diệu Nhi

THE INCOMPARABLE BENEFITS OF REVERING BODHISATTVA KŚITIŚVARA

tieu_de: Reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva brings immeasurable merit
tom_tat: Reciting the name of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha brings immeasurable and boundless merit. Any sentient being, regardless of suffering or calamity, only needs to sincerely recite: Namo Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. He will, according to his vow, silently assist.
noi_dung:
Reciting the Title of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha Brings Infinite Merit

Reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva brings immeasurable and boundless merits.

Ordinary beings, no matter what suffering they encounter, only need to sincerely recite: Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. He will, according to His vow, silently help them be relieved from suffering and find peace.

In the Diamond Samadhi Sutra, Chapter Eight on General Maintenance, the Buddha further extensively explained to the assembly the merits of upholding the sutra and reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva:

This Bodhisattva is inconceivable, always saving sentient beings from suffering out of great compassion. If there are sentient beings who recite this sutra or the name of this Bodhisattva, they will not fall into evil paths, and all obstacles will be completely eliminated. If there are sentient beings who recite this sutra without any other distracting thoughts, focusing solely on this sutra and practicing according to the proper method; then at that time, the Bodhisattva will constantly manifest to teach the Dharma and support that person without ever abandoning them; enabling those people to swiftly attain Supreme Perfect Enlightenment. You Bodhisattvas, if you wish to teach sentient beings, should all instruct them to practice the Mahayana in this definite, enlightening manner.

MERIT OF RECITING THE NAME OF BODHISATTVA KĪLĀNĀTHA

Therefore, in the Mahāyāna Mahāsaṃgraha Kṣitigarbha Ten Cycles Sutra (translated by Xuanzang), the Buddha compares: Sincerely taking refuge, calling the name, reciting, worshiping, and offering to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha Mahāthāta to request one's wishes is the most superior. The sutra records:

“Suppose someone, over a hundred lifetimes, sincerely takes refuge, recites names, chants, performs rituals, and makes offerings to figures such as Maitreya, Wonderful Auspiciousness, Avalokiteshvara, Samantabhadra… who are the leaders of the great Mahasattva Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, to fulfill their wishes; It is not equal to a person who, within the time of a single meal, sincerely takes refuge, recites names, chants, performs rituals, and makes offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva to fulfill their wishes and quickly achieve complete fulfillment.”

Why is that so? Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha benefits and brings peace to all sentient beings, enabling the wishes of sentient beings to be fulfilled. He is like a Cintamani gem, and also like a treasure. Such a Great Being, in order to perfect sentient beings, has long practiced great vows and great compassion, being firm, courageous, and diligent more than other Bodhisattvas. Therefore, you should make offerings to him.

19 GREAT BENEFITS OF RECITING THE NAME OF BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA

In the Thừa Ðại Tập Ðịa Tạng Thập Luân Sutra, the Buddha teaches: “If anyone sincerely calls the name, recites, pays respect, and makes offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-sattva, they will obtain various benefits and peace.” The Sutra teaches:

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 1

“Anywhere, if sentient beings desire something, are beset by suffering and hardship, and can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay homage, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-sattva; then all their wishes will be fulfilled according to the Dharma, and they will be freed from suffering. Depending on their aptitude, the Bodhisattva will guide them toward rebirth in the heavens or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 2

Anywhere, if sentient beings are suffering from hunger and thirst and can sincerely recite the name, chant, show reverence, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahāśāstra; then all wishes will be fulfilled according to the Dharma, and food will be abundant. Depending on their aptitude and suitability, the Bodhisattva will place them on the path to rebirth in Heaven or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 3

Anywhere, if sentient beings lack clothing, precious ornaments, medicine, bedding, and necessary items; they can sincerely call upon the name, recite, show reverence, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, and all their wishes will be fulfilled in accordance with the Dharma: clothing, precious ornaments, medicine, bedding, and necessary items will be entirely sufficient. Depending on their aptitude and suitability, the Bodhisattva will place them on the path to rebirth in the heavens or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 4

Anywhere, if sentient beings who love each other are separated, even if there is hatred, they still must be together; One can sincerely declare the name, recite, pay homage, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-Sattva; Then all will be united in love, and hatred and separation will end. Depending on [their capacity to accept], the Bodhisattva will place them safely on the path to being reborn in Heaven or Nirvana.

The benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 5

Anywhere, if sentient beings experience physical and mental suffering; if they can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay respect, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva; then all will attain peace of body and mind, and be free from all illnesses. Depending on their capacity and suitability, the Bodhisattva will guide them on the path to rebirth in Heaven or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 6

Anywhere, if sentient beings oppose each other, causing conflicts; if they can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay respects, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; then all can abandon harmful thoughts, harmonize with one another, endure joyfully, develop mutual shame, and treat each other with a compassionate mind. According to their appropriate capacities, the Bodhisattva will guide them onto the path toward Heaven or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 7

Anywhere, if sentient beings are imprisoned, shackled, and bound with chains, enduring all kinds of suffering; if they can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay respects, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva; then all will be liberated, the prison, shackles, and chains will be gone, and they will be at peace and free. Depending on their aptitude and suitability, the Bodhisattva will guide them on the path to be reborn in Heaven or to Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 8

Anywhere, if sentient beings are supposed to be imprisoned, beaten, interrogated, or about to be harmed; if they can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay respects, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-sattva; then all will be spared from imprisonment, beating, and harm. According to their aptitude and disposition, the Bodhisattva will place them on the path to rebirth in Heaven or Nirvana.

The benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 9

Anywhere, if sentient beings are physically and mentally fatigued, with weak energy; if they can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay respect, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-Sattva; then all will gain physical and mental comfort, and their energy will be robust. Depending on the aptitudes and dispositions, the Bodhisattva will guide them either on the path to becoming a Deva or to Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 10

Anywhere, if sentient beings' faculties are insufficient, if any faculty is impaired; if they can sincerely recite, chant, pay homage, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, all faculties will be fulfilled and not impaired. Depending on the individual's affinity, the Bodhisattva will place them on the path to rebirth in the heavens or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 11

Anywhere, if sentient beings are frenzied in their minds, disturbed by demons and spirits, if they sincerely call upon the name, recite, pay respect, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-Sattva, all will have calm minds, free from afflictions. Depending on their individual aptitudes, the Bodhisattva will guide them to be born in the heavenly realms or to Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 12

Anywhere, if sentient beings are afflicted by desire, anger, ignorance, resentment, stinginess, jealousy, arrogance, pride, wrong views, laziness, recklessness, delusion, etc., all of them will be disturbed, with their body and mind in turmoil, often not at peace or happy. If one can sincerely call the name, recite, pay respects, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, all desires and anger, etc., will be dispelled, and the body and mind will be at peace and joyful. Depending on individual capacities and dispositions, the Bodhisattva will guide them towards rebirth in the heavens or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 13

Anywhere, if sentient beings are burned by fire, submerged by water, swept away by wind; or fall, tumble from mountains, cliffs, edges, trees, houses, in terror. If they can sincerely recite the name, chant, show reverence, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, all dangers will be avoided, they will be safe, and unharmed. Depending on their capacity and affinity, the Bodhisattva will guide them safely on the path to rebirth in the heavens or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 14

Anywhere, if sentient beings are bitten by poisonous snakes or venomous insects, or struck by any kind of poison, if they sincerely recite the name, chant, show reverence, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, they will be freed from all afflictions. According to their aptitude and predisposition, the Bodhisattva will guide them either to rebirth in the heavenly realms or to Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 15

Anywhere, if sentient beings are possessed by demons, it will lead to various illnesses, so they will fall sick every day; or they may get sick every other day, or only once every three or four days; or the demon causes the person to go mad, their body and mind trembling, bewildered, completely losing awareness and knowing nothing. If one can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay respect, and make offerings to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha Mahā Bodhisattva, all of these will be liberated without fear, and the body and mind will be at peace and happy. Depending on the individual's capacity and affinity, the Bodhisattva will guide them safely on the path to being born in Heaven or to Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha: 16

Anywhere, if sentient beings are attacked by Yakshas, Rakshasas, hungry ghosts; Pisachas, Vetalas, Pishachas, Yaksas; spirits that drain vital energy, and beasts like tigers, wolves, lions, vicious beasts, serpents; various sorceries, malevolent spirits, war formations, and other fearsome things causing distress; with body and mind startled, fearing for life, clinging to life, hating suffering and seeking pleasure... If they can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay homage, and make offerings to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha Mahāsattva; then all fears will be dispelled, and their lives preserved. According to their aptitude and responsiveness, the Bodhisattva will establish them on the path to rebirth in the heavens or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 17

Anywhere, if sentient beings act because of love of learning, or because of pure faith; Or because of pure precepts, or because of pure reflection, or because of supernatural powers, or because of Prajñā; Or because of liberation, or because of beauty, or because of a pleasant voice; Or because of fragrance, or because of delicious taste, or because of gentle feelings; Or because of gain and nourishment, or because of fame, or because of virtue, or because of skill; Or because of fruits, or because of forests, or because of beds and seats, or because of mats; Or because of roads, or because of money, rice, or medicines; Or because of houses, or because of servants, or because of colors; Or because of beneficial rain, or because of water for irrigation, or because of crops...

Whether for a fan, a whisk, or for cool breezes, or to request fire; Whether for vehicles, or for children, or for means, or for cultivating merit; Whether for warmth, or for coolness, or for remembrance, or for worldly or transcendental benefits; In the process of seeking these things, if one is pressed by severe suffering, one can sincerely call the name, recite, show reverence, and offer to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. By virtue of merit and the miraculous, powerful concentration of this good man (that is, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva), all will be relieved from suffering, and their wishes will be completely fulfilled. According to each person's aptitude, the Bodhisattva will guide them safely on the path of rebirth.Heaven or Nirvana.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 18

No matter where they are, if sentient beings plant seeds in barren or cultivated fields (3), whether they diligently take care of them or not, but sincerely recite the name, chant, venerate, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-Sattva, the merit and wondrous miraculous power of that virtuous man (that is, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva) will cause all the fruits and seeds to flourish abundantly. Why is that so?

This good man has, in countless eons of the past, made a great vow of diligence and steadfastness before an incalculable number of Buddhas and World Honored Ones. Due to that vow, wishing to perfect sentient beings, he often guards all the great lands. He often protects all seeds and frequently enables all sentient beings to enjoy according to their desire. By the spiritual power of this good man, the roots, tendrils, sprouts, bulbs, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits of all plants in the great lands grow; medicinal herbs, cereals, rice seedlings, flowers, and fruits flourish, ripen to golden perfection, remain fresh, fragrant, soft, and delicious.

Benefits of reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: 19

Wherever sentient beings, due to greed, anger, ignorance, etc., commit acts of killing; or do not give when asked, or wish to engage in wrongful conduct, or speak falsehoods; or speak harshly, or sow discord, or speak impure words, or are greedy, or angry; or even hold wrong views, creating the Ten Evils... But if they can sincerely call the name, recite, show reverence, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-sattva, all afflictions will be completely eliminated, they will stay away from the Ten Evils; they will accomplish the Ten Virtues, and generate a heart of compassion and a mind for the benefit of all beings.

This virtuous man has accomplished the power of merit, miraculous divine concentration, courage, and diligence. Within the span of a meal, he can be present in countless, innumerable Buddha realms. In each Buddha realm, within the meal period, he can save countless, innumerable sentient beings, teaching them as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges River, enabling them to be free from suffering and attain joy. Depending on their aptitude, the Bodhisattva will place them in the path of rebirth to the Heaven or Nirvana.

(The Benefits of Reciting the Name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva – According to the Mahāyāna Mahāsaṅgīti Kṣitigarbha Caturbhūmakasūtra)

tieu_de: HOW TO KEEP THE BODHICITA ALWAYS FROM DECAYING???
tom_tat: WHAT IT MEANS TO TRULY BE GRATEFUL. Excerpt: According to the teachings of the Master
noi_dung:
HOW TO KEEP THE BODHICITTÁ FROM DECAYING???

WHAT IS TRUE GRATITUDE.

Excerpt: According to the Master's teaching

⚘⚘⚘⚘⚘

When I first started learning Buddhism, I asked the Master. "Master, I find it very difficult to believe in Buddha and in karma. So how can we always maintain the Bodhi mind without faltering?"

The Master said:

- You practice so that every day when you wake up, you feel more love and respect for the Bodhisattvas than the day before, and that is enough.

- How can the heart love and reverence for the Buddha and Bodhisattva also lose the teacher?

- No, when the mind first developed, everyone was resilient and brave, but in the first year the Buddha was in the mind, the second year the Buddha was already outside. The reverence not only did not increase, but it also gradually disappeared, so much so that many people who initially entered the temple even bowed down earnestly. After a while, they only put their hands together and folded their skirts. After a few years, sometimes they no longer look at the Buddha. I said that this means that the mind of reverence has lost a lot. Then how can the bodhicitta still be possible???

According to the teachings of our beloved teacher

Since then, DN, alongside practicing, always wholeheartedly loves the bodhisattvas, respects the master, and is reverent toward the teacher.

That mind of DN absolutely never wants to lose, so every day in the heart, DN reminds oneself: "What have I practiced today, is there anything good?"

Every action, every arising thought or intention, or preparations to do anything are paused for a few seconds to consider, fearing that the teacher and the bodhisattvas would be saddened if they knew.

Am I doing this correctly? Can this be taken, being so casual—is it theft? Using office supplies, even just a piece of paper, already makes me feel like I have committed theft. Scolding students and then immediately feeling regret and promising oneself to be gentler next time. Gradually improving day by day, little by little.

It is true that there are deities above our heads. Every being has two deities following to record their actions. They record all good and bad deeds. In the past, when one did not understand the way, they acted freely, but now one must be careful. Everything should be done mindfully. One must absolutely not be negligent. For example, if one happens to be negligent, they must immediately repent (feel remorse and make sure not to repeat it next time).

Also, imagine that the spirits and demons are all mocking.

- You claim to study Buddhism, act as a layperson, and even recite sutras and mantras, but what do you think you are doing? Are you not defaming Buddhism???.

Thinking like that made me break out in a sweat from shame. Next time, I will definitely not dare to do it again.

In his teachings, the master always said.

- Cultivate so that each day your mind becomes a little more reverent. If you do not have this mindset yet, you must learn it.

Sadly, until now we have only heard about learning to speak, learning letters, learning to write. Learning to cook, arranging flowers... but respectfulness is a virtue that we also have to learn?

That's right, we really have to learn it. Why is that?

Nowadays, our good-heartedness is too poor. The minds of beings today are like a piece of land that has been deserted and wild for a long time. Grass and various miscellaneous plants grow up haphazardly. Reverence and morality are like stunted trees being crowded out by all kinds of weeds so that they have no room to grow. Because such good-heartedness is too limited and small, it must be nurtured, weeding, cleaning up trash, and getting rid of all the surrounding obstacles. Care for it every day so that the tree of reverence grows quickly and healthily. Without reverence, what kind of practice can there be?

That is why we need to learn. The virtues that we do not have, or have but have long been forgotten and become old, should now, having learned Buddhism, be taken out and polished until they shine.

Learning respect must start from those with the lowest status in society. The poor, the disabled, those in dishonest professions, prisoners, or offenders, even children. Everyone should be treated with respect.

When you offer them kind words without any sense of hierarchy, fair and sincere... think about it, if towards a beggar we give money with both hands, bow respectfully, and speak words of kind encouragement as if making an offering to the Buddha, then if at that moment it is not a beggar but a Buddha or Bodhisattva trying your patience, how delighted they would be.

That mind will grow day by day through cleansing and training. Therefore, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha said that people nowadays must learn reverence in this way.

Studying Buddhism requires a heart of gratitude toward the Buddhas, and gratitude toward the teacher and the master.

How should one repay gratitude? Do they also demand repayment? There are no Buddhas or Bodhisattvas who love us unconditionally. But we cannot use that as an excuse to be idle or lazy. Relying on them would make us a useless child.

To repay the Buddha, one must diligently practice the Mahayana scriptures, strictly observe the precepts, and encourage others. Be conscious of preserving the Dharma of the Tathagata. Live and work for the benefit of sentient beings. Do not indulge in immorality, do not break precepts, and do not defame or tarnish Buddhism.

To be grateful to teachers, one must follow their instructions, diligently study, and practice. In life, fulfill your own responsibilities. A father acts as a father, a mother as a mother, a child as a child. A teacher as a teacher, a student as a student... if the entire world observed the five precepts and practiced the ten wholesome deeds, how could this society ever degenerate?

tieu_de: BUDDHIST Q&A.
tom_tat: "EGO" AND HOW TO TAME IT. A disciple once asked his Master as follows: 'Yes, Master, I respectfully ask, Buddhism is the path of "No-Self"; studying according to the philosophy of no-self means there is no self, no me, all.'
noi_dung:
BUDDHIST Q&A.

"EGO" AND THE WAY TO TAME IT.

A disciple once asked his Master as follows: "Yes, I respectfully ask, Master. Buddhism is the path of 'No-self'. Studying the philosophy of no-self means that there is no self, no 'I', all is due to the coming together of conditions that form this temporary body. Yet, sentient beings in the age of degeneration are always caused by 'the Ego' to discriminate, attach, and be deluded by illusions.

It can also be said that 'Ego' is the root of the cycle of birth and death."

Conquering the 'ego' is also letting go of 'greed, anger, and ignorance.' Therefore, to eradicate these 'Three Poisons,' it is only when we let go of this 'ego.' Today, for the sake of the community, I have a few words to ask, humbly hoping the Master will compassionately teach us.

🙏🙏🙏

Question:

Dear Master, when anger arises, I can recognize it and immediately restrain it and repent at that moment. But when arrogance arises, how can I become aware of it?

Answer:

"As long as there is ego, there will be fame and gain, greed, anger, ignorance, jealousy, envy, dislike; in general, if one becomes a clod of earth, there is no ego, so how can one practice and not become foolish, never acting for one's own benefit?"

Question:

"Ego has been following me for a long time, it has become a habit, eating and sleeping together with me for a long time. How can I know if I am suffering from severe ego, Master?" (Because most people with the ego problem do not know they have it; if one knows their enemy, only then can it be destroyed.)

Answer:

Then you should consider whether you often boast and feel proud, arrogant. When others criticize you, do you feel sad or uncomfortable, do you get angry and want to walk away, do you know how to listen, or do you always hold onto your own prejudice? Furthermore, you should see whether you know how to yield to someone else or not. Generally, if you achieve a little and consider it excellent, that is great arrogance.

Question:

I respectfully ask the Teacher to compassionately reveal the Dharma method to help the public have an effective way to counter the disease of great arrogance.

Answer:

"When a thief wants to enter your house and you know he is a thief, how would he dare to enter your house and take things, unless you consider him a relative."

Question:

If this 'ego' still exists, then practicing any method will not be successful. Teacher, then what should we do to tame this ego every day?

Answer:

Observing the precepts, cultivating virtue and morality is the fundamental root of a person on the path of practice. Moreover, you must always remain steadfast in your vows, pursue the path without sparing your life, sincerely follow through to the end of the path you have chosen, and always generate the Bodhi mind for the true benefit of all beings... then there will be no time to be arrogant or proud; sincerity and perseverance will create a strong will for you, training you to be able to let go of this ego.

🤍 "The Master carries the sweet Dharma,

Spreading it everywhere far and wide.

Taking refuge with the Sangha,

And everlasting peace...

Excerpt: Teachings of the Master

tieu_de: What is 'paying respect to the Buddhas and praising the Tathagata'?
tom_tat: (Excerpted from the teachings of the Master) As a Buddhist practitioner, almost everyone is very familiar with the ten great vows of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and many people even use this as a scheduled recitation practice.
noi_dung:
What is "honoring the Buddhas, praising the Tathagata"?

(Excerpted from the teachings of the Master)

As a Buddhist practitioner, almost everyone is very familiar with the ten great vows of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and many people even use them as part of their daily recitation schedule. However, the meaning and the realm of the Ten Great Vows of Samantabhadra are extremely profound. Although we recite them daily, we may not necessarily understand even a part of that boundless sea of meaning, because these ten great vows encompass all the practices of the great Bodhisattvas, aimed at leading to the ultimate perfect Buddhahood. The principles are very deep, but the reality is accessible from top to bottom—from the level of an Equal Enlightenment (Samyak-sambuddha) Great Bodhisattva down to those who have just begun on the Bodhisattva path—according to one's capacity for understanding.and the practice may vary in depth, but once the resolve to practice arises, all will attain benefits beyond imagination. Here, we only delve into the first two practices, which are "revering the Buddhas" and "praising the Tathagata," because if these initial practices cannot be accomplished, then all the subsequent eight practices will not be fulfilled.

When it comes to "paying respect to the Buddhas," the vast majority of us immediately think of the image of a person bowing with all five limbs touching the ground before a Buddha statue seated majestically on a lotus throne, and then assume that paying respect to the Buddhas surely only means showing reverence to the image of the Buddha. In fact, the meaning of this respect is very broad. "The Buddhas" includes all the Buddhas of the three times: past, present, and future. The past and present Buddhas are easy to understand and recognize, but who are the future Buddhas? They are all sentient beings. All sentient beings are future Buddhas, because every sentient being has Buddha-nature, and alsoall have the potential to become Buddhas. People usually only know how to show respect to Buddhas of the past and present, and rarely have they heard of anyone showing respect to future Buddhas. If there is someone who can truly do so, that person is practicing the vow of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

I remember once my Master said: "You should remember, showing respect to the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, senior masters, ancestral teachers, and those above you is nothing to talk about, that is natural, but being able to show respect to those who are lower, inferior to you, or even down to mosquitoes and gnats, that is truly difficult." At this point, perhaps many people wonder: "So if they are extremely wicked, engaging in prostitution, theft, murder... do we still have to show respect to them? People like that have nothing worthy of respect." This, in turn, relates to the second practice, 'praising the Tathagata.' The best way is to learnaccording to Sudhana in the Avatamsaka Sutra. Sudhana went to seek good spiritual friends, meeting 53 of them, among whom 3 appeared in an evil form: one representing lust, one representing anger, and one representing ignorance, symbolizing the three fundamental afflictions of sentient beings. Before the other 50 good spiritual friends, Sudhana was wholeheartedly respectful, circumambulating three times, praising and lauding them, asking questions and learning. Even to these 3 good spiritual friends, he still respectfully circumambulated three times, but did not praise them. From this, it can be seen that one should maintain respect toward all sentient beings, as this is a respect for their Buddha-nature, which is called 'reverence to all Buddhas.'Virtuous, able to set an example for the world, one shows respect along with praise and learning; if otherwise, one still shows the same respect, respectful but without praise, without imitation, respecting from a distance, this is called 'praising the Tathagata.'

Saying so, yet the practice is truly not simple! Before people with virtues worthy of respect, it is very easy to arouse a sense of reverence and admiration, but if that respect remains unchanged even toward the lowly and base, whose moral status is low, then it is truly genuine reverence, in harmony with the practice of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. In the past, during the time the Buddha was still alive, among the ten great disciples of the Buddha, Sariputra was considered the foremost disciple in wisdom, honored as the Commander of the True Dharma; in such a high position, he still maintained his virtue and held a humility and respectful demeanor that few could match.Just in time. Once, while preparing to go on alms round, he carelessly left his robes unarranged. In the Sangha, a seven-year-old novice noticed and reminded him. The Great General of the Dharma quickly adjusted his inner and outer robes and then went up to the novice, saying: "Venerable, now my robes are properly arranged." He left a saying: "Anyone, even just seven years old, who instructs me in anything, I will forever regard as a teacher." This touching story about the foremost wise disciple of the Buddha is truly worthy for us to learn from, regarding the spirit of reverence towards the Buddhas.

Suddenly seeing some ants crawling on the ground, he bent down and whispered: "Hello, little ants, future Buddhas"...

Excerpt: Teachings of the Master

tieu_de: Human Life, 10 Animal Lives
tom_tat: “I am a monastic. One evening, while sitting in meditation and entering a state of concentration, I recalled and verified my past lives from 600 years ago. Now I would like to recount them. 600 years ago, I also
noi_dung:
HUMAN LIFE, 10 ANIMAL LIVES

"I am a monk. One evening while meditating and entering samadhi, I recalled and verified my past lives from 600 years ago. Now I would like to recount them.

600 years ago, I was also a monk who ordained. I ordained at the age of 20, received the full ordination in the Three Halls, and practiced for more than 50 years. In the process of practicing and studying Buddhism, I did quite a few good deeds. But even though I practiced according to the Buddha, my mind still clung to worldly affairs, desiring to enjoy the blessings in the human realm, and in the end, not only did I fail to escape the cycle of six realms, but I also fell into the three evil paths and endured suffering.

After dying as a monk, I was reincarnated into a wealthy merchant family and grew up to become a pampered young master, spending my days indulging in a life of partying and drinking. I had eight female servants beside me; although I was not lustful, my heart was very greedy for fame and wealth, which sowed quite a bit of evil karma.

After living a wealthy life in my previous life, I was reborn into a family of officials. When I grew up, I became a general commanding armies. At that time, I was majestic and awe-inspiring, having everything I needed, enjoying wealth and honor, savoring the finest foods endlessly, and spending all day indulging in a life of drinking and pleasure. Because of eating, drinking, partying, and seeking pleasure, I created evil karma once again. In particular, I had led troops to kill many people, beheading them and throwing their corpses into the river. Whenever enemy soldiers hid in the grass, we had to find them and drag them out to kill them, resulting in countless grudges and enmities for the future lives.after.

After I died as a general, I had to be reincarnated three times as frogs. Because I had chopped off people's heads, I became a frog without a neck. Killing people and throwing their bodies into the river, when I became a frog I was beaten with sticks, hooked, and died floating belly-up on the water, rotting and stinking, even suffering the misery of being caught and killed, having my tendons pulled and my skin flayed to repay the karma from my past life. After living three lifetimes as a frog, I was reincarnated as a jungle chicken, and for four consecutive lifetimes I was caught and killed by people, to repay the debt from when I was a general commanding soldiers to kill those hiding in the grass.

When I lived a life of luxury, indulging in the pleasures of eating, spending the whole day eating delicious and spicy foods, I was therefore reincarnated as a wild chicken to endure the suffering of being stabbed with a spear, cut with a sword, stewed, cooked, stir-fried, and boiled to repay the karma of my previous life.

After four lifetimes as a wild chicken repaying karmic debts and then dying, I was reincarnated as a pig, continuously for three lifetimes. This is the evil karma from my life as a wealthy young man, lazy and indulgent, eating without working, always wanting to eat meat, so I had to become a pig to repay it. Turning into a pig that eats leftover, spoiled food, being whipped and beaten unbearably, even having to endure thousands of cuts to the flesh to repay the karma of two lifetimes of enjoying food.

600 years… What a precious period of time, yet it slipped away so vaguely, how could one not be heartbroken?

At that time, when I saw the cycles of my past lives, I wept very sorrowfully even though I had always been someone who rarely shed tears. At that moment, I thought, why was I so greedy? Because of a single word of greed, a wrong thought at the moment of death, I had to fall into the three evil paths for ten lifetimes. How could I not feel heartbroken and regretful about this? Six hundred years… such a precious period of time, just passing by in a blur, how could I not feel pain?

I, who previously did not believe in any spirits or deities, have now become a person who believes in karma, and moreover, I have seen my own karmic retribution in a very real way.

As a monk in one lifetime, blessed in two lifetimes, I did not know to do good deeds or accumulate virtue; instead, I sowed countless evil actions, and therefore had to be reborn 10 times into the three evil paths. I had to endure extremely painful retribution, and only after repaying my bad karma could I be reborn as a human – this is karma, which never errs even by the tiniest thread.

Some people may ask, why not reincarnate into the realm of hungry ghosts or suffer in hell? This is perhaps a blessing obtained from practicing Buddhism in my previous life.

(Translated by Tiểu Thiện)

Commentary:

The cause and effect in this story is very subtle; if you pay close attention, you will notice many interesting things.

First: In the sutras, the Buddha once taught about good deeds that result in bad karma, which are: being eager to study and learn the scriptures for the purpose of competing and arguing, keeping precepts for the sake of personal gain (for monastics), giving alms to control others, and meditating to seek the merit of the Formless Realm (from the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra).

In general, it is about creating good deeds, but originating from a mind seeking fame – profit – wealth – worldly pleasures..., so in the early period, the karmic reward manifests according to desire, enjoying fame, profit, pleasures... but the benevolent mind is no longer there, overshadowed by greed for profit and enjoyment, leading to the creation of all kinds of sins.

Haven't we always often encountered this type of person: great blessings, wealth, fame, and power all at once, yet they live selfishly and commit all sorts of sins. Then, when their blessings run out, the retribution comes extremely tragically and lasts for a long time. In this story, it is 3 lifetimes as a frog, 4 lifetimes as a pheasant, and 3 lifetimes as a pig, being painfully slaughtered many times.

All of this is because at the beginning, people perform good deeds seeking rewards of fame, wealth, talent, and beauty in this world. Therefore, a disciple of the Buddha must understand this from the very start: whether cultivating wisdom or merit, one must aim to be liberated from the cycle of birth and death, or aspire for rebirth in the Pure Land, or strive to attain the Arhat state, or seek the Supreme Buddha fruit. One should not foolishly desire the fleeting, temporary pleasures of the cycle of birth and death, such as love, lust, beauty, money, power, or fame...

Secondly: it is the issue of the timing of retribution. Many people always wonder why they see wicked people but they do not suffer retribution. Simply because that person's merit has not run out yet; only when the merit is exhausted will the retribution for their evil deeds manifest. Sometimes the retribution is only seen after several decades, sometimes only in a few lifetimes later.

In this story, in his first life he was a monk for 50 years, doing many good deeds. That merit caused him in the next two lives to always have happiness; in his first rebirth, he was a rich young man, indulging in pleasure, lazy, vain, killing animals, … yet everyone around still saw that he did not suffer any consequences at all. Even in the next life, he was still able to become a general, powerful, with abundant wealth.

Simply because the merit from 50 years of monastic practice, accumulated in the previous life, had not yet run out, and when that merit was exhausted, he immediately fell into downfall.

descend to become an animal, being slaughtered over many consecutive lives. Fortunately, he had a connection with Buddhism, used to pay respects to the Buddha, and served the Triple Gem (the natural duty of a monk), so he was only subjected to 10 lives as an animal; otherwise, he could have gone down to hell for countless years, being reborn as an animal hundreds of thousands of times, not just a few.

Therefore, when considering cause and effect, one must always examine it over a long period across many lifetimes, and should not make judgments based on just a few years or a few decades.

(Quang Tu)

Source: nhanqua.com.vn

tieu_de: THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THE GREAT SACRIFICE OF THE BUDDHA SHAKYAMUNI.
tom_tat: (Excerpt from the Master's teachings). "A supernormal being descends to the world,"
noi_dung:
THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THE GREAT SACRIFICE OF SHAKYAMUNI BUDDHA.

(Excerpts from the Teacher's teachings).

"There is a transcendent being descending to the world,

Born to enlighten the golden path.

Bringing peace and happiness to humanity,

From the first step of the seven lotus petals..."

It can be said that, until now, we have mostly heard about Amitabha Buddha, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva... The Original Buddha is also known but few people truly understand. In this article, DN asks the Teacher’s permission to share a little more about Him.

Yes! Our original teacher Shakyamuni is the Buddha, the one who founded the Dharma we follow today. Without Him, there would be no Buddhism for us to practice.

The name Shakyamuni can be understood as the sage of the Shakya clan or the brave and steadfast Buddha.

He is one of the 16 greatest Buddhas in the universe, throughout the past, present, and future lifetimes. With 500 vows, all of which aim to endure suffering on behalf of all sentient beings, he only vows to be born in evil realms to teach and guide them. (Our Earth is such a realm, extremely evil, with beings that are obstinate, cruel, ignorant, and prideful.) The realms that other Buddhas do not wish to be born into, he tirelessly enters these evil worlds. Why is that? Because he possesses vast vow power, supreme compassion, and unmatched merits and spiritual power.

When we read the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, we see that the Buddhas mentioned there all have lifespans lasting tens of thousands of kalpas. As for our Original Teacher, His lifespan is only 80 years. Why is that? Because this world of Saha is too evil, sentient beings have little merit and heavy karma, are ignorant and unwise. Therefore, He manifested, took on vows to bear karma and teach sentient beings, leaving a source of wondrous Dharma for the world. Sentient beings rely on the Buddha's teachings, following them in order to transcend birth and death.

However, even though He is a fully enlightened being with perfect wisdom and unimaginable supernatural powers, He only remained in the world for 80 years. From this, we can see how compassionate our Blessed One was...

Furthermore, even though the time of His preaching lasted only 40 years, the legacy He left behind is priceless. He always looked at the capacities of each sentient being to give teachings that were suitable. Very few Buddhas could do this, and from this, we can see how great our Buddha Master was. He not only saved beings in this world but also saved the entire universe.

Although He did not remain in the world for long, the time He practiced spans countless kalpas. When He began His practice is unknown to anyone, but it can be said that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas such as Amitabha Buddha, Avalokiteshvara, Manjushri, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, ... all rely on His spiritual power, merit, and vows to generate the aspiration for Supreme Bodhi. Thanks to this, today we have these great Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; this is a truth we should know. Why? Because He has sacrificed so much for sentient beings in this Saha world, a silent sacrifice without seeking recognition. Therefore, we, the children of the Buddha, mustWhat can be done to repay this kindness?

When he was still alive, the Buddha taught: "Precepts are the lifeblood of the Dharma; as long as the precepts exist, the Dharma exists; if the precepts are lost, the Dharma is lost." Therefore, we should remember these important principles. "Precepts are the foundational root of a person in practicing the path; cultivating virtue and observing precepts were always emphasized by the ancient Patriarchs, because maintaining the precepts is also maintaining the teachings of the Tathagata. Thus, today we must strictly observe the precepts, as a sincere way to repay the kindness and virtue of the Tathagata."

Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra daily is to ward off evil spirits, while strictly observing the precepts is to preserve the Dharma. If the monks strictly observe the 250 precepts and the lay Buddhists all maintain the 5 precepts (do not kill, do not steal, do not commit sexual misconduct, do not lie, do not use intoxicants) and together practice the 10 wholesome deeds (the Ten Virtues), then external forces will not dare to criticize, but rather must respect and wholeheartedly admire.

Nowadays, there are many false practitioners; they cleverly use reasoning and debate to deceive people's hearts, causing sentient beings to be confused by wrong views. So, how can we know who is genuine and who is deceitful? Well, it’s actually not too difficult, everyone. We just need to look at their precepts to see whether they strictly observe them or not. Are they greedy, angry, or do they boast for self-gain? Why? Because a true Master or a Good Knowledgeable Friend genuinely possesses virtue and dignified conduct, they will never crave profit or praise. A truly practicing person has little desire and is never secretive; their boundless Bodhi mind is always oriented towards the benefit of sentient beings, without a trace of selfishness.greed, desire, or arrogance.

Today's technology is extremely advanced, and lawbreakers rely on science and technology to deny spiritual factors. Yes! As society progresses, human nature declines; it always exists with two sides. It is worth considering how science develops, yet every element 'after death returns to the four elements, the spirit must follow evil deeds and face punishment' (obeying the law of karma and repayment). Yet sentient beings today remain ignorant, not believing in this, which is truly pitiable. Similarly, awareness of deeply believing in karma and exploring the teachings of the Tathagata is extremely poor; they do not know how to think or be self-aware. They always wait to be urged.

urge. If one day there is no one to encourage, then one becomes sluggish and eventually forgets to practice, leaving oneself to be controlled by karma, and then continues to reincarnate forever.

It can be said that the more we learn about Him, the more we admire and bow before a person who is so compassionate and virtuous. The Master of this world has performed deeds beyond imagination. We hope that beings today will generate courageous aspirations, seek the path of liberation, and diligently practice in order to partially repay His great merit and sacrifice.

Namo Shakyamuni Buddha! 🙏🙏🙏

tieu_de: SOME SIGNS OF A HUMBLE PERSON:
tom_tat: - Polite, gentle speech, with proper forms of address, with a beginning and an end when interacting even in comments. No joking, no making others feel inferior or uncomfortable when speaking. - Respectful attitude
noi_dung:
SOME SIGNS OF A HUMBLE PERSON:

- Polite, gentle speech, with proper forms of address, complete sentences when interacting even in comments. No joking around, no making others feel inferior or uncomfortable when speaking.

- A respectful, helpful, and considerate attitude toward everyone in concrete ways.

- A mind that always intends love, tolerance, respect, and recognizes the strengths of others.

- Daily self-reflection on one’s actions and intentions to gradually improve.

- If strictly teaching or admonishing, do not be harsh, sarcastic, or disparaging. If expressing close affection, do not be sentimental or melodramatic.

- Always see oneself as small as dust. Always see what one achieves as a responsibility.

- Always aim for something more perfect, more absolute, but practically improve little by little.

- Very loyal.

- In the face of suffering, take responsibility, repent, and hope for positive outcomes. In the face of joy, be grateful, humble, and continue to strive for everyone.

- In life, be cheerful, diligent, perceptive, and subtle, not rigid, stubborn, or annoying.

- In practice, carefully guard the mind, repent when wrong thoughts arise, always wish others to be better than oneself, and always keep the mind in accordance with the Buddha's teachings.

- Always be an optimistic and positive person, bringing good energy to everyone.

- Ready to listen to feedback, happy to correct mistakes, and protect the dignity of those around, even those who have made mistakes or committed sins. Never obstruct anyone’s progress.

- Be a person who lives confidently, kindly, and neatly, not timid or scandalous.

- Speak about morals when necessary. If not necessary, remain silent and act. Adapt flexibly to beings without being rigid or negative.

- Enjoy uplifting others, enjoy humbling oneself. Always skillfully use various means to bring others back to Morality.

- When speaking about oneself, always be humble and encourage goodness. When speaking about others, always respect and praise them. When judging negative matters, always be tolerant.

- Likes unity, reconciliation, and sharing with the community.

- Lives for the benefit and happiness of the people around them.

- Very good at taking care of oneself to maintain appearance, life, property, and works while caring for all beings. If necessary, ready to sacrifice when justified, even willing to give up their life.

- Does not seek credit.

- Knows how to seize opportunities when the time comes, knows when to give up opportunities at the right moment, and knows how to decline when not needed.

- Always live in balance and harmony.

- Maintain respect for the Buddha, keep a loving heart for all beings, and firmly nurture humility.

- Always aim toward the goal of Non-Self and deeply believe in Cause and Effect.

- The distance between ourselves and others gradually fades.

- Think very moderately…

What is the value of a cup or a bowl? It is precisely the emptiness inside. Thanks to the emptiness to hold things, it becomes valuable.

What is the value of a humble person? It is humility within. Thanks to this virtue, people can acquire more knowledge, practice more skills, recognize their mistakes to continuously improve, and diligently cultivate to aim for the ultimate good.

What is the value of the universe? It is emptiness. Thanks to emptiness, it can hold countless beautiful and vast galaxies...

Appears empty yet exists

Appears as nothing yet is great and sublime

It feels like there is nothing left, yet it lasts forever

It feels meaningless, yet the meaning is immense.

St

tieu_de: BODHISATTVA KṣITIGARBHA AND HIS GREATNESS.
tom_tat: It can be said that for a very long time, the image of the Bodhisattva, with the right hand holding an elephant goad, the left hand holding a wish-fulfilling jewel, appearing as a monk, standing on a treasure lotus, originally
noi_dung:
Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and His Greatness.

It can be said that, for a very long time, the image of the Great Bodhisattva, holding a scepter in the right hand and a wish-fulfilling jewel in the left hand, appears as a venerable monk standing on a precious lotus, has been deeply ingrained in the consciousness of the Vietnamese people.

... And with a heart of great compassion, pitying all beings, through countless kalpas, He has made a vast vow to benefit sentient beings: "I, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, vow that until the very end of the world, I will teach and save all sentient beings throughout this entire universe."

For this reason, the Buddha always praises Him as a Great Being with supreme wisdom and virtue, with power and clairvoyance beyond imagination.

Again, speaking about Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, we cannot fail to mention the Kṣitigarbha Three Sutras, which are also the three major sutras of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha:

- First: The Sutra on Observing the Retribution of Good and Evil Karma (leaning towards the practice of repentance, clearly describing the conditions of sentient beings during the Dharma-ending age and the method of observing retribution).

- Second: The Kṣitigarbha Ten Chains Sutra (leaning towards cause and effect, virtues, and the spiritual power of Kṣitigarbha).

- On Tuesday, it is the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra, also the most famous and revered Sutra in the present time.

When the Buddha was still alive, He also carefully instructed many great Bodhisattvas, Heavenly Beings, Sages... etc., to respectfully preserve it, in order to widely disseminate and allow sentient beings to follow the teachings according to His last wishes.

According to the sutras, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is the only one entrusted by Shakyamuni Buddha (the Buddha Tathāgata) with all sentient beings, from the time the Buddha entered nirvana, when the Dharma declined and disappeared.

During the empty period when there was no Buddhist teaching, until the birth of Maitreya Buddha, the work of saving sentient beings belonged to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Even when the Buddhist teachings had ceased, had completely disappeared... and even when there was no longer the time of the true dharma, the image dharma, or the fundamental dharma, He still had to carry out the work of sowing causes and conditions, saving sentient beings according to His great vow: "If hell is not empty, I vow not to become a Buddha,

If sentient beings are not saved completely, I vow not to attain Bodhi".

Let's try to think about it. During His time, there were many famous Bodhisattvas with talent and virtue. But! Why did the World-Honored One not write biographies for Bodhisattvas like Manjusri, Samantabhadra, or Avalokiteshvara, but only for Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva?

Why is that? Because from a very long time ago, He has practiced for countless lifetimes, it can be said that He is an Ancient Buddha. Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha sacrificed Himself and made such extraordinary vows as: “To save sentient beings with stubborn and difficult temperaments, hard to teach and correct, seemingly impossible to save, especially those in the three evil paths... From this, we can see His patience and compassion as inconceivably accomplished. He possesses extraordinary endurance and is able to achieve it.”things that other Bodhisattvas find difficult to do...

As mentioned clearly in the Kṣitigarbha Sutra: “He does not only want to save one or two sentient beings, but must save all, without leaving anyone behind...” at that moment, His great vow can truly be called fulfilled.

Therefore, with his great cultivation and vows, wisdom, merit and virtue, and skillful means... from that, the Buddha chose him to be the one to replace the Buddha in guiding sentient beings during this degenerate era of the Dharma, according to the Buddha's prophecy: “In a future life, he will become a Great Bodhisattva, named Kṣitigarbha, rescuing countless countless sentient beings, with a reputation renowned throughout the ten directions of the worlds.”

When mentioning Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, we cannot forget the immense grace of the Lord of the Dark Realm. In this degenerate era of Dharma, beings are ignorant, unintelligent, and naturally stubborn, difficult to teach or admonish; yet, He tirelessly manifests everywhere to teach and save them. Beings today should remember these principles, strive to cultivate diligently, seek the path of liberation, be diligent every day without retreating, for this is truly a way to repay His grace.

🤍Great Compassion, Great Vows, Great Sage, Great Kindness, Principal Deity Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā Tathāgata!

🙏🙏🙏

tieu_de: SHOULD PRINT THE PICTURE OF MONK LANG NGHIEM TO HANG IN THE HOUSE (useful article, includes a photo)
tom_tat: 🌿 If there are sentient beings, depending on the items available in the country one resides in, such as: tree bark flowers, Bai leaves, white paper, white velvet… write this Mantra on them and then put it in a fragrant bag. Such a person is foolish
noi_dung:
SHOULD PRINT CHU LANG NGHIEM PAINTINGS TO HANG IN THE HOUSE (useful article, includes images)

🌿 If there are sentient beings, depending on the items available in the water where they reside, such as: tree bark, flowers, leaves of the Bo tree, white paper, white velvet… write this Mantra on them and then put it in a fragrant pouch. If that person is ignorant and unable to recite and remember it, then keeping it on their body or at home will ensure that throughout their life they will not be harmed by any poisons.

🌿 Those virtuous and wise beings who either recite, wear, or offer this Mind Mantra will never be born into poverty, lowliness, or unsafe places in any lifetime. Even if these beings themselves do not perform meritorious deeds, the Buddhas of the ten directions will bestow virtue upon them. Therefore, over countless lifetimes, they often are born in the same place as the Buddhas, closely connecting innumerable merits to practice together in one place.

🌿 If those who in the past committed the five transgressions of Rebellion and the grave sin deserving of banishment to Avici Hell, or monks and nuns who committed the sins of the Four Vital Elements and Eight Vital Elements, have not yet had the chance to repent in previous lives, now by reading, reciting, and compiling this Mantra, wearing it on their body, or keeping it in their dwelling place, all accumulated negative karma from before will be completely extinguished, and before long, they will attain the Patience of Non-birth (Asamkhya-samadhi).

🌿 Like a woman who has not had children. If she wants to pray for children and sincerely contemplates or wears this Charm, she will give birth to sons and daughters endowed with the blessings of Wisdom. Whoever prays for longevity will live long, and whoever prays for Merit will receive Merit; even praying for a beautiful and healthy body will achieve that as well. After death, depending on one’s vow, they will be reborn in the lands of the ten directions, certainly not in borderlands, lowly families, and will not have impure bodies.

🌿 If there are countries, districts, villages, or hamlets suffering from famine, epidemics, or places afflicted by war, bandit attacks, and all other accidents… just write this Charm, post it on the four gates of the city, on the temples, or write it on banners, flags, and have the beings there respectfully receive this Charm, reverently worship it, wholeheartedly offer to it, and at the same time have each person wear the Charm on themselves or place it in their residence, then all disasters will be completely eliminated.

🌿 If they exist in the Kingdoms. Wherever there is this Charm, the Heaven Dragon rejoices, the weather is favorable, the crops are abundant, and the people are happy. All calamities caused by all Evil Stars transforming into monsters everywhere cannot arise, people do not die prematurely, chains and shackles do not attach to the body, day and night sleep peacefully without encountering bad dreams.

🌿 This Saha world has eighty-four thousand calamities caused by Evil Stars, led by 28 Evil Stars as Supreme Leaders. There are also 8 Great Evil Stars that preside over or appear in the world in various forms or cause strange disasters for sentient beings. As long as there is this Mantra, all of them are eliminated. Within the scope of 12 Do Tuần, severe and fierce calamities cannot invade.
