tieu_de: WHAT IS A MIXED PRACTITIONER?
tom_tat: AND DILIGENTLY PRACTICE TRAINING THE RIGHT WAY. (This article is based on the guidance and instruction of my teacher 🙏)
noi_dung:
WHAT IS MEDITATION PRACTICE?

AND THE PRACTICE OF DILIGENT SPIRITUAL TRAINING THE RIGHT WAY.

(This article is based on the guidance and instructions of the teacher 🙏)

🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿

Recently, many people have been messaging DN about the issue of diligent spiritual practice. DN sees that most of you are very diligent. You follow the daily practice schedule consistently. However, there is still one issue, which is that your practice is scattered, spending too much time on many different methods instead of focusing on one the most.

Looking back, I see that most of you still practice many different methods. Therefore, today DN is writing this instructional article, precisely to help you determine your path of practice and know how to reorient your daily practice schedule.

So, what is mixed practice? Yes! It can be said that mixed practice is practicing too many methods during your daily practice schedule. You cannot distinguish which one is the RIGHT PRACTICE (the main method according to the intended goal).

For example: if your goal is to receive the blessings of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, then the right practice is to recite Kṣitigarbha 1,000 times, for instance.

So what is ASSISTING MERIT? Assisting merit is a supportive practice for the main practice. (Usually, it involves reciting the Great Compassion Mantra or Shurangama Mantra to increase merit and eliminate negative karma, to prevent disturbances from external evil forces, to avert accidents, and to break obstacles from demons, helping life to be comfortable and allowing one to practice with peace of mind without regression).

Mixed practices are like having two hands but trying to do too many things at once, and none of them turn out well.

It's like if you only have one mouth but chew too much food, wanting to put every dish into your mouth, if there are too many things, you won't chew thoroughly and it won't taste good. Therefore, practicing multiple methods at once often leads to practice without peace. The schedule becomes long and tedious, the mind is full of distractions, and the results are not as desired. In cultivation, embracing too many methods can easily lead to mixed practice.

To have an EFFECTIVE PRACTICE SCHEDULE, you need to clearly understand what your goal is.

Example: The immediate goal of the practitioner is to receive the blessings of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and to overcome all obstacles, completely eliminating karmic conditions. The long-term goal is to recite the Buddha's name and be reborn in the Western Pure Land. Therefore, the daily practice schedule of the practitioner includes:

🍀Main Practice:

- Taking refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.

- Reciting the name of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha at all times.

(When practicing the main practice, one must note that the time spent should always be more than that for auxiliary practices, because it is the main practice and should be emphasized).

🍀Support practice: recite the solemn mantra 3 times + repent for karmic obstacles (if you do not know how to make a vow to repent, we can simply say as follows: the karmic obstacles I have are inherently heavy, now I sincerely repent, reflecting on the things I have done and confessing my repentance).

Many practitioners recite the names of many Buddhas and Bodhisattvas during their practice sessions. DN sees that this is not necessarily a bad thing, but when in trouble, practitioners may not be able to concentrate and remember which Principal Deity to call upon. Why? Because in times of difficulty, one's consciousness may become drowsy or dull, making it hard to remember whose name to recite if one does not consistently recite the name of a single Principal Deity every day. Moreover, at that time, the mind may simultaneously arise with various chants or images such as the Rites of Purity, the Great Compassion Mantra, Amitabha Buddha, Medicine Buddha, and so on, making it difficult to focus. Conversely, if each day one concentrates on reciting a single Principal Deity...With the deepest respect, then the moment of an accident I will immediately think of you. It's like a wifi connection: if too many people are accessing it, the wifi will be weak, but if only one person is accessing it, the wifi is extremely strong.

As for why one chooses the Lăng Nghiêm mantra for assistance, it is because the Lăng Nghiêm mantra has extremely supreme merits. Even if you have distracted thoughts while reciting the mantra, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will still bless you to eliminate disasters, maintain health, and bring good fortune. It also helps protect the body and eradicate internal and external evil spirits. In general, reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is extremely beneficial. Those who have more time can additionally recite sutras as much as possible. However, you should focus on reciting just one sutra consistently, which is also more likely to bring results.

When you have a proper schedule of practice, you will see immediate effects. What are the manifestations?

- That is when you cultivate peace, happiness. Not having many wandering thoughts.

- Life, work, and family are all arranged smoothly.

- A calm mind does not fear any adversity.

- Naturally seeing people being more respectful than usual.

- A healthy body with few illnesses.

- A bright, beautiful, and fresh face, ....etc...

🍁People might wonder why the goal is rebirth in the Pure Land rather than always reciting Buddha Amitabha, yet the recitation is of Kṣitigarbha instead???

It is said: I will chant the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha for three years according to the Kṣitigarbha Sutra as the Buddha instructed, to pray for the Bodhisattva's blessing so that all karmic obstacles will be completely eliminated. Because before entering Nirvana, the Buddha entrusted sentient beings to Kṣitigarbha, so today, if we want to practice without hindrance, we must strive to FEEL HIS PRESENCE. Once we have felt Him, He will bless all internal and external karmic obstacles to be completely eradicated, and even external heretical Mara lords will have no way to disrupt. Whatever wishes we seek will naturally be fulfilled. Therefore, the path of practice at that time will be wide and without fear. I will chant to the Bodhisattva until He tells me:"Alright, today your karmic obstacles have been lightened, now you should recite the Buddha Amitabha, and it is the right time for you to recite the Buddha to be reborn in the Pure Land." Then at that moment, Dn will recite the Buddha Amitabha.

Please remember: "In the first 3 years of practice, it is the time to clear the karma obstacles; this is not the stage to vigorously exert effort. Why? Because if our karmic force is still too heavy and has not been sufficiently repented to lighten it, it will become a blocking stone, obstructing us, causing afflictions in both worldly and spiritual matters, and things will not go as desired.

Again, when it comes to the scheduled time, you will feel bored, discouraged, and uneasy, seeing it as a form of punishment, not excited at all. Therefore, although these teachings are simple, you need to pay attention to avoid improper practice and incorrect cultivation.

tieu_de: Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is protected by deities and spirits across many generations and lifetimes.
tom_tat: ——————————————————————- On a trip with my fellow monks to the river areas of the Mekong Delta. We came here to help a young girl who suddenly became mute for unclear reasons. The family suspected it was due to been punished
noi_dung:
THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA HAS BEEN PROTECTED BY DEMONS AND SPIRITS FOR MANY LIFETIMES

——————————————————————- During a trip with fellow disciples to the riverine areas of the Mekong Delta, we came here to help a young girl who suddenly became mute for unknown reasons. Her family suspected it was a spiritual issue and asked us for assistance. Through this trip, we discovered something extremely miraculous. I am writing it down so that everyone can gain more faith and diligently practice cultivation. Once you have faith, strive to make use of your free time to devote yourself to practice. Do not doubt or be lazy anymore.

We set off very early at 6 a.m. The girl's father, Mr. Dung, took us to have breakfast at a small roadside vegetarian restaurant. The restaurant had a simple thatched roof and was very cool. Opposite this restaurant was a larger eatery, arranged fairly cleanly and neatly. But customers crowded at this small restaurant.

I asked Mr. Dung: "Is this restaurant good or why are there so many people?"

He said: "The cooking is ordinary, but I don't know why everyone prefers to eat here."

The owner of this eatery is around 40 years old, short, with tanned skin, and does not have the appearance of a boss. The one good thing is that he always smiles. I jokingly said to my senior monk: "Could it be that this place uses a charm to attract wealth?"

As usual, my senior brother opened his divine eye to observe. He saw something very strange: many Demon Gods were helping this person guide customers into the shop. Observing further into the shop owner's house in the distance, he saw rays of light of all colors. The benevolent gods passing by would stop to pay respects; it must not be an ordinary type of talisman, really strange. Since we still had to continue to Mr. Dung's house, as the car could not get in and we had to go by boat, we temporarily put aside this question.

After traveling by boat for more than 45 minutes, both sides were full of trees and deserted, with only an occasional house. Finally, we reached Mr. Dũng's house. When the senior monk stepped off the boat, he saw that the area around this house was surrounded by thick gray-black smoke, sensing that something was wrong. When Mr. Dũng brought up his 15-year-old daughter, the senior monk saw behind the girl a long-toothed and ferocious demon that had cultivated for many years. It used a black orb to block her mouth. The senior monk approached the altar, lit incense, and prayed, asking the deities to grant him the ritual. The senior monk, along with everyone, recited the AN THỔ ĐỊA CHƠN NGÔN chant 21 times. At this moment, the smoke surrounding the house disappeared. The earth deity appeared.This land is approaching. The Demon became angry and said: 'Who are you to interfere in my matters?' The senior monk asked: 'Why are you harming this girl?' The aggressive demon did not answer, saying: 'If you interfere again, do not blame me.'

The local deity could only shake his head and say, "This girl inadvertently touched them, so I cannot intervene. The matter is that when this girl was rowing a boat, she saw a small raft with offerings set afloat on the river. She laughed, saying that in this world, there are no ghosts or spirits, and used a pole to smash the raft. This made the spirits extremely angry, so they punished her with muteness and will take her away." At this point, the demon threw a sphere at us. Fortunately, everyone had protective charms, so the sphere was blocked. However, the force of the impact was so strong that everyone had to hold their breath because of chest tightness. This invisible power still strongly affected the visible world. Afterwardswhen the senior brother presented to the demon and pleaded for the girl’s life because of this ignorance but still was not granted. The girl’s father also promised to chant Buddha’s name if this demon spared the girl. This demon seemed like we couldn’t do anything to it, so it went along the way and continued.

The senior monk, along with everyone, chanted the Lăng Nghiêm mantra 108 times and prayed for the Vajra Protectors to assist. At this moment, four Vajras appeared along with a Demon King wearing Golden Armor. When this Demon King arrived, the ferocious demon had to bow its head in respect, and then he led it away to dissolve into emptiness. After this demon left, the girl screamed loudly to express her gratitude for our help. She also promised to practice vegetarianism and recite Buddha's name to atone for this wrongdoing.

After bidding us farewell, we did not forget the illuminating talisman at the restaurant. We then returned to meet the restaurant owner.

I asked: "What kind of talisman do you have in the house that glows like this?"

The owner said: "There is nothing at all."

Senior monk: "Does anyone in your house practice cultivation?"

Owner: "Yes, my father used to recite mantras when he was alive."

Senior monk: "May we have your permission to look inside the box on this altar, because this area is glowing."

When the monk opened the box, he saw a short rosary with 21 beads. On each bead was a Lăng Nghiêm seed, the sound of the mantras still resonating, with a faint scent of sandalwood.

Owner of the shop: “When my father was alive, he often recited the Lăng Nghiêm mantra using this 21-bead rosary, he was very healthy without any illness. When he passed away, it was very peaceful.”

The monk said, that’s right, thanks to him chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra with sincerity, each recitation made with respect, that he was able to attract spirits and deities to protect him while he was alive and still help his son, the owner of this vegetarian shop.

The virtuous deities regard this Dharma Jewel as if it were the Lankavatara Mantra, as if it were the Buddha's relics, and sincerely pay homage.

Set aside these mystical magical matters. Here we can see exactly as the predecessors said in the Lankavatara Mantra: the names are those of the Demon Kings who protect the Dharma. All types of demons must respectfully take their place and comply. And this power not only benefits one lifetime but also many future lives. If everyone can recite the Lankavatara Mantra once daily, it is to protect the Dharma, purify the righteous energy of the land and sky. It benefits oneself, one’s family, and widely across the Dharma realm.

OM MA HA TÁT ĐÁT ĐA BÁT ĐÁT RA

#experiencefrompracticingLangNghiemScripture

noi_dung:
METHODS OF CONTEMPLATION TO OVERCOME LUST, ADULTERY, AND AFFAIRS

ADVICE FOR MERCHANTS, FARMERS, AND CRAFTSMEN[1]

Merchants, farmers, and craftsmen should often reflect that: Whether we engage in business or rely on this or that trade, enduring the wind and weather, braving the sun and rain, it is merely for the purpose of accumulating a little money.

Others have wives and children, and we also have wives and children; others have older and younger sisters, and we also have older and younger sisters. If others harbor evil intentions [wanting to harm our loved ones], we surely clench our teeth in hatred. So if we harbor even a slight wicked thought [wanting to harm their loved ones], they will surely be angry just as we are.

Nowadays, we can witness people here and there, because of adultery, contracting diseases and dying, or being punished by the law, families being torn apart, and even children having to be sold to others. Families become unstable, wealth is lost, all ultimately because of a wrong notion that leads them into such situations.

Today we should quickly understand the issue ourselves and immediately eliminate such wicked and lewd thoughts. When seeing an elderly woman, imagine her as your own mother. When seeing a woman older than yourself, imagine her as your sister; if she is younger, think of her as your younger sister; or if even younger, imagine her as your daughter. Daily, one should not discuss or exchange matters of intimacy, nor should one read pornographic books.

Furthermore, in every action, one must strive to accumulate merit, and frequently think about practicing means to benefit others. By doing so, both blessings and longevity will gradually increase, and descendants in the future will naturally be honored and prosperous. What could be better than doing good deeds in life?

tieu_de: LAUNCH THE PRACTICE OF RECITING THE MANTRA LĂNG NGHIÊM EVERY DAY TO REDUCE UPCOMING NATURAL DISASTERS AND EPIDEMICS AND INCREASE
tom_tat: Dear all! Currently, the COVID pandemic situation in the world in general and in Vietnam in particular is developing with increasingly dangerous outbreaks, this is also due to the Delta variant.
noi_dung:
LAUNCHING THE PRACTICE OF RECITING THE LĂNG NGHIÊM COMMENTARY 7 TIMES DAILY TO REDUCE UPCOMING NATURAL DISASTERS AND EPIDEMICS AND INCREASE

Dear everyone!

Currently, the COVID pandemic situation in the world in general and in Vietnam in particular is developing increasingly dangerously. This is also because the industrialization of humanity at this time is extremely heavy, so natural disasters and epidemics occur more and more complexly and frequently.

Information from the Masters who practice and receive foreknowledge from the invisible realms indicates that from June to September this year, the epidemic will begin to spread strongly and cause extremely serious consequences, more severe than the outbreak last year. Therefore, I, Quang Từ, am now encouraging everyone to collectively recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra to reduce the impact of the epidemic in Vietnam in particular and the world in general. In addition, the mantra also helps practitioners receive protection from the dharmapalas, gain unimaginable merit, and avoid natural disasters and epidemics if sincerely recited.persevere without giving up and maintain sexual purity.

The ritual of mantra recitation you can view here: https://bom.to/TryzB0H7lAIw8

Everyone should, according to their own time and circumstances, try to recite at least 1 round per day ^^

Venerable Master Hsuan Hua once said:

"……..All Buddhist scriptures are very important, especially the Śūraṅgama Sūtra. Wherever the Śūraṅgama Sūtra exists, there is the Dharma firmly established in the world. When the Śūraṅgama Sūtra is no longer present, the era of the Decline of the Dharma appears immediately. The Śūraṅgama Sūtra is the true body of the Buddha, the Śūraṅgama Sūtra is the Buddha's relics, the Śūraṅgama Sūtra is the stupa enshrining the Buddha. Therefore, all Buddhist followers must exert all their strength and ability to support and preserve this Śūraṅgama Sūtra. Why?"

In the Dharma of Extinction, it is said: "In the Final Dharma Age, the Shurangama Sutra disappears first, and other scriptures gradually disappear afterward." If the Shurangama Sutra is not lost, the True Dharma will manifest in the present. Therefore, as Buddhists, we must use our very lives to uphold the Shurangama Sutra, putting all our strength and abilities into protecting it, establishing vows and practices to uphold the Shurangama Sutra, so that the Shurangama Sutra may remain in the world forever, flourish widely, circulate in every particle of dust, spread to all corners of the world, and extend infinitely throughout the Dharma realm. By doing so, the radiance of the True Dharma will illuminate everywhere.place.

If in this world, there is no one reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, then the Demon King will appear. If even one person continues to recite it, the heaven demons of Ba Tuần will not dare to appear. Because what they fear the most is the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. What they want to destroy the most is the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. When the Dharma begins to decline, the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra will disappear first, including the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra. At that time, the heaven demons of Ba Tuần will appear and rampage everywhere. Then there will be no heaven and earth, no Buddha, and they will be absolutely fearless. Therefore, I advise every Buddhist (both laypeople and monastics) to memorize the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra and recite it every day; this is exactly the act of protection.Dharma, and make Dharma endure for a long time, do not underestimate meaningless things and relationships.

Buddhist practitioners not only need to deeply understand the principles contained in the Shurangama Sutra in order to ensure that the True Dharma endures for a long time and that false teachings are eternally eradicated, but they must also advocate the Shurangama Sutra – promoting the Shurangama Sutra everywhere, preaching the Shurangama Sutra in all places, and safeguarding the Shurangama Sutra everywhere, reciting the Shurangama Mantra. Buddhist devotees need to devote themselves wholeheartedly to this responsibility.

In the Shurangama Sutra, the Buddha teaches:

• Oh Ananda! If there are sentient beings in any country in the world who can use flower bark, palm leaves, white paper, or white cloth to transcribe this Lankavatara mantra, and then keep it in a fragrant pouch. Even if someone's mind is dull and they have not yet been able to recite or memorize the mantra, if they carry the fragrant pouch with them or keep it in their house, they should know that throughout their life, they will not be harmed by any kind of poison.

• After I pass into nirvana, if there are sentient beings in the time of the Decline of the Dharma who are able to recite this mantra themselves or teach others to recite this mantra, it should be known that those who recite and uphold such a mantra: fire cannot burn them, water cannot drown them, and whether it is strong or weak poison, it also cannot harm them. Likewise, all evil spells of gods, dragons, ghosts, or demons cannot control them. When their mind has attained true concentration, any substances created from spells, curses, poisons mixed with gold or silver, herbs containing insects or snakes, or any toxic matter, once these things enter the mouthWhatever belongs to that person will all become sweet nectar. All vicious demons and malevolent spirits who intend to harm others will not be able to harbor evil thoughts. Obstacles of gods, demon kings who have committed evil, and their followers, because they have received the deep grace of the Buddha and have been transformed, will always protect those who recite the mantra.

• Any virtuous men who recite or transcribe this Lankavatara mantra, carry the mantra with them, or place the mantra in a suitable location for offerings, from this life to future lives, they will not be born into poor or lowly families or in places without peace and happiness. Suppose these beings do not personally perform meritorious deeds, the Buddhas of the ten directions will also transfer their own merits to that person. Therefore, across countless lifetimes, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, innumerable lifetimes, unspeakable, unspeakable, they will often be born in the same place as the Buddhas. Their boundless merits will be as dense as clusters of narrow-leaved fruits. They will dwell togethera place to cultivate wholesome Dharma and permanently not be separated from the Buddhas.

• Furthermore, this mantra can restore purity to those who have violated precepts, allow those who have not yet received precepts to receive them, inspire diligence in those who are not yet diligent, grant wisdom to those lacking it, quickly purify those who are impure, and help those who have not yet maintained vegetarianism and precepts to accomplish them on their own.

• Hey Ananda! Suppose that good men have violated precepts before receiving the mantra. After reciting the mantra, their precept-breaking sins, whether major or minor, will simultaneously be destroyed. Suppose these people may have drunk alcohol, eaten the five pungent foods, or consumed all kinds of impure foods, yet all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, vajra spirits, celestial beings, immortals, and deities will not regard that as a fault. Or suppose these people wear tattered clothes, yet all their actions remain pure. Even if they do not establish a Dharma platform, do not enter the Dharma assembly, and do not practice the Way, if they recite the mantraThen the merit is like having entered the sacred assembly to practice the Path – not a bit different. Or suppose these people have committed the five gravest rebellious sins and should fall into the Avici Hell, or they are monks who have violated four serious precepts punishable by expulsion, or they are nuns who have violated eight serious precepts punishable by expulsion, but once they have recited this mantra, all such grave karmas are entirely destroyed, not even a hair remains, just like a whirlwind blowing away a sandbank.

• Ananda! Suppose there are beings in the present life or in past lives who have never repented for all the heavy and light offenses they have committed over countless countless eons until now. Yet if they can recite, transcribe, carry a mantra with them, or place a mantra in their dwelling – in the house, garden, or inn – then the accumulated karmic offenses of theirs will dissolve like snow being melted. Before long, they will all attain the Patience of Non-birth (Amala-vijñāna).

• Again, Ananda! Suppose there is a woman who is childless and wishes for children, if she can sincerely recite and memorize the mantra or can carry this Great White Pagoda Tán Cái Mantra with her (Lăng Nghiêm Mantra), she will give birth to children with blessings of wisdom. Or those who wish to live long will indeed live long. Or those who desire perfect results will swiftly achieve fulfillment, and this also applies to life span and physical strength. After death, they will go, according to their wishes, to be reborn in the realms of the ten directions and will certainly not be born in lowly border regions. Let alone be born among miscellaneous kinds of sentient beings.

• Hey Ananda! You should know that this mantra is always protected by 84,000 Bodhisattvas in the lineage of Vajra Treasury King. Each of them has numerous vajra attendants, and day and night they always follow to protect the person who recites the mantra. Even if there are sentient beings with a distracted mind and lacking proper concentration, if their mind remembers and their mouth recites the mantra, the Bodhisattvas in the lineage of Vajra Treasury King will still always accompany to protect them. Especially for those virtuous men who have generated a firm aspiration for the Way.

• Moreover, the Bodhisattvas in the lineage of the Vajra Treasury King will silently concentrate on awakening the consciousness of the mantra practitioner. Then the person's mind will be able to clearly remember all things throughout 84,000 eons without any confusion. From that point onward until the final body, in every lifetime, they will not be reborn as tormented ghosts, violent ghosts, filthy ghosts, extremely filthy ghosts, stunted-form ghosts, chi-sucking ghosts, hungry ghosts, or any other kinds of evil beings, whether with form, formless, with thought, or without thought.

• O Ananda! Suppose anywhere, whether in a village, district, or any nation, there occurs famine, disease, armed forces, robbers, conflicts, and all sorts of calamities, then write down this mantra and place it at the four city gates, the towers, or hang it on flags. Teach all the people in that nation to welcome, honor, bow to, and wholeheartedly offer this mantra. Instruct each citizen there to carry the mantra with them or place it in their home. In this way, all misfortunes will be eradicated.

• O Ananda! In any country or anywhere where beings follow this mantra, the gods and dragons will rejoice, the weather will be favorable, grains will ripen abundantly, and all people will be at peace. This mantra can also prevent all calamities caused by the strange and evil transformations of the stars in each region. The people will not die prematurely, will not be bound in chains, will sleep peacefully day and night, and will not experience nightmares.

• Ananda! In the Saha world, there are 84,000 stars that signal misfortunes. Among them, 28 major stars are omens of the worst events. And among these, there are eight great stars that are omens of extremely bad events. They appear in all kinds of forms and can give rise to all kinds of unusual disasters when they appear in the world. However, in any place where this mantra exists, within 12 du-week cycles it will become a protected area, and all misfortunes and bad omens will be eradicated and can never penetrate it.

• Therefore, the Tathagata has proclaimed this mantra to protect new practitioners in future lives, helping them attain right concentration, peace of body and mind, and a state of security and freedom. Moreover, they will not be harmed by all demons, evil spirits, and enemies, nor by the misfortunes and karmic debts from past lives from beginningless time.

• This mantra can save the world, help sentient beings escape terrifying fear, and accomplish transcendent wisdom.

• Suppose that you and fellow practitioners, along with other aspirants in the future, establish the altar exactly as I have taught and uphold the precepts according to the Dharma, receive the precepts from a pure Sangha, and also recite this mantra without doubt or regret; if such a virtuous man, at his very own body born of his parents, does not understand with his mind, then it is as if the Tathagatas of the ten directions have spoken falsely!

• Ananda, suppose there is a person who brings seven kinds of treasures filling the emptiness across all ten directions, offering them to the Buddhas as numerous as the grains of dust, with a mind of respectful devotion without any negligence. What do you think, this person, due to the causal conditions of offering to the Buddhas in this way, would receive much merit or not?

• Ananda replied, the space is limitless, and treasures are also infinite. In the past, someone offered the Buddha seven coins, and upon giving up their life, they even attained the position of a Wheel-Turning Sage King. Let alone now, with space being boundless, the Buddha realms have been filled with seven kinds of treasures offered. Even if one were to contemplate endlessly for countless eons, it could not be known. How could such meritorious virtue have any bounds?

• The Buddha told Ānanda, all Buddhas, Tathāgatas, do not speak false words. For example, if someone commits the four great crimes and the ten pāricchattaka offenses, they will, in a moment, have to experience the Avīci hell in one place and then another, continuing until countless uninterrupted hells in the ten directions, with no place where they do not suffer. If this person, with a single thought, uses this Dharma gate to enlighten someone who has not learned it in the degenerate age, then that person's karmic offenses are immediately eliminated. Transforming the cause of suffering in hell into a land of bliss. Their merit surpasses the merit of their previous offerings by hundreds, thousands, millions, or even countless times. In this way, even the number of examples cannot fully describe it.cannot fully express.

• Ananda, if there are beings who know how to recite the sutra, know how to chant this mantra, even if the Tathagata speaks for countless eons, it will never be exhausted. If one follows the Tathagata’s instructions and practices according to the teachings, one will directly reach the Bodhi path without being obstructed by worldly hindrances.

Rejoicing to share, copying without permission is not needed. Currently, Quang Tu and friends have devoted themselves to chanting this mantra 7 times daily. Those who wish to participate may comment below the post!

tieu_de: WHAT OBSTACLES WILL FAMILY FEUDS AND HOSTILE RELATIONSHIPS CREATE?
tom_tat: The consciousness of animals after being killed, when a person's righteous energy is strong, can only silently wait for an opportunity to seek revenge. However, when a person's righteous energy is weak, for example when
noi_dung:
WHAT OBSTACLES ARE CREATED WHEN KARMIC ENEMIES HARASS?

After animals are killed, their spirits, when a person's righteous energy is strong, can only silently wait for an opportunity to claim revenge. However, when a person's righteous energy weakens, such as when their blessings decrease or in old age with a frail body, these grudges and vengeful spirits will begin to take advantage of the situation to retaliate; some people may develop serious illnesses, families may not be harmonious and peaceful, and careers may face obstacles...

What obstacles will these grudges and vengeful spirits create when they cause trouble?

1. (Hostile ghosts and karmic enemies will disturb the mind), causing oneself to sometimes speak words that are opposite to one’s intention, (having nightmares, a bad temper, and worsening memory.)

2. When reciting sutras or chanting the Buddha's name, (thoughts are incessant, and the mind is unstable.)

3. They will cling inside the body, causing (the things one eats, the amount of food, to have to increase significantly.)

4. Some animal consciousnesses will cling to the human body, (causing one to become increasingly foolish.)

Enemies and adversaries, some are from this life, and some are enemies and adversaries from many past lives, even from time without beginning until now. If we continue killing and eating meat, and continue creating bad karmic connections with sentient beings, we are creating new enemies and adversaries.

Recite sutras, do good deeds abundantly … dedicate the merit back to the enemies and adversaries, make apologies and repent to the enemies and adversaries, and sincerely invite the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Immortals to help resolve these karmic ties, dedicating the merit accumulated back to the enemies and adversaries.

Normally, by diligently performing many meritorious deeds and dedicating them to your past enemies and those who have wronged you, your body and mind will be well, and your life, work, and career will become better and more favorable, while minimizing obstacles, and your spiritual practice will become increasingly peaceful and smooth.

Homage to Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva

Compassion of the Ancient Buddha of the South Sea.

tieu_de: PRACTICE MUST BE CONSISTENT EVERY DAY AND NOT SKIPPED.
tom_tat: ( SCHEDULE FOR BEGINNERS ). 🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿
noi_dung:
PRACTICE MUST BE CONTINUOUS EVERY DAY, NOT TO BE SKIPPED.

(SCHEDULE FOR BEGINNERS).

🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿

If a student has to learn new lessons and review old ones every day to be ready for teachers to call on them for quizzes at any time, then training in spiritual practice is similar. One must always practice without interruption. Why? Because in the process of practice, if we are inconsistent, practicing one day and resting for ten, then when faced with circumstances, we will be confused and not know what to do. Without focused effort, one cannot develop concentration; when encountering adversity, one will be shaken. It is no different from a student being called by the teacher to recite lessons, but who has been lazy every day and refuses to review, and thus fails the exam.

For those who are just starting to have good intentions. When beginning to practice Buddhism, you must clearly understand this. If you are new, start with the simplest things; do not be greedy for the difficult and complicated. It is like a child: if they try to run before learning to crawl, they cannot do it. Therefore, we must finish kindergarten before going to grade 1. Do well in grade 1 before moving on to grade 2... it must be step by step like that.

What should beginners practice?

1/ Recite the holy name of one Buddha or Bodhisattva that you love and respect the most every day 1000 times (equivalent to 10 malas).

2/ Learn the Great Compassion Mantra. If you haven't memorized it yet, write it down and read it by hand 5, 7, 9, or 21 times, up to 108 times. Recite the Vajra Mantra 1 to 3 times, with the heart mantra of Vajra recited 108 times...

(If you still have time, read a few chapters of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra or any sutra you like best, or copy a sutra to cultivate merit).

Diligently do good deeds and abandon evil deeds so that your merit will increase; sufficient merit and virtue will help you practice diligently without fear of obstacles or afflictions.

Try to diligently cultivate your mind and accumulate virtue, frequently repent, and maintain a consistent daily practice schedule like this for the first one to two years to eliminate karma. Once you gradually get used to such a practice schedule, it can then be gradually increased.

During the initial period of practice, you will face challenges. Each person's challenges are not the same. But these are unannounced tests. Here, QT says to reassure you that if you practice fully every day, you will be able to overcome them all. Each time you pass a test, it means that your level of practice has also increased by one step.

Finally, one must keep a pure heart and maintain clean thoughts. Keep speech proper. Do not let it become tainted.

QT hopes that all of you try to spend time practicing daily in order to eliminate karmic obstacles and also to find long-lasting peace in mindfulness.

tom_tat: ( Excerpts from the teachings of our beloved Teacher ). ☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️

SHOULD NOT BE ARROGANT WHEN DOING BUDDHIST WORKS.

☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️☘️

You must understand that, Buddhist affairs always have two sides; essentially, they are secondary, while practicing the path is the main matter. If fame arises from Buddhist activities, it can be said 1000/1000% that one will become arrogant, just like everyone else. Therefore, you must understand why you are doing these things: For fame and profit, to help others practice, or for the sake of praise?

Those who engage in Buddhist activities but are arrogant are as numerous as the sand of the Ganges River, whereas those who remain the same whether famous or not are the ones who are truly commendable; you must not let these things consume you.

It can also be said that in the destiny of many people, they are born to have great fame and fortune, but why don't they choose it? Simply because they do not like those things, they feel that it truly has no meaning at all. Why is that? Because at any time, fame, position, money, material things, ... they are all double-edged swords. They can turn you into a completely different person from your true nature, and once you obtain something superior, you will think you are outstanding, talented... Let me tell you... if you only know how to chase external appearances to polish your name, to bring back thingsIf the temporary, unreal things exist, then I sincerely tell you that you are extremely pitiable when you have to live in a long night full of dreams, when being made insane by the 'Ego' with delusions, and you have to endure the influence of the law of karma and reincarnation for hundreds of thousands of lifetimes.

tieu_de: TODAY I MUST DIE, NO MORE DELUSIONS! LET EVERYTHING GO, JUST THINK OF AMITABHA BUDDHA: 'I AM HERE WAITING'
tom_tat: 🌲You cannot enter the realm if you do not let go; as soon as you let go, you immediately enter the (realm) 💧In modern times, Master Yin Guang had an extremely wonderful method, teaching us how to realize and enter it. When
noi_dung:
TODAY I MUST DIE, NO MORE DREAMING! LET EVERYTHING GO, JUST THINK OF AMITABHA BUDDHA: "I AM HERE WAITING"

🌲You cannot enter the realm if you do not let go; as soon as you let go, you immediately enter (the realm)

💧In modern times, Master Yin Guang had an extremely wonderful method, teaching us how to attain enlightenment. During the elderly master's lifetime, there was a long period when he secluded himself at Lingyan Mountain Temple in Suzhou, which was the final place for his spiritual practice. I visited that seclusion room (the room used for seclusion). It was very small, extremely simple, with only a square table. On the altar was a statue of the Buddha; there was absolutely nothing else, very simple! One Buddha statue, a pair of candlesticks, an incense burner, a wooden fish (small percussion instrument), and a small wooden clapper. Behind the Buddha statue was a large character written by the master himself. He wrote the character "Tử".This method is very clever! It makes you feel that death is near the moment you see it, so tell me, is there anything you still cannot let go of?

🍁 Therefore, in the current era, I myself often think: Our life span to this day is over, we must die today, what else is there to dream about? Therefore, we will be zealous, thinking about death, already dead, death is ahead, can we even think about eating, wearing, staying, going? Can we still hope to enjoy it? No, there is not! At the moment, there is only one idea left, praying for the birth of the Pure Land. Everything is dropped, only thinking of Amitabha Buddha, "I am here waiting for you, please come and guide me." Except for this one thought, there is no idea at all

.

🍒Is there anything in this world that truly belongs to me? Even my own body does not! We must use this mindset to recite the Buddha's name, just as the Amitabha Sutra says: “Whether for one day, or two days, up to seven days,” one will be reborn in the Pure Land. It is true, not false! Today, if Amitabha Buddha has not arrived, it is as if the time has not yet come; tomorrow, think the same way; every day, think the same way. What does this mean? It is setting an example for fellow practitioners to learn Buddhism, affirming that one day, Amitabha Buddha will come. Amitabha Buddha says: “You have set an example, you can come to the Land of Ultimate Bliss.”

✍️Excerpt: Commentary on the Larger Sutra of Perfected Purity, Volume 9

Lecturer: Elder Dharma Master Jing Kong

tieu_de: ACHIEVEMENTS MANIFESTED WHEN RECITING LANG NGHIEM MANTRA
tom_tat: 1. After overcoming the obstacles, after a period of practice, one will see the effects of the Lingyan Mantra manifested in life. Initially, there may be headaches, or pain in the limbs and various parts of the body.
noi_dung:
ACHIEVEMENTS MANIFESTED WHEN CHANTING LANG NGHIEM MANTRA

1. Overcoming the following obstacles after a period of practice, one will see the effects of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra manifest in life.

First is a headache, or pain in the limbs, or other parts of the body.

2. If the head aches, and the pain is in the center of the head (not the entire head), it means that ignorant and deluded karma is being eliminated.

Once you have memorized the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, in the future you will be able to memorize anything.

Headaches are often caused by the body's reaction, for a very simple reason: Master Lăng Nghiêm himself has a very high frequency, so when a new practitioner begins practice, there will be a period of adjustment to adapt to that frequency. Headaches are one of the manifestations of the elimination of karma.

3. Research by Japanese doctors and PhDs indicates that if in the morning you read words very quickly and loudly, it will affect the brain, brain cells, and brain regions. If you regularly wake up in the morning and practice the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, chanting very quickly and loudly (be careful of neck pain), over time your brain cells will develop well.

4. If you have a headache on the right side, only on the right side and not the entire head or the top of the head, it could be that beings in the invisible realm are affecting you to request to follow you in studying and practicing. It could also be vengeful spirits or grudge-holders coming in hope of receiving dedication. Or it could be ancestors, grandparents, or parents who have passed in many previous lives seeking help.

If the right side of the head aches, pray and dedicate merit to those who follow you, or to the nine generations of ancestors, grudge-holders, praying that these beings may be liberated. Pray and practice, and if the headache disappears, then you will know that it was indeed caused by the influence of the invisible realm.

5. Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra will grant whatever you wish. If you want a house, you will have a house; if you want a car, you will have a car; if you want a lover, you will have a lover... Therefore, try to reduce your desires, because getting whatever you want is actually spending your merit.

There is only one wish: to become a Buddha in order to save sentient beings. When you make such a vow and practice accordingly, naturally, other small wishes will be fulfilled, supplementing your greater wish.

Always remember, whether you are rich or have money, ... it is to help sentient beings.

6. When practicing the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra successfully, if I get angry at someone even a little, they will be affected by my mental power and feel restless or uncomfortable.

If my mental power is strong, then when I get angry at someone, they might even be struck by my Guardian Deities until they feel soreness, or the person I am angry at might encounter an accident.

Therefore, when reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, one should also recite "Nam Mô Đại Bi Quán Thế Âm Bồ Tát" to transform anger into compassion and loving-kindness, as only then will it be beneficial.

Pay close attention to this, Mantras are like a double-edged sword; once you have mastered them, you can use them however you want. The Vajra Protectors are neither good nor evil, and they usually follow to protect you, so whatever you think, they act accordingly.

From my personal experience, Lam, when I am angry at someone or irritated by someone, they become very exhausted, even those who are practiced in cultivation are heavily affected, let alone those who are not practiced; just a little anger from me can cause them to have an accident immediately.

This practice is so powerful that it can follow you into the next life. Even if in the next life you know nothing about Buddhism and have no practice, the intentions you generate will still strongly affect others.

Therefore, to practice the Shurangama Mantra, one must be compassionate, extremely compassionate.

7. If you happen to make mistakes, break precepts, or harbor negative thoughts toward those who are practicing diligently, you will often be heavily affected. Therefore, you should repent and chant "Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva" many times, and this will resolve it.

8. Currently, the only one who explains each line of the Shurangama Mantra is the Late Venerable Master Hsuan Hua, and he also said that his explanation is just one of the countless meanings and wondrous functions of the Shurangama Mantra, which shows how subtle and inconceivable the mantra truly is.

Simply reciting the Shurangama Mantra allows a person to emit boundless light, not to mention attaining realization or achieving Dharma.

9. Reciting the Shurangama Mantra according to Eastern Esoteric (Dongmi) methods, or specifically in Vietnam, does not require receiving the Empowerment (Abhisheka) yet can still achieve its extraordinary effects.

So you can practice the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra on your own without needing anyone to initiate you, because the verses in the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra primarily ask for initiation within them.

However, if you are permitted or guided by a Master who specializes in practicing the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, you will receive stronger energy resonance and achieve results faster.

10. In reality, many temples have removed the morning practice involving the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, with only a few temples following the old tradition still retaining it.

The Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is fundamentally necessary for everyone, regardless of which Mahayana or Vajrayana tradition they follow.

Practicing Pure Land Buddhism with the recitation of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra will gain very strong spiritual support to protect them in reaching the Western Pure Land. In the first section of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, there is a line "Resorting and paying homage to Amitabha Buddha," so practicing the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra does not conflict with Pure Land practice.

However, some current temples following the style of the Pure Land Learning Association omit the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra in the morning - which is truly very regrettable.

Those who practice meditation should especially recite the Lengyue Mantra, because meditating without the Lengyue Mantra can easily lead one astray into demonic paths and be possessed by demons. Usually, in the present time, because meditation is done carelessly, no demon would bother to look at oneself.

11. The Lengyue Sutra is said because of the Lengyue Mantra. In the Lengyue Sutra, the perfect penetrative wisdom of Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta is mindfulness of the Buddha, and that of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara is the ear sense; both of these Bodhisattvas reside in the Land of Ultimate Bliss beside Amitabha Buddha. One may ask, with the Lengyue Sutra and the Lengyue Mantra being like this, how could they oppose Amitabha Buddha or the Pure Land path?

Don't say that practicing a lot makes one less focused; you only need to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra once a day, and during the rest of the time focus on reciting Buddha's name throughout the day—how can that not be focused?

Moreover, when the mind is fully concentrated, whatever you recite is done with full focus.

Giving up one thing to take another is precisely an attachment.

Master Ấn Quang often advised people to recite the Great Compassion Mantra.

Late Venerable Tuyên Hóa advised that, in addition to the Great Compassion Mantra, people should also learn and recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra.

The two mentioned figures are both exceptionally wise, both are incarnations of Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva (Master Yinguang) and Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva (the late Venerable Master Xuanhua); they both advise us to hold onto the Great Compassion Mantra and the Śūraṅgama Mantra.

12. The Masters and Patriarchs who passed away in Vietnam, who preserved the lineage of Buddhism in ancient Vietnam, did any of them abandon the Śūraṅgama Mantra? No, they still passed away beautifully indeed.

Nowadays, abandoning the Śūraṅgama Mantra is precisely the crux of the decline of Buddhism.

As the Sutra says, in the degenerate age of the Dharma, there remain four words "A Di Đà Phật". Nowadays, if we only know how to recite "A Di Đà Phật", that in itself is promoting the degenerate age of the Dharma.

One must practice the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra and when reciting, one must say "Nam mô A Di Đà Phật"; one must not omit the words "Nam mô"—this is how one preserves the Buddhist Dharma.

The arguments about single-mindedness, or exclusive focus, are only theoretical discussions and do not constitute actual practice.

Don't just talk about the six syllables of the holy name; if someone has deep practice and continuously recites the Rebirth Mantra, how many syllables there are, at that time it is not just six but twenty or thirty syllables that can still be focused on single-mindedly.

13. The accomplishment of all Dharma practices should rely on the Śūraṅgama Mantra as the foundation; preserving the Śūraṅgama Mantra is precisely to propagate the True Dharma so that it does not decline.

Those who encourage others to recite the Śūraṅgama Mantra, practice the Śūraṅgama Mantra, or wear the Śūraṅgama Mantra are all protected by Vajra Treasury Kings.

14. If possible, recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra once in the morning, and if possible, recite it once more in the evening; in this way, reciting it twice a day adds righteous energy to heaven and earth.

Lam Son Village,

12/03/2021

tieu_de: Experience Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra Shared by You 'LeePhan'!
tom_tat: I take advantage of eating vegetarian and reciting the five-section morning and evening long dharani, and in my free time, I recite the heart dharani. Within 3-6 months, concentration improves very clearly, syllables are easy to visualize, and obstacles are revealed.
noi_dung:
Experience Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra Shared by Friend "LeePhan"!

I take the opportunity to eat vegetarian and recite the full-length sutra five times in the morning and evening; during free time, I recite the mantra with focus. Within 3-6 months, my concentration improves noticeably, the syllables become easy to visualize, and any entanglements are instructed to be resolved.

The mind and temperament are subdued, with less anger, resentment, and ignorance. Desires are extinguished, no longer influenced by lustful tendencies except when the intention arises from marital life.

In dreams, one can see the realms interacting and the karmic consequences one is currently experiencing will appear clearly as a reminder. For example, in the past, when I consumed a lot of pork, I dreamed that my body grew a pig's tail, which was very frightening... Once in a dream, I saw the wealth and land gods in a glass cabinet sighing and tapping on the glass as if they wanted to come out. When I checked, I saw many statues of wealth and land gods inside the cabinet. I reminded my family to take them out for worship. The spirits present in the house appear in dreams...

Wisdom is increasingly improving and expanding. There is no longer the desire for supernatural powers as before. Only the aspiration for liberating wisdom remains.

Being exposed to many meaningful materials and writings, reading scriptures is easier to understand than before.

When eating vegetarian food, the body is fragrant, even the excrement has a gentle sweet smell. When eating non-vegetarian food, sweat is unpleasant and smells bad.

Besides, there are many issues that cannot be shared here. This is just for reference; everyone has different foundations, so please do not get attached to these phenomena. Regards

tieu_de: MIRACULOUSLY RESPONDING, THE VENERABLE MONK LĂNG NGHIÊM
tom_tat: Roughly about 10 years ago, back when I was still studying in the city, I went home to visit my mother during the Lunar New Year. When I returned, I brought along the "Diamond Sutra" and "The Vows and Practices of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra," quietly thinking to myself
noi_dung:
MIRACULOUS SPIRITUAL POWER OF CHU LANG NGHIEM

Roughly about 10 years ago, at that time I was still studying in the city, and during the Lunar New Year I went home to visit my mother. When I went back, I brought along the "Diamond Sutra" and "Bodhisattva Samantabhadra's Vows and Practices," thinking to myself that during my free time over the New Year I would take the opportunity to chant and read them.

At home, there was a young grandson, and while I was reading, he played around nearby. Seeing me chanting, he closed his eyes and listened. So I deliberately read aloud, thinking to myself that perhaps it would be beneficial for him.

At that time, I was reading the “Diamond Sutra,” and after finishing one section, he said, “When I read this, I saw a very strange scene; I saw in another world a Buddha, surrounded by many monks sitting and listening.” Hearing that, I was also startled, thinking to myself that my nephew must be imagining things, making up stories. (*Cữu: Uncle).

Then I switched to reading “The Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,” and just as I finished one round, my grandchild turned to me and said, “I see a very large elephant, it has three pairs of tusks. When you read, there is a Bodhisattva holding a small bowl pouring water over your head, and then that water turns into rays of light. The elephant does the same, it uses its trunk to spray water over your head. Then those rays of light seem to wash away all the impurities on your body in one go.”

After experiencing this twice, I also vaguely believed it, because a child could not imagine such things. Moreover, since childhood, he had never been exposed to Buddhist teachings, and in the house, apart from me, no one believed in Buddha, and of course, there were never any Buddha paintings or statues worshiped in the house. Isn't the six-tusked elephant the mount of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra? And the six tusks symbolize the perfection of the six paramitas.

This startled me quite a bit because at that time I was fond of reciting the “Lăng Nghiêm Mantra.” One day, while I was reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, my grandchild ran up and exclaimed, “When I recite this Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, I see on the left and right of the altar, each side has 2 Great Heavenly Kings standing. They are very large people, and also tall. I recognized that these 4 people are none other than the Four Great Heavenly Kings. In the animated Journey to the West, there are 4 Heavenly Kings, one holding a lute, one holding a pagoda, one holding a sword... so I recognized them as soon as I saw.”

“Outside the Four Great Heavenly Kings, there were many other Devas, with very strange appearances and clothing, all different. Some of them weren’t wearing any clothes at all, but I felt they were very good, as if they had come to protect you. Outside of these Devas, there were also many people, layer upon layer like soldiers, holding staffs and various weapons in their hands. The more you chanted, the more of them appeared. Behind you stood a Bodhisattva, this Bodhisattva was extraordinarily tall, with a snake coiled around the body, a blue-colored face, many bumps on the body, upward-curving teeth, and fire rising from the back. This Bodhisattva was very tall and large, resemblinglike a mountain, an extraordinarily ugly appearance, extraordinarily terrifying, but it seems as if all the Angels and soldiers were arranged and controlled by him.

Hearing that, I was even more startled. Isn't it that in the "Lankavatara Sutra," the Buddha expounds on all kinds of merits of the mantras? In the Sutra, there is a passage: "King Brahma, Indra, and the Four Great Heavenly Kings all at once bowed before the Buddha, then said to the Buddha: 'If there are any virtuous people practicing in such a way, we will wholeheartedly protect them and make their deeds in this present life fulfill their wishes.'" Perhaps my grandson saw the Four Great Heavenly Kings as written in the Sutra. Following them were countless River Gods, Mountain Gods, and Sea Gods, all clamoring to stand and vow. Finally, there were 84,000 innumerable Vajra Scripture Kings.Bodhisattvas, along with countless followers before the Buddha, we also vow to protect those who practice, and if evil spirits disturb us, we will use the Vajra Mallet to smash their heads like dust particles.

84,000 is just an example figure, meaning infinite, countless billions, millions of millions multiplied by a countless number. Amazed, at the same time I also think, we, ordinary people, so deeply attached to greed, anger, and delusion, have no merit at all, so on what basis can chanting the Mantra summon so many Vajras, so many Angels and heavenly warriors to protect us? The only explanation is perhaps that they come to protect the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. As the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra says: “All Buddhas in the ten directions are born from this mantra, so the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra can be called the mother of all Buddhas. All Tathagatas in the ten directions rely on this mantra to accomplish the path to awakening.Supremely perfect, completely enlightened.

They manifest in countless forms like the number of dust particles in the worlds of water to turn the wheel of Dharma, teach sentient beings, give them assurance in the ten directions, and save beings from suffering. The Lăng Nghiêm mantra is precisely the heart of the Buddhas in the ten directions. Wherever this mantra exists, there is the Buddha; whoever can recite this mantra is in harmony with the Buddha, and therefore all Vajra Dharmapala protect him.

The scene above is described from the perspective of a child; we believe that no child could imagine what is described in the scriptures in such a way. Having gone through this experience, I have become even more steadfast in my faith in Buddhism, as the "Diamond Sutra" says: "The words spoken by the Tathagata are true, like truth, not false."

Source: Mat Hy_ Collected and Translated.

tieu_de: A TREE ON YOUR HEAD
tom_tat: When you recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, a white 'umbrella' (Bạch Tản Cái) appears above the top of your head. Depending on your level of precept observance and dedication, this umbrella may be large or small, able to cover you.
noi_dung:
A UMBRELLA TREE ON THE TOP OF YOUR HEAD

When you recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, a white "umbrella" (Bạch Tản Cái) appears above the crown of your head. Depending on your level of precepts and diligence, this umbrella can be large or small, protecting you more or less.

Of course, the larger the umbrella, the more people it can protect.

If the umbrella is small, it protects only you; a larger umbrella can protect two people, three people, a family, a village, and even the whole country.

The pure Masters, by reciting once, can cover the entire Dharma realm with an umbrella.

If you have just started practicing and your skill is not yet proficient, reciting 10 times or 20 times, the umbrella would only cover yourself.

Nevertheless, keep trying, because a Master who recites once and can make the umbrella encompass the entire Dharma realm has reached the pinnacle of practice.

If you recite 10 times or 20 times and the umbrella still only covers yourself, it is because you are only at the beginning.

Sufficient in quantity will transform into quality, so even knowing that reciting it 100 times, this umbrella can only cover oneself, one should strive even more to advance in practice.

What is the benefit of a tree providing shade for you? You will be "invisible". Just like practicing the Marici Dharma, when you practice the Lankavatara Dharma, you can also be "invisible." If you stand under this tree, no one can see you or know your skills, you can conceal your identity, those who want to harm you cannot find your trace, thieves or robbers cannot take your property, and water, fire, or poison cannot harm you.

Lăng Nghiêm is the King of Mantras, because it encompasses the assemblies of Buddhas, the assemblies of Bodhisattvas, the assemblies of Devas, the assemblies of Ghosts and Spirits, and the assemblies of Vajra Guardians. Lăng Nghiêm also includes means of Dharma that are hearing, benefiting, venerating, summoning, and subduing, so there is no Dharma that is not contained in Lăng Nghiêm.

The Lăng Nghiêm Mantra can also liberate sentient beings, and not only can it liberate, it does so in an excellent way. Within the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, there is Amitabha Buddha as well as Akshobhya Buddha or Medicine Buddha. When you recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra to invoke liberation, the person being liberated will be protected and guided to the Pure Land.

Every morning when you wake up, recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra once, and an umbrella immediately appears above your head, shielding you. At night before going to sleep, recite it once, and the umbrella is also there protecting you, ensuring you a peaceful sleep.

If you want to protect someone or pray for someone’s safety, think of that person and recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, and an umbrella will immediately appear above the person for whom you are praying.

If you love someone and care for them, you should pray for their peace by reciting Sutras or Mantras instead of letting random thoughts wander in your mind. Wandering thoughts are not as effective as reciting Mantras. Reciting various Mantras is not as effective as the Lankavatara Mantra. So the best is to sincerely recite the Lankavatara Mantra to pray for safety and deliverance.

Today, whether the umbrella has been created or not, whether it protects you or not all depends on your sincerity.

A canopy shining white

Radiating five-colored beams

Covering the entire Dharma realm

By those who cultivate and attain.

A white bright canopy

Abides over all practiced dharmas

The practitioner keeps wholesome mindfulness

Whatever they wish for will be granted.

A white bright canopy

Eliminates greed, anger, and ignorance

The Buddha mother smiles

The practitioner reaches a blissful realm.

Lam Son Village,

tieu_de: ONCE A THOUGHT OF ANGER ARISES, SACRED LOTUS TEA TURNS INTO BOILING WATER
tom_tat: In Tainan, there is a monastery led by a Nun. One day, the Nun was awakened by the sound of crying. As soon as she opened her eyes, she saw a group of people, old and young, men and women, all of their bodies burned, kneeling before her. The Nun was shocked.
noi_dung:
WITH ONE ANGERED THOUGHT, KAMLO'S LAVA TURNS INTO BOILING WATER

In Tainan, there was a temple led by a Buddhist nun. One day, the nun was awakened by the sound of crying. As soon as she opened her eyes, she saw a group of people—old and young, male and female—whose bodies were all burned, kneeling before her. The nun was astonished and asked, “Why are you all suffering like this? Who has done this to you?”

Among them, a person at the front said, “This was all done by the disciple in charge of protection, named [Name], of our master, who threw boiling water on us!”

Upon hearing this, the nun was horrified and asked further, “When did this happen?”

The leader answered, "Just a moment ago, we didn’t understand why she threw boiling water at us. Seeing her holding a glass of clean water and chanting the Great Compassion Mantra, we thought she would bestow nectar upon us. Who would have thought, she would throw boiling water at us instead! Please, Master, take control for our sake!"

The nun wanted to continue asking for clarification, but suddenly heard a rooster crow. Awakening, she realized that it had all been a Nam Kha dream.

The more I think about it, the more confusing it seems. That Dharma protector disciple they talked about is usually very compassionate, so why would he use boiling water to pour on invisible beings today?

After finishing the meal, the nun immediately asked a disciple to call that Dharma protector over to ask about it. When the Dharma protector arrived, the nun asked.

- This morning, did you do anything unusual at home?”

The disciple replied:

- No, this morning I was at home still practicing the morning session, and suddenly I felt that the atmosphere in the house was somewhat strange, so I recited 21 repetitions of the Great Compassion Mantra to purify it.

The nun, after hearing this, thought for a moment, then suddenly stared at her and said:

- What were you thinking when you sprinkled the Great Compassion water?

The Dharma protector replied:

- I used the Great Compassion water to drive away evil spirits, so what could be wrong, Master?

The nun replied:

- You were terribly mistaken. When you practiced your morning session, all your envious enemies and creditor spirits were very happy to come to listen to the sutras. Seeing you reciting the Great Compassion Mantra and sprinkling the blessed water, they were very delighted and wanted the blessing of the Great Compassion water. Unexpectedly, you used anger in your heart when sprinkling the water, and as a result, the Great Compassion water turned into boiling water, unintentionally causing them to get burned. How pitiful and sorrowful.”

The Dharma protector girl asked the Nun in horror, “How did you know about that?”

- This morning they all came to me to file complaints, how could I not know!”

Here in the story, we all see the guardian sprinkling the Great Compassion water with a mind of driving away, not a mind of compassion.

In personal, family, and social life, we have all had our own experiences with the destructive power of anger. It has more destructive power than any weapon. Anger causes irritability, tension, and suffering; we should practice to eliminate the mind of anger. This is not only a personal issue but also a social issue, because “If we want to change society, we must first change ourselves.” If we want this world to become more compassionate, we must first approach people with compassion; if we want people to be less violent, we must first be peaceful and calm. "Smile""Happiness will always come to you."

This was mentioned by the Buddha in verse 5 of the Dhammapada:

"If anyone repays hatred with hatred

Hatred will be continuously returned, sorrow lasting for aeons

With a compassionate mind, the law works wondrously

Repay hatred with kindness, and where is there any more enmity?"

According to the account of Venerable Chenqul Shi-

tieu_de: A MESSAGE
tom_tat: Dharma Study - Listening to Dharma....End of the Dharma period. 🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿
noi_dung:
MESSAGE

LEARNING DHARMA - LISTENING TO DHARMA....THE LATE DHARMA AGE.

🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿

Recently, more and more people have been using the Internet to speak Dharma. Speaking Dharma helps those who are confused to awaken, and of course, that is a good thing. But currently, the main issue is that many people teaching Dharma are largely mistaken, and most sentient beings today are far from the Buddha, have dull faculties, and no longer have much ability to distinguish right from wrong, true from false, proper from improper, so when they hear mistakes, they do not even realize they are mistakes.

Currently, beings are called sentient beings without the Dharma-discerning eye, without the eye that knows how to choose the true Dharma. When seeing someone who seems somewhat intelligent, they nod along approvingly at whatever is said. The situation unfolding before our eyes is truly distressing. What is called Dharma nowadays has too many people speaking about it. When too many people speak about it, it becomes easily accessible. When it becomes too easily accessible, it leads to a confused mind.

The Sutra of Lankavatara teaches that in the last days of the Dharma, false teachers will preach as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. A false teacher can be anyone; they do not necessarily have to be monks or members of the clergy. Anyone who acts as a teacher and speaks wrongly is a false teacher. Laypersons, whether male or female, who do not understand the principles of the Buddha but go and give lectures are also false teachers. Those who do not understand themselves but wish to save or teach others, speaking beyond their own understanding, are also false teachers.

The Four Pure Repentances in the Śūraṅgama Sūtra teach about four purities: not having lustful thoughts, not killing living beings, not stealing, and not lying. These four rules can serve as very effective standards for judging wrong and right. A student seeking learning, if they do not understand, may not fully grasp these four teachings and thus need to seek guidance from a mentor. However, a teacher guiding others, if not clear about them, is considered a false teacher regardless of who they are. One cannot, in front of others, teach people to uphold vegetarian precepts and then secretly take what does not belong to them to eat meat, drink alcohol, or freely lie and indulge in sexual misconduct without feeling disgusted.

In the circle of spiritual followers, the greatest lie is claiming to have attained sainthood without genuinely having achieved it, in order to enhance one's reputation and gain benefits. Before passing away, the Buddha instructed his disciples, the Bodhisattvas and Arhats, to be reborn in the time of the final Dharma to teach sentient beings on his behalf. However, absolutely no one claims to be a Bodhisattva or an Arhat on their own. Therefore, anyone who claims to be a reborn Arhat, Pratyekabuddha, or Bodhisattva is deceiving us.

Cases of major lying speech or secretly eating meat, drinking alcohol, and committing sexual misconduct when caught red-handed are very easy to recognize. Just by hearing about them, one can immediately know; is there any reason we would be blinded and unable to see them?

However, there is another type that is harder to recognize. It is the same person, sometimes speaking the truth, sometimes speaking falsely, more false than true, mixing truth with lies so that others do not know which way to follow. A guiding teacher is indeed the bright eye for sentient beings who are blind in the darkness. Currently, there are even people who specialize in using a little clever talent, a few easily gained benefits along with a touch of mystery to lure and manipulate sentient beings for personal gain and praise. This is precisely exploiting the desire of sentient beings to attract and manipulate them. Practicing spiritual cultivation is not about being mystical or having a bit of intelligence and calling it the Way. Sentient beingsCurrently, due to my own greed, I willingly allow this kind of person to bewilder me; therefore, we must pay special attention to this point.

If the leader is still blind, where will sentient beings step forward? If we ourselves cannot clearly discern right from wrong, we should not blindly believe anyone who preaches. When we are not clear and transparent, and our wisdom is insufficient, it is better to adhere to the teachings of the Patriarchs and eminent monks from the past, such as Venerable Tuyên Hoá, Venerable Quảng Khâm, Venerable Hư Vân, Master Ấn Quang... etc., and practice accordingly. They are Bodhisattvas and Arhats reborn, but they only quietly reveal their teachings near the time of passing. Only after they have passed away do people come to know. They will definitely not lead us astray.

It is better to follow these masters from the beginning without knowing much than to impulsively and indiscriminately seek learning on your own, which would make black ink blot white paper that cannot be erased later. Knowing a lot but mostly being wrong causes inner turmoil and troubles the teacher, who has to exert effort to help us erase it. So what is the point of knowing a lot? That is very undesirable. A person with wisdom, who can discern right from wrong by themselves, will not be misled by reading erroneous teachings.

However, there are also quite a few sincere people who genuinely aspire to teach sentient beings so that they understand the Dharma and practice. This aspiration is very commendable. But in whatever you do, you should do it for the benefit of others.

If the motivation behind it is not for others, but for fame, for praise, or if someone receives a little compliment and thinks they are as great as the sky, such a mind should only learn, not teach. Venerable Master Hsuan Hua established the monastery using six principles as its guiding tenets. Most people have probably heard of them.

1. Do not contend

2. Do not be greedy

3. Not seeking

4. Not selfish

5. Not self-serving

6. Not speaking falsely

If we do not do things properly, it is best not to go and teach others. That matter is still far away.

tieu_de: HOW TO SELF-INITIATE THE FULL BODHISATTVA VOWS OF THE EIGHT PRECEPTS FOR ONE DAY AND NIGHT AT HOME
tom_tat: Observing the Eight Precepts is learning from the ascetic practice of the Arhats. The merit of observing the Eight Precepts for one day is complete. It is said to be even greater than the merit of the kings of the heavenly realms. Especially
noi_dung:
HOW TO SELF-TAKE THE EIGHT PRECEPTS FOR A FULL DAY AND NIGHT AT HOME

Observing the Eight Precepts is learning from the ascetic practices of the Arhats. The merit of observing the eight precepts for one day is complete. It is even said to be greater than the merit of the kings of the heavenly realms. Especially on Buddha's special days. For Bodhisattvas, that merit multiplies a hundred thousand times more.

(You can write it down on paper to read each time you observe the precepts)

🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿

(Excerpt from the lecture of Teacher Quang Tu)

Homage to the Ten Directions’ Eternal Three Jewels (bow three times)

Homage to the Lord of the Underworld, the One Who Resolutely Vows to Save Lives,

Who vows not to become Buddha until the hells are empty,

Who saves all sentient beings and attains Bodhi on all sides,

Great Compassion, Great Vow, Earth Holy, Great Mercy Root Deity, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-Sattva. (recite 3 times, each time bow once)

Homage to the Enlightening Bodhisattva (bow three times)

Homage to the Buddha

Homage to the Dharma

Homage to the Sangha

(x3)
