tieu_de: BODHISATTVA DIZANG'S TEACHINGS ON THE FIVE PRECEPTS
tom_tat: Ah Ngoc pays respect to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva! Very happy to once again benefit from the wondrous dharma! Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva enlightens Ah Ngoc about the five precepts; keeping the five precepts can secure human rebirth, which is the fundamental basis of being human, and prevents falling into lower realms, it seems.
noi_dung:
BODHISATTVA Kṣitigarbha TEACHES ABOUT THE FIVE PRECEPTS

A Ngoc salutes Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva! Very happy to again benefit from the wondrous Dharma!

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha teaches A Ngọc about the Five Precepts. Keeping the Five Precepts can allow one to attain a human body; it is the fundamental condition of being human and avoids falling into lower realms. It may seem simple, but most sentient beings violate them without realizing it. We often hear many people around us say, 'I have not stolen, killed, or harmed anyone by arson; I am an honest person.' In fact, killing people or committing arson are already very serious crimes that must result in punishment in hell. Now let us listen to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha's compassionate teaching. If there is any mistake in understanding, it is the problem of A Ngọc. A Ngọc simply recounts the Bodhisattva's teaching as follows:

1. No killing: strictly prohibit taking the life of any sentient being. Pure vegetarianism is the foundation of observing this precept. Why is it called pure? One must strictly uphold the teachings of the Lankavatara Sutra. Anything related to oneself must not be used or consumed. All foods related to animals must not be eaten. For example: cow's milk, eggs, honey, cheese, beef fat—anything related to animals is prohibited. Most cosmetic products contain animal components and should not be used. When we are ill and need to take medicine, especially traditional Chinese medicine, many contain animal ingredients.

2. No stealing: Taking possession for oneself without the consent of others is stealing. Many people at the company take office supplies for personal use or take them home, make phone calls for personal matters, charge their mobile phones at the company, use the photocopier or fax machine for private purposes, etc. If not approved by the company, all of these constitute stealing.

3. No sexual misconduct: Any sexual activity outside of marriage is considered sexual misconduct. Watching pornography, masturbation, or using sexual aids are all considered violations of the rule against sexual misconduct.

4. No false speech: speak the truth, do not deceive others. If it exists, say it exists; if not, say it does not exist. Intentionally deceiving is a serious violation; in cases where lying is convenient, try not to speak, because speaking falsely often will become a natural habit.

5. No alcohol: alcohol and drugs are prohibited. Products related to alcohol should not be consumed, for example, fermented tofu, most of which contain alcohol and should not be eaten, even if the seller claims that only a very small amount of alcohol is used. Even a small amount is considered alcohol, except when used with medicine to save a person's life, which is permissible. Many cosmetic products also contain alcohol, so it is best not to use them...

(Excerpt from Âm Luật Vô Tình 1)

tieu_de: Does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva regret his vows or not?
tom_tat: Excerpt: Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows - Venerable Master Tuyên Hóa's Lecture 🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿
noi_dung:
DOES Kṣitigarbha BODHISATTVA REGRET HIS VOWS OR NOT?

Excerpt: Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows - Lecture by Venerable Tuyen Hoa

🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿

"The hells are not yet empty, the vow is not yet fulfilled to become Buddha; only after saving all sentient beings, will one attain Bodhi."

(The hells are not empty, the vow not fulfilled to become Buddha,

Only when all sentient beings are saved, will one attain Bodhi.)

As long as hell is not yet empty, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha has not yet become a Buddha; only when all sentient beings have been liberated will He become a Buddha. If there is still even one sentient being not yet liberated, He has not yet become a Buddha.

Having gone through such a long period, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha still has not attained Buddhahood, because whenever He saves these sentient beings, there are always other sentient beings coming, continuously without end. It is not the case that for every sentient being born, one sentient being dies; nor is it that when one sentient being dies, another is born. The number of sentient beings being born in general still

exceeds the number of sentient beings dying by ten times, a hundred times, a thousand times, and possibly even ten thousand times.

Try to make statistics to see whether the death rate or the birth rate is higher in the city of San Francisco today? Usually, people die because of old age, weakness, or illness, so on average, humans live for only several decades; meanwhile, almost after ten months of pregnancy, a new person is born, hence the population increases very quickly, and the probability of reproduction can be thousands or tens of thousands of times higher than the probability of death.

That is why until now Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is still hard-working, busy, and still cannot become a Buddha. However, do you think that Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva regrets the vow of

Do I often not? Of course, He does not regret it! The more beings there are, the more work He has to be busy with; if there were no beings, He would have no work to do and would have become a Buddha long ago, and once becoming a Buddha, there would be nothing left to do! Therefore, this is Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha who "finds work to do when there is none"! Actually, He could live in great ease and leisure, but He prefers to be busy day and night saving beings, for that is exactly His vow and practice.

Why did Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva make this great vow? Because He realized that He and sentient beings are essentially of the same nature; if sentient beings have not attained Buddhahood, His attainment of Buddhahood has no meaning. Therefore, He voluntarily waits for sentient beings, preserving the cause-and-condition of being "eternally of the same nature" with sentient beings.

The vow power of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva cannot be measured or fully understood. What we can express is only a very small part, because in reality, His vow power cannot be comprehended or discussed.

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-Tathāgata.

tieu_de: THE BIGGEST MISTAKE IN LIFE IS ARROGANCE
tom_tat: PRIDE CAN NEVER ATTAIN HOLINESS What is pride?
noi_dung:
THE BIGGEST MISTAKE IN LIFE IS ARROGANCE

PROUDNESS CANNOT ATTAIN HOLY PATH

What is pride?

Pride is often understood as arrogance, haughty, presumptuous, or vanity. Simply put, pride is a bad habit of thinking oneself superior to others. In this life, perhaps there is no one who is without pride. Each person is proud in different ways, in different degrees.

Seeing someone inferior, instead of supporting, encouraging them to advance, one takes pleasure in the fact that the person is worse than oneself and praises oneself as talented and capable for being better than such a person; this is a form of 'arrogance'.

Seeing someone equal to oneself but refusing to consider oneself on the same level as that person, on the contrary, finding all kinds of reasons to justify that one is superior; this is another form of 'arrogance'.

Always believing oneself to be right causes a person to go from one mistake to another.

Buddhist scriptures often refer to three pride, seven pride, and twelve pride, but all originate from conceit (asmimana). In the Shurangama Sutra, seven prides (seven pride) are listed, as follows:

Pride: Having an attitude of contempt toward those who are inferior to oneself in knowledge, status, wealth, or career. In reality, they may indeed be inferior, but only in certain aspects, not entirely. Therefore, one should not act arrogantly because of this.

Excessive conceit: Considering oneself superior in all aspects to people who have similar education, wealth, status, or degrees.

Overly excessive conceit: Always thinking oneself superior to those who are genuinely better in all aspects.

Egoistic conceit: Always placing one's ego above everything, believing others are inferior, viewing oneself as the center of the universe, and superior to others.

Spiritual pride: Claiming to have attained enlightenment before actually achieving it, to be admired, respected, or offered gifts by others.

Arrogance of pride: Losing to others in every aspect but considering oneself as losing little, even declaring that one has not lost anything at all.

Arrogance of falsehood: Being ignorant, unethical, and narrow-minded but claiming oneself to be virtuous, compassionate, and knowledgeable.

The Buddha also pointed out three other forms of arrogance in the mind: youth arrogance, health arrogance, and life arrogance. Youth arrogance is a subjective, overbearing, and mistakenly stubborn attitude. Health arrogance is a sense of invulnerability due to absence of illness, relying on the body. Life arrogance is relying on longevity to commit unwholesome deeds involving the three actions of body – mind – speech.

4 applications of Buddhism in life 4 applications of Buddhism in life Moving meditation for health cultivation - Gaining energy to cure all diseases Moving meditation for health cultivation - Gaining energy to cure all diseases Why does happiness slip away from our hands? Why does happiness slip away from our hands? To always live with love for life! To always live with love for life! SHOULD READ

In summary, the prideful mindset is always comparing oneself, measuring whether one is better or worse than others. If one truly feels superior, they feel pleasure and boast. If they are inferior, they refuse to admit defeat. Those who are ambitious and prideful are always competitive, arrogant, lacking grace, lacking humility, and unwilling to yield to anyone. Prideful people often coexist with stubborn, conservative, and domineering mentalities. Its karmic effect is to always value oneself while looking down on and belittling others. When pride rules, it will block blessings, prevent happiness, and bring suffering.

Eliminating pride is erasing afflictions

Pride is one of the six fundamental afflictions, which are: greed - anger - ignorance - pride - doubt - wrong views, with deep roots arising from delusion and attachment to the self.

Once the mind of arrogance arises, one will not listen to sincere advice from others, will not be willing to learn more, so it is easy to do wrong things, look down on others, and increase one's sins. Because arrogance considers oneself above all, there is no harmonious mind; the prideful and arrogant mind leads to many distorted and confused actions, thereby diminishing virtue, losing blessings, and eventually, when all fortune is gone, disaster comes. When disaster arrives, fortune departs, resulting in suffering. Therefore, one must endure endless cycles of birth and death.

However, the root of arrogance is very deep and not everyone can easily eradicate it. Because everyone exalts their own ego. Those who study Buddhism should self-examine; if there is arrogant pride, they must try to eliminate it.

The only way to eliminate it is to make an effort, practice diligently, and let go of each thought as soon as it arises in order to gradually transform it. If one is not vigilant, one will become its slave, and the consequences can be very harmful. Only with awareness can one clearly recognize it, and thus, it cannot harm us. This is the will, effort, and dedicated practice of each person that determines how quickly or slowly it is eradicated.

It is important to remain mindful, deeply contemplating its nature to see that its essence is emptiness; only when encountering adverse conditions that go against one’s will or feelings does it arise.

The only measure to transform an arrogant and prideful mind is humility, living joyfully, and in harmony with everyone.

A person with a humble and simple lifestyle always loves and respects everyone, does not look down on anyone, and does not flatter anyone. Humility shows us our own shortcomings so that we can correct them, not appearing arrogant or conceited, so we are always calm and willing to listen to the contributions of those around us. Humility helps people not to be arrogant or haughty when standing at the peak of power and fame. Thanks to this, they can accomplish many useful things and gain the support of many people.

For worldly people, one should be humble in order to continue learning, constantly expanding knowledge and understanding to achieve success. For practitioners, one must be even more humble to listen, learn, know how to let go, not cling to this body and mind as self, and live a life of peace and liberation.

tieu_de: HOW TO REPENT, BUDDHIST CEREMONY OF THE 9 Kṣitigarbha SUTRAS - THE OCEAN OF MERIT IS BEYOND IMAGINATION!
tom_tat: (IF YOU CAN'T HAVE TIME TO RITUALIZE THE WHOLE VOLUME OR THE WHOLE BOOK, THEN RITUALIZE THIS 1 PART 9, GUYS) 🌷🌷🌷🌷🌷
noi_dung:
METHODS OF REPENTANCE, BUDDHIST RITUALS IN THE 9 Kṣitigarbha SUTRAS - INCOMPARABLE SEA OF MERIT!

(IF YOU CANNOT FIND TIME FOR the entire ceremony or the whole chapter, then you can perform this 9-section ceremony, everyone)

🌷🌷🌷🌷🌷

Dear friends! Since many of you ask how to repent in order to quickly eliminate karma, today I would like to introduce to you a way of bowing and repenting that is simple, fast (only about 15 minutes), but the benefits are incredibly wonderful—both strongly eliminating karma and greatly increasing merit beyond imagination. This is the ceremony of bowing to the Buddhas in chapter 9 of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra.

Everyone, pay attention to this: in the void of the universe, there are countless worlds, each world having an infinite number of Buddhas that cannot be fully enumerated. So why, in Chapter 9, does Kṣitigarbha only mention the names of 19 Buddhas? It is because Kṣitigarbha has already selected for us the Buddhas whose vows to save and increase the merit of sentient beings are of the highest order, so that sentient beings only need to worship once to gain the maximum benefit, putting in little effort but receiving much. In Chapter 9, the Buddha urges Kṣitigarbha to quickly proclaim the names of the Buddhas; in this way, even if the Original Teacher enters Nirvana, He will notWe still have to worry about sentient beings in this life and the next. Do you see that? It means the role and merits of the titles of these Buddhas are immense. Just by sentient beings hearing about them and paying homage, they can eliminate their own karma and increase their own blessings, which makes the Buddhas very reassured. We have encountered this priceless sutra, which gives us the opportunity to be saved! This is an incomparable treasure, and we should always remember the merits of the Buddhas and Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha!

In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, everywhere it mentions "good men and good women," but in Chapter 9, Praising the Names of the Buddhas, Kṣitigarbha does not say good men and good women; instead, he says, "any man or any woman who hears the name of this Buddha...," meaning that the scope of the Buddhas' salvation extends even to those who are evil and have committed many sins during their lifetime. Normally, people are encouraged to cultivate virtue to become good men and good women, but at the moment of death or in times of danger, merely reciting or hearing the names of the Buddhas allows them to compassionately save everyone, leaving no being behind.

No being, whether good or evil. Chapter 9 does not require one to be a virtuous man or woman; any sentient being who sincerely bows to the Buddhas can receive great blessings. Therefore, if you do not have enough time to chant the entire Kṣitigarbha Sutra, at least each day you should bow to the Buddhas in Chapter 9 once—it only takes 15 minutes. Let us not betray the compassion of the Buddhas and Kṣitigarbha!

Now is the execution part, I find the ceremony fast, neat, and very joyful:

🌻INVOCATION OF THE THREE JEWELS

Prepare fruits, candles, incense... and offer them to the Three Jewels (if not possible, just a glass of clean water is enough). Wear clean, neat clothes, and respectfully bow and recite:

- Namo to the Three Jewels who universally abide. (3 times, each time 1 prostration)

- Namo to the Original Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha. (1 prostration)

- Namo to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva. (1 prostration)

Kneeling with hands clasped, I respectfully say: I, your disciple..., dharma name..., today sincerely invite the Three Jewels of the ten directions, the Buddha Shakyamuni, and Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, to graciously descend and witness my prostrations to the Buddhas described in the ninth chapter of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, seeking repentance. I invite all sentient beings suffering in the vast dharma realm to gather here, to join me in prostrating to the Buddhas to attain great benefit. May the Three Jewels bless me and all sentient beings, swiftly eliminate karmic obstacles, increase merit and wholesome roots, and from now on, for countless lifetimes, take refuge in the Three Jewels, and by karmic affinity, encounter virtuous teachers who guide us in practice and study.the true Dharma of the Tathagata until the day of attaining Buddhahood. (1 bow)

🌻CEREMONY OF THE BUDDHAS' NAMES (I included in the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra Chapter 9 the merits of reciting the names of the Buddhas so that you may increase your faith and devotion in bowing; you may skip the verse, just reciting their names is also fine)

1. Wholeheartedly bow to Namo Infinite Body Tathagata. (1 bow)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha, and has a temporary feeling of reverence, they will immediately be liberated from heavy sins and the cycle of birth and death for forty lifetimes. How much more so if they also create images, praise, and make offerings, they will gain immeasurable merit.

2. Wholeheartedly prostrate to Namo Precious Nature Tathagata. (1 prostration)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha and in a moment generates the aspiration for refuge, that person, practicing towards the supreme position, will never regress again.

3. Wholeheartedly prostrate to Namo Three-Headed Demon Conquering Tathagata. (1 prostration)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha pass through their ears, they will be reborn a thousand times in the Six Desire heavens, let alone those who wholeheartedly recite the name.

4. Wholeheartedly bow to Namo Lion's Roar Tathagata. (1 bow)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha and generates a mind of refuge in just one thought, that person will have countless Buddhas touching their head and granting empowerment.

5. Wholeheartedly bow to Namo Gou Lou Zun Tathagata. (1 bow)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha, wholeheartedly pays homage, or praises it, then in the assembly of dharma during the Age of Fortunate Life with a thousand Buddhas, that person will become a Great Universal King and will be entrusted to the supreme throne.

6. Wholeheartedly prostrate and pay homage to Namo Tī Bā Thī Như Lai. (1 prostration)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha, they will no longer fall into evil paths, and will often be born in the heavenly or human realms, enjoying supreme and wondrous happiness.

7. Wholeheartedly pay homage to Namo Treasure Victory Tathagata. (1 prostration)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha, they will certainly no longer fall into evil paths, and will often enjoy unparalleled pleasures in the heavenly realms.

8. Wholeheartedly pay homage to Namo Treasure Form Tathagata. (1 prostration)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha and develops a heart of reverence, it will not be long before they attain the fruit of Arhatship.

9. Wholeheartedly bow to Namo Cassa Tràng Tathagata. (1 bow)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha, that person will be free from the sin of birth and death for a hundred great kalpas.

10. Wholeheartedly bow to Namo Great Communication Mountain King Tathagata. (1 bow)

If any man or woman hears the name of this Buddha, that person will encounter countless Buddhas preaching the Dharma extensively and will surely attain Bodhi enlightenment.

11. Wholeheartedly bow to Namo Pure Moon Tathagata. (1 bow)

12. Wholeheartedly bow to Homage to Nam Mo Mountain King Tathagata. (1 prostration)

13. Wholeheartedly bow to Homage to Nam Mo Victor of Wisdom Tathagata. (1 prostration)

14. Wholeheartedly bow to Homage to Nam Mo Pure Name King Tathagata. (1 prostration)

15. Wholeheartedly bow to Homage to Nam Mo Accomplisher of Wisdom Tathagata. (1 prostration)

16. Wholeheartedly bow to Homage to Nam Mo Unsurpassed Tathagata. (1 prostration)

17. Wholeheartedly bow to Homage to Nam Mo Wondrously Pure Tathagata. (1 prostration)

18. Wholeheartedly bow to Homage to Nam Mo Full Moon Tathagata. (1 prostration)

19. Wholeheartedly bow to Namo Moon-Faced Tathagata. (1 prostration)

20. Wholeheartedly bow to Namo Amitabha Tathagata. (1 prostration)

🌻CONFESSION OF FAULTS

All the Buddhas and World Honored Ones in the world are rare and usually present in the world; those World Honored Ones should feel compassion for me. Whether in this life or in past lives, from the beginningless cycle of birth and death until now, I have committed sins: either by doing them myself or by persuading others to do them, witnessing them done and rejoicing in them; whether it was taking objects from stupas, or from the Sangha, or from distant Sangha, either taking them myself or persuading others to take them and rejoicing when taken; the five heinous crimes, either done by myself or by persuading others, witnessing and rejoicing in them; the sins already committed, whether hidden or not, worthy of falling into hell, becoming hungry ghosts, animals, other evil paths, the lowly and wicked individuals, all the sins I have committed in this way, I now repent.pray)

Now, O World Honored Ones, you should realize me, you should remember me; I again stand before the Buddhas, the World Honored Ones, and speak as follows: Either in this life or in another life, I have given alms or kept the precepts, even to the extent of giving just a portion of rice to hungry animals, or practiced purity, having good roots, accomplished beings with good roots, practiced Bodhi with good roots, and attained supreme wisdom with good roots. All of these gatherings and calculations are dedicated to Supreme Bodhi, just as the Buddhas of the past, the future, and the present dedicate in this way. (1 prostration)

All offenses are confessed and purified

All merits are dedicated with joy

And the virtues of all Buddhas

May they lead to supreme wisdom

Past, future, and present Buddhas

Foremost among all beings

An ocean of boundless virtues

Now I respectfully bow and take refuge. (1 prostration)

🌻DEDICATION

Today I dedicate the merit of worshiping the Buddha and repentance, and I wish to transfer it to all beings in the empty dharma realm, especially to those beings in the three evil paths. May I and all sentient beings swiftly eliminate karmic obstacles, cultivate virtuous roots, may all our wishes be fulfilled, and may we follow the Buddha and Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha in practice until the day of complete Buddhahood. (1 prostration)

🌻TAKING REFUGE

I take refuge in the Buddha by myself, sincerely wishing for all sentient beings,

to understand the great path and develop the unsurpassed mind. (1 prostration)

Taking refuge in the Dharma myself, I vow for all beings,

to deeply penetrate the Buddhist scriptures, wisdom like an ocean. (1 prostration)

Taking refuge in the Sangha myself, I vow for all beings,

to govern the assembly, without any obstacles. (1 prostration)

🌻NOTE:

- Some titles of the Buddhas compared to the Kṣitigarbha Sutra translation may seem different, this is only due to the translation of their titles. You can rest assured in your prostrations!

- The final part adds the title of Amitabha Buddha to help you achieve the most complete liberation in the future.

- After repentance, remember to strictly uphold the five precepts of laypeople (not killing, not stealing, not committing sexual misconduct, not lying, not drinking alcohol or using intoxicants), to abandon past wrongdoings and bad habits from now on; only then is it called true repentance, and the blessings of the Buddhas can shine upon you.

- You can watch the video with images of the Buddhas talking about the merits of their names attached here.

https://youtu.be/OTCucX9Z2VM

🌷Wishing you good luck and success!

Source: Huynh Qua Anh

tieu_de: Phuoc Dien
tom_tat: Phước Điền means the field of merit. A good field will absorb seeds and have the power to produce rice. For example, if a farmer sows seeds in a good field, he will get a lot of rice, just as virtuous men and faithful women make offerings to n
noi_dung:
PHƯỚC ĐIỀN

Phước Điền means the field of merit. A good field can accept seeds and has the capacity to produce rice. For example, when a farmer sows seeds in a good field, he will harvest a lot of rice. Similarly, virtuous men and faithful women who make offerings to true practitioners, to those who have attained enlightenment, and to those worthy of offerings, those are the fields of merit, and they will receive immeasurable merit in this life and in future lives.

The Phạm Võng Sutra mentions eight types of fields of merit (namely the eight fields of merit), which include: the Buddha, virtuous persons, high monks, lay disciples, the Sangha, father, mother, and the sick.

Infinite Life Sutra: Bodhisattvas are the supreme field of merit.

In the sacred assembly of the Sutra, the Fifth Patriarch taught the disciples that: Being in the world, birth and death is a great matter. You all spend your days seeking only the field of merit and do not seek liberation from the sea of suffering of birth and death. If your own nature is still deluded, how can merit possibly save you?

Nirvana Sutra, Volume 24: What is a field of merit? From non-Buddhists who observe precepts upward to the Buddhas, that is a field of merit. But if someone thinks that only practitioners and those who have attained liberation are true fields of merit, they should know that this is a narrow-minded thought. The Bodhisattva Mahasattva observes that all countless sentient beings are fields of merit.

👉 TYPES OF FIELDS OF MERIT:

1. RESPECTFUL FIELD: That is, we respectfully offer to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Holy Ones, and Sangha...

2. FAVOR FIELD: That is, those from whom we have received favors such as Parents, Teachers,...

3. RIGHTEOUS FIELD: That is, the close relatives and kin around us when the fire goes out and the lights are off, ...

4. COMPASSIONATE FIELD: That is, being compassionate, showing mercy to the poor, the sick, the destitute beings, those in calamity...

📿Namo Fundamental Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha! 🙏

📿Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahātma! 🙏

📿 Namo Great Compassion Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva! 🙏

tieu_de: OPENING THE HEAVENLY EYE - BLESSING ANCESTORS & BEINGS IN THE FORMLESS REALM TOWARDS THE GOOD REALM.
tom_tat: (A true miraculous story of the Buddhist Phổ Minh). My name is N.H.A, Dharma name Phổ Minh, taking refuge at Phúc Mỹ Pagoda (Đô Lương - Nghệ An).
noi_dung:
OPENING THE HEAVENLY EYE - BLESSING ANCESTORS & BEINGS IN THE FORMLESS REALM TOWARDS THE GOOD REALM.

(A true miraculous story of the Buddhist layperson Phổ Minh).

My name is N.H.A, Dharma name Phổ Minh, and I took refuge at Phuc My Pagoda (Do Luong - Nghe An).

I am a lay Buddhist. Here, I would like to share with fellow practitioners the wondrous experiences of the Dharma that I personally went through, so that everyone may increase their diligence, vows, and conduct in self-cultivation, believing in the Law of Cause and Effect.

First, I would like to talk about my mother. Her name is P.T.C, and her life has been very difficult, with continuous illness. For more than 15 years, she could only sleep (from 8 PM to 1 AM) every day, so she often suffered from headaches...

Five years ago, even though at that time my mother and I had not yet known about Buddhism, perhaps due to converging causes and conditions, both my mother and I were able to open the heavenly eye and the heavenly ear, thus being able to see many invisible realms...

My mother began to reflect on why she often fell ill and was so sickly. She saw that her body was full of fish heads because in her daily life she frequently cleaned fish and smashed their heads... At that moment, she realized that her illness was due to the karma of killing, caused by wronged spirits seeking revenge, but she still didn't know how to resolve it...

Later, after learning about Buddhism, every night before going to bed, my mother would chant the Buddha's name, repent to the wronged spirits, and dedicate the merit of her chanting for their liberation.

I also joined my mother in offering prayers for their souls, asking them to forgive her, and for a whole month, we recited sutras, bowed for 1,500 Buddha titles, released animals, performed many good deeds... then the wronged spirits came to report:

“We have forgiven your mother, and we have also been liberated and reborn into the human realm. From now on, we will no longer follow you to seek revenge, mother...”

From that time on, my mother no longer had headaches and could eat and sleep normally again after more than 15 years of sleepless nights.

As for me, when I practice, I open the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for all beings across the ten directions to hear, I see beings from many invisible realms coming to listen to the sutra. I see two Dharma protectors, guardians of the sutra, and all beings are with hands clasped listening to the sutra. Looking up at the sky, I see beings in the higher realms; beneath the ground are ancestral spirits similar to my own ancestors being worshiped, and countless beings in animal forms. Every night I also bow to the Buddha, recite sutras for repentance, and see my ancestors coming to practice with me, dressed beautifully and joyfully.

Once I made a vow for my lineage, praying to Buddha to liberate my ancestors. Because my heavenly eye was opened, my ancestors came to inform the family that several of them had fallen into hell, chained because in their lifetime they were landlords and committed suicide, along with some other sins of ancestors from 200 years ago...

When Master Huệ Nghiêm and I made the vow to bow 1,500 names of Buddhas from the ten directions at Phúc Trí Temple, Tân Sơn, Nghệ An, it was truly miraculous. When bowing to repent, thanks to this merit, we prayed for the Buddhas’ blessing. After the ceremonies were completed, the ancestors came to report that they had escaped from hell and were now in an intermediate realm, meaning neither high nor low. All chains were broken thanks to the power of the Buddhas.

_______________________________________

THE STORY ABOUT A SUICIDAL SPIRIT WHO HANGED ITSELF.

Next to my house, there is a spirit named N. H. T. from Đô Lương, Nghệ An. During their lifetime, due to many reasons, they hanged themselves (not convenient to mention). Because I have opened the yin-yang eye, I saw this spirit come to cry for help many times. I saw this spirit repeatedly hang themselves in suicide every day, their soul swollen, like their hands, feet, and neck in the mortal world were all swollen and felt painful.

Day after day, I saw that spirit appear, especially at night, I saw them crying for help in suffering.

This family has no faith, thinking that death is the end. Living next door, I saw that scene and felt compassion and kindness, so I said to them:

- Perhaps the destiny between you and me has come, which is why I see you like this!

Then, I generated the intention to pray and requested the Buddhas, the Dharma protectors, the local deities, and the earth gods who govern that piece of land, as well as those who govern the underworld, to allow this being to follow me to the temple, to have the intention to repent with me, and to bow 1,500 times to the names of Buddhas throughout the ten directions. I bow 150 times each day. After that day, when I went to the temple to bow to the Buddha, I could still see that this being followed me and bowed together with me.

Every day, performing 150 prostrations, their spirit also reduced its swelling a little, no longer feeling pain. After ten days of prostrating to the Buddha, that person no longer repeatedly experienced the phenomenon of self-strangulation, and their spirit was no longer swollen as before.

Although the merit of the Buddhas is inconceivable, due to their heavy karma, this person was allowed to reside at the grave, which before they were never allowed to return to despite having that grave.

From then on, this person was able to return to the family's ancestral temple and the family altar when they held memorial ceremonies. After that time, they came to thank me, and from then on, they no longer troubled me.

Until now, on that piece of land, I have not seen that spirit appearing to hang itself anymore. I hope that through the story I have shared above, everyone will increase their diligence, vows, and virtue to cultivate themselves, and believe in the law of Cause and Effect.

(Hoài Cường - rewritten based on the account of Phổ Minh - 06/23/2021).

tieu_de: ONLY VIRTUE AND PRAYERS CAN SAVE US
tom_tat: Powerless to watch sentient beings slowly die in the epidemic. I feel great compassion, but my ability is so small, what can I do... Only virtue and PRAYER POWER can overcome KARMA POWER.
noi_dung:
ONLY VIRTUE AND PRAYER POWER CAN SAVE US

Helplessly watching sentient beings die gradually in the epidemic. I feel deep sorrow, but my strength is so small—what can I do...

Only virtue and PRAYER POWER can overcome KARMA FORCE.

Honestly, I advise friends in the epidemic area, as well as those who are sick, not yet sick, fo, f1, f2... all of us must quickly take refuge in the Buddha. Every day during home quarantine, read this refuge text over and over, and wholeheartedly pray to the Bodhisattvas for help. If truly sincere in this way, we will surely be safe through the violent epidemic....

Quang Tu received blessings from the bodhisattva also thanks to daily sincere refuge in him, but actually I am poor in practice, ignorant, with heavy karmic obstacles and no virtue, what I have today is because of his grace and guidance!

If your relatives don't believe, do it on their behalf.🍀🍀🍀

tieu_de: WHAT IS REAL AND WHAT IS ILLUSION?
tom_tat: FROM DREAM TO DREAM BECOMING NOTHING 💦 Life is like a long movie, we ourselves are the actors, talented artists in those plays.
noi_dung:
WHAT IS REAL AND WHAT IS JUST A DREAM?

DREAMS END, RETURN TO DREAMS WITHOUT FORM 💦

Life is like a long movie, and we are the actors, the talented artists in those plays.

This life is inherently very fair; those who come first die first, those who come later die later, dying in an orderly manner to make space for the next generation. Should we really want to live forever to hold funerals, when everyone must die eventually? Then, perhaps at some point, due to extreme loneliness, pain from loss, separation, and when we are left alone, we feel that life is truly dull and monotonous... In that moment, we probably only wish: "Buddha, please let me die." Yes! Dying is something very fair. We all must die eventually; it's just a matter of sooner or later.

We can skip stages from birth until aging without illness, which is due to past-life blessings allowing a body with little disease, but being free of illness does not mean being free from death. From the moment of birth until old age, we can avoid the door of "ILLNESS," but let us ask, who can run away from or escape the final door of life, which is the door of "DEATH."

Therefore, we are lucky to still have the opportunity to obtain a human body, strive to cultivate ourselves (that is, to reform by observing precepts to perfect oneself), accumulate merit to transform karma, generate the Great Bodhi mind, sow good seeds to be reborn in a good realm. Naturally, we do not have the right to escape death, but we do have the right to choose where to be reborn. "I cannot change the direction of the wind, but I can adjust my sails to reach my intended destination."

Therefore, while we are still healthy, we should strive to practice liberation; do not wait until this body is lost, for then, even if you regret, it will be far too late."

"'HUMAN BODY IS HARD TO COME BY - BUDDHIST TEACHINGS ARE HARD TO HEAR.' Let's contemplate impermanence to be more diligent each day, friends. One pandemic, yesterday we could still see each other, but today we are already separated by a thousand miles...

"Reflecting on life, what is there really,

From youth to old age, from spring to white hair,

The four elements return to the four elements,

Leaving only dust drifting in the void."

We come to this world, and when we leave, we can only take with us two things: MERIT AND KARMA, so, do not dream for too long, please be mindful in every thought.

The Buddha taught that: "THE SEA OF SUFFERING HAS NO SHORE TO TURN BACK TO" Let us guide and support each other, striving to practice daily to accumulate virtue and merit as provisions for the Buddha's realm!

EVERYONE EVENTUALLY LEAVES

WHY BE DISTRESSED ABOUT LOSS

WHAT IS TRUE

HEAVEN ITSELF WILL RECORD...

📿Namo Shakyamuni Buddha, the Original Teacher, Greatly Prove 🙏

📿Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, Greatly Prove 🙏

tieu_de: INTERVIEW WITH THE UNDERWORLD PEOPLE.
tom_tat: (Hong Van) Through this conversation, we will see that what the Buddha has said in the scriptures is accurate. His compassion through the teachings not only saves the suffering of people
noi_dung:
INTERVIEW WITH THE UNDERWORLD PERSON.

( Hồng Vân )

Through this conversation, we will see that the things the Buddha spoke of in the scriptures are accurate. His compassion, expressed through the teachings, not only alleviates human suffering but also that of all sentient beings in all realms.

*************************

Knowing that I (Hồng Vân) often write about the world of the dead (the bardo), a colleague friend called and shared that:

– Sister, I have a very strange matter. My grandfather passed away 36 years ago during the period of re-education through labor.

Recently, he returned, possessing my brother-in-law's younger sibling, and asked the family to perform the ceremony of taking refuge in the Three Jewels for him.

My family asked: Where is his body so that the family can bring it back to establish a grave, and why did he return to request taking refuge in the Three Jewels?

He answered:

– There is no need to look for his body to bury it. He sees himself as having heavy karma and is facing what he has caused. Therefore, he wants to plant the seeds of Buddhism so that when he is reborn as a human, encountering the Buddha's teachings, he can develop the aspiration to practice.

My family has sought Thich Giac Hanh – Chua Hoi Phuoc, Ba Ria – Vung Tau – to ask him to take refuge for him, and the monk agreed.

A few days later, my friend called again and asked me if I wanted to go with her to meet Thay Giac Hanh. I agreed!

On the morning of the day on the way to see the teacher, the teacher said: “Yesterday, your grandfather came back and said that besides seeking refuge with the Triple Gem through me, remember to hold a vegetarian ceremony to make offerings for him and those who worked with him in the past, dedicating merit to help him and everyone attain liberation.”

Thich Giac Hanh is a fairly well-known monk in exorcising spirits that possess living people. He has a good understanding of the world of the deceased.

After meeting Master Giac Hanh, I intended to have a direct encounter with him (a person from the spirit world) to interview and chat about the world in which he currently exists.

The most important thing I wanted to ask was why he returned to the living world to take refuge in the Triple Gem when, during his lifetime, he had never been exposed to Buddhist knowledge.

But then, due to work commitments, I could not directly approach and interview him as planned. Fortunately, earlier I had discussed with a colleague some of the questions I wanted to ask.

Because she is also a newly ordained disciple, my friend (the granddaughter of someone from the spirit world) raised the issues that I mentioned earlier to ask him. Fortunately, that conversation was recorded.

To help readers understand and have deeper faith in Buddhist teachings, I would like to record the conversation below.

Because I had multiple interactions with him when he returned, the interview recorded below is a compilation of several conversations. There is a lot of information in the interview that I am not including due to sensitive family matters, but it will be discussed in part two of the article – Reflections on the Interview.

Through this conversation, we will see that what the Buddha said in the scriptures is accurate. His compassion, expressed through his teachings, not only alleviates the suffering of humans but also of all sentient beings in the various realms.

A conversation with my grandfather.

Before getting into the content of the conversation, I would like to present the sermon of Mr. Huỳnh Văn Lương during the last family meeting in Rạch Kiến. Having understood Buddhist teachings, Mr. Lương (a soldier of the Republic of Vietnam army) asked the spirits of soldiers from both sides (Bộ đội Cụ Hồ and the Republic's soldiers) to stand before the vegetarian meal and declared.

Today, I, Huỳnh Văn Lương – Dharma name Minh Tâm (specifically on the evening of July 27 in the year of Tân Mão), along with my children, respectfully invite both sides and the local people here, as well as "the spirits from the homeland," to listen to my sermon.

Today, I have taken refuge before the Three Jewels. Our time has ended, so we lay down our weapons. We are all people of the Vietnamese nation, all human beings. Each serves their own master, but we should negotiate amicably, reconcile grievances, and lay down our weapons. Let us return together to one path.

We are humans who, due to the karma of killing, have been reborn as soldiers. I have realized the path of Buddhism, so I wish that you and the people here would join me in returning to Buddha.

Let us awaken and realize again. Put down all folded hands like I am doing here, Namo Amitabha Buddha (3 times). I am very grateful to all of you for listening to such words.

Today, my grandson and his friends have come here to assist. Please, may you graciously accept this vegetarian meal so that the monks can dedicate the merit to guide us to the Western Pure Land. Please witness my sincere heart. Namo Amitabha Buddha (3 times). You have all knelt down and clasped your hands to chant Buddha's name. Minh Tam has succeeded. The people here are very joyful now.

Question:

– What circumstances led you to encounter the Buddha and aspire to practice in the realm of the deceased?

In his past life, when he was young, he had gone to the Buddhist temple but mainly to misbehave and play. Thanks to his merits, he was able to plant the seed of Buddha in his consciousness. After his death, he still often returned home but could not make contact with anyone, because his relatives did not remember him. On his death anniversary, he could not eat anything because the date on the death notice did not match the actual date of his passing. He had to endure hunger, thirst, and cold throughout the past years.

He often relied on his aunt-in-law and sister-in-law for meals, so he followed her back to the countryside when there were ancestral rituals. He stayed in the countryside (Rạch Kiến). Here, he often listened to Buddhist scriptures every evening, recited daily by his two older sisters who were Buddhists.

Because of heavy karmic offenses of killing, he could not enter the temple. After taking refuge, he could enter the temple to listen to Dharma teachings from the monks.

Question:

– Why did he not take refuge in the Triple Gem in the afterlife, but instead borrowed a physical body to take refuge in the human world?

To take refuge in the Triple Gem, one must observe the Three Refuges (take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha) and the Five Precepts (do not kill, do not drink alcohol, do not lie, do not commit sexual misconduct, do not steal). One can take the Three Refuges, but not the Five Precepts, because there is no physical body to follow the Five Precepts.

Question:

– Can beings in the realm of the dead practice? That is, can they meditate, chant sutras, or practice mindfulness of the Buddha?

It is impossible to practice; without the body, how can one practice? (Thoughts and illusions constantly arise, and cannot be eliminated). The human body is precious. The spirit within the human body can only practice. If anyone still has a human body, they should strive to practice. In the next rebirth, you will be able to practice. Your taking refuge this time is to plant the seed in your consciousness, so that in the next rebirth when you are born as a human and encounter the Buddha's Dharma, you will practice immediately. You had a master-disciple relationship with Thầy Thích Giác Hạnh in a previous life.

Question:

– Could you explain more about the master-disciple connection between you and Thầy Thích Giác Hạnh?

In a past life, he was a rebellious young man who came to play in the temple. At that time, Venerable Giac Hanh was a novice monk practicing in the temple. The monk advised him to take refuge in the Triple Gem. He said that he would only take refuge when he no longer had a physical body. From this karmic connection, the teacher-student relationship was formed.

Today, the Venerable has taken him to refuge. But because he does not have a physical body, the teacher-student bond is only 50% complete. Usually, the teacher-student bond must meet over three lifetimes. In the future, Venerable Thich Giac Hanh will be a monk for one more lifetime, and at that time he will be a 100% disciple of the Venerable.

Question:

– Does that mean in this lifetime, Master Giac Hanh has not yet been reborn into the Western Pure Land?

Not yet, because the Buddhas and patriarchs still want him to stay to continue saving sentient beings for another lifetime before he can be reborn there.

Question:

– He has been without his physical body for 36 years. Has he been in contact with the Dharma for long? When will he be reincarnated?

He has only recently approached it, but the power to alter karma is very fast, in every instant. He is about to be able to transcend and be reborn. In about three months, when you dream of the Buddha, that will be when he is reborn.

Question:

– What is his state of mind after death (that is, after losing the physical body)? Why doesn't the dead person leave immediately but returns to the living world?

A person has two parts: the spiritual part and the physical part. The spiritual part is called the soul by Buddhists. When a soul is worshiped, it is called a fragrant soul.

Humans have two ways of dying. One is dying suddenly due to an accident, illness, or some reason without prior preparation. The second is dying of old age, having let go of everything and being prepared in advance.

Those who die young or suddenly often have many unresolved issues, so they cling to their current life. The state of mind at the time of death still lingers until now. That is why he returned to see his family.

Question:

– Why didn't he come back earlier, and why is he returning only now?

He could not return earlier because the person lending him the body had not accumulated enough merit and had not vowed to save sentient beings. Now, that person has made the vow, "Abandon evil, do good, save all sentient beings," so they have enough merit. Because the body lender has good roots and has practiced deeply, they were able to see him when he returned.

Question:

– After losing his body, what did he see happening around him?

He saw that all around him was only a dark red and black color. He felt extremely miserable and could see nothing ahead. He had to live in a state of hunger, cold, and could not return home. No one would let him in. He understood that it was due to the killing karma he had to pay for.

After approaching Buddhism (repenting, reciting the Great Compassion Mantra), he saw that his surroundings gradually became bright, his body and mind felt lighter, and he clearly saw his path.

Question:

– What about the people around him?

They also have colors that are similar. Only those who regularly recite Buddhist sutras and those who practice can have a bright white color after leaving their physical body. He has seen that bright white color around the head of the chief nun Thích nữ Như Vân at Long Hoa Ni Tu – Rạch Kiến Temple.

Question:

– Are there many people who return to the earthly realm like you?

Many. If a living person does not keep a clear mind, they are immediately possessed by them. Because they also really want to have a body. As soon as greed, anger, and ignorance arise, they immediately know. The stronger the delusions, the easier it is for them to possess.

Question:

– When one has a human body, how should one practice so that after losing the body, one can be reborn in the Western Pure Land?

If one wishes to be reborn in the Western Pure Land, one must recite the six-character phrase 'Namo Amitabha Buddha' regularly and continuously. One should eat vegetarian, recite Buddha's name, and perform meritorious deeds. Practice the Ten Virtuous Deeds and observe the Five Precepts. At the time of death, one must recite ten times with a single-minded focus without distraction. If there is a good opportunity and someone assists in reciting, one will certainly be reborn in the Western Pure Land.

Question:

– Previously, I heard from my grandmother that he never taught anyone anything. Why is it that now, when he returns, he advises everyone to practice and recite Buddha's name? What about other religions?

Don't think that death is the end. Life in this world is just a fleeting and impermanent dream. He wants to awaken everyone. Because when the human body is lost, there is nothing left here except one's manifested consciousness. When only consciousness remains, one sees that Buddhism is the true doctrine; only Buddhism can save people from suffering and lead them to liberation. The karma one has created in the past will cling to oneself endlessly, with no knowing when one will be freed.

Namo Amitabha Buddha! If anyone, after reading this interview, suddenly develops the aspiration to practice or those who are already practicing naturally feel more diligent, please dedicate this merit to Mr. Huỳnh Văn Lương along with his colleagues and the soldiers on both sides so that they may attain liberation.

_________________________

( Part 2)

The deceased do not have a guardian to help repel resentful spirits. Therefore, no matter how hard they try, they cannot be reborn in the Western Pure Land. They can only sow blessings by planting the seeds of Buddha in their consciousness abundantly so that when they take human form and come into contact with the Buddha's teachings, they will practice.

Although I could not interview Mr. Huỳnh Văn Lương (a person in the spirit world) directly, through the recorded tape of his conversation with my family members, I was truly moved and gained many realizations.

Nearly 10 years of studying and practicing according to the Buddhist teachings, I have never come across a witness who understands the realms of the living and the dead so profoundly. Referring back to the corresponding Buddhist scriptures, I found it accurate down to every detail.

In the second part of this article, I would like to quote some doctrines taken from the Buddhist scriptures so that readers can understand and believe even more. As followers of the Buddha, we will realize how truly fortunate we are to have access to the teachings of Buddhism. To have the fortune of encountering the Buddha in this lifetime, perhaps among us, there were many lives of practice in the past.

_____

Karmic reception causes the spirits to suffer greatly

In Buddhism, the moment of death and a person's karma are very important. Through Mr. Lương's lectures to his colleagues and soldiers on both sides, we see that after death, people still maintain the state of mind they had at the moment of death when entering the realm of the dead (bardo body).

Therefore, after decades, the soldiers who died in battle because their killing mindset clung to them continued to fight and kill each other. Even without their bodies. If they could not come into contact with the Dharma of the Buddha, perhaps no one knows when they would ever escape that vengeful state of mind.

All people, after death, if they are not extremely virtuous or extremely evil (who are reborn immediately), must face the actions they created in countless past lives. Daily habits such as eating, sleeping, moving around… greed, anger, and delusion are ingrained in the subconscious, so the deceased still feel needs similar to those of a living person with a body.

Not accepting that they have died has led them into a state of coldness, loneliness, hunger, and suffering. According to the reincarnated Lama Lobsang Ramp, because they do not accept the other realm, the dead do not completely move on to the afterlife but remain in the transitional place between the two worlds.

Spirits that cannot be released are very miserable; they are not aware that they have moved to another realm and cling to the earthly world, their minds confused and chaotic.... Only when the spirit becomes sober, able to clearly perceive the events happening around them, aware of their own death, and accepts that death, can they be released.

All those sensations arise due to the attraction of karma. In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha said to Bodhisattva Samantabhadra: "O Human! It is all because sentient beings in the hell realm commit evil deeds, which according to karma attract such hells. The force of karma is immense, comparable to Mount Sumeru, as deep as the ocean, capable of obstructing the path of the saints.

Lama Lobsang Ramp also stated that: not attaining liberation will create much suffering. Their souls are trapped, wrapped in a shell created by themselves, so they can no longer see anything outside.... Over time, as desires diminish, this shell will gradually dissolve, and at some point, they will become aware of this and will achieve liberation.

After losing his physical body, Mr. Luong said that around him was enveloped in a red-black color and he could see nothing at all.

The Esoteric Buddhist practice holds that only when the physical body and the desire body completely dissolve can a person attain liberation and be reborn into a new life. The desire body is made up of desires, cravings, and emotions in general... The desire body determines how long a person must remain in the underworld. Those with fewer desires and a pure heart can attain liberation more easily than those with many desires.

The Theravada school believes that if a person has not been reborn after 49 days, they are classified as wandering ghosts or spirits. Therefore, the doctrine of the Theravada sect does not recognize the existence of an intermediate or bardo world.

Those who have not attained liberation after 49 days are beings who are still overly attached to worldly life, so in their next rebirth, they are likely to enter the realm of hungry ghosts.

Now they understand why it is said that after losing a human life, 70–80% reincarnate into the realm of hungry ghosts. Our karma after losing a human life is still precarious. If the mind clings too strongly to the earthly life, it remains in the spirit world for too long. The longer it stays, the more karma connects it to hungry ghost existence, and thus our next realm will be that of a hungry ghost.

The miraculous, inconceivable nature of the Buddha's mantras.

To transform the mind, change karma, and eliminate karmic obstacles… the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have given sentient beings many mantras. Many of us often take chanting sutras and reciting mantras lightly, because we have not yet seen immediate results.

When a person still has a physical body, due to the heaviness of the material form, the power of mantras has little effect on the mind. When a person loses their physical body, it acts like a magical medicine that transforms the mind very quickly.

Therefore, Mr. Luong said that he has only recently approached Buddhism, but the power to transform karma is very fast, happening in every moment.

According to him, it is only when he approaches the path of Buddha that his mind begins to let go.

After reciting the Great Compassion Mantra and listening to Buddhist teachings, he noticed that the colors around him changed from black and red to bright colors. The colors or the light field surrounding both living people and spirits reflect the thoughts, state, and emotions of the mind (I have discussed this issue in depth in my article on photographing spirits – Why glowing circles appear).

Through what he said, we see that Buddha's Dharma is truly boundless. The mantras are truly wonderful and inconceivable.

Thus, letting go is not only for those who practice while alive, but it is also extremely necessary for souls in attaining liberation. If we do not cultivate the habit while still alive, it will be difficult for us to develop a mind of letting go when we cross into the other world.

Not all sentient beings are fortunate enough to access the Dharma in the spirit realm like Mr. Luong. If one does not have the affinity to encounter the Dharma and does not recite sutras and mantras, perhaps the next realm of rebirth would make it difficult for him to escape from animals and hungry ghosts.

Tantric Buddhism believes that prayer, especially using mantras, will produce special sounds that can vibrate in the spiritual realm, affecting consciousness and helping souls trapped in the cocoon of ignorance to awaken. It is not only mantras that are effective; sincere prayers from loved ones are equally beneficial...

Prayer has a mental power that exerts a very strong force in the otherworldly realm.

Dedicate merit to support reducing the karmic consequences for the deceased.

If spirits are unable to be liberated, the longer they remain in the realm of the dead, the more karma they create, leading to rebirth in the world of hungry ghosts. Tibetans believe that the period immediately after death is extremely important because at that time the soul has just left the body and is emotionally agitated, needing guidance and reassurance.

If not properly guided, the soul may wander without being able to be liberated and become types of lost spirits without a place to rely on, or sometimes be exploited by beings of the underworld and led into dangerous paths.

For the dead not to linger long in the underworld and to be quickly liberated, the role of relatives is very important. It is not by chance that Mr. Huỳnh Văn Lương requested his children and grandchildren to set up a ceremonial feast to pray for his own salvation and for those around him to be liberated. Living in that realm, he understood that without the support and assistance of relatives, it is very difficult for souls in the underworld to be liberated.

In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, there is a passage: "The soul of the deceased, before being reborn, remains for forty-nine days, constantly looking forward to the relatives performing virtuous deeds to save them… The close relatives of the dying should prepare a grand offering, recite the Sutras, chant the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and cultivate such karmic blessings. By doing so, it can help the deceased escape the realms of evil; all kinds of demons, ghosts, and evil spirits will all be driven away."

When the granddaughter said she was making merit to dedicate it to her grandfather because (he was experiencing the retribution of being reborn into a suffering realm), Mr. Luong replied that the most effective dedication is by his closest relatives, the children, followed by grandchildren. When doing good deeds and creating merit, one should not kill any living being. If there is still killing, it will only create more bad karma for the beings in the afterlife.

In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha also spoke to the Buddha: “For this reason, I now stand before the World-Honored Buddha together with the assembly of devas, dragons, the eight classes of beings, humans, non-humans, etc., to give counsel to sentient beings in the hell realm, that at the time of death, their relatives must be careful not to kill or create unwholesome karma, and also must not make offerings to ghosts or spirits, nor make prayers to demons or monsters… Why is this so? Because acts of killing or making such offerings bring no benefit at all to the deceased; they only add to the deceased's karmic burden, making it even heavier.”

Kṣitigarbha explained as follows: “It is like this: suppose someone comes from a distant land, having been without food for three days, carrying items weighing over a hundred pounds. Suddenly, a nearby person sends them some additional items, which only makes the person from the distant land suffer even more.”

Psychic Nguyễn Văn Nhã also proved this. When he recited 108 times 'Nam Mô A Di Đà Phật,' not only he but also the seven psychics present at the Trường Sơn cemetery saw the spirits sitting down in a meditative posture, reciting along.

Psychics believe that only the Buddha's name is the most precious gift for beings in the realm of the dead. The Buddha's name inspires a mind that lets go of all attachments and can lead to liberation. If we are constantly worried about burning paper offerings for chickens and ducks, or building huge tombs for the deceased, we are effectively wishing them to live longer in that extremely miserable world.

Keeping a pure heart, reciting sutras and mantras, and chanting the Buddha's name are also ways of generating merit.

Because they have escaped from their physical body, the spirits can read all the thoughts of the living. They can sense what others are thinking. There is a very interesting detail. While having a conversation, the female colleague (the niece) thought about the sick dog at home that no one was taking care of. Mr. Lương suddenly exclaimed, why do I see all dogs around me like this!

This shows that, after losing a loved one, if the people in the family recite Buddhist scriptures daily and often remember the deceased, the spirits will be able to access the Dharma. Because at that time, they have not gone anywhere and are still lingering around the house.

Chants and consoling prayers will affect the consciousness of the deceased; the spirits will experience peace and liberation. This is a very good form of support for the departed.

From this detail, we can see why it is necessary to always maintain purity in the mind. Because when we generate ill thoughts, the world of demons will invade due to synchronization in sound and intention.

Because cause and effect are inescapable, one must practice virtue while having a human body.

Many times in conversations with his family members, Mr. Luong advised his relatives that "one must cultivate virtue." Whenever he met someone, he would say "one must cultivate virtue" because human life is very short. What is the point of having a lot of money, or high power and prestigious positions? The more one has, the more karmic suffering one accumulates. Just having enough to eat and clothes to wear is sufficient. Only through cultivation can one change one's karmic obstacles. Without cultivation, one will continue to follow karma and be reborn into realms of suffering.

When no longer having a physical body, he was able to approach Buddhism, the surroundings around him gradually brightened, and he could clearly see the law of cause and effect through past, present, and future lives.

There is a dialogue pattern when talking about the future lives of family members that is very interesting. He was able to see which realm some of his relatives would go to after death. The reason why they were reborn in that realm. A person with merit will be reborn as a man. A person who refuses to work, is lazy, and owes others will be reborn as a dog. A person who is addicted to gambling will be reborn as a poor person, carrying baskets, begging for half of their first life...

It is all due to the deeds sown in this life, which must bear fruit in the future.

A conversation failed because of the girl's stubbornness; he immediately saw that her retribution would be having a father who does not love her in a future life. His entire life, from when he had a physical body to when he existed in the spirit world, moved according to the law of cause and effect. He saw clearly and understood the importance of practicing virtue while still in the human body.

In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra it is said: “Therefore, sentient beings should not despise even small wrongdoings and consider them harmless; after death, everyone will face retribution, even down to the tiniest detail.”

Through the interview, we can clearly see why sentient beings in the underworld cannot cultivate and must have a human body to practice. Beings in the underworld cannot uphold the Five Precepts and practice the Ten Wholesome Deeds. Beings in the underworld cannot recite the 10 phrases of Amitabha Buddha without distraction, because the delusions in the consciousness of spirits increase ninefold compared to those with a physical body.

The dead do not have monks to perform chanting rituals to ward off vengeful spirits. Therefore, no matter how hard they try, they cannot be reborn in the Western Pure Land. They can only create merit by sowing the seeds of Buddha in their consciousness so that when they attain a human body and encounter the Dharma, they will practice.

Namo Amitabha Buddha! I dedicate this merit to the Western Pure Land. I also dedicate this merit to Mr. Huỳnh Văn Lương and his associates, to the soldiers on both sides, and to all sentient beings advancing on the path to Buddhahood!

tom_tat: HOW MANY PEOPLE TRULY UNDERSTAND YOU? THAT'S RIGHT, EVERY PERSON YOU MEET IN THIS LIFE IS A DESTINED ARRANGEMENT OF KARMIC RELATIONSHIPS.
noi_dung:
THE FLOW OF TIME PEOPLE COME AND GO,

HOW MANY PEOPLE REALLY UNDERSTAND YOUR HEART?

THAT'S RIGHT, EVERY PERSON YOU MEET IN THIS LIFE IS AN ARRANGEMENT OF FATE.

No one appears in your life without reason; the presence of each person has a purpose and is worthy of gratitude.

Everything begins with fate, and everything ends also because of fate.

+ The person you love brings you warmth and courage, bravery to face difficulties in life.

+ The person you love will teach you what it means to love and cherish, to treasure what you have.

+ The person you dislike teaches you to be tolerant and to know how to respect, forgive others and yourself.

+ The person who dislikes you helps you grow, making you cautious, reflecting on yourself.

If destined, we come together; if fate ends, we part ways. We are merely passersby in each other's lives, and can only accompany someone for a certain stretch of life.

In fact, meeting each other is truly a heavenly fate. Whether we feel joy or sorrow, stay together or part, be close or distant, go or stay, hold on or let go, lift up or put down, accept or reject—all of these seem to be determined by worldly matters, all lie in the hearts of humans.

No matter how much of life there is, it is merely a stretch of road where we can meet and get to know each other. Whether it is ten years, twenty years, or a hundred years of a person's life, it is still just a stretch of road. And we can only have the fate to walk together for just a certain part of it.

THERE IS A SAYING:

"Because we take things lightly, we are joyful.

Because we take things plainly, we are happy."

Between heaven and earth, we are all merely passing travelers; there are many aspects of life and situations that we can never truly control. For example, as time passes, how can we grasp it... etc... the more we try to hold onto it, the more it tends to slip away from us quickly.

Everything depends on fate; if the connection is deep, it will cling and reunite, if the connection is shallow, it will naturally go away. In life, the more we can regard things lightly and take them lightly, the more suffering will distance itself from us.

Everyone fears that there will be times when they are not clear-headed, wishing that their mind could be as bright as a mirror. In fact, why does life need to be too alert?

+ Porridge should be cooked with 3 parts rice and 7 parts water.

+ In dealing with others, one should act 3 parts for oneself and 7 parts for others.

+ With friends, one should have 3 parts discernment of true feelings and 7 parts tolerance.

+ With family, one should have 3 parts love and 7 parts responsibility.

+ Reading literature requires focusing 3 parts on form, 7 parts on the quality of content.

+ Drinking alcohol requires 3 parts intoxicated, 7 parts sober.

"3 PARTS... 7 PARTS..." IS TRULY THE PROPORTION OF LIFE.

In the sutras, the Buddha spoke of four types of conditions.

All of us being present here together is not by chance but because we have had connections over many lifetimes, so we meet today:

- There are people I have never known before, but upon meeting them, they seem friendly, familiar, as if I have met them somewhere before.

- Or there are people I meet and immediately dislike. That is a sign that we have karma together from many past lives, and are only now meeting again.

- People I have once been grateful to, I feel affection for as soon as I see them.

- People who have caused enmity, I feel annoyed as soon as I see them.

We humans, due to creating mixed causes of good and evil, are born in the realm of suffering and must endure this. Things come together because of causes, and they dissolve because of causes. When there are sufficient causes, it remains; when the causes are gone, it ends. When causes are still present, no matter how much destruction occurs, it cannot be ruined; when the causes are gone, no matter how one tries to hold on, it will simply fall apart.

"SIT ANYWHERE AND SEE PEACE

WHEN YOU HAVE RETURNED TO REALITY

NO MATTER HOW COUNTLESS THINGS COME AND GO

THE NATURAL HEART REMAINS..."

tieu_de: CONSCIOUSNESS WARNED ABOUT THE UPCOMING GREAT DISASTER
tom_tat: Yes, I would like to tell my story as follows! I have been vegetarian for more than 5 months and have been copying the Kṣitigarbha Sutra as well as reading the Sutra! By this July, I vowed to read the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra every day at least once.
noi_dung:
CONSCIOUSNESS WARNED ABOUT THE UPCOMING GREAT DISASTER

Yes, I would like to tell my story as follows!

I have been vegetarian for more than 5 months and have been copying the Kṣitigarbha Sutra as well as reading the Sutra! This July, I made a vow to read at least one complete volume of the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra (upper, middle, lower) every day, and during the 10-day retreat, I read it once a day!

Today, just like every time I take a nap, before I sleep I chant Buddha's name and the Bodhisattvas. When I wake up unexpectedly at the hour when I usually prepare for the scripture session, today I was a bit tired, so I thought in my mind to sleep a little longer and then wake up for the session!

Then, during that nap time, it was as if a certain message naturally came to me, but it spoke through consciousness, and I also heard it through consciousness!

I would like to quote exactly what I heard:

"In the coming time, something terrible will happen that has never occurred in heaven and earth. Even the Buddha and Bodhisattvas, who save the ranks of Devas and Spirits, would find it difficult, let alone sentient beings. More than anyone else, right now, sentient beings must recognize this and save themselves. Just like when I read the sutras, merely reading them aloud is no different from other books, but when I deeply absorb the words of the sutras and nurture the seed of moral virtue within me, that is when I truly save myself!"

And I feel it as though it were the words of the Buddha or the Bodhisattvas, which I can only sense and listen to through the consciousness of everyone!

I don't know if my story can help everyone be more diligent, but I feel that the Dharma is truly wonderful! Let's strive to practice in order to overcome this difficult pandemic!

Source: Tran Ruby

tom_tat: (Severely infected with negative energy, having a spirit, a resentful entity relying on you or disturbing you, being tested in cultivation, falling into a ghostly realm) CHECK BY READING OR LISTENING TO ONE OF THE 3 MANTRAS for about 30-45 minutes
noi_dung:
HOW TO CHECK IF YOU HAVE SPIRITUAL ISSUES - Full SUPPORT FOR NEW PRACTITIONERS

(Severely affected by negative energy, having wandering spirits, relying on or being disturbed by resentful entities, undergoing spiritual trials, or falling into ghostly existence)

CHECK BY SELF-READING OR LISTENING TO ONE OF THE 3 MANTRAS for about 30-45 minutes

1. LANKYEN MANTRA🙏

2. 6-SYLLABLE MANTRA: OM MANI PAD ME HUM🙏

3. LOTUS BORN MANTRA:

OM AH HUNG BENZA GURU PADMA SITI HUNG🙏

- Spiritual issues manifest when hearing or reading one of the three mantras, causing shivers, fatigue, restlessness, heaviness in the head, unbearable headache, and sticky sweat...

- The exorcising power of these three mantras is very strong; those with issues just hearing the name of the mantra can feel fear or unwillingness—daring not to listen or read.

Other daily manifestations:

- Preference for cold food and drinks, and raw, fishy food.

- Frequently dreams of strange things that cause confusion or fear.

- Hearing a stranger's voice telling you that your practice is not good or to give up practice, or praising that your practice is good enough and you no longer need to practice.

- Not wanting to do daily spiritual practice anymore.

- Claiming enlightenment without proof, arrogantly declaring oneself as having attained the level of Spirit, Sage, Immortal, or Buddha.

Or believing oneself to have a divine mission, becoming fanatical about the path, with a haughty and arrogant temperament.

- Being informed of or seeing certain future events and then mistakenly thinking one is enlightened or truly has a divine mission.

- After undergoing internal trials, external trials, favorable trials, adverse trials, and devilish trials,

+ First is fear causing loss of resolve, or abandoning the path.

+ Second is doubting the method or practice one is following.

+ Third is feeling pride due to favorable circumstances, developing arrogance that leads to scrutinizing and speaking ill of other paths or methods, unknowingly becoming someone who destroys their own path.

* Those who have just generated the intention to practice or those practicing with blessings and determination will encounter such spiritual issues.

- For beginners in meditative practice, it may be because they have just started their practice (chanting sutras, reciting Buddha's name, reciting mantras) and do not yet know about dedicating merit.

- In cases where wandering spirits or resentful beings attach themselves to us or disturb us, we should sincerely repent, practice diligently, and dedicate merit to them.

(Remember that they are also suffering; we must sincerely repent and sincerely practice in order to help them be free from suffering, not just as a formality, because if we try to end their karmic debts superficially, they will not accept it).

- In the case of falling into a ghost realm, it is because through practice one has attained concentration power, and when the spiritual channel opens, delusive thoughts arise, leading to falling into the ghost realm. The way to counter this situation is to strictly observe moral precepts and study the Heart Sutra daily. The Heart Sutra is very important, so it should be recited and the meaning of the verses understood and practiced. It is better at this stage to have a guide who has gone before to instruct.

+ In special cases, when reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra with strong spiritual power, some may experience headaches or soreness in the beginning due to karmic forces, or dream of insects flying out of the body, or black energy escaping, which indicates the purification of karma.
