tieu_de: EIGHT LIVES OF REINCARNATION & EXTRAORDINARY DEBTS AND GRUDGES.
tom_tat: (Tĩnh Như rewrote from Thu Hương's account). Cause and Effect - Reincarnation - Fated Enemies … Some people may doubt, half believe and half question these concepts. But for me, it is absolutely certain. I believe in it a thousand
noi_dung:
EIGHT REINCARNATIONS & BIZARRE GRUDGES.

(Tĩnh Như wrote this based on Thu Hương's account).

Cause and Effect - Reincarnation - Fated Enemies … Some may doubt, half-believing and half-skeptical about these concepts. But for me, it is completely certain. I believe in it a thousand times over, as firmly as nails in wood. Because I myself am the living proof, a real-life example.

Over the years, I have had to bear the consequences of my own karma. Fortunately, thanks to practicing cultivation, my karma has lessened. Otherwise, at this moment, I would no longer be alive to be here and tell you my story. Those who still doubt the Law of Cause and Effect, and happen to come across my life story, should awaken immediately, lest it be too late.

My real name is Phạm Thu Hương, 49 years old (in 2021), living in Ba Đình, Hanoi. I have been a strict vegetarian for 15 years. I took refuge in the Three Jewels and received the Dharma name Ngọc Hương. My Master is Zen Master An Lạc Hạnh, whose Dharma name is Thích Giác Sự, abbot of Liên Hoa Monastery, Bạch Đằng commune, Tân Uyên, Bình Dương.

My Master is a highly accomplished practitioner, capable of seeing the past lives of others. With his guidance, I have discovered at least 8 of my previous lives. Below, I will briefly recount them for you to hear:

In one lifetime, I was of Indian origin. In that life, I came to Vietnam and participated in the war against French colonialism. Unfortunately, I died right here in Vietnam at that time. You know, everything that happens in life, whether big or small, has its own cause and condition. Even the fact of which country you are born in is like that. It is precisely because of the karmic connection from a past life, having once fought and died here, that in this life, I was reborn as a Vietnamese person.

In many previous lives, I was also an Indian, and then a Cambodian. In these lives, I served as an execution officer for the court, that is, I carried out the task of executing criminals. Although I only performed the duties and responsibilities assigned by the court, this work has brought me much pain and suffering in my present life. The souls of those I executed in past lives still follow me to seek revenge in this life.

You know, in ancient feudal times there was the law of exterminating three generations. When a person committed a serious crime, their entire family would also be executed. Not only was the offender executed, but many other relatives also suffered unjustly. Therefore, the number of people I executed in those lifetimes was very large.

They follow me, cling to my body to take revenge, tormenting me up to this life. Not only these resentful spirits, but also the ones I have killed and eaten in this life. All of them stick to my body. They are right inside me, in my head. My head hurts so much that I have to keep hitting it with my hand all day long to overpower the painful feeling.

Fortunately, I know about Buddhist Dharma, diligently practicing to resolve the karmic debts with these resentful spirits. I recite sutras, chant mantras, chant Buddha’s name, offer alms to monks, dedicate merits to them, and repay their debts. Therefore, the karma also becomes a bit lighter.

After making merit and dedicating it to repay debts in this way, my master saw that the number of karmic enemies attached to me was only half of what it was initially. Since then, I have also experienced fewer headaches. As for the remaining karmic enemies, I continue to persistently resolve them gradually.

There are many strange stories related to my ghostly enemy. I often hear weird noises all over the house, without knowing who is making them. I hear a booming sound as if someone is beating a drum. Sometimes, when I am sitting on the bed, I hear very strong knocking sounds in the attic, which startle me. When I cook in the kitchen, there is knocking right next to the stove. Sometimes, there are knocks coming from the refrigerator. Only later did I realize it was caused by the ghostly enemy.

In a past life, I was a weasel, and I ate a lot of different insects. In this life, their spirits still reside within my body. I kept reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and at night I dreamed of catching many insects from within my flesh; they were all over my body. Seeing this made me panic and be completely horrified.

In this life, before I knew about Buddhist teachings, out of ignorance, I took many lives. Once, I roasted a bird to eat. Later, recalling that act, I repented and recited the fivefold Lăng Nghiêm 60 times DEDICATING MERIT to the bird.

(Please note, I recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra to dedicate the merit to my karmic enemies, not to rely on the power of the mantra to drive them away; the two are fundamentally different, and the results are also different).

By night, I dreamed that the spirits of those birds had escaped from my body. Around 3 a.m., I woke up, feeling my face burning, probably because I had roasted birds before, causing them to endure the torment of their bodies being burned. Afterwards, I chanted the Avalokiteshvara mantra into water, then used that water to wash my face, and the burning sensation finally subsided.

One day, I had a strange dream. I dreamed that I was inside the house when many people came to knock on the door, asking me to open it. When I opened the door, I saw two people carrying an injured man, his left leg covered in blood.

Finding it strange, I immediately asked my master about the dream. Upon hearing this, knowing that it was an omen, he guided me to repent by bowing to Buddha 108 times and releasing animals. After that, he told me to take a bowl of roasted salt and then burn all of it to dispel all negative energy. I followed this exactly as instructed.

Not long after, that day it was drizzling and the road was slippery. I was riding a motorbike down the Lang Ha overpass slope, carrying a sack of sand, so I had to stretch my legs out to both sides. Because I didn't see the car driving right next to me, my leg stretched all the way under the car beside me.

At that moment, I was too surprised and panicked, and I only had time to chant Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. The vehicle ran over my left leg twice in a row. Seeing this, people from the roadside came out to help and even told me not to move at all, fearing that all the bones might come out. Yet in the end, I only ended up with muscle bruising, guys.

Later I found out that it was due to a foe who pushed me into the car. That day was supposed to be the day I would die. Luckily, I was warned by a dream, and by following my master's guidance, I was able to resolve the karma and escape death, and my legs were not seriously injured.

In another lifetime, due to some issues, my wife made me jealous, so I went to a sorcerer and performed a talisman spell to make my wife's body itchy.

So after dying, the consciousness of my wife in that life is still in me, making me also itchy and uncomfortable in all delicate, unspeakable places, greatly affecting daily life and mental state. I went for check-ups and tried various treatments, but it did not go away. Finally, I repented and recited mantras to dedicate merit to repay the debt to my wife in the previous life, and now the itching has improved by 80%.

A few years ago, I suffered from insomnia because I was tormented by hostile spirits. One night, I was pressed down by shadows 20 times. I would recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra three lines, and they would be released. Then they would press me down again, making me unable to move. I kept reciting, and they released me again. This happened 20 times throughout the night. After many nights, I was extremely exhausted, both physically and mentally affected.

Furthermore, in the past, I bought a house, and during renovations, the builders placed a Lỗ Ban charm, a type of talisman commonly used by construction workers. The spells cast by dark practitioners always harbor evil spirits. My house that was cursed was no exception.

They caused my family a lot of trouble. They influenced my child to be stubborn and disobedient to parents. They secretly ate food in the house. Even in winter, if left for a day, the food would spoil completely, including the food stored in the refrigerator.

My master guided me to paste Bagua images on baskets, racks, and the refrigerator. That way, they wouldn't be able to eat. I followed the instructions and it was truly effective. Any food I covered with a basket or rack that had the Bagua image stuck on it would not spoil, but food covered with a basket or rack without the image would spoil immediately. If the refrigerator didn't have the Bagua image, the food stored inside would spoil as usual.

Knowing that there were such spirits in the house, I recited the Lăng Nghiêm scripture to dedicate the merit to help them attain liberation. After 15 years, most of them had gone, leaving only 2 spirits around 30 years old. These 2 spirits were bound and chained due to a Lỗ Ban talisman, so they couldn't go anywhere. My master said that I am still very fortunate to be able to live in this house.

The spirits were really very afraid of Master Lăng Nghiêm. One day, half asleep and half awake, I saw a male ghost lying right next to me. Panicked, I intended to recite Master Lăng Nghiêm's mantra. Before I could start, it seemed that the ghost could read my mind, he immediately said: "Please don't recite the mantra," then the ghost ran out very quickly, making thundering footsteps down the stairs.

Understanding the law of cause and effect and reincarnation, I know that everything is due to my own karma. I dare not resent those adversaries who have caused troubles and difficulties in my life. On the contrary, I know it is because in past lives I created bad karma with them, so now I am facing this. Therefore, I always practice, generate merit, and dedicate it to them, hoping to partially atone for my own sins.

Do you know, because I have accumulated too much karma, when I diligently practice, the power of sutras, of chanting mantras, and of reciting Buddha's name has helped me eliminate karma, causing my body to emit a very strong, fishy smell. I know some people often feel very hot during their practice, even sweating in the middle of winter. It's okay, these are just normal phenomena, and they will gradually disappear.

I remember one time when I practiced diligently, at night I even dreamed of a bird bursting out of my chest, and then I completely recovered from heart disease. Another time I dreamed of pulling worms out of my anus, and then I completely recovered from hemorrhoids. Buddhist Dharma is so wondrous.

Not only is my health poor, but in my married life, I am also not happy. I don’t understand why my husband always seems to dislike me and constantly scolds me harshly. But upon reflection, it is true that when husband and wife meet and form a bond, it is also due to karma from many past lives. Whether husband and wife treat each other well or badly depends partly on their present behavior and partly on the debts and grievances from distant past lives.

Later, I found out that it turned out, due to a previous life, there were also unresolved issues between us. In that life, we had been husband and wife, but we switched roles: I was male, the husband, and he was female, my primary wife. I also had a second wife. Because the first wife could not bear children, I lived with the second wife. This caused the first wife to feel sorrow and hatred towards me. That hatred was the cause, and its effect carried over to this life, where I am hated and scolded by my husband.

Not only that, there is another matter that I could never have imagined. My husband often attracted the spirit of a woman, who frequently possessed him to scold me. This female spirit was Chinese and 23 years old.

When possessing him, the spirit said that she had a relationship with my husband before we got married. And they even had two children together in the spirit world. Hearing this, I was utterly shocked. Strange, can a human and a ghost have children together?

There are events and realms that, although the human eye cannot see, it does not mean they do not exist. In fact, the lives of the living and the dead can be interconnected in such ways. For that reason, this female spirit became jealous, repeatedly possessing my husband to scold me to satisfy her anger. Because of such a tragic situation, my husband and I no longer live together; each of us stays in our own house.

Not only marital relationships, but all relationships with us in this life come from karmic ties of gratitude and resentment. If the affinity is small, we only come together for a short time, experience a few minor events, and then our connection ends and we part ways. If the affinity is stronger, we can become family members.

I also have a younger sister. In a previous life, we were married to the same husband. When sharing a husband, the wives are rarely happy together; most often, there is jealousy and resentment among them. Carrying that mindset into this life, my sister keeps feeling jealousy toward me in the same way.

It seems that I have been cultivating and dedicating merits for my enemies and creditors caused by grievances over many lifetimes, so now my younger sibling dislikes me less, although not completely, but it has reduced by half. Then there is also my neighbor, it turns out that in the previous life we were sisters-in-law.

In this world, whenever people encounter unfavorable living conditions, they often think they are being treated unfairly, complain to heaven and blame the earth, believing that the one at fault is the other party, not themselves. Who would have thought, everything still originates from oneself. The very thoughts and actions we have will determine our living circumstances in the future. That is clear cause and effect.

My life has been full of such hardships. My health is not good, my family is broken, and my business isn't going well either. All of it is because I created too much evil karma, harmed others, and now I am being obstructed by them in every possible way.

In one lifetime, I was a butcher, specializing in killing various animals such as dogs, cows, and buffaloes. Some people advised me to give up this cruel profession, but at that time I was determined not to quit, using the excuse that I still needed to make a living.

How foolish and ignorant I was, in so many past lives, I committed heavy killing karma. Therefore, in this life, I endure all kinds of suffering. Avenging enemies and debtors continuously came, ruining me so I couldn't make a living. If I had not practiced according to the Buddha's teachings as I do now to lessen my karmic obstacles, I would be begging on the streets by now, my friends.

Speaking of repentance and praying for the deceased, my master also mentioned that usually, those who recite sutras, chant mantras, and dedicate merit to help the deceased attain liberation must have strong power for the spirits to be able to move on. The strong power here refers to the virtue and diligence of the practitioner.

This is said so that we understand that it is not the case that a mind full of greed, anger, and ignorance, without knowing how to repent or regret, committing evil deeds without restraint, living corruptly, can resolve issues just by reciting a single sutra or mantra.

Simply chanting like that brings very little merit in the present. If the merit is small, how can it be dedicated to others? Therefore, the practice of chanting and reciting must always be accompanied by virtue, precepts, etc., to fully bring out the power of sutras and mantras. Without moral conduct, one can only achieve good results by being five or ten times more persistent than others.

My master also taught: during the practice of cultivation, chanting sutras, reciting mantras, and reciting Buddha's name, one should not use the five pungent spices. These things have a very strong, sharp smell, which makes the mouth impure and will reduce the merit of practice. For those who specialize in chanting sutras and mantras, if they want effectiveness, they should only use the five pungent spices if necessary for medicinal purposes; once healed, they should stop.

Throughout many lifetimes, I have committed too many crimes. So in this life, I must repay all kinds of accumulated karma. But perhaps, because I have also had a karmic connection with Buddhist Dharma, in this life, fortunately, I can still resolve some of it, helping to lighten the karmic obstacles. I, in a past life in India, also once left home to practice monastic life. Now I also vow that in my next life I will again leave home to cultivate the Buddhist path.

But don't think that in this life we can repay all our debts. We have lived in the cycle of reincarnation for countless past lives, and the evil karma created is also boundless, infinite. That is why everyone has an incalculable number of enemies and karmic creditors. It's just that in this life, whether they have sufficient karma to find and stick to us, to demand repayment, remains to be seen. Therefore, the number of enemies attached to me now is only within the scope of current karmic connections.

If someone thinks they can completely eliminate all karma in this lifetime, that is an illusion. We strive to repay our debts, receiving as much good as we can. There is a saying among people: “Repay karma, do good deeds, practice the path.” That is the fastest way to achieve liberation soon. You should look at the story of my life to awaken early.

The scope of the Law of Cause and Effect is infinite; suffering is not only experienced during life, and even after death, one cannot escape it. For example, my maternal grandfather-in-law's brother, in his previous life, committed murder and robbery, and in this life, even after death, he is still being pursued and severely beaten, suffering immensely. My master was able to see this and guided us to have our close family members create merits and dedicate those merits to help our father escape disaster.

But his descendants don’t believe anything at all. If I were to say directly now, "Your father once killed people and robbed," they might even beat me up before I could react. I have offered him joss paper, but in the underworld they take it all into storage and he can’t receive it because of severe sins.

Why does it have to be the biological descendants who perform merit-making and dedicate it to their father? Because the closer people are to each other, the deeper the bond. When these people dedicate merit, the amount of merit the deceased receives is greater. If it is someone distant, with no connection, the amount of merit received is smaller.

That is my story. My life has been full of all kinds of suffering. Fortunately, the Dharma has brought me the light of truth, giving me the remedy to transform suffering. I also express my gratitude to the merits of my Master – Zen Master An Lac Hanh, who has enlightened me on many things.

Meditation master An Lac Hanh, in a previous life, was from India and was a king of that land. Continuing the karmic connection from past lives, now I again meet the master. The master said that the name “An Lac Hanh” was given to him by Buddha Shakyamuni. Invisible beings in the underworld, when looking at the master, do not see his form as we do; they only see a halo of light emanating from him. Perhaps it is because the master’s virtue is too powerful.

Currently, the epidemic caused by the coronavirus is raging severely, causing many people to die extremely quickly. This is also due to the karmic retribution of humanity. The Zen Master shared that: This virus is sent by the deity of epidemics, following the will of heaven, to spread everywhere. The purpose is to purify those whose karma requires them to endure this retribution.

In particular, the Master advised sentient beings: Recite the White-Robed Mantra of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, bless water with it and then drink it, and you will be cured. Other methods such as repentance, reciting sutras and mantras, chanting the Buddha’s name, etc., also have similar efficacy.

But it is also due to karma and fortune; anyone who has enough affinity and merit to avoid this disaster will surely encounter a successful remedy. Those who do not have enough affinity or merit, even if they come across it, will ignore it, turn a deaf ear, or not believe and not practice. Cause and effect is always fair, not a bit of it is wrong.

My master has never craved fame or fortune. For over 40 years, he has been treating people for free every day. In cases of clear cause-and-effect retribution, he has recorded videos to upload on YouTube on the channel named "Tịnh Xá Liên Hoa," or you can search with the keywords "Zen Master An Lạc Hạnh," with the purpose of warning everyone to clearly understand the law of cause and effect.

Many people do not understand the truth and instead accuse the master of fabricating things to deceive. Some have falsely accused him and faced retribution, being "unable to live in life, nor at peace in death." That is the sin of slandering and defaming a virtuous person.

However, now the Zen master is already 85 years old, so he no longer directly treats illnesses. He has compiled a book of repentance and debt repayment rituals for everyone to follow on their own. Partly because of his advanced age, his strength is limited. In addition, we must understand that nothing is better than the offender themselves repenting by their own effort. That is the way to cure the root of the illness, which is our own mind.

My master instructed me to repent every day for the crimes we have committed, which are truly too numerous to count. Just like Maitreya Bodhisattva – the bodhisattva who is sent to be reborn in each lifetime, in the Tushita heaven still repents six times a day. So we, as ordinary people with such heavy karma, how can we not repent?

I tell this story for no other purpose than to awaken everyone to cause and effect, and hope that everyone can see the subtlety of the Buddha's teachings. It is with the hope that more and more people will deeply believe in cause and effect, abandon evil, do good, and soon return to the shore of enlightenment, relying on the Triple Gem, awakening and practicing cultivation.

tieu_de: HOW TO TAKE REFUGE AND OFFER SACRIFICES TO LORD KṢITIGARBHA TO QUICKLY RECEIVE BLESSINGS
tom_tat: Currently, there are many places offering offerings to the statue of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha to create connections and support practitioners. However, the true meaning and the method of taking refuge, making offerings, worshiping, and practicing according to His teachings
noi_dung:
HOW TO TAKE REFUGE AND MAKE OFFERINGS TO KSIROK Kṣitigarbha TO QUICKLY RECEIVE BLESSINGS

Nowadays, many places offer reverence to the statue of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha to create a connection and support practitioners. However, the true meaning and the proper way to take refuge, make offerings, pay homage, and practice according to His teachings in order to achieve the immeasurable benefits mentioned in the sutras are not well understood, and there is no one clearly explaining it. Today, I would like to guide you on how to take refuge and make offerings to the Bodhisattva to quickly receive His blessings!

1. HOW TO TAKE REFUGE IN BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA:

Every day when beginning the ceremony, you should face the Buddha altar or the statue of Kṣitigarbha (if not available, you can clasp your hands and recite the refuge prayer; the important thing is to be utmost respectful and faithful) and make the following vow to take refuge in the Bodhisattva, consistently without missing any day:

My name is..., Dharma name is..., today I hear the Buddha expound on the inconceivable matters of the Great Holy Kṣitigarbha, which moves my heart. Wholeheartedly before Him, I wish to make this vow: from today until the end of future lives, until the day I attain Buddhahood, I vow to take refuge in Him for countless lifetimes; from today until the end of future lives, until the day I attain Buddhahood, I vow in countless lifetimes to use numerous skillful means to guide and encourage all sentient beings so that they may know Him and take refuge in Him.

Great Saint Kṣitigarbha! I earnestly hope that You will be compassionate and merciful to witness my refuge and this vow, so that I will never forget it in all my lifetimes. Currently, I am an ignorant and foolish being, profoundly burdened by karma. I humbly beseech the Great Saint to show compassion and mercy to me and all sentient beings, granting that I and all living creatures may attain peace, have all wishes fulfilled, expand our wisdom, eliminate karmic obstacles, swiftly achieve the purity of our original mind, and ultimately quickly transcend the cycle of birth and death to attain Buddhahood. Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahā-sattva. (3 times, 1 prostration)

Taking refuge in a Bodhisattva means relying on and following their teachings. In the sutras, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva repeatedly speaks of the painful retributions in hell, all caused by killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and lying. Therefore, once you have faith and take refuge in the Bodhisattva, you should try your best to uphold the five precepts without violating them (regarding the precept of killing, if you cannot completely follow a vegetarian diet, you may eat vegetarian on certain days, but under no circumstances should you kill yourself or instruct others to kill).

2. HOW TO MAKE OFFERINGS TO KṢITIGARBHA BODHISATTVA:

- Using offerings to make offerings: The Buddha and Bodhisattvas are holy beings who have transcended the three realms; they do not expect us to offer them this or that. In reality, this is merely a way to use objects to express our respect and reverence for the Buddha and Bodhisattvas. You can freely offer anything to the Bodhisattvas according to your circumstances and preferences: fresh flowers, fruits, incense, candles, clean water, cakes, white rice, food, and even jewelry or a favorite item of yours. When making offerings, you should solemnly lift the offering with both hands and bow three times (note: bowing when making offerings is very important)important, you need to sincerely make the request for the Bodhisattva to acknowledge and accept it, and only then will you receive merit):

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahāsattva. I, whose dharma name is ..., offer this small offering to Kṣitigarbha. I humbly pray that the Bodhisattva, out of compassionate mercy, will witness and accept it.

If you wish, you may also recite a verse praising Kṣitigarbha, or sing, compose poetry... to make offerings to the Bodhisattva and make requests as above. Chapter Six of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra clearly explains the great merit of offering music, praise, and poetry before the Bodhisattva; therefore, these are all proper ways of making offerings according to the Dharma. As long as you regularly and sincerely practice each day, you will soon receive blessings.

- Using the method of inspiring others to make offerings: you can advise and guide others to take refuge, pay respects, make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, or encourage others to practice His Dharma methods, typically by reciting the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, dedicating the merit of inspiring everyone to offer to the Bodhisattva, and the resulting good karma is something that needs no doubt or debate!

3. HOW TO WORSHIP AND PRAISE KṢITIGARBHA BODHISATTVA:

- Chiêm lễ means to admire and worship. Admiring the Bodhisattva with sincere and joyful reverence brings very great merit, so you should not bow quickly in order to count the number of bows. The Bodhisattva will examine your heart rather than the quantity of bows. First, carefully observe the Bodhisattva's face, feel admiration and respect in your heart, and then slowly bow, with your head contemplating the image of the Bodhisattva or thinking of His compassion. When you feel sufficient reverence, stand up and continue to admire and worship for the second time, and so on...

- Praising a Bodhisattva means to commend, express admiration, and respect for them. You can read the verses in the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, or play music chanting their name to sing along, or frequently praise and talk to others about the Bodhisattva's compassion and great deeds of saving sentient beings. The sutra says that such people will be protected day and night by hundreds of thousands of spirits and deities, and all disasters will be avoided.

4. HOW TO READ THE KṢITIGARBHA SUTRA:

- Before starting to chant sutras, you should clean the altar thoroughly, prepare incense, candles, and pure fruits to offer to the Bodhisattva. If this is not feasible, even a cup of clean water offered to Him is sufficient. Sutras should not be chanted in the bedroom, except in special cases (such as chanting for a sick person, or if the house does not have a separate worship space). Clothing and body should be kept clean and dignified.

- You should invite the ancestors, wronged spirits, and beings in the spiritual realm to come listen to the sutra and practice together. Do not fear them as they are from the realm of the dead, because when reciting the sutra, there will be Dharma protectors to safeguard you. The Kṣitigarbha Sutra rescues beings in the three evil paths extensively, so invisible beings who hear this sutra are very joyful and delighted. If they are liberated upon hearing the sutra, they will become protectors to assist you in advancing your practice.

- When reciting sutras, maintain a moderate pace, neither fast nor slow, and pronounce each word clearly so that the beings around you can hear, understand, and benefit. After reciting the sutras, dedicate the merit to your adversaries, ancestors, parents, and all beings throughout the Dharma realms, wishing them to quickly be free from suffering and attain happiness, to follow the practice of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, to swiftly develop the Bodhi mind, and to attain Buddhahood soon.

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is currently acting as the spiritual leader of the Sahā world, replacing Shakyamuni Buddha, and His position is very magnificent. If you can follow the instructions above to venerate the Bodhisattva, the merit you gain will be beyond imagination!

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

(Excerpt from the teacher's lecture)

tieu_de: BE CAREFUL OF COUNTERFEIT AND IMITATION PRODUCTS IN BUDDHIST STUDIES!
tom_tat: (How to recognize and “expose” a fake monk posing as a practitioner) https://www.facebook.com/groups/samhoitieunghiep/permalink/4386525584772809/
noi_dung:
BE CAREFUL WITH FAKE AND COUNTERFEIT PRODUCTS IN BUDDHIST STUDY!

(How to recognize and “expose” a fake sorcerer posing as a practitioner)

https://www.facebook.com/groups/samhoitieunghiep/permalink/4386525584772809/

🍀Currently on Facebook, there are hundreds of pages and groups spreading and sharing Buddhist teachings, actively operating. Meditation practice communities are gradually emerging everywhere, and preachers continuously appear, including both monastics and laypeople. However, finding among them those who truly practice correctly according to the true Dharma of the Buddha is not an easy task!

Currently, there are many types of high-end counterfeit goods on the market. Gone are the days of clumsy packaging and smudged printing, where you could tell at a glance that a product was a cheap Chinese knockoff. Nowadays, counterfeit and fake products are made very meticulously; sometimes the external labeling looks as sharp as the real thing, but the quality of the product inside is really different, and you only realize the loss after you have used it and wonder why you wasted money buying it.

It is the same in practicing the way! Nowadays, false masters giving teachings are rampant, countless as the sands of the Ganges River, while genuine enlightened masters are hard to meet, rare as turtle hair or rabbit horn. There are many who also carry the title of practitioners, establish places of practice, and use the words of the Patriarch as a guiding principle for direction and learning goals, preaching publicly online every day, attracting thousands and tens of thousands of followers. But what they are truly teaching inside, whether it is Buddhist dharma or demonic teachings, is something that must be carefully considered and examined.

🌿Recently, there was a controversy online, where a certain person, when directly called a practitioner who fell into the devil's trap, retaliated and attacked the person criticizing them, pulling their followers to support them. Many comments below wholeheartedly defended their sect and mocked the other side, not realizing that this inadvertently caused speech karma of slandering the Triple Gem, slandering the true Dharma, and the Sangha. This is something extremely forbidden in the practice of the path, completely contrary to the teachings of the Buddha and the Zen masters.

🌻Do we think that whenever a person or a Buddhist practice group claims to follow the path of the ancestors, we can be assured that they are sincerely practicing? It's not that simple! Anyone can imitate the words of the Buddha or the ancestors, right? Every day they lecture to each other, about seeing through things, about letting go, about being indifferent to fame and gain, about not judging right or wrong in the Dharma, about seeking the path of liberation, etc... Doesn't it sound like the teachings of the ancestors? Indeed, these are the words the ancestors have always taught, nodding in approval, thumbs up, thousands of likes, thousands of likes!Talking sounds very nice, so nice that flowers fall, the heavens weep rain, but when it comes to situations and circumstances, as soon as their honor is slightly touched, they immediately respond with a contest of superiority, tit for tat. So where is the letting go, and where is the insight? Observe their attitudes and behaviors when they go through real tests; only then will it be revealed whether they are genuine or fake.

🍁A true practitioner avoids getting involved in controversies the most. If such matters occur, we need to view them objectively, without defending one side or supporting another, not taking any side at all; everything should be judged according to the Buddha's teachings and the examples of practice set by the patriarchs. The patriarchs, who are Bodhisattva incarnations like Master Xuan Hua, Master Xu Yun, Master Yin Guang, Master Hai Xian, in their practice life, encountered countless instances of slander, false accusations, and even beatings and torture that nearly cost them their lives. How did they respond to such controversies? Not a single word of defenseMind, reactions or complaints, are all silent endurance, creating a model of virtue that is immensely admirable. Looking at these typical examples, it is very objective, isn't it? The ancients had a saying: 'The virtuous do not argue, those who argue are not virtuous.' A genuinely cultivated person is like that, without ego, without a mind of personal gain or dispute, does not compete or seek, does not pay attention to praise or criticism, silently does everything from within for the benefit of sentient beings, without needing crowds or supporters to display fame or power, virtue will naturally shine. A truly cultivated person possesses virtue,Those with cultivated minds are not affected by worldly praise or criticism, nor by scandals; they can even regard scolding as an opportunity to eliminate karma and train their own patience. For true practitioners, criticism is as if it were not criticism, and humiliation does not feel humiliating. By looking at the practice of those from the past and then reflecting on it, one can see the truth very clearly.

🍂Venerable Master Tịnh Không once warned: "In these times, demons preach the Dharma, and out of 99 statements, 99 follow the true Dharma, only 1 is heretical. Can you, with your wisdom, recognize where that one heretical statement lies? Everything else is in accordance with the true Dharma, only one statement is heretical, and that alone is enough to lead you to downfall." Therefore, having the discernment to distinguish true from false Dharma in these times is far from simple!

👉So how can one distinguish a true ascetic from a pretender? We need to follow the teachings of the Buddha to be able to recognize whether a person is a wise teacher based on criteria like this:

- They strictly observe moral precepts themselves, frequently give teachings, and train their disciples in discipline and virtue. In instructing disciples, they are very principled, rigorously training them, but inside, they have great compassion, caring for their disciples not only in their spiritual practice but also in their daily life.

- Not greedy, not materialistic, rarely content, does not draw followers to become famous.

- Simple, frugal, does not adorn their appearance.

- Possesses the virtue of patience, never gets involved in personal disputes or seeks praise and gain.

- Not deceitful, words match actions; normally preaches one way and acts consistently. Speaks well, acts well, not just empty words, actions follow words.

- The more a person is a true practitioner, the more ordinary their behavior appears, and the more humble they are, hiding themselves without letting anyone know. Conversely, the more someone is a fake practitioner, the more they show off and flaunt their status everywhere. We must be extremely cautious about this when choosing a teacher or making friends!

- The final way to recognize a wise teacher is to observe, after some time studying under that teacher, whether you feel personal progress in virtue, a gradual weakening of greed, anger, and ignorance, a reduction in ego, and increased wisdom compared to before. If so, you are truly learning from a genuine wise teacher, and vice versa.

🙏May those who have accidentally committed the sin of blaspheming the Triple Gem soon realize their mistake, turn back and repent, and may all sentient beings gain clear insight in their practice, follow the right Dharma of the Tathagata, cultivate the Bodhi mind, and soon attain the Supreme Path.

NĀM MÔ BUDDHA.

NĀM MÔ DHARMA.

NĀM MÔ SANGHA.

MAY I, from now until the end of future lives, single-mindedly revere.

tieu_de: Venerable Thuyen Hoa says
tom_tat: You must know that: If it were not for Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva making such a vast vow, we would certainly still be suffering the retribution in the realms of Hell, Hungry Ghosts, and
noi_dung:
Venerable Thuyen Hoa Says

You must know that:

If it were not for Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva having made such a great vow, certainly right now we would still be suffering in the realms of Hell, Hungry Ghosts, and Animals.

The reason we are able to be human today is all thanks to the power of the great vow that Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva made countless eons ago.

It is His own vow power that has saved us from hell, from the path of hungry ghosts, and from the animal realm. However, at present, because we have not yet attained the Power of Karmic Retribution and do not yet possess the Divine Eye, we cannot know the past blessings we have enjoyed, the compassion, and the many good and beneficial things bestowed by Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.

If it were not for Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha making this great vow early on, we would have had to face many dangers. Therefore, in every second and every moment, we must always remember to repay the profound kindness of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha!

"Sow good deeds, and you will reap good results,

Sow evil deeds, and you will surely face evil consequences."

Moreover, if you only associate with bad friends, those who are not upright, sooner or later you will be influenced and become a bad person yourself. On the contrary, if you only socialize with good friends, even if you are a bad person, gradually you will become a good person. Therefore, everything is Cause and Effect, do not seek it far away in vain! Do not hastily condemn others as not being good to you; first, examine your own conscience and see whether you have been good to them! In everything, we should "turn the light inward and reflect, seeking within oneself," to examine ourselves; rather than being like a camera, constantlyTaking pictures of others, but what your own appearance looks like is completely unknown, you neither notice nor know!

The lustful speak false words, those with double-tongued evil mouths. We must always remember never to commit the sin of "double-tongued, evil speech" (speaking with a two-sided tongue, speaking cruel words). What is "double-tongued"? For example, with one person you use this "face," with another person you show a different "face"—meeting A and speaking ill of B; meeting B and criticizing A—this is committing the sin of "double-tongued, evil speech." Or you slander, use words to create resentment, sow internal division, and destroy the unity of a group to the point that the organization must fall apart—this also constitutes the sin of "double-tongued, evil."mouth" like that.

Regarding the offense of 'duplicity and harsh speech,' the most serious matter is the act of 'disrupting the harmony of the Sangha.' What is meant by 'disrupting the harmony of the Sangha'? Lay practitioners are not allowed to publicize the faults of monastics—those Bhikshus and Samaneras who have received the Samanera or Bodhisattva precepts. Because you learn the Dharma from monastics, from these Bhikshus and Samaneras, you should not study the Dharma and then go on to destroy it, creating discord within the Sangha community. If you use words to cause disharmony in the Sangha, then you have 'disrupted the harmony of the Sangha,' and committed the offense of 'duplicity.'really, such harsh words.

In Buddhism, "breaking the harmony of the Sangha" is one of the five gravest offenses (Five Heinous Crimes); and they are:

1) Killing one's father (thí phụ);

2) Killing one's mother (thí mẫu);

3) Killing an Arahant (thí A La Hán);

4) Destroying harmony among the monks (disrupting sangha harmony). For example, with this monk, you tell about the faults and mistakes of that monk, how he was at fault to this one...; and with that monk, you tell about the weaknesses and shortcomings of this monk, how he was at fault to the other, what envy and obstacles occurred... causing the monastics no longer to have harmony, the monks cannot live together (cohabit) with each other anymore, and eventually, the sangha becomes divided and scattered—thus, you have "disrupted sangha harmony".

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Source: Lotus

tieu_de: HOW TO DEDICATE MERIT TO TRANSFORM BAD KARMA
tom_tat: Source copy: Ta Bà Ha First, we need to understand what dedicating merit is?
noi_dung:
HOW TO DEDICATE MERIT TO TRANSFORM BAD KARMA

Source copy: Ta Ba Ha

First, we need to understand what merit dedication is?

Merit dedication is the act of directing the merit from our practice or the good deeds we have done toward a certain goal of our own, or for another sentient being.

If the dedication is for oneself, aimed at a higher goal, then here we see that the merit from practicing has direction, clearly sets the path, creating the cause for us to progress in future lives according to the goal we have aimed for when dedicating.

If one directs the merit from their practice to another being outside, then here we can tentatively understand it as a gift of practice merit; however, the amount of merit that the recipient receives will not be very much.

As taught in the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra:

If a living person performs a meritorious deed, for example offering to the Triple Gem, and then dedicates this merit to a deceased relative, then out of 7 parts of the merit, the deceased will only receive one part, while the remaining 6 parts belong to the living person.

Therefore, it is best that we help our relatives create virtuous deeds while they are still alive, rather than waiting until after they have passed away to perform deeds and dedicate merit, as the merit they receive will not be much.

In this article, I do not go into depth on this issue; I only mention the method of dedication so that you can transform negative karma. I have practiced this experience and found it very effective, so I want to share it with you to practice together:

Every day, if we perform any good deeds, or after a session of spiritual practice (chanting sutras, reciting mantras, meditating, or chanting Buddha's name, bowing to the Buddha...), at the end of the session, you can join your hands and dedicate as follows:

(Look at yourself to see what bad traits or negative karma are difficult to transform)

1. If I am someone who has the habit of speaking ill of others, then I will dedicate the merit as follows:

I vow to dedicate this cultivated merit to all beings in the Dharma realm, especially those beings who have the habit of speaking ill of others, hoping that they may rely on this merit and no longer speak ill of others.

2. If I have the karma of being fond of killing, then I will dedicate the merit as follows:

I vow to dedicate the merit of this practice to all sentient beings in the Dharma realm, that those beings who still have violent, murderous karma will change their disposition, become gentle and compassionate, and abandon killing.

3. If I have karma that is heavy in lust, it will be dedicated as follows:

I vow to dedicate the merit of this practice to all sentient beings in the Dharma realm, that those beings who are still heavily attached to sexual desire will have their disposition changed, becoming lighter in love and lust, and turn towards a pure and desire-free inner mind.

4. If I have heavy karma related to a selfish, stingy, and miserly mind, then we will dedicate the merit as follows:

I vow to dedicate the merit of this practice for all sentient beings in the dharma realm, so that those beings who still have a stingy, miserly, and selfish mind will broaden their hearts, enjoy giving, delight in generosity, and offer gifts selflessly without attachment to the merit.

.........

Similarly, for other bad and evil karmas, you will also dedicate the merit in the same way.

When we dedicate merit and wish for others to receive good things, our own mindset will change in a positive direction, and we will obtain the things we desire for them.

This is a very important principle of cause and effect.

After learning this secret, please try practicing it and you will see it is very effective.

I wish you success in transforming your harmful thoughts or bad karma.

Namo Amitabha Buddha 🙏

tieu_de: THE MINISTER HAS PASSED AWAY
tom_tat: Source: FB Ân Pháp Lưu THE REVEREND QUẢ KHANH HAS PASSED AWAY 😥
noi_dung:
LORD QUẢ KHANH HAS PASSED AWAY

Source: FB Ân Pháp Lưu

MR. QUẢ KHANH HAS PASSED AWAY 😥

"Many people asked me to translate about Quả Khanh's passing. But due to very limited and hard-to-find materials, I could only find and translate a little about him. On other websites, people post articles but do not mention the author. After several days of difficult searching, I finally found out that the author of the memorial article was Hải Ba [a character in Báo ứng hiện đời 1-2], and it was thanks to Hải Ba that I learned about Quả Khanh's death. (Because no newspaper reported it). I also learned that Quả Lâm has passed away, but I could not find any article about her - so I can only report on Quả Khanh. Anyway, I have tried my best."

Many people mourn because they left too suddenly. But in my opinion, once their duty in this world is completed, they simply depart. We cry to see them off, but perhaps they are smiling.

To cherish and honor those who have departed, we can only follow the guiding principle:

CEASE EVIL, PRACTICE GOOD, BELIEVE DEEPLY IN KARMIC RESULTS, FOLLOW THE TEACHINGS OF THE BUDDHA.

Now, please view the article:

IN MEMORY OF QUẢ KHANH

Classical Chinese: Hải Ba

Vietnamese translation: Hạnh Đoan

Mr. Khanh - Mr. Dương Tác Tướng passed away at 18:43 on August 21

After Mr. Khanh's farewell ceremony on August 23, I wanted to write something. But it has been several years since I logged into this forum, and I had forgotten the password and had to try many ways but to no avail. I sent a message to the administrator, Mr. Lưu, and tried to register a new account on my mobile phone but was unsuccessful. Today, I tried again on the computer and registered again under the name Hải Ba. Finally, I succeeded.

When I received the news that Mr. Quả Khanh had passed away while I was on a business trip abroad, I hurried back to Tianjin on the earliest flight. I regret not being able to see Mr. Quả Khanh's face in his final moments. According to Tianjin customs, the deceased are cremated just three days after passing. Therefore, I could only see Mr. Quả Khanh's portrait placed among the flowers on the altar. He still looked gentle and respectable, impressively so, just as I remembered him about 25 years ago.

Throughout the journey, I recall the first moment of meeting Master Quả Khanh in 1993, it feels as if it were just yesterday. I always call him Master Dương. At that time, he had not yet been to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, he was just like many ordinary middle-aged men.

After that, he went to Master Tuyên Hóa's City of Ten Thousand Buddhas in America. When he returned, he became renowned throughout the country and traveled everywhere to teach and spread the Dharma.

Once, when I was at his home, I was fortunate enough to answer a call from Master Tuyên Hóa. More than ten years ago, Elder Dương was truly extremely famous. I saw in Taiwan his renowned work "Reaping the Consequences in This Life" widely printed and displayed in monasteries. Until 2010, he began to retreat and nurture his health. I met him for the last time three years ago. His face was still rosy as before, but his movements were not very comfortable. I specially invited Elder Thi Kim Mặc's eldest son, one of the four famous doctors in China, to accompany me to visit Master Quả Khanh.

In 1994, Master Ngoc Ham, the abbot of the Great Compassion Monastery, was diagnosed with colorectal cancer. He was transferred to another facility, did not undergo Western surgery, and was diagnosed and treated by a famous Chinese medicine doctor from Tianjin, the father of Coc Chan Anh, known as Professor Coc. Now the abbot is 98 years old.

Unfortunately, when Mr. Qua Khanh heard that some animal ingredients were included in Professor Coc's prescription, he gently declined.

In the blink of an eye, three years have passed. I thought that after my son entered university, I would visit Mr. Quả Khanh again. Unfortunately, he had already left, but regrettably he had passed away, though I still feel that he is not truly gone, just far away.

I am very grateful to Mr. Quả Khanh for leading me to Buddhism. I am thankful because 19 years ago, before I met him, I was pregnant. He advised me to recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. I obediently followed his advice, and after reciting the sutra forty-nine times, my son was born smoothly. I have also written many posts on the forum.

In the blink of an eye, it's already been 19 years. As Mr. Quả Khanh said, a child who comes to repay gratitude will give me a limitless sense of appreciation. My child has never studied for exams, but academic achievements have always been excellent. Just in the second year, he was invited to study at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Zhejiang University Qiushi and won a silver medal at the national Olympic competition. This year, he entered his ideal university with a score of 683. He is praised by everyone for his gentle, polite nature and eagerness to help others. Kindness is sometimes more praiseworthy than talent or appearance. The principal of his school often tells me: a kind-hearted child is always at peace wherever they go.where, because selfless kindness will illuminate its life.

Although I have known Mr. Quả Khanh for a long time, I was not diligent and did not memorize the scriptures, so I was always afraid to meet him. However, I have always been deeply grateful for the guidance he gave throughout my life. I heard that many people from all over the country tried to rush to see him one last time, and I am very thankful for his contributions to the propagation of Buddhism.

Professor Dương's family was also very resilient and strong, so they did not cry, because when he passed away, it was very peaceful, with many fellow practitioners offering support and prayers, and everything was perfectly complete.

A person departs, completing the cycle of a lifetime, carrying with them the affection and blessings of many others, countless minds enlightened by the spring breeze. An ordinary life thereby becomes extraordinary.

Wishing you liberation from suffering and attainment of happiness, and may your vow be fulfilled in your return.

Hai, August 27, 2018

Source: Tinh Nhu

tieu_de: Twelve illnesses cannot see the Buddha
tom_tat: The Buddha said, in human beings, there are twelve diseases, deep and severe illnesses, one cannot see the Buddha. Ananda asked the Buddha: 'What are these diseases?' The Buddha replied: 'Disrespecting parents, that is one disease; ignorance leading to evil, that is
noi_dung:
TWELVE ILLNESSES THAT DO NOT SEE BUDDHA

The Buddha said that in humans, there are twelve diseases, deep-rooted diseases, that prevent one from seeing the Buddha. Ananda asked the Buddha, "What are these diseases?" The Buddha replied: "Not respecting parents, that is one disease; ignorance leading to wrongdoing, that is the second disease; deceitfulness and trickery, that is the third disease; harmful speech towards others, that is the fourth disease; frequently looking for others' faults, that is the fifth disease; the sixth disease is killing living beings; not feeling shame, that is the seventh disease; lust for sexual pleasure, that is the eighth disease; arrogance and looking down on others, that is the ninth disease; committing sins without remorse, that is the tenth disease; praising oneself while criticizing others, that is the eleventh disease; not knowing right from wrong,is the twelve disease."

Ananda asked: “For such illnesses, how should they be treated?”

The Buddha answered: “Using the right medicine for the illness will bring relief. Practicing compassion, joy, and forgiveness, being humble and modest, praising the Mahayana, speaking kindly, correcting mistakes with diligence, caring for the poor, respecting the elderly, not getting angry or upset when criticized, praising others, aspiring to save all beings, resolving conflicts with enemies, showing respect to superiors and yielding to inferiors, these are the medicines that treat the above illnesses.”

Ananda asked again: "Where can those medicines be found?" The Buddha replied: "On Mount Tu Di." Ananda asked again: "What is Tu Di?" The Buddha replied: "It is the human body. All sentient beings face six hardships: First, it is difficult to obtain a human body; second, it is difficult to have a complete human body; third, it is difficult to develop a good mind; fourth, it is difficult to hear the True Dharma; fifth, it is difficult to be born in China; sixth, it is difficult to encounter a place of practice."

The Buddha said in a verse: Suppose one creates karma, even over hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, the karma will not disappear. When the conditions and causes come together perfectly, the person who created the karma must face the consequences. A joyful expression on the face is an offering; a mouth that does not lie is a fragrant virtue; a heart without anger is the Pure Land; a mind without impatience is the place of the Way. A person who studies the Way but does not understand causality, busy all day and attached to earthly desires, only knows how to use water to wash the face but does not use virtue to cleanse the heart, stopping all evil deeds, that is the cause of the Pure Land. Whether wise or ignorant, the most important thing is to abandon greed and anger.

If someone hears this Dharma, with firm faith, diligently practicing, frequently doing good deeds, they will attain the joy of Nirvana. The Nirvana Sutra says: "When the Buddha was still alive, in the Ca La pond, there was a clam that, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, crawled onto the shore, hiding in a clump of grass, listening attentively to the Buddha. A herdsman, seeing the gathering of listeners surrounding the Buddha, ran over to see, wanting to hear the Dharma. In his haste, he stepped on the clam; it immediately died and was reborn in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven. Then it wondered why, being originally a clam, did it have the conditions to be born in heaven? At that time, the celestial being, knowing its previous body, realized that by listening to the Dharma, it had attained rebirth in heaven, and then it departed."Palace, come before the Buddha, pay respects and offer thanks. The Buddha then expounds the Dharma for that person to hear, and after hearing it, they attain the First Fruit, solely by listening to the Dharma, achieving Right Enlightenment. If sentient beings in lower realms can do so, all the more so for humans, therefore one must strive, diligently listen to the Buddha's teachings, and reflect sincerely on every word that enters the ear, which will plant the seeds for the Bodhi path, which will endure countless lifetimes; good roots will grow, evil karma will gradually dissipate, the Bodhi mind will arise, firm determination will be established, seeking the Supremely Perfect Way, broadly saving sentient beings, cultivating the path together, attaining Bodhi together, diligently practicing, never turning back, understanding one's own mind, resolutely attaining Buddhahood, escaping the cycle of birth and death, and entering Nirvana. Present great assembly, please wholeheartedly and sincerelyRespectful regard and ceremony, Virtuous Great Compassionate Father.

tieu_de: TEN MERIT-DEEDS OF PAINTING IMAGES OF BUDDHAS – BODHISATTVAS
tom_tat: 1. For countless lifetimes, may there be bright, clear eyes that see clearly. 2. May you never be born into the evil realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals. If born as a human, may your friends and neighbors all be good people, and may you not encounter bad people.
noi_dung:
TEN MERITS OF PAINTING IMAGES OF BUDDHAS – BODHISATTVAS

1. In every lifetime, there are clear and bright eyes that see clearly.

2. Never be born into evil paths, hells, hungry ghosts, or animals. If born as a human, friends and neighbors are all good people, never encountering evil people or wild beasts.

3. Always be born into wealthy households, receiving respect.

4. Achieve a golden body.

5. A life of wealth and prosperity.

6. Be reborn into virtuous and kind households.

7. May be born as a king.

8. Reborn as a Wheel-Turning Holy King.

9. May be born into the heaven of Brahma and live as long as one kalpa.

10. In all future lifetimes, always respect the Three Jewels, take refuge in the Three Jewels, and will not be reborn in lower realms.

REFLECTION:

In the Lotus Sutra, in the second chapter, there is a verse teaching the merit of drawing the image of the Buddha, whether done intentionally or unintentionally, as follows:

“Drawing the Buddha statue brilliantly

A hundred manifestations of merit and adornment

Whether doing it oneself or having others do it

All have already attained the path of Buddha.

Even children playing

Using grass, plants, or a brush

Or using their own fingernails

To draw a Buddha statue

People like that

Gradually accumulate merit

Full of the mind of great compassion

All have already attained the path of Buddha

Teaching the Bodhisattvas

Delivering countless beings.

Long ago, in Sichuan, there was a person who specialized in reciting the Diamond Sutra, and when reciting, he would use his hand to write the Diamond Sutra in the air. Every day, he would stand in the same spot and "write out" with his hand in the air. Later, whenever it rained, around the place where he wrote the Diamond Sutra, no rain would fall to the ground. This happened regularly.

Those who had opened their Heavenly Eye newly saw that although he used his hand to write the Diamond Sutra in the void, the Eight Classes of Heavenly Dragons also came there to protect this Sutra, preventing rainwater from falling into the empty space where he wrote. Later, a temple was built at this location. Therefore, you can see that the man, merely writing in the void with his hand, could have such a great spiritual response; the merits of painting Buddha images are truly beyond imagination.

(This story is recorded in the book "Strange Records of the Diamond Sutra").

Therefore, the verse in the Sutra teaches that those who paint or create statues of the Buddha, gradually accumulating merit with a heart full of great compassion, will all attain enlightenment and supreme Buddhahood.

In the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra: Chapter Six "The Tathāgata Praises".

The Buddha expounded to Bodhisattva Pu Guang that:

– Hey Phổ Quảng! If any virtuous man or virtuous woman paints an image of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and then gazes at it once, and pays homage once, that person will be reborn in the heaven of Trāyastriṃśa a hundred times, no longer falling into the evil realms. Any virtuous man or virtuous woman who personally or instructs someone to create the image of the Bodhisattva, that person will surely receive great benefits when they reap the results of their deeds”… If any woman is weary of her female body and wholeheartedly offers homage to the painted image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, and to images made of clay, stone, gum, paint, bronze, iron, etc., she should daily offer flowers, incense, food, drink, clothing, brocade, ceremonial banners, and money,treasures, etc… offering like that endlessly…. Moreover, any virtuous man or virtuous woman who personally transcribes this sutra, or instructs someone to transcribe it, or personally creates images of the Bodhisattvas, even instructs others to create them, that person will surely obtain great benefits when receiving the results of their actions…

Chapter Twelve: “Seeing and Hearing Are Beneficial”.

5) Benefits for the sick:

– Likewise, Avalokiteshvara! In the worlds of the present time and the future, those beings in the six realms, if someone is about to die and happens to hear even a single mention of the name of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha passing through their ears, that person who is about to die will no longer fall into the suffering of the three evil realms.

Let alone at the time of imminent death, when parents and close relatives use the deceased person's property, treasures, clothing, etc., as expenses to decorate or paint the image of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.

Then the sick person, before death, or with their eyes seeing and ears hearing, knows that close relatives use their house, treasures, etc., to decorate or paint the image of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha for them.

6) The departed receive blessings:

– Again like this, O Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara! In the future life, if there is any male or female, whether at the time of nursing, at three years old, five years old, or up to ten years old, who dies leaving behind siblings.

When that person grows up, thinking of their parents and relatives, it is unclear into what situation they fall, or into which world they are born, or to which heaven they ascend?

That person seems to be able to depict the image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, even upon hearing His name, they would once gaze upon it and once bow in reverence, from one day up to seven days without abandoning their initial mind, hearing the name and seeing the image, they would contemplate, worship, and offer tribute.

If that person's deceased relatives, due to evil karma, were sent to a bad realm, they would originally have to endure the allotted number of lifetimes. Now, thanks to the merit of depicting the image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and the contemplation, worship, and offerings made by children, or by brothers and sisters, they are immediately liberated, born into the heavenly or human realm to enjoy the supreme and marvelous bliss.

(Author: Minh Chinh)

tieu_de: Kṣitigarbha is the teacher of the Buddhas, the mother of the Bodhisattvas
tom_tat: THE DHARMA OF MASTER INHERITOR ẤN QUANG ☘️In the collection "The Continued Writings of Master Ấn Quang," the Master has many passages of guidance and praise for Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha as well as the Sutra of the Original Vows of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. Here are a few excerpts.
noi_dung:
Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is the Teacher of the Buddhas, the Mother of the Bodhisattvas

TEACHINGS OF MASTER AN QUANG

☘️ In the compilation of Yin Guang Dharma Master’s Collected Writings, there are many passages in which the Master expounds upon and praises Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and the Sutra of the Original Vows of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Here are a few excerpts: The Master said: Mount Jiuhua is the miraculous transformation monastery of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, countless eons ago, had already realized the Dharma Body, had attained Buddhahood, yet did not take the position of a Buddha. Because of the vow: "One will not attain enlightenment until all sentient beings are saved; no Buddha will be realized while hells remain," he longed tenderly for sentient beings suffering the profound pain of birth and death, with an earnestness that cannot be expressed! Therefore, when the Buddha delivered the Dharma for his mother on the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, tenAll the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the world, as well as the eight classes of heavenly beings, came to attend the assembly; even using the Buddha’s eye, one still cannot comprehend it.

☘️Those Buddhas and Bodhisattvas attained enlightenment because they were guided by Kṣitigarbha, yet Kṣitigarbha still manifests in the form of a Śrāvaka. Besides manifesting in all kinds of forms to preach the Dharma in the ten directions of the world, he often resides in the utmost suffering of darkness to save sentient beings. No Buddha or Bodhisattva in the ten directions does not praise his profound heart of 'kindness and compassion in motion.' Master Ngau Yik, upon reading the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows, immediately generated the great Bodhi mind, for Kṣitigarbha is the teacher of all Buddhas, the mother of all Bodhisattvas, still tirelessly devoted to saving us; if we do not regard 'ourselves and others together“Escaping birth and death” is the aspiration, the career, then neglecting gratitude is also very great indeed

☘️In the section of Praising the Statue of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, Master ẤN QUANG praised: How noble is the Great Being! The vow is vast and deep, thinking compassionately of sentient beings in long cycles of rebirth, bearing a heart of shared Compassion, awakening the unbiased heart of Loving-kindness, often residing in hells to hope to save those who are suspended upside down. "Only after saving all sentient beings can one attain Bodhi, if hells are not emptied, one certainly cannot become a Buddha," due to these causes and conditions, he is praised by all Buddhas; let alone those who are in the six realms, how can they not feel compassionate attachment? The sky has a limit, but the vow is boundless. Wishing to repay deep gratitude, he specially prints and venerates the sacred sutras, hoping that all who see and hear will generate pure faith, gradually spreading the sutra, with benefits that are limitless.

tieu_de: The Ten Unwholesome Deeds
noi_dung:
Ten Unwholesome Actions

*********************

I heard it like this:

Once, the Buddha resided in the kingdom of Shravasti, in the garden of Jeta's Grove, in the Parna forest.

At that time, the World-Honored One said to the monks:

"Beings who practice killing, promote killing, and cultivate actions leading to hell, hungry ghosts, and animals; if born among humans, their lifespan is extremely short. The reason is due to harming the lives of other beings.

"Beings who steal or rob others’ possessions, committing the heavy sins of the three evil paths, when born as humans, often face poverty, insufficient food to fill their mouths, and inadequate clothing to cover their bodies; all this is due to stealing and robbing others’ possessions, which cuts off their own life potential.

"If there are beings who indulge in lust, committing the three evil paths, when born as humans, their families are unchaste due to secret indulgence in lust.

“Or there are beings who lie, committing the sin of hell; when born among humans, they are despised by others, their words are not believed, and they are looked down upon; all of this arises because of lying in previous lives.

“Or there are beings who are two-tongued, committing the sin of the three evil paths; if born among humans, their minds are often unsettled and they frequently carry sorrow. This is because the person spread lies from both ends.

“Or there are beings who speak harsh words, committing the sin of the three evil paths; if born among humans, they become ugly and are often scolded. This happens because the person’s words were not sincere.

“Or there are sentient beings who cause disturbances here and there, committing sins of the three evil paths; if they are born among humans, they are mostly hated, and their relatives are separated. The reason for this is all due to incitement to turmoil in past lives.

“Or there are sentient beings who are jealous, committing sins of the three evil paths; if they are born among humans, they lack clothing. The reason for this is that the person aroused feelings of greed and jealousy.

“Or there are sentient beings who generate an evil mind to harm, committing the sins of the three evil paths; suppose they are born among humans, they often have many falsehoods, do not understand the ultimate truth, and their mind is unsettled. The reason for this is all due to great anger and hatred in past lives, lacking benevolence.

“Or there are beings who practice wrong views, sowing the three evil paths; if they are born among humans, it is only in border areas, not in central places, and do not encounter the Three Jewels, the meaning of the Dharma; or they may be deaf, blind, mute, physically deformed, unable to understand good dharma, often following evil dharma. The reason for this is all due to lacking the root of faith in previous lifetimes; also not believing in monks, brahmins, parents, or siblings.

“Bhikkhu, you should know that the results of these ten evil deeds lead to such calamities. Therefore, Bhikkhu, stay away from the ten evil deeds and practice right view.

“Monks, learn this in this way.”

Then the monks, hearing what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.

The Āgama Sūtra of the Saṅgha

Chapter Ten: Unwholesome Deeds

Classical Text Translation: Tripitaka of Gautama Saṅgha

Vietnamese Translation: Thích Đức Thắng – Corrected & Annotated: Tuệ Sỹ

Source: Giác Ngộ

noi_dung:
THE HERETICAL ANT DRAINS THE THREE JEWELS

"I have a junior disciple named Quả Trí in Shanghai. Her mother-in-law has believed in Buddhism for several decades, but she holds wrong views, is stubborn and hard to guide, always thinking she is right. She also tends to speak harshly, likes to criticize, and points out others' faults. During the time when the heretical cult Falun Gong was popular, she turned into a 'Great Vanguard General,' eagerly gathering scriptures, Buddha statues... in the house to burn and destroy, and began propagating the heretical cult [Falun Gong], slandering the Buddhist Dharma."

Half a year later, she developed a tumor in her mouth and had to undergo surgery twice, and then both sides of her mouth had to be stitched, leaving it often to leak foul, dirty fluid. So she frequently had to wipe it with a cloth and ended up needing a third surgery. After the surgeries, the illness kept recurring and never healed. When I went to Quả Trí's house, I saw that her face had turned a dark greenish-black. Although her body was no longer strong, she remained very stubborn, clinging strongly to wrong beliefs, and was aggressive, refusing to listen to any advice.

I told Quả Trí to chant the Kṣitigarbha Sutra to help my mother-in-law because she committed too many evil deeds: slandering the Three Jewels, lying with wrong views, and her verbal karma is too heavy. She also often kills living beings to eat meat and does not listen to anyone's advice; her life will not last long. Fortunately, she has a daughter-in-law practicing the true Dharma, who knows how to help her; otherwise, she would surely descend into the Avīci hell to suffer.

On April 14, 2007, Quả Trí called to report: Her mother-in-law passed away that very morning, an indescribable sorrow. Although under Quả Trí's guidance, the family community, even those who did not believe in Buddhism, tried to recite prayers for her for nearly two hours. Throughout the recitation process, Quả Trí always knelt beside her mother-in-law; she saw her face transforming very fiercely and silently guessed that she had gone to an unfortunate place.

Excerpt from: The Explanation of Cause and Effect, Lương Hoàng Sám - Volume 2.

Compiled by: Layperson Quả Khanh.

Vietnamese translation: Nun Hạnh Đoan.

• COMMENTS ON THE DHARMA PHILOSOPHY.

CHINESE TEXT: LAYPERSON QUA KHANH.

Vietnamese translation: Nun Hanh Doan.

"If you don't keep the precepts, even if you can cultivate as well as Li Hongzhi (the ancestor of Falun Gong), this guy is good at cultivating without abstaining, so he can only become a Demon King, he belongs to the rank of a high-class Demon King. Have you met him? He looked very good-looking, had two long, very beautiful earlobes. I observed that in his past life, Li Hongzhi studied Buddhism, also ordained as a monk, practiced everything well, and helped many people, but his personality was too filial and refused to be cut off from sexuality.So the conclusion: He cultivated into the Demon King, which is Lý Hồng Chí at present.

He is revered and worshiped by a majority of intellectuals. I observe that the group of people who follow him as disciples are faithful, because in the past, they once received his kindness and help. That affection has been deeply engraved in their consciousness. Therefore, whenever they see him, their hearts immediately fill with feelings of admiration and veneration, and they view everything he does as extraordinary.

This is the past affinity between teacher and students. In a previous life, Ly Hong Chi had often helped many people, so when these people saw Ly Hong Chi, they immediately admired and followed him. However, those who followed him could not avoid committing evil deeds and would soon descend to Hell, because Ly Hong Chi specialized in slandering Buddha and the Dharma. Buddha said in the Lankavatara Sutra: "Practicing the path without abandoning desire will lead the highest to become a King of Demons, the middle to become Demon subjects, and the lowest to become Demon women." These words are not wrong.

One must recognize their own mistakes, always acknowledge their own wrongdoings. When being scolded or blamed by many people, one must examine oneself and think, "There must be something wrong with me; if not, why do people hate or scold me?" One must find their own faults, recognizing that they have shortcomings, which is why others dislike them. From now on, you should vow not to scold others, not to lose your temper, and always recognize and apologize for your mistakes. If you understand and can do this, annoyance will turn into enlightenment—this is called living.

Be alert, because realizing your own mistakes is awakening; if you keep focusing on pointing out others' faults, it will only bring trouble. You must skillfully turn trouble into Bodhi, only then is it cultivation.

(Excerpt from the unpublished book “SPIRITUAL EXPERIENCE” - the final translation work on Qua Khanh)
