tieu_de: IT DOESN'T MATTER WHAT KIND OF CRIMES YOU COMMITTED BEFORE, AS LONG AS YOU SINCERELY TURN AROUND AND TAKE REFUGE IN THE BUDDHA AND BODHISATTVA, YOU WILL ALL
tom_tat: 🌷🌷🌷 In Buddhism, there is often a saying:
noi_dung:
NO MATTER HOW GREAT THE CRIMES ONE HAS COMMITTED BEFORE, AS LONG AS ONE TRULY REPENTS AND TAKES REFUGE IN THE BUDDHA AND BODHISATTVAS, ONE WILL

🌷🌷🌷

In Buddhism, there is often a saying:

_ "It does not matter how much negative karma one has created in the past, as long as one sincerely turns back and takes refuge in the Buddha and Bodhisattvas, one will be saved."

Here we see that the most important thing is the two words "Taking Refuge". Nowadays, in Buddhism, the two words "Taking Refuge" are mostly formal rather than genuine refuge. To be honest, if taking refuge is only on the surface, it is useless. So, what exactly is taking refuge? The word "Taking" means turning back and correcting one's own mistakes, and from now on deciding not to do them again, while the word "Refuge" means following the teachings of the Buddha in the scriptures. If one can genuinely fulfill the two words "Taking Refuge", then regarding the karmic offenses that we have committed in the past...can only be eradicated. Once sins are eradicated, in the future after death one will definitely not be condemned to the three evil paths to suffer punishment. Therefore, the word "Save" here carries such a meaning.

So why not fall into the three evil paths? Because the evil karma we created in the past is the cause of the three evil paths. If today we continue to create it, what we create now becomes the condition for the three evil paths. When the cause and condition are complete, we naturally must enter the three evil paths to undergo suffering. As for the past evil karma we created, if from now on we do not continue to do so, then although the bad cause exists, the evil condition does not. Therefore, the retribution in the three evil paths cannot manifest, so it is said that one will not fall into the three evil paths. This clearly explains the reasoning that those who sincerely take refuge in the Buddha and Bodhisattvas from the beginning will not fall into the three evil paths. YetOf course, one must truly, from the very beginning, follow the standards of the Scriptures in order to study; only then can one achieve it.

It is absolutely not the case that if I stand before the statues of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas every day, bow three times, and recite the refuge verse three times, the Buddha and Bodhisattvas will then bless me and eliminate my own karmic sins. There is no such principle. Therefore, fellow practitioners must clearly understand this true reality.

As for disciples in Buddhism, in the morning and evening chanting sessions, they all chant the Three Refuges. In fact, what we chant is only a formality and has no real substance. Why? Because after each session, when we step outside, we throw this Three Refuges out behind our backs. We truly do not turn back to ourselves in our words, thoughts, and actions, nor do we follow the teachings of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas. Chanting the Three Refuges morning and evening only exists as verbal goodness, while in our own mind-actions-language, the karmic results do not change at all. This is also the reason why nowadays peopleStudying Buddhism is abundant, but those who truly benefit from studying Buddhism are very few.

🌷🌷🌷

🌻Namo Amitabha Buddha 🌻

tieu_de: SIGNS WHEN WE TRANSFORM KARMA AND BEGIN TO HAVE MERIT
tom_tat: 🪴 The circumstances in which we begin are just changing, our karma is just shifting. The karma of giving, loving, and helping others in the right place will manifest some results. For example, sometimes there is something we like, secretly intending
noi_dung:
SIGNS WHEN WE TRANSFORM KARMA AND BEGIN TO HAVE BLESSINGS

🪴 The circumstances in which we start anew have changed, and our karma has shifted. The karma of giving, caring for and helping others in the right way will manifest certain results. For example, at some point, if we like something and secretly have the thought in our mind without letting anyone know, it will automatically come to us right away - that is the beginning of the result of the karmic action of giving and loving, which has ripened.

🪴 But don't dream too big because our blessings are still small; they are not enough for us to dream of a mansion and have one appear for us. However, if we dream of something moderate and small, and it comes immediately, that means the virtue of giving has ripened. For people whose merit is substantial, if they dream of a mansion, the mansion will appear immediately. How does it appear? It does not appear by chanting spells, but naturally, circumstances flow rapidly, allowing them to buy materials, buy land, and build the house quickly within a few months if their blessings are abundant.

🪴 I haven't reached that point yet, but I dream of having whatever I want, the moderate things. For example, if my car just broke down, I say: I need to have a new car to go, and a few weeks later, it suddenly happens. I just think it in my head, without complaining to anyone even once, and it immediately comes true, meaning I have already begun to transform my karma, and I am fortunate enough to transform my karma.

🌟 STAGES OF THE PROCESS OF TRANSFORMING KARMA

♥️ • First is to recognize your mistakes, understand your weaknesses, and identify where your errors lie. That is the first step.

♥️ • The second thing is to take that fault and observe it, analyze it, and summarize it. Self-suggest the opposite, for example, if I am stingy, I tell myself I AM A GENEROUS GIVER AND A WONDERFUL RECEIVER.

✨ If I often get angry, I will realize my fault is being stubborn, lacking a multi-dimensional perspective on issues, and tell myself every day: I LOVE, I UNDERSTAND, I ACCEPT DIFFERENCES.

✨ Or if I feel jealous of someone who is talented, I have to understand that I am being envious and say:

"May my heart be joyful."

When seeing someone successful

Or creating blessings

As if you could do it yourself."

✨ Like that, the second thing is correcting mistakes with positive words.

♥️ • The third is to start taking action, to give generously, to love, to help, to rejoice, to support, to assist… that is to take action.

(Understand the mistake. Accept the mistake. Change your thinking. Adjust your thoughts and words. Act according to what you think)

♥️ • After taking action, depending on the time, sometimes it takes 3 years, sometimes 5 years, some people 10 years, some people 20 years, only then do we reach the fourth stage where we see the circumstances around us change.

✨ My heart had already changed 5 years ago, but 5 years later, new circumstances began to change: I suddenly noticed that people treated me better, and everything came to me more smoothly. But luck and joy that come to me will be gone if I just enjoy them. What I have to do is make sure that whatever luck comes to me, I share a part of it with others, just like when you have rice, you don't eat it all but should sow some again. It's like winning the lottery; our elders often say you should donate a part to charity. That is the reason!

🌿 I hope that anyone facing difficulties can firmly believe and live well. As long as our hearts are bright, the blue sky will naturally arrange everything.

🌿 Believe in the wonderful arrangement of the universe. The law of sowing and reaping always exists whether we believe it or not.

🌿 Just as the sun rises when the rooster crows, but even if the rooster does not crow, the sun still rises. Whether the sun rises or not is not because of the crowing. That is the law of creation.

♥ Once it is a law, no one can change it.

♥ Learning to accept is a kind of strength.

♥ Understanding and transforming the mind is the effort of a long journey.

----------------------------------------

Source: Quan Am Cat.

tieu_de: Buddha's Enlightenment 8/
tom_tat: - WHY SHOULD BUDDHIST DISCIPLES REMEMBER THIS HOLIDAY? Since ancient times, countless uncountable periods, humans and all beings in different realms have always been immersed in suffering. Whenever a person is born
noi_dung:
BUDDHA'S ENLIGHTENMENT 8/

- WHY MUST BUDDHIST DISCIPLES REMEMBER THIS FESTIVAL?

Since ancient times, countless unmeasurable periods, humans and all sentient beings in different realms have always been immersed in suffering. Humans, once born, are immediately surrounded by suffering, continuing until they close their eyes for the last time.

How many wars have lasted throughout human history, with rivers of blood flowing and mountains of corpses. How many epidemics have arisen one after another, never fully cured by medicine. Then how many times natural disasters like earthquakes, how many times famines have ravaged, how many times separations by death have occurred…

Even in daily life, there are always hundreds of thousands of kinds of suffering tormenting human existence: birth – aging – sickness – death – separation from loved ones – resentment meeting or not meeting – desires unfulfilled – the suffering of the five aggregates.

Even if death comes, it is not the end at all. It is merely a milestone marking the transition from one type of suffering to another. Because after death, the soul must reincarnate into a new realm.

If one is born into hell, it will be the utmost of pain with millions of horrific tortures that can last from hundreds of years up to billions of years.

If one is born as a hungry ghost, they will have to endure persistent hunger and thirst for hundreds of years up to millions of years. Not to mention many other torments such as extreme cold or scorching heat, being tortured by demons or gods, beaten, gnawed by poisonous insects, etc...

If one is born as an animal, being controlled by instinct, eating flesh or being eaten, biting and tearing each other, suffering in ignorance and darkness.

The suffering of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals is indescribable, but even if one is luckier, born into the human realm, the realm of gods or Asura, or rises to the heavens, the suffering is only less, not absent.

The most important thing is that no matter which realm one is born into, it all has a time limit. When the lifespan ends, even in the highest heavenly realm, one must be reincarnated into lower worlds, sometimes being born into hell, hungry ghosts, or animals to endure suffering.

Thus, life follows one after another, sometimes being born in higher realms, then being born in lower realms, with no stopping point. Because the cycle of reincarnation is endless, the suffering of sentient beings is also endless. Each sentient being throughout countless lifetimes cries from pain, cries from separation, and the accumulated tears amount to more than the waters of the entire ocean.

In those days, there was a sage with extraordinary wisdom, who could see the full panorama of suffering of all beings throughout the universe. Out of boundless compassion for sentient beings, he resolved to save all beings so that they would never have to endure any suffering again.

But how could he do it?

When encountering the poor and hungry, if he gave money, food, drink, clothes, or necessities, he could help them be full for a few days or months, but how could he make them full for a lifetime? Even if they were full in this lifetime, they would not be full for all the lifetimes to come?

When meeting sick people, even if you cure all their diseases, it does not mean they will never get sick again. Moreover, there are always illnesses that no medicine can completely cure. Eventually, death will still come, sooner or later, by one way or another; who can live forever?

Then, when encountering people suffering from heartbreak and separation, resentment over missed encounters, unfulfilled desires, etc., what can be used to help them completely ease their suffering?

There is only one way to end all suffering permanently for sentient beings, which is the Bodhi Path. Only when sentient beings awaken to the Bodhi Path and attain the Enlightened Fruit can they be liberated from the cycle of birth and death.

Understanding this, the sage made a vow that, even if blood is shed, heads fall, bones are broken, and flesh is torn throughout countless lifetimes, he would still resolutely seek the Bodhi Path for sentient beings, to save them permanently from the suffering of the cycle of birth and death.

From that time, that sage, due to the cause and effect of the vow he had made, became a Bodhisattva, going through countless lifetimes consecutively, he practiced the Bodhisattva Path with tireless diligence.

To seek the profound Dharma, that Bodhisattva was willing to risk his life to attain the Way, enduring countless lifetimes full of trials, having thousands of nails driven into his body, carving thousands of holes into himself, jumping into blazing fire pits… Peeling his skin to make paper, using blood to make ink, splitting bones to make brushes, these were used to transcribe sutras and fields, determined to study the Dharma.

To sow the affinity to save sentient beings, He does not spare treasures or even His life. In this life, He jumps into a ravine to be torn apart by a hungry tiger; in another life, He cuts off His skin and flesh to feed all kinds of sentient beings.

He never refuses anyone who asks. When the poor lack and ask, He opens the storehouse to give gold, silver, and jewels. Those who desire a throne, He will yield the seat; even to those who ask for a head, He cuts off His head, and to those who ask for skin, He peels off His skin.

Traveling across the globe, wherever a pin is stuck, that place is where the Bodhisattva once sacrificed His life for the sake of sentient beings.

Having experienced more lifetimes than the number of dust particles crushed by the Three Thousand Great Thousand Worlds, that Bodhisattva, in seeking the Bodhi Path to save sentient beings, practiced perfectly the profound Six Perfections of the Paramitas, used the Four Methods of Attraction to create deep karmic connections with countless sentient beings, accumulating tremendous merits impossible to calculate or envision, was praised by the Buddha Dipankara in the past and many other Buddhas across the ten directions, and was foretold: “In the future, you will become a Buddha, named Shakyamuni.”

Finally, in the era known as the Fortunate Aeon, in a land called Saha, when humans had an average lifespan of about a hundred years, that Bodhisattva had perfectly cultivated the difficult and arduous Bodhisattva path, which was long and profound, and all conditions had ripened. He descended from the Tushita heaven into the human realm as a prince, the son of King Suddhodana of the kingdom of Kapilavastu, and was named Siddhartha.

Even though he grew up surrounded by luxury, the Prince paid no attention to wealth and power. At the age of 29, the Prince left the royal palace, abandoning the throne that awaited him, leaving behind all the supreme pleasures of kingship, to go forth and practice asceticism.

After 6 years of extreme asceticism, no one had been able to do it, and he still did not achieve enlightenment, proving that the path of asceticism does not lead to liberation, he turned to meditation.

In the middle of the desolate forest of Pipphala, under the canopy of a great tree, he spread grass as a chair, sat down, and made an oath:

-Even if our skin, flesh, bones, and tendons are dissolved and our blood is dry. If we don't attain enlightenment, we will not leave this place.

In the lotus position, He entered deep meditation, lasting for 49 days and nights.

On the final night, just before that fateful moment, Mara, the King of Demons, along with his demon army, surged forward, determined to prevent him from continuing his meditation and attaining Enlightenment, escaping the net of demons.

They appeared in all kinds of demonic forms, sometimes tempting him with celestial maidens of heavenly beauty, other times manifesting as fierce armies of soldiers and horses, shouting and launching volleys of arrows, but whatever they were, He remained seated motionless, not leaving his meditation.

Because the merit and spiritual power of the Bodhisattva were complete, the arrows shot at Him could not hit Him, but turned into flowers and then vanished. Realizing that nothing could be changed, Mara left in anger.

Finally, at the moment the morning star just appeared, a light burst forth, tearing apart the veil of darkness that had covered countless eons. He attained the Bodhi Dharma, becoming the Supremely Enlightened One, perfectly awakened, known as Siddhartha Gautama Buddha.

From then on, the dawn of the True Dharma shone everywhere. For 45 years, He taught the Bodhi Dharma throughout the Three Realms.

From that time, sentient beings became aware of the path of Enlightenment, attaining permanent liberation from the ocean of suffering in the cycle of countless rebirths.

From that time, innumerable sentient beings across all realms—from hells, hungry ghosts, animals, to the human realm, Asuras, and the heavens—took refuge and became disciples of the Buddha, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the Benevolent Father of all beings, enjoying the nectar of the Dharma and resolving all kinds of suffering.

Relying on the True Dharma of the Tathagata, thousands have attained the state of Arahant, ended the cycle of birth and death, and reached Nirvana, countless others have generated the Bodhi mind, vowing to follow in the footsteps of the Buddha to practice the Bodhisattva Path to save all sentient beings.

For more than 2,500 years, through many vicissitudes, the light of the Buddha's Dharma has continuously guided humanity, gradually leading sentient beings to the shore of joy and Enlightenment.

How wondrous, how fortunate for those who are enlightened by the Bodhi Path, by the truths that the Tathagata attained only after countless aeons of arduous practice.

Thanks to these truths, life is alleviated of much suffering, and the soul dispels much darkness.

Thanks to these truths, the mental soil in sentient beings is sown with the seeds of Bodhi, so that in countless future lives they may grow into the fruit of Liberation, ending the cycle of suffering forever. Following in the footsteps of the Tathagata, bringing the joy of Enlightenment to all beings.

_____________________

With boundless gratitude, with sincere reverence, we disciples kneel at Your feet, following the words of Great Vow Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wholeheartedly making ten vows, which are the seeds of the Bodhi Mind continuing the line of the Buddha-Dharma, resolutely following the footsteps of the Buddha through countless great eons until the day of perfect Buddhahood, dedicating those merits to Venerable Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha and offering them to the Permanent Abode of the Ten Directions Triple Gem.

TEXT OF MAKING THE TEN GREAT VOWS OF BODHISATTVA SAMANTABHADRA

Namo Venerable Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha!

(1 prostration)

Homage to the Greatly Virtuous Samantabhadra Bodhisattva!

(1 prostration)

Homage to the Eternal Abiding Three Jewels of the Ten Directions!

(1 prostration)

I sincerely bring my heart

Boundless and ardent, reaching to the blue sky

At the feet of the Compassionate Father, embracing all

To raise an infinitely boundless vow

(1 prostration)

May the holy Buddhas

The ten directions: past, present, future

I respectfully bow to You

With wholehearted devotion, never fading in mind

(1 prostration)

May my words and thoughts be pure

Extolling to the utmost Virtue - Deep and abundant Merit

The Buddhas of the ten directions, past and present

Infinite Wisdom – Conduct, great and boundless.

(1 prostration)

May I offer treasures in devotion

Lotus throne, lanterns, incense flowers, etc... countless

I joyfully offer to the Buddha

Even if flesh decays, bones crumble, I accept

Offering Dharma - nothing compares:

Following the Right Path, practicing deeply.

Completely attaining the miraculous Buddha Fruit

Saving countless beings, fulfilling the word "offering".

(1 prostration)

May all remaining mistakes be forgiven

Bring forth repentance, eliminate the path of delusion

Infinite sins – heavy obstacles

Determined to eradicate, entirely pure in all aspects.

(1 prostration)

May throughout the entire realm of space

Upon seeing or hearing merits, a joyful heart arises

Above of Buddha – Saints, below ordinary beings

Wholeheartedly rejoice, countless, boundless.

(1 prostration)

May at the sacred moment

When the World-Honored One attained Enlightenment, I immediately earnestly

Kneel and offer countless celestial flowers

Sincerely requesting the Buddha to expound the vast and wondrous Dharma.

(1 prostration)

May when the Buddha has dwelled for a long time,

He intends to manifest entering deep Nirvana.

I earnestly and sincerely pray

Requesting the Buddha to remain in the world for countless thousands of eons.

(1 prostration)

May abundant Virtue and Wisdom be immense

From the Buddhas of the ten directions, through countless lifetimes of practice

I vow to learn, even if

My body is shattered, my life abandoned, determined to practice to attain success.

(1 prostration)

May all sentient beings

Entangled in countless errors, bound in the cycle of birth and death

Even throughout infinite lifetimes, never cease

I vow to serve, to nourish the Mind of the Way

To help all beings escape the suffering of the cycle.

Attaining the stage of Perfect Enlightenment, completely at peace. (1 bow)

May all the aforementioned merits

I dedicate the boundless blessings

To all sentient beings everywhere

Fully achieving Buddhahood, fully realizing the Dharma body. (1 bow)

Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's ten vows

I resolve to uphold them with unwavering determination for countless eons.

Until the end of space-time, there will be

Those ten vows never cease.

Body – speech – mind karma never stops

Connecting continuously in every moment.

Never able to be shaken

Please, O Three Jewels, witness this sincere heart.

(1 prostration)

Namo Shakyamuni Buddha, the Original Teacher! (1 prostration)

Namo Great Virtue Samantabhadra Bodhisattva! (1 prostration)

Namo Ever-Permanent Ten-Directions Three Jewels!

(1 prostration)

_Quang Tử_

tieu_de: WHY DO WE LOVE SOMEONE?
tom_tat: (The love story spanning many lifetimes of lay practitioner Nguyen Tri – Hue City) As a disciple of the Buddha, having listened to many teachings and practiced a lot, I know that love is suffering. But as an ordinary person, having not attained anything yet in practice, I
noi_dung:
WHY DO WE LOVE SOMEONE?

(The love story across many lifetimes of lay Buddhist Nguyen Tri – Hue City)

As a Buddhist disciple, having attended many teachings and practiced a lot, I know that love brings suffering. But as an ordinary human being, having not attained any realization, I could not resist the allure of romance.

The very first time we met, looking into her eyes, I felt like a lightning bolt struck straight into my heart... And so, I fell in love!!!

It was a beautiful day at the age of 32 when cruel fate brought me to her. After getting to know her for a while, my heart felt like it had been struck by lightning a second time when I found out that she was engaged to someone else. What bad luck!

“If I had known that one day you would get married,

I would go home, close the door, and practice internal cultivation.

Determined to meditate, cleanse the mind

Erase that person's name to ease the heart.”

Being struck by lightning so many times, my heart became very miserable, it kept stabbing in pain whenever I thought of her, unable to control it.

I tried many different ways to relieve the pain, like Panadol, Efferalgan 500… but failed, so I had to let it torment my heart.

When I could no longer bear it, I changed strategy. I knelt before the statue of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, recited sutras and bowed to Buddha, praying for the Buddhas to bless me so that I could know the cause from a past life for why I am suffering like this today, hoping the Buddhas would grant me a way to resolve it.

After kneeling for a while, I couldn't bear it anymore, so I lay down there and recited Buddha's name, looking very exhausted. But my mind was still very sincere, not superficial.

Suddenly, surprisingly, I saw a stream of light shining towards me. My mind was still clear, not asleep or confused, and I saw the Buddha appear, not just one, but three.

In the middle was Shakyamuni Buddha, on the left was Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, and on the right was Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva. After a short while, they disappeared.

The next day, after chanting, I began to meditate as usual. But that day, another miraculous phenomenon occurred, surely the Buddhas had responded to my prayer: I saw my past lives!

I was still awake, yet vivid images appeared before my eyes like a movie projected in my mind. Scene by scene, they flowed continuously, lively and realistic, showing my past lives. Later, when I researched, I learned that quite a few people also experience past lives while awake, just like I did.

The first life I remember, I saw myself as a very beautiful butterfly, fluttering and playing in the flower forest along with another cute butterfly. The two butterflies were affectionate, close to each other. But soon they both died, because the lifespan of a butterfly is very short.

Another life appeared, and the two butterflies had reincarnated as humans. I reincarnated as a charming young man, and the other butterfly reincarnated as a graceful young lady. (Just joking, actually my family background back then was quite normal) Time passed, we grew up, met each other, and fell in love.

But ironically, my two families at that time opposed this romance. They forced me to marry another girl. It was during the feudal period, so the customs were very strict; children’s marriages were decided by their parents. I had no choice but to reluctantly marry the girl my parents had chosen.

On the wedding day, over a hundred relatives from both sides came to celebrate joyfully. And my girlfriend also came, her face sad, yet her eyes revealed a trace of coldness.

I was momentarily startled, because I knew her character was very reckless, she had been practicing martial arts since she was young, and her swordsmanship was extremely formidable. I knew this, so I began to worry, not knowing what she was planning to do.

Sure enough, the worst thing happened. She suddenly stood up and drew the sword she had been hiding until now. As fast as lightning, she shot over to the side of the bride. Without saying a word, she swung the sword, the blade flashing like a blinding lightning, a stream of bright red blood spurted out, and the bride died on the spot.

Everyone present was utterly shocked, frozen for a moment. Then, like a waterfall, as fast as possible, they all rushed to stand up at once, fleeing desperately, running for their lives. The wedding, in just a few seconds, was like a beehive shattered.

Unluckily for them, my cruel friend was too fast, too dangerous. In the blink of an eye, she caught up. Stroke after stroke of the sword flashed brightly. Following that, blood gushed everywhere, screams rang out, faces were in extreme panic…

In the blink of an eye, hundreds of bodies lay down. A wedding that was joyful suddenly turned into a sea of blood.

The only person still standing is me. Overwhelmed with shock, I froze, trembling as I looked at the horrifying scene.

This tragedy happened because of me. Because of me, the parents, relatives from both families all died tragically. What should I do? Hold resentment against her? But even that cannot bring everyone back to life. How should I face those who have fallen?

My wife is struggling, my heart is tormented, and life is more miserable than death. I only know how to cling to the Buddha's mantra. "Nammo Great Compassion Guanyin Bodhisattva ! Nammo Amitabha Buddha! …” But the pain didn't stop.

In the end, I thought about it, and decided to commit suicide to go with everyone.

I walked to the edge of an abyss, intending to jump down. But just as I was about to set foot, a man in white appeared out of nowhere.

I was startled to realize that it was Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. He looked at me with compassion and began to explain the principles of suffering and impermanence.

Then He disappeared, but His teachings still echoed in my mind, helping me regain the courage to continue living, to face reality. I decided not to commit suicide anymore.

The image vanished, and I did not know what happened in that life. And then I saw another life appear.

In that life, I met that violent lover of mine again, and we fell in love. After the massacre at the wedding, whether she went to hell or suffered any retribution, I don’t know; maybe she did, I just didn’t see it.

Better than the previous life, our parents didn’t oppose us, and in the end, we still got married.

At that time, she had a pig, and she loved it very much. She always fed it by hand, bathed it, and took care of it meticulously from when it was small until it grew up.

Therefore, the pig was very fond of the mistress. Yet, on the wedding day, the mistress's beloved pig was still taken out to be slaughtered for the guests, how cruel!

The moment I saw the pig being slaughtered, a perception arose, telling me immediately: that pig was actually her future husband in this current life.

Everything was clear at that moment, I understood the cause of the matter.

She and I have had many lifetimes of fate being husband and wife, being lovers, so now when we just meet, past fate urges me to love her at first sight.

But the pig from a past life, now reincarnated as a human, is actually the groom, the one who will be tied in a hundred-year bond with her, because there is a very large debt between her and him. As for me, I only have fate but no debt, so it only stops at a one-sided love.

But suppose she and I were to be together, what would happen? This love has gone through many lifetimes, sometimes together, sometimes apart. Even if we could be together, wouldn't we still have to die, endure the suffering of separation by death?

Moreover, how much blood debt and karma would be caused with others? Whether it is hundreds of people killed by her in a fit of jealousy, or a pig along with other creatures killed at the wedding feast to please the guests, it would all be karma.

It is this very karmic retribution that creates boundless suffering for myself, and the pain of heartbreak I am enduring is only a small part of it.

Once I understood this, the sorrow within me gradually eased. I suddenly realized that the Buddha's teachings were not wrong in the slightest. Life is a sea of suffering! And if one lingers within this sea of suffering, one will surely be tormented by it for a long time, in one way or another.

From the moment we are born, we are already holding death in our hands, because has anyone ever lived forever without dying? In the span between birth and death, life is already laid out with all kinds of suffering, exactly like the Eight Trigrams formation of Old Kongming, you enter but cannot get out.

Illness, failure, loss... Today unemployed, tomorrow heartbroken, and then occasionally going mad.

All the exhaustion from competition, fighting for a piece of bread with life, and then one day it will also decline. Success does not last forever with anyone; at most, by the time of death it will all vanish anyway.

In conclusion, the dominant color of life is the sad color of suffering. Yet the vast majority still like to wander in this sea of suffering. Why is that? Because life also has joys: shopping, traveling, love, sex, fame, profit, money, power...

They are indeed present, yes, life has joys, but far fewer compared to suffering. Moreover, they quickly fade away, due to something called boredom.

It takes great effort to create moments of joy, yet when enjoying these joys, people quickly become bored. And if they do not become bored, life itself is always constantly changing, what exists now may be gone later, nothing lasts forever.

The joy of having something will be replaced by suffering when it is lost. Ironically! What once made us happy will turn into sorrow when it is no longer there.

And seemingly, joy plays exactly the same role as hooks inside worms. Very skillfully, they lure us to bite. But once, like a fish that has bitten the hook, how can one get free? This is a trap for each other.

They make people temporarily forget an entire endless sea of suffering, full as it is, and plunge into enjoying pleasures. This enjoyment of pleasure, the Buddhist scriptures call it Attachment, it makes humans want to stay longer in life. And life is a sea of suffering, meaning it makes humans want to linger in pain.

So that's it. The Buddha is truly wise; he pointed this out a long time ago. He said:

“Worldly pleasures bring little joy, much suffering, many worries, and even greater danger.”

Therefore, the Buddha taught that one needs to practice to liberate oneself from the suffering of samsara. Unfortunately, not everyone is wise enough to understand the teachings of the Buddha.

No! I must find a way to escape! I do not want to prolong the sufferings of this cycle of reincarnation.

__________________

When my mind had stabilized, I continued practicing chanting sutras and maintaining my schedule. The strange thing is that images of past lives did not stop.

While practicing chanting and reciting the Buddha's name, I continued to see scenes of past lives appear. Some people might think I was simply hallucinating. But if it were a hallucination, there would be no pattern at all. What I saw always closely followed the law of Cause and Effect. Thanks to this, I understood the complexities in my life and where they originated.

Once, recalling a past life, I was an eagle flying over the dharma assembly where Buddha Shakyamuni was giving a sermon. Not an ordinary eagle, but a Golden Vajra Bird, one of the Eight Classes of Devas and Nagas, always protecting the Dharma. I felt the boundless compassion and power of the Buddha, so I wanted to fly over to safeguard his dharma assembly, preventing anyone from causing harm.

Suddenly at that moment, a bat flew across above the Buddha's head; I don't understand what it was thinking, but it defecated on the Buddha.

You bastard! That rudeness drove me crazy, and I immediately flapped my wings to attack. Snap! A strike as fast as lightning, and the bat died instantly. Haizz… now I've committed the sin of killing. How virtuous! How virtuous!

The scene changed to another life; the eagle—that is, me—was reincarnated as a human, a general in China. As for the bat, it was also reincarnated as a human, becoming a civil official in the same dynasty as me—the general.

Because in my previous life I killed him (the case where the eagle tore the bat to death), old enemies met again, that civil official always regarded me as a thorn in his eye, always wanting to confront me.

By the king's order, I led the three armies, campaigning everywhere. Year after year, achieving many military exploits, yet as everyone knows, “when a general achieves success, ten thousand bones dry,” behind the glorious military achievements that immortalize a general are tens of thousands of the dry bones of soldiers who died in battle. Karma piled up, retribution begetting retribution, the scenes of “stab and kill each other” thus emerged, not knowing when they would end. As expected…

Some time later, the civil official at home slandered and accused me of all sorts of things to the king. Somehow, the king believed him and ultimately executed me. How unjust, Officer Bao! (Just kidding, at that time there was no Officer Bao.) And so one human life came to an end...

Right there, I was suddenly stunned. I realized that the bat I had killed was actually the civil official who, in my past life, caused my death in the present. It turned out to be a laywoman who did meritorious deeds at the temple where I had taken refuge in the past.

That was when I was 25 years old. After a period of studying Buddhism, I took the refuge ceremony at a pagoda in Hue. In the seven years that followed, I tried to diligently practice, repent, and chant the Universal Gate Sutra and the Suffering Relief Sutra...

At that pagoda, there was a laywoman who had been volunteering for many years. The moment we met, she already openly disliked me. Perhaps she did not know that in a past life she had been a bat that I had killed, but causality is like that—there are grievances and karma; just looking at each other made us uneasy.

Month after month, she always tried to prevent me from going to the temple to study and practice. Sometimes she spoke ill of me behind my back, sometimes she cursed and hinted insults, sometimes she slammed the temple door shut when she saw me coming, and sometimes she used a broom to drive me away.

The conflict between her and me grew increasingly intense, leading to arguments, quarrels, and exchanges of insults. In the end, I couldn't bear it anymore and had to stop going to the temple.

Now I understand the real reason for this matter. In this world, no one hates another without cause, friends; there must be some grievance from a past life, it's just that we don't remember it due to reincarnation.

________________

Are you feeling tired of these long-winded details yet? That's how reincarnation is, very tedious and cyclical. Try to be patient and keep reading, because I recall many past lives, each of which is connected to the people I meet in this present life.

The Buddha's teachings are truly profound; all sentient beings have been our relatives through countless lifetimes. Whenever we meet, there must be some connection or karma from past lives.

Take my current wife, for instance; it surely could not be without fate or debt that I am able to marry her. Let me tell you the story…

Back then, after the unrequited love I mentioned earlier, feeling sad and frustrated, I returned to my hometown.

"Wife and children are debts

Better to stay single, nourishing oneself"

I planned to live alone and stay single, taking care of and repaying my parents until old age. But then I met a girl...

I don't know how fate led it, but my plan to "stay single and pamper myself" was taken away by that girl. The wedding was held not long after.

One time, while practicing chanting sutras and remembering Buddha, I recalled a previous life, in a remote mountainous area, probably during the feudal era, because the clothing I saw looked like in historical films.

My current wife and I, at that time also joined in matrimony, lived peaceful months together in a simple thatched house by the quiet mountains.

It turns out that if it is destined to be husband and wife in the past, then now, it is very possible to continue the husband-and-wife life. (Actually, I remember 6-7 more lifetimes, we were all husband and wife, but it is quite lengthy, so let's leave it for another part where I will tell you.) In those days, we gathered firewood and caught fish daily to sustain ourselves, living a modest life through the years...

One day, I caught a goby fish. It looked shinier than ordinary fish, I don't know if it was because it had practiced spiritual cultivation, or if people had released it into the wild, recited sutras and mantras for it, but it looked very beautiful, and importantly, it had an aura. Its soul was probably stronger than that of ordinary fish. “But whatever! – I thought at that moment – It's just a fish, cooking it will be a full meal.”

Surely that goby fish hated me a lot. Right then, a perception appeared, letting me know where that fish had reincarnated. Oh no, it had followed me through reincarnation to this life; it is my third elder sister.

I was born into a family of farmers in the countryside of Hue. My family has four siblings, and everyone gets along well with each other, except for me and my third elder sister.

When I was a child, I just couldn't understand why, every time I ran into her, we would argue, like fire and water, like Tom and Jerry, over one thing or another. Even now, as I'm nearing old age, she still continuously torments me, constantly being hostile, without a break. Haizzz… all because of a piece of braised fish, now the grudge has grown as big as a communal house.

________________

So, what about those people we feel affection for whom we meet in life? I would say, they all also have bonds of kindness and gratitude.

I remember when I was a student studying in Da Nang, once I had a traffic accident and was covered with injuries. At that time, being far from home, in a 'foreign land,' having an accident was very serious.

Fortunately, the owner of the vegetarian restaurant I often went to eat at liked me very much. Knowing I had an accident and had no family around, she often came to take care of me and tended to my medicine very devotedly.

Once I recalled a past life (during my practice as usual), it turned out that in a previous life, the owner of that vegetarian restaurant had been my mother.

And I realized one thing: the affections we give each other in life are never accidental. Meeting someone and feeling affection must be due to fate. Without fate, people would have just passed by each other indifferently...

______________

At that time, after graduating from high school, I took the university entrance exam for three consecutive years without passing. Not knowing where to go, I finally decided to go to Da Nang to study at a private school. It was just an excuse to go out and have fun, as I really had no intention of studying.

By a twist of fate, when I was 24 years old, I met a lay Buddhist woman who practiced Eastern medicine. She was around 60 years old, and although we had just met, it felt as if we had known each other for a long time. She was very fond of me, and not long after, I became her disciple, learning the skills of pulse diagnosis and dispensing medicine.

In addition, I also met an uncle who was also a physician, and he was very fond of me, and taught me a lot about medicine. Thanks to the devoted guidance of those two mentors, up to now, I have gained considerable experience in the profession and have my own Traditional Medicine Clinic.

Once, I recalled a past life. At that time, I was an old herbal doctor living in seclusion on a mountain, specializing in preparing traditional herbal medicine and acupuncture to treat the local people.

The old man was aged, with long hair and beard, looking very much like a “sage with a transcendent spirit.” He had taken on two disciples, one male and one female, and carefully taught them until they became talented.

Many lifetimes later, the female disciple, still "attached" to me, became my relative for up to seven lifetimes, sometimes as a mother, sometimes as a younger sister, sometimes as a classmate, sometimes as a fellow practitioner, as a student, and then in one lifetime we both became monks in the same temple as senior and junior brothers...

In this lifetime, I have met again two disciples from the past, and not only that, they have also become my two masters teaching me medicine. How fascinating is the law of cause and effect, what we bring to others, they will return those things back to us.

Living through this life and the next, we are like acting in different roles in an endless play. Sometimes a father, sometimes reduced to a child. Sometimes a teacher, sometimes a disciple. Sometimes a human, an official, a general, and sometimes just a small anonymous creature…

The lives I can remember above are just a few tiny grains of dust in the boundless desert of lives I have experienced. And you, like me, along with all beings, are the same.

Life after life, one is born as a human, calling oneself by such a name. When born as a deity, one proclaims oneself a divine being, with a certain name. Then, after death, one is reborn as an animal, a butterfly, an eagle, thinking of oneself now as a creature without name or family... Thus, reincarnation continues, experiencing all kinds of suffering, living, then dying again, illness, aging, mourning the loss of what was loved, being irritated by the things one despises that cling, sadness from unfulfilled desires, and various other torments... Hell, hungry ghosts, animals, humans, gods, celestial beings, every kind of life has been experienced.

So ultimately, WHO AM I? If we think that I am the person with this name, given by my parents, then who was I before being born?

Before being born, I was an illusion bearing the name of a previous life.

After being born, I continue the illusory realm called this life.

After death, the illusion reincarnates into another life,

And calls that life, that existence, me.

Illusions follow one another in succession

Which one am I among the infinite continuous lives?

Cause and effect cycle, then impermanence dissolves

Ultimately, it is just like a series of connected dreams

Infinite fearful and miserable lifetimes

Born then perish, what is there to possess?

Because everything is merely an illusory manifestation

Why take the thousand-changing illusion as the Self???

Let it all go, no self, no other, no experiencer...

If nothing is sought, then nothing is lost

The true nature of the mind gradually reveals itself

Neither born nor dying, the Mind remains eternally unchanged

Endless peace without a trace of disturbance

This is Nirvana – let's temporarily call it that

No self, no suffering, no entanglement.

________________

Also during my time studying medicine in Da Nang, I came to know Buddhism. Gradually, I followed the Buddha, became a vegetarian, practiced spiritual cultivation, and sought liberation from birth and death. I often recited the Diamond Sutra, the Medicine Buddha Sutra, the Scripture for Deliverance from Suffering, other Mahayana sutras… and most of all, the Lotus Sutra.

Alongside that, I chanted the names of Buddha Shakyamuni, Buddha Vairocana, Amitabha Buddha, and Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara.

When I recall many past lives, I realize that I have actually had a connection with Buddhism through countless lifetimes, especially a connection with Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. It was he who planted the affinity and guided me from lifetimes when I was still primitive, tiny beings like specks of dust, gradually advancing to a human body suitable for practice.

Then, in many lifetimes, I ordained as a monk, and I also once attended the Dharma assemblies where the Buddha expounded the teachings, even though at that time I was only a great eagle.

In other lives, most of them were also laypeople, wholeheartedly aspiring to break free from the cycle of reincarnation, making vows, wishing to help sentient beings escape the sea of suffering; as long as there are beings still suffering, they vow not to become Buddhas.

Thanks to that karmic connection, I often received the blessings of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, encountered many miraculous occurrences, and was led by Bodhisattvas to see many other realms, such as hells and heavens...

But here, the story I am telling has already become quite long, so I have to save the rest for the next part (and only if you all show interest, I will continue). Goodbye and see you again!

(Quang Tu, rewritten from the account of senior brother Nguyen Tri)

tieu_de: Layman Quả Khanh is the incarnation of a Bodhisattva
tom_tat: Layman Quả Khanh, the author of the book series 'Cause and Effect in This Life,' is an incarnation of a Bodhisattva. This secret teaching comes directly from the incarnation of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, spoken by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua. Precisely, he is
noi_dung:
LAY PRACTITIONER QUẢ KHANH IS THE INCARNATION OF A BODHISATTVA

Lay practitioner Quả Khanh, the author of the book series "Cause and Effect in This Life," is an incarnation of a Bodhisattva. This hidden truth comes directly from the incarnation of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, as spoken by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua. More precisely, he is an incarnation of Bodhisattva Vimalakirti!

When the layperson Quả Khanh first met Venerable Diệu Pháp, he experienced 'a single hearing, a thousand awakenings.' From then on, he diligently practiced and opened the great wisdom. He, along with his sons and daughters, could see through various lifetimes and realms. Although he could perceive past and future causes and effects, he only referred to this ability as 'the development of wisdom.' He used this power to untangle difficulties and save many people. Many cunning thieves, upon encountering him, were also awakened to practice. They all became virtuous individuals, continuing the mission of saving sentient beings...

It means that anyone who meets him and listens to him give Dharma talks, the majority vow to stop doing evil and practice goodness. Then they give up meat and become vegetarian, strictly observe the precepts, change their entire life, and live happily.

Even Master Xuan Hua, from distant America, spent money to buy tickets to invite him and his daughter, Quả Lâm, to the U.S. He entrusted the Dharma seat to the father and son to answer questions and teach in his place… Just this alone shows how important layperson Quả Khanh's position was.

☆ Why it is said that Layperson Quả Khanh is an incarnation of a Bodhisattva

Venerable Master Hsuan Hua said: “Lay practitioner Quả Khanh deeply studied the Buddhist scriptures and successfully guided many people. Under his guidance, in 1992 alone, more than 20 people attained: Celestial Eye, Celestial Ear, Mind-Reading, Recollection of Past Lives, and Divine Awareness.” If he were not an incarnation of a Bodhisattva, who could accomplish this?

Because in the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, the Buddha teaches: "Sentient beings in the Sahā world are stubborn and difficult to save. They commit many evil deeds, perform few good deeds, are accustomed to bad habits, and have weak virtuous actions. Therefore, he and the Bodhisattvas have always manifested themselves in countless forms, taking 'responsive bodies' in various realms to transform and save them. They even transform into rivers, ponds, trees, and plants... to skillfully adapt to conditions in order to save beings. And the Buddha also once 'entrusted' the sentient beings of the Sahā world to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, instructing him to take care in saving them toward enlightenment, so they would not remain deluded and fall into the three evil realms."

However, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, when entering the human realm to save beings in this degenerate age, cannot sit on lotus thrones or hide under the name of Buddha or Bodhisattva. Doing so would make ordinary people feel inferior: Always thinking that they are inherently lowly and ignorant. They would not dare to believe that they have the ability to attain enlightenment and practice as Buddhas or Bodhisattvas. Therefore, they must "manifest in the body": meaning being born into the human world in the form of ordinary beings, with normal parents, carrying the full social and class identities… to be able to relate to and stand alongside them. Only in this way can they guide all layers of sentient beings.

Personal account by Layperson Quả Khanh

18 years ago, I happened to read the book “Giác Hải Từ Hàng.” Thanks to that, I entered the sea of Buddha’s teachings and it changed my whole life. The first time I went to the temple, I brought home the book “Collected Teachings” by Master Tuyên Hóa. This is an easy-to-understand guidebook that helped me clearly distinguish between good and evil.

For the first time, I learned about the six realms of reincarnation and how to transcend the three worlds. This book was like a lamp that dispelled all darkness in my mind. It made me feel like a blind person gaining sight, my mind enlightened as if I had just escaped from a deep, dark abyss.

I really enjoy watching Master Hsuan Hua's teachings on the sutras. I watch them with great enthusiasm and feel extremely uplifted. I often read through the night until morning, enjoying the abundant joy of Dharma every day. At that time, I began to understand the Way, which made me very happy. Whenever I met anyone or had a chance to talk, it was all about the Buddha-Dharma. I would explain why I gave up smoking and drinking. Why I vowed to stop eating meat and earnestly advised others to strictly observe the precepts and maintain a vegetarian diet.

☆ Encountering the incarnation of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva

On the night of December 8, 1993, just past midnight, at about ten minutes past midnight. I was intently reading the scriptures that Master Hsuan Hua was teaching, deeply immersed in thought, pondering and reflecting. Suddenly, I saw that Master Hsuan Hua was calling my house.

This was so unexpected that I have to confess I would not have dared to think of it even in a dream. For the first time, the incarnation of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara called me. It was also the first time I had the honor to converse with him, and I was so moved that I could not find words to express it. Moreover, I had the privilege of hearing him extend an invitation to me and my daughter, Quả Lâm, to come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

Throughout the time abroad, every day morning and evening I was always close to him. I was able to follow him to everywhere, to the "Buddhist Association Conferences" around the world. My master was a model figure, we monastics were solemn, the precepts pure, making us offer respectful bows. Personally, I once again broadened my horizons and stepped into a new path of human life.

Layperson Quả Khanh and Karma and Retribution in This Life

In 1995, Venerable Tuyên Hóa passed away, and my daughter and I returned to the Mainland. From that point on, I deeply realized the principle of impermanence, and the word 'death' became even more indelibly imprinted in my heart. Although I could not hold onto what had passed, I had the opportunity, both in the Mainland and in the United States, to witness many vivid and miraculous stories of cause and effect. Unwilling to let them fade away, I boldly wrote the book "Cause and Effect in Modern Life."

I hope that after reading this book, readers will clearly understand the karmic principles taught by the Buddha and become aware. Then they will develop the intention to self-reflect, embark on the path of studying Buddhism, observing precepts, and eating vegetarian. They will purify their own minds to enjoy the taste of Dharma, leaving suffering to attain happiness.

For delicate reasons, I am obliged to conceal the names and locations of the characters. But I want to affirm: The events I recount are entirely real, only the names and places have been temporarily changed. I share these stories of cause and effect in the hope that they can serve as a warning to people.

(Layperson Quả Khanh – According to the newspaper 'Manifesting in This Life')

Tuệ Tâm 2021.

* Venerables:

Layperson Quả Khanh was the person who stood beside Venerable Master Tuyên Hóa

tieu_de: LEFTOVER FOOD, SPOILED, WHAT TO DO
tom_tat: Today I share with all Buddhists a very small act; if you do not know it, you will suffer the retribution of hungry ghosts, but if you know it, the merit is limitless and boundless, and when you die, you will be reborn in the Pure Land in the future.
noi_dung:
LEFTOVER FOOD, SPOILED, WHAT TO DO

Today I share with the Buddhist followers a very small act which, if not known, will be subject to the retribution of the Hungry Ghosts, but if known, the blessings are immeasurable and boundless; upon death, one will be reborn in the Pure Land and will eventually become a Buddha.

From ancient times until now, whenever we overeat, we usually throw away the excess food, sometimes it is still edible, sometimes it has already spoiled. In a person's lifetime, an enormous amount of food is wasted, whether it is savory dishes or vegetarian meals, drinks or fruits or cakes. It is such a waste. So what should be done so that a very small act does not result in the retribution of hungry ghosts but instead brings immeasurable merit, and upon death allows one to be reborn in the Pure Land, and in the future, attain Buddhahood.

Before discarding food and drinks, as I mentioned, one should first face the Buddhas of the ten directions and make the following vow:

Today I wish to offer the food that I no longer consume to all sentient beings who are hungry and thirsty in the ten directions of the Buddha realms. May the Buddhas of the ten directions bless all the hungry sentient beings to gather here and partake of the food I offer. May this food transform into precious water and pure, sweet nourishment, like celestial ambrosia, so that sentient beings can be fully satisfied. May the merit generated from this act produce countless other merits, which I dedicate so that sentient beings in the ten directions may also be fully satisfied, through the 84,000 teachings of the Tathagata. May they be reborn everywhere as Bodhisattvas, emerging on lotus ponds adorned with seven treasures, like in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the future, when they attain Buddhahood, may the merit of this deed also be attained, as I wish.dedicated toward the fruition of my Buddhahood."

Then recite the PHỔ CÚNG DƯỜNG chant:

Án nga nga nẵng, tam bà phạ. Phiệt nhựt ra hồng. (7 times)

Source: (St)

tieu_de: FOR THOSE WHO FOLLOW THE PATH, ONE SHOULD PREPARE MENTALLY TO LEAVE EVERYTHING BEHIND BEFORE GOING
tom_tat: 🙏🙏🙏 FOR THOSE WHO FOLLOW THE PATH, ONE SHOULD PREPARE THEIR MIND TO LEAVE EVERYTHING BEHIND BEFORE GOING
noi_dung:
FOR THOSE LEARNING THE WAY, ONE SHOULD PREPARE MENTALLY TO LEAVE EVERYTHING BEHIND BEFORE GOING

🙏🙏🙏

FOR THOSE WHO STUDY THE PATH, ONE SHOULD PREPARE MENTALLY TO LEAVE EVERYTHING BEHIND BEFORE GOING

A bird that wants to fly needs to be light; if there are too many attachments, how can it spread its wings and fly far? If one still holds a lot of love and affection for a glance or a smile, is still drunk on a song or a melody, a little wealth, a little fame, a little temple, a few disciples, then Nirvana is still very far away.

How admirable are those wandering monks, needing no one to know their faces, needing no one to remember their names. When they go up into the mountains, they live with grass and trees; when they go down to the streets, they live with vegetables and porridge. They learn the practice of the stone: silence; they learn the practice of the wind: lightness; they learn the practice of the earth: tolerance; they learn the practice of water: compassion. They do not preach, because the Dharma is in every breath, every step. Watching them, just watching, is enough to want to cleanse all worldly dust.

Before death, all titles are meaningless; why crave a little worldly praise.

Before the god of death, all degrees are like passing clouds; why desire a bit of birth-and-death paperwork.

At the moment of dying, even if one has disciples forming an assembly, even if one has countless temples and towers, it is hard to exchange for a single ticket to ascend.

At the moment of dying, thinking of a little personal affection, a little property, how can one avoid the path of degeneration.

It is just that

If there is still some karmic connection with each other, then remind to diligently practice,

Life still remains, help whoever you can.

With the same aspiration, one naturally forms a place of practice,

With the same faith, one naturally becomes a disciple.

Loving and caring for each other means sharing the same mind, the same direction, the same faith(1), the same path(2)

Not because of shared benefit, shared fame, shared temple, or shared group(3).

Diligence allows one to catch up with the ferry,

Being lax leads one into the path of life and death.

Living,

must be prepared for

mentally

to leave.

OM AH HUNG

🙏🙏🙏

tieu_de: WHERE SHOULD ONE RECITE MANTRAS?
tom_tat: (Permission to answer readers' questions) A reader raised a concern:
noi_dung:
WHERE SHOULD ONE RECITE THE MANTRA?

(May I respectfully answer questions for readers)

A reader raises a question:

Dear Venerable Nun,

My Master teaches us not to chant the Lăng Nghiêm mantra in hospitals, funeral homes, morgues, or cemeteries because these places have many wandering spirits and ghosts, and the mantra could harm them, causing them suffering.

As for the Great Compassion mantra, it can be chanted anywhere.

Q.U

Please provide an answer:

Everything that the master teaches you all has reason and its own meaning in the Dharma instructions.

I dare not speak lightly.

But according to what I know and have witnessed, or heard recounted, there are special cases as follows:

In fact, the Great Compassion Mantra or the Lankavatara Mantra both have great power, because they were spoken from the golden mouth of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Especially the Lankavatara Mantra, which was once solemnly promised by the Devas and celestial beings before the Buddha to appear and serve the mantra and protect anyone who recites it at any time. Therefore, these mantras are often recited in sacred places.

Depending on one's ability to concentrate, adherence to precepts, abstaining from the five pungent spices, and practicing strict vegetarianism, the mantra can manifest effects to varying degrees. But what is clear is that when reciting the mantra, one must remain in a mind of great compassion and kindness.

The reason demons fear it is because they see the presence of eighty-four thousand deities attending (their presence is due to a promise made long ago before the Tathagata).

We have read history and seen that an empress, upon entering the meditative state of compassion, (was shot by an arrow because the king listened to the nonsense of a concubine) had the arrow return to the shooter, because the more malicious the person, the more they hurt themselves. This happened even without the manifestation of a protective deity's power, but it was the force of compassion itself.

Therefore, you cannot cause harm if the spirits or ghosts have no malicious intent.

A story I just learned is that at Van Phat Thanh temple, they allow wearing the Lăng Nghiêm charm. (Although previously, when Master Tuyên Hoá was alive, he often recited blessings into the charm to give to his disciples to wear. But later he thought that relying on wearing the charm would make people lazy in reciting, so he stopped doing it. Nevertheless, there were still some fortunate disciples who received his blessed charm, and it was so miraculous that even placing a piece of paper wrapping his charm under the pillow would permanently stop cases of sleeping paralysis caused by spirits.)

When Master Hsuan Hua passed away, his disciples still offered the amulets to Buddhists, and of course, outside the bathroom and toilet there were hooks for people to temporarily hang the amulets before going inside to keep the amulets respected.

But that time, a mother brought her daughter, about 17 years old, in; this daughter was easily possessed without anyone knowing. When she took a long time in the bathroom, the mother shouted, and everyone broke down the door to find the girl being pushed headfirst into the toilet by a force (an invisible ghost). If it had been a little longer, she would have died. People quickly tied a talisman around her neck and saved her from danger. Since then, a new rule was introduced at VPT: allowing talismans to be worn in the restroom because of this case.

Temples, hospitals, cemeteries... are places with the most ghosts and spirits. According to my writing and translation experience, a person with the third eye once advised the relatives caring for a mother in the hospital: You must chant the Lingyan Mantra all night to protect your mother; otherwise, even if the mother has truly recovered, she will still be tormented by spirits and suffer greatly, unable to be discharged. The child followed this advice, and the mother who was in severe pain was safely discharged from the hospital.

Some of my friends are laypeople, vegetarian, and diligent in their practice, but whenever they go to assist in chanting for the deceased, or enter temples or hospitals, they experience heaviness in their shoulders and legs... unable to walk, because spirits follow them and absorb their yang energy, or the vibrations of their energy field match that of the spirits, causing them to be frequently attached.

They are compelled to recite the Lankavatara mantra, or use a mantra string to trace the heavy or painful areas before it eases.

Within the temple grounds, spirits and ghosts are the most numerous. Even individual spirit altars have their own resident spirits who are allowed to stay. No one can drive the spirits away from taking refuge in the temple.

I tell these stories so that you can choose how to act to protect yourself.

Due to lack of time, this is as far as I can tell.

Zen, Pure Land, and Tantra are all precious teachings of the Buddha; please do not feel uncomfortable, attack, or slander the Buddha's teachings just because my explanation differs from your own practice.

Honestly, many times due to lack of time, coupled with discouragement and fatigue, I have wanted to permanently close my Facebook account.

I will pause here. I only prescribe according to illness and medicine; if you want to find a practice suitable for yourself, please visit specialized practice sites to satisfy your curiosity, rather than viewing it with the intention to attack or argue because you see that I did not say what you wanted.

I only recount what I have witnessed or know and do not lie. I only tell these stories out of necessity because the readers need them.

My health is inherently weak, and I am very busy writing and translating, but out of care for those who do not know yet, I try to use my modest strength to provide answers in the hope that you benefit and take good care of yourselves.

Respectfully.

Hạnh Đoan

Reader writes:

Thank you, Teacher, for taking the trouble to explain to me.

I think that each individual circumstance, each student's level, will have suitable teachings. Therefore, I don't think I am too rigid. Teachings change according to each case, and sometimes one person is not the same as another. So I have never thought that what I know is correct for all situations.

The nun is recuperating from illness, but perhaps because she cares for us, she still works hard on Facebook to share the practice with us during the pandemic, to grant us the gift of Fearlessness. I sincerely thank the nun. 🙏

Q.U

(Source: Luu Lần Cuối)

tieu_de: NEED TO PRESERVE GOOD KARMA, MINIMIZE THE LOSS OF KARMA IN DAILY ACTIVITIES, EXPENSES...
tom_tat: Over the past few years, reading and listening a lot, I finally understood that I should not waste my merit. All daily activities such as eating, using conveniences and electricity and water, going on trips... are all ways of using up merit
noi_dung:
NEED TO PRESERVE MERIT, MINIMIZE THE LOSS OF MERIT IN DAILY ACTIVITIES, EXPENSES...

Over the past few years, after reading and listening a lot, I finally understood that one should not waste their blessings. All daily activities such as eating, using conveniences and electricity and water, going out for travel, etc., all rapidly consume one's merit. In the future, one will have to work hard under difficult conditions or at the end of life, run out of blessings and constantly suffer from illness, lying in one place. Parents should not spoil their children too much by giving them excessive food or buying unnecessary toys.

Children should be taught to recite Buddha’s name, chant mantras, or a short verse and dedicate the merit to all sentient beings to reduce the loss of blessings.

Teach children to use red envelope money, birthday money, etc., to help difficult situations, release animals, make offerings... to cultivate compassion in them, so that they will become good citizens in the future!

EVERYTHING THAT PASSES THROUGH YOUR HANDS IS MERIT.❗

For example, when you use electricity at the company, and after using the computer you don't turn it off, even though your salary is not deducted, your merit has already been depleted. Don't think that only using money from your own wallet is what consumes merit. Also, don't just assume that wasting your own belongings is the only way merit is wasted.

Everything that passes through your hands that you waste is indeed wasting your own merit.

For example, if friends invite you to a meal and order a table full of food, but you end up wasting more than half of it, whose merit are you wasting? It is still your own merit.

Another example, if the company sends you on a business trip and reimburses your expenses, you are supposed to take public transport, but you choose to take a taxi instead, whose merit are you wasting? It is still your own merit.

Everything that passes through your hands is your own blessing, so why is that? Think about it, it is because you have blessings that friends invite you to meals, that business trips can be reimbursed for expenses, yet we waste them, feeling that they belong to others and therefore can be wasted. This is a very big mistake!

In fact, what you are wasting is your own merit. Merit is nurtured by oneself, and also exhausted by oneself; when it is depleted, one is unaware. In the past, someone gave Master Thái Hư a ginseng root, but Master Thái Hư felt he did not have the merit to use it, so he passed it on to Master Đàm Hư. When someone offered items to Master Hoằng Nhất, including medicinal herbs, he also gave them away to others. Thus, the merit of these great monks is immense.

Think about it, before learning Buddhism, how much merit have we already squandered? Taking advantage of others' conveniences is also a way that causes us to lose merit. We just think that it belongs to someone else, it is communal property, or the property of the owner, so we can waste it. But in reality, the things we waste are all our own merits.

Amitabha Buddha

Respectfully taught by Venerable Master
