tieu_de: IF YOU WANT TO DISTANCE YOURSELF FROM EVIL DHARMA, YOU SHOULD RECITE THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA AND STUDY THE LĂNG NGHIÊM SUTRA
tom_tat: The phenomenon of chaos in the world is increasing day by day, and the more chaos there is, the more it proves the importance of the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra and the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. Author: Dương Quả Cường
noi_dung:
IF YOU WANT TO DISTANCE YOURSELF FROM EVIL DHARMA, YOU SHOULD RECITE THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA AND STUDY THE LĂNG NGHIÊM SUTRA

The phenomenon of chaos in the world is increasing day by day, and the more chaos there is, the more it proves the importance of the Lankavatara Sutra and the Lankavatara Mantra.

Author: Duong Qua Cuong

When I was thirteen years old (in 1987), my father suddenly passed away from a stroke. This event was a very shocking experience in my life. My father was a person who never lost his temper, a person who, in anything he did, preferred to suffer losses himself rather than let others. I wanted to learn from my father's spirit, so I took refuge in Buddhism and began to get in touch with Buddhist teachings.

In Taiwan, I searched for a long time but could not find a virtuous teacher suitable for my capacity, and so I wandered aimlessly in Buddhism for two whole years. During this time, I observed some phenomena of the decline of the Dharma, which made me develop doubts about Buddhism. It was not until 1989, for the sake of my studies, that I had to rent a room on the upper floor of a Buddhist office. Around that time, the landlord invited a lay practitioner from the United States to teach him the Dharma. I was staying in his upstairs room at that time, so I was also invited to participate.

Among the twenty-some brothers participating, each of them gradually received the spiritual influence, including what they called "opening the heavenly eye" (which in fact was just "communicating with spirits"). Sometimes spontaneously, they would suddenly start dancing or striking as if performing martial arts. Only I and another layperson not only did not feel any influence, but also found their reasoning strange (because we recited the Lingyan Mantra every day). However, since we had read too few scriptures and lacked sufficient understanding, we were unable to point out where the problem lay.

After that, this layman from America told us that practicing Buddhism does not necessarily mean one must be a strict vegetarian; eating meat is fine too! He also secretly told some people privately: "I have a Pure Land such and such in the heavens; all of you were once my children, spouses, guardians in the heavens. I have come here to guide you back to the heavens!" At that time, I truly did not know what to do, so I prayed to Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara, asking for wisdom to be able to discern right from wrong; then I searched through and looked for answers in thousands of Buddhist books at the library. When I opened the first bookAt first, I saw it explained in the book on the Five Hundred Aggregates of Demons (Fifty Manifestations of the Demon Aggregates), and the explanation was given by Venerable Hsuan Hua. I was very happy because it proved that my own view was correct, while the layman's view on eating meat was contrary to the Four Types of Pure Clear Repentance in the Lengyan Sutra. The arguments he made about “a certain pure land in heaven” were precisely the phenomena of the Fifty Demon Aggregates.

When I saw the precepts set by the Venerable:

“The corpse has no affinity,

The hungry ghost has no transformation affinity,

The poor has no seeking affinity.”

Translation:

(Frozen to death has no affinity,

Starved to death has no transformation affinity,

Poor to death has no seeking affinity.)

I have just realized that the strange phenomena in Buddhism that I had observed before were all created by humans; at the same time, in that context, on the other side of the globe, there is still an elderly Venerable Monk along with his disciples, striving to prolong the period of the Buddha's true Dharma, especially his spirit of "taking the lead in bearing the burden"—"as long as I am here, I will not allow the decline of Dharma to occur!" With a spirit of "selfless justice, forgetting oneself for others," he has made great vows of compassion, willing to endure suffering on behalf of all sentient beings, which deeply moved me, and also caused thoseMy doubts about my previous Buddhism suddenly became clear, and this also led me to find a Teacher with character, spirit, and genuine practice.

In 1990, when the Venerable Master went to Taiwan to propagate the Dharma, I took refuge with the Venerable Master and chose him as my lifelong spiritual guide, and at the same time, I requested to receive the Five Precepts.

In the period of the decline of the Dharma, chaotic phenomena are occurring more and more frequently, and the more such chaotic phenomena appear, the more it proves the importance of the Lankavatara Sutra and the Lankavatara Mantra. In recent years, I have persistently been reciting the Lankavatara Mantra without interruption, and I hope that all of us can also recite the Lankavatara Mantra together. Furthermore, we should memorize the Lankavatara Sutra, so that, besides enabling ourselves to distinguish between right and wrong, most importantly, we can extend the late master's vow—to ensure that the True Dharma endures for a long time!

Source: dharmasite.net

tieu_de: HELL – ONLY AFTER EXPERIENCING IT DO YOU SEE HOW HORRIFYING IT IS
tom_tat: (A true story of an officer in Ho Chi Minh City in 2021) When mentioning the two words "Hell", many people often think that this is a concept that does not exist. They believe that humanity invented this place to
noi_dung:
HELL – ONLY AFTER EXPERIENCING IT DO YOU SEE HOW TERRIFYING IT IS

(A true story of an officer in Ho Chi Minh City in 2021)

When mentioning the two words "Hell," many people often think this is an unreal concept. They believe that humanity invented this place to warn evil, immoral, greedy, and harmful people.

However, in reality, I have seen many true stories happening. Those people recounted that they had visited hell, knowing clearly about the prisons and the tortures and executions there. Like Ms. Ba Cháo Gà, nun Diệu Hân, layperson Hứa Ngọc Thủy, Korean female painter Me Kyeoung Lee ...

In particular, until I personally experienced it myself, I no longer had any doubt. Hell truly exists. Even now, I have not fully recovered because it was too terrifying. No words can fully describe it.

I am an officer working at the Military School of Military Zone 7. My full name is Lê Ngọc Tú, currently living at 479 Tô Ký Street, Trung Mỹ Tây Ward, District 12, Ho Chi Minh City. The journey just happened last night. At 0:00 AM on the morning of September 13, 2021, in a dream, I was led to hell.

First, they led me to an extremely dark road, where I saw many people lying dead all over the street. Seeing that, I thought: "why are so many people dying?"

I did not speak a word, just thought it in my mind. Yet suddenly, from the void, a voice replied: “These people, because they committed extremely heavy karma of killing while alive, must die on the road.”

Strangely, there was no sound at all, but that answer seemed to be pinned straight into my heart. It turns out that in this realm, beings do not communicate with language, but with the mind. Seeing the scene of the dead scattered all over the road looks no different from the end of the world. Truly heartbreaking.

Killing karma is not only about killing humans. Those who, while alive, kill or slaughter animals also commit killing karma. Thinking about this, I suddenly realized. Then humanity is still committing heavy slaughter every day.

War and violence have killed so many people. Butchers who specialize in skinning, cutting meat, and taking the lives of animals. Even in the kitchen of every household, we still nourish ourselves, nourish our families with the lives of those animals.

Yet we remain ignorant and confused, even taking dishes made from those lives as delicacies. Gradually, humans kill animals not just to live, but also to satisfy their mouths, to enjoy drinking and feasting. But whatever the reason, it is still wrong. That is why the number of deaths is so overwhelming, filling entire streets. If humanity does not soon awaken and stop the act of killing, we will all have to bear the consequences in this way, and even many times more.

Next, they took me to another road. On the road, there were many vehicles. Each vehicle was the same as the others, filled with a lot of money and gold, to the brim. Everyone had their own vehicle. Whichever vehicle belonged to a person, that person got on it. I also had such a vehicle. I thought again: “Where does so much money and gold come from?”

They replied: “This money and gold were accumulated by each person during their lifetime. But after a life has ended without using it all, it remains there.”

We got on the car and traveled for a very long distance. Then, they said: "The wealth on the car, anyone who wants to take it can take as much as they like." I got off the car but did not take any gold or money with me.

They asked me why I didn’t take anything. I replied that I didn’t need those things. Then they led me further. But oh, when I turned back to look, I saw a horrifying scene like in a movie. Anyone like me who didn’t take anything was safe. But those who took gold and money, their bodies burned black as if doused in gasoline, lit on fire, and were burning. Burned black like that, they then disappeared completely.

It is true that when we die, money no longer has any meaning. We cannot take it with us. So why cling to property, making the path to liberation heavier and more difficult.

Today's humanity values money, fame, and honor. Earning a living to support oneself is not enough; people also want to have a lot of money to satisfy all sorts of desires, racing after the trend of materialism.

Many people even go so far as to commit crimes and create evil karma to earn a lot of money. In the end, they can't spend it all in a lifetime. Once dead, that pile of money can't be taken along, while the evil karma follows us like a shadow, causing countless suffering consequences.

After that, I was taken to the prison for rebellious and unfilial people. Before entering this prison, they advised me that during interrogation, I must tell the truth exactly as it is, neither adding nor omitting anything. If it happened, say yes; if it didn't happen, say no. If one lies about the truth, the punishment will be doubled. Remembering those words, I went into the prison.

As soon as I stepped in, the jailer asked me:

-In the human world, were you ever unfilial or rebellious?

I answered:

-I am not guilty of unfilial behavior. But I am guilty of being rebellious. When I get too angry, I often say unpleasant words that make my mother sad.

Speaking of that, the prison guard pointed to the shackles and said they were mine. Seeing my shackles ready and waiting, I was terrified, my limbs completely giving way. Suddenly, from the void, I was reminded to recite Buddha's name. I followed and recited, and naturally, my shackles disappeared.

I looked around this prison and saw the criminals being tortured in an extremely horrific manner. They used iron hooks to tear out the prisoners' tongues and then poured boiling copper onto the tongues. As they poured, the flesh fell off because it was too hot. It was even worse than pouring acid onto the tongue.

The sin of being unfilial to one's parents is a very serious sin. Parents are the ones who give us life, form, endure the pains of childbirth, raise us, and care for their children every minute, every day. The merits of parents are enormously great, perhaps there is no need to say more. Therefore, whoever commits the sin of unfilial disobedience will have to enter hell to suffer indescribable pain and suffering.

Through the Hell of Unfiliality, I was led to the Hell of Retribution. This hell is reserved for punishing those who commit the sin of killing. Upon entering, I heard wailing cries, pitiful and agonizing, echoing throughout the entire hell.

When alive, any sinner who killed sentient beings in any way must now suffer being killed in the same manner, no different. Whoever once beheaded, disemboweled, or skinned living beings will now also be beheaded, disemboweled, and skinned to truly feel that pain.

I saw the scene of punishment, with blood flowing like a torrent. The stench was so foul that it was almost indescribable. Then they pointed to one spot and said that spot belonged to me. At that moment, I recited the Buddha's name, and that spot disappeared.

Just think about it. When a person gets a little cut, bleeds a bit, they already feel aching, pain, discomfort, suffering. Yet when witnessing beings being slaughtered, dismembered, skinned, cut into pieces, boiled in hot water ... they still show no compassion at all. Isn't that extremely cruel?

If one cannot feel the pain of sentient beings, and is so cruel to them, then one will inevitably enter hell to experience it firsthand and repay their karma.

In the next hell, I saw a scene that was somewhat more peaceful. But since it is hell, there is no place where sinners do not suffer. Here, there is a very large green river. On the river, there is a raft with seven beautiful colors.

Particularly in this hell, the sinners are even more numerous than the river, filled everywhere. I saw a monk, so I asked,

- A monk can have sins too?

They answered that although they carry the title of having left home to practice the Way, in reality they do not sincerely cultivate, and even commit serious sins, daring to do anything without restraint.

When a person leaves home, it means they have relied on the merits of the Buddha and the Triple Gem. They should diligently practice, follow the Buddha's teachings correctly, diligently cultivate wisdom, and propagate the Dharma to help people in the world.

But nowadays, in the age of the decline of the Dharma, the number of people pretending to be monks to profit and deceive sentient beings is not small. These “parasites” have affected the reputation, purity, and loftiness of the Buddha Dharma, causing extremely serious consequences, making those who do not understand develop a mind of disparaging the Triple Gem, thereby committing a great sin and destined to fall into the Avici Hell.

This can cause people with low faith to give up practicing, losing the path to liberation. Moreover, it also leads to the decline and eventual destruction of the Buddha Dharma. When that happens, sentient beings will no longer have anyone to rely on.

As soon as he finished speaking, the prison guard drove all of us onto the raft. Anyone without a raft who fell into the river would instantly turn into water. When I got onto the raft, a voice from the void told me to close my eyes and wholeheartedly recite the Buddha's name in order to cross the river.

As I recited, I saw the raft sink to the bottom of the river and then sprout up to the surface of the water, reaching the shore. But out of countless thousands, only one or two people could cross the river. The rest sank to the bottom and resurfaced only as white skeletons like snow.

As soon as I got ashore, I felt incredibly thirsty. Without hesitation, they took me straight to the Retribution Prison. From the void above, I was reminded:

- When the prison officer scoops coconut water in a bowl and offers it, do not drink. There is someone there cutting the chicken's throat. Take that water and pour it over its wound, do not let it die.

I remembered and followed. As for the others, because they didn’t know, they were parched with thirst, and when they saw a bowl of coconut water, they immediately drank it up. Oh, woe! Wherever the body had openings to the outside like the eyes, nose, ears, mouth, etc., fresh blood gushed out. Watching that scene, I felt like fainting, unable to stand any longer.

After that, the jailer gave me a cake similar to a gai cake, telling me to take it and eat. But I did not dare to eat it. At this moment, I was taken to the Lustful prison.

I saw many people eating the cake that I was holding, so I boldly ate it. As soon as I ate it, my body immediately went limp like cooked noodles, and I couldn’t walk anymore. Those who couldn’t continue walking were lifted under the armpits by the guards.

We were taken up to a rack of iron spikes, each person in a separate compartment, each compartment bearing the full name of the individual. As soon as the prisoner stepped in, their arms and legs were spread in all directions like the shape of an X, locked so they couldn't move. In front of each person was a cluster of spears aimed straight at them, only about a handspan from their face.

The prison master posed questions to each person; anyone who answered one question correctly would have a lock opened, and anyone who answered incorrectly would immediately be impaled with iron spikes.

For men, sharp iron spikes like spear tips were thrust from the throat downward. For women, spears were inserted upward from the anus. People moaned in agony, a scene so horrific that no writer could find words to describe it.

I had already stood in my own cell, but I was not bound like the other criminals. Witnessing what happened there, I nearly fainted, unable to bear it any longer. They told me that the prisons I had passed through were exactly the karmic retributions for the sins I had committed. I should have been executed in this way. But since I realized from a young age, refrained from killing, diligently accumulated virtue, and practiced good deeds until now, I was absolved.

They also warned me not to repeat my mistakes from now on. If I do, those punishments will not disappear; they will still be there waiting for me to face.

They warned me a lot, telling me that even taking a chili, a bit of fish sauce, or salt without asking is considered theft. Don’t think that a small amount doesn’t matter. Small acts have small consequences, big acts have big consequences. Whether severe or light, the outcomes must also be considered.

They also reminded me not to forget to pay attention to my words, to consider carefully everything I say. Statements that seem merely playful or joking, which make the listener upset, are also considered sins and fall into verbal misconduct.

They also advised me to remember to accumulate virtue, do good deeds, and avoid any actions that violate the Buddhist precepts. When I have enough strength, they will take me to many more places. Right now, my energy is still weak, so I can only go this far. There were many other things I was advised on, but because I was too tired and scared, I cannot remember them all.

---

When I woke up, I saw that the clock had passed 12 o'clock. I felt very thirsty. I sat up and tried to calm myself down. But I sat for nearly half an hour and still couldn’t regain my composure.

The story above is my true experience. I do not dare to say a single word falsely. If I were to lie, I would take the punishment in hell. By telling this story, I only want everyone to see it as a lesson and awaken. To abandon evil deeds early, to quickly perform good deeds, and to cultivate merit to eliminate the karma that has been created.

This shows that when a person dies, they cannot take anything with them, except for their merits and demerits. Those with many merits have an easier path and sufficient provisions. Those with many demerits have a dark, heavy path that is difficult to escape.

Nowadays, most of us are obsessed with superficial things, spending our energy chasing meaningless fame and wealth. It wastes a whole lifetime. When we close our eyes and let go of this body, even the wealthiest people or those in high-ranking positions cannot save themselves from their own bad deeds.

Tĩnh Như, rewritten from the narration of Lê Ngọc Tú

tieu_de: THE WAY OF GIVING LITTLE WITH ENDLESS BLESSINGS, THE WAY OF OFFERING FOOD:
tom_tat: ❤This is a way to create miraculous merit for all those who have a compassionate heart for the hungry and suffering wandering spirits, without spending much at all. It is not limited to days like the Vu Lan Festival, the 2nd day
noi_dung:
THE WAY TO GIVE LITTLE BUT RECEIVE ENDLESS GREAT BLESSINGS, THE WAY TO OFFER FOOD SACRIFICES :

❤This is a way to create miraculous merit for all those who have a compassionate heart and pity for the hungry wandering spirits and hungry ghosts without spending much. It is not limited to days like the Vu Lan Festival, the 2nd, or the 16th of each month; you can make offerings on any day.

❤This method was preached by the Buddha in the sutra "BUDDHA'S TEACHING ON THE RESCUING SUTRA OF THE DIEMA KALPA CHANT" and is a treasure that helps disciples cultivate compassion, while simultaneously generating immeasurable merit and planting the seeds of Bodhi with countless beings in the metaphysical realm.

🍀The Buddha told Ananda: "There is a mantra called Infinite Majestic Self-Reliant Radiant Supremely Wonderful Power. Whoever recites this mantra will immediately receive abundant superior food and drink, offering to countless hundreds of thousands, innumerable hungry ghosts, Brahmins, and deities. Eventually, all of it will be transformed into 49 containers of food, each container as large as the water of Makitada."

🍀In a previous life, Ananda, when he was a Brahmin, in the residence of Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara and the Tathagata Worldly Self-Existent with Revered Authority received this mantra. Therefore, it is possible to prepare offerings of food and drink for countless hungry ghosts and celestial beings, while also helping them to be free from the suffering of being a hungry ghost and be born into the heavenly realm. Ananda! You should now uphold it so that your merit, virtue, and lifespan will be increased.

🍀At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra to Venerable Ananda:

"NASICT PHA DA THA NGA DA PHA LO CHI DE, AN TAM BAT RA TAM BAT RA HONG"

(Sanskrit: Namaḥ sarva tathāgata-avalokite_ Oṃ_ sambhāra sambhāra hūṃ)

Transliteration: Nam ma Sa rơ va Ta tha ga ta A va lô ki tê. Om Sam ba ra Sam ba ra Hum.)

🍀The Buddha told Ananda:

– If there are any good men or women who wish to pray for blessings, longevity, increase in goodness, and quick fulfillment in almsgiving, they may do so early every morning or at any time without obstacles. One should take a clean vessel filled with water, put in a little food, noodles, and various cakes, etc., then hold the vessel in the right hand, recite this mantra seven times, and afterward invoke the names of the 4 Virtuous Tathagatas:

🍀 Namo Ratna Tathagata.

(Nang mo ba nga pha de bat ra bo si ra dat nang da tha be da a.)

By praising and invoking the name of the Buddha Many Treasures Tathagata, one can destroy all kinds of demons, all stingy evil deeds, and karmic traces from many past lives are completely eliminated, immediately attaining perfect merit and virtue.

🍀 Namo Sublime Form Tathagata.

(Nang mo ba nga pha de to ro ba da nga da tha nga si da.)

By invoking and reciting the name of the Buddha Sublime Form Tathagata, one can destroy all ugly forms and immediately attain complete beauty.

🍀 Namo Boundless Compassion Tathagata.

( Nang mo ba nga pha de vi bo la nga dat ra da dat tha be si da.)

Because of the blessings of invoking the name of the Glorious and Compassionate Tathagata, the throats of all kinds of spirits become wide. All the food offerings made are fully as wished.

🍀 Namo Ly Bo Uai Tathagata

( Nang mo ba nga pha de a ba dung ca ra dat tha be si da.)

Because of the blessings of reciting the name of Ly Bo Uai Tathagata, all fears of the spirits are completely destroyed and removed from the path of hungry ghosts.

🍀The Buddha said to Ananda:

If your family line praises and upholds the merit of the four virtues of the Tathagata, they should clasp their hands seven times and then pour the food from the container onto clean ground. After performing this offering act, all of it will transform into 49 large storehouses of food, like the water of Maketa. In the four directions, countless numbers of hungry ghosts will receive this food in abundance, and at the same time, those hungry ghosts will abandon their ghostly bodies and be reborn in the heavenly realms.

🍀Hey Ananda! If one offers alms to monks, nuns, male lay followers, or female lay followers for the sake of various kinds of spirits, one will immediately receive abundant limitless merit, equal to the merit of offering to hundreds of thousands of Tathagatas, truly without error. One will enjoy a long life, increased beauty and health, full of wholesome roots, and all non-human beings, rakshasas, and malevolent spirits will not dare to harm them. Moreover, one can accomplish limitless merit and longevity.

🍀If you want to make offerings to the Brahmin celestial beings… use a bowl filled with food and drink, recite the aforesaid true mantra 21 times, and then release it into a stream of clean water. Doing so will immediately provide delicious food and drink in the heavenly realm, offered to hundreds of thousands, countless Brahmin celestial beings. These celestial beings, due to the virtue of the mantra infused in the food, will all fulfill fundamental wishes and virtuous deeds, and simultaneously make the vow that:

🍀“May the person who offers food have a long life, health, beauty, and peace. May that person understand truthfully and purely all that is seen or heard in their heart, fully accomplish the virtues of the Heavenly Brahma, practice the conduct of the Brahma Heaven, and through the merit of offering, may invoke countless Tathagatas. May all enemies be unable to cause harm.” Or, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, if they wish to make offerings to the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, they should bring flowers, incense, and clean foods, bless them with the aforementioned mantra 21 times, and dedicate them to the Triple Gem; then those men and women will achieve delicious flavors.Strange in the heavenly realm, they dedicate and offer the Buddha's teachings and the monastic treasure throughout the ten directions of the world. They are also praised and encouraged to rejoice in the merits, often being protected and praised by the Buddhas, with celestial beings frequently coming to support them, fully accomplishing acts of generosity.

🍀Now Ananda, you must listen to my words and practice them properly, circulating them widely, so that sentient beings everywhere hear and see them and gain immeasurable merit. This is what is called Saving Speech for Hungry Ghosts and the sufferings of sentient beings. Hence it is named the Dhāraṇī Sūtra, which you should uphold. All the great assembly and Ananda… after hearing the Buddha speak, wholeheartedly believe, joyfully and obediently follow.

tieu_de: Stinginess and miserliness result in extreme suffering.
tom_tat: (According to Phap Uyen Chau Lam). Stinginess and miserliness in Buddhism are called 'Greed'. Ordinary people are ignorant and go astray because greed is the root. Therefore, good deeds are as tiny as a hair, while evil deeds are as deep and heavy as a high mountain; merit
noi_dung:
STINGY AND MISERLY BEGET EXTREME SUFFERING.

(According to Pháp Uyển Châu Lâm).

Stinginess, in Buddhism, is called "Xan Tham". Ordinary people are deluded and go astray because stinginess is the root cause. Therefore, good deeds are as little as a hair, while evil deeds are as heavy as a high mountain; merit is as thin as spring ice, while poverty is as abundant as autumn drizzle. Those who are stingy and do not give alms, after death, are born as hungry ghosts, experiencing many lifetimes without hearing the name of food or drink, let alone the act of eating or drinking, and that suffering is truly boundless.

Dear friend! Stinginess is the primary cause that leads one to become a hungry ghost, resulting in a life of poverty in countless future lifetimes. Therefore, whether you are rich or middle-class, please do not be greedy or stingy. You should help your family members, or give a little charity to the poor. Giving is the cause of wealth, and giving away is everlasting. A piece of food that we gladly offer to help someone through hunger today will become a refuge for us in many lifetimes to come!

_______________________________________

A STINGY PERSON WILL RECEIVE THE KARMIC CONSEQUENCE OF DESCENDING INTO HELL.

(According to the Ekottara Āgama Sūtra).

“In the past, during the time when the Buddha was alive, in the city of Sāvatthī, there was a wealthy householder named Bā-đề, who possessed immense wealth at home, with gold and silver beyond calculation. Although he was rich, he was miserly and kept everything without daring to eat or wear; the clothes he used and the food and drink he consumed were very poor and meager; he also did not give alms to his wife and children, relatives, servants, attendants, friends, acquaintances, or to the monks and Brahmins… not a single thing. Moreover, he developed wrong views, losing his wholesome roots.”

He had no descendants. After he passed away, all his wealth and treasures were collected by the state. King Bāsanaka himself went to gather the assets. After collecting them, he went to the Buddha and said to the Buddha:

- Where did the wealthy man Bāḍi go after he passed away?

The Buddha told the king:

- The wealthy man Bāḍi had exhausted all his previous merits and did not create new good deeds. Because he developed wrong views that destroyed his roots of goodness, after death he was reborn in hell, crying miserably.

The king, hearing this, was heartbroken and shed tears, saying:

- Wealthy Patron Bà Đề, what karmic deeds did you commit in the past to be born into a wealthy family? And what evil deeds did you commit so that you could not enjoy such happiness?

The Buddha said to the king:

- Long ago, there was the Buddha Kassapa. After he entered Nirvana, this wealthy patron was born in the kingdom of Sāvatthī as the son of a farmer.

One day, a Jeta Buddha came to that house. At that time, the householder immediately offered rice and food as alms. The Jeta Buddha, upon receiving the food, flew up into the sky. Seeing this, the householder made a vow, saying: "Keep this good karma so that in future lives I may be born in places with abundant wealth and treasures, never falling into the three evil paths." After giving alms, he then felt regret, thinking to himself: "I should have given the food to my servants and attendants earlier, not to the shaven-headed monk."

The Buddha said to the king:

- The wealthy woman Bhadra, due to her merit of giving food to the Buddha of the Pīṭha realm, was always born with abundant treasures and wealth, lacking nothing. However, because after giving she would develop remorse, in her successive births, although she lived in wealth and luxury, she could not enjoy the pleasures of such richness. Stingy and miserly, she carefully guarded her wealth, did not clothe or feed herself lavishly, nor did she give alms to her husband, children, relatives, friends, or to the Brahmins and Sramanas...

Therefore, a wise person, upon hearing this cause and condition, if possessing wealth or property, should practice giving and not cultivate a stingy heart. When giving, do so sincerely with your own hands. After giving, rejoice and do not harbor thoughts of regret. By giving in this way, one can receive immense, limitless rewards.

________________________________________

THE REWARD FOR STINGINESS OCCURS IMMEDIATELY.

(According to the Xuất Diệu Sutra).

In the past, during the time when the Buddha was alive, in the country of Shravasti, there was a wealthy man named Nanda. His household was extremely rich, with a great amount of gold and silver; elephants, horses, carriages, servants attending to him, clothes and ornaments, fields and gardens—his property was so vast it could not be measured; no one in the country was wealthier. Despite living in such luxury, he had no faith, and was greedy, stingy, and envious; his house had seven layers, and he instructed the gatekeepers that if anyone came asking for charity, no one was to be allowed into the house.

In the space above the yard, a sparse iron net was installed, fearing that birds would fly in to eat the rice, beans, and sesame. At the base of the fence on all four sides, white clay was used to coat it, fearing that rats would dig burrows and damage the belongings. He had only one child named Chiên Đàn Hương.

When he was about to pass away, he advised his child:

- My illness will surely lead to death. After I die, do not waste the treasures and property carelessly; do not help the Sramanas or Brahmins; if anyone asks, do not give even a single coin. These possessions are enough to provide for seven generations.

After giving the instructions, he passed away and was immediately reborn in the womb of a blind mother, who belonged to the Chandala family in the city of Sravasti. After being born, he was also blind. The blind mother, realizing her child was born blind, felt sorrowful and shed tears of grief, saying a verse:

"The child is blind and the mother is also blind,

Mother and child have no eyes,

Facing this unfortunate circumstance,

My mother's heart is also full of sorrow and suffering."

The blind mother worked hard to raise her children. When her children were 8-9 years old, she handed one of them a stick and a container for food, then said:

- You have to beg for food and survive on your own; there's no need to stay here. I am also blind and cannot protect you.

This blind child went to beg everywhere. Later, when he went to the house of Chiên Đàn Hương to beg, the gatekeeper threw him into a deep pit. The boy broke his left arm, his head was bleeding, and all the food he begged for fell to the ground. Some bystanders who saw this felt pity and went to inform the mother. The blind mother hurriedly leaned on her stick, embraced her child, and lamented:

- What wrongdoing have you committed to encounter this misfortune and suffering?

The child said:

- I went to the gate of Chien Dan Huong's house to ask for food, so I was beaten by wicked people like this.

At that moment, the Buddha, perceiving this, immediately said to Ananda:

- Disaster, truly a disaster! The wealthy Nan Da, upon death, is reborn as the daughter of a blind woman in the household of Chiên Đà La. She was born without eyes. Formerly, she lived in a place of immeasurable riches, with elephants and horses, and treasures that cannot be counted. Today, she encounters such a tragic situation! This is the result of greed and stinginess, and she bears the corresponding karmic consequence. From now on, upon death, she will fall into the Avīci Hell.

Around noon, the Buddha, together with the monks, entered the city. He saw the people surrounding the blind child and went there. Chiên Đàn Hương, upon hearing that the Buddha was outside, came to the gate, paid homage, and then stood aside. For the sake of all people, the Buddha preached about the karma of greed, stinginess, and jealousy, which must result in countless sufferings. He also taught the practice of generosity, bringing immeasurable blessings to people.

At that time, the Blessed One wished to relieve the child and Chiên Đàn Hương from the sufferings of hell, and he said to the child:

- Are you the wealthy man Nanda?

The child answered:

- Yes, I really am Nanda.

Thus, for the third time. The assembly, hearing this, said in surprise:

- Does the wealthy man Nanda have to endure such consequences?

When Chiên Đàn Hương saw this, heartbroken, she shed tears and knelt to pray to the Buddha for help for her father. She also invited the Buddha and the Sangha to come to her house the next day to receive alms offered. The next day, after the Buddha had taken the meal, He immediately taught the marvelous Dharma to Chiên Đàn Hương. At that very moment, Chiên Đàn Hương attained the stage of Stream-entry.

The Buddha said to Ananda:

- If a person hoards wealth, does not clothe themselves properly, and does not give alms, that person is the most foolish of all fools. Therefore, a wise person must practice giving, wishing to be free from birth and death; do not cultivate a miserly and stingy heart, which brings endless suffering.

__________________________________________

THE MISERLY OLDER PERSON LO CHI.

(According to the Lo Chi Elder Scripture)

Long ago, during the time of the Buddha, in the city of Sravasti, there was a wealthy man named Lò Chí. His household was extremely rich, with countless possessions, similar to a sage. This wealth was the result of meritorious deeds and offerings made in the distant past, a form of karmic reward. However, because these offerings were not given with sincere intention, even though he was wealthy, his mindset was always lowly. In clothing, he wore ragged and dirty garments; in eating, he subsisted on rice bran and vegetables to stave off hunger; when thirsty, he drank only plain water; and for travel, he used a dilapidated cart. Though he managed a sizable estate, he was no different from a servant. Therefore, people of the time often mocked him as a fool.

Luo Zhi was extremely wealthy but also very stingy and miserly. His wife, children, and household servants all suffered because of his stinginess. One fine day, Luo Zhi sneaked out with four coins to buy meat and wine. He went to a desolate, deserted graveyard and ate and drank alone. However, Luo Zhi was not accustomed to drinking, so he got drunk almost immediately. In his drunken excitement, he burst into a song saying:

"Today I encounter all kinds of good fortune,

Savoring fine wine, feeling extreme pleasure.

Truly more honest than King Tissa,

"Surpassing even the king of gods, Indra."

At that time, Indra, upon hearing the song, laughed and said:

- The food of this person is worth no more than four coins. Yet he dares to say it is more delightful than mine. I must find a way to disturb him.

Thinking so, he transformed into a form like Lo Chi, came to his house, and then called everyone in the house to say:

- I have treated you all badly until now. That was because a stingy demon had attached itself to me and caused me to act this way. Today, I was fortunate to escape it while out walking. Now, if any of you need anything in this house, please feel free to take and use it.

After saying that, he immediately opened the storage room, distributed everything to everyone, and also said:

- That miserly demon looks exactly like me. In a moment, it will surely come. You all must drive it away. If you let it into the house, it will enter me, causing me to become miserly and stingy again, just like before.

Everyone in the house obediently listened. Suddenly, they saw Lô Chí, sober, returning. The gatekeeper immediately chased him away, not allowing him in. Lô Chí loudly called out to his wife and children. It turned out that even his wife and children held sticks and rushed out to drive him away. Lô Chí was utterly terrified and then went to his close friends to lament and recount everything. Those friends then together brought him back home.

Lo Chi's wife and children saw this and said again:

- No, that's not it, he is the stingy devil, why do you believe him?

The friends looked into the house and saw De Thich impersonating Lo Chi. They thought Lo Chi was indeed still inside the house, and immediately turned to scold Lo Chi:

- You are a stingy devil, how dare you deceive us.

At that time, Lô Chí was speechless, finding it difficult to defend himself, so he managed to borrow a piece of silk from an acquaintance, intending to offer it to the king to recount his grievance. The gatekeeper refused to accept it and would not let him in, so Lô Chí shouted loudly:

- I want to offer my property, I want to offer my property.

The king, upon hearing this, ordered him to be brought in. Lô Chí entered the hall, and just as he was about to present the piece of silk to plead his case, suddenly his arms were tightly pressed against his body, holding the silk so that no matter how hard he tried, he could not spread his hands apart. At that moment, Đế Thích transformed the silk into a bundle of grass. Lô Chí felt extremely embarrassed. The king then laughed heartily and said:

- Alright, alright, you don’t need to present the silk; just go ahead and speak whatever grievances you have quickly.

Lô Chí shed tears, crying and telling the whole story. After hearing it, the king ordered both Lô Chí and their wives and children to come before the palace. When the king saw the two men, from their voices to their appearances, they were exactly alike, so he ordered them to take off their shirts to expose their arms and compare moles to identify them, but they still looked identical, impossible to distinguish. The king then ordered the two men to be taken to separate places and asked each of them to personally write down the most secret and hidden matters of their lives. The result was not only that the content was the same, but even their handwriting was identical.

At that time, the king lamented:

- I am a mere mortal with physical eyes, easily deceived in this matter, unable to distinguish. Now I should go and inquire of Śākya Tathāgata.

Having said that, he mounted his chariot and, along with the two Lô Chí, went to the Jetavana Monastery.

When the Buddha saw them, he immediately went toward the disguised Lô Chí and called out once. Indra instantly revealed his true form as the king of heaven. Seeing Indra, the king immediately knelt and paid homage, then turned to tell Lô Chí to return home.

Lô Chí said:

- Today, when I returned home, all my possessions were gone.

Deva Indra said:

- You performed acts of charity, the wealth in the storehouse has not moved at all.

Lo Chi became angry and said:

- I only trust the words of the Buddha, not the words of Deva Indra.

The Buddha said:

- You should go back home, what Deva Indra said is not wrong.

Lô Chí returned home and indeed found that the property in the warehouse was still intact, with nothing missing. From then on, he gradually changed his character, often performing charitable acts to help others, no longer being as stingy and miserly as before.

_________________________________________

STINGINESS AND MISERLINESS LEAD TO THE HELL OF GHOSTS.

(According to the Book of a Hundred Causes).

The Buddha resided in the Trúc Lâm-Ca Lan Đà monastery in the city of Vaishali. At that time, Maudgalyayana was under a tree and saw a hungry ghost. Its body was like a dry pillar; its belly like Mount Tai; its neck thin as a needle; hair like sharp blades; tightly bound, piercing into its body; fire exuded from all its joints. The hungry ghost wanted to die, its lips and mouth were burned dry. Whenever it went to a river, the water would dry up; whenever it rained, the water falling on the hungry ghost's body would turn into burning fire.

Mục Liên immediately asked about karma, and the hungry ghosts replied: I am burning with thirst and cannot answer; Venerable Sir, please ask the Buddha yourself.

Mục Liên then went to the Buddha. He recounted the previous events in full and asked the Buddha about the karma of the ghosts. The World-Honored One told Mục Liên: Now listen, I will explain clearly for you to understand. In this fortunate age, in the country of Varanasi, a Buddha named Kassapa appeared. A monk was traveling on a distant road, very exhausted from the heat and thirsty. At that time, there was a girl named Akiki, standing by a well drawing water.

The monk went to ask for a drink of water, but the girl refused and said: Even if you are thirsty to death, I will not give it. Because if I give it to you, my water will be depleted. Hearing this, the monk left. That girl was greedy and stingy. Whoever came to ask for something, she firmly refused to give. Later, when she passed away, she fell into the realm of hungry ghosts. Because of this karmic cause, she had to endure such suffering.

The Buddha said to Maudgalyayana:

- That stingy girl is now this hungry ghost.

When the Buddha taught about the cause of this Evil View, the monks all abandoned the karma of greed and stinginess; some attained one of the four fruits of the Śramaṇa; some generated the aspiration for Supreme Bodhi. All of them listened to the Buddha's teachings and joyfully followed in practice.

(Source: Buddhist Experience Studies - Tue Tam 2022).

tieu_de: IMPORTANT THINGS THAT A PERSON WHO PRACTICES VIRTUE SHOULD DO.
tom_tat: In the past, during lectures, I advised those who cultivate merit to do three things: First, reciting scriptures, which will definitely be a good thing, with no side effects, and no harm; second, helping those who are sick or suffering; third, releasing animals.
noi_dung:
IMPORTANT THINGS THAT A MERITORIOUS PERSON SHOULD DO.

Previously, in my lectures, I advised people practicing merit to do three things: Printing scriptures, which will certainly be a good deed, has no side effects, and does no harm; second is helping those who are sick or suffering; third is releasing animals, which is something I strongly advocate. Fasting and releasing animals, I also practice repentance. When I was young, I enjoyed hunting and killing too much, accumulating heavy karmic debts from taking life. After studying Buddhism, I realized this clearly, especially by reading the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, learning about the results of the heavy karma from killing, so after reading this sutra, I immediately dared not eat meat anymore. Not only did I choose to eat vegetarian, but I also devoted all my effort, allthe intention to release animals, practicing the repentance Dharma. These three things are absolutely good deeds, definitely will not have any harmful effects.

If we say that building a temple is not necessarily a good deed; if the temple is completed, and the people residing there, both lay and monastic, the four groups of disciples, all practice in accordance with the proper teachings, truly it is a good retreat center, then the merit of that is immeasurable. If the retreat center is completed, but the four groups of disciples fight every day, compete for fame and gain, then building such a retreat center is creating karmic retribution. You are leading those people to hell, so is there any reason you yourself would not go to hell? Therefore, that matter is not necessarily a blessing, and throughout my life, I would never advocate it. If one encounters a retreat center of true Dharma, the merit of offerings will be boundless. In my life, I have very rarely encountered such a retreat center.

true dharma.

- Excerpt from the Lecture Notes on the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, Dharma Master Venerable Tịnh Không as the main lecturer.

tieu_de: THE SECRET TO COMPLETELY CHANGE YOUR LIFE
tom_tat: The LAW OF CAUSE AND EFFECT is not a strange term for those who practice or study Buddhism. However, in reality, very few people delve deeply to fully understand it.
noi_dung:
SECRETS TO COMPLETELY CHANGE YOUR LIFE

KARMA LAW is not an unfamiliar term for those who practice meditation, or often study Buddhism. But in reality, very few people delve deeply to thoroughly understand Karma, most only stop at a few vague phrases like "you reap what you sow," "good meets good"…

Is that enough to understand? No!

Because if one only stops at such a shallow understanding, one will see many things in life that seem to have no cause and effect at all: seeing people full of guilt or innocence yet wealthy and noble; seeing children just born who have done no wrong yet are abandoned by their parents, die tragically, or suffer from rare diseases and extreme poverty, etc… so many examples. They see this, not understanding the underlying principles, and then lament, "Heaven has no eyes," and ask, "Where is the law of cause and effect? Where is justice?"

The essence of the law of cause and effect is not wrong; the mistake lies in people knowing too little about the law of cause and effect yet already considering themselves sufficiently knowledgeable, unwilling to spend time and effort researching to fully understand it. Although the law of cause and effect is indeed the source of the operation of all things, the decisive factor in all successes and failures, all joys and sorrows of human life, its level of importance is the highest.

Yet, most people are extremely indifferent when it comes to understanding, studying, and contemplating Cause and Effect. On the contrary, they are willing to spend a lot of time watching game shows, trivial programs, entertainment, or wasting time on many other meaningless activities. When the years and months pass by aimlessly, they feel no regret, but when it comes to setting aside a few hours or days to read books about Cause and Effect, they complain, lamenting that they don't have time...

When suffering comes, people blame heaven and fault others, not knowing why they are in pain, not realizing that it is because, all along, they have been “tying the noose around their own necks” without even noticing.

When karma has ripened and suffering surrounds them, they rush to seek out monks, enlightened teachers, and wise people to ask for ways to dissolve it. But not everything can be resolved; many regrettable things have already happened, and by then…it’s too late! The only thing left is to try to endure, as there is no way to save it.

Therefore, if one is an intelligent person, recognizing the level of importance—or rather, the weight—of studying to deeply understand the law of Cause and Effect, and wanting to find a document or a certain source to be able to study, deeply contemplate the specifics of Cause and Effect, in order to build a 'lighthouse of wisdom' for oneself, to guide oneself along the path of light, to arrange one's own destiny through the understanding of Cause and Effect.

If you want so, Quang Tu is very pleased to introduce to you:

First, it is a document, or you could also call it an old story: "42 JUDGMENTS OF KING YAMA" which analyzes in detail the way King Yama judges the karma of sins with dozens of different subjects.

When simultaneously examining the karma of many people throughout their lives in this way, we will gain a comprehensive view of the "picture of karma" with the most detailed level possible. Although lengthy, it is very important and cannot be overlooked when studying karma. Quang Tử will post a part right below here, (but cannot post everything because Facebook articles are limited in characters)

Second, if you truly want to study more deeply, you need many articles and reputable sources for reference. I would like to introduce you to the website: nhanqua.com.vn

The website is organized by categories and subcategories, making it easy to search, such as: Retribution – Merit and Demerit – Reincarnation – Spiritual Manifestation – In-depth, etc., which is very suitable for you to systematically explore karma both in depth and breadth.

And if you are ready, please start studying. The materials are quite long; if you cannot finish reading them in one session, you can save them by sharing to your personal Facebook, or saving somewhere to read gradually.

42 JUDGMENTS OF KING YAMA

Original work: Lam Tu Ki

Edited by: Quang Tu

During the Qing Dynasty, in Huguang Province, China, in Xiaogan County, Le Tho Village, there was a Confucian scholar surnamed Lin, named Tu Ki, who usually ate vegetarian and did not kill living beings, and often recited the Diamond Sutra, but did not fully understand the meaning of the sutra. He had a fair and kind temperament. The villagers all respected Tu Ki.

On the morning of the second day of the third month in the year of Mậu Thìn, during the reign of Emperor Gia Khánh, Lâm Tự Kỳ woke up early to light incense and make offerings. Suddenly, several demons appeared from somewhere, captured Lâm Tự Kỳ's soul, and took it away, then brought it to the local Earth God temple for inspection. The next day, it was taken to the City God temple (which is the deity of the local communal house) for further inspection, and on that same day, it was taken to the West Music King temple, the gathering place for newly deceased souls, where there were about three to four hundred souls. The West Music King reviewed the petitions and then transferred the case to the Chief Judge for adjudication.

On the third meal, when they arrived at Do Thong Ti, Lam Tu Ky saw that all the souls were wearing shackles and had tattered clothes. The demons herded them all into the mansion of the Chief Judge (the judge in charge of examining cases) and issued a tag for each soul to wear around their neck, indicating the crimes they had committed. When it was time to call the name Lang Si Ky from Ly Tho village, Hieu Cam district, he wore a tag with the four characters "Ac pham nguu do" (meaning the criminal who slaughtered an ox), and the demon led Lam Tu Ky's soul into an investigation. The judge saw that a sparkling halo shone above Lam Tu Ky's head.

The judge asked:

– You have been a butcher for so long, how many buffaloes have you killed?

Tu Ky replied:

– Buddha, I have never killed a single buffalo.

– You haven’t killed buffaloes, so why do you wear a tag with the four characters ‘evil offense buffalo diagram’? And you must be from Ly Tho village, right?

– I am from Le Tho village, not Ly Tho village.

– How old are you?

– I am forty-one years old.

– What month, day, and hour were you born?

– Born at the hour of the Dragon, on the third day of the first lunar month.

The examiner checked the records and then said:

– Lâm Tự Kỳ from Lê Thọ village has reached 78 years old, why would anyone want to arrest him! Moreover, although the names in the records sound the same on the name tag, the characters are different, and the village names are homophones but written differently. Besides, their birth dates are also different. You are Lâm Tự Kỳ from Lê Thọ village, while I ordered the arrest of the butcher named Lăng Sỉ Kỳ from Lý Thọ village. He is only 36 years old and makes a living slaughtering hundreds of buffaloes and dogs. There are many other crimes that cannot be fully listed, so he deserves the three punishments, which are execution in three ways: drowning, boiling in oil, and hacking with blades, called water punishment, fire punishment, and blade punishment. As for you, you have a halo above your head, probably because you often do good deeds, right?chanting sutras and verses.

– In my life, I have not done much good, but I dare not do evil. Since I turned seventeen, I have been vegetarian; until now it has been more than twenty years. On ordinary days, no matter how urgent the work is, I still make sure to complete the recitation of a Diamond Sutra chapter and chant the name of Amitabha Buddha a few hundred times before starting any work.

– In that case, he is a good person, and the demon certainly committed a sin by mistakenly taking an ordinary person, let alone a good one! Moreover, the local Earth God and the examining deities also made mistakes, so they are at fault as well. This matter is serious and not trivial at all! Therefore, good person, please sit under the west roof and wait for me to report to the king, then you will be returned to the living world (meaning your soul will be restored to life).

Then two boy attendants wearing blue robes led Tự Kỳ's soul to the guest house under the west roof. Seeing the plaque inscribed with four characters "Western Hall of Records" and also a couplet hung on the main columns like this:

‘A true man, hands unwilling to open the path of life and death.

Extraordinary man, eyebrows destined to break through fame and officialdom’

At that time, Tự Kỳ entered the guest house and saw three people; one woman, two men, all dressed in the style of Taoist practitioners, holding a string of prayer beads in their hands, and all stood up, clasped their hands, and invited him to sit. The attendant boy said:

– Good sir, please wait a moment, when the king arrives he will invite you.

After a while, three drum beats were heard signaling the opening of the temple gate to announce that King Yan had arrived (King Yan has ten officials; this one is King Qin Guang – in charge of the first hall). A courtier came to invite Tu Ky to the temple gate, and saw a horizontal board hanging above the gate, inscribed with eleven characters:

‘Kinh Chau deng xu sanh hon thien ac du thong ti’.

(The Sở official in charge of handling the good and evil souls of Kinh Chau.)

On both sides of the gate were couplets that read:

‘Yin and yang originally have no different principle. Cause and effect clearly have evident manifestations.’

At that time, all the souls knelt under the steps. The judge collected the documents and reported clearly about the mistaken capture, etc. King Tan Quang looked at them and said:

– This person is indeed gentle, also practices vegetarianism and recites scriptures, moreover, it is not yet his time, so it is appropriate to restore his soul. As for the 4 Yaksha demons who captured by mistake, each is to be punished with eighty lashes, then imprisoned for further investigation. The fault of the Earth Deity of the village was only in capturing incorrectly, I will also submit a report to the Jade Emperor to punish him.

Then he asked Tu Ky:

– Which scripture have you been reciting all this time?

– At night, I recite the Diamond Sutra.

– Very good! But how many volumes have you chanted?

– I don't remember, but I have been vegetarian for over twenty years, and have only been chanting scriptures for seven years.

The king ordered the Official to check how many volumes had been chanted. The Official opened the counting book and counted 3,503 volumes.

The king said:

– You still have quite a lot to go; roughly, you have chanted one tripitaka (one tripitaka is 5,848 volumes) more than needed. Do you understand the meaning in the scriptures?

– I cannot fully understand it.

– Reciting sutras has immeasurable merits. However, if one recites without understanding, the merit is only three parts out of ten.

– Can hiring someone to recite sutras on your behalf bring you blessings?

– Hiring someone to chant can give one part of the seven merits. But it is still better than not chanting at all. Previously, when you chanted the Diamond Sutra, it was not standard. While chanting, your mind was not pure, often wandering, not focused. That was just chanting with the mouth, with only two or three parts of the merit out of ten. From now on, you must strive to understand the meaning clearly, chanting with the mouth and contemplating with the heart. Whenever you meet someone, explain the subtle teachings of the Diamond Sutra, then pray for rebirth in the Pure Land, only then can you hope to reach the Western Paradise.

At that time, the Judge reported:

– This person has been gone from the world for several days, the heart must be cold, probably already in the coffin at home, it would be difficult to revive. If the Jade Emperor finds out, it certainly would not be convenient. I beg the prince to immediately restore the soul.

The king said:

– It's nothing! On the 2nd, 12th, 22nd, the 5th, 15th, 25th, and the 8th, 18th, 28th days, these are the days for judging the guilty spirits here. Today is the 8th day, which is the time for the trial. I see that people do not believe in cause and effect, easily disregard the words of sages, and criticize the Three Jewels (Buddha, Dharma, Sangha) for many sins. Today I will keep the virtuous one for a day to see how I handle it, and then when they return to life, they will tell people about it. Quickly give the virtuous one a sip of Noãn Tâm medicine, so that their heart will be warm for seven days. Generally, any spirit that comes to this first gate and takes more than seven days to be released through the nine kings of the Ten Courts, will not be able to return to life.

Tự Kỳ reported:

– Your Majesty, why is there a guest house in the west called: Western Room of Restraint? Can ordinary people go there?

– They cannot go. For ordinary people who die, their souls are brought to the King of Western Yue for examination, and only after approval are they sent here. I review carefully to determine if they are immediately eligible for reincarnation and if so, I note it on the record, then send it to the King of Eastern Yue for confirmation before issuing a paper that allows them to be reincarnated. Only then can the soul reincarnate. As for those who are purely virtuous and not evil, or those who practice vegetarianism, recite scriptures, and truly cultivate, I do not have the authority to judge, so they are allowed to stay temporarily in the western hall, waiting for me to issue orders to the Golden Child and Jade Maiden, bring the treasured items, and escort the soul to the Heavenly Realm.

– What is called Heaven?

– Heaven is bright, vast, and just. If someone’s heart is bright, their behavior is generous and upright, then their soul goes to Heaven.

– And what about Hell?

– Hell is low, dirty, and dark. If someone’s heart is cowardly, filthy, wicked, and ignorant, then their soul falls into Hell.

– Do the souls that go to Heaven or fall into Hell reincarnate again?

– Having ascended to heaven or fallen into hell, it takes a long time to be reborn. Although it is long, when the merit is exhausted or the sin is at an end, one still reincarnates, except for those who have attained the Saintly fruit of Liberation such as Arahants or the Buddha, who then end the cycle of reincarnation.

– So, who will be reborn immediately?

– Among a thousand people, maybe one or two go to Heaven, a few hundred go to Hell. The rest are all reincarnated. Because only those who do many good deeds and commit few evil acts during their lifetime will go to Heaven. Those who do many evil deeds and rarely do good will be imprisoned in Hell. Those who are neither good nor evil, or are half and half, must be reincarnated.

– Or someone who was good at first but later did evil, or someone who was evil at first but later did good, some with many evil deeds and few good deeds, others with few evil deeds and many good deeds, what will the King decide?

– Doing good first and then doing evil will halve the merit of the good deeds, and then account for the evil deeds. Doing evil first and then repenting and doing good will halve the guilt of the evil deeds, while the merit of the good deeds is counted. If there is much evil and little good, or much good and little evil, they cancel each other out, and whatever remains is what one receives. Why is that so? Because a person who does good but does not complete their life without turning to evil is not allowed by the heaven, so half of the merit of the good deeds is reduced. On the other hand, someone who repents, corrects mistakes, and changes from wrong to right is greatly favored by the Jade Emperor, so half of the evil deeds are reduced.

– I often see good people being poor. Meanwhile, evil people become rich. The retribution of heaven is not clear, so one cannot fully understand it! – When a good person faces misfortune, perhaps it is because outwardly they appear good but their heart is not truly good. When an evil person is blessed, perhaps it is because outwardly they seem evil but inwardly they are not evil. God values the sincerity in the heart, not the outer appearance. One can deceive people with appearances, but how can one deceive heaven? Throughout history, karmic retribution is certainly accurate. However, the workings of cause and effect have many forms. Sometimes the good or evil of a previous life is only repaid in this life. The good or evil of this life may only be repaid in the next life.

Or each life reaps according to that life; sometimes evil is done, and the retribution comes immediately before one's eyes. As for the saying ‘Evil receives blessings, good meets misfortune,’ it is because doing evil in this life is little, yet one enjoys blessings from past lives, or doing good in this life is little, yet one receives retribution from previous lives. Reincarnation conceals it, making it hard for people to understand fully.

Because of the merit and sin from their past lives, good deeds allow one to enjoy blessings, evil deeds cause one to encounter misfortune, and exhaust the karma of past lives. Then we examine the true good and evil of this life, whether much or little, large or small, to settle any unmet debts—either repaid in this life, or carried over to the next life, or repaid through their descendants.

Retribution according to the law of cause and effect, whether early or late, whether discreet or obvious, is certainly never wrong even by the slightest bit. The mysterious and complex principle of karma, how can humans fully understand it?

– Your Highness, why is it said that in this life, one must suffer the consequences of actions from a previous life?

– Like children who die by drowning, fire, being stabbed or cut, sickness or disability, or being eaten by tigers, bitten by snakes, trampled by horses, run over by carts, gored by buffaloes, or other risky incidents, in this life they had not done any evil, yet they face consequences; that is because of the karma from a previous life. Similarly, students just in their twenties who pass exams, or descendants who attain positions, or enjoy the blessings of their ancestors, or encounter fortunate events, even though in this life they have not done good deeds to receive merit, they enjoy blessings due to the good deeds in previous lives. Observing this, one understands that experiencing misfortune despite being good, or receiving blessings despite being evil, occurs for this reason.

– If good people are caught to reincarnate, then good people would really be at a disadvantage! And if evil people also get to reincarnate, then aren't the evil people very lucky? Why doesn't the law of heaven distinguish between them?

– That's not the case! Giving the virtuous a rebirth to enjoy wealth and glory is Heaven on earth, so how can it be called suffering? And giving the wicked a rebirth to endure hardship, humiliation, and misfortune, just like hell on earth, how can it be called very lucky? Moreover, when the good enjoy favorable circumstances, if they practice virtue and accumulate merit, they will ascend to Heaven. But if they enjoy wealth and still commit too many evils, after all merit is exhausted, any remaining sins must still be punished as usual.

If an evil person faces adverse circumstances but knows to repent for past mistakes and strives to atone, they will also end their suffering; otherwise, without cultivation, they descend into the hells, countless and terrible.

From this, one can see that although misfortune and blessing are determined by heaven, a person's good or evil heart can change; luck and misfortune may be assigned at birth, but those who do good or evil can have their destiny rearranged.

– So heaven and hell, salvation or damnation depend on the mind that one freely controls. If I am someone who does not control my mind, that is: that heaven has a path I do not walk; that hell has no door yet I seek it!

– Yes, it seems you are someone who will ascend to heaven, so your mind should awaken soon like this.

After finishing the conversation, the judge reported:

– The offending souls have gathered fully and are waiting to be examined.

King Qin Guang Wang saw the comment from the King of Western Yue that: “Tu Huc and the 752 souls are in reincarnation.”

The king also approved for them to be transferred through the King of Eastern Yue to receive the sheets of rebirth and enjoy blessings. Zi Qi reviewed the king's virtuous endorsement declaring that the three souls were born into the Heavenly Realm, as follows:

1) A virtuous woman named Lieu Thi, extremely filial to her mother-in-law, cared for her sick children with great hardship, was generous in almsgiving, fed prisoners, contributed money to repair bridges and build roads, carried out many good deeds, never spoke a word that damaged virtue, and never did any cruel act. She also observed the ten-day vegetarian fast for ten years and often chanted the Universal Gate Sutra.

2) A good person is Dương Thăng, who is filial to his parents, loves his siblings, respects elders, lives kindly and generously, and often shows compassion to others. He does not cheat a single coin, nor is he greedy for silver and money. He rescues people in dire situations and helps those in urgent need. Hundreds of people have benefited from his assistance, and dozens of families have been saved by his hand. His acts of giving are greatly meritorious.

3) A virtuous gentleman was Truong Quan Dien from Vo Lang district; although his family was poor, he fulfilled his duties, enduring hardships with steadfast heart. He wrote several hundred books, all discussing moral advice for life. He taught his students to uphold humanity and righteousness first, to make friends with integrity, and to value reputation as a foundation. Although he did not practice vegetarianism, his heart was as pure as if he did. Although he did not chant sutras, his words were as wise as verses from scriptures, with a pure mind and speech free from malice.

All three of them deserved to be born in Heaven, gaining higher reincarnated forms.

The king, after reading the remarks of the king of Tay Nhac, proclaimed:

– Quickly invite the Golden Boy and Jade Girl to carry the treasured banner down and escort the three souls up to the Heavenly Realm (the Golden Boy escorts the male soul, the Jade Girl escorts the female soul), while here, drums must be beaten, music played, incense lit, and flowers scattered to send off these three. As for the souls who have committed crimes, they should be taken, according to the sequence on the tally, to the Emperor for judgment.

The judge reported:

– The first criminal is of the Du family, from Huynh Chau district, who passed the junior bachelor’s exam and later the higher exams to become a bachelor, and twice passed the doctoral exams. He was appointed as the magistrate of Tu Thuy district under the Qing dynasty, then promoted to the position of Director of the Ministry of Justice, later became Lang Trung of the Ministry of Public Works; then he served as Deputy Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, and finally moved to the Ministry of Personnel where he died after five months. Investigating this criminal, from the day he passed the junior bachelor’s exam to when he became a district official, he did not do a single good deed. When he worked in the Ministry of Justice, he wrongfully killed 13 people. While serving in the Ministry of Public Works, he accepted many bribes. At the Ministry of Revenue, he also took a lot of silver in bribes. Later, when promoted to the Ministry of Personnel, he became even more audacious, selling official positions for profit, filling his own pockets, without the slightest concern for anyone.Cry, someone laughs. This sin deserves to be tormented in the hell of Avīci, for millions of years without being reborn.

Du stood up, bowed, and reported:

– I have held high office, Your Majesty, please grant me some face.

The king rebuked and said:

– Damn you! In the human world, people value high positions, but in the Underworld, virtue is honored, not petty ranks. A person of great virtue, even if a beggar, I would respect. And now you still rely on your official status to oppose me? Where is the Night Devil? Take the iron mace and strike this one to death.

– I have observed ten vegetarian fasts and chanted the Zhuan De sutra.

– You observe the ten-day vegetarian practice and recite the Chuan Di mantra, yet you seek lasting fame and success. You have not yet understood the meaning of the two words 'Chuan Di.' Generally, those who wish to seek wealth, fame, children, or longevity must refrain from ten evils: disrespecting heaven and earth, disrespecting the Three Jewels, being unfilial to parents, not harmonious with siblings, being disloyal to the ruler, not believing in justice, neglecting rites and propriety, not acting according to righteousness, lacking integrity and purity, and having no sense of shame. After refraining from these ten evils, one must also follow the rules of Gong Practice, reciting scriptures daily to remember and correct the heart, not daring to miss a single meal, and not daring to think of anything against righteousness. Only then can one observe the ten-day vegetarian practice,Reciting the Chuantide mantra moves the heart of heaven.

As for you, for so long committing many evil deeds, yet relying on the fame of Chuẩn Đề and hoping to receive blessings, it is like chasing the branches while neglecting the roots—what effect does it have? On the day of the ten-day fast, you accidentally forget to eat vegetarian, planning to make it up on another day, or if forced into a banquet by others, you abandon the fasting day to eat meat. According to the rules of fasting, can missing a day be compensated by eating differently on another day? You must not abandon the fasting day to eat meat. If you do so, it is not sincere, what use is it then? Fasting on the ten-day period like you do, what merit is there? Do not argue unnecessarily! Quickly lead him to the Avici Hell.

– – – – – – –

The judge reads the verdict:

– Next, the second case is of the surname Tần, in Hướng Dương district, who passed the doctoral examination as a bachelor, became an official as the prefect of Thái Nguyên, and died after three years. This sinful soul despised heaven and earth, disregarded human life, held office for three years, accepted bribes totaling over one hundred thousand taels, and neglected state affairs. In this life, you have passed the examination and become an official because in your previous life you were a temple monk who had the merit of clearing mountain paths and building embankments of several hundred trượng (several thousand meters of wood). Who could have known that in this life you would change your heart and mind like this!

The Tần family reports:

– When I was alive, I was foolish and never imagined that the Underworld would punish me in such a way. Now I have repented and awakened. In my house, there are still a few tens of thousands of silver taels. Seeing that Your temple is dilapidated, and beneath it are many hungry and miserable souls, I am willing to donate all my silver to repair the king's temple, and whatever remains can be given to the hungry souls to atone for sins. I wonder what Your Majesty intends?

King Tần Quảng replied:

The adjudicating officer read the sentence as planned:

– The Tôn family from Võ Xương district, at 19 changed their surname to Trương and joined the military service at the government office. The Tôn family reported:

– I used fifty taels of silver to gild the Buddha statue at Bao An Pagoda. I also offered money for oil to light the lamps, and I practiced vegetarian meals, reciting the name of Amitabha Buddha one thousand times.

King Tan Quang said:

– You wretched name! If you do evil, why don’t you repent, abandon your faults, and perform good deeds to honor Buddha, then I would forgive your sins. The magistrate read the next judgment:

– Ngô family, from Huỳnh Cang district, when young, went to school, failed the secondary examination, then learned the profession of writing petitions for hire.

The king said:

– From ancient times, those who specialize in writing petitions and lawsuits have never been virtuous.

Ngô family reported:

– I am merely a scribe helping the ignorant who do not know how to write petitions, not doing anything evil.

– The one who gives alms, the merit does not come from the alms but from the heart; the one who kills, the sin is not in the sword but in the intention. When you write a complaint, in your mind you intend to accuse harshly, like a thousand flames burning fiercely and hard to extinguish. Ink is more poisonous than a pond of blood, a pen sharper than a sword. Writing one word can easily destroy someone's house and home. Changing a stroke can kill a person like playing. Under the poisonous fire, all the implements of execution; on the petition, all the gates of prison and punishment. Write over and over to make it truly good, accuse first and then accuse later to make it really severe! The guilty are not caught quickly, the innocent are deliberately framed for sure. The judge read the verdict:

– The Trần family in Kỵ Thuỷ district committed theft.

– When I was young, I lacked food and clothing. My parents and younger siblings were constantly hungry. Moreover, there were years of poor harvests, rice was expensive, taxes were heavy; I had no choice but to steal!

The king looked at the judge and said:

– This person, although a thief, what he says is also reasonable. Check the records carefully to see what else he has done.

The judge checked the records and reported:

– The Tran family stole goods from a merchant while passing through Mai Lanh Mountain in Ki Thuy district. The Tran family then wrote a poem as follows:

“First interrogation, then torture,”

Your mind is more malicious than mine.

Your hand hooks the liver, then pierces the blood,

Prefect Tu read the poem, then spoke to the clerks:

The dental apprentices all admitted, "We have gotten used to doing evil, and we also have families to support; it is really hard to repent and correct our mistakes!" After saying this, he recited a poem as follows:

“The mirror of karmic retribution urges the hearts of evildoers,

The temple bell teaches people to do good?

Swords and knives are inherently harmless; it is the heart that is wicked,

In the past, lost in the five desires, indulging without measure,
