At that time in the palace gate: many people repented and resigned to become monks, more than ten of them.

King Tan Quang said:

– Indeed, that is a virtuous act, enough to atone for the crime of theft. Not to mention stealing, without harming anyone's life, deserves to have half the crime reduced. What is detestable is the crime of adultery, because indulgence leads to vice. As for thieves, it must be examined, as poverty and hunger may drive one to take risks. Extreme circumstances can transform one's actions, and the crime may be pardoned. Forgive them, give paper to pass to King Dong Nhac to take the first step in reincarnation as a traveling monk at Thien Thai Mountain. If they endure ascetic practice, they will eventually attain salvation.

– – – – – – –

The magistrate reads the sentence:

– The Tran family in Vien Duong district, since childhood, lived a reckless and lazy life, causing their parents to suffer from cold, hunger, and hardships, worry leading to illness and death, because the children did not save money to support them. And he died at the age of 49 from hunger.

King Tan Quang commented:

– Although he does not do anything very evil, he is lazy and spends extravagantly. Those who steal and rob do not do it because they want to kill people or burn houses to commit evil; it is merely because of laziness and wastefulness, and extreme hardship gives rise to such a profession. Therefore, diligence and frugality are truly the roots of establishing a household, and also the foundation for cultivating oneself and correcting one's character. A gentleman, everyone needs to be thrifty. Because you are neither diligent nor frugal, you let your parents starve and suffer from the cold until death.

Thus, while wastefulness is a minor fault, the sin of not supporting one's parents is an unforgivable act of filial impiety. He is to be brought to the execution ground, his belly to be cut open, his stomach shaken, and his intestines pulled out as punishment for squandering. All the lazy tendons are to be drawn out as punishment for idleness. Now his father has reincarnated as a clerk in Thường Châu district, living behind Tây Môn, and he is to be reincarnated as a pig in his father's household, to be sold for money to atone for the filial impiety of his previous life.

– – – – – – –

The judge read the sentence as follows:

– The Khuong family in Hung Province were wealthy but ruthless; at fifty-one years old, he was killed by a poor man named Ho. The Khuong family was richer than the entire province combined, with large rice storehouses selling to merchants from everywhere. One year, when many in the region starved due to crop failure, the Khuong family did not donate even a handful of rice to the poor. At that time, the local magistrate and district officials summoned him and told him to give alms to the starving people, but he focused on bribing them to avoid giving anything. As a result, even relatives suffering from famine died of starvation, and he showed no concern!

King Tang Quang said:

– You have always valued money, never lending to anyone to prevent them from starving. Your heart is extremely cruel, more vicious than the sin of murder, and can never be forgiven.

– Only now do I realize that I have sinned against the laws of heaven. I beg Your Highness to pardon me, and I will reform my ways, giving away all my wealth, money, and grain to the poor. I ask the king to be merciful and hear my plea.

– Do you still hope to live? The granaries in your house still belong to you? Your children are all enemies reincarnated to claim debt; in less than a year they will destroy all your wealth, leaving nothing behind!

Khuong heard clearly, crying bitterly and lamenting:

– All this time I have been painstakingly saving every penny for the long term. Only out of necessity did I spend a few coins to buy firewood or vegetables, and even then I felt very reluctant. – The sin of stinginess is like that of deceitfulness – King Tần Quản Phán said – First, he will be made a hungry ghost, starved for a long time. Later, he will be allowed to reincarnate as a beggar, suffering hunger and rags to atone for his sins until he squeezes water from a mortar.

—————

The verdict officer read the case judgment:

– The Doan family in Quy Duc district practiced as quack doctors, giving random medications that caused the deaths of eleven people, both men and women. —————

Decreed, the official read out the judgment as planned:

– The Li family in Thần Châu district specialized in matchmaking. —————-

The judge reads the next verdict:

—————

The judge read the verdict:

– The Uông family in Than Âm district: the father is devout and practices vegetarianism, but his son does not listen to his father's teachings. The king looked at the judge and proclaimed:

– This name goes against the benevolence of God, because Heaven wants all creatures to be born in abundance, not to be killed.

The judge reported:

– The prince usually values filial piety; this name, when his mother was ill, he devoted himself to her care and treatment wholeheartedly. When she was paralyzed, he sliced the calf meat to cook porridge for her to help nourish and sustain her, so this should be considered to mitigate his crime.

– Unfilial to his father, but devoted to his mother, well then I should also be generous and mitigate. Consider a crime of gambling, causing him to be reborn as a violent child, at twenty years old to be executed by the authorities, and then we will continue to reckon further down.

—————–

The judge read the verdict:

– The Tran family in Han Tranz is very deceitful and scheming, not concerned with honest work or making a living. Every day they entice the children of good families to gamble in order to make money, and they also cheat at chess and board games, to the extent that many people become bankrupt, yet their evil habits persist. King of Hell decreed:

– The gambling profession harms people more than fire and thieves. If one loses too much, they may have to abandon their occupation, forsake the right path, and men and women may become immoral, leading to ruinous families, financial ruin, and risking their own lives. You have no shortage of senses, hands, or feet; why not learn an honest profession to make a living day by day? First, be righteous and law-abiding, and later be a good person, avoiding bringing disgrace to your ancestors. How could you think of using your senses to do wrong, scheming to deceive people?

The useful body, yet used to commit immense sin. It's no different from: 'eating someone to fill your stomach, destroying someone's house for pleasure.' Therefore, one must reap the consequences. Even though the person has been punished with extinction of lineage, for the crime of plotting to take girls as servants. As for the crime of gambling, it cannot be pardoned. Demon! Cut off ten fingers, and both hands, then open the belly to remove the heart and intestines. Afterwards, imprison in Hell, not even considering reincarnation.

The Tran family reported:

– I am slow-witted and cannot succeed in studying; practicing gambling to earn money is easier. Once in that trade, one becomes deceitful and cunning. But when winning, one takes, and when losing, one pays, both sides are equally willing. I do not snatch from others, I beg Lord Wang to forgive me.

– Luring honest people, cheating and deceiving, even with brothers you are determined to skin them, let alone with friends. Making people lose money and property is when you are satisfied. Who would foolishly volunteer to give you their possessions? It is because you devise schemes and set traps, speaking sweet words on the outside, pretending to be deeply affectionate, offering food, offering drinks, or using female charms to intoxicate. The judge reads the case plan:

– The Ly family from Hoanh Duong district went to serve in the militia army. The Du family from Huynh Mai district also enlisted, specifically carrying flags and beating drums. The Thanh family, also from Huynh Mai district, served as artillery soldiers under Inspector Ly Tu Giang. All three of them had participated in battles.

King Yama decreed:

– Soldiers in the battlefield, wielding swords and knives with aggressive hearts, when victorious, would abduct and violate others’ wives and children, even go so far as to eat human flesh. Such crimes are heinous and deserve to be thrown into the Prison of Blade Mountain for their due fate.

– Specifically, the Thanh family, when they captured Yangzhou - the official reported – they caught three people but did not kill them. They caught two women but did not harm them, and both were returned to their husbands. The two husbands offered money in gratitude, but he also refused to accept it. – Having such merits, I am also worthy of respect and praise, so I grant them a rank through the King of Dong Nhac, to be reincarnated as a seventh-rank civil official, living seventy-nine years, passing away without illness, and their descendants for two generations will all attain fame and honor. As for the other two spirits, they are to be judged according to the previous sentence.

————–

The judge read the judgment as follows:

– Lady Tien Mau Nuong from Gia Ngu district, known for being intensely jealous and rebellious toward her parents-in-law.

King Yan spoke:

– Even a single act of filial impiety towards one’s in-laws deserves imprisonment in the Avici Hell.

Mẫu Nương reported:

– While alive, I often practiced vegetarianism and gave alms.

– Even with such vegetarianism and almsgiving, it cannot atone for the sin of being unfilial to one’s in-laws. However, since you practiced vegetarianism and gave alms, we will forgive the sin of pounding and grinding, but still send you to the Hell to serve as an example for disobedient daughters-in-law.

Venerable Tuyên Hóa Explains About Fetal Deformities

HUSBAND AND WIFE ULTRASOUND REVEALS FETAL ABNORMALITIES, SHOULD THEY KEEP THE PREGNANCY?

* QUESTION: If an ultrasound detects that the fetus has congenital defects, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, developmental delays… is it possible to have an abortion?

- Abortion is considered the crime of murder (taking a human life). If a miscarriage happens by chance, or if the fetus dies naturally, that is fine. Deliberately having an abortion, regardless of any reason, is still a violation against life and creates bad karma.

Abortion will put parents in a tragic situation, unintentionally turning them into people who repay kindness with resentment. If the soul that comes to be conceived in this life was once a benefactor of the parents in a past life, not knowing this, the parents may use every means to harm the child to death, causing the aborted soul to die unwillingly. A former kindness then turns into resentment, creating a vicious karmic bond between both parties.

* QUESTION: But if the parents have to raise that child with a congenital disability, must they endure hardship for their whole life?

----> Of course it is very difficult. But everything has a cause due to karmic retribution. When a child with a disability is born, it is because they have a connection with their Parents.

“Husband and wife also belong to past connections: good connections and bad connections (if there is no connection, they would not meet). As for children, they are also the debts from previous lives (coming to collect a debt or repay a debt), debts of gratitude, or debts of material wealth – if there were no debt, they would not come – when a child comes to be born, three connections must be fulfilled for it to succeed: the connection with the Father, the connection with the Mother, and the connection of the child. The child and the Parents share the same karmic causes and combined karma, so they come together.

When we are born as human beings, the eighth consciousness comes first. At death, the eighth consciousness departs last. As soon as the spirit leaves, the body becomes cold; if the spirit has not left, the body remains warm. The spirit always arrives first and departs last. After a person dies until the time of rebirth (waiting to take a new body), this stage of the spirit is called the “Intermediate Body,” also known as the “Body During Existence.” At this time, the Intermediate Body sees everything as completely dark; in fact, it sees nothing. However, if there is a connection with any Father or Mother, this is called the corresponding karmic attraction. Then, at that time, even if separated by the farthest ends of the earth,It is extremely far away, but whenever the Parents are close, the Intermediate Body will immediately see the light emitted from the Parents, and it rushes to enter the womb! This is clearly explained in the Lankavatara Sutra.

After the mother conceives, the first week of the embryo is a 'smooth mass, opaque like condensed milk.' Only in the second week does the embryo take shape and gradually develop.

In the 'Twelve Links of Dependent Origination', it clearly states that ignorance conditions formations - ignorance refers to the arising of affection and love between the man and woman, leading to intimate relations between the two genders. 'Formations condition consciousness', and at that very moment, the consciousness (Bardo body) is drawn to the fetus, becoming a life.

It must be understood that the bond between children and their parents is very strong and deep. Therefore, even if a child is sick or has a disability, it is all shared karma, and the parents are obliged to accept it. If the parents are determined to reject it, they may avoid it in this life, but in the next life, they will still have to pay the consequences, and the negative results they have to bear will be much heavier.

In the past, there were no ultrasound machines, no methods of contraception or abortion. People were also honest and simple; if they became pregnant, they would give birth. Now, with ultrasound machines, when a pregnancy is detected to have mental retardation or deformities, people immediately terminate it, thinking that this will avoid future troubles. But little do they know that the suffering they will have to endure later will be far more tragic.

To be honest, usually the conditions that cause a child to have a disability are not good karma, but rather the retribution that the parents must endure; they have the responsibility to bear this communal karma. If the parents do not show compassion to the fetus, insisting on avoiding the consequences of karma by destroying the child, then this action only increases the evil karma. And this karmic relationship, in the next life, will expand even more terribly.

In the "Lăng Nghiêm Sutra," twelve types of rebirth are described, including a type of being called "Non-Thinking." This type is not without thoughts, but their thoughts are very unusual. It is like an owl that, after being born, will eat its mother, using its mother's flesh and blood to nourish itself. Science has also discovered a species of dung beetle that specializes in eating its own mother. Why does it eat its mother? Because, in the past, they had a very deep enmity.

tieu_de: HOW TO STUDY CHÚ LĂNG NGHIÊM!
tom_tat: EVERYONE CAN MEMORIZE THE LANG NHIEM CHANT. The Lang Nhiem Chant is very powerful; as long as we (laypeople or monastics) recite it every day, the merits are truly immeasurable, helping our practice
noi_dung:
HOW TO STUDY THE CHU LANG NGHIEM!

EVERYONE CAN MEMORIZE THE LANKAVATARASŪTRA CHANT

The Lankavatara Sutra chant is very powerful; as long as we (laypeople or monastics) recite it daily, the merit is truly immeasurable, helping practitioners develop wisdom, overcome all obstacles and challenges on the path of practice, while also helping to preserve the Dharma in the world for a long time, benefiting sentient beings.

It is important to practice regularly every day, at any time, anywhere, reciting aloud or silently, the merit is beyond measure. Because the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is of great concentration, also the king among all concentrations. The concentration power of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra subdues all evil and foreign paths; as long as it is recited, the deities, Dharma protectors, and good spirits all respectfully protect the practitioner. The Buddhas of the past, present, and future also rely on the great concentration of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra to achieve accomplishment. In general, a practitioner cannot be without the great concentration of Lăng Nghiêm, because on the path of practice, one encounters many obstacles and challenges, and without the blessings of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Dharma protectorsIf one relies on benevolent spirits, it is very difficult to achieve spiritual practice.

Venerable Lang Nghiem is essential provisions and spiritual sustenance for those practicing Buddhism. As long as we strive to recite daily, the merits are not small, and it also contributes to protecting the Dharma to endure long in the world, benefiting all sentient beings.

Everyone knows that the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is powerful in conquering obstacles, but when people talk about the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, they all say: “The Lăng Nghiêm mantra is very long, very difficult to recite, and even harder to memorize.” As a result, very few people recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and even fewer memorize it. In fact, everyone has the ability, they just don’t recognize it! This is similar to the children in the Lotus Sutra, who have a jewel in their clothing but do not realize it.

Why is it said that everyone can easily memorize The Śūraṅgama Mantra's teachings? Because the memorization method is very simple: just recite one verse and then continue to the next, and naturally you will remember them. There is no need to force yourself to memorize, because forcing memorization is quite exhausting, the effectiveness may not be good, and it is very easy to give up halfway.

Perhaps some people will say: My memory is very poor, I can't memorize it! Memorizing the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is not like doing math, because numbers are beyond help for someone a little less intelligent, but memorizing the Lăng Nghiêm mantra can truly be overcome by the method of "diligence to make up for intelligence." Therefore, everyone must absolutely believe in their ability to memorize the Lăng Nghiêm mantra!

Perhaps some people will say: I don't have time! In fact, in daily life, there is a lot of time that can be utilized: You can recite while walking on the street, you can recite on the bus, you can recite at red lights while riding a motorcycle, you can recite in the elevator, and whenever you have free moments, you can recite. I believe there is no one who is so busy that they have no time at all!

In addition, there are other techniques that can be easily memorized: Breaking it into small sections for learning can help make memorization easier. Practitioners who recite, reciting the entire text once a day, can at other times break it into sections for memorization. Remember, it is “memorizing through recitation,” not “memorizing by heart”; you just need to recite a lot, and naturally it will be memorized. Never put pressure on yourself, requiring yourself to forcefully memorize, or pretending that every day you must memorize a certain number of verses, because that will cause distress.

Memorizing the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra can be said to be an “extremely difficult and rare” task, because the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is “hard to encounter even in hundreds of thousands of lifetimes.” But from another perspective, memorizing the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is also a very simple task, because anyone who genuinely wishes to memorize it can do so. By using a joyful and relaxed mind, and reciting it with sincere respect, success is guaranteed!

A simple conclusion: how can one memorize the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra?

1_ Believe that you will definitely be able to memorize the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra.

2_ Recite naturally, without the need to forcefully memorize.

3_ Recite with a joyful and respectful mind.

4_ Make use of all free moments, skillfully use time, and recite regularly, and success will surely come.

Finally, I wish everyone the blessing to be able to joyfully and freely memorize the Lăng Nghiêm mantra!

tieu_de: WHAT DOES TAKING REFUGE IN Kṣitigarbha BODHISATTVA TRULY MEAN?
tom_tat: In the Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows, Chapter Four, the World-Honored One spoke about taking refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva as follows: 'In future lives, if there are men or women who do not do good but do evil, even those who do not ti'
noi_dung:
WHAT IS THE TRUE MEANING OF TAKING REFUGE IN KSHITIGARBHA BODHISATTVA?

In the Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows, Chapter Four, the World-Honored One speaks about taking refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva as follows:

“In the future life, if there are men or women who do not perform good deeds but commit evil, including those who do not believe in cause and effect, those who practice sexual misconduct or false speech, those who speak maliciously with a double tongue, or those who slander the Great Vehicle; beings with such karma are certain to fall into the evil paths.

If one encounters virtuous and knowledgeable teachers who advise in such a way that one immediately takes refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva at the slightest thought, those beings will instantly be freed from the suffering retribution of the Three Evil Paths.

If one can sincerely take refuge, show reverence, and admire through prostrations, offering incense, flowers, clothing, various treasures, or food and drink, then in the hundreds of thousands of billions of lifetimes to come, one will often reside in the heavenly realms and enjoy supreme and wondrous happiness. When heavenly merit is exhausted and one must be born into the human world, one will still experience hundreds of thousands of lifetimes as a sovereign, while remembering past lives and the roots of karmic causes and effects.”

So what does genuinely taking refuge mean here (According to the teachings of Venerable Thích Tịnh Không)?

“The two words 'Taking Refuge' are extremely important; it is not merely taking refuge in form. Taking refuge in form has no benefit; it is only a form, but without sincerity, what use is it! Why does it have the form but not the sincere intention, why cannot one develop the mind? Because one does not thoroughly understand the Truth and Principle. Naturally, this is a matter for virtuous friends; mere knowledge is not enough, it must be virtuous friends who explain clearly and thoroughly about the forms, merits, and true benefits of Taking Refuge. 'Taking' means returning, 'Refuge' means relying upon, relying upon whom? Relying upon Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. 'Kṣiti' refers to what? To nature, 'Mind Nature.' What is Kṣiti? Infinite wisdom, merits, and virtuous characteristics inSelf-nature, that is 'Kṣitigarbha'. If you see the image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, you can consider yourself taking refuge in that image; this is as commonly said in Buddhism: 'It is hard even for a Bodhisattva made of earth to cross the river safely.' That image helps you, so when you see it, you can awaken and realize that it is the Treasure of the Mind of the Earth, and we must rely on this, rely on the nature and virtues; only then do you truly take refuge. The Treasure of the Mind of the Earth is fully endowed with merit in its original mind, but we do not know it. Where is it? It is in the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra of Original Vows; the World-Honored One reveals the treasure of self-nature to us, so that we can have a true refuge.Taking refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva means practicing in accordance with the theories, methods, and realms recorded in the Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows; only then is it called 'taking refuge.' Previously, if our concepts, speech, and actions were contrary to the teachings in this sutra, we should promptly turn back and follow the teachings of the scriptures to correct ourselves to become good people—this is 'Yi.' Returning from mistakes is 'Gui,' and correcting mistakes according to the scriptures is called 'Yi.' Taking refuge means practicing genuinely.

If possible, sincerely respect and revere.

‘Quy’ means taking refuge, ‘kính’ means reverence. In this passage, the important word is ‘chí tâm’, which means sincere heart, without any trace of false hope or fantasy. A sincere heart follows the teachings and practices; whatever the Buddha teaches us, we must remember carefully and practice every day, ‘retaining and reciting, explaining for others’, this is sincere heart taking refuge, this is following the teachings and practicing. ‘Thọ’ means what? The principles taught by the Buddha in the scriptures, we fully accept without doubt; the methods of practice taught by the Buddha, we fully accept and completely follow. The realms described in the scriptures we fully enter. Fully entering means 'realizing', likeThat is why it is called 'wholehearted reverence.' Below are some appearances; to be honest, in daily life the aspects of practice and study are very broad and very deep. Here are some things listed below.

+ Worship and Praise: This is entirely for the speaker. Offering to the images of the Buddha and Bodhisattvas, one must offer and bow every day according to the proper rites. Reciting their names is praising them; reading the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows Sutra is also praising Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva; chanting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is likewise praising Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. For example, nowadays at the Buddha Chanting Hall on the fourth floor of Cư Sĩ Lâm, before preaching the sutras, everyone goes to chant the Buddha's name. Chanting the Buddha's name is 'worship and praise.' For whom is this done? For all sentient beings to see. Among all sentient beings, humans are only a few; people coming to the fourth floor of Cư Sĩ Lâm will see everyone and develop a joyful mind.Joy, planting virtuous roots in the Alaya consciousness, sowing the seeds of the Buddha, once it reaches the ears it permanently becomes the seed of the path, so you have guided them. Even more wonderful are the heavenly dragons and demon spirits; you should know how many guardian deities are in this practice hall, all the gods and demon spirits are there. When you recite Buddha's name and teach the sutras, our physical eyes cannot see them, yet countless guardian deities are on all sides, not only on the four sides but also above, below, in the sky, and under the ground. If your mind is truly pure, you can sense them; you will feel that they are there, moreover, their number is beyond imagination. Why do these guardian deities come? During the practice of cultivating virtueThey have vowed that as long as it is a temple of true dharma, they will definitely come to support it. If they do not support it, they would be going against their vow. So how could this not be an offense against the Buddhas Tathagata? They made the vow in front of the Buddha. Today we are completely propagating the true dharma, and within the true dharma there is absolutely not a single thought of self-interest. If there is even a hint of such a thought, the Dharma-protecting deities may not come, then the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas cannot blame them. When the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas ask: 'Why do you not protect the dharma?', they might say: 'Somebody has a private intention.' They may not come, and the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas cannot blame them. If those practicing in the pathThis assembly has no private intentions, the person preaching the sutra has no private intentions, and if the guardian deity does not come, it is their fault. We must understand these Matters and Principles, we must be sincere, wholeheartedly, respectfully bow and prostrate, we must worship, we must praise.

+ Fragrance, flowers, and clothing: These are offerings that must be burned with incense. Incense symbolizes many meanings; as mentioned earlier, incense represents ‘Faith, Precepts, Concentration, The Five Aspects of the Dharma Body,’ embodying these meanings. Flowers symbolize virtuous deeds, so flowers must be offered. Offering flowers serves to remind the community in the monastery to cultivate virtuous deeds; outstanding deeds surely lead to outstanding results in the future, which is why fresh flowers must be offered. In the past, there were no artificial flowers, so fresh flowers were always offered and replaced every day. You should understand that flowers symbolize the Dharma. In the past, if there were no fresh flowers, what would be done? People in ancient times alsoThere is a method: they use 'treasure flowers,' made from gold, silver, and lapis lazuli. These flowers do not need to be changed. In the past, these offerings were used: fruits made of gold, silver, and the seven treasures were offered to the Buddha to symbolize one's respect. If we lack the ability, and nowadays our work is busy, buying flowers every day is also very troublesome. The Buddha understands human conditions very well and does not want you to be troubled. If there are high-quality artificial flowers, they can also be used for offerings; it absolutely does not mean a lack of respect for the Buddha. Whether one is respectful or not lies in your heart. If your mind is 'devoted and respectful,' then the offeringAnything can express your respect; if your mind is not respectful, even if you offer flowers made of seven treasures, it will mean nothing, it is still not respectful. This is a kind of symbol, representing your own intention, and also contains the meaning of 'self-practice to transform others'. In general, one must offer incense and flowers.

‘Clothing’, offering robes. What is a robe? It is not the shirt we wear today, it is not this type of garment. You have to think about Buddhism being transmitted from India three thousand years ago; what kind of robes did they wear three thousand years ago? What is called a robe? A robe is an entire piece of cloth. In Singapore, it is very convenient; we often see Indian people walking on the street, the clothing of Indian people is made by wrapping a single piece of cloth around the body. The word 'robe' here refers to this piece of cloth; it is not a shirt with a collar and sleeves like ours, such a robe is not beautiful. A robe is a whole piece of cloth; today, the kasaya we wear is this robe. People in the secular world, if they are blessed, the clothes they wear are as long as a whole piece of cloth as well.so.

In the past, the Buddha's monastic community had the practice of alms begging, eating one meal a day, going out on the streets with their alms bowls, which made it easy to receive a meal, but obtaining a piece of clothing was extremely difficult, not easy to ask for. In the past, all fabric was woven by hand, which was very labor-intensive, so obtaining a garment was not easy. To be honest, even getting a bowl of rice was not easy; sometimes, one had to go to many houses to get a single bowl, with one place giving you a little, another place giving you a little, needing to visit six or seven houses to obtain one bowl. In the past, tools and resources were not as abundant as they are today, life was very difficult, so where could a piece of clothing for an ordained person be found? The old clothes that people had worn,Discarded and no longer used, called 'phan tao yi', thrown away, torn and no longer usable. Monastics collect these robes, find pieces of fabric that are not yet torn, cut these pieces into patches, and then sew them together to make a new robe. Because collecting such pieces of fabric results in different materials and colors, making a robe would look very mismatched, so it must be dyed. The meaning of dyeing the robe is like that. Today, the robes we offer are the kasaya, we offer this robe. What does this robe represent? It represents patience and forbearance. The robe is used to cover the body, hide modesty, and represents patience. This is talking about 'clothing'.

If it is possible to do so, the Buddha said: Those beings will immediately be freed from the karmic consequences of the three evil paths.

Why is that? These beings created countless limitless karmic offenses in the past, so why are they now free from the suffering of the three evil paths? Does this way of speaking contradict cause and effect? Why do those who commit evil not suffer evil results? It certainly does not contradict cause and effect. Why do they not suffer evil results? Because today they have severed the bonds of evil. You must understand, for a cause to bear fruit, there must be conditions; if there are no conditions, even if there is a cause, the result cannot manifest. For example, a watermelon seed is a seed that can potentially grow into a watermelon in the future, but it needs conditions; it needs soil, fertilizer, sunlight, and water, the full conditions must be metThe new seed sprouts, matures, and will eventually bloom and bear fruit. If the connection of this seed is severed, and the seed is placed in a cup of tea, even after a whole year it will not be able to bear fruit. This means that the karmic offenses of Avīci Hell that you have created in the past must result in going to Avīci Hell to receive retribution.

Today, the Buddha and Bodhisattvas teach you to sever these harmful karmic ties. Although you have created these karmic causes, you may not suffer the results at present. Saying this is very consistent with the Dharma; it is the severing of karmic connections. From now on, if you deeply believe in cause and effect, refrain from sexual misconduct, do not lie, do not speak double-tongued words, do not utter harsh speech, and praise the Mahayana, then the karmic connections will immediately reverse. Is there sin remaining from past lives? Yes, it still exists; the seeds remain in the Ālaya consciousness, just as if you placed a seed into a cup of tea, the seed will not disappear. You should know that these seeds of good and evil never completely vanish; when the conditions arise, they will be awakened, otherwise...Fate will permanently reside in the Alaya-consciousness; the Alaya-consciousness is like a storehouse, storing everything inside. If you have the seed of the Avici Hell, in the future you may go to the Avici Hell to deliver sentient beings. If your Alaya-consciousness does not have the seed of the Avici Hell, then you have no part in hell, and you will not see hell. Therefore, all karmic causes created in the past, when one becomes a Buddha, will take effect, universally saving all good and evil sentient beings in the nine dharma realms. Because at that time, you will understand clearly and will no longer be deluded. What does descending into hell mean? It means delivering sentient beings. To be honest, in hell there is no actual suffering, it is only a manifestation. Therefore, if you have no connectionHow can a hungry ghost save a hungry ghost? If you have no affinity with animals, you cannot save animals. We see Buddhas and Bodhisattvas manifest in the three evil realms because they created karma in the three evil realms when they practiced virtue in the past, and at that time they could use the karma of the three evil realms. They 'use' it, not to receive retribution, to save sentient beings. Therefore, we do not need to be overly sorrowful about all the sins we have committed before; we should understand that after becoming a Buddha, we will use them. If one does not become a Buddha, there is no need to speak further. If you continue to create evil karma now, you will certainly enter the three evil realms and suffer retribution. Therefore, after enlightenment, there is the effect of enlightenment, which is...The three evil paths exist to help sentient beings in suffering, this is something we must definitely understand…

According to the teachings of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua, "Taking refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva" means to respect and entrust one's entire body, mind, and life to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva; to regard Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva as a compassionate father, while oneself as his child.

This means that if we sincerely take refuge in Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, we need to daily, with utmost reverence, face the image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and make the following vow: “My name is [name], my surname is [surname]. Today I hear the teachings of the World-Honored One in the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows Sutra. For my past faults, I now confess them all before the Bodhisattva. From now on, I vow to abstain from all evil, to practice all good deeds, to refrain from contention, greed, desire, selfishness, self-interest, and lying. I sincerely request Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva to compassionately bless me so that I may diligently cultivate and become a virtuous man.(or virtuous woman), may I, after abandoning this body in an instant, be reborn in the Pure Land of Buddha Amitabha, quickly attain Buddhahood and universally save all sentient beings in the Dharma realm.

Afterwards, you can, whenever appropriate, praise the title of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, recite the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Scripture, and offer incense, flowers, and clothing to him with wholehearted reverence. In addition, from now on you must practice good deeds; even small good deeds should not be neglected, and even small bad deeds should not be committed. By following the teachings of the Sutra, within at most three years, no matter how difficult one's life may be, it will certainly change if this practice is carried out according to the Dharma.

The sex websites and CDs today that disturb people's minds are even more serious than erotic books; anyone who producesauthors, selling, renting, transferring into circulation, then the terrible disasters they have to endure, are they not even more dreadful and violent!

TWO BROTHERS IN NAM XUONG

In Nam Xuong, there were two twin brothers, identical in appearance and even in voice, so much so that even their parents had difficulty distinguishing them and had to use different clothing to tell them apart. As they grew up, they married wives at the same time, went to school at the same time, and in almost every matter of right and wrong, their actions were also very similar.

By the day the two went to take the exam, they were staying in the same rented house. There was a girl living near that house who intended to tease the older brother, but he immediately refused and also warned his younger brother to be cautious. The younger brother pretended to obey, but secretly he impersonated his older brother to meet that girl, even promising that after passing the exam, he would come to marry her.

When the results were posted, the older brother passed, while the younger brother failed. The girl could not distinguish between the two and thought that the one who passed was the one who had been involved with her, so she was extremely happy and even worried about giving him money for travel expenses to return to his hometown.

The following spring, the older brother passed the doctoral examination again. The girl was overjoyed upon hearing the news and busily prepared her belongings, waiting for him to come and marry her. Waiting endlessly without any news, she finally died with resentment.

Later, the brother lived a long life, and his descendants all enjoyed honor. As for the younger sister, who had died early, she had no children to carry on her lineage.

Commentary: The good or bad destiny of a person is all created by the consciousness in the previous life. If one did good deeds in the previous life, then when conceived, one naturally has good traits, and is born at an auspicious hour. If one did evil in the previous life, the result in this life will be the opposite. Therefore, the matter of good or bad destiny cannot be denied. However, once destiny is born, it is fixed, but the human mind is not fixed. Thus, misfortunes or blessings are created by the mind, not by destiny. Therefore, the matter of good or bad destiny cannot be considered absolute. Consider, for example, the case of the two brothers in Nam Xương [having the same destiny but different outcomes].different lives] can understand this.

tieu_de: MADAM QIN (Meritorious and Evil from a Previous Life, In This Life Married as Husband and Wife, Suffering to the Point of Wanting to Commit Suicide, Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara Appears)
tom_tat: ⁕⁕Tan Cu Si was a very beautiful woman, who had an artistic talent since childhood. At a young age, she had already become a famous hair-cutting and styling teacher known throughout the city. She was a skillful and clever person, capable and diligent. After the revolution ended
noi_dung:
MADAM TAN (Good and Evil in Past Lives, Married in This Life, Suffering to the Point of Wanting to Commit Suicide, Bodhisattva Guanyin Appears)

⁕⁕Tan Cu Si is a very beautiful woman, who has had an artistic talent since childhood. At a young age, she became a renowned hair-cutting and styling teacher throughout the city. She is agile, skillful, and capable. After the liberation revolution, she opened a home hair salon, which has now developed into a large, well-established beauty salon. Tan Cu Si is very filial to her mother. When her mother was on her deathbed, she knelt by the bed for 8 hours, continuously chanting Buddha's name, causing the whole family of more than ten people to kneel down and chant along. Suddenly, everyone, without prior agreement, shouted in unison: “Oh my! I see Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara"Then!" At that moment, the patient's room was filled with a miraculous fragrance that refreshed every organ. Everyone simultaneously saw Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva descend above (to the right of the sickbed), but only layman Tan saw his mother smile, ascend toward the sky, and even heard the resonant Buddhist music (Rebirth in the Western Pure Land). At that time, the entire family was extremely excited, all turning to look at their mother's face, seeing her gently smiling, having peacefully passed away. From then on, the whole family believed in Buddhism.

⁕⁕It was this sincerely virtuous Taoist recluse who had repeatedly asked me to help her arrange for becoming a nun. Through our conversations, I came to understand that the reason she wanted to become a nun was that she had no affection for her husband; they often quarreled, and at times he even physically abused her. On such occasions, I always advised her not to escape reality by becoming a nun. Moreover, she still had an underage daughter who needed her care and upbringing.

⁕⁕Not long ago, one evening she suddenly called, crying uncontrollably, saying that after quarreling with her husband, she had gone to her brother's house and stayed there for three days, and now just wanted to see me immediately, otherwise she didn't want to live anymore. As soon as we met, Ms. Tan burst into tears and recounted: “I am currently living in a three-room building, which I bought just half a year ago for 400,000, all of which I earned myself. I live together with my husband; when we viewed the house, we liked it, but because I was busy with many matters, I entrusted my husband to handle the money and take care of the house purchase procedures. Not long after, we already had the keys to the new house. I thought that my half a life of suffering and hardship had been compensated by theThe house we liked. But who would have thought, three days ago late at night, my husband came home and said: –Tomorrow morning or at the latest the day after, you need to prepare a full 200,000 in cash to hand over… if not, you’ll have to leave the house. •I was stunned, and asked: –Didn't I already give you 400,000 to buy the house? What’s this extra 200,000 for? •He shouted: –I only gave them 200,000, the other 200,000 I used to buy stocks to make a profit, but unexpectedly lost it all. To recover, I mortgaged this new house for 200,000, but also lost everything. Now they are asking for the money, and if we don’t have it, we have to leave the house… I felt like thunder hit my ears and hurriedly blamed my husband for playing the stock market.He didn’t discuss it with me beforehand. Who would have thought he not only didn’t admit his fault, but also hit me (as she spoke, she showed me the injury on her arm). •She snuffled and said: -I really find it hard to get through today. I also thought that in the past I owed him, so I had endured for almost 20 years to keep things peaceful. In the house, everything related to food, clothing, and shelter… I earned and provided all by myself. Could it be that I still haven’t fully repaid my debt to him? Now, if I have to compensate money, my beauty salon would also have to close. I truly can’t understand it! I really want to ask you to request Venerable Dieu Phap to explain (over the phone) to me, so I can understand karma. Only then can I be willingconscience. Even if I die, I must die for clarity! Boo hoo!

⁕⁕Pause for a moment to calm the mind, then Mr. Tan recounted to me the full story of her marriage… -“My younger brother was sent back to the countryside right after liberation. After that, the family thought of ways to bring him back to the city. So my mother took me to the chief's house to ask for help. The chief's wife, upon seeing me, seemed very enthusiastic, asked a long series of questions, and then persuaded her husband to quickly arrange this matter for us. After that, my mother went alone to the chief's house, and my younger brother was soon transferred back to the city. At that time, my mother arranged for me to meet the chief's son, and of course, I did not like the marriageI was arranged by my mother (like a trade), but since my younger brother had been helped by them to return to the city, I had to accept meeting him. When we met, neither side felt anything or spoke. But seeing that he was educated (had graduated from university and was a government officer), it wasn't completely off-putting. Because my mother had persuaded and advised me many times, I finally agreed to the marriage arranged by both sides, and my younger brother was able to get a satisfying job. Who would have known, on the wedding night, when the groom took off his clothes, I was extremely shocked to see his entire body covered in spots and lumps, looking like leprosy or scales.So it was. Focusing carefully, I only wanted to vomit violently. This man is my husband: except for his face, neck, and hands, the rest of his body is diseased, covered with rough bumps and flaking like fish scales. I stood as if turned to stone, full of horror, tears streaming down my face. Just think, from now on, how am I supposed to face a life like this? I’m sure that if other girls saw a groom this terrifying, they would have no choice but to rush out the door and run away. But because I didn’t have the courage to face my mother’s tearful face, and thought about my younger brother’s future and the ridicule of society… I had no choice but to bow my head and accept my fate.

⁕⁕At that moment, I finally realized and understood why the family of the 'director' was so eager, enthusiastic, and sincerely helping us – Because of their son, they had ruined my life! After that, I advised my husband to seek treatment, and he said: “I had treatment before but it didn’t work, so I don’t want to go anymore because I don’t like being laughed at, it’s very humiliating!” I then bought a lot of medicine for him, but none of it had good results. I again advised him to go to the hospital, and he would hit and scold me. What made it even more miserable was that I could not bear to share a bed with him; whenever he came close, I felt disgusted and nauseated. Perhaps this would hurt his pride further.his pride and self-esteem, so he was even more brutal and violent toward me. My heart is full of wounds; we hadn't been married for many days before we started sleeping in separate rooms. Later, I became pregnant and gave birth to a daughter. But what is perplexing is that a person who received a university education and was born into a family of high-ranking officials still lacks even the most basic hygiene habits. He leaves leftover bits of food in bowls, throws clothes anywhere, throws off his socks wherever he takes them off, and he hasn't changed in over ten years. If I don't urge him, he wouldn't even bother with bathing. Regarding these bad habits, I only need to show a little dissatisfaction and it would immediatelyimmediately got a severe beating. From the outside looking in, everyone thought we were a talented man and a beautiful woman, a small happy family, little did they know that I 'smiled outwardly, but cried silently inside'…

⁕⁕Once I went to Qingdao for work and stayed at a seaside hotel. That night I lay comfortably in my room, listening to the roaring sound of the waves, and in such a romantic setting, I unconsciously thought about my fate, unable to hold back my tears, which wet my pillow. Tossing and turning for a long time, I still found it hard to sleep, blaming the sky for being so unfair, for marrying me to a violent, terrible, miserable, dreadful man… Could this really be the fate that people often talk about? Suddenly I remembered the legend of Bodhisattva Guanyin in the South Sea, who is said to be very compassionate and often saves those in suffering. Could it be that He would not save?Help me? Why is my fate so miserable? Outside the window, the sound of the sea waves roared loudly, as if wanting to console me, to give me hope… I sat up, put on my coat, stepped out of the hotel, and walked to the beach. In the deep night, I strolled slowly alone on the deserted sand without a soul in sight. I looked up at the sky sparkling with thousands of stars, my heart wanting to cry but no tears could fall. Suddenly, I vaguely saw the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara riding on the back of a fish standing at the edge of the sea (at the horizon)… at this moment, all the injustices, humiliations, resentments, and hopes… within me surged simultaneously like a fountain. I knelt on the sand, facing towards Avalokiteshvara.The bodhisattva burst out crying loudly. With a heartfelt wish, hoping that He would save me, bringing me out of this world of suffering and misery!

⁕⁕After that, I got to know elder brother and took refuge in Buddhism. Perhaps the heavens heard my prayers and responded. However, no matter how many times I chanted sutras and paid homage to the Buddha, it still could not improve my tragic marriage. After all, how much debt did I owe to my husband in past lives? And why is it impossible to repay it no matter what? I heard that Director Kim's family also encountered complicated and difficult problems, and they sought the help of Venerable Diệu Pháp. So, could you help ask on my behalf? If not, I truly do not wish to live anymore!”…

⁕⁕Hearing layperson Tan cry and tell her story was heartbreaking. Seeing her in a state of despair, I could hardly believe that "such misfortune could befall a kind, filial, capable, and responsible woman," and I couldn’t find the words to comfort her. I couldn’t refuse, and once again had no choice but to hurriedly call my master for help. I pressed the speaker button so everyone could clearly hear the master’s guidance. •The master’s gentle voice rang out: -"About 100 years ago, there was a man who brought along his young daughter to a small town to open a restaurant for a living. The girl’s mother had fallen ill and passed away; the restaurant owner feared that he mightHuyen would suffer for the child, so he decided to stay there. One day he went out, on the way back to meet a boy about 5-6 years old who had been abandoned by people. The owner then calculated: "The leftover rice soup that the guests eat can feed this boy. If you save his life now, when he grows up, he can work for you (without having to pay for rent). It was a "double whammy". So he decided to take in the boy and build a wooden cattle shed with thatched roof (near his house) for him to live in. Every day he helped him wash the dishes, sweep, and eat leftovers to get through the day. In the eyes of the old owner and his daughter, this child was nothing more than a talking animal, even if he had a headachefeverish, bitten by mosquitoes, having wounds… whatever, it doesn’t matter! They let it live and die on its own. But it turns out this boy was tough, he just kept growing up like that. However, from childhood to adulthood, no one considered him a person; besides constantly ordering him around, no one bothered to talk to him. Whenever anything displeased them, the father and the master would take their anger out on him; if they didn’t beat him, they would scold him, even though he spoke very little and was clumsy and silly… yet he was still treated very poorly. When the daughter came of marrying age, the old master also wanted to choose a son-in-law to live in their house, but on second thought, he feared 'if I die, the property would be taken by the son-in-law.' Therefore, even though there were many peopleHe asked for betrothal, but he hesitated, reluctant to marry off his daughter. In the end, he suddenly came up with a clever idea, turning to look at the orphan boy he had raised for so long: 'If I marry my daughter to this servant, in reality he is just a slave who obeys my daughter, so there is no need to worry about the family estate falling into the hands of outsiders.' Thus, the wise master arranged a 'perfectly safe' marriage for his daughter. Although the daughter obeyed her father’s orders, she absolutely refused to share a room with her husband (the stupid, dirty servant), so she lived her life indulging in secret passions. As for the boy, he spent his entire life in forced labor, suffering injustices and humiliation… The daughter in the story isThe talented consort today, also known as the orphaned servant, is precisely her current husband.

• Living habits that are unhygienic and unhealthy – this is due to years of living in the previous life's animal pen – The skin on the body is rough and scabbed (partly due to the consequences of past wrongdoings and partly due to long-term living in filth, constantly being bitten by mosquitoes). The proverb says: “Every grievance has a source, every debt has a debtor; it's not that there is no retribution, it's just not the right time yet… Bad karmic connections from past lives have resulted in the sufferings in marriage for Master Tan in this life. In the previous life, the child had been exhausted, serving the master all life without receiving any payment, and in this life, it comes to claim the debt. Master Tan being beaten and scolded is exactlyIn the past, she used to scold and beat him. Even the married life in this life is a version of the previous life... •“If you want to know the karma of the past life, look at the rewards of this life.” In the past, the scholar Qin did evil deeds, mostly influenced by his father from a young age. In this life, she is filial and respectful to her mother, has a kind and benevolent heart, likes to listen to Buddhist teachings, knows how to take refuge in the Buddha, practices vegetarianism and recites Buddha's name. Only Buddhist teachings can help her resolve and end past debts.

•Therefore, Venerable Tan, once you fully understand the causes and conditions of your past life, should no longer harbor resentment, hatred, or dislike towards your current husband. Instead, you must seize the opportunity of meeting in this life, sincerely repent for the karma of your past life. In living, always observe your own faults, speak little of others' faults, and you will surely turn misfortune into good fortune, transforming calamity into safety. You should recite a lot of the “Ksitigarbha Sutra” and the “Universal Gate Sutra” dedicating the merit to your “former servant” from the previous life, and your husband will surely change.”

⁕⁕After I hung up the phone, I turned to look at Mr. Tan sitting quietly; the “rain” on his face had stopped, and now it was “clear skies.”

⁕⁕More than half a year had passed, and Mr. Tan had called twice. Once to ask about some Buddhist scriptures, and another time to say that she was busy with a lot of work, and when she had free time she would come to visit me. Hearing her voice showed that her mind was happy. I exhaled in relief. I silently prayed that her married couple would soon resolve their past grievances, that the family would be harmonious, and that they would overcome difficult challenges together. (***KARMA IN THIS LIFE… Translated by Hanh Doan)

tieu_de: THE LIFE-EXTENDING ABILITY OF UNCLE LANG NGHIEM
tom_tat: Master Thong Lai teaches that when a parent or relative is about to die and Master has not yet been able to perform the vigil, children should try to recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra for the dying person because the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra has the power to prolong life.
noi_dung:
THE LONGEVITY ENHANCING ABILITY OF MR. LANG NGHIEM

Master Thong Lai taught that when a parent or relative is about to die and the Master has not yet arrived to perform the chanting, the children should try to recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra for the person who is about to pass away, because the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra has the power to extend the lifespan of the dying person from 10 days to a year. Ms. Diệu An applied this when chanting for her own family member; the elderly woman sat and practiced and remained healthy until the time P heard that Dharma talk, which was already a year later.

At home, it is recommended to play the Surangama Mantra in Sanskrit so that ghosts do not come near your home; it can avoid the 12 earthly cycles. By chanting the Surangama Mantra, one will be protected, and ghosts will not dare to approach. I heard the Master say that the mother of Mr. Nguyen Tri, he played the Surangama Mantra in her room 24/7, but a few people who came to listen could not bear it and turned it off. Every time it was turned off, the elderly lady would ask to draw the window curtains closed, hiding fearfully in the room, because she saw ghosts filling the windows. When Mr. Nguyen Tri turned it back on, she would ask to draw the curtains open. Without the Surangama Mantra, she could not live in peace until now."Now, although the old lady is elderly, she attends every retreat and dons the robe every time 🙂

If you want to recite the Mantra but don't have time, you can copy the Mantra onto a CD, and listen to it whenever you drive to work. Listening for a long time will engrain the Mantra deeply in your mind; if you have a strong seed in your heart, you will always memorize the Mantra and also always be at peace 🙂

If you want to maintain this Mantra, you must abstain from the five pungent substances (ginger, green onion, garlic, shallot, and asafoetida). The teacher said that even leek is related to onions, and even galangal cannot be eaten. If you do not abstain, the guardians of the Mantra will avoid you because of the smell, and then reciting the Mantra will not be effective. It is best to follow a vegetarian diet. Do you see the contradiction when I confess to the Buddha that I repent for the sin of killing while my mouth still chews the flesh of sentient beings? That’s why, even if I recite constantly, I don’t see any results. I think probably the Buddha will smile and feel pity for me: poor thing, you say you repent, but the Tathagata sees that you do not yet know what true repentance is 🙂 and one thingAnother important thing is that you have to be a good person for it to be effective; if you dare to do anything without discernment, when you chant, the result will be the opposite, and the protective deities will punish you because you are not worthy of their protection 🙂

The teacher explained: Master Lăng Nghiêm has 5 disciples:

The first disciple is to resolve the precept of "Killing",

the second disciple is to resolve the precept of "Stealing",

the third disciple is to resolve the precept of "Sexual misconduct",

the fourth disciple is to resolve the precept of "Bad speech",

the fifth disciple is to resolve the precept of "Drinking alcohol".

For example: if one creates a lot of harmful speech karma, then reciting the 4th chapter of the 21-variable set for 21 consecutive days in a day will be able to resolve the harmful speech karma. See what you are entangled with and then recite the corresponding chapter.

Excerpt from a lecture,

Thầy Thông Lai

tieu_de: PATIENCE
tom_tat: 🍁✨Patience and forbearance (Paramita) is one of the most important practices on the Bodhisattva path. When anger arises in the mind, you need to directly observe and contemplate the anger, and it will transform into the Great Perfect Wisdom. ☀️🍃Before
noi_dung:
FINANCE

🍁✨The perfection of patience is one of the most important practices on the Bodhisattva path. When the mind arises with anger, you need to directly contemplate that anger, and it will transform into the Great Perfect Awareness.

☀️🍃First of all, when you are in extreme suffering, never give up or become discouraged. You need to stay optimistic, continue practicing good deeds, and persist in practicing the Dharma. When favorable and smooth things come to you, you should also not become proud of yourself. You need to understand why you have happiness and be grateful for what you have. But you also need to contemplate impermanence to understand that all these good things are also impermanent and not lasting.

🍁✨If others perform better than you, instead of feeling sad, you should cultivate a joyful heart as if you yourself are succeeding like them. Therefore, in any situation that occurs in life, whether favorable or adverse, you should use it as an opportunity to practice. In this way, you become proficient in practicing life in preparation for death—the greatest practice of a human being.

tieu_de: WANT A HARMONIOUS, PROSPEROUS FAMILY?
tom_tat: IF YOU FOREVER THINK THE OTHER PERSON IS RIGHT, IS GOOD. WHEN THERE IS A CONFLICT, WE ADMIT OUR OWN WRONGS AND COMMIT TO CORRECTING THEM, THEN FAMILY HARMONY AND EVERYTHING THRIVES. REMEMBERING THE GOOD OF OTHERS IS THE ONLY WAY TO BE HARMONIOUS, TO TRANSFORM.
noi_dung:
WANT A HARMONIOUS, PROSPEROUS FAMILY?

IF YOU ALWAYS THINK THE OTHER PARTY IS RIGHT AND GOOD, WHEN THERE IS A CONFLICT, WE TAKE THE FAULT ON OURSELVES AND COMMIT TO CORRECTING IT, THEN THE FAMILY WILL BE HARMONIOUS AND EVERYTHING WILL PROSPER. REMEMBERING THE GOOD IN OTHERS CAN LEAD TO HARMONY AND RESOLVE CONFLICTS.

The phenomenon of disharmony in families is very common; marital discord and conflict often occur.

What is the cause? It's because of the belief that we are right and others are wrong; if both only see the faults of the other, how can there be harmony?

Before getting married, we often look at our partner with idealized eyes; everything about that person seems beautiful and pleasing, which is why we can proceed to marriage. That is the psychological state before marriage.

However, if we always think the other person is right and good, when conflicts arise, we take the blame upon ourselves and commit to change, then harmony will lead to prosperity. Remembering the good qualities of the other person allows for harmony, can resolve conflicts, and truly promotes peaceful stability.

The family is the cell of society, the most basic organization. When every household is harmonious, society is harmonious, and the country is prosperous and strong.

Everyone should reflect on themselves and recognize their own faults. Saying that others are wrong is a great mistake. Nowadays, most of us make this mistake. No one else is truly wrong; this principle is rarely understood, only Buddhas and Bodhisattvas understand it. Why is it said that others are without fault? Because the fault lies within ourselves.

"The environment changes according to the mind." The mind is one’s own mind; the external environment changes according to one’s mind. The external is unwholesome because our mind is unwholesome; we ourselves transform the environment into unwholesomeness. When the mind becomes wholesome, isn’t the external environment wholly wholesome as well?

Therefore, reflect on where the fault lies; the fault is within oneself due to the arising of afflictions and habitual tendencies. Morality - Concentration - Wisdom do not arise in the present moment,

The Buddha often taught in the major sutras, “All sentient beings possess the wisdom and virtuous characteristics of the Tathagata.” Our wisdom and virtuous characteristics are not manifested because of greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, selfishness, and self-interest, which give rise to actions that cause conflict among people. On the other hand, if one possesses wisdom and virtuous characteristics, conflicts will not occur among individuals. Since our own mind is not good, as it contains selfishness and self-interest, desire for fame and gain, greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, as well as the five desires and six external sense objects, the great mistake lies within ourselves.

In Mahayana scriptures, the Buddha often said: "In one's own nature, everything is empty." Master Huệ Năng, who attained enlightenment, also said in his Dharma assembly: "Originally, there is nothing, where could dust of defilement cling?" In a pure mind, in the true nature of oneself, there is nothing, it is clean and pure, containing only wisdom and virtuous characteristics. When we are deluded, we lose our true nature, turning wisdom into afflictions, turning virtuous power into evil, committing all kinds of wrongdoing, turning good appearances into coarseness, transforming into a wicked world of five turbid periods, transforming into the three realms and six paths. Where does it come from? It arises from our own transformations. By oneselfturn into it, enjoy it yourself, then who can you still blame.

Therefore, to be wrong is completely wrong in oneself. In the present reality, everyone is wrong, the whole world is wrong. Therefore, enlightened beings suffer greatly, enlightened beings cannot save the world. However, enlightened beings can save themselves; deluded beings are in conflict with enlightened beings, but enlightened beings can be harmonious with deluded beings because enlightened beings do not compete with them. They want money, we give money; they want fame, we give fame; they want something, we give them that. If we do not desire anything, no conflict arises. Conflict occurs because both parties are desiring. The deluded believe that if they do not compete, they will not get anything.

, a wise person who understands to yield this place will then be given another place, sometimes even more than what was given. The more one lets go, the more one gains, without needing to ask. This is the principle that the Buddha taught, but unfortunately, sentient beings do not believe it.

VENERABLE TEACHER TỊNH KHÔNG.

tieu_de: THANKS TO SINCERELY REPENTING, THE WIFE HAS CHANGED HER HUSBAND, HELPING HIM GET OUT OF ADDICTION, AND THE CHILDREN ARE WELL-BEHAVED
tom_tat: Mr. Kiến Châu (my father-in-law) kept telling this story and asking why I didn't publish it in the newspaper so that everyone could benefit from it? When I heard him tell it, I was very doubtful, even though he
noi_dung:
THANKS TO SINCERE REPENTANCE TO HIS WIFE, HE COULD CHANGE, GETTING RID OF ADDICTION, WITH WELL-BEHAVED CHILDREN

Teacher Kiến Châu (my father-in-law) kept telling this story and asked why I didn't publish it in the newspaper so that everyone could benefit from it. When I first heard him tell it, I was very skeptical, even though he said this story was one hundred percent true. But later, after translating many works and understanding the stories within them, I thought that it should also be written here (as it was told to the teacher by the people involved).

"When she was young, Mrs. Thu was the beauty of the village, so many young men pursued her for marriage. Coming from a poor family, she asked to work for a foreign milk company and held the position of treasurer. By cleverly skimming a bit of money from the company each day to keep for herself, she saved up to two cans of Guigoz Gold.

From then on, her life improved, and her financial situation became quite comfortable. After a period of courtship and deliberation, she married a fair-haired prince and gave birth to three sons, living prosperously in the city.

Friends secretly looked on with envy at her happiness – she was beautiful and rich, had children as desired, and married a worthy husband. It seemed as if heaven favored her too much. Yet that happiness was as fragile as dew. Her husband gradually changed, no longer diligent in work, spending every night drinking. After drinking, he would come home and beat her. She had to sell the house to provide money for her husband’s spending. Not only that, she also had to raise two children addicted to heroin. Before long, both of them contracted AIDS and died.

Her fortune was completely gone, and now she had become destitute, yet her husband still drank heavily as before. Every day she had to collect scrap to sell in order to support her husband and their son. The family was falling apart, but her husband remained oblivious. Every time he got drunk, he would brutally beat her, especially when she gave him money that was insufficient for his spending, he would strike without mercy. After that, he would move to live elsewhere, but every day he would come by to collect money, and if she didn’t have it, he would continue to torment her.

He was so cruel that he humiliated her in every way, making her clean, wash his feet, kneel, and serve him... only then would he relent. He was also very jealous, so the beatings continued relentlessly. She lived through days of extreme suffering, only wanting to end her life.

After that, she went to the temple and cried while telling the story to the monk. Monk Kiến Châu advised her not to despair and also not to commit suicide. Because if one tries to escape the consequences of karma before repaying it, one will have to pay double in the next life, with even greater suffering.

The master performed the refuge ceremony for her, advising her to return home to pay respects to the Buddha and repent for all the sins she has committed until now, and sincerely make vows to abandon evil and do good, wholeheartedly correct wrongdoings, and pray that bad karma will be eliminated. The master explained:

– Minor repentance lasts 80 days, medium repentance 100 days, major repentance 120 days. She must definitely repent in order to reduce suffering.

Following Master Kien Chau's advice, she returned home to repent, earnestly confessing her past thefts, chanting the holy name of Avalokiteshvara, sincerely regretting, vowing from now on to live an honest and upright life, praying for her husband's reform, her children to be obedient, and for her family to be peaceful…

The woman who had been repentant for 100 days had a dream one night. In the dream, she saw herself as a young secretary, also living deceitfully, manipulating, greedy, and embezzling from her boss. Strangely, that boss was now her husband…. Upon waking, she felt very confused, with countless tangled thoughts. At that moment, she no longer resented her husband but only felt an inescapable remorse for the evil actions she had committed in the past. She could only cry and repent, praying for her husband's well-being and for forgiveness from those whose property she had once wrongfully taken.

Not long after, her husband suddenly found a job. The surprising thing was that he completely changed, being far kinder to her than she could have imagined, making her feel as if she were dreaming... He gently told her that from now on she could stay at home to cook, recite Buddha’s name, and do penance, while he would go to work to support them. In his firm hand, she felt the love and felt the invisible forgiveness. From then on, she no longer dared to be greedy or dishonest; on the contrary, she became generous, offered alms, and sincerely directed her repentance toward those she had wronged in the past, hoping to atone for her former sins.

Currently, she no longer worries about her family. Her youngest son now knows to respect and believe in Buddhism. She always teaches him about cause and effect; she does not want him to follow in her downfall.

As for her husband, she thinks he has every right to act cruelly, but he has changed, learning to be mindful and dedicated to work, gentle and kind beyond expectation. Surprisingly, seeing her recite sutras and bow to the Buddha often, he feels no resentment at all; on the contrary, he is very happy.

She silently expressed gratitude for the miraculous Dharma, regretting that she had realized the path too late.

If in the past she had been born in a family that knew the Dharma, had listened to the teachings, and understood the law of cause and effect, she certainly would not have ignored others' suffering. Because she did not understand the path, she accumulated unwholesome deeds and had to endure a life full of difficulties.

Although the woman gave birth to all sons, the first two were rebellious, addicted to drugs, and died from AIDS. As for her husband, he continued to punish her severely until she repented, and then everything began to improve in a positive direction.

Then, thanks to good karma, she had the opportunity to hear the venerable monk's teachings on cause and effect, she awakened and was determined to repent, to start over from the beginning… The result was truly miraculous. To the Buddha, she only had boundless gratitude. Every night she prayed that everyone would know of the Buddha's teachings so that they would not sow the causes of going astray and would not suffer as she had before.

She wishes that the lesson from her life will help many people avoid the mistakes of creating evil karma. Accumulate virtue and do charity; whatever seeds you sow, you will surely reap the corresponding results. Please remember!

Namo Amitabha Buddha!

Excerpt: Phenomena of Cause and Effect

Translator: Hanh Doan
