tieu_de: VENERABLE PHO QUANG ILLUMINATES ABOUT CHU LANG NGHIEM
tom_tat: Hạnh Đoan recruiting translators (Newly translated articles not yet published - If copying, please clearly credit the translator and source, and do not change the title. Thank you very much)
noi_dung:
Venerable Phổ Quang Illuminates About Master Lăng Nghiêm

Transcribed and translated by Hạnh Đoan

(New translation, not yet published in a book - If copying, please clearly state the translator, the source, and do not change the title. Thank you very much)

It is necessary to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, memorize it, and chant it, as it can lead to becoming a Buddha in one lifetime. The merits of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra cannot be fully expressed. Everyone can memorize it. Whoever memorizes it will benefit, but if you only listen without memorizing or practicing, it is of no use. The Lăng Nghiêm mantra has endless benefits - there are hundreds of trillions of benefits! -

So, does the recitation of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra have a specified time?

For us monastics, we can recite during the day, at night, or even 24 hours continuously. The Buddha said: ANYONE WHO SAYS THAT YOU CAN RECITE AT THIS TIME BUT NOT AT OTHER TIMES... ANYONE WHO SAYS YOU CAN RECITE IN THE MORNING BUT NOT IN THE AFTERNOON... ANYONE WHO SAYS YOU CAN ONLY RECITE IN THE TEMPLE AND NOT AT HOME... such a person is exactly a demon or heretic, a sin that cannot be forgiven. They will fall! Because they obstruct those who wish to recite. Therefore, you must never say such things, even a thousand or ten thousand times over!

Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra can help the world be peaceful and the nation and people be safe, achieving both loyalty and filial piety.

Those who say there is a fixed time to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra are slandering the Dharma. The Lăng Nghiêm Sutra was personally preached by the Buddha, and the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra was to explain the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. Every word of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, every stroke, every line is a teaching for people to become Buddhas.

Therefore, one should diligently and patiently practice. The Lăng Nghiêm mantra is very miraculous, but the practice is not easy.

First, do not be selfish, and second, do not be self-interested; one must have an altruistic and forgiving heart, always wishing to save all sentient beings.

Having such a mind, chanting mantras will be accomplished very quickly. You should pay attention, it is essential to follow the five precepts, maintain a vegetarian diet, and practice the ten wholesome deeds. These are the minimum rules that must be followed.

This is like having to study for ten, twenty, or thirty years to gain understanding. Practicing spirituality is also like that; if you want to recite the Shurangama Mantra, you must be diligent without interruption. Practicing is as important as wearing clothes, eating, and sleeping, and cannot be neglected daily. Regardless of whether it is effective or not, if you persist in chanting every day, you will build a foundation over a long time and naturally achieve results. If you want to accomplish miraculous virtue and gain inconceivable power, your mind should not indulge in wandering thoughts or fantastical visions.

If you recite intermittently, you will not attain samadhi. Practicing the Lingyan mantra must be done sincerely and continuously. To practice the Lingyan mantra, you forget time and space, not caring whether it is day or night, eating, sleeping... everything is forgotten, nothing matters; one thought is countless kalpas, countless kalpas are one thought.

If you have this mindset, wholeheartedly practicing the Lingyan mantra will certainly achieve samadhi. If not, do not even talk about genuinely practicing the Lingyan mantra. This is not only true for practicing the Lingyan mantra; practicing other dharmas is the same.

Each verse of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra has countless meanings, and each meaning possesses innumerable powers. One must understand that the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is the sacred scripture of heaven and earth, the sacred scripture within the miraculous, the secret within the secret, the supreme Dharma treasure, and the life-saving treasure for all sentient beings. It encompasses all existence, from the ten directions of Buddhas above to the hells of Avīci below. Both the four holy ones and the six ordinary ones respect the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra.

THOSE WHO CAN RECITE THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA ARE ALL BEINGS WHO HAVE ACCUMULATED VIRTUOUS ROOTS FOR COUNTLESS LIFETIMES. ONLY THEN CAN THEY READ IT FLUENTLY, AND NEVER FORGET IT. THIS IS A MANIFESTATION OF VIRTUOUS ROOTS. IF YOU DO NOT HAVE VIRTUOUS ROOTS, NOT ONLY CAN YOU NOT RECITE IT, BUT YOU CANNOT EVEN ENCOUNTER THE NAME OF THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA, AND IF YOU DO ENCOUNTER IT, YOU STILL CANNOT RECITE IT. THEREFORE, THE FACT THAT WE CAN NOW READ AND LEARN IT IS ALL THANKS TO GREAT VIRTUOUS ROOTS.

When you diligently recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, if you often dream of worshiping the Buddha, or dream of the Buddha radiating light, or dream of the Buddha touching your head, or dream of the Buddha teaching the scriptures and expounding the Dharma to you, or see Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, holy monks, or if you dream of yourself flying in the air, these are all auspicious signs… or seeing yourself riding a horse, or crossing a river, seeing all kinds of good lights, or all very strange omens… If you experience these manifestations, you should be careful. You must cultivate the Bodhi mind, keep your body, speech, and mind pure, and diligently recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra even more. But you should not boast to others that you have had such experiences.Miraculous manifestations so that people believe in you and have an aesthetic feeling toward you.

You cannot boast or advertise in order to promote your practice of cultivation. If you do this, you will have a vulnerability, and demons will take the opportunity to destroy it. It's like having a treasure but not hiding it, instead leaving it at the door—you will definitely have it stolen.

Therefore, in practicing the dharma, one must be very careful not to give celestial demons or heretics any opportunity.

However, with fellow practitioners, you can speak out to share miraculous things, not for fame or gain, not to seek respect or praise, but to encourage one another.

In the Lankavatara Sutra, if you recite the Lankavatara mantra with diligence and benefit, then 84,000 Vajra Bodhisattvas and Bodhisattva disciples and their followers will often protect you, helping you fulfill your wishes. Even if the demon king tries to find a loophole to cause trouble, he cannot. There is no way to create problems for you.

In the past, the Fifth Patriarch Hongren cultivated at Dongshan, Hubei… and observed the precepts very strictly.

Once, when bandits besieged a city, the Fifth Patriarch, wanting to save the people in the city, went down the mountain and traveled from Dongshan to the city in Hubei.

When the bandits saw the Fifth Patriarch appear, they ran away, dropping their helmets and armor. Why was that? Although the Fifth Patriarch came down the mountain alone, the bandits saw countless heavenly soldiers wearing shining golden armor, like angels descending from the sky… all wearing golden helmets and golden armor, holding swords in their hands. When the bandits saw this scene, they were terrified and fled, retreating quickly, not daring to fight with knives, guns, or bows and arrows anymore…

It was all because the Fifth Patriarch Hongren had recited the Lankavatara Mantra, so those robbers became terrified and fled at first sight. This is called true skill. Otherwise, how could there be such inconceivable spiritual response?

Because Shakyamuni Buddha protects all of us who are currently beginning to practice, He has praised the "Lankavatara Mantra" to help us achieve concentration, making our body and mind peaceful and undisturbed by afflictions. Therefore, we must never forget the Dharma at any moment. If we can sincerely and wholeheartedly recite the "Lankavatara Mantra," it will be a way to flourish the Buddha's teachings and uphold the true Dharma in the world.

Source: Nun Hanh Doan

tieu_de: EVERY DAY WE SHOULD RECITE 7 TIMES THE LENG YAN MANTRA.
tom_tat: 🪷 The Buddha told Ananda: "After I pass away, if someone recites this Mantra seven times daily, all extremely heavy sins will be eliminated, great vows will be fulfilled, and boundless merits will be gained. For example, if someone uses jewels..."
noi_dung:
EVERY DAY WE SHOULD RECITE 7 CHANTS OF LĂNG NGHIÊM.

🪷 The Buddha said to Ananda: "After I pass into parinirvana, if there is someone who recites this Mantra seven times every day, they will eradicate all major sins, attain great righteous vows, and infinite merit. For example, if someone uses treasures from all four corners of the world to practice the Perfection of Giving (Dana Paramita), the merit they gain, multiplied by hundreds of thousands, still CANNOT compare to that of a person who, early in the morning, sincerely recites this Mantra seven times before the Buddha statue."

🪷 This mantra often helps those who recite it diligently quickly attain perfection in the Bodhi path. All Tathagatas of the ten directions praise: In your next life, you will become a Buddha without fail. The radiance from your body illuminates all Buddhist realms.

🪷 Ananda! Wherever this mantra exists, the beings of that land will experience joy among gods and dragons, timely rain and wind, abundant rice and beans, and the people will be peaceful and happy. It also subdues all evil stars, and all disasters will not arise.

🔥 P/s:

🪷 Every day I practice like this, plus 108 recitations of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. Thanks to this, my energy is always abundant. Even though I never sleep before 1 a.m. when working, my mind remains alert, fresh, and not tired, always optimistic.

🪷 If there is no Buddha altar at home, then while chanting, imagine that you are facing the Buddha while reciting the Mantra.

🪷 Although the Buddha said that reciting seven times brings such great merit, if we can recite more than that number each day, the merit becomes many times greater!

Source: collected.

tieu_de: A TOUCHING TRUE STORY TO SHARE, WORTH WATCHING TO UNDERSTAND WHY THERE ARE SO MANY SUBSTANCES IN THE HOUSE ..., DISEASE
tom_tat: ************ Last night, after posting a sales post, I was so tired that I lay down to sleep. At that time it was 12 o'clock. I recited a Buddha prayer and began to close my eyes to sleep when I saw a young man with a handsome face, and he was looking at me.
noi_dung:
A TRUE AND TOUCHING STORY TO SHARE, VERY WORTH WATCHING TO UNDERSTAND WHY THERE ARE SO MANY OBSTACLES AT HOME..., DISEASE

************

Last night, after posting a sales post, I was too tired and lay down to sleep. It was 12 o'clock when I started reciting Buddha's name and began to close my eyes to sleep. Then I saw a young man with a handsome face; he looked at me and smiled. Instantly, I opened my eyes but didn't see him. When I closed my eyes again and recited Buddha's name, I saw the person looking and smiling. At that moment, I used my mind to talk to him. I asked, "Who are you and why are you following me here?" He smiled and replied, "I saw that you are a good person, so I followed you to protect you, I have not done anything to harm you." And I answered, "My body is very ugly, why are you following"What am I for?" the person laughed and said, "It's just your body, it's not important. I see that you are a very good person, so I will follow to protect you." Then I laughed and replied, "If you follow me, you must chant Buddha's name with me, but you absolutely must not harm others," and the person replied, "I will chant Buddha's name with you, I will not harm your relatives, and if anyone outside harms you, I will help you." I laughed again and said, "You must not harm anyone outside, even if they hurt me, that is my own karmic retribution to bear, so don’t do anything to them, okay?" The person onlylaughed and then continued to say, "But when you go home, I won't be able to enter your house because right now you are here, so I can be next to you." Because my house is old and dilapidated, my parents have had to tear it down and rebuild it, for months I have had to stay in a rental house with my younger sister. I still didn't understand why that person said they couldn't enter my house, so I asked them again, "Why can't you enter my house? I see that there are many spirits around my house." The person said, "Because I am a stranger, I cannot enter your house unless everyone there allows it. Do you know why so many can enter your house or not? BecausePeople in the world often buy animals to eat and those animals are not human bodies, but their consciousness is the same as me, and those people transform into dishes so they can enter your house, do you understand what I say?" but I didn't understand that I said, "Then why don't you transform into dishes to enter my house", and the person replied, "I transformed into food for others to eat, I can't protect you because I was the one who was on the body of the person who ate me" and I advised that person, "Before I go home, you have to recite the Buddha with me, you recite"If Buddha comes often and you don’t think about anything at all, he will naturally be able to enter my house," and that person said, "I will recite Buddha’s name along with you, so you can go to sleep now, I’ve disturbed your sleep." At that moment, I opened my eyes and didn’t see that person anywhere. Sometimes I hear the saying that when someone recites Buddha’s name, many benevolent spirits come to protect the practitioner, but many spirits do not like practitioners; sometimes they actively try to harm them. I have seen and experienced this to understand it. Could it be that the young man was a Dharma protector for me? I only needed that person to recite Buddha’s name and pray to Buddha; I did not need that person to help me. A MITA BUDDHA.

Chant together every day

St The Nameless Flower

tieu_de: FIVE GREAT HEART SURANGAMA MANTRA
tom_tat: Following the respect for A ca, he established the Bát rị, caused Nảnh yết rị Chedanim [49] akala mri-tyu pari, traya, na kari [50] === WHY ARE THE FIVE GREAT HEART MANTRAS SO POWERFUL? Elder Master Phổ Quang provided the instruction:
noi_dung:
FIVE GREAT HEART MANTRAS OF THE SURANGAMA [FIVE GREAT HEART SURANGAMA MANTRA]

Sat-da reveres A-ca-ra Mat-ri-stu Bat-ri, produces da Nanh yet-ri Chedanim [49] akala mri-tyu pari, traya, na kari [50] === WHY ARE THE FIVE GREAT HEART MANTRAS SO POWERFUL? Venerable Phổ Quang gave instruction: In the first assembly there is a phrase, “Sat-da reveres, A-ca-da, Mat-ri-stu, Bat-ri dat da ra, Nanh yet-ri.” These are the five great heart mantras of the Five Tathagatas. This mantra is the king of 54 great divine mantras; reciting it is even more effective than reciting the 108-turn Great Compassion Mantra, for reciting the seven turns of the king mantra is superior...... Venerable Tuyên Hóa also gave instruction: These five great heart mantras are encountered only once in hundreds of thousands of eons.It is also possible that you have encountered it countless times over hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, but you cannot know it clearly. These Five Great Heart Mantras are the most revered, the most useful mantras in Buddhism. 'The Five Great Heart Mantras are infinitely wondrous' from 'Tất Ðà Nễ to Nảnh Yết Rị,' these five great heart mantras are incredibly mystical; even if described extensively, it cannot be fully conveyed. Any mantra of heavenly demons, of heretics, of spirits, of monsters, or of heterodox sects can all be dispelled. That is, a mantra that dispels all cannot be dispelled. The mantra dispels heavenly demons and heretics not because it has an intention to oppose them, but rather like practicing Tai Chi, using softness to neutralize hardness. Any mantra, when applied with this heart mantra, will be neutralized.It is allowed, but do not harm the other party. This Great Heart Mantra, why is it called a Heart Mantra? It means it flows from the heart of compassion. Using this Mantra requires using a mind of loving-kindness, joy, and forgiveness, embracing all sentient beings; it is not about saying, 'I recite this Mantra to want to kill you, harm you, or destroy you.' Rather, the power of the Mantra neutralizes all other mantras, just as ice melts into water when exposed to the sun. Originally, mantras of external heretical schools are sustained by a mind of anger. When you recite this Shurangama Mantra, it transforms into something auspicious—this is the wonderful point. It is not that by reciting this Mantra, the other person will inevitably suffer, but that the Shurangama Mantra breaks [negative influences].It dispels all the power of other Mantras, rather than harming anyone. The power of the Mantra comes from the hearts of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and those who chant the Mantra, flowing out as a kind of compassionate mind, therefore it can subdue all heavenly demons and heretics. ____________________ Writer's note: These 5 Great Heart Mantras can break all spells, curses, charms, and sorcery. They can also destroy all kinds of evil, wicked spirits. Everyone should cherish these Heart Mantras. Although it is said that the Mantras have such powers, you should not use them with a mind of anger, competitiveness, desire to win, or hatred to exorcise demons, evil spirits, or ghosts…. Using them with such a mindset will bring consequences to yourself. Chinese Buddhists really like the 5This Great Heart Mantra, besides the full mantra, when walking, standing, lying down, or going to unsafe places, they often silently recite in their mind the 5 Great Heart Mantras. p/s: Please share so that more people can know about it. _Mật Hỷ_

Author: Mật Hỷ

First assembly

1. Nam mas, ta tha ga ta da, su ga ta da, a ro ha te, sam mi ak, sam bu da da

18. Namo, Gochara, Cula da.

23. Namo, ba ga goa te, ak so bi da da, ta tha ga ta da, a ro ha te, sam mi ak, sam bu da da

24. Namo, ba ga goa te, ba sa da, guru, vai dua ri a, pra bo, ra cha da, ta tha ga ta da

28. Tě bi ô, nam mas, Cơ Rít Toa, I Dâm, Bhagavati, Tathagata, Usu Ni Sam, Si Ta Ta Pa Tô Ram, Namo A Para Chi Tâm, Pơ Rát Ti ăng Gi Râm

29. Sa ra goa, bu ta, go ra ha, ni go ra ha ca, ca ra, ha ni pa ra, guyt di a.

30. Che da nim, a ca la, mo rit tiu, pa ri, tra da na, ca rim (Five Great Heart Mantras)

31. Sa ra goa, ban da na, mok sa nim

32. Sa ra goa, du so ta, du hu, so goap na, ni goa ra nim.

33. Cha tu ra si ti nam, go ra ha, sa ha so ra nam, guyt do goam sa na, ca rim

34. At so ta, guym sa ti nam, nack sa, tra nam, po ra sa da na, ca rim

35. At so ta nam, ma ha go ra ha nam, guyt de goam sa na, ca rim

36. Sa re goa, sa to ru, ni goa ra nam.

37. Go ram, du hu, so goap nam, cha na sa nim

38. Guy sa, sa so to ra, ack ni, u da ca, ra nam

39. A pa ra chit ta, go ra, ma ha ba la, chan da, ma ha dip ta, ma ha te cha, ma ha sue ta choa la, ma ha ba la, pan da ra, goa si ni, a ri a ta ra, bo ri cu tim, che va, vi cha da.

40. Goa chờ ra, ma lê ti hi, vi sờ ru ta, pát ma cà ha, goa chờ ra, chi vát, cha ma la, chê va, a pa ra chít ta, goa chờ ra, đan đà hà, guy sa la, cha san ta, suê tê va, pu chít ta, sau ma, rú pà.

41. Ma hà, suê tà, a ri a ta ra, ma hà, ba la a pa ra

42. Goa chờ ra, săm ca la, chê va, goa chờ ra, câu ma ri, cù lâm đà ri

43. Goa chờ ra, ha sờ ta cha, guýt đi a

44. Căn cha na, ma li ca há, cu sum ba ca, rát na há

45. Goa ro cha na, cu li da dà, a rờ tha, u sờ ni sa hà

46. Guy chờ rim ba, ma ni cha, Goa chờ ra, ca na ca, pờ ra bờ, lô cha na

47. Goa chờ ra, tun đì cha, suê tà cha, ca ma la, ắc sa, sà si, pờ ra ba

48. Ít ti, I ti, mu đờ ra, ga na, sa rờ guê, rắc cờ sâm, cơ van tu, I man, ma mà si a

Second session

49. Um, rờ si ga na, pờ ra sa sờ ta, ta tha ga ta, u sờ ni sâm

50. Hum to rum, cham ba na, hum to rum, so tam ba na

51. Hum to rum, pa ra guyt di a, sam ba co sa na, ca ra

52. Hum to rum, sa ro goa, dac co sa, rac co sa sa, go ra ha nam, guyt de goam sa na, ca ra

53. Hum to rum, cha tu ra si ti nam, go ra ha, sa ha so ra nam

54. Hum to rum, rac co sa, rac co sa, mam

55. Ba ga goam, ta tha ga ta, u so ni sam

56. Porattiang Ghi Re, Maha, Saha Sora, Bude, Saha Sora, Sirese, Coti Saha Sora Nete

57. Abel De, Choalita, Tata Ca, Maha, Goa Choro Dara, Tri Bu Goanna, Manda La

58. Um, Sava Soti Ro, Bagoa Tu, Mama, I Man, Mama Si A

Third session

tieu_de: DEBT OF TEARS MUST BE PAID WITH TEARS🍁. (Once you understand cause and effect, you will no longer complain to heaven or blame others
tom_tat: 🙏🙏🙏 🏵️ The Buddha in the scriptures tells us very clearly that relationships within the family, such as husband and wife, parents and children, brothers and sisters in this life, are all relationships of Cause and Karmic Debt with each other. If there is no
noi_dung:
DEBT OF TEARS MUST BE PAID WITH TEARS🍁. (Once you understand cause and effect, you no longer complain to the heavens or blame others)

🙏🙏🙏

🏵️ The Buddha in the Scriptures clearly tells us that relationships within the family, such as husband and wife, parents and children, siblings, in this life, are all relationships of Cause and Effect (Karma) with each other. If there were no Cause-and-Effect relationship, what would happen? Then we would not meet each other.

🏵️ Therefore, we must understand that living together among people, between oneself and others, always involves affinity and fate. In this affinity, there are Good causes and Bad causes.

What is a good cause?

This predestined relationship brings joy and happiness to those involved.

What is an ill-fated relationship?

It is a relationship that only brings suffering and sorrow to those involved.

🏵️ Speaking of Debt means there is repaying debt or collecting debt. In today's society, we can clearly see the phenomenon of debt collection and repayment in marital relationships.

At first, when coming together, wasn't everything very beautiful, but in a short time, things quickly turn, and they break up.

What is the reason?

Debt has been settled; when one of the two has finished collecting the debt, and the other has repaid it, they immediately break up, immediately leave.

🏵️ So what does it mean to come together to collect debt?

This person in the family is often very domineering, doesn't like to work, but enjoys taking pleasure; they do not like their husband or wife to upset them, but they themselves do not really care about the feelings of their husband or wife.

🏵️ If the debt is small, this person will collect the debt in a short time, and once the debt is settled, they will immediately break up and leave. If the debt is large, it may take a lifetime before they are willing to leave.

So what does it mean to be together to pay off a debt?

This person loves and worries greatly, doing everything solely to provide for and serve their husband or wife.

🏵️ Although this person earns money, they do not dare to spend even a single penny on themselves; everything is reserved for their husband or wife.

Where does the fate and debt between husband and wife come from?

It comes from the karmic connections borrowed and repaid from past lives. In a previous life, we may have owed someone, but also had a romantic bond with them, so in this life, that person comes to be our husband or wife to continue the unfinished romance from the past life, and also to settle the debt we owed them.

🏵️ This makes it clear that between people, there is no debt left unpaid; if it is not settled in this life, it will have to be paid in the next life, and if not in the next life, then in the life after that. The novel "Dream of the Red Chamber" expresses this very well:

_ "Debts of tears to others must be repaid with tears."

🏵️ From this, we understand that it is we ourselves who cultivate merit, it is we ourselves who enjoy it; no one can interfere with any stage of our cause-and-effect process.

Now that we understand the true nature of the predestined bonds between husband and wife, in daily family life, the debts we owe should be repaid joyfully, without measuring gains or losses, without clinging to gains or losses.

🏵️Why?

Because knowing that if I don't repay now, I will still have to repay later, if not in this life, then in the next life, so why extend the time to make myself suffer? Just repay happily, once the debt is paid, blessings and peace will immediately come.

🏵️ What about the person who owes me?

I no longer need this debt, I forgive the person completely. Then I will be free and at peace. Some people say:

_ "The debt is because the person owes me, now I forgive them completely, does that mean I am too disadvantaged?"

🏵️ I would like to say that, not only is there no loss, but it is actually a blessing. If we do not let go and are determined in this life to collect a debt from someone, then in the next life we will be the one who has to repay the debt.

We and the debtor repay each other from this life to the next endlessly. This means that we constantly go through the cycle of birth and death only to borrow and repay, repay and borrow again with the same person.

🏵️ Therefore, the gain we get immediately is not enough to make up for what we will lose in the future; this is a very, very great loss.

Amitabha Buddha!

Reference: Dharma words of Dharma Master Chin Kung

tieu_de: EVERY DAY WE MUST ASK OURSELVES: HOW MUCH HAVE WE PREPARED FOR OUR MATTER OF LIFE AND DEATH?
tom_tat: All things and beings in this universe are formed by the combination of causes and conditions. When conditions come together, it is called birth; when conditions disperse, it is called cessation. Coming together and separating happen, birth and death are impermanent. We have the condition to meet each other in one place.
noi_dung:
EVERY DAY WE MUST ASK OURSELVES: HOW MUCH HAVE WE PREPARED FOR OUR LIFE-OR-DEATH MATTER?

All things in the heavens and the universe come into being due to the harmony of causes and conditions. The gathering of conditions is called birth, and the dissolution of conditions is called death. Coming together and breaking apart occurs with the impermanence of birth and death. We have the condition to meet in one place to learn Buddhism, all due to past lives' conditions leading to the present, planting countless causes and conditions of Bodhi. Each of us should skillfully cherish and regret this rare and superior opportunity. Remembering impermanence, skillfully take advantage of the chance to practice learning. One must strive diligently, not slack or be lazy, to achieve in one lifetime the great undertaking of liberation from birth and death.

The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra spoke this verse:

The days now have passed

Life gradually diminishes

Like fish in drying water

What is there to rejoice in?

One must diligently strive

To save the fire burning the oil

Always remember impermanence

Do not be negligent.

Bodhisattva Samantabhadra teaches us to always remember the enemy of impermanence in every moment. Because human life is in each breath, when the breath no longer comes, before the perilous path of samsara, how would one know where to turn?

Every night before going to bed, we need to question our conscience: how much have we prepared today for the great matter of life and death? Or have we wasted the whole day? Life is always changing and unpredictable. Studying Buddhism and reciting the Buddha's name requires preparation, because great and unpredictable disasters can come to us at any time. Therefore, we must proactively prepare for the great matter of life and death for ourselves early.

Excerpt from Lien Tri Canh Sach

Translated by Thich Quang Anh

Source: Tinh Nhi.

tieu_de: VU LAN - REMEMBERING THE DEEP GRATITUDE TO PARENTS
tom_tat: "Monks! There are two people whom you can never fully repay, that is your father and mother. If someone carries their father on the left shoulder, their mother on the right shoulder, travels a thousand miles, provides all kinds of food, clothing, and blankets
noi_dung:
VU LAN - REMEMBERING THE DEEP GRATITUDE TO PARENTS

“Monks! There are two people to whom you can never fully repay your gratitude: father and mother. Even if someone carries their father on the left shoulder and their mother on the right, travels a thousand miles, provides all kinds of food, clothing, bedding, and medicine, and even if the father and mother relieve themselves on their shoulders, it still would not repay the deep gratitude to parents. You should know, the gratitude to parents is very heavy, nursing and raising you at the right time, allowing you to grow up. Therefore, it is hard to repay that gratitude. Thus, a filial child who wants to repay the parents' merit properly according to the true Dharma must practice the following things:

- If parents do not have faith, one must encourage them to develop trust in the Triple Gem.

– If parents are greedy, one must encourage them to cultivate generosity.

– If parents follow evil, one must encourage them to turn towards the good path.

– If parents hold wrong views, one must encourage them to return to right view.

Doing this is repaying parents according to the right Dharma, enabling them not only to be happy in the present but also to sow blessings in the future.”

(The Ekottara Āgama of the Buddhist Canon)

tieu_de: Only those with VIRTUE have BLESSINGS
tom_tat: A person's true temperament is not their beautiful appearance, but the richness of their inner self; the most important thing in a person's life is not wealth, but virtue! A person with morality
noi_dung:
Only those with VIRTUE have BLESSINGS

The true temperament of a person is not their outward beauty, but the richness of their inner self; the most important thing in a person's life is not wealth, but character! A person with virtue is respected wherever they go; a person without virtue is disliked wherever they go.

A virtuous person will surely have blessings! A person's virtue not only encompasses self-cultivation, but also holds the life blessings of a person. Being human must pay attention to one's own morality to truly be virtuous.

Being a person must be kind, kindness is the most beautiful virtue

If asked what is the most beautiful quality in the world, I would definitely say it is kindness. Kindness is the positive energy in the world, it can send warmth and the spring breeze to others, while also making oneself feel at peace.

Peace of mind is the greatest blessing in life, people live their whole lives only seeking peace of mind. In fact, choosing kindness is not for others but for oneself, to be worthy of one's own heart, to keep one's conscience clear and without regret.

People say good people are deceived by others, but I think no matter what, we must maintain our kindness, not lose our goodness because others are not virtuous. Kindness is not wrong, but kindness must have measure, degree, and sharpness.

Being human requires sincerity, and sincerity is the most beautiful quality.

Even if others are not sincere, we must still be sincere, worthy of our own conscience, worthy of our own behavior. Moreover, I think that only by treating everyone sincerely can we receive sincerity from others.

As a person, one must keep their word; trust is the best principle.

A person who does not keep their promises will lose everyone's trust in them, the path ahead will only become narrower, and future luck will gradually disappear. Once trust is used up, it is lost; only by maintaining your own principles can you retain trust for a long time.

Trust is actually luck; the more reliable you are, the more people trust you, the luckier you become. Therefore, the more you keep your word, the luckier you are. Luck is a blessing; the more luck you have, the more blessings you will receive!

A virtuous person will surely have blessings; a person's virtue is contained in their actions.

In fact, we should not consider being human as some kind of profound knowledge; as long as you are the most genuine person, kind, treat others sincerely, and keep your promises, you will be a virtuous and blessed person!

The blessings of life are hidden in your virtue; the deeper your virtue, the greater the reward. Although no one can see the accumulation of virtue, performing good deeds is known to heaven itself; the more good deeds you do, the more virtue you accumulate, and blessings and luck come to you.

tieu_de: EIGHT THINGS WISE PEOPLE ALWAYS KNOW CLEARLY
tom_tat: **************** 1. First point: The wise understand clearly that life is impermanent, nations are inherently not lasting, the four elements are essentially void, the five aggregates have no self, birth and death are ever-changing, and emptiness has no master. The mind is the seed of all
noi_dung:
EIGHT THINGS THE WISE ALWAYS KNOW CLEARLY

****************

1. The first point: The wise know clearly that life is impermanent, nations are inherently not lasting, the four elements are empty, the five aggregates are without self, birth and death change, illusion has no master. The mind is the seed of evil things. The body is the place where sins accumulate. Contemplating in this way, one gradually frees oneself from birth and death.

2. The second point: The wise know clearly that abundant desire is suffering, living and dying is laborious, desire begins from greed, having little desire leads to a life without creating karma, and the body and mind attain freedom.

3. The third point: A wise person clearly understands that the mind is never satisfied, only knowing to desire more, thereby increasing wrongdoing. A bodhisattva is not like this, often remembering to be content, living a simple life to practice virtue, taking wisdom as their vocation.

4. The fourth point: A wise person knows that laziness leads to downfall, so they are often diligent, eliminating evil afflictions, subduing the four demons, and surpassing the bondage of body and mind.

5. Fifth point: The wise know clearly that ignorance is the root of birth and death. Bodhisattvas often remember this carefully, therefore they strive to study broadly and understand deeply, in order to expand and increase wisdom, achieve mastery of skilled teachings, and guide everyone to attain great joy.

6. Sixth point: The wise know clearly that poverty often brings many grievances, easily creating many negative causes. Bodhisattvas often engage in acts of giving, with a mind that is always equal, making no distinction between friends or enemies, not remembering past grudges, and not hating wrongdoers.

7. The seventh principle: The wise understand that the five kinds of pleasures (wealth, physical beauty, fame and gain, food, and sleep) are five sources of sin and five dangers. Therefore, although being worldly, the wise live without being tainted by the pleasures of the world, often reflecting on and relying upon three precious things (Buddha as the clear mind, Dharma as the true mind, Sangha as the pure mind). The wise have the aspiration to become monastic, maintain a pure path, practice high virtue, and show compassion to all beings.

8. Eighth: The wise know clearly that life and death are like blazing flames, suffering is endless; therefore, they develop a vast mind, to save all beings. They vow on behalf of sentient beings, to endure infinite suffering, so that sentient beings may ultimately attain peace and joy.

A DI ĐÀ PHẬT_/_

St Van Anh Nguyen

tieu_de: Depending on the affinity when reciting the Ling Nhiem mantra at home
tom_tat: 1. Whether to eat vegetarian or meat when chanting mantras depends on circumstances, as there is no specific rule. Because Devadatta once advocated vegetarianism, but the Buddha refused, as it did not represent all the capacities of sentient beings.
noi_dung:
DEPENDING ON CONDITIONS WHEN CHANTING THE LANG NGHIEM MANTRA AT HOME

1. Whether to eat vegetarian or non-vegetarian food while chanting mantras should depend on the circumstances, as there is no specific rule. Devadatta once advocated for vegetarianism, but the Buddha refused, because it did not represent all the capacities of sentient beings, and in many places grains could not be grown, making vegetarianism impossible. However, Mahayana Buddhism encourages vegetarianism. So, we should adapt this practice appropriately to the situation. We should not, from one perspective, criticize another aspect and thereby interrupt the karmic connection of sentient beings practicing the Shurangama mantra.

2. Depending on conditions, either silently recite or chant aloud. The purpose of reciting or maintaining a mantra is to bind the mind in one place, no longer chasing external circumstances, no longer thinking of good or evil. This is called the state of Supreme Non-Attachment. From this state emerge countless merits or mysteries. At home, if everyone is sleeping but you chant loudly, it may bother the beings around. Then when at the temple, if everyone loudly recites the Lankavatara mantra, murmuring it quietly in your mouth is no longer appropriate. Practicing Buddhism only requires understanding the four words 'Act According to Conditions and Respond Accordingly,' similar to how the Buddha behaved daily.

3. If the house has a solemn altar, then pay attention to the solemn aspect when reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. If the living conditions do not have an altar and the surroundings are cluttered, then recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra focusing mainly on inner concentration. Practice according to your own circumstances.

4. Those who are free can recite more, while those who are busy can recite a little less, so as to balance daily life with work and necessities. You can recite at any time of the day. It is not necessary to wake up at 4 AM like the monks in the temple. As long as you are consistent, it is fine. You should not force yourself too hard just to imitate someone else.

5. Being single and reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra is fine, and having a family and reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra is also fine. One should not have an extreme thought that reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra destroys sexual desire, invites demons, or causes family discord. After 1975, many historical events forced monks to return to lay life, and they later had wives and children, even though they recited the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra every day. If I recite the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra but my mind keeps chasing worldly desires, then no mantra can truly eliminate sexual desire. It’s just that the karma of ignorance gradually dissipates over time, wisdom arises, and enlightenment comes slowly. Therefore, it cannot be blamed that reciting the LN mantra causes couples to be distant, and there is no ghost idly following you either.

I constantly hear myself chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra to avoid headaches, so don’t be afraid of ghosts disturbing you.

tieu_de: Self-Cultivation Policy
tom_tat: 1. Studying Buddhism is to correct oneself, not to correct others. [Venerable Thich Tinh Khong] 2. Knowing one's own mistakes is enlightenment, correcting one's own mistakes is practice. [Venerable Thich Tinh Khong]
noi_dung:
SELF-DISCIPLINE POLICY

1. Studying Buddhism is to correct yourself, not to correct others. [Venerable Tinh Khong]

2. Realizing your own mistakes is enlightenment; correcting your mistakes is cultivation. [Venerable Tinh Khong]

3. Benefiting others is good, benefiting yourself is evil. [Venerable Trung Phong]

4. Hurting others is misfortune, others hurting us is a blessing. [Ancients]

5. In favorable circumstances, remember the impermanence; in adverse circumstances, contemplate cause and effect. [Ancients]

6. Circumstances themselves are neither good nor bad; goodness and badness arise from the mind. [Master Ngẫu Ích]

7. The fool changes circumstances but not the mind; the wise change the mind but not the circumstances. [Master Ngẫu Ích]

8. A genuinely virtuous practitioner does not see the faults of the world. [Master Huệ Năng]

9. Compassion has no enemies; wisdom does not give rise to afflictions. [Venerable Thánh Nghiêm]

10. Examine yourself with a mind of humility, and view the world with a mind of gratitude. [Venerable Thánh Nghiêm]

11. Gratitude can help us grow, repayment of kindness can help us achieve. [Venerable Thánh Nghiêm]

12. How others treat us is the result of our own karma; how we treat others is our own cultivation. [Anonymous]

13. Use your mind to reproach yourself when reproaching others, use your mind to forgive yourself in order to forgive others. [Phạm Thuần Nhân]

14. Let go of your own afflictions and accumulated tendencies, go along with the afflictions and accumulated tendencies of others. [Venerable Tịnh Không]

15. Only require yourself to be sincere and harmonious with others, never require others to be harmonious with you. [HT. Tịnh Không]

16. Regardless of whether others fully fulfill their duties to us or not, we must fully fulfill our duties to them. [Master Yin Guang]

tieu_de: FORTUNE COMES FROM 1️⃣0️⃣ SMALL HABITS
tom_tat: 1️⃣. Every morning when waking up, one should offer a cup of clean water to the Buddha; over time, merits increase, wealth arises, and misfortunes are removed. 2️⃣. Before leaving the house, one should bow to the Buddha three times; by doing so, one will be safe and peaceful.
noi_dung:
BLESSINGS COME FROM 1️⃣0️⃣ SMALL HABITS

1️⃣. Every morning upon waking up, one should offer the Buddha a cup of clean water; over time, virtue will grow, wealth will arise, and misfortunes will be eliminated.

2️⃣. Before leaving the house, one should bow to the Buddha three times; if done, you will be safe. When returning, wash your hands and face and bow to the Buddha three times. At minimum, each day you should bow to the Buddha six times, which amounts to 2,190 bows a year. By doing so, good appearances will arise, and you will cultivate complete humility.

3️⃣. When going out, whether riding a motorbike or walking, every time you pass by Buddha statues, monks or nuns, and temples, you should bow your head to show respect to the Triple Gem. The Lotus Sutra, in the Chapter on Skillful Means, says: “Even just a slight bow of the head will lead to Buddhahood.”

4️⃣. Always set aside a little money to give alms to beggars. If you encounter stones, branches, screws, or anything that blocks the path and endangers others, you should resolve to move them to a safe place.

5️⃣. If you see animals that are captured and confined along the road, you should buy them to release them.

6️⃣. If one does not have money to release animals, one should recite Buddha's name for the animals that are imprisoned or killed along the way, dedicating the merit so that in their next life they are born as humans and meet the Buddha's teachings sooner.

7️⃣. One should sprinkle sugar, candy, or cakes to give alms to ants, or scatter rice for birds to eat. In the garden, if harvesting crops, a little should be left for the animals. If one does not form good relations with sentient beings, in the future one's enlightenment cannot help others, because "Buddha transforms those with causes and conditions."

8️⃣. When offering to the Buddha, you should use the best items. Avoid the future blessings being flawed due to offering poor-quality items.

9️⃣. Each time before eating rice or any pure food, you should first make the intention to offer it to the Three Jewels before eating.

1️⃣0️⃣. Before going to sleep, you should recite the Buddha's name 10 times and dedicate the merit, wishing to be reborn in the Western Pure Land.

It is worth thinking that small evils accumulate into great evils, so do not underestimate small evils and consider them guiltless. For a small hole can sink a ship. And a person who moves a large mountain does so by removing small stones one by one. Therefore, do not look down on small acts of kindness and neglect to do them. Because small acts of kindness gradually accumulate into great blessings. One does not need money to practice generosity or make offerings. The greatest generosity is to "abandon greed, anger, and ignorance."

Thich Nhu Dung

tieu_de: Recently, many people have been saying. Next year the economy will be even more in recession.
tom_tat: Recently, many people have been saying that next year the economy will worsen, and the economy might collapse. How did you feel after hearing that? Feeling a crisis, fear. How did I feel after hearing it? Helpless, excited.
noi_dung:
RECENTLY MANY PEOPLE SAY. NEXT YEAR THE ECONOMY WILL RECESS FURTHER.

Recently, many people have been saying that next year the economy will deteriorate further, and the economy might collapse. How do you feel after hearing that? Feeling crisis, fear. How do I feel after hearing it? Irresistible, prosperity is also irresistible, recession is also irresistible, the mind is calm. How should one live? The Buddha teaches us to cultivate merit.

As long as we have blessings, when we are prosperous we have blessings, and when in decline we still have blessings; not knowing how to cultivate blessings is wrong. Therefore, when we have strength, we should strive to cultivate blessings. You will then know that a blessed person, even when going to Avīci hell, still enjoys blessings. This is all telling you the true reality; if you do not understand or believe this, then there is no remedy. It is essential to cultivate blessings.

How does one cultivate merit? By giving alms. Do not wait until your finances collapse, until those piles of stocks turn into worthless paper, then you won't be able to cultivate merit—it would be truly regrettable. You must seize the opportunity and cultivate merit in a timely manner, so that the rewards of merit can be fully enjoyed. The Buddha's words to us are all the true reality.

- Venerable Master Jingkong.

tieu_de: TOI THANG DANG VUONG DA RA NI (THOSE WHO HAVE STRONG SEXUAL DESIRES SHOULD READ THIS ARTICLE)
tom_tat: This charm is indeed used to bring peace to the house, or sincerely read to pray before renovating the house to be safe. 1. Uses
noi_dung:
TÔI THẮNG ĐĂNG VƯƠNG ĐÀ RA NI (THOSE WHO HAVE STRONG SEXUAL DESIRES SHOULD READ THIS ARTICLE)

This mantra is indeed used to bring peace to the house, or sincerely recited to pray before renovating the house to ensure safety and well-being.

1. Uses

This mantra brings many benefits, making beings peaceful through the long night, gaining great auspicious advantages, beauty, health, and honor.

2. Reciting the mantra: You can walk around the land reciting this mantra 108 times or 3-7 times depending on whether the land is large or small.

3. Mantra recitation ritual

3.1. Purification of the Dharma Realm and Purification of the Three Actions

– Mantra for Purification of the Dharma Realm: Om lam sho ha. (3 times)

– Mantra for Purification of the Three Actions: Om ta pha ba pha, tru da ta pha, dat ma ta pha, ba pha tru do ham. (3 times)

3.2. Vow of Incense Offering

May I offer with sincere devotion

Sent along with the cloud of incense

Lingering throughout the ten directions

To make offerings to the Three Jewels.

Vow to keep the Way for life

Follow the nature to do good

Together with all sentient beings in the Dharma realm

Completely fulfill the Buddha Way.

If you do not recite in front of the altar and do not burn incense, you may omit this part. Read the part below:

Incense Vow:

Precept Incense, Wisdom Incense, and Concentration Incense

Liberation, Liberation of Seeing-Knowing Incense

Namo, clear in the cloud tower, Seeing the Dharma Realm

Offering to the Supreme Buddha of the ten directions.

3.3. Reciting the Tối Thắng Đăng Vương Mantra (reciting once counts as one recitation per day; the more you recite, the better, depending on your available time)

Ta đi a tha, ba rê, chu rê, chu rê, chu rê, rê, sa ma thê, ma ha, sa ma thê, sa măn tê, ma ha, sa măn tê, sâm rê, sa ra lê, sờ voa ha.

(tadyathā pare jure jure jure re ṣamathe maha ṣamathe samante maha samante saṃre sarale svāhā).

3.4. Dedication of Merit

May we dedicate this merit

Eradicate past karma

Increase virtues and blessings

Perfectly accomplish the roots of holiness

All karma of desire

All karma of anger and delusion

Including the karma of body, speech, and mind

All entirely destroyed, no longer remaining

Relatives together attain Peace

Enemies return to Nirvana

Together with all sentient beings in the Dharma realm

Completely attain Buddhahood.

4. Meaning

The Buddha told Ananda: "If you enter a place of robbers, you should recite this mantra. If you enter a fiery place and want to reach the king's palace, you should also recite this mantra. If faced with all kinds of struggles, diseases, or frightening situations, you should remember to recite this mantra."

Or there are kings, enemies, water, fire. Or Heaven, Dragons. Or Yaksha, or Pula, or Bhuta, or Pisacha, or Hungry Ghosts, or Gandhāra Ghosts, or Madman Ghosts, or ghosts that disturb the human mind, or Pathway Ghosts, or Initiating Ghosts, or ghosts that absorb human vital energy.

Or ghosts that cause illness for one day, two days, three days, four days at a time. Or the sun, moon, stars, lions, tigers, leopards, poisonous snakes, wolves, dogs, or bats, or humans or Non-Humans… going to cause harm (making) fear, that does not happen.

Hey Ananda! If there are Bhikkhus, Bhikkhunis, virtuous men, virtuous women... if they uphold, recite, write, explain, and widely propagate this Dharani verse, then fire cannot burn, water cannot drown, swords cannot injure, poisons cannot harm, and they will not be afflicted by demonic forces.

If you use this Charm to tie a rope, and tie it on a dry tree while praying for mercy and help, the tree will bear flowers and fruits again, let alone for a human. (That is, practicing this method can help a person who is about to die to live, have children, or recover from illness). Only except for Karma from previous lives that has already determined the Resulting Retribution (when it is time to die, it cannot be saved).

Hey Ananda! If at the three times: early morning (Mao hour), midday (Ngo hour), and dusk (Dau hour) one chants and practices without abandoning it, then heavy sins become light. If there are capital offenses and one is punished with a beating… (imprisonment) will immediately cease. Those who deserve to be beaten or reprimanded will immediately cease. If there is something to be wished for, it will be immediately fulfilled. By the power of this Mantra, one is protected and guarded by the Buddhas and sages.

In particular, this Mantra can resolve issues for those who have karma of sexual desire or lust, intentions of adultery, or diseases related to vital energy (reproductive), or who have obstructive karma caused by Mantras with too much power that lead to vengeful spirits or celestial demons disrupting and hindering the practitioner's spiritual path. The purpose of the Supreme Victor Lamp King Tathagata is to enable monks or Buddhists in the human realm to live peacefully and not be affected by such obstacles!

Moreover, Bodhisattvas over many lifetimes accumulate Merit by reciting this Mantra for 7 days. Anyone who sincerely recites this Mantra for 7 days can eradicate hundreds of thousands of lifetimes of committing unwholesome deeds, 10 evil deeds, 5 heinous actions such as hitting one's father, killing one's mother, slandering the Buddha and Dharma... It can also help parents, siblings, and relatives avoid misfortunes and decline.

As Venerable Tuyen Hoa taught, if someone wants to recite mantras such as the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, the Bảo Khiếp Ān Dhā Raṇī, or all mantras that require a mandala such as the Ngữ Đàn Mantra, Tâm Tưởng Mandala, and Ān Mandala, but does not know the Esoteric Methods, they should follow the method below. Then, at will, a mandala can be formed, and after that, recite any deity mantra they wish:

– Úm phạ nhật ra đà đổ một. (7 times)

– Úm lam xóa ha. (7 times)

– Úm hạ hồng. (7 times)

Pray that everyone who reads this article will receive many benefits and a complete period of practice in the Buddha's path

Those who have strong sexual desires, through the power of the mantra, will gradually eliminate lust and move toward a joyful, pure life!

tieu_de: WAIT FOR THE FRUIT TO RIPEN
tom_tat: (Source: Eliminating Lust 1, Confessions of an anonymous friend sent to young people nowadays) Mantra for eliminating lust:
noi_dung:
WAIT FOR THE FRUIT TO RIPEN

(Source: Eliminating Lust 1, Confessions of an anonymous friend sent to young people today)

Mantra to eliminate lust:

Supreme Victory King Dharani

1. Ta đi a tha, ba rê, chu rê, chu rê, chu rê

2. rê, sa ma thê, ma ha sa ma thê, sa măn tê

3. ma ha sa măn tê, sâm rê, sa ra lê, soa ha

_________________________

For those of you determined to exhort, even swear to the Buddhas, but still cannot overcome desires and continue to relapse, I advise that you masturbate once a day, so that when the time of fruition comes, you'll stop at the right moment. It's very effective; you won't dare to relapse, only that, by then, your life will be ruined.

I used to be someone who had everything in hand, tasted success, honor, abundant finances, so my mind became arrogant. And then, because I could not overcome desire, I sinned continuously for nearly three months. And what had to happen eventually happened: work stalled, superiors and colleagues suddenly misunderstood, oppressed, despised, and tried to ruin me to the point of losing my job. Coincidentally, the side job that provided my main income also immediately went dark in that very month. After that turning point, I stopped committing sexual misconduct immediately. I didn't even dare to let my thoughts wander on lustful fantasies. Truly astonishing. So it is indeed the karma of desire.Lust and arrogance can together cooperate with each other, like two swords joining to produce a 'remarkable result' like that.

Actually, the unfortunate and humiliating things that happened to me are not necessarily bad. As the elders say, bitter medicine cures illness. This was a 'habit' that had formed for more than ten years, and now it has been cured, which is truly something to be glad about.

I realize that I am very lucky to have bit into this "fruit," even though every day I wash my face with tears because of sorrow and humiliation. Why lucky? Because I could be some star who ended up in prison and, after serving the sentence, was deported, despised by my own nation and many people in the world; I could be a pleasure-seeker who died burned painfully in some karaoke bar, in panic, surrounded by thick darkness, with skin burnt and peeling in the final moments; or simply I could lie covered in sores, carrying the disease of the century, with pain like torment until my last breath. So, just losing the sourceA stable income and job to have the opportunity to live as a real person, with a bright and open future, isn't that too cheap a price?

To the young people who keep relapsing 'regularly.' I understand you very well. We can never stop ourselves once desire has arisen. What we can do is only try to prevent it from appearing in the first place. Every time someone expresses that they have just relapsed, I become worried for them, because who knows the next day, the next week, or the next month, when the unexpected consequence will arise, and you won’t be able to withstand it like the unfortunate ones? Who knows whether your consequence will be heavy or light, who knows if you will still have the chance to start over like I did?

Everyone in the group gives advice, threats, and complaints. But in reality, in this world, there is only you. When you lose your job, they won't come and offer you a job; when you run out of money, no one will lend you money. No one can recite Buddha's name for you, no one can repent for you, no one can contemplate impurity for you. When you are in pain, it is only yourself; when you are tired, it is only yourself; when poor, humiliated, and shamed, it is only you who knows. Even if others know or can empathize, that is all; no one can be in pain for you or be exhausted for you. You also cannot always rely on others continuously.ask for advice, a method that you yourself already know the answer to.

There is a foreign account (seemingly from China) that said in a group that young people in their country work very hard, studying day and night, and don’t even have time to sleep, let alone masturbate. I was skeptical, so I searched on TikTok for the phrase "Study Motivation Douyin" and found that it was indeed true; these are all extremely inspiring videos, which you should watch every day instead of adult websites. And when compared with Japan, where the rate of young people being "Hikikomori" or "NEET" (people in their teens/20s/30s/40s who stay at home, disconnected from society, unemployed, relying on elderly parents) can be seen, one can realize, a countryA country can become powerful or devastated mainly from the immoral bricks built by the youth.

I used to indulge myself, neglect abstinence, and be lazy in studying and working for a long time due to laziness and lack of motivation.

Until one day,

I realized that while I was feeling bored and gradually giving up, my parents were still trying tirelessly day by day FOR ME.

Actually, my parents are no longer healthy, it's just that they never said that because earning money is hard, they wouldn't earn it, so we also do not have the right to say that we're tired and will give up.

If any of you under 20 have known this group, then I congratulate you.

If any of you under 25, I also congratulate you, you still have a chance to start over, though it will be more difficult, because you have to start entering society now.

If you are currently nearing 30, I will no longer congratulate you, I will seriously tell you to stop immediately and be strong.

If you are over 35, I can only sigh, telling you, it's late, but well, do as much as you can.

If you are over 40, I want to ask you, what does the taste of a lifetime of unachieved goals, living half-alive and half-dead feel like, and are you still planning to masturbate, because I haven't reached that age yet and want to ask for your experience.

So, each passing day, the chances for us to start over become fewer, each passing day brings us closer to the day we "enter the furnace." Opportunities and blessings are both limited. So should one quit now, or wait until your life turns as miserable as mine and the older generation before you to finally quit?

Your parents, us, and this country are all counting on you.

Make an effort, teenagers!

tieu_de: PURE LOVE VS IMPURE LOVE
tom_tat: PURE LOVE VS IMPURE LOVE When you love someone, it is important to examine whether your love is pure or impure. If you only care about your own happiness
noi_dung:
PURE LOVE VS IMPURE LOVE

PURE LOVE VS IMPURE LOVE

When you love someone, it is important to examine whether your love is pure or impure. If you are only concerned with your own happiness and expect others to make you happy, this kind of love will turn into jealousy and possession, and then will become suffering for both people.

Pure love is when you do not care about your own happiness; your only concern is the happiness of the person you love, and [wish] that that person is healthy and happy no matter what happens to you. At that time, your love is selfless love.

What if the person you love does not often appreciate your selfless love? Verse sixteen in the Thirty-seven Practices of a Bodhisattva says that

"Although the person whom we care for and love as a child regards us as an enemy, treat that person like a kind mother loves her sick child. That is the bodhisattva practice." Therefore, if someone you love does not act properly, you should still take care of that person, as you would care for a sick child, and trust in karma. If you do not do this, doubt will enter your mind, destroy the love you have for that person, and ruin your bodhi mind.

If your love is pure, then you will want your friend to do whatever makes them happy, and you will support them without attachment or expectation. This kind of relationship is stable.

Excerpt from the book “Chenrezig – The Compassionate Mother Protecting from Eight Fears” by Garchen Rinpoche

Vietnamese translation by KOD

Source: Garchen Vietnam - Drikung Garchen Phuntsok Choling

--------------------

English

When you love someone, it’s important to examine whether your love is pure or impure. If you only care about your own happiness and expect the other person to make you happy, then this kind of love will turn into jealousy and possessiveness, resulting in suffering for both of you. Pure love is when you are not concerned about your own happiness; your only concern is the happiness of your friend, wishing for her to be well and happy no matter what happens to you. Then your love is altruistic.

What if the person you love doesn’t always appreciate your selfless love? Verse sixteen in The Thirty-seven Bodhisattva Practices says:

Even if someone you have cared for as dearly as your own child considers you an enemy, love that person even more, just as a mother would her sick child. This is the practice of a bodhisattva.

So, if the person you love doesn’t act properly, care for him anyway, just like for a sick child, trusting in karma. If you don’t do that, doubts will enter your mind, spoil the love you have for this person, and destroy your bodhicitta. If your love is pure, you want your friend to do whatever makes him happy, and you support him without attachment or expectation. This kind of relationship is stable. Extracted from the book “Tara Who Protects From The Eight Fears” by Garchen Rinpoche

tieu_de: If you choose the right teacher, your intellect will become brighter, and your mind will become more peaceful.
tom_tat: If you choose the wrong teacher, your mind will become increasingly confused, dark, and your heart increasingly anxious and troubled. 🌷If you follow the right path, you will increasingly know understanding and compassion.
noi_dung:
If you choose the right master, your intellect will become increasingly bright, and your mind increasingly peaceful.

If you choose the wrong teacher, your mind will become more confused, dark, and your heart increasingly anxious and troubled.

🌷If you practice on the right path, you will increasingly understand and be tolerant.

If you practice on the wrong path, there will be more struggles and conflicts.

🌷If you act according to the right teachings, you will increasingly become liberated, peaceful, and compassionate.

If you act according to the wrong teachings, you will increasingly become rigid, aggressive, and stubborn.

🌷If you know how to protect your body and mind from Wealth, Beauty, Fame, Food, and Leisure, no one can tempt you.

If you use greed, anger, and ignorance to help life, you are only opening the way for the karmic consequences and conditions of suffering to arise.

🌷If you take other people's matters to judge right-wrong or criticize good-bad, claiming that you are helping them understand the issue clearly, it is like gathering garbage into your house and saying that you are cleaning the environment!

🌷As human beings, if you need peace and happiness, others do too; corresponding realms will understand and empathize with you.

Higher realms will support you if you have a kind heart.

But lower realms will wait for an opportunity to disturb you if you are careless. Therefore, do not sow thoughts that disturb the peace and happiness of others if you do not want to fall into realms lower than human.

🌷Intentional actions lead to karma; what you receive today is the result of past seeds you have sown, and what you are releasing into the world, you will receive in the future, even if it is just a thought.

A hundred years living between heaven and earth

How difficult it is to become a virtuous person

Only when the heart is full of love

Can one pass through the ordinary paths of the world

Everyone eventually wants peace

Because not knowing the way, life is full of hardships

Chasing after distant things

Even if satisfied, life is still uneasy!

When the heart knows how to separate from desire

Knowing to stay away from temptation - happiness clearly appears!

Trúc Lan Nhã.

tieu_de: MASTER  AN QUANG: MIND-OPENING TEACHING
tom_tat: Whether one is a lay practitioner or ordained, one must respect those above and harmonize with those below, endure what others find difficult to endure, do what others find hard to do, and take on arduous tasks on behalf of others, accomplishing them.
noi_dung:
MASTER AN QUANG: GUIDANCE

Whether one practices Buddhism at home or in monastic life, one must be respectful to those above and harmonious with those below, endure what others find difficult to endure, do what others find difficult to do, take on arduous tasks for others, and accomplish good deeds for others.

When sitting in meditation, often reflect on your own faults. During casual conversation, do not speak of others' wrongdoings.

When walking, standing, lying down, sitting, dressing, from morning to evening, and from evening to morning, continuously recite the Buddha’s name: either aloud or silently.

Besides reciting Buddha's name, do not arise any other thoughts. If deluded thoughts arise, they must be immediately abandoned.

Always have a sense of shame and a mind of repentance.

If you have practiced, you should understand that your cultivation is still shallow and should not be proud or boastful.

You should only take care of your own household, and not involve yourself in others' matters.

You should only focus on beautiful forms, and not set your eyes on ugly and corrupt forms.

Consider everyone as a Bodhisattva, and oneself as merely a mortal.

If one can cultivate according to the practices mentioned above, one will surely be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss!

Master Yin Guang

Namo Amitabha Buddha.

tieu_de: PREDISPOSED DESTINY
tom_tat: (NEWLY TRANSLATED ARTICLE NOT PUBLISHED - please do not change the title when sharing) PREDETERMINED FATE OF RELATIONSHIPS
noi_dung:
PREDICTED FATE TRANSFER

(NEW TRANSLATION NOT YET PUBLISHED - please do not change the title when sharing)

PREDICTED FATE IN RELATIONSHIPS

Original Chinese text: Diệu Đạo

Vietnamese translation: Hạnh Đoan

Marriage truly is arranged by destiny, but I avoided an unfavorable fate by using Buddhist practices to transform it.

I began to believe in and study Buddhism on the 1st day of the first lunar month in 2015.

Eight months later, I met my Master and practiced according to his guidance. At that time, my Master transmitted to me some dharma, emphasizing that "if in the future I encounter any spirit-related matters, I only need to recite the Heart Mantra of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara: Om Mani Padme Hūm."

I always keep it in my heart and recite the Avalokiteshvara mantra very many times every day. Today, I would like to write a piece to recount the story I personally experienced.

About 10 years ago, my grandfather was very skilled and accurate in fortune-telling. Therefore, he predicted my fate and looked into my marriage prospects.

My grandfather said that my future husband was one year younger than me, but he said that my marriage would be very problematic, so he did not approve and was not happy.

In 2013, I met another prophet, who told me that my "white horse prince" husband would appear in 2014. But after I left, they secretly told my friends: "Diệu Đạo's marriage will be very bad, but she doesn't have to worry about money, she just needs to do a lot of good deeds and it'll be OK."

By 2014, indeed I met a man who was a year younger than me, we had matching and similar points up to 99%. To the extent that everyone around admired and said we were a very beautiful couple.

But strangely, the moment I met this guy, I only wanted to scold him in my heart.

He is a talented journalist, currently surrounded by many women, so he is like a butterfly fluttering among thousands of flowers, with a personality that appears savvy and bold… Yet strangely, the moment he met me, he suddenly became so timid that he couldn’t utter a single word, and turned into someone seemingly naive and foolish… whenever he was beside me.

Every time he enthusiastically talked or spoke, I felt annoyed and displeased! Because of that, I deleted contact with him twice, and he always tried to reconnect.

Over time, he kept going like that, letting everyone laugh at him for chasing after me only to end up facing harsh rejection, yet he remained patient, trying to stay in touch with me to the point where it was hard for me to find fault with him.

Then, I attended a hypnosis session and saw my past life. If what happened in the past was correct, I could explain why, the first time I met him, I became angry and raised all my claws in a challenge… and why, when he first saw me, his attitude was like a mouse facing a cat, terrified to the point of trembling but unable to leave me and walk away.

During that hypnosis session, I saw myself as a young woman from Guangxi.

Scene one: My fiancé wanted to go abroad to study something, so I went to the riverbank to see him off. After the boat had gone far, I turned back and encountered a pair of eyes full of hatred and resentment… belonging to a strange man in the forest.

Scene two: He raped me, and I became pregnant.

Scene three: After my family learned about it, they felt very ashamed, so they drowned me in the river to die. Although my fiancé witnessed this scene, he simply waved his sleeve and left, believing that I was a fiancée to be discarded.

Scene four: After I was drowned in the river... the rapist also jumped into the river, I don't know if it was because he wanted to save me. But he died for love, he also sank into the river, holding my body in his arms and said: "In the next life, we will live together."

I think the reason he could never forget me and was so loyal, unwilling to give up, was mainly because of the POWER OF THE CURSE HE SPOKE BEFORE DYING: "I hope we can live together in the next life"... therefore, I extremely did not want to have any contact with him.

There was a time when I avoided that journalist like crazy, but later, through studying Buddhist teachings, I realized that fate can be transformed; just like Liufan, he was also able to change his own destiny through cultivation and accumulating merits. If he could do it, then I could do it too.

Thinking this way, I expressed my thoughts to Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, I said that I did not want the journalist to die because of me, and I absolutely did not want to marry him. I even promised: When I achieve cultivation, I will save him.

So every month I began releasing life and reciting the Avalokiteshvara heart mantra daily, dedicating the merit to all beings with whom I have affinity (of course, including him).

At the end of 2015, I prayed to the Bodhisattva to see the vision of the future of me and him. I dreamed of the future scenario: we would still have to live together as husband and wife, so I continued to follow the guidance of the virtuous mentors.

1. I observe the five precepts; at first, I only practiced them physically, but gradually I also maintained them in my thoughts. The practice process is indeed arduous, difficult, and full of suffering. Because even impure thoughts of lust must absolutely not arise.

2. Besides setting aside 5% of my salary each month for releasing animals, I also participate in many other charitable deeds.

3. I often contemplate my mind, striving each day to control my thoughts, avoiding selfishness and self-interest, not living only for myself, but thinking and acting in ways that benefit all sentient beings.

4. I recite the Avalokitesvara Heart Mantra five thousand times every day; there were times when I increased it to twenty to thirty thousand times (two or three hundred thousand) per day, and I also recited the Buddha Mother Heart Mantra.

As for other small, detailed acts of goodness, I won’t bother to mention them.

In 2016, my appearance began to change. First, my nose became higher, my eyes bigger, and my mouth smaller (no longer that big wide mouth). Everyone kept praising how my features had miraculously transformed into beauty.

At the end of 2016, I prayed to the Bodhisattva, asking if the karmic bond that tied me and the journalist had finally ended. If it had, or if it hadn’t, I asked to be shown precise evidence.

That night, I dreamed of meeting another strange man. The next morning, I knelt before the Bodhisattva and wondered… not knowing what was happening?

At night, I would dream of the scene: Ten years later, I was sitting face to face with my spouse. Anyway, I felt relieved because it wasn’t that journalist. But since I was still curious to know the traits of my new husband to verify, on the third night, I dreamed of his name.

At the beginning of 2017, through another fortune teller, I learned that the remaining fate between me and the journalist was fragile; I only needed to diligently recite around one hundred thousand (100,000) mantras to eliminate the obstacles and it would be fine.

As a result, on April 1, 2017, he got married, finding new happiness. It was only then that I could breathe a sigh of relief. Under the blessings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, I finally successfully severed the ill-fated bond between him and me!

I think this story may help brothers and sisters who are studying Buddhism to increase their faith. Therefore, after seeking advice from wise and virtuous teachers, I was permitted to write down and share my experience. I hope that after reading it, you will know how to cultivate and increase merit, correct your mind, practice self-improvement… so that you can transform your destiny for the better.

(Hạnh Đoan - Translated from the Taiwan Buddhist Research Network)

—————

(1) Heart Mantra of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. 觀音心咒:

Sanskrit pronunciation: Om Mani Padme Hūm

Vietnamese pronunciation: Án ma ni bát di hồng
