tieu_de: BUDDHA PAGODA CEREMONY TO SAVE MOTHER FROM HELL
tom_tat: During the Tang Dynasty, there was a man with the surname Pham, whose mother was Madam Vuong, who completely did not believe in the Three Jewels. Although he had advised her many times, his mother would not listen. Later, he went to the Eastern Capital to study under Lawyer Chi Khanh at the Q Temple.
noi_dung:
BUDDHA TOWER CEREMONY TO SAVE MOTHERS FROM HELL

During the Tang Dynasty, there was a man surnamed Pham, whose mother was Madam Vuong and completely did not believe in the Triple Gem. Although he repeatedly tried to persuade her, his mother refused to listen. Later, he went to the Eastern Capital to follow Lawyer Chi Khanh at Quang Ai Pagoda, became a monk, and took the Dharma name Tu Lan.

When Master Tử Lân returned to his hometown, his mother had passed away three years earlier. On the occasion of visiting the temple dedicated to Đông Nhạc Đại Đế, Master Tử Lân sincerely recited the Lotus Sutra there, wishing to meet Nhạc Đế to ask which realm his mother had been reborn into after death. One night, he dreamed of Nhạc Đế appearing and said: "Your mother is currently in hell, enduring immense suffering. You should go to Mậu Mountain and pay respect at the stupa of King Ashoka there; through that merit, you may be able to save your mother." Master Tử Lân then followed the instructions to worship King Ashoka's stupa. There, he wept and prayed, performing the long ceremony. Suddenly, he heard his mother’s voice giving thanks, saying: "Thanks to your prayers, I have now been reborn.ascend to the heavenly realm of Devas.

*************************

More than a hundred years after the Buddha entered Nirvana, King Ashoka was born. He was a Wheel-Turning King who governed a realm of Jambudvipa and had the ability to command spirits and gods. The king built 84,000 stupas to enshrine and venerate 84,000 relics left by the Buddha. According to the king's division, a stupa would be built for every 100,000 people. In China, according to the records seen in books, there were a total of 19 stupas. The stupa at Mao Mountain is one of them.

tieu_de: DEDICATION OF MERIT IS THE ONLY WAY TO DISSOLVE THE ENMITY BETWEEN US AND ALL OUR DEBTORS AND SPIRITS OF GRUDGE.
tom_tat: In the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, in the chapter on Pure and Bright Repentance, there is a saying: 'One worldly being's karmic conditions endure for a hundred thousand kalpas, always existing in birth and death.'
noi_dung:
DEDICATING MERIT IS THE ONLY PATH TO RESOLVE KARMIC BONDS BETWEEN US AND ALL OUR DEBTORS AND ENEMIES.

In the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, in the chapter on Pure and Bright Repentance, there is a saying:

"A single worldly cause and condition lasts for hundreds of thousands of kalpas, always in birth and death."

This means that in a previous life, I owed someone, and in this life, that person comes to collect, so I am obliged to repay the debt. However, this debt is not simply settled once it is paid off. Why? Because when repaying a debt, it's rarely exactly the same amount—either a little less or a little more. If I pay a little less, then in the next life I must continue repaying the debt. If I pay a little more, then in the next life I will come to collect again. Therefore, the relationship between myself and all sentient beings is one of endless debts through countless lifetimes; this is the truth. It is precisely because the debts and grievances between myself and sentient beings are endless and unresolved that in this life, whether in daily life, orOn our own path of spiritual practice, we always encounter many obstacles. The term "obstacles" does not refer to our own afflictions, but rather to all the negative influences from outside that obstruct our life as well as our path of practice. Why do these negative influences not happen to others, but fall upon us? It is because we are constantly entangled with karmic debts with these adversaries; we must definitely understand this clearly.

So how should this issue be resolved? Is there any method to address it? Yes. The Buddha often teaches in the scriptures that in our practice, we must dedicate our merits to all sentient beings and to all our enemies and wrongdoers. It can be seen that dedication of merit is the only path to resolution. The merits and blessings accumulated from our daily practice, when dedicated to these enemies, we are in a way practicing on their behalf. Hopefully, the merits and blessings of our lifelong practice can repay kindness if there is any, and if there is hostility, they can use these merits and blessings to dissolve enmity and eliminate resentment. If we useWith a sincere heart to dedicate the merit, these debt-holding adversaries will also gladly forgive us, not continue to cause difficulties or obstacles for us anymore. This benefits both ourselves and others.

From this, one realizes that in this world, no one truly loses, and no one truly gains an advantage. If in this life someone gains a benefit and turns another person's convenience into their own, they will still have to return it all in the next life. If it is not fully repaid in the next life, it will continue to be repaid in the life after that, until the debt is completely settled. Similarly, if in this life one suffers many losses, then in the next life, someone else will come to repay them.

Therefore, once we understand the true reality, we need to be content with our circumstances and live according to the time and conditions. We should not cultivate the thought of encroaching on the interests of others, or taking advantage of others' conveniences as our own. Even if we are constantly at a disadvantage or deceived, we must absolutely not harbor resentment, nor should we calculate gains and losses. Only then can the practice of reciting Amitabha Buddha's name quickly bear fruit.

Amitabha Buddha!

_ Reference: Dharma Words of Dharma Master Jingkong_

tieu_de: Beauty eventually fades - only Nirvana is eternal.
tom_tat: In ancient times, the Buddha resided on Mount Kosambi in the city of Ludiqi. At that time, in the city, there was a courtesan named Lian Hua. She was exceptionally beautiful, unmatched in the entire country. Young men, the sons of noble families,
noi_dung:
Beauty eventually fades - only Nirvana is eternal.

Long ago, the Buddha resided on Mount Kỳ-xà-quật in the city of La-duyệt-kỳ. At that time, there was a courtesan in the city named Liên Hoa. She was incredibly beautiful, unmatched in the entire country. Young men from noble families all admired her and competed to visit her.

One day, Lien Hoa suddenly developed a kind heart and wished to leave worldly life to become a Bhikkhuni. She gave up everything and went to Mount Kosambi, where the Buddha was residing. On the way, she came across a clear, cool stream. Lien Hoa stopped to drink water and wash her hands. The clear, sparkling water reflected her image: her radiant face, smooth dark hair, and perfectly proportioned body.

Seeing her own beautiful appearance, Lien Hoa regretted, thinking: "I was born with such charming beauty, why would I give it up to become an ascetic? I should take advantage of my youth and indulge in my own desires to the fullest."

After thinking this way, she went back home. The Buddha, knowing that Lien Hoa could be guided, transformed into a beautiful young woman approaching from the opposite direction. This girl's beauty was far more extraordinary than Lien Hoa's. Lien Hoa, seeing her, felt extremely fond and asked:

- Where are you from? Where is your home that you are walking alone like this?

The young lady replied:

- I have some matters in the city and am just now planning to return home. We have only just met, so shall we go together on the same way? Recently there is a riverbank nearby, let's go there first to rest and chat.

Lien Hoa happily replied:

- That sounds great!

The two of them went to the water's edge to talk and confide in each other. After a while, the young woman, exhausted, rested her head on Lien Hoa's shoulder and fell asleep. Unexpectedly, the young woman had already died; her body had swollen, maggots wriggled around, her teeth and hair had fallen out, her limbs were disintegrated, and a foul stench emanated, making it very difficult to bear.

Lien Hoa was utterly terrified, thinking: "She was so young and beautiful, and now she is gone. As for me, how can I be sure of longevity?"

After thinking about it, she immediately made up her mind to diligently return to studying the Way, continuing to seek the Buddha. Upon arriving, she paid respects to the Buddha and then recounted fully everything she had seen.

The Buddha said to Lotus:

- There are four things people cannot rely on. What are they?

1. Youth must grow old.

2. Health must end in death.

3. Beloved people must be separated.

4. Accumulated wealth must be dispersed.

Then, the Buddha spoke the verse:

"With old age, the body deteriorates

Illness causes this body to decay

When life comes to an end

The body disintegrates, rots away.

***

What is precious in this body

Filth continuously flows

Surrounded by sickness

One must endure the misfortune of old age and death.

***

Indulging in desires

Increases unlawful acts

Unaware of change

Human life in a breath!

***

Even if it is one's own child

Or parents and siblings

When death comes

No one can be relied upon."

After hearing the Dharma, Venerable Lotus rejoiced in enlightenment, realizing that the body is like an illusion, life is not long, and only Nirvana is eternally peaceful. Therefore, she went before the Buddha to request ordination as a Bhikkhuni.

The Buddha said:

-Well done!

Lotus' hair immediately fell off, and she became a Bhikkhuni. Later, through diligent meditation and contemplation practice, Bhikkhuni Lotus attained the stage of Arahant. All those who heard the Dharma at the assembly rejoiced immensely.

(Excerpt from "Dhammapada Stories" - Translator: Thich Minh Quang)

Namo Fundamental Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha _()_

May everyone understand and apply these Buddhist teachings in their lives, and life will be much more peaceful and beautiful.

tieu_de: LOVE
tom_tat: To love someone is to make them suffer less. If not, it is only passion, a temporary infatuation, not true love. Compassion in love does not arise out of nowhere. It must be learned, it must be practiced.
noi_dung:
LOVE

Loving someone means making them suffer less. If not, it is only passion, temporary infatuation, not true love. Compassion in love does not arise spontaneously. It must be learned, practiced. It takes time to observe, listen, and understand the sufferings and pains of the loved one, in order to help them overcome, untangle, reduce their suffering, and increase their happiness.

Compassion is the ability to give happiness to the one you love. Loving is not about enjoyment; loving is giving.

Love that does not bring happiness to the beloved is not true love. Loving but making each other suffer is not love.

There are people who love each other, yet suffer every day; that is a burdensome love, bringing only pain. Truly loving someone means making them happy every day.

Compassion is the ability of a person to take suffering away from others. If I have suffered, and someone adds to my suffering, that cannot be true love. What is left to give each other if there is only pain and despair? A lover must be someone who knows how to share, soothe, and lessen one's suffering in life. Thus, according to Buddha's teaching, compassion is the ability to bring happiness to each other.

Loving someone means making them suffer less. Otherwise, it is merely passion, temporary infatuation, not true love. Compassion in love does not appear spontaneously. It must be learned and practiced. It takes time to observe, listen, and understand the sufferings and pains of the loved one in order to help them overcome, resolve, reduce their suffering, and increase happiness.

Joy is happiness. True love must make both parties happy. The hallmark of true love is joy. The more you love, the happier you become; the greater the joy, the happier the entire family. Such a karmic relationship is a success.

Letting go / means not discriminating, not being prejudiced in love. Whomever I love, their happiness, difficulties, and suffering are mine. I cannot say this is your problem, you have to endure it.

When in love, the two people are no longer two separate entities, happiness and suffering are no longer personal matters. All we have to do is treat it as the problem of both, transform the suffering, and increase the happiness.

Zen Master Thich Nhat Hanh

tieu_de: HOW TO REPENT COMBINED WITH THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA
tom_tat: - POWERFUL KARMIC OBSTACLE ELIMINATION Are you wanting to regularly repent in order to reduce your karmic obstacles, but do not have much time?
noi_dung:
METHOD OF REPENTANCE COMBINED WITH GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA

- POWERFUL KARMIC OBSTACLE ELIMINATION

Do you want to regularly repent to reduce karmic obstacles, but don’t have much time?

In this article, Quang Tử would like to introduce a brief repentance ritual, combining the Great Compassion Mantra – the Repentance Chapter in the Golden Light Sutra together with vows, all of which can be completed in about 5-10 minutes. Yet its power to eliminate karmic obstacles is very strong and complete, suitable for people with little time.

Of course, this ritual is not as effective as the long repentance texts like the Liang Huang Repentance, or as detailed as the Compassionate Water Repentance, but not everyone is patient enough to repent daily with these two texts. Therefore, this ritual may be suitable for many people who are busy yet still want to repent to reduce karma and lessen suffering in life.

Why should one recite the Great Compassion Mantra during repentance?

If you pay attention, you will notice that in most of the Repentance Ritual books, or other sutras, the compilers often place the Great Compassion Mantra at the beginning. This is because in the Great Compassion Dharani Sutra, Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara teaches:

“...If any sentient being harms the belongings, food, or drink of a monastic, they will bear a very heavy sin. Due to the obstruction of evil karma, even if a thousand Buddhas were to appear, repentance would not be effective; even with repentance, the sin would not be eliminated. If such a sin has been committed, one must repent before the Buddhas and Teachers of the ten directions in order to be able to eradicate it.

Today, by reciting and practicing the Great Compassion Mantra, one is immediately purified from all sins. Why is that? Because when reciting the Great Compassion Mantra with an earnest heart, teachers from the ten directions come to witness, therefore all obstacles and sins are completely eliminated.

Any sentient being who recites this mantra will have all their ten evil deeds, five gravest offenses, blasphemy of the Dharma, harming others, violating precepts, breaking vows, destroying temples and stupas, stealing from monks, defiling moral conduct—any severe evil karmic deeds—entirely eradicated.

Except for one thing: if the person reciting the dharani still harbors doubt towards the dharani, then even small sins and minor negative karma cannot be eradicated, let alone serious sins. However, even though serious sins are not immediately eliminated, it can still create the seed of Bodhi for future lifetimes…”

Thus, when reciting the Great Compassion Dharani, there will be teachers from the ten directions – that is, Buddhas from the ten directions manifesting to witness the practice, greatly enhancing the effectiveness of repentance.

The Great Compassion Mantra itself is already a powerful mantra that eliminates karmic obstacles, renowned for its efficacy since ancient times, with thousands of true stories of real people experiencing its effects, so people everywhere often recite it.

Therefore, before repentance, you should read the Great Compassion Mantra first, reading it once is fine, seven times, twenty-one times is even better, and more than that is even greater, as it will eliminate more karma.

As for the Repentance portion extracted from the Golden Light Sutra, taught directly by Buddha Shakyamuni, just reading through it once, you will immediately see that although the content is brief, it is extremely concise, encompassing all types of bodily, verbal, and mental offenses to be repented, leaving no sin unaddressed, with immense effectiveness.

Additionally, making the vow that in future lives we will no longer commit harmful deeds – preventing sins from arising from the very beginning, so that they cannot arise. And if the actions of committing negative deeds do not arise, then in subsequent lives, there will be no karmic consequences to suffer, right?

As for the time, place, and manner of reading the repentance prayer?

Kneeling before a solemn Buddha statue, with full incense, flowers, and candles is best. But it is not mandatory; be flexible depending on the time. If there is no Buddha altar, just sit somewhere quiet to repent. You can even stand on the street to recite the repentance prayer, as long as your attire is reasonably proper. The time can be anytime, any day, any number of times, or even not at all. Do not be rigid about the timing, because it is not important.

The method of reading repentance prayers, to be considered correct reading, is not to focus excessively on the act of reading, but to concentrate on understanding.

Reading slowly is fine, stumbling while reading is fine, repeating a sentence or a passage is fine… the essential thing is to thoroughly understand the meaning of those repentance words.

Repentance does not focus on reading fluently, continuously, without mistakes or stumbling over words, or reading through the entire book to earn merit. Instead, if the mind does not understand, if the heart does not recognize that each word and letter is uncovering faults within oneself, prompting a feeling of remorse and repentance. Reading repentance without seeing its relevance to one's own life, thinking it is someone else's matter, does not meet the requirement and earns little merit.

Reading each sentence, each paragraph, I relate: "Ah, I used to make this mistake (I can pause to remember—recall) now I realize it. I feel truly sorry, truly regret having done that. From now on, I am determined to amend, not to do that anymore," then continue reading… This is how the merits of this repentance text, as well as any other repentance text, are fulfilled.

If you have understood the method, please begin the Repentance Ritual:

REPENTANCE

(Excerpt from the Golden Light Sutra, Chapter on Eradicating Karmic Obstacles – Shakyamuni Buddha instructs the method of repentance)

“…I respectfully take refuge in the Buddhas of the ten directions at present, those who have attained Supreme Bodhi, turning the wheel of wonderful Dharma, the radiant wheel of Dharma, showering the great Dharma rain, sounding the great Dharma drum, blowing the great Dharma trumpet, raising the great Dharma banner, holding the great Dharma torch, constantly practicing the giving of Dharma for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings, teaching those who are deluded to progress, enabling them to attain great fruits, always blissful.

O World Honored Ones, like that, I humbly bow with my body, speech, and mind to pay homage and surrender. O World Honored Ones, like that, with true wisdom, true vision, true realization, and true equality, you fully know and see all the wholesome and unwholesome actions of sentient beings.

From beginningless time until now, I have gone along with the stream of sinfulness and created karmic obstacles together with sentient beings, bound tightly by greed, anger, and ignorance. When I did not know the Buddha, did not know the Dharma, did not know the Sangha, did not know good and evil, I committed through body, speech, and mind the five heinous crimes: having an evil heart that shed the Buddha's blood, slandering the Buddha and Dharma, breaking the harmony of the Sangha, harming Arhats, and harming father and mother.

A child with three bodily evils (killing, stealing, sexual misconduct), four verbal evils (lying, exaggerating, double-tongued speech, harsh speech), and three mental evils (greed, hatred, delusion) commits ten unwholesome actions by doing them oneself, instructing others to do them, or rejoicing when seeing others do them.

For the virtuous, the child is arrogantly slandering; for measuring tools, he is deceitful; he calls evil good, gives bad food to others; towards parents of many generations in the six paths, the child causes harm; towards the wealth of the Stupa, of the monks in the four directions, or of the present monks, the child steals, freely uses it; towards the precepts and teachings of the Blessed One, the child does not wish to observe or practice them, does not comply with the instructions of the master, and when seeing anyone following the vehicle of the Śrāvaka, the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddha, or the vehicle of the Mahāyāna, he insults and disrupts them.

When seeing someone better than me, I immediately feel jealous; concerning giving Dharma or wealth, I regret it, letting ignorance block me, being confused by wrong views, I do not cultivate wholesome deeds but instead increase unwholesome deeds. I even slander the Buddhas, calling what is Dharma not Dharma, and what is not Dharma as Dharma, etc...

With so many offenses, the Buddhas, with true wisdom, true vision, true realization, and true equality, know everything and see everything, so today I sincerely take refuge and pay homage. Before the Buddhas, I do not dare to hide anything.

For sins not yet committed, I dare not commit them; for sins already committed, I sincerely repent. The karmic obstacles that lead to the six realms and eight sufferings which I have committed, and the karmic obstacles I am currently committing, I vow to eliminate them all. I vow that in the future I will not have to bear the retribution of those karmic obstacles.

Just as the great Bodhisattvas of the past, who practiced the path of Bodhi, have repented all their karmic obstacles, so too, I now sincerely repent all my karmic obstacles. I reveal everything openly, daring not to conceal anything. For sins already committed, I vow to eliminate them; for sins not yet committed, I vow that I will no longer dare to commit them.

Just like the future Great Bodhisattvas who practice the Bodhi path, all their karmic obstacles are repented of; likewise, my karmic obstacles, today I also repent of all. I reveal everything, dare not hide anything. The sins I have committed, I vow to completely eliminate; the sins I have not committed, I vow not to do them anymore.

Just like the present Great Bodhisattvas who practice the Bodhi path, all their karmic obstacles have already been repented of; likewise, my karmic obstacles, today I also repent of all. I reveal everything, dare not hide anything. The sins I have committed, I vow to completely eliminate; the sins I have not committed, I vow not to do them anymore…”

(sincerely kneeling and confessing)

VOW TO MAINTAIN PURE MORAL DISCIPLINE

"I vow from now until countless lifetimes, regardless of the realm I am born into, to wholeheartedly bring my body, speech, and mind to abide by the precepts taught by the Buddha, from the precepts of laypeople to those of Bodhisattvas. Moment by moment, I resolve never to follow bad habits, defilements of desire, anger, ignorance, arrogance, doubt, and wrong views... but only to purely long to live in the pure moral discipline of the Buddha, like a dying person thirsting to reach a cool stream, like someone freezing to death yearning to be by a warm fire.

May all my body, speech, and mind always remain pure in the precepts of the Buddha naturally, smoothly like breathing, steadfastly without anything able to obstruct, without anything able to destroy.

May whenever my mind harbors any unwholesome thought, my mouth is about to speak unwholesome words, or my body is about to commit unwholesome deeds contrary to the precepts taught by the Buddha, my whole body immediately suffers pain and anguish, until I can completely uproot those unwholesome thoughts, I may return to peace.

May I continue from lifetime to lifetime like this until I become a Buddha, always perfectly observing the Perfection of Morality, maintaining every thought within the moral conduct of the Buddha, without seeing anyone practicing morality, without seeing morality itself, because all is illusory and unattainable.

Supplementary Mantra:

OM HU RU HU RU GIA GIA MU KHE SO HA (7 times)

THREE REFUGE

Taking refuge in the Buddha, hereby I vow for sentient beings, realizing the great path, and generating the supreme mind.

Taking refuge in the Dharma, may I vow for all sentient beings, to penetrate the Buddhist scriptures, with wisdom as vast as the ocean.

Taking refuge in the Sangha, may I vow for all sentient beings, to harmonize the great assembly, with all matters unobstructed.

tieu_de: WHY THE LANG NGHIEM INCANTATION IS NOT EFFECTIVE
tom_tat: Venerable Tuyen Hoa's Lecture on Simple Practice of Virtue (Abridged Translation)
noi_dung:
WHY THE INCANTATIONS OF LANG NGHIEM ARE NOT EFFECTIVE

Master Xuan Hua's Lecture

Translated by Hanh Doan

The Lankavatara Dharma is a practice that is difficult to encounter even over hundreds of thousands of kalpas. If you recite the Lankavatara mantra but do not adhere to moral precepts, casually killing living beings, stealing, engaging in sexual misconduct, lying, drinking alcohol… then you will not gain merit and you will not be able to enjoy the miraculous effects of the Lankavatara mantra.

Nowadays, there are people who do not pay attention to maintaining moral virtue for themselves, so even if they recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, they will not achieve any efficacy or great spiritual response.

Therefore, if you want to practice the method of reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, your behavior must be righteous, your mind sincere, without generating impure and deluded thoughts, and without doing unwholesome deeds. You must strictly observe precepts and maintain high moral virtue. If you both recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra and violate precepts, living in impurity, you will bring about harm to yourself due to the karma of your own evil actions.

If you recite the Lăng Nghiêm dharani without observing precepts and living a virtuous and kind life, you will certainly cause the Vajra Treasury Bodhisattva to feel disrespected, not obedient, and unwilling to protect you!

IF YOU WANT TO PRACTICE THE DHARANI OF LĂNG NGHIÊM, YOU MUST MAINTAIN RETREATS AND KEEP THE PRECEPTS, abandon evil and practice good, dwell in a compassionate mind, THE MIND MUST BE PURE, THE INTENTION MUST NOT ARISE IMPURE THINKINGS, you must ALWAYS MAINTAIN purity, cleanliness, AND NOT COMMIT EVEN THE SLIGHTEST ACTS THAT VIOLATE THE RULES.

Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra brings more benefits than trading gold and silver. Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra once is equivalent in value to tens of thousands of ounces of gold. However, you cannot recite it with a greedy mind. If you strictly observe the precepts, are free of jealousy, hindrances, and greed, anger, and delusion, then practicing the recitation of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra will bring spiritual responses and great benefits. If you engage in actions that break the precepts, then when practicing the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, you will not receive significant spiritual responses.

THIS IS COMPLETELY NOT BECAUSE YOU ARE UNLUCKY, BUT BECAUSE YOU DO NOT MAINTAIN MORAL PRECEPTS, WHICH MAKES THE DHARMIC PROTECTOR GODS STAY AWAY FROM YOU; THEREFORE, NO MATTER WHAT CALAMITY HAPPENS TO YOU, THE DHARMIC PROTECTOR GODS WILL NOT CARE, NOR WILL THEY PROTECT YOU ANYMORE!

Therefore, those who practice the Dharma by reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra must not have deceitful, cunning, or fraudulent intentions, and must always abandon evil and practice good. You must always guard your body, speech, and mind, act with integrity and transparency, live with a mind to benefit others, disregard personal gain, have the mindset of a Bodhisattva, and practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva!

It should be known: Reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra brings benefits to sentient beings; if one cannot recite it, it does not bring benefits to sentient beings. You should read and study the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, memorize it, and study it thoroughly—that is the proper behavior of a Buddhist follower.

In Buddhism, nothing is more important than the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, because the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra represents the True Dharma—WITH THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA THERE IS TRUE DHARMA, WITHOUT THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA THERE IS NO TRUE DHARMA; if one does not know the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, one is not worthy of being called a Buddhist follower!

WE, THOSE WHO CAN RECITE THE LANKAVISHA SUTRA, IT IS ALL BECAUSE FROM COUNTLESS AGES UNTIL NOW, WE HAVE CULTIVATED GREAT VIRTUE, SO THAT NOW WE CAN MEMORIZE THE LANKAVISHA SUTRA; once memorized, it is never forgotten, this is the manifestation of virtuous roots.

IF YOU DO NOT HAVE VIRTUOUS ROOTS, NOT ONLY WILL YOU NOT BE ABLE TO RECITE IT, BUT EVEN THE NAME OF THE LANKAVISHA SUTRA YOU WILL NOT ENCOUNTER, AND EVEN IF YOU DO ENCOUNTER IT, YOU WILL NOT BE ABLE TO RECITE IT AND WILL NOT BE ABLE TO BELIEVE AND UNDERSTAND THE WONDROUSNESS OF THE LANKAVISHA SUTRA.

Therefore, if at present you are able to recite regularly and memorize the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, it is all thanks to your profound virtuous roots.

Breaking precepts is something that cannot be repaired or cured, but if you know how to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, you can restore the purity of your precepts. However, knowing how to recite does not mean just reciting; you must achieve the Samadhi of Mantra Recitation, which means reciting to the point where the mind and the mantra are united, so that all distracting and impure thoughts vanish, leaving only the Lăng Nghiêm mantra.

If you can chant to that extent, then even if you have previously broken precepts, you can still attain pure ethical foundations.

If in the past you did not have a diligent and lofty mind, did not study the Buddha's teachings, but if you can steadfastly recite the Shurangama Mantra many times over a long period, you will naturally develop a diligent mind; even without wisdom, your wisdom will be opened.

If you practice but are not pure, having violated the precepts, yet you do not forget and diligently recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, you will quickly restore your purity. If in the past, before knowing how to recite the mantra, you violated the precepts, then after reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, all acts of violating the precepts, whether minor or major sins, even sins that cannot be repented, can all be completely cleansed.

If you diligently and wholeheartedly recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra without getting tired, no matter how serious your sins are, they can all be eradicated. That is why it is said that the power of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is so wondrous and beyond comprehension.

THE INCREDIBLE MYSTERIES OF THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA

1. Those who practice the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra will not be reborn in unfortunate places.

2. Those who recite the Lingyan Mantra, even if they themselves do not perform any virtuous deeds, merely reciting the Lingyan Mantra alone, the merit of all the Buddhas in the ten directions will be dedicated to them. Look, in this way, don't you gain so much benefit and happiness?

If you diligently recite the Lingyan Mantra, you will often be born in the time when the Buddha appears in the world, and be able to cultivate along with the Buddha.

3. Suppose your mind is extremely distracted and cannot concentrate because you have no mental stability, but if deep in your heart you always remember and think of the Lankavatara Mantra that the Buddha taught, and recite it with your mouth, then Bodhisattva Vajra Treasury King will use a refined mind to quietly follow the person reciting the Lankavatara Mantra with a distracted mind like yours, supporting bit by bit so that your distracted mind disappears, and gradually you can achieve mental stability.

4. If you can read the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra fluently and tirelessly as if the mantra is flowing from your own heart, then the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is your mind, and your mind is the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. It is considered that you have attained Mantra Recitation Samadhi, chanting continuously without interruption. At the very least, you may be wealthy for seven lifetimes, like an American oil tycoon, but do not think upon hearing this: I must quickly learn the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra to become a billionaire for seven lifetimes! If your only desire is something shallow like that, then there is no reason to study the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, for wealth over seven lifetimes is merely a period of time.brief!

So, why do you recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra? To become a Buddha, to attain Supreme Perfect Enlightenment. The miracle of the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra is truly beyond comprehension. You cannot imagine it, and even if I speak, I cannot fully explain it.

5. Wherever there are people reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, at that place, a large white precious umbrella (called a white parasol) will immediately appear in the sky. IF YOUR SPIRITUAL PRACTICE IS VAST AND PROFOUND, THEN WHENEVER YOU RECITE THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA, WITHIN A RADIUS OF THOUSANDS OF MILES FROM WHERE YOU ARE, NO ACCIDENTS WILL OCCUR; IF YOUR PRACTICE IS SMALL, THIS PRECIOUS UMBRELLA WILL BE RIGHT ABOVE YOUR HEAD, SILENTLY PROTECTING AND SHELTERING YOU.

6. If you are a venerable monk with virtuous conduct, then whenever you recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, the entire country benefits, and no disasters will occur. (Even if a disaster occurs, a great disaster will turn into a minor one, and a minor disaster will turn into none!)

7. If any country suffers from famine, infectious diseases, war, robbery, or many accidents, IF EVERYONE CAN COPY THIS LANKHEN INCANTATION to place it above the four gates of the city, OR place it in protective places such as forts, city walls, or bunkers, IT CAN MAKE ALL beings in that country WELCOME, REVERENTLY BOWING AND SALUTING THE LANKHEN INCANTATION, WITH A HEART FULL OF RESPECT LIKE OFFERING TO THE BUDDHA, OR IT CAN MAKE EVERY CITIZEN OF THIS COUNTRY KEEP A COPY OF THE LANKHEN INCANTATION WITH THEM, OR PLACE IT IN THE HOUSE THEY STAY IN, THEN ALL DISASTERS WILL BE ELIMINATED.

8. WHEREVER MONK LANG NGHIEM IS, HEAVENLY DRAGONS ARE ALWAYS DELIGHTFUL, SO THERE ARE NO CALAMITIES LIKE HEAVY RAIN OR STRONG WINDS, ALL GRAINS ARE ABUNDANT, AND THE PEOPLE ARE FULL, WARM, AND PEACEFUL. THEREFORE, THE MERIT OF MONK LANG NGHIEM IS BEYOND COMPREHENSION; EVEN IF YOU IMAGINE, YOU CANNOT PICTURE IT, THIS IS THE WONDERFUL EFFECT OF THE MONK.

tieu_de: WHAT IS LIFE RELEASE?
tom_tat: *What is meant by releasing life? Releasing life means seeing sentient beings with lives being captured, imprisoned, about to be killed, terrified and confused, their lives in a moment of danger,
noi_dung:
WHAT IS RELEASED LIVING BEINGS?

*What is meant by releasing living beings?

Releasing living beings means seeing sentient beings whose lives are being captured, confined, about to be destroyed, terrified and confused, with their lives in immediate danger, and then generating compassion and seeking ways to save them. In this way, it is an act of liberation, release, and saving life.

The Treatise on Great Wisdom teaches: 'Among all sins, the sin of killing is the gravest; among all merits, releasing life is the foremost.' 'Among all crimes, the crime of taking life is the heaviest. Among all virtues, saving life is the greatest virtue.'

*Why should we release life?

Simply put, releasing life means repaying a debt, repaying the debt of killing that we have accumulated through heavy karmic offenses over many lifetimes until now.

The Avatamsaka Sutra teaches: "If this evil karma had a form, even the entire emptiness would not be able to contain it all." In this very life, the karma of killing living beings that we have created is truly incalculable, let alone that which has been created over many lifetimes!

Therefore, one should know the truth: "Debts must be repaid, sins must be accounted for."

Reflecting on oneself, the whole body itself is filled with killing karma, having created countless acts of killing, inevitably one must face crisis, shame, truly having no place to contain it! How could one not timely repent, strive to release life, in hopes of repaying debts in every possible way! The act of releasing life can cultivate one's compassionate heart. Therefore, one should develop compassion by releasing life, seeing the lives of all beings as one's own life. By doing so, one will no longer be deluded or chaotic; will no longer create killing karma; will no longer lack repayment of killing debts; will no longer have to undergo karmic retribution in samsara.

The Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Sutra on Original Vows and Merits teaches: "Releasing living creatures eliminates diseases and helps them escape accidents. Those who practice releasing life and perform virtuous deeds, helping all living beings escape suffering, will themselves avoid misfortunes."

*What are the merits of releasing life?

The merit of releasing life is vast and immeasurable, beyond counting. Here is a brief summary:

1. There will be no danger from weapons, and one can avoid the calamities of war and massacre.

2. Long life, strong health, and few illnesses.

3. Avoid natural disasters, epidemics, and accidents.

4. Have many descendants, prosper for generations, and continue the lineage continuously.

5. Wishes and desires are fulfilled.

6. Business and work develop and flourish, encountering many advantages, going smoothly like a sailing boat with the wind.

7. Align with Heaven's will, follow Buddha's nature, be appreciated by animals, and delight the Buddhas.

8. Eliminate hatred, destroy evil things, and be free from worry, sadness, and grief.

9. Enjoy peace and security, being safe throughout the year.

10. Be reborn in the heavenly realm and enjoy infinite blessings. If practicing Pure Land, one will be born into the Western Pure Land.

In the Avatamsaka Sutra, the chapter on the vows of Samantabhadra teaches: “Sentient beings cherish life the most, the Buddhas cherish sentient beings the most. Saving the lives of sentient beings fulfills the vows of the Buddhas.”

After releasing lives, what changes happen to oneself?

Releasing animals can cultivate our compassion. While performing the act of releasing animals, we can consequently understand the truth that all things are equal, all have feelings, all have Buddha nature, and all can become Buddhas. As a result, we can generate a compassionate heart toward all beings, while also respecting and cherishing them. Taking it a step further, in daily life, one can practice abstaining from killing, eating vegetarian, helping the lives of all creatures; refrain from doing evil deeds, strive to do good deeds; and cultivate a compassionate heart toward all living beings in the world.

It should be known that the Buddha's mind is compassionate. When we cultivate compassion, our mind aligns with the Buddha's mind, and when the Buddhas are pleased, it naturally facilitates spiritual responsiveness and connection, making the study of Buddhism easily accomplished.

In the Brahmajala Sutra, the Bodhisattva Precepts, in the precept against killing, it is taught: If a Buddhist kills by themselves, commands others to kill, uses means to kill, praises killing, rejoices at seeing killing, even uses spells to kill, causes killing, plans killing, or engages in killing karma. All sentient beings that have life should not be intentionally killed. A Buddhist should always have compassion and filial devotion, establishing a practice of saving all beings, yet if they instead deliberately harbor a heart to kill, this Buddhist commits the (Bodhisattva grave offense).

*Why nowadays are there many people opposing and criticizing the act of releasing life?

Releasing living beings is the easiest method to eliminate karmic obstacles, and it is simple and easy to do. One only needs to cultivate the intention according to the time and place, whether alone or with others, whether with much money or little money, anyone can release living beings. Because releasing living beings is so supreme and miraculous, over countless lifetimes up to now, we have had so many enemies, karmic creditors, and evil external forces that do not want us to eliminate karmic obstacles and achieve the path in such a simple way. Therefore, they use myriad schemes to increase ignorance, confuse what we see and hear, delude the human mind, and obstruct people from releasing living beings.

The Sutra of Right Mindfulness teaches: "Creating a temple does not compare to saving a life." The merit of life liberation is so great!

(Excerpt from the book "Merit of Life Liberation" - Author: Dharma Master Vien Nhan - Edited by: Nguyen Minh Tien).

Namo Amitabha Buddha - Please often recite _()_

Hopefully, everyone will believe and understand the teachings in this article, practice them, avoid sinful deeds, and increase virtuous actions!

tieu_de: A PERSON KILLED BY A CAR, A PERSON WHO COMMITS SUICIDE DOESN'T NECESSARILY BECOME A DEMON AND GO TO HELL. WHY DON'T THEY FOLLOW KARMA?
tom_tat: ❓QUESTION: Dear old wizard, isn't a person who is hit by a car and dies supposed to become a ghost and descend to the ghost realm? Why are they still by the roadside waiting to find someone to take their place? Or someone who hanged themselves in a room is still around in the brothel
noi_dung:
PEOPLE HIT BY CARS AND KILLING THEMSELVES DON'T NECESSARILY BECOME DEMONS GOING TO HELL. WHY DON'T THEY FOLLOW THEIR KARMA?

❓QUESTION: Dear venerable Sorcerer, if a person is killed by a car, don't they become a ghost and fall into the path of ghosts? Why are they still waiting by the roadside to find someone to replace them? Or if someone hangs themselves in a room, why are they still in the room causing chaos? Why don't they follow karma to go to the path of ghosts? In Buddhist teachings, there is mention of the space of humans and ghosts; is the confusion caused by overlapping spaces? Is it necessary to follow worldly ways, seek a Sorcerer to perform a ritual (exposing the path) to guide the soul, or is there a better way?

✍️ ANSWER: This matter really exists, both in China and abroad, and we have encountered quite a few such cases. There is one point that should be especially noted: after humans die, they do not necessarily go to the path of ghosts; you cannot call them ghosts. The idea that the dead become ghosts comes from not understanding the current state of the six realms; after death, humans have not yet entered any path. This stage is called the bardo. In Chinese, we often refer to the bardo as the soul. Because they have not been reincarnated, if they were already on the ghost path, they would have taken a form in that path, but they still haven't gone. Generally, sudden death or suicide is very troublesome.Complex. In Buddhist scriptures, this matter is explained very clearly, why is that? Because they want to find a substitute. While searching for a substitute, they are still in a bardo body. We call it a ghost, a soul. They do not go to the path of ghosts; after they find a substitute, depending on their own karma, they will be reborn into a certain realm. If they enter the path of ghosts, they will no longer interact with humans. The bardo body can sometimes be very short, usually most of them are reborn after 49 days. Which path they go to, no one can know. One must carefully observe their karma and actions in the world to make a judgment.

🩸 In Buddhist scriptures, it is taught that if a person has a strong desire, they will go to the realm of ghosts; if they have intense anger, they will go to hell; if they are very ignorant—ignorance meaning not understanding clearly right from wrong, good from evil—they mostly go to the realm of animals. If a person's mind is very virtuous, practicing the five precepts and ten good deeds, they will be reborn in the human realm. Those who perfectly practice the ten virtuous deeds with compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity will go to the heavenly realm. From these aspects, by observing, you can judge where they will go. When someone is on their deathbed, look at their death posture; if at the time of death their body is soft and their appearance is beautiful, they will go to a good path and will not enter the evil realms. On the other hand, those who die with a stiff body...Stupidity and an ugly appearance all lead to the evil path. This is some common knowledge we should be aware of. Therefore, no matter how difficult and arduous our circumstances are, we must never have suicidal thoughts, because suicide cannot solve the problem. If suicide could solve the problem, the Buddha would have advised us to commit suicide. You would only make the problem worse and more troublesome.

🩸 Your life in this world is for receiving retribution; suffering is also for receiving retribution. If you have not yet finished experiencing your sufferings and commit suicide, in your next life as a human, you will still have to undergo this suffering. Therefore, this is not a method to solve the problem. The method to solve problems is to stop doing evil and practice goodness, repent for your karmic obstacles in order to improve, and be able to transform your karma. If you study Buddhism but cannot achieve this, then it has no meaning; what use is it for us to study Buddhism? It is truly so. Transforming poverty into wealth is what worldly people pursue; transforming ignorance into wisdom, but the highest isTransforming the mundane into the sacred. If you clearly understand this principle, grasp this truth, and know the method of transformation, then you should study diligently; your future will be bright. Although there may be suffering in the present, do not be afraid. The greatest fear for humans is at the end of life; if the end of life is filled with suffering, it is truly painful. If one suffers when young, it is not a problem. At the end of life, one can live happily. Once one’s own karmic obstacles are eliminated, there will be blessings at the end of life.

[Learning Buddhism Q&A, Venerable Master Jingkong]

Namo Amitabha Buddha. Advise people to have Faith, Vow, and recite the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land.

Source: Youth Protecting the Body

tieu_de: HOW TO ACCUMULATE INFINITE MERIT AND CHANGE FATE ACCORDING TO BUDDHISM
tom_tat: (Those who are too poor, life is too difficult and troublesome, please follow this method) Every day, set aside 1k, 2k... up to 5k, any amount is fine. Even the poorest person in the world will surely have 1k, then offer it to the Buddha 3 times
noi_dung:
HOW TO ACCUMULATE BOUNDLESS MERIT TO CHANGE DESTINY ACCORDING TO BUDDHISM

(For those who are very poor, life is too difficult and troublesome, please follow this method)

Every day, save 1k, 2k... up to 5k, it’s okay, even the poorest person in the world can surely have 1k, then offer 3 bows to the Buddha and make the following vow:

Chant NAM MÔ BỔN SƯ THÍCH CA MẦU NI PHẬT 3 times with 3 bows

Chant NAM MÔ A MI ĐÀ PHẬT 3 times with 3 bows

Chant NAM MÔ ĐẠI BI QUÁN THẾ ÂM BỒ TÁT 3 times with 3 bows

Recite NAMO Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva 3 times with 3 prostrations

+ My name is.... Dharma name (if any)... Today I vow to make offerings to the Three Jewels on behalf of my grandparents, parents of the past and present, on behalf of enemies and debt holders of many past lives, and for all sentient beings suffering throughout the vast emptiness and throughout the Dharma realm, using a sincere heart to offer the amount of....... thousand dong.

I vow that all sentient beings may, through the merit of this offering, develop the Bodhi mind, be free from suffering and attain joy, and all be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

+ NAMO AMIDA BUDDHA, we vow to be reborn together in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. (Say this 3 times, bow 3 times).

- The money each day can be put into a box; when the box is full or after 1-2 months, use that money (it can be exchanged for cash). Bring it to the temple and put it into the donation box at the main hall.

- Because the Triple Gem (Buddha, Dharma, Sangha) is the field of merit where sentient beings sow seeds; this merit is infinite and boundless.

- I vow that the offering to the Triple Gem must be done according to this vow, and this money must not be used for any other purpose.

- Doing good deeds like this brings infinite merit.

- Sincerely doing this can change your entire life.

- Those who are very poor should do it this way, or guide poor people who do not know.

- Whoever follows the above correctly and regularly without skipping, at the latest within 3 years (possibly sooner), will overcome difficulties, have money to cover living expenses, no longer be as poor as before, and have a smooth life with all wishes fulfilled.

* Special cases

+ First: If there is no Buddha altar and no Buddha picture, place the box in a clean, elevated place, face it westward, then worship, make wishes, and dedicate merit.

+ Second: For those who have a Buddha picture, face it towards the Buddha picture and then proceed.

+ Third: If not using the above two methods, use a phone to display the image of the Buddha you venerate, place it on the altar, and worship as usual.

- The three methods are different but have the same merit.

It depends on each person's sincere heart, and the merit will vary.

- The minds of Buddha and sentient beings are originally of the same essence. When the mind of sentient beings thinks of the Buddha, the Buddha's light already shines in that mind,

The mind is Buddha, Buddha is the mind; one should not cling to forms or appearances.

- Using a sincere mind will certainly bring about a response.

* Besides the above method, in daily life we can accumulate merit by giving alms as taught in the sutras.

SUTRA OF THE ORIGINAL VOW OF BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA

Chapter Ten: Comparing the Causes and Merits of Giving Alms

At that time, the Buddha said to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha: 'Now I am in the entire assembly in the palace of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, explaining the comparison of the merits of giving in Jambudvīpa. You must listen closely; I will speak for your sake!'

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha replied to the Buddha: 'I indeed have doubts about this matter. I sincerely wish to hear it.'

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha: 'In the southern realm of Jambudvīpa, there are kings, high-ranking ministers and officials, great noblemen, brave and valiant men, great Brahmins, and so on...

If they encounter someone extremely poor, even someone disabled, mute, deaf, or blindly foolish, encountering those whose bodies are not intact.

When those kings, etc., wish to give alms, if they can have a great compassionate mind, along with a joyful humility, giving alms with their own hands to all those people, or instructing others to give, and comforting them with gentle and kind words.

Those kings and great ministers, etc., obtain benefits through the merit of offering to an uncountable number (a hundred countless) of Buddhas.

Why? It is precisely because that King, etc., generated great compassion towards the extremely poor and towards those disabled people, that blessings were bestowed and such results attained, in hundreds of thousands of lives usually enjoying all the seven treasures, let alone things for use such as clothing, food, drink, etc....

tieu_de: THE SCARY STORY OF A RICH DIRECTOR WHO WAS DAMNED TO HELL AND THEN REINCARNATED AS AN ANIMAL
tom_tat: In the autumn of 2003, on a beautiful day with a gentle breeze blowing, my elderly friend and I went to the famous Ban Long Pagoda in Nguyen Thi District, Ha Bac Province. After lighting incense to worship Buddha, we
noi_dung:
THE SCARY STORY OF A RICH DIRECTOR WHO WAS DAMNED TO HELL AND REINCARNATED AS AN ANIMAL

In the autumn of 2003, on a beautiful day with a gentle breeze blowing, my friend and I went to Ban Long Pagoda, famous in Nguyen Thi district, Ha Bac province. After lighting incense and paying respects to Buddha, we strolled around to admire the scenery of the pagoda. At that moment, a nun with a cheerful face and a smile welcomed us; she looked very amiable and friendly. My friend stepped forward first and greeted:

– Venerable, we are laypeople visiting the pagoda from afar. May we have a chat with you?

She hurriedly replied: – Amitabha Buddha. Yes, sir!

I spoke: – Miss, you still look very young, why do you want to become a nun?

Then the nun recounted the truly frightening story that she had personally witnessed to us.

"I was born into a family of influential officials in city X, in the northeast region, with a very affluent and comfortable household. Since childhood, I only carried books to school until I graduated from the University of Finance. After graduation, I worked at an agency for more than ten years, and later moved on to work at a bank. My husband works in a government office, and our son is attending high school."

I have always felt that my life is very happy. I have loving parents, a warm family, and there is nothing to worry about at home. Everything goes extremely smoothly. But three years ago, I encountered a major event that drastically changed my life, taking it in a different direction.

Three years ago, I was working at a bank while also serving as a "Financial Officer at a real estate company."

He is the General Director of a real estate company at the age of 46, with strong vitality. In the past, he worked at a grain company, then switched to real estate business. He is immensely wealthy, owning hundreds of millions in assets, running a grand business, very capable.

That year he played the stock market and suffered a heavy loss. That day, in just fifteen minutes, he lost over forty-seven million. The shock was so great that he had a cerebral hemorrhage and died.

After he died, the spirit kept following me everywhere. When alive, he was 1.84 meters tall, but now he appeared to be only around 1 meter tall (According to Buddhist scriptures, a deceased person takes on a bardo body that resembles their living form but is only the height of an 8-9 year old child. This aligns with what I saw). His skin was the color of earth, and his appearance was exactly like when he was alive. Just by looking, you could immediately recognize him as Mr. Tổng. At that time, no matter where I went, he followed me. I couldn’t close my eyes, because whenever I did, the headache became unbearable, and even with my eyes closed, I could still see him.

My family thought I was unusually restless, so they sent people to watch over me all day. But the situations I witnessed, no one else saw. So even if I spoke about them or described what I saw, no one would believe me. I couldn’t even escape from Mr. Tổng. Whether I took a plane to Beijing or went to Qingdao, he also followed. This situation tormented me for 100 days.

Even more terrifying is that, after he died, every 7 days marked the end of a week. Each time I passed through a level, I would vividly see each scene of hell before my eyes, the place where he suffered intensely, watching him be punished miserably, horrifying.

In the first week, I saw some underworld officials dragging his two hands into the roasting furnace. I only heard his agonizing screams, and when his hands were pulled out, they were twisted, red-hot like molten iron, and his body shriveled up tightly.

By the second week, what I saw before my eyes was the hell of burning feet. In the third week, I saw him barefoot climbing a mountain of blades, blood pouring everywhere. Then in the fifth, sixth, and seventh weeks, I saw him being flayed, having his stomach cut open, eyes gouged out, legs sawed off, etc... It was truly tragic and horrifying to the point that I couldn't bear to look. I also heard him loudly moaning and begging me to save him. But at that time, I didn't know anything about the Dharma, nor did I know how to save him.

Throughout 100 days, at the end, in the present scene, I suddenly saw Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara standing on a pink lotus, wearing white garments, with a majesty and dignity that was incomparable. I gazed at the serene demeanor of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, astonished by the radiant light before my eyes, my body and mind instantly feeling pure, and my spirit immensely refreshed.

I only heard Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara earnestly say:

– You must recite Buddha’s name!

Then He waved His hand, and in the blink of an eye, He had disappeared.

I hurriedly cried out, shaking awake my roommate, telling her about the time I saw Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. So we went together to buy incense, an incense burner, and a statue of Avalokiteshvara.

When I lit the first stick of incense, I saw the Bodhisattva in a blink of an eye merge completely with His statue, and then heard Him say:

– Go to Bao Hoa Temple!

Bao Hoa Temple is in Liaoning, Dalian Province. My friend and I immediately went to Bao Hoa Temple. It seemed that the monk in the temple knew we were coming, because as soon as he met me, he said:

– I have been waiting for you for a long time!

He also said:

– You need to become a monk!

By June 19, the monk held a memorial ceremony for Mr. Tổng. At that time, I felt the earth tremble and saw Mr. Tổng being rescued from hell. I also saw countless arms coming out of hell, as if calling for help. After the salvation ritual, the monk told me:

– Mr. Tổng has been rescued from hell and has been reincarnated into the animal realm.

A year later, also on June 19, I was walking on a nearby road when I happened to encounter a mule. As soon as it saw me, it refused to move, and when I called it, it started to tear up. I did not understand why this was happening. When I returned to the temple to pay respects to the senior teacher, he said:

– This mule is actually the general director of those children.

So relatives and friends hurriedly went everywhere looking for the mule, but they could not find it.

Another year passed, that day was April 28, the donkey had slipped its rope and ran to the temple gate; no matter if people pulled or chased it, it refused to go.

At that time, the abbot was meditating, but He still told me:

– There's a donkey outside looking for you!

I hurried out to the gate, and the donkey, upon seeing me, ran over quickly, braying and tearing up.

I told it:

– You are the General Director of X, right? If so, nod your head.

He listened and understood what I said, then nodded.

Then I said:

– I take refuge for you, listen carefully.

I then followed the method taught by my master, taking refuge in the Triple Gem for the mule.

After finishing the ceremony, I said:

– Now take me to your owner's house!

The donkey nodded. It went ahead, and I followed, watching it walk along the road just like Mr. Tổng did when he was alive.

When we arrived, the donkey looked at me and then at its owner, as if silently indicating that I was its master.

I asked him when the donkey was born. When he mentioned the day, month, and year... it turned out to match perfectly with the time Mr. Tổng passed away. Right then, I was certain that this was Mr. Tổng, having escaped from hell, reincarnated as an animal in the human world.

After that, Mr. General's family went to redeem the donkey and took it to the temple to release it.

This event shocked many people's hearts. The company had a huge debt to the bank (about seventy million), but when Mr. General was still alive, he had no intention of repaying it. So, when this "earth-shattering" event happened and everyone in the company saw everything with their own eyes, the Deputy General Director immediately went to the bank to repay the entire debt. After the payment was completed, the company still had surplus money.

My relatives, friends, and colleagues, after that incident, mostly took refuge in Buddhism. Because I personally went through this event, I deeply believe that the six realms of reincarnation are indeed real, and I quietly understand that the Law of Cause and Effect is completely accurate without the slightest error.

Why did the abbot go to hell and endure all kinds of painful punishments? Of course, it was due to committing bad deeds, but that is his personal matter; I don't want to bring it up anymore. The important thing is that his experience has awakened and made many people vigilant, teaching them to self-correct and practice mindfulness in cultivating their body and mind more carefully.

Even if you are currently wealthy and possess millions of assets, once you die you cannot take a single penny with you! As the ancients often said: 'You cannot take a single thing with you, only your karma follows you!'

Since I was young, I was born into a wealthy family, and moreover, a family with high status and power. Counting all kinds of creatures—those that fly in the sky, crawl on the ground, or swim in the water…there is no creature I haven’t eaten. My evil karma accumulated deeply and heavily. I secretly thought: “In the future, if I, my parents, and relatives were condemned to hell, who would save us from there? So I made up my mind that I must become a monk to practice, vowing to cultivate until I attain supreme enlightenment”....

After finishing the story, she was still very emotional, sighing deeply.

We were shocked by the story she told; our spirits were profoundly stirred. Because the knowledge we had about the six paths of reincarnation and the law of cause and effect from before had all been read from books, it felt very distant. But the true story that the female monk just recounted happened very close by in this 21st century. The time, place, and real people involved were clearly presented before our eyes, how could it not make one feel utterly terrified?

Excerpt: Retribution in the Present Life

Author: Layperson Qua Khanh

Translator: Nun Hanh Doan

COMMENTARY:

No matter who you are, whether you have faith or not, whether you believe in Karma or not, you still have to be subject to the law of Karma. Sowing good deeds results in good outcomes, sowing evil deeds will inevitably bring adverse consequences, sooner or later. Good and evil karma always cling to us like a shadow follows a shape. Retribution does not mean it will never come, but that the conditions are not yet sufficient for it to occur; once the seeds have been sown, even after countless lifetimes, when the conditions are ripe, they must be repaid.

Therefore, the Law of Cause and Effect does not overlook a single hair or a speck of dust. I hope you remember this well and deeply believe in cause and effect, preventing evil thoughts, evil words, and evil deeds so that your life can be peaceful and happy.

Please often recite Amitabha Buddha.

Diệu Âm Lê Hiếu
