tieu_de: SINCERELY PRAYING - BEING BLESSED BY BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA TO KNOW THE FATHER'S NAME.
tom_tat: At the age of 3, I was orphaned of both parents, changed my name, and lived as a lodger. By the age of 24, I entered monkhood, still not knowing who my parents were. Now staying at a Buddhist temple, I still often think about my mother, but the trouble is I do not know what my parents' names are.
noi_dung:
SINCERELY PRAYING - BLESSED BY Kṣitigarbha BODHISATTVA TO KNOW THE FATHER'S NAME.

At the age of 3, I became an orphan, changed my name, and lived with others. By the age of 24, I became a monk, still not knowing who my parents were. Now residing at the Buddhist monastery, I still often think of my mother, but sadly I do not know the names of my parents and cannot dedicate merit to them.

Recently, I visited Pho Da Hong Buddhist Temple and learned that on April 18, there is the Great U Minh Precepts Buddhist event. So I asked the abbot, Tru Tri Zhao Gong, because I do not know my parents' names, I cannot pray for their liberation.

Hearing this, I felt even more sorrowful in my heart. So I asked further:

“Is there any method that can be performed for my parents?”

Abbot Chiêu Công said:

"The only way left is to sincerely and earnestly pray, beseeching Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha to know the full names of your parents; you must try hard, there is no other way."

Dư immediately followed Abbot Chiêu Công’s instructions, earnestly praying before the statue of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. At the hour of Tý on the night of the 17th, Dư dreamed of a piece of paper with the three characters of his father’s name, Kim Chung Liên, written on it. Overjoyed, Dư awoke...

The next morning, Du came to report the events of the dream from the previous night to the abbot Chieu Cong. The abbot and all the monks who heard this news considered it inconceivable...

Bodhisattvas of Great Vows and Great Power grant according to one's wishes. Du now recounts this story so that people in similar circumstances may develop the intention to pray. Bodhisattvas are immensely compassionate and fulfill the wishes of sentient beings, except for those whose hearts are not sincere, do not believe in the Dharma, as it will surely be difficult to receive any response. If one truly prays with a sincere heart, following the teachings of the Buddha and with correct faith, they will naturally receive a response.

- Dat Thanh - July, 33rd/1944 - according to Hoang Hoa Monthly -

(Excerpt from "The Spiritual Response Record of the Original Acts of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha" - Verified by Master Yin Guang).

tieu_de: LOOK DOWN
tom_tat: Look down to see that you are blessed to be human with all six senses intact
noi_dung:
LOOK DOWN

Look down to see that you are blessed

To be human with all six faculties complete

Out there, some people do not have all six faculties

Mute, blind, deaf... or unable to walk.

Look down to see that you are blessed

Among those suffering from chronic illness

We are strong and have few ailments

Even able to actively help ourselves and others when necessary.

Look down to see that you are Blessed

Having a house, enough clothes to wear, food to eat

Many people's lives are still very difficult

Wishing to be like you but cannot.

Look down to see that you are Blessed

Having an honest job to support yourself

Having the minimum money to spend whenever needed

There are people who wish to be like you but haven't gotten it yet.

Look down to see that you are Blessed

Having a complete family with both Mom and Dad...

Having siblings, friends near and far...

In joy and sorrow... having someone to care and share with.

Look down to see that you are blessed

Being able to live in peace in a country

Valuing feelings, morals, and Buddhist teachings

Not supporting war and killing...

Look down to see that you are blessed

Fortunate to be a disciple of Shakyamuni Buddha

Knowing to rely on the Three Jewels to realize:

Life is a sea of suffering, how can we escape suffering...

Every morning I am still able to wake up

Around me, my loved ones are still complete

It is so much blessing and happiness

Thank life for giving me much Merit

(St)

Please Always Recite

-Namo Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva

-Namo Amitabha Buddha

tieu_de: CAREER
tom_tat: Family affection, as well as romantic affection between men and women, is a type of emotion related to Karma. Only when there is a Karmic connection between you and someone will you meet, but how long you stay together depends on
noi_dung:
𝐂𝐀𝐑𝐄𝐄𝐑 𝐏𝐀𝐓𝐇

Family affection, as well as romantic affection between men and women, is a type of feeling related to Karma. Only when there is a Predestined Relationship between you and someone will you meet, but whether you stay together for a long time or a short time also depends on Karma. Included in the concept of Karma, there is both Gratitude and Resentment. Gratitude is called affectionate sentiment, which is Good Fate, while Resentment is called Enmity Fate.

If someone treats you well, worries about you, and loves you a lot, it shows that they owe you kindness from a past life. But if you love them a lot and always care for them, yet they still make you suffer again and again, it is because in a previous life you borrowed their kindness, so in this life, when the karmic connection is right, you must repay the old debt. All suffering has its deep-rooted cause; nothing is accidental.

In Karmic Fate, there is often more RESENTMENT than GRATITUDE; meeting each other is to repay Karmic debts. When Karmic Force attracts, you see the person you love as your whole world, even more important than your own life.

(That is why many people are willing to die for the one they love).

No matter how they treat you, you still accept it; no matter whether they are bad or beautiful, in your eyes they are still the most beautiful, irreplaceable person. No matter how much they make you suffer, you cannot leave them; even you do not understand why and cannot escape until you have paid off your Karma, then you unexpectedly feel your heart cool toward that person.

When Karma has ended, looking back at the path you have traveled, you will not understand why at that time you were so foolish, why you did not break up sooner with the person who caused you suffering, why you loved them to the extent of forgetting to love yourself, only to now meet them again without any feelings left for them.

When you are being influenced by Karma, even if you struggle to escape that suffering, it is difficult to break free. Only if you know how to practice, deeply understand the principle of CAUSE AND EFFECT OF KARMA, contemplate it yourself, and regularly practice mindfulness and repentance, can you hope to change the results of Karma.

Karmic fate is truly so tangled and frightening, so when we understand it, we should try not to sow kindness or hatred with anyone in this current life, so that in the future we won't have to reincarnate and repay anyone's debt.

- Despite facing a thousand days, why can't we remember

Just one meeting is hard to forget!

- Human emotions are essentially a matter of fate

The sea of life is vast, yet one person stands out to us.

That's how it is!

Homage to Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva of Great Compassion 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻

tieu_de: HOW TO MAKE GREAT COMPASSION WATER - HOW TO DRINK GREAT COMPASSION WATER CORRECTLY?
tom_tat: 1. Choose uncooked water for the Great Compassion water, tap water that is clean is fine. 2. For a glass of raw water, before chanting the Great Compassion Mantra to make offerings to the Buddha, you must first recite:
noi_dung:
HOW TO MAKE GREAT COMPASSION WATER - HOW TO DRINK GREAT COMPASSION WATER CORRECTLY?

1. Choose uncooked water for the Great Compassion water, clean tap water is fine.

2. For a glass of raw water, before reciting the Great Compassion Mantra to offer to the Buddha, first you must recite:

The mind mantra of the Tathagata of the Treasure Stupa:

Oṃ va svara maṇi svāhā (7 sounds)

Because the Buddha observed that a bowl of water contains 84,000 insects, if this mantra is not recited, it is equivalent to eating sentient beings. It is said that the Tathagata Kê has a vow: Whoever recites my heart mantra will save all sentient beings in the water. Whether it is water for Buddha recitation or water for the Great Compassion Mantra recitation. One should not use boiled water or raw water without reciting this mantra!

3. Recite the Great Compassion Mantra. (7, 21, 49, 108 times)

Join your hands and face the bowl of water, the disciple… wholeheartedly beseeches Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, seated on the altar, with compassion.

Meditate on Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva with compassion, holding a willow branch in hand, seated on a high place, sacred and solemn. Sprinkle honey flowers. I begin to concentrate on reciting the Great Compassion Mantra. Choose according to physical condition and the number of recitations. Usually, the number of times to memorize for chronic and severe illnesses is at least 49 or 108 times. In emergency cases, recite 7 times, while for regular recitation for the sick person, say 'Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva'.

4. When drinking water, one should not use the Great Compassion Bowl directly placed in the Buddha hall, but should choose another glass of water and pour the Great Compassion water into half of the glass. The patient should only drink half a glass of water.

5. There is still half a glass of water left. Use the ring finger to dip into the water and flick it with the thumb, sprinkling the Great Compassion water on the body, around the Buddha hall, on the patient, on the bed, inside the house, outside the door, outside the window, etc. While chanting and reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, visualize that many sentient beings, such as hungry ghosts and other beings, can eliminate all hatred and achieve happiness free from suffering by drinking the pure and fragrant amrita water. Follow Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara and be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

6. If there are green plants inside and outside the house, you should sprinkle a little to take in the air; plants have resilient vitality and a lot of oxygen, which is very good for health.

7. If it is raining outside, you can also recite the Great Compassion Mantra, visualizing Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara holding a willow branch, standing on a dragon riding the clouds, releasing fish, and sprinkling ambrosial water. When you recite the Great Compassion Mantra, the rain will also turn into ambrosia, and all beings soaked by the rain can be saved. They will all escape the sea of suffering and attain ultimate bliss! Thus, they can practice even when it is raining, save beings, and receive blessings! They can also accumulate immeasurable merit. I will not only be healthy and happy but also accumulate merit for rebirth in the Western Pure Land.

Please drink the water of great compassion

The water of great compassion cures all diseases:

The power of this Great Compassion Water can cure all kinds of incurable diseases. Those who drink this water must recite “Namo Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva” 10 times (if children or sick people cannot recite, those around them can recite together, for example: disciples, etc. recite Namo Great Compassionate Avalokiteshvara ten times, then start chanting), then hold it, and it will take effect immediately. If those who drink this water or their family members can make a vow to release living beings, or follow a vegetarian diet a few days each month, the effect will be particularly evident. If you practice the Dharma and recite the Great Compassion Water, the water can be unlimited and the charity can be boundless.

When drinking water, one should not use directly the Great Compassion Bowl placed in the Buddha hall, but should choose another cup of water, pouring Great Compassion water into half of the cup. The sick person is only allowed to drink half a cup of water.

The remaining half glass of water, use the ring finger to dip into the water and flick it with the thumb, sprinkling the Great Compassion water around the Buddha hall, on the body of the patient, on the bed, inside the house, outside the door, outside the window, etc. While doing this, continue chanting the Great Compassion Mantra, and imagine that many beings, such as hungry ghosts and other sentient beings, will have all their resentments eliminated and be freed from suffering, experiencing happiness by drinking the pure and fragrant ambrosial water. Follow Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara and be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

If there are green plants indoors and outdoors, sprinkle a little on them; the plants are resilient and full of oxygen, which is very good for health.

If it is raining outside, you can also recite the Great Compassion Mantra, visualizing Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva holding a willow branch, standing on a dragon riding clouds, releasing fish, and sprinkling ambrosia water. When you recite the Great Compassion Mantra, the rain will also turn into ambrosia, and all sentient beings wet by the rain can be saved. They will all have escaped the sea of suffering and attained supreme bliss! In this way, they can practice even when it is raining, save sentient beings, and receive blessings! They can also accumulate limitless merit. I am not only healthy and happy but also accumulate merit to be reborn in the Western Pure Land.

The power of the Great Compassion Water

To understand the power of the Great Compassion Water, one must first understand the power of the Great Compassion Mantra.

The Great Compassion Mantra has certain effects, and Great Compassion Water has the same effects. The effects of Great Compassion Water are similar to the effects of the Great Compassion Mantra. The Great Compassion Dharani Sutra clearly explains the efficacy of the Great Compassion Mantra. Everyone who reads it will understand. In general, Great Compassion Water is used for healing, and some is used to expel evil spirits. If there are spirits somewhere, chant the Great Compassion Mantra a few times in that place, and the spirits will become honest. Chant the Great Compassion Mantra many times over a bowl of water, then sprinkle that water, and the spirits there will honestly not dare to cause trouble.

How to consecrate Great Compassion Water?

The easiest way is to chant the Great Compassion Mantra on the surface of the water. It is also the most practical.

No additional mantras are needed, and no extra prayers are necessary. Just recite the Great Compassion Mantra facing the water. It is simple, and it is very effective. For example, if someone is possessed by evil spirits, you can recite the Great Compassion Mantra 5 times to bless the water, and just have that person drink it. Healing others requires multiple recitations; everyone should understand that all illnesses are caused by karma. The Great Compassion Mantra has a tremendous power to eliminate karmic effects. In Buddhism, there are many sects, and no sect dares to underestimate the Great Compassion Mantra because it is very powerful.

Another point is that the effectiveness of having someone else prepare Great Compassion water is not as good as making it yourself. Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva clearly states in the Buddhist Scriptures. Inviting someone to perform Buddhist services or to chant sutras earns six merits; if you transfer merit to someone, that person receives one merit. Making Great Compassion water is the same; doing it yourself is the most cost-effective. If you have physical issues, you just need to recite the Great Compassion mantra more, or make extra Great Compassion water to drink. To recite the Great Compassion mantra effectively, one must be diligent; if chanted excessively, it becomes powerful. Some ignorant people may say that Great Compassion water chanted by a certain master is very effective,I said that no matter how effective it is, it cannot compare to the water that I myself have chanted over.

tieu_de: PRAYING FOR REBIRTH IN HEAVEN IS VERY DANGEROUS
tom_tat: Reciting Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land is the supreme practice; being reborn in the Ultimate Blissful World, one will no longer be reborn in the lower realms, will completely cease creating karma, and will diligently cultivate oneself until the day of attaining Buddhahood to save others.
noi_dung:
THE PHOENIX ASCENDING TO HEAVEN IS VERY DANGEROUS

Reciting the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the Pure Land is the supreme practice. Being reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss ensures no more rebirths in suffering, completely halts the creation of karma, and allows one to diligently cultivate until the day of attaining Buddhahood to save sentient beings. Practicing other methods is certainly also good. However, if the cultivation does not reach the ultimate goal, one will inevitably fall into lower realms. In the past, there were three Bodhisattvas: Vasubandhu, Asanga, and Lion’s Roar (Sarvajñātman), who practiced Consciousness-Only meditation. The three made a vow to be born in the Tuṣita Heaven to see the Bodhisattva Maitreya. They promised each other that whoever was born there first would return to inform the others.Different knowledge. First, Lion Enlightened Master passed away, and three years went by without any report of his return. Three years later, Vasubandhu also passed away. When Vasubandhu was about to die, Asanga told him: “After you go to the Tusita Heaven, no matter what reason, you must return here to inform me.” Vasubandhu passed away, and exactly three years later he returned. Asanga asked Vasubandhu: “For what reason did you return here so late?” Vasubandhu replied: “I went to the inner courtyard of Tusita, folded my hands and made three prostrations, circled around Bodhisattva Maitreya once, and then immediately returned.” Asanga asked again: “Where is the Lion Enlightened Master now? Why hasn’t he returned?” Vasubandhu replied: “He was born in heavenThe Outer Realm of Heaven, not within the Inner Realm. Because being born into the celestial outer realm is still bound by the five desires, one does not see Bodhisattva Maitreya. It is for this reason that one cannot return here.” After hearing that being born in heaven is very dangerous, Vô Trước made a vow not to be born in heaven but to be born in the Pure Land (according to the Ten Treatises on Pure Land by Master Trí Giả). It is worth thinking that Master Lion's Awareness was a Mahayana Bodhisattva; even being born in heaven is still led by the five desires, let alone us ordinary beings. This shows that being born in heaven is extremely dangerous! For those practicing meditation, if one’s practice has not reached a level transcending the three realms, it does not matter to be born in a heaven.Well, after enjoying all the blessings, one will fall into suffering, then according to karma, receive retribution. These words were spoken by the Buddha to Ananda in the Lankavatara Sutra. Indeed, practicing Pure Land has no danger. Therefore, it should be said:

“Many people practice until they reach the Realm of Great Aspiration

But it is not as good as turning towards the Western Pure Land.”

It means that being reborn in the four formless realms of the Realm of Great Aspiration, when one's lifespan ends and merit is exhausted, one will fall into lower states of existence. It is not as good as being reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, because even if reborn in the lower levels, one can gradually attain the higher levels, which is much better than being reborn in the heavens of the Realm of Great Aspiration.

During the practice of Buddha remembrance, each day we should read the Amitabha Sutra, usually during the evening session. Reading it once means that once you have cultivated the pure and splendid realm into your store consciousness. It is like watching a movie; watching it once means those images in the movie have been cultivated in your store consciousness. Similarly, when you read the Amitabha Sutra over a long period, the magnificent and splendid realm of the Pure Land will gradually be cultivated into your store consciousness. Although at present you have not been reborn in the Pure Land, your mind is already surrounded by the Western Pure Land's realm. In the future, at the moment of your death, besides the merit of reciting and remembering the nameIf you cultivate the Buddha daily, the Buddha and the assembly of saints will appear to guide you. Additionally, the serene and solemn realms that you have cultivated daily by reading the Amitabha Sutra will also emerge from your consciousness to help you attain rebirth more swiftly.

Excerpt: Treatise on Contemplating the Buddha

Original Author: Master Dam Hu

Translator: Thich Tam An

tieu_de: KILL A BUFFALO
tom_tat: WHAT WILL BE THE CONSEQUENCES? In the time of the Buddha, the country of Dāṭhavatī and the country of Sāvatthī had conflicts over trade, so disputes between the two countries often occurred. Nevertheless, the king of Dāṭhavatī
noi_dung:
KILLING A BUFFALO

WHAT WILL BE THE CONSEQUENCES?

During the time of the Buddha, the kingdoms of Dakkakāṭha and Sāvatthī had disputes regarding trade, so conflicts often arose between the two countries. Nevertheless, the king of Dakkakāṭha was still cautious, fearing that Sāvatthī had many talented people, so the king devised a plan to test whether it was so, in order to consider war strategies. The first time, he sent someone to Sāvatthī with two mares, to see if they could distinguish which was the mother and which was the foal. It was very difficult to tell because both were the same size.

At that time, all the kings, officials, civil and military ministers could not distinguish who was the mother and who was the child.

Mr. Lê Kỳ Di - a high-ranking official, worried about that matter, seemed sad when he returned home! His daughter-in-law, named Tỳ Xá Ly, asked:

- Father, what happened at court today? I see that you are unhappy!

- My child! The country of Dak Xoa Thi Loi is sending people to bring over two mares, to see which one is the mother and which one is the offspring. None of the court officials, both civil and military, have any idea. If we cannot explain it, they will send troops to attack, so that is why I am worried!

- Father, this is not difficult! Just take a bunch of good grass, give it to them, and if you see one eating leisurely and yielding, that is the mother, and the one eating greedily and hastily is the offspring.

Father thought it made sense, so he reported to the king as the lady suggested. The king sent someone to give grass for the horses to try, and indeed, it was as the lady said. The king called the envoy over and pointed to the horse that ate slowly as the mother and the one that ate eagerly as the child. The envoy admitted it was correct. After the envoy returned home, the king was very pleased! He awarded a large honor and wealth to Mr. Lê Kỳ Di.

When the envoy arrived back in his country, he reported the truth to the king as above. The king then brought over two snakes, equal in length and size, and challenged him to identify which was male and which was female.

Following the second order, the Envoy brought the snakes to ask King Ba Tu Nac. This time, from the king to the ministers, no one could answer.

Mr. Le Ky Di went home and said to his daughter-in-law:

- My dear! Today, the country of Dac Xoa Thi Loi brought two snakes to ask which one is male and which one is female. All the kings and ministers in the court could not decide, so do you know any way to figure it out? Tell me clearly.

- Father, that is not difficult! Just take a very smooth, soft, slippery silk, spread it over a sieve, put it in, and then observe: whichever lies still or runs around is known. The females, being yin, feel the cool softness in their belly and their sexual desire is aroused, so they lie still; the males, being yang (active and hot-natured), are frightened by people and try to escape, so they run around chaotically.

He listened and thought it made sense, and reported to the king as suggested. The king had the silk prepared exactly as described, and indeed, the truth became clearly visible.

This clever scheme, if the truth were known, led the king to send someone to call the Envoy and ask for an explanation. The Envoy had to admire the king's talent for judging the truth correctly.

After the Envoy left, the king was very pleased and rewarded Mr. Lê Kỳ Di with a lot of gold and silver.

The Envoy returned and reported to King Đặc Xoa Thị Lợi about the correct judgment of King Ba Tư Nặc, but the king still did not fully believe it, so he again had the Envoy bring across a wooden stick one trượng long, with both ends smooth without knots or marks, to ask how one could tell the base from the tip?

The envoy obediently carried it to the country of Sāvatthi, but this time no one knew about it. Mr. Lê Kỳ Di returned to ask his daughter-in-law:

- My dear! This time the country of Takkasīla has sent over a smooth piece of wood without any knots. It's hard to tell the root from the tip, and no one at the court can decide. So, do you have any way to tell me?

- Father, that matter is even easier. Just throw it into the river, and you’ll know: the end that sinks is the root; the end that floats is the tip; because the root is always heavy, so it sinks; the tip is always light, so it floats.

Mr. Lê Kỳ Di reported to the king as previously mentioned, and the king ordered it to be thrown into the river. Indeed, one end sank while the other floated. The king called the envoy and said:

- You, the envoy, should know: the sinking end is the root, the floating end is the tip.

The envoy said:

- Yes, Your Majesty, just as You said, I, your humble servant, accept!

The envoy returned to his homeland and reported to his king that:

- Your Majesty! This time, following Your Majesty's order to send wood over, they all spoke correctly, so it is known that the country of Sāvatī has many talented people, as I have observed.

The king, upon hearing this, also felt admiration and ceased considering waging war against Sāvatī. Wanting the two countries to have friendly relations, the king of the Kosala kingdom sent people with gold, silver, and various precious items to present to the king of Pāṭaliputra, along with saying:

- We praise the merits in Your Majesty’s country, having so many talented people; from now on, effort should be made to cultivate virtue and filial piety, and teach the people to follow the correct teachings.

At that time, the Persian king summoned Mr. Lê Kỳ Di to the palace and asked:

- Regarding the answers given just now, how do you know them?

- Your Majesty! That is my daughter-in-law, sir; I myself do not possess extraordinary intelligence beyond that of the male scholars of the civil examination.

The king, upon hearing this, held Miss Tỳ Xá Ly in great esteem, rewarded her generously, and even conferred upon her the title of "Third Sister".

Over many years, Lady Tỳ Xá Ly gave birth to thirty-two sons. The first son was exceptionally dignified, and as he grew older, he possessed unparalleled strength, able to defeat a thousand men. His parents loved him dearly! Everyone in the country respected him. Later, when arranging marriages for the sons, they all married daughters from prominent and virtuous families in the country.

Lady Tỳ Xá Ly was originally a devout follower of the Triple Gem and often went to listen to the Buddha's teachings. That day, she invited the Buddha and the monks to a meal offering. After the Buddha finished eating and ascended the seat to give a sermon, everyone in the household, both adults and children, attained the stage of Stream-entry, except for her youngest son, who had less understanding and therefore did not attain any stage of enlightenment.

He was still aggressive, riding a white elephant every day for entertainment. One day, he passed a large wooden bridge. On the bridge, the son of the Deputy General sat on a carriage, and the two boys quarreled: each boy relied on being from a prestigious family and refused to yield. The son of Lady Tỳ Xá Ly became angry, jumped off his elephant, pushed over the carriage and the Deputy General's son into the muddy moat, watching him being covered in mud, bloodied, struggling to get up, walking while crying, and went home to report to his father:

- Father, the son of Lady Tỳ Xá Ly unjustly pushed the carriage and the boy into the moat, causing me such pain!

The Assistant Minister saw his son in too much pain and angrily said:

- He is strong and healthy, moreover he is close to the king. Stop crying, my son, and let me take revenge for you!

This Assistant Minister borrowed thirty-two magic whips made of precious treasures, with a sharp knife inserted inside each whip, and then gave one to each of the sons of Tỳ Xá Ly.

These boys were still young and impulsive, and they were delighted with the whips, often taking them to play, being careless, and not understanding the deep intention of the Assistant Minister.

The country's law strictly forbids carrying knives when entering the king's palace; anyone who disobeys the order will be sentenced to death. It was common for the children of Lady Tỳ Xá Ly to enter and leave the king's house, and no one could forbid it, because the king was very favorable toward Lady Tỳ Xá Ly.

That day, the Deputy Minister reported to the king:

- Your Majesty, Lady Tỳ Xá Ly's thirty-two children are very strong; one person could match a thousand. They are plotting to harm the king!

The king heard him but did not fully believe it; he further reported:

- Your Majesty, regarding this matter, I have observed the truth and there is much evidence! Because I saw that each of the boys had a whip; inside each whip there was a sharp knife!

The king immediately sent someone secretly to check the whips, and indeed found the knives inside, proving the truth. The king then ordered the strongmen to call thirty-two boys into the palace, confiscate all the whips, and secretly execute them without anyone knowing, beheading the thirty-two boys and placing their heads into a wooden box, carefully sealed, and delivered it to Lady Vaiśālī.

In the middle of that day, Lady Visakha invited the Buddha and the monks to her house for an alms-giving feast. The house was bustling; some were carrying rice, others were pouring water in a lively manner. She saw the king's men bringing a chest, and she silently rejoiced, saying:

- Perhaps today the king has sent these fine foods to help me offer them!

She ordered someone to open it and see.

The Buddha said:

- Wait! Let me finish eating first, then we will open it!

After receiving the alms, the Buddha called her to sit beside Him and said:

- This body is impermanent; it endures suffering! Then it becomes emptiness, which is no-self; life is full of dangers and accidents, and fear arises because it cannot exist for long; it is bound by all kinds of afflictions, with indescribable bitterness, and attachments will eventually part! Loving and clinging to one another tires both the body and the mind, which is of no benefit to the path. I say this, only those with wisdom can understand this essential Dharma.

After hearing the Buddha, she had faith and insight, then attained the fruit of Anāgāmi, joyfully clasped her hands and respectfully said to the Buddha:

- Homage to the Blessed One, I make the four offerings as follows:

1. I offer to the sick Bhikkhus, and the foods suitable for their illnesses.

2. I offer to those who diagnose illnesses.

3. I offer first to Bhikkhus who come from afar.

4. I offer provisions to Bhikkhus who travel far.

O Blessed One! The sick, because they do not have good medicine and delicious food, recover slowly, or are difficult to heal, or die in this world. Those who examine and care for the sick must look after the patients, so they cannot go on alms rounds; therefore, I offer food. Those who come from distant places, not yet acquainted with anyone, when going on alms rounds may encounter fierce dogs or inhumane people who harm the body or insult them; therefore, I offer food beforehand. Those who travel far must have companions; if they do not have food to bring or cannot go in time, and the roads are dangerous with many wild beasts, traveling alone may result in accidents; therefore, I provide food.

The World-Honored One, seeing that she requested those four things, praised her by saying:

- How precious it is to have such a mind; the merit is very great, in this way it is no different from offering to the Buddha!

After speaking, the Buddha and the monks returned to the Parileyya Forest.

After the Buddha had gone, she sent someone to open the chest to see what the king had given; instead, she saw thirty-two human heads, which were her sons. Because she had understood that life is impermanent, and had attained the fruit of Anāgāmi, her attachment to the world was completely gone, so there was no illusion or grief to mourn, but she only thought briefly:

- How sorrowful! How pitiful! Wherever there is birth, there is death; sinking and rising among the five desires; what suffering can be like this!

At that time, the thirty-two families of the wives, upon hearing that their sons-in-law had been killed by the king, said:

- The king unjustly kills innocent, righteous people!

Their love for their sons-in-law and indignation rose to an extreme! They brought troops to surround the king’s capital to seek revenge.

King Bà Tư Nặc fled to the Buddha, and they pursued him, surrounding the Kỳ Hoàn forest. At that time, venerable Ananda came out to invite them in to ask what the original cause of the matter was.

Thirty-two fathers-in-law of Mrs. Tỳ Xá Ly, after paying respects to the Buddha, withdrew to one side, and Venerable Ananda, kneeling straight, said to the Buddha:

- Revered World-Honored One! Did the thirty-two children of Mrs. Tỳ Xá Ly commit any evil in the past with the king? Why are they now being killed by him? We humbly ask for Your guidance so that we may understand clearly.

The Buddha taught:

- This story of the unjust fate of past lives happened a long time ago. At that time, there were thirty-two people who were close friends. One day, they caught a buffalo to eat together and enjoy themselves. Nearby, there was an elderly poor woman who had no children, so they brought the buffalo to her to help slaughter. She happily allowed it, providing firewood, pots, knives, and fans to borrow. When it was about to be killed, the buffalo knelt down pleading for its life, but their hearts were callous and they did not listen, gathering together to wrestle the buffalo down, kill it, butcher it, stir-fry, braise, and prepare it until they ate to fullness. The old woman that day also had a full meal and then said: "Thanks to you, I have had a meal of meat."no longer craving."

Venerable Ananda should know:

The buffalo of that time, who is now King Bāṭu Nāk, the people who stole the buffalo at that time, are now the thirty-two children of Lady Tỳ Xa Ly. Because of that karmic retribution, in five hundred lifetimes, they are repeatedly killed by you, and this continues even up to the present day. The old lady was someone who helped and rejoiced in the killing of the buffalo, so in five hundred lifetimes she has to become the mother of these people, and endure that bitter suffering!

Upon hearing and understanding clearly the story of mutual retribution, Venerable Ananda asked the Buddha:

- Homage to the Blessed One! What merit do these people have to be born into wealthy households with healthy bodies? I humbly ask You to teach them?

The Buddha said:

- Ananda, you should know: This was also a past life, during the time of the Buddha Kassapa. There was an old woman who believed in and respected the Triple Gem. She was very wealthy. One day, she took incense, flowers, and oil to paint the Buddha's stupa. On the way, she met thirty-two young men, and she took the opportunity to advise them: "Where are you going? There is a very meritorious task. Today I am going to paint the Buddha's stupa. If you help me paint it, you will gain strength, health, and beauty in your lives!"

They replied: "Is that so, grandmother? Yes, grandmother, as you have instructed, we will go."

After finishing painting, they all respectfully said: "Respected elder! Because you advised us to cultivate blessings, we sincerely dedicate this merit, wishing that wherever we are born, we will be honored and prosperous, and may we always be your children; you are our mother, and may we encounter the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and swiftly attain enlightenment!"

The old lady said: "How precious! You all make such vows! With the blessings of the Three Jewels, whatever you wish in the future will certainly be fulfilled!"

Ananda, you should know: the old lady back then is now Mrs. Visāli, and these thirty sons are now her children.

At that time, the soldiers besieging the Kỳ Hoàn forest, after hearing the Buddha speak, realized that it was due to the mutual karmic retribution, so their anger naturally dissipated, and they themselves went before King Pasenadi to apologize.

Then, the World-Honored One, for the sake of the four groups of disciples, extensively spoke about wholesome deeds to practice, unwholesome deeds to abandon, and clearly explained the Four Noble Truths.

After the Buddha finished preaching, everyone rejoiced and paid their respects before departing.

(Excerpt from the Sutra of Wise and Benevolent Causes)

tieu_de: Commemoration of the day of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara's Enlightenment
tom_tat: June 19 commemorates the enlightenment of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, wishing for the complete liberation of all beings. Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, also called Guanyin Bodhisattva, is the Bodhisattva who rescues from suffering and disasters, and saves and transforms living beings. 'Lotus Sutra'
noi_dung:
Commemoration of the day of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara's Enlightenment

June 19 commemorates the enlightenment of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, wishing all sentient beings complete liberation. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, also called Guan Shi Yin Bodhisattva, is the Bodhisattva who saves beings from suffering and disaster, and guides sentient beings. The "Lotus Sutra" states: "When sentient beings are in suffering and distress, if they wholeheartedly call the Bodhisattva's name, they will immediately be liberated, taking the name Guan Shi Yin." He is one of the Three Saints of the Western Paradise, together with Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva, serving as attendants to the Master of the Western Pure Land, Amitabha Buddha. The seventh chapter of the "Lotus Sutra," titled "The Universal Gate of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara," clearly states that Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva regards the salvation of sentient beings and relieving suffering as his work.Rescuing those in distress, saving sentient beings from sorrow and difficulties. He has many manifestations, which could be the Buddha body, a monk, and for each different audience, he appears in a different form. The “Avatamsaka Sutra,” volume 6, records that Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara resides in the South Sea. However, in the “Larger Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra” and the “Infinite Life Sutra,” it is said that Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara often resides in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, that is, the Western Pure Land. Avalokitesvara manifests in countless ways, with a thousand eyes and a thousand hands, transforming in unimaginable ways, using the Great Compassion Sutra to eliminate misfortunes and end suffering. Wherever he is, he can hear and understand the suffering of sentient beings, always ready to extend his hands to support and protect. In particular, Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara isConsidered as the Bodhisattva who transforms fate for women, protecting mothers and children. The 19th of the 6th lunar month is the day when Quan Am attained enlightenment, and sentient beings commemorate, remember her merits, and offer lamp ceremonies. On this day, one should go to the temple to purify the mind, follow a vegetarian diet, recite the Buddha's name, and chant the Great Compassion Mantra to bring peace to the whole family, avoid calamities, and turn misfortune into blessing. Anytime in life, if encountering difficulties or suffering, recite 'Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva' to receive blessings. And most importantly, follow the example of learning from the Buddha, turn toward goodness, practice virtuous deeds, accumulate a good heart; everything will flow smoothly, easily, completely fulfilling, and always remain calm and at peace.

tieu_de: THE_MIRACLE_WHEN_CHANTING_LĂNG_NGHIÊM_MANTRA
tom_tat: #VALUABLE_SHARING Messages from Nun Hạnh Đoan:
noi_dung:
THE_MIRACLE_WHEN_CHANTING_LANG_NGHIEM

#VALUABLE_SHARING_WORDS

A message from Nun Hạnh Đoan:

Recently, there have been rumors like this: Anyone who recites the Lăng Nghiêm mantra will have their house collapse, and if you are a layperson, you are not allowed to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra at home. There are even many slanderous theories claiming that the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra does not exist and that the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is completely useless.

I myself have also received many attacks and slanders. But to me, these words are worthless, and I do not pay any attention to them at all. What is important is that each person practices and experiences for themselves; when you have experience and firm faith, indifferent criticisms become meaningless and have no effect at all. If they do, it is only a test of whether your practice is good and whether your determination is strong and steadfast.

Through many articles I have posted, you already know that a person reciting the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, if they want to achieve good results as the Buddha taught, must strictly follow a vegetarian diet, observe strict precepts, avoid eating the five pungent substances (onion, chives, garlic bulbs…), and maintain focused mind without idle thoughts during chanting.

The Lăng Nghiêm Mantra should be chanted as much as possible (at least a few times a day, at most 21 times a day); in this way, you yourself will experience the benefits that the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra brings and realize whether what the Buddha taught in the sutras is true or just theoretical.

If you do not strictly follow a vegetarian diet, do not observe precepts, and constantly have idle thoughts while chanting, then do not ask me why the Lăng Nghiêm mantra is not effective. Do not hastily attack or slander (when you have not yet observed the mandatory conditions required during chanting).

Everyone eats to fill themselves, everyone practices to benefit themselves. Whether the practice succeeds or fails depends on each individual.

The Buddha is the one who shows the way, and his disciples must walk it. No one can do it for you, practice for you… or grant you any miraculous ability if you do not practice and do not experience it for yourself.

If you do not practice and only worry about criticizing, attacking, or creating obstacles… then you are creating unhappiness for yourself and others.

After finishing translating this article, I did not intend to post it, because translating is extremely difficult and finding the article is very hard. For me, this is a precious gift, and if I give it too easily… I fear people will take it lightly, not appreciate it.

But after a while of thinking and calculating, I feel compassion for those beginners who do not yet have enough faith, and for those who have patiently practiced, even if they face much criticism and slander…

I reconsidered, if I don't share it now, then in case... my breath suddenly stops, and no one gets to read it, I will cause those who deserve to see it to miss a good opportunity!

Well then, because life is impermanent, since we live today but cannot guarantee that we will exist tomorrow (or a little later) in this world...

You should consider this translation as a precious gift that I sincerely share with those who are destined to receive it, hoping that anyone who reads it will gain many benefits and strengthen their firm faith to practice, so that my effort in translating and publishing it is not in vain.

This heartfelt letter will stop here, sincerely sending all my love and respect to the citizens of FB, wishing you all the best! Now, please start reading:

A 10-YEAR-OLD CHILD SEES A STRANGE SIGHT WHEN I RECITE THE SUTRAS

Original Chinese text: Facebook edmcany (post dated January 13, 2012)

Hanh Doan translated in April 2019

I have a grandson who is 21 years old this year. About eleven years ago, when he was ten years old, I was still studying far from home and only returned to visit my mother after the Lunar New Year. I always carried with me the book "Diamond Sutra" and "The Chapter on Universal Virtue and Vows of Samantabhadra."

At home, whenever I was free, I would chant sutras. One day, while I was chanting the Diamond Sutra, my grandson, seeing it was strange, came over to stand beside me and watch, then closed his eyes and listened attentively.

I chanted aloud (silently hoping that my nephew could hear the Diamond Sutra, wishing that he could benefit from it).

After I finished one round of chanting, my nephew suddenly told me:

- Uncle, when you were chanting, I saw a very strange scene...

In front of my eyes, a beam of white light suddenly appeared from afar, shining into my eyes, followed by four or five other halos entering; this scene was as clear as being projected on a television screen, but bright and looking very real.

Moreover, I saw another realm: I saw a Buddha being surrounded by many monks listening to Him...

At that moment, I was extremely surprised, but my heart was still doubtful, wondering: Could it be that my grandchild is imagining or fabricating this? Because honestly, it is hard for me to believe!

Then I began chanting the "Universal Worthy Bodhisattva's Practices and Vows". As soon as I finished one recitation, my grandchild told me again:

- Hey, when you were chanting this sutra, I saw a Bodhisattva appear. This Bodhisattva looked very strange because he was riding… it seemed like… a big pig. I couldn’t see the whole body of the pig clearly, but the strange thing was that its legs looked round and thick from top to bottom!

I said:

- Legs that are round and thick all the way like you described… then they must be elephant legs!

- Oh, then maybe it’s… a giant elephant? Because it’s really big!

I said:

- Chant once more, and take a look at how the scene changes!

After I finished chanting, my grandson said:

- Uncle, this time I can see it clearly, it really is an elephant, not a pig! I can see it from head to tail, and even its fur! And this great elephant looks very strange, it has… six teeth, three on each side!

My grandson is only ten years old, and until now he had never come into contact with any Buddhist sutras, books, stories, or sacred objects. Initially, no one in our family believed in Buddha, nor did we have any Buddha altars.

At that moment I was extremely astonished, because I understood that the boy could not possibly imagine a white elephant with six tusks (symbolizing the perfection of the Six Paramitas).

Then he continued to tell:

- While you were chanting sutras, I saw that in the Bodhisattva's hand was a vase; He poured water over you, and then this water turned into light, making your body shine. Then the large elephant also sprayed water on you, and when the water touched your body, it all turned into radiance, cleansing all the impurities on your body.

After this incident happened, I began to believe, my heart full of joy. Because I felt that the child could not possibly lie, could not imagine or make up a story about a six-tusked white elephant, since in reality, in our life, THERE IS NO SIX-TUSKED WHITE ELEPHANT!

The incident astonished me greatly.

There was another thing that the child saw and recounted, which amazed me even more: Back then, I really liked chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, this mantra was quite long. After I finished chanting, I would contemplate the mantra, I must say that I extremely enjoyed chanting.

One day, while I was chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, the boy came up to me and said:

- Uncle, while you were chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, I saw a very strange scene!

He recounted: In the place where you were sitting, I saw on both sides the appearance of two Great Heavenly Kings, extraordinarily huge, much taller than you, looking very majestic! And outside, there were four others, I recognized these four as the Four Great Heavenly Kings!

I asked:

- How do you know and are so certain about that?

The boy replied:

- Because I saw these four figures holding treasures such as a pipa, a sword, an umbrella, etc., and I had seen four great heavenly kings with exactly the same appearance in the Journey to the West movie before, so I knew and recognized them immediately! Behind these four heavenly kings, there were many angels, appearing in all kinds of forms, colors, and shapes... In general, these deities wore different clothes and armor, which looked very strange! But I felt that all of them seemed good; it seemed like they came... to protect you!

Besides these angels, there are countless other layers and layers of gods, as many as... rice ripening fully, thickly spread in autumn fields, glowing golden across the sky! Each of these gods is neatly dressed, looking like celestial soldiers and generals, because everyone holds weapons in their hands. DEPENDING ON THE PRAYER VERSES THAT ARE CONTINUOUSLY CHANTED, THEY APPEAR MORE AND MORE, WITH DENSITY BECOMING INCREASINGLY THICK.

Except for this place, I also saw at the back of his body another Bodhisattva, extremely tall in appearance, with snakes coiled around his body. But his facial skin was blue, covered in rough warts, coarse, with fangs protruding from his mouth… Behind him, there was even fire! I saw that this Bodhisattva was very tall, as tall as… a mountain, but his appearance looked extremely ugly, terrifying, very frightening! But strangely, it seemed that all the celestial generals and deities present here were under his command and took orders from him; all of them followed his arrangements, directions, and deployments!

This amazed me. Indeed, in the Lankavatara Sutra, when the World-Honored One expounded on the Lankavatara Dharani, He described in detail and recounted many merits of the Lankavatara Dharani.

The sutra records it like this: At that time, there were the Brahma Devas and Indra Devas, who rose from their seats and vowed: IN THE FUTURE, IF ANYONE RECEIVES AND MAINTAINS THIS SUTRA, WE SHALL PROTECT AND UPHOLD THE DHARMA FOR THEM, HELPING THEM ELIMINATE OBSTACLES, AND ALL THEIR WISHES WILL BE FULFILLED.

Thus, the two beings who appeared beside me, whom my child saw first, are very likely Phạm Thiên and Đế Thích Thiên.

The scripture also records: After Phạm Thiên and Đế Thích made their vows, then the Four Great Heavenly Kings stood up and made their vows: WE VOW TO PROTECT THOSE WHO RECITE THIS MANTRA, TO HELP THEM ELIMINATE OBSTACLES, AND THAT ALL THEIR WISHES WILL BE FULFILLED! Therefore, it is clear that my child saw the Four Great Heavenly Kings behind Phạm Thiên and Đế Thích.

The scripture also records: After the four Heavenly Kings made their vows, countless river gods, mountain gods... (all gathered to stand up and make similar vows) Eventually, there were EIGHTY-FOUR THOUSAND NADOTHAS, countless deities, Vajra Treasury Kings, along with innumerable followers, all made the vow: We vow to protect those who practice just as this before the World Honored One. They also said: If anyone comes to disturb or trouble the practitioner, we will use this precious club to smash that person's head to pieces like dust (EIGHTY-FOUR THOUSAND NADOTHAS – is an illustrative number, implying countless. One nadoṭha: ten trillion. One cūṣa: one hundred).Hundreds of thousands: It means there are countless, limitless Vajra Treasury King Bodhisattvas who will come to protect this mantra.)

Because my grandchild is still young, he can only describe the immeasurable and boundless Bodhisattva Vajra Treasury King appearing as numerous as rice ripening golden in the field, their bodies radiating immeasurable and boundless dazzling golden light.

This profoundly shook my mind. Because I thought: We are ordinary beings, still in the cycle of reincarnation within the six realms, with such deep greed, anger, and ignorance, so what merit do we have that deserves protection? But how is it that when I recite the mantra, countless vajras, celestial beings… appear to protect me, innumerably?

There is only one explanation: THOSE BEINGS CAME TO PROTECT THE LANKA SUTRA MANTRA!

In the Lanka Sutra, it is said: All Buddhas of the ten directions are born from this mantra, so the Lanka Sutra Mantra can be called the mother of the Buddhas. The Tathagatas of the ten directions rely on this mantra to attain the supreme, equal, and perfect enlightenment.

They manifest in as many forms as there are particles of dust in the worlds of water to turn the wheel of Dharma, teach sentient beings, give predictions for sentient beings in the ten directions, save sentient beings from suffering, and enable all beings to attain liberation; all of them rely on the power of the Shurangama Mantra!

The Buddhas of the ten directions, through this mantra, subdue all demons and heretical teachings. If one wishes to achieve good results in practice, one must recite this mantra… The merits of this mantra are beyond counting…

THIS LENG NGHIEM INCANTATION IS EXACTLY THE HEART OF THE TEN DIRECTIONS BUDDHA. WHEREVER THIS INCANTATION EXISTS, THERE IS BUDDHA. WHOEVER CHANTS THIS INCANTATION CAN HARMONIZE WITH BUDDHA. THEREFORE, ALL DHARMA PROTECTORS, VASUDEVAS… WILL COME TO PROTECT THEM.

I am a person who studies science, so everything I lecture on always requires evidence.

If I had not personally experienced this, then for all the merits of Tantric sutras and Buddha incantations, I would not easily have enough firm faith.

The events occurred as narrated by a ten-year-old child, who had absolutely no knowledge of Buddhist teachings, so I believed it. Because I thought that the child could not possibly fabricate or imagine such a strange and unimaginable realm. And what the child described, by coincidence, matched the ancient scriptures that had recorded it!

That is why my faith became firm, surely believing without doubt: The words that the Buddha spoke in the sutras, every single one, are true, just as the Diamond Sutra said: THE WORDS OF THE TATHAGATA ARE TRUE WORDS, GENUINE WORDS, NOT ILLUSORY!

In the past, when chanting sutras, I usually focused on the meaning, while I often did not pay attention to the merits that the Buddha listed and described in detail in the sutras. I only thought: "The World-Honored One describes the merits so thoroughly because He has good intentions in wanting to guide beings to practice"… so I completely ignored them and did not believe in them at all.

But after this experience, after hearing my nephew describe what he saw, I no longer deny all the merits that the Buddha has preached, and I completely believe in what the Buddha taught, believing every word and every sentence he spoke, not as empty theory, but as something completely real to a shocking extent.

Nun Thich Nu Hanh Doan translated on 24/6/2019

tieu_de: RECITING THE GREAT COMPASSION MANTRA & THE MANTRA 'OM MA NI PAD ME HUM' - THE BLIND SEE AGAIN.
tom_tat: I am Nun Thich Nu Le Phat, the abbess of Chau An Pagoda at 498/1/2 Le Quang Dinh, Ward 1, Go Vap District, Ho Chi Minh City. I would like to recount here a miraculous and truly 100% real event about the sacred power of the Great Compassion Mantra.
noi_dung:
DHARANI OF GREAT COMPASSION & THE MANTRA "OM MANI PADME HUM" - THE BLIND EYE BECOMES SIGHTED.

I am Nun Thich Nu Le Phat, the abbess of Chau An Pagoda at 498/1/2 Le Quang Dinh, Ward 1, Go Vap District, Ho Chi Minh City. I would like to share here a truly miraculous and 100% real story about the mighty power of the Great Compassion Mantra and the mantra "OM MA NI PAD ME HUM," so that fellow monks, nuns, and Buddhists both inside and outside the country, upon reading this article, will be inspired to recite the mantra and thereby share in the blessings of the Buddhas.

I would like to briefly explain the reason why I practice recitations. Who is the teacher that transmitted the teachings? What is their spiritual conduct like? If one wants to learn a certain practice, one must choose a teacher who is both talented and virtuous, with exemplary spiritual conduct, in order to entrust one’s soul properly, right?

"In 1992, our Chân An Monastery welcomed a monk from overseas. The teacher came to give gifts to a number of young, impoverished, and studious monks and nuns (nearly 30 of them).

The Honda carrying the Master stopped. I anxiously looked to see what the monk was like. (At that time, very few overseas monks returned to the country). A tall, thin foreigner, with a graceful appearance, wearing a floppy hat, leather sandals, and a brown robe faded by the elements. The Master was a French person born in Vietnam. An immense astonishment! Looking at the Master, there was no difference from the FRANCISCAN priests who had ascetic lives in Vietnam and helped the poor a lot. A feeling of reverence swept over my soul.

The vast majority of teachers returning from abroad dress luxuriously without any complaints, so why is this monk so austere? The teacher solemnly sits down. After the introduction and expressing the intention to help monks and nuns in need to be able to continue their studies, the teacher stands up to speak. His words are so gentle and polite, reminding the young monks and nuns to strive to maintain their moral conduct in their practice and studies, and not to be lax. Practicing abroad is very hard, not at all comfortable... The teacher handed each person an envelope (One Hundred Thousand VND).

Seeing the humility of the Master like that! After the intimate meeting, the Master left. The image of this ascetic monk kept me thinking. How could I have a chance to talk with the Master once to understand his practice? The Master’s work is too busy, he has no free time, when would he come here? I silently prayed to the Buddha for me to be able to talk with this person.

Surprisingly, a week later the Master visited Tu Quang Pagoda at night to see Master Nhat Thien. The Master wanted to stay, but it was difficult to find accommodation there, so he went to Chau An to request to stay for one night. While everyone was preparing a room for the Master, I invited him to sit down to get to know him.

I asked:

- Master! Life in Vietnam is very difficult; the purpose of escaping to the West is to find a comfortable life for oneself and to help family. On the contrary, what reason led you to enter the monastic path with such great courage and strength?

At that time, the Master sincerely shared about a period of his childhood until he escaped to a foreign land and finally ordained into the religion. The Master said:

- I entered retreat for three years, three months, three days, and three hours at a Tibetan Buddhist monastery in France. At the end of the retreat, I traveled everywhere to teach the Dharma, but my mind still attained realization during the retreat period.

I replied:

- Regarding friendship, Master, were you fortunate to meet any gurus who taught you anything in the secret chamber? Please, Master, have compassion for those who are still in darkness and ignorance, and teach us. Or if there are any good materials about the path in the future, please send them to us so that we can study and learn.

The Master nodded and said:

- In the secret chamber, I was able to teach the Great Compassion Mantra and the "OM MA NI PAD ME HUM" mantra with all my heart, and I trained some Yoga movements to support health.

The teacher taught me how to perform the 'Four Great Five Continents' mudra while chanting the mantra and the special methods to open the Sara. I memorized it by heart, but my mind wasn’t very interested, somewhat looking down on that mantra.

The teacher stayed in Vietnam for several months. The teacher’s virtue is beyond what words can describe. The closer you are to the teacher, the more you admire him, a true Bodhisattva virtue manifested, not just lip service. The teacher printed hundreds of millions worth of scriptures, led groups everywhere to offer them. For remote temples one, two, three kilometers off the road, under the blazing sun or pouring rain, the teacher alone carried the scriptures and money there to offer them (at that time, none of us in the group were willing to go with the teacher because of the sun, rain, and fatigue). An hour or two later, the teacher would walk back, his face showing an unusual joy. The teacher smiled and said:

- The scriptures are the Buddha's teachings and must be spread everywhere so that the people can benefit from them.

Whenever visiting any poor temple lacking food, any temple lacking drinking water in need of a well, or a place needing a water reservoir, or a temple that is dilapidated, the Master always supports according to the actual needs. The Master sincerely helps the poor and starving fellow people, taking all the money in His pocket, sometimes fifty or seventy thousand, sometimes even a hundred thousand. Everywhere, people rely on the Master to give Dharma talks. The Master teaches the Dharma like a silkworm spinning silk. Everyone who listens becomes enlightened, and the Master gives them scriptures to read and strive in their practice.

I thought: "This monk has truly been practicing the path of loving-kindness, compassion, empathetic joy, equanimity, with very profound spiritual power. I must follow and practice likewise."

That said, the work at the temple was busy. Then the Master returned to France...

There were only two and a half months left until the Quí Dậu New Year (1993) when, suddenly, my eyes started to hurt. I hurried to see Dr. Kính, an eye specialist with a private practice on Kiêu Bridge slope. The doctor prescribed medicine to take and eye drops, but my eyes worsened day by day, aching terribly, unable to endure even a bit of light. Despite the doctor examining me repeatedly and continuously changing the medicine, there was no improvement. Finally, the doctor told me that I had a difficult-to-treat viral infection. Vietnam does not have sufficient facilities, and I would need to go abroad to have a chance of recovery. The doctor's statement made my hands and feet go limp, and I felt like fainting.

I went home feeling depressed, miserable, and hopeless. Oh dear! What kind of karmic retribution is so heavy? This pain cannot be fully described with words. I have cried a lot, silently thinking whether my youth has done any wrong: at 17, a young, graceful Gia Long schoolgirl, I cut my green hair and became a young nun at the temple since 1963, surely I did not commit any unvirtuous act against anyone? What karmic obstacle is making me suffer so much? Buddha, please save me!!!

In a moment of poor judgment, I intended to seek death, so I asked my disciple to buy a pack of sleeping pills, and the disciple, hearing this, also bought them. In the morning, holding the pack of pills, I had already made my decision... Then in the afternoon, I received materials from Master of Buddhist Practice sent from France. The disciple opened them and read them to me. It was a lecture on the miraculous power of the Great Compassion Mantra and the mantra "OM MANI PADME HUM" given by the Dalai Lama in France; translated into Vietnamese by the Buddhist Pham Cong Thien.

After listening, I suddenly woke up thinking, why? Why haven't I recited the mantra? Relying on the divine power of the secret mantra and Avalokiteshvara to save me. I resolved to recite the mantra, rely on the power of the mantra, and pray for karmic resolution.

Then I carefully went to burn three incense sticks in the darkness of the meditation room, and at the ancestral altar I knelt and earnestly prayed to Avalokiteshvara to witness my recitation of the Great Compassion Mantra and the mantra "OM MANI PADME HUM" to resolve the karmic consequences of my sickly body. After the prayer, I sat cross-legged and made the hand seal "Four Great Five Continents" as taught by Master Phat Dao.

Strangely, as soon as I made the seal, my hand naturally trembled, then my whole body started to shake. I was so scared! Did I commit some sacrilege that caused this strange phenomenon? The other day, the Master also taught, but when I made the seal back then, nothing happened. I tried to pull my hand away, but I couldn't. I focused my mind, thought about it, or was it that making the seal, the Buddha was giving me a sign?

Five minutes later, my body gradually stopped shaking. I began to focus all my mind on reciting 108 times the mantra "OM MA NI PAD ME HUM" and 21 times the Great Compassion mantra. Then, I knelt and prayed to Avalokiteshvara, asking for the Buddha's blessed water, taking a sip, wiping some on my face, and putting some in my eyes. The next morning, when I opened my eyes, I noticed that the pain in my eyes had significantly lessened...

Starting from that day, I recited the mantra four times a day: 8 a.m., 2 p.m., 7 p.m., and midnight. I followed the same routine the next day, and when I made the hand gesture, I no longer felt any trembling, and my eyes were no longer painful.

On the third day, I found my eyes extremely comfortable...

On the fourth day, my eyes could see clearly in the dark. Oh, what a great miracle! I became even more devoted to reciting the mantra.

On the fifth day, my eyes began to receive daylight without feeling uncomfortable as before, even light passing through the eye drops did not cause glare.

By the sixth day, I opened the door and could see the sky, my eyes felt very comfortable...

On Saturday, after I finished reciting the mantra, I opened the door and stepped into the courtyard, looking at all the scenery in the temple. Oh! So delighted! This joy cannot be expressed in words. Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva has saved my life and healed my illness!!! The majestic power of the mantra is incredibly miraculous and effective...

Respected Monks, Nuns, and Buddhists who visited were all amazed at my miraculous recovery from illness. My eyes regained their sight, and the benefactor who helped me was Thay Phat Dao. Under the blessing of Avalokiteshvara, Thay Phat Dao sent me the materials at exactly the right time, right when I was completely desperate.

I hope that, in the future, I will have the opportunity to travel all the way to Europe to pay my respects and give thanks to the Master, and to share the indescribable joy of someone who has died and is now living again. Above is a miraculous story of the efficacy of the Great Compassion mantra and the mantra "OM MA NI PAD MÊ HUM" in resolving karmic obstacles... and I HAVE COMPLETELY RECOVERED.

(A miraculous story of Nun Thich Nu Le Phat - Abbot of Chau An Pagoda, Ho Chi Minh City).

tieu_de: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU DESCEND INTO THE INFERNAL HELL TO RECEIVE PUNISHMENT?
tom_tat: In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, it is said that those who commit grave sins and are sent to the Avīci Hell will experience the following. The instruments used to execute the sinners include: tridents, sticks, hawks, snakes, wolves, dogs, pestles, mills, and cư
noi_dung:
WHAT HAPPENS WHEN ONE IS SENT TO THE INESCAPABLE HELL?

In the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, it is said that those who commit grave sins and are condemned to the Avīci Hell will suffer in the following ways. The instruments used to punish the guilty include: tridents, rods, hawks, snakes, wolves, dogs, pestles, mills, saws, chisels, knives and machetes, boiling oil, iron nets, iron chains, iron donkeys, iron horses, flaying skins while pouring hot iron and oil, fed with hot iron when hungry, and forced to drink boiling iron water when thirsty. These tortures continue from one complete lifetime to countless lifetimes, with suffering that does not cease for a single moment, hence it is called Avīci.

Regardless of being male or female, Muong, Man, or barbarian, young or old, noble or humble, or whether one is a Dragon, a Heaven being, or a Deity, a Ghost, as long as one commits a crime, one will feel its consequences; all equally endure suffering, hence it is called Avici (Endless Suffering).

If someone is condemned to that hell, from the moment of entry to hundreds of thousands of kalpas, every single day and night they die countless times and are reborn countless times; even to wish for a brief pause in torment is impossible, except when their karmic debt is fully exhausted can they be reborn. Because this suffering is continuous without cessation, it is called Avici.

(Excerpt from the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, Chapter 3)

P/s Even if one is a Dragon, a Heaven, a God, or a Demon, when their blessings are exhausted, they will also be condemned to the Avici Hell. Therefore, on the earthly realm, those who commit sins will enter this realm. The sinners there suffer day and night, going through countless lifetimes without any pause, hence it is called Avici. Once in this place, it is very difficult to escape.

Which Buddhist practice or path you follow is up to you; no one forces you to follow any. However, if you sincerely and devotedly recite the Buddha's name or the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, the Great Compassion Mantra, without distracting thoughts, and abandon sexual misconduct and masturbation, letting go of bad habits, then any prayer you make can be fulfilled. Dharma protectors will always be by your side to protect you. Doing the opposite will be counterproductive and may lead to hell.

In the Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, Chapter 13, page 184, it teaches: Again, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, in future lives, if there are gods or humans who, due to karma, must undergo retribution and fall into the hell realms, when they have just entered the gates of hell, if these beings are able to recite the name of the Buddha, or the name of a Bodhisattva, along with a verse or a line from the Mahāyāna scriptures, you should use your spiritual power to find a method to save them. You should manifest yourself before them, destroy hell, and allow them to be reborn in the heavenly realms to enjoy subtle and supreme bliss. However, in order that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma realm may benefit.Just as they are beneficial to each other and complete each other, the Kṣitigarbha Sutra is the greatest winner, because the Kṣitigarbha Sutra clearly explains the results of good and evil deeds, so people in the three realms can easily awaken when they hear it.

Every religion teaches people to do good and avoid evil. However, no matter how diligently and excellently practitioners of other religions cultivate, they will only go to heaven, become fairies, saints, or kings of the heavens. After they use up their blessings and do not continue practicing, they will fall into hell. The Buddha showed us the path of enlightenment, wishing that we would be reborn and attain Buddhahood. Once we become Buddhas, we escape the cycle of birth and death and are not condemned; the Buddha does not want us to be reborn in heaven. Being in heaven is too pleasurable, and one may neglect practice and eventually fall.
