WHY MUST ONE REPENT?

The practice of repentance is precisely correcting past mistakes, eliminating evil, and doing good. Everyone in the world makes mistakes; even a learned person who loses mindfulness can have afflictions arise, and Arahants can still commit bodily, verbal, or mental actions while gathering to inspire; how much more so ordinary people, who cannot avoid sins.

Those with foresight immediately repent and correct their mistakes, while the ignorant hide them, so their sins accumulate abundantly, stored up over time without knowing when they will be realized. If one feels shame and openly confesses repentance, not only are sins eradicated, but countless merits are also added, establishing the subtle Nirvana of the Tathagata.

To practice the method of Repentance, first, the body must be solemn and properly arranged, contemplate the sacred image, the mind must arise with reverence, follow the method of visualization, and wholeheartedly beseech, reflecting on two matters:

First, one must consider that life is difficult to maintain and impermanent; once it is shattered, it is uncertain when it will return. If one does not encounter Buddhas and virtuous sages, but instead meets evil companions and creates more sinful karma, one will fall into deep and perilous abodes.

Secondly, one must reflect: nowadays, although we encounter the True Dharma of the Tathagata, we do not know that for the sake of the Buddha's teaching to continue the lineage of the Enlightened Ones, we must purify the three karmas of body, speech, and mind to act according to wholesome dharma, yet we separately engage in evil deeds, deliberately hiding them; saying that others do not know, this person does not see, keeping it in the heart, boldly without shame. Such behavior is truly one of the utmost foolishness in the world.

The Buddhas of the ten directions, the great Bodhisattvas, and the benevolent deities, at any time, do not use their pure divine eyes to see all the evil deeds we commit?

Moreover, the deities in the netherworld record merits and sins without missing the slightest detail.

Speaking of those who have committed sins, after death, they are captured by the infernal guards and their souls are brought before King Yama at night for examination of right and wrong. At that time, all the wronged parties witnessing the scene say: "You once dissected me, killed me, boiled, stewed, roasted, grilled me..." or say: "In the past, you robbed all my money, caused discord among my relatives; today I finally have the chance to testify clearly in front of you, unable to hide anything, I can only endure."

the previous sins".

The Sutra clearly states: In hell, no injustice is done. Whatever sins a person commits in daily life, even if forgotten, when death comes, all those forms created by previous evil karma will appear, saying: "In the past, you committed these crimes with me, how can you hide now?" At that moment, the sinner has nowhere to hide. At that very time, Yama King grits his teeth, reproaches, and then casts them into hell, enduring countless kalpas with no hope of escape. This matter is neither strange nor unrelated to anyone; each person creates and must bear the consequences themselves. Even the closest bonds, like that of father and child, once karma is confronted,cannot replace each other.

So today we are given the chance to be healthy humans without illness, so we should strive to practice diligently, competing with the span of life, for when great calamity comes, there will be no time for regret. Therefore, we wholeheartedly pray and ask for repentance.

From beginningless time until now, we have been obscured by ignorance in our minds, causing afflictions to create evil karma in three lifetimes. Either being intoxicated with sensual pleasures, giving rise to "afflictions of desire," or anger and resentment, giving rise to "afflictions of harm," or having a darkened mind, giving rise to "afflictions of misunderstanding," or being arrogant and prideful, giving rise to "afflictions of conceit," or doubting the True Dharma, giving rise to "afflictions of hesitation," or denying cause and effect, giving rise to "afflictions of wrong views," or not knowing that the body and circumstances are formed by dependent causes, giving rise to "afflictions of attachment to self," or being deluded over three lifetimes, giving rise to"Afflictions attached to permanence and attachment to annihilation," or closely related to false dharmas, give rise to "afflictive view attachment," or following a mistaken teacher, give rise to "afflictive sphere attachment," up to the point that all four kinds of attachment result in mistaken preoccupying afflictions...

Nowadays, sincerely, all ask for repentance.

From the beginningless time until now, due to the nature of attachment and regret, arises the "affliction of greed and stinginess" because of not restraining the six senses; arises the "affliction of negligence" because of allowing the mind to engage in evil deeds; arises the "affliction of impatience" because of laziness and procrastination; arises the "affliction of lack of diligence" because of frequent doubt and trivial worry; arises the "affliction of faulty discernment" because of being deluded by sensory objects; arises the "affliction of ignorance" because of following the eight vices in the world; arises the "affliction of ego" because of deceit, praising in front while criticizing behind, leading to the "affliction of a crooked mind".

Straightforward", because it is difficult to teach, giving birth to "unconditioned afflictions", because it is easy to get angry and unhappy, giving birth to "disturbing emotions of resentment", because of jealousy and hatred, giving birth to "aggressive afflictions", because of cruel and poisonous violence, giving birth to "poisonous afflictions", because it is contrary to the Holy Way, giving birth to "afflictions of attachment", because they do not know the Four Noble Dharmas: Suffering, Practice, Cessation, and Way, giving birth to "crazy afflictions", because in the direction of birth and death, they cannot destroy the twelve causes and conditions, and they give birth to "circulating afflictions", until due to ignorance of the apostles, from the beginning arises eternal afflictions, and the four pillars arise, causing suffering in the three realms. Suffering FruitsCountless and limitless afflictions, disturbing sages and saints, the four kinds of sentient beings in the six realms, today I present before the Buddhas of the ten directions, honoring the Dharma and the holy beings, and sincerely repent.

May the merit of having repented for the afflictions of greed, anger, and delusion, which arise from volitional actions, help to break the chain of arrogance in every lifetime, dry up the waters of desire, extinguish the fire of anger, dispel the darkness of ignorance, uproot doubt, tear apart the net of wrong views, understand clearly that the three realms are like prisons, the four elements like poisonous snakes, the five aggregates like enemies, the six sense bases plant emptiness, deceitfulness is friendly, diligently cultivate the eightfold Holy Path, cut off the source of ignorance, aim directly for Nirvana without ever resting, always keep the mind in accordance with the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and constantly practice the ten Perfections, so that they are always present.

Having made the vows of repentance, wholeheartedly trust and respectfully worship the Eternal Three Jewels.

Excerpt from the scripture COMPASSIONATE HEART OF THE WATER OF REPENTANCE

Source: Alisa

tieu_de: EXPERIENCE IN MEMORIZING THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA ALONG WITH A FEW SMALL TIPS AND NOTES WHEN CHANTING
tom_tat: 1️⃣ MEMORIZING LANG NGHIEM: - This matter requires determination and perseverance. Because Lang Nhiem is not difficult to memorize due to the characters, since any Mantra is translated from Sanskrit, they are all equally difficult to remember, but
noi_dung:
EXPERIENCE IN MEMORIZING THE LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA ALONG WITH A FEW SMALL TIPS AND NOTES WHEN CHANTING

1️⃣ MEMORIZING THE LĂNG NGHIÊM:

- This issue requires determination and perseverance. Lăng Nghiêm is not difficult to memorize because of the characters, as every Mantra is translated from Sanskrit, so they are all equally hard to remember. However, the difficulty of memorizing the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra lies in its length. The length of Lăng Nghiêm is the longest among all Mantras, around 2,620 words divided into 554 sentences according to most versions translated in Vietnam. Therefore, memorizing Lăng Nghiêm is also a challenging issue for most Buddhists who do not have enough persistence.

In fact, the Lăng Nghiêm Sūtra is not something that cannot be memorized. It's just that people who study often have many distractions and then complain it is difficult and tedious. In reality, each of us has an affinity and has memorized the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra countless lifetimes ago, which is why in this life we are able to listen to Lăng Nghiêm. Whoever wants to memorize the Lăng Nghiêm must wholeheartedly devote themselves to memorizing the Mantra and not demand how long it should take. Because everyone's blessings and affinities are different, setting a time limit to memorize it can easily create obstacles, unless you are extremely determined, in which case you might be able to memorize all five sections in one or two months.

- There is a truth that things that are hard to remember or memorize must be learned day by day. Reading again and again what is difficult to remember each day without skipping will naturally, at some point, become memorized subconsciously. The same goes for the Lăng Nghiêm mantra; although there are many parts that are a bit difficult to remember, just persistently reading them over and over, over time the mind will become familiar with the Sanskrit characters and imprint them deeply, so that when reciting, it will be accurate without mistakes. If initially you misread it, don't worry too much, because in the past, when we memorized Chinese-Vietnamese poems in literature class, we also made mistakes, let alone a Mật Chú! If you read it wrong, just read it again, it's no problem, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not blame or punish.It's like when the Teacher returns the assignments in class, it's not that, it's just that we mistakenly think that reading incorrectly is wrong and fear committing a fault. Even if you read incorrectly, if your mind is respectful, the merit still grows as usual.

Once upon a time, there was a story about an old lady who was taught the Six-Syllable Great Bright Mantra of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. She had a poor memory and was illiterate, so when she recited the Mantra, she read the line "Om Mani Padme Hung" as "Om Mani Padme Green." Every day she recited it incorrectly about 100,000 times, for 30 years. During that time, she often used her devotion to count the recitations by transferring mung beans from one bowl to another. After a long time, the beans no longer needed her to move them; moved by her sincere devotion to the practice of the Mantra, they would leap to the other bowl by themselves. Later, a certainA high monk happened to come to her house and asked her what she was chanting. She said she was chanting the phrase "Om Mani Padme Xanh," and then the monk said she was chanting it wrong and should read it as "Om Mani Padme Hong." She realized that she had been chanting it incorrectly all along, so her faith collapsed. After that, even though she chanted correctly, it could no longer make the bean jump into the bowl. Therefore, practicing Buddhism primarily comes from the mind, not from external forms.

- The tip for memorizing the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra effectively and retaining it for the longest time is to apply the method taught by Venerable Tuyên Hóa. That is to learn in order from the first sentence to the last sentence. When memorizing, you must follow the sequence and avoid "skipping around," meaning if sentences 1 to 10 have not been fully learned, jumping to sentence 20 or 30 can easily cause confusion. Just set the number of sentences you need to memorize each day. For example, decide to first learn the first 10 sentences of the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, then, whether standing, walking, sitting, or lying down, recall and read them over and over. If you read incorrectly, refer to the Sutra or a phone, then remember and keep reading. Once you have memorized the first 10 sentences, continue by connecting these 10 sentences with the following ones.In this way, it is both less confusing and more fluent. Any sentence or section that is difficult to remember or to connect with the following sentences can be studied for more days to memorize it.

Applying this method is just a matter of time and personal determination. In the past, Phap Tinh also thought that they would probably never memorize the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, but after six months of persistence, remembering it in every meal, drink, and sleep, they ultimately memorized it fluently without mistakes or confusion. However, because each person's foundation and karmic conditions are different, the time and method for memorizing the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra will vary. Whoever sees a method that allows them to memorize perfectly and recite without confusion should follow that method, and whoever memorizes it within whatever time frame should simply rejoice in that achievement. Do notwhether one should take learning fast or slow as a measure for good spiritual practice.

2️⃣ ISSUE OF LĂNG NGHIÊM CHANTING:

- There is an article by Pháp Tịnh advising everyone to chant the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra at least 7 times a day. That is a small number of repetitions; even fewer, like 3, 2, or worse, just 1 repetition, is also acceptable. HT Phổ Quang teaches that chanting the Five Great Heart Mantras 7 times is equivalent to chanting the Great Compassion Mantra 108 times, but chanting the Lăng Nghiêm 7 times completes the 5 levels, including the Five Great Heart Mantras, which is still better.

But for those who want to recite the Lăng Nghiêm Sūtra dozens or hundreds of times, it should be noted that the Lăng Nghiêm Sūtra is very long, and if recited aloud for a long period of time, it is easy to lose vital energy and become exhausted. Therefore, the best way to recite many times daily with minimal effort is to recite SILENTLY.

Humans in this Saha World have very keen ears, so silently chanting will maximize the effectiveness of listening. Practicing listening is also a method of 'Reflecting on the nature of words' taught by Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. Listening through the ears is easier for entering concentration compared to other senses. Initially, silent recitation may be quite difficult to focus on because the power of concentration is not yet strong enough; therefore, you can move your lips while chanting and let the listening follow the movement of the mouth. Practicing gradually over the long term will train concentration, and the power of concentration will gradually grow from there. The important thing is not to get discouraged.

Chanting silently has the benefit of allowing one to concentrate and listen more, and it has less impact on those around. Do not think that silent chanting is not as wholehearted as chanting aloud, because to be wholehearted, practice must be long-term. Beginners who chant aloud are still distracted in their mind, let alone chanting silently!

- Another issue in reciting the Lăng Nghiêm is time. The Lăng Nghiêm is very long, so one cycle of it may take more time than a cycle of other Mantras, but whether it takes more or less time also depends on how proficiently it is recited. Proficiency means that one must memorize the Mantra first. Once memorized, long-term recitation can become fluent, and fluency naturally leads to proficiency. If someone recites the Lăng Nghiêm proficiently without stumbling, it would take at most 5 minutes per cycle, while those who have not memorized it and hold the text or scripture to recite will spend more time (meaning in the caseHey, it’s not unusual for a session to take 45 minutes to an hour. Therefore, the key condition for reciting fluently is MUST MEMORIZE IT FIRST.

And if you want to spend less time when reciting many mantras, you have to RECITE FAST. And the faster you recite, the inevitable thing that happens is swallowing words while reciting. This is an unchangeable truth. If anyone fears that swallowing words will reduce merit, they can additionally recite the Vajra Supplementary Mantra to correct errors caused by pronunciation during the process of reciting mantras, such as stumbling over words or swallowing words...

However, whether reciting quickly or slowly, aloud or in a whisper, the most important thing is still to live in accordance with the spirit of Thủ Lăng Nghiêm, which is to live in Great Steadfast Concentration. You can also check this link to learn more about that spirit: https://www.facebook.com/groups/444458153796937/permalink/845229133719835/?mibextid=Nif5oz

Once you are able to live in Great Steadfast Concentration, then no matter the form of recitation, fast or slow, all are equally the same.

- For those with great dedication, wanting to recite 108 repetitions of all 5 chapters of the Lankavatara Sutra each day, the trick is to just practice the method of reciting silently or mouthing the words. This way, you can sustain the recitation long-term with minimal energy expenditure. But 108 repetitions are not few, and the Lankavatara Sutra is very long, so another tip is to initially arrange to recite a few repetitions each day so that the time is reasonable, either 7 repetitions or 21 repetitions, as long as the time for practice and work do not interfere with each other. Recite gradually day by day, so that the recitation becomes proficient, and then gradually increase the speed of recitation. For example, one repetition of your Lankavatara Sutra initially takes 5 minutes,then practice so that one recitation takes as little time as possible, or 2-3 minutes, or even 1 minute. After achieving that, gradually increase the number of recitations per day, the important thing is not to rush, because one must slowly get used to focusing on the Mantra in order to accomplish it. Zen Master Phổ Quang teaches that if you recite 108 repetitions of the Lăng Nghiêm five times a day, the body will emit the scent of incense (the evidence is Zen Master Phổ Quang himself, who concentrates on reciting 108 repetitions of Lăng Nghiêm every day; anyone who comes to where he practices can smell the strong aroma of incense). If successfully applied, then 108 repetitions of the five Lăng Nghiêm each day only takeAbout 2 - 3 hours is normal; the most important factor in this practice is the mindset of 'wanting to be like that,' then it will be so. This is exactly the meaning of the phrase 'The situation changes according to the mind.'

Many people say that the purpose of reciting a Mantra is to have a single-minded focus, and if one is single-minded, one should not count the repetitions. That is indeed true, but reciting a Mantra is not only for the sake of being single-minded; it is also about living with the spirit that the Mantra brings. The Lăng Nghiêm Mantra teaches people to live with Great Steadfast Concentration, which is also to teach people to become Buddhas. Therefore, reciting many times each day is mainly to allow those teachings to permeate the mind more thoroughly and carefully.

Therefore, reciting many verses every day is also a practice among the 84,000 other practices taught by the Buddha. As for you, if you recite fewer verses and spend time on everyday matters like food, clothing, and money, you still have a way to practice to live with your own firm Great Concentration. Both of these ways are equally valid, there is nothing contradictory at all; if anything, it is only because your mind is too attached and discriminating that you might think they contradict each other. Single-mindedness is only a very small part of accomplishing a Mantra; if you have recited to the point of single-mindedness but do not clearly understand or practice according to the spirit of the Mantra, it is not yet perfect and ultimate.

3️⃣ AUXILIARY PRACTICE OF THE THIỀN LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA

If someone can only recite 1 round of the Lăng Nghiêm mantra of 5 levels each day, due to being busy or due to... laziness, they can additionally recite 108 rounds of the Lăng Nghiêm Heart Mantra. Venerable Master Tuyên Hóa taught that if someone can at least practice in this way, the merit gained will be boundless and limitless, capable of benefiting 7 generations of descendants endlessly. The Lăng Nghiêm Heart Mantra is the phrase:

"Án A Na Lệ Tỳ Xá Đề, Bệ Ra Bạt Xà Ra Đà Rị, Bàn Đà Bàn Đà Nễ, Bạt Xà Ra Bán Ni Phấn, Hổ Hồng Đô Lô Ung Phấn, Ta Bà Ha."

If someone encounters obstacles and difficulties at work every day, then before reciting all 5 volumes of the Lăng Nghiêm, one should recite the Five Great Heart Mantras at least 5,000 times (tip: reciting quickly will take less time). A Buddhist who took refuge with Venerable Phổ Quang used to recite the Five Great Heart Mantras from 7,000 to 10,000 times per day, and he noticed that reciting the Five Great Heart Mantras first, then all 5 volumes of the Lăng Nghiêm afterward, would have great power, making all daily tasks extremely smooth and always 'smooth sailing.' It seems that the Five Great Heart Mantras, in addition to their ability to remove curses of external paths, can also fulfill all desired wishes.The Great Heart Mantra consists of the following 5 lines:

"Sất Đà Nễ, A Ca Ra, Mật Rị Trụ, Bát Rị Đát Ra Da, Nảnh Yết Rị."

Those who frequently encounter accidents should study the lecture explaining the Lankavatara Mantra by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua and focus on the master's explanations in the Third Section. In the Third Section of the Lankavatara Sutra, most of the mantras are meant to eliminate all worldly calamities, such as: fire, drowning, untimely death, hunger and suffering, mutual destruction in wars, killings by sword, robbery and theft, etc. If one faces a particular calamity frequently, one should recite that specific mantra at least 1080 times per day after completing the recitation of the five Lankavatara sections. For example:

- The phrase "Ra Xà Bà Dạ" wards off misfortune from kings and officials, meaning that if one is wrongfully persecuted by kings or people in high authority, reciting this phrase many times will help overcome that misfortune.

- The phrase "A Kỳ Ni Bà Dạ" wards off the danger of fire, meaning that if a house catches fire naturally, reciting this phrase many times will help overcome that danger.

- The phrase "Xá Tát Đa Ra Bà Dạ" wards off danger from knives, meaning that if someone tries to harm you with a knife or stick, reciting this phrase many times will help overcome that danger.

- The phrase "Giả Đô Ra" is to ward off harmful Karma from enemies, meaning that if you are obstructed by relatives (tangible enemies) or other beings (intangible enemies), reciting this phrase many times will help you overcome that misfortune...

==> Just keep in mind that each of these mantras is the name of a different Deity who acts as a Dharma Protector for the Lăng Nghiêm and eliminates misfortunes for practitioners who recite them. Therefore, each time you recite these mantras individually, you should add the phrase "Nam mô" in front. For example, if you are afflicted by fire, you must recite "Nam mô A Kỳ Ni Bà Dạ" many times to show respect to these Dharma Protectors.

But because in the 5 volumes of Lăng Nghiêm, each volume has its own supportive power to help practitioners eliminate misfortunes and suffering and achieve auspiciousness and happiness, reciting all 5 volumes will be better. And the more wholeheartedly one recites, even just reciting one time already has great power.

Another thing is that many practitioners who practice and chant the Lankavatara Sutra may experience internal heat (hot eyes, hot head, hot body...) as if burning, which can sometimes make such people irritable and quick-tempered for no reason. This is a very normal condition for Mantras that have strong energy and great blessing power from the Wrathful Vajra Secret, fierce like the Lankavatara Mantra.

When encountering such a situation, one should immediately recite a few more mantras that have the power to purify and cool the body and mind, such as the Great Compassion Heart Dharani, the White-Robed Great Master Spiritual Response, etc., and naturally the heat will go away. This is not taught by the Buddha, but comes from practical experience, from the practice and realization of later practitioners. This has been mentioned many times, so it will not be discussed further.

~ End ~

Source: DUONG LIEU PHAP TINH

tieu_de: BORN AND DIE ALONE, COME AND GO IN SOLITUDE.
tom_tat: People live in desire, are born alone, die alone, go alone, and arrive alone. At the moment of death, life ends, love and affection part, but once separated, even if we meet again in the next life, we will not be the same.
noi_dung:
BORN ALONE, DIE ALONE.

People live in desire, are born alone, die alone, go alone, come alone. At the moment of death, life ends, love parts, but once parted, forms change, and even if we meet again in the next life, we cannot recognize each other.

IF AFTER TRUE ENLIGHTENMENT, WE FULLY UNDERSTAND THIS MATTER, IT IS ALSO A VEIL; HUMAN LIFE IS LIKE A DREAM, JUST A LONG DREAM.

WHEN WE SLEEP IN DREAMS EVERY DAY, TIME IS SHORT, BUT HERE, TIME IS EXTENDED. WHAT EXISTS IS LOST, CANNOT BE HELD.

If in the previous life one did not cultivate merit, in this life there will be many enemies and karmic adversaries; this is a nightmare, truly so. We must awaken, we must be alert!

If we regard the world as a dream, in the dream we have awakened to 'I am dreaming,' then regarding all favorable or adverse conditions, naturally we no longer contend. When achieving our desires, we do not rejoice excessively; when encountering disappointment, we do not generate distress because we know this is false, a dream, not reality.

WE MUST CREATE A GOOD DREAM, A BEAUTIFUL DREAM, AND WE MUST MAKE THIS DREAM COME TRUE ONLY BY RECITING "A DI DA PHAT" TO BE REBORN IN THE WESTERN PARADISE. THIS IS THE METHOD TO CREATE A BEAUTIFUL DREAM, AND THIS BEAUTIFUL DREAM WILL BECOME REALITY.

People living in this world have very short lives, especially during chaotic times, when many unintended disasters occur, and no one can guarantee how many years they will live.

BE ALERT ABOUT THIS! WHEN YOU HAVE ONE DAY, THEN RECITE THE BUDDHA'S NAME WELL FOR ONE DAY.

IF THERE IS TIME IN A DAY, ONE MUST STRIVE TO ABSTAIN FROM EVIL DEEDS AND PRACTICE GOOD DEEDS; ONLY BY DOING SO CAN ONE HOPE TO ELIMINATE MISFORTUNE IN THIS CHAOTIC WORLD AND TRULY HELP ONESELF BE BORN IN THE PURE LAND, NOT LETTING IT PASS BY.

IF ONE WISHES TO ESCAPE THE CHAOS OF THE WORLD, TIME IS THE MOST PRECIOUS. THIS PRECIOUS TIME MUST BE USED TO DO RIGHTEOUS WORK. RIGHTEOUS WORK IS RECITING THE BUDDHA'S NAME. NOT WASTING THIS PRECIOUS TIME IS TRULY BEING AN ENLIGHTENED PERSON.

NÁM MÔ AMITÀ BUDDHA 🙏

Excerpt from: "Reciting the Buddha's Name to Become a Buddha," Chapter 1

Lecturer: Elder Monk Jingkong

tieu_de: Evil Report Close to Death
tom_tat: THE FOREST CAT SPIRIT, HATRED BORN AS A CHILD IN THE FAMILY At the beginning of spring, on the train returning home, I met a young couple bringing their three-year-old daughter to a medical check-up. While chatting, I learned that the child's illness was
noi_dung:
OMINOUS SIGN OF MURDER

THE VENGEFUL FOREST CAT GOD BORN AS A CHILD IN THE FAMILY

Early in the spring, on the train ride home, I met a young couple bringing their three-year-old daughter to see a doctor. As we talked, I learned that the child's illness had been present since birth and was very difficult to treat.

The girl's father lifted her shirt for me to see, which was truly startling: she had such a delicate and lovely face, yet her back was covered with burns of various sizes and heights… lying in a chaotic and disorderly manner (like someone who had suffered severe scalds). Listening to the couple's painful account… a scene suddenly appeared before me:

"There was a wild cat with gray-black fur that often came to a farmer couple's house to steal food... One day, the husband bought 10 ducks to let them roam in the garden. But every day, two ducks went missing. On the third day, he secretly watched and discovered that the culprit was the wild cat. So the couple set a trap and caught it, then locked it in an iron cage, and cruelly poked and stabbed it with a sharp stick... while hitting and scolding:

– You beast, how dare you steal our ducks! You won't die peacefully!”

Seeing that the cat was already injured yet still struggling with all its strength, they cruelly boiled water and poured it over its back… The wild cat in pain screamed continuously until it died, and only then did the couple stop.

At that time, the wife was pregnant… the consciousness of the wild cat, filled with resentment, immediately seized the womb (took over – entered the pregnancy), resulting in it being born into this family, which is now the girl before your eyes…

I asked the couple:

– Did you ever burn a wild cat to death?

The husband, upon hearing this, turned pale, startled and surprised, and responded tensely:

– “How do you know that three years ago we killed a wild cat?”

– Your daughter is ill; it is a karmic illness, and only by practicing Buddhism can your whole family be helped…

– Yes sir, we all believe in Buddha, every year we go to the temple to light incense and pray for peace…

– True Buddhist practice is not just closing your eyes to burn incense and perform rituals for peace. Doing so is acting with a mind that seeks worldly benefits! – You must correct your impatience and unhealthy temperament! – After returning home, you must repent for the killing karma you have created in the past, eat vegetarian meals, and recite 100 sets of the “Kṣitigarbha Sutra,” and you must wholeheartedly engage in releasing life and dedicate the merit to your daughter. Because the two of you have created killing karma that resulted in negative karmic connections, you have a child like this… The husband and wife were both fearful and relieved, showing remorse. Immediately, they vowed that for the child they would eat vegetarian, recite sutras, and dedicate the merit, and that when they return home they would practice well according to the instructions…

Further explanation: Humanity considers itself the most intelligent species among all living beings, yet out of desire we commit acts of slaughter against sentient beings without any compassion or mercy. Master Hsuan Hua once said, one should never harbor hatred toward sentient beings, because if not, when retribution comes, we will suffer unbearably…

If we believe in the Buddha, we must deeply believe in cause and effect, strictly observe the precepts: "Cut off evil: is to help oneself close the door to hell. Practice goodness: is to open the door to heaven for oneself. Study Buddhism: is to cultivate oneself, stepping onto the bright and radiant path to escape the three realms"…

RETALIATION IN THE PRESENT LIFE VOLUME 4

LAY PRACTITIONER QUẢ KHANH – QUẢ HỒNG

NUN HẠNH ĐOAN VIETNAMESE TRANSLATION

tieu_de: Karma of destroying Buddha statues, burning scriptures
tom_tat: The story happened around the full moon of July 2014, at Lien Hoa Monastery, District 11 – Ho Chi Minh City, I was sitting chanting sutras with my master. Suddenly, a couple came carrying a small child, with crooked arms and legs, about 6 years old.
noi_dung:
RETRIBUTION FOR DESTROYING BUDDHA IMAGES, BURNING SACRED TEXTS

The story happened around the full moon of July 2014, at Lien Hoa Monastery, District 11 – Ho Chi Minh City, I was sitting chanting sutras with my master. Suddenly, a couple carried a small child, about 6 years old, with twisted limbs and a naive-looking face. The child's mother knelt at the Buddha altar and said to my master:

– I don’t know what mistake I made to be born with a son who all year round neither smiles nor cries, just lies quietly in one place. I have to do all of his daily activities. His father goes to work to provide for the two of us. Our family life is suffering beyond words!

My master told me to bring the baby closer to him. Suddenly, it screamed. It cried as if it had never cried before. Its parents were surprised because until now it had never cried or laughed even once. Then the master said:

– This baby in its past life was a soldier. It followed the king's orders to burn temples, burn scriptures, smash Buddha statues, and force monks to leave the monastery. Therefore, in this life, it has to be like this. It has no wisdom and must lie in one place.

At that time, I asked the master:

– Why must it be like that? Is it because if one does not obey the king, one will be beheaded? That king should have been the one to be punished. In the past, soldiers had a saying: “The soldier executes the minister. If the minister does not die, he is not loyal.” Master, why did the soldier also suffer karma?

Master then explained to me like this:

– Hey Phuc Dieu, suppose you go to the market. You buy fish but are afraid of the sin of killing. You ask the fish seller to prepare the fish for you. The fish seller also knows that killing the fish is sinful. But because of the profession of earning money to support themselves and their family, they have to do it, though they are also very afraid. It's like a soldier who earns a salary from the king and follows the king's orders even if it involves sinful acts, then the sin is shared. It's like both the person eating the fish and the person preparing the fish are guilty.

After that, the master spoke to the child's parents:

– From now on, both of you should eat vegetarian, do good deeds, and recite sutras to dedicate the merit to this child so that their karma will be reduced, and illnesses will also be eliminated from now on.

The child suddenly stopped crying. The child's parents joined their hands respectfully and sincerely accepted the master's words.

On this occasion, the master also gave advice to his disciples when visiting temples: do not take anything from the temple on your own, no matter how small. When invited by the temple to have a meal, after eating, offering a small amount of money is acceptable. Do not climb trees or sit on Buddha statues; if you see trash or dirty areas in the temple, take a broom and sweep them, and the merit gained is immeasurable.

(Quang Tu - rewritten from the account of Phuc Dieu)

tieu_de: HOW TO ELIMINATE KARMA OBSTACLES
tom_tat: Kim Hoa: – Quang Tử, let me ask:
noi_dung:
HOW TO ELIMINATE KARMIC OBSTRUCTIONS

Kim Hoa :

– Quang Tử, may I ask:

CAN THE KARMIC CONSEQUENCES I HAVE CAUSED BE ELIMINATED or LOST? AND BY WHAT MEANS?

When long ago the Shakya family of Buddha was massacred, even though it was foreseen, it could not be prevented; so if Karma has been caused, must it be paid for, right?

There are many stories about the repayment of Karma by many Masters and practitioners. There is a saying, "Virtue can overcome destiny"... how should we understand this regarding practitioners who still have karma and must repay it?

Thank you, Quang Tu.

Quang Tu:

Dear friends, Quang Tu would like to humbly answer the questions from my own naive and limited perspective. If there are any mistakes, I kindly ask fellow practitioners to correct me:

1. Karma that has been caused, if left untouched without any interference, no matter if it is left for hundreds of millions of lifetimes or even longer, no matter if one flees to some distant planet, karma will still find its way to produce its result.

But if one knows how to follow the methods taught by the Buddha, it is possible to reduce karma and even completely eliminate it. There are many ways:

– Repentance: eliminates light karma, erodes heavy karma

– Create a great amount of merit to seek the elimination of karmic obstacles; depending on the amount of that merit, it can cause karma to be worn down to complete eradication. Such merits include reciting the Buddha's name, bowing to the Buddha, chanting sutras, reciting mantras, helping people, rescuing animals and releasing them, printing Buddhist texts, giving alms, etc.

We should combine both methods above and practice persistently and steadily, which will surely and powerfully eliminate past evil karma.

2. Regarding the event of the Shakya clan being massacred, it is not an easy matter to discuss. The life of the Buddha is not like that of ordinary people; we are swept away by the currents of karma, knowing nothing in advance. Everything is arranged by karmic force beforehand, coming as it will, and we cannot freely arrange our current lives.

But the Buddha is different; even before becoming a Buddha, before being born into the world, He was already the Great Bodhisattva with Supreme Abode, with boundless spiritual power, and merit filling the universe. He was completely free to arrange all events in His journey to Buddhahood, including the day of birth, place of birth, lineage, parents, assembly of disciples, time of attaining Buddhahood, etc. … every single matter, from small to large, was skillfully arranged by Him with merit, so that each event would leave profound lessons for future generations, or enable sentient beings to cultivate extraordinary merits.

According to the narrow vision of Quang Tử himself, the Sakyamuni family being massacred was naturally due to karmic consequences that had matured from the past, but it is not impossible to resolve, and more importantly, it is an extremely meaningful lesson left for future generations.

Most beings in this realm often tend to be dependent and like to achieve good, grand results… but do not want to put in much effort. Instead, they prefer to pray to the deities for blessings or absolution for them (That’s very easy! We can see such people everywhere, in all religions; they spend their whole day begging the deities, relying on the compassion and divine power of the Saints. But if asked to put in effort to practice as taught by the Saints, they would avoid and evade it.) Such people do not understand that, even though the Saints can use their virtue to bless them, it is not thatAbsolutely, but that is a form of support; the main thing is that each person must strive to cultivate themselves, abandon evil deeds, and diligently practice virtues… If a person frequently does evil, neglects cultivation, and only prays to the Deities for everything to go smoothly and perfectly, for all their sins and karma to be eliminated, then what need is there to practice cultivation, what need is there to live rightly? This would only make society worse and worse, completely lacking in morality, and that is not what the Buddhas and Saints want.

The event of the Shakya family is a resounding bell for those who like to rely on divinity, on Buddhas, without cultivating themselves, repenting for bad karma, and accumulating merit. They look at it and realize that "Even the close relatives of the Buddha, if they have bad karma, must also bear the consequences as usual. Now, I am not a relative of the Buddha, and if I create bad karma, and do not cultivate myself, repent… just hoping and praying to the Buddha to escape the consequences, that would be truly unreasonable."

Thanks to this lesson, intelligent people who know how to reflect will strive to cultivate themselves according to the Buddha's teachings, instead of merely begging or relying on the Buddha and expecting to escape punishment and gain merit. That is what is truly important.

3. The evil karma of each of us, caused from countless previous lives, is extremely enormous. Fortunately for us, that mass of evil karma does not manifest all in one lifetime (otherwise, no one could endure it) but is gradually repaid over many lifetimes. Each lifetime has already been predetermined with how much bad karma and how much merit will manifest as successes or failures, gains or losses, luck or misfortune in life.

If a person diligently practices repentance and creates merit, then we can make the bad karmas predetermined to be repaid in this life vanish, so that we will find life very pleasant, without seeing misfortune, only peace, happiness, and luck. However, that is only for this life; in the next life, the karmic debts from countless past lives will still have to be repaid, and there will still be sickness, misfortune, and all sorts of suffering... stretching across many lifetimes.

But what would happen if someone practiced asceticism intensely, accumulating merit in enormous amounts, rather than practicing superficially and lightly?

If one practices with such determination, then, instead of merely eliminating the karma destined to occur in this lifetime, that person will eliminate and erode the huge mass of karma accumulated over many past lifetimes. That mass of karma, instead of having to descend into hell, become an animal, or endure terrible retributions such as being stabbed, being cut, severe disasters... over many lifetimes, will now, thanks to determined practice and generating great merits, be gathered and reduced into a much lighter retribution, which the determined practitioner only needs to endure (for example, a few illnesses, a fewbeatings, a humiliation…) then in future lives one will not have to face continuous retribution for many lifetimes. This is called turning heavy karma into light karma.

We often see that famous great practitioners frequently encounter such severe retributions. For example, Master Xuanzang (Tang Seng) fell seriously ill at the end of his life. In a dream, he saw a deity appear and told him that thanks to this near-death illness, countless past karmic sins were entirely eliminated. In this way, a huge accumulation of karma was transformed into light karma, settled in one go, without lingering for many lifetimes.

___________________

Van Du :

– Quang Tu, may I ask a bit, “all dharmas arise from the temporary combination of causes and conditions guided by karma”.

The part “guided by karma” refers to karma from many previous lives, so the entire span of one’s life until death is guided by past life karma, with every action, gesture, and thought already set in a pattern. So if all past life karma guides us, does that mean in this life we are merely repaying debts, and so on over many lifetimes, repaying karma? Is there eventually a stopping point?

And just as karma guides, so the volitional karma that just arises in this life is also influenced by past karma within certain bounds, right?

Quang Tử :

– Karma is a continuous flow and is not separated into past life – present life – future life. We need to correct it to Past Karma (that is, karma that has been created) – Present Karma (that is, karma being done) and Future Result (the future counted from the present moment, until death, and through subsequent lives as well, not “the entire span of one’s life until death,” because from now until the time you die, that is already the future).

In which, past karma greatly influences the present and the future, but it does not completely determine the present and the future. What we can change are the things in the present, and through that, a portion, more or less, of the future can be rearranged.

Saying 'a portion, more or less, of the future' is because the future is formed by both: past karma and present karma. If there is no significant creation of merit or demerit in the present, then the future will proceed according to the arrangement of past karma.

If we want the future to change and not be controlled by past Karma anymore, we need to strive to create good Karma in the present. How should we make such efforts?

That is, we need to follow the principle of Cause and Effect, sowing a lot of merit through body, speech, and mind; thereby, the future will gradually change according to our wishes.

In summary, even though past karma has been predetermined, if in the present we know the way and make an effort, it is still possible to change the future to some extent. But if there is only one direction: past karma determining the present and the future, unchangeable, then sentient beings will never be able to cultivate to escape the cycle of birth and death.

The basic level is like that, but if we examine it thoroughly at a deeper level. A person who has the ability to understand cause and effect, to know how and have the strength to change past Karma, must also be someone with the fortune of wisdom sown from the past, not something random. And such people are not many compared to countless others who do not know.

So, tracing the origin further, why does this person have that fortune of wisdom? While others do not?

Because there are the Noble Virtuous Friends in Buddhist teachings (the supreme Noble Virtuous Friends are the Buddhas, followed by the Bodhisattvas, the Śrāvakas, the Pratyekabuddhas, the disciples of the Buddha, and those who thoroughly understand the Dharma…), some people, by listening to the teachings of these Noble Virtuous Friends, accumulate merit and wisdom. As a result, in future lives, their wisdom opens, enabling them to understand and believe in cause and effect and to practice according to the Dharma, thereby transforming past karma.

As for those who do not heed the teachings, they do not perform any good deeds; therefore, their wisdom does not unfold, they do not understand or believe in Cause and Effect, they cannot live according to the principles of the Way, and thus it is impossible for them to transform the enormous Karmic load of the past. Consequently, they just follow the past Karma, drifting along, suffering in the cycle of birth and death.

So, tracing the origin further, why does one person have the affinity to follow the words of the Virtuous and Wise, while another does not?

It is because they have a debt of gratitude with the Virtuous and Wise.

The virtuous and wise ones who wish to teach the Dharma to sentient beings must first create conditions to make sentient beings indebted to them; only then, when they speak the Dharma, will sentient beings listen. Without any such karmic connection, sentient beings will have countless ways to avoid listening—either not believing, or feeling bored and unwilling to listen, or forgetting, or being lazy, or being busy, or being distracted by external circumstances in another direction, or not understanding, etc. … the simplest reason being that they do not meet or interact in any way with the virtuous and wise ones.

It is because the Noble and Wise when creating conditions, cannot simultaneously save all sentient beings, since there are too many beings, so some beings will be helped first, while others must wait. For example, when setting animals free, we equally wish to release all animals about to be killed in the world, but with limited money, we can only afford to save a small portion of those to be killed. In the next life, only the animals we released will heed our words, while countless others that we did not save will not listen. It's just that simple.

Memorial prayers, blood donation, charity, gift-giving, etc., will all be like that. Even if one helps all sentient beings in an entire Buddha-world of countless particles, there will still be innumerable sentient beings in other infinite Buddha-worlds of countless particles who have not been saved.

Returning to the original issue, in the present life, if one knows how and exerts effort, it is possible to change some portion of past karma.

Only a small portion because the mass of past karma is extremely enormous. To change the entire massive karma would require effort over many, many future lifetimes.

Among them, karma related to health is the easiest to change. Next is karma related to money, … the most difficult to change is the merit of wisdom, which is the most precious and valuable, so one must accumulate an extremely large amount of virtue over many lifetimes to make progress.

For example, if equally performing the merit of releasing 1,000 turtles, one person who seeks wealth may see results in just a few decades, while another person who seeks wisdom may not notice any progress even after several decades. Only after many lifetimes will it gradually increase.

_____________________

*Note: These are the experiences and personal views of Quang Tu during the process of studying the Buddhist scriptures, and do not represent any particular school.

You can regard this as sincere advice from a fellow practitioner. If there are any shortcomings, Quang Tu hopes to receive contributions from virtuous and knowledgeable individuals everywhere.

Sincere thanks!

tieu_de: THE EARTH TREASURY SUTRA HELPS TRANSFORM KARMA & FATE IN AN EXTREMELY MIRACULOUS WAY!
tom_tat: On the 1st day of the 10th month of 2006, Master Diệu Chân went to Dương Châu to open a meditation hall. Passing by my place, He stopped by to give a Dharma teaching and lectured on many valuable things about practicing Buddhism for the laypeople who came to pay respect: - Layperson h
noi_dung:
Kṣitigarbha Sutra Helps Transform Karma & Destiny in an Extremely Miraculous Way!

On the first day of October, 2006, Master Diệu Chân went to Dương Châu to open a meditation retreat. Passing by my place, He stopped to give a Dharma talk and taught many valuable things about practicing Buddhism to the laypeople who came to pay respects:

- A layperson who has been studying Buddhism for ten years, and even has the aspiration to travel everywhere giving charity, yet does not make an effort to recite the sutras and commentaries fluently! Doing good deeds is precious and hard to accomplish, but studying the Tripitaka to gain insight, help increase wisdom, and dispel ignorance... is very necessary and much more important!

Hearing my master’s teachings, I felt ashamed and silently thought that I must strive diligently in my cultivation in the future. My family life is very happy; my daughter is over ten years old, intelligent and clever, yet I still long to have another baby boy, secretly wishing to let him receive Buddhist teachings from prenatal education, and then follow the Buddha’s teachings throughout his life, truly continuing His wise legacy. This dream has always burned passionately within me, but now my daughter is already 12 years old, and a long time has passed without my conceiving again, so I feel very regretful.

After studying Buddhism, I diligently practiced and recited sutras… then a miracle happened. One day, I went to the market, and as soon as I saw a fresh, delicious apple, I just stood still, staring blankly… suddenly, an extreme craving arose in me, just like pregnant women craving food. Later, I went to the hospital for a check-up, and indeed, I was pregnant!

This happy news made my husband and me overjoyed, extremely happy. However, after the excitement, I thought: "My husband is almost 50 this year, I am nearly 40 too, what if the baby turns out to be a girl, what should we do?”

After thinking for a while, I suddenly realized and thought: “As someone who studies Buddhism, I absolutely should not have an abortion, because abortion is also killing, and the karmic consequences will be extremely painful!”

Later, after being instructed by Master Diệu Chân, my husband and I decided to keep the baby.

During the early stages of pregnancy, my body was very uncomfortable, always craving sleep, feeling tired, exhausted, and uneasy. I heard fellow practitioners say that during pregnancy, reciting the "Kṣitigarbha Sutra" and the "Universal Door Sutra" would be very beneficial for the baby. So I decided, for the sake of my child, to try reciting the "Kṣitigarbha Sutra"…

Oh! It really is a miracle, every day I recite a set, no longer having the symptoms of wanting to vomit, my mind is no longer troubled or restless, during the recitation I am sincerely attentive, reciting for nearly two hours to complete one set.

Whenever there is a holiday (the birth or the celebration day of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas), I and my fellow practitioners go on life release. I also go to "Thong Giao Temple" to invite a few dozen monks and laypeople to organize the chanting of the "Kṣitigarbha Sutra" for one week and the "Universal Gate Sutra" for three days to dedicate the merit to the fetus. I hope that this child (whom I had great difficulty conceiving) will have profound blessings and wisdom, becoming a pillar of the nation in the future.

Around six months pregnant, I had the fortune to meet lay practitioner Quả Khanh in Beijing - the author of the book "Reaping Karma in This Life" - and hearing him affirm that the baby I was carrying was a girl, I felt disappointed and deeply saddened.

Because prior to that, a traditional Chinese medicine doctor had also diagnosed the fetus in my womb as female, and even my experienced friends in child-rearing also said the fetus in my womb was a girl! But I already had a daughter, and now I was eagerly hoping to have a son. So why couldn't my wish come true?

I anxiously asked lay practitioner Quả Khanh:

- So… what should I do?

He replied:

- Although you believe in Buddha, practice giving, releasing life, printing Buddhist scriptures, and creating great merit… because your husband still eats non-vegetarian food and does not follow vegetarianism, and your own precepts are not completely pure! If you truly wish to give birth to a son, then both husband and wife should make a vow before the Buddha:

“From now on, vow to completely give up all salty foods and practice strict vegetarianism, earnestly observe the Five Precepts, and pray to Buddha to grant a baby boy who can propagate the Dharma and benefit sentient beings in the future”… Every day, you must also recite a set of the “Kṣitigarbha Sutra” and chant the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara ten thousand times; if you can do this, the female fetus will turn into a male!

I anxiously asked again to be sure:

- Sir, there’s only one month left until birth, if I do this… is there really hope?

Khanh replied:

- The Buddha said: 'All is created by the mind.' In the Buddhist scriptures, everything taught is the truth, not false, if you do not believe, then consider as if I have said nothing!

Seeing that my faith was still insufficient, he continued to tell me:

- In Hà Nam, there was a woman who was pregnant, and three ultrasounds all showed it was female. With only seven days left until giving birth, thanks to the couple's mutual vow: 'If it is a boy, we pledge to give up all meat, and enter the path of studying Buddhism! ... As a result, with the blessing of Buddha, after a week, they gave birth to a son.

This story increased my faith. That night, I stood before the Buddha and made a vow: “As long as I give birth to a healthy and intelligent baby boy, from now on I vow to strictly observe the Five Precepts, follow a vegetarian diet, study Buddhism, recite the Buddha's name, and offer one hundred thousand (equivalent to 16,000 USD) to print sutras for Buddhist work, furthermore, whenever I have the ability in the future, I vow to broadly do good deeds, propagate the Dharma, and benefit sentient beings…

The fetus grows bigger every day, but I still persist in chanting sutras, eating vegetarian, and doing life release; every day I drive myself everywhere, without any discomfort. On the first day of hospitalization, I even drove myself to perform life release. Although the expected due date had arrived, I showed no signs of labor, so I drove myself to the hospital for a pre-birth check-up.

Thirteen years ago, when giving birth to my daughter, I had a hemorrhage. Now, being older and giving birth for the second time, I truly feel anxious...

During the check-up, the doctor said:

- Too little amniotic fluid, fear the fetus is in danger, must be hospitalized immediately!

Already hospitalized, for three days, every day the doctor injected labor-inducing medicine for me, but I didn't notice any signs of imminent labor. I went for an ultrasound check-up, and saw that the amniotic fluid had increased compared to before. On the fourth day, the doctor didn't inject the labor-inducing medicine anymore, letting me rest for a day. On the fifth day, I walked from the hospital to the nearby temple to pay respects to the Buddha (for each hall, each Buddha, each Bodhisattva, I kowtowed three times. From beginning to end, it was approximately several tens of prostrations). Then I returned to the hospital, feeling neither tired nor uneasy. On the sixth day, I started to feel some abdominal pain, but still persisted in reciting the "Earth Treasury Sutra."Just after finishing reciting a set of prayers, my amniotic fluid broke, and my stomach hurt fiercely, yet I still persevered in chanting Buddha's name.

About 15 minutes after entering the delivery room, the doctor said they could see the baby's head. I continued chanting Buddha's name and gave birth to a plump baby boy easily. The first person the baby saw was his father. The whole family was extremely happy, and I was overjoyed.

Friends, hearing the news that I gave birth to a boy, came together to bring gifts to congratulate me, giving all sorts of things: pork hock, carp, birds, chicken… Once they left, I gave the remaining live animals to my family to release them.

I breastfed my child, but my milk was very little. Everyone in the family said it was because I didn't eat meat or pork hock soup that I didn't have much milk.

Because I was too worried about my son, I no longer had the patience to maintain my precepts, thinking: 'Well, if I eat meat from the three purity categories, it should be fine.'

After I started eating meat, I indeed had more milk, but my son only drank a little and refused to continue, and then he became ill. The doctor said he had polycythemia, and if it did not improve, he would have to be sent to 'Beijing Hospital' for treatment.

But the boy's illness kept increasing, I had plenty of milk but he refused to nurse, so I had to spoon-feed him other things and thought to myself: "Why, when he was just born, even though my milk was little, he still nursed greedily? Now that I have plenty of milk, why does he stubbornly refuse to nurse?" - I rack my brain to find the cause: "Could it be because I ate pig's trotter soup? Clearly, I had made a vow, promised to eat vegetarian, asking the Buddha and Bodhisattvas to grant me a smart, wise boy… but I broke my vow and returned to eating meat. I used pig's trotter soup to stimulate my milk, therefore my milk was also tainted with the salty, fishy taste, making it unsuitable for the baby to suck"Just recently fell ill… That's why the baby absolutely refuses to drink milk?”… Thinking of this, as I lay on the bed, I suddenly became so scared that I trembled, my heart full of remorse and regret, tears streaming down… I sat up, put on my robe, got off the bed, knelt before the Buddha to repent, and made a renewed vow, resolutely declaring from now on: “I swear to completely give up all salty foods, praying for the baby to get through this dangerous period soon“…

After confessing and making vows, I tried breastfeeding the baby… Oh, I was so relieved that the baby finally nursed. When the doctor drew blood for a test, the polycythemia was gone; it was truly an unimaginable miracle!

After that, I donated three hundred thousand, offered alms, did good deeds, and dedicated the merit to the baby.

Now the baby is one and a half years old and daily goes on its own to kneel before the Buddha, perform prostrations and worship. The baby is extremely intelligent, has a bright and radiant face, is as beautiful as a gem, and everyone who sees is fond of them.

From that time onward, I increasingly believed: "Buddhism is a precious practice for both life and the path." As long as we are willing to follow and practice accordingly, we will surely gain immense benefits.

Right here, I also wish to express my gratitude for the great kindness of the venerable Masters and laypersons who have wholeheartedly assisted us…

*Quả Khanh further explains:

- This is a true story, demonstrating the extraordinary wisdom of the Buddha, and further proving that the "Kṣitigarbha Sutra" is a scripture that can transform destiny and karma in a miraculous way. This is the truth without deception.

It is hoped that readers can make a vow to recite the "Kṣitigarbha Sutra" one set daily or one set weekly, which will surely bring auspicious and inconceivable blessings to you and your family. It is necessary to note that the person reciting must strictly observe the precepts, completely abstain from meat, and maintain vegetarianism continuously in order to attain boundless merit and have hope of transcending the three realms.

Moreover, this story also warns us: "never betray or break your vow!"

(Collected & translated by: Hạnh Đoan)

tieu_de: THE FOX TURNS INTO A WIFE TO PAY OFF AN OLD DEBT
tom_tat: Mr. Thanh Viễn once told me (Kỉ Hiểu Lam) a story like this: The Chu family had a young maid, who at that time was not very beautiful. As she grew up, she gradually became intelligent, and her face became more and more beautiful.
noi_dung:
THE FOX TRANSFORMS INTO A WIFE TO REPAY AN OLD DEBT

Mr. Thanh Viễn once told me (Kỉ Hiểu Lam) a story like this:

The Chu family had a young maid, who at that time was not very beautiful. As she grew up, she gradually became wise, and her face became increasingly beautiful. Once, Mr. Chu noticed that her temperament seemed different from before, so he asked:

- You are not the same girl as before, are you?

The maid replied:

- That's right.

A few years later, Mr. Chu took the maid as his concubine.

The concubine was very calculating and attentive to household matters. From rice, firewood, oil, and salt to the doors inside and outside the alleys, she managed everything thoroughly; neither servants nor tenants dared to cross her.

Anyone who still did not behave appropriately would be punished accordingly. The concubine was also very skilled in making money, anticipating things better than anyone, and goods stored from past years could be sold the following years at high prices.

Because of this, the Chu family became increasingly prosperous, and Mr. Chu loved his concubine even more. One day, the concubine asked Mr. Chu:

- Do you know who I am?

Mr. Chu laughed:

- Are you crazy? Why would you ask that?

The concubine continued:

- Actually, I am not human. I was originally a fox spirit who had cultivated for centuries. In my ninth previous life, I was a wealthy merchant and I served as his treasurer. He treated me very well, but I embezzled more than three thousand taels of silver from him. So when I died, Yama ordered me to be reborn as a fox. I cultivated for several hundred years, and fortunately attained the Dao, allowing me to transform into a human form. However, because I am still bound by past mistakes, I cannot become an immortal.

Seizing the opportunity when I saw your maid run away, I transformed myself into her form to follow you and repay my debt. It has been ten years, and the old debt has been fully repaid. This is the moment I can return to my original form and depart.

When I leave, my body will be that of a fox. You should order a servant in the house to bury me. He will surely strip my body to take my skin. Do not punish him. Four lifetimes ago, he starved to death, and I, back then a fox not yet enlightened, once gnawed on his corpse to satisfy my hunger. Therefore, even if he strips my skin, it is also a way to settle all predestined debts and grievances from the past.

After speaking, the concubine transformed into a fox and collapsed onto the floor. Then, the figure of a small, beautiful girl appeared, flying out from the fox's mouth like a puff of air, slowly disappearing without leaving any trace.

Mr. Chu could not bear to ruthlessly follow the instructions of his fox wife, so he took care of the burial himself. But in the end, the servant in the house dug up the grave and sold the fur. It was only later that Mr. Chu realized that this was the fair cause-and-effect repayment, and there was no way to avoid it. All he could do was silently lament!

* Kỉ Hiểu Lam, (1724 – 1805), passed the doctoral examination in 1755, served as an official for 41 years under the Qianlong reign

tieu_de: THE LEGACY ENMITY OF TRẦN TIỂU HÚC
tom_tat: Stories about reincarnation always give us a sense of mystery and contain valuable lessons about human life. Today, we will explore the mystery of past lives.
noi_dung:
THE ANCESTRAL ENMITY OF TRAN TIEU HUC

Stories about reincarnation always give us a sense of mystery and contain valuable lessons about human life. Today, we will explore the past life mystery of a once-famous actress - Tran Tieu Huc (October 29, 1965 – May 13, 2007)

She is a person from Anshan city, Liaoning province, China. In 1984, thanks to her special temperament, Chen Xiaohu was assigned the role of Lin Daiyu in the television series "Dream of the Red Chamber." By 1987, after the series was broadcast, her portrayal of Lin Daiyu was very well received and loved by the public, and from then on, the name Xiaohu became closely associated with Lin Daiyu.

There was a time when she met a meditation monk who had opened the insight into past lives. This person could see others' past lives. He recounted to Tiểu Húc the twists and turns of her last five lives, two as a man, three as a woman, specifically as follows:

In a previous life, Trần Tiểu Húc was reincarnated as a human and became an official, rising to the position of prefect. During a year of severe drought, this official spent all his wealth on purchasing food to provide relief, saving more than a thousand people from starving to death. Afterwards, he was promoted to governor-general. Due to his upright personality and disdain for flattery, he offended the imperial family, was dismissed and sent back to his hometown, and had all his assets confiscated.

After death, thanks to his merit in saving thousands of people from famine, he was reborn into the heavenly realm at the lowest level (the Heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings), becoming a celestial being and enjoying heavenly blessings for 3,500 years; after his heavenly fortune ended, he was reborn into the human world as the eldest son of a wealthy family, inheriting a great deal of property.

The strange thing is that the former enemy from his past life was now reincarnated as the steward of that family. Once, believing that the steward had stolen something from the house, this son beat him to death.

After the incident of killing a person, his body began to deteriorate. A few years before his death, he did many good deeds, built temples ... After dying, he was reincarnated as a woman in a wealthy family with many children. This is a brief story about two lives of Trần Tiểu Húc's male body.

In the next life, Trần Tiểu Húc was reborn as a woman, the wife of a scholar. The housekeeper, too, was reincarnated and became a bandit.

Once, on the way back to her parental home, in a narrow alley, she encountered that bandit and was raped by him.

Because she was too miserable, she committed suicide; after dying, her vengeful spirit sought revenge, causing all of these bandits to be captured and executed.

After avenging herself, she reincarnated in another life, again as a female, and when she grew up, she married a wealthy man, becoming his first wife. As for the bandit, he reincarnated as the daughter of a poor family.

At this time, the suffering and resentment arising from committing suicide in the previous life had transformed into a strong feeling of jealousy and hatred in her.

After marrying a wealthy man, many years passed but she still could not have children, so her husband took a poor girl as a concubine (who was actually the bandit who had humiliated her in her previous life).

Although she did not remember what had happened in her past life, when she saw the young concubine, her heart was filled with intense hatred, so she always sought ways to torment the concubine.

The young concubine was humiliated by her in countless ways and, after becoming pregnant, was brutally beaten to the point of miscarriage, leading to her death.

Therefore, she was abandoned. In the last years of her life, she secluded herself in a nun's hut, devotedly reciting Buddhist scriptures and repenting for her sins. Before passing away, she made a vow before the Buddha, praying to be liberated from the cycle of rebirth in future lives...

After death, through the six realms of reincarnation, in this life she was reborn as a female, named Trần Tiểu Húc, carrying the merit of saving thousands of lives when serving as a county magistrate. This merit brought her fortune and success in this life, being both a famous actress and a prosperous businesswoman, and she was once voted as one of the 30 outstanding female entrepreneurs in the mainland advertising industry in 2004.

When she became famous, there were many fans who admired her; it is very likely that they were people she had saved in the past.

In this life, she still carried a heart of reverence and admiration for the Dharma. She often went to the temple, directed her mind toward the Three Jewels, devoted herself to doing good deeds, and was willing to spend a large amount of money to help those in difficult and unfortunate circumstances. Ultimately, she shaved her head and became a nun following the Buddha, with the Dharma name Diệu Chân.

In addition, due to the karmic retribution of having killed her husband’s concubine and unborn child in a previous life, from a young age, Trần Tiểu Húc was frail, frequently ill, melancholic, and disheartened with life.

In 2007, the karmic result of killing had ripened; she was tormented by cancer and passed away at the age of 43, leaving sorrow among many devoted fans. This is a rough account of three generations of a woman's family.

It can be seen that being reborn in the six realms of samsara is truly exhausting; even after being born in heaven for 3,500 years, one still has to return to being human with all kinds of lingering grievances.

Especially, the cycles of mutual enmity seem to never end. Take, for example, Miss Tiểu Húc: in one life, as an official, she was harmed by Quốc cữu, which made her harbor a desire for revenge. In her next life, she was reborn as a young master and killed the steward (i.e., Quốc cữu reborn) to avenge herself,

and in the following life, she was repaid with revenge, being born as a common woman and raped by bandits (i.e., the steward reborn). In another life, still carrying the desire for revenge, she, as the first wife, killed her husband's concubine (i.e., the bandit reborn), and also caused the death of a fetus… and it is unknown when this prolonged cycle of hatred will ever end.

Therefore, we must understand that only the path of practicing according to the Buddha, seeking to escape from the cycle of life and death, is truly the shore of happiness, peace, and eternity. All other goals, whether seeking to ascend to heaven or pursuing fame and glory, are merely a dream that vanishes in an instant.

On this occasion, it is worth adding about the nature of human life. The early lives of Tiểu Húc were as a highly ranked and honorable person, possessing great virtue, meaning that his heart contained much goodness, and he was even reborn into the heavenly realm for 3,500 years.

However, when the merits of heaven are exhausted and one is born as a human, the human body is immersed in the flow of karmic debts, not yet freed from reincarnation, it is difficult to avoid the arising of wicked minds, committing evil deeds, and thus virtue diminishes day by day, the resulting karmic obstacles increase, and destiny becomes increasingly bleak.

The Buddha taught that being human is suffering. It is also because of this principle that once humans enter the dusty mundane world, filled with countless temptations, if they do not know how to cleanse and adjust themselves, sooner or later they will become polluted. Once polluted, then Hell and the animal realms are not far away. Those who do not know how to cultivate and accumulate virtue for themselves will find it difficult to live comfortably in future lives. The principle of "accumulating virtue," which ancestors used to educate and guide their descendants, is truly profound.

The story of human reincarnation over hundreds of thousands of years is difficult to fully recount in detail, but the tales that are told more or less serve as a warning to the world, and also to explain the joys and sufferings of human life. Being a person, accumulating virtue and practicing goodness is the important matter to pursue.
