tieu_de: COMPASSION CAN CHANGE DESTINY.
tom_tat: Cao Ban was a famous general of the Song dynasty, helping Emperor Taizu of Song to pacify the world, with great achievements in military campaigns. Once, Cao Ban met Tran Hi Di, a person with extensive knowledge, skilled in observation.
noi_dung:
COMPASSION CAN CHANGE ONE'S DESTINY.

Cao Bin was a famous general of the Song Dynasty, who helped Emperor Taizu of Song unify the country and had great achievements in military campaigns. Once, Cao Bin met Tran Hi Di, a person with profound knowledge, skilled in physiognomy.

He looked at Cao Bin's appearance and said:

- The bones on both sides of his face are prominent, his forehead is broad, his eyes are long and radiant, surely he will become wealthy early, but he has an unattractive feature: a high jaw and a downturned mouth, suggesting he will not enjoy blessings in old age. Based on this, whenever he goes to war, he should act with leniency and cultivate merit for his later years.

Cao Bin listened to Tran Hi Di, then bowed his head in gratitude, remembering those words.

Once, when Cao Ban went to battle, Deputy General Toai Ninh and many of his subordinate officers advocated for killing all the people in the city to show force. Cao Ban immediately knew and issued a strict order forbidding harming innocent people, women, or plundering the possessions of the people. After the conflict ended, he even provided food for those who were far from home and wanted to return; the people all expressed their gratitude for his benevolent heart.

Then, Cao Ban received orders to lead troops to attack Giang Nam. Because he could not bear to see the people suffering terribly due to the war, he feigned illness and did not go. The military generals under his command at that time all came to visit him before the expedition. Cao Ban said to everyone who came to visit him:

- My illness has no cure, but as long as all of you sincerely swear that when we attack Giang Nam you will absolutely not arbitrarily kill the common people, then my illness will naturally ease.

The generals and soldiers greatly respected Cao Ban, so they immediately took an oath together accordingly. On the day of the attack on Jiangnan, thanks to this, countless civilians were spared from slaughter.

The benevolent heart of General Cao spread throughout Jiangnan, and the people were all deeply moved. Therefore, everyone went together to bring provisions to welcome the imperial army. The resistance of the rebel forces was thus very weak. As a result, this battle did not cost many lives, and moreover, the people’s property was protected from destruction.

Not long after, Cao Ban happened to run into Tran Hi Di again. He looked at the gentleman for a moment and then said:

- How strange! Last year, I examined your face and saw a high jaw and a drooping mouth. At that time, I was certain you would not have blessings in old age, but now it has changed; your lips are full and beautiful, and the golden light shines marvelously, visible across your face and hair, surely indicating a long life with many blessings.

Cao Ban asked again:

- What do you mean by golden light?

- That is the manifested light of virtue; if a person has hidden virtue, their face will show a yellow-gold light, bright eyes, and the whole face radiates a good and auspicious aura. Such a person not only increases their lifespan, but future generations of descendants also benefit from this virtue.

Indeed, in his old age, Cao Ban lived a life of ease and leisure, and when he passed away, it was very peaceful. He died at the age of 69 and was posthumously granted the title of Lord Tế Dương. The gentleman had a total of 9 sons, the eldest named Vi, the second named Tong, and the third named San, all of whom were distinguished generals; for many generations afterward, his descendants were all honored and unmatched.

NAM MO HOAN HY TANG BO TAT MA HA TAT_()_

(Excerpt from "Historical Records of Response and Sensitivity" - Đức Dục Cổ Giám and Pháp Tướng Bí Truyện)

tieu_de: FOLLOWING CONDITIONS AND HARMONIZING WITH THE DHARMA
tom_tat: Going along with conditions according to the Dharma means responding to people, dealing with things, and handling situations according to the time, circumstances, context, and conditions in a way that is appropriate to the Right Path. Simply put, it means knowing which conditions to go along with in order to see clearly.
noi_dung:
FOLLOWING CONDITIONS AND PROSPEROUS PHENOMENA

Acting according to conditions and in accordance with the Dharma means responding to people, engaging with events, and conducting oneself appropriately according to the Right Path, depending on the time, circumstances, situations, and conditions. To put it simply, it means knowing which conditions require clear awareness, which require careful consideration, which require truthful speech, which require proper and good actions, which require living in accordance with the Dharma, which require diligent effort, which should be fully embraced, and which call for tranquility and serenity.

For example: When encountering favorable conditions, one should not have random imaginations but needs to clearly recognize the body, mind, and circumstances at that moment (right view), not think excessively to embellish that favorable condition, but needs to contemplate seriously (right intention), not boast about one's favorable conditions but needs to speak the truth (right speech), not act to harm others for the sake of protecting favorable conditions but needs to behave rightly (right action), not exploit one's advantageous opportunities to live unethically but should live contentedly, moderately, and share with others (right livelihood), not be lax or indulgent because of favorable circumstances, but always diligently return to reality.(Right Effort), not clinging to or being immersed in favorable conditions, but fully knowing oneself (Right Mindfulness), not being distracted or scattered by those favorable circumstances, but often remaining peacefully and clearly established in the mind (Right Concentration). The same applies to adverse conditions.

To live in accordance with conditions and in harmony with the Dharma, no matter what circumstances arise, one must respond to those conditions with mindfulness, being careful and attentive in observation. Only then can the mind fully return to awareness of reality, allowing it to remain pure, stable, and clear. In this way, whether facing favorable or adverse conditions, the mind remains spacious, calm, and luminous. This is truly living in accordance with conditions and Dharma, selfless and altruistic—not following conditions in a careless or lax way, because that would be called clinging to conditions, not being in harmony with them.

Master Vien Minh (Excerpt from Q&A, trungtamhotong.org)

tieu_de: HEALED, DELIVERED FROM DISASTER, ATTAINING REBIRTH IN THE PURE LAND THROUGH RECITING THE LOTUS SUTRA.
tom_tat: During the Vĩnh Minh era, in Dương Đô, at Cao Tòa Pagoda, Thích Huệ Tấn, in his youth, was very strong, sociable, and had a heroic spirit. Upon reaching the age of forty, he suddenly realized the truth of impermanence and then went to become a monk to study the Way. Only used
noi_dung:
HEALING, ESCAPING DANGER, AND ATTAINING REBIRTH IN THE PURE LAND THROUGH RECITING THE LOTUS SUTRA.

During the Vinh Minh era, in Duong Do region, at Cao Toa pagoda, Thich Hue Tan, when he was young, was very vigorous, liked socializing, had a heroic ambition, and upon reaching the age of forty suddenly realized the truth of impermanence, he then went to become a monk to study the Way. He only ate vegetable paste, wore coarse cloth, and vowed to recite the Lotus Sutra.

Because he worked too hard with great dedication, he fell ill. He then made a vow to print one hundred sets of sutras to atone for the karmic obstacles from his past lives. When he had collected one thousand six hundred coins, a group of robbers came to question him about his valuables. He showed them the money and told them it was for printing sutras. Ashamed, the robbers left.

Later, he managed to print the one hundred sets of sutras, and his old illness also healed. He had chanted sutras many times, and with a fulfilled mind, he dedicated the merit of chanting sutras to pray for rebirth in the Pure Land.

One day, suddenly a voice was heard in the void saying: "The dharma vow is complete, you will surely be reborn in the Pure Land."

He did not suffer from any illness but passed away, having lived for more than eighty years.

(Excerpted from the collection Tường Di Ký)

*During the Tang dynasty, there was an official of the Ministry of Rites named Wang Yem. In his lifetime, he was extremely ignorant and slow-witted, and only had one copy of the Lotus Sutra, which he studied for a long time before he could recite it fluently. Later, he fell ill and passed away, then appeared in a dream to his younger brother, who was a governor in Xin'an, saying: "By reciting the Lotus Sutra, I was able to be reborn in the Western Land, but because of my ignorance, I am still in the lotus womb. Now I convey this message to you, from now on, you must diligently recite the sutra and should not be lazy or negligent."

After saying this, he bid farewell....

(Excerpted from the Lotus Sutra Practice and Test)

*During the Song Dynasty, Thich Hue Khanh was a native of Quang Lang, who became a monk at Lo Son Pagoda, studying the scriptures and precepts, with pure and strict morality. He often recited the Lotus Sutra, the Ten Grounds Sutra, the Si Yi Sutra, and the Vimalakirti Sutra. Every night when he chanted, he often heard the sound of fingernails snapping in the void, praising him.

One day, while he was on a boat, he suddenly encountered a severe storm with heavy rain, fierce thunder and lightning, and waves rising three fathoms high. The boat rocked as if it were about to capsize, yet Khanh continued chanting the sutras without stopping. Suddenly, he felt as if someone was pulling and supporting the boat in the middle of the river, and in an instant, it reached the shore.

From that time on, Mr. Khánh became even more diligent.

(Extracted from the collection Pháp Uyển Châu Lâm)

*During the Liang dynasty, Master Thích Pháp Lâm, surname Nghiêm, from Chi Giang district, became a monk at Ngọc Tuyền Pagoda. He often recited the Lotus Sutra, fasting on only one midday meal each day, sitting continuously and not lying down. The master enjoyed traveling, often carrying a staff and wandering across mountains and regions such as Lô Sơn, Thai Đảnh, Hoành Lãnh, La Phù, etc.; there was no distant place he did not visit. He only sought shelter in secluded caves and remote places, dedicating himself entirely to meditation practice.

The master often went to Đại Mountain and had to pass through Châu Từ, where the district magistrate questioned him to test his authenticity, seeing that the master only carried a copy of the Lotus Sutra. The magistrate did not believe him and angrily had him imprisoned. The master did not eat for seven days, continuously chanting the sutra. The magistrate had a nightmare while sleeping, so he respectfully asked the master to pray for repentance.

Later, the master went into seclusion in a quiet place, devoting himself to meditation and sutra chanting. At the time of his death, a strange fragrance lingered for ten full days before dissipating.

(Extracted from the Lotus Sutra Practice and Verification)

*During the Tang Dynasty, there was a man named Xam Van Bon, styled Cảnh Nhơn, who was from Luoyang. From a young age, he believed in Buddhism and recited the Universal Gate Chapter in the Lotus Sutra. Once, he was traveling by boat on the Wu River. In the middle of the river, the boat capsized, and everyone drowned. Van Bon also sank into the water, when suddenly he heard a voice saying:

“Those who recite the Lotus Sutra will be saved from death.”

Having said this three times, he immediately surfaced and was carried to the shore in an instant.

*During the Tang Dynasty in Bozhou, Master Thích Pháp Triệt, while young, was diligent and hardworking in reciting the Lotus Sutra, often using this sutra to guide and educate everyone.

In the hamlet, there was Master Co Son, and Mr. Phap Triet came to seek guidance from him to practice, founding the Lang Nha sect. He once traveled to various places and suddenly encountered a person with leprosy, brought him to the mountain, dug a cave for him to live in, and nurtured him. He encouraged him to recite the Lotus Sutra, but the leprous person could not read, and was also mentally dull. Mr. Phap Triet taught him each phrase, never showing fatigue. By the time they reached the sixth volume, the leprosy was cured, and after studying, the eyebrows and hair grew back, and the skin was restored to its original state.

(Excerpted from the Lotus Sutra Research and Practice)

*During the Song Dynasty, she was of the Phi family, the wife of Mr. La Du, from Thuc Ninh. Her father, named Duyet, was a deputy governor of Ninh prefecture. When she was young, Lady Phi sincerely believed in the Three Jewels. She diligently chanted the Lotus Sutra for several years without feeling tired.

Later, she suddenly suffered from heart disease. She closed the door, feeling sad and anxious, and instructed her family to prepare funeral items, waiting for the time.

Lady Phi thought to herself: "I have diligently chanted the sutra, surely I will be blessed and possibly avoid death."

Thinking that way, she lay down and peacefully slept for a while. When she woke up, still in a daze, she saw the Buddha by the window, reaching out and touching her heart; her illness was instantly cured. The entire household—men, women, and servants—saw a bright golden halo throughout the house, and there was also a strong fragrance. Mr. Dự's younger sister, who had come to visit the sick person and was standing by the bed, saw everything clearly as well.

From that time on, Mrs. Phí developed even greater faith and constantly reminded herself to strive her whole life, often using this event to encourage and instruct her children and grandchildren.

(Excerpted from the collection Dị Ký)

THE SUPREME BUDDHA MANTRA DHARANI

The mantra of Buddha's Supreme Vajra Dharani, also known as the Supreme Vajra Buddha Mantra, consists of 92 verses and was spoken by the World-Honored One in the Sutra of Buddha's Supreme Vajra Dharani. The power of this mantra to destroy karmic obstacles is also considered extremely fast, as mentioned in the sutra:

"This Dharani often completely eliminates the five heinous sins and the ten evils of sentient beings; often saves all suffering in the realms of Yama, animals, hungry ghosts, and hell; often liberates all sentient beings who have heavy karma and thin merit, who are poor, lowly, sick, disabled, short-lived, ugly, mute, or blind and deaf; often rescues various types of Asuras, Yakshas, Rakshasas, Pundarikas, Catra Pundarikas, and other demonic bodies; even often liberates species of aquatic creatures, non-flying birds, terrestrial animals, snakes, centipedes, flies, mosquitoes, and insects. These sentient beings, according to their fate, will be born into peaceful realms and will successively attain the fruit of liberation."

Those with a karmic connection who wish to recite this mantra should ideally recite it in Vietnamese. The patriarchs labored to translate the scriptures and mantras into Vietnamese so that many people could recite them. Whether the mantra brings results depends on the mind, not on whether it is in Vietnamese or Sanskrit. Many people do not understand this principle and mistakenly spread the idea that: the mantra must be recited in Sanskrit to be effective – This is a false teaching, and I hope readers with karmic affinity pay close attention!

The Wonderful Effects of the Buddha’s Supreme Dharani

"After explaining the mantra, the Buddha said:

– O Heavenly Emperor! The Tathagata's Pure and Sacred Dharmākara Crowned Virtue Dharani with eighty-eight verses, countless hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have proclaimed it, and guarded it strictly and secretly, rejoicing and praising it. All Tathagatas unanimously confirm it.

If there are monks, nuns, good men, or good women who uphold or recite it; due to that merit, all the offenses of rebellion, the ten evil deeds over hundreds of thousands of kalpas will be eliminated; they will attain the fruit of Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. That person in the present will acquire knowledge of past lives; then reborn from this heaven to another heaven, from this Buddha realm to another Buddha realm. That person will receive the head-patting and empowerment from Bodhisattvas such as Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteshvara, Mahasthamaprapta; they will often remain in the assembly hall, listen, understand, and uphold the true Dharma.

A person who constantly keeps their body, speech, and mind pure will have a joyful mind, their physical suffering will be eliminated; they will experience gentle, wholesome sensations, have their lifespan extended, and be free from sudden death. Such a person will be protected by the celestial beings, benevolent Bodhisattvas, and will be remembered by the Buddhas. Anyone who recites this mantra will reach the hell realms, hungry ghost realms, and even be read by Yama, the lord of death; all sins committed there will be liberated, the realms will be empty; the heavenly palaces, Bodhisattva palaces, and the palaces of the Buddha realms will open their doors to welcome the practitioner.

– Why is that? Because this Dhāraṇī can eliminate completely the five grave sins and the ten evils of sentient beings; it can relieve all suffering and calamities in the realms of Yama, intermediate beings, hungry ghosts, and hell; it can save all sentient beings with heavy karma and little merit, who are poor, lowly, sick, disabled, short-lived, ugly, mute, blind, or deaf; it can also rescue various kinds of Asura, Yaksha, Rakshasa, Gandharva, Kinnaras, and other divine or demonic forms; furthermore, it can deliver aquatic beings, birds, wild animals, snakes, scorpions, flies, mosquitoes, and insects. These sentient beings, according to their karma and destiny, will be reborn into peaceful realms, and eventually all will attain the fruit of liberation.

Oh Heavenly King! If someone recites and upholds this mantra, from this current life onward, they will forever be free from the path of evil; they will often be born into noble families in the human realm, or be born into the heavenly realms; until they reach the presence of all Buddhas in the ten directions, befriend all Bodhisattvas, and ultimately attain the Supreme Enlightenment.

O Heavenly Emperor! My Buddha Recitation School of Venerable Supreme Dharani possesses full divine power and authority; its merit is vast like the auspicious sun, like a perfectly pure and clear jewel, without any stain, and wherever it casts its light, it illuminates that place. Furthermore, like the seven supreme treasures in the world, which are all valued and cherished by kings, officials, and the people, never growing tiresome to behold, this Dharani School is alike; whoever recites, records, or makes offerings will gain immeasurable merit; all heaven, dragons, and the eight classes of beings will respect, cherish, and admire it.

O Heavenly Emperor! If the kings and ministers of the four directions copy this dharani and place it in the seven-treasure stupa, in the lion throne hall, at the crossroads stupa; or at the top of tall banners, and also offer various flowers, incense, grains, clothing, food and drink, and medicines; that person's merit is limitless and boundless, and their blessings and wisdom cannot be measured. That person is a true son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva, because they can save countless sentient beings who pass by there.

If there are sentient beings who commit the four grave sins, the five heinous crimes, the ten evils, the major precepts, and all serious offenses, they should undergo suffering in the three lower realms; yet if they pass by a stupa or banner where this arhat is represented, and even a speck of dust or a bit of wind from the stupa or banner touches their body, or they are shaded by the stupa or banner, all their serious offenses will be eradicated, and they will be reborn in the heavenly realm to enjoy supreme joy; alternatively, depending on karmic conditions, they may be reborn in the Pure Land.

Anyone who regularly observes this Dharani, when about to recite it, uses water to wash their hands; if this water falls to the ground and sprinkles on insects and ants, these beings also benefit from the merit created and are born in the heavenly realm. Therefore, monks, nuns, righteous men, and faithful women, if they keep their precepts pure and observe this Dharani during the six periods, all grave sins, including the four heavy offenses, the five heinous crimes, the ten evil deeds, and all major sins over three lifetimes, will be extinguished, and they will receive the Buddha and Bodhisattvas’ blessing and endorsement.

By that time, it was already past midnight. Yama, the King of Hell; Vaisravana, the Guardian of the World; Dhatara; Virudhaka, the Heavenly King of Sword; Virupaksha, the Heavenly King of the Night Demons; Dhritarashtra, the Heavenly King of Contentment; Hahuta, the Heavenly King of Transformation; Indra, the Heavenly King; Mahendra, the Great Indra… led their hundreds of thousands of followers, bringing incense, flowers, and various ornaments, and circumambulated seven times to the right of the Buddha, prostrated at His feet, and then offered the food offerings. After completing the ceremony, they further requested as follows:

– Noble World-Honored One! We have heard the Tathagata expound the Scripture of the Supreme Buddha-Adoration Dharani, so we have come here to request to receive it and to guard it in accordance with your teachings. We respectfully beseech the Celestial and Human Teacher to explain to us the essential teachings of this mantra, so that our practice of recitation may be thorough and accomplished.

Essence of the Supreme Buddha-Adoration Mantra

The Buddha spoke to King Yama and the celestial kings:

– Listen! I will explain it for you:

* If there are sentient beings who are suffering, burdened with extremely heavy karma, and no one can save them; one should choose a full moon day, take a bath, wear clean clothes, observe the eight precepts for laypeople; kneel before the Buddha statue and recite this Dharani 1,080 times, then all sins and karmic obstacles will be eliminated. That person will attain purity and liberation, gaining mastery over the General Dharani and unobstructed eloquence.

* If someone has not yet recited this mantra, but merely hears the sound of this dharani entering their ear, they immediately become a seed of Buddha. It is like a drop of diamond falling to the ground; it will penetrate to the point of the original nucleus before stopping, and even though the ground is thick, it cannot obstruct it. This mantra is the same; once it enters the ear, it gradually cultivates and leads to the fruition of enlightenment, and even heavy afflictions cannot block it. Even if that person falls into the realms of Hell, hungry ghosts, or other unintended births, the karmic consequences will not extinguish that seed; rather, the power of the mantra continues to help them practice progressively until they attain Buddhahood.

* If any sentient being hears this Dharani even once, in this current life they will no longer suffer from diseases and afflictions; they will also no longer take birth in a womb, instead being born wherever a lotus flower manifests. From then on, the five eyes will gradually become pure, they will obtain the wisdom of a complete life; impurities will be eliminated, and they will attain the supreme perfect enlightenment.

* If someone has recently died or has been dead for a long time, and someone recites this 21-verse Dharani into a handful of soil or sand and sprinkles it on the corpse, that person will be reborn in one of the ten Pure Lands. For those whose spirits have fallen into hell, become hungry ghosts, or are born in non-human forms, when the soil or sand touches their remains, they will also be freed from evil beings and be reborn into the heavenly realms.

* If any sentient being recites this mantra 21 times daily, they should be able to receive the vast offerings of all the world; upon leaving the physical body, they will be reborn in the Pure Land; those who often recite it will gain longevity, enjoy supreme happiness; in the future, they will be reborn in the Pure Lands of the ten directions, hear the wondrous Dharma; receive prophecies, the light within their body will shine across all Buddha realms, and attain Great Nirvana.

* If one wishes to gain sovereign spiritual power, the practitioner uses substances like glutinous rice flour, rice flour, etc., molding them into human shapes to place in the eight directions of the ritual platform, and day and night faces the eight directions while reciting the mantra, all will be as desired.

* If the flood water rises, face that direction and recite this mantra 108 times in prayer, the water will recede.

* If suffering from the king’s disaster, the officials’ disaster, war, bandits, or verbal attacks; recite this spell 21 times in the year of fragrant water, pour it over the Buddha's head, and the disasters will be eliminated.

* If any sentient being has a short lifespan and wishes to live long; one should choose a full moon day, observe moral precepts, bathe, wear clean clothes, and recite this spell 1,080 times; longevity will be granted, and all sins and obstacles will be eradicated.

* If someone recites this spell once into the ear of any kind of beast, that type in this life will no longer take on a beastly body; even if it has heavy karma and would be condemned to hell, it will also be liberated.

* If anyone suffers from a serious illness and endures much pain, hearing this mantra will relieve them from illness and suffering, and their sins will be destroyed. Even beings among the four types, if they hear this spell, will be freed from illness and suffering, leave the fetal body, and be reborn on a lotus flower; depending on where they are born, they will remember their previous lives without forgetting.

* If there is a sentient being who has just grown up and has committed the four gravest sins, the five heinous acts, and the ten evil deeds; by the time of old age, they reflect and realize that due to these evil karmas, after death they will fall into Avīci Hell, endure great suffering for many lifetimes, and continuously revolve in the three evil realms without anyone to save them. That person should choose a full moon day, bathe and wear pure clothes; use a bowl made of gold, silver, or copper, with a capacity of about one thăng, fill it with clean water to place before the Buddha statue, take the Bodhisattva precepts, and observe pure fasting.

At the altar, I stand in the East facing the Buddha statue in the West, sincerely bowing to repent. Then I chant this Dharani 1,080 times without interruption; after that, I use that water to sprinkle in all four directions and above and below, wishing that all beings be purified. Upon completing this ritual, all sins and obstacles are destroyed, escaping the karmic retribution of the three levels of hell; King Yama releases, the God of Destiny is pleased, without anger or resentment; returning, I join my hands respectfully, rejoicing and praising the merits.

* If you want to save a person with heavy sins, choose a full moon day, recite this mantra 1,080 times into honey or milk, and then give it to that person to consume. Doing so, the individual will eliminate their sins, be reborn into a good realm, gradually advance in cultivation, and attain the supreme enlightenment.

* If you recite this mantra 21 times and empower it onto a toothpick, then using it can help relieve toothache, gain strength, intelligence, and longevity.

* If you want to save the suffering of animals, you should empower this mantra onto sand or golden soil 21 times, then sprinkle it over their bodies and the four directions; their sins will be eliminated.

* If there are sentient beings who wish to have complete blessings, desire to obtain wealth and treasures as they wish, and wish to save themselves and others, they should cultivate a kind heart; every day make vows and repent, facing the Buddha statue, perform the mudras and recite this mantra seven times; with an undistracted mind, eyes fixed on the Buddha statue without moving, then dedicate the merit to all sentient beings. Practicing in this way with a kind heart will surely fulfill your wishes; it will increase blessings and fortune in the present life, as well as in future lives.

* If the practitioner stays at the altar every day for three sessions; during each session, recite this mantra 21 times into a cup of clean water, then respectfully hold the cup of water in your mind and drink it. Doing so will eliminate illnesses, grant long life up to a hundred years, resolve all enmities; the voice will be melodious, speech and talent fluent, and in each life one will often gain Knowledge of Past Lives, remembering previous existences. If this cup of water is sprinkled in a room, or even in the pen of oxen or horses, that place will be safeguarded by the power of the true mantra, warding off disasters: demons, snakes, dragons. If the cup of water, with the mantra recited over it, is sprinkled on the head of a sick person and given to them to drink, all serious illnesses will be eliminated.

* If you want to eliminate obstacles and calamities, you should use scraps of silk in five colors, making them into a fly whisk. Then chant a mantra over the fly whisk, sweep dust over the Buddha statue and sutras. By doing so regularly, your own calamities will be eradicated, and the karmic offenses of sentient beings will also be eliminated.

* If you are afflicted with many verbal slanders or arising rumors, you should use vermilion mixed with white honey, or white sugar; chant a mantra into it 21 times, then apply it to the lips of 100 Buddha statues. By doing so, verbal slanders and rumors will be eradicated.

* If a husband and wife dislike each other and want to be harmonious; chant the spell onto cloth or silk 21 times, then use it to make clothes for the husband or wife to wear, doing so will make the husband and wife harmonious.

* If a man or woman is disturbed by demons, or the yin spirit is overly attached and cannot let go; one should maintain mindfulness while chanting the spell and rubbing it all over the victim's body, then clap hands on the body, the demons will immediately flee.

* If a woman has no one coming to propose marriage; one should use good clean salt, chant the spell onto it 108 times, then offer it to the present monks, it will surely bring desired results.

* If the dwelling is disturbed by evil spirits, one should chant a mantra 21 times onto the food and then offer it for them to eat. At the same time, say: "Today I offer this to you; if it does not harm living beings, you may stay as you wish; if it causes harm, you must go elsewhere." If the aggressive spirits do not obey, use a 12-finger-long iron stake, chant the mantra onto it 21 times, and then drive it into the ground. By doing this, the evil spirits must leave the area.

* If a patient is possessed by a spirit, the rescuer should look attentively at the patient's face and chant this mantra; the spirit will leave.

* If there are La Sát demons or other evil spirits entering the country causing illness, terror, and disturbing the minds of the people; one should recite the Triple Gem, chant this mantra day and night, and execute the Buddha's Supreme Seal to spread it to the four directions, then all disasters will be eliminated. Doing so can also save sentient beings suffering in the three realms.

* If you wish to offer water to hungry ghosts; chant this mantra into clean water seven times, then spread it in all four directions, with mindful thoughts and spoken words, praying that they may enjoy it, then the hungry ghosts will be able to drink the nectar water.

* If someone whose business is sluggish wants to attract customers, they should usually perform this charm 21 times, place the Buddha image in a clean and private spot, and offer it; it will certainly bring about the desired outcome.

* If someone, three times a day, recites this mantra 21 times each session, respectfully offers, sincerely upholds it, and explains it for others, that person will attain peace, live a long life, be free from illness, develop wisdom, gain knowledge of past lives, and at the time of death, like a cicada shedding its shell, will be reborn in the Pure Land, no longer hearing the sounds of hell, let alone being condemned. That person will gradually progress on the path to enlightenment until achieving Buddhahood.

The Buddha told King Yama and the heavenly kings:

– If any sentient beings wish to establish this Dera Trà Ra Ni altar, they should use golden soil mixed with fragrant water to apply on the surface of the altar. The altar should be square, each side four arm widths, surrounded by five-colored silk threads in three layers. Mantras should be chanted into white mustard seeds, or fragrant water scattered on all four sides. At the four corners of the altar, place four containers of pure water, all with equal volumes. In the center of the altar, scatter various flowers, burn various incense, and light oil lamps with fragrant materials.

In front of the Buddha statue, use clean and beautiful containers to hold foods such as white rice, glutinous rice, milk, sugar, or other fruits for offering. Practitioners should wear clean clothing, observe the Bodhisattva precepts, and avoid eating foods that are black in color. Each time, one should make the mudra and recite this mantra 108 times, or if possible, 1,080 times. Reciting in this way will eliminate karmic obstacles, increase merit and virtuous roots, be reborn in Pure Lands, and receive the prophecy to become a Buddha.

Mantra of the Exalted Buddha Crown: Method of Making the Mudra

To make the Buddha's Supreme Vajra Seal, one should clasp both hands together, curl the index fingers into the palms, and press the thumbs against the middle joints of the index fingers to form the seal.

When making this seal and chanting the mantra 108 times, it is considered that one has offered 88 ganapti of infinite numbers of prostrations to countless Buddhas, receiving praise from the Buddhas and being acknowledged as a Buddha's disciple.

If a person performs this seal and chants this mantra 108 times every day, they will receive the prediction of enlightenment from the Buddhas of the ten directions, without any doubt. If one performs the seal and chants 1080 times daily, that person will gain an indestructible Vajra body and swiftly attain the fruit of enlightenment.

Any practitioner who recites this mantra daily, then forms mudras toward the four directions, reciting the mantra once for each direction and scattering it in one turn, will receive the reverent support of all gods, dragons, and spirits. Their beauty will be radiant, whatever they need will be brought to them by the gods according to their thoughts, they will have immeasurable blessings, boundless merit, be praised by all Buddhas, and be able to be reborn at will in the Pure Lands of the ten directions.

In short, the power of the Exalted Victory Dharani is immense, can be applied according to one’s wishes, and is beyond description!

The Buddha spoke to the heavenly king and the assembly:

– The Buddha's Crown Supreme Dharani, in the age of the degenerate Dharma, if there are kings, officials, and laypeople who, according to the proper ritual, establish an altar for practice and offerings, this is called the practice of Generosity. When setting up the altar to practice, maintaining the three pure karmas, free from anger and resentment, this is observing precepts and practicing patience. Daily recitation without interruption or laziness is the practice of diligence. Following the Dharma rules consistently, with a focused mind, is the practice of meditation. Establishing the altar for generosity correctly, understanding the method of preservation, appropriately measuring and knowing what actions to perform or avoid is the practice of Prajna (Wisdom).

– O Heavenly Emperor and all the assembly! If he establishes the Dharma practices according to the teachings, he will fully accomplish the six paramitas. You should repeatedly instruct and enlighten, so that sentient beings gain much benefit and attain the Bodhi fruit!

When the Buddha finished speaking of this Dharma gateway, Indra, Shripati, and the heavenly beings heeded the teaching and returned to the heavenly abode. Shripati, the heavenly ruler, followed the instructions and practiced for seven full days. Using his divine eye to observe, he saw that all his karmic retributions had been eliminated, and his blessings and longevity in the heavenly realm greatly increased. He rejoiced and exclaimed in praise: "Marvelous indeed, O Buddha Śākyamuni! Marvelous indeed, O Dharma! Marvelous indeed, O Saṅgha! Marvelous indeed, the power of the Buddha's Ādi Śrī Dhāraṇī, which dispels all suffering, allowing me to be freed from such retributions!"

Practice and Recitation of the Buddha's Ādi Śrī Dhāraṇī

The Venerable Buddha-Adorned Revered Dharani, during the Tang dynasty, was often recited by the court censor Wu Zhe. Later, he heard that his colleague Xiang Xing also received and recited it, but most of the text and pronunciation were different; upon inquiry, it was found that the court censor Xiang Xing had learned it from Wang Kaishi, and Wang Kaishi had received transmission from the Venerable Vajra Wisdom Tripitaka. During the transmission, he said: "There are few copies of this in the Western Regions. I brought the Sanskrit version here, so I secretly transmitted it to him."

During the Kaiyuan era, there was a lay practitioner devoted to cultivation on Mount Wutai. People often called him Wang Shan Ren, and he also recited this mantra. Later, to pray for the salvation of his father, he recited the mantra tens of thousands of times, seeking to know the merits and demerits of his karma and the place where his father would be reborn. But in the end, he saw nothing, and he lost heart, wanting to leave the mountain. Suddenly, he met an old sage who stopped him and said: “Virtuous one, your recitation has been diligent. But since it has been long away from the Buddha, the text has become lost, with many omissions. That is why you have not quickly received results. Now that we meet here, I will transmit to you the complete version of this sacred mantra.”

Vuong Son Nhon invited him to pay respects and receive the Dharma. The elderly man said: “The virtuous one who recites this mantra a thousand times will see its effect.” The lay practitioner followed and recited it accordingly. A few nights later, suddenly he heard the sound of jade pendants clinking melodiously, accompanied by a gentle flute and zither, gradually descending before the courtyard. Amazed, the lay practitioner stepped out to see and saw dozens of celestial beings surrounding and supporting a celestial immortal of extraordinary appearance approaching.

The celestial immortal asked: “Do you know me?”

The lay practitioner replied: “This humble being has just had the honor to meet.”

The celestial being said: "I am your father. Last year, when you recited the Supreme Buddha Mantra of Enlightenment, I was able, through that merit, to be reborn in the heavens. In the past few days, that merit has increased exponentially, and I have become a king among the celestial beings. The mantra you recited is truly incredibly effective!" After saying this, all of them flew back to the higher realms. The layperson, overjoyed, bowed and saw them off. From that time onward, he practiced even more diligently.

Also at that time, in Dong Do, Mr. Vuong Thieu Phu recited the Tôn Thắng mantra according to the version of Lord Phat Da Ba Ly several tens of thousands of times. One night, he dreamed of a Buddhist monk who came and said: "You have recited very sincerely, but unfortunately the mantra text is incomplete, so the effectiveness is limited!"

Thiếu Phủ respectfully performed the ritual to request the complete written incantation. The compassionate monk approved, orally transmitting each true mantra. After memorizing everything, he thanked the monk and escorted him outside, seeing the sky bright as daytime. Thiếu Phủ returned home to find the servants still asleep. Just then, he suddenly woke and hurriedly called the attendant, asking why they hadn't woken up yet when it was already daylight. They replied that it was only midnight. At that moment, the light suddenly vanished, returning the night darkness as before.

Thiếu Phủ remembered the divine dream, found it strange, closed his eyes, chanted the mantra several times, and saw that he still understood clearly. From then on, he practiced according to the oral teachings of the monk Phạm.

In the first year of the Thiên Bảo era, Thiếu Phủ was lying in his private chamber when he suddenly passed away. Because his chest was still warm, his family did not dare to embalm him. Seven days later, he suddenly came back to life. At that time, curious onlookers in the city encouraged each other to inquire about the cause of his rebirth. The rumor spread, and Vương Khai Sĩ and Vương Sơn Nhơn, who were in Đông Đô and did not know each other at the time, also came to visit. In front of the officials and guests, Vương Thiếu Phủ recounted as follows:

– I was just lying down to rest when I suddenly fell into a trance and saw two messengers coming to take me away. After traveling a few dozen miles, we arrived at the base of a large tree, and the two messengers stopped to rest briefly, so I sat down as well. Suddenly thinking of Master Tôn Thắng, I closed my eyes and recited the mantra 21 times. When I opened my eyes and looked around, the two messengers were nowhere to be seen. After a moment, four other beings approached, knelt, and said: "We do not know by what wondrous method you practice that caused the two messengers to be reborn in the heavenly realm?"

I replied: "I, a humble person, only recite the Tôn Thắng Buddha Mantra."

Those four people pleaded: “Please, for the sake of us disciples, chant and save us from suffering and calamity!”

I also closed my eyes and chanted 21 times; when I opened my eyes, I no longer saw those four people.

In a moment suspended in emptiness, there was the sound of weapons; A deity dressed in a purple robe, wearing armor, with a large retinue of guards, came forward and knelt, saying: "I am the god Ngũ Đạo Minh Ty. Though my position is exalted, I still serve the divine path. The six others, thanks to your spiritual power, have all been born into the heavenly realm. I humbly invite you to graciously come and preside over the ritual, so that the disciples and sentient beings there may receive blessings and be born into the celestial realms together."

According to the deity, I went to a large fortress, with a perimeter of several dozen miles. Inside the city, there were many criminals, shackled and gathered in the broad courtyard in front of the palace, perhaps waiting to be interrogated and punished. The deity instructed the soldiers to set up a beautiful throne, conducted a ceremony inviting me to sit on it, while he himself knelt below, hands clasped, listening attentively. I then focused sincerely and recited 49 times. When I opened my eyes to look around, I saw no one at all, only broken chains lying scattered everywhere.

Still astonished, suddenly four messengers came to tell me: "The king orders you to go elsewhere, because you have caused disorder and disrupted the order of our council."

After that, they took me into a mountain cave, and I was revived. This rebirth was certainly due to the inconceivable power of the Buddha's Vajra Supreme Dharani mantra.

Wang Kai Shi and Wang Shan Ren, upon hearing this, each read their own mantra to compare it with Wang Shao Fu's mantra and found them identical. All three were overjoyed and celebrated together.

Vuong Son Nhon said: “I received instruction on my version from the holy master on Mount Ngũ Đài.” Vuong Thieu Phu said: “I studied this mantra from a divine monk.” Vuong Khai Si said: “As for my version, it was transmitted by Venerable Kim Cang Tri Tam Tang, and the Pham family scrolls are still preserved.” Everyone who heard this was astonished and praised it as a rare occurrence.

In addition, there is the story of Mr. Trương Diệc reciting Tôn Thắng's mantra to save his parents from the suffering of hell and help them be reborn in the heavenly realm. The story of Mr. Trương Thừa Phước reciting this mantra, when he was being arrested by the authorities, he did not suffer punishment but instead saved the souls in the underworld and helped them attain liberation. The story of several monks reciting Tôn Thắng's mantra describes occurrences of relics appearing and many auspicious realms.

The above matters are recorded in the collection Gia Cú Linh Nghiệm Phật Đảnh Tôn Thắng Đà Ra Ni Ký. After this collection, the complete text of the mantra is recorded, called the Cụ Túc Bản. The author, following the Cụ Túc Bản, compares it with the transliterations of other versions and consults dictionaries to translate it into Vietnamese accurately according to the Sanskrit sounds. As for the translation by Pháp Thiên Tam Tạng titled Tối Thắng Phật Đảnh Đà Ra Ni, compared to the Cụ Túc Bản text, it is more extensive. After proofreading, the author added texts that the Cụ Túc Bản did not have to make it more complete. It is hoped that this work will bring many benefits to those who recite and uphold it.

(Mantra of Buddha Ādi-Tathāgata – According to the Sutra of Buddha Ādi-Tathāgata Mantra)

Source: TUỆ TÂM

tieu_de: Whether you want it or not, life is still the same
tom_tat: Just go along, following the flow of time, whether a poor person or a rich one
noi_dung:
Whether you like it or not, life is still the same

Going along gradually, following the flow of time

The poor, or the wealthy

When they die, still leave with empty hands

Being well-fed and warm is already a blessing

Keep it, live a peaceful life

There are things, let nature decide

Don't force it, lest trouble covers you

Bitter or not, because of luxurious appearances

Then by yourself, pushed into the deep abyss

If the mind does not want to be entangled in sorrow

Then do not force desires in delusion

Know to repent and recognize mistakes

Remember to remind yourself to change

Even material things are needed by everyone who lives

But do not let the bonds of love and family break

Matters of life and death are always predestined

Life is impermanent, the truth cannot be changed

As human beings, everyone is the same

In the end, we all must return to dust

tieu_de: In the past, Emperor Tang Taizong once said to the monk Xuanzang:
tom_tat: I intend to offer a feast to the monks, but I hear that many of the monks do not fully observe the precepts. What should be done? Master Xuanzang replied:
noi_dung:
In ancient times, Emperor Taizong of the Tang once spoke to the monk Xuanzang:

I intend to offer alms to the monks, but I have heard that many monks do not fully observe the precepts. What should I do?

Master Xuanzang replied:

In Kũn Sơn, precious gems are also mixed with mud and sand;

In Lệ Thủy district, there is gold, so is it possible that there are no tiles, bricks, or stones there?

Clay or wood used to make Arhat statues, when made with a heart of reverence, will certainly bring blessings;

Tin statues of Buddha made of tin, whoever destroys them will definitely be guilty.

Dragons molded from clay, although they cannot make rain, to pray for rain one must use that clay dragon.

Although ordinary monks who are cultivating cannot bestow blessings, if one wants to pray for blessings, one must know to respect them.

Even if the moon is not bright, even if it is dim, it is still better than a thousand shining stars.

Without virtuous causes... even stepping into the Buddha's door is difficult, let alone joining the Sangha community.

To become a monk... one must go through many lifetimes close to serving the Triple Gem, only then can this life's merit be perfected.

Even if he has not yet purified to become a Saint, compared to ordinary people, he is a person with millions of times more good fortune, Your Majesty.

When Emperor Taizong of Tang heard these words, he was alarmed and said, "From now on, even if I meet a young novice monk, I will respectfully treat him as the Buddha."

Namo Shakyamuni Buddha

Thank the Dharma Master for compassionately lifting the clouds of confusion for me, otherwise I would hardly have complete karmic blessings.

(Excerpt from AN SỸ TOÀN THƯ – Advise People to Recite Buddha's Name to Be Reborn in the Pure Land)

Namo Amitabha Buddha

tieu_de: THANKS TO BUDDHA RECOLLECTION, MY MOTHER FINALLY RECOVERED FROM ILLNESS
tom_tat: My mother has absolute faith in Buddhism, has been vegetarian since she was young, but she still has not had the opportunity to take refuge in the Triple Gem. Her name is Truong Thi Tuyet (born in 1956), currently residing at 74/61 Dao Duy Street.
noi_dung:
THANKS TO CHANTING BUDDHA'S NAME, MY MOTHER FINALLY RECOVERED FROM ILLNESS

My mother has absolute faith in Buddhism, has been vegetarian since she was young, but she still has not had the opportunity to take refuge in the Three Jewels. Her name is Trương Thị Tuyết (born in 1956), currently residing at 74/61 Đào Duy Từ Street - Đập Đá Ward - Đập Đá Town - An Nhơn District - Bình Định Province.

In 2013, my mother suddenly suffered from severe back pain, and my family took her to many different hospitals, both large and small:

First was An Nhon District Hospital, then the provincial hospital in Quy Nhon City, but they couldn’t find my mother’s illness. Then the family agreed to take her to Hoa Hao Hospital (District 10 - Ho Chi Minh City) for four consultations, next to Hong Duc International Hospital (Go Vap District) for one consultation, and then to the International Neurosurgery Hospital (Luy Ban Bich Street - Tan Phu District) for four consultations...

After a relentless journey of consulting at all the big and small hospitals, my mother was diagnosed with “lumbar vertebral compression,” but none of the hospitals could find the cause of this disease...

Doctors at both International Hospitals treated my mother with the same method: injecting medicine directly into the vertebra to reduce pain (like a painkiller injection), but they actually did not diagnose the disease, and my mother's pain became increasingly severe...

For each collapsed vertebra, doctors at Hong Duc International Hospital injected a dose costing 25 million VND, and a year later my mother had another collapsed vertebra, and treatment at the International Neurosurgery Hospital cost 45 million VND.

The total cost of my mother's treatment was nearly 300 million VND, yet there was still no improvement, and in the end, the doctors discharged her...

At this point, my family's finances were almost depleted when my mother suffered compression in two more vertebrae. The family was very worried and cared for my mother, trying every possible way to take care of her...

At the end of 2017, a brother who worked at 115 People's Hospital (Su Van Hanh Street - District 10) introduced my family to a male doctor named Tuyen, a "neurosurgery specialist" who was very skilled.

My father hurriedly took my mother to Ho Chi Minh City to see Dr. Tuyen. He started having my mother undergo an MRI and a bone density test, and it was then discovered that the cause of my mother's three compressed lumbar vertebrae was severe osteoporosis, which could cause the compressed vertebrae to press on the nerves leading to the legs, preventing blood from circulating down to the legs, causing numbness in the legs and gradually leading to complete paralysis...

Dr. Tuyen added that my mother is elderly and currently has severe osteoporosis, so he does not dare to perform surgery. First, the cost of the surgery is 200 million VND, and second, even if 200 million VND is spent on the surgery, the likelihood of success is not high...

The doctor was sad and advised my family to take my mother home for care, then prescribed painkillers, medications to support osteoporosis, and calcium good for her bones, to prolong my mother's life.

By the summer of 2018, my mother's legs gradually went numb and then became paralyzed, unable to walk, and she also could not take care of her personal hygiene...

The increasing pain caused my mother's health to deteriorate, leaving her exhausted... My mother was sad and desperate, so she kept praying to the gods and Buddha to let her die soon, so she would no longer have to endure the tormenting, agonizing pain every day.

The atmosphere in my family right now is very heavy... On one hand, my mother wants to pray for an early death, but deep down, she still longs to live to see her children and grandchildren, to gather with the family every day...

Then I arranged my work and went to be with my mother, seeing her emaciated, withering day by day, I choked back tears, my heart tightened... Hospitals, doctors, medicines... is it really true that everything is powerless against my mother's illness?

"How can I save my mother?"

This question kept repeating in my mind... Then I suddenly remembered, I had three times experienced spiritual responses from Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva. That's right!

Only the Dharma can save my mother at this moment... The Buddha is compassionate, He will not abandon His people.

Thinking that, I immediately began telling my mother to regularly recite the name of Nam Mo A Di Da Phat! Nam Mo Bon Su Thich Ca Mau Ni Phat! Nam Mo Dai Bi Quan The Am Bo Tat! and to recite the Great Compassion Mantra with sincere heart and absolute trust.

Already having a deep and firm faith in Buddha Dharma, when she heard me speak, my mother immediately began practicing according to my guidance.

When she started chanting Buddha's name, my mother suddenly exclaimed joyfully:

- How strange! Every time I chant Buddha's name, my pain gradually decreases; the more I chant, the less the pain ... I can feel it very clearly, my child!

In this way, my mother was delighted, gaining more motivation to diligently maintain her practice schedule without pause...

It wasn't until four months later that a real miracle happened to my mother: The back pains gradually decreased, noticeably lessened, and then completely disappeared. My mother's legs regained feeling, and she was able to stand and walk. Now, my mother can cook for the family herself and move around the house...

My entire family and the neighbors were moved to tears, everyone said it was truly a miracle. They didn't know it was the wondrous power of Buddhist teachings, so they kept asking my mother what medicine she took to get better. But I quietly felt grateful for the protection and blessings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who saved my mother from the brink of death.

Now every time I make a video call, seeing my mother walking around the house, my mouth smiles but tears keep flowing because I recall the months when she was sick. I feel so sorry and love her so much...

I often tease my mother:

- How can you walk so well, Mom?

She smiles brightly and says:

- Thanks to the blessings of Buddha, I was saved!

Perhaps many people still doubt, and then provide various scientific explanations, along with all sorts of arguments to refute it. It’s up to them, it’s just theories...

Perhaps they didn't realize it, but reality is truly the decisive answer. My mother's story of recovering from illness through chanting Buddha's name is a reality, and I hope that reality will help everyone deepen their faith in the miraculous ability of Buddhist practice to transform karma and heal diseases.

NAM MÔ BỔN SƯ THÍCH CA MÂU NI PHẬT!

NAM MÔ A DI ĐÀ PHẬT!

NAM MÔ ĐẠI BI QUÁN THẾ ÂM BỒ TÁT!

(Thien Nhu, rewritten from the account of Dieu Nghia)

tieu_de: ABSTAIN FROM LUSTFUL EVIL, GOOD LUCK OPENS THE DOOR
tom_tat: We should know that a factor that severely affects life is "lustful acts" because it affects vitality, vital energy... causes mental exhaustion, clouded mind, not to mention it will invite demons.
noi_dung:
AVOID EVIL LUST, GOOD LUCK OPENS THE DOOR

We should know that a factor that severely affects life is "lust" because it impacts vitality, energy... it weakens the mind, clouds the intellect, not to mention it will invite demons and continuous bad luck.

This year I am 27 years old. When I was in the 3rd grade in elementary school, through someone, I was introduced to sex films, and from that point, I bid farewell to the innocent soul of a child, increasingly sinking into the abyss of lust.

By the time I reached high school, I was increasingly exposed to sex tapes and discs, which caused my academic performance to deteriorate. When going through exams, perhaps due to the blessings of my ancestors and some luck, I was able to pass and get into university with relatively high scores.

At university, I began to obsessively pursue lust, to the extent that: studying, playing, eating, sleeping, exercising, even in my dreams... I couldn't separate from sexual desire. As a result, my mind was always dazed, sometimes wandering like a soulless shell.

Although my mind is intensely immersed in fornication, I am shy by nature, so I haven't had the opportunity to learn much about women to develop my

lustful nature.

In the second semester, I bought a computer, this is when I started to indulge in fornication, instead of entertaining and socializing with friends, I spent time hunting and downloading sexually stimulating black movies, nude photos... unhealthy and watched frequently, at this time I showed all my debauchery and showed immoral desires.

And of course, these dirty forms of entertainment have invisibly polluted the pure character that I originally had.

By the end of my second year of university, during the summer break, I still maintained the habit of masturbation (this habit is the root of all suffering), having to relieve myself every two days. Looking back now, that was the most extremely miserable and uncomfortable period of my past.

Once one has "masturbated," it is very easy to become indulgent and loose with oneself, making me increasingly addicted to pleasure, craving eating and drinking, sleeping a lot, having a foggy mind, being impulsive, and easily irritable... all of these things in turn cause us to continue drowning in the cycle of reincarnation, with no way to rise above it.

Throughout four years of university, I only studied to get by day by day, my mind was no longer clear, my academic performance was terrible and declining, it can be said that I failed. It can be seen that masturbation is like an addiction to drugs (but its consequences are even worse than drugs).

I graduated from university, but I still stayed at home living off others, still maintaining my indulgent habits, my spirit was always gloomy and declining, even though I was preparing to take the entrance exam to the Research Institute. In the end, I could not take the exam because I lacked the spirit. This result made my parents extremely sad and disappointed.

At the beginning of 2010, I was depressed and then self-reflecting, and started reading materials advising the cessation of sexual misconduct, began to understand a little about Buddhist teachings, and suddenly realized: The reason I encountered so much bad luck and my sufferings were all due to my lustful habits!

Immediately afterward, I studied and practiced Buddhism, repented, and vowed to practice decisively to abandon bad habits, break away from unhealthy cultures, and cultivate virtue.

Thanks to the blessings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, I gradually managed to abandon my bad habits.

Specifically, from August 2010 until now, except in dreams (because my practice power is not yet sufficient, so I still get haunted by lustful spirits), I gradually overcame myself and found tranquility. From that, I realized: the best remedy to completely give up sexual misconduct is Buddhism!

Since I decided to cultivate virtue and observe abstinence from sexual misconduct, after many days of practice, reforming my body and mind, I finally topped the list at an Advanced Research Institute and received a government scholarship. Later, I became even more firmly convinced when I realized that "Karma" does not deceive. I further understood and deeply felt what is called "Luck"; it does not fall from the sky, but entirely lies in our hands in this way: Eliminating sexual misconduct and cutting off evil while practicing goodness!

We should know that a factor that severely affects life is "lust" because it impacts vitality, energy... weakens the spirit, clouds the mind, not to mention it can attract evil spirits and continuous bad luck.

If you know how to abstain from lust, you will be a person full of energy, with a clear and flexible mind, and good fortune will continually come. During exam season, if you can control lust, the results will be much better.

This made me startled and I tried even harder to cultivate and preserve virtue, and then everything went smoothly, my career advanced, and my parents were pleased. This is all that I want to confess and share, hoping that you will spread it.

Looking back now, mainly everything was because I was too indulgent and reckless... it is indeed true: sexual misconduct swiftly and greatly depletes good fortune.

Excerpt from "Retribution in This Life 7”

Vietnamese translation: Hạnh Đoan

******************************

HOW TO EXTERMINATE THE LUSTFUL DEMON?

Relying on Buddha's power will bring liberation. The method is to recite the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra. Do not think that the spirit who absorbs essence will let you go. The spirit who absorbs essence can read your thoughts.

So it knows everything that goes on in your mind. As for your mouth, you may say you give it up, but if your heart still desires it, it will cling and disturb you relentlessly. If you think that giving up sexual misconduct for a few months or even a few years means it’s over, that’s not necessarily true; if anyone tries to tempt you, you might immediately fall into it without resisting. The Demon can read your thoughts and will find every way to seduce you into its trap. Therefore, IF you truly repent and NO LONGER FALL INTO IT, only then can the sin be eradicated. If your mouth says no but your intentions are unwholesome, remember that even having lustful thoughts is considered SEXUAL MISCONDUCT. All of these are serious sins, let alone if you seek out someone to satisfy your base desires.

Whether you believe it or not is up to you, but once you get entangled and cannot break free, life will always be in poverty, work will be stagnant, and you will always be scolded by your boss or oppressed at work. People have a foul odor, and others avoid them. Additionally, if one has excessive lewd desires, various illnesses such as insomnia, gout, kidney problems, urinary tract infections, etc., lead to an early death, and after death, one descends to hell to endure much suffering.

The solution is: Lock yourself in the same room as in a prison with 4 narrow walls, no Internet and only one lamp. Unless you eat and clean your body, sit and recite the Lingyan Mantra continuously. If you are tired, you can continue to recite it regardless of the time, and if you don't sleep, it will be 100% effective. Sitting there and complaining, there is no teacher who can save you but yourself. Otherwise, prepare to go to the underworld. The spirit demons have already sucked up all your vitality. Hurry up and do it this way.

No matter which method of practice you follow, sincerity is the most important. Do not think that merely reciting sutras is like giving answers to the Buddha while your mind and nature remain unchanged, full of greed, anger, and ignorance. Indulgence in sexual immorality and masturbation continues unabated. Drinking and womanizing are not abandoned. Demons are extremely clever. They observe if a person has desires; whatever someone wants, they will use suitable means to delude that person. We do not need to recite any special spells, nor do we need any specific method. As long as we are genuine, do not quarrel, are free from greed, do not crave, are unselfish, and practice diligently with renunciation, letting go of all attachments, no demon can harm you.

How to eliminate them?

Recite the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva many times!

From the Universal Gate Chapter of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva: "If there are beings with much lust, regularly respectfully reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will lead them to be free from lust. If there is much anger, regularly respectfully reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will lead them to be free from anger. If there is much ignorance, regularly respectfully reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will lead them to be free from ignorance."

As long as you have greed, pride, a desire to seize conveniences, or a wish to find shortcut paths to cultivation, you will easily get involved in demonic practices. Just a reminder, please don’t throw stones, thank you.

Source: ALISA

tieu_de: THE STORY OF USUALLY TURNING ON THE SCRIPTURE RECITATION MACHINE AT HOME, BEING FRAMED BY ENEMIES.
tom_tat: An elder said that in his house he often played the Dharma sermons, but he himself did not often listen. Later, a layperson came to the house and was able to have the sentient beings listen to the Dharma sermons.
noi_dung:
THE STORY USUALLY STARTS WITH RECITING SCRIPTURES AT HOME, THEN GETTING INTO CONFLICT WITH ENEMIES.

A monk said that in his house, he often plays the Dharma teachings on a machine, but he himself does not often listen. Later, a lay practitioner came to his house, was listened to by the sentient beings listening to the Dharma, and said:

I am a dog who was previously killed by you, I did evil in the past, so I fell into the animalistic path, but you are too despicable, I am alive and you take me out to beat me to death, even skinning, gutting, and pulling all my internal organs out; you keep thinking that I deserve to be eaten, but who do you deserve to be eaten by? Before I was about to die, there might have been a single bitter word, which was definitely to seek revenge. I waited many years, always looking for an opportunity.

🍁 You open the sutras in the Buddha hall, you are busy with this and that, and have no time to listen to the sutras, but we have all listened.

Now you do not clearly understand the principles, but we understand them clearly; you do not have enlightenment, but we have already attained enlightenment.

🙏 I no longer want to seek revenge, I must go to the Pure Land.

Now I have left your house, without saying these words, and you still do not know.

Today, taking this opportunity to speak everything out, I no longer hold resentment towards you ladies. Could you please chant Buddha's name to send me off?

In the end, they want us to be less busy with work, listen more to the Dharma Master's teachings, and chant Buddha's name more.

PS: TỊNH KHÔNG

-----------------------------------

The merit of giving the Dharma is greater by hundreds of billions of times compared to giving material wealth; only the Buddha-eye of the Tathagata can clearly see and fully understand it. If you want to transform your destiny without having money in hand, then give the Dharma....
