tieu_de: WHAT MERIT DOES AN ORDINARY PERSON GAIN BY CREATING BUDDHA IMAGES?
tom_tat: (Excerpt from the Sutra of Blessings for Creating Buddha Images) At that time, the Buddha went to the garden of the wealthy man Mỹ Âm in the country of Bất Tĩnh. The king of this country was named Xuất Ái, only 14 years old. Upon hearing
noi_dung:
WHAT MERIT DOES AN ORDINARY PERSON GAIN BY CREATING BUDDHA IMAGES?

(Excerpt from the Sutra on the Merit of Creating Buddha Images)

At that time, the Buddha went to the garden of the wealthy man Mỹ Âm in the country of Bất Tĩnh. The king of this country was named Xuất Ái and was only 14 years old. Upon hearing the news that the Buddha was approaching, the king immediately ordered his ministers and entourage to accompany him in welcoming the Buddha. When he saw the World-Honored One from afar, his heart was filled with immense joy. The king ordered the carriage to stop, then descended to walk on foot, not allowing the ministers, entourage, or those carrying parasols to accompany him.

The king immediately walked forward, then bowed his head and paid homage to the ground. After he finished paying homage, he stood up, then walked forward and repeated the same action three times.

The Buddha said:

"Great king, come here."

At that time, the king went in front of the Buddha, then bowed with his forehead touching the Buddha's feet, circled the Buddha three times, kneeled on both knees, joined his hands, and said to the Buddha:

"In the heavens and on the human world, no one can compare to the Buddha. The face and body of the Buddha today radiate splendid light. I gaze at the Buddha endlessly without ever feeling bored. The Buddha is the master of gods and humans. The Buddha's compassion spreads to all beings."

The Buddha remained silent and did not answer.

The king then respectfully said to the Buddha:

"O World-Honored One! Those who do good will surely gain merit, but where will it lead them? After the Buddha departs, I fear I will no longer see the Buddha. I wish to create an image of the Buddha to respectfully worship. Then what merit will I gain in the future? I sincerely hope that the Buddha will have compassion and teach me. I wish to know about this."

At that time, the Buddha said to the young king:

"The question you ask, O great king, is very good. Listen carefully to My words. After hearing, remember them in your heart."

The king immediately bowed his head and said:

"Yes, I will obey the Buddha's teachings."

The Buddha said to the king:

"I will now explain to Your Majesty the merits obtained by those who make statues of the Buddha."

The king replied:

"Yes, I thank You, O Lord."

❖

The Buddha said:

"If someone makes a statue of the Buddha, in their next life, they will have clear eyes, a proper appearance, and a body and limbs that are always beautiful and soft. Suppose they are reborn in heaven, their clear eyes and proper appearance will surpass those of the deities. It is precisely because they made a statue of the Buddha that they receive such merit."

If anyone makes a statue of the Buddha, in the next life, they will not encounter evil deeds; their body will be completely intact. After death, they will be reborn in the realm of Brahma. Moreover, their upright and unparalleled beauty will surpass that of other heavenly beings, and they will also be revered by the gods. It is because of making a statue of the Buddha that one receives such blessings.

If anyone makes a statue of the Buddha, in the next life, they will be born into a noble and influential family; their longevity and health will surpass that of ordinary people. Wherever they are born, they will not be born into a poor family. It is because of making a statue of the Buddha that one receives such blessings.

If anyone makes an image of the Buddha, in the next life, they will have a beautiful body with a gold-purple color and unmatched purity. They will always be respected and loved by everyone. It is only because they made an image of the Buddha that they receive such blessings.

If anyone makes an image of the Buddha, in the next life, they will be born into a wealthy family; their wealth and precious treasures will be immeasurable. They will always be loved by their parents, siblings, and respected by relatives. It is only because they made an image of the Buddha that they receive such blessings.

If someone makes an image of the Buddha, in the next life, they will often be born into the house of emperors, princes, or in a virtuous family in the region of Thắng Kim. It is because they made an image of the Buddha that they receive such merit.

If someone makes an image of the Buddha, in the next life, they will become an emperor. Among kings and rulers, they will be the most noble, respected, and honored by other sovereigns. It is because they made an image of the Buddha that they receive such merit.

If anyone makes a Buddha statue, then in the next life, they will become a Wheel-Turning King. All the rulers in the four continents and under heaven will revere them and become their followers. It is because they made a Buddha statue that they receive such merit.

If anyone makes a Buddha statue, then in the next life, they will become a Wheel-Turning King, able to ascend to heaven and return at will; everything they do will be accomplished completely. It is because they made a Buddha statue that they receive such merit.

If someone makes an image of the Buddha, in the next life, they will be reborn in the Brahma realm, live longer than a lifetime, possess supreme and unsurpassed wisdom that no one can match. It is because they made an image of the Buddha that they receive such merit.

After fully enjoying the merit in the Brahma realm, they will be reborn into a filial family that understands the Buddha's teachings. It is because they made an image of the Buddha that they receive such merit.

If anyone makes a Buddha statue, then in their next life, they will be loved and respected by their parents. After passing away, they will be reborn in heaven. It is because they created a Buddha statue that they receive such blessings.

If anyone makes a Buddha statue, then after death, they will never be reborn into an evil path. They will always know how to exercise self-restraint and their heart will always be oriented toward the Buddha's Way.

If anyone makes a statue of the Buddha, in future lives, they will respect the Scriptures. Their hearts will always wish to offer to the Buddha's stupa with many kinds of beautiful flowers, precious incense, colorful silk, lighting lamps, and the rarest treasures in the world. In countless lifetimes to come, they will attain the Buddha's Nirvana. Those who have the intention to offer marvelous treasures to the Buddha are not ordinary people; they are certainly those who have also made Buddha statues and practiced the Bodhisattva Path in previous lives. It is because they made Buddha statues that they receive such merit.

If anyone makes a statue of the Buddha, then in the next life, their merit will be inexhaustible, beyond description. Even if one could measure all the water in the rivers and seas throughout the four continents of the world, the merit obtained by making a Buddha statue would still be ten times greater than all that water in those four continents. In the next life, they will be respected and helped by others.

A person who makes a Buddha statue is comparable to someone with a solid, sturdy house; even if it rains, they have nothing to fear.

If anyone makes a statue of the Buddha, then after death, they will no longer be reborn in the evil realms, which include hell, hungry ghosts, and animal beings.

If anyone sees the statue of the Buddha, and with reverence, they put their hands together and take refuge in front of the Buddha's stupa, then for a hundred lifetimes to come, they will never be reborn in the realm of animals, hungry ghosts, or hell. After death, they will immediately be reborn in heaven. When their heavenly blessings are exhausted, they will be reborn in a wealthy and powerful human family, and the merit they receive cannot be described. Eventually, they will attain the Nirvana of the Buddha's Way.

❖

The Buddha said to King Sudhana:

"A person who does good deeds and creates an image of the Buddha will receive such blessings—it will certainly not be in vain."

At that time, King Sudhana used a verse to praise the Buddha, saying:

"The Buddha is the Great Sage

Who teaches the Dharma to all beings

In the kingdom of Bà Tĩnh

In the garden of Mĩ Âm

At that time, King Sudhana

Hands clasped, respectfully asking,

Hearing the true Sanskrit sounds,

Motionless, a hundred blessings are formed,

Whoever makes an image of the Buddha

What merit will they receive?

At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse, saying:

"Great king, please listen,

The field of merit is vast and limitless,

No one surpasses the virtue,

Through making an image of the Buddha.

Always born into a wealthy house

Respected and honored, with many treasures

Relatives often show reverence

Because of making Buddha statues

Generation after generation free from calamities

Always able to open the heavenly eye

Eyes beautiful, bright blue

Because of making Buddha statues

Parents feel joy

Full of love, never weary

Great majesty and virtue truly upright

Because of making the image of the Buddha

Shining brightly with a golden body

Beautiful like a lion statue

Beings feel joy upon seeing it

Because of making the image of the Buddha

Born in the precious land of Jambudvipa

From the lineage of kings

Often possessing the great nature of Brahma wisdom

Because of making the image of the Buddha

Not born at the borders

Not blind, not ugly

Six faculties always complete

Because of making a statue of the Buddha

When approaching the end of life

Knowing the deeds of past lives

Seeing the Buddha in front

When dying, not in pain

Because of making a statue of the Buddha

Or becoming a great emperor

Or a Wheel-Turning King

Ruler of the Four Continents of the world

Because he made the image of the Buddha

Or became the Năng Thiên Đế (Heavenly Emperor)

With divine power, possessing authority and virtue

King of the Thirty-Three Heavens

Because he made the image of the Buddha

Or rose beyond the realm of desire

Became the Great Heavenly King Mahādeva

All beings respectfully honor him

Because he made the image of the Buddha

Whoever carves or paints the image of the Buddha

One will receive such blessings

Even heaven and earth can measure

But that blessing cannot be measured

Therefore, offer to the Buddha

Incense and flowers, sprinkle scented water

Offer to the Great Sage

Ending all defilements and realizing the unconditioned

When the Buddha finished preaching this sutra, the king was extremely joyful, immediately stood up, and paid respects before the Buddha with his forehead touching the Buddha's feet. At that moment, the monks, nuns, male lay followers, female lay followers, along with 500 courtiers on the left and right, all felt joy and paid respects to the Buddha. At the time of their passing, they all were reborn in the land of the Buddha Amitayus and became the foremost great Bodhisattvas. Upon hearing the Buddha's teachings, King Xuất Ái was very happy, received, embraced, and understood them, and immediately attained the Fruit of Stream-entry.

Collected by: Ngộ Quang Từ

tieu_de: SEVEN CASES WHERE ONE SHOULD NOT KILL
tom_tat: (TEACHINGS OF MASTER LIEN TRI) 1. Birth date should not involve killing:
noi_dung:
SEVEN CASES WHERE ONE SHOULD NOT KILL

(TEACHINGS OF MASTER LIEN TRI)

1. Do not kill on the day of birth:

Parents suffer greatly to give birth to us. The day we are born is the day our mother gradually dies. Therefore, one must absolutely avoid killing, practice vegetarianism, do many good deeds, and pray for the increase of parents' blessings and longevity. How can one forget the hardships of parents and have the heart to kill living beings?

2. Do not kill when giving birth to children:

Not having children surely causes worry, while having children brings great joy. Why not consider this: even animals know how to love their offspring, so why does giving birth to our children result in the death of others' children? Can one be at peace with that? Alas, a newborn child, if not encouraged to accumulate virtue, it is fine, but now it also takes lives and harms beings, adding more sins. Isn't this extremely foolish?

3. Offerings for death anniversaries should not involve killing living beings:

When offering a memorial or visiting the grave of the deceased during the spring and autumn festivals, it is advised to avoid killing animals, in order to accumulate merit and virtue. Nature already provides eight types of precious foods for offerings, so how could one dig up bones from the underground realm to eat? Killing to make offerings is a great act of unfilialness!

4. Weddings must not involve killing animals:

Marriage in this world, if it follows all the proper rituals, results in becoming husband and wife; it does not depend on killing living beings. When establishing a family, one already begins to think about having children. Committing acts of killing before having children is truly paradoxical. Thus, celebrating a good occasion while performing violent acts and killing living beings—isn't that very foolish?

5. Do not kill living beings when entertaining guests:

On a beautiful day, in a lovely setting, the kind host treats guests with vegetables, rice, fruits, and tea, without hesitation, in the Buddhist environment. Why then destroy life, indulge in extreme richness and sweetness, reveling in cups and bowls, killing so many innocent beings right on the dining table? Alas! Those with a compassionate heart, seeing this, are not very saddened?

6. Praying for peace should not involve killing living beings:

People have the habit of killing animals to offer to gods, hoping for their blessing. They do not realize that: they are making offerings to gods to avoid death and seek life, but they kill other lives in hopes that their own life will be long, which is truly paradoxical, cruel, and vicious.

7. In commerce and livelihood, one must not kill living beings:

All humans must secure food and clothing. Either they have to hunt, or catch fish, gather shrimp, or slaughter buffalo, cows, pigs, dogs… all just for a living. But on reflection, those who do not engage in these occupations still have food and clothing; does that mean they starve or freeze to death? Engaging in killing will inevitably lead to the retribution of being killed in the future. Why not change your profession, choosing a gentler way of making a living—wouldn't that be better?

Buddhist practitioners must always keep these seven things in mind as a guiding principle in daily life! …

Those who keep precepts and do not kill are protected by benevolent spirits, their disasters are eliminated, their lifespan is long, their children and grandchildren are filial and virtuous, and everything is fortunate and good. If one devotes efforts to releasing living beings and also concentrates on reciting the Buddha's name, they will certainly be reborn as wished, forever free from the cycle of reincarnation, and advance to an unshakable state.

------------------------------------------

CULTIVATE VIRTUE - A METHOD TO CHANGE FATE. THOSE WHO HAVE PRACTICED BUDDHISM FOR MANY YEARS BUT HAVE NOT SEEN RESPONSES OR THINGS NOT GOING AS WISHED, PLEASE READ CAREFULLY AND REFLECT

(Excerpt from the Teachings of Master Yin Guang)

1. Filial piety towards parents

The body, hair, and skin are received from the parents. Parents and I are truly one entity. If you love your own body, be filial to your parents; not dishonoring your body is how you bring honor to your parents.

2. Harmony and love among siblings

Brothers and sisters, flesh and blood, closely connected, joy and suffering together; elder siblings love, younger siblings respect, in harmony, happily, supporting and loving each other, the family will be blessed!

3. Respect teachers

The teacher is strict, moral, and sets an example of ethics and knowledge, surely to be followed, taking that as a model. The teacher nurtures us, teaches us the basics, guides us as an example; if we do not respect the teacher, how can it be beneficial?

4. Choosing friends

Near cinnabar, it turns red; near ink, it inevitably turns black. When making friends, some harm us, some bring benefit. For benefit, stay close; for harm, stay away. Advising good and correcting faults all depend on this!

5. Cloth clothes

Clothing covers the body and protects against the cold. Wear coarse fabric garments, cherish virtue, cultivate humility. Do not crave ironing, brocade embroidery, or ornate designs. Fortune and longevity are depleted, one abandons oneself, one rejects oneself.

6. Vegetarian Diet

Eat vegetarian food in a nutritious way. Eating meat harms living beings. The mind resents when they are killed, making the meat's toxicity unbearable. Refrain from craving meat, whenever eaten, it must be repaid, until the time of repayment, how truly pitiable it is!

7. Cherishing Characters

Words are the most precious; gold and jewels cannot compare. People are intelligent because of words; without them, they will be ignorant. If the world had no words, nothing could be accomplished, and humans and animals would differ only in name!

8. Cherishing grain

Grains in the fields are used to feed the people. Knowing how to cherish and take care of grains is the embodiment of a kind heart. Those who practice goodness will keep it, while the wicked will surely lose it. Cherishing grains brings blessings, while wastage leads to misfortune.

9. Cherishing time

Seventy years are rare in the past and present; snap your fingers and they are gone. Once they pass, they are no more, so how could one dare to be lazy? Strive to study diligently, establish virtue as well as career, benefit oneself and others, and set an example for life.

10. Righteousness (value morality)

In every action and movement, focus only on righteousness; whenever righteousness exists, nothing is not beneficial. The petty person sees profit and immediately forgets morality. Although gaining small benefits, in the end, they suffer loss!

11. Integrity

Blessings in a person's life come from the cultivation in previous lives. Taking what is unjust is like consuming poison. Being pure without contamination and honest without greed will be revered in life; nothing surpasses this glory!

12. Knowing Shame

A single word, shame, brings immense benefit; whenever there is a feeling of shame, one is close to the sages. Without it, one is no different from a beast! Maintaining a sense of shame makes anything controllable. The Buddha's teachings, adorned, are supreme.

13. Utmost Loyalty

Steadfastly sincere, never deceitful, honoring parents, treating others properly, never having a divided heart. Only wishing to fulfill one's duties completely, not worrying about whether others notice or not. A person like this is a model for the world.

14. Keeping promises (faithfulness)

A person who keeps their word does not speak carelessly, and immediately acts on what they say, without boasting or showing off. A person lacking faithfulness fakes everything, is abandoned by others, and is not even comparable to an ox or a horse!

15. Benevolence

Compassion and kindness, the goodness of the heart. The more sincere the heart, the deeper the blessings. If this heart is lacking, it becomes cruel and harsh. Even with inherited blessings, when they are depleted, danger will arise.

16. Do not kill living beings

All living creatures have consciousness, crave life, fear death, and value their existence. If one playfully kills or kills for food, in this life or the next, there will definitely be retribution.

17. Do not steal

Do not steal what belongs to others. Stealing small things buries one's virtue, stealing big things brings great disaster. Taking others' property diminishes your own fortune; seeking convenience this way leads to great loss!

18. No sexual misconduct

Lust is harmful, harms the body, and buries the will. Even as husband and wife, self-restraint is necessary. Continual sexual misconduct is greatly unreasonable. From ancient times until now, people of ambition have never violated this!

19. Do not lie

Words express virtue, narrate the true mind. If the mind is not sincere, how can virtue be correct? I hope you children, do not lie. If the mouth is correct but the mind is wrong, it amounts to nothing!

20. Do not smoke

Do not smoke any kind of substance, because it is unhygienic and illegal. The mouth often has a bad odor, and the smoke annoys others. Opium, fragrant cigarettes, are the strongest poisons. Spending money to harm yourself makes the foolish truly pitiful!

21. Do not drink alcohol

Alcohol is a drug that causes madness; drinking it inevitably leads to disorderly behavior, drunkenness against reason, surpassing manners, and violating duties. It is best not to drink, to avoid excessive drinking! Intelligent and wise people often keep themselves pure.

22. No gambling

Gambling includes all kinds, even Chinese chess. It is cowardly and a waste of time. If you focus on it, you abandon proper matters. You spend your limited energy on childish games. It ruins homes, wastes assets, and the sin never rests!

23. Do not be extravagant

Luxurious display invites misfortune and poverty. A gentleman does not pay attention to it, while thieves come to seize. Wearing simple clothes and eating vegetables is the way of sages. In this life and the next, everyone follows the example.

24. Do not be arrogant

An arrogant person despises others, actually exposing their own flaws, which wise people can clearly see; such a person's knowledge and cultivation are limited. Even a saint does not look down on others. They always keep in mind: "There is no absolute saint – all are ordinary."

25. Do not be jealous

People with virtue and talent, we should praise. That person will surely contribute to society. If one is born with jealousy and criticizes, it is foolish; karma from past lives takes away the roots of wisdom.

26. Do not be biased

People with little wisdom, who have not heard the great way, often insist that their own ideas are the best. Looking at the sky from the bottom of a well, the perspective is tiny. If one climbs a high mountain, one will clearly understand the previous view.

27. Do not get angry

There are those wealthy in riches but narrow in heart, who often get furious when things go against them. Anger is useless, it brings distress to ourselves and others, generosity and tolerance are priceless treasures.

28. Do not be shy to ask

Ask about things that are normally unaskable, inquire often about what you lack, hoping others will indulge you—you must humble yourself first. If you are ignorant, you should ask others even more, learn broadly, ask thoroughly, true competence.

(ENLIGHTENING WORDS COLLECTED)

tieu_de: PAINFUL RETRIBUTION, FALLING INTO THE HELL OF 4 MOTHER AND CHILD ENGAGED IN 'PROSTITUTION'.
tom_tat: As a rule of life, when the socio-economic development is rapidly advancing, spiritual values seriously decline. People in today's era are becoming increasingly depraved, increasingly creating
noi_dung:
PAINFUL AND EXTREME RETRIBUTION, BEING SENT TO HELL BY A MOTHER AND HER 4 CHILDREN WHO PRACTICE "PROSTITUTION".

As a rule of life, when the socio-economic situation develops rapidly, spiritual values seriously decline.

People of today are increasingly depraved, increasingly doing evil, with no evil they dare not commit. And according to the law of cause and effect, committing evil results in receiving evil consequences, which is inevitable.

On that day, Lien Hoa Monastery (Tan Uyen, Binh Duong) also had visitors, all of whom were people facing spiritual problems seeking help from Zen Master An Lac Hanh.

When it comes to the Grandmaster, everyone is immensely respectful, because of his compassion and virtue along with special abilities, so his good reputation spreads far, and many people travel from all over to seek the Grandmaster's help.

Sitting inside the guest house and looking out at the yard, the sunlight had softened in the late afternoon. Two women hurried in to present their circumstances. The younger woman wore a navy blue sun-protective jacket with a few yellow patterns. Her face was dark and harsh, perhaps from exposure to wind and sun, and her hair was neatly tied back.

She gently and humbly picked a chair from the long row of wooden seats, right near the monk to easily ask questions. The other woman was a nun, small in stature, with a serene and calm face.

Ms. Thanh Binh recounted the event:

After inquiring, it was found out that she was actually the mother-in-law of the young girl, formerly called Ba Coc, a Buddhist of Hoang Phap Pagoda in Ho Chi Minh City, who had just become a nun less than a year ago at Thuong Chieu Monastery, Phuoc Thai Commune, Long Thanh District, Dong Nai. She was the one who guided her daughter-in-law to seek help from the monk.

Usually, the people who come here rarely smile; everyone has a look of sorrow, melancholy, and despair. It's understandable, otherwise, people wouldn't come to see the monk. Most beings nowadays only seek refuge in the temple when their suffering becomes unbearable. It's true that they only jump when the water reaches their feet. How truly sad!

Seeing the timid and hesitant appearance of the mother and child, the monk spoke gently and compassionately, asking about their specific circumstances. It had been a long time since the monk last treated anyone, but now with these two coming to ask, he still attended to see if they fell under the category for consideration and assistance. For now, being old and weak, this body-machine, according to the law of impermanence, would eventually reach a point where the oil dries up and it can no longer run smoothly.

Mrs. Cóc's family lives on Nguyễn Hữu Hào Street, Ward 6, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City. Her daughter-in-law, Nguyễn Thị Thanh Bình, also has some affinity with Buddhist teachings, so she took refuge at Linh Quang Monastery on Nguyễn Khoái Street, District 4, with the dharma name Diệu Chung. The reason the two of them came here today is that for the past year, Ms. Bình has suffered from insomnia, and at night she often sits talking to herself in a very strange way.

Her family thought she was suffering from paranoid mental illness, so they took her to the Ho Chi Minh City Tropical Disease Hospital for examination. The doctors there concluded that she was depressed and prescribed medication, which she has been taking for a while.

Although she continued to follow the doctor's treatment, Ms. Bình insisted that she was not depressed, and because she often had spontaneous shivers, she vaguely suspected that she had been possessed by a spirit. Unable to let this situation continue any longer, mother and daughter immediately hurried down to Bình Dương to visit the Liên Hoa Monastery right after being discharged from the hospital.

Seemingly realizing the problem, to not waste much time, the monk did not ask any further questions and immediately spoke to the spirit with his familiar warm, compassionate tone: “If any suffering soul wishes to be saved, just borrow this voice to speak, and I will save them, but if a living person asks me, I will not save them.”

As soon as the monk finished speaking, in an instant, Ms. Binh's expression immediately changed; her face suddenly contorted, her mouth twisted to one side, and she stammered a few words without forming proper sounds. Indeed, a spirit had entered Ms. Binh's body to speak with the monk.

She thought it was some vengeful spirit causing trouble and resentment towards Miss Bình, but it turns out it was no stranger at all. The spirit revealed her name was Huỳnh Thị Phụng, who died on the 2nd of October in the year of Kỷ Mão, and she is actually Miss Bình's biological mother. The spirit had possessed her body many times over the past period, only hoping to be helped because of her immense suffering.

Mrs. Phung has many children, but only Miss Binh is the most filial, so she only hopes to rely on this daughter to help her. After hearing Mrs. Phung's spirit say this, the master looked over at Mrs. Coc (that is, Mrs. Phung's co-relative by marriage) to verify whether Binh's biological mother was indeed named that. Mrs. Coc nodded repeatedly in agreement.

The spirit of Mrs. Phụng continued to speak with a look full of remorse and pain, recalling a period of her past. She recounted that several decades ago, her parents-in-law (that is, Mr. and Mrs. Bình's grandparents) built a private temple on the family's land, naming it Quốc Ân Temple. Later, her parents-in-law passed away one after another, and her husband also passed away, leaving the temple to her along with seven small, helpless children. The sky seemed to collapse before the eyes of this frail woman. Life's hardships weighed heavily on the mother's shoulders, and seeing her little children waiting for each meal, Mrs. Phụng could not feel at ease.

Not knowing what to do to live and support seven children, Mrs. Phung suddenly came up with the idea of turning her husband's family's private temple into a place to rent rooms for couples to use for prostitution. Each time she let them rent the place, she earned 20-30 thousand dong, which at that time was quite a lot, not a small amount at all.

Every day, about 5-10 people rent, so each day she also has some money coming in for her children to have a warm meal. Who would have thought that from here, her life and that of her children would begin to become extremely miserable. This work was not wholesome to begin with, and it was carried out right within the premises of Quoc An Tu Pagoda, a place where Buddha is sincerely worshiped. These circumstances caused Ms. Phung to suffer severe and terrible consequences that she herself created.

Quoc An Tu Temple was a private temple, not affiliated with the Buddhist Church, so later it was cleared to build other constructions. The house is no longer there, and the people have left, but does that mean everything has ended? No!

Mrs. Phung left without being able to take anything with her, except that karma constantly clung to her like a shadow that couldn’t be dispelled. Perhaps in the past she was also deluded and ignorant, unable to fully understand the evil deeds she was creating, thinking only that it was a way to make a living for her children, but little did she know that those actions would cause severe and harmful consequences. With eyes full of fear, the spirit of Mrs. Phung continued to speak.

It is indeed immediate cause and effect, because she assisted men and women in engaging in prostitution, later, Mrs. Phụng developed cervical cancer and had to undergo multiple radiation treatments, enduring agonizing pains day and night without end. Already facing difficulties, now with illness added, truly the house that was poor is now even more burdened, suffering beyond words. Thought it would be just that? But it is really not simple, because her sin is by no means light, allowing people to commit wrongdoing right within the temple grounds is a tremendous crime, an extremely severe crime, defiling the temple, a place that should require purity and reverence.

Periodically, Mrs. Phung would go to the Oncology Hospital. That day was also her next scheduled radiation treatment, and it was on that very day that she suddenly suffered a stroke due to a ruptured brain blood vessel. Her mouth twisted to one side, her eyes still wide open, and she passed away immediately, at the age of 55, without having time to leave any last words.

Everything seemed to end when a person left this world, but no, she went down to the underworld and still had to bear the consequences of her actions. She recounted that when she first arrived there, she saw the whole space shrouded in complete darkness, with flickering red lights appearing and disappearing intermittently, making anyone shiver with fear. Then she was led in front of the palace, where King Yama clearly outlined her crimes without any errors or omissions, so that Ms. Phung could fully understand her wrongdoings, and then decreed to send her to hell to suffer punishment, being imprisoned and beaten, without food or water.

Extremely miserable, Mrs. Phung groaned and sobbed for each word, begging the monk to help her; she was full of regret. When Mrs. Phung died, although her family invited a monk to chant sutras, offered alms to the monks, doing everything completely, it still was not enough to compensate for her evil deeds.

Those things are indeed very good deeds that descendants can do to help the deceased's soul accumulate more merit and attain liberation sooner, but the main matter still lies in the merits and sins of the deceased. Otherwise, it would be simple and no one would have to descend into hell or ascend to heaven.

Feeling pity for the spirit of Mrs. Phụng who sincerely admitted her mistakes and knew how to repent and be remorseful, the monk advised Mrs. Phụng to first immediately perform 108 bows of repentance, but afterward, she had to bow 1,000 times each day to atone for her sins. The spirit of Mrs. Phụng did not hesitate at all and immediately carried it out, because that was the only lifeline she could grasp at that moment, otherwise, she would only descend into hell to continue being tortured until her bones were shattered and her flesh torn, with no knowing when she could ever be released.

The venerable monk emphasized that only spirits who truly know how to repent can he use his own merit from practice to bless so they can be freed from suffering, giving them the opportunity to turn towards good deeds and resolutely practice with refuge in the Three Jewels. It is the same for living people; one should regularly repent for their own sins, and repent to their wronged enemies and creditors, because sentient beings have been drifting in the cycle of birth and death since time without beginning, having committed countless sins, with countless wronged enemies and creditors. Therefore, repentance is a very necessary practice to undertake.

At this moment, the spirit of Mrs. Phung directed herself towards the Triple Gem, clasped her hands sincerely, and vowed to follow the guidance of the venerable monk: “I have committed sins, and now I pledge to cultivate and practice according to the Buddha from this day forward. I dare not commit wrongdoings anymore. I pray for the blessings above to witness this, and whatever merit I cultivate will be dedicated to all sentient beings so that they may also attain enlightenment through practicing Buddhism and achieve liberation. Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva Mahasattva.”

The venerable monk then also devoted himself to praying further for the spirits so that they could quickly be freed from the sufferings of hell. Of course, not everyone has the ability to help Mrs. Phung as effectively and quickly; this is thanks to the profound merit and practice accumulated by the monk over many past lives. As for ordinary people, to save their relatives from hell, they need to persist in chanting sutras and mantras, performing many great acts of virtue and dedicating the merit to their relatives so that they can be freed. Moreover, although Mrs. Phung did wrong, it is also due to certain blessings she had accumulated in her previous lives that she now has the good fortune to have a favorable connection with Zen master An Lac Hanh.

When Mrs. Phụng was alive, she engaged in immoral activities and probably never imagined that because of her, the lives of her three daughters would also become shattered and bitter. Growing up in such a family environment, all three daughters learned to work as prostitutes to make money. Later, they got involved with heroin and drugs, contracted HIV, and died tragically. Only Bình managed to overcome the circumstances and avoid the path of sin, and now she is sitting here to help her mother and sisters escape suffering.

Having rescued her birth mother from suffering in the underworld, Miss Binh could not contain her heart and pleaded with the monk to have mercy and save her three sisters who were also suffering greatly. Miss Binh knew this because during her sister Nguyen Ngoc Minh’s memorial ceremony, the family offered alms to monks for her, and Minh’s spirit possessed someone and asked for help for herself and her two younger sisters, Hong and Loan.

Once again, Bình clasped her hands, waiting for her sister's spirit to come and borrow her body. After a while, Bình shivered, suddenly smiled absentmindedly, then suddenly burst into tears, her face contorted. Everyone knew that Minh had come, borrowing her sister's mouth, Minh revealed about her own life.

Father passed away, leaving seven poor siblings with no one to rely on. Feeling pity for her siblings' hardships and suffering, Minh saw that people who worked as prostitutes earned money. So at the age of 16, Minh followed that path, earning money to help support her family. Not only that, Minh also became a mistress, taking someone else's husband and destroying their happiness, causing their family to fall apart.

It is because of this crime that now Minh's soul must descend into hell to endure severe punishment, hugging a molten bronze pillar. The pillar is so large that she cannot embrace it entirely, and the intense heat is horrifyingly painful. While hugging it, she is repeatedly whipped from behind in excruciating pain, beyond what words can describe.

All the blessings and misfortunes of sentient beings are recorded and are governed by the law of cause and effect, precisely down to the smallest detail, without the slightest error, not even as small as a hair. Sister Minh, out of a desire to help her family in difficult circumstances, sacrificed herself and allowed her body to become defiled. Born from that heartfelt intention, her sin was also mitigated; otherwise, after finishing the punishment of embracing the hot copper pillar, she would still have to go to other hells to endure other terrible tortures.

The law of cause and effect is very flexible; creating karma requires facing its consequences, but if the actions are done to help family members, the karma is mitigated, and occasionally one is allowed to return to the living world to help loved ones find a way to save them. And today, her relatives have found a way to rescue her, which is not something everyone can receive. Next, the spirits of her other two daughters, Hồng and Loan, were also rescued in a similar manner.

Too many consequences, and each one is extremely tragic. If Madam Phung had known such an outcome, perhaps 20 years ago, she would not have dared to rent out the room like that. It is truly heartbreaking for her family and children.

The monk sighed, and spoke words full of meaningful advice to people:

"Relatives, see this, no matter how difficult life is, try hard to choose an honest profession, do not, because it is too hard, choose this immoral profession, or in the end, would there not be suffering?”

After receiving guidance from the monk on repentance, making a vow to abandon and not dare to commit sins, and dedicating effort to chanting and prayers to help, both the soul of Mrs. Phung and her three daughters were able to escape hell, return to the mortal world, and reside at Lien Hoa Monastery, vowing from now on to practice goodness and rely on the Triple Gem for cultivation. The monk also reminded them not to follow Ms. Binh anymore, so that she could remain healthy to focus on her work.

Zen master An Lac Hanh is like an old father sending a message to his foolish, naive children; his compassion moves everyone. Binh woke up, and at this moment suddenly felt relieved, peaceful, and light, as if she had just fulfilled her duty as a filial child to her mother and helped her sisters escape from the dark night.

Filial piety is not just about taking care of your parents' living conditions, meals, and clothing, or bringing them everyday worldly joys. Those are merely impermanent things that are not lasting. The most filial child is one who can help their parents form a good connection with the Buddha's teachings, helping them find the path of light that leads out of the dark ignorance of the cycle of birth and death. That is true filial piety.

Currently, Zen Master An Lac Hanh no longer accepts cases of spiritual healing, because the Zen master is advanced in age and partially weakened, but more importantly, because he no longer wishes to interfere with people's karma in this period.

(Tinh Nhu - recounted from real events at Lien Hoa Monastery, Binh Duong - Stories about Zen Master An Lac Hanh).

-----------------------

Commentary: Actions that violate the precepts of the Buddha all create karma; actions that benefit oneself while harming others will inevitably bear consequences, even if only to the smallest hair or feather. The teachings of the Buddha in the Kṣitigarbha Sutra are not false. When your faith is not yet deep, you may think that hell might not exist, or that if you do not follow Buddhism, you will not go to hell. But in reality, whether you believe it or not, hell still exists. No matter which country you are in or which race you belong to, as long as one creates karma, one inevitably falls into hell. However, if we believe in cause and effect and trust the teachings of the World-Honored One, then we understand and know.It is clear. Therefore, nowadays, hastening in practice to be reborn in the Pure Land is the most important thing. Practice lies in the virtue of the heart, not in outward appearances. When doing something, whatever intention arises in your heart will be the result you receive. Cultivating the right mindset means having a humble heart, a patient heart, enduring, a heart that is not selfish, does not compete, does not crave, does not seek personal gain... if you always maintain this mindset, the blessings that come later will be supreme. Otherwise, even if you perform good deeds, the resulting merits will only cause you to sink deeper into endless cycles of rebirth in the future. Therefore, nowadays, I advise you all to urgently devote yourselves to practicing the Pure Land method, this is the Dharma.the most superior discipline of this era, additionally, one should frequently recite the Great Compassion Mantra for personal protection because starting from 2024, karmic consequences will manifest very strongly. As you can see from the news, in 2023, many officials, whether currently in office or retired, were prosecuted for corruption or wrongdoing, many companies went bankrupt, many people became unemployed, countless people died suddenly or died unexpectedly, and some prophets even predicted upcoming epidemics, natural disasters, and wars....whether to believe it or not depends on your own merits, I hope you accept this with joy(Compassionate Light)

Whisper:

(I have been searching for articles sharing experiences about chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra in order to translate them for readers. But on foreign and domestic websites, sometimes the posts do not mention the author's name, or the author prefers to remain anonymous. Occasionally, I had to painstakingly search through dozens of websites to trace the author's name (because when posting translations, I always want to clearly credit the translator to confirm authenticity and show gratitude for the work). Therefore, when some articles do not have the author's name, I hope you understand and sympathize.)

Because I want readers to soon have new articles to read, thereby increasing their faith and gaining benefits, I uploaded the translation immediately after finishing it.

To avoid distracting those practicing other methods, this series of translations is only intended for those who specifically recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra and use it as a reference.

Now, I invite you to view this translation as a gift from me):

THE KING LĂNG NGHIÊM MANTRA'S MIRACULOUS RESPONSE

Translated by Hạnh Đoan

I have been chanting the Lingyan Mantra for nine months now and have gained a lot of benefits. Following the request of friends, I am writing down these experiences, hoping they will bring benefits to many sentient beings who are karmically connected.

Around July of last year, both my body and mind were in extremely poor condition. I felt as if I was about to die. I was helpless to escape this situation, yet I still tried to cook, go shopping, and clean the house, feeling very difficult to endure.

I am the administrator of a website that copies scriptures from the Internet, and I have a fellow practitioner friend named Tâm Đăng. At that time, she was copying the Lăng Nghiêm Sutra, also beginning to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and experienced very good spiritual responses. This means her life changed very quickly both physically and mentally, so she happily shared it with me. I listened and felt interested, so I said: Then I will recite it too! Tâm Đăng sent me the text of the mantra and a video so I could practice reciting it.

At first, I chanted a mantra for 20 minutes. On the first day of chanting, I didn’t feel anything after finishing. Life continued as usual, but at night while sleeping, I dreamed of a little girl bringing water to help me bathe and wash my hair. The waste water was dirty, black, with a murky red color, foamy, unimaginably filthy.

The next morning, I felt my head was very light, my thinking clear, a very good feeling, at least my head felt very comfortable. Previously, I often suffered from dizziness and headaches, unbearable as if wearing a yoke.

I thought: Oh! How magical, I didn't take any medicine, didn't do anything, just read the Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, and yet it was so wonderful?

After that, I continued chanting, spending 20 minutes a day, finishing one round of chanting, and chanting didn't slow down my gaming and chatting (at that time I really liked playing the game Ma Thiên Đại Lâu).

I continued reciting like that for three consecutive days, once a day. And every night, I dreamed of bathing, washing my hair, doing laundry, and similar activities, generally related to washing… then every morning when I woke up, I found that some uncomfortable sensations in my body had disappeared.

For example, I felt a gradually increasing sense of relief, such as on the first day, my head felt light. On the second day: below the knees. On the third day: from the knees to the waist, and on the fourth day: from the waist to the neck… all were comfortable. Thus, after four days, the uncomfortable sensations in my body completely vanished.

You can't imagine my joyous surprise at that moment, it was beyond imagination, because it was extraordinarily miraculous; before, I felt as if I were about to die, yet now I had been brought back to life! So, what reason would there be not to read the Lăng Nghiêm mantra? I will continue reading. In this way, first the Lăng Nghiêm mantra helped me resolve physical pain. Next, it began to help me deal with the suffering in my mind.

At that time, I always believed in the 2012 apocalypse rumors and even believed that I would die on December 26th. It was ridiculous to say this, but this was the way I thought at the time, and I believe that because I saw a strange dream, I always thought in my heart that the end was coming, and my mind was very miserable.

When I recite the Ling Yan mantra and recite it every day, the thoughts of boredom and fear gradually disappeared, and thinking back on it, I even find it funny, secretly asking why I can be so stupid?

Since then, I have become increasingly confident and full of vitality. While everyone was panicking about the doomsday theory, I remained very calm and even told people on the Internet: This cannot happen!

I have a strong and peaceful mindset, all thanks to The Śūraṅgama Mantra.

After that, I continued chanting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and my life improved further. I chanted every day from once to twice, three times, five times, seven times, and ten times. Since my work is relatively light, I have chanted up to 60 times at the office. I became addicted to chanting and found it very easy, smooth, and comfortable.

It's not that I am diligent! It's because my heart is full of afflictions. Precisely because there are so many afflictions, I am compelled to be diligent, waking up early every day to recite the Lankavatara Mantra. If I wake up early to recite the Lankavatara Mantra, everything goes extremely smoothly that day. But if I am lazy and don't wake up early to recite it each morning, then my mind is filled with countless, countless distracting thoughts, all negative, afflicted, dark, causing me to collapse! For example, if I harbor hatred or affection for someone, dissatisfaction or annoyance toward someone, or long for a boyfriend (which I cannot live with, for instance, because I am single), even though I know those thoughtsI thought this wouldn't help me in my current life, but I couldn't control them; the thoughts in my head kept arising chaotically, hard to restrain, so I would rather recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra to stabilize my mind and find peace.

Because I fear being surrounded by vexations, if I do not chant in the morning, I have to make up for it at noon that day. When vexations arise all at once, I persist in chanting the mantra. Although while chanting I feel nothing, after finishing, I realize the miraculous thing: All negative thoughts have disappeared, without any advice or suppression, without doing anything, they vanish on their own, making me laugh at myself: How could such foolish, silly thoughts even arise?

Storms and tempests are nothing compared to the torment of the mind! It is precisely the torment that has helped me. It forced me to quickly recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. If I didn't recite it, distress would arise, but if I recite it, I feel very happy, and that is exactly the case for me.

Moreover, at night I often had nightmares. Previously, I had no way to escape them. Now I know how to recite the mantra. At that time, because I hadn't memorized it yet, I could only read: Nam Mô Lăng Nghiêm Hội Thượng Phật Bồ Tát, Nam Mô Lăng Nghiêm Hội Thương Phật Bồ Tát! I kept repeating it over and over, and as long as I focused wholeheartedly, the nightmares would disappear; it is incredibly miraculous.

Later, I chanted more and more fluently, chanting as much as I had memorized, and whenever I did not reach the end, I would start chanting from the beginning. Before sleeping, while riding my bicycle on the road, whenever a bad thought arose, I would quickly chant whatever I had memorized, and it was very effective.

I really cannot stay away from Master Lăng Nghiêm, especially since I am a person with heavy afflictions. According to Buddhism, it is called deep karmic obstruction. I have very bad habitual tendencies, often generating many discouraging and negative thoughts. Although I know this is wrong, I cannot control it. Yet, the Lăng Nghiêm mantra has helped me overcome it, skillfully freeing me from afflictions.

In this way, I had no intention of memorizing the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, but because I chanted it so much, after three months, I naturally memorized the Lăng Nghiêm mantra! Being able to do so made things even more convenient. On the way to work and back home, since I had memorized the mantra, I set a rule for myself to chant it at least ten times a day; if I didn’t finish today, I definitely had to make up for it tomorrow.

During the process of chanting the mantra, hidden negative thoughts in the mind will emerge, such as: sadness, complaints, impatience, dissatisfaction, hatred toward others, (even resentment toward parents, siblings, or children), meaning a mind that often sees everything as not good in people, etc... These bad thoughts, even though they arise violently like rolling waves and the surges of suffering constantly rush as if to drown me, causing my mind to be painfully bitter and tears to flow uncontrollably! Yet I resolutely do not give up chanting the mantra. Because the Lankavatara Mantra is like a life-saving float, no matter how many disturbances arise, I still persist in chanting the Lankavatara Mantra.

Then I realized that: The troubles in life are entirely caused by the evil thoughts in my own heart. Mantra Lang Nghiem helped my mind become clear, allowing me to discover my own bad habits and faults. When I recognized the wrongness and faults within myself, I determined to reform, and I corrected my body and mind by reciting Mantra Lang Nghiem's incantation. As a result, the evil thoughts gradually decreased. This process may sound simple, but getting through it was truly difficult, and I always needed to practice and repair myself. Because in order to progress on the path from suffering to happiness, it is necessary to change oneself in a positive direction.

I am happy that I have encountered Buddhism and fortunate to have met Venerable Lăng Nghiêm. Otherwise, I wouldn't even know where my afflictions come from. Even if I know that my afflictions arise from the mind, I still feel powerless to escape them. I am truly lucky! Thanks to Venerable Lăng Nghiêm, I can experience happiness!

Then I participated in charity work and had to make CDs for Buddhist meeting recordings, so I no longer had time to browse the web, read the news, or watch videos; all personal activities were canceled because I was too busy. Therefore, I reduced the number of times I chanted to dedicate all my time to work, and I thought I didn't need to chant anymore. Although I reduced the number of times I chanted, I could still recite it on the way to and from work.

Then I felt unwell and realized: I really need to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. Because even though I am busy with work, I occasionally still get upset, so I cannot stop reciting the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. Therefore, I continued to chant it ten times a day.

Now I don't think much. I don't want to distinguish between reciting mantras and doing charitable work. Both of these activities are beneficial to me. I just need to allocate my time properly. I think I don't yet have clear wisdom, so I decided to recite the Lăng Nghiêm mantra ten times a day.

Because life without true wisdom is suffering. The Lăng Nghiêm mantra gives me peace, clarity, and many miraculous benefits. I have discovered many wonderful things from the Lăng Nghiêm mantra, and naturally, I have become diligent, because the benefits gained are so great and I have also achieved significant accomplishments.

The above is my experience with the Lăng Nghiêm mantra. My writing is not eloquent; I only wish to share it for fellow practitioners' reference.

May all sentient beings be able to walk the path away from suffering to find happiness, encouraging and supporting one another, together reaching the shore of bliss.

(Hạnh Đoan abridged translation)

tom_tat: "A STORY ABOUT GOING TO THE TEMPLE FROM AN ANONYMOUS BUDDHIST ABOUT SOMEONE IN THE FAMILY PARTICIPATING IN A RETREAT AT BA VANG TEMPLE I won't talk for long, I would like to honestly share my family's story. It was my own mother who went to Ba Vang Temple"
noi_dung:
IN THE LATE PERIOD, ONE SHOULD BE CLEAR-MINDED IN STUDYING AND PRACTICING DHARMA TO KNOW RIGHT AND WRONG, WHAT SHOULD AND SHOULD NOT BE DONE, AND NOT JUDGE BY APPEARANCES

"THE STORY OF A NAMED BUDDHIST ABOUT A FAMILY MEMBER ATTENDING A RETREAT AT BA VANG PAGODA

I won't talk around it, I want to sincerely share my family's story. My own mother was brainwashed by Ba Vang Pagoda. It felt like she was no longer my mother, and I hope there is a way to wake her from this trance. When I point out various incidents involving the pagoda, she says that other pagodas are jealous of Ba Vang Pagoda and fabricate things to slander it 🙄 I'm speechless. She practices night and day, signing up for every retreat whenever there is one. The pagoda allows devotees to use their own printed study books, whose content is not at all like usual sutras; after reading for a while, you can see it mainly emphasizes karma, a lot of karma, and that you have to practice to resolve karma.

Although my mother is known for following the temple, when asked about the origins of Buddhism, the Buddhas, and the bodhisattvas, she doesn't know. She only sincerely follows the temple, practicing whatever the temple tells her to, in order to overcome all kinds of karmic obstacles and sufferings. And it must be the Ba Vang temple; practicing at other temples is not effective 🙄. My mother is so obsessed that she disregards the distance of dozens of kilometers and rides her motorbike regularly, sometimes going once every 2 or 3 days.

At first, it was said to go once a month, then the frequency increased to once a week, then gradually even more often, eventually renting a house near the temple for convenient practice. They said to keep Buddha in your heart and practice at home, you could just go to a nearby temple to listen to sutras or attend Dharma talks, but it wasn’t insisted that it must be Ba Vang Temple. This part is unclear but seems like a threat that if you are already at Ba Vang Temple, you are forbidden to go to any other temple, otherwise you will incur bad karma or lose spiritual power or something like that. Basically, it makes one obsessed with only Ba Vang Temple. At the beginning of the year, the family usually went to visit various temples, go on pilgrimages, and enjoy the scenery, but since getting involved with Ba Vang Temple, the family has frequently conflicted, life has been disrupted, and she is afraid to go to any temple and afraid of Buddha.

No proof of sincerity. Just kidding! My family is so exhausted, every day grandma prays at all four times—morning, noon, afternoon, night, even at 10, 11, 12 at night you can see her holding the phone, praying to the phone. Whenever anyone mentions the temple, she immediately switches to battle mode, karma is always hanging over every conversation, so much karma 🤧. It's infuriating! In our family, whether it’s something tiny like a child falling, or something huge like an elephant-sized problem, we still pray, bow in all four directions, and the phone deity appears. Even a single argument can bring up karma and fate from a thousand years ago. At the slightest thing, there’s a full online ritual script about the matter, praying.Accordingly, burning it is like fulfilling the wish; not fulfilling the wish is due to not being sincere. Bonus of a disguised pyramid scheme, like terraced fields. Each district, each area has a group of Do Trang, gathering people to practice together. It sounds good, but they just incite each other to disrupt families; anyone who stops them is labeled ignorant, and our enemy is ignorance. I swear I don't even know what ignorance is, this temple is really surreal. After that, each Buddhist in that Do Trang society, whenever they meet someone, would introduce and propagate that Ba Vang Pagoda is very good. You must practice at Ba Vang Pagoda to achieve enlightenment and become an immortal, then in the next life, you get to go to some realm, don't quite remember. Until when peopleThey have to accept, agree that Ba Vang Pagoda is the best.

When you asked, it turns out they attach the label of sowing merits— the more you sow, the more blessings you accumulate. Every woman competes to propagate it even more fiercely than pursuing KPIs; who doesn’t want more blessings? Spending a little saliva to enjoy blessings, who wouldn’t like that? That’s how powerful the temple is, with Facebook and YouTube running intensively, plus online Buddhist devotees from all directions promoting the temple. When asked where the temple’s money goes as it pours in, the madam says, “Anyone who wants to inspect the temple’s money must shave their head before being allowed to touch it” — poetic, isn’t it? Recently, I saw the news reporting that Ba Vang Temple collected several billion, but the expenses exactly matched the revenue, so there was no need to submit reports or notify higher authorities, as I understand.The business of temples is always fierce; temples doing business are even scarier than the government collecting taxes. They have billions, tens of billions, even thousands of billions, yet you never see the leadership react. There are thousands, tens of thousands of other things, I can’t remember to tell everything. So everyone, see if this is exploiting faith, religious freedom to speculate for profit? I want to emphasize that this temple does business exactly like a pyramid scheme with terraced fields.

At the top are the temples, divided by area with each headed by a Dao Trang association. A newcomer to the association is like someone starting a game. To level up, one must either 1) pay money in the form of a retreat fee, or 2) introduce as many people as possible into the group. The set goal is to level up; leveling up allows one to attend the temple's travel retreats. One must reach a certain level, contribute to the temple to a certain extent, before being allowed to register for discounted trips. Recently, I heard my mom boasting that she practices day and night just to be able to travel to India, to the Ganges River, the cradle of Buddhism 😞 Oh mom! The amount of money you burn monthly at the temple, added up over half a year, would be enough for a month-long trip to India. It's really frustrating and maddening.which the family helplessly could not speak.

Burning money is even worse than burning joss paper, it always gives the ladies the feeling that they are about to achieve it, about to get it. If it doesn’t happen, it means they haven’t been sincere enough, so they go back to practicing frantically. It’s really frustrating, I hope the government steps in so families are less broken, I’m worried that the day I hold the debt papers won’t be far off, but my mother insists she won’t believe it.

ANONYMOUS AUTHOR

----------------------------------------

COMMENTARY:

In the degenerate age described in the Buddha's Sutras, it is said that many descendants of demonic rulers will pretend to be children of the Tathagata to destroy the Dharma; there is no evil deed they would not dare to commit. Considering the practice of the Buddha's Teachings, the later the time, the more one needs to be vigilant so as not to be exploited by heretical groups using the name of the Dharma for their own benefits. The story above was shared by Quang Tu from a friend. Quang Tu is not sure about the accuracy of the story; however, he posted it here to give the faithful a more objective perspective, so that belief in the Dharma does not turn into superstition. Faith in practice is very important because all merits originate from it.Regarding faith, if there is no faith, we would not be able to accomplish anything; however, when faith is blind and exploited, it will create dire consequences for society, such as the cult "World Mission Society Church of God"... causing many families to break apart.....

When you begin to believe in something, QT hopes that you can calmly reflect to see whether that content is actually taken from the Sutras of the Tathagata. If it is indeed content taken from the Sutras, then you must personally examine whether it aligns with the virtue and precepts that the Buddha taught, and you yourself must practice and experience it to understand the miraculous efficacy. Simply hearing others speak, even if many people say the same thing, is not necessarily correct, because we are easily psychologically manipulated when we see everyone following something. Therefore, when doing anything, reflect to see whether your actionsIt must be an act of filial piety. Is it something that harms others or affects others, and is it in accordance with the precepts taught by the Buddha? If it is an act that benefits others, benefits oneself, benefits sentient beings, and is filial, then it is in accordance with the Buddha's teachings. But if it benefits oneself, harms others, harms sentient beings, and does not observe the precepts, then it is contrary to the Buddha's teachings!

I hope respected Buddhists will reflect for themselves 🙏
