tom_tat: 1. BRIEF INTRODUCTION ABOUT KṢITIGARBHA BODHISATTVA When we hear about the great Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, we immediately think of the great Bodhisattva who often saves sentient beings in the paths of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, or the newly deceased souls.
noi_dung:
THE GREATNESS OF Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, A BODHISATTVA WHO SILENTLY TRANSFORMS WITH VAST AND INCOMPREHENSIBLE VOWS

1. BRIEF INTRODUCTION TO BODHISATTVA KṢITI

When we hear about the great Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, we immediately think of the great Bodhisattva who often saves sentient beings in hell realms, hungry ghosts, animals, or spirits who have just passed away within forty-nine days, or saves our grandparents, parents, siblings, or numerous relatives across many lifetimes in the past, present, and future... We often invite monks or recite ourselves the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Original Vows and Merits Sutra, hoping to rely on His spiritual power to help alleviate suffering for our loved ones who have just passed away. However, few people may know or understand more about His vows, great power, or the profound meaning of His name.

EARTH: is the great earth, everyone lives within the great earth, it is the place that nurtures all sentient beings, plants, and grasses, the nurturer of all kinds of treasures, the nurturer of all kinds of sentient beings equally. EARTH encompasses all sentient beings in the void of the Dharma realm, and is the origin of all sentient beings, the place where all sentient beings are gathered. His vow covers all sentient beings, bearing suffering on behalf of all sentient beings. We are all living within his Dharma body; wherever there are sentient beings, there he is.

KANG means containing all merits and treasures. Just as the earth can contain everything, the human mind is the same, also containing both good and evil. Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha vows to save all beings in hell before attaining Buddhahood, just like practitioners who vow to transform all the evil things in the mind into good; in this way, they have also become a Buddha.

Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is one of the bodhisattvas revered in Mahayana Buddhism and is depicted as a monk from the East. Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is one of the six great bodhisattvas of Mahayana Buddhism, including Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and him. Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is often portrayed with a compassionate appearance, wearing a monk's hat, with a radiant halo around his head. He stands on a lotus throne or sits on a lotus throne held by Ti How (shaped like a dog, his sacred animal). His staff is usually held in his left hand, and he often holds the Cintāmaṇi jewel, symbolizingto let light dispel the darkness of evil night, while His right hand holds a staff, which is an instrument to open the gates of hell. Some paintings and statues in Vietnam and China depict Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva wearing a red cassock and a seven-Buddha crown. In Japan, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is worshiped as the guardian Bodhisattva of children and protector of unborn babies and the spirits of children, so His images are portrayed with a very innocent and pure face, looking like a child; some paintings and statues even depict Him holding a baby, with two or three other children at His feet clinging to His staff and monk's robe. In Japan, there are also many miraculous stories about Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Many Buddhas of the past also predicted that he would become a Bodhisattva, yet it is also possible that he may never become a Buddha, because his vow is endless, for this space is never-ending, sentient beings are never-ending, the karma of sentient beings is never-ending, hells are never-ending, due to the countless, immeasurable, and infinite numbers without limit. Hell will never be empty, and Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will be the last Buddha if he can become a Buddha; he waits for all sentient beings in this universe to become Buddhas before he himself becomes a Buddha. Because of great compassion, becauseSentient beings have not all been saved, because sentient beings still suffer, so he sacrificed himself. His great vow power is incredibly magnificent. Great Bodhisattvas like Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Maitreya, Avalokiteshvara… after fulfilling their vows also enter Nirvana, leaving only him alone, yet he continues to save sentient beings. He often manifests in the form of a Śrāvaka, the appearance of a monk, not in the form of a Bodhisattva. Close to sentient beings, he is a Master guiding them, leading sentient beings onto the path of the Dharma, guiding sentient beings to enlightenment; his compassion and humility cannot be described by words. We need to diligently cultivate more, in order to have the opportunity to meet him.His name is special; no Bodhisattva shares the same name with him, and the demon king cannot impersonate his form (due to the reverence for the authority and divine power of the Bodhisattva).

2. THE MERIT OF BODHISATTVA KṣITIGARBHA

After attaining Buddhahood, Buddha Shakyamuni taught the Dharma continuously for forty-nine years, giving sermons at more than three hundred Dharma assemblies, yet he still had not liberated Queen Maya, the Buddha's mother. Buddha Shakyamuni was originally born from the left side (above the abdomen) of his mother, and she passed away soon after giving birth to him. After attaining Buddhahood, he reflected and realized that his Holy Mother had been reborn in the heavenly realm. At that time, after finishing the Lotus Sutra and before teaching the Nirvana Sutra, Buddha Shakyamuni, thinking of his mother, ascended to the Tavatimsa Heaven for three months to teach the Dharma for his Holy Mother to hear.

What Dharma did the Buddha preach in the Tavatimsa Heaven? The Buddha preached the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, a sutra that teaches the path of filial piety. Therefore, wishing to save his mother, Śākyamuni Buddha ascended to the Tavatimsa Heaven to expound the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Original Vow Sutra. That the Buddha delivered the Dharma of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra for his mother shows how important the Kṣitigarbha Sutra is! The principle of this Sutra consists of four points and is encompassed in the eight words 'Filial Piety, Saving Lives, Relieving Suffering, Repaying Kindness.' What do these eight words signify? They signify 'diligent practice of filial piety'—the moral principle of being devoted to one's parents. If a person knows how to uphold filial piety, heaven and earth shine brightly. What makes heaven and earth feel movedFilial piety is also a form of movement, so it is said: "Heaven and earth value filial piety, and filial piety comes first" (heaven and earth both regard the path of filial piety as important, and filial piety is foremost), and this is also the essential principle if one wants to resonate with Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha!

The Dharma Assembly for the Sermon of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra is the largest special Dharma Assembly during the 49 years that the Buddha gave teachings, and it is the greatest assembly of Shakyamuni Buddha, because in this assembly all Buddhas of the ten directions—past, present, and future—and all great Bodhisattvas are gathered without exception, making it an extraordinarily Supreme Assembly. Shakyamuni Buddha delivered the teaching in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven in remembrance of his mother, and to repay the kindness of his mother, who was residing in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, thereby expressing filial piety and also revealing the boundless merit of this Scripture. The Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Scripture expounds broadly on his fundamental vows, that isIt is the vow of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva that has been expressed over many lifetimes, since the time when he was still an ordinary being. So that we can learn his vows, follow his vows. It speaks of his noble virtue, his vast and great vow power, therefore this sutra is named according to his fundamental vow. Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, among the great Bodhisattvas, is one of the most ancient and long-lived Bodhisattvas, with a duration beyond imagination, a time that cannot be measured. To the extent that in the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, in the first chapter, Shakyamuni Buddha had to say, “For example, as many as the grasses, trees, shrubs, forests, rice, sesame, bamboo, reeds, stones, mountains, and dust in the three-thousand-great-thousand world system, each of them becomes a river.Hằng, then take the number of grains of sand in each Ganges River, one grain of sand makes one world, then in one world, each tiny speck of dust makes one life, and all the tiny specks contained in one life are all considered as lives. From the time when Venerable Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva attained the stage of the ten grounds of a Bodhisattva until now, it is a thousand times longer than the number of lives given in the example above, let alone the times when Venerable Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva was still at the stage of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas!” we can see that the time he has practiced is extremely long and unimaginable! Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva up to now, originally with wisdom and supernatural powers equal to the Buddhas, it can be said that he is already an ancient Buddha, but because his vow is so vast and deep, he still has not yet chosen to become a Buddha!

Today, thanks to science, we know that the universe has billions upon billions of galaxies, each galaxy has billions of planets, and science has discovered some very distant planets that may have life, but these things were taught by the Buddha 2,600 years ago; recently, the appearance of many extraterrestrials on Earth has sparked human suspicion about extraterrestrial life; among the billions upon billions of planets with life, there are many planets with numerous civilizations, humans living in different worlds, and countless sentient beings living in different dimensions as well. In those worlds, there are worlds that have the emergenceThe life of a Buddha is to teach and guide sentient beings there, but there are also worlds where no Buddha is born to guide sentient beings there. In such worlds, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not appear because the evil karma of sentient beings there is too heavy for anyone to save them. However, out of compassion for the sentient beings there, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva has compassionately manifested as a deity or a figure to patiently guide sentient beings there little by little, so that they understand the law of cause and effect, know to avoid evil and do good, and gradually guide them to cultivate and attain enlightenment. Therefore, through this, you can see how great the power and compassion of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva are! When you develop the mind to revere himBodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, please remember these things!

In the Mahayana Sutra, the Mahāvaipulya Kṣitigarbha Ten Revolutions, the first chapter, when speaking about the merits of Buddha Śākyamuni, states: "In any place of residence, if sentient beings, due to their desires for various things, are oppressed by sorrow and suffering, they can sincerely recite the name, chant, pay homage, and make offerings to the Great Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, and all their wishes will be fulfilled properly, they will be freed from sorrows and suffering, and according to their karmic affinity, they may be born in heaven or attain Nirvāna... O good man! Suppose someone sincerely takes refuge, recites the name, chants, bows, and makes offerings to the leading Bodhisattvas among countless great Bodhisattvas such as Maitreya, Mañjuśrī..."

Beneficially, Avalokiteshvara, Samantabhadra, even after hundreds of lifetimes, cannot compare to a person who sincerely takes refuge, recites the name, reads, worships, and makes offerings to the great Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha in a single meal; their wishes will quickly be completely fulfilled. Why? – Because the great Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha brings benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, making the desires of sentient beings fully accomplished like wish-fulfilling jewels, also like treasures. This great being, desiring to teach and guide sentient beings, has long cultivated steadfast great compassion and great vows, being more vigorous and diligent than other Bodhisattvas. Therefore, you should make offerings to Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha...

Again, in the Sutra on Observing Karmic Retribution, both good and evil, in the first chapter, the Buddha teaches that ".... Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, for the past eleven aeons, has continuously adorned the world of Śākyamuni, perfected sentient beings; therefore, in this grand assembly, His appearance is dignified, and His virtuous power is unparalleled. Except for the Tathāgata, no one can surpass Him. Moreover, all the endeavors in teaching and transforming beings in this world, except for great Bodhisattvas such as Mañjuśrī and Avalokiteśvara, no one can match. This is also due to the original vow and aspiration of this Bodhisattva, which is to swiftly fulfill all the wishes of sentient beings, or to eliminate all grave sins, orremoving all obstacles for all sentient beings, so that they may have peace in this life…

Again, in the Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows, chapter 12, the Buddha taught that "...Again, O Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva! In the next life, if there are any good men or good women who wish to fulfill hundreds of thousands, millions, or countless desires both in the present and the future, they should simply take refuge, gaze upon, bow to, offer, and praise the image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. By doing so, all their wishes and desires will be accomplished. Furthermore, if one prays to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and is supported by his great compassionate power, that person will, in a dream, receive Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's blessing and empowerment... If that person is also able inReciting the name of the Bodhisattva 1,000 times every day continuously for 1,000 days. At that time, the Bodhisattva will assign the local spirits and demons to protect that person for life. In the present life, one will have abundant food and clothing, will be free from all illnesses and sufferings, and even misfortunes will not reach the door, let alone the body…

From the above quotations, we can see that for sentient beings in the present age of the Dharma's decline, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva has countless benefits. For those who are just beginning on the path of practicing the Way, wishing to progress quickly in their cultivation, not be obstructed, not be affected by demonic hindrances, swiftly eliminate karmic obstacles, and not be impeded by unfavorable conditions in their practice, the first thing they should do is sincerely recite the name, read the teachings, pay respect, and make offerings to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Initially, dedicate at least the first three years wholeheartedly to paying respect to Him, focusing on confessing karmic offenses, relying on His spiritual power to help repent toward adversaries and deceased creditors. At the latest, after three years (possibly sooner), when one receives the inspirationThen you can practice other Dharma methods.

3. METHOD OF TRANSFORMING FATE THROUGH THE BLESSING OF BODHISATTVA KṣITIṢaṭTva

For those who are in debt, in a deadlock, or because of romantic issues, family troubles, lack of money, inability to find a satisfactory job, wanting to conceive a child, aiming for career advancement, or suffering losses in business… you should read this part very carefully. To transform your destiny by being in resonance with Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, first, you must be a filial child, because among a hundred virtues, filial piety comes first. Moreover, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, in countless past lives, has always been an extremely filial child. Therefore, anyone with a filial heart, even if they have heavy sins, can easily resonate with him. After that, depending on the circumstances, you may set up an altar.At home, one should daily offer fruits and clean water on the altar of the Bodhisattva with absolute reverence. For those who do not have a home, or are renting, or do not have a convenient place for worship, it is recommended to acquire a scroll painting of the Bodhisattva. When practicing, hang the painting out for bowing; after practice, roll the painting up and store it in a clean, elevated place. Remember that cultivation depends on the mind, so if one constantly fears that this or that will incur sin or disrespect and thus delays practice, one will forever lose great benefits. Daily, in front of the image of the Bodhisattva, one can sing songs praising their merit, or recite verses to extol their virtues.(You can refer to the verse by Quang Tu), before leaving the house for work and after returning from work, always pay three bows to His image, just as we greet our parents! During practice, kneel before His image and recite 10,000 times the name NAM MÔ ĐẠI NGUYỆN ĐỊA TẠNG VƯƠNG BỒ TÁT (it can be broken down into 1,000-2,000 recitations per day). Complete the 10,000 recitations no later than within 7 days to pray for your wishes to be fulfilled. Below is the mantra practice that Quang Tu has applied over the past 4 years; whenever faced with a deadlock in life and did not know how to resolve it, QT always used this method and, in a miraculous way by theThe skillful means through which you have helped me solve all problems that I could not foresee, in order to repay the boundless kindness of the Bodhisattva, I now write this article to help everyone receive benefits as I have.

The recitation ritual of Quang Tu: https://bom.so/Zz8lAf you can print it out to read daily

4. SOME INSPIRING STORIES ABOUT BODHISATTVAS

Long ago, there was a story about a girl born into a lowly servant family. Her family was very poor, and knowing that this was due to bad karma from a past life, she devoted herself to repentance, chanting the name of, and respectfully worshiping the image of, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha for 3 years. Afterwards, one night when she returned home, she saw ants crawling all over her house. When she turned them over, she found a large amount of pure gold. From then on, she used the gold to do business and became prosperous, completely escaping the life of a servant. Later, a wealthy man who also believed in Buddhism, guided by a dream from the Bodhisattva, took her as his wife and cherished her wholeheartedly. There are also many stories of beings who, at the point of clinical death (not fully dead), had their spirits taken by demons down to hell.bearing the punishment, when King Yama was about to interrogate to send to hell to endure the punishment, Kṣitigarbha came, King Yama hurriedly stood respectfully, clasped his hands, knelt, and said: “Great Sage, why have you come here?” He said: “This Lang is my disciple (follower/supporter), Your Majesty should pardon him.” The king said: “The decision has already been made, the fate is exhausted, the allotted merit is finished, it is difficult to forgive.” He said: “In the past, I was in the Hall of Good Dharma in the 33rd heaven, the Buddha had decreed that I may save those with destined punishment. Since then, moreover, this Lang has not committed a grave sin, how could I not save him?” The king said: “The Great Vow of the Great One is steadfast and immovable like the Diamond Mountain, I will comply with the words.“Issue a decree, let him return to the human world,” thanks to which the person is completely saved from the sins of hell. Some people are merely grandchildren of one of Kṣitigarbha's disciples, yet when they die, he also petitions Yama King to absolve them from the sins of hell. Even if someone sincerely pays respect before his image only once, they can be saved by him from the three evil paths. There are even people who worship and pay homage to Kṣitigarbha all their lives, reciting Buddha's name to pray for rebirth in the Western Pure Land, but have not entered the Samādhi of Buddha Recitation, nor achieved undistracted single-mindedness (two conditions required for guaranteed rebirth), yet before their life ends, Kṣitigarbha not only informs them but also uses his supernatural powers to assist them.This person, when reciting Buddha's name, was able to do so with a single-minded focus and was certain of rebirth in the Pure Land. There are many such cases in both our country and China. Now, Quang Tu only wishes to present a few such stories; you can read more related stories of him at: https://bom.to/dlR7HM

Therefore, we can see that the merit and benefits of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva for sentient beings are beyond measure. If you wish to pray for anything in this present life, simply wholeheartedly pay respects and sincerely recite his name with utmost reverence, and your wishes will certainly be fulfilled quickly (note that this excludes unwholesome deeds).

In the era of the declining Dharma, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha took on a very great responsibility, being entrusted to propagate the teachings to all sentient beings after the Buddha entered Nirvana. The Buddha Shakyamuni taught us how we should practice! Each of us needs to follow the Buddha's instructions. What did He ask us to do? The Buddha instructed us to wholeheartedly pay respect and take refuge in Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha in order to be attuned to Him and receive His blessings. The Buddha clearly showed us the path to follow. In practice, a portion of respect brings a portion of benefit. Ten portions of respect bring ten portions of benefit. Spiritual cultivation is based on heartfelt respect.Reverence is very important; we should practice reciting the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva with respect every day. If we maintain this practice, one day you may feel the presence of Him. Once you sense Him, you will never again fall into the three evil paths!

May all devotees, upon reading this article, wholeheartedly revere, pay respects, praise, and recite the name of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha. By doing so, even in this lifetime and at the moment of leaving this body, you will receive profound and supreme bliss, forever liberated from the three evil realms!

Feel free to joyfully share without asking for permission; the merit is boundless!

tieu_de: HOW TO HAVE MERIT AND EFFECTIVE VIRTUE.
tom_tat: The other day, someone said that seeing rich people doing charity and releasing animals makes them very eager, but unfortunately, being poor and having no money, they can only watch them do it and feel sad for their own situation. Today I am writing this article to share with you that
noi_dung:
HOW TO HAVE EFFECTIVE MERIT AND BLESSINGS.

The other day, someone said that seeing wealthy people doing charity work and releasing animals made them feel envious, but unfortunately, since they were poor and had no money, they could only watch and feel sad for their own situation.

Today I am writing this article to share with you: "If you see others doing charity, releasing animals, or doing other meaningful things, and you feel happy and wish to be like them, it means you can still enjoy 10% of the merit, just like them."

Similarly, just as when you recite sutras, copy sutras, or do any virtuous deeds, remember to dedicate the merit to those who have passed away, to your resentful enemies and karmic creditors, to your parents of many generations, and to all sentient beings in the Dharma realm. That is precisely liberating the spirits and giving the gift of Dharma. In those 7 parts, you receive 6 parts, and they (the deceased) receive 1 part. There is no difference.

Heaven and Buddha are always very fair; they do not accept bribes from anyone, nor do they make concessions to the rich while despising the poor. Even if you bring a bag of salt to offer to the Buddhas at the Temple, that merit is praised by countless Buddhas. Those who steal, rob, or embezzle from the people and then, out of fear of retribution, try to offer bribes to Buddha, gain no merit at all and only increase their guilt. Wealth and blessings, whether abundant or poor, depend on the character and actions one sowed in previous lives.

If you want to know what kind of karma you have in this life, you can predict it by seeing what you sowed in your past life.

“If you want to know whether in the next life you will have a brilliant career and reputation, in this life you should chant sutras often to become intelligent and excel in learning. If you want to live long and be free from illness, you should eat vegetarian without killing living beings, and perform many acts of releasing life; then you will not die young, have less illness, and live a long life. If you want to be wealthy, you must give alms and perform charity.” People today who are poor, with not enough food to eat, living in distant and remote places, are due to being stingy and miserly in past lives, not knowing how to give alms. I take this advice from the scriptures just to let you understand.

However, there is a small reminder for you to keep in mind: once you have done something good or given something to anyone, consider it done and forget about it. If you have given it, then in the evening you go home, place your hand on your forehead, think about it and feel regretful, it is as if everything is poured into the river, and there is not a bit of merit at all.

Do not let even a trace of doubt remain in your mind, and when giving, there is no need to record it on a golden plaque, nor should you issue a merit certificate or broadcast it throughout the village, from the head of the village to the alleyways; every deed you plant is recognized by heaven, and boasting loudly will only lose your merit. Instead, share good words, justice, correct truths, and the precious teachings of the Buddha to guide and advise others; or follow the Buddha's precepts sincerely in your practice to serve as a model for others to imitate, turning away from evil toward good, correcting wrongs and returning to righteousness—all these are acts of giving (dana).

Giving the Dharma has a value far greater than giving material wealth, and giving material wealth only helps others alleviate material scarcity for a period of time, or at most, it can save a person's life. But giving the Dharma helps people greatly in the spiritual aspect, not only for the poor, but also for the rich and powerful; it does not only have a positive influence in one period, but also sows good seeds for many future lifetimes.

If we see others doing good deeds and we feel joy, the merit is immeasurable; but if we see others doing bad deeds and we join in being happy about it, our guilt is the same as theirs. For example, when receiving good news that benefits us, we immediately have an attitude of joy, happiness, and optimism. For instance, seeing them release animals, give alms, or do good deeds, even if we are poor and cannot contribute money, if we feel glad about their actions, we also receive merit just like them. Conversely, if we receive good news about someone we dislike, at that moment we will feel uncomfortable, sad, annoyed, and may even be irritable toward others.

Then urging them means sharing the same guilt equally. That is giving charity through the eyes and giving charity through actions if one does not have the means.

You sow seeds of affinity on Facebook for everyone, but has anyone taken it upon themselves to sow seeds of affinity by bringing lectures or scriptures to remote areas? If you want people to turn toward the Buddha's teachings, first you must print the cause-and-effect lectures and bring them to those distant places, and that is true limitless merit. In their past lives, they may have slandered the Triple Gem, so in this life they are sent to places with no Dharma at all. Therefore, we need to sow seeds of affinity and give the Dharma in those places. Many people still do not understand the meaning of giving the Dharma. You might see a good post about the Buddha's teachings and share it with others, or you might print out many copies and bind them together.becoming many sets to give to many people, or giving the scriptures to people to read and recite, and then showing people what is good and right is the merit one creates. Remember!

For these reasons, a true Buddhist never misses any opportunity to practice giving Dharma. In short, cultivating both Merit and Wisdom is the most superior.

Dedication:

May the merit of this practice

Adorn the Buddha’s Pure Land

Repay the four great debts

And relieve the suffering in the three realms below

May whoever sees or hears this

Develop the Bodhi mind

Throughout the course of this life

Rebirth together in ancient ultimate bliss.

Author: Alisa

tieu_de: RELATED TO THE BUDDHA'S HAIR RELICS CASE
tom_tat: Blessings one creates are enjoyed by oneself, karma one causes is endured by oneself. Right and wrong are judged above by the Deities, below by officials and authorities, while good and evil are felt by people's hearts.
noi_dung:
RELATED TO THE BUDDHA HAIR RELIC INCIDENT

The blessing that someone creates is what they enjoy, the karma that someone causes is what they bear. Right and wrong are already judged by the Celestial Beings above, and by officials and authorized agencies below. Good and evil are felt by the human heart. As laypeople and ordinary individuals, with heavy karma, thin blessings, dense ignorance, and dull innate wisdom, we should hear and perceive with intelligence and awareness. WE SHOULD ONLY WORRY ABOUT PRACTICING TO LIBERATE OURSELVES, and not let the crowd-driven media lead us, lest the resultant sins entangle us and cause suffering.

A few heartfelt words shared with good friends 🙏🙏🙏

----

10 Things Not to Believe Hastily

1. Do not hastily believe anything just because it is a legend.

2. Do not hastily believe anything just because it belongs to tradition.

3. Do not hastily believe anything just because it is mentioned or propagated by many people.

4. Do not hastily believe anything just because it is recorded in books or scriptures.

5. Do not hastily believe anything, just because it is supported by metaphysical reasoning.

6. Do not hastily believe anything, just because it aligns with your own position.

7. Do not hastily believe anything, just because it fits your own prejudices.

8. Do not hastily believe anything, when it is based on superficial facts.

9. Do not hastily believe anything, just because it is supported by power and authority.

10. Do not hastily believe anything, just because it is proclaimed by your missionaries or gurus.

Anguttara Nikaya (The Anguttara Nikaya/The “Further-factored” Discourses)

tieu_de: BUDDHA TEACHES ABOUT MARITAL HAPPINESS: COMING TOGETHER IS A PREDESTINED FATE, JUST NEED TO DO THESE 2 THINGS WELL, AND PROSPERITY WILL BE FULL
tom_tat: According to the Buddha's teachings on marital happiness, there are two simple things that play a decisive role in a family's happiness, but not everyone can do these two things well. Once they are done,
noi_dung:
BUDDHA TEACHES ABOUT MARRIAGE HAPPINESS: COMING TOGETHER IS PREDESTINED, JUST DO THESE 2 THINGS WELL, AND PROSPERITY WILL BE FULL

According to the Buddha's teachings on marital happiness, there are two things that are simple but play a decisive role in the happiness of a family, yet not everyone can do these two things well. Once they are accomplished, blessings and prosperity will come naturally without needing to ask for them.

Buddhist teachings say that all things in life come together because of the word "fate"; that fate has already been predetermined by destiny.

Every encounter is inevitably bound by the cause and effect of life. It is precisely because of this karmic relationship that we are able to meet each other in this vast sea of people.

As the Buddha teaches:

In the previous life, turning back 500 times can only change into a fleeting meeting in this life.

Buddha's teaching:

People who meet in this life do so because of karmic connections cultivated over many past lives.

Fate is something very strange; no one can really explain it clearly.

If there is fate but no debt, meeting each other still cannot lead to living together. If there is debt but no fate, one cannot become husband and wife either. Fate and debt together form the bond of marriage, or more accurately, karmic force plays an important role in bringing two people together to have the opportunity of marital connection.

When two people meet, fall in love, and become husband and wife, originally being two strangers with somewhat different personalities, if they can find a way to reconcile those differences, that is happiness.

According to the Buddha's teachings on marital happiness, as long as you do these two things well, any storm can be overcome, and happiness will come to the family without asking for it.

1. Patience is the secret to maintaining marital love

The ancients have a saying:

It takes a hundred years of cultivation to share a boat trip, and a thousand years of cultivation to become husband and wife.

Two strangers who do not know each other can travel the same path together; that is all due to fate.

Fate is determined by heaven, while destiny is determined by humans. It is indeed so: meeting each other is heaven's intention, being together is human intention. Relying on both sides to cherish and nurture it, a chance encounter can turn into a hundred-year destiny.

A harmonious family is the foundation for the development of society. To have a harmonious family, it is still important for individuals to adjust themselves, or in other words, family happiness is determined by the efforts of both spouses to nurture it.

In this, emotions and attitudes play a major role in the harmony of a family.

For spouses to be happy, both sides must yield and lower their ego to live together.

Husband and wife should be tolerant when living together; only then can they hope for a long-lasting and happy life. Buddha considers marriage not only as a bond through which people connect in love and happiness but also as an opportunity for individuals (husband and wife) to perfect themselves.

Because no one is born perfect, men need time to mature. Women also need a space to perfect themselves.

Marriage is two flawed people finding each other and forming a bond, so they must be tolerant of each other in living together. On the outside, it doesn't matter who wins or loses, but at home they must respect each other.

Once you step into marriage, pride and ego should be temporarily set aside to prioritize the collective good. Husbands and wives should "watch their words" if they hope to have lifelong happiness together.

Family is not a place for anyone to display strength or argue to the end to prove they are right. When "conflicts" arise, compromising, sacrificing a little, and being a bit humble will help both parties gain more happiness.

Buddha taught that fulfilling one’s duties and responsibilities in marriage is more worthwhile than any struggle for rights. Therefore, He considered duties and responsibilities as effective means to establish a successful marital relationship.

2. Fidelity is the key to opening the door to happiness

According to Buddha's teachings on marital happiness, fidelity is the key that leads to the happiness that everyone desires.

“Thủy” means beginning, “Chung” means end. Once bearing the title of husband and wife, one must be consistent from start to finish, firm in heart and mind, not wavering in the face of life's challenges.

Husband and wife, although not of the same blood, share a feeling that is extremely sacred, beautiful, and worthy of respect; it can only be one. Only when both are gone can they no longer live together.

The Buddha taught that women must know how to maintain chastity, and men must not harbor perverse (dishonest) intentions. Fidelity in marital life is extremely important and is a standard for evaluating a person's morality.

There is a thought-provoking story of the Buddha teaching about fidelity in marriage as follows:

Late at night, in a temple, a person knelt at the feet of the Buddha asking Him for guidance to find a way out of the current troubles.

That person said: 'Honorable Buddha, I am a married man, and I am currently deeply in love with another woman. I truly do not know what to do now.'

The Buddha replied: 'Can you be certain that the woman you are in love with now is the last and only woman in your life?'

The person answered: 'Yes, I can.'

The Buddha: 'Then will you divorce now, and marry her afterwards?'

The man: But my wife is a gentle, kind, and virtuous person. If I leave her, would it be cruel? Would it be immoral, Venerable Buddha?

The Buddha: A marriage without love is what is truly cruel and immoral. You now love someone else, and no longer love your wife. What you are doing is right.

The man: But my wife still loves me very much, Venerable Buddha.

The Buddha: Then your wife is happy.

Other person: After I divorce my wife to be with someone else, my wife will be very sad. Why would I be happy, Sir?

Buddha: In marriage, your wife still has love for you, while you have lost love for your wife. Because you love someone else, it is precisely due to this happiness that losing your previous love causes suffering, so the one who suffers is you.

Other person: But I cut ties with my wife and then marry someone else, so she has lost me. She will always be the one who suffers, won't she?

The Buddha said again: You are mistaken, you are only the wife you truly love in marriage. When a person like you does not exist, the true love of your wife will transfer to someone else, because the true love of your wife in marriage has never been lost. Therefore, your wife is the one who is happy, and you are the one who is suffering.

The other person: My wife once said that in this life she would only love me. She would not love anyone else.

The Buddha: You also once said that, didn't you?

The other person stammered and could not continue speaking upon hearing this.

Buddha: Now look at the three candles in the incense burner in front of you, which one is the brightest?

The other person: Honestly, I don't know, they all seem to be equally bright.

Buddha: Those three candles are like three women. One of them is the person you are currently in love with. There are countless beings, many women. If you cannot even identify which of the three candles is the brightest, cannot find the person you are currently in love with, then how can you determine that the woman you are in love with now is the last and only one in your life?

The other person stammered, unable to speak.

Buddha: Now, hold a candle before your eyes, and focus your mind to see which flame is the brightest?

Other person: Of course, the one in front is the brightest.

Buddha: Now put it back in its place, then look again to see which one is the brightest.

Other person: Indeed, I still cannot tell which one is the brightest.

Buddha: Actually, the candle you just held is like the last woman you are currently in love with; love arises from the heart. When you feel love for it and focus on observing, you will see it as the brightest and most beautiful. When you put it back in its place, you can no longer find the good feelings as before. What you call your last and only love is just a flower in a mirror, the moon reflected on water; in the end, it is nothing, a meaningless romance.

The other person: I understand now, I have realized the truth that You want to convey. Now I truly know who I love, that person is my current wife, Lord Buddha.

Buddha: Amitabha...

From the story above, it can be seen that happiness does not need to wait for the next life, nor does it need to be sought in distant places; it can exist right now and here.

Everyone wishes to achieve true happiness, but many people, being temporarily blind, do not know how to cherish the happiness they already have, being busy chasing meaningless things out there.

Loyalty and sincere love create deep and lasting happiness because they form the bond for a long-lasting romantic relationship. The bond between husband and wife must transcend life and death to find each other, so please do not betray true feelings.

tom_tat: THE ONLY MASS EXECUTION OF ENTIRE CLANS IN HISTORY During the Ming Dynasty, under the reign of Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang, there was a man with the surname Phuong who, wanting his family's fortune to prosper, invited a skilled feng shui master to search
noi_dung:
THE SEVERE KARMA BEHIND

THE ONLY GENOCIDAL MASSACRE IN HISTORY

During the Ming Dynasty, under the reign of Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang, there was a man with the surname Phương who, wanting his family to prosper, invited a highly skilled feng shui master to find a dragon vein to build a tomb for his father. After finding a good site, the feng shui master set a date for the construction to begin. The night before, Mr. Phương dreamed of an old man in red clothes who appeared before him and said:

– The grave that you have chosen is my dwelling place. I beg you to postpone for a few days so that my descendants have time to move elsewhere before you break ground.

After speaking, the old man pleaded and kowtowed before leaving. Mr. Phương woke up, thinking it was just a meaningless dream, so he paid no attention. But strangely, when the grave was being dug, it was discovered that beneath the grave was a large snake den containing hundreds of red snakes. Remembering the dream, Mr. Phương began to hesitate, but in the end, he still ordered the snakes to be burned completely with fire.

That night, the Phuong family member dreamed again of the old man in red appearing, angrily coming before him, crying and blaming:

– I begged you to postpone for a few days so that my descendants would have time to move elsewhere before starting the construction. Not only did you refuse to postpone, but you also used fire to kill more than 800 members of my clan. Your heart is truly cruel. You have wiped out my clan, so I will also wipe out yours.

After saying that, the old man in red disappeared.

The following year, in 1357, the Phuong family had a son and named him Phuong Hieu Nhu. It is unknown whether it was due to the influence of the feng shui of the grave, but indeed young Phuong Hieu Nhu was very special, possessing both talent and virtue, and he was upright and straightforward. When he grew up, Phuong Hieu Nhu passed the imperial examination and became an official, his career continuously advancing, eventually becoming a high-ranking minister under the reign of Chu Doan Van.

So does having good feng shui mean that everything will go smoothly and there is nothing to worry about? In reality, it is not that simple; there is another law much stronger than feng shui, which is the law of cause and effect, and this law is very harsh.

In 1402, King Yan Zhu Li (the uncle of Zhu Zhan Wen) led his army to seize the throne from Zhu Zhan Wen. The coup was successful, Zhu Zhan Wen had to flee the capital, and Zhu Li ascended the throne as Ming Chengzu. Immediately afterward, Zhu Li ordered the execution of all the high officials who were determined to remain loyal to Zhu Zhan Wen.

While some high-ranking officials feared death and thus proactively surrendered, Phuong Hieu Nhu resolutely refused to submit. Initially, because of Phuong Hieu Nhu's talent and the fact that many people praised him, it was believed that retaining him would be beneficial for the country in the future. Therefore, Chu Le still tried to have trusted subordinates advise him, hoping Phuong Hieu Nhu would surrender. Even when Chu Le conducted the enthronement ceremony, he wanted Phuong Hieu Nhu to be the one to write the royal edict for him.

Being forced to write a decree to ascend the throne, Phuong Hieu Nhu refused, he screamed and declared that even if all ten clans were killed, he would not write it. Hearing these words, Chu Le also lost his composure. He ordered people to dismember Phuong Hieu Nhu and then threw his body into the market.

Then he ordered the extermination of the ten clans of Phương Hiếu Nhụ as he had said. Normally in history, no matter how serious the crime, the worst punishment would be the extermination of the nine clans, which is executing relatives up to nine generations. But this time, the king killed even Phương Hiếu Nhụ's friends and disciples, calling it the extermination of ten clans. The number of people who died in this case reached 873! Equivalent to the number of snakes that Phương Hiếu Nhụ's father had killed long ago.

Could this just be a coincidence? What are your thoughts on this tragic true story in Chinese history? In your opinion, from the beginning, what should Phương Hiếu Nhụ's father have done?

noi_dung:
NOWADAYS, IF ONE IS TRAPPED IN DEBTS, SURROUNDED BY KARMA, HINDERED BY CIRCUMSTANCES FROM PRACTICING, GREAT OR SMALL DISASTERS CAN OCCUR

The Kṣitigarbha Sutra was encouraged for chanting by Venerable Tuyen Hoa, a contemporary holy monk. The main principle of the Kṣitigarbha Sutra revolves around eight words: Filial piety, Saving lives, Relieving suffering, and Repaying gratitude.

- What is filial piety: This sutra emphasizes filial piety, which is the foundation of human beings.

- Saving lives is the original vow of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha; in our practice, we first save ourselves and then save others, rescuing sentient beings.

- Relieving suffering means that when we chant and practice it, we can eliminate all miseries.

- Repaying gratitude means we recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra to repay the four kinds of gratitude: gratitude to parents, gratitude to teachers, gratitude to the Buddha, and gratitude to all sentient beings.

HOW SHOULD IT BE RECITED?

Depending on our work and time, we dedicate time to chanting sutras. If possible, you can spend a little time early in the morning or late at night to read and chant. It is best to maintain it regularly for a period that you have set (vowed), or daily is even better. It is better to maintain it consistently rather than occasionally. Why is it very beneficial? Because you have spent time reviewing the words of the Buddha, through which you can apply them to practicing in life. The time you spend chanting sutras is useful time, focusing the mind rather than letting it wander into trivial matters.

WHERE TO READ, HOW TO READ?

You can recite sutras anywhere except in places that are not solemn or clean, such as toilets, places for marital activities, etc. Depending on the circumstances, you can read aloud, read silently, read with your eyes, etc. If there is a properly arranged Buddha altar, that is even better; busy people can read at work during breaks, etc., it's all acceptable.

You should read slowly, clearly, and distinctly to help yourself understand easily, and invisible or visible beings around can also understand and penetrate the words of the sutra to attain enlightenment.

WHEN TO RECITE THE Kṣitigarbha SUTRA

If we can recite daily, that is very good; if not, we can recite once a week or once a month. It is best on the days of the 1st, 8th, 14th, 15th, 18th, 23rd, 24th, 28th, 29th, 30th, or on the holy days of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, to eat vegetarian, observe precepts, and recite sutras, so that merits will be multiplied greatly. Especially when we have matters that require sincere recitation, such as: when a family member has passed away, preparing for pregnancy, during pregnancy and childbirth, praying for marital harmony, praying for children, wishing for smooth work, and so on....

Moreover, when life is in turmoil and we are under work pressure, whatever prayer or wish we have, we should make the resolve to recite the Kṣitigarbha Sutra continuously for 7 days, 21 days, or 49 days; then any wish (for good deeds) will be fulfilled as desired. Whether things are effective or not depends solely on whether we are sincere or doubtful.

THINGS TO NOTE!

If you have resolved to follow a strictly vegetarian diet and avoid the five pungent spices including: onions (including baro), chives, garlic, shallots, and húng cù (a type of plant with a garlic-like smell), and strictly observe precepts (for laypeople, first and foremost, observe the Five Precepts: do not kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, masturbate or watch obscene films, do not drink alcohol), then when reciting sutras, you should brush your teeth, rinse your mouth thoroughly, bathe, wash your hair, change into clean clothing, and then recite.

For those of you who cannot follow a strict vegetarian diet, you should still strictly observe the Five Precepts, avoid the five pungent spices, treat your colleagues and family with respect, and avoid arguing (remember this ^^, patience comes first). After eating non-vegetarian food, you should brush your teeth, rinse your mouth thoroughly, bathe, and change into clean clothes before starting to chant Sutras; otherwise, it will be considered an act of disrespect! You should pay close attention to this!

tieu_de: THE CLOSER WE GET TO SOMEONE IMPORTANT'S DOOR, THE MORE SERIOUS OBSTACLES WE ENCOUNTER, WE MUST USE
tom_tat: Speaking of practicing the path of cultivation and spiritual practice, there are many obstacles. Many people who practice, as soon as we set our intention, are like runners in a race, stumbling right from the starting line; some surge ahead to take the lead, while others fall behind.
noi_dung:
THE CLOSER WE GET TO THE DOOR OF IMPORTANT PEOPLE, THE MORE SERIOUS OBSTACLES WE ENCOUNTER, WE MUST USE

When it comes to practicing the path of cultivation, there are many obstructions and obstacles. Many people who begin to practice, at the moment they make the initial resolve, are like runners in a race; some surge ahead to the lead, some fall behind, and some are eliminated.

Due to what reason?

Because there are too many obstructions and obstacles against oneself.

Some obstacles come from other people, some from circumstances, some from objects, and there may even be enemies or spirits opposing you, both visible and invisible. These are the obstructions and obstacles.

Who can overcome that layer of obstacles?

Who can achieve attainment?

Nothing else! A single mind directed toward the Path!

Day by day read the sutras, day by day study the teachings, not being lazy for even a single day, all obstacles need not be paid attention to, as long as the mind is focused on the Path, and conduct is in accordance with the Path. Observe oneself carefully, contemplate, if one's mind and conduct do not stray from the Path, do not go against the teachings of the Buddha, then all obstacles need not be concerned with, and it will be sufficient!

Countless people do not use their energy or time to STUDY ways to deal with obstacles. IF they do so, the obstacles become EVEN BIGGER.

For example, when someone slanders you, and you want to find a way to retaliate, isn't that inviting trouble for yourself? At that moment, what will happen? Once that THOUGHT EXISTS, your mind has ALREADY CONTRADICTED righteousness; the Buddha does not teach us to retaliate! So what method does the Buddha teach us? Endurance. What does endurance mean? Absolutely not paying attention; let them slander, and I go my own way. It's like if someone punches me, I do not resist; that punch is as if it doesn't exist. When someone slanders, we retaliate. Ah! Then both sides will end up fighting. Being CURSED without reciprocating, being HIT without hitting back, focus your mind on the Dharma, fix your virtues on the Dharma, be courageous, and diligent.Honestly, that thing is really difficult! Ordinary people cannot endure it. If it is hard to endure but you can endure it, hard to practice but you can practice it, then you can smoothly walk on the Bodhi path!

The closer we get to an important gateway, the more serious obstacles we encounter, and we MUST use those obstacles to TEST ourselves. At present, if we have reached that level of practice, we must pass that test. Therefore, obstacles are not inherently bad.

In the scriptures, the Buddha often teaches us: IN THE WORLD, AND IN LEAVING THE WORLD, NOTHING IS ABSOLUTELY RIGHT OR WRONG.

Fortune or misfortune, disaster or blessing—where do they come from?

To be honest, it all comes from a single thought of oneself. A single 'right' thought of oneself can turn danger into safety, transform disaster into blessing; what could be bad about that? Your cultivation practice is useful, it generates effect. If you CANNOT endure, if there is a thought of anger, a thought of revenge, you WILL regress significantly, you WILL be expelled from the Bodhi path. Such a person is not just ninety-nine percent, no! The worry is that among a thousand people, or among ten thousand people, the one who can truly break through is only a fraction of ten thousand; to be honest, it's not even a fraction of ten thousand! Think about it: People studying BuddhismIf it were truly one in ten thousand [that could achieve a breakthrough], there would be quite a few Buddhist practitioners, up to hundreds of thousands, even millions; if it were one in ten thousand, then those who truly achieve accomplishment would number a few hundred, possibly even a thousand, [but in reality] it is not like that! Therefore, you understand that this matter is very difficult, and one must subdue their own afflictions and habitual tendencies.

We are extremely fortunate; if you ask why we are able to overcome the accumulated vexations and habits,

Nothing else at all, DAY AFTER DAY reading sutras, day after day giving lectures on sutras, day after day studying, ALL of my mental and spiritual energy is devoted to the scriptures. THEREFORE, I have neither the spirit nor the time TO PAY ATTENTION to anything else; it really is like that. Not only do I not have time to care about anything else, I also don't have the spirit. Many fellow practitioners write letters to me, and I don't have time to read them. That’s why I often advise people not to send me letters; I really don't want to look at them. By chance, I opened an old book and found a letter tucked inside, the envelope unopened, I opened it to see, roughly seven or eight years old, completely forgotten!

Therefore, I hope everyone recites sutras and chants the Buddha's name. IF THERE IS A PROBLEM, then recite the Buddha's name more, read sutras more, and you WILL NATURALLY understand. The greatest good in both worldly and transcendental Dharma is reading sutras and chanting the Buddha's name, because for the sake of others, as stated in the sutras, the World-Honored One called it “reading, reciting, receiving, and preserving, explaining for others.” That is precisely the highest good deed, the supreme virtuous conduct, purely and purely good among the worldly and transcendental dharmas. Both worldly and transcendental dharmas are NOT STAINED, and that is truly GREAT LIBERATION. Even if one does not achieve full liberation, one will certainly achieve small liberation.

In the Western Pure Land world, cultivation has no obstacles, and there are no hindrances there. Therefore, the Worthy One introduced to us the “wonderful land creatures” (beings in that realm). Beings in that realm are all those born into the Western Pure Land world; they do not experience suffering, but “receive all happiness” (just enjoy the pleasures). The joys within these pleasures are numerous, but only two points are highlighted: first, they do not decline; second, there are no obstacles. Hence it is called the Pure Land.

Trung Phong Tam Thời Hệ Niệm

tieu_de: A LIFE FROM HELL TO MILLIONAIRE IN 2 YEARS THANKS TO BUDDHISM.
tom_tat: (Sharing from an anonymous male member in the Sexual Control group) Hello everyone. You are not reading it wrong. It really is not a mistake. A young man paying a heavy price for his mistakes
noi_dung:
LIFE FROM HELL TO MILLIONAIRE IN 2 YEARS THANKS TO BUDDHIST TEACHINGS.

(Sharing from an anonymous male member in the Sexual Control group)

Hello everyone. You are not reading it wrong. It really is not a mistake. A young man who once had to pay dearly for his mistakes has become a completely different person with a fortune of 25 billion at the age of nearly 29. In the past, I would never have dared to imagine today; everything I have achieved is thanks to Buddhist teachings. Today, I sit here writing these heartfelt words about my life to share with everyone, to serve as motivation for all those who are destined to deeply believe in karma and the miraculous power of Buddhist teachings, to a degree that words cannot describe.

It could be due to the heavy karma you have accumulated over many lifetimes; it could also be due to the collective karma of your family and lineage; it could also be that you are like a black sheep lost among white sheep to repay common karma, or you could be someone chosen to make mistakes, to walk into the muddy swamp in order to understand its filth and then advise others to stay away from it; or it could be due to some reason that you have not yet realized...

The bad karma that led to your sufferings is the sin of sexual misconduct, one of the grave sins frequently mentioned by karma or Buddhist teachings in many scriptures. Your parents, after getting married, only had you two years later. And during the two years before your mother became pregnant with you, she had been pregnant once, but the pregnancy failed (I have looked into some causes that lead to this phenomenon in the scriptures and books of ancient Chinese scholars such as the Shou Kang Bao Jian, An Shi Quan Shu – which advise people to abandon lust… stating that families or individuals who are lustful have difficulty conceiving, or even if they conceive, the child is likely to die in the womb because of their essenceThe father's bloodline and the mother's health were not good enough to sustain the life of that child, or even if the child was born, it would be weak and prone to many illnesses; or the family did not possess great fortune to keep the child. When the younger sibling was born, he was told that he was a very difficult child to raise, constantly sick, suffering from chronic illnesses, many digestive problems, and mild illnesses whenever the weather changed (books noted that this was due to persistent negative energy, spirit possession, or vengeful spirits haunting to cause harm). As he grew up, he witnessed many heartbreaking events involving the entire extended family, the siblings of his parents, his grandparents, and everyone was always immersed in poverty and quarrels.Fighting, every time those arguments happened, I would cry and beg everyone. All difficulties were always looming over my family, my parents were also in conflict, always in a state where they could divorce. Witnessing such sorrowful scenes made me a closed-off and introspective person, often wandering alone in deserted places, then wandering in the temple near my house, even wandering to the cemetery to sit alone at night. By the time I reached middle school, starting from grade 6, I became aware of my studies, I studied very diligently, excelled academically, and earned a lot of admiration from everyone and the teachers. But the family was still unstable, still fighting, all the sadness still continuedalways present every day, every hour. By the last years of middle school, the mind and body start to change, and perhaps bad karma begins to grow heavily from here, from the actions of parents, from the family, from all causes and karma from many lifetimes, and perhaps because the virtuous merits of oneself and the family are not enough to enjoy goodness. The fire of lust in you is too heavy and terrible, every thought is very impure and dirty appearing in your mind. This continues from the last years of middle school until the end of high school. And ignorance, the meager virtue is not enough to guide a person on the right path, study gradually declines, even though still alwaysBeing in the top honors class of the school. Perhaps your blessings have not run out yet so that things haven’t gone too far, because within you there are always two opposing states tearing each other apart, knowing what is right and wrong. Everyone who meets you always praises you for being handsome, very attractive to the gaze of many people in school or even outside society, yet the fire of desire still grows and controls you.

The instability in the family continued; I failed the university entrance exam my first year because I no longer felt motivated to study, wanting instead to work to earn money for the family, thinking that money would solve all the family's problems. Perhaps all the thoughts in my mind were influenced by some karma guiding me. But then, my family persuaded me, and I attended my second-choice university. After that, I quietly retook the entrance exam and got accepted. I continued studying, and then secretly, without telling my family, I started working on my own in this unfamiliar city, taking care of myself, and studying to earn a scholarship each semester. But really, the fire of desire still bound me; coming to the city and witnessingThe scenes of adultery of the neighbors around where I live, they have sexual relations right next to my rented room. Every unfortunate circumstance clings to me, leading me down the path of lewdness. And then I started to know masturbation, doing all the dirty deeds of every lewd sin that I cannot conveniently share here, I am like a wild animal, my filthy lust like the demons and beasts described in the scriptures. Although outwardly I appear very clean and handsome as everyone comments, inside I am completely filthy.

Throughout the early years of university, not much karma occurred. But by the third year of university, karma started coming down rapidly and terribly. Renting a place and being cheated out of money, then being kicked out of the house, having to sell the motorbike that I had saved for a long time to buy in order to continue the life of the two siblings (at this time I was supporting a younger sibling in university). Everything I did was met with deception and failure, illnesses started to appear more frequently, the body became weak, and it was very easy to get sick.

I have always been aware that karma exists, but I have not yet had the opportunity to deeply study Buddhism, and within me there is always an internal struggle between right and wrong. In difficult times, I still have people who help me at the right moments so that I do not collapse. I lack money to support the lives of the two of us in a big city. I still live decently in certain aspects, but my lust burns strongly, pushing me to go the wrong way. Karma comes and goes.

By the time I graduated, I had an accident right in front of a material truck, almost losing a finger; if the truck hadn't stopped in time, I probably wouldn't be alive today to write these confessions.

After graduation, I was also introduced to work at a large organization. But life remained difficult due to great lust, karma continued to descend, sickness and disease still followed, and immoral sexual behavior could not be stopped, so misfortunes continued. Family life remained discordant; even my siblings were in conflict. Money could not be earned, falling into debt, borrowing small amounts to make ends meet. And then I quit my job, wandering alone throughout the city for a long time.

When I first met a girl, I thought my life would be okay. But no, when I put all my trust in them, perhaps fate was arranging my life to be this way, they deceived me bitterly. I sank into pain, thoughts, confusion, not daring to tell anyone.

In difficult times, I wandered alone, thinking, then still sought some spiritual belief to rely on. I wandered to temples to pray for blessings in my life, still kneeling before the altar of my ancestors.

And then, the Covid pandemic occurred at the end of 2019, the beginning of 2020, and all difficulties came crashing down. All the savings gradually ran out, and I had to take some jobs to make money for daily expenses that were not in my field of study to support the two of us in the city. All the dead ends during the severe pandemic made people desperate. I once had thoughts of selling blood for money, becoming a male escort to earn money—these were all desperate thoughts that appeared in my mind at the last resort of poverty—but I still managed to get through until the end of 2020.

At the beginning of 2021, the epidemic began to break out again. After a long period of unemployment and debt, after celebrating Tet, I received a message from a friend asking about my work situation. He introduced me to a company. During the severe epidemic, when money was hard to earn and debt was pressing, I decided to accept the job and travel for work. This was the time to go far from the big city, both to earn money and to isolate myself, and it was also during this time away that I had the opportunity to reflect on my life, read many books, and develop a deeper affinity with Buddhism. Although the job was difficult at first, due to economic pressure, I had toraising my sibling, taking care of myself, so I still try.

During this past year, while working, I also had time to separate myself from the hustle and bustle of the city to reflect on my life. One day during a break, I accidentally scrolled through TikTok and came across a video titled "The Mantra That Will Change Your Life Forever," which was a mantra in Tibetan Buddhism, "OM MANI PADME HUM." After reading that title, I closed my eyes and listened very attentively, falling asleep during the afternoon. And on that very day, I took the time to read about that mantra. The more I explored it, the more I was gradually guided. This was exactly the beginning of my spiritual awakening. I think that during the pandemic, when people had timeSlowing down, many people like me experience a very strong spiritual awakening. During the phase of purifying good and evil, even more people awaken spiritually, turn to Buddhism, karma, and are also guided by some kind of karmic connection to change.

The more I delved into it, the more I was guided in the right direction. From learning about mantras, spells, chanting Buddha's name, to copying the Kṣitigarbha Sutra. I started gradually learning to practice, and the deeper I went, the more karma I encountered due to heavy past karma and also because I was being tested on the path of spiritual development. Desires continued to arise, controlling me in thoughts and actions, preventing me from practicing, just as the sutras describe how the Buddha was disturbed, and demons interfered with practitioners. Although work was favorable as my boss greatly appreciated me, colleagues around me shifted from admiration to hatred, gossiping, and trying to causeharmful, causing all sorts of trouble, heavy pressure from many sides, and I understand that it is karma falling upon me. Still keep working, every night continue to read Sutras, copy the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, recite the Great Compassion Mantra, Lăng Nghiêm Mantra, persist daily.

After a period of copying the Kṣitigarbha Sutra, reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, and the Śūraṅgama Mantra, the opportunity came again, leading me to accidentally watch videos about vegetarianism. Then I began to explore vegetarianism. I practiced eating vegetarian, but it was very difficult because I wasn’t used to it. However, I still wanted to continue because my compassion was gradually increasing. Colleagues increasingly criticized, spoke ill of me, tried to disrupt my work, and mocked me for being vegetarian (since I was on a business trip far away, I was currently having meals with others).

By early 2022, when the pressures from work, disturbances from those around me, and even the desire to practice vegetarianism urged me, one night after copying the Kṣitigarbha Sutra and reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, I lay down thinking about my life, and just kept crying. Lying there crying and praying for guidance from Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, I asked them to lead me to change my workplace. And truly, a miracle happened once again: the next morning, a long-lost friend, who works in the same industry, called to ask about my work situation and whether I wanted to work in the city. After that event, I increasingly deeply believed in Buddhism and continued copying the Kṣitigarbha Sutra.

Tripitaka, recite the Great Compassion Mantra, the Śūraṅgama Mantra, and pray for daily repentance.

Continuing to accept a new job, a new company, preparing for the move to the city for work.

Regarding working in the city, I continued to be challenged. The new boss offered going out to eat, sing karaoke, drink alcohol, and engage with women, but I refused all of that from the beginning. Perhaps life continues to test me again. In the early days, the boss really disliked me and wanted to fire me, but I kept trying every day, remaining persistent. Every day I still copied the Kinh Dia Tang, repented, read the Great Compassion Mantra, and recited Buddha's name whenever possible, and my desires significantly decreased at that time. After working at the new company for a while, it was precisely the energy field from my practice that changed the work environment: people drank and sang less, and then the boss also changed, showing affection for me.

more, trust in work more because I can do the job. I understand that the less desire there is, the more intelligence grows, people are more trusted, and luck increases accordingly.

After a period of practicing, bad relationships almost completely fell apart and there was no more contact, while both old and new quality relationships began to reconnect in work. In August 2022, I received a phone call from a friend in the same field whom I had studied with at university and hadn’t spoken to for a long time. He asked me to collaborate on a project because his company lacked capability, hinting that he wanted me to introduce my boss to cooperate. And this was the first time in my life that I received 500 million VND in commission. I couldn’t believe it was real, but truly, after receiving that amount, I felt both happy and worried, asking myself questions in my mind.

that why money comes to my life at this time so suddenly and so much.

Continuing to practice, work, eat vegetarian, and using that money, I began to release animals, give away, and do charity to atone for all the mistakes I had caused. During these periods of practice, I studied and read a lot of books about changing destiny. I read Liễu Phàm Tứ Huấn, the An Sĩ Toàn Thư collection, Thái Thượng Cảm Ứng Thiên, Thọ Khang Bảo Giám…

The more I practice, the more I go in the right direction: eating vegetarian, meditating every night, reading sutras, confessing, copying Buddhist scriptures, releasing lives… my work becomes increasingly smooth. Working in the morning, reading sutras and meditating in the evening, life becomes more peaceful, I sleep deeply and only sleep 5 hours a day but feel no fatigue. Every morning I wake up by myself at 5 a.m., get up to read the Confession Sutra, and pay respects to the Buddha.

In November 2022, once again luck came into my life, three projects were introduced through friends' connections to bring back to our company for cooperation, with commissions shared reaching up to 1.6 billion.

Up until that point, I myself, from being a person stuck in difficulties, impoverished by years with the Tà Dâm people, could not have imagined that everything would change so dramatically for me.

During Tet 2023, perhaps good fortune came from my practice of Buddhism, as I was introduced to meet a girl simply because I went to get a haircut. The salon owner chatted with me while cutting my hair and casually asked if I had a girlfriend or wife and children yet. The owner said, "You look decent, haven't you got a girlfriend yet? I can introduce someone to you." I was also hesitant because I thought about the stains of my life, having committed the heavy sin of sexual misconduct, feeling too dirty, and I still had some self-consciousness. But I tried to push aside my feelings and asked for her number to get acquainted. And truly, it was fate, an arrangement I could hardly believe.

The girl was introduced as the daughter of a regular customer who often gets her hair done at the salon owner’s place. She is four years younger than me, in the university stage, also often doing charity work, participating in summer retreat courses, and studying Buddhist teachings. My girlfriend and I got to know each other for two months and decided to move towards marriage because we had a lot in common. Her family is also a well-educated, well-off family, but they never looked down on me, maybe because my karma still allowed me the luck I have today. Although there is still some sense of inferiority within me, I try to practice and transform it.

When my wife and I decided to get married, we received a lot of support from her family, including loaning us extra money for business. My wife and I lived in harmony, working together, doing business together, practicing spirituality together, and luck continued to come our way. From the time we got married until today, the day I am writing these heartfelt lines, I truly believe in the miraculous power of Buddha's teachings that have changed my life. A person who emerged from the mud with an unbelievable amount of assets, with a happy family, and about to welcome twin babies in 2024.

All these heartfelt confessions are shared from the bottom of my heart with everyone so that people can see the miracle of Buddhist teachings, practice, and karma is completely real. All the destinies in our lives can change in a positive direction, as long as we are persistent and sincerely willing to change.

Wishing everyone good practice! Namo Amitabha Buddha!
