tieu_de: THE GOD OF WEALTH DOES NOT TEACH YOU TO KILL AND GRILL CATFISH TO OFFER HIM! IF YOU WANT TO PRAY FOR WEALTH, YOU MUST GIVE CHARITY, ONLY GIVE
tom_tat: The karmic reward of wealth is almsgiving, offering, and helping sentient beings to be free from suffering and danger! Ancient books record: “Only the intelligent and righteous become Deities,” and the God of Wealth is precisely the “number one Meritorious Deity,” even if you have...
noi_dung:
THE GOD OF WEALTH DOES NOT TEACH YOU TO KILL GRILLED SNAKEHEAD FISH TO OFFER HIM! IF YOU WANT TO PRAY FOR PROSPERITY, YOU MUST GIVE CHARITY, ONLY GIVE

The karmic reward of wealth is giving alms, making offerings, and helping sentient beings escape suffering!

Ancient texts record: “Only the intelligent and upright can become Gods.” The God of Wealth is in fact “the foremost merit-worthy God.” Even if you offer countless amounts of gold, silver, and treasures in order to curry favor or flatter Him to grant you wealth and prosperity, He would still only shake His head. Let alone the flesh of sentient beings, like grilled snakehead fish?!

The God of Wealth does not teach you to kill and roast snakehead fish as an offering to Him. Doing so only shortens your own life, you cannot not know this! He only teaches you the way to become wealthy by setting an example: "When wealth accumulates, it must circulate; after circulating, it accumulates again, and after accumulating, it circulates again" (Money must flow to survive, just as water must flow to avoid stagnation.)

This means that when we have money, we should give charity and do good deeds (called "circulation"). Through giving and doing good deeds, we gain merit, so that when conducting business, money will return (called "accumulation").

Once again, there is the rush to buy gold on the day of the God of Wealth to wish for luck, so among all the people who go to buy gold on that day, how many are truly lucky? As for those who are not lucky, would they blame the God of Wealth?

It is truly superstition to the extreme! "People nowadays accept falsehood rather than truth, like to hear deceiving words rather than heed wise advice," this is indeed true. As soon as they hear something is beneficial, they rush to follow it blindly and believe it. Why not calmly and thoroughly consider the cause and effect? You can't expect to eat fruit without planting the tree, how can there be such logic?

If you want wealth, you must give alms; this is a clear and practical law of cause and effect, but how many are willing to believe it?

Please always recite Amitabha Buddha - Keep a Kind Heart, Peace to the World.

Welcome to the dissemination, boundless merit. Namo Amitabha Buddha.

tieu_de: MANI BUDDHA SPELL BÁT DI HỒNG (OM MANI PADME HUM)
tom_tat: Even if you do not know much about Buddhism, even if the only thing you know is Om Mani Padme Hum, the happiest life is still a life lived with an attitude of liberation from the eight worldly concerns.
noi_dung:
MANI MANTRA OF MA NI PADME HONG (OM MANI PADME HUM)

Even if you do not know much about Dharma, even if the only thing you know is Om Mani Padme Hum, the happiest life is still a life lived with an attitude free from the eight worldly concerns.

If you live your life with a pure attitude free from attachment to this life and simply dedicate your life to reciting Om Mani Padme Hum — this six-syllable mantra is the essence of the entire Dharma — then that is the purest Dharma. The practice of recitation seems very simple, very easy.

But if you think about its benefits, it is not entirely simple. Here I will only refer to the core of its infinite benefits.

Reciting the compassionate Buddha's mantra even once will completely purify the breakage of the four fundamental vows of Individual Liberation and the five negative karmas that are uninterrupted.

In the tantras, it is also mentioned that by reciting this mantra, you will achieve four qualities that allow you to be reborn in the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha and other Pure Lands; at the time of death, you will see the Buddha and light appearing in the sky; the deities will offer you their homage; and you will never be reborn in hells, hungry ghost realms, or animal realms. You will be reborn in the Buddha’s Pure Land or as a favorable reborn being.

When a person recites ten strings of mantras a day while swimming, whether in a river, the sea, or any other aquatic creature, the water that touches that person will also be blessed.

We also know that the person's seven generations of ancestors (Nine generations, seven ancestors) were not reborn in lower realms. This is thanks to the power of the mantra, with the body being blessed by those who recite the mantra and visualize their body in the divine form like Chenrezig (Avalokiteshvara). As a result, the body becomes very strong, full of blessings to the extent that it affects the mind for seven generations, and consequently, if the person dies with an unwholesome thought, they will not be reborn in a lower realm.

Therefore, when a person recites ten strings of Om Mani Padme Hum every day and goes down to a river or the sea, the water that touches that person's body is blessed, and then the blessed water will purify trillions of beings in the water. This person helps the creatures in that water escape from unimaginable suffering in the lower realms. This act is so beneficial that it is hard to believe.

When a person like that walks down a road, the wind touches their body and then continues to touch insects, purifying their negative karma and thereby allowing them a good rebirth. Similarly, when a person like that touches the body of another person, the negative karma of those people is also purified.

The act of a person like that gazing is truly meaningful; being seen and touched becomes a means to liberate sentient beings. This means that even the breath of that person touching the body of another sentient being purifies their negative karma. Any living being that drinks water in which a person like that has once swum is also purified.

We are unusually fortunate to have encountered the Dharma and have the opportunity to recite and meditate on the Compassionate Buddha. It is an easy method to purify any negative karma we have accumulated, not only in this life but also in many past lives.

Because we have encountered the Buddha Dharma and especially this method - the practice of the Compassionate Buddha and reciting His mantra - it is truly easy to purify negative karma and accumulate vast merit, thereby achieving enlightenment. We are incredibly fortunate beyond expectation.

Thus, there is nothing more foolish than refusing to take advantage of this great opportunity. In general, we continuously distract ourselves and waste our lives. Moreover, every action done with a self-centered mind and a consciousness tainted by the three poisons—greed, hatred, and ignorance—creates negative karma, which is the cause of suffering. Throughout our lives, there is nothing more foolish than using this perfect human body solely to create suffering.

In places like Tibet, Nepal, India, and Ladakh, there has long been a beautiful tradition of undertaking retreats focused on the Compassionate Buddha and reciting 100 million Om Mani Padme Hum mantras. The retreat held at the Chenrezig Institute was the first such retreat to be conducted in the West and the first retreat within the FPMT organization (Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition). This takes place there once a year - only once a year!

If you are tormented by guilt in your life, you can overcome that emotion through purification by attending this retreat course. The retreat not only involves reciting mantras with sadhanas but also includes observing the Eight Mahayana Precepts, if not daily then at least regularly. Any merit you accumulate during that day will grow a hundred thousand times. This becomes an easy and quick method to purify, accumulate vast merit, attain enlightenment, and liberate sentient beings from unimaginable suffering, swiftly leading them to enlightenment.

Attending a mani retreat (Six Syllable Mantra) is an incredibly lucky opportunity. Even if you cannot be present for the entire retreat, you can still participate for two months, one month, or at least a few weeks. You could even attend for just one week. I particularly hope that this retreat will be held in Mongolia, because their main diet is meat and too many animals are killed there every day. This practice helps to purify that. Once our monasteries in Mongolia are completed, I hope that thousands of people will attend mani retreats there. Gradually, I hopewant to lock this room can also be organized in many other places in the West.

This retreat also blesses the nation where it is held and brings much peace, happiness, and prosperity.

Even if you understand the teachings on how to meditate on the Bodhichitta, you still need to receive the special blessings of the Root Deity, the Compassionate Buddha. You receive these blessings by engaging in the meditation and recitation practices that we perform in the Mani retreat. In this way, reciting Om Mani Padme Hum is a practice to embody Bodhichitta – to transform your mind into Bodhichitta and make your meditation on Bodhichitta more effective.

In general, according to my experience, at my parish in Solu Khumbu in the Himalayas in Nepal, there are people who live their lives reciting Om Mani Padme Hum but have no notion of emptiness – not even in words. Although they cannot read and do not even know the alphabet, they have great devotion to compassion and the Bodhicitta and live their lives in the recitation of Om Mani Padme Hum. Such people have a warm heart, extremely good-natured, and immensely compassionate. This is evidence from my experience that it is effective in transforming the mind into a heart.good and merciful.

Without Bodhicitta, you cannot bring happiness to all sentient beings. You cannot perform perfect deeds for all sentient beings; and you cannot achieve the wholesome qualities concerning realizations and cessation, even for yourself.

Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche

Translated by: Thanh Lien

Original text: The Benefits of Chanting Om Mani Padme Hum

*******************************

P/s What is the effect of the mantra Om Mani Padme Hum?

This is surely a question that many people are interested in when learning about this mantra. Reciting the Om Mani Padme Hum mantra brings many benefits to the practitioner, such as:

Praying to Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva to help sentient beings, bringing peace and dispelling all suffering and worries.

Enhancing compassion, bringing good luck and peace.

Helping illness to dissipate, driving away evil spirits, and increasing happiness.

Increase strength and enhance physical fitness, develop the level of meditation.

When a person recites the mantra Om Mani Padme Hum for deceased relatives, it will help them be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss and gradually achieve Buddhahood.

In the tantras, it is mentioned that when reciting the mantra Om Mani Padme Hum, what effects it has, you will obtain four qualities to be born into the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha. These are the Pure Lands where you are reborn (reincarnated) as good beings.

When at the moment of death one sees the Buddha and a light appearing in the sky, the deities offer respects so that one will never be reborn in the hell realms. In addition, when chanting the mantra, the body will be blessed by Avalokiteshvara. Therefore, the body becomes strong and full of blessings.

Collected

tieu_de: KARMA AND THE MANTRA 'ELIMINATE KARMIC DESTINY VERSE' OF BODHISATTVA Kṣitigarbha
tom_tat: On the occasion of the holy day of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, CST NT would like to share about the meaning of KARMA and its miraculousness: ELIMINATING DEFINITE KARMA THROUGH TRUE MANTRA. Currently online, there are also many fellow practitioners sharing the efficacy when reciting
noi_dung:
KARMA AND THE MANTRA "ERADICATE KARMIC DESTINY" OF BODHISATTVA Kṣitigarbha

On the occasion of the memorial day of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, CST NT would like to share about the meaning of KARMIC DEEDS and the miraculous: ERADICATING AND SETTLING KARMIC DEEDS WITH THE TRUE MANTRA.

Currently online, there are also many fellow practitioners sharing the efficacy when reciting this mantra, especially Mr. Quang Tử.

☘️In the scriptures, it is recorded that during the Ming Dynasty, in the reign of Chongzhen: Li Zicheng caused chaos, making life very miserable; the lands in Central Plains experienced crop failures and severe abandonment. At that time, the Great Master Ngau Yik, a high-ranking monk residing on Mount Jiuhua, held a 100-day altar ceremony, reciting the Kṣitigarbha Determination Karma Mantra 5 million times. Afterwards, he also summoned disciples from the four assemblies to recite it together 1 billion times. This had a significant effect in eliminating the calamities of war at the end of the Ming Dynasty.

Many people also recite this mantra in their daily rituals.

☀️1. CHARACTERISTICS OF KARMA

Karma, in Pali, Kamma, and in Sanskrit, Karma, means action or deed. All intentional actions of a being, whether of body, speech, or mind, are called karma.

Nowadays, many people misunderstand KARMA according to the teachings of the World-Honored One, or misuse this term, using it inappropriately.

Author Trinh Nguyen Phuoc has compiled three characteristics of KARMA according to Buddhism.

"Karma like this means action, but according to the spirit of Buddhism, it is not just any action:

☘️1- First, it is an INTENTIONAL ACTION, that is, there must be a will to act, an intention.

This important point was emphasized by the Buddha himself: 'Monks! It is intention (cetana) that I call karma (cetanaham bhikkhave kammam vadami). Because through intention, one acts with body, speech, and mind...'

(Anguttara Nikaya, Saṃyutta Nikaya VI).

Volition (cetana, volition) belongs to the formations (samkhara, mental formations), one of the five aggregates (upadana khanda) that temporarily come together to form an individual and are constantly changing. This group includes 52 formations, including will, attention, concentration, effort, desire, faith, anger, pride, delusion, etc. Volition functions to direct the mind (citta, mental) in actions that are good, bad, or neutral, and thus is equivalent to karma, the will to live, the continuation of existence, becoming.

Thus, an accidental, unintentional action is not karma. This is the fundamental difference compared to Brahmanism, Hinduism, and Jainism. For a follower of Hinduism or Jainism, even an unintentional act generates karma. If that person inadvertently steps on and kills an animal, they have created bad karma. But for a Buddhist, that action does not create karma, because there was no intention to kill. Everything arises from the Mind, as stated in the opening verse of the Dhammapada:

"Among all things, the Mind leads, the mind rules, the mind creates. If karma is made by speech or action with a defiled mind, suffering will follow the karma like a wheel follows the foot of the animal pulling the cart."

"Among all things, the Mind leads, the mind rules, the mind creates. If karma is made by speech or action with a pure mind, happiness will follow the karma like a shadow follows the form."

☘️2- Second, contrary to a common belief among the public, KARMA IS NOT THE RESULT OF THE ACTION THAT CREATES KARMA.

Karma should not be understood in a negative sense, as the consequence of an action that one must endure. In Mahayana countries, influenced by Sino-Vietnamese terms such as "nghiệp quả" (karma result), "quả báo" (retribution), "nghiệp chướng" (karmic obstacles), people often confuse karma with the result. For example, people often say: "That is my karma. I am paying for the mistakes in my previous life." This is completely wrong, because KARMA IS THE ACTION itself, not its result. Moreover, in the spirit of Buddhism, the result of an action is never a reward or punishment imposed by any power: God, spirits, or supernatural forces.naturally, influenced by external factors.

According to Bhikkhu Nyanatiloka, "Believing that following Buddhism everything is the result of past actions is completely wrong… Karma in Buddhism does not mean the result of an action, and certainly is not the fate of a person or even of an entire nation…".

☘️3- Third, it is a good (or wholesome) action, kusala, or conversely bad (or unwholesome), akusala. "Good" or "bad" DOES NOT RELY ON MORAL or LEGAL STANDARDS but on the mind, concerning the suffering (dukkha) it may cause.

A "good" action (kusala) is an action that frees from suffering, a "bad" action (akusala) is an action that leads to suffering. In contrast, an action that is neither good nor bad, called neutral, is not karma and does not generate karma.

Thus, we should not forget these three main characteristics of karma according to Buddhism: actions motivated by intention, leading to "good" or "bad" results, and not being the result of an action.

It can be said that karma in Buddhism includes psychological and ethical aspects, while karma in Brahmanism - Hinduism has ritualistic and metaphysical characteristics.

☀️2. THE MECHANISM OF KARMA: Follow the LAW OF CAUSE AND EFFECT!

According to the mechanism of karma, creating good causes leads to good effects, and creating bad causes leads to bad effects. When a cause has matured and the time for experiencing its effect has come, it becomes like a force beyond one's intention, and at that point, trying to change its result cannot be done in time. This is called Predetermined Karma.

Regarding classification, according to the Treatise of Yogācāra, definite karma and indefinite karma can be categorized into 3 types:

The first is definite and indefinite regarding the result:

The second is definite and indefinite regarding the time.

The third is definite and indefinite regarding both the time and the karmic result.

☀️3. HOW TO PROPERLY RECITE MANTRAS:

The Blessed One Himself, along with many other gurus, have spoken about this, and I will summarize it for everyone to note:

☘️*. Keep the precepts pure: By keeping the precepts pure in body, speech, and mind, many results of karma have no conditions to arise.

☘️*. Venerable H.T Tuyen Hoa explained as follows:

"If you only remember the Mantra, learn the Mantra simply, but neither RECITE nor CHANT it, it will have no effect at all!

You NEED TO CHANT! 'CHANT' means to depart from books, without looking at the books while reciting; while 'RECITE' means to persist, regularly, without interruption.

"Reciting the Dhāraṇī" means reciting every day—it is not that today you recite, then tomorrow you do not, and the day after that you continue to recite...

If today you recite 108 times, then tomorrow you must also recite 108 times, and the day after that you must recite 108 times—day after day continuously, regularly, diligently reciting without stopping—that is what is meant by "reciting and upholding"; if interrupted, it does not have the meaning of "reciting and upholding"!

☘️*. When reciting the mantra, the most important thing is to maintain purity in BODY - SPEECH - MIND:

🌷BODY: One must maintain personal hygiene, bathe regularly, change into clean clothes, and not allow the body to have a bad odor. Before reciting mantras, one should also brush their teeth, rinse their mouth, and wash their hands thoroughly.

One should sit upright, with the back straight and facing forward.

🌷SPEECH: Upon entering the place of chanting, do not laugh or talk. The only words should be the mantra sounds!

The mantra sounds should be chanted loudly, with a deep and robust tone, quickly and continuously, taking breath from the abdomen.

Huynh ‎Lê Nguyễn Quỳnh shares 6 ways of chanting (you can refer to them).

🌷Meaning: The most important thing is to focus on the mind while chanting, without distractions.

When chanting mantras, we should maintain a positive, joyful, and relaxed feeling. Do not be too tense.

Regarding visualization, some practitioners advise:

"When reciting the mantra, you must visualize your mind transforming into a pure, full, and clear moon. Above the moon of the mind, imagine there is a blue letter 'HRIH.' The letter 'HRIH' radiates light that spreads to all beings in their karma, who possess karmic imprints that even the Buddhas do not allow to be atoned for, thereby purifying them all.

☘️* THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IS:

When reciting the mantra, dedicate the merit of this practice to all beings for their enlightenment and happiness. Do not do it solely for personal benefit or in pursuit of fame and profit.

☘️When reciting the mantra of any Buddha or Bodhisattva, it is necessary to remember and reflect on their great deeds and vows. Only then will the blessings of them and the Dharma protectors be at their strongest.

As recorded in the Sutra about the great supreme power of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: “This virtuous male has fully accomplished innumerable and unparalleled supreme merits, constantly diligently advancing, benefiting and bringing joy to all sentient beings. In the past, he was in the presence of countless Tathāgatas in the heavens and elsewhere. In order to perfectly benefit and bring joy to sentient beings, he aroused an unbreakable great compassion, acted courageously and diligently, with endless vows, and attained unsurpassed steadfast spiritual power. In a single day and night or even a single meal, he could liberate countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings of various types from all kinds of suffering, along withmaking everything as France had wished to fulfill their desire

He made the GREAT VOW:

"Hell is not yet empty, the Vow is not fulfilled to Buddhahood.

Only when all sentient beings are saved, Then enlightenment is attained."

☀️4. YE DING KARMIC TRUE MANTRA

This mantra has many versions:

* Chinese transliteration:

"Ông, bát la ma ninh, đả ninh, thoa cáp"

* Sanskrit transliteration:

OṂ_ PARAMANI DHANĪ SVĀHĀ

But I was taught that this version:

OṂ _ PRAMAṆI-PATI _ SVÀHÀ

☀️5. ORIGIN AND MEANING:

This mantra is based on the recordings of the Dharani Scripture, specifically the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Dharmakaya Seal Mantra. Its meaning conveys: to restore, to eliminate, to break into dust all karmic offenses, sinful obstacles, and evil deeds… Therefore, since ancient times, this mantra has been called the Mantra for Eradicating and Fixing Karmic Obstructions. Practicing this mantra can allow one to mutually enter and integrate with the Dharmakaya of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, merging into one.

_Reciting the Mantra of Extinguishing Fixed Karma is the most supreme place, using it to pray for the Great Vow Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva's compassionate protection... only then can all Fixed Karma, Collective Karma, Karmic Obstacles be alleviated and transformed, and merit and wisdom be increased.

NAMO GREAT COMPASSION, GREAT VOW, GREAT SAINT, GREAT MERCY ORIGINAL HONORED ONE KṣITIGARBHA KING BODHISATTVA MAHĀTATHĀGATA

tom_tat: During the Tang dynasty, there was a monk named Phap Thuong, who became a monk at the age of thirty, residing at Hue Nhat Pagoda in Hoa Prefecture, belonging to China. Before Phap Thuong practiced Buddhism, he often went hunting. One day, weaving
noi_dung:
LISTENING TO THE WORDS OF BODHISATTVA KṢITIGARBHA, REMEMBERING THE BUDDHA WILL IMMEDIATELY LEAD TO REBIRTH IN THE PURE LAND.

During the Tang Dynasty, there was a monk named Phap Thuong, who became a monk at the age of thirty, living in Hue Nhat Pagoda, Hoa Prefecture, belonging to China. Before Phap Thuong practiced cultivation, he often went hunting.

One day, while chasing some animals in the middle of the green forest, he suddenly saw on a high, dry piece of land, with lush grass and plants, a dazzling light that made him stop to look, feeling strangely puzzled, not understanding what this sign meant. He then jumped down to the ground, led his horse to tie it to a tree, and went to the place of the light to observe for a long time, but saw nothing other than a completely decayed piece of wood, only a core about a foot long lying in the grass. Seeing this, Mr. Pháp Thượng paid no attention to it and untied his horse to return home, as it was already dark.

The next time, also on the occasion of chasing an animal running in that direction again, Mr. Pháp Thượng saw a bright halo just like before. Feeling it was strange in his heart, he dismounted, approached, and carried a tree trunk to place it on the fork of a large old tree nearby, then turned his horse back.

Suddenly, while walking along the road, he encountered a tiger chasing him, baring its fangs and swinging its claws, frightening the horse so much that it reared, while he fell to the ground, seeing the tiger ready to pounce on him. In a moment of panic that left him dazed, he suddenly saw a monk coming from afar, vigorously driving the tiger away, which, frightened, ran into the forest.

Pháp Thượng, having escaped the danger, knelt on the ground to thank the monk and asked:

- Master! I do not know who you are, why did you have to go through this forest to encounter my accident and exert yourself to rescue me like this?

That monk replied:

- I am Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Long ago, your great-grandfather established a temple in this forest and created a statue of me for worship. Over the long years, no one inherited the responsibility to maintain it, so the temple fell into ruin, leaving nothing at all. My statue also decayed, leaving only a core. Because you have a sincere heart, placing that core on the tree branch brings some merit within the Three Jewels, so I manifested here to save you and help you escape the tiger's danger!

As soon as the monk finished speaking, he disappeared. Mr. Pháp Thượng was very joyful and resolved to repent, embracing faith in Buddhism and giving up his hunting profession. Later, he brought craftsmen to the foundation of the old temple to rebuild it into a new temple named Huệ Nhật, and took the wooden Kṣitigarbha statue that had decayed but retained its core, repairing it to enshrine it with great reverence.

When he was 78 years old, on the 24th day of the 2nd lunar month, being in good health, he invited fellow practitioners to gather and said:

- The Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha revealed to me: "You are the person who attained the Dharma in the second Dharma assembly of the Tathāgata of Mercy. Therefore, after passing away, you will be reborn in the Heaven of Tusita."

I then replied that that Heaven is a realm with all five types of desires, an unparalleled pleasure, so I fear being deluded and losing the Bodhi mind; it is better that presently I vow to be reborn in the Western Paradise.

Hearing me express the main idea like that, Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha said: "As you wish! If you want to be reborn in the Pure Land, you must focus on reciting Amitabha Buddha daily with a single, undisturbed mind; only then is there hope of being reborn in that realm."

I obeyed the instruction and have been constantly reciting the Buddha. Now I am about to be reborn in the Pure Land, so I advise good friends to strive to recite the Buddha!

As these words were finished, Dharma Master Pháp Thượng sat facing west, clasped his hands in recitation of the Buddha, and then peacefully passed away.

Excerpt from "Miraculous Stories of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva"

Source: Phatgiao. org. vn

noi_dung:
LESSON ON PLANTING TREES

🌿When we plant a tree, and the tree does not grow well, we do not blame the tree, but look into the reasons why it is so: lack of water, lack of fertilizer, or lack of sunlight.

However, when we have problems with friends or family, we blame them. If we know how to care for them, they will also "grow well", like trees. Blaming someone is completely meaningless, as is arguing.

That is my experience. Not blaming anyone, not arguing, just simply understanding. If we understand the problem, and express that understanding, we will always be able to love, and that problem will be solved.☘️

(Zen Master Thich Nhat Hanh)

--------------------------------

Discussion: In life, when something undesirable happens, we often try to find a reason to blame someone or something else, usually because our ego cannot admit that we are wrong. However, if we can calmly reflect, in reality, all the good and bad things that happen to us in life are due to ourselves. Friends or colleagues treating you badly or often criticizing you is likely because your way of dealing with people is not good enough. For example, if you treat them very well but they still treat you poorly, you should know that you and they have harbored enmity across many previous lifetimes leading up to this place.Repaying karma is not just about treating them well for a while and expecting them to love you; cause and effect are inherently fair. For example, if you happen to become wealthy and others think it’s due to some luck or thanks to some person, in reality, you should know that if your merit is not great enough, you would not be able to receive it. Therefore, whatever happens in life, whether favorable or adverse, we should calmly accept it, keep a balanced mind, always observe cause and effect, and most importantly, do not blame ordinary people for judging our mistakes. This is also one of the important virtues if later you want to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss!

Respectfully sending to dear fellow practitioners with karmic affinity!

Ngộ Quang Từ

NAM MO A DI DA PHAT

tieu_de: THE EFFICACY OF THE AMITABHA MANTRA
tom_tat: The Vānarāja Recitation was extracted from the scripture 『Bat Nhat The Nghiep Chong Can Ban Dac Sinh Tinh Do Da Ra Ni』. Reciting this mantra means to eliminate the five grave offenses, the ten evils, and blasphemy of the Dharma. Reciting this mantra is to support not
noi_dung:
THE EFFICACY OF THE AMITABHA MANTRA

The Rebirth Mantra is extracted from the Sutra of Eliminating the Fundamental Obstacles to Attaining the Pure Land through Zen Mantras. Reciting this mantra is to eliminate grave sins, the five heinous crimes, the ten evil acts, and blasphemy. Reciting this mantra supports preventing wandering spirits from causing harm, ensures peaceful rebirth, and allows one to meet Amitabha Buddha. The rebirth mantra has truly miraculous efficacy, but it is also very secret, true to its name "secret mantra," making it difficult to perceive the divine manifestation of its words.

THE STORY WAS TOLD BY A BUDDHIST LIVING IN CALIFORNIA

“In 2005, I had a younger sibling who was seriously ill and was admitted for treatment at Stanford Hospital. After undergoing treatment at the hospital, my sibling was discharged. Being discharged did not mean going home, but had to stay for 3 months in a rented apartment right on the hospital campus to be present at the hospital every day for the doctors to monitor their condition, with the requirement that a family member must always be by their side. So my siblings and I had to take turns, each staying for a period to look after the patient.”

I am retired, so I volunteered to look after for two weeks. The rented room is a small house on the third floor, with a living room, dining room, and bedroom, but to let the patient have peace, I sleep in the living room on the sofa. The first two nights I slept comfortably, but on the third night, just as I lay down and turned off the light for a moment, still half-asleep, I suddenly saw a large number of people coming from afar.

I suddenly thought there was a protest, but I quickly realized that I was on the 3rd floor, so how could there be so many people moving like that? I was a bit scared, hurriedly chanted Buddha's name, and gradually the crowd dispersed, thinning out, though some still flickered in sight. Then I recited the Amitabha mantra for rebirth, once, twice, three, four, five times, and then there was no shadow of anyone left.

Although it is effective, I still do not dare to think that the rebirth mantra has helped the dark shadows disappear. But then once again, I witnessed the efficacy of the rebirth mantra, once again I had to believe that indeed there is yin and yang, and the rebirth mantra is truly miraculous.

About 2 years ago, I attended a retreat course at a place about two hours' drive from the city. The course ran from Thursday noon to Sunday noon, which is 2 days and 2 nights. The retreat center is very large, consisting of two buildings: one with spacious rooms equipped with all amenities for the students to stay and dine; further away is the second building with a large hall used for the course. After registering and paying, the four of us were assigned to a spacious room with clean beds and mattresses, glass windows all around offering a view of nothing but vast empty fields. Once we had settled in, we hurried across aThe walkway was quite long to cross over to the hall for the ceremony. In the evening, after dinner, everyone was exhausted, hurriedly getting ready to sleep because tomorrow, Friday, the ritual begins at 5 a.m.

At four o'clock the next morning, the alarm rang, and we excitedly called each other to get up and get ready to go to the hall. Stepping out of the room, the wind was biting cold, yet we could already see many fellow practitioners gathering in small groups, enthusiastically setting off to practice. Then throughout Friday, from 5 a.m. until evening, except for two meal breaks, we were continuously busy, either following the ceremony, listening to lectures, walking meditation, or listening to Dharma talks. Although it was very enjoyable, by the time we returned to our room, we were... exhausted. So we agreed to go to bed early to gain energy for the next day, both to follow the lessons and to prepare for the closing ceremony of the course.

The lights in the room had just gone out, I had just laid down, still thinking about tomorrow’s class, when I suddenly saw some dark figures moving around the room, then saw larger black figures dressed all in black leaving and then coming back. My whole body felt frozen, my eyes watched while my limbs felt numb, when suddenly a large dark figure bent down and looked at my face. I quickly woke up and recited out of habit, "Nam Mo A Di Da ba da, da tha gia da da da diet gia tha…" then remembered that I was chanting the rebirth mantra. So I continued chanting non-stop, "A di ri do ba ty, A di ri da tat dam ba ty.." and kept reading continuously, once, twice, then three-four-five times.I don't remember much, until I opened my eyes and there was no shadow left. Rest assured, I fell asleep until the alarm clock rang.

That morning, I kept thinking about the scene from last night, but I didn’t dare tell my fellow practitioners in the same room because they were younger than me, and I didn’t want to scare them.

The next day was Saturday, the second day of the course and also the last day. The schedule was the same as before, but with an added section for the closing performance, so everyone seemed busier. And in the evening after class, after the performance, we returned to the room quite late, so everyone hurriedly packed their belongings and turned off the lights to sleep early in order to leave the next morning.

Saturday night was very peaceful. I was half-asleep, listening to the steady breathing of my little friends lying in the bed next to me, when suddenly I saw many white shadows appearing and disappearing. There were quite a few of them, gently hovering around the room. Some had the look of wearing white shirts, some appeared to be in full suits. I realized that... they had come to visit. I didn't feel scared like last night; instead, I calmly chanted the rebirth mantra and silently prayed for their peaceful transcendence. This time I only chanted three times, and they... had already left. I felt at ease and slept until morning.

Because it was the last night, I only told the ladies about the story of having... visitors for two consecutive nights. Perhaps they were restless souls lingering here, and when they saw strangers, they came to visit. Fortunately, I had some experience, so I calmly recited the rebirth mantra to help them attain liberation, exactly according to the meaning of reciting the rebirth mantra:

"Reciting the rebirth mantra means eliminating the grave sins of the five heinous acts, the ten evils, and blasphemy, supporting the prevention of harm from restless souls, attaining peaceful rebirth, and having the opportunity to meet Amitabha Buddha."

Through my near-death experience during Hurricane Katrina, and through several times seeing black and white shadows appear, each time I witnessed the miraculous efficacy of chanting the Rebirth Mantra, I can only sincerely acknowledge the ancient saying "Where there is a prayer, there will be a response" is indeed true, and I bow with all my heart in reverent belief in the miraculous effectiveness of the mantras.

Rebirth Mantra in Sanskrit

1. Namo Amitàbhàya (Pronunciation: Na-mo A-mi-ta-pha-gia)

2. Tathàgatàya (Pronunciation: Ta-tha-ga-ta-gia)

3. Tadyathà (Pronunciation: Ta-di-gia-tha)

4. Amrto dbhave (Pronunciation: A-mờ-rật-tô đờ-pha-vê)

5. Amrta sambhave (Pronunciation: A-mờ-rật-ta sam-pha-vê)

6. Amrta vikrànte (Pronunciation: A-mờ-rật-ta vi-kờ-răm-tê)

7. Amrta vikrànta gamini (Pronunciation: A-mờ-rật-ta vi-kờ-răm-ta ga-mi-ni)

8. Gagana kìrtti kare Svàhà (Pronunciation: Ga-ga-na kít-ti ka-rê Sờ-va-ha)

Vietnamese Version of the Vãng Sanh Text

1. I take refuge in Infinite Light (Amitabha)

2. Tathagata

3. Thus, immediately recite the Mantra as

4. Sweet Dew appears

5. Sweet Dew arises

6. Sweet Dew is mighty

7. Reaching Mighty Sweet Dew

8. Spreads throughout the Void, accomplishing auspiciousness

Thus, Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in the Dharma assembly at Mount Ling requested the World-Honored One to expound the Rebirth Mantra for the sake of sentient beings in the latter age of the Dharma.

According to the Bodhisattva's teaching, if anyone vows to be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss but, due to scant merit and heavy karma, cannot focus single-mindedly on reciting the Buddha's name, they can rely on the merits of the Rebirth Mantra to fulfill their vow. Practitioners who observe the precepts, keep the three karmas—body, speech, and mind—pure, and recite the mantra six times daily, 21 repetitions each time, will surely eliminate all karmic obstacles, even those of the five grave offenses or ten heinous sins.

The mantra of rebirth has such importance, so those who practice the Pure Land method always recite it with the aim of being reborn in the Land of Bliss.

According to the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sutra of Buddha Remembrance, Chapter 7 (translated by Venerable Thích Thiền Tâm), Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, out of compassion for sentient beings in the Dharma's declining age, spoke this dharani to facilitate their swift rebirth in the Pure Land: “At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra addressed the Buddha, saying: 'World-Honored One! I now, out of compassion for sentient beings in the declining age of the Dharma—when lifespans are short, merits are lacking, and disorder and defilements increase, with very few truly practicing—will grant this dharani of Buddha remembrance to people to protect their body and mind, eradicate karmic obstacles at the root, eliminate afflictions, and quickly attain rebirth in Ultimate Bliss; it is called the Dharani That Completely Eliminates All Karmic Obstructions.'The Dharani for Rebirth in the Pure Land. Then recite the mantra: Namo Amitabha, Tathagata, Tathata, Adi Riddhopa, Adi Rida Sattambha, Adi Ridata Kalan De, Adi Ridatya Kalan Da, Jini, Jina, Jina, Chida Kala, Tathahaha.

Those who recite the Buddha's name must keep precepts, eat vegetarian, and purify body, speech, and mind. Day and night, at six times, recite 21 repetitions each time. In this way, one eliminates the four gravest sins, the five heinous acts, the ten evil deeds, and the slandering of the True Dharma. One is often visited by Amitabha Buddha appearing above the head. Life is peaceful and blessed. At the final breath, one can be reborn according to one's wish. By reciting up to thirty thousand repetitions, one immediately sees the Buddha before them.

Traditionally, most practitioners of the Pure Land practice often recite the Rebirth Mantra according to the Chinese phonetic transcription. We can recite it in the original Sanskrit (transliterated) and also explore a little about the "meaning" of this mantra.

Chinese Rebirth Mantra

(Commonly recited in temples)

Nam-mô a di đa bà dạ

1. Ða tha dà đa dạ

2. Ða điệt dạ tha.

3. A di rị đô bà tỳ

4. A di ri da tat dam ba ty

5. A di ri da ti ca lan de

6. A di ri da, ti ca lan da

7. Da di ni da da na

8. Chi da ca le. Ta ba ha.

Collected.

tieu_de: SECRETS USED FREQUENTLY
tom_tat: Wishing you a year with everything as you wish, good fortune and peace, luck and prosperity, health and happiness 🫶🙏🏻🪷 These are the mantras that Na frequently recites and are very powerful, so happily sharing
noi_dung:
FREQUENTLY USED SPELLS

Wishing you a year with all things as desired, auspicious peace, prosperous luck, health and happiness 🫶🙏🏻🪷

These are the sacred mantras of Na that are frequently recited and have powerful effects, so I am happy to share them with you 🙏🏻

1. Blessing mantra for the prayer beads:

OM RUCHIRA MANI PRAVARTAYA HUM (7x)

Pronounced as

Om ru chi na ma ni pờ ra va ta ya hung

Recite this mantra 7 times and then blow it onto the prayer beads.

This will increase the power of the mantras you recite by 10 million times.

This is mentioned in the sutra: Unfathomable Celestial Mansion, Great Increasing Jewel.

2. The following mantra has the effect of increasing the offerings millions of times; even if you offer just a little, countless offerings will appear in space:

OM NAMO BHAGAVATE VAJRA SARA PRAMARDANE / TO THE TATHAGATA / ARHAT / PERFECTLY ENLIGHTENED ONE

TO THE BUDDHA / THUS / OM VAJRA VAJRA / GREAT VAJRA / GREAT RADIANT VAJRA / GREAT WISDOM

VAJRA / GREAT BODHICHITTA VAJRA / GREAT BODHI MANDALA ASCENSION VAJRA / ALL

KARMA OBSTRUCTION POISON DESTRUCTION VAJRA SVĀHĀ (X3)

Homage to the Blessed One / Vajra / the essence / supreme crusher / Tathagata / Arhat / perfectly enlightened Buddha

Ta ya tha/ om va chờ rê/ va chờ rê/ ma ha va chờ rê/ ma ha tê ja va chờ rê/ ma ha vít ya va chờ rê/ ma ha bô đi chi ta va chờ rê/

Maha bô đi man đô pa săm kờ ra ma na va chờ rê/

Sa va ka ma a va ra na vít shô đa na va chờ rê sô ha (x3)

3. The purification mantra, eliminating karmic obstacles.

This mantra has immense power and was explained by Buddha for many benefits in the Kangyur.

For example, if you recite it seven times a day and benefit others, then when death occurs, you have the opportunity to go to a pure land.

If you recite it and blow it onto incense sticks, perfume, or clothing, then those who come into contact with the scent or fabric receive healing and purification of negative karma, and if you place it above a door, anyone who passes beneath it will purify 1,000 lifetimes of bad karma.

Usually, in these monasteries, this mantra is hung on the door. When hands are dirty, and there is no water to wash but you want to touch the sacred objects, you can recite this mantra to purify yourself.

Or when women are menstruating, they should also recite this mantra.

OM PADMO USHNISHA BIMALI HUM PHAT

Pronounced as: Om pat mo u nit sha bi ma li hum pet

4. The mantra that blesses meat:

Recite it 7 times and then blow on the meat or fish before eating.

This mantra transforms meat into divine offerings

The practitioner will not incur much heavy negative karma from eating meat or fish.

Om Ah Bira Khe Chara Hum (7 times)

It is read as

Om a bi ra kê cha ra hung

I myself am a vegetarian, but if I go to the market or eat with friends, I will recite this mantra.

5. Detox Mantra

When reading and blowing onto food, it will neutralize diseases (diarrhea…), spoilage, and toxins. It is recommended to recite this chant when eating unfamiliar food or traveling...

“Án, tam bạt la dà đa, ta bà ha”.

6. Heart Mantra of Vajra

At the end of the day before going to sleep, one should recite the heart mantra ''Om Benza Sat tô Hum” to immediately purify the negative karma created during the day. Or when one has just committed a wrongdoing, one can recite the heart mantra 21 times with a repentant heart to purify bad karma right at that moment.

𝐎𝐌 𝐁𝐄𝐍𝐙𝐀 𝐒𝐀𝐓𝐓𝐎 𝐇𝐔𝐌

7. Medicine Buddha Mantra

If a living being (for example, an ant) is accidentally stepped on by us causing its death, we can recite the Medicine Buddha mantra, and then blow it onto their body.

Thanks to this action, they have the opportunity to escape rebirth in the evil realms and will obtain a better rebirth. When you think about the number of animals that continuously die, such as worms, insects, and countless other creatures... The number of them who accumulate enough virtuous karma to have someone recite a mantra for them and then blow it onto them is extremely rare (like seeing stars rise during the day).

In the Medicine Buddha Sutra, it is also taught that if anyone regularly recites the Medicine Buddha mantra, they will be healthy and live long.

Ta ya tha Om Bech kan ze Bech kan ze Maha Bech kan ze ra za sa mong ga te so ha

8. EARTH DEITY MANTRA:

Nam mo tam man da mot da nam, an do ro do ro, dia vy tat ba ha. (7 times)

This mantra is recited when you want to purify a piece of land, when moving to a new place… You can combine reciting the mantra with sprinkling mustard seeds around to ward off evil.

tieu_de: Descend to Hell for the Crime of Filial Impiety
tom_tat: On the Saturday night after her mother passed away, she saw her mother return, the story she told made her stunned. This woman with the surname Chau was about forty years old. According to her story, she had only recently begun to have a belief in God and Buddha.
noi_dung:
DESCENDING TO HELL FOR THE CRIME OF UNFILIALITY

The seventh night after her mother passed away, she saw her mother return, and the story she told made her feel stunned.

This woman, surname Chau, is around forty years old. According to her account, she had only recently embraced faith in the Buddha and often printed free scriptures for people with the wish of using the name of her recently deceased mother to perform merit. Her mother's story was extremely strange, making unfilial children gasp in shock.

During the Mid-Autumn Festival in 2009, her mother fell gravely ill and passed away. Speaking of the cause of her mother's illness is truly sorrowful; it was actually because her sister-in-law once quarreled with her mother, causing her mother so much distress that she died from shock. Her sister-in-law is a person who is not filial to her parents-in-law; quarreling with her mother-in-law was a daily occurrence. Her father-in-law was paralyzed on one side of his body, yet she never paid any attention or cared. After her mother-in-law passed away, the daughter-in-law did not show any remorse or regret. Her elder sister-in-law could not remain silent about this.

In the middle of Saturday night, she sat alone in the living room holding a photo of her mother, recalling the love her mother had given her while she was alive. Exhausted and sorrowful, she dozed off. At that moment, she suddenly heard her mother calling her. Startled, she woke up. Her mother suddenly appeared in front of her, but her mother's appearance shocked her. Her mother was still wearing the clothes she had on before she passed, but her body was covered in chains. Looking at her, she seemed to be in great suffering. She had to summon all her courage to ask:

"Mom, is that you?"

Her mother answered: “My daughter, after I die, when I look at the incense altar, seeing you really makes my heart ache. Every day I cry a lot, and tonight is the night of soul return, so the King of Hell has agreed to let the bull-headed, horse-faced ghost take me to visit you.”

She quickly asked: “Mother, what do you mean by looking at the incense altar, the bull-headed, horse-faced ghost… what are those?”

Her mother replied: “The incense tower is used after death; through it, one can see the situation of the family in the living world. The ox-headed, horse-faced ghosts are the guardians of hell; they are like the police on earth. They are outside the door waiting for me, and I am about to be taken back to hell to undergo punishment.”

“Mom, why are you being sent to hell to undergo punishment?”

“My child, only after death did I realize how great my mistakes were. I died so early because your sister-in-law made me so angry that I died from it; this is also the retribution that I have to endure.”

When my mother was young, she used to treat my grandmother badly. My grandfather died young, and my grandmother lived with her father and mother. Whenever she did something that wasn’t to my mother’s liking, my mother would get furious and scold her severely. She was afraid of my mother, no different from a mouse fearing a cat, and she didn’t even dare to breathe heavily. At that time, my mother felt very proud, believing herself to be the true mistress of the house; when my mother said one thing, she didn’t dare to say another. There is a secret I didn’t know: my grandmother became ill and died because she was angry with my mother.

The day before my mother passed away, she saw a devil with a bull's head and a horse's face coming with chains to tie her up. She screamed very loudly, and we thought she was having a nightmare. At that moment, her soul had already been taken away. It wasn't until she reached hell that she realized that being unfilial to one's parents carries such a heavy sin.

"Mother said that grandmother died because she made her angry... (at this moment, there was the sound of footsteps; her husband stepped out of the room) he said:

"Who are you talking to?"

- "I'm talking to my mother, she came to visit me today."

– “Where is Mom? Why can't you see her? Have you been hallucinating because you've been so sorrowful lately?”

– “No, tonight is the night of soul return, the day when Mom comes home to visit. I was talking to Mom, can't you see she is standing there?” – “I can't see anything.”

– “Mom, why does he say he can't see you?”

“Your husband cannot see me, my daughter. Your fate is also very unfortunate; the karma your father created is being passed down to you, which is why you ended up with a domineering and strict husband like him.”

At that moment, her husband dragged her back to the room; she didn’t want to go. Suddenly, her husband shouted:

“There’s a ghost,” and ran straight into the room, slamming the door shut.

“Mom, what’s wrong with him?”

– The mother turned to the door and said: “Thank you for letting me tell everything to my daughter.”

Then she turned back and continued:

“Your husband is scared by a devil with a bull’s head and a horse’s face. It's hiding in the room; it probably won't dare come out to bother us anymore.”

"Wasn't it them who tied you up and brought you here?

Why are they even helping you and me?" the daughter asked in surprise.

"That is their responsibility. Today I am telling my own story so that later you can tell everyone, hoping they will understand how severe the sin of being unfilial is. I also wish that unfilial children will know to repent and feel remorse. If not, later they will also be sent to hell to endure torment like I am today, and they might even be boiled in a cauldron."

"What? Boiling oil? I thought it was just a rumor, I didn't expect it to be true?"

"My child, how could it not be true? Evil people will definitely go to hell. They don't believe in cause and effect and are not afraid of punishment, so they dare to do anything."

"Tomorrow you and your sister go buy a grave, because your father doesn't have many days left to live."

"Mom, why are you saying that?"

“His guilt is also not light at all; when my mother scolded his grandmother, he not only did not stop it, but also joined in scolding her very harshly. He is truly a completely unfilial son. But there was also a time when my mother blamed my grandmother, and my father beat my mother to a pulp. He is very disgusting and terrifying, even ghosts and gods would shake their heads because of him.

The officials in hell look down the most on domestic abusers and unfilial children. A few years ago, he suffered a stroke that paralyzed half of his body; this is also the karma he created himself. Moreover, he lived a life ignored by his children, and after death, he was condemned to hell to endure suffering.

"That's really scary, but how can that be? When mother was alive, although she didn't treat grandmother well, she did a lot of good deeds. Didn't she donate a lot of money during last year's earthquake? Mother can't be considered a bad person, so how could she be punished?"

"My child, how can you understand that doing a few good deeds cannot make up for the sin of being unfilial. Think about it, a child who is unfilial surely is not truly a good person. I donated money for your grandmother when she was in trouble because I was afraid your youngest aunt would say I was stingy, but I never expected that every thought, every intention of mine would be recorded. The judge said that throughout my life I did very few good deeds, and if I did any, they were only small things, or just pretending to do good deeds, so how could I make up for the great sin of unfiliality."

“Mom, what should I do so that you suffer less? I will go to the temple to perform a liberation ceremony for you, right? I heard that a liberation ceremony can reduce the sins of the deceased and might even allow them to go to Heaven?”

"If everyone goes to the temple to perform rituals to liberate their relatives and friends in order to ascend to heaven and no longer endure suffering, then giving money to children for them to perform liberation rituals before death would allow one to go to Heaven? How could there be bad people in Heaven? Children who wish to show filial piety can perform liberation rituals for deceased parents and grandparents, and that is fine. However, it is best for children to do many good deeds, wholeheartedly help others, and advise people to do good, so that the mother can reduce her karmic sins. The judges in the underworld also said that you are someone who has a connection with Buddha; in the future, you will walk on the path of cultivation, and you must remember to be diligent."Truly practicing, if your child becomes accomplished, the mother down here will also be saved, and only then will the mother truly ascend to Heaven.”

“My daughter, it's time, the ox-headed, horse-faced demons are urging me, I have to go now.” “Why can't I see them?” she asked.

“Silly, it's best that you don't see them. They are the fearsome gods of hell, who punish evildoers. Only the wicked have to face them.”

"Yes, I will definitely follow what you said, Mom, so don't worry." After that, Ms. Chau immediately recorded her mother's words, hoping to share her mother's story with everyone to awaken children who are not filial to their parents and grandparents... She also said that her husband, having gone through that day's events, now believes in the existence of gods, Buddhas, ghosts, and spirits. She said she wanted to perform a ritual to help her mother find peace in the afterlife, and when she mentioned donating for charitable deeds, he agreed and proactively gave her money. This is why people say: "Why don't people shed tears when they haven't seen the coffin?"

Thieu Ky (translator)

Question: I often hear that children are happy or suffering because of the Merits and Virtues left by their parents or grandparents. If we do good deeds or create bad karma, will the people around us also be affected even if they do nothing at all?

Answer: The merits or karma of a person can affect those around them (including grandparents, parents, spouses, children, as well as people living nearby such as neighbors, colleagues...) There are the following ways of influence:

1. "Like attracts like": grandparents and parents create virtue, and then karma arranges for them to be born as children and grandchildren who created virtue in the past. When they are born, they enjoy happiness and honor. That virtue was created by them in the past, while the grandparents and parents, because they also have virtue, give birth to honorable children and grandchildren to enjoy a good reputation... conversely, grandparents and parents who create evil karma experience the same in a similar way.

2. Those who have created merit are reborn as their own grandchildren to enjoy blessings. (Doing evil is the opposite.)

3. "Attracting karmic merit or demerit": a person with great merit or heavy karma can attract circumstances so that the good or bad karma of those around them manifests when they appear. For example, a father commits such great evil that, after some time, his child has an accident and dies. Normally, the child would only experience such an accident two lifetimes later, but now that karmic result manifests in the present (in fact, each person has a lot of hidden merit or sin; the child is not lacking in karma from consuming meat or killing from countless past lives). Or a husband, due to great merit, is sure to get a beautiful wife, but when he marries, he chooses a woman of average looks.Usually, not beautiful, after a period of time, the appearance of the wife will change and become beautiful. That is due to the wife’s merit. Normally, she would need three lifetimes to become that beautiful, but because of the husband’s merit attracting her own, her merit manifests early. There are some very special people; wherever they go, everyone around them experiences misfortune, also due to this principle.

4. "Mutual karmic connection", due to deep affinity and debts with parents, children may bear the punishment on behalf of their parents; this act of bearing punishment is considered as settling the debt with the parents (as in the story "Blessing" previously posted in the group 'Reincarnation & Karma'). Usually, we encounter the opposite situation, where parents owe a debt to their children, so the parents' merit is enjoyed by the children (as an inheritance), which is considered as repaying the debt. Sentient beings who have a deep karmic debt with each other also experience similar situations.

Collected

tieu_de: DO NOT GIVE BLOOD CHARITY TO MONSTROUS CREATURES!
tom_tat: Currently, on social media, a post about giving leftover food to hungry spirits, to avoid committing the sin of wastefulness, is widely followed and shared by many Buddhists. However, this is a misguided view and should not be held.
noi_dung:
SHOULD NOT OFFER CARNIVOROUS ALMS TO DEMONIC BEASTS!

Currently, on social media, there is a circulating post about giving leftover food to hungry ghosts to avoid committing the sin of wastefulness, which has attracted a lot of attention and sharing from Buddhists. However, this is a wrong view and should not exist among Buddhist practitioners. The danger of that post is that it encourages people to rely on it, freely wasting food without developing the habit of contentment and frugality, and also creating the bad karma of giving poor-quality food to hungry ghosts while hoping for temporary merit. This is completely contrary to the scriptures, so this is, indeed, the words of a demon.

According to the Trung A-hàm Sutra, in the Pham Chi section, Tu-đat-đa Sutra, number 155, the Buddha taught:

“O lay practitioner, if one gives coarse and inferior alms, gives without faith, gives without intention, does not give with one’s own hands, does not go personally to give, gives without contemplation, gives without faith, gives without considering karma and its results, one should understand that one will receive retribution accordingly. The mind does not desire to have a beautiful house, does not desire a beautiful carriage, does not desire fine clothes, does not desire delicious food and drink, does not desire the goodness of the five senses. Why? Because almsgiving is not done sincerely. O lay practitioner, you should know that one will receive retribution accordingly.”

This means that with a mindset lacking reverence, taking your leftover food and instead of throwing it away, pouring it onto an empty patch of land while praying to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in all ten directions to witness the merit of this act of giving of leftover food—namely, bad food to the beings of hungry ghosts—in the hope of receiving good karmic results is impossible. Because it is giving without faith, giving without reflection, and giving without intention, not out of compassion for the spirits of those deceased who suffer in the realm of hungry ghosts, even if they may be relatives of many generations of your own. Therefore, it is impure giving, arising from the motive of fear of karmic consequences for wasting food, which will attractto give poverty in the future. Not like what the Buddha taught.

According to the Essence of the Vinaya Sutra, Rescuing Ānanda from the Mouth of the Hungry Ghost Ritual (Chinese translation: Tang Dynasty - Tripitaka Monk Butong's translation, Vietnamese translation by Huyen Thanh), when the Buddha was in the city of Kāśī, Ānanda saw a hungry ghost named Diệm Khẩu who said to Ānanda: “In three days your lifespan will end, and you will be reborn in the path of Hungry Ghosts (Pretas).” At that time, Ānanda asked the ghost king if there was any way to escape this retribution. Diệm Khẩu said: “If you can give alms to hundreds of thousands of countless, innumerable hungry ghosts, Brahman sages, Yama judges, karmic officials, underworld deities, attendants and subordinate spirits, and the souls of the deceased,long…equality alms are given everywhere so that the hungry ghosts can eat and drink, then he will have a longer life.

Ananda was alarmed and begged the Buddha for guidance. The Buddha taught because Ananda taught the Dharani called the Infinite Sovereign Self-Existent Radiance Tathagata Dharani, to save the realm of hungry ghosts. However, the Buddha instructed that one must "use pure food, never used before, keep for offering, store in clean vessels, and then offer to the spirits and demons."

If so, "one will be endowed with immeasurable Merit, certainly equal to the group of merits earned by offering hundreds of thousands of verses to the Tathagata without deviation, lifespan will be extended; health, beauty, and wholesome faculties will be increased and complete. All non-human beings, Yakshas, Rakshasas, and evil spirits will not dare to harm. Furthermore, one will accomplish immeasurable authority and virtue."

"It will also make that person's mind, regarding what is seen and heard, cleanly understand, complete with wholesome faculties, quickly attaining Supreme Perfect Enlightenment. All enemies will not be able to harm."

Thus, according to the scripture “Dhāraṇī for Ananda to save the hungry ghost Diệm Khẩu, for all sentient beings,” the Buddha affirmed that making offerings to the preta (hungry ghosts) is as meritorious as making offerings to hundreds of thousands of countless Tathāgatas. Therefore, how could one throw away leftover food and then pray to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions for that leftover to be transformed into nectar to be offered to the pretas?

Moreover, such giving will bring about the consequences of poverty, illness, and accidents in the present life due to wasting food and offending spirits, and in the future will be reborn as hungry ghosts, eating leftover food, or will be born as poor, miserable humans who only eat leftovers because of a selfish, narrow-minded heart, constantly suffering from unfulfilled desires, due to impure giving.

It is best for leftover food to be poured into ponds, lakes, rivers, or streams to offer to fish; or at the base of trees, to offer to birds, dogs, cats, ants. This should be done if it is a type of food that animals can eat. In addition, one should practice the virtue of 'desiring little, knowing sufficiency,' 'valuing merit, saving virtue,' to avoid food waste. Each day, you can use a little less, to dedicate the merit to those who are suffering from hunger around the world.

Or, for pure foods, one should cultivate the intention to make offerings to the Three Jewels before eating and dedicate the merit to all beings in the dharma realm so that they may be satisfied, abundant in both material and dharma gifts.

For laypeople at home, during the Ullambana season, Lunar New Year, death anniversaries, or when performing any religious rite, it is advisable to invite monks or follow the Mengshan Food Offering ritual oneself to make offerings to the hungry spirits. In this way, it aligns with the compassion of the Buddhas.

In general, food offerings have seven merits:

1. Protection by spirits and deities.

2. Avoid unexpected accidents.

3. Not disturbed by spirits.

4. Longevity, vitality, and abundant wealth.

5. Enemies and grudges cannot harm, easily resolving grievances.

6. Sow vast connections with sentient beings. Virtue covers all creatures.

7. Ultimately attain Buddhahood.

Even in the Tu Dat Da Sutra, the Buddha teaches: "If one gives even coarse or unattractive food with faith, giving with a giving mind, giving with one's own hands, going personally to give, thinking while giving, giving out of faith, contemplating karma and its results while giving, one should consider that the rewards will be exactly as such, arising from the mind's desire for a beautiful house, a fine vehicle, beautiful clothes and blankets, delicious food and drink, and the good results of the five desires. Why? Because one gives with sincerest intention."

However, look at the example of King Ashoka; it was also due to his sincere devotion in a previous life when, as a child, he offered a handful of sand to the Buddha to be spread along the path for walking meditation, that he was reborn as a king. But because sand is an inferior offering, although he became king, he had a dark and unattractive body. That is the result of sincere intention in giving inferior things. How much more so if one intentionally offers leftover food to hungry ghosts? That is truly a deluded view born of ignorance. Therefore, if one wants to enjoy good results in future lives, one should offer the best things for giving and donation.

Namo Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.

tieu_de: Struggling in work because of ingratitude and betrayal
tom_tat: In the story of cause and effect, it is said that long ago there was a very poor person, struggling in work, who could never get a job or was fired shortly after starting. One day, this person went to see a Zen master to
noi_dung:
STRUCK WITH PROFESSIONAL SETBACKS DUE TO INGRAITITUDE AND DISLOYALTY

In the story of cause and effect, it is said that long ago there was a very poor person, struggling in work, unable to find a job, or if employed for a short time, would be fired.

One day, this person went to see a Zen master to ask about the reason why life was so unsettled and difficult. The Zen master, a saintly monk who had attained enlightenment, said: "The karmic causes from your past life are nothing extraordinary. It is precisely your ungrateful heart toward those who have helped you and toward your superiors."

In a previous life, he worked as a rickshaw puller. Because he was hardworking, he was often assigned tasks by his employer. That day, the employer sent him to pull the rickshaw for an official who had an urgent matter. On the way, he became acquainted with the official and, in turn, received assistance from the official for a good job with a good salary, an easy workload, and no need to pull rickshaws anymore. However, once he got the new job, he immediately left without saying goodbye or thanking his old employer. Because of his ungrateful heart, not considering the merits of his former employer who helped him switch professions and work in a good place, he is now experiencing karmic retribution, such asso.

In another past life, he was a wealthy, influential man, but without an official title, so he asked a matchmaker to help him obtain a government position. The matchmaker needed to be paid, but he didn't pay immediately and promised to pay the matchmaker once he received the position. However, after he was appointed, he turned his back and cheated the person who had helped him out of payment.

Due to this karmic connection, he was punished with obstacles in his career path. In that past life, he had to be a rickshaw puller because he sowed two causes:

- First, because of owing money, he has an unstable job, having to work as a cart puller, a servant to others, pulling a cart to pay off debt for others.

- Second, he cannot have a career because when he becomes an official, he is ungrateful to those who help him, betraying them. When he is an official, he is above many people; now he must be below for others to ride on his back.

In this Dharma world, we see interwoven conditions; one thing becomes the cause for another, which then becomes the condition for something else. Therefore, understanding the principle of cause and effect is understanding the Dharma, but not everyone finds it easy to comprehend.

Furthermore, we should remember that as disciples of the Buddha, no matter who helps us even with a drop of water, we should always remember it. Even if someone’s help is as small as a speck of dust, we must be grateful. The Buddha taught that when someone does a favor, we must remember it, but when we do a favor, we should forget it. That is the virtue of a child of the Buddha.

**********************************

BAD KARMA HAS BEEN SOWN, WHAT SHOULD BE DONE TO PREVENT BAD REPERCUSSIONS?

People often consider themselves very kind because they have done quite a number of good deeds. When they encounter accidents or difficulties, or illness, if they do not blame heaven, they surely blame others. They think that heaven is not fair to them, wondering why, despite having done many good deeds, they still end up in dire circumstances. From that, they lose faith, no longer wish to continue doing good deeds, and few think about repaying karma, which leads to feelings of regret and desire to reform.

According to the law of Cause and Effect, planting melons yields melons, planting beans yields beans. The melon seed is the cause; if the initial cause is not good, then when sown into the ground, it will result in melons that are not good in the future. A bad cause is an example of evil, a good cause is an example of good. When we sow melon seeds into the ground, knowing they are not good seeds, and then we also sow good bean seeds, will the harvest be all beans? It cannot be, planting melons gives melons, planting beans gives beans, melons cannot turn into beans. It is not that if we plant many beans, melons cannot bear fruit; each type yields its own distinct fruit.Therefore, merit and sin cannot be mixed together. Although they have done many good deeds, there are also quite a few evil deeds. The good deeds, due to insufficient conditions, have not yet borne good results. As for the evil deeds, because the conditions are complete, the evil consequences manifest. This is where the principle lies.

It should be known that every day we sow both good and evil seeds. These seeds absolutely do not disappear; they are stored in our store consciousness. The process from seed to fruit always requires a condition. Therefore, the Buddha said that dependent origination is like that. If we create too many evil seeds, we will suffer evil results. If we want to completely eliminate evil results, it is like taking a melon seed and preventing conditions for it to sprout, by putting the seed into a sealed jar so it does not come into contact with soil, water, or air... Even after 100 years, it will never bear fruit because there are no conditions for it to germinate.

If a Buddhist plants that seed into the ground with sufficient conditions such as water, light... it will grow very well. Therefore, if we want to achieve good results, we must sow good seeds and good conditions.

In the past, due to ignorance, we created countless evil causes. Now, after having attained enlightenment, seeing the evil causes we have sown makes us startled and fearful, and we wish for these evil causes not to bear evil results. Is it possible? Yes, it is. How? By avoiding contact with evil conditions, then without conditions, the causes cannot bear fruit. So how can we avoid evil conditions? Reciting the Buddha's name can avoid evil conditions. In daily life, apart from our responsibilities and duties, do not try to add anything else. When there is free time, in the four postures: walking, standing, lying down, or sitting, do not depart from reciting the Buddha's name A.Amitabha Buddha. Thus, one will avoid contact with external evil conditions. And when there are no conditions, even if there are evil causes, they cannot bear evil results. If there is no evil retribution, then life, as well as our path of study and practice, will certainly be smooth. Venerable Master Jingkong

Please Regularly Recite Amitabha Buddha 🙏🙏🙏

St ADIDAPHAT

NAMO REPENTANCE BODHISATTVA🙏🙏🙏

**********************************

The Retribution of the Evil Acts Against Buddhism by King Chu Vu Emperor

According to Chinese historical records, during the Southern and Northern Dynasties, Buddhism in Northern Zhou and Northern Qi was very prosperous. After ascending the throne in Northern Zhou, Emperor Wu of Zhou had the thought: "Monastics have no property, do not work, and do not pay taxes, which reduces the state's financial income and affects the grand enterprise of unifying the realm." Afterwards, he issued an edict to suppress Buddhism, so that all Taoist practices, statues, and scriptures had to be destroyed, the monks (i.e., the Sangha) were abolished, and all Taoist priests were ordered to return to secular life.

In many places, Buddha statues were melted, scriptures were burned, Buddhist stupas were destroyed, temples became residences for secular people, and all monks and nuns were forced to return to lay life. At this time, quite a few monks went to the capital to protect Buddhism, presenting arguments of right and wrong to Emperor Wu of Zhou, but they were all suppressed and expelled by the king.

By the year 557, after Emperor Wu of the Zhou Dynasty destroyed the Northern Qi, he issued a decree to eliminate Buddhism in Northern Qi, resulting in the burning down of all temples and shrines. At that time, Venerable Huiyuan (the Patriarch of the Pure Land School) loudly condemned this violent act and advised Emperor Wu of the Zhou, but the emperor did not listen and continued to destroy Buddhist Dharma openly.

As a result, over forty thousand temples in Northern Qi were converted into residences for royal and noble families, all Buddhist sutras and statues were destroyed, monks and nuns were forced to return to lay life, and the property of the temples was transferred to the government offices.

Not long after, King Zhou Wu of Chu suddenly suffered from a very strange illness; his whole body was covered with sores and ulcers, and there was no medicine that could cure it. King Zhou Wu of Chu died tragically, and when his son ascended the throne, he was also destroyed three years later, and the Sui dynasty replaced the Chu dynasty.

Through the above stories, it is hoped that everyone understands that cause and effect are real. From there, we should deeply believe in karma, always diligently practice Buddhist teachings, cultivate ourselves, and plant wholesome seeds so as not to receive bad consequences later.

COLLECTION

P/s Reciting sutras, chanting mantras, copying scriptures, bowing to the Buddha should all be done with a sincere heart, not merely reading for the Buddha to hear. Chanting sutras for the Buddha to hear in hopes of receiving something in return is like giving a few cakes and expecting cookies in return. That is why many people offer a lot in charity, yet cannot become Buddhas, because these people, although doing many good deeds and accumulating much merit, have not truly acted from the heart. There may still be traces of vanity, arrogance, harmful speech, false speech, sexual misconduct, lack of virtue, excessive greed and selfishness, and they have not truly attained enlightenment, then they blame that chanting the Buddha’s name is not effective. People make excusesYou can cover the eyes of the world, but you cannot hide from the eyes of King Yama. The net of heaven is vast; whether one is virtuous or deceitful, everyone must abide by the law of cause and effect and cannot escape it. Buddha does not need you to write beautifully for Him to see. Copying scriptures without sincerity is not as good as writing the phrase NAM MÔ A DI ĐÀ PHẬT. Why? Because when you just copy, your mind does not pay attention to the meaning or understand it. Often, you might even miss punctuation. Therefore, please diligently copy by yourself instead of just copying superficially. It’s useless. Buddha wants to see the mind. Remember, it is the mind, not the writing, that matters if the mind is still full of greed, anger, and hatred. Writing without the mind present is useless.

Through these actions, you can donate money, participate in humanitarian blood drives, help elderly people who are lonely and helpless, assist children without shelter in returning to school, repair bridges and roads, release animals… to work on improving your fate. This is the practice of doing good deeds to alter one’s destiny: practicing vegetarianism, giving alms, releasing animals, smiling, and being grateful to everyone even if they treat you badly. Sharing food and clothing with the poor and knowing how to help friends when they are weak or in need.

And it is important that in everything you do, think more for others than for yourself, then your good karma will increase over time. Try to work hard, not be lazy, and you should not ask for help from anyone when you still have your hands and your mind to discern right from wrong. Do not complain to the heavens or blame the earth for why you are suffering. Instead, strive, strive with all your strength to work. You should not beg anyone when you still have healthy hands, constantly asking or doing dishonest work; that will not bring merit, but instead make you a debtor in the next life.
